Then they spent some more time playing in the park. It was a wonderful day!

Tom and Anna were playing with scissors and paper. They wanted to make snowflakes and stars. Tom was very good at cutting shapes. He showed Anna how to fold the paper and cut along the edges. Anna tried to copy him, but she was not very careful. She cut her thumb with the scissors. It hurt a lot and it bled.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Anna cried. "I cut my thumb! It hurts!"

Tom heard her cry and ran to her. He saw her thumb and the blood. He felt sorry for her, but he also felt disgusted. He did not like blood. It made him feel sick.

"Anna, don't cry. Let me see your thumb," Tom said. He took her hand and looked at the cut. It was not very big, but it was deep. He knew he had to help her. He remembered what his mom told him to do when he got a cut.

"Anna, we have to wash your thumb and put a band-aid on it. Come with me to the bathroom," Tom said. He led her to the sink and turned on the water. He washed her thumb gently and dried it with a towel. He found a band-aid in the cabinet and put it on her thumb.

"There, all done. Does it feel better?" Tom asked.

Anna nodded. She felt less pain and more calm. She smiled at Tom and thanked him.

"Thank you, Tom. You are very kind. You are a good friend," Anna said.

Tom smiled back. He was glad he could help her. He was a good friend.

"Anna, you are welcome. You are a good friend too. Do you want to play something else?" Tom asked.

Anna nodded. She did not want to play with scissors and paper anymore. She wanted to play something safer and funnier.

"Tom, can we play with the blocks and make a castle?" Anna asked.

Tom nodded. He liked blocks and castles. He agreed with Anna.

"Anna, yes, let's play with the blocks and make a castle. That sounds like fun," Tom said.

They went to the playroom and found the blocks. They started to build a big and beautiful castle. They forgot about the scissors and the cut. They had fun. They were happy.

Sam and Mia were hungry. They wanted to eat something good. They asked their mom what they could have for lunch.

Mom said, "I have a surprise for you. I made a special meal for you. It is very impressive. You will love it."

Sam and Mia were curious. They wondered what the meal was. They followed their mom to the kitchen. They saw a big pot on the stove. Mom lifted the lid and showed them what was inside.

"Look, it is macaroni and cheese with broccoli and chicken. It is very yummy and healthy. I recommend you try it," Mom said.

Sam and Mia smiled. They liked macaroni and cheese. They liked broccoli and chicken too. They thought the meal looked impressive. They thanked their mom and took their plates to the table. They ate the meal and enjoyed it very much. They told their mom it was the best lunch ever. Mom was happy. She hugged them and said, "You are welcome. I am glad you liked it."

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the field near their house. They liked to run, jump, and pick flowers. One day, they saw a big red plant in the field. It had many small round things on it.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Let's try it," Tom said.

He picked one of the round things and bit it. He made a funny face and spit it out.

"Ow! It's spicy! It hurts my mouth!" he cried.

Lily laughed. She wanted to try it too. She picked another round thing and bit it. She also made a funny face and spit it out.

"Ow! You're right! It's spicy! It hurts my mouth too!" she cried.

They ran to the stream and drank some water. They felt better.

"Let's not try that plant again," Lily said.

"OK. Let's play something else," Tom said.

They went to the other side of the field and found a swing. They took turns swinging and had fun. They forgot about the spicy plant.

Once upon a time, there was a warm little house in the woods. In this house lived a kind man who liked to mind the lumber. He would cut the lumber and stack it near his warm house. He loved his job very much.

One day, while the man was minding the lumber, he heard a tiny sound. He looked around and saw a little bird. The little bird was cold and hungry. The man felt sad for the bird, so he took it to his warm house. He gave the bird some food and a warm place to sleep.

The little bird was so happy to be warm and full. It stayed with the man, and they became good friends. The man would mind the lumber, and the little bird would sing happy songs. They lived in the warm little house together, and they were very happy.

One day, Jack heard a noise coming from inside his kitchen. He went inside to take a look and saw his brother Sam. Sam was hungry and had opened all of the cupboards, hoping to find something to eat. 

"What are you looking for?" asked Jack. 

"Food!" answered Sam. 

Jack smiled and grabbed a cup from the table. He said, "Here, hold this cup and I'll look for something for you." 

Sam happily took the cup and watched as Jack looked for food. Jack soon found an apple and put it into the cup. 

"Here you go," said Jack, handing the cup to Sam. 

Sam smiled when he saw the apple. He thanked Jack and they both went outside to eat and play.

Once upon a time there lived a tall clown. He was special because he could make everyone laugh. The clown just loved seeing people smile. One day he wanted to learn something new, so he decided to search for something fun. 

He looked left and right but couldn't find anything. Suddenly, he spotted a funny looking hat on top of a tree. He climbed up the tall tree to get the hat. When he put it on, he felt funny and started laughing. People around started laughing too!

He liked the hat so much, he decided to wear it forever. He learned that when he wore the hat, he could make people smile. He was so happy to learn this secret. From then on, the clown was the happiest in town!

Mummy and Daddy took baby to have a bath. Baby smiled and splashed. Mummy warned baby that the bath water was dangerous and to be careful. Baby nodded, understanding mummy's warning. 

Then Daddy put bubbles in the water and baby was so excited! As the bubbles filled the tub, baby started to laugh. Mummy and Daddy watched, laughing too. 

Mummy explained again that the water was dangerous, but Daddy helped baby to stand up and the fun began! Baby squealed with joy as the bubbles and the warm water tickled their skin. Daddy told baby to splash and jump, and baby happily did. 

Finally, Mummy and Daddy decided it was time for baby to come out. Baby pouted, but Mummy said it was okay. They all got out of the tub, and Mummy wrapped baby in a big, warm towel. Baby felt safe and happy, and they all headed off to bed.

Once upon a time there was a harmless cage in a meadow. Every day, sheep and deer came to the meadow to eat the fresh green grass. Chief among them was Little Pete, a lamb who loved to explore.

One day, Little Pete noticed something strange in the meadow. It was a cage with a strange lock. Little Pete went close to the cage to get a better look. He could see something inside, but he could not see what it was. He called out to the other animals, â€œWhat is this?â€

The other animals said to Little Pete, â€œItâ€™s nothing to worry about. Just stay away from the cage.â€ Little Pete was curious but he did as he was told.

A few days later, Little Pete was playing in the meadow when he heard a loud noise. He ran to the source of the sound and he saw the strange cage. The lock had been opened and something was coming out of it. It was flying, but it was not a bird.

Little Pete was scared, but soon he realized that the flying creature was harmless. It was a butterfly! It had been trapped in the cage but Little Pete had released it and set it free.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends in the park. One day, she found a funny-looking map on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look, Timmy! I found a map!" Lily exclaimed.

"What's a map?" Timmy asked.

"It's a picture that shows us where to go," Lily explained.

"Let's follow the map and see where it takes us!" Timmy said.

So, Lily and Timmy followed the map and it led them to a big tree. Under the tree, they found a box full of dress-up clothes. They put on silly hats and dresses, and had a lot of fun pretending to be different characters.

"This is the best day ever!" Lily said.

"I agree! Thanks for finding the map, Lily," Timmy said.

From that day on, Lily and Timmy went on many adventures together, always using the funny map to guide them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play at the beach. One day, she found a shiny oyster shell and decided to take it home with her. She showed it to her mom and dad, who were very proud of her.

But later that night, Lily started to worry. She was afraid that the oyster's family might be missing it. She told her mom and dad, "I'm worried that the oyster is frightened and wants to go back to its family."

Her mom and dad smiled and told her not to worry. They explained that the oyster was just a shell and that it didn't have a family. Lily felt better and went to bed happy, with her new oyster shell by her side.

Once upon a time, there was an eager elephant. He wanted to turn around the world. So he packed a small bag and headed out. He turned left at the forest and kept turning left until he reached the sea. He saw a beautiful boat and decided to turn it into his own. So he hopped on it and turned the boat around to sail far away. He sailed for days and nights, turning left and right when needed. He was so eager to explore the world. Finally, after weeks of turning and sailing, he made it back home. What a wonderful journey!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to jog in the park with her mommy. One day, they saw a big tower in the distance. Lily asked her mommy, "What is that big tower?" Her mommy replied, "It's a serious building where people work."

As they got closer to the tower, they saw a man standing outside. He looked serious too. Lily asked the man, "What do you do in the tower?" The man replied, "I work in an office and help people with their problems."

Lily was very curious and asked the man more questions. The man was happy to answer and they had a nice conversation. After that, Lily and her mommy continued their jog in the park, feeling happy and curious about the world around them.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lola. She loved to help her mom with lots of things around the house. One day, Lola was in the kitchen helping her mom make lunch.

But then, she started talking to her mom too much. "I want to make the sandwich! Let me do it!" Lola said. But her mom was very careful and shook her head no.

Lola became very frustrated and angry. She wanted to help her mom make the sandwich. She pouted and made a sad face. Her lips were sticking out.

Lola's mom smiled at her. Then, her mom kneeled down and told Lola to be careful. She said that if Lola wanted to help, she had to be extra careful.

Lola was happy and she smiled big. She nodded her head and promised to be careful. Then, the two of them went back to making lunch and having fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a man and a dog. The man wanted to test the dog to see if it was a smart dog. He pretended to like a fake bone and asked the dog to fetch it. The dog was so clever! It knew the bone was not real and tried to escape. The man could not catch the dog and it ran away! He was so proud of the dog. The man was very happy and he brought the dog some real bone!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play. Every day the girl would go searching through the forest to see what fun she could find.

One day, the little girl spotted something special - a beautiful mushroom! She decided to play a game and hid the mushroom and then searched for it again.

The little girl quickly tired of the game, but she knew she'd found something special and decided to keep the beautiful mushroom. 

She took it to her garden, when she got home, and planted it there. Every day she would go to check on the mushroom and sing it a special song. 

When the mushroom grew bigger and bigger, the little girl was so proud. She kept playing with it, and it became her very best friend. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a chimney. It was boring. It just sat there.

One day, something very exciting happened. A big gust of wind came and changed the chimney! It blew the chimney over onto its side.

The chimney was now a lot more fun than before. Kids in the neighbourhood came to play on it. They climbed up the chimney, jumped off, and slid down its side.

Suddenly there were all sorts of games to play with the chimney. Kids had a lot of fun!

The chimney that was once boring was now full of energy and life. It was a very exciting change!

Once upon a time, there was a big board. It was hot in the sun and the board glowed. Two friends, Dan and Jo, were having so much fun. They ran up and down, jumped, and laughed all day.

Dan found a big stick and started writing words on the hot board. His words glowed in the sun. He wrote "happy", "kind" and "nice". Jo thought it was cool and wanted to write too. She wrote "funny" and "smile". 

When they were done, they stepped back and smiled. The hot board glowed with their special words. They agreed to keep this board forever, so their friendship and kindness could glow in the sun, always.

Once upon a time there was a fish who lived in the sea. He loved swimming and exploring. One day, he wanted to try something new. He used his fin to dig a hole in the sand. He used it as a secret spot to hide from the other fish.

The fish found a soft toy and put it in the hole. He had lots of fun playing with it. Soon, more fish came and wanted to join in the fun. They used the soft toy to have a game. They all had so much fun playing together.

One day, a big wave came and took the fish's soft toy. The fish was very sad. He was about to swim away when he saw something strange in the hole. It was a shiny, special fish. He was so excited! He used the fish as a new toy and they played together. 

The fish was so happy to have a new friend and they played happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and caring bird named Tweetie. Tweetie loved to fly around and feel the motion of the wind beneath her wings. One day, Tweetie saw a little mouse who was very sad. The mouse was too small to fit into his hole, and he didn't know what to do.

Tweetie felt compassionate for the little mouse and decided to help. She tried to make the hole bigger so the mouse could fit, but she accidentally knocked over a big rock. The rock fell on the mouse and hurt him badly. Tweetie felt so sad that she couldn't help the mouse, and she flew away, feeling very guilty.

From that day on, Tweetie made sure to be more careful when helping others. She learned that sometimes even the kindest actions can have bad consequences.

Once there was a little girl. She was ready to fill up her big bucket. She had a big bag full of pins. She was so excited! She started filling the bucket with pins. She filled it so full that the pins started spilling out over the sides. She kept going until the bucket was overflowing with pins! The little girl smiled as she looked at her work. She was very happy and proud that she had filled her bucket up with so many pins. Now she was ready for her next adventure!

Sara and Ben like to play in the park. They run, slide, swing and laugh. They also like to look for pebbles. Pebbles are small and hard and have different colors and shapes. Sara and Ben have a game. They try to find pebbles that remind them of something.

One day, Sara finds a pebble that is orange and round. She shows it to Ben and says, "Look, this pebble reminds me of an orange. It is the same color and shape. Do you like oranges?" Ben nods and says, "Yes, I like oranges. They are sweet and juicy. Can I see your pebble?" Sara gives him the pebble and he holds it in his hand.

Ben looks around and sees a pebble that is white and flat. He picks it up and says, "Look, this pebble reminds me of a paper. It is the same color and shape. Do you like paper?" Sara nods and says, "Yes, I like paper. I can draw and write on it. Can I see your pebble?" Ben gives her the pebble and she holds it in her hand.

They keep playing and finding more pebbles that remind them of different things. They find pebbles that remind them of a leaf, a star, a cookie, a ball and a flower. They have fun and learn new words. They put all their pebbles in a bag and take them home. They show their pebbles to their mom and dad and tell them what they remind them of. Their mom and dad smile and hug them. They are proud of Sara and Ben. They say, "You are very smart and creative. We love you and your pebbles." Sara and Ben are happy and say, "We love you too. And we love our pebbles."

Once upon a time there were two friends, Larry and Ann. They were both very nice and liked to play together.

One day, Ann had an idea. She wanted to make some pictures. "Let's find a painter!" she said to Larry.

The two of them ran to find a painter. When they arrived at a shop, they saw a nice painter on the shelf. They decided to buy it.

When they got home, they opened the painter. Inside were two brushes and many colours. They were both very excited. 

Larry and Ann started to paint. They worked together to make a beautiful picture. When they had finished, they hugged each other. 

Suddenly, Larry and Ann had a problem. The painter was too big to fit back into the box!

Larry had an idea. "Let's separate the brushes and colours and put them in different boxes," he said.

The two friends worked together to separate the paint and brushes. When they were done, they put all the small boxes inside the painter box. They smiled with satisfaction. 

The two friends had solved their problem. They hugged each other and went on to make more pictures.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the beach with her family. They brought a cooler filled with yummy snacks like apples and crackers. Lily loved the beach because she could build sandcastles and play in the water.

One day, Lily saw a crab walking towards her cooler. She didn't want the crab to eat her snacks, so she yelled, "Stop!" The crab didn't listen and kept walking towards the cooler. Lily's dad saw what was happening and gently picked up the crab and moved it away. He told Lily that the crab was harmless and just wanted to explore.

Lily was happy that her snacks were safe and she could continue playing at the beach. She even saw some dolphins jumping in the water and it made her smile. She had a great day at the beach with her family. The end.

Anna liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they made shapes with their bodies and breathed slowly. It made them feel calm and happy. Anna's favorite shape was the tree. She stood on one foot and lifted the other to her knee. She put her hands together and looked at a spot on the wall.

"Good job, Anna, you are a beautiful tree," her mom said.

"Thank you, mom, you are a beautiful flower," Anna said. Her mom was lying on her back and had her legs in the air. She moved them like petals.

They heard a noise from the door. It was dad. He came home from work. He tried to open the door, but it was locked. He knocked and called, "Hello, anyone home?"

Anna and her mom smiled. They had a surprise for dad. They had made a cake for him. It was his birthday. They had put candles and sprinkles on it. It was delicate and yummy.

"Shh, don't say anything," Anna's mom whispered. "Let's go and unlock the door and surprise him."

They got up from their yoga mats and tiptoed to the door. Anna turned the key and opened the door. She saw dad's face. He looked surprised and happy.

"Surprise, dad, happy birthday!" Anna and her mom shouted. They hugged him and gave him the cake.

"Wow, thank you, Anna and mom, this is the best surprise ever!" dad said. He kissed them and blew out the candles. They all went to the kitchen and ate the cake. They laughed and talked and had fun. Anna felt warm and cozy. She loved her mom and dad. She loved yoga and cake. She loved surprises. She was happy.

Dave was very frustrated. He wanted to move, but he couldn't. There was a giant standing in his way. Dave had never seen anything so big.
He tried to find a way around the giant but it was too big. He couldn't even see over it or around it. He was stuck.
 Dave felt very sad and angry. Suddenly, he had an idea. He moved around to the back of the giant and started pushing. The giant began to move! 
Dave was so happy that he had moved the giant and he could now move around. He waved goodbye to the giant and ran off. He had never been so excited in his life!

Once upon a time there lived a shy little girl named Denise. Denise loved adventures and playing outside. One day Denise went to the beach and asked her mom if she could swim in the ocean. Her mom said to be careful, because there might be a hurricane coming. 

Denise's mom was worried, but Denise wasn't scared. She felt like she could do anything. So Denise kept playing and swimming in the ocean.

After a while her mom noticed there was a storm coming. She yelled for Denise to come back and get out of the water. But Denise wanted to keep swimming. She wanted to prove that storms couldn't stop her.

Suddenly the scariness of the hurricane came closer and the waves were getting bigger and bigger. Denise was so frightened that she started to cry.

Her mom ran to Denise and said, "Honey, you were so brave, but you should always listen to me so you don't get hurt. You can be brave, but still be careful."

Denise hugged her mom and felt relieved. She had learned a very important lesson that day â€“ you can be brave, but it's important to listen to the advice of others.

Once upon a time, there was a team of four friends. They played together every day. They liked to play ball in the big park. One day, the sky was dark and the wind was rough. The friends knew something fun was coming.

The next day, the team went to the park. They saw a big tree had split in half! The friends were excited. They knew they could play a new game with the tree. They made a plan to play hide and seek.

Two friends hid behind the split tree, and the other two friends looked for them. The team played all day long. They had so much fun hiding and finding each other. The rough wind and the big split tree made their day even more special.

Jack was a sleepy boy. He liked to mix things to make new things. One day he was mixing things for fun when he had an idea. He put his hands over his brain and thought really hard. Then he knew what he was going to mix! He took two spoonfuls of sugar, a pinch of salt and some juice, and he mixed them together. When he was done, he had made a delicious treat! Jack was so happy with the mix that he gobbled it up right away. He smiled as he licked his fingers, and went off to find his next mix.

Once upon a time there was a taxi. It was an amazing taxi. It could take people to lots of different places. It had lots of fun passengers and even prizes.

One day, a little girl wanted to go on the amazing taxi. She went inside and it started to move. She was excited!

The taxi included different games and lots of surprises. It made lots of noises and was really fun. Then, it brought the little girl to her destination.

It was an amazing journey that the little girl would never forget!

One day, a girl named Sue found a clean bottle in her room. She liked the bottle very much. Sue wanted to show the bottle to her friend, Tim. She ran to Tim's house.

At Tim's house, Sue said, "Look at my clean bottle!" Tim looked at the bottle and said, "I want it!" Sue did not want to give her bottle to Tim. They both got mad at each other.

Tim grabbed the bottle from Sue's hand. They both pulled the bottle. The bottle broke, and the clean bottle was now gone. Sue and Tim both felt sad. The fun day had a bad end.

Once upon a time, there was a crocodile who lived in the river with his friends. He was very selfish and liked to count things. He liked to count the fish that would swim past, the birds in the sky, and the clouds.

One day, he wanted to count something really special, so he looked around and couldnâ€™t find anything to count. He decided that he would count himself, so he started counting his arms and legs. â€œOne, two, threeâ€¦ seven!â€ he said.

What he didnâ€™t expect was for all his friends to join in. â€œOne, two, threeâ€¦ seven!â€ they all said along with the crocodile. He was so happy that his friends were joining him and having fun.

They all went on counting together, and the crocodile learned a very important lesson that day - it is not selfish to count the things around you, as long as you take the time to share it with friends!

Once upon a time, there was a hippo. She stayed in the river all day and all night long. One day, the hippo had an idea. She decided to explore the forest near the river.

When the hippo was walking through the forest, she saw a rabbit. The rabbit said, "Hi Hippo, why are you so far from the river?" The hippo replied, "I have come to explore the forest. I am curious to see what this new land has to offer."

The rabbit warned the hippo, "Be careful, there's a lot of danger out here. You should remain in the river." The hippo thanked the rabbit, but she wanted to explore. So the hippo said goodbye and continued her adventure.

Unfortunately, the hippo encountered some trouble in the forest. She encountered a fierce lion. The lion roared and said, "You must leave my forest now!" The hippo was scared and quickly ran back to the river.

When the hippo returned to the river she was glad that she had listened to the rabbit's advice to remain in the river. The moral of the story is that it's important to listen to the advice of others. They might be able to provide us with important insights that could save us from danger.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They see a big red ball on the grass. They run to the ball and both want to play with it.

"Give me the ball!" Lily says.

"No, it is mine!" Tom says.

They both pull the ball hard. But the ball is not strong. It pops with a loud noise. Lily and Tom fall on the ground. The ball is empty and flat.

"Oh no, we broke the ball!" Lily says.

"I am sorry, Lily. I did not want to break it." Tom says.

They look at the empty ball and feel sad. They do not want to play anymore.

Then they see a man walking to them. He has a big smile and a bag. He is the owner of the ball.

"Hello, kids. I saw what happened. It is okay, the ball was old and had a hole. I have a new ball for you. Do you want to try it?" he says.

He takes out a shiny blue ball from his bag. It is big and round and full of air. He throws it to Lily and Tom.

"Wow, thank you, mister!" Lily says.

"Yes, thank you, mister!" Tom says.

They catch the ball and start to play with it. They are happy again. They share the ball and do not pull it. They bounce it and roll it and throw it in the air. They have fun in the land with the new ball.

Once upon a time, there was a cold forest. It was filled with trees and animals. Every day, the animals happily explored the forest.

One day, they heard a loud noise. As they looked up, they saw a big balloon! It was flying above the trees and released a rope down.

The animals were very excited and they took the rope. They climbed the rope and the balloon carried them high into the sky.

The animals could see the cold forest below. They felt happy and free as they flew above the trees. They flew for a long time before the balloon released them.

The animals said goodbye to the balloon and returned safely to their cold forest. They were happy to be home and continued exploring the forest each day.

Once there was a cute little bear. He loved to go for walks in the woods. One day he took his gun and decided to go for a walk. He loaded his gun with special bullets and set off. When he reached the woods, he started to run and play! He discovered plants and animals that he had never seen before and was so excited. Suddenly, a big grey rabbit stepped out from behind a tree. The little bear couldn't believe his eyes, it was so cute! He wanted to take a closer look and he slowly loaded his gun to make sure the rabbit didn't run away. As he crept closer, the rabbit hopped away, and the bear laughed with delight at his adventure.

Once there was a girl who was very curious about the world. She was only three years old so she was very new to the world and the things around her. 
One day, whilst out in the garden, she spotted something soaring through the sky above her - an impressive butterfly! She immediately stopped what she was doing and admired the beauty of its wings as it fluttered above her. She followed it around the garden, keeping her eyes firmly fixed on it. The butterfly suddenly landed in the sun and relaxed. 
The girl couldn't believe her luck and was so amazed that she decided to go and find her mum to share the news.
Her mum was so proud of her discovery, and they spend the rest of the afternoon together in the garden, watching such an impressive sight before them. 
Before they knew it the sun went down and the girl had to say goodbye to the butterfly. The experience left her feeling so relaxed and content, which she will always remember fondly.

Once upon a time, there was a strong pebble. It wanted to be something more then just a pebble. It wanted to be a rock. Every day the pebble complained to the other rocks that it wanted to be like them. The rocks just laughed at the pebble and told it that it was too small and weak. The pebble didn't give up, no matter what the rocks said.

One day, a man came and took the pebble with him. The pebble didn't know what would happen to it but it was excited and hopeful. The man put the pebble in a strong machine and soon the pebble was becoming bigger and stronger. Finally, it looked just like the other rocks!

The pebble was so happy that it danced and sang with its new rock friends. It no longer had to complain about being small and weak, it was now just like the other rocks and could join their adventures.

One day there was a little girl named Jenny. She was 3 years old and she liked to explore. One day, she saw something that made her very excited â€“ a basket of toes! 

Jenny asked her mom if she could take one of the toes. Her mom said, "sure, that's a safe thing to do as long as you stay close to me."

Jenny was very excited and grabbed the first toe she saw. It was a big toe that was painted orange. She ran around the house with it, pretending it was a puppet.

When Jenny was done playing she asked her mom if she could put the toe back in the basket. Her mom said, "I'm sorry, sweetie, but we need to put it in the same exact spot it was before you ordered it out."

So, Jenny carefully placed the toe back in the basket, making sure it was the same kind of orange as before.

Then, Jenny gave her mom a big hug and said, "Thank you for keeping me safe from all the toeshoes!"

Once upon a time, there was a restless boy. His mommy told him to never touch her pistol because it was very dangerous; she took care of it and made sure it was put away in a safe place. 

One day, the boy found the pistol when he was playing in the house. He knew he wasn't supposed to touch it, but he was very curious. He picked it up and played with it for a while before his mommy came in. 

She was very mad and scolded him for touching it. She told him that she always took care of the pistol for his safety and he should never touch it again. The boy was so sad and he never touched the pistol again. He listened to his mommy and always kept away from the pistol. 

The boy was now doing a better job of being obedient and taking care of things. He understood why his mommy wanted him to stay away from the pistol and he was glad that she always took care of it.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Lucy and Jack. Lucy and Jack had a special journey to go on. They were a bit nervous but excited too.

Jack and Lucy hugged each other tight and held hands. They both knew that this was a big journey and it was up to them to unite.

They crossed many fields and met lots of animals. They climbed high hills and waded through streams. With determination, they kept going and going.

Soon enough, they arrived at a place they had never been before. They could see a bright blue sky, puffy white clouds and orange-red trees. It was so beautiful they couldn't believe it.

They'd done it. They had united together to go on a huge journey and they'd made it to the end. Now they could be friends forever.

Lily had a boo-boo on her knee. She fell down when she was playing with her bike. It hurt a lot and she cried. Mommy came and gave her a hug and a kiss. She put a band-aid on her boo-boo and said, "Don't worry, sweetie. It will heal soon. You are very brave and strong."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I love you." She looked at her band-aid. It had a picture of a princess on it. She liked princesses. They were beautiful and wore pretty dresses and crowns. She asked Mommy, "Can I be a princess too?"

Mommy nodded and said, "Of course, you can. You are my princess. Do you want to play dress-up?" She took Lily to her room and opened her closet. Lily looked at herself in the mirror and said, "Wow, I look like a real princess!" She twirled and danced around the room. She felt happy and forgot about her boo-boo. Mommy watched her and said, "You are the most beautiful princess I have ever seen. I'm so proud of you." She hugged Lily and said, "I love you too."

Once upon a time, in a small old house, there lived a girl named Mia and her cat, Tom. They were very happy together. Every day, Mia would gather pretty rocks to play with.

One sunny day, Mia saw a big red ball in her yard. "Whose ball is this?" she asked Tom. Tom just meowed and played with the ball. Mia decided to find the owner of the ball.

Once upon a time, there was a humble little girl who lived near a park. Each day, she would wander around, looking at the birds and flowers.

One day, she saw a hose in the park. It was long and colourful, and she thought it was so fun. She wanted to play with it, so she asked the park keeper if she could.

The park keeper smiled and said yes. He gave the little girl the hose and showed her how to use it. Together, they watered the garden and made the flowers grow. The little girl was so happy!

The next day, the little girl was back, with the hose in tow. She was ready for another fun game of water and plants. The little girl was happy and humble, and she enjoyed the simple activity each day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They wanted to find out who was tough. So they decided to have a race around the hall. 

Jack went first. He ran as fast as he could and grabbed the wall first.

Jill was not ready to give up. She said, "I can be tough too!" She ran after Jack and grabbed the wall behind him.

But Jack said, "I was here first! I'm the toughest!" He pushed Jill away and she fell hard on the ground.

The moral of the story is that being tough is not always the best way to be. Instead, try to be kind and understanding, no matter how tough the situation is.

Once upon a time, there was a hot day. All of a sudden, a kangaroo appeared. It looked like it was in trouble! Then Tom the brave knight came and saw the kangaroo. Tom knew he had to save it! So he jumped off his horse and ran over to the kangaroo. He picked it up and carried it away from the hot sun. Tom and the kangaroo went to the shade of a big tree and the kangaroo felt safe. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and cuddle with her teddy bear. One day, Lily's grandma came to visit and brought her a new toy. It was a shiny red car that could go vroom vroom!

Lily was so happy and gave her grandma a big hug. She played with her new toy all day long and it became a special memory for her. Every time she played with the car, she remembered how her grandma gave it to her and how much she loved her. From that day on, Lily cherished her new toy and the special memory it brought her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big, comfortable tent. He liked to play in the tent with his toys. Tim would smile and laugh when he played in the tent.

One day, Tim's friend, Sue, came to play with him. They both went inside the tent and played with the toys. They had so much fun! Tim and Sue smiled and laughed together.

Later, Tim's mom came to see them. She saw the two friends playing in the tent and smiled too. She was happy to see them having fun. Tim and Sue played in the tent all day, feeling comfortable and happy.

Tommy loves to play with his fireman toy. He likes to make it zoom and siren and spray water. He pretends to save people and animals from fires. He holds his fireman toy very tight.

One day, Tommy sees a real fireman outside his window. He is wearing a big yellow hat and a red coat. He has a long hose and a big truck. He is putting out a fire in a trash can. Tommy is very excited. He wants to see the fireman up close.

He runs to the door and opens it. He runs down the stairs and outside. He shouts, "Fireman, fireman, can I see your hose?"

The fireman hears Tommy and turns around. He smiles and says, "Hello, little boy. Do you like firemen?"

Tommy nods and says, "Yes, yes, I love firemen. I have a fireman toy. See?" He holds up his fireman toy for the fireman to see.

The fireman says, "That's a nice toy. Do you want to see my hose?"

Tommy says, "Yes, please, can I?"

The fireman says, "Sure, but be careful. It's very wet and strong. Here, hold my hand and I'll show you."

The fireman takes Tommy's hand and walks him to the hose. He lets Tommy touch the hose and feel the water. Tommy giggles and says, "It's wet and cold and fun!"

The fireman says, "It is, but it's also very important. It helps us put out fires and keep people safe. Do you know what to do if there is a fire?"

Tommy says, "Yes, I do. I have to stop, drop and roll. And call 911. And get out of the house."

The fireman says, "That's right. You're a smart boy. And a brave boy. Do you want to be a fireman when you grow up?"

Tommy says, "Yes, I do. I want to be like you. You're my hero."

The fireman says, "Thank you, Tommy. You're very sweet. Maybe one day you'll be a fireman too. But for now, you have to go back to your house. It's not safe to be outside alone. Where is your mom or dad?"

Tommy says, "They're in the house. I ran out to see you. I'm sorry."

The fireman says, "It's okay, Tommy. But you have to be careful. Always ask your mom or dad before you go outside. And never play with fire or matches. They're very dangerous. Do you understand?"

Tommy says, "Yes, I do. I'm sorry, fireman. I won't do it again."

The fireman says, "It's okay, Tommy. I forgive you. But you have to promise me. And you have to go back to your house now. I have to finish my job here. But maybe I'll see you again. Goodbye, Tommy."

Tommy says, "Goodbye, fireman. Thank you for showing me your hose. And thank you for being a fireman. You're the best."

Tommy holds his fireman toy and waves to the fireman. He runs back to his house and hugs his mom and dad. He tells them about the fireman and the hose. He says he wants to be a fireman when he grows up. His mom and dad smile and say they're proud of him. They say he can be anything he wants to be. They say they love him. Tommy says he loves them too. He is happy. He is wet. He is a fireman.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He was so excited because his mommy was taking him to see a witch. He had heard lots of stories about witches and he was so eager to meet one.

When they arrived, the witch was so welcoming. She offered Tom a sweet treat and he was delighted. She showed him all her magic tricks and Tom was speechless. Everywhere he looked, he saw magic!

The witch then offered Tom a very special gift. She gave him a magic wand. Tom was so excited. He could not believe that he was the proud owner of a magic wand. He twirled it around in his hands and he felt magical.

Then it was time for Tom to say goodbye and head home. He thanked the witch for the magical gifts and waved goodbye. She gave him one last gift, a hug. Tom was so surprised and so excited that he hugged the witch right back. 

He couldn't wait to show his mom and his friends all the magical things the witch had offered him.

Once there was a little boy named Timmy who liked to guess. One day he was guessing what was inside a peanut. He guessed it was a toy. But when he opened it, it was a fake. He was so disappointed!

His mom said to him, "Remember Timmy, if you don't know what something is, it's best to ask first."

Timmy nodded and thought, "I guess it's not always a good idea to guess!" 

But then he remembered all the times he had guessed right and smiled. He loved guessing and wasn't about to stop!

Once upon a time there was a boy and girl. The boy wanted to catch a duck, but he was having trouble. The girl said to him, "Don't worry! I can help you."

The girl grabbed a thick stick. She told the boy, "Run after the duck and I will try to catch it with the stick." The boy ran after the duck, but it kept jumping away.

Suddenly, the duck got too close to the stick. The girl leapt forward and whacked the stick onto the duck's back. Miraculously, the duck was caught. The girl and the boy cheered in joy. The girl had succeeded!

The girl and the boy took the duck back home. They quickly cooked it up and it tasted delicious. They both enjoyed the thick, juicy duck meat and had a wonderful time as they munched away.

Once upon a time, there was a new cabin in the woods. A boy named Tom and a girl named Sue lived in the cabin. They were very happy in their new home.

One day, Tom and Sue saw a big ball. They wanted to play with it. They started to pass the ball to each other. They were having fun and laughing. The ball was their new friend.

But then, the ball went too far away. It went into the dark woods. Tom and Sue were scared, but they wanted their ball back. They went into the woods to find it. They looked and looked, but they could not find the ball. They were lost and could not find their way back to the cabin. Tom and Sue were very sad and scared.

Once upon a time, there was a smooth pig. The pig liked to run around in the sunshine and feel the grass under her feet. One day, the pig saw a man with a big sharp knife. She got scared and ran away quickly.

The man with the knife followed the pig and said, "Don't be scared! I just want to cut some grass." The pig felt a little better but she still stayed far away from the man.

As the man cut the grass, he looked up and said, "Would you like to come closer and help me Cut? I promise I won't hurt you!" The pig thought about it for a moment, then slowly moved closer to the man.

The man smiled and said, "See? That wasn't so bad! Would you like to hold the knife while I cut?" The pig was still a bit scared, but the man's smile was so friendly that she agreed.

The pig watched carefully as the man showed her how to cut. After a while, she was doing it all on her own! The man thanked the smooth pig and then both of them went on their way with big smiles on their faces.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She wore her favorite scarf. It was a deep blue color. Lucy loved her scarf very much. In the park, she saw her friend Tom. Tom liked to play hide and seek.

"Let's play hide and seek," said Tom. Lucy was happy to play. She started to count while Tom went to hide. But as Lucy was counting, her scarf fell off. She did not know it was gone.

When Lucy was done counting, she looked for Tom. She found him hiding behind a big tree. But then, Lucy saw her scarf was gone. She was sad and asked Tom to help her find it.

They looked all around the park. They found the deep blue scarf on the ground. Lucy was so happy to have her scarf back. They played hide and seek all day, and Lucy held her scarf tight.

Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide. They also liked to look at the sky. The sky was blue and had many white clouds. Sometimes they saw birds or planes.

"Look, Ben, a big cloud!" Lila said, pointing. "It looks like a bear!"

"I see it, Lila. It does look like a bear. And that one looks like a flower!" Ben said, pointing at another cloud.

They lay down on the grass and watched the clouds change shapes. They made up stories about what the clouds were doing.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a car horn. They looked up and saw a red car speeding on the road. The car was very close to the park gate. The driver was careless. He did not see the stop sign. He did not see the old lady crossing the street.

"Stop! Stop!" the old lady shouted. She was scared. She tried to move away, but she was slow.

Lila and Ben were scared too. They hoped the car would stop. They hoped the old lady would be safe.

But the car did not stop. It hit the gate. The gate broke. The car shut the gate with a bang. The car stopped too, but it was too late. The old lady fell down. She was hurt.

Lila and Ben ran to the old lady. They wanted to help her. They saw blood on her leg. They saw tears in her eyes.

"Are you okay, lady?" Lila asked.

"No, no, I'm not okay. That car was bad. It hurt me. It hurt the gate. It could have hurt you too." the old lady said.

"Sorry, lady. Sorry, sorry." Ben said.

They heard sirens. They saw lights. They saw people. They saw a police car and an ambulance. They saw the driver of the car. He looked sorry too. He looked scared.

The police and the paramedics came. They talked to the driver. They talked to the old lady. They took her to the ambulance. They gave her a blanket and a bandage. They said they would take her to the hospital.

"Bye, lady. Get well soon." Lila and Ben said.

"Bye, kids. Thank you for being kind." the old lady said.

Lila and Ben waved to her. They felt sad. They felt angry. They felt sorry.

They looked at the sky. The sky was still blue. The clouds were still white. But they did not look like bears or flowers anymore. They looked like nothing.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Timmy's mom told him she needed to measure him to see how much he had grown. Timmy was excited to see how much he had grown.

As Timmy's mom measured him, they heard a big noise. It was lightning! Timmy was scared of the noisy lightning. "Mommy, what is that?" Timmy asked. "It's just lightning, honey. It's very bright and loud, but it won't hurt us," his mom replied.

After the lightning stopped, Timmy's mom finished measuring him. "You've grown two inches, Timmy! You're getting so big," she said. Timmy was happy to hear that he had grown. He went back outside to play, but kept an eye out for any more noisy lightning. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lily's mom asked her to turn off the light in her room. Lily didn't want to do it because she was scared of the dark.

Once upon a time there was a humble boy named Jack. One day Jack decided he wanted to go out and see the sunset. He gathered some of his favourite things which included a toy truck and a ball. He ran outside and found a spot in his garden with a great view of the sunset.

Lisa and Ben are friends. They like to play together. They have a modern house with many toys. They can play inside or outside.

But the rainbow does not come down. It does not say anything. It just shines in the sky.

"Rainbow, you are very nice!" Ben says. "Thank you for making us happy!"

The rainbow seems to smile back. It makes a little wink. Lisa and Ben laugh.

They hold hands. They go back to their modern house. They play with their toys. They are happy. They have a rainbow in their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around. One day, she was running so fast that she fell down and hurt her knee. It hurt a lot, but she didn't cry because she was brave.

Later that day, Lily's mom was cooking dinner on the stove. She left the kitchen for a moment and forgot to turn off the stove. Suddenly, the food caught on fire and the flames began to burn everything in the kitchen. Lily's mom tried to put out the fire, but it was too big.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures in her backyard. One day, she saw a huge event happening at the park near her house. She wondered what it was, so she asked her mom.

"Mommy, what's happening at the park? It looks so big!" said Lily.

The next day, Lily and her mom went to the carnival and had a great time. Lily learned that sometimes you have to be patient and wait for good things to happen. She was happy that she didn't miss out on the huge event and was grateful for her mom's wisdom.

Sara and Ben like to dig in the dirt. They look for shiny rocks and pretty shells. They have a big box where they keep their treasures. One day, they find a new spot to dig. It has many different colors of dirt and sand.

"Look, Sara, I found a red rock!" Ben says. He holds up a small stone that glows in the sun.

"Wow, Ben, that is a nice rock. Maybe it is a mineral. A mineral is a kind of rock that has something special inside," Sara says. She knows a lot of things because she likes to read books.

"Can we break it and see what is inside?" Ben asks. He wants to know if the rock has more colors or sparkles.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe we should not break it. It might be hard to break, or it might hurt our fingers, or it might be a rare rock that we should keep whole," Sara says. She is careful with her things and does not like to break them.

"But I want to see what is inside! Please, Sara, let me break it. Just a little bit. Maybe we can find another one like it," Ben says. He is curious and likes to try new things.

Sara thinks for a moment. She does not want to make Ben sad, but she also does not want to ruin the rock. She decides to encourage Ben to do something else.

"Ben, I have an idea. Why don't we take the rock home and show it to Mom and Dad? Maybe they know what kind of mineral it is. Maybe they have a book or a tool that can help us learn more about it. Maybe they can tell us if it is okay to break it or not. What do you think?" Sara says.

Ben thinks for a moment. He still wants to see what is inside the rock, but he also wants to share it with Mom and Dad. He thinks they might be proud of him for finding such a cool rock. He agrees to Sara's idea.

"Okay, Sara, let's do that. But can we dig a little more first? Maybe we can find more rocks or shells or something else," Ben says.

"Sure, Ben, let's dig a little more. But be careful not to break anything. We want to keep our treasures safe and beautiful," Sara says.

They smile at each other and continue to dig in the dirt. They are happy to have each other and their box of treasures. They are happy to explore and learn new things. They are happy to encourage each other.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was an enormous tree. Many animals lived near the tree. One day, a little squirrel named Tim found a sharp rock. He had a worry in his heart. He did not want anyone to get hurt by the sharp rock.

Tim decided to hide the sharp rock. He knew that the big tree had a hole in it. He thought that the hole would be a safe place to put the rock. But he had another worry. What if someone found the rock in the tree?

Tim asked his friend, a wise old owl, what to do. The owl told Tim to put the rock in the river. The river would make the rock smooth and not sharp anymore. Tim liked this idea. He took the sharp rock to the river and threw it in.

After some time, the rock became smooth. Tim's worries went away. He knew that no one would get hurt by the sharp rock now. All the animals in the forest were safe and happy. Tim learned that it was good to ask for help when he had a worry.

One day, a playful dog named Spot saw a new path in the park. He wanted to explore it and see what was there. He ran to the path and barked at his friend, a shy cat named Fluffy.

"Come on, Fluffy, let's go to the new path. It looks fun and exciting. Don't you want to see what's there?" Spot said.

Fluffy looked at the path and felt scared. He saw that it was dark and narrow and had many thorns and rocks. He did not think it was fun or exciting. He thought it was dangerous and scary.

"No, Spot, I don't want to go to the new path. It looks bad and scary. I want to stay here where it's safe and sunny. You should stay here too, Spot. The new path might hurt you or get you lost." Fluffy said.

Spot laughed and wagged his tail. He did not listen to Fluffy. He thought Fluffy was silly and boring. He wanted to have an adventure and show Fluffy how brave he was.

"Fluffy, you are silly and boring. You are afraid of everything. I am not afraid of anything. I am brave and curious. I dare you to come with me to the new path. If you don't, I will call you a chicken and a coward." Spot said.

Fluffy felt sad and angry. He did not like being called a chicken and a coward. He wanted to be Spot's friend and have fun with him. But he also did not want to go to the new path. He did not know what to do.

What do you think Fluffy should do? Should he go with Spot to the new path or stay where he is? What do you think will happen to Spot and Fluffy? What is the moral of the story?

Mia was playing in the garden with a sparkly diamond. She spun it around and around, watching all the colors glow in the sun. She loved how bright and beautiful the diamond was. She thought it was the most special thing ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys on the table. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to be quiet because his baby sister was sleeping. Timmy didn't want to be quiet, he wanted to play with his toys. He insisted that he could play quietly.

Jen and Sam are young. They like to play with toys and books. One day, they go to the grocery with Mom. Mom says, "You can help me find some things. But you have to stay close to me and be good."

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. One day, Lily's mom said they could go to the museum. Lily was very happy and told Tom. Tom said he wanted to go too, but his mom said they had no money for the museum. Tom was very sad and angry.

"Why can you go and I can't?" Tom asked Lily. "Is it because you are rich and I am poor?"

Lily said she was not rich, but her mom had a ticket for the museum. She said she could share the ticket with Tom, and they could go together. Tom said he did not want to share, he wanted his own ticket. He said Lily was selfish and mean.

Lily was hurt by Tom's words. She said she was trying to be nice and show him the museum, but he was being rude and ungrateful. She said she did not want to play with him anymore, and left with her mom.

Tom felt sorry for what he said, but he did not know how to say sorry. He stayed at home and cried. He wished he had been kinder to Lily, and had gone to the museum with her.

The moral of the story is: Be thankful for what you have, and do not be jealous of what others have. Sharing is caring, and friendship is more valuable than money.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw pictures. One day, she wanted to draw a blue picture of the sky and the sea. She looked for her blue crayon, but it was gone. Lily was sad.

Once upon a time there was a sleepy boy. He was walking on a track. He saw a pretty girl on the track.

The boy asked her if she wanted to marry him. She said yes. They hugged and they were very happy.

The boy and girl went on the track and went around and around and around. They laughed and talked and played together.

The sleepy boy went home and went to sleep with a big smile on his face. He was very happy to be married, even if it was only pretend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old and she loved to play.

One day Amy's mum told her that it was time to go for a walk. When they arrived outside it was dark, but Amy wasn't scared.

Once upon a time, there was a big, ugly monster. It lived in a dark cave in the woods. One day, a little girl named Lily went into the woods to pick flowers. She saw the monster and was very scared.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle with a guard outside. The guard wore a shiny armor and carried a sword. One day, a little girl with an orange dress walked by the castle. She noticed the guard and said hello. The guard smiled and said hello back. The little girl was happy to see the guard and continued on her way. The end.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.

But one day, Ben is not in the park. Anna waits and waits, but he does not come. She feels lonely. She does not want to play by herself.

The lady says, "That would be nice. Maybe we can be friends too."

They walk to the bench. They call Anna's mom. They have lunch. They talk and laugh. They are not lonely anymore.

Once upon a time there was a mommy cat and a baby cat. They both had big eyes and fluffy fur. The baby cat was so cute and original. The mommy cat loved her baby cat so very much. Every morning the mommy cat would rock the baby cat in her arms. The baby cat felt so cozy and safe.

Once upon a time there was a bear who liked to take walks. One day, the bear was walking through the woods when he spotted a zigzag on the ground. Once there was a little girl who wanted to give something special to her mom. She thought for a long time about what to give, until she decided: a square!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Grace. Grace was very sad because she couldn't find the truth. Everywhere she looked she couldn't seem to find it, so she asked her mom what she should do.

Her mom said to her, "truth can be hard to find, but if you take your time and do your best, you'll find it". Grace thought about it and decided to try.

So she took a deep breath and started looking. She looked inside and outside, in the trees and the sky, but she still couldn't find it. She felt sad and wanted to give up.

But then, suddenly, she heard a whisper in her ear. She listened carefully and it said, "look inside your heart and you'll find the truth". Grace was surprised but decided to try it.

So she took another deep breath and closed her eyes. She focused on her heart and after some time she felt something. It was warm and peaceful, like a hug. She opened her eyes and realized that she had found the truth! She felt amazing and happy.

Grace was so glad she had decided to do her best and look inside her heart because that's where she found the truth.

Once upon a time, there was a race between two animals, a rabbit and a turtle. The rabbit was very fast and the turtle was very slow. The rabbit liked to win and be the best. He was very competitive. 

The turtle said, "I may be slow, but I will try my best." The race started and the rabbit ran very fast. The turtle was very slow and the rabbit was very far ahead. The rabbit thought he was going to win. 

But, the rabbit got tired and took a nap. The turtle kept going and going. The turtle finally passed the rabbit and won the race! The turtle gained a lot by not giving up and trying his best. The moral of the story is to never give up and always try your best.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends, but she was scared of the dark. Every night, she would have a nightmare about monsters under her bed. 

One night, Lily's mommy tucked her into bed and said, "Don't worry, Lily. There are no monsters under your bed. Just close your eyes and go to sleep." 

Lily tried to sleep, but she couldn't stop thinking about the monsters. She decided to look under her bed to make sure. She found nothing but some toys and a thick blanket. 

But when she crawled back into bed, she heard a voice say, "I'm not a monster, Lily. I'm your nightmare." Lily was so scared that she screamed and woke up her mommy. 

From that night on, Lily never looked under her bed again. She learned that sometimes, it's better not to find out what's hiding in the dark.

The sun shone brightly in the jungle that day. Bob the monkey was sad. He watched the other animals in the jungle playing together. He wanted to join in the fun, but nobody asked him to play.

Suddenly, an elephant stomped into the clearing and roared. He was mad! Everyone else looked scared. The elephant turned to Bob and said, "You need to help me find my lost trunk!" 

Bob didn't want to help, but he knew he had to. He climbed onto the elephant's back and off they went. But when the elephant couldn't find his trunk, he got even madder! He turned to Bob and slapped him with his trunk. 

Bob ran off, never to be seen in the jungle again. He was sad. He wished someone had played with him when he had the chance.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big wardrobe where she kept all her clothes. One day, she went to her wardrobe to pick out a pretty dress to wear, but she found that all her clothes were wrinkled and messy. Her mommy had forgotten to put them away properly, so they got spoiled.

Lily was very grumpy because she had nothing nice to wear. But then, her mommy came and saw the mess. She apologized to Lily and promised to help her fix it. Together, they took out all the clothes and put them back in the wardrobe neatly. Lily was so happy to see her clothes looking nice and tidy again.

From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her wardrobe clean and organized so that her clothes would never get spoiled again. And whenever she felt grumpy, she would remember how happy she felt when her mommy helped her fix her wardrobe.

Once upon a time, there was a river where many animals lived. One of these animals was an otter. The otter liked to swim and play in the river. One day, the otter saw a colorful fish swimming by. The otter wanted to catch the fish, but it was too fast.

The otter felt sad because it couldn't catch the fish. Then, the otter saw a wise old turtle. The turtle told the otter that it needed to learn how to be patient and wait for the right moment to catch the fish.

The otter listened to the turtle's advice and practiced being patient. It learned that sometimes it's better to wait for things instead of rushing into them. Finally, the otter was able to catch the colorful fish and felt very proud of itself. From then on, the otter was known as a patient and wise animal in the river.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to collect shiny rocks. She kept them in a jar and showed them to her friends. One day, she saw a big castle on a hill and wanted to collect a rock from there. 

Lily went to the castle and climbed up the stairs. It was very cold and windy, but she kept going. She found a shiny rock and put it in her pocket. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew her off the stairs and she fell down. 

Lily got hurt and couldn't move. She wished she never went to collect the rock. Her friends came looking for her, but it was too late. They found her lying there, cold and still. From that day on, they never went to the castle again.

Once there was a little girl called Lilly. She loved to sing and dance around her house. Every morning, she would go outside and repeat her favourite songs to the clouds. One day, she found a wide veil in the garden. She had never seen anything so beautiful before. So she grabbed it and put it around her neck.

The veil was so light and airy. When Lilly moved, the veil moved with her, twirling and floating in the air. Lilly couldn't help but admire it. She began to dance and sing, repeating the same songs over and over. 

Soon, the day was coming to and end and the sun was setting. Lilly grabbed her veil and reluctantly went inside. As soon as she got in, she put it on again and started to repeat her songs. Every time she sang a song, the veil seemed to make the notes sound more beautiful. 

Lilly was so delighted that she wore the veil all night long, until she finally fell asleep. The next morning, she put it on again and was soon twirling in the garden, repeating her songs once more.

Jack wanted a bow. He had always been regular and dreamed of having one. He asked his mom for it but she said no.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big vine with many red fruits on it. They wanted to try the fruits. They looked very delicious.

"Can we pick some fruits, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, but be careful. The vine is high and the fruits are heavy. Don't drop them on your head," Mom said.

Lily and Ben climbed on a ladder. They reached for the fruits. They picked some and put them in a basket. They were happy.

But then, Ben saw a very big fruit. He wanted it. He stretched his arm. He grabbed the fruit. But it was too heavy for him. He could not hold it. He dropped it.

"Ouch!" Ben cried. The fruit fell on his head. It hurt him. He was sad.

Lily saw what happened. She felt sorry for Ben. She climbed down the ladder. She gave him a hug. She gave him a fruit from the basket.

"Here, Ben. Have this fruit. It is delicious. And it is not too heavy. You will feel better," Lily said.

Ben smiled. He took the fruit. He bit it. It was sweet and juicy. He liked it. He thanked Lily.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. I am sorry I dropped the fruit. I was greedy. I will share with you," Ben said.

Lily and Ben hugged again. They ate the fruits. They were happy. Mom smiled. She was proud of them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, fat cat named Fluffy. One day, Lily was playing with Fluffy when she accidentally poked him in the eye. Fluffy meowed and Lily felt very sorry.

"I'm sorry, Fluffy," said Lily. "Does it hurt?"

Fluffy just shrugged and licked his paw. Lily didn't know what to do, so she asked her mommy for help. Her mommy said they needed to take Fluffy to the vet.

At the vet, the doctor gave Fluffy some medicine and said he would be okay. Lily learned that it's important to take care of our pets and be gentle with them. She hugged Fluffy and promised to always be kind to him.

Once upon a time there was an old man. He was planting vegetables in his garden. The sun was shining down on him and he was sneezing. 

Suddenly, a little boy walked into the garden. He looked around, surprised to see all the vegetables. The old man smiled at him and said "Hello there! What are you doing here?"

The little boy looked up and said "I am looking for my sis-tor. I can't find her." The old man thought for a moment and said "Perhaps she is in the vegetable patch." 

The boy smiled and said "That's the perfect place! Thank you!" He ran off to find his sister.

The old man kept planting the vegetables and when the sun went down, he stopped sneezing. He was pleased with the work he had done. And he was also very pleased that he had helped the little boy find his sister.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mary and Tom. Mary was very thoughtful and always tried to do nice things for Tom. One day Mary made Tom a special waffle for breakfast. Tom was so happy! He couldn't believe it! He smiled and thanked his friend.

From then on, every Saturday morning Mary would make Tom a waffle for breakfast. Tom always thought it was so thoughtful of her.

One Saturday morning Tom decided to surprise Mary by making breakfast for her. He made a delicious waffle! Mary was so surprised. She smiled and thanked Tom for being so thoughtful and for believing in their friendship. 

Tom and Mary enjoyed the waffles and their time together. They believed that their friendship would last forever.

Once upon a time there was a playful boy. He loved to explore and have adventures. One day, he came across a big, shining tooth. He screamed with joy and ran to his mom to show her his treasure. 

"Mom, look! I found a tooth!" he said, holding it up.

The boy's eyes lit up. "So can I keep it?" he asked. 

His mom nodded. "Of course you can. Now, why don't you go and play with it?"

The boy smiled and nodded. He skipped off, happily playing with his new tooth. Every now and then, he would stop and scream with joy, so excited to have a real tooth. He spent the whole day playing and exploring with his new treasure. 

When the sun went down, he returned home with a smile on his face and the tooth firmly held in his hand.

Anna and Ben are on a trip with Mom and Dad. They are going to a big city. They see many cars, buses, and shops. They are happy and excited.

"Why do I feel funny?" Anna asks.

"It is because the elevator is going fast. It makes your tummy feel weird. But it is okay. It will stop soon," Mom says.

The elevator stops. It makes another ding sound. The doors open. They get out. They walk to their room. They open the door with the key. They see a big bed, a TV, and a bathroom.

"Wow, this is nice!" Dad says.

"Maybe later. First, let's unpack our bags and rest a bit. Then we can go out and see the city," Mom says.

Anna and Ben agree. They are tired from walking. They put their bags on the floor. They jump on the bed. They giggle and hug. They like the hotel. They can't wait to see more.

Tom and Jen like to act. They act like animals, like people, like cars. They make loud noises and funny faces. They have fun.

One day, they act like lions. They roar and run and jump. They chase each other and pretend to hunt. They act like big and strong lions.

But then, Tom trips on a rock. He falls to the ground. He hurts his knee. He cries. He does not act like a lion anymore. He acts like a baby.

Jen hears Tom cry. She stops acting like a lion. She runs to Tom. She sees his knee. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you OK?"

She hugs Tom. She helps him up. She acts like a friend. She says, "Let's go home. Mom can make your knee better."

Tom nods. He stops crying. He acts like a brave boy. He says, "OK, Jen. Thank you. You are a good friend."

They walk home. They hold hands. They do not act like lions anymore. They act like Tom and Jen.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who wanted to create something special for her little girl. One day, she decided to build an amazing armchair for her!

The mommy worked hard, cutting the wood and sewing the fabric. After a few days of hard work, the armchair was finally ready!

The little girl was so happy when she saw it. She couldn't wait to sit on it and watch her favorite cartoons. She loved her mommy even more for creating something special just for her.

But one day, while the little girl was playing, she accidentally spilled some paint on the armchair! She was so upset and felt terrible.

Mommy saw how upset the little girl was and tried to help. She worked hard again and used her painting skills to cover the stain and make it look as good as new. The little girl was so happy to see her newly painted armchair and hugged her mommy with a big smile.

Tommy likes to listen to music. He has a toy guitar and a toy drum. He plays them every day and makes loud noises. He wants to be a musician when he grows up.

One day, he sees a man playing a real guitar on the street. The man sings and plays very well. Tommy is amazed. He runs to the man and says, "Hello, mister. You are a good musician. Can you teach me how to play?"

The man smiles and says, "Hello, little boy. Thank you for your kind words. I can show you some things, but you have to practice a lot. Do you have a guitar at home?"

Tommy nods and says, "Yes, I have a toy guitar. It is blue and shiny. I play it every day."

The man says, "That's great. A toy guitar is a good start. But if you want to play a real guitar, you need to learn some rules. Like how to hold it, how to strum it, and how to make different sounds. Do you want to try?"

Tommy says, "Yes, please. I want to try."

The man gives Tommy his guitar and helps him to hold it. He shows him how to pluck the strings and how to make a chord. Tommy tries to copy him, but it is hard. He makes some funny noises and laughs.

The man says, "Don't worry. It takes time and practice. You are doing well for your first time. You have a good ear and a good sense of rhythm. Keep playing and you will get better."

Tommy says, "Thank you, mister. You are very nice. Can I come back and see you again?"

The man says, "Of course. I play here every day. You are welcome to join me anytime. But now I have to go. I have a show tonight at a big place. Do you want to come and watch?"

Tommy says, "Yes, I do. But I have to ask my mom first. She is over there. She bought me a yummy ice cream. Do you want some?"

The man says, "No, thank you. I have to save my voice. But you enjoy your ice cream. And thank your mom for me. Maybe I will see you tonight. Bye, Tommy."

Tommy says, "Bye, mister. Thank you for teaching me. You are the best musician ever." He runs to his mom and tells her everything. He is very happy. He hopes to see the man again and learn more. He dreams of playing a real guitar someday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved going for walks by a creek. She visited the same creek every day and she always noticed something special about it. She couldn't quite put her finger on it, but she knew that something special was near the creek, something sweet.

One day, as she was walking by the creek, she met an old man. He was sitting by the creek, with a smile plastered on his face, and he mentioned something about a secret that could be found near the creek. The girl was curious, so she asked him what it was, but the old man said she would have to find out for herself. 

That night, the girl couldn't stop thinking about the old man's words. The next morning she ran to the creek as fast as she could and there, next to the water, she found a big sweet cake. She laughed with joy and thanked the old man for mentioning this delicious surprise. She ate some of the cake and shared the rest with her family. Since then she often brings treats to the creek and it always reminds her of the sweet surprise she found that day.

Once upon a time there was a tall tree. Its branches reached high up in the sky and it was full of ripe fruit. The birds loved to eat the fruit and often nested in the tree.

The tree laughed and said, â€œNo need to pay, just enjoy them.â€

Ben and Lily were playing in the old house. They liked to pretend they were explorers and find new things. They saw a big hole in the wall and went to look inside.

"Wow, what is this?" Ben asked. He saw a lot of wires and buttons and lights. "It looks like a machine."

"Who are you?" Ben asked, scared.

"I'm Gus, the ghost," the ghost said. "I live here. This is my machine. I'm trying to repair it. It's broken."

"What does it do?" Lily asked, curious.

"It can make me travel to different places and times," Gus said. "I like to see new things and learn new stories. But one day, it stopped working. I don't know why. I've been trying to fix it for a long time, but I can't."

"That's sad," Ben said. "Can we help you?"

"Really? You would do that?" Gus asked. He looked surprised and happy. "You are very kind and humble. Most people are afraid of me or mean to me. They think I'm scary or bad. But you are different. You are my friends."

"Yes, we are your friends," Lily said. "And we like to explore and learn too. Maybe we can find the problem and repair your machine together."

"Thank you, thank you," Gus said. "That would be wonderful. Come, let me show you how it works. Maybe you can see something I missed."

Ben and Lily followed Gus to the hole in the wall. They looked at the machine and asked him questions. They tried to understand how it worked and what was wrong. They worked together as a team. They hoped they could repair the machine and make Gus happy. They also hoped they could travel with him and see new places and times. They were excited and curious. They had found a new friend and a new adventure.

Jill was a little girl who loved to play outdoors. One spring morning, she put on her yellow raincoat and went outside. She saw a nearby pond filled with waste. Jill didn't like how it looked and wanted to clean it up. She quickly got to work and began to pick up the waste. She put it in a bag and took it to the garbage can. All morning, Jill worked as the sun shone brightly in the sky. By the end of the day, the pond was clean and sparkling. Jill was so proud of her hard work. She threw her hands in the air and shouted with happiness. Springtime was the time for fun and new beginnings. Jill said goodbye to the pond and went home with a big smile.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hedge. It has many green leaves and small red berries.

Lily trusts Ben. She is a good friend. She follows him into the hedge. They crawl and push through the leaves. They see many bugs and birds. They hear funny noises.

"Wow, this is beautiful," Lily says. "You were right, Ben. This is a secret place."

They hug and laugh. They play in the secret place. They have fun. They are glad they trusted each other. They are glad they found the hedge.

Jack: Hello little horse! 

Little Horse: Moo!

Jack smiled and petted the horse. He wanted to stay with it, but he had to move on. He said goodbye to the little horse and moved towards the sun that was setting in the horizon.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big hill. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

They start to walk up the hill. They see many rocks and flowers. They hear birds and bugs. They are happy and curious. They talk to each other.

"Look, Mia, a red rock!" Tim says.

"Wow, Tim, it is so bright!" Mia says.

"Maybe there is something special on the other side of the hill," Tim says.

"Maybe there is a treasure or a castle," Mia says.

They keep walking. They are almost at the top of the hill. But then, they see dark clouds in the sky. They hear thunder and wind. They are scared and cold. They need a shelter.

"Tim, it is going to rain!" Mia says.

"Mia, we have to find a place to hide!" Tim says.

They look around. They see a big hole in the hill. It looks like a cave. They run to the cave. They hope it is safe and dry.

They enter the cave. It is dark and quiet. They see some sticks and leaves. They make a bed with them. They cuddle together. They feel warm and cozy.

They wait for the rain to stop. They hear the raindrops on the hill. They hear the thunder and wind. They are glad they have a shelter.

But then, they see something else in the cave. It is big and furry. It has sharp teeth and claws. It is a bear. It is sleeping. It is impressive.

Tim and Mia are very still. They are very quiet. They are very afraid. They hope the bear does not wake up. They hope the rain stops soon. They hope they can get out of the cave. They hope they can go home. They hope they can play outside again. They hope they can see the other side of the hill.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bull named Betsy. Betsy was very important because she was the leader of all the other cows. One day, Betsy decided to sail away on a big boat. She wanted to see the world and have an adventure.
