Betsy's friends were sad to see her go, but they knew she was brave and strong. Betsy sailed across the ocean and saw many amazing things. She saw dolphins jumping and whales swimming. She even saw a big, red octopus!

After many days of sailing, Betsy decided it was time to go back home. She missed her friends and her important job as the leader of the cows. When she returned, all her friends were waiting for her. They were so happy to see her and hear about her adventure. From that day on, Betsy knew that even though it was fun to sail away, there was no place like home.

Molly and Tim were best friends. They loved to play outside together every day.

Today, they were playing with a big piece of paper. Molly grabbed one end and yelled, "Let's skip!" 

Tim smiled and nodded. "OK!", he said. They grabbed their ends and skipped away with the paper.

After a while, they saw a regular park. It had a slide, some swings and a big sandbox. Molly and Tim ran inside to explore the park.

Molly said, "Wow! This looks like so much fun!"

Tim agreed. "Let's go on the swings first!", he said.

Molly and Tim quickly forgot about the paper as they had so much fun playing in the park. They skipped around and laughed for hours. Finally, it was time to go home tired but happy.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and dress up. One day, they found a pretty box under Lily's bed. It had a lock and a key.

"What is in the box?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. It is a secret," Lily said. She took the key and opened the box. Inside, there were many shiny things. There were rings, necklaces, bracelets, and earrings.

"Wow, they are so pretty!" Anna said. She reached for a ring.

"Stop! Don't touch them!" Lily said. She pulled the box away from Anna. "They are mine! They are from my grandma. She gave them to me before she went away. She said they are very special and I have to keep them safe."

"But I just want to look at them. Please, can I try one on?" Anna said. She felt sad and angry. She thought Lily was being mean and selfish.

"No, you can't! They are not for you. They are only for me. Go away!" Lily said. She closed the box and put it back under the bed. She turned her back to Anna.

Anna felt tears in her eyes. She did not want to play with Lily anymore. She got up and ran out of the room. She did not say goodbye.

Lily heard Anna leave. She felt lonely and sorry. She did not mean to hurt Anna. She loved her friend. She wanted to share her pretty things with her. But she was afraid to lose them. She remembered how her grandma hugged her and told her to take good care of them. She missed her grandma very much.

She got the box out again and opened it. She looked at the shiny things. They were pretty, but they did not make her happy. She wished Anna was there with her. She wanted to say sorry and give her a hug. She wanted to tell her the secret of the box. She wanted to play with her again.

She took the key and ran after Anna. She hoped she would find her and make up with her. She hoped Anna would still be her friend. She hoped they could seat together and look at the pretty things and smile.

Jill and Ben like to play in the park. They see a big slide and run to it. Jill goes first. She climbs up the steps and sits on the slide. She slides down fast and laughs. Ben follows her. He slides down too and smiles.

They see a man with a big pink balloon. The balloon is filled with gas. The man gives the balloon to Jill and Ben. They say thank you and hold the balloon. The balloon is light and floats in the air.

They want to play with the balloon. They try to balance the balloon on their heads, their hands, and their feet. They giggle and have fun. But the wind is strong. It blows the balloon away from them. They chase the balloon. They run and jump and try to catch it.

But the balloon flies higher and higher. It goes over the trees and the houses. Jill and Ben can't reach it. They stop and look at the balloon. They feel sad. They lose their balloon.

They go back to the slide. They slide down again and again. They forget about the balloon. They have fun. They are happy.

Maddie was deaf, so she couldn't hear very well. But she had a new game to play, and it made her so excited. She was going to play a matching game. Maddie's mom put 10 different desserts on the table. Maddie had to match the same desserts together. She carefully looked at all of them, and then she started to match them up. Her mom helped her whenever she got stuck. It was so much fun for Maddie. Finally she finished the game. Maddie was so happy that she had matched all the desserts. She clapped her hands and said, "Yay!"

Once there was a family that wanted to go to the mall. But they couldn't decide what to do there. Mom suggested they go shopping. But Dad said he didn't want to. Then the little girl said, â€œLetâ€™s go get ice cream!â€ Everyone agreed this was a reliable idea. 

At the mall, Dad suggested getting new shoes for the little girl. But she didn't want any. She wanted to get new socks with her favorite characters printed on them. Mom and Dad agreed that this was a reliable idea.

The family stopped at a store where the girl could pick out her socks. She looked at the colorful socks, and then spotted just the right pair with her favorite characters on them. She was so happy and said, â€œThese are the ones!â€ Mom and Dad agreed that these were reliable socks, and the little girl smiled. 

The family went home with the little girl wearing her colorful socks and happy smile.

Once upon a time there was a big house with a little window. One day, the window was feeling very tired and wanted to get a good rest.

So the window said to the house â€œI need to get some rest. Could you help me?â€ The house replied â€œYes, you can take a rest. I can help you.â€

The house opened the window, so the window could look outside. The window was so happy. It was a good day. The birds were singing, the sun was shining and the flowers were blooming.

The window was so exhausted, it fell asleep right away. The window had the best sleep ever.

When the window woke up, it felt so refreshed and strong. Then it said to the house, â€œThank you for helping me get a good rest!â€ The house smiled and said â€œYouâ€™re welcome!â€

Once there was a little girl who wanted to build something special. She had a big box of interesting things to help her. She looked around and chose some screws. She carefully put the screws together. Then she chose another part and connected it quickly. She was so proud of what she was making! 

Next, she chose some more pieces. This was more tricky, but she was determined. She moved the pieces around until they fit well. Then she used her screw to secure them together. 

Finally, she chose the last piece and put it in place. Now her special project was finished. She stepped back to admire her work. It was really interesting!

Once upon a time there was a tall tree in the woods.

Every night, the tree would whisper stories to the animals that slept beneath it.

The animals loved to hear the stories and the tree was the best storyteller in the woods.

One night, a little rabbit heard something shifting beneath the tree.

He hopped over and saw a zipper on the ground.

The zipper had a long, tall handle and the rabbit thought it must be full of secrets.

He quickly zipped it open and heard the tree whispering something inside.

The rabbit couldn't believe his ears!

The tree had been telling secrets to the zipper all along.

The rabbit smiled and thanked the tall tree before hopping away, back to his cozy burrow with the special zipper in hand.

Once there was a little boy who was very scared. He was walking down a street when he heard a loud "zip". He got scared and ran away. 

Then he came to a tree that had a big tie around it. The boy was really scared of the tie. But then he saw a butterfly. The butterfly flew around the tie and made it look beautiful. 

The boy was no longer scared. He took out his own tie and started playing games with it. He made shapes in the air, he threw it up and caught it and he even made it dance. 

Finally, the boy was so happy he wanted to share his game with someone else. He picked up his tie and ran off to find his friends. His friends loved it so much, they all started playing with their own ties. 

The boy was so excited that he and his friends were playing together! They all laughed and played, and they had so much fun. And they never heard another loud "zip".

Once there was a little girl named Kin. She was only three years old, but she already wanted to do so many things. One day, Kin went to pick some apples in the fields nearby. She was very excited to pick them!

However, the field was very big, and Kin started to get tired. She lay down by a tree and started to cry.

Suddenly, a funny looking man appeared. He said to Kin "Do not be so weak! Come and pick with me!" Kin looked at him and shook her head.

The man got angry and he forced her to pick apples with him. He held her very tightly and she was too scared to move. She was so weak that she couldn't Pick herself away from him.

Kin was forced to pick apples with the man for a long time. Eventually, the man left, but Kin was left so scared and upset. She had a bad feeling about the man, and never went to the fields again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear. He liked to walk in the forest and eat honey from bees. One day, he saw a weird bird in a tree. It had a long, green tail and a red beak. The bear wanted to get a closer look, so he leaned against the tree. Suddenly, a bottle of wine fell from the tree and broke on the ground. The bear didn't like the smell of the wine, so he walked away and continued his walk in the forest.

Once, there was a girl. She had a garage. Inside the garage she kept her toys.

One day, the girl noticed something was wrong with her toys. She went in the garage and saw that they had broken.

She decided she would repair them and make them as good as new. She made sure to wash them all so they were nice and healthy.

Then she took some glue and fixed all the toys until they looked perfect. She was very pleased with her work.

When she was done, the girl could play with her toys again and have lots of fun. She was very happy.

Lila and Lulu were twins. They liked to play with their dolls. They had many dolls, but their favorite was Molly. Molly had smooth hair and a pretty dress.

One day, Lila and Lulu had a fight. Lila wanted to play with Molly, but Lulu said no. She said Molly was her doll. Lila said no, Molly was their doll. They both pulled Molly's arms. Molly's dress ripped.

Lila and Lulu stopped pulling. They looked at Molly. They felt sad. They had hurt their doll. They had hurt each other.

"I'm sorry, Lulu," Lila said. "I didn't mean to rip Molly's dress."

"I'm sorry, Lila," Lulu said. "I didn't mean to be mean to you."

They hugged each other. They hugged Molly. They said they loved each other. They loved Molly.

They went to their mom. They showed her Molly's dress. They told her what happened. Mom smiled. She said she was proud of them for saying sorry. She said she could fix Molly's dress.

She took Molly and a needle and some thread. She sewed Molly's dress. She made it look new. She gave Molly back to Lila and Lulu. They thanked her. They said they would share Molly. They said they would not fight.

They went back to their room. They played with Molly. They made her shake her smooth hair. They made her talk. They made her laugh. They laughed too. They were happy. They were twins.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play together. Today, they are at Lila's house. Lila has a new gift. It is a flexible snake. It can bend and twist in many ways.

"Look, Tom, this is my gift. It is a snake. It is flexible. Do you want to play with it?" Lila asks.

"Yes, please. It looks fun. Can I hold it?" Tom says.

Lila gives the snake to Tom. Tom holds it in his hands. He makes it wiggle and curl. He laughs. He likes the snake.

But then, Tom drops the snake. It falls on the floor. It makes a loud noise. Lila and Tom are scared. They look at the snake. It is broken. It has a crack in its head.

"Oh no, Tom, you broke my gift. It is not flexible anymore. It is ruined. I am sad. You are a bad friend." Lila cries.

"I am sorry, Lila. I did not mean to drop it. It was an accident. I am sad too. You are a good friend. Can we fix it?" Tom says.

Lila and Tom hug. They are sorry. They look for glue. They find some in the drawer. They try to fix the snake. They put glue on the crack. They press it together. They wait for it to dry.

"Look, Lila, the snake is fixed. It is flexible again. It can bend and twist. It is a good gift. Thank you for sharing it with me." Tom says.

"You are welcome, Tom. The snake is fixed. It is flexible again. It is a fun gift. Thank you for helping me fix it. You are a good friend." Lila says.

Lila and Tom smile. They play with the snake. They are happy. They are friends.

Lily and her mom went to the shop. Lily liked the shop. It had many things to see and touch. Lily saw a big cake. It was pink and white. It had flowers and stars on it. Lily thought it was tasty.

"Mom, can we have some cake?" Lily asked.

"Not now, Lily. We have to buy some bread and milk first. Then we can have a snack at home." Mom said.

Lily was sad. She wanted the cake. She tried to reach for it. But the cake was too high. Lily stood on her toes. She stretched her arms. She lost her balance. She fell. The cake fell too. It landed on Lily's head.

"Oh no!" Mom said. She ran to Lily. She picked her up. She wiped the cake off her face and hair.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Mom asked.

Lily was scared. She was also sticky and messy. She started to cry.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted the cake. It looked tasty." Lily said.

Mom hugged Lily. She was not angry. She was worried.

"It's okay, Lily. I know you wanted the cake. But you have to be careful. You could have hurt yourself. And you made a mess. We have to say sorry to the shop lady." Mom said.

Lily nodded. She felt bad. She said sorry to the shop lady. The shop lady was nice. She gave Lily a napkin and a small cookie.

"Here you go, sweetie. This is for you. Don't cry. Accidents happen. Just be more careful next time." The shop lady said.

Lily smiled. She thanked the shop lady. She ate the cookie. It was tasty. She felt better.

Mom paid for the bread and milk. She also paid for the cake. She said it was fair. She took Lily's hand. They left the shop.

"Let's go home, Lily. We can have some more cookies and milk. And maybe a little bit of cake. But only a little bit. Okay?" Mom said.

Lily nodded. She held Mom's hand. She was happy. She loved Mom. She loved the shop. She loved the cake. But she learned a lesson. She would not fall again.

Once upon a time there was a big sheet in the sky. It was so big that it almost touched the ground. One day, the sun came out and the sheet started to melt. It melted until just one little corner of it was left. Then, something special happened! The tiny corner of the sheet started to rise up in the air and soon there were millions of balls! All the colors in the world! Red and blue, yellow and purple. They looked so beautiful! The melted sheet had changed into a big bunch of colorful balloons. Everyone was so happy that the melted sheet had changed into something so joyful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play her flute. She would practice every day and dream of playing in a big concert. One day, she saw a very attractive flute in a store and begged her parents to buy it for her.

Her parents said no, but Lily didn't listen. She took the money from her piggy bank and bought the flute herself. She was so happy and played it all day long.

But then, something bad happened. Lily accidentally broke the attractive flute. She was scared of punishment from her parents, but instead of getting angry, they helped her fix it. From then on, Lily learned to be responsible and take care of her things. And she continued to practice her old, but still beautiful flute, dreaming of the day she would play in a big concert.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a chubby face and loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she was walking in the park when she saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a palm tree tattoo on his arm.

Lily went up to the man and said, "Hi! I like your tattoo." The man smiled and said, "Thank you, little one. Do you like palm trees?" Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, they are tall and pretty."

The man then asked Lily if she wanted to hear a story about a palm tree. Lily was excited and said, "Yes, please!" The man told her a story about a palm tree that grew in a far-off land. The palm tree was so tall that it could touch the sky. Lily loved the story and thanked the man before running off to play some more.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady. She lived in a big house with lots of rooms. Every day, the old lady would lay out her clothes in an organized way. 

One day, the old lady decided to have a tea party with her friends. She laid out the cups, plates, and spoons in an organized way on the table. Her friends came over and they had a great time together. 

After the tea party, the old lady felt tired. She went to her bedroom and laid down on her bed. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. When she woke up, she felt refreshed and happy. She realized that having friends over for tea was a great idea. From that day on, she organized tea parties every week.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was very brave.

The little boy wanted to borrow a shrimp from the beach. He went down to the shore and put his toes in the cold water. 

He had never seen a shrimp before! He was a little bit frightened. But he stayed brave.

He looked and looked, until finally he spotted a shrimp. He reached into the water and grabbed the shrimp. It felt funny and slimy! 

The little boy was very happy and he went home with his new friend, the shrimp. He kept him in his bucket and they were best friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite red shoes because they were so comfortable. One day, Lily and her mommy went for a walk in the park. 

While they were walking, Lily saw a bird and tried to whistle to it. But she couldn't whistle very well yet. Her mommy showed her how to pucker her lips and blow air out to make a sound. 

As they kept walking, Lily noticed that her shoe buckle was loose. Her mommy helped her fix it so she wouldn't trip and fall. They continued their walk and saw some ducks swimming in the pond. Lily tried to whistle again, and this time she made a little sound. She was so happy! 

Finally, they arrived back home and Lily was tired from all the walking. She took off her shoes and snuggled up on the couch with her mommy. She was so comfortable and happy, she fell asleep with a smile on her face. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She loved to go to the park with her mommy and daddy. They would swing and slide and play together.

One day, they brought some honey sandwiches to the park for a picnic. Lily loved the sweet taste of the honey. She ate it all up and even licked her fingers clean.

After they finished their picnic, they played some more and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Lily was tired but happy. She couldn't wait to come back to the park again and have more honey sandwiches with her mommy and daddy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy who was three years old. She was so cute and only wanted to play. One day, her family decided to bring her to the beautiful beach for the day. When they arrived, it was so lovely; the sand was warm, the waves were crashing, and seagulls were flying in the air. 

Lucy was so excited. She spent the day playing, collecting shells, and even building a sandcastle. At the beach, she made many new friends. Everyone was playing together and having lots of fun.
 
But then, a loud noise came from far away. It was the sound of war. Lucy's mom and dad knew they had to take her home quickly. So they brought Lucy back home safely to their house. 

Lucy's mom and dad hugged her and kissed her, telling her how much they love her. All ended well, and the little girl was happy to be home with her family. She was reminded that a home with love was much better than a beach with war.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. The bear was very anxious because he needed food to eat. He decided to go to the river to catch some fish. When he arrived at the river, he saw that the fish were too fast for him to catch.

Suddenly, a kind fox appeared and said, "I will provide you with some fish." The fox stacked the fish on top of each other and gave them to the bear. The bear was very happy and thanked the fox. From that day on, the bear and the fox became good friends and went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Tom. He was a very alert boy and always looking around for something to do. One day his mom said it was time to unpack! 
Tom was so excited and asked what was in the box. Inside the box there was a costume with a black mustache! He couldn't believe his eyes! 
Tom put on the costume and ran around the house making silly faces. His mom laughed and said "I'm so glad you like it!" Tom was so happy and decided to wear the costume every day. 
From that day on, Tom was alert, always looking around for an adventure to have while wearing his mustache.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together. But sometimes they fight over toys and treats. One day, Mom gives them a big bar of chocolate to share. She says, "Be fair and nice to each other. Break the chocolate in half and each take one piece."

Anna and Ben nod and say, "Okay, Mom." But when Mom leaves, they look at the chocolate. Anna thinks her piece is smaller than Ben's. She says, "Hey, that's not fair! You have more chocolate than me. Give me some of yours."

Ben says, "No, I don't. We have the same amount. You are being greedy. Go away and leave me alone."

Anna gets angry and tries to grab Ben's chocolate. Ben holds it close and pushes Anna away. They start to yell and pull and hit each other. The chocolate breaks into many small pieces and falls on the floor.

Mom hears the noise and comes back. She sees the chocolate on the floor and the twins crying. She says, "What happened? Why did you waste the chocolate? Why did you fight with each other?"

Anna and Ben feel sorry and ashamed. They say, "We're sorry, Mom. We were not fair and nice to each other. We wanted more chocolate and we did not share."

Mom says, "That's very sad. Chocolate is a treat, not a reason to fight. You should be happy and grateful for what you have. And you should love and respect each other. You are twins, after all. You are special and lucky to have each other."

Anna and Ben hug and say, "We love you, Mom. And we love each other. We're sorry we made a mess. Can we have some more chocolate, please?"

Mom smiles and says, "Maybe later, if you behave well. But first, you have to clean up the floor and say sorry to each other. And then you can play nicely together."

Anna and Ben say, "Okay, Mom." They pick up the chocolate pieces and put them in a bowl. They say sorry to each other and give each other a kiss. Then they go to play with their toys. They are happy and fair and nice to each other. They do not fight over chocolate anymore.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play and eat together. But sometimes they want different things. Today, Mom says they can choose their own meal for lunch.

Lily says, "I want cheese and bread and apple. Yummy!"

Ben says, "No, I want soup and crackers and banana. That is better!"

Mom says, "You can both have what you want. But you have to share and be nice. And you have to eat in the kitchen, where it is safe. No food in the living room, where there are toys and books and rugs."

Lily and Ben nod. They go to the kitchen and sit on their chairs. Mom gives them their plates and cups. They say, "Thank you, Mom!"

They start to eat. Lily looks at Ben's soup. It is hot and steamy. She says, "Can I try your soup?"

Ben looks at Lily's cheese. It is yellow and melty. He says, "Can I try your cheese?"

They smile and swap their spoons and bites. They taste each other's food. They say, "Mmm, this is good!"

They finish their meal and drink their water. They say, "We are full and happy!"

Mom says, "I am glad you liked your meal. And I am proud of you for choosing and sharing. Now you can go and play, but remember to wash your hands and faces first."

Lily and Ben say, "Okay, Mom!" They run to the sink and wash up. Then they hug Mom and go to the living room. They play with their toys and books and rugs. They are safe and happy.

There was a boy called Will. He loved to play outside. One day, he found a wagon and he thought it was his. He was so excited and he said to himself, "It belongs to me now."

Will took the wagon with him to the park. He was having fun playing and pushing the wagon. Suddenly, a big boy came running towards Will. The big boy said, "That's my wagon. Give it back!"
Will was scared, but he said, "No! It belongs to me."

The big boy was getting angry. He shouted, "Stupid boy! You don't belong here!" He grabbed the wagon and ran away. Will was so sad. He learned that not everything he wanted belonged to him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Lily accidentally ripped her teddy bear's arm off. She was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom saw how sad she was and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can replace your teddy bear's arm with a new one." Lily was happy to hear that and asked, "Can we do it now?" 

Her mom said, "No, we have to go to the store to buy a new arm for your teddy bear. We'll stay here for a little bit longer and then go to the store." 

Lily was excited to get a new arm for her teddy bear. She asked her mom, "Will it be an ancient arm?" Her mom laughed and said, "No, it will be a brand new arm for your teddy bear." 

Lily was happy to hear that and hugged her mom. She couldn't wait to play with her teddy bear again when it had a new arm.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, he went outside and saw that it was very cold. The ground was icy and he almost slipped. 

His mom saw him and said, "Be careful, Timmy. It's very slippery outside." 

Timmy replied, "I know, Mommy. I'll be careful." 

But then he saw his friend Jack playing outside too. Jack said, "Come on, Timmy! Let's play!" 

Timmy replied, "I can't play now. I have to study. I have a test tomorrow." 

Jack said, "Oh, okay. Good luck, Timmy! Don't forget to wear a hat to keep your head warm!" 

Timmy smiled and said, "Thanks, Jack! I won't forget." And then he went inside to study for his test while Jack continued to play outside in the icy weather.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny yellow bug. He was a very determined bug, and wanted more than anything to reach the top of a big tree. But it was very tall and he was so very small.

The bug searched around the tree for something to help him. He found a twig and grabbed it tight. Then he began to climb and climb.

The twig was long and wiggly, and the bug had to struggle to keep his balance. He started to feel a bit discouraged, until finally he reached the top!

He looked proudly around from the top of the tree, and congratulated himself on being so brave and strong.

But then he heard a voice from below. It was a small bird, looking very friendly.

"Hello little bug!" chirped the bird. "That was such a brave climb you made! I'm so proud of you!"

The tiny bug smiled, feeling even more proud. He thanked the bird and then hopped back down the tree again, the twig still in his mouth.

He'd made it to the top, with the help of a twig, and he was so happy. That little yellow bug had definitely earned his bragging rights.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to travel with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went to a bakery to buy a pastry. Lily saw a unique pastry that looked like a rainbow. She wanted it so much, but her mommy said no.

Lily was sad, but they continued their trip. They went to a park and had a picnic. Suddenly, Lily felt sick and her tummy hurt. Her mommy and daddy rushed her to the hospital. The doctor said she ate something bad and it made her sick. 

Lily's mommy remembered the pastry and realized it must have been the cause of her sickness. She regretted not buying the unique pastry that Lily wanted. From that day on, she promised to always listen to Lily's wishes.

On Sunday, Lily and Max went to the park with Mom and Dad. They saw many things in the park: trees, flowers, birds, dogs, and people. Lily and Max liked to run and play on the grass. They also liked to go on the swings and the slide.

"Look, Max, a plane!" Lily said, pointing to the sky. She saw a big, white plane that made a loud noise. It was flying very fast and high.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Max said, pretending to be a plane. He spread his arms and ran after the plane. He liked to make noises and act like different things.

Lily laughed and joined him. She also spread her arms and ran with Max. They zoomed around the park, making plane noises. They felt the light wind on their faces and the sun on their backs.

Mom and Dad watched them and smiled. They were happy to see Lily and Max having fun. They also liked the plane and the sky. They thought it was a beautiful Sunday.

Tom and Mia liked to play on the farm. They liked to feed the chickens, pet the cows and run with the dogs. But their favorite animal was Molly, the mule. Molly was very kind and gentle. She let Tom and Mia ride on her back and gave them soft nuzzles.

One day, Tom and Mia wanted to do something special for Molly. They decided to make her a wreath of flowers. They picked some daisies, roses and sunflowers from the garden. They tied them together with a ribbon. They were very proud of their gift.

They ran to the barn, where Molly was resting. They called her name and showed her the wreath. Molly lifted her head and smiled. She walked over to them and sniffed the flowers. She liked them very much. She thanked Tom and Mia with a loud bray.

Tom and Mia put the wreath around Molly's neck. They hugged her and told her they loved her. Molly felt very happy. She wanted to show them how much she appreciated their generous gesture. She decided to do something fun for them.

She started to spin around in a circle, making the wreath fly in the air. Tom and Mia laughed and clapped. They joined Molly in the spinning game. They spun faster and faster, until they all fell down on the hay. They cuddled with Molly and giggled. They had a wonderful time. Molly was the best mule ever.

Once there was a girl named Molly. She liked to explore the world around her. She liked to look out of her window and see what her neighbor was doing.

One day, when she was looking out the window, she saw something disgusting. She thought it was pretty gross. She asked her mom, "Mom, why is our neighbor doing that?"

Molly's mom said, "Molly I don't think that is very nice. Our neighbor is doing something that's not safe."

Molly said, "Okay. I won't look out the window any more."

Molly learned that day that it's not nice to think bad things about your neighbor and that sometimes it's better to mind your own business. She also learned that being curious is ok, as long as it's done in a way that respects others and keeps them safe.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go on adventures with his family. One day, they went to the beach. Timmy's mom packed a blue bag with all the things they needed for the day.

When they arrived, Timmy saw a boy who didn't have any toys to play with. Timmy felt sad for him. He wanted to share his toys with the boy, but he didn't want to give his favorite one away. So, he decided to ask his mom to drive them back home to get another toy for the boy.

On the way back, Timmy's mom told him that it's important to share with others. When they got back to the beach, Timmy gave the boy a new toy. The boy was so happy, and Timmy felt good for sharing. From that day on, Timmy always remembered to share and help others.

Once upon a time Tommy was playing in the garden on a hot summer day. He was running around, chasing the butterflies. Suddenly, Tommy noticed something bright and shiny in the grass.

Tommy got close and could see that it was a magical ball of light. He picked it up, and it felt fit in his hands. He was so excited.

He said to himself, "What should I do with this?"

Suddenly the ball started to glow brighter and brighter, until it vanished in a puff of sparkles. Tommy was very sad. He searched everywhere, but there was no trace of the magical ball.

Tommy went inside to tell his mom what had happened. Mom said, "Don't worry Tommy, it's just some summer magic!"

Once there was a dad, a mom, and a little boy named Max. They all wanted to go on an adventure. So, they packed up their things and headed off. 

They stood at the side of a river that flowed fast and clear. A nosy duck swam up to them and asked what they were doing. Dad said they were just on a little adventure.

Max was so excited! He wanted to play in the river. Dad and Mom said it was okay, as long as they watched him closely. So, they all stripped down and jumped in the water. It was so cool and wet!

Max loved standing in the river, jumping up and down and splashing the nosy duck. They played for a really long time, but eventually it was starting to get dark. 

So, Dad and Mom got out and dried off. Max was sad but knew it was time to go home. They said their goodbyes to the nosy duck and headed home, dreaming of their next big adventure!

Once there was a kid named Ted. He really liked colors and one day he decided to paint things around the house. He painted the walls, his toys, and even his bed. He made everything colorful!

He started to get tired while he was painting, but he thought he was finished. So, he decided to take a nap on his bed. When he woke up, he had forgotten to turn off the paint! It was everywhere! He was so sad and he ran to his mommy.

His mommy found a way to make it better. She took him to the store to buy more paint. Ted was so excited. He got to choose the colors and paint things more. He soon forgot about his mistake. 

When he was done, everything was so colorful and he was so proud. Ted learned that it was important to always turn off the paint and remember to do it. That way, he wouldn't forget it ever again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a man called Joe. Joe was very successful, and he had a beautiful statue in his garden. Everyday he would take care of it, making sure it was clean and looking nice.One day, an old lady came to Joe's house, she was very poor and desperate for money. She asked Joe for help. Joe said no, so the old lady decided to try to steal the statue from Joe.

Joe noticed the old lady sneaking around his garden and he rushed over to stop her. He shouted "what are you doing?!" The old lady was so shocked she dropped the statue on the floor and ran away. Joe was sad, but he knew nobody was hurt, so he was successful in stopping her.

Joe was happy that his statue was safe, and he made sure to keep a closer eye on it from then on.

Once there was an elderly man who lived by himself. He was sad because he had no one to keep him company. One day, he went for a walk and noticed something odd on the ground. It was a mitten! He picked it up and gained a little hope. He looked around for whoever lost the mitten but couldn't find anyone. So, he decided to go home with the mitten and have it as a companion. 

He took care of the mitten and named it Mitt. Mitt was a great listener and the elderly man found joy in talking to it. After a while, the elderly man realized that the mitten had brightened his day and he was no longer alone. 

The man and Mitt continued to spend their days together and the elderly man even gave Mitt a warm bed to sleep in. The man was happy and thankful that he had gained a special new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna who had fun playing in her backyard. She loved to run, jump and swing on the swingset. One day, as she was playing, Anna heard a voice say, "Hey! What are you doing in my backyard?"

Anna looked and saw a small, harmless creature wearing brown pants. The creature told Anna it was an elf, and asked if she needed help. Anna told the elf she had torn her own pants, so the elf offered to replace them.

The elf used some magic to make a new, blue pair of pants for Anna. Anna thanked the elf and tried on her new pants. She liked them so much she wanted to keep them!

The elf said, "I'm glad you like them! Just remember, these pants are just a temporary replacement. When you get tired of them, you can always come see me and I'll help you find a new pair!"

Anna smiled and thanked the elf again. She ran off, wearing her blue pants and feeling happier than ever. The elf watched her leave, and smiled a harmless smile.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. They have a big box of toys. They have dolls, cars, balls, and books.

One day, Anna and Ben find a letter in the box. The letter is old and yellow. It has a stamp and a name on it. Anna and Ben do not know who the letter is for.

"Who is this letter for?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is for someone who lived here before," Ben says.

"Maybe we should give it to the mailman. He can find the person who wants the letter," Anna says.

"Good idea. Let's go outside and wait for the mailman," Ben says.

Anna and Ben take the letter and go outside. They see the mailman coming down the street. He has a big bag of letters and packages. He is dependable. He always brings the mail on time.

"Hello, mailman!" Anna and Ben shout.

"Hello, Anna and Ben! What do you have there?" the mailman asks.

"We have a letter for you. We found it in our toy box. We don't know who it is for," Anna says.

"Let me see. Oh, this is a very old letter. It is from a long time ago. It is for someone who used to live in your house. His name is Tom," the mailman says.

"Wow, that is cool. Do you know where Tom is now?" Ben asks.

"I'm sorry, I don't. He moved away a long time ago. I don't know if he ever got this letter. Maybe it got lost in the mail," the mailman says.

"That is sad. Maybe he was waiting for this letter. Maybe it was important," Anna says.

"Maybe. But you know what? You can still do something nice for Tom. You can throw the letter in the air and make a wish for him. Maybe he will feel it and be happy," the mailman says.

"Really? Can we do that?" Anna and Ben ask.

"Sure, why not? It's a nice thing to do. And maybe the letter will find its way to Tom somehow," the mailman says.

"Okay, let's do it. Thank you, mailman!" Anna and Ben say.

They hold the letter together and throw it in the air. They close their eyes and make a wish for Tom. They hope he is happy and has a good life. They smile and wave to the mailman. He smiles and waves back. He goes on his way to deliver the rest of the mail. Anna and Ben go back to their toy box. They have more fun playing together. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, in a great big garden, there were many flowers. One little flower was sad because it did not bloom like the other flowers. It was a small flower with a loop in its stem. The other flowers would laugh at the loop and the little flower would feel bad.

One day, a kind bee came to the garden. The bee saw the little flower with the loop and said, "Do not be sad, little flower. I have a secret for you. Soon, something great will happen to you." The little flower did not know what the bee meant, but it hoped that the bee was right.

Days went by and the little flower started to feel something happening. It felt a warm and happy feeling inside. Then, one sunny day, the little flower bloomed! It had the most beautiful and colorful petals in the whole garden. The other flowers were amazed and they stopped laughing at the loop. The little flower was very happy and knew that the bee was right. The loop in its stem made it special, and it was now the most beautiful flower in the garden.

The sun was shining on a fine Sunday. It was the perfect day to fly!

Two birds woke up early to see the sunrise. They were excited to go on an adventure.

The birds flapped their wings and went up, up, up into the sky. They flew over the trees and watched their shadows below.

Suddenly, they saw beautiful butterflies flying around them. As they watched the butterflies, they kept flying higher and higher.

Soon, the birds saw a rainbow ahead. The colors were so bright and pretty! They flew through the rainbow, ready for a new adventure.

They kept flying until they saw the sun set. Then they flew down and landed back in the tree where they started. The birds had a wonderful Sunday together, they were so happy and proud of their adventure!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was called Megan. Megan was very cheerful and liked to play with her friends. One day, Megan noticed something was broken. She didn't know how to fix it. But she remembered her mom had taught her how to repair things.

So Megan got to work. She took out her tools, just like her mom. After a few tries, Megan managed to fix it. She was so delighted! She ran to her mom and showed her what she had done.

Her mom was so proud of her! She gave Megan a big hug and a special prize for doing such a good job. Megan was so happy! She gave her mom a big hug and thanked her for the prize.

From then on, Megan was always excited to try and fix things. She felt so cheerful each time she was successful. She knew just how to repair things, just like her mom showed her.

Once upon a time there was a small girl. Her name was Sue. She was 3 years old.

One day Sue went for a walk in her garden and noticed something special. It was a delicate note that blew in on the wind. Sue felt excited. She wanted to read it and find out who the note was for.

So Sue picked up the note and opened it carefully. On the note was a large heart with a message inside. It said "Happy Birthday".

Sue felt happy. She put the note in her pocket and skipped back home. She smiled all day long as she thought of the special note.

That night, Sue put the note in an envelope and gave it to her mummy and daddy. She said "I found this note in the garden. It made me feel happy." They all smiled and hugged Sue.

The note reminded them all of how delicate and special life can be.

One day, Mom and Dad took Timmy to the park. The park was huge and had lots of exciting things to do. Timmy loved it there! He played with all his toys and laughed with his mom and dad. Suddenly, Timmy looked up and saw a huge gate with a lock on it. He wanted to open it so badly and see what was inside but he knew his mom and dad wouldn't let him. 

Timmy became very jealous and started to panic. He felt sad that he couldn't open the locked gate. His parents noticed he was panicking and came to him. Mom hugged him and said, "It's okay Timmy. We'll show you what's inside, but we need the key to open the lock." Timmy felt better and smiled. Dad took out a shiny and golden key from his pocket and opened the gate. Timmy gasped in surprise. Inside the gate was a big playground filled with lots of exciting things. 

Timmy squealed with delight and ran towards the playground. He was so happy that he was no longer jealous. He was now able to join in the fun!

Lily liked to clap her hands. She clapped when she was happy, when she saw something funny, or when she wanted to make noise. She clapped so much that her hands were red and sore.

One day, she saw a big bird in the park. It had a long neck and colorful feathers. Lily thought it was pretty and wanted to clap for it. But the bird did not like the noise. It turned around and pecked Lily on the nose.

Lily cried and ran to her mom. Her mom hugged her and kissed her nose. She said, "That bird was not normal. It was mean and rude. You should not clap for mean birds. You should clap for nice things, like flowers and stars and friends."

Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She saw a flower on the ground and picked it up. She gave it to her mom and said, "I clap for you, Mom. You are nice and sweet and normal."

Her mom smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. I clap for you, too. You are brave and smart and normal." They clapped their hands together and laughed. The bird flew away and did not bother them anymore.

Once there was a little boy who was very careless. One day, he went to the park and saw a big cactus. He wanted to touch the cactus, but he knew it was not a good idea because it had sharp spines. He thought about it for a moment, but then he was too curious. So he touched the cactus. 

It was not a nice feeling. He quickly pulled away because it hurt. He was surprised at how sharp the cactus's spines were. He looked at his hand and saw lots of little scratches.

The boy learned a lesson that day. He knew he must be careful and not touch a cactus again. He also knew he must always listen to his parents and not do something careless.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She lived in a big house with a big fence. The fence was very tall and made of wood. Every day, Lucy's dad would raise the fence higher and higher.

One day, Lucy wanted to help her dad with the fence. She wanted to show him how intelligent she was. So, Lucy went up to the fence. She put her little hands on the fence and tried to raise it. But the fence was too heavy for her!

That's when Lucy's dad explained to her that she was too small to raise the fence by herself. But, he said that she could still help him. Lucy's dad said that if she held the tools, he could use them to make the fence bigger.

So, Lucy and her dad worked together to raise the fence higher and higher. Lucy was so proud of herself for helping her dad with the fence. Together, they had made the fence taller and stronger.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to dig holes. One day, the bunny was digging a hole when it fell in and got stuck. The bunny was scared and cried for help.

Luckily, a kind bird saw the bunny and flew down to provide assistance. The bird used its gentle beak to pull the bunny out of the hole. The bunny was so grateful and happy to be free again.

From that day on, the bunny was more careful when digging holes and always made sure there was no danger around. And the bird felt good knowing it had helped someone in need.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny. The bunny was walking through the forest when he saw a funny-shaped stone. He hopped over to look at it more closely. The bunny touched it, and suddenly the stone began to roll away. The bunny tried to chase the stone, but it rolled faster than he hopped.

The bunny followed the stone until it rolled down into a deep, dark hole. Unfortunately, his foot got stuck and he couldn't get it out!

The bunny started crying, when suddenly he heard a voice. "Don't cry, little bunny," the voice said. "I can help you!"

It was a tiny green frog who hopped out of the hole. "See this rope?" the frog asked, pointing to a rope near the hole. "You can climb out if you grab hold of the rope and pull." 

The bunny was so happy that he thanked the frog and grabbed hold of the rope. He pulled, and he pulled, until finally he was out of the hole. 

The bunny looked at the stone and said, "I'm glad I didn't get hurt, like that stone did." He hopped off, happy to be back on solid ground.

Once upon a time, there was a youth named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom came into his room and said, "Timmy, we need to clean up your toys so we can fit more in your toy box."

Timmy replied, "But Mom, I love all my toys. I don't want to give any away."

His mom said, "I understand that you love your toys, but we need to make some space. It will be great to have a clean room and more room to play."

Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, Mom. Let's clean up together!" And they spent the rest of the day fitting all of Timmy's toys into his toy box.

Once upon a time there was a nice man who lived in a small house. He wanted to help his friends, so he went to look for stones. 

It was a hot sunny day, and he was feeling very tired, yet he kept looking. Suddenly, he found a nice big stone. "This will help my friends!", he thought. 

He lifted up the stone and started carrying it home, but it was too heavy. He tried his best to carry it, but it was just too big! 

Just then, a kind lady saw him struggling. She asked, "Can I help you?"

The man was so happy and said, "Yes, please help! I'm trying to carry this stone home so I can help my friends."

The kind lady smiled and said, "Come on, let's try together. I'm very patient and I think we can do it!"

They worked together and managed to carry the stone all the way home.

When they arrived, the man thanked the kind lady. "You have been so patient. Thank you so much for helping me!" 

The kind lady smiled and said, "You're welcome! Friends always help each other."

Once there was a frog. He loved to sing. He opened his mouth wide every day and sang a green song. Everyone around him would stop and listen.

One morning he woke up feeling extra sleepy. He tried to sing his green song, but all he could do was yawn. He stretched out his arms, but the yawns kept coming!

He gave up trying to sing and instead decided to take a nap. He found a nice spot in the sun and yawned himself to sleep.

When he woke up, he felt much better. He opened his mouth wide and sang his green song with all his heart. Everyone around him was smiling as they sang along. 

It was a special moment - one that he would never forget. And he never yawned while singing his green song ever again!

Once there was a boy who loved to point. He would point to everything he saw. He had a mom who was very patient with him.

One day, he pointed to a big wall. His mom said it was called a pattern. He was so excited to learn the new word. He started pointing to different patterns, like the stripes and circles on his mom's shirt.

His mom's patience made him learn new and exciting things. He kept pointing to new patterns everywhere he looked and learned a lot that day. He liked to point and was very happy that his mom was so patient and taught him new things.

Ben and Mia like to play with their toys. They have a big box of toys in their room. One day, they find a new toy in the box. It is a gun that can shoot balls. The balls are soft and colorful.

"Wow, look at this!" Ben says. He picks up the gun and aims at the wall. He pulls the trigger and a ball flies out. The ball bounces off the wall and hits the lamp. The lamp falls down and makes a loud noise.

"Oops!" Ben says. He looks at Mia. Mia looks scared. She does not like loud noises.

"Ben, you are bad!" Mia says. She runs to the door and opens it. She wants to tell Mom.

"No, Mia, wait!" Ben says. He runs after her. He does not want to get in trouble. He still has the gun in his hand.

He reaches the door and tries to stop Mia. But he is too late. Mia runs out of the room and bumps into Mom. Mom is holding a tray of cookies. The tray slips from her hand and falls to the floor. The cookies break and scatter. The tray makes a hard sound.

"Oh no!" Mom says. She looks at Ben and Mia. She sees the gun and the ball. She sees the lamp and the cookies. She is not happy.

"Ben, Mia, what did you do?" Mom says. She sounds angry. She puts her hands on her hips.

Ben and Mia look at each other. They feel sorry. They do not know what to say. They wish they did not play with the gun. They wish they did not make a mess. They wish they did not make Mom angry. They wish they had a hug.

Mum and Dad had a special night planned. They were going to a restaurant and they were very excited.

At the restaurant, they looked at the menu. Mum wanted to order a salad, Dad wanted a burger.

Finally, they chose the burger. It looked very fat and juicy. Mum and Dad were happy.

After dinner, it was time to go home. Dad looked around the restaurant, sadly he missed something. It was something special that he wanted to have for dinner. But it was too late.

Mum and Dad said goodbye to the restaurant. They were sad but happy that they'd had a good time.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars, but he only had one black car. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play and he brought his own toy car. It was a red car and Timmy wanted it so badly. 

Timmy asked his friend if he could have the red car, but his friend said no. Timmy got sad and didn't want to play anymore. His mom noticed that Timmy was upset and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told his mom that he wanted the red car and his friend wouldn't give it to him. 

His mom told him that it's not nice to take things that belong to others and that he should be happy with what he owns. Timmy realized that his black car was still fun to play with and he didn't need the red car. He apologized to his friend and they continued playing together with their own toy cars. The end.

There was a small boy who loved animals very much. He had a wish to see an unknown animal. One day, he saw a beautiful bird that he had never seen before. He loved it so much and wished he could keep it forever. He loved the way it sang and flew around the trees. Then, one day, the bird flew away and the boy was so sad. He knew he would never see it again, but he will always love it in his heart. The unknown animal was gone, but the boyâ€™s love was still there.

Once upon a time there was a loyal boy. He was very kind and often helped his friends. One day, the boy noticed something strange in the forest. He saw an old broken tree. He decided to try and restore it.

The boy worked very hard and with great dedication. For days and days he worked, building and repairing the old tree. After some time, with help from his friends, the tree was finally restored.

The boy was so proud. He said to his friends, "Look at this strong, tall tree! We did it together!"

Everyone cheered and hugged the boy for his hard work and loyalty. The old tree was standing proudly, a symbol of their friendship. From then on, the boy was known as the loyal tree restorer!

Once upon a time there lived a green barber. Every day he would improve his skills by cutting lots of hair. One day, he decided to make a special change to his barber shop. He bought lots of paint and painted everything green. He even painted himself green so he matched the shop!

The green barber was very happy with his new look. Everyone who came to the barbershop was impressed. Even though the barber was green, he was still the best barber in the city. All of his customers stayed loyal because he always improved his services.

The green barber was so happy with his barber shop that he gave a big party. All of his friends and family came to the party and celebrated the green barber's success. They enjoyed cake and ice-cream and everyone had a great time!

The green barber continued to improve his skills and the barber shop was always a buzzing place. All the customers loved the green barber and the way he improved things every day.

Once upon a time there was a fountain. In the fountain, there were lots of little fish. The fish were swimming around and were having lots of fun.

One day, a boy and his dad came to visit the fountain. The boy saw the fish and was happy. His dad encouraged him to try to catch one of the fish.

The boy tried and tried. At first he didn't catch anything, but he kept trying. His dad encouraged him not to give up.

Suddenly, the boy caught one of the fish. He was so happy! He and his dad put the fish in a special organized container.

The boy was so proud. He thanked his dad for encouraging him to never give up. They had lots of fun at the fountain that day.

Once upon a time, there was a ship in the ocean. It was sailing by itself and it was in trouble. The ship was very big and there were a lot of scary waves around it.

Suddenly, there was a loud bang! Something was wrong and the ship couldn't move. It was stuck in the water and it was very difficult to get out.

Then a brave knight came to help! He was strong and he had a big boat. He sailed his boat towards the ship and was able to rescue it.

He worked very hard, pushing the ship away from the waves. The waves were very big and it was a difficult job, but the knight was brave and he did it!

The boat was safe at last. The knight was very pleased with himself and the people of the boat thanked him for saving them from the ocean. They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest near her house. One day, while she was walking, she found a mushroom. It was big and red, and it looked very yummy. She picked it up and smelled it, but she didn't know if it was safe to eat. 

Lily felt dizzy and didn't know what to do. She decided to ask her mom. "Mommy, can I eat this mushroom?" she asked. Her mom looked at it and said, "I'm not sure, Lily. Let's guess that it's not safe to eat. We don't want you to get sick." 

Lily was sad that she couldn't eat the mushroom, but she was happy that her mom helped her. From then on, she always asked her mom before eating anything she found in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved fashion. She spent all of her time imagining what it would be like to have the perfect outfit for her. Every day, she would go searching for new clothes that she could wear.

One day, she found the most perfect dress. It was her favourite colour, and it fit her perfectly. She was so excited, she decided to wear it that same day.

When she got to school, all the other students crowded around to admire her dress. She was so proud and happy. She knew that it was the best choice she had ever made.

But then her teacher told her she couldn't wear it. The dress was too fancy, too 'fit' for school. She felt so sad and embarrassed. Tears ran down her face, and she had to go home without her perfect dress.

The little girl was never able to wear her dress again. She still remembers it with sadness. She never imagined it would end this way.

One day, a sailor went to the sea on his boat. He liked to see the fish and the birds and the waves. He had a big bag of bread and cheese to eat when he was hungry.

But he sailed too far and got lost. He could not see the land or any other boats. He was very scared and sad. He ate all his bread and cheese, but he was still hungry. He had no water to drink, only salt water.

He saw a small island with some trees and flowers. He hoped to find some food and water there. He sailed to the island and jumped off his boat. He ran to the trees and looked for fruits. He saw some red and yellow and purple fruits that looked like balls. He picked one and bit it. It was sweet and juicy. He was happy and ate more fruits.

He heard a voice behind him. "Hello, sailor. Who are you?" He turned and saw a girl with long hair and a dress made of leaves. She was holding a basket of flowers. She smiled at him.

"I am Lila. I live on this island. These are my flowers. I like to pick them and make them into necklaces. They bloom every day and make the island beautiful. Do you like them?"

The sailor was surprised and glad. He said, "I am Sam. I came from far away. I got lost and hungry. I found your fruits and ate some. They are very good. Thank you for sharing them. I like your flowers. They are very pretty. Can I have one?"

Lila nodded and gave him a flower. She said, "You are welcome, Sam. You can have as many fruits and flowers as you want. You can stay on this island with me. I have a hut and a well and a fire. We can be friends."

Sam smiled and took the flower. He said, "Thank you, Lila. You are very kind and nice. I would like to stay with you and be your friend. Maybe we can find a way to go back to my home someday. But for now, I am happy here with you and your island."

They held hands and walked to the hut. They ate more fruits and drank some water. They made necklaces of flowers and put them on each other. They laughed and played and sang. They were not scared or sad or hungry anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He liked to ride his bike in the park. One day, he saw a big insect flying around. It was a butterfly! Timmy thought it was famous because it had lots of pretty colors on its wings. He wanted to ride his bike and follow the butterfly. 

So, Timmy got on his bike and started to ride. He followed the butterfly all around the park. The butterfly flew up high and then down low, and Timmy rode his bike fast and slow. Timmy had so much fun riding his bike and following the famous butterfly. 

Finally, the butterfly landed on a flower. Timmy stopped his bike and watched it for a while. Then, the butterfly flew away. Timmy was sad to see it go, but he was happy that he got to ride his bike and see the famous insect. From that day on, Timmy loved to ride his bike and look for insects in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. They had a big yard with lots of trees and flowers. One day, Lily saw a little bird sitting on a branch. The bird looked sad.

Lily said to the bird, "Why are you sad?" The bird replied, "My home burned down last year. Now I have no place to live." Lily felt sad for the bird and she wanted to help. She thought about what she could do.

Lily had an idea. She asked her mom and dad if they could help her build a new home for the bird. They said yes, and together they built a little birdhouse. They hung it on a tree in their yard. The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you, Lily!" From that day on, Lily and the bird became good friends.

Once there was a man and a small girl. The girl was only 3 years old and was called Alice. She wanted to go on an adventure.

The man took Alice to the river. He showed her a big boat that she could sit on and play.

Alice ran over to the boat, jumped in and grabbed the handle. She held it tight.

The man then said, â€œnow we will go and explore!â€

Alice was very excited and the man started to row the boat along the river. However, the boat was suddenly stuck in some mud.

Alice started to worry. The man said, â€œdonâ€™t worry Alice, I know what to do. Iâ€™ll get a big stick and try to move the boat.â€

Alice watched the man use the stick to push the boat loose. The boat was free!

Alice was amazed and asked the man, â€œdid you lie to that boat to get it to move?â€

The man laughed and replied, â€œno, I didnâ€™t lie. I just had to use the stick to get a good grip and push it tight against the mud!â€

Once upon a time, there was a sheep who wanted to impress her friends. She had an idea of how to do it. She found a smooth stone and decided to show them. When she arrived, she was shy and embarrassed. She didn't want to make a fool of herself.

The sheep's friends saw the stone and said, "Wow! That looks really cool!" The sheep smiled and was really happy.

Suddenly, a loud voice boomed through the area. "What're you doing with that smooth stone?"

The sheep's face went red and she felt embarrassed. Her friends giggled and the sheep quickly put the stone away.

The sheep was embarrassed but happy that she had made her friends smile. She learned that it's alright to take risks, even when you're scared.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys on the carpet in the living room. But sometimes they make a big mess and do not clean up. Mama is not happy when she sees the mess. She tells them to put their toys away and help her with the chores.

One day, Sara and Ben are playing with their blocks and cars on the carpet. They build a tall tower and a long road. They have a lot of fun, but they also drop some blocks and cars on the floor. They do not notice the mess they make. They are too busy playing.

Mama comes into the living room and sees the mess. She is very angry. She says, "Sara and Ben, this is very bad! You made a big mess on the carpet and the floor. You did not listen to me when I told you to clean up. Now you have to stop playing and help me with the chores. And no more toys for you today!"

Sara and Ben are sad and sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mama. We did not mean to make a mess. We were just playing. Please do not take our toys away. We will help you with the chores. We will clean up the carpet and the floor. Please forgive us, Mama."

Mama sees that Sara and Ben are sincere. She says, "I forgive you, Sara and Ben. But you have to learn to be more careful and responsible. Playing is fun, but you also have to do your part and help me with the housework. And you have to listen to me when I tell you something. Do you understand?"

Sara and Ben nod and say, "We understand, Mama. We will try to be better. We love you, Mama." They hug Mama and then they help her with the chores. They manage to clean up the carpet and the floor. They also help Mama with the dishes and the laundry. They feel good about themselves and they make Mama happy.

The moral of the story is: You have to listen to your parents and help them with the chores. You also have to be careful and clean up your mess. Playing is fun, but you also have to be responsible.

Once there was a girl named Isla. She was three years old and loved playing in the backyard.

Today, Isla was feeling excited. She put on her apron, which was bright and clean. Isla looked around and saw the big, green grass outside.

She stepped outside and smiled. Then she began to skip. She skipped up and down the garden. She laughed and smiled as she skipped. Every now and then she would stop to smell the beautiful flowers.

The sun was setting and Isla knew it was time to go inside. She skipped one last time before she went back inside.

Isla smiled and felt happy. She couldn't wait to play outside again tomorrow.

Once upon a time there was a big house with a tall, tall tree by it. Climbing the tree was fun, but one day the kitten got stuck way up in the top. He meowed sadly for help.

The cat's mommy and daddy got very worried and looked for a way to save him. They ran to the garage and found a ladder. They put the ladder up against the tree and quickly climbed up.

The mommy and daddy were so happy to get to the kitten and bring him back down safely. He was purring loudly with happiness.

The mommy and daddy were very sorry for not watching the kitten closer. They hugged him tight and said they would never let him get stuck in a tree ever again.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there was a gifted bird named Blue. Blue could sing very pretty songs. One day, Blue met a tall giraffe named Spot. Spot had a very long neck.

Blue said to Spot, "Can I sit on your long neck? I want to gain a better view of the forest." Spot nodded and let Blue sit on his neck. From up high, Blue saw a big red fruit on a tree. Blue knew it was a yummy fruit.

Blue thanked Spot and flew to get the fruit. Blue shared the yummy fruit with Spot. They became good friends and had many fun days in the big green forest.

Lily and Ben were bored. They had nothing to do. They looked out the window and saw a dull sky. They wished they could go outside and play.

"Let's make our own parade!" Lily said. She had an idea. She ran to her room and got some toys. Ben followed her.

They took their toys to the living room. They lined them up on the floor. They had dolls, cars, trucks, animals, and blocks. They added some hats and scarves to make them look funny.

"Now we need some music!" Ben said. He found a drum and a whistle. He gave the whistle to Lily and kept the drum.

They marched around the living room, blowing the whistle and banging the drum. They made their toys follow them. They pretended they were in a big parade.

They had so much fun. They forgot about the dull sky. They made their own sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom loved to play with his ball. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends.

At the park, Tom and his friends saw a big pitch. They all wanted to play on it. Tom had to choose who would play on the pitch first. He thought it was a hard job, but he did not want to be stupid.

Tom chose his best friend, Tim, to play first. Then, he chose the others one by one. They all played on the pitch and had lots of fun. They did not think Tom was stupid. They were all happy and played until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was an arrow. It was so happy and shiny. It flew high in the sky all day.

Then suddenly, it saw a game to play. It was a fun game of tag. The arrow went very fast and finished first. It made all the other things playing tag laugh. They thought it was so funny.

But then the arrow got tired. So it flew to its home. At home the arrow was safe and happy. It stayed there until the end of the day.

Then it was time to finish the game. So the arrow said goodbye and flew away. It was off to find another fun game to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big head and liked to play with his friends. One day, he saw a distant hill and wanted to go there.

Tim asked his friend Sam, "Do you want to go to the hill with me?" Sam said, "Yes, let's go!" They walked and walked until they reached the hill. They were very tired, but they were happy to be there.

At the top of the hill, they found a small tree with red berries. Tim saw the berries and said, "Let's eat these!" But Sam said, "No, my mom said they might pinch our mouths." Tim listened to Sam, and they did not eat the berries. On their way back home, they told their friends about the hill and the berries. They were happy they did not eat the berries, and they all had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy figure who was always looking for ways to relax. One day, he saw a big tree in the distance and decided to take a nap. As he was lying there, a small voice shouted, â€œHey! Wake up!â€

The lazy figure opened his eyes and saw a small child standing in front of him. The child was insisting that the figure should come play with him. But the lazy figure was feeling too lazy to move so he politely declined the friendly offer. 

The child was very persistent, though, and he kept insisting that the figure should come play. So the figure finally gave in and agreed to follow the child's lead.

And so, the lazy figure followed the boy and had the most amazing day! They laughed and played for hours and soon their day had come to an end. The figure was very grateful for the company and said goodbye to the wonderful little child. 

The figure returned home feeling refreshed and kids all around continued to insist that he join them to have lots of fun. 

The end.

Once upon a time, in a humble nation, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim had a special toy, a magic ball. This ball could vanish and come back when he called it.

One sunny day, Tim was playing with his magic ball in the park. He threw the ball high up in the sky. The ball vanished! Tim looked around, but he could not see it. He called out, "Ball, come back!" But the ball did not come back.

Tim was very sad. He walked home with a heavy heart. When he reached his house, he saw the ball on his bed. The ball had come back! Tim was so happy that he hugged the ball tightly. They played together every day and never let the ball vanish again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a special tool. It was a toy shovel. He liked to play with his shovel in the sand. One day, Tim saw a big ice cube. It was very cold.

Tim wanted to make the ice cube go away. He used his toy shovel as a tool to hit the ice cube. It did not work. Tim had an idea. He remembered that the sun can melt things. He put the ice cube under the sun.

Tim waited and watched from a distant spot. As the sun shone on the ice cube, it started to melt. Tim was happy. He knew the sun would help. The ice cube became smaller and smaller until it was all gone. Tim went back to play with his toy shovel in the sand.

One day, Sally saw a carrot in her garden. She wanted to pick it and eat it. She made a plan to fly up and grab it. She jumped as high as she could, flapping her arms. She felt so dizzy while she was flying!

Suddenly, a car drove past. It was her mom! She came to pick Sally up in the car. Sally was so excited that she waved and smiled.

On the way home, Sally got hungrier and hungrier. When her mom stopped the car, Sally opened the door and ran to the garden. She flew up, grabbed the carrot and ran inside.

Sally was so happy! She had a crunchy, juicy carrot waiting for her.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. They see the dishwasher. It is big and shiny. They want to see what is inside.

"Let's open it!" Anna says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They pull the door. It is heavy. They see plates and cups and forks and spoons. They are wet and clean.

"Wow!" Anna says. "Can we hold them?"

"Sure!" Ben says. "But be careful. They might break."

They take out some plates and cups. They hold them in their hands. They feel cold and slippery. They pretend to eat and drink.

"Yum!" Anna says. "This is fun!"

"Uh-oh!" Ben says. He drops a plate. It falls on the floor. It breaks into pieces. It makes a loud noise.

"Ben!" Anna says. "You broke it!"

"I'm sorry!" Ben says. "It was too slippery!"

They hear footsteps. They see Mom. She looks angry. She sees the broken plate. She sees the open dishwasher. She sees the wet plates and cups in their hands.

"Anna! Ben!" Mom says. "What are you doing? You are not supposed to touch the dishwasher! You could have hurt yourself! And you made a mess!"

She takes the plates and cups from them. She puts them back in the dishwasher. She closes the door. She picks up the broken pieces. She throws them in the trash.

She turns to Anna and Ben. They feel scared. They feel uncomfortable. They know they are in trouble.

"Go to your room!" Mom says. "Now!"

Anna and Ben run to their room. They cry. They hug each other. They wish they had not played with the dishwasher. They wish they had listened to Mom. They are sorry. But it is too late. They have a bad ending.

Once upon a time there were two friends. They were called Sarah and Henry. Sarah and Henry were very competitive and always wanted to try harder than each other.

One week, Sarah and Henry had decided to play a game. They both wanted to see who could quiet the room the fastest. Henry shut the door and Sarah shut the window. Both of them worked quickly.

They both raced to the living room and shut the television. Then to the kitchen where Henry shut the cupboard doors and Sarah shut the fridge. Finally, they shut the lights in the hall.

They had done it! They had shut the entire house. Sarah and Henry looked at each other with huge smiles on their faces. They had done it in the same time â€“ they were tied! And they both felt very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Floppy. Floppy loved to play in the garden and nibble on carrots. One day, while hopping around, Floppy saw a shiny rock. He picked it up and started to play with it. Suddenly, he accidentally scattered the rock and it hit a root.

The root was very important because it helped the flowers grow. Floppy tried to fix it but it was too late. The flowers started to wilt and the garden became sad. Floppy felt very bad and wished he had been more careful.

The next day, Floppy saw a snake in the garden. He tried to run away but his leg got stuck in a flexible branch. The snake came closer and closer until it was too late. Floppy was very scared and sad. The garden was never the same without him.

Once there were two frogs who lived in a green closet. Their names were Dave and Lulu. Dave and Lulu were always fighting. Even though they were good friends, they still argued a lot. 

One day, Dave and Lulu started fighting again. They were hopping around the closet and shouting at each other. Dave wanted to go play outside, and Lulu wanted to stay inside and think. They just couldn't agree. 

Eventually, Dave decided to take a nap. Lulu was tired too, so she crept over and lay down next to him. As the two friends drifted off to sleep, the quarrel was forgotten. 

In the morning, Dave and Lulu hopped out of the closet. They went outside and had a wonderful day playing. Even though they fought sometimes, they still loved being friends.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who lived in a small house. One day she decided to go for a walk in the woods near her house. While she was walking, she saw a small door in the ground. She used all her strength to push it open and saw some stairs that led up to an attic.

She went up the stairs and when she entered the attic, she saw someone. He was dressed in all black and he looked like he was in a hurry. He spoke to the young girl, "You should not be here. Hurry, go back the way you came".

The young girl was scared and she quickly ran back the way she had come. But before she could get very far away, the man chasing her appeared. He was coming closer and closer. 

The young girl started to cry and she ran faster, but she couldn't outrun the man. He quickly caught up to her and grabbed her. 

The young girl was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat yogurt every day. She would eat it for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. One day, Lily's mommy told her that eating too much yogurt would make her weigh more and more.

Lily didn't want to be heavy, so she started to eat less yogurt. She also started to eat more fruits and vegetables. Lily's mommy was happy to see her daughter making healthy choices.

As Lily grew up, she learned that being wealthy wasn't just about having lots of money. It was also about being healthy and happy. Lily was grateful for the lesson her mommy taught her about the importance of taking care of her body.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit who loved to chew. He would spend all day nibbling away on different things. One particular day, he found himself at a mill. He started to chew on some of the grain, but it was too spicy for him! He started to feel a burning sensation in his mouth and he was very uncomfortable.

He tried to find something else to chew on, but there was nothing around in the mill. He looked up and down the mill, a bit desperate, but he couldn't find anything. He was really stuck and he started to get worried. 

Suddenly, at the other end of the mill, he spotted some juicy apples! He hopped over as fast as he could and started to chomp on one of them. The apples were just enough to take away the spiciness from the grain and he felt much better. 

The little rabbit was very happy to have found something to chew on, and went happily on his way.

Little Emily was a brave girl. But one day when she opened the gate she was frightened. As she went through the gate, she heard a strange noise. Emily wasn't sure what it was. She wanted to believe it was an animal, but she was scared. She closed her eyes and held her breath, she was too scared to look. After a few minutes, she slowly opened her eyes.
