And to her surprise, it was just a bird singing! Emily was no longer frightened, she was happy. She opened the gate and went through it to see the bird. The bird flew away, so Emily just waved and said goodbye. She then closed the gate and went home. She had learned that you should always believe in yourself, no matter how scared you are.

Once upon a time there was a deep, dark forest. In the forest, there was a little cottage and inside the cottage there lived a very old queen.

Every morning, the queen would wake and look out of her window, into the deep darkness of the forest. The queen felt all alone in her cottage and she was very lonely.

One night, the queen heard a noise outside of her window. When she looked out into the darkness, she saw something that made her gasp with delight and joy. There, standing in the deep, dark forest was a little girl. The little girl smiled and waved at the queen and the queen waved back.

From then on, the queen and the little girl would play together in the forest every morning when the queen woke up. They would pick flowers and run around like two friends. The queen was no longer lonely and the little girl had a new friend to explore the deep, dark forest with.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to travel with his mom. He was very excited. He took his toy car, his teddy bear, and his thermometer. Tim was a persistent little boy.

On their way, Tim saw a big dog. Tim said to his mom, "Look, a big dog!" The dog looked at them and wagged its tail. Tim's mom said, "Yes, it's a big and friendly dog."

Tim and his mom walked and walked. Tim looked at his thermometer. It was hot. He said, "Mom, it's hot. Can we rest?" His mom said, "Sure, let's rest under that tree."

They sat under the tree and had a snack. Tim was happy he could travel with his mom. He knew being persistent helped him have a fun day.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play at the beach. They make sand castles and look for shells. One day, they see a big whale in the water. The whale is happy. It jumps and splashes and makes loud noises.

"Wow, look at the whale!" Tim says. "It is so big and fun!"

"I want to see it closer!" Sam says. "Let's swim to it!"

Tim is scared. He does not want to swim to the whale. He thinks the whale is too big and might hurt them.

"No, Sam, don't go!" Tim says. "The whale is not a toy! It is a wild animal! It might not like us!"

But Sam does not listen. He runs into the water and swims to the whale. He wants to touch it and play with it. He thinks the whale is friendly.

The whale sees Sam. It is curious. It swims to Sam and opens its mouth. It does not want to eat Sam. It just wants to say hello. But Sam does not know that. He thinks the whale wants to bite him. He is very scared. He screams and tries to swim away.

"Help, help!" Sam cries. "The whale is going to get me!"

Tim hears Sam. He is worried. He wants to help his friend. He runs into the water and swims to Sam. He grabs his hand and pulls him away from the whale. He is brave.

"Come on, Sam, let's go back!" Tim says. "The whale is not bad, but it is not safe to swim with it!"

Sam and Tim swim back to the shore. They are wet and tired and scared. They hug each other and say sorry.

"I'm sorry, Tim, I was silly," Sam says. "I should have listened to you. You are a good friend."

"I'm sorry, Sam, I was angry," Tim says. "I should have been nicer to you. You are a good friend, too."

They smile and laugh and play again. They are happy. They watch the whale from a distance. The whale is happy, too. It waves its tail and says goodbye.

Mary and her brother Sam love to play together. One day they decided to clap their hands and see who could clap the loudest. Sam clapped extra loudly, and Mary clapped extra fast. 

Mama heard the noise and came in to see what was going on. She saw Mary and Sam clapping, and she smiled.

Mama said, "You two were being very naughty, but because you were having fun I will give you each a cookie!"

With that, Mary and Sam stopped clapping and each one grabbed a cookie. They were both very happy. 

Mama said that from now on, they had to be good whenever they clapped because it was too loud. Mary and Sam agreed, giggling and eating their cookies. 

The two had so much fun together, and Mama was happy to see them happy.

John was a young boy who had a mom and a dad. They loved him very much and wanted to raise him well. Every morning, they would wave goodbye to him as he went to school.

One day, John's dad told him he was going on a trip. His family was going to help him pack his luggage. John was excited! He was allowed to choose his own suitcase. He chose a white one that sparkled and shone in the sunlight.

On the day of the trip, John raised the white luggage up and put it in the car. He said goodbye to his mom and dad. He knew he would miss them, but he was ready for his trip.

Once there was a brave girl. She wanted to balance on a tough triangle. At first it seemed difficult, but she kept trying. She had to balance on just one foot and using her arms to keep her steady.

She kept practicing and soon she understood how to balance on the triangle. She practised every day and got better and better. 

She kept going, until one day she could balance on the triangle without any help. She smiled with joy and was proud of herself. 

From then on she kept practicing, challenging herself to stay on the triangle even longer. Her friends were amazed when they saw her balancing on the triangle. 

She was really proud of herself and kept going until she was the best at balancing on the triangle.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was three years old. He was playing with his friends in the park. It was a nice day and Tom was having fun.

Suddenly Tom saw that he had torn his shirt. He was very sad. He didn't know what to do. He looked around, but there was no one who could help him fix it.

So Tom decided he would have to try and fix it himself. He got out some scissors, some thread and a needle. It was tough, but Tom managed to sew up his shirt. Tom was very pleased with his work, and he went to show his friends.

They were all very impressed with how tough Tom had been. He had decided that he could do it, and he had! From then on, Tom had a special shirt, which he was very proud of. The end.

Lily and Ben are playing in the living room. They have a new picture book with many animals. Lily likes the giraffe and Ben likes the lion. They take turns to look at the pages and make noises like the animals.

"Look, Lily, this is a lion. Roar!" Ben says, holding the book.

"Wow, Ben, he is big and yellow. Can I see the giraffe?" Lily asks, reaching for the book.

Ben does not want to share. He pulls the book back. Lily pulls harder. They tug and tug until the book rips in half. They hear a loud tear and see the pages fall to the floor.

"Oh no, we broke the new picture!" Lily cries.

"Mommy, mommy, help!" Ben shouts.

Mommy comes running from the kitchen. She sees the mess and the tears. She is not happy.

"What happened here? Who broke the new picture book?" Mommy asks.

Lily and Ben look at each other. They feel sorry and scared. They do not want to get in trouble.

"We did, mommy. We are sorry. We wanted to see the animals. We did not mean to break it." Lily says.

Mommy sighs. She picks up the pieces and hugs the children.

"I know you did not mean to break it, but you have to be careful with your things. And you have to share and take turns. The picture book was a gift from grandma. She will be sad if she sees it like this." Mommy says.

Lily and Ben nod. They say sorry again. Mommy smiles and wipes their tears.

"It's okay. I will try to fix the picture book with some tape. But next time, be gentle and kind. And maybe we can go to the zoo and see the real animals. How does that sound?" Mommy says.

Lily and Ben cheer up. They hug mommy and say thank you. They promise to be good and share. They are excited to see the zoo. They hope the lion and the giraffe are there.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the big yard behind his house. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her rake the leaves. Timmy grabbed the rake and started to gather the leaves into a big pile.

After they finished raking, Timmy's mom brought out some cookies. Timmy was so happy! He took a cookie and spread some butter on it. It tasted so good! Timmy's mom told him that it was important to share with his friends and be fair. So, Timmy shared his cookies with his little sister and they both had a great time playing in the yard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was very hungry and wanted to eat a sandwich. She asked her mom, "Mommy, can I have a sandwich please?" Her mom said yes and made her a yummy sandwich.

Lily was so excited to eat her sandwich, but it was on the table and she was too short to reach it. She said, "Mommy, I can't reach my sandwich!" Her mom said, "Don't worry, let me help you." She reached the sandwich and gave it to Lily.

Lily took a big bite and said, "This sandwich is crazy good!" Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, sweetie." And they both ate their sandwiches happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a cat. She was a selfish cat; she only wanted to take care of herself. One day, she was walking outside and saw a sign. It said: "Help others!" She didn't know what it meant.

Suddenly, she met an old lady. The old lady asked the cat for help carrying her groceries up the stairs. The selfish cat thought to herself, "I don't want to help her; I want to take care of myself." But then, she remembered the sign she saw earlier. She decided to help the old lady.

After helping her up the stairs, the cat felt really happy. She realised that helping others was more satisfying than being selfish.

From then on, the cat always chose to help others, even if it meant she had to give up something for herself. She knew it was the right thing to do. And that's the moral of this story: it's better to help others than to be selfish.

Jenny liked to bake cakes with her mom. They had a big book with many recipes and pictures of yummy cakes. Jenny liked to look at the book and choose a cake to make. Mom was very organized. She always had all the ingredients and tools ready before they started.

One day, Jenny picked a cake with pink frosting and sprinkles. She showed it to mom and said, "Let's make this one, mom. It looks so pretty and sweet." Mom smiled and said, "Okay, Jenny. That's a good choice. But we need one more thing. We need sugar. We don't have any sugar left in the jar."

Jenny was sad. She wanted to make the cake now. She asked, "Can we go to the store and buy some sugar, mom?" Mom shook her head and said, "No, Jenny. The store is too far and we don't have time. But maybe we can ask our neighbor, Mrs. Lee, if she can lend us some sugar. She is very nice and she likes to bake too. Maybe she has some extra sugar we can use."

Jenny liked Mrs. Lee. She was an old lady who lived next door. She always gave Jenny cookies and candies when she visited. Jenny agreed and said, "Okay, mom. Let's ask Mrs. Lee. Maybe she can help us." Mom and Jenny put on their coats and shoes and went to Mrs. Lee's house. They knocked on the door and waited.

Mrs. Lee opened the door and smiled. She saw mom and Jenny and said, "Hello, my dears. What can I do for you?" Mom explained that they wanted to bake a cake but they ran out of sugar. She asked, "Do you have some sugar you can lend us, Mrs. Lee? We only need a little bit. We will return it to you later." Mrs. Lee nodded and said, "Of course, my dears. I have plenty of sugar. Come in, come in. I have something else for you too."

Mom and Jenny followed Mrs. Lee into her kitchen. They saw a big cake on the table. It had pink frosting and sprinkles. It looked just like the cake Jenny wanted to make. Jenny gasped and said, "Wow, Mrs. Lee. That's a beautiful cake. It's the same as the one in our book." Mrs. Lee smiled and said, "Yes, Jenny. It is. I made it this morning. And you know what? It's for you. I wanted to surprise you and give you a treat. You are such a good and sweet girl. You can have the cake and the sugar. Happy baking, my dears." Mom and Jenny were very happy and grateful. They thanked Mrs. Lee and hugged her. They took the cake and the sugar and went back to their house. They had a wonderful time eating the cake and baking another one. They shared some with Mrs. Lee too. They were very lucky to have such a nice and generous neighbor.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a nice note that she wanted to show her friend, Max. So, she went to Max's house and knocked on the door. Max opened the door and said, "Hi, Lily! What do you have there?" 

Lily replied, "I have a nice note for you to see." 

Max took the note and said, "This is great! But I want to keep it forever." 

Lily said, "No, Max. We can share it. We can separate it and each keep a piece." 

Max thought about it and said, "Okay, that's a good idea. Let's do that." 

So, they separated the note and each kept a piece. They were both happy and their friendship continued to grow. The end.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy some food. Tim saw a big pick of apples. He said, "Mom, can we get some apples?"

His mom said, "Yes, Tim. You can pick some apples." Tim picked red apples and green apples. He put them in a bag. Then, they went to pay for the apples.

At the store, it was very cold. Tim said, "Mom, I am cold." His mom said, "Let's pay and go home." They paid for the apples and went home.

At home, Tim and his mom ate the apples. They were happy. The apples were good and not cold anymore.

Max was out sailing on his boat. He loved everything about it - the big blue water, the wind and being out on the open sea. But Max wasn't alone today. Suddenly, a fierce pirate appeared on the horizon. He wanted to cut Max's boat!

Max was scared. He didn't know what to do! But then he had an idea. He started sailing very fast. The pirate tried to catch him, but he was too fast. He sailed away and finally reached the shore, where he was safe.

Max looked back and saw the pirate sailing away. He was still a bit scared but felt very brave. He had been fierce in the face of danger. He was proud of himself for showing so much courage.

Sara likes tuna very much. She eats tuna every day for lunch. She thinks tuna is yummy and good for her. She also likes to share tuna with her cat, Luna. Luna is a white cat with blue eyes. Sara thinks Luna is very attractive and soft.

One day, Sara's mom gives her a sandwich with tuna and cheese. Sara is happy and says, "Thank you, mom. I love tuna and cheese." She takes her sandwich and goes to the backyard. She sees Luna sitting on the grass. She says, "Hi, Luna. Do you want some tuna?" She breaks a piece of her sandwich and gives it to Luna. Luna purrs and eats the tuna.

Sara and Luna enjoy their lunch together. They play with a ball and a string. They have fun and laugh. Sara forgets about her sandwich. She leaves it on the table. She runs and chases Luna. They roll on the grass and hug.

A bird sees the sandwich on the table. It thinks the sandwich looks tasty. It flies to the table and pecks at the sandwich. It takes a big bite of the tuna and cheese. It likes it very much. It takes another bite and another. It eats the whole sandwich.

Sara and Luna get tired. They go back to the table. They want to eat more tuna. But they see the sandwich is gone. They see the bird flying away with a piece of bread in its beak. They are sad and angry. They say, "Hey, bird. That's our tuna. Give it back." But the bird does not listen. It flies away and sings. Sara and Luna feel hungry and sorry. They wish they did not forget their sandwich. They go inside and ask mom for more tuna. Mom smiles and says, "OK, but next time, don't forget your lunch." Sara and Luna nod and say, "We won't, mom. We love tuna."

Once there was a little girl named Sophie who loved to drink fresh juice. She would always ask her mom for a juice wherever they went. One day when mommy and Sophie were out shopping, Sophie saw something that she just had to have. It was a cup filled with a yellow liquid.

"Mommy, what's in the cup?" Sophie asked.

"It's a juice, honey" said mommy. "It smells delicious!"

Sophie carefully took a sip. It was mild and didn't have too much heat. She drank so much her mommy had to buy her two more cups. Sophie happily gulped it down and smiled.

"That was the best juice I ever had!" said Sophie.

Mommy smiled and hugged Sophie. She was glad Sophie loved the mild sunshine juice so much.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She was happy and very thoughtful. One day, when Sarah was playing in her house, she noticed something strange.

The stairs were moving!

Sarah thought this was odd, but then a bearded man in a funny hat stepped out of the moving stairs. 

"Hello, Sarah," the man said. "Would you like to play with me?"

Sarah felt very excited and she said yes.

The bearded man laughed and showed Sarah all the fun things she could do inside the moving stairs. They played lots of games and Sarah laughed and smiled the whole time.

When it was time to go, Sarah said goodbye to her new friend with a big hug. As she waved goodbye to thestairs, she felt very happy and thoughtful.

John saw something very cute in the park. He went to look and saw a huge, fluffy white kitten. He was so happy that he just wanted to hug it. He ran over and tried to pick up the kitten, but it ran off! John chased it for a long time, but the kitten was very fast and soon he couldn't see it anymore.

John was sad, but then he saw something else. A huge tree with lots of leaves! He went to look at it, and the kitten was hiding in the branches! John smiled, and the kitten jumped down and came up to him. John patted the kitten and laughed with joy!

One sunny day, Lily and her mom were walking in the park. Lily loved the park; she could smell the sweet smell of nature, and enjoy the sunshine on her face.

"Mom, let's go play on the slides," Lily said, as they passed the playground.

"Okay," her mom said with a smile.

Lily ran over to the slide, but as she tried to climb the ladder, she began to slip. She grabbed onto the rungs, but soon both of her feet were in the air.

"Oh no!" Lily said, feeling embarrassed.

Her mom ran over, and caught her in her arms. Lily looked up at her mom's eye, and saw how sweetly she was smiling.

"We'll try again," her mom said, lifting her up and setting her back down on the ladder.

Lily began climbing again, and this time, she made it all the way up to the top. She gave a victorious smile, then quickly slipped down the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, she was playing with her friend Timmy when they saw a charming little frog hopping towards them.

"Hello, Mr. Frog!" said Lily.

"Hi there, little ones. Can you help me find my way back to the drain?" asked the frog.

"Sure, we can help!" said Timmy.

They followed the frog to the drain and helped him part the leaves that were blocking his way. The frog was very grateful and said, "Thank you, you two are very kind."

Lily and Timmy smiled and said goodbye to the charming frog as he hopped away. They felt happy that they could help a new friend.

Lily was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to make them talk and have tea parties. She heard a loud noise from downstairs. It sounded like a big bang. She was frightened. She wanted to see what it was, but she was scared to go alone.

She ran to her brother's room. He was older and bigger than her. He was reading a book on his bed. She said, "Tom, Tom, come with me. There is a loud noise downstairs. I am frightened."

Tom put down his book and looked at Lily. He saw that she was shaking. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will come with you. Maybe it is just the wind or the cat. Let's go and see."

They held hands and walked downstairs. They saw that the telephone was on the floor. It was broken. The cord was cut. There was a window open. The wind was blowing the curtains. They heard a voice from outside. It said, "Help, help, I am stuck in the tree."

They looked outside and saw a man in a mask. He was holding a bag. He was trying to climb down from the tree, but he was stuck. He had thrown the telephone out of the window to cut the cord. He had tried to rob their house, but he had heard them coming and ran away. He had climbed the tree to escape, but he had fallen and got caught.

Tom and Lily were very brave. They ran to the kitchen and got a big knife. They cut the cord that was holding the man in the tree. He fell to the ground with a thud. He was hurt and angry. He said, "You little brats, let me go. I will get you."

Tom and Lily did not let him go. They ran to the door and locked it. They called the police with their cell phone. They said, "There is a bad man outside. He tried to rob our house. He broke our telephone. He is stuck in the tree. Please come and get him."

The police came very fast. They saw the man in the mask. They put him in handcuffs. They said, "You are under arrest. You are a very bad man. You will go to jail."

Tom and Lily were very happy. They hugged each other. They said, "We did it. We stopped the bad man. We are not frightened anymore."

The police praised them. They said, "You are very brave and smart. You did the right thing. You are heroes."

Tom and Lily smiled. They said, "Thank you, police. You are very nice and strong. You are heroes too."

One day, a girl named Mia went to the park with her mom. When she arrived, she saw a delicate butterfly flying in the air. Mia was so excited that her face lit up with a smile. She quickly ran to the butterfly, trying to catch it with her hands. Her mom smiled and said to her, â€œWhy donâ€™t you try and kiss it?â€

Mia thought this was a fun idea, so she quickly puckered up her lips and blew a kiss to the butterfly. To her surprise, the delicate butterfly stopped flying and landed right on Miaâ€™s nose! Mia and her mom laughed, and Mia couldnâ€™t help but smile. She was so proud that her kiss was strong enough to make the butterfly stop flying and come to her. 

They spent the rest of the day playing together, with the butterfly joining in on the fun. When it was time to go home, the butterfly flew away, leaving a smile on Miaâ€™s face. She waved goodbye to the delicate butterfly and went home with her mom.

Once, Bob saw a tall pool. He wanted to stay inside it. So, he hopped in.

Bob was happy to feel cool in the pool. He swam around and got a lot of splashes! 

"Can I play too, Bob?" asked his sister Helen.

"Yes!" shouted Bob, and he quickly showed Helen how to swim.

The two of them stayed in the tall pool for hours and hours. They were having so much fun that they forgot how late it had gotten!

Mom came to the pool and called out, "Come on. It's time to go home now!" 

So Bob and Helen reluctantly stayed out of the big pool, and went home to bed.

Once upon a time, there was a sad girl. Her mum had said she had to go upstairs and collect her toys, but the girl did not want to. She wanted to stay and play outside.

The girl started to cry and her mum was very cross. The girl was scared and she ran up the stairs. But, when she got at the top, she realised that all of her toys had been taken away! 

The girl was very sad. She sat on the stairs and started to cry again. Her mum heard her and came upstairs to have a look. Seeing the girl's sad face, she found it in her heart to forgive her. 

Mum said that even though the girl had been naughty, she was still loved. The girl smiled and hugged her mum. Together, they gathered up the toys and the girl was no longer sad.

Tim and Mia were at the zoo with their mom. They liked to see the animals and learn their names. Tim's favorite was the lion, because it was big and strong and had a loud roar. Mia's favorite was the monkey, because it was funny and smart and liked to play.

They walked around the zoo and saw many different animals. They saw the elephant, the giraffe, the zebra, the bear, and the penguin. They also saw a vendor who sold ice cream and popcorn. Mom bought them some treats and they sat on a bench to eat.

"Look, there's the lion!" Tim said, pointing to the cage. "He's sleeping. I wish he would roar."

"Maybe he's tired," Mia said. "Or maybe he's bored. He doesn't have much to do in there."

"Let's go closer and see if we can wake him up," Tim said. He got up and ran to the cage, holding his ice cream cone. Mia followed him, holding her popcorn bag.

They stood in front of the cage and looked at the lion. He was fat and furry, with a big mane and a long tail. He was lying on his side, with his eyes closed and his mouth open.

"Roar, lion, roar!" Tim shouted, waving his ice cream cone. "Show us how loud you can be!"

The lion did not move. He did not hear Tim. He was dreaming of the savanna, where he could run and hunt and be free.

"Roar, lion, roar!" Mia shouted, throwing some popcorn at the cage. "We want to hear you!"

The lion did not move. He did not see Mia. He was dreaming of his pride, where he had a mate and cubs and friends.

"Roar, lion, roar!" Tim and Mia shouted together, making their own roars. "You're the king of the zoo!"

The lion did not move. He did not care about Tim and Mia. He was dreaming of a better life.

But the vendor heard them. He was not happy. He did not like the noise. He did not like the mess. He did not like the waste.

"Hey, you kids, stop that!" the vendor yelled, walking towards them. "You're disturbing the animals and the visitors. And you're throwing away your food. That's not nice."

Tim and Mia saw the vendor. He was angry and scary. He had a big hat and a big apron and a big stick. He looked like a giant.

They dropped their ice cream and popcorn and ran away. They were afraid of the vendor. They did not want to get in trouble.

They ran back to their mom, who was waiting on the bench. They hugged her and told her what happened.

"Sorry, mom," Tim said. "We just wanted to hear the lion roar."

"Sorry, mom," Mia said. "We just wanted to have some fun."

Mom smiled and kissed them. She understood. She was not mad.

"It's okay, my loves," she said. "But you have to be careful and respectful at the zoo. The animals are not toys. And the vendor is not a monster. He's just doing his job."

She took their hands and led them to another cage. There they saw a tiger, who was awake and alert. He looked at them with his yellow eyes and opened his mouth.

"Roar!" he roared, loud and clear.

Tim and Mia gasped. They were amazed and thrilled. They had heard a real roar.

"Wow!" they said. "That was awesome!"

They clapped and cheered and thanked the tiger. The tiger nodded and roared again.

Mom smiled and took a picture. She was happy and proud. She had given them a memorable day.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a poor monkey. The monkey lived in a big forest with lots of trees. The monkey had no friends and was very lonely. One day, the monkey saw a group of children playing outside the forest. The monkey wanted to play too, so it decided to go and say hello. 

When the monkey got closer, one of the children poked the monkey with a stick. The monkey was scared and ran back into the forest. The monkey felt sad and alone once again. The next day, the monkey saw the children again and decided to try and make friends. But unfortunately, the children poked the monkey again and this time, they didn't stop. 

The poor monkey was hurt and couldn't move. The children ran away and left the monkey alone. The monkey lay there, hurt and lonely, until it eventually passed away. From that day on, the children never saw the monkey again, and they never knew how much they hurt it.

Lily liked to play with her toys on the big cushion in the living room. She had a doll, a bear, a car and a ball. She made them talk and move and have fun. One day, she saw a fly on the cushion. It was not moving. Lily touched it with her finger. It was dead.

Lily felt sad for the fly. She wanted to help it. She ran to the kitchen and got a cup of water. She poured some water on the fly. Maybe it was thirsty, she thought. But the fly did not wake up. It was still dead.

Lily got an idea. She ran to her room and got a blanket. She wrapped the fly in the blanket and put it on the cushion. She said, "Good night, fly. I hope you have good dreams." Then she got her doll and hugged it. She said, "Thank you, doll, for being my friend. You are not dead. You are alive and happy."

Lily's mom came into the living room and saw Lily and her doll on the cushion. She smiled and said, "What are you doing, Lily?" Lily looked up and said, "I am playing with my toys, mom. And I am saying thank you to them. They are good toys. They make me happy."

Lily's mom sat down next to Lily and said, "That's very nice of you, Lily. It's good to say thank you to the things and people that make you happy. And it's good to be kind to the things and people that are not happy. Like the fly. You tried to help the fly, didn't you?" Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. But the fly was dead. I could not make it alive. I was sad."

Lily's mom hugged Lily and said, "I know, Lily. Sometimes things die and we can't do anything about it. It's okay to be sad. But it's also okay to be happy. Because you have a lot of things and people that love you. Like me. And dad. And your toys. And the cushion. And the sun. And the moon. And the stars. And many more. Can you say thank you to them, too?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, mom. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. Thank you, toys. Thank you, cushion. Thank you, sun. Thank you, moon. Thank you, stars. Thank you, thank you, thank you."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. She was very curious, and today she was exploring her kitchen.

Sally saw a bowl full of yellow and brown. It smelled sweet and yummy so she went closer to have a better look. It was a bowl of banana and she could stir it with a spoon.

So she grabbed a spoon and started to stir. Around and around the spoon went, until something yummy happened - the banana was turning into a big, yummy pancake!

Sally was so excited, so she asked her mum. â€œMum, can I have it?â€ She asked.

Mum said, â€œYes, but itâ€™s cold, so youâ€™ll have to wait until itâ€™s warm.â€

Sally waited patiently and when the pancake was warm and ready to eat, she was so excited that she ate it in one bite!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her dog, Max. One day, Lily and Max went to the park to play. 

At the park, they saw some children playing with a ball. Lily wanted to join in, but the children said, "No, you can't play with us." Lily was sad and went to sit on a bench. 

Just then, a police officer came over and asked, "What's wrong, little girl?" Lily told the police officer what happened. The police officer said, "Don't worry, I'll talk to the children." 

The police officer went over to the children and spoke to them. Soon, the children invited Lily to play with them. Lily was so happy and said, "I win!" The police officer smiled and said, "That's lovely." 

From that day on, Lily and Max went to the park every day to play with their new friends. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived an obedient rhinoceros named Remy. Remy had many friends, but his best friend was a little bird named Benny. They loved to play together all day long.

One morning, Benny flew to Remy's side to wake him up. "Remy, Remy, wake up! It's time to play!" Benny chirped. Remy opened his big eyes and smiled at his friend. "Okay, Benny, let's play!" he said.

They played hide and seek, and tag, and had so much fun. They laughed and ran until the sun went down. At the end of the day, Remy and Benny were very tired. They said goodnight to each other and went to sleep, knowing they would wake up and play again the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a silly puppy named Bob. He loved to explore the world and see new things. One day he decided to go on an adventure. 

Bob put on his buckle and stopped to look in a nearby pond. But when he got to the edge of the pond, Bob started to wobble. He was about to fall in! 

Luckily Bob's friend the mouse was there to help. The mouse scurried over and grabbed Bob's collar to support him. Bob stayed up and he was safe again. 

The two friends had a good laugh and decided it was time to continue their adventure. Bob put his buckle back on, and the mouse slithered along behind him as they went on to explore new places.

Once upon a time there was a rich flower. The flower was very special and it was the most beautiful flower in the world. Every day, it would bloom the brightest colours. It made all the other flowers in the garden look dull in comparison.

One day, a little girl visited the garden. When she saw the flower, she was amazed by its beauty. She wanted to take the flower home with her. She had a fork in her pocket and she carefully dug it up with the fork.

When she took the flower home, something truly magical happened. Every day, the flower would bloom again and again. It kept giving the little girl gifts. She had the most beautiful garden in the world with the flower. Everybody was very happy.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very hungry and wanted to eat some food. So, the bird flew to a tree and saw some berries. The bird ate the berries and felt happy. 

On Tuesday, the little bird woke up early. It was a gray day outside. The bird wanted to play with its friends, but it had to weigh itself first. The bird flew to a scale and saw that it weighed 2 ounces. 

Later that day, the little bird met its friends and they played together. They flew around and sang songs. The bird had so much fun that it forgot about the gray day outside. When it was time to go home, the little bird felt tired but happy. It went to sleep dreaming of more fun adventures with its friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy who liked to play outside. One day, he saw something in the sky. It was a flag, waving in the wind.

The boy wanted to get a closer look, so he ran to it. On it, he found a letter. 

"What's this?" he said, picking it up.

Just then, a voice called out, "Be careful! That's a dangerous letter!" It was his mom. 

The boy was curious. "What's it say?" he asked.

"It's a message from someone telling us to be careful," his mom explained. 

The boy was excited. He asked, "Can we mail it back to the person who sent it?" 

His mom smiled. "Yes, we can mail it to let them know that we are safe." 

So the boy and his mom mailed the letter back, and the boy learned about the importance of being careful. He was happy that he could help spread the message of safety using his own flag.

One day, a little boy was walking in the park. He saw a bird sitting on a branch. The little boy was so excited, he wanted to get a closer look!

He tried to sneak closer, but the bird saw him and flew away. The little boy felt terrible. He knew he hadn't meant to scare the bird, but he had made a mistake. 

The boy learnt that birds are very sensitive creatures, and he should be careful whenever he sees one. He decided to ask his parents to help him learn more about birds, so that he could understand them better. 

From then on, the little boy never wanted to make a bird feel scared or uncomfortable ever again. He was careful to be gentle and kind whenever he saw a bird.

Once upon a time, there were two little bees called Buzz and Zizz. 
They lived in a big hive made of thick wood and warm wax. Everyday, Buzz and Zizz flew out of the hive to collect sweet nectar from the flowers in the garden. 
They were very happy and lived happily together in the hive. 
But one day, the hive was so full of nectar that Buzz and Zizz knew they had to find a way to store it. 
So they decided to fold leaves and use them as little boats to sail their nectar away. 
They worked together, folding many leaves and soon the hive was much less full. They were so proud of all their hard work! 
Every day they went out and collected nectar, and filled the hive with their treasures. Life was good in their thick and cozy hive.

Once upon a time there was a lazy bear. He liked to splash in the river near his home. Today he decided to treat himself with a splash in the river. He hopped in the water and then his body started to move. He splashed and splashed until he was too tired to splash anymore. But he had a treat waiting for him when he got out! He reached for it and started to eat, yum! He was happy to have a treat after a splash in the river. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane wanted some rice for dinner. She asked her mom, "Mom, can I have some rice for dinner?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Jane. You just have to be patient."

So Jane waited patiently while her mom cooked the rice. When it was ready, Jane ate some of it, but she was so full, she fell asleep while eating her rice!

Her mom came over and carefully picked up Jane. She carried her to bed and tucked her in. Jane was so tired she went straight to sleep.

Mom smiled and said, "Jane, you should take a good nap so you're ready for school tomorrow."

Jane happily snuggled into her blankets and went to sleep, dreaming about the delicious rice she had for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a mother and her little daughter who loved to go on walks. One day, the mother and daughter went for a walk in the countryside.

When they arrived, the mother pointed to a big, red barn in the distance.

"Look, honey!" she said. "Isn't that barn pretty?"

The little girl smiled. "Yes, it sure is," she agreed.

The mother patted the little girl's head. "Let's go and give the barn a kiss," she said.

The little girl was excited!

They walked over to the barn, and the little girl kissed it gently. The wood was warm and mild, and the sky was beautiful and blue. After the kiss, the little girl clapped her hands.

The mother gave the little girl a hug.

"That was a nice kiss," she said, smiling.

The little girl smiled back. "Yes, it was," she said.

And they both laughed and enjoyed their sunny day in the countryside.

One day two friends, Dan and Mia, were walking in the park together. Dan loved the park, it was bright and sunny and full of fun places to explore. Mia was a bit tired and started to complain.

"I'm so tired," said Mia. "Let's stay here and rest."

Dan thought this was a good idea, so they sat down on a bench and watched the people go by. After a while, Mia's complaining became too much for Dan.

"Stop complaining," said Dan. "Let's get going again, it's more fun."

Mia wasn't too sure about this, but Dan kept persuading her until finally she agreed. They started walking again. 

Then suddenly, out of nowhere, a big inchworm appeared! It was funny looking and it scared Mia. She jumped back and screamed. In her hurry, she stepped on the inchworm and it squeaked in pain.

Mia was so frightened that she didn't stop complaining all the way home. Dan was irritated and wanted the bad ending of the day to go away. It was a day filled with complaining, and it was not fun at all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a little boy who was sad. 

Lily went over to the boy and asked him what was wrong. He said he lost his gold toy car and couldn't find it. Lily wanted to help the boy, so she looked around the park with him. They searched high and low, but they couldn't find the gold car. 

Lily didn't want the boy to be sad anymore, so she gently hugged him and said she would support him in finding the car. They searched some more and finally found the gold car under a tree. The little boy was so happy and gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, they became good friends and played together at the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to gaze at the big, blue sky. He liked to see the white clouds and the bright sun.

One day, Spot went for a walk. He found a path in the forest. The path was long, but Spot felt safe. He liked to walk on the path and see the pretty trees.

As Spot walked on the path, he met a big, friendly bear. The bear said, "Hello, Spot! Let's be friends." Spot and the bear walked on the path together, feeling safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she went outside to play with her friends. They played hide-and-seek and tag until it was time for lunch.

Lily's mom called her inside and gave her a sandwich and some juice for fuel. Lily ate quickly so she could go back outside and play some more. But when she tried to put on her favorite dress, it was too tight. "Oh no!" she said. "My dress is too tight. I can't play like this."

Her mom heard her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll help you find something else to wear. You don't want to miss out on all the fun!" And with that, Lily and her friends went back outside to play some more.

One day, a girl was looking for something to do. She found a glass on the ground and picked it up. The glass was very flexible, so she decided to cover it with her hands. She used her fingers to make shapes on the glass. She liked the way the glass felt. It was like it was alive. She was so happy that she kept playing with the glass. She moved her hands around the glass and pretended that she was the only one who could make it move.

Suddenly, she heard someone saying her name. It was her mom! She had been looking for her for a long time. The girl put the glass back down on the ground and quickly ran to her mom. She hugged her and thanked her for finding her.

The girl never forgot about that magical glass. Whenever she was feeling bored, she remembered how the glass felt and held her hands the way she had when she was covering the glass.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was so cute, with a huge smile and twinkling eyes. She always wore her favorite sunglasses, even in winter. She thought they made her look cool.

Every day, Daisy would admire her beautiful, sparkly sunglasses when she looked in the mirror. She would say, "I love my sunglasses. They make me look so cool."

One day, Daisy went outside and saw a group of older children wearing the same sunglasses she had. She felt so proud and smiled. She wanted to go talk to them and show off her sunglasses.

The group of children looked in amazement at Daisy and her cute, sparkly sunglasses. They admired her glasses and wanted to buy their own. Daisy was so happy that everyone liked her sunglasses.

Ever since then, Daisy loves wearing her sunglasses and showing them off to all of her friends. She always remembers to admire her sunglasses each day, because she loves how cool they make her look.

Jasmine was a three-year-old. She was visiting her mom at the university where she studied. It was a light day with fluffy white clouds in the sky. 

When they arrived, Jasmine felt overwhelmed and asked her mom, "Mommy, what's this place?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "This is a university, Jasmine. I go here to learn new things." 

Jasmine liked the idea of learning things and started running around the campus. She soon got a little tired and asked her mom, "Mommy, can we relax now?" 

Her mom nodded and they both lay down on the grass. Jasmine looked up into the light blue sky and took a deep breath. She felt relaxed and she smiled as she looked around. 

Mommy and Jasmine then had a great day together.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play and laugh together. They shared their toys and snacks. They said they would marry when they grew up.

One day, a new boy came to their class. His name was Max. He had a big bike and a loud voice. He said he was better than everyone. He took Anna's doll and Ben's car. He said they were his now.

Anna and Ben were troubled. They did not like Max. They wanted their toys back. They asked Max to give them back. But Max said no. He said he liked Anna. He said he would marry her. He said Ben was silly.

Anna and Ben were angry. They did not want to marry Max. They loved each other. They said Max was mean. They said they would not play with him. They said they would tell the teacher.

Max was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. He did not want to lose Anna. He said he was sorry. He said he would give back their toys. He said he would be nice.

Anna and Ben were happy. They got their toys back. They thanked Max. They said they would be friends. They said they would still marry when they grew up. They hugged and smiled.

Once upon a time there was a brave little boy, who always wanted to go swimming in the sea. He was eager to go and explore all the big waves. On the way, he noticed a big, scary shark swimming near him. He was very scared, so he began to yell with excitement!

The shark was also very excited, it began to jump and pull out of the water. The little boy thought it was so fun, that he started to yell even louder, encouraging the shark to come closer.

"That's an aloe vera plant," Mom said. "It's not sharp, but it's very useful. If you ever get a cut or a burn, you can break one of the leaves and rub the gel on your skin. It will make you feel better."

"Wow, that's cool," Lily said. "Can we keep it?"

"Sure, you can keep it," Mom said. "But you have to take good care of it. It needs water and sun, but not too much."

Tom and Lily thanked Mom and took the plant to their room. They put it on the windowsill and gave it some water. They were happy to have a new friend in the garden. A friend that was not sharp, but useful.

Lily and Sam were playing with their trucks in the backyard. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving on the road. Lily had a red truck and Sam had a blue truck.

"Look at my truck, it is so fast and strong!" Sam said, zooming his truck on the grass.

"My truck is faster and stronger!" Lily said, chasing Sam's truck with her own.

They raced and bumped their trucks until they reached the fence. There, they saw a big sign that said "Lemonade for sale". It was made by their neighbor, Ben, who had a table with a pitcher and some cups.

"Let's go get some lemonade, I am thirsty!" Sam said, leaving his truck by the fence.

"Me too!" Lily said, following Sam with her truck.

They ran to the table and saw Ben smiling. He had a big yellow hat and a green apron.

"Hi, Lily and Sam! Do you want some lemonade? It is only one penny a cup!" Ben said, holding a cup.

"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam said, giving Ben a penny each.

Ben poured them some lemonade and handed them the cups. Lily and Sam took a sip and made a face. The lemonade was very sour!

"Yuck! This lemonade is sour!" Lily said, spitting it out.

"Me too! It is not good!" Sam said, putting down his cup.

Ben looked sad. He had worked hard to make the lemonade, but he had put too much lemon and not enough sugar.

"I'm sorry, Lily and Sam. I wanted to make good lemonade, but I guess I made a mistake. Do you want your pennies back?" Ben said, reaching for his jar.

Lily and Sam looked at each other. They felt sorry for Ben. He was their friend and he had tried his best.

"No, Ben, it's okay. You can keep the pennies. Maybe you can try again another day." Lily said, smiling.

"Yeah, Ben, don't be sad. We still like you and your sign. It is very nice. You can display it again when you make better lemonade." Sam said, pointing at the sign.

Ben smiled back. He was glad that Lily and Sam were nice and did not get mad at him.

"Thank you, Lily and Sam. You are good friends. Do you want to play with me and my truck? I have a yellow truck that matches my hat." Ben said, showing them his truck.

"Sure, Ben, we would love to play with you and your truck. Let's go to the backyard and have some fun!" Lily said, grabbing her truck.

"Come on, Ben, let's go!" Sam said, picking up his truck.

They ran to the backyard, leaving the sour lemonade behind. They played with their trucks and had a good time. They forgot about the lemonade and were happy.

Once there was a boy. His name was Ben. One day, he went to the store with his mom. He saw some beef there. He wanted to buy it, so he asked his mom. She said if he was a good boy she would buy it. Ben was so happy he started to sign with excitement.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But they also liked to look for bugs. They had a jar with holes in the lid. They put some grass and leaves in the jar. Then they searched for bugs to put in the jar.

"Look, Lily, I found a green bug!" Ben said. He showed Lily a small beetle with shiny green wings. "It is so pretty! Can we keep it?"

Lily nodded. She liked the green bug too. She opened the jar and Ben put the bug inside. They closed the lid and shook the jar gently. The bug crawled on the grass and leaves.

"Let's find more bugs!" Lily said. She ran to a flower bed and looked for more bugs. Ben followed her.

They found a red bug, a yellow bug, a black bug and a blue bug. They put them all in the jar. They were happy. They had a lot of bugs.

But then they heard a loud buzz. A big bee flew near them. It saw the jar with the bugs. It wanted to see the bugs too. It flew to the jar and tried to get in. It pushed the lid with its head.

"Go away, bee!" Ben said. He waved his hand at the bee. "These are our bugs! You can't have them!"

But the bee did not go away. It was angry. It stung Ben on his lip. Ben cried out. His lip hurt. It was red and swollen.

Lily saw Ben's lip. She felt sorry for him. She hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. The bee was mean. Let's go to mom. She will make your lip better."

Ben nodded. He held Lily's hand. They took the jar with the bugs. They ran to their mom. She was sitting on a bench. She saw Ben's lip. She said, "Oh, Ben, what happened? Did a bee sting you?"

Ben nodded. He said, "Yes, mom. The bee wanted our bugs. We found a lot of bugs. Look, mom, we have a green bug!"

Mom smiled. She said, "You have a lot of bugs. They are very pretty. But you have to be careful with bees. They can sting you. Let me see your lip."

Mom took a tissue and put some ice on Ben's lip. She said, "This will make your lip feel better. It will go down soon. Don't worry."

Ben felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Ben. You are very brave. Now, why don't you and Lily settle on the grass and watch your bugs? Maybe they will do something funny."

Ben and Lily settled on the grass. They watched their bugs. They saw the green bug fly, the red bug crawl, the yellow bug jump, the black bug hide and the blue bug shine. They laughed. They were happy. They forgot about the bee. They had fun with their bugs.

Max was so grateful he could swim. He would remember this day forever.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see big clouds in the sky. They hear loud noises. They feel cold wind.

"It is a storm!" Tom says. "We should go home."

But the path is rough. There are rocks and sticks. Tom stumbles on a rock. He falls down. He hurts his knee. He cries.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very excited for a big event at her school. She wanted to wear her favorite dress, but it was too big. Lily had an idea to shrink the dress so it would fit just right.

One day, Lily saw her mom use a hot box to make clothes smaller. Lily thought, "I can use the hot box too!" She put her dress in the hot box and waited. When she took it out, the dress was not just a little smaller, it was very, very small. Lily was sad and knew she had done a bad thing.

Lily told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay. We can fix it." They went to the store and found a new dress for the event. Lily learned not to use things without asking for help first. From that day on, Lily always asked her mom or dad before trying something new.

In the forest, there lived a little bear. It liked to play hide and seek with its friends, but today was different. The little bear was feeling alert - something just wasn't right. As it looked around, it noticed everything was quiet - no other animals were around. The wind blew, and the ground had an unusual texture; it was firm, but loose like sand. 

The little bear decided to investigate, and soon enough it noticed a new commotion. Nearby, an old tree was being cut down. The little bear was so surprised, it quickly started to cry. It knew its home was in danger - if that tree was cut down, it would include the little bear's home too. 

The little bear ran to help, but it was too late. The tree had been cut down and the little bear's home was destroyed. But the little bear had been so alert, it thought fast and realized there was something it could do to save the day. 

With the help of its friends, the little bear used the blocks of wood left behind to build a new home!  Everyone was so proud of the little bear and its amazing home, the entire forest cheered together. Even the texture of the new home was perfect; it was strong, yet cozy like a warm bed.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear named Benny. Benny lived in a forest with his friends, the birds and the squirrels. One day, it started to rain really hard and Benny wanted to protect his friends from the rain. 

He remembered that he had a shelter he built a long time ago. Benny led his friends to the shelter and they all stayed there until the rain stopped. The shelter was small, but it was very attractive with pretty flowers and green grass around it. 

Benny was happy that he could keep his friends safe and dry in his shelter. From that day on, whenever it rained, Benny would always protect his friends and take them to his attractive shelter.

Sara liked to write in her diary every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her secrets. She kept her diary under her pillow and never let anyone see it. She thought it was her special and mysterious book.

One day, her brother Tom was bored and curious. He wanted to know what Sara wrote in her diary. He sneaked into her room when she was outside and looked under her pillow. He found her diary and opened it. He saw Sara's drawings and words and laughed. He thought they were silly and funny.

Sara came back and saw Tom with her diary. She was very angry and scared. She shouted at Tom and ran to him. She tried to grab her diary back, but Tom was bigger and stronger. He held it high and teased her. He said he would read her secrets to everyone. Sara and Tom started to fight. They pushed and pulled and yelled and cried.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Sara and Tom fighting over the diary. She was very upset and disappointed. She took the diary from Tom and gave it to Sara. She told Tom to say sorry and go to his room. She told Sara to calm down and hug her. She said fighting was bad and writing was good. She said she was proud of Sara for having a diary and asked if she could read it with her. Sara smiled and nodded. She felt happy and safe. She opened her diary and showed Mom her stories. Mom listened and praised her. They hugged and laughed. Sara and Mom had a good time with the diary. Tom felt sorry and lonely in his room. He wished he had not fought with Sara. He wished he had a diary too.

Tim and Mia like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see many things in nature: trees, flowers, birds, bugs. They like to pretend they are explorers.

One day, they find a big hill. They want to climb it and see what is on the other side. They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. But the hill is very steep and slippery. They slip and slide and fall. They get dirty and tired.

"Tim, I don't want to climb anymore," Mia says. "It is too hard and scary."

"Come on, Mia, don't give up," Tim says. "We are almost there. I want to see what is on the other side. Maybe there is a treasure or a castle or a dragon."

"No, Tim, I want to go back," Mia says. "I want to play on the swings or the slide or the sandbox. They are more fun and safe."

Tim and Mia look at each other. They have different ideas. They don't know what to do. They feel sad and angry.

Then, they hear a voice. It is their mom. She is calling them from the bottom of the hill.

"Tim, Mia, where are you?" she says. "It is time to go home. Come down, please."

Tim and Mia look at each other again. They smile. They have a way to end their fight. They both say the same word.

"Surrender!"

They let go of their hands and roll down the hill. They laugh and scream and enjoy the ride. They land on the grass and hug each other. They are not mad anymore. They are happy.

They run to their mom and tell her about their adventure. She listens and smiles. She hugs them and says they are brave and smart. She says she loves them.

They go home and have a snack and a nap. They dream of nature and deep hills and treasures and castles and dragons. They are friends. They are explorers.

Lily did not like soup. She liked bread and cheese and cake. But her mom said she had to eat soup for lunch. She said soup was good for her and made her strong.

Lily did not want to be strong. She wanted to be happy. She pushed the bowl of soup away and said, "No, no, no! I do not want soup!"

Her mom was not happy. She said, "Lily, you have to eat your soup. It is rude to waste food. And you have to be tidy. Look at the mess you made on the table!"

Lily did not care. She did not like being rude or being tidy. She liked being free. She stood up on her chair and screamed, "I do not like soup! I do not like soup! I do not like soup!"

Her mom was very angry. She said, "Lily, stop screaming! You are being naughty and loud. You have to sit down and eat your soup. Or you will have no cake for dessert."

Lily did not like being naughty or loud. She liked cake. She looked at the bowl of soup and thought. She did not want to make her mom angry. She wanted to make her mom happy. She said, "Sorry, mom. I will try the soup. Maybe I will like it."

Her mom smiled. She said, "That's a good girl. I am proud of you. The soup is yummy. You will see."

Lily took a spoonful of soup and tasted it. It was not so bad. It was warm and salty and had carrots and potatoes. She said, "Mmm, the soup is yummy. You are right, mom."

Her mom hugged her. She said, "I am glad you like the soup. You are a good and tidy and strong girl. And you can have cake for dessert."

Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love soup. And I love cake."

Once upon a time there was a lovely fox. Every day it loved to run and play in the forest. One day while playing with its friends, it saw something in the distance. It was a war ship! It was speeding across the lake.

The fox asked its friends what it was and they had no answer. It was so scared that the fox started to run. All its friends ran together too.

The ship got closer and closer and soon it had stopped right next to the shore. Then three men came down to the shore and looked around.

The fox and its friends stayed very still and did not move. The men on the ship saw the fox and its friends. They laughed and said, "We're taking these foxes for our dinner!"

The fox and it friends were so scared. But they didn't know what to do. All they could do was run away and they ran as fast as they could.

The men chased them, but the fox and its friends were faster and managed to escape. Sadly, they never got to play in the forest again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. Timmy was very excited to go to the park. He was so enthusiastic that he ran to the park as fast as he could. When he arrived, he saw a person sitting on a bench.

"Hello!" Timmy said.

"Hi there, little one," the person replied.

"Can I sit with you?" Timmy asked.

"Of course, you can," the person said.

Timmy sat down next to the person and they started talking. They talked about the birds and the trees and the flowers. After a while, Timmy had to leave.

"It was nice to meet you," Timmy said.

"It was nice to meet you too," the person said.

As Timmy left the park, he felt happy that he had made a new friend. He couldn't wait to come back and see the person again.

One day, a girl named Sue found an enormous diary. She wanted to look inside, but it was locked. Sue felt sad because she wanted to read the diary. She asked her friend, Tom, for help. "Tom, can you help me open this locked diary?" Sue asked.

Tom tried to open the diary, but it was too hard. He told Sue, "I can't open it. We need a key." They looked all around for a key, but they could not find one. Sue and Tom started to argue. Sue said, "You are not helping!" Tom said, "You are not being nice!"

They were still fighting when a big wind came. The wind blew the enormous diary away. Sue and Tom stopped fighting and tried to catch the diary, but it was too late. The diary was lost, and they never found out what was inside. Sue and Tom felt bad for fighting and not working together.

Mama looked through the fridge. She saw a juicy orange piece of meat. She said â€œyes, this looks perfect!â€

Lily liked to play with her violin. She had a small violin that her mom gave her for her birthday. She liked to make sounds with it and pretend she was a musician. Sometimes she played happy songs, sometimes she played sad songs, and sometimes she played silly songs.

One day, she decided to play a song for her cat, Max. Max was a big, fluffy cat who liked to sleep on the couch. Lily sat next to him and started to play her violin. She played a soft and gentle song, hoping to make Max happy. But Max did not like the sound of the violin. He opened his eyes and looked at Lily with a grumpy face. He hissed and jumped off the couch.

Lily was surprised and sad. She wanted to be friends with Max, not scare him away. She followed him to the kitchen, where he hid under the table. She tried to play another song, a fun and fast song, hoping to make Max laugh. But Max did not like the sound of the violin. He opened his mouth and roared at Lily with a loud voice. He scratched the table and ran away.

Lily was shocked and scared. She did not know that Max could roar like a lion. She dropped her violin and ran to her mom, who was in the living room. She hugged her mom and cried. She told her what happened with Max and the violin.

Her mom listened and comforted her. She told her that Max was not a mean cat, just a scared cat. He did not understand the sound of the violin, and he thought it was a strange and scary thing. He roared to protect himself, but he was harmless. He would not hurt Lily or her violin. He just needed some time to get used to it.

Lily felt better and wiped her tears. She asked her mom if she could try to play the violin for Max again, but this time with a different song. A song that was calm and quiet, like a lullaby. Her mom smiled and nodded. She helped Lily pick up her violin and walked with her to the bedroom, where Max was hiding under the bed. Lily knelt down and played her violin. She played a sweet and soothing song, hoping to make Max calm. And this time, Max did not hiss or roar. He peeked out from under the bed and looked at Lily with a curious face. He came out and sniffed the violin. He rubbed his head against Lily's hand and purred. Lily smiled and petted him. She was happy that Max liked her song. She told him that he was a good cat, and that she loved him. And Max loved her too.
