Once upon a time, Jane was walking through the forest. Suddenly, she saw a skull in the grass. It looked messy, like someone had been digging around.
"Hmm... What does this skull taste like?", Jane wondered. She bent down, grabbed the skull and carefully licked the bone. It tasted salty and sour at the same time.
Jane continued her walk, thinking about the skull. She knew she shouldn't have tasted it. Suddenly, a voice said "Why did you taste the skull?".
It was a small creature with red wings. "It looked interesting so I thought I'd try it", Jane replied. "That was a very wrong thing to do," said the creature. "Skulls are not meant to be tasted."
Jane agreed, suddenly feeling embarrassed. "I'm sorry," she said. "I won't do it again." The creature smiled, flew away and disappeared into the forest.

From then on, Jane was careful not to taste any messy skulls she found in the forest!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a park with her mom and dad. When they arrived, Lily looked around and saw lots of trees, flowers, and kids playing.

Lily saw a staff member and she got excited. She ran up to him and asked, "Can I have a balloon, please?" The staff member smiled and said, "Of course, which color do you want?"

Lily picked a pink balloon and held it tightly. She was so excited that she ran to her parents and said, "Look, I got a balloon!" They smiled and said, "That's great, Lily. Let's go play on the swings." They all had a fun day at the park and Lily was happy with her new balloon.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He was very excited because he had just found a unique lollipop. It was big, purple, and sparkly. He wanted to show his friends, so he ran outside to find them.

When he got outside, he saw his friends playing a game. They were bouncing a ball back and forth. He thought it looked like fun, so he asked to join. His friends agreed, and soon he was bouncing the ball too.

When the game was over, the boy showed them his special lollipop. His friends were very happy. They said it looked delicious. The boy smiled and showed it around. Everyone was excited. 

The friends decided to divide the lollipop among themselves. They each got their own piece, and each piece was unique. The boy was so happy to share his lollipop with his friends. They all had a great time. 

The end.

Once there was a farm with a lazy mule. One day the farmer decided to pretend that the mule was his best friend. He petted and talked to him as if he was a real person.

The mule liked all the attention and he started to pretend too. He walked around like he was the boss of the farm. Everyone laughed at the mule pretending.

The farmer liked it when the mule pretended, so he even let him sit on a special chair at the end of the day. Soon, the mule and the farmer were pretending to be the best of friends.

Every day, the two of them were playing together and they never got tired of pretending. It was just like they were part of the same family. The lazy but friendly mule was so very content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and toys. One day, she found a figure of a princess in her toy box. The princess had a clear, sparkly dress and a crown on her head.

Lily was so happy to have found the princess figure. She called her mom and said, "Look, Mommy! I found a pretty princess!" Her mom replied, "Wow, Lily! That's a beautiful figure. Where did you find it?"

Lily said, "In my toy box. Can I keep her, Mommy?" Her mom said, "Of course you can, Lily. She's all yours." Lily hugged her new princess figure and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I love her so much." From that day on, Lily played with her princess figure every day and they had lots of fun together.

Lily likes to play dress-up with her mom's clothes. She goes to the big closet and finds a pink dress that is very pretty. She wants to wear it, but it is on a hanger. She does not know how to take it off.

She tries to pull the dress, but it does not move. She tries to lift the hanger, but it is too high. She tries to push the hanger, but it is stuck. She feels sad and angry. She wants the pink dress.

She sees her brother Sam in the hall. He is older and taller than her. She asks him for help. He comes to the closet and sees the pink dress. He likes to tease Lily. He says he wants the pink dress for himself. He reaches for the hanger.

Lily does not want to share. She says no and grabs the dress. Sam says yes and pulls the hanger. They both tug and tug. The dress is very strong. It does not rip. But the hanger is not. It breaks in two.

Lily and Sam both fall down. They each have a part of the hanger in their hands. The pink dress is on the floor. They look at each other and feel silly. They laugh and say sorry. They hug and make up. They decide to play something else. They leave the pink dress and the broken hanger in the closet. Mom will find them later.

Once upon a time, there were two friends living in a small village. Their names were Ted and Pat. They both liked to play together.

One day, they were playing a game of match. This was Ted and Pat's favorite game. Every day they would match numbers and shapes together.

Ted was always polite to Pat, so he let her win every game. They both laughed and smiled as they matched the colorful shapes.

Later that day, Ted and Pat went to the park together. They played tag and laughed the whole time. It was so much fun.

At the end of the day, Ted and Pat said goodbye. They both hugged each other and thanked each other for the lovely day.

Lily was a lonely lady. She lived in a small house with her cat, Tom. She did not have many friends to talk to or play with. She liked to read books and watch TV, but sometimes she felt sad and bored.

One day, she saw a flyer on her door. It said, "Learn to dance with us! Fun and easy classes for beginners. Meet new people and have fun!" Lily thought, "Maybe I should try this. I always liked to dance when I was a little girl. Maybe I can make some friends and feel happy."

She called the number on the flyer and signed up for the class. The next day, she put on her best dress and shoes and went to the dance studio. There, she met a nice man named Sam. He was the teacher. He smiled at her and said, "Hello, Lily. Welcome to the class. I'm glad you came. Are you ready to learn some dance moves?"

Lily nodded and smiled back. She felt nervous, but also excited. Sam showed her how to hold his hand and follow his steps. He taught her how to sway, spin, and hop. He praised her when she did well and helped her when she made mistakes. He made her laugh with his jokes and stories. Lily felt happy and relaxed. She forgot about her loneliness and boredom. She enjoyed dancing with Sam and the other students.

After the class, Sam asked her, "Did you have fun, Lily? Do you want to come back next week?" Lily said, "Yes, I had a lot of fun, Sam. Thank you for teaching me. I want to come back next week and learn more." Sam said, "You're welcome, Lily. You're a good dancer and a good friend. I'm happy to see you again." He gave her a hug and a kiss on the cheek. Lily blushed and smiled. She felt a warm feeling in her heart. She thought, "Maybe I'm not so lonely after all. Maybe I have a new friend. Maybe I have a new love."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint and would often spend hours making colorful pictures. One day, her mom took her to a shop to buy some new paints. The shop was filled with delicate items, like glass figurines and fragile vases.

Lily was very excited to see all the pretty things, but her mom warned her to be careful and not touch anything. Lily promised to be good and followed her mom around the shop. Suddenly, she saw a beautiful vase and reached out to touch it. But as she did, she accidentally knocked it over and it shattered into a million pieces.

Lily was very sad and scared that she had done something wrong. Her mom hugged her and explained that accidents happen, but it's important to be careful and respectful of other people's things. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be careful and never touched things that didn't belong to her. She continued to paint beautiful pictures, but now she knew to be delicate with other people's belongings.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sam. Today was a special day because Sam's mother had something for her. Sam was very excited and asked her mum what it was.

Mum said, "It's a surprise, you'll see!" She handed Sam a big, brown box. Sam couldn't wait to see what was inside, so she started to unpack it.

When she opened the box, there were lots of wonderful things. She could see a shiny toy car, some big, fluffy teddies, and some games to play. Sam was so happy that her mum had given her all these things.

But, there was something else in the box that made Sam sad. It was a broken toy rabbit with missing ears. Sam's mum saw the sad look on her face and gave her a hug. "It's OK, Sam," Mum said. "We can fix the rabbit together, I promise."

Sam was happy again. Unpacking the box with her mum was the best surprise of all.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his red jacket with a zipper. He would always zip and unzip it.

One day, Timmy's mom asked him to print some pictures for her. Timmy was happy to help, but the printer was empty of paper. He asked his mom to buy more paper, but she said they didn't have any money.

Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do. He went outside to play with his friends. While playing, he saw a man with a bag of money. Timmy thought he could take some money to buy paper for the printer.

Timmy ran to the man and tried to take the bag, but the man caught him. Timmy was scared and ran away. The man called the police and Timmy was in trouble. He learned that stealing was wrong and he should always ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside in the park. He would run and jump and laugh with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to go home for dinner. 

As they walked home, Timmy saw a bench. It looked like a good place to sit and rest. So, Timmy told his mom he wanted to sit on the bench for a little bit. 

His mom said it was a good idea and they sat down. Timmy felt happy and content on the bench. He told his mom that he liked the bench and wanted to come back and sit on it again. And they did, many times after that. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house near a big, ancient tree. In the spring, the tree had many flowers and birds that sang beautiful songs.

One day, Lily saw a tiny bird near the tree. The bird could not fly. "Oh no!" said Lily. "I will help you, little bird!" She carried the bird to her house and gave it food and water.

After a few days, the bird felt better. It said, "Thank you, Lily! Now I can fly again!" The bird flew back to the ancient tree. Every spring, Lily would visit the tree and listen to the bird's sweet song.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Teddy that she loved very much. Teddy was special to her because he was unique and no one else had a teddy bear like him.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and she accidentally left Teddy on the bench. When she realized that Teddy was missing, she started to worry and cry. But her mom told her not to worry and that they would go back to the park to find him.

Lily trusted her mom and they went back to the park. Luckily, Teddy was still on the bench where Lily had left him. She was so happy to have him back and hugged him tightly. From that day on, Lily made sure to always keep Teddy close so she wouldn't lose him again.

Once there was a furry bear named Bob. He liked to play in his crib during the day and sleep in it at night. Whenever Bob heard a sound, he would look around.

One day, Bob heard a loud noise that sounded like a roar. He peeked out of his crib and saw something change. What was it?

Bob hopped out of his crib and saw a big lion! He was surprised and shouted "ROAR!".

The lion just laughed and said, â€œIâ€™m not here to hurt you. I just wanted to change up the look of your crib for you.â€

Bob smiled and thanked the lion. The lion said goodbye and flew away.

Now, when Bob wakes up in the morning, he can look at his furry crib and smile. He is never scared by the loud noise anymore. He knows it's just the lion helping him change.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with dough and make shapes with it. One day, her mom showed her how to clean the table before playing with dough. Lily thought it was a good idea to keep things clean.

As she played with dough, Lily noticed that she could improve her shapes by adding more dough. She made a big ball and added more and more dough until it was huge! Lily was so proud of herself.

When it was time to clean up, Lily helped her mom by putting away the dough and wiping the table clean. Her mom was happy to see how much Lily had improved at keeping things clean. And Lily was happy to have made the biggest dough ball ever!

Once upon a time, there was a small gray mouse named Joe. Every day, Joe ran around in search of food. One day he found a menu on the floor and it looked delicious. "I'm so hungry, I must have this," Joe thought to himself. 

Joe quickly looked around, but no one was around. He grabbed the menu and started nibbling away. 

Suddenly, Joe heard a loud voice. "Hey, what are you doing? That's my menu!" 

Joe looked up and saw an old man standing next to him. Joe remained silent and motionless in fear. 

The old man smiled at Joe. "Don't worry, you can keep the menu. I'll make you a new one." 

Joe smiled back, as the old man left to write a new menu. Joe was so thankful to remain fed and thanked the old man with a squeak before he went on his way.

Once upon a time, there was a safe elephant. His name was Elly.

Elly lived in a big forest with lots of other animals. One day, Elly saw a problem in the forest. Some trees were falling down. Elly wanted to help but he didn't know how. 

Then, Elly heard a voice. It was a friendly raccoon. He said, "Hi Elly! I have an idea to solve the problem."

Elly was excited. He said, "What is it?" 

The raccoon said, "Let's work together. With your long trunk, you can hold up the trees while I tie them together with string. That will make them stay safe."

Elly was so happy that he had found someone to help him solve the problem. He and the raccoon worked together and in no time, the trees were safe and strong. Elly was proud of his work.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very restless and couldn't stay in one place for too long.

One day, when she was walking along, she stopped to stare at a strange object on the ground. It was a big, round rock. She tilted her head and opened her mouth, not knowing what to say.

Just then, her big sister appeared. She bent down, placed her hand on the little girl's back, and said to her, "Remember, you must be careful when walking!"

The little girl nodded and smiled. She looked up into her big sister's eyes, and said, "I remember!"

The big sister smiled back. "That's my brave girl," she said.

The little girl beamed with pride. She was so happy to have her big sister to remind her to be careful. She knew she could always trust her big sister to keep her safe.

Once upon a time there was a bubble floating in the sky. It was a delicate bubble, so light that it seemed like it would float away any moment. Two children saw it from the ground below and wanted to look at it more closely. The two kids ran and jumped, stretching their arms up high try to touch the bubble. But the bubble kept floating away, too far away to reach.

The two children looked around them, trying to think of a way to get to the bubble. Then they saw a big tree with lots of sturdy branches near them. It was tall enough to reach the bubble in the sky, so the two kids started to climb.

The children climbed up, higher and higher until they could just reach the bubble. Carefully they grabbed the bubble, being careful not to burst it. The bubble felt so delicate in their hands!

Once the children had the bubble safely in their hands, they made some wishes. Suddenly the bubble started to shine so brightly that it lit up the sky. When the light faded, the bubble popped. All that was left were tiny bits of sparkling dust drifting in the air.

Once upon a time, there was a little wheel. The wheel wanted to become wise. It wanted to learn many things. The wheel rolled around the town, looking for a wise friend.

One day, the wheel met a big tree. The tree had been living in the town for a very long time. The wheel asked the tree, "How can I become wise like you?" The tree smiled and said, "To become wise, you must listen and learn from others."

The wheel listened to the tree and started to learn from all its friends. It talked to the sun, the moon, and the stars. They all shared their stories with the wheel. The wheel became very wise.

Now, the wheel knew many things. It was very happy. The wheel shared its wisdom with other wheels in the town. They all became wise, too. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who had a loyal dog named Max. They loved to play together in the park. One day, Lily's mom baked some cookies for her. She gave one to Lily and reminded her to share with Max. 

Lily took a bite of her cookie and said, "Max, do you want some cookie too?" Max barked happily and wagged his tail. Lily broke off a piece of her cookie and gave it to Max. "Good boy, Max," Lily said, patting his head. 

After they finished their cookies, Lily's mom called out, "Lily, it's time to go home!" Lily turned to Max and said, "Max, we have to go home now. Bye-bye, park!" Max barked and followed Lily as they walked back home. From that day on, Lily always remembered to share her cookies with Max.

Once upon a time, there was a big and powerful lion. He lived in a hut made of sticks and leaves in the jungle. One day, the lion went out to hunt for his dinner. He saw a small rabbit and tried to strike it with his paw, but the rabbit was too quick and ran away.

The lion was very hungry, so he decided to keep looking for food. He walked around the jungle and saw a group of monkeys eating bananas. The lion thought he could strike them and take their bananas, but the monkeys were too high up in the trees.

The lion was getting very tired and hungry. He went back to his hut and lay down to rest. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise outside. He got up and saw that a storm was coming. The wind was so powerful that it knocked down some of the trees around his hut. The lion was scared, but he felt safe inside his hut.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her mom. They brought a big bag full of toys to play with. When they got to the park, Lucy's mom sat down on a bench and said, "Lucy, let's unpack the toys now."

Lucy started to unpack the toys from the big bag. She found a red ball, a yellow plastic shovel, and a blue teddy bear. Lucy wanted to play with the red ball first, but the ball was very stubborn and did not want to roll.

"Please, ball, roll for me!" Lucy said. The stubborn red ball did not want to roll, but when Lucy asked nicely, it finally started to roll. Lucy was very happy to play with her red ball, the yellow plastic shovel, and the blue teddy bear.

After playing for a long time, Lucy and her mom packed up the toys and went home. Lucy was tired but happy from playing with her toys at the park. The stubborn red ball, the yellow plastic shovel, and the blue teddy bear were happy too, because they had a fun day with Lucy.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty butterfly. It had colorful wings that were so graceful when it flew in the sky. One day, a little girl saw the butterfly and she had an opinion that it was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. 

But then, the butterfly flew too close to a rose bush and its wings got caught on a thorn. The little girl saw that the butterfly was struggling to get free and she wanted to help. She gently tore the butterfly's wings from the thorn and set it free. 

The butterfly was so happy and it flew away, but its wings were no longer as graceful as before. The little girl still thought it was beautiful though, and that was her opinion. From that day on, the little girl always looked for butterflies and made sure to be careful around thorns so that they wouldn't tear their wings.

One day Jane was walking with her mommy. Jane saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky. It had many colors like yellow and purple. Jane was so excited, she pointed to it and asked Mommy what it was.

Mommy explained that it was a rainbow. She told Jane that rainbows were made when the sun and the rain joined together. Jane thought the rainbow was amazing. She asked her mom if they could plan a special trip to the rainbow.

Mommy said it sounded like a great plan. They both started thinking of how they would make the trip. Then, Mommy remembered that Jane was a gifted girl. She knew that if Jane thought hard enough, she could make the rainbow come to her.

Jane tried and sure enough, the rainbow came a little closer to the ground. Mommy was very proud of Jane and Jane was so pleased that the rainbow was there for her to see. They both enjoyed seeing the rainbow and all the beautiful colors it had. Seeing the rainbow was truly a special moment for them.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. They saw a squirrel on a tree. The squirrel had a big nut in its mouth.

"Look, a squirrel!" Ben said. "Let's go and say hello!"

"No, Ben, don't!" Mia said. "The squirrel is busy. It wants to settle its nut in a hole. Leave it alone!"

But Ben did not listen. He ran to the tree and tried to touch the squirrel. The squirrel was scared. It dropped its nut and ran away.

"Ben, you are naughty!" Mia said. "You made the squirrel lose its nut. Now it has to find another one."

Ben felt embarrassed. He did not mean to scare the squirrel. He just wanted to be friendly.

"I'm sorry, Mia," he said. "I'm sorry, squirrel. I won't bother you again."

He picked up the nut and put it back on the tree. He hoped the squirrel would come back and get it.

"Come on, Ben," Mia said. "Let's go and play somewhere else. Maybe we can see some birds or flowers."

Ben nodded. He followed Mia to another part of the park. He learned his lesson. He would not disturb the animals anymore. He would watch them from a distance and be quiet.

Once there was a boy. He liked to lay on the grass in the sun. One day, he wanted to explore a dangerous place. So he lay on his belly and crawled through some tall grass. 

He was careful not to move too much, because he didn't want to get hurt. The place was very dark and he heard strange noises. He was a bit scared but he kept going. 

Finally, he saw something. It was a big and dangerous snake! He was very scared and he wanted to run away, but he couldn't move. The snake just laid there and was watching him. 

The boy was very brave and kept still. After a few moments, the snake slowly moved away. The boy was so relieved and happy to be safe again. 

He ran away from the dangerous place and back to his sunny spot. He lay in the sun, feeling lucky to have been so brave.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in the sand by the beach. One day, she found a pale seashell and wanted to keep it. But her friend, Max, also wanted it.

Lily didn't want to share the seashell because she didn't trust Max to take care of it. Max got upset and they started to argue. Suddenly, a big wave came and washed away the seashell.

Lily and Max realized that their argument was silly and that they should have trusted each other. They decided to build a sandcastle together instead and had lots of fun. From that day on, they always shared their toys and never argued again.

Once upon a time there was a man who lived all alone. He never had anyone around to talk to or play with. He was sad and lonely. That was until one day, when he heard a voice. It suggested he go out into the woods and find some friends. He was curious so he chose to follow the voice.

The man walked through the woods and soon he heard the sound of laughter. The voice had suggested he find some friends and now he had. They were all animals that lived in the woods--a bear, a rabbit and a fox. The man spent his days playing and talking with his new friends.

Even though the man was happy, he still felt something was missing. One day, the bear suggested a campfire. The man thought it was a great idea. They started a fire and gathered around it in a circle.

At first, the fire was empty, but soon stories and songs filled the air. As the group sang and laughed, the man felt truly happy for the first time. He was no longer alone. He was part of a community. And the voice in the woods had made it all possible.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and collect pebbles. One day, he found a big pebble that was too heavy for him to carry. He felt weak and couldn't lift it.

Timmy's mom saw him struggling and came to help him. She picked up the pebble and said, "Wow, this is a big one! Do you want to count how many pebbles you have now?" Timmy nodded and they counted the pebbles together. They found out that Timmy had 12 pebbles in total!

From that day on, Timmy always remembered to ask his mom to help him when he felt weak. And he loved to count the number of pebbles he collected every time he went outside to play.

Sara likes to draw with ink. She has many colors of ink in her organized box. She likes to make pictures of animals, flowers and stars. She is very careful not to spill the ink on the paper or the table.

One day, she wants to draw a big lion. She takes out the yellow and brown ink and a big brush. She starts to make the lion's head, mane and eyes. She is very happy with her lion.

But then, she hears a noise. She looks up and sees her little brother Tom. Tom is holding a red ink bottle. He is smiling. He says, "Look, Sara, I can draw too!"

Before Sara can stop him, Tom pours the red ink all over her lion. The ink makes a big mess on the paper and the table. Sara is very angry and sad. She says, "Tom, you ruined my lion! That was not nice!"

Tom does not understand. He thinks he made the lion better. He says, "No, Sara, I helped you! Now the lion has blood. He looks more real!"

Sara stares at Tom. She stares at her lion. She stares at the ink. She does not know what to say. She feels like crying. She wishes Tom would leave her alone.

One night, there was a dead reindeer in the snow. Everyone was so sad. They wanted to give the reindeer a good sendoff, so they decided to count it.

One, two, three reindeer! Four, five, six reindeer! Seven, eight, nine reindeer! Ten, eleven - oops, no more reindeer!

The people said goodbye to the dead reindeer and put it to rest. Everyone was a bit sad, but they soon cheered up when they saw a bright star in the sky. The star reminded them of the reindeer, and they knew the reindeer was happy now.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch her favorite cartoons on TV. One day, her mom told her they were going to visit her grandma's house. Lily was excited to see her grandma and play with her cat.

On the way to her grandma's house, Lily's mom told her they were going to see a big network of trees. Lily was curious and asked what a network was, but her mom said she would explain when they arrived. Lily was excited to see the big trees and the mysterious network.

As they arrived at her grandma's house, Lily saw the big network of trees in the backyard. She was amazed at how they were all connected and talked to each other. Her mom explained that the trees were like friends who help each other and share things.

Lily played with her grandma's cat and had a great time. As they were leaving, Lily's mom told her they had to go home soon. Lily felt miserable because she didn't want to leave her grandma's house and the beautiful network of trees. But her mom promised they would come back soon and see the network again.

John wanted to buy a present. He went to the shop to look for something nice. He saw an ugly perfume. He didn't like it and he wondered if anything nicer was in the shop.

"Do you have any nicer perfumes than this ugly one?" John asked the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper shook his head. "That's the only one we have," he said. 

John felt sad. He was hoping for something special. But then he noticed a little sparkle coming from the bottle. He asked the shopkeeper what it was.

"That's a glittery top," the shopkeeper said. "It makes it look nicer, doesn't it?"

John smiled. He thought it was a perfect present. He bought the perfume and wrapped it up. 

When he gave it to his mom he said: "I hope you like it. It's ugly, but it has a sparkle." 

Mom hugged John and thanked him for the perfume. She smiled and said: "It's beautiful. Just perfect."

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. They saw a big hole near a tree. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go and look," Tim said. He was brave and curious.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said. She was a little scared and careful.

They walked to the hole and leaned over to see. It was dark and deep. They could not see the bottom. They heard a strange noise. It sounded like a growl.

"What is that?" Lily asked. She felt a shiver.

"I don't know," Tim said. He felt a shiver too.

They saw something move in the hole. It was white and furry. It had big teeth and claws. It was a bear!

The bear saw them and roared. It was angry and hungry. It wanted to come out of the hole.

"Run!" Tim shouted. He grabbed Lily's hand and ran away.

The bear tried to follow them, but it was too big for the hole. It got stuck and growled some more.

Tim and Lily ran to their mom and dad. They told them about the bear in the hole.

"Wow, that was a close call," their dad said. He hugged them and praised them for being smart and fast.

"Maybe the bear lives underground," their mom said. She kissed them and comforted them.

"Maybe, but we don't want to see it again," Tim said.

"Me neither," Lily said.

They decided to play somewhere else in the park. They stayed away from the hole and the bear. They had fun and felt safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big game. It was locked and no one could play. But then, a boy came and he had a key. He used the key to unlock the game. The boy was very happy because he could play the big game now. He played and played until it was time to go home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big field with a fence around it. The fence was regular, with no holes or gaps. A group of birds lived in the field and loved to play together.

One day, a big storm came and scattered the birds all around the field. They couldn't find each other and were very scared. They tried to fly over the fence, but it was too high and regular.

The birds realized they needed to work together to get back to each other. They started to chirp and call out to each other. Finally, they heard their friends and flew back together. They were happy to be safe and together again. From that day on, they knew they could overcome any challenge as long as they worked together.

The family went shopping at the market. They wanted to buy something special. Mommy was looking for something pretty but Daddy wanted something quiet. 

They found a popular toy. It was bright and colorful! The family bought it and they were very happy. The toy was quiet too, which made Daddy very happy. 

When they went home, they saw that the poplular toy was liked by all the children. Everyone wanted to play with the toy. The parents were pleased because it kept the kids so quiet!

Once upon a time there was a brown animal in a tree. The animal was balancing on a branch high in the tree.
The sun shone brightly and birds were chirping in the nearby bushes. Suddenly the animal noticed something on the ground.

It used its big brown eyes to see better and it noticed that it was a little brown cat!
The animal was so happy and shouted, â€œMeow!â€
The cat looked up at the animal and said, â€œMeow, hello there! Can we be friends?â€
The animal nodded and said, â€œYes, letâ€™s be friends!â€

Once upon a time, there were three friends. They were playing in the park when the sky grew dark and a chill wind started to blow. One of the friends said, "Let's do a dance to stay warm!"

The three friends started to jump and hop around, twirling and laughing. They kept on dancing until they were so silly that the wind stopped.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. She was three-years-old and she loved to jump. Every morning, she jumped out of bed and ran to take a shower.
