Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was so excited because she heard about a special game. She heard that whoever won the game would get a hut all for themselves.

So, Daisy got ready and started the game. She was really concentrating on it and working hard to win. After a while, Daisy did it! She had won the game!

Now that Daisy had won, she was given a key to open the hut which was behind the trees. Daisy ran to the hut but it looked very strange. It was full of crazy shapes and colours.

Inside the hut, Daisy discovered lots of fun things to do. She could jump, swing, and spin until she was so dizzy. Daisy loved her hut and she plays in it all day.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Julia. She was only three years old and loved to play in her family's kitchen. One day while she was playing, Julia decided to climb up the original stove to look out the window.

"Julia, please don't climb on the stove!" said her mom. But Julia didn't stop. She kept climbing until she reached the top of the stove.

Suddenly, the stove started to shake and Julia lost her balance. She fell and scraped her knee on the hard floor. She started to cry and her mom rushed to her side.

"Oh, Julia, I asked you to please be careful," said her mom. "It's time for you to take a break from playing in the kitchen."

Although Julia's mom gave her a kiss and a hug, the pain from her scraped knee was still there. She realized that it was important to always listen to her mom, and she vowed not to climb on the stove again.

Lily and Ben were having lunch with Mom. Mom gave them each a plate with yummy food. There were carrots, cheese, bread and apple slices. Lily and Ben liked all the food, but they liked the cheese best.

"Can I have more cheese, please?" Lily asked Mom.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said.

Mom smiled and gave them more cheese. "You can have more cheese, but you have to eat your carrots too. Carrots are good for you. They make your eyes bright and your teeth strong."

Lily and Ben nodded. They ate their cheese and some of their carrots. But soon they were full. They wanted to go and play with their toys.

"Mom, can we go now?" Lily asked.

"Not yet, sweetie. You have to finish your plate. There is still some bread and apple left. You don't want to waste food, do you?" Mom said.

Lily and Ben sighed. They did not want to waste food, but they did not want to eat more. They wanted to have fun.

"Mom, please. We are not hungry anymore. Can we just stay here and play with our plates?" Ben asked.

He picked up his plate and pretended it was a flying saucer. He made zooming noises and flew it around the table.

Lily giggled and did the same with her plate. She made beeping noises and pretended it was a robot.

Mom shook her head. She was not happy. She did not like them playing with their plates. She thought it was rude and messy.

"Stop that, you two. Plates are not toys. They are for eating. Put them down and finish your food. Or you will have no dessert." Mom said.

Lily and Ben stopped. They looked at each other. They did not want to make Mom angry. But they did not want to eat more. They wanted dessert. They liked dessert. It was yummy.

They looked at their plates. They saw the bread and the apple. They made a face. They did not like them as much as cheese.

They looked at Mom. They saw her frown. They did not like her frown. They wanted her to smile.

They looked at each other again. They had an idea. They smiled.

They picked up their plates and swapped them. Lily gave her bread and apple to Ben. Ben gave his bread and apple to Lily.

They ate each other's food. They did not mind it so much. It was different. It was fun.

They finished their plates. They showed them to Mom.

"Look, Mom. We ate all our food. Can we have dessert now?" Lily and Ben said.

Mom looked at them. She saw their plates. She saw their smiles. She saw their trick.

She smiled too. She was not angry anymore. She was proud. She thought they were clever and cute.

She nodded. She gave them dessert. It was ice cream. It was yummy.

Lily and Ben thanked Mom. They ate their ice cream. They were happy.

They stayed at the table and talked with Mom. They told her about their plates. They told her about their toys. They told her they loved her.

Mom hugged them. She told them she loved them too. She was happy.

They stayed together and had a good time.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But today, they have to go to a big event with their mom and dad. The event is for their dad's work. Sara and Ben do not want to go. They think it will be boring and noisy.

"Mom, can we stay home?" Sara asks.

"No, you have to come with us. It will be fun, I promise. You will meet new people and see new things," Mom says.

"But we like our toys. We do not like new people. They are scary and loud," Ben says.

"Please, do not be silly. You have to be polite and nice. Dad is very proud of his work and he wants to show you off. Maybe you will find some other kids to play with there," Mom says.

Sara and Ben sigh. They put on their coats and shoes. They follow Mom and Dad to the car. They are not happy.

The event is in a big hall. There are many people there. They are all wearing fancy clothes and talking and laughing. Sara and Ben feel shy and small. They hold Mom and Dad's hands. They see a table with cookies and juice. They want some.

"Can we have some cookies, Mom?" Sara asks.

"Sure, but only one each. And be careful not to spill your juice," Mom says.

Sara and Ben take a cookie and a cup of juice. They look around for a place to sit. They see a corner with some chairs and a big plant. They go there.

They eat their cookies and drink their juice. They are still bored. They wish they had their toys. They see a big red ball on the floor. It looks like fun.

"Look, a ball!" Ben says.

"Let's play with it!" Sara says.

They put down their cups and run to the ball. They kick it and throw it and catch it. They laugh and giggle. They do not see the man who is standing next to the ball. He is holding a microphone. He is about to speak to the people.

"Hello, everyone. Thank you for coming to this important event. I am very honored to introduce our guest speaker, who is a very distinguished and respected leader in our field. He is also my boss and my friend. Please welcome..." the man says.

But before he can finish, the ball hits him in the face. He drops the microphone. It makes a loud noise. Everyone looks at him. They see Sara and Ben. They are shocked and angry.

"Who are these kids? How did they get here? What are they doing?" the people say.

Sara and Ben are scared. They did not mean to hurt the man. They did not know he was there. They run back to their corner. They hide behind the plant. They cry.

Mom and Dad hear the noise. They see what happened. They are embarrassed and sorry. They go to the man. They apologize. They go to Sara and Ben. They hug them. They scold them.

"What were you thinking? You cannot play with a ball here. You cannot interrupt the speech. You cannot hit the man. You have to be quiet and respectful. You have to say sorry," Mom and Dad say.

Sara and Ben say sorry. They are very sorry. They do not like the event. They do not like the people. They do not like the ball. They want to go home. They want their toys. They want to play in their room. They hope the event will end soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, she went to the mailbox with her mommy to mail a letter to her grandma.

As they walked back home, they passed a big temple. Lily asked her mommy what the temple was. Her mommy explained that it was a special building where people go to pray and be peaceful.

Lily thought the temple looked very pretty and wanted to go inside. Her mommy said they could go another time when they were dressed in clothes that fit the occasion.

Later that day, Lily's friend came over to play. They had a fun time together and played with dolls and blocks. As they were playing, Lily's friend said, "I have to mail a letter to my grandma too!" Lily was excited because she just went to the mailbox with her mommy. She showed her friend how to mail a letter and they both felt proud.

Once upon a time there was a mighty opera, which boasted some of the best singers around. They put on a dazzling performance every night, to the delight of the audience.

One night, as the opera was about to start, something magical happened. From out of the sky came a huge spaceship! The spaceship part to reveal a giant robot!

The robot was greeted by the audience with awe. It was the most magnificent sight they had ever seen. The robot spoke to them, saying "I come in peace! I am here to enjoy the opera."

The opera began, and the robot enjoyed the performance immensely. He clapped, laughed, and even sang along to some of the tunes, much to the amazement of the others.

The night eventually came to an end, and the robot prepared to depart. But before leaving, he thanked everyone, saying "Thank you for a mighty opera experience. I look forward to coming back soon!" With that, the robot flew off into the night sky.

Once upon a time there were two teams. The two teams wanted to have a bouncing competition. They both wanted to see who could bounce the highest. The blue team wanted to win, so they practiced very hard. But the red team also practiced hard.

On the day of the competition, the blue team jumped their highest, but the red team still beat them. The blue team was so sad that they lost. They asked the red team why they were able to jump so high. The red team said that they practiced very hard together and that was why they won.

The blue team was very sad, but then they realized that if they all worked together, as a team, they could also bounce high. So they practiced hard, together as a team.

Finally it was time for the competition again. This time the blue team was ready. They all bounced up very high, and they won the competition. The blue team was so happy that they worked together as a team.  From then on, they knew that any challenge could be conquered if they worked hard together.

It was a warm summer day and Becky wanted pizza for lunch. She asked for her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said no.

Becky had to figure out a way to get the pizza herself. She paused for a moment to think and then an idea came to her.

She walked up to the house of a wealthy man. She knocked on the door, and when he answered, she asked if he could buy her a pizza. He smiled and said, "Yes!"

Becky ran back to her house with the pizza in hand. Her mom was surprised, but pleased. She said, "Well done!"

Becky smiled. She had figured out a way to get the pizza she wanted. It was a great day!

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a large dog with brown fur and a red bow on its neck. The dog is friendly and wags its tail.

"Hello, dog!" Anna says. "You are very pretty. Can I pet you?"

The dog nods and licks Anna's hand. Ben is scared of the dog. He hides behind a tree.

"Ben, don't be afraid," Anna says. "The dog is nice. Come and say hi."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to go near the dog. He sees a shiny purse on the bench. The purse is pink and has flowers on it.

"Look, Anna, a purse!" Ben says. "Maybe it has something inside."

Ben runs to the bench and grabs the purse. He opens it and finds a cookie, a ball, and a whistle.

"Wow, this is a great purse!" Ben says. "I want to keep it."

The dog barks and runs after Ben. The dog wants the purse too. The dog jumps on Ben and knocks him down. The purse falls on the ground and the cookie, the ball, and the whistle roll out.

"Hey, stop it!" Ben cries. "This is my purse!"

The dog picks up the cookie with its mouth and eats it. The dog also plays with the ball and the whistle.

"Bad dog!" Ben says. "Give me back my things!"

Anna comes to help Ben. She sees a lady running towards them. The lady is wearing a blue dress and a hat. The lady is the owner of the dog and the purse.

"Spot, come here!" the lady says. "I'm sorry, kids, he took my purse. He likes to chew on things."

The lady takes the purse and the whistle from the dog. She gives the ball to Ben and the cookie to Anna.

"Here, you can have these," the lady says. "I'm sorry for the trouble. Spot is a good dog, but he is very curious."

The lady puts the bow back on the dog's neck and walks away. The dog wags its tail and says goodbye.

"Bye, dog!" Anna says. "You are very funny. Thank you for the cookie."

Ben is still angry. He does not like the dog. He does not like the ball. He wants the purse.

"Anna, let's go home," Ben says. "I don't want to play here anymore."

Anna nods and follows Ben. She likes the cookie. She likes the dog. She thinks the purse is too big for her. She is happy.

Once, there was a little girl called Grace. Grace was only three years old, and she was very happy. One lovely day, Grace went out to play. She ran quickly to the park and found a big tree. She wanted to reach the leaves so she could touch them.

Grace looked around but she did not have anything she could use to help her reach the leaves. But then she saw it - in the grass was a deep pink sweater. Grace smiled and picked it up.

The sweater was a little too big for Grace, but she managed to wrap it around the tree. Then she used it to help her reach the leaves. She could feel them tickling her fingers and it was so much fun.

Grace laughed and thanked the sweater for helping her reach the leaves. She was very happy and went home with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy. One day, they made a yummy soup. Mommy put a big pot on the stove and Lily helped stir it. She stirred and stirred until the soup was just right.

After they finished cooking, Lily's mommy poured the soup into bowls. Lily saw a line of bowls on the counter. She counted them out loud, "One, two, three, four, five!" Then, she picked her favorite bowl and sat down to eat.

Suddenly, their nosy neighbor knocked on the door. She smelled the soup and wanted to know what was cooking. Lily's mommy invited her in and they all ate soup together. It was a happy day in Lily's house. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a vine growing on a tree. It was long and green and looked like it would be fun to swing on.

Lily asked her mom if she could play on the vine. Her mom said, "You can choose to play on the vine, but be careful and don't hurt yourself." Lily was excited and climbed up the tree to reach the vine.

As she swung on the vine, she felt very independent and free. She loved the feeling of being in control and making her own choices. Suddenly, she heard a voice calling out to her. It was her mom, reminding her to be careful and come down from the tree.

Lily listened to her mom and carefully climbed down the tree. She felt proud of herself for making the right choice and being responsible. From that day on, Lily knew that she could be independent and make her own choices, but also listen to the important advice of her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old. She loved to play in the garden, swing in her swing and be independent.

One day, Amy had an exciting adventure. She went for a ride in a funny vehicle. She had never seen anything like it before! It was bright and colourful. She loved the feeling of being inside of it and exploring.

The vehicle took her to a big park. She saw so many things: trees, flowers, birds and other animals. She felt excited and wanted to remember it all.

When the ride was over, Amy thought back to the fun she had. She remembered how much she enjoyed the vehicle and being independent. She knew she'd never forget her adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a nice boy who loved to play. Every morning he would go outside and roll in the big green field. He rolled over the soft grass and enjoyed the sunshine.

One morning, the boy wanted to make something special for his friends. He went to the kitchen to get some ingredients. He got some flour, sugar, butter and an egg. He mixed them all together and created some dough.

The boy then rolled the dough into balls, and put them into the oven. He waited and waited, until finally, the dough had become nice and golden. He took the dough balls out of the oven and ate one of them. It tasted so yummy!

The boy shared the rest of the dough balls with his friends. Unfortunately, he left the rest of the dough out and it became spoiled. His friends were still happy with what they had, but the boy was sad because he knew he had wasted some of the dough. 

He learnt an important lesson that day: always make sure food doesn't get spoiled! From then on, he would never let his dough roll too much!

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the park with their moms. They see a big pond with ducks and fish.

"Look, Sara, ducks!" Tom says. He runs to the pond and throws some bread for the ducks. The ducks swim and eat the bread. They quack and flap their wings.

"Look, Tom, fish!" Sara says. She runs to the pond and throws some rice for the fish. The fish swim and eat the rice. They splash and flick their tails.

Sara and Tom are happy. They clap their hands and laugh. They watch the ducks and the fish for a long time.

"Time to go, Sara and Tom," their moms say. They come to the pond and hold their hands. "Did you have fun?"

"Yes, mom, we had fun!" Sara and Tom say. They hug their moms and say goodbye to the ducks and the fish. They walk to the car.

Sara and Tom are dependable friends. They always share and help each other. They always have fun together. They are glad they have each other.

Lily and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They saw Mom in the kitchen. She was making dinner.

"Mom, what are you making?" Lily asked.

"I'm making corn and chicken and salad," Mom said. "Do you like corn?"

"Yes, we love corn!" Ben said. "Can we help you?"

"Sure, you can help me. You can wash the corn and peel the husks," Mom said. She gave them a big bowl and some water.

Lily and Ben took the corn and went to the sink. They turned on the faucet and splashed the water. They pulled the green husks and the silky hairs from the corn. They put the husks in the trash and the corn in the bowl.

"Look, Mom, we peeled all the corn!" Lily said. She showed Mom the bowl.

"Wow, that's impressive!" Mom said. "You did a great job. Thank you for helping me."

"You're welcome, Mom," Ben said. "Can we eat the corn now?"

"Not yet, we have to cook it first. But it won't take long. Come on, let's set the table," Mom said.

Lily and Ben followed Mom to the dining room. They helped her put the plates and forks and napkins on the table. They smelled the chicken and the salad. They were very hungry.

Soon, Mom brought the corn to the table. She put some butter and salt on it. She gave each of them a piece of corn.

"Here you go, enjoy your corn," Mom said.

Lily and Ben took a big bite of the corn. It was sweet and juicy and delicious. They smiled and said, "Mmm, this is the best corn ever!"

Mom smiled too. She was happy to see them eat. She said, "I'm glad you like it. You are the best helpers ever!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jill. She was three years old and she loved to explore.

One day, as Jill was walking, she noticed something. It was a beautiful flower! She was so excited that she wanted to touch it.

"Can I touch the flower?" Jill asked.
Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, but be careful, sweetie!"

Jill carefully touched the flower. It was soft and smooth. She smiled and said, "It's so beautiful!"

Jill and her mom went home and talked about the flower all night. From then on, whenever she saw a flower, Jill would always notice how beautiful it was.

Once upon a time there was a shy little bird. It liked to stay in its nest and chirp away quietly. But it kept feeling like something was missing. 

So one day, it decided that it was time to fly away. It grabbed some feathers, stretched its wings and hopped out of the nest. The bird felt so scared and excited. 

It flew away, higher and higher. The bird went above the clouds and soon it was at the next stage of its journey. It flapped its wings and released itself into the sky.

The bird felt so free and it flew in circles, enjoying the wind against its feathers. The shy little bird was no longer scared. It was filled with joy. 

And from then on, the bird flew higher and higher every day, feeling free and happy.  The end.

Peter was a smart bunny who liked to go on adventures. One evening, he decided to explore in the garden. He marked the grass with pieces of string so he could find his way back. Peter hopped around, marking trees and flowers until he was so tired. He sat down under a tree and admired his work. The sun had already started to set in the sky. 

By now, Peter had marked the entire garden. He was so proud of himself, he hopped with joy around the garden. Suddenly, he heard the sound of his mother. It was almost nighttime and it was time to go back in. Peter gathered up the strings and hurried back to the house. 

Inside, Peter's mother had dinner ready. Peter was so excited to show off his markings from his adventure. His mother was so impressed by his smart idea that she gave him a hug. Peter wiped his paws and said goodbye to his garden for the evening. He ran inside for dinner, happy to be done exploring for the day.

Sara likes to receive books from her mom. Mom always picks books with nice pictures and stories. Sara has a shelf in her room where she keeps her books. She likes to look at them and read them with mom.

One day, mom gives Sara a new book. It is about a slow turtle and a fast rabbit. Sara is happy and says thank you. She puts the book on her shelf and waits for mom to read it with her.

But mom is busy. She has to cook and clean and do other things. Sara waits and waits, but mom does not come. Sara feels sad and bored. She wants to hear the story of the slow turtle and the fast rabbit.

She decides to try to read the book by herself. She takes the book from her shelf and opens it. She looks at the pictures and tries to say the words. She does not know all the words, but she knows some. She makes up the rest.

She reads the book slowly and carefully. She sees how the slow turtle and the fast rabbit have a race. She sees how the fast rabbit is very proud and lazy. She sees how the slow turtle is very humble and hardworking. She sees how the slow turtle wins the race and the fast rabbit is surprised and ashamed.

She likes the story. She thinks the slow turtle is very smart and brave. She thinks the fast rabbit is very silly and mean. She learns a lesson. She learns that being slow is not bad, and being fast is not good. She learns that being kind and honest is better than being proud and lazy.

She finishes the book and smiles. She is proud of herself. She reads the book by herself. She puts the book back on her shelf and runs to mom. She tells mom what she did and what she learned. Mom is happy and proud too. She hugs Sara and says she is a good and clever girl. She says she will read the book with her again later. Sara is happy and says she loves mom. Mom says she loves Sara too. They both smile.

Once upon a time, there was a goose. He was amazing! One day the goose was standing by a lake. He was looking at his reflection and said, "Look how amazing I am!" Suddenly, a little girl came by and said, " Hi Goose! What are you doing?"

The goose replied, "I'm just looking at my reflection and admiring how amazing I am."

The little girl smiled and said, "That's so cool! I wish I could be that amazing!"

The goose laughed and said, "It's not so hard, just put your mind to it! Now, why don't you tell me why you're here?"

The little girl started to complain. She said, "Mama sent me out here to look for feathers for her quilt, but I can't find any. Do you know where I could find some?"

The goose smiled and said, "You can always find feathers on my back! Just take some of mine, they're perfect for quilts."

The little girl thanked the goose and said, "That's so kind of you! You're amazing, Goose!"

The little girl took some feathers off of the goose's back and thanked him again. As she walked away, she felt amazing herself. She knew that with a little hard work and dedication, she could be just as amazing as the goose.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and he wanted to eat something good. He asked his mom what was on the menu for dinner. His mom said they were having pizza.

Timmy was very excited because he loved pizza. But his mom warned him not to bite his tongue while eating. Timmy didn't understand why his mom said that, but he promised to be careful.

During dinner, Timmy bit into a hot slice of pizza and burned his tongue. He remembered his mom's warning and felt sad. But then his mom gave him a cold glass of milk to soothe his tongue. Timmy felt better and realized his mom's warning was a good one. From then on, he always listened to his mom's advice.

Molly wanted to have an adventure! She had just heard about igloos and she wanted to see one for herself. She put on her hat and mittens and went outside. She looked around for an igloo and saw something different. She saw a castle made of ice â€“ it looked just like an igloo!

Molly was amazed. She had never seen anything like it. She wanted to explore the castle, so she ran up to the door and knocked. "Let me in!" she demanded.

But no one answered the door. Molly knocked again, a little louder this time. "Let me in!" she demanded.

Finally, the door opened and an old-looking polar bear stepped out. Molly was a bit scared, but she was also very curious. The polar bear smiled and said, "Come in, Molly! I'll show you around my igloo!"

Molly was delighted! She stepped inside and found all kinds of different things. She saw chairs made of ice and ice sculptures. She even saw a mini igloo inside the bigger igloo. At the end of the tour, Molly thanked the polar bear and said farewell.

Molly couldn't wait to tell her friends about her adventure and all the different things she had seen in the igloo.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. Tom was a very honest boy. He always told the truth and did what was right. One day, he saw something he shouldn't have seen. He dreamed that if he owned it, he could have lots of fun.

Tom took the thing and ran away. But he was very weary, as he knew it wasn't right. He was caught by the Policeman and told to go home.

Tom's Mother was so angry and sad. She told him that he had been naughty and needed to be punished. She said to him, â€œIf you want something, you must be honest. Taking something without asking, is wrong.â€

Tom knew that his Mother was right and said he was sorry. He was given a punishment, but it was gentle.

Tom learned a valuable lesson and was careful to be honest in the future. He still dreamed but knew to get the right things, he must be honest.

One day, a little girl called Lucy was playing in her garden. She was having lots of fun looking at the bees and helping her mum tend the flowers. Suddenly, she saw a stranger. He came closer and closer. Lucy felt scared and helpless. She didn't know what to do.

Lucy ran inside and found her mum. She told her about the stranger and her mum said not to worry. She quickly called Grandma who lived nearby. Grandma came quickly and she and Lucy's mum went to the garden to see what was going on.

When they got there, Grandma shooed the stranger away. Lucy was so relieved. Grandma said it was important to always be careful when strangers go near. Lucy nodded and gratefully thanked Grandma for coming to help. From then on, Lucy was always very careful when strangers came close.

Once upon a time there was a farmer, Joe. He was an ignorant farmer and would never shop around for the best price. He would just send his money away each time he needed to buy something. 

One day, Joe saw a pretty flower that he wanted. He asked the storekeeper how much the flower cost and the storekeeper told him the price. Joe didn't even bother to see if he could find it cheaper somewhere else, he just sent his money away and paid for the flower. 

At the same time, Joe's neighbour, Becky, also saw the same flower. But she was not ignorant like Joe. She went to different stores and checked the prices to make sure she was getting the best deal. After checking, Becky found the flower for a lot cheaper than what Joe had paid. 

Joe was very disappointed that he had been so ignorant and sent his money away without checking. He made sure to never be ignorant again and always make sure he got the best price before sending away his hard-earned cash.

One day, a grumpy cow was walking around in a meadow. As she was walking around, looking for something tasty to eat, she spotted a pond. She walked over to the edge of the pond and saw that it was filled with yummy water. She bent down to take a big drink.

Suddenly, a little frog jumped out from behind a rock. He said, "Why are you drinking from my pond?!" The cow was a bit surprised, she hadn't expected to hear a voice coming from a frog. She said, "Because I am thirsty."

The frog said, "Oh, that's okay! But can you please only drink a little bit each time you come here? That way, we can both enjoy the same spot."

The cow nodded and said that she would. From that day on, she always took small drinks from the pond, and the frog and the cow were friends. They were no longer grumpy with each other.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Stella. Stella was very brave and she loved to explore!

One sunny day, Stella decided to go for a walk in the woods near her house. She followed the long trail through the trees and tall grass. As Stella walked she heard strange noises in the bushes. She started to feel scared but kept walking.

Soon enough, Stella found out that the noises were just a family of foxes! She was so excited she wanted to get closer for a better look. But the foxes got scared and ran away in a hurry. Stella smiled and kept following the trail.
 
After a while the trail got narrower and narrower. Suddenly, Stella saw something that scared her even more. It was a big, grey wolf! Stella started to shake and wanted to turn around, but the wolf was blocking the path.
 
Stella was so scared she couldn't move. Then, she had an idea. She slowly backed away and the wolf stepped aside. Stella quickly ran home following the same long trail that she had come down.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a whale who loved swimming and exploring. Every day, the whale travelled to a new place. One day it swam to a big cliff that made the whale very excited. It quickly reversed and zig-zagged around the cliff until it had gone all the way around. The whale was so enthusiastic that it started swimming faster and faster until it swam so fast that it was free! The whale had gone through the water in reverse and made it back to the sea! It was now free to explore more places and have lots more adventures. The End.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Bill. He was three years old and he was very happy.

One day, his parents asked him to do something very special and difficult. He had to put away all the toys in his room. Bill worked hard and he was perfect.

When he finished, his parents gave him a big reward. It was a big box of chocolates! Bill was very excited.

Bill ate some of the chocolates and saved the rest for later. He was very happy and it was a perfect day.

The day ended and Bill was tired. He lay down in bed, happy and full of joy.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to watch cartoons on TV. They sit on the couch and talk about the cartoons.

"Look, Sam, it's the dog and the cat!" Tim says. "They are funny. The dog is big and the cat is small."

"Yes, Tim, they are funny. The dog is silly and the cat is smart." Sam says. "They always chase each other and make noises."

They laugh and clap their hands. They watch the cartoons for a long time.

Then, Tim's mom comes in. She sees Tim and Sam on the couch. She sees the TV. She is not happy.

"Tim, Sam, you have watched enough cartoons. It's time to go outside and play." She says. "You need some sun and fresh air. You look pale."

Tim and Sam do not want to go outside. They want to watch more cartoons. They make sad faces.

"But mom, we like the cartoons. They are fun. Can we watch a little more?" Tim says.

"No, Tim, you can't. You have watched too much. You need to move and run and jump. That's good for you." She says. "Come on, put on your shoes and jackets. I'll take you to the park. You can play with other kids and have fun."

Tim and Sam sigh. They turn off the TV. They put on their shoes and jackets. They follow Tim's mom to the car. They hope they can watch more cartoons later.

Once upon a time, there was a wild bunny named Bob. Bob lived in the woods near a big tent. The tent was red and blue. Bob liked to play near the tent every day.

One day, Bob saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was sad. "Why are you sad?" asked Bob. "My toy just vanished," said Lily. "Don't worry," said Bob, "I will help you find it."

Bob and Lily looked all around the tent. They looked under the trees and in the bushes. Then, they found the toy behind a rock. Lily was happy again. They both played together and had a fun day. From that day on, Bob and Lily became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a silly player named Timmy. Timmy loved to play games with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends decided to play a game of matching. 

Timmy said, "Let's match the colors of the blocks!" 

His friend, Lily, said, "That sounds like fun!" 

They started to match the colors of the blocks. Timmy was so silly that he matched a blue block with a green block. 

Lily laughed and said, "Timmy, that doesn't match!" 

Timmy laughed too and said, "Oops, I made a mistake!" 

They continued to match the colors of the blocks and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to swing. She loved the feeling of the wind ruffling her hair as she swung higher and higher in the air.

One day, her mommy gave her a very special present: a birdcage! It was a very useful birdcage because it had a special swing inside it. The little girl was so happy she could swing inside her birdcage.

Every day, the girl and her new birdcage would swing together. She felt so free and happy, it was like flying through the air! And her birdcage ensured that she was always safe.

The girl and her birdcage happily swing together for many days and years. Whenever she looked at the birdcage, she was reminded of the special times she had spent swinging together.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toy cars. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. They saw a big crane near the road. It was lifting heavy things and putting them on a truck.

"Wow, look at that crane!" Lily said. "It can lift anything!"

"I want to see it closer!" Ben said. He ran towards the crane, leaving his toy car behind.

"Ben, wait!" Lily shouted. "It's not safe! Come back!"

But Ben did not listen. He wanted to touch the crane. He thought it was light and easy to move. He reached for the crane's arm, but it was too high. He jumped and grabbed it. He felt a jolt of pain. The crane was not light. It was hot and hard. It burned his hand.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He let go of the crane and ran back to Lily. He showed her his hand. It was red and swollen.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I was wrong. The crane is not light. It is heavy and hot. It hurt me."

Lily hugged him and gave him her toy car. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you're back. The crane is not for playing. It is for working. We should not touch things we don't know. We should be careful and listen to each other."

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. I will listen to you next time. And I will share my toy car with you."

They played together with their toy cars, happy and safe. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that things are not always what they seem. And they learned to be kind and respectful to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy was running too fast and he stumbled and fell down. He got a little scratch on his knee, but he was okay.

After playing for a while longer, Timmy started to feel very tired. He told his friends that he needed to take a nap. They said goodbye and went home.

Timmy went home too and took a nap in his cozy bed. When he woke up, he felt upset because he had missed playing with his friends. He decided to call them and invite them over to play again. They all had a great time and Timmy was happy again.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to bounce on the big ball. They bounced high and low, fast and slow. They laughed and had fun.

Near the ball, there was a statue. It was a man with a hat and a coat. He looked very serious. He did not move or smile. Anna and Ben wondered what he was doing.

"Who is he?" Anna asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe he is a king or a hero."

"Maybe he is sad or bored," Anna said. "He needs a friend."

Anna and Ben decided to be his friends. They bounced to the statue and said hello. They told him their names and asked him his. They tried to make him laugh with jokes and faces. They gave him a flower and a hug.

But the statue did not answer or change. He stayed still and quiet. Anna and Ben felt sorry for him.

"Maybe he likes to be alone," Ben said.

"Maybe he is peaceful," Anna said.

They bounced away from the statue and waved goodbye. They hoped he was happy in his own way. They went back to the ball and played some more. They were happy in their own way too.

Sara and Ben are brother and sister. They like to play in the park. They swing, slide and run. They have fun.

One day, they see a big hill. They want to climb it. They hold hands and go up. They see many things. They see birds, flowers and clouds. They are happy.

But then, Ben slips. He falls down the hill. He rolls and rolls. He cries. Sara is scared. She runs after him. She wants to help him.

She catches him at the bottom. She hugs him. He is hurt. He has scratches and dirt. He is sad. Sara is sad too.

She helps him stand up. She wipes his tears. She says, "It's okay, brother. I am here. You are brave. We will go home. Mom will make you feel better."

They walk back to the park. They see their mom. She sees them. She is worried. She asks, "What happened?"

Sara says, "Ben fell down the hill. He is hurt. But he is okay. I helped him."

Mom says, "Oh, no. Poor Ben. You are a good sister, Sara. You are kind. Come here. I will hug you both. I will clean your wounds. I will give you a kiss. I love you."

Sara and Ben smile. They hug their mom. They love her too. They are glad. They are a family. They are ordinary. But they are special.

Tom and Anna liked to play in their big wardrobe. It had many clothes and hats and shoes that they could try on. Sometimes they pretended to be kings and queens, or pirates and fairies, or doctors and teachers.

One day, they found a big red cape in the wardrobe. It was soft and shiny and had a golden clasp. Tom put it on and said, "Look, Anna, I am a superhero! I can soar in the sky and save the world!"

Anna laughed and said, "You are silly, Tom. You cannot soar in the sky. You need wings or a plane or a rocket to do that."

Tom said, "No, I don't. I just need to believe and run fast and jump high. Watch me!" He ran to the window and opened it. He felt the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He said, "Here I go!" and jumped out of the window.

Anna screamed and ran to the window. She was scared and worried. She looked down and saw Tom lying on the grass. He was not moving. She cried and shouted, "Tom, Tom, are you okay? Please wake up!"

A wise old owl was sitting on a branch near the window. He saw what happened and flew down to Tom. He said, "Hoo, hoo, little boy, what were you thinking? You cannot soar in the sky with a cape. You are not a superhero. You are a human. Humans need to be careful and listen to their sisters. They are wise and love you."

Tom opened his eyes and groaned. He felt pain in his legs and arms and head. He saw the owl and said, "Who are you? Are you a superhero?"

The owl said, "No, I am not a superhero. I am an owl. I can soar in the sky with my wings. But I do not save the world. I just watch and learn and teach. You should do the same."

Tom said, "I am sorry, owl. I was silly and foolish. I wanted to soar in the sky and have fun. But I did not think and I did not listen. I hurt myself and I scared Anna. I love Anna. She is wise and kind."

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, that is good, little boy. You learned a lesson today. You should always be careful and listen to your sister. She loves you too. Now, let me help you. I will call your mom and dad. They will come and take you to the doctor. He will make you feel better. Then you can play in the wardrobe again. But remember, no more jumping out of the window. Okay?"

Tom said, "Okay, owl. Thank you for helping me. You are wise and nice. Can I be your friend?"

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, of course, little boy. You can be my friend. And I will be yours. But only if you promise to be careful and listen to your sister. Deal?"

Tom said, "Deal, owl. Deal." He smiled and hugged the owl. Anna ran down the stairs and hugged Tom too. She was happy and relieved. She said, "I love you, Tom. You are my brother. And you are my friend."

The owl said, "Hoo, hoo, what a happy ending. You are a lucky family. You have each other. And you have me. Now, let's go and find your mom and dad. They will be worried too. Come on, let's go." He flapped his wings and soared in the sky. Tom and Anna followed him. They held hands and looked up. They saw the owl and the cape and the sun. They felt the wind and the grass and the love. They were happy and grateful. They learned a lesson today. They learned to be careful and listen and love. And they learned to soar in their hearts.

Once upon a time there was a dad who loved his little girl very much. Every day he gave his daughter a big hug before she went to bed. But one night, dad was so tired that he forgot to give his daughter a hug. 

The little girl was very sad. She waited and waited for her hug, but it never came. After waiting for a long time, she finally went to bed without it. 

In the morning, dad remembered that he forgot to give his daughter a hug. He was so sad and he felt so bad that he didn't give her a hug. 

The little girl was also sad. She never felt so alone, and she never felt so uncared for. She didn't feel proud anymore. 

The dad and the little girl never hugged each other again. They both felt sad and lonely. Unfortunately, they never forgot the night Dad forgot to give his daughter a hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a charming smile and loved to play with her toys. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While she was playing, she saw a boy steal a toy from another child. She knew it was wrong, so she went to tell the teacher.

Later that day, Lily's mom came home from work and was very tired. Lily wanted to help her mom feel better, so she gave her a massage. Her mom felt much better and thanked her for being so thoughtful.

Before bed, Lily's dad read her a story. She loved listening to stories and asked her dad if he could read her one more. He said yes and Lily fell asleep with a smile on her face, thinking about the adventures in the story.

Once upon a time there was a boy who wanted to see the world. He had heard lots and lots of stories about different countries and he wanted to explore them all. So he saved up all his coins, said goodbye to his mum and dad, and set off on a journey. 

He went to lots of exciting places, but the one he liked the most was the country with the cheap prices. Everything he bought was really affordable and he enjoyed browsing the shops and markets.

At last he came to the end of his journey but he couldn't believe how fast the time had gone. He was sad to be leaving, but he was happy too because he had managed to finish his big adventure.

He learned lots of things about different countries, but most of all he learned that even the most amazing journey must one day come to an end.

Once upon a time there was a family who had a broken wrap, but they didn't know how to fix it.

The mum asked her little girl if she would help, so the little girl decided to try.

The little girl looked around and found some string, some tape and some glue. She first tried the glue, but it didn't help much.

Then the little girl used the string and the tape to try and make the wrap better, but it was still a bit broken.

Finally, the mum and the little girl took the wrap to a shop. The shopkeeper smiled, fixed it and returned the wrap to them. The wrap was good as new!

The little girl had learned an important lesson - when you have something broken, sometimes you need to ask someone else for help.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy family of four. They had two children, a boy and a girl. One day, the boy and girl were playing in the garden and they stumbled upon a strange box. They wondered what was inside and so the boy reached out to take it.

Suddenly, his hand was squeezed tightly. A voice asked the boy to open the box. His sister was scared so she ran away. The boy opened the box, and inside he found a monster. It was a giant angry beast with sharp teeth. 

The beast began to squeeze the boy, who started to cry. The family heard the cries and tried to help, but it was too late. The monster had squeezed the boy to death. The family was filled with sorrow. 

They all realized how dangerous the box was and how lucky they were before it was opened. Unfortunately, it was too late to save the boy, and the family was heartbroken.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She decided to visit the nearby woods. As she walked through the forest, she came across a big, round barrel. She walked up to it, and it felt very soft and fine. She put her ear up to it and she could hear a faint sound coming from it. Whatever it was, it sounded like it wanted to come out. She opened the lid, and out popped a friendly little rabbit! She smiled, and asked the rabbit if it wanted to go play and explore with her. 

The rabbit happily hopped around the little girl, and they followed the forest path together. They had a wonderful time visiting all sorts of places- they saw a cool lake, and they played with some curious birds. The little girl and the rabbit had so much fun, they decided to stop and take a rest under an old tree. 

When the little girl got back home, she told her parents all about her fine adventure. They were so proud of her, and thanked the rabbit for being a wonderful companion. 

From that day onward, the little girl visited the barrel once a week to see if she could find any other exciting animals to come out and explore with her. They visited all sorts of amazing places, and had so much fun!

Once upon a time there lived a small girl who lived in a palace. The palace was the most beautiful palace in the land and it was the colour purple. The little girl loved her palace and she always kept it very clean.

One day, the little girl had made a big mistake. She was very round and she had broken something important in the palace. Everyone was very angry but the little girl was very sorry and she asked them if they could forgive her.

The people in the palace were so surprised by her kind words that they gave her a great big hug and said that they forgave her. The little girl was very happy and she thanked them for being so kind.

From that day on, the little girl learnt the importance of being kind and forgiving. She realised that even though she had made a mistake, it was ok because she had learnt a valuable lesson and could be happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, they decided to play at the park where there was a big fountain. Lily's friend, Timmy, said, "Let's hide behind the fountain!"

Lily ran to hide, but she couldn't find a good spot. Timmy was hidden very well, and Lily couldn't see him. She said, "I can't find you, Timmy! Can you give me a number so I know where you are?"

Timmy said, "Sure! I'm behind the fountain, next to the number three!" Lily looked and saw a small number three painted on the ground. She ran over and found Timmy hiding behind the fountain. They laughed and played some more, but Lily was happy she had found her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny called Tom. Tom loved to eat vegetables and fruits, so his mom gave him a dish full of them every day. Today, however, something strange happened when Tom was eating his breakfast. All of a sudden, the dish started to shrink until it was small enough to fit in his hand.

"Mommy, what's happening?" Tom asked.

"Oh, Tom. That's just a special dish. It's a magic dish, and it shrinks when you finish eating," mommy answered.

Tom stared in amazement at the shrinking dish. Then he noticed that he was feeling a bit dizzy.

"Mommy, I'm a bit dizzy," he said.

"Oh, I think you've had enough to eat," mommy said. "Let's put the dish in your pocket and go outside and play!"

So, Tom put the magic dish in his pocket and they went outside. He felt much better after playing in the fresh air. Every day, he enjoyed his snack from the magical shrinking dish.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Ruby. She was only three and she liked to explore everything.

One day, Ruby found a cabinet that she had never seen before. It was very old and it was covered with dirt. So she wanted to take a closer look inside. 

When she opened the door, Ruby saw that the cabinet was filled with things that were rotten. She started to feel sad, so she asked her parents why things were so dirty inside the cabinet. 

Her parents smiled and said, "You know what Ruby, if you take care of things, they will last longer. But when you don't, things can rot away like these things inside the cabinet."

From then on, Ruby always took care of her things and made sure everything was clean.

The moral of this story is that if you take care of things, they will last longer, but if you don't, the things will rot away and become useless.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a beautiful purse that she loved to carry everywhere she went. One day, while walking in the park, Lily saw a butterfly. The butterfly had beautiful wings that were very colorful. Lily was so happy to see the butterfly and wanted to catch it. She tried to catch it with her purse, but the butterfly flew away too quickly. Lily was sad, but she still had her beautiful purse to make her smile.

Once upon a time, there was a filthy tank. It had been there for a long time and never been cleaned. One day a little boy decided to visit the tank. He was curious and wanted to know what was inside.
He reached in and pulled out a toy. It was an old toy, but the little boy was excited and it started to repeat something strange. The boy was even more curious and wanted to know what it was saying. He listened carefully.
The little boy was surprised to find out that the toy was actually saying, "Clean the tank!" He knew it was time to start cleaning. He went and got a brush and started scrubbing. He worked hard and soon the tank was no longer filthy. He was proud of his work and put his toy back in the tank.

From then on, every time the little boy visited the tank, the toy would repeat the same message, "Clean the tank!" The boy would smile and repeat the message back to the toy. He always made sure to keep the tank clean.

The little boy was playing in his front yard. He had been given a basket and he was looking for bugs and daddy had taught him all the different kinds of bugs. He was having so much fun!

The sun was setting and the boy heard a strange noise. He was scared, but he peered into the dark and saw a graceful deer. It was beautiful!

The deer seemed scared too and ran away. The boy said, "Goodbye, deer!" and went back to his basket. As he was picking up his things, he felt something on his leg. He looked down and saw a big bug!

The boy jumped back and screamed! Then he remembered Daddy telling him not to be scared, so he started to laugh. He crouched down and looked at the bug carefully. Its body was so shiny and its legs moved so gracefully!

The boy smiled and gently put the bug back into the grass. He said goodbye and waved at the bug, thinking the bug was a friendly one. The little boy went back to playing in the yard, happy that he could enjoy the bugs and still not be scared.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to read books. He would read them all day long. One day, Timmy's mom asked him if he wanted to help her make dinner. Timmy said yes and they went to the kitchen. Timmy's mom gave him a small potato to peel. Timmy peeled it very carefully and then they cooked it for dinner. After dinner, Timmy read his favorite book before going to bed. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a tiny white rhinoceros. He was so small that he could fit in the palm of a grown up's hand. Everyone in the neighbourhood thought he was so cute and often wanted to pick him up and play with him.

One day, the rhinoceros was walking through a big whimsical forest, exploring and enjoying the sights. Suddenly, he heard a mysterious voice. 

"Shhhhrrrrrriiiiiiinnnnnkkkkk" said the voice.

But the rhinoceros was scared and he ran away. 

Much later, after conquering his fear, he returned to the forest and he heard the same mysterious voice again. 

"Shhhhhrrrrrriiiiiiinnnnnkkkkk" said the voice again.

This time, he was brave enough to follow the voice and he saw a small white door. He opened it and found himself in a secret world full of tiny animals and plants. The mystery voice had been coming from a friendly, magical wizard who shrank animals to the size of his tiny world. 
The rhinoceros was so excited that he stayed and had many fun adventures. He became best friends with the wizard and even agreed to be shrunk whenever the wizard wished. 

So every time the white rhinoceros wanted to explore the tiny magical world, he simply had to hear

Thomas was walking in the city when he suddenly saw a barber. His mommy said "Thomas, don't go there! That place is dangerous!"

Thomas didn't understand. He asked, "What's dange'ous?" 

"It's when things can hurt you," mommy said.

But Thomas wanted to see inside. He asked, "Does it have any toys?"

Mommy replied, "No, honey, it's a place for grown-ups. It doesn't belong to us. Now let's go home."

Thomas was sad. He wanted to go inside to explore. But he knew it wasn't allowed and so he followed his mommy home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was all alone in the world and she had no one to play with. All she had was her little flute, which she could play music with. One day, however, it began to rain. The rain made the little girl so happy! She got out her flute and began to play a merry tune in the rain. Every drop of rain seemed to hit just the right note and make the most beautiful music. The little girl danced and played in the rain, enjoying her little flute and the beautiful music it made. She stayed outside until the sun came out and the rain stopped. With one last tune, she put her flute away, feeling so happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and loved exploring the garden. One day she was looking around the old shed when she saw a cobweb in the corner. It was filthy and full of dirt.

'What is that?' she said, not understanding what it was.

A voice then echoed from behind her. It was her mum.

'That Lucy is a cobweb. It's made by a spider,' she said.

Lucy wrinkled her nose. 'Why is it so filthy?'

'That's because the spiders catch flies and they are very dirty,' her mum told her.

Lucy nodded and smiled. Now she understood.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. One day, they decided to go on an adventure to the big city.

Lily was so excited to ride the subway! She had never been on one before. As they rode, she looked out the window and saw all the tall buildings and bright lights. It was so different from her small town.

Suddenly, Lily's tummy started to rumble. "I'm hungry," she said. "Let's get something to eat." Her mommy and daddy took her to a fancy restaurant. The food was so delicious and rich!

After they ate, they walked around the city some more. Lily saw a toy store and urged her parents to go in. "Please, please, please!" she begged. They finally gave in and bought her a new toy. Lily was so happy and thanked her parents. It was the best adventure ever!

Once upon a time, there was a popular robot. He liked to roll around and explore the world. Every day he would pause and look around the garden, to see what he could find. 

One day, while he was paused, he noticed a little yellow bird. He watched as it hopped from tree to tree, singing a happy song. The robot smiled and began to sing along. 

The little bird heard his singing and stopped still on a branch. It looked down, curious about the robot. It sang back to him, as if it was asking a question. 

The robot smiled and sang a little louder. The bird fluttered its wings in excitement and flew away. The robot waved goodbye, then rolled off to explore some more. 

The robot and the bird became the best of friends. They sang together all day and night, playing games in the garden. Everyone who saw them were amazed by their special friendship. 

The robot and his little yellow friend became very popular as people heard their beautiful singing. They continued to explore and sing together every day and soon everyone in the city knew their song.

Max was feeling tough. He had been playing all day and was ready for a snack. He asked his mom for tuna, but she said she didn't have any. He was so upset he started to cry.

His mom felt bad and wanted to make him happy. She ran to the shop and bought some tuna, so she could make Max a special snack. She put it on the table and called out, "Max! Tuna's here!"

Max was so excited! He stopped crying and ran over to his mom. She made him a delicious tuna sandwich and he gobbled it up.

Max was so happy to have a tasty snack. He smiled at his mom and said, "Thank you!" His mom gave him a big hug and said, "You're welcome, my love!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived near a tunnel. She had a trouble. She wanted to get inside the tunnel to explore it.

So one day, she asked her mom if she could get inside. Her mom said no, she was too little. The little girl was sad, but she had an idea. She decided to make a little train from wooden blocks and rolled it inside the tunnel.

It was a tight fit, but the train made it all the way inside. The little girl laughed with joy.

She looked around the tunnel, but it was very dark. She was a bit scared, but she wanted to keep exploring. She scooted a little bit further in and she saw a magical light!

The little girl was amazed. She had found a secret world! She couldn't wait to tell her mom about it.

She enjoyed exploring the tunnel, and eventually she got back out. She was so grateful that she'd gone in. She had made a new discovery!

One day, Jenny's dad was feeling very happy. He asked Jenny if she wanted to play a game he had called chess. Jenny said yes, even though she didn't really know how to play.

Her dad laughed and said that it was alright because he was going to teach her. He took out a big board and two bags of little pieces. He show Jenny how each piece moved and explained the objective of the game.

Jenny soon got the hang of it and they both started playing. Jenny's dad was amazed at how quickly she was learning. He couldn't believe how much fun he was having.

After an hour or so, Jenny's dad said it was time for a break and he asked if Jenny wanted to go outside and play. Jenny was so excited that her dad permitted her to go out. She grabbed her favorite toy and ran to the backyard. 

Jenny was so happy to be able to play outside and it made her dad happy too! He thought it was nice to see his little girl smiling.

Once there was a messy lizard. He wanted to move around the garden. He saw a beautiful flower and said to himself, "I can move that way." So the lizard moved towards the flower. 

He saw a big tree and said to himself, "I can move that way." So the lizard moved towards the tree. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a ladybug. The ladybug said, "Where are you going?" The lizard said, "I'm moving around the garden." 

The ladybug said, "Would you like help?" The lizard said, "Yes please!" So the ladybug and the lizard moved around the garden together. 

They found a muddy puddle and the ladybug said, "Let's move that way." So they moved towards the puddle and made a mess. But they had a lot of fun!

Once there was a boy named Will. He was only three years old and loved to whistle. All the time he could be heard whistling a happy tune.

One day his mom was cleaning and she asked Will, "Do you want to help me? I need to organize my room, and it'll be quicker with two people." Will was excited and said yes. 

Will and his mom set to work and before long the room was very organized. When they were finished they both cheered and Will gave his mom a big hug.

To celebrate their hard work, Will started to whistle. His mom joined him and soon they were both whistling the same tune. After a few minutes they stopped and just smiled at each other. 

Will's mom said, "That was so much fun. Let's do it again sometime soon!" Will happily agreed and they both went off to do something else.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to climb. One day she decided to climb a tree. She was so excited! The tree was tall and she had never climbed one before. She started to climb and it was fun.

Half way up, she stopped and rested the tree trunk. Her feet were tired. Then she felt something warm. She looked down and saw a hot frog on the ground. 

The little girl was so surprised. She said to the frog, "Hello! What are you doing here?"

The frog answered, "I'm so warm here. Can I climb your tree too?"

The little girl smiled and said, "Sure! Let's climb this tree together!"

So the little girl and the hot frog climbed together. They had so much fun! When they reached the top, they both shouted, "We did it!" 

The girl and the frog were friends forever after that and they enjoyed many more days of climbing together.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Nora wanted to explore nature. She went to a meadow filled with white flowers, and she picked one that was the prettiest. She smelled it, and it was so sweet.

Then Nora saw a small bunny hopping in the grass. She giggled and smiled, and she softly called the bunny over to her. The bunny hopped closer and closer until it was right beside her. Nora was so happy, so she bent down and kissed the bunny on its nose.

The bunny was very happy, so it hopped off into the meadow and found it's family. Nora smiled and looked out into the meadow, taking in all the whiteness and beauty of nature. It was so gorgeous, like a picture from a fairy tale.

Nora kept playing until the sun started to go down. She thanked nature for this amazing day and kissed her hand and blew it towards the sky.  And with that, Nora went home and went to bed, dreaming of all the wonderful things nature had to offer.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to wear his superhero mask. He felt strong and brave when he wore it. One day, Timmy saw a shiny toy in the store and wanted it badly. His mom said no, but Timmy didn't listen and took it anyway.

Later that day, Timmy was playing with his new toy when he accidentally broke it. He felt ashamed and didn't know what to do. He thought about telling his mom, but he was too scared. So, he hid the broken toy under his bed.

The next day, Timmy's mom found the broken toy and asked him about it. Timmy couldn't lie and admitted that he took it without asking. His mom was very disappointed and told him that he had to return the toy and apologize. Timmy felt ashamed again, but knew he had to do the right thing.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with toys and cars. One day, they saw a big box in their living room. It had a shiny paper and a bow. It was a gift for their dad.

"Wow, what is in the box?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, but it must be something good. Dad is very wealthy, he has a lot of money and things," Sam said.

"Let's open it and see. Maybe it is a new toy or a car for us," Tom said.

"No, we can't do that. It is not ours. It is for dad. He will be angry if we touch it," Sam said.

But Tom did not listen. He was curious and naughty. He ripped the paper and opened the box. Inside, he saw a shiny watch. It had a lot of numbers and buttons. It looked very cool.

"Wow, look at this. It is a watch. It is so pretty and smart. I want to try it on," Tom said.

He took the watch out of the box and put it on his wrist. He pressed the buttons and saw the numbers change. He felt very happy.

"Tom, stop it. You are being bad. Put the watch back in the box. We have to wrap it again. Dad will be home soon," Sam said.

But Tom did not listen. He liked the watch too much. He wanted to keep it. He ran away from Sam and went to his room. He locked the door and hid the watch under his pillow.

"Tom, open the door. Give me the watch. We have to fix the gift. Please, Tom, please," Sam said.

But Tom did not listen. He ignored Sam and played with the watch. He did not care about the gift or dad. He was selfish and greedy.

Soon, dad came home. He saw the big box in the living room. He saw the ripped paper and the empty box. He was very angry and sad.

"Who did this? Who opened my gift? Where is my watch?" dad shouted.

Sam came out of his room. He was scared and sorry. He told dad the truth. He said it was Tom who opened the gift and took the watch. He said he tried to stop him but he did not listen.

Dad was very disappointed and mad. He went to Tom's room and knocked on the door. He told Tom to open the door and give him the watch. He said he was in big trouble.

But Tom did not listen. He did not want to give up the watch. He did not want to face dad. He was stubborn and foolish.

Dad broke the door and entered the room. He saw Tom on the bed with the watch under his pillow. He grabbed the watch and looked at it. He saw that it was broken. Tom had pressed the wrong buttons and damaged the watch. It was not working anymore.

Dad was very upset and hurt. He had worked hard to buy the watch. It was a special gift for himself. He had saved money for a long time to afford it. It was his dream watch. And now it was ruined.

He looked at Tom with anger and sadness. He said nothing. He just walked away with the watch. He left Tom alone in his room.

Tom felt very bad. He realized what he had done. He had been bad and stupid. He had hurt dad and Sam. He had lost the watch and the gift. He had no toys or cars to play with. He had no friends or family to love him. He had nothing.

He cried and cried. He wished he had listened to Sam. He wished he had not opened the gift. He wished he had not taken the watch. He wished he had been good and smart.

But it was too late. He had made a big mistake. He had ruined everything. He had a bad ending.

Lily and Ben were playing in the backyard. They saw a big pile of lumber near the fence. They wanted to build a fort with the lumber.

"Let's take some lumber and make a fort!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful. The lumber is heavy and hard," Ben said.

They took some lumber and carried it to a corner of the yard. They stacked the lumber to make walls and a roof. They found a door in the pile and put it on the front of the fort.

"Look, we have a door! We can lock it and keep out the monsters!" Lily said.

She turned the knob and heard a click. The door was locked.

"Yay, we locked the door!" Lily said.

But then they heard a voice from outside.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing with my lumber?" It was Mr. Jones, the neighbor who owned the lumber.

"Oh no, it's Mr. Jones! He will be angry!" Ben said.

They tried to open the door, but it was stuck. They pushed and pulled, but it did not move.

"Help, we are locked in!" Lily said.

Mr. Jones came to the door and saw the kids inside the fort.

"What are you doing in there? How did you lock the door?" He asked.

"It's OK, kids. I'm not angry. I was going to use the lumber for a project, but I can wait. You can play with it for a while. But you have to be careful and not hurt yourselves. And don't lock the door again. Here, let me help you," He said.

He took a key from his pocket and unlocked the door. He opened it and let the kids out.

"Thank you, Mr. Jones. You are nice," Lily said.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun, but be safe," Mr. Jones said.

He went back to his house and the kids continued to play with the lumber. They made a fort, but they did not lock the door. They had a lot of fun.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with loops. Loops were round things that you could roll, spin, or wear. They had many loops of different colors and sizes. One day, they received a big box from their aunt. Inside the box, there were many new loops that they had never seen before.

"Wow, look at these loops!" Lily said. "They are so shiny and pretty. Can we play with them?"

"Of course we can!" Tom said. "Let's see what they can do."

They opened the box and took out the loops. Some of the loops had bells, some had beads, some had ribbons, and some had lights. They tried to roll, spin, and wear the loops, but they did not work well. The bells made too much noise, the beads fell off, the ribbons got tangled, and the lights hurt their eyes.

"These loops are not fun," Lily said. "They are too different from our old loops. I want to play with our old loops."

"Me too," Tom said. "Let's put these loops back in the box and play with our old loops."

They put the new loops back in the box and went to look for their old loops. But they could not find them. They looked everywhere, but they were gone.

"Where are our old loops?" Lily asked. "Did someone take them?"

"Maybe the aunt took them," Tom said. "Maybe she wanted to trade them for the new loops."

"That's not fair!" Lily said. "We did not want to trade our old loops. We liked our old loops. They were our favorite loops."

They started to cry. They wished they had not opened the box. They wished they had not played with the new loops. They wished they had kept their old loops.

The moral of the story is: Be careful what you wish for. Sometimes, the things that seem new and exciting are not as good as the things that you already have. You should appreciate what you have and not be greedy for what you don't.
