Once upon a time there lived a boy called Dave. Dave loved to joke and make people laugh. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the wild. 

The wild was full of big, tall trees and funny looking bugs. Dave was having an adventure! Then, he heard a noise. It sounded harsh and scary. Dave looked around and saw a big bear! 

The bear roared and Dave was so scared. But then, he remembered that he likes to joke. He started to make funny noises and the bear laughed! 

The bear liked Dave's jokes so much, that it decided to let Dave go home. Dave laughed and thanked the bear and then ran home to tell his family the funny story. Dave was so happy!

One day, a small boy named Tim found a penny. This penny was not like other pennies. It was unusual. It was big and shiny. Tim was very happy. He put the penny in his pocket and went to play.

While Tim was playing, he saw a big dog. The dog was nice, but it started to tremble. It was scared of something. Tim didn't know why the dog was scared. He wanted to help the dog.

Tim remembered his unusual penny. He took it out of his pocket. The dog saw the penny and stopped trembling. The dog was not scared anymore. It was happy. Tim and the dog played together all day. The unusual penny had made a new friend for Tim.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat candy and cake all day long. She never ate any healthy food like fruits or vegetables. This made her very sick and sad.

One day, Lily's mom took her to the doctor. The doctor put Lily on a scale to see how much she weighed. The scale showed that Lily was too heavy for her age. The doctor told Lily's mom that Lily needed to eat healthy food to be healthy.

Lily's mom started to give Lily fruits and vegetables to eat. At first, Lily did not like it. But soon she started to feel better and smile more. She realized that eating healthy food made her feel good. From that day on, Lily ate healthy food and was happy and healthy. The moral of the story is that eating healthy food is important for our bodies to be strong and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a silly boy who liked to break things. He didn't think things through, and was very ignorant.

One day, he saw a stream near his house. He thought it would be fun to break the stream. He ran up to it, threw rocks in it, and started to break it up.

The boy was so proud of himself for breaking the stream, until he saw his mom standing there watching him. She was mad that he had broken it, but the boy didn't understand why.

But the boy quickly realized why. All the animals and plants in the stream needed that water to drink. He had taken away the water, so now the animals and plants were thirsty and couldn't drink.

The boy now understood that he had been ignorant for breaking the stream. He vowed never to break things again, and to always think before he did anything.

Once upon a time, there was a bulb. He was feeling very anxious. He wanted to have a friend, so he looked around.

Suddenly, he saw a bee. He waved to the bee and asked if it wanted to be his friend. The bee said yes, and the bulb was so happy.

Every day, the bulb and the bee had lots of fun. They would fly around together, play games, and go on adventures.

One day, they decided to go exploring. They found a beautiful garden with lots of flowers. They stayed there, playing games and exploring, until the sun went down.

The bulb and the bee were the best of friends, and their friendship made them both very happy. They'll always be together, no matter what.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big box under a tree. It has a red bow on it.

"Look, a gift!" Tom says. "Who is it for?"

"I don't know. Maybe for us?" Mia says. She runs to the box and tries to open it.

"Wait, Mia. We should not touch it. It is not ours." Tom says. He is alert. He thinks someone might be angry if they take the gift.

"But I want to see what is inside. Maybe it is a toy or a book or a candy." Mia says. She pulls the bow and tears the paper.

"Stop, Mia. Stop!" Tom says. He runs to her and tries to wrap the paper back on the box.

But it is too late. The box is open. And inside is a big, furry, angry dog. It jumps out of the box and barks at them.

"Help! Help!" Tom and Mia scream. They are scared. They run away from the dog.

A man comes out of the tree. He is the owner of the dog. He is not happy. He sees the box and the paper on the ground.

"Hey, you kids! What did you do to my gift? That was for my youth club. They wanted a dog for their pet day." He says. He is mad.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pencil. Her pencil was very thin, and she liked it that way.

Peter was a little boy who loved adventure. He was out in his backyard, exploring one day when he saw something sparkly. He pushed away the leaves and saw it was a tiny box. He opened it up and saw a bright green mint inside. It looked clean and smelled sweet.

Peter kept the tiny box and enjoyed the mint every day. He kept it clean by wrapping it in his handkerchief. He would smile and push away the leaves to find it each morning and bite into the delicious, clean mint.

The mom looked happy, â€œNow the squash has a safe home.â€

Once upon a time there was a thin tower. It was so tall that it stretched up into the clouds. Every day a girl would come and stare up at it.

The girl had been wishing that the tower would get closer so she could touch it. And her wish had come true! The tower came so close that the girl could reach up and touch it. 

The girl felt happy and amazed. This was the best day ever!

Anna and Ben like to play with shapes. They have a big box of shapes that they can put together and make things. Anna likes to make houses and cars and animals. Ben likes to make rockets and robots and monsters.

One day, they are playing with shapes and they have a problem. Anna wants to use the red triangle for her house roof, but Ben wants to use it for his rocket nose. They both reach for the red triangle at the same time and pull on it.

"Let go! It's mine!" Anna says.

"No, it's mine! I saw it first!" Ben says.

They talk loud and angry. They do not want to share the red triangle. They do not want to play with other shapes. They do not want to play with each other.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees them fighting over the red triangle and the other shapes on the floor.

"What is going on here?" Mom asks.

"Anna took my red triangle!" Ben says.

Mom shakes her head. She is not happy. She says, "Shapes are for sharing, not for fighting. You have many shapes in the box. You can make many things with them. But you have to be kind and fair. Once upon a time, there was a charming boy named Jack. He lived by a deep, dark forest. One day, Jack had a special mission - to find a magical pass at the heart of the forest. So, Jack grabbed his hat, and walked into the forest. 

The sun was setting, and Jack began to feel scared. He was about to turn around, when he heard a noise. He looked up and saw a glittering pass hanging from a tree. Jack was so surprised he could not move. He just blinked, until the pass flew away.

Jack followed the pass, and soon found himself standing in front of a giant castle. The sun had fully set now, and it was getting dark. But still, Jack blinked a few times to make sure this was real. Then, he reached out and grabbed the pass. 

The castle was alive! Everywhere Jack looked he saw little lights sparkling and shimmering. Jack held his breath, and three big doors opened. A beautiful secret garden lay in front of him. Inside he could see a small pond, with many colourful fish swimming in it. 

Jack's mission was complete. He had found the magical pass. He smiled and stepped into the garden, feeling very proud of himself. He was sure he had just experienced something quite charming!

John was a little boy. He liked to play in his garage. One day, John was in the garage when he heard a strange sound. He went to see what it was and saw a wild animal. It was a fox! It jumped around the garage and then ran away. John was very excited and ran to tell his mom. Mom said that foxes like to play in garages sometimes. John was happy he got to hear a wild animal!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy was playing soccer with his friends. He kicked the ball really hard with his foot and it went flying into the bushes. Timmy was sad because he couldn't find the ball.

While Timmy was looking for the ball, he saw his friend Johnny. Johnny was being careless with his hand and accidentally broke a toy. Timmy helped Johnny pick up the pieces and they became friends again. Then, Timmy found the ball and they all played soccer together again.

In the end, Timmy learned that it's important to be careful with your hands and not be careless. And he also learned that it's okay to make mistakes, like kicking the ball too hard, as long as you try your best to fix them. The end.

Lily and Sam went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked the sand and the water. They made a big castle with a bucket and a shovel. They put shells and stones on it.

"It is the best castle ever!" Sam said. "Can we touch it?"

Mom and Dad smiled. "Yes, you can touch it. But be careful, don't break it."

Mom and Dad hugged them. "It's okay, don't be sad. The wave took your castle, but it gave you a new one. Look, there are more shells and stones on the sand. You can make another castle, or something else."

"Okay, let's make something else!" Lily said.

"Maybe a boat, or a fish, or a star!" Sam said.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sack near a tree. They are curious.

"What is in the sack?" Lily asks Tom.

"I don't know. Let's look," Tom says.

They go to the sack and open it. Inside, they find a lot of toys. There are dolls, cars, balls, and books. They are happy.

They take out the toys and start to play with them. They have a lot of fun. They share the toys and make stories with them.

After a while, a man comes to the park. He looks for the sack. He sees Lily and Tom playing with the toys.

"Hey, those are my toys!" he says. "I put them in the sack to donate them to the children's hospital. Give them back to me!"

Lily and Tom are scared. They did not know the toys were not for them. They feel sorry.

"We are sorry, mister," Lily says. "We did not know. We thought they were for us."

"We just wanted to play," Tom says.

The man sees their faces. He feels sorry too. He smiles.

"It's okay, kids," he says. "You can keep some of the toys. But you have to give the rest to the hospital. There are other children who need them more than you."

The man takes the sack and leaves. Lily and Tom hug their toys. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They learned to be grateful and to share. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing in the park when they saw a bird with a broken wing. The bird was helpless and couldn't fly.

Lily went over to the bird and said, "Don't worry little bird, I will help you." She gently picked up the bird and brought it to her mom. Her mom called a special person who knew how to take care of birds. The person measured the bird's wing and gave it some medicine.

The next day at noon, the bird's wing was all better and it could fly again! Lily felt happy that she was able to help the bird. Her mom told her that it's always important to help others when they need it. Lily learned that helping others can make a big difference.

Once upon a time there were two ants. They wanted to gather food. They were very polite to each other.

One day they went to a garden. They started to gather fruits and vegetables. Suddenly a big bird came near them. The ants were scared and tried to run away.

But the bird was too fast. It snatched one of the ants in its beak and flew away. The other ant was sad. But it kept on gathering food for its family.

When the ant arrived home, it saw that its friend was not with it. It was very sad and it knew that its friend was lost forever. It was a bad ending.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together. Today is a sunny day. They want to go to the park.

"Mom, can we go to the park?" Anna asks.

"Yes, you can. But first, you need to put on your pants," Mom says.

Anna and Ben run to their room. They look for their pants. Anna finds a pair of pink pants. She likes pink. She thinks they are pretty. She puts them on.

Ben finds a pair of blue pants. He likes blue. He thinks they are cool. He puts them on.

"Look, Mom, we are ready!" Anna and Ben say.

Mom smiles. She thinks they are cute. She gives them a hug and a kiss.

"Have fun at the park. But don't spend too much time in the sun. Wear your hats and drink water," Mom says.

"OK, Mom. We will. Bye!" Anna and Ben say.

They take their hats and water bottles. They hold hands. They walk to the park. They are happy. They spend a lot of time playing on the swings, the slide, and the sandbox. They make new friends. They have a lot of fun. They love their pants.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny peanut. It wanted to fly very badly, but it was so weak that it just couldn't take off. Everywhere it went, it wanted to fly, but it just didn't have enough strength. 

One day, while it was resting in a tall, grassy field, the tiny peanut saw a butterfly. It watched in awe as the butterfly gently flitted through the air and admired how powerful it was. 

The tiny peanut, feeling inspired, asked the butterfly for help. The butterfly agreed and grabbed the little peanut in its gentle claws. Then, it flew all around the field, taking the little peanut higher and higher and higher until the peanut's feet were touching the clouds. The tiny peanut felt so free and powerful!

At the end of the day, the little peanut and the butterfly said goodbye and went their separate ways. From then on, the tiny peanut knew that no matter how weak it felt, it could always fly.

One day, Jane wanted to think about something fun. She wanted to find something exciting. She went to the library and saw a novel. It had a spicy cover that she liked.

She thought the novel would be fun to read. Jane grabbed the book and opened it. She began to read and started to think about the characters and the plot. It was very exciting.

Eventually, Jane finished the novel. She thought it was very interesting and spicy. She was happy she read it and went back to get more books from the library. She wanted to think about exciting new stories.

The princess was so happy. She had a perfect dress and a beautiful veil. She was getting ready - the day had finally come.

Suddenly, the prince stepped outside. He had a big smile on his face and was holding a perfect bouquet of flowers. He was ready to deliver the flowers to the princess. She smiled and couldn't believe how perfect everything was.

The prince stepped inside and headed straight for the princess. He handed her the bouquet, and she was filled with delight. They smiled at each other and the prince delivered a wonderful kiss.

Afterwards, the prince carefully took the veil and put it around the princess. It fit her perfectly and made her look even more beautiful than before.

The princess and the prince closed their eyes and breathed in the moment. Everything was perfect.

Once there was a modern bell that hung around a neck. It was a beautiful necklace, and every morning it would ring. The bell shined brightly, and made a very happy sound. 

Nearby, a 3 year old girl heard the bell ringing. She followed the sound and found the necklace. She loved its beauty and the happy sound it made.

The girl put the bell around her own neck, and it felt like it was a part of her. Every time she moved, the bell rang and made her feel very special. 

The girl went outside to play, and the bell rang as she ran and jumped. Everywhere the girl went, she heard the sound of her modern bell. 

The bell was a reminder for the girl of sunny days, the sound of happiness, and the feeling of being special.

Once there was a bald man. He had a very special birdcage. He wanted to attach it to the wall, so he went to get a hammer and some nails. He banged the nails into the wall and then hung the birdcage. It looked beautiful.

The man filled the birdcage with birdseed and put a small ladder inside so that birds could climb in and out. Soon, lots of birds started to visit the man every day. They would chirp and fly down to eat the birdseed and take baths in the water dish. The man enjoyed watching all of the birds.

The birds stayed in the birdcage for a long time, and the man was very happy. One day, a bigger bird came to visit the man. It was a tiny parrot! The man was so excited, he quickly attached another birdcage to the wall so that the parrot had its own special place.

The parrot and all of the other birds were very happy. They would fill the man's days with song and he would smile every time he heard their beautiful voices.

Once upon a time, there was a King. He had a big castle and a big sword. He liked to show it off to everyone who visited him.

One day, a brave knight came to visit. He asked the King for the sword, but the King refused. He said it was too hot and the knight must wait. 

But the knight didn't want to wait. He wanted the sword. He begged the King and begged the King, but still the King refused.

Eventually, the knight gave up. He did not get the King's sword. But the King remembered how brave the knight had been, and gave him a surprise. He gave the knight a golden sword of his own! The knight was so happy, he hugged the King and thanked him.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy who lived in the forest. One day, Teddy went for a walk and it started to rain. Teddy got wet and felt very cold. He wanted to go back to his cave to dry off.

On the way back, Teddy saw a little rabbit who was trying to escape from a fox. Teddy told the rabbit to hide behind him and he scared the fox away. The rabbit was very grateful and thanked Teddy. 

When they got to Teddy's cave, the rabbit saw that Teddy was very tired and sleepy. The rabbit said, "Teddy, you saved my life. You must be tired. I will stay here with you until you fall asleep." Teddy was very happy and thanked the rabbit. They both fell asleep together, feeling safe and warm.

Mama and Jesse went to the park. They saw lots of people playing, and dogs running around. 

Mama said, "Let's play catch, Jesse."

Jesse said, "Yes!"

They threw a mild ball to each other.

Mama said, "That was fun. I think it's time for your exam now."

Jesse was sad. He said, "No. I don't like exams."

But Mama said, "Don't worry. It will be fun. I'll be with you."

So Jesse smiled, and Mama and Jesse went home to get ready for the exam.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a big cup. She liked to fill it with water and pretend she was drinking tea. 

One day, Lily's mom brought home a new kitten. The kitten was very small and very graceful. It would run and jump all around the house. Lily loved the kitten and wanted to play with it all the time.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to help weigh some apples for a pie. Lily was excited to help and put the apples in the cup. She was surprised at how heavy they were and giggled with delight. 

From that day on, Lily loved to help her mom weigh things and would always remember her favorite cup and her new kitten.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim was a normal bird with blue feathers. He lived in a big tree with his family. Every day, Tim would watch his family soar high in the sky. Tim wanted to soar too, but he was too small.

One sunny day, Tim saw a bright light in the sky. He told his mom, "Mom, I want to soar to the light!" His mom said, "You can do it, Tim! Just flap your wings and try your best."

Tim was excited. He flapped his wings and tried to soar. At first, he could not do it. But he did not give up. He kept trying and trying. Soon, Tim was able to soar high in the sky. He soared all the way to the bright light. Tim was very happy, and his family was proud of him.

One day, a little girl named Lucy had a question. She asked her mom, "Where is my comb?" Her mom looked around and said, "I don't know, let's find it."

They looked in the bathroom, but the comb was not there. Lucy started to feel angry. She really wanted to comb her hair. Then, Lucy's mom had an idea. "Let's look in your room," she said.

When they went to Lucy's room, they found the comb under her bed. Lucy was happy and not angry anymore. She combed her hair and thanked her mom for helping her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he saw a big tree with a good swing. Tim wanted to play on the swing, but he was too small to reach it.

Tim had an idea. He found a box and put it under the swing. He climbed on the box and got on the swing. Tim was happy and started to swing high. But then, the box started to shake.

The box was not strong enough for Tim. It broke and Tim began to fall. He fell down and got hurt. It was an emergency. Tim's mom came running to help him. She was sad to see Tim hurt.

In the end, Tim learned that he should not play on the swing without help. He had a bad day, but he knew he would be more careful next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy cart. He would push it around the house and fill it with his favorite toys.

One day, Tim saw his friend, Sam, playing with a big, shiny new cart. Tim felt envious of Sam's cart. He wanted one just like it. Tim's face showed a frown because he was sad.

Tim's mom saw his frown and asked him what was wrong. Tim told her about Sam's cart. His mom said, "It's okay to feel envious, but remember to be happy with what you have." Tim thought about it and smiled. He played with his cart, happy that he had a toy he loved.

Once there was an old radio. It lived in a house and was very quiet. Then one day the radio started to get louder and louder.

"What is that sound?" asked a little girl. 

A grownup replied, "That is the radio. Its sound is increasing." 

The little girl was excited. "I want to hear what the radio has to say!" she said. 

The grownup smiled. "It is playing some music for you to listen to," she said. 

The little girl was delighted. She listened to the music from the old radio and sang along. She had so much fun. 

The grownup smiled. "The radio sound is increasing," she said.

The little girl kept singing and dancing. She was so happy. The old radio made her day shine brighter.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She liked to go for bike rides with her mom and dad. 

One day, her mom and dad said that it was time for the little girl to wear a helmet. The helmet was a fine one. It was pink with silver stars. 

The little girl noticed that the helmet felt comfortable on her head. She was so happy. 

The little girl said thank you to her dad and mom. She was excited to go on a bike ride with them.

The little girl went outside, got on her bike and off she went. She had a lot of fun. 

After the ride, the little girl noticed that the helmet had kept her head safe during the ride. She was happy to have it on her head. 

The little girl thanked her mom and dad again. 

The family all went inside, satisfied and happy after their fine bike ride.

Annie was playing in her classroom. She loved to play in the mild sunshine that shone through the windows. Her teacher had asked her to stay in the classroom until it was time for their lunch break. Annie tried very hard to stay but she was so excited that she couldn't help but jump around and giggle with her friends. They ran around the classroom and had lots of fun. 

Whenever Annie felt like she was going to get too carried away, her teacher would remind her to stay. Annie got the message and slowed down, but inside she was still bursting with joy! She would stay in the classroom with her friends until lunchtime arrived. 

Finally, it was time for lunch. Annie was so happy to leave the classroom and enjoy some lunch outside. The time she spent in her classroom was still so much fun and she couldn't wait to come back again the next day.

John was only three. He loved jumping on the rug in his room. Every day he would hope to jump higher and higher. But then one day something changed. His room became noisy. He heard a buzzing sound and he soon realized it was coming from the rug! It was broken! John was sad. He hoped that the rug could be fixed so he could jump on it again. He asked his mom to help him and she took him to the store. After looking around, they found a new rug. John was so happy! He bought the rug, brought it home and was able to jump on it that same day. The rug was so much fun, he hoped it would never break!

One morning, Jack woke up feeling adventurous. He shouted for his mum, but she was busy. He put on his shoes and went outside.

Suddenly, Jack saw a package at his front door. He was excited, but also a bit scared. He got closer to look.

Then, the package called out to Jack!

"Hey, little Jack!" it said. "Take me with you on your adventures!"

Jack hesitated, then he decided to pick up the package and take it with him.

They explored the forest and the beach. Jack and the package had a lot of fun. Then, it started to get dark.

"It's time to return home now," said the package.

Jack sighed, but he knew it was time to go. He said goodbye to the package and went back home.

He returned with lots of stories to tell his mum.

Once upon a time, there was a big party. All the animals came to play and have fun. They were happy and excited. The sun was bright and the sky was blue.

At the party, there was a smooth slide. All the animals took turns sliding down. They laughed and clapped their hands. The smooth slide was their favorite part of the party.

A big fish named Fin wanted to show his friends a new trick. He went to the top of the slide and yelled, "Watch me dive!" Fin dove down the smooth slide and splashed into the water. All the animals clapped and cheered. They all wanted to try diving too. The party was so much fun, and everyone loved diving down the smooth slide.

One day, a young boy noticed a large, fluffy white cloud in the sky. He watched it in fascination as it slowly floated by. The cloud was heavy and it moved slowly across the sky. Suddenly, the boy noticed the cloud was starting to block the sun. Before long, it had covered the entire sky and the boy knew it was going to rain. 

The boy felt happy, because he had never seen rain before. He jumped up and down excitedly as the first raindrop fell from the cloud. He started to laugh as the rain continued to fall around him. The heavy cloud was producing lots of rain and soon his yard was filled with puddles. 

The boy ran and jumped in the puddles, feeling how the rain cooled his skin. He looked up in admiration at the heavy cloud, grateful for the gift of rain.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Bob. Bob was very careless. He liked to play in the park, and one day he went to the park with his friends.

When they arrived, they saw a lime tree. It had many bright green limes on it. Bob thought it would be fun to wrap the limes with string. So, he and his friends got some string and carefully wrapped the limes.

When they had finished, Bob held the strings, and his friends danced around him and the limes. They laughed and smiled as they twirled around and around in circles.

Soon, it started to get dark and the boy's parents called them home. Bob carefully unwrapped the limes and took them home with him.

From then on, Bob remembered to be more careful, and to be kind to the limes!

Tom and Amy are new friends. They live near the sea. They like to play on the sand and look at the water. Sometimes they see big boats and fish and birds.

One day, Tom and Amy find a big shell on the sand. It is shiny and smooth and has many colors. Tom picks it up and puts it to his ear.

"Listen, Amy, I can hear the sea!" he says.

Amy wants to hear too. She takes the shell from Tom and puts it to her ear.

"You are right, Tom, I can hear the sea too!" she says. "It sounds like waves and wind and bubbles."

They are very happy. They take turns to listen to the sea in the shell. They call it their sea shell. They decide to keep it and share it.

They run to their moms and show them their sea shell. Their moms smile and hug them.

"What a nice find, Tom and Amy!" they say. "You are very lucky to have such a new and beautiful sea shell. And you are very lucky to have each other as friends."

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Max. Max loved to play and run around all day. One day, Max chased a cat and got hurt. His leg was hurting, and he was suffering. 

Max's owner took him to the veterinarian. The veterinarian was a nice person who helped animals when they were sick or hurt. The veterinarian told Max's owner that Max had a broken leg and needed to stay in the clinic for a few days. 

Max was sad and missed his owner. He thought chasing the cat was a foolish thing to do. Max learned that it's important to be careful and not do silly things that could hurt us. Max also learned that veterinarians are good people who help animals when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight named Max. Max had a dependable shield that he always carried with him. One day, Max went on an adventure to find treasure. He walked for a long time until he found a big castle. Max went inside the castle to look for treasure. Suddenly, Max heard a loud noise. It was a dragon! The dragon was big and scary. Max knew he had to use his shield to protect himself. He turned around and saw the dragon coming towards him. Max held up his shield and the dragon breathed fire on it. Max's shield was strong and dependable, so it protected him from the fire. Max was able to defeat the dragon and find the treasure. He was very happy and proud of his dependable shield.

One day, a little girl named Sally was walking in the forest and came across a new hut. She was very excited because she had never seen such a thing. She excitedly ran to the hut and put her hand on it. She was just about to knock when she heard a voice from inside the hut saying â€˜Listenâ€™.

Sally was very surprised and scared. She couldnâ€™t see anyone inside the hut. She took a few steps back and asked, â€˜Who said that?â€™

Again, she heard the same voice saying â€˜Listenâ€™. This time, the voice was a little louder. Sally was still scared but she was also curious. She carefully took a few steps forward and listened carefully.

The voice said, â€˜Come inside. I have a surprise for you.â€™ Sally was excited and scared at the same time. She slowly opened the door and saw a little old lady inside the hut.

The old lady smiled and said, â€˜I have something special for you. Itâ€™s a new toy!â€™ Sally was so happy. She thanked the old lady and started playing with her new toy. She had a lot of fun and listened carefully to the old lady's stories.

Ben likes to study ants. He has a book with pictures of ants and he learns their names and what they do. He likes to watch them in the garden, how they carry food and dig tunnels. He thinks ants are smart and busy.

One day, he sees a big ant hill near the fence. He wants to study it closer, so he brings his book and a magnifying glass. He kneels down and looks at the ants. He sees red ants and black ants and some ants with wings. He says, "Wow, so many ants!"

But then, he hears a loud bark. It is Rex, the neighbor's dog. Rex is big and scary and he does not like Ben. He runs towards the ant hill, barking and growling. He wants to dig up the ants and chase Ben away.

Ben is afraid. He does not want Rex to hurt the ants or him. He shouts, "No, Rex, bad dog! Go away!" He picks up his book and his magnifying glass and runs to the house. He hopes the ants are safe.

He tells his mom what happened. She hugs him and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. Rex is a mean dog. He should not bother you or the ants. You are brave and kind. You love to study ants and learn new things. Maybe we can find another ant hill for you to study. A more mysterious one, where Rex can't find it."

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Angel, a soft doll with wings and a halo. Lily loved to hug Angel and pretend she was flying with her in the sky.

One day, Lily's brother Tom came into her room. He was bored and wanted to play with Lily. He saw Angel on the bed and grabbed her. "What is this?" he asked. "It looks silly."

Lily was angry. She ran to Tom and tried to take Angel back. "No, Tom, that's my doll!" she said. "Her name is Angel and she is very nice. Give her back!"

Tom did not listen. He laughed and pulled Angel's wings. "She is not nice, she is boring. Look, her wings are falling off. She is not a real angel."

Lily felt very sad. She slapped Tom on the face. "Stop it, Tom, you are mean!" she shouted. "You hurt Angel and you hurt me. Go away!"

Tom was surprised and hurt. He dropped Angel and ran out of the room. He had a red mark on his face where Lily slapped him. He started to cry.

Lily picked up Angel and hugged her. She saw that one of her wings was torn. She felt sorry for Angel and for Tom. She knew she should not have slapped him. She decided to say sorry to him and to share her dolls with him. She hoped he would be nice to her and to Angel.

The moral of the story is: Do not hurt others or their things. Be kind and share with your siblings. Slapping is not a good way to solve problems.

John and his mommy were playing. Mommy said, "Let's go to the park, John!" John said, "Yes!" They went to the park and saw a big tree. John said, "I want to climb the tree." Mommy said, "Okay, be careful."

John started to climb the tree. He was going high and higher. He felt so proud. He almost reached the top when he saw a tomato. It was a big, round tomato on a branch. It looked so tasty! John was so excited. He wanted to grab the tomato. 

John was a bit scared too. It looked a bit crazy to reach for the tomato. He thought for a few seconds and decided he wanted the tomato. So he jumped up and grabbed it! He was so happy with his tomato. 

John started to climb down from the tree. He was very proud that he got the tomato. Mommy said, "Nice job, John!" He smiled and said, "I'm so happy!"

Once upon a time there was a wise old fox who lived near by a big forest. The fox had a beautiful coat of bright red fur. All the other animals of the forest admired the fox for his wise ways.

One day, a small rabbit hopped into the fox's den, hopped right up to the fox, and started to yell.

"Why are you yelling, little one?" asked the fox.

"I'm lost! I don't know how to get home," the rabbit said, between sobs.

The fox looked at the rabbit and thought for a moment. "Now listen to me, little one. I can help you find a way home. Follow my directions and you'll find your way back safe and sound," the wise fox said.

The rabbit followed the fox's directions and soon enough, he had found his way home. From that day on, the rabbit always looked out for the wise old fox and thanked him for helping him find his way home.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw with his ink pen, but he always seemed to drop it on the floor. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to draw a picture of a bird.

Timmy picked up his ink pen and started to draw. But then, he dropped his pen on the floor. "Oops!" he said. "I dropped my pen." 

"Don't worry, Timmy," said his mom. "Just pick it up and keep drawing." 

Timmy picked up his pen and finished his picture. It was a beautiful bird with colorful feathers. "Look, Mom!" he said. "I drew a bird!" 

His mom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Timmy. Even if you are a little clumsy sometimes."

Once upon a time, there was a little mule named Momo. Momo had a big orange ball. He loved to play with his ball all day.

One day, Momo saw a big pot. He wanted to stir the pot. But his ball fell into the pot. Momo was sad. He wanted his ball back.

Momo tried to get his ball. He asked his friends for help. His friends helped him stir the pot. The ball came out. Momo was happy again. They all played with the orange ball together.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their ball. One day, they see a big hill in the east. It looks impressive. They want to climb it and see what is on the other side.

"Let's go, Ben!" Anna says. "We can do it!"

"OK, Anna!" Ben says. "But be careful. The hill is steep and high."

They hold hands and start to walk up the hill. They have to go slow and steady. Sometimes they slip and slide on the grass and dirt. But they do not give up. They manage to reach the top of the hill.

"Wow!" Anna says. "Look, Ben! We can see the whole park from here! And the lake! And the trees!"

"It's beautiful, Anna!" Ben says. "We did it! We climbed the hill!"

They hug and smile. They are proud of themselves. They sit on the hill and enjoy the view. They are happy. They have a new adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was three and she loved to bake. Every day, she would put on her bright red apron and bake all sorts of things in her kitchen. 

One day, Mia said to her mom "I'm gonna bake a heel, Mommy! Can you help me?" Her mom said "Yes, I can help you bake a heel. What kind of heel do you want?" Mia said, "I want a black heel. Can you get the ingredients we need?"

Her mom went to the grocery store and got all the ingredients they needed to make the black heel. 

When they got home, they started mixing the ingredients and put it in the oven. While they waited, Mia's mom said "Be careful, the heel might be hot when it's done." 

Mia said "I can't wait to see the black heel!" finally, the black heel was done. It smelled delicious. They both took it out of the oven and they both looked at the beautiful black heel. Mia was so happy she couldn't contain herself.

They both tasted the delicious heel. It was hot and sweet, just like Mia had dreamed.  Mia smiled and said, "I love it!" 

Mia and her mom shared the black heel and enjoyed it together. It was the best heel Mia had ever baked.

Molly was a happy girl. She loved to swim in the ocean. Every day, she would take her favourite toy and head to the beach. The waves would splash against her toes as she dove into the sparkling blue waters. 

Molly was very excited one day when she saw a big boat with a fancy flag flying on top. Molly knew that the boat was full of luxury items. 

Molly swam closer to the boat to get a better look. Suddenly, she heard someone shout,

"Get away from here, little girl!"

Molly could see that the man was very upset. She hurried to the shore, sad and scared. When she got back to the sand, she curled up and started to cry.

Molly was never so upset as she was that day but she still loved to swim in the ocean. She would go back to the beach again and again, happy to feel the cool water lapping against her toes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she found a brilliant red flower and put it in her basket. 

Lily's mom asked her, "What did you find?" 

"I found a pretty flower," said Lily. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Be careful not to chew on it. Some flowers are not good to eat." 

Later that day, Lily's little brother came over to play. He saw the flower in her basket and said, "I want to chew on it!" 

Lily remembered what her mom said and told him, "No, it's not for chewing. It's just for looking at." 

Her little brother was sad, but Lily knew it was important to listen to her mom. And when they got home, Lily's mom gave her a special treat for being such a good listener.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sasha. She was a very special girl, who every day wished to become a princess.

One day, she found a magical crown. She was so excited and quickly put the crown on her head. Suddenly, she felt something very special happening to her. She was becoming a princess!

Sasha was so happy and started twirling around. It was the most wonderful feeling ever! But after a while, she started feeling a bit confused. How would she show everybody she had become a princess?

Sasha decided to use her imagination and make a beautiful dress for herself. She also wore her magical crown and looked like a real princess! Everyone was so happy for her and Sasha felt very proud!

Grandma was angry at her grandpa. He had been naughty and had not done his chores. Grandpa was very scared. He kneeled down on the floor and begged for forgiveness. 

Grandma did not respond. She picked up a pair of scissors and pointed them at him. Grandpa closed his eyes and waited to see what would happen. 

Suddenly, Grandma put down the scissors and hugged grandpa. She kissed his forehead and said that she still loved him, even when he was naughty. Grandpa smiled and was relieved that he was not in trouble anymore. 

Grandma had been angry, but she always found a way to forgive. Grandpa felt very lucky to have an awesome grandma like her.

Once upon a time in a land far away, there lived a young girl. Her name was Sarah and everyday she would wake up in her beautiful bedroom. She would look out the window and see bright birds, green trees and blue sky. One morning, Sarah woke up and decided she wanted to explore the world. 

So, she put on her shoes and went outside. As she walked, she saw different things like tall buildings, little animals and nice people. She said hi to them all and waved. 

She came to a big field with a river through the middle of it. Sarah lay down and looked up. The sky was so blue and the clouds so white. She saw them move and change shapes.

Suddenly she noticed a little baby rabbit near her. Sarah smiled and the rabbit hopped away. She followed the baby rabbit and saw something even more beautiful. A big garden of many colours - green, pink, yellow, orange and purple. 

The young girl was in awe and said, "This place is so beautiful". She spent the rest of the day playing and discovering the world around her. At night, she went back home, dreaming of all the beautiful things she'd seen.

Once upon a time, there was a car. The car was very old and needed a mechanic to fix it. The mechanic was a serious man who worked hard to make the car better.

One day, the car went for a drive. The driver forgot to shut the door properly. The door opened and the driver fell out of the car. The car kept driving and crashed into a tree.

The driver was hurt very badly and had to go to the hospital. The car was broken and the mechanic could not fix it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play outside and dig holes in the ground. One day, Fluffy found a big pile of dirt and decided to dig a tunnel. It was difficult work, but Fluffy was determined to make a big tunnel.

Fluffy dug and dug, and finally, the tunnel was finished. Fluffy was so happy and proud of the tunnel that he decided to show it to his friends. But when Fluffy went back to the tunnel, he found that it had caved in and he couldn't get out. Fluffy was buried alive in the tunnel.

Fluffy's friends searched and searched for him, but they couldn't find him. It was a sad day in the forest when they finally found Fluffy's buried body. They all cried and wished they could have helped Fluffy before it was too late.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight named Max. Max had a shiny shield that he loved to carry everywhere. One day, Max was walking in the forest when he saw a little bunny. The bunny was scared and asked Max, "Can you help me, please?"

Max replied, "Of course! What's wrong?"

The bunny said, "I lost my mommy and I don't know how to get back home."

Max looked at the bunny and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find your mommy. But first, you need to be careful and stand right here. I'll go look for her."

Max searched the forest and finally found the bunny's mommy. He brought her back to the bunny and they were reunited. The bunny was so happy and said, "Thank you, Max! You are my hero!"

Max smiled and said, "No problem, little friend. It's always important to be careful and help those in need."

Once upon a time, there was a chubby rabbit named Floppy. Floppy loved to eat carrots and lettuce, but she always wanted more. One day, she saw a big plate of vegetables on the table. She wanted to fill her tummy with all of them.

But the plate was on a high shelf, and Floppy couldn't reach it. She tried to jump, but she couldn't get high enough. She asked her friends for help, but they were all too busy.

Feeling sad and hungry, Floppy decided to climb up the shelf. But she slipped and fell, and the plate crashed down on top of her. Poor Floppy was hurt and couldn't eat any vegetables. From that day on, she learned to be patient and ask for help when she needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a crib. But it was not just any crib - it was a very special crib that she loved more than anything else. Every night she would climb into her crib and go to sleep.

One night, when the little girl was fast asleep, she heard someone in her room. She opened her eyes and saw her brother, who was bigger than her. He was very envious of her special crib. He walked over and tried to take it, but the little girl said no.

Still, the brother was very determined and he kept trying to take the crib away. Finally, he got angry and he slapped the little girl. She was so scared that she started to cry and went away, never to come back again.

The little girl was left all alone, without her special crib. And the brother was left with only one thing - the feeling of being envious.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play outside, but today it was very cold. They put on their coats, hats and gloves, and went to the park. They saw a big swing there. They both wanted to swing on it.

"Me first!" Anna said. She ran to the swing and sat on it. She pushed with her feet and went high in the air. She felt happy.

"Me too!" Ben said. He ran after Anna and tried to grab the swing. He was angry. He wanted to swing too.

"No, it's mine!" Anna said. She did not want to share. She swung faster and faster. She did not see Ben behind her.

"Ouch!" Ben said. He fell to the ground. The swing hit him on the head. He cried. He felt hurt.

Anna stopped swinging. She saw Ben crying. She felt sorry. She got off the swing and went to Ben. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?"

Ben nodded. He wiped his tears and said, "I'm okay, Anna. I'm sorry too. I should have waited for my turn."

Anna smiled and said, "It's okay, Ben. We can swing together. We can take turns. It's more fun that way."

Ben smiled too. He got up and said, "Yes, let's swing together. It's less boring that way."

They hugged again and went to the swing. They swung together, high and low, fast and slow. They laughed and sang. They felt warm and happy.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It's better to play together than to fight.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady who lived in a small house. She liked to go for walks in the forest every day. One day, she found a shiny pebble on the ground. She picked it up and put it in her pocket.

As she continued her walk, she saw a group of kids playing in a nearby field. They were playing a game where they would start running when one of them said "go". The elderly lady wanted to join in the fun, so she asked if she could play too.

The kids were happy to have her join, and they gave her a special job. She had to hold the pebble and start running when they said "go". The elderly lady had so much fun playing with the kids and holding the shiny pebble. From that day on, she would always bring the pebble with her on her walks and remember the fun she had with the kids.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily who loved to fly. She would reach her arms up in the air and soar through the sky.

One day, Emily's daddy saw her flying and had a thoughtful idea. He said, "Emily, we can pretend that you can fly like a bird. I will be a giant bird for you to sit on, so you can soar like never before!"

Emily thought it was a terrific idea and immediately ran to her daddy. Daddy carefully lay down on the ground and Emily carefully climbed onto his back.

He said,"Ready? Okay, hold on tight now! Here we go!" 

Emily was filled with joy and excitement, as her daddy began to jump around the park as if he was a giant bird. She squealed and laughed with delight as she soared through the air with her daddy.

When the fun was over, Emily hugged her daddy tightly and whispered, "Thank you, daddy. That was so fun!" 

Daddy smiled and said, "You're welcome, my little bird! I'm so glad you enjoyed it." 

From that day onward, Emily and her daddy often pretended that she could fly like a bird. It was one of Emily's most treasured memories. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little purple bird named Poppy. Poppy had a tiny tooth that she used to eat her food. One day, she saw a big, tall tree with a branch that was just right for her to sit on.

Poppy flew to the tree and tried to balance on the branch. She wobbled and wiggled, but she did not fall. "I can do it!" she said to herself. Poppy was very happy that she could balance on the branch.

A little squirrel named Sam saw Poppy balancing on the branch. He was amazed by her skill. "Wow, Poppy!" he said. "You are so good at balancing! Can you teach me?" Poppy smiled and said, "Of course, Sam! Let's practice together!" And so, Poppy and Sam became the best of friends, and they spent their days balancing on branches and having fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved pizza. One day, she went to the pizza store with her mommy. They ordered a big pizza with lots of cheese and pepperoni. Lily was so happy that she started to tremble with excitement.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. A big storm was coming! Lily felt troubled and scared. "Mommy, what's happening?" she asked. "It's just a storm, sweetie. We'll be okay," her mommy replied.

They quickly grabbed their pizza and ran back to their car. The wind was blowing hard and the rain was pouring down. But Lily held onto her mommy's hand and felt safe. When they got home, they ate their pizza and watched the storm from the window. Lily was still a little scared, but she felt better with her mommy by her side.

Jack and Molly were good friends. They always had so much fun when they got together.

One day they decided to start their own club. They invited all their friends to join. Every Saturday they would get together to celebrate.

Jack and Molly were always very rich at the club. They had lots of fun treats. They would buy lots of sweets and toys to share.

Their club was very special because they always celebrated with lots of laughter and excitement. All the kids in the club had so much fun.

At the end of each day, they would all gather together, give each other big hugs and say goodbye until their next club celebration.

Once upon a time there was a happy bear who loved to rub his tummy in the sun. He was having so much fun that he stopped to look around. He saw a tree with lots of apples, so he stopped and rubbed his nose against the warm bark. It felt so nice that he wanted to stay there forever. 

But then the bear heard a noise. It was a happy duck quacking in the pond. He stopped for a minute and listened to the duck's happy sounds. 

So the bear decided to go over and have a rub. He waddled over to the pond and rubbed his back against the soft grass. It felt so good that he stopped for a bit and just enjoyed the cool water on his fur. He was so happy! 

The bear was so happy from the rub that he ended up staying at the pond all day, enjoying the happy sounds of the duckâ€™s quacks.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty scarf that was smooth and soft. One day, Lily went to a party where she saw her friends dance. She wanted to dance too, but she was too shy.

Suddenly, a boy asked Lily to dance with him. She was so happy and started to dance with him. But then, the boy accidentally stepped on her scarf and it ripped. Lily was very sad and ran away from the party.

When she got home, her mom tried to fix the scarf, but it was too torn. Lily was heartbroken and couldn't wear her favorite scarf anymore. She learned that sometimes things can break and not be fixed, but she still had her memories of the fun dance.

Once upon a time there was a castle, high in the sky. Everyone thought it was the most beautiful castle they had ever seen.

One day, a little girl called Mia came to visit. She was so happy to see the castle. It was so big, so tall and so clear! She wanted to see inside.

Mia asked the king for permission to enter the castle. He said yes and opened the door for her. Inside the castle, Mia was amazed! There were so many wonderful things to see.

When Mia came back out, the people around her applauded. They were all so impressed with how brave Mia had been. Mia blushed and smiled. She loved all the attention!

Mia will always remember that special day. She had seen a beautiful castle and made lots of new friends.

Once there was a boy named Joe. Every day Joe liked to mix things together. He mixed his toys, his clothes, and even his food. One day Joe asked his mom what was the truth. His mom said, "The truth is that being glad is the best way to be."

Joe was glad when he heard this, so he went outside to mix up some things in the garden. He mixed the soil and the water, the grass and the flowers. He mixed everything until it was all mixed together.

When his mom came outside to see what Joe was doing she saw that he was glad. She smiled and said, "Whatever you mixed up looks great." Joe was so happy that he hugged his mom and said, "This is the best mix ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a dependable monkey named James who lived in the woods. He went out every day looking for food and play. All the animals in the forest respected him and always followed his lead.

One day James heard a strange noise coming from the top of the tallest tree. He asked his friends what it was and they told him it sounded like a x-ray machine. James wanted to find out what it was, so he started climbing up the tree.

When he got to the top of the tree, James saw a man was spraying a weird powder all around. The man noticed James and said "Hey kid, don't you never spray anything without thinking first. It could be dangerous". 

James understood the message and thanked the man for his advice. From then on James was more thoughtful when it came to taking risks. He remembered that being dependable is the most important thing to be. 

The moral of the story is to always be careful when taking risks and to trust yourself when it comes to making decisions. Always remember to be dependable!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found a rare toy car that he had never seen before. It was shiny and had a bright red color.

Timmy was so excited about his new toy car that he wanted to show it to his friends. He took the car to the playground and showed it to his friends. They all thought it was cool and wanted to play with it too. Timmy was happy to share his toy with his friends.

Later that day, Timmy and his friends played a game of matching. They had to match different colors and shapes. Timmy was really good at matching and won the game. He felt proud of himself and his friends cheered for him. Timmy realized that he had a big world to explore and many more toys to discover.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they were playing hide-and-seek when Lily's ball went into the garage. She tried to open the garage door, but it was locked.

Lily asked her friend, "Can you help me unlock the garage?" Her friend said, "Sure, let's find the key!" They searched and searched until they found the key. When they unlocked the garage, they found an amazing surprise inside. It was a big trampoline! They jumped on it and had so much fun.

After they finished playing, Lily's friend said, "That was an amazing surprise in the garage!" Lily replied, "Yes, it was! Thank you for helping me unlock it." They high-fived and continued playing outside.

Once upon a time there was a team of brave and adventurous animals. They lived in the park, and knew each other very well. Every spring when the sun was out, they liked to explore the park. One day, the team decided to go on a grand adventure. They hopped and ran and played, discovering new places each day. Everywhere they went they found new things, like trees and birds and bugs, and they played games together in the sunshine. As the sun began to set, they made it back home together, full of smiles and joy. Every spring they'd go on a new adventure; they were always excited to see what they'd discover!

Once, there was a small boy named Charlie. Charlie loved stories more than anything else. Charlie's mommy always said that stories were special and delicate. 

One day, Charlie's mommy said "Let's go to the store and get something special for dinner. Today, you can have whatever you want to eat!"

Charlie was so excited! He wondered what he should pick. As they walked through the store, Charlie reached out and touched a strawberry. He asked his mommy, "What does this taste like?" 

His mommy replied, "Oh, it's very sweet! If you taste it, you'll love it!" 

Charlie was so excited! He couldn't wait to get home and have his special dinner. 

When they arrived home, Charlie couldn't believe his eyes. On the table was a plate full of fresh strawberries! He smiled and said, "Mommy, did you know strawberries were my favorite?" 

His mommy smiled and said, "I had a feeling you would like them! Go ahead and taste them, they are so delicate and sweet." 

Charlie picked one up, took a bite, and smiled. He had experienced the special and delightful taste of a strawberry. What a delicious dinner!

There was a boy and his name was Tom. Tom had an ordinary toy gun. Every day, Tom would run around and shoot with his gun. He would make noises like "bang, bang!" and pretend he was an action hero. 

One day, Tom and his Daddy went to the park. Tom was so excited! He jumped from one end of the park to the other, shooting at imaginary villains. 

Then, Tom came across something he hadn't seen before. Something that was shaped like a shiny, round object. He ran up to his Daddy and asked, "Daddy, what's that?"

His Daddy smiled. He said, "It's a mine, Tommy. An ordinary mine. It's like gold, but more valuable."

Tommy smiled wide and said, "Can I shoot it?"

His Daddy laughed and said, "No, Tommy. You can't shoot it. It's much too valuable." 

Tommy was disappointed, but he did listen to his Daddy. Instead, he just looked on in awe at the special mine.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Mark. Mark wanted to have a super-power, so he made a wish and something incredible happened. Suddenly, he could fly! 

Every day Mark would flap his arms and soar high above the trees. It felt like the world was his playground. 

But one day Mark was so high up that he didn't see a tree branch. He slammed into it and was covered in scratches. 

His mom was worried, so she cleaned his cuts and put bandages on them. She hugged him and said, "Be careful, Mark!" 

Mark smiled. He knew he could fly again soon and he would be careful not to crash into anything. It was incredible!

Anna liked to store things in her box. She had many things in her box: a ball, a doll, a book, a hat. She liked to look at them and play with them. But one day, she found something new in her box. It was an insect.

The insect was small and green. It had six legs and two wings. It moved very fast and made a buzzing sound. Anna was curious. She wanted to touch it and see what it felt like. She reached out her hand and tried to catch it.

But the insect was too quick for Anna. It flew out of her box and around the room. It landed on the window, on the lamp, on the chair. Anna followed it with her eyes and tried to grab it. She thought it was incredible. She had never seen an insect like that before.

She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen, what it was. Her mom came to see and smiled. She told Anna it was a fly. She said flies were insects that liked to eat and fly. She said flies were not good to store in boxes. They needed to be free and go outside.

Anna understood. She opened the window and let the fly go. She waved goodbye to the fly and said thank you for the incredible visit. She closed the window and went back to her box. She wondered what else she would find in her box. She liked to store things in her box.

Spike was a brave rabbit. He liked to explore and play in the forest with his friends. One day, Spike saw something that made him feel very fearful. He looked closer and saw a big pile of dirt and garbage! Spike was so worried that he ran back to his burrow as fast as he could.

When Spike got back to his burrow, he knew he had to do something about the pile of dirt. He knew he couldn't do it alone, so he gathered his friends and told them about the messy pile. Everyone cheered when Spike said they should clean it up.

The friends all grabbed a broom or a shovel and worked hard to clean the mess. After a few hours, the dirt and garbage was all gone! Spike was so proud of all his friends for helping him clean. He thanked them for their hard work.

Spike and his friends celebrated by jumping and dancing around the clean forest. Spike was glad that his friends had helped him with the cleaning. As Spike looked around, he knew that the forest was now safe and beautiful again.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bunny named Benny. One day, Benny went to the garden to pick some yummy carrots. While he was there, he saw a big tree with lots of prune fruits. Benny wanted to taste the prune, so he asked his friend, a bird, to bring one to him. The bird was happy to help and flew up to the tree to pick a prune. She brought it back to Benny and he took a big bite. It was so delicious! Benny was grateful to his friend for bringing him the prune.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a radio that could play music and talk. They liked to listen to the radio and dance and sing along.

One day, Ben found a new game on the radio. It was a quiz where you had to answer questions and win prizes. Ben was very good at the quiz. He knew the names of animals, colors, and shapes. He answered many questions and won a sticker book.

Lily was jealous of Ben. She wanted to play the quiz too, but Ben did not let her. He said he was the best and he wanted to win more prizes. Lily felt sad and angry. She tried to grab the radio from Ben, but he pushed her away.

"Stop it, Lily! This is my radio and my game!" Ben shouted.

"No, it is our radio and our game! You are not nice, Ben!" Lily cried.

They started to fight over the radio. They pulled and tugged and yelled. The radio fell to the floor and broke. The music and the talk stopped. Ben and Lily looked at the radio and felt sorry. They had broken their favorite toy.

They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They realized that playing together was more fun than playing alone. They decided to share their toys and their games. They went to their mom and asked her to fix the radio. She said she would try, but she was not sure if she could succeed. She told them to be more careful and kind with their things and each other.

Ben and Lily nodded and said they would. They hoped that their mom could succeed and make their radio work again. They wanted to listen to the music and the talk and dance and sing along. They wanted to play the quiz and win prizes together. They were not jealous anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a baby called Max. He was very excited because it was his birthday! He wanted to have some fun.

He said, "I want to get cake!" So his mummy said, "Okay Max, let's go get the cake."

Max and Mummy went to the shop and saw so many different cakes. There was a round cake, a square cake and an orange cake. The orange cake looked so yummy and delicious, so Max chose it.

Mummy said, "That's a great choice Max, let's get the orange cake." Max was so happy, he knew it was going to be yummy.

When they got home, Max waited patiently for the cake to be ready. Finally, it was ready and Max could not wait to eat it. The cake looked so tasty and it tasted even better. Max was so happy that he got an orange cake for his birthday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was going on a trip with her family. They had to pack their luggage with clothes and toys. Lily's mom said, "We have to be careful not to forget anything important." 

Lily's dad said, "Let's check if everything is inside the luggage. We don't want to lose anything expensive." 

Lily asked, "What does expensive mean?" 

"It means something that costs a lot of money," her dad replied. 

After they checked their luggage, they went to the airport. Lily was excited to go on an airplane for the first time. When they landed, they had to wait for their luggage to settle on the conveyor belt. 

Lily said, "Look, our luggage is here! Let's go have fun on our trip!"

Jim was an eager little boy. He loved finding things and going on adventures. One day he decided to go explore the park. As he walked, he noticed a strange liquid coming out of the ground. He was careful and looked around. He saw a man fixing the ground and noticed it was a leak.

Jim shouted, "Hi! What's that?"

The man looked up and said, "It's a leak. It happens when the pipe breaks."

Jim was amazed and thanked the man. "Thanks for showing me!"

The man smiled. He was happy that Jim was eager to learn. He said, "You are welcome. Now run along, have fun!"

And Jim did! He dashed off, exploring the park and admiring the nature around it. 

At the end of the day, Jim was tired but happy. He thanked the man once more as he waved goodbye and headed home.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit who was very hungry. She hopped around looking for something to eat. Suddenly she came across some carrots in the garden. "Ah, a healthy snack!" she said to herself. She grabbed the carrots and started to pass them to her friends.

"I have some carrots, here you go!" she said.
Her friend, a squirrel, popped out from the nearby tree. "Yum, carrots!" he said, taking the carrots.

The rabbit asked, "Would you like to pass some carrots to your friends too?"
The squirrel answered, "Sure! I'll pass them to my friends the birds!" 

The rabbit handed the squirrel the carrots and the squirrel flew away to give them to the birds. Everyone was happy that they had a healthy snack to eat. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mom asked her to clean up her toys and put them away. Lily didn't want to do it because she thought it was boring.

Her mom said, "Lily, it's important to keep your toys organized so you can find them easily next time you want to play with them."

Lily didn't understand what "organized" meant, so her mom explained it to her. After she understood, she said, "Okay, Mommy. I will clean up my toys and put them away nicely."

Later that day, Lily heard a bell ringing outside. She asked her mom what it was and her mom said, "It's the mailman. He's here to send us a package."

Lily was excited and asked if she could help. Her mom said yes, and they went outside to meet the mailman. Lily helped her mom sign for the package and then they thanked the mailman for sending it.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be organized and to help others whenever you can.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat pasta. Her mommy always made her pasta with mild sauce. One day, Lily and her mommy were playing outside when Lily saw a butterfly. She wanted to catch it, so she started to run after it. Suddenly, Lily's feet froze and she fell down. Her mommy picked her up and asked if she was okay. Lily said she was fine and asked if they could go inside and have some pasta. Her mommy smiled and said yes. They went inside and had a delicious dinner together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and a dad and they had a little girl. The mom and dad were busy, so they asked the little girl to do an important job. 

"We need you to tie this knot," said the dad. He handed her a rope and showed her how to tie it up.

The little girl was excited about her job and began to tie the rope into a knot. But it was a bit tricky.

The dad saw that she was having trouble and said, "It's ok if you need help. We can do it together."

So the dad and the little girl worked together and eventually were able to tie the knot. Everyone was so proud of the little girl and her accomplishment.

The mom and dad thanked the little girl for being such a big help and said, "We couldn't have done it without you. You are very important and include."

The little girl felt so happy and smiled. She couldn't believe she had done such an important job and helped her mom and dad!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Dave. Dave was three years old. Dave liked to learn about life. One day, he asked his mom what life was like. His mom told him it was a very attractive thing and it was important to understand it. Dave thought that sounded interesting. So, he decided to go outside and explore life. 

He found the most fascinating thing he had ever seen. It was a big, colorful butterfly. Dave thought the butterfly looked very attractive. He wanted to understand how it was alive. He watched the butterfly as it flew gracefully in the sunlight. Dave was amazed by the beauty of life.

Then, he heard a buzzing sound and saw a little bee. Dave wanted to understand how the bee could fly. He watched the bee as it flew around and around. Dave was so inspired by how much life he saw around him. 

Finally, Dave came to a conclusion. Life was a beautiful and fascinating thing. Dave was so happy he had the chance to understand it. He ran back to his mom to tell her about all the amazing things he had learned about life.

Once there was a greedy man who was very wealthy but wanted more money. He had an idea to make lots of money. He thought he could buy a teaspoon and use it to serve the public.

One day he took his teaspoon to a small village and he began offering his services - he would serve tea to anyone who wanted it.

At first the villagers were happy to have free tea but then the greedy man began to charge money for his tea. He wanted more money than he should have and the villagers were angry.

So, they all got together and told the greedy man that he couldn't use his teaspoon anymore. The greedy man was so angry!

He was so disappointed that he couldn't serve people anymore and he went away very unhappy. The villagers were safe, the greedy man could no longer charge them too much money and they no longer had to serve him.

Jill and Jack were best friends. They would play together each day.

One day, Jill had to leave for a little while. "Don't worry Jack," she said. "I will be back soon."

Jack felt very worried. He didn't know what to do while Jill was gone. Suddenly, he had an idea! He ran to the kitchen and grabbed a bottle of wine.

Jack smiled as he opened it. He took a big sip and bubbles tickled his nose. He felt a lot better. Suddenly, he had another idea! He would make a necklace with the cork from the wine bottle.

When Jill returned, she was surprised to see Jack wearing the necklace. "It's so unique," she exclaimed.

Jack smiled and felt no more worry. He was happy to share his unique creation with his best friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She loved to decorate her house for special occasions. Today was no exception.

Amy and her family were getting ready to celebrate her third birthday. She gathered all the decorations and asked her mum, "How can I decorate?"

Her mum smiled and said, "Why don't you hang a pretty hoop on the wall?"

Amy excitedly ran to get the hoop. She carefully hung it on the wall, and stepped back to admire her work.

There was a small voice coming from the hallway. It was Amy's little brother. He said, "Can I help you decorate, Amy?"

Amy smiled and said, "Yes! You can help me hang the balloons around the hoop and the walls."

So, Amy and her brother set to work. They carefully hung the balloons in the quiet room. Finally, everything was decorated and ready for the big party. 

Amy and her brother hugged and said, "Happy birthday, Amy!"

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They loved to play together, but sometimes they would quarrel. One day, they went to the park to play with some rocks. They were throwing the rocks and having fun until one of them accidentally hit the other one. The friend got angry and they started to quarrel. It was very noisy, and people around them were looking at them. But then they realized that they were being silly and apologized to each other. They hugged and continued to play with the rocks, but this time, they were more careful.

Once there was a girl named Maya. She was three years old. One day, Maya and her mom went to a store. Maya saw a pretty cup. It was bright blue with stars all around. She felt so excited. She asked her mom to buy it for her. 

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, this cup looks great. Let's get it for you."

Maya was so happy she could hardly contain herself. She grabbed the cup and hugged it tight. Then she said thank you to her Mom.

On the way home, Maya held the cup tightly in her hands. She felt so happy and excited, like she was the luckiest girl in the world. When she reached home, she put the cup on her shelf and smiled. It made her feel great.

Once upon a time, there lived a young girl. Her name was Molly and she was three years old. Molly's mummy was so proud of her daughter.

One day, Molly was feeling a bit wild. She wanted to do something daring. So, she asked her Mum, "Mummy, can I wear a skirt?"

Mummy thought carefully and then suggested, "Why don't you try wearing a shorts? Wearing a skirt is a bit difficult."

Molly thought this was a great idea. She got very excited and ran to her wardrobe to find a nice pair of shorts

Once upon a time, there was a cute little crab named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the sand and watch the water go in and out. He would wait for the big wave to come and then scurry away when it got too close.

One day, Timmy saw a tiny fish caught in the tide. The fish was so small and adorable that Timmy knew he had to help. He waved his little claws and tried to push the water back, but it was no use. 

Just when Timmy thought the fish was doomed, a big wave came and lifted the fish back into the safety of the ocean. Timmy was so happy that he waved his claws again and again, feeling proud that he had helped the little fish. From that day on, Timmy knew that even the smallest creatures could make a big difference.

Once upon a time, there was a small pond. One day, two friends who loved to explore together decided to go over and see what they could find.

The first friend said, "Let's plan to meet at the small pond tomorrow!"

The second friend replied, "Great idea! I'll bring some snacks, too."

The next day, the two friends were so excited to get to the pond. When they arrived, they were amazed at all the things they saw. The pond was filled with turtles and frogs, and even some little fish.

They spent the day exploring and playing games, and they had so much fun. The two friends even made a plan to meet at the pond again the following Saturday!

Once there was a little boy. He was playing in the garden when he saw a dove. He was so excited that he started to rush towards the dove. But before he could touch it, the dove flew away! The little boy was very confused. He ran to his mother to tell her what he saw. His mother told him that it was a dove and that it was in a hurry to get somewhere. He was still very confused, but he decided to rush around the garden until he found the dove again. After a few minutes, he spotted the dove in the sky. He was so happy he jumped up and shouted in delight. His mother was very proud of him for spotting the dove again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was quite brave. One day, she decided she wanted to go for a walk in the forest.

But when she got there, she was scared, because she saw a big, furry wolf. She turned to run back, but the wolf started coming closer.

The little girl was scared, but she tried to be brave. She yelled at the wolf to stop, and it did.

Then she said: "I need to get back home. Can you manage that safely?"

The wolf looked sad, but it nodded its head. The little girl continued home, and the wolf followed her.

When she got home, her parents were very surprised. But the wolf was very friendly and they managed to get along. The little girl even gave the wolf a name â€“ Bruce!

From then on, Bruce and the little girl were best friends, and she was never scared of the forest again.

Once upon a time there was a gentle mouse who lived in a small home. He had a cobweb in his bedroom and he loved to play in it. One day he heard a loud noise and he was scared. He wanted to make sure he was safe, so he quickly ran up to the bedroom door and locked it. 

From the other side of the door, he heard a big, scary voice. It said, "Let me in!". The gentle mouse froze. He did not know what to do. He wished he could go away, but he was too scared. 

Then he heard a different voice. It was a softer voice, like a mother's voice. The voice said, "Hey there little mouse. I just want to give you a hug. I know you are scared, but it is ok. We can all be friends". 

The gentle mouse felt the fear slowly ease away. He opened the door and there stood a happy three year old child with their arms open wide. The child gave the gentle mouse the biggest hug and together they explored the cobweb and played until it was time to go to bed. 

The mouse learned that day that there is nothing to be scared of and that friendship makes everything better. The gentle mouse and the child were friends ever since.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. They were Lily and Rose.

Rose said to Lily, "Do you want to come to my party?" 

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I do! Can I bring my friend Tom? He is a good friend too."

Rose hesitated for a moment, "I don't think so. We don't have much food, and Tom might not get enough." 

"That's selfish," replied Lily. "I recommend that we invite Tom too."

Rose thought about this and she agreed. She said, "Ok, let's give him an invitation and make sure he knows how much food there will be."

So they sent Tom an invitation and all three went to the party. They had a wonderful time and ate lots of food. 

The End.

Once there was a bunny who loved to hop. He hopped here and there, all around the place. He hopped over the hills, he hopped through the woods, he hopped faster than any other bunny in town.
