Mummy took Sally to the park. Sally was so excited! She saw lots of fun things to do. Firstly she saw a slide. She ran over to the slide quickly and climbed the ladder. She slid down so fast and it felt so amazing! Mummy gave Sally some gum and she chewed it. It was sweet and tasted so good. 

Next, Sally and Mummy went to the beach. It was very hot outside. Sally could feel the sun's warmth on her face. She ran to the edge of the sea and saw the waves crashing against the shore. She put one foot in the water and was surprised at how warm it was! Sally put both feet in the water and laughed as she felt the waves slide against her feet. 

It was such a fun day out and before long it was time to go home. Sally was tired but happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little spider. She wanted to make her home look nice. So, she decided to decorate it. She spun a cobweb in the corner. She worked and worked, wrapping the web around and around.

But then something happened. One of her neighbors was making too much noise. He was so loud, he made the spider jump. She was so startled, the cobweb fell down. But the spider wasn't angry. She was just quiet and patient. 

The spider started to spin again. She spun the cobweb even nicer this time. As she worked, she noticed something. The neighbor had stopped making noise. He was being very quiet now.

The spider realized why. The neighbor was deaf. He couldn't hear the noise he was making. So, the spider was very kind. She smiled, finished her cobweb and headed off to bed. Everyone was happy and the cobweb was so pretty.

One day, Lily was walking in the park. Suddenly, she saw a thing with spikes. It was huge and very scary. "Oh no! What's that?" Lily shouted. 

Lily's mom came running to help. When she saw the spikey creature, she said "That's a porcupine. Don't worry Lily, it won't hurt you." 

But Lily was still scared. She was so scared, she shouted "I don't like the porcupine. It looks terrible!" Her brave mom just smiled and said "Let's go back home now. Everything's ok."

Lily was relieved they could go home, but she still thought the porcupine was very scary. That was one of the most terrible things she had ever seen!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mia. She was three years old and loved to look at the stars in the night sky. Every night, she would rush out of her house and look up at the sparkling stars. 

One night, she rushed out of her house and called out loudly, â€œWhere are you, stars?â€ Then, to her surprise, one of the stars started to move. As it moved closer to her, Mia realised that it wasnâ€™t a star at all, but a fairy!

The fairy asked Mia, â€œWhat are you doing out here so late, little one?â€ Mia replied, â€œI am looking for a serious star.â€ The fairy smiled and said, â€œYou donâ€™t need to look far. All stars are serious and wonderful.â€ 

Mia smiled and thanked the fairy. Then, she rushed back inside to show her mum that she had found a real star.

Once there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and loved to play in the park. One day, when she was exploring, she came across a giant scale. She stepped up on the scale and it moved all the way up.

Anna was very excited and began to yell. She loved the feeling of being so high. Her mom saw what she was doing and ran over.

Her mom said, "Anna, you must come down now! You are feeling helpless on the scale!"

Anna tried to ignore her mother's words, but she knew she was right. Slowly she climbed down the scale until she was safely back on the ground.

Her mom smiled and praised her for being such a brave girl. Anna then ran off to find something else to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little lock. It wasn't a fun lock, because it was all closed up, and it just looked sad and boring.

The little lock was very fragile, so it couldn't handle getting too much banging or pushing. There was a puzzle that had to be solved in order for the lock to open.

The little lock waited for someone to come along and solve the puzzle. Soon, a very smart three-year-old came along and looked closely at the little lock. She thought hard and worked on the puzzle. After trying a few things, she finally found the right solution, and the lock opened!

The little lock was so excited to be open and be used. It was grateful to the little three-year-old for helping it solve the puzzle. They were happy together!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Joe. Sam and Joe wanted to go outside and play, but it was so cold! Sam said, "It's too cold, let's go inside where it's warm."

Joe said, "No way! I'm ready for a challenge."

Then, he slowly walked outside, and Sam followed him.

Suddenly, a strong gust of wind struck them. Joe shivered, then said, "It's too cold, let's go back inside."

Sam smiled and said, "I have an idea! Let's play a game."

The two friends played their game, and had lots of fun. Joe said, "It's not so cold anymore." 

They kept playing until it was time to go home. Sam and Joe were glad they had braved the cold and enjoyed their game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was only three years old, but she already knew how to fit lots of things together. One day, Mia was playing in the backyard when she saw something she had never seen before â€“ a jog! It was moving so quickly it made Mia very frightened.

Mia quickly ran inside and asked her mom, "What is that thing outside, Mommy?"

Mia's mom replied, "That is something called a jog. People use it as a way to exercise and stay healthy. It is like running but faster."

Mia was so intrigued by the jog she decided to try it out. She put on her sneakers and went outside to give it a try. She was a bit frightened the first time, but after a few tries Mia soon fit right in and was jogging up and down the street.

Mia was so thrilled to know that she could fit in with a jog and now she loves to exercise and stay healthy!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He had a toy bookcase. It was very silly. One day, Jack was playing and accidentally bumped into the bookcase and knocked it over. Suddenly, the bookcase started to burn!

Jack started to cry and screamed, "Help! My bookcase is burning!"

His mom ran to the room and asked, "What happened?"

Jack pointed to the burning bookcase and said, "It was an accident. I knocked it over and it caught fire."

His mom grabbed him and moved him away from the flames. Then she said, "Stay here and I will take care of it."

She filled a bucket with water and dumped it on the burning bookcase. The fire went out quickly and the smoke dissipated.

His mom then said, "Now let's clean up this mess and put the bookcase back up."

Jack helped his mom pick up the pieces of the bookcase. Then they put it back up and it looked as good as new.

The moral of the story is: when something bad happens, moms can help fix it!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to look at the flowers in her garden. One day, while she was looking at the pretty flowers, she saw a sign. The sign said "Beware of the dog". Lily was frightened because she didn't want to see a scary dog. 

She decided to go inside her house and tell her mommy about the sign. Her mommy listened to her and told her not to be scared. Mommy explained that the sign was there to keep people safe from the dog. 

Lily felt better and decided to go back outside to look at the flowers again. She knew that she didn't have to be frightened because the sign was there to protect her. From that day on, Lily always looked out for signs to keep her safe.

One day, a little fish named Fin was swimming near the shore. He saw a big crab and wanted to be friends. "Hi, I am Fin. Do you want to play?" asked the little fish. The crab looked at Fin and said, "No, I don't want to play. I am cold and I don't feel fine."

Fin felt sad but wanted to help the crab feel better. He swam away and thought of a plan. He remembered that the sun could make things warm. So, Fin swam to the top of the water and called to the sun, "Please, sun, help my new friend feel fine and not freeze!"

The sun heard Fin's call and shone its warm light on the shore. The crab started to feel better and not so cold. He saw Fin and said, "Thank you, little fish, for making me feel fine. I don't feel like I will freeze now. Let's play together!" And so, Fin and the crab played and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big black bear. He lived in a large cave in the forest. One day, the bear went outside to play. He found a big rock and started to play with it. He rolled the rock around and around until it was time to go back to his cave. The bear was happy because he had fun playing with the large rock.

Sara and Lily are sisters. They like to play with dolls and dress them up. Sara has a pink doll and Lily has a blue doll. They share a big box of clothes and shoes for their dolls.

One day, Sara wants to put a hat on her doll. She looks in the box and sees a yellow hat. She likes the yellow hat. She tries to take it out of the box, but it is stuck. She pulls hard, but the hat does not move.

"Help me, Lily!" Sara says. "I want the yellow hat for my doll!"

Lily comes over and looks at the box. She sees that the hat is under a pile of other things. She says, "You have to remove the things on top of the hat first. Then you can get the hat. Be gentle, Sara. Don't break anything."

Sara nods and listens to Lily. She removes the things on top of the hat one by one. She puts them on the floor. She is gentle and careful. She does not tear or bend anything. Finally, she sees the yellow hat. She smiles and takes it out of the box.

"Thank you, Lily!" Sara says. "You are a good sister. Here, you can have this purple scarf for your doll. It matches your blue doll."

Lily smiles and takes the purple scarf. She wraps it around her doll's neck. She says, "Thank you, Sara! You are a good sister too. Let's play together. We can make a tea party for our dolls."

Sara and Lily hug and play with their dolls. They are happy and share their things. They are gentle and kind sisters.

Once upon a time, there lived a small black bird. He all alone in the world and his wings were broken. He often wished he could fly like the other birds and so he kept trying to make his wings work.

But one day, the black bird found a skull on the ground and the skull was shiny and black. The skull looked strange and it made him wary.

Despite this, the black bird hobbled closer, and then he noticed that the skull was not just black and shiny, but it had a strange form of power. He suddenly felt safe.

The black bird felt that the skull had the power to heal his wings and so he touched the skull gently with his beak.

Suddenly, the black bird felt a jolt of energy that coursed through his body.

His wings grew strong and he could feel that he was healing. He then flew away happily, realising that he had been healed by the skull.

This story teaches us that although there may be unknown dangers in the world, we may find strength and courage in the most unexpected places.

John had his own paint. He was very excited and happy to show it to his mom. He said, "Mommy, I own paint!" His mom replied, "That's great John, let's paint together!" So, they opened the paint and John started to draw with it.

After a while, John finished his masterpiece and it looked so beautiful to him. He said to his mom, "Look mommy, I own tight paint!"

His mom was surprised and said, "Wow John, that's very impressive. Let's hang it up!" But, before they could hang the painting, John had an accident and the paint got smeared all over the place. His mom tried to console him but John was devastated and sad. 

The bad ending had been foreshadowed ever since John opened his paint; his mom had warned him several times to be careful and not play around with the paint too much. But, inevitably, he went against his mother's advice and it cost him dearly in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream and always wanted a cone. One day, Timmy and his mom went to the ice cream truck. Timmy asked the man for a cone with chocolate ice cream on top. The man gave Timmy the cone and said, "Be safe and don't run with the cone."

Timmy walked back to his mom and showed her his cone. Suddenly, a bird flew by and scared Timmy. The cone fell on the ground and Timmy started to cry. His mom said, "It's okay, Timmy. Accidents happen. Let's go get you another cone." Timmy stopped crying and smiled. He was happy to get another cone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jeanie who loved to explore. One day, she saw a big oyster on the beach. She was so excited and picked it up.

Jeanie said happily: "I'm gonna bury this oyster in my garden!"

Her Mum said: "No, Jeanie. You can't do that. Oysters are too fragile to bury. How about you take it home instead?"

But Jeanie didn't want to listen. She was a very quiet little girl and always does what she wanted to do. So she decided to bury the oyster in her garden.

The next day, she went to her garden to check the oyster, but found nothing. The ground was too hard and the oyster had disappeared. Jeanie was so sad and started to cry.

Her Mum came over and said: "I have told you so. Oysters cannot be burried like this. You should have listened to me."

Jeanie learnt a very important lesson that day. From then on, she always listened to her Mum and be quiet.

Jimmy was very excited. He was packing for a trip! He put all of his favorite objects in his suitcase. He packed his teddy bear, some cars and a blanket. Everything fit nicely into the suitcase.

Jimmy put on his shoes and grabbed the suitcase. He said goodbye to his family and walked out the door. Jimmy was feeling hot outside, but he kept walking until he reached the beach.

Jimmy put down his suitcase and ran to the ocean. He started playing in the sand with his objects from his suitcase. He built sand castles with his cars and wrapped his teddy bear in his blanket.

Soon, it was time for Jimmy to go home. He packed his objects back into the suitcase and walked back home. He had the best trip ever!

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with boats. They have a big boat that is navy. Navy is a dark blue color. The boat has a flag and a horn.

One day, they take the boat to the pond. They put the boat in the water and watch it sail. They feel happy and excited. They make boat sounds with their mouths.

"Look, Tim, our boat is fast and strong!" Sam says.

"Yes, it is, Sam. It is the best boat ever!" Tim says.

But then, a wind blows. The wind is strong and makes waves. The waves push the boat away. The boat goes too far and they cannot reach it.

"Oh no, Tim, our boat is gone!" Sam says. He feels sad and scared.

"Don't worry, Sam, we will get it back!" Tim says. He feels brave and helpful.

He sees a stick on the ground. He picks up the stick and runs to the edge of the pond. He tries to use the stick to get the boat. But the stick is too short and the boat is too far.

"Tim, it is not working!" Sam says. He feels hopeless and angry.

"Wait, Sam, I have an idea!" Tim says. He feels smart and hopeful.

He sees a duck on the water. The duck is swimming near the boat. Tim has some bread in his pocket. He takes out the bread and breaks it into pieces. He throws the pieces to the duck.

"Hey, duck, can you help us?" Tim says. He feels friendly and polite.

The duck sees the bread and eats it. It likes the bread. It sees Tim and Sam and hears them. It feels curious and kind. It swims to the boat and pushes it with its beak. It brings the boat closer to Tim and Sam.

"Wow, Tim, the duck is helping us!" Sam says. He feels surprised and grateful.

"Yes, Sam, the duck is very helpful!" Tim says. He feels happy and proud.

They use the stick to get the boat. They take the boat out of the water and hug it. They thank the duck and give it more bread. The duck quacks and wags its tail. It feels happy and helpful too.

Tim and Sam smile and hug each other. They feel happy and relieved. They have their boat back. They have a new friend. They have a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very hungry. She looked around to see if she could find something to eat. Suddenly, she spotted a door. It was locked. The little girl reached for the door handle and jiggled it. With a click, the door unlocked. 

The little girl opened the door and found a room full of food! There were pies, cakes and candy. Her eyes lit up and her tummy rumbled. She grabbed a big handful of food and started munching away. She ate and ate until her tummy was full. 

The little girl was so pleased that she had unlocked the door. She had found a way to get food. She smiled and waved goodbye as she skipped away, with a very full tummy.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pete. Pete lived in a big igloo with his family. The igloo was smooth and white, just like snow. Every day, Pete would wake up early and go outside to play with his friends.

One day, Pete saw the sun rise over the horizon. It was the most beautiful thing he had ever seen! The sky turned pink and orange, and the clouds looked like cotton candy. Pete ran back to his igloo to tell his family about the pretty sunrise.

From that day on, Pete woke up early every morning to watch the sun rise. He loved how the sky changed colors and how it made everything look so different. And every time he saw it, he felt happy and grateful to be alive.

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Sandy. Sandy wanted to find treasures to keep but all she found was dirt. She kept digging and digging and then she hit a mine. Sandy heard a loud bang, and it made her feel hurt.

Sandy's mommy heard the loud sound and she came to see what had happened. She asked, "What's wrong, Sandy?"

Sandy said, "I found something in the ground. It made a loud sound and it made me feel hurt"

Mommy said, "Oh Sandy, that was a mine. Be careful and don't touch it ever again."

So Sandy never touched the mine again. But she kept digging. And every day she found more treasures. She was so happy, her happiness began to increase. Sandy never felt hurt again and found many treasures to keep in her mine.

John and his mom were in the kitchen. His mom was cooking a big cake. John was watching closely and he asked his mom, "What are you making?". She replied, "I am making a cake". John was very excited and he started jumping up and down. His mom said, "Oh John, please be quiet". He stopped jumping and said, "Ok, I will be quiet".

John and his mom finished making the cake. They put it in the oven and waited for it to bake. After awhile, the timer rang and the cake was ready. John asked his mom, "Can I have a piece?". She replied, "Yes, you can have a piece but be careful, it's very hot".

John took a piece of the cake and it looked very delicious. He took a bite and it tasted yummy. He said with a loud voice, "This cake is delicious!" His mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it". John kept eating the cake and enjoyed it very much.

Sammy and his mommy were going on a special trip. They had never been to a camp before, but Sammy was very excited to go on this journey. 

On the way there, Sammy could feel the car going up and down the hills. His mommy pointed out the sky and told him it was bright blue, just like the ocean. 

When they finally arrived at the camp, Sammy was so happy to see the other children playing. He noticed how everyone was being so thoughtful and sharing their things with each other. 

Sammy was having so much fun, and his mommy was happy to see him playing with all the other kids. She wanted to make sure he was having the best time and was there to support him every step of the way. 

The time went by so fast. Later on, as they drove home, Sammy was very tired but still smiling, thinking of all the fun he had at the camp. He was grateful for the thoughtfulness of his mommy and all the people he had met.

Once there was a little girl named June who loved to drive. She had a beautiful car that was blue and silver and she loved it very much. One day, June wanted to drive to hear her favorite band play.

June asked her mom, â€œCan I drive to the band?â€
