One afternoon while out exploring, he met a small and very friendly fish. They soon became friends, and the anchor always looked forward to his daily fishing trips with his new buddy.

On one such outing, he noticed something unusual - a big round object up ahead. As he got closer, he realized that it was an old boat. He was so excited to explore this new discovery! He and his new friend swam around the boat, swimming all the way to the top. The anchor knew it must be a very special boat as it was so old.

When he reached the top, he saw something even more amazing. There was an elderly man, wearing a blue hat and coat, slowly moving about the boat. The anchor welcomed the old man and thanked him for allowing him and his friend to explore the boat.

The old man smiled, and said it was his pleasure. He had been living on the boat for many years, ever since his wife had passed away. He said he was happy to have some company, and shared many stories with the anchor about his life at sea. 

The anchor and his friend listened to the old man's stories, feeling so lucky to have met such

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play outside in the sun. One day, they find a big puddle of mud. They look at each other and smile.

"Let's play in the mud!" Lily says.

"Yes, let's!" Ben says.

They run to the puddle and jump in. They splash and laugh and make mud pies. They get very dirty and wet. They think it is very funny.

But then, they hear a voice.

"Lily! Ben! Time to go home!" It is Lily's mom. She is standing at the gate. She looks at them and shakes her head.

"Oh no! Look at you two! You are covered in mud!" She says.

Lily and Ben stop playing. They look at each other and giggle.

"Sorry, mom!" Lily says.

"Sorry, mom!" Ben says.

They get out of the puddle and walk to the gate. They hug Lily's mom and say goodbye.

"Bye, Lily! Bye, Ben! That was fun!" They say.

"Bye, bye! See you soon!" Lily's mom says.

They wave and go home. They have to take a bath and change their clothes. But they don't mind. They had a lot of fun in the mud. They can't wait to play again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a tank. It looked just like any ordinary tank. Inside the tank was a long, stretchy rope. Every day, a little girl named Sarah would play with the rope.

She would take both ends of the rope and stretch it out until it was super long. Then she would let it go, and it would shrink back down. She would do this many times and laugh.

One day, Sarah decided to take the rope for a walk. She went outside with the rope and started to stretch it out again. She kept stretching it until it was so long that it reached all the way to the end of her street.

Sarah and the rope had lots of fun! When it was time to go home, Sarah gathered both ends of the rope and put them back in the tank. She didn't want to leave the rope out in the ordinary street.

The end.

Ben and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big dog. The dog has a medal on its neck. It is shiny and red.

"Wow, look at that dog!" Ben says. "It has a medal. It must be rich."

"I want to touch it," Sam says. "Maybe it will let me have the medal."

"No, Sam, don't!" Ben says. "The dog might bite you. It might not like you."

But Sam does not listen. He runs to the dog. He tries to grab the medal. The dog growls. It shows its teeth. It bites Sam's hand. Sam cries.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sam says. "The dog bit me! It hurts!"

Ben runs to Sam. He helps him. He takes him to his mom. His mom is in the park. She sees Sam's hand. It is bleeding.

"Oh, Sam, what happened?" she says. "Did the dog bite you?"

"Yes, mom, it did," Sam says. "I wanted the medal. It was shiny and red."

"Sam, you should not touch other people's dogs," she says. "They might not like it. They might bite you. The medal is not yours. It belongs to the dog. You should say sorry to the dog and its owner."

Sam nods. He feels bad. He says sorry to the dog and its owner. The owner is nice. He says it is okay. He says the dog is not mean. He says the dog was scared. He says the medal is a reward. The dog is a hero. The dog saved a child from a fire.

"Wow, really?" Ben says. "That is amazing. The dog is a hero. The medal is special."

"Yes, it is," the owner says. "Do you want to pet the dog? He is friendly. He will not bite you if you are gentle."

Ben and Sam pet the dog. The dog licks them. They smile. They are happy. They learn a lesson. They do not touch other people's things. They respect the dog and its medal. They make a new friend. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ella. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she asked her mummy if she could go on an adventure. Her mummy said yes, so Ella put on her coat and went outside.

Ella walked for a long time until she arrived at a station. She had never seen one before, but knew that it was a special place. Ella looked around and saw some tracks running away from the station. 

Ella asked a friendly man, "What are those tracks for?"

The man said, "That's the train line, it takes people on journeys. When the train reaches a stop, it makes a special sound and yields."

Ella smiled. She was so excited that she was going to take a train ride. Ella asked if her mummy could come too and the man said she could. So Ella and her mummy got on the train. 

The train moved fast and Ella felt healthy and happy. Soon they arrived at their destination and Ella waved goodbye to the friendly man at the station. The adventure had been so much fun. 

Ella and her mummy returned home after their adventure. Ella said she couldn't wait to take her next train trip.

Once there was a girl. She was very sad. All day long she had to do things that made her feel terrible.

When the sun started to go down, the girl got on her bike. She wheeled down the street until she could see the most beautiful sunset.

The girl stopped to enjoy the wonderful sight. The colours were so bright, they filled her with joy.

When the breathtaking sunset eventually ended, the girl felt much better. She was so happy, she went home with a smile on her face. 

Her terrible day had finally come to an end, and the beautiful sunset had made it all worth it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old and loved to explore everything around her. One day, while looking around in her backyard, Amy noticed something strange. It was a big, colorful cloud of steam in the sky. Amy was fascinated and started to mention the cloud to her mom.

"Mommy, what is that? I think I saw a big, colorful cloud of steam in the sky!" said Amy.

Her mom looked up and smiled. "Oh that? That is just the steam from the nearby factory," said her mom.

Amy thought for a moment and decided she wanted to explore this steam cloud. She asked her mom if she could go over and take a closer look at the cloud.

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course you can. Just make sure you come back before it gets too dark."

Amy happily ran off to explore the colorful steam cloud. She had the best time ever, flying around it and playing in the steam. After a while, Amy remembered that she had to go back home before it got dark, so she said goodbye to the steam cloud and ran home.

The next day, whenever Amy mentioned the steam cloud to anyone, big smiles appeared on their faces. Everyone remembered that Amy had found something they all enjoyed.

Lily and Max were playing outside in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They threw snowballs at each other and laughed. They had a lot of fun.

But soon they started to feel cold. Their fingers and toes were numb. Their noses were red. They shivered and hugged each other.

"Let's go inside, Lily," Max said. "We can have some hot chocolate and cookies."

"OK, Max," Lily said. "But first, let's say goodbye to our snowman."

They ran to their snowman and gave him a big hug. They thanked him for playing with them. They told him they would come back tomorrow.

Then they ran to their house. Their mom was waiting for them in the office. She was working on her computer. She smiled when she saw them.

"Hi, kids," she said. "You look like you had fun. But you also look very cold. Come here and warm up."

She wrapped them in a big blanket and gave them each a cup of hot chocolate and a cookie. They sipped and nibbled and told her about their snowman. She listened and nodded and kissed their cheeks.

They felt warm and cozy and happy. They loved their mom and their snowman and their hot chocolate and cookies. They loved playing in the snow. They loved winter.

Once upon a time, there was a battery who wanted to have fun. So he went outside and decided to spray water everywhere. He sprayed and sprayed, until his mom saw and got mad.

The mom said, "No! You must not spray like that!" Then, the battery felt ashamed.

So the battery stopped spraying and said he was sorry. His mom said, "It's okay. From now on, only spray when I say it is okay."

The battery was happy to hear that and was glad that he was forgiven. So he ran and played happily, and never sprayed without asking his mom first. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very smart. He was walking in the park when all of a sudden the wind started to blow, and he was scared. He started to panic.

He turned around and saw his friend, Sarah. She calmed him down with a gentle, reassuring voice.

Sarah: "What's wrong sweetie? Why are you panicking?"

Boy: "The wind is too loud and making me scared."

Sarah: "It's alright. It's just the wind."

The boy took a deep breath and started to feel better. He looked around and noticed how pretty the trees were, even though the wind was blowing. He and Sarah held hands, and they enjoyed the moment together. 

The boy thought to himself, it's nice to have a smart friend like Sarah who knows what to say in scary moments.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack who liked to skip. He was so joyful and excited when he skipped! He skipped through the forest, and he skipped past the flowers. 

One day, Jack wanted to get a new skip rope, because his old one was worn out. He went to a store and found the perfect new skip rope! It was pink and sparkly and Jack knew it was perfect. 

Jack went outside to try out his new skip rope. But, soon Jack realized that he was being careless and not paying attention to his surroundings. He felt sad, because he was stepping on flowers and skipping on top of dirt instead of the grass. 

Jack remembered the lesson of the day - when you have something new, it's important to be careful. So, he carefully put away his new skip rope and decided that he would save it for another day, just to be safe. 

From then on, Jack reminded himself of the importance of being careful when he had something new. And, he always made sure to try and skip more on the grass than on the flowers and dirt!

Once upon a time there was a very brave girl named Sue. She wanted to go and explore the big, dark forest. As she set off, she felt afraid but knew she had to be brave and trust that things would be okay.

When Sue reached the forest she tried to explore but felt a bit lost and scared. Then, she heard a voice telling her to be patient and wait for help. Suddenly an old man appeared offering to show her the way. She was very fearful but then remembered his words to trust and wait.

With the old man's help, Sue made it safely out of the forest. From that day on, she trusted that she could be brave and face her fears. Whenever she felt fearful, she remembered to wait and trust that everything was going to be okay.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug. The bug was rare and very small. The bug liked to crawl all day long. One day, the bug wanted to crawl to the big tree. The big tree was far away.

The bug crawled for a minute, but then he saw a big rock. The rock was in the way. The bug tried to crawl around the rock, but he could not. The bug was sad. He wanted to get to the big tree.

Then, a nice bird saw the bug. The bird wanted to help. The bird picked up the bug and put him on the other side of the rock. The bug was happy. He could crawl to the big tree now. The bug and the bird were now friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to draw and create pictures with his crayons. One day, Timmy wanted to trade his picture with his friend, Johnny. Johnny had a toy car that Timmy wanted.

Timmy went to Johnny's house and showed him his picture. Johnny liked it and said he would trade it for his toy car. Timmy was happy and they made the trade.

But when Timmy got home, he realized the toy car didn't fit in his toy box. He was sad and went back to Johnny's house to trade it back. But Johnny said no and wouldn't trade back. Timmy was very upset and went home crying.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin. He loved to travel and explore the world around him. One day, he decided to join a group of other animals. He asked them if he could join them, and they said yes! 

The group of animals was very friendly and they all welcomed the penguin. It was easy to join them and they had lots of fun together. They ran, they played, and they laughed. The penguin was so happy to be part of the group. 

As time went on, the group went on more adventures. They explored the jungle, swam in the ocean, and visited beautiful places. Everywhere they went, the penguin was with them, always having fun. 

Soon the penguin was part of the group. He was accepted and loved by everyone. He was so happy to have found a place where he belonged. 

The penguin and his new friends stayed together for many years. They had many fun and easy adventures together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Every morning, Bob gets dressed. He puts on his special measuring hat. He won't leave the house before measuring how tall he is.

Today, he is going to a restaurant with his family. He is careful not to forget his measuring hat!

At the restaurant, Bob is so excited. He likes to look at all the tables and chairs. But first, he has to measure himself again. 

It's a big restaurant and lots of people are there. Bob hears them talking about how he looks so cute with his measuring hat on. He stands up straight and measures himself again.

Bob is so excited. He is sure he has grown a little bigger! His family is so proud of him. The restaurant staff say they will remember the day they met Bob with the special measuring hat.

Jim had a whistle. He loved to whistle with it. One day, he saw something in the sky. It was bright and loud. It was a helicopter! Jim was very excited. He wanted to make the helicopter come down. So he whistled with his whistle. The helicopter came down and surprised Jim. 

Soon, Jim was flying in the helicopter. He saw the clouds and the trees below. He waved to all the other people. They all waved back. Jim was very happy.

Suddenly, Jim saw his little brother. He was very jealous of Jim. He wanted to have a ride in the helicopter too. So Jim's brother whistled really loudly. The helicopter heard and came down. Then his brother had a turn in the helicopter.

Jim smiled. He was happy that his brother got to ride the helicopter too.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big cross on the grass. It is made of wood and has flowers on it.

"Who put this here?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe someone who is sad," Ben says.

They go closer to the cross. They see a card with words on it. They cannot read the words. They only know some letters.

"Look, there is an A and a B. Like our names!" Anna says.

"Maybe this is for us!" Ben says.

They are happy. They think someone sent them a gift. They pick some flowers and put them on the cross. They want to say thank you.

But then, a man comes. He is angry. He has a hat and a coat. He is very dry. He does not like the sun.

"Hey, what are you doing? This is my cross! This is for my wife! She is gone!" he shouts.

Anna and Ben are scared. They did not know. They thought they were nice.

"We are sorry, mister. We did not know. We wanted to say thank you. We thought someone sent us a gift," Anna says.

"A gift? This is not a gift! This is a memory! You have no right to touch it! Go away!" the man says.

He takes the flowers and throws them away. He picks up the cross and walks away. He is still angry.

Anna and Ben are sad. They did not mean to hurt him. They did not understand.

They go back to the playground. They hug each other. They are still friends.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Joe stood at the edge of a big field. It was quite frightening, he felt so small and scared, looking out over the open stretch of green.

Joe's mother had made him promise not to go too far, so he stayed at the edge of the field. He watched as the sun sank down and the field was bathed in its orange-pink light.

Suddenly, there was a loud crack and Joe saw flames leaping up from the center of the field. His heart went thump, thump and he felt very afraid.

He rushed towards his mother. Splutter, panting and shouting that there was a fire! He trembled, eyes wide, as his mother yelled "Stay here!".

She ran to the field and Joe watched, fearful and wide eyed. She found a big bucket, filled it with some water from the nearby stream, and then ran back to the field.

She threw the water and soon the fire was put out. Joe ran towards her, relieved that the fire was gone.

Joe's mother held him tight and said, "It's important not to play with fire, Joe. Fire can burn and hurt."

Joe nodded and from that day on always remembered his mother's words: "Don't play with fire!"

Once there was a boy named John. He was very happy and liked to play all day. He liked running around in circles and racing his friends. 

One day, his mom gave him a lemon. It looked very sour, so he didn't want it. He asked his mom, "Why do I have to eat this lemon?"

His mom smiled and said, "When you race around the circle and make it back here, then you can have it."

John smiled and ran as fast he could. He raced around the circle one time, then two times and finally made it back.

John was delighted! He ate the sour lemon and it tasted delicious! He then raced around the circle again, cheering as he went.

Once upon a time, there was a man who didn't have any hair on his head. His name was Mr. Bald. One day, a little girl saw him and said, "Hi Mr. Bald, you look funny!" Mr. Bald smiled and said, "Thank you for saying hello." 

The little girl felt bad for making fun of Mr. Bald, so she decided to be his friend. They played together and had lots of fun. Mr. Bald was happy to have a new friend. 

One day, the little girl's mom asked her who she had been playing with. The little girl said, "I played with my new friend, Mr. Bald." Her mom smiled and said, "That's a nice name. You should always be kind to your friends, no matter what they look like." The little girl nodded and said, "I know. I'm thankful for my new friend."

Once there was a young boy who was very healthy. His name was Sam. Every day he would play football with his friends. They would have so much fun running around and kicking the ball. 

One day, Sam scored a great goal. He was so proud. His friends cheered and cheered. They were so happy for him. 

The next day, Sam wanted to play again. But when he got to the park, everyone was playing a different game. All the kids had sacks in their hands and they were trying to see who could throw theirs the highest. 

Sam wanted to join in. So, his friends lent him a sack and showed him how to play the game. He was soon throwing it up as far and as high as he could. In no time, he was the winner. 

Sam was so proud. He had scored a goal yesterday and now he was the winner in the sack game. He was so happy to have had such a healthy and fun day.

Sara was a wealthy girl who lived in a big house with many toys. She liked to play with her dolls and dress them up in pretty clothes. She also had a pet cat named Fluffy, who was white and soft. Sara loved Fluffy very much and always fed him milk and fish.

One day, Sara's mother told her they were going to visit her aunt, who lived in the city. Sara was excited, because she had never seen the city before. She packed her favorite doll and some clothes in a small bag. She also wanted to bring Fluffy, but her mother said no. "Fluffy will be happier here, with our gardener. He will feed him and take care of him while we are away. Don't worry, we will be back soon," her mother said.

Sara was sad, but she kissed Fluffy goodbye and got in the car with her mother. They drove for a long time, until they reached the city. Sara saw many tall buildings, noisy cars, and busy people. She also saw some children who looked dirty and hungry. They were playing with sticks and stones, and had no toys or pets. Sara felt sorry for them, and wondered why they were so poor.

She asked her mother, "Why are those children so sad? Why don't they have toys or cats like me?"

Her mother sighed, and said, "They are not wealthy, like us. They have no money to buy toys or food. They live in small and dirty houses, and have to work hard to survive. They have a very different life from yours, Sara."

Sara thought about this, and felt sad. She wished she could share some of her toys and clothes with them. She wished she could feed them and make them happy. She wished she could give them Fluffy, who was so white and soft and loved to cuddle.

She said to her mother, "Can we give them some of our things, mama? Can we help them?"

Her mother smiled, and said, "That's very kind of you, Sara. Yes, we can. We can buy them some food and clothes, and maybe some toys. And maybe, we can find a nice home for Fluffy, too. He might be lonely here, without you. Maybe, one of those children would love to have him as a friend."

Sara smiled, too. She liked this idea. She hoped Fluffy would be happy with a new friend. She hoped the children would be happy with some new things. She hoped they would all be happy together. She hugged her mother, and said, "Thank you, mama. You are the best."

Once upon a time there was a wise old kangaroo. She moved slowly in her big, fluffy body. One day she spotted a brown rabbit hopping across the field. The kangaroo called out to the rabbit, "What do you need?". The rabbit replied, "I need to find something to spoil me!". The kangaroo said kindly, "I can help you. Follow me!". And so the rabbit followed the kangaroo. 
The kangaroo led the rabbit to a tall tree. "Climb up this tree," said the kangaroo. The rabbit did as was told. Then the kangaroo cheered, "Look up! You will find a special surprise!".
