Every night before bed, Mommy brought Sammy to the bathtub and they would snuggle together until it was time to get out. Sammy never felt shy when he was in the bathtub with Mommy. He knew he was safe and loved.

Once upon a time, there was a factory filled with delicious treats. Every day people came from far and wide to order their favourite treats from the factory.

One day, a little boy named Tom arrived at the factory with his mother. He looked around in amazement at all the yummy things. He wanted it all!

Tom turned to his mother and asked, "Can I have one?"

His mother hugged him and said, "Yes, you can order one treat today."

So, Tom ran around the factory with delight, picking out his favourite treats. He ordered a big chocolate cake, big biscuits, and lots of other delicious treats. 

Tom was so happy with all the yummy treats he had ordered. He waved goodbye to the factory, with his tasty goodies in hand. He knew he'd be back soon for even more delicious treats!

Once upon a time, a poor hedgehog named Jennifer lived deep in the woods. She was very sad because she wasn't rich like the other animals. One day, as Jennifer was walking, she found a sparkly gold coin. Then she heard a distant voice. 

"Slide that coin over here," said the voice.

Jennifer looked and saw a big, glossy fox. He had a long tail and a golden cap. Jennifer slid the coin towards the fox.

"I am very rich," the fox said, "and one gold coin won't make a difference. But why don't you have it? Keep it and do something nice for yourself!"

Jennifer's eyes lit up with joy. She said thank you and hugged the fox. From then on, whenever Jennifer needed something, she would spend a few coins and feel rich. She would slide her coins to the shopkeeper and smile. 

The fox was so pleased that he visited Jennifer from time to time with more coins. Jennifer was happy and the fox's tail wagged in joy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a little bird called Polly. Every day, she would go to the top of the tallest tree in the forest and shake her little wings. One day, when she was shaking her wings in the sunshine, she saw a brilliant rainbow spreading across the sky. It was so beautiful that Polly couldn't help but smile!

She asked her friend, a wise old owl, what the rainbow meant. The owl said that the rainbow meant that a new and happy day was coming, no matter how hard life is.

Every day, Polly would shake her wings and look for the rainbow. When she saw it, she would remember that there was hope. And when life was tough and the sky was grey, she would be reminded that it was only for a little while. She was so happy to have the rainbow that she was able to keep going and be brave.

Polly learned an important lesson: no matter how hard life gets, courage and hope will always shine through - like a brilliant rainbow!

Once upon a time there was a modern mom with a design idea. She wanted to make a special stomach for her two children.

Using her creative abilities, she chose colors and shapes that she thought the children would like best. She found some cloth and began to stitch the fabric together.

After working hard, the mom had made a beautiful modern stomach that the children could use during their playtime. They hugged her and thanked her for the gift.

Every day the children used the modern stomach for many activities. They pretended it was a boat, spaceship, and even a secret hiding spot.

The stomach was always there for them. Whenever they needed a rest or wanted to feel safe, they sat in the modern stomach.

The mom was happy that she had designed such a wonderful present for her children. In the end, the modern stomach was a gift that the children would always remember and treasure.

Tim and Sue were playing with their dolls in the garden. They liked to make up stories and act them out. Tim was the king and Sue was the queen. They had a big castle made of cardboard and a lot of toys.

One day, a big dog came into the garden. It was black and hairy and had sharp teeth. It saw the castle and the toys and wanted to play with them. It ran towards them and barked loudly. Tim and Sue were scared. They hugged their dolls and ran behind the castle.

"Go away, dog!" Tim shouted. "This is our castle and our toys. You can't have them!"

The dog did not listen. It jumped over the castle and knocked it down. It grabbed some toys and tore them apart. It growled and wagged its tail. It thought it was fun.

"Stop it, dog!" Sue cried. "You are mean and harsh. You are ruining our game. You are a threat to us!"

The dog did not care. It saw more toys and ran after them. It did not see Tim and Sue's dad coming into the garden. He heard the noise and saw the mess. He was angry.

"Hey, dog! What are you doing here?" he yelled. "Get out of my garden! Leave my kids alone!"

He picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. The dog was afraid. It dropped the toys and ran away. It did not want to fight. It wanted to find another place to play.

Tim and Sue's dad hugged them and checked if they were okay. He was sorry for their castle and their toys. He said he would help them build a new one and buy them new ones. He said he was proud of them for being brave and smart.

Tim and Sue smiled and thanked him. They were happy and relieved. They clapped their hands and cheered. They said they loved him and their game. They said they did not like the dog and hoped it would not come back. They said they wanted to play some more.

Tom and Lily are brother and sister. They like to play in the living room with their toys and cushions. They make a big fort with the cushions and pretend they are in a castle.

One day, Mom comes home with a new cushion. It is big and soft and has a picture of a dog on it. Tom and Lily both want the new cushion for their fort. They start to pull and tug on it.

"Let go, it's mine!" Tom says.

"No, it's mine!" Lily says.

They make a lot of noise and Mom hears them. She comes to the living room and sees them fighting over the cushion.

"Stop, stop, stop!" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over the cushion? There are plenty of cushions for both of you."

"But this one is the best!" Tom says.

"No, it's the best!" Lily says.

Mom shakes her head. She takes the cushion from them and puts it on the couch.

"Listen, Tom and Lily," Mom says. "The cushion is not the best. The best thing is to share and be kind to each other. That's what makes you good brother and sister. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily look at each other. They feel sorry for fighting. They nod their heads.

"Yes, Mom, we understand," they say.

Mom smiles. She gives them a hug and a kiss.

"Good," she says. "Now, why don't you play nicely with the other cushions and the toys? And maybe later, you can take turns with the new cushion, okay?"

Tom and Lily agree. They say sorry to each other and hug. They go back to their fort and play happily. They learn to share and be good. Mom is proud of them.

One day, Rhea couldn't find her favorite book. She looked high and low, but it was nowhere to be seen. She asked her mom and dad if they had seen it, but they said no. Rhea thought long and hard about where the book might be. Then, she had an idea.

She ran to the kitchen and opened the big freezer. Sure enough, her book was tucked inside. "How did it get there?", she wondered. Then she remembered that earlier, she had put it in the freezer to give it a nap. She had read that sometimes, books go to sleep when they get too tired.

Rhea carefully grabbed the book out of the freezer. It was a bit tough because it was so cold, but she was very careful. She hugged the book close and ran to her bedroom. She opened the book and the stories were back! She smiled, happy to have found her book.

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. He saw his friend, Sue, in her yard. Sue was holding a long hose. Tim did not know what a hose was, so he asked her. "Sue, what is that long thing?" Sue looked at Tim and said, "This is a hose, Tim. It helps us give water to the plants."

Tim felt ignorant because he didn't know about the hose. Sue wanted to show him how the hose worked. She turned on the water and the hose started to spray water. Tim was happy to see the water coming out of the hose. "Wow! That's so cool, Sue!" he said.

They both took turns using the hose to water the plants in Sue's yard. The plants were happy too because they were thirsty. Tim and Sue had a great day playing with the hose and helping the plants. Tim was glad that Sue showed him something new.

Mia loves to go to the park with her dad. He is bald and has a big smile. He always brings a leash for Mia's dog, Spot. Spot is a brown and white dog who likes to run and play.

One day, they see a big sign at the park. It says: "Dog Show Today". Mia and her dad are excited. They want to see the dogs. They walk to the field where the show is. There are many dogs of different colors and sizes. Some have long hair, some have short hair, some have spots, some have stripes.

"Look, dad, that dog has a hat!" Mia says, pointing to a poodle with a pink bow on its head.

"Yes, it does. And that dog has a sweater!" dad says, pointing to a chihuahua with a blue knit top.

They watch the dogs do tricks and jump over hurdles. They clap and cheer for the dogs. Spot barks and wags his tail. He wants to join the show.

"Can Spot be in the show, dad?" Mia asks.

"I don't think so, Mia. He is not trained for the show. He is just a pet. But he is a very good pet. And we love him very much." dad says, hugging Mia and Spot.

Mia nods. She loves Spot very much. She does not care if he can do tricks or wear clothes. He is her best friend. She puts the leash on Spot and they walk back home. They are happy.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to travel. He enjoyed the peaceful days and wanted to find more. So he packed his bag, kissed his mom goodbye and set off on his way.

He traversed the land for many days and many nights. He discovered different places and even stumbled into a peaceful village. All of the villagers were so friendly and helped him on his journey.

Then one day he came to a large river and noticed a strange wrecked boat in the distance. He decided to cross the river in the boat and he waved goodbye to the villagers. His journey continued until the river became too strong. He was pulled into the raging waters and all he could hear were the villagers shouts for help.

But he slowly sank into the deep and dark water. He never made it to his destination, and the last thing he remembered was the peaceful river.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra named Ziggy. Ziggy was very sleepy because he had stayed up all night playing with his friends.

One day, Ziggy's friend the giraffe came over to visit. "Ziggy, you look very sleepy," said the giraffe. "I recommend that you take a nap."

Ziggy agreed and went to his cozy bed. As he was falling asleep, he heard a rustling outside his window. It was his other friend, the monkey.

"Ziggy, wake up!" said the monkey. "I have a surprise for you!" Ziggy rubbed his eyes and went outside to see what the surprise was.

To his amazement, the monkey had brought a giant pile of hay for Ziggy to munch on. Ziggy was so happy and grateful for his thoughtful friends. He ate the hay and fell back asleep, dreaming of his fun day with his friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a nosy cat named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys, but he also liked to see what everyone else was doing. One day, Tim saw a big box with a bow on it. It was a gift for his friend, Tom the dog.

Tim was very curious about the gift. He tried to open it, but it was too hard. He wanted to know what was inside, so he tried to slip the bow off. But as he did, he made a big mess. The gift fell on the floor and the bow came off.

Tom came into the room and saw the mess. He was sad because his gift was ruined. Tim felt bad for being nosy and making a mess. He said sorry to Tom and helped him clean up. They found a new bow and put it on the gift. In the end, they opened the gift together and had fun playing with the new toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Midnight. One day, Lily's mom asked her to go to the store to buy an avocado. Lily was excited to go on a trip to the store with Midnight.

When they arrived at the store, Lily saw her friend Sarah. Sarah had a toy that Lily wanted to play with. But Sarah didn't want to share her toy. Lily was sad and said, "I miss my toys at home." Midnight rubbed against her leg to make her feel better.

As they walked through the store, Lily accidentally dropped the avocado and it rolled away. Midnight chased after it and brought it back to Lily. She was happy and said, "Thank you, Midnight!" On the way back home, Lily said to Midnight, "I'm happy we're friends. I don't want to miss you when we're apart." Midnight purred and cuddled up next to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny silver necklace that she loved to wear. One day, Lily's friend Tom came to visit her. "I like your necklace," said Tom. "Can I borrow it?" Lily thought for a moment and then said, "Sure, you can wear it to the party tonight." Tom was very happy and said, "Thank you for inviting me to the party. I can't wait to see your modern house!" Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. Let's go have fun!" And off they went to the party, wearing Lily's shiny silver necklace.

Once there was a bouncy girl named Lucy. She was always so full of energy. She always wanted to bounce around and never stay still. 

Today Lucy had a special plan. She told her family, â€œLet's go to a restaurant!â€ Everyone was very excited. 

They got ready and all hopped in the car. The restaurant was very nice and had all sorts of delicious food. Everyone was so hungry. 

But when it was time for Lucy to eat, something strange happened. She didn't want to anymore. Lucy just wanted to bounce around the restaurant. 

Her family was very confused but eventually understood that Lucy just wanted to have fun! So they all took turns trying to catch her as she bounced around the restaurant. It was so much fun for everyone!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. She wanted to find something special, something no one else had. So one day she set off on an adventure.  
Sally walked to the top of a big hill. When she got there she started to dig. She dug for hours, and eventually she found something amazing - a mine! It was full of sparkly treasures, more than she'd ever seen before. 

Sally was so excited. She decided to keep her mine secret and kept it a secret from everyone.

Every day Sally went to her mine, full of honest joy. She'd settle down in the corner and play with the sparkly treasures until tea time.

Sally would often tell her parents about her mine. She told them it was her little secret and asked them to keep it that way. 

Sally's mine was her special place, full of honest fun. She kept it a secret and visited it every day. It made Sally so happy - she'd found something no one else had!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One amazing evening, the sun was going down and the sky was full of pretty colors. Lily saw her friend Tom by the big tree.

"Hi Tom!" said Lily. "Let's play a fun game before it gets dark!" Tom smiled and said, "Yes, let's play hide and seek!" So, Lily and Tom started to play. Lily closed her eyes and counted to ten while Tom ran to hide.

Lily looked and looked for Tom. She found him hiding behind the big tree. "I found you!" said Lily. They both laughed and played until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and went to their homes. The amazing evening was over, but they knew they would play together again the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy went to school every day, but he was always scared. He didn't like the big kids who would sometimes snap at him. 

One day, Timmy was walking to school when he saw a pretty flower. He picked it up and smelled it. Suddenly, he heard a loud snap behind him. It was a big kid who wanted to scare him. 

Timmy was so scared that he dropped the flower. But then he remembered something his mom had told him. She said, "If you ever get scared, just take a deep breath and count to three." So Timmy did just that. He took a deep breath and counted to three. When he opened his eyes, the big kid was gone. Timmy felt proud that he didn't let the big kid scare him anymore. And he went to school with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a duck who liked to rub himself. He would make circles on his feathers, back and forth. He did it so fast, it looked very impressive.

One day, he got very caught up in his rubbing. He was so busy he didn't even notice the green pond in front of him. He kept rubbing until he noticed a reflection in the water.

It was a small duckling, looking up at him. He was so cute! The duck stopped rubbing and smiled down at the little duck. That made the duckling so happy it started to rub its feathers too!

The bigger duck watched in surprise. He was so impressed! The smaller duck was already so good at rubbing his feathers.

The bigger duck was proud and smiled happily at his duckling friend. Together they rubbed and played in the water. It was the happiest day ever!

Once there was a man who liked to fix things. He was very good at it. One day, he saw something bad. The rice in his cupboard was all mixed up. He couldn't eat it like that!

The man said to himself, "I must fix this! I need to separate the rice."

He got some bowls and started to separate the rice. Soon, he had the white rice in one bowl and the brown rice in the other.

The man smiled. He was happy he fixed the rice.

He said to himself, "It's nice to fix things. Now I can eat the rice!"

One day, a boy and his dad were going on an adventure. The boy was so excited because his dad was going to lead him somewhere new and exciting. First, they went to a park. Everywhere the boy looked, he saw lots of colorful things. His dad pointed out a huge cross with lots of colors on it. The boy was amazed by its beauty.

Then, his dad lead him to a lake. The lake was so blue and shiny. The boy was amazed by the sight. Dad kept leading him and the boy followed with curiosity.

They eventually came upon a small colorful building. When they got closer, the boy saw that it was a pet store. His dad lead him inside. The boy was excited to pick out a pet!

His dad took him around the store, letting him decide what animal he wanted to take home. Finally, the boy chose a colorful bird. He was so excited to take it home! 

His dad lead him out of the store and they started their journey home. The boy couldn't wait to share his new bird with his mom. What an exciting adventure!

Lila and Ben were playing in the pool. They liked to dive under the water and see who could hold their breath longer. Lila had a toy weapon that looked like a shark. She used it to scare Ben sometimes.

"Look, Ben, I have a shark!" Lila said, holding the weapon in her hand.

"Let me see!" Ben said, swimming closer.

Lila smiled and dived under the water. She swam behind Ben and touched his leg with the weapon. Ben felt something and turned around. He saw the shark and screamed.

"Help, help, a shark!" Ben shouted, splashing the water.

Lila came up and laughed. "It's not a real shark, Ben, it's just a toy!" she said.

Ben looked at the weapon and saw that it was not hairy or scary. It was just plastic and had a smiley face. He felt silly and laughed too.

"Ha ha, you got me, Lila, that was a good trick!" he said.

Lila and Ben hugged and played with the weapon together. They had fun diving and pretending to be sharks. They were happy and did not want to get out of the pool.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog has a black spot on his back. He looks nice.

"Can we pet him?" Jen asks Tom.

Tom shrugs. He does not know. He likes dogs, but he is a little scared. The dog is bigger than them.

They walk closer to the dog. The dog sees them. He wags his tail. He barks. He sounds happy.

"Hello, dog!" Jen says. She reaches out her hand. The dog licks her hand. He is warm and soft.

Tom smiles. He pets the dog too. The dog likes them. He rolls over. He wants them to rub his belly.

They laugh. They rub his belly. The dog is their new friend.

They do not see the man who is looking for the dog. The man is angry. The dog ran away from him. The dog does not like the man. The man is mean. He hits the dog. He makes the dog do tricks. He does not give the dog treats.

The man sees the dog in the park. He sees Tom and Jen. He runs towards them. He yells.

"Hey, that's my dog! Get away from him!"

Tom and Jen are scared. They do not want to leave the dog. The dog is scared too. He growls. He does not want to go with the man.

What will happen next? Will Tom and Jen help the dog? Will the man take the dog away? Will someone else come to help? The end.

The moon shone brightly in the sky. It was a beautiful night for two polar bears. They were about to measure the stars. 
Suddenly, there was an incredible earthquake. The polar bears were frightened and ran away. 
The earthquake became bigger and bigger. They ran and ran, but it followed them. 
Finally, they stopped in a small cave and hid. They knew they couldn't escape. 
The earthquake grew more and more intense until it was too much to handle. The bears were engulfed in an avalanche of rocks and ice, and they were gone. 
The earth was silent, and the stars still shone in the sky. It was a sad ending for the poor polar bears who just wanted to measure the stars.

Lily and Max were at the zoo with their mom. They wanted to see the penguins. They liked how they looked in their black and white coats. They followed the signs to the penguin house.

When they got there, they saw a big pool of water with ice and rocks. There were many penguins in the water and on the land. Some of them were swimming and diving. Some of them were standing and flapping their wings. Some of them were marching in a line.

"Look, mom, they are marching!" Lily said. "They look like soldiers!"

"Yes, they do," mom said. "They march to keep warm and to stay together. It is very cold where they live."

"Can we march like them?" Max asked.

"Sure, why not?" mom said. "Let's march around the pool and see if they notice us."

Lily and Max started to march like the penguins. They lifted their feet high and swung their arms. They made funny noises with their mouths. They had fun.

But one penguin did not like their marching. He was the leader of the penguin group. He thought they were mocking him and his friends. He felt angry and annoyed. He decided to teach them a lesson.

He jumped out of the water and ran towards Lily and Max. He opened his beak and squawked loudly. He pecked at their shoes and legs.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily and Max cried. "Stop it, stop it, stop it!"

They ran away from the penguin. They were scared and hurt. They ran to their mom and hugged her.

"Mom, mom, mom!" they said. "The penguin is mean! He bit us!"

Mom looked at the penguin. He was still chasing them. He looked angry and proud. She picked up Lily and Max and carried them away from the penguin house.

"I'm sorry, kids," she said. "That penguin was not nice. He did not like your marching. He thought you were making fun of him. He wanted to protect his group. He did not know you were just playing."

Lily and Max nodded. They understood. They felt sorry for the penguin. They did not mean to upset him. They just wanted to have fun.

"Can we say sorry to the penguin?" Lily asked.

"Maybe later," mom said. "Let's go see some other animals first. How about the monkeys? They like to play too."

Lily and Max smiled. They liked the monkeys. They hoped they would be nicer than the penguin. They followed their mom to the monkey house. They forgot about the penguin. They were happy again.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big cable hanging from a tree. It looks like a snake, but it is not. It is harmless.

"Let's catch the cable!" Lily says. "It will be fun!"

Ben nods. He likes to catch things. They run to the tree and grab the cable. They pull and swing on it. They laugh and shout.

But then, the cable breaks. It makes a loud noise. Lily and Ben fall to the ground. They are scared and hurt.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cries. "My knee is bleeding!"

"Me too!" Ben says. "My elbow is sore!"

They look at the cable. It is not harmless. It is bad. It has wires and sparks inside. It is dangerous.

"Help, help!" Lily and Ben call. "We need help!"

A man hears them. He is a worker. He is fixing the cable. He runs to them. He sees the broken cable and the children.

"Oh no!" he says. "What have you done? This cable is very important. It gives power to the lights and the machines. You should not touch it. It can hurt you."

He picks up Lily and Ben. He takes them to his truck. He gives them bandages and water. He calls their parents. He is sorry and angry.

Lily and Ben are sorry and ashamed. They did not know. They just wanted to play. They learned a lesson. They will never catch a cable again.

Fred pushed open the door and stepped outside. He saw an orange taxi sitting in the driveway. He wanted to go on an adventure.

He trotted over to the shiny car and said, â€œTaxi, take me on an adventure!â€

The taxi driver answered, â€œWhere would you like to go?â€

Fred closed his eyes and thought, â€œI want to climb the tallest mountain!â€

The taxi driver said, â€œThatâ€™s a long way. Are you sure you can make it?â€

Fred smiled and said, â€œYes! I will climb the mountain and make friends with everyone there.â€

So, the taxi driver drove off and soon Fred was on his way. He was so excited.

But when he got to the mountain, he found it was very hard to climb. He was tired and troubled, but he refused to give up. After a few hours, he finally made it to the top.

He looked around and smiled. He had made it! Now he had made lots of friends, just like he wanted. He was so proud of himself.

Fred hopped back into his taxi and said, â€œTake me home now!â€ The taxi driver drove him back home, and with a smile on his face, Fred went to sleep dreaming of his new mountain friends.

Once there was a truck. It was big and strong and very reliable. Everyone in town knew they could trust the truck. It was always there to help.

But there was a problem. Someone did not like it. He was small and mean. He was always mean to the truck. He called it names and tried to break it. He was very naughty and he hated the truck so much.

But the truck was too strong. He could not break it, no matter how hard he tried. He would get mad and start shouting. But the truck would just stay happy and strong, no matter what happened. It was always there when people needed it.

At the end, the man had to admit the truck was too strong. He stopped being mean and tried to be helpful instead. He realized the truck was very reliable, and he was glad he had it nearby.

Once upon a time, in a small village there lived a young girl called Lucy. She was very popular among her friends for her vibrant and happy personality. One day, when Lucy was walking past the park, she spotted something in the grass. When she looked closer, she saw it was an old purse! 

Lucy was so excited and she bent down to pick it up. When she opened the purse, she found lots of coins inside. She was so happy that she could now buy herself some new toys. 

But when she tried to stand up again, Lucy suddenly realised that she was stuck. She had been using her purse to balance herself and in the process had become tangled up in the long grass. 

Lucy started to struggle to try and get untangled, but the long grass was too powerful. She began to cry and shout for help. 

Just then, one of her friends walking past the park heard her cries and came to her rescue. 

Her friend put down his popular baseball cap and helped Lucy free herself. After a few minutes of struggling, Lucy was free. She thanked her friend and gave him a big hug. 

The two of them stopped to count the coins inside the purse before walking back to Lucy's house. 

The End!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She liked to twist, twist, twist. Everywhere she went she would twist and turn, always on the go. One day the little girl went outside. It had been raining so everything was all wet.

The little girl didn't care. She spotted a helmet on the ground. She picked it up and put it on her head. She looked very funny. She began to twist and turn all around the garden. Suddenly she slipped and fell in the mud. She was very wet!

The little girl laughed and laughed, knowing she had had a great time. She picked up the helmet and went inside. She couldn't wait to tell her mom all about her fun twisty adventures with her helmet!

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and pretend they were flying to faraway places. One day, they decided to fly to an island where they could have fun and find treasure.

They swung higher and higher, and closed their eyes. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They imagined they saw the blue sea and the green island below them. They shouted, "We're almost there!"

But when they opened their eyes, they saw something else. They saw a big pile of trash and dirt next to the swings. It was filthy and smelly, and it had old cans and bottles and papers and clothes. They felt sick and scared.

"Yuck! What is that?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. It's not an island. It's a mess!" Ben said.

They wanted to get away from the trash, but they were still swinging. They tried to stop, but they couldn't. They swung faster and faster, and the trash seemed to get closer and closer.

"Help! Help!" they cried.

They saw a man walking by with a dog. He heard their cries and came to see what was wrong. He saw the trash and the swings and the children.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing here? This is not a place to play. This is a dump. Someone left all this garbage here and didn't clean it up. It's dangerous and dirty. You could get hurt or sick. Come down from the swings and I'll take you to a safer place."

He helped Anna and Ben get off the swings and took them by the hand. He led them to another part of the park, where there were flowers and trees and a pond. He gave them some water and cookies and told them to be careful where they play.

"Thank you, mister. You're very kind," Anna said.

"Yes, thank you. We're sorry we played in the dump. We didn't know," Ben said.

"That's okay, kids. I'm glad you're safe. Next time, use your imagination, but also use your eyes. Not everything you see is what you think. And remember, don't litter. Keep the park clean and beautiful for everyone," the man said.

He smiled and waved goodbye, and walked away with his dog. Anna and Ben looked at each other and nodded. They learned their lesson. They decided to play somewhere else, and never to swing to the filthy island again.

Sue and Mike were planning a picnic in the park. They wanted to have the best time ever! Sue and Mike packed snacks for their picnic. They brought lots of different snacks, but their favorite was the beans.

When they arrived in the park, they spread out their blanket and started to get ready for the picnic. Suddenly, Sue noticed something strange â€“ there was a deaf rabbit in the middle of the park.

Sue was excited. She called out to Mike, "Let's give him some beans!" Mike nodded with a smile and together they took out an extra portion of beans and placed it near the rabbit.

The rabbit hopped around the beans and started to eat. Sue and Mike were delighted to see the rabbit enjoying their snack. They had a wonderful picnic and plan to visit the park again soon.

Lily and Ben are playing hide and seek in the park. Lily is the seeker and Ben is the hider. Lily counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!"

Lily looks around the park and tries to find Ben. She sees a big tree, a slide, a swing, and a bench. She does not see Ben. She searches behind the tree, under the slide, on the swing, and next to the bench. She still does not see Ben.

She hears a giggle from behind a bush. She runs to the bush and sees a strip of blue shirt sticking out. She pulls the strip and says, "I found you, Ben!"

Ben comes out of the bush and laughs. He says, "You are good at seeking, Lily!"

Lily smiles and says, "You are good at hiding, Ben!"

They hug and say, "You are my kind friend!"

They decide to play again and switch roles. Ben is the seeker and Lily is the hider. They have fun playing hide and seek in the park.

Once upon a time, there was an old rabbit. He lived in the woods with many other animals. Every day, he wanted to learn something new. He saw the other animals scurrying around and noticed how much they knew. He wanted to be just like them! 

One day, he decided to learn how to climb the trees. He hopped to the base of the tree, but it was too high. He tried and tried, but he couldn't reach the top. He was starting to get frustrated. 

Then, a beautiful blue bird flew by. She noticed the old rabbit trying to climb the tree. She swooped down and offered to help. She flew to the branches above and told the old rabbit which way to jump. 

Finally, the old rabbit made it to the top of the tree. He was so excited! He could feel the wind in his fur and see the other animals below. He had learned a new trick! From then on, the old rabbit was never afraid to try something new.

Lily and Max were playing in their room. They had many toys, but they liked to look at the photo book best. The photo book had pictures of their family and friends. They liked to point at the faces and say their names.

"Look, this is Grandma and Grandpa," Lily said, showing Max a photo. "They are very nice and give us hugs and cookies."

Max nodded and smiled. He liked Grandma and Grandpa too. He turned the page and saw a photo of a big dog. He pointed at it and said, "Woof, woof!"

Lily giggled. She knew the dog's name was Spot. He was their uncle's dog. He was very friendly and liked to play fetch. She said, "Spot, Spot, good dog!"

They turned more pages and saw more photos. They saw their mom and dad, their cousins, their friends, and their teacher. They said hello to each one and made noises or gestures to match them.

They were having fun, but they did not know that their mom was sleeping in the next room. She had a headache and needed to rest. She heard their voices and felt frustrated. She wanted them to be quiet and let her sleep.

She got up and went to their room. She opened the door and saw them with the photo book. She said in a loud voice, "Lily and Max, what are you doing? You are making too much noise! You need to be quiet and let me sleep!"

Lily and Max were scared. They did not mean to make their mom angry. They loved their mom and did not want to hurt her. They said, "Sorry, mom, sorry!"

Their mom saw their faces and felt sorry too. She knew they were just playing and did not know she was sleeping. She said, "It's okay, my loves, I know you did not mean it. But you need to whisper when I am sleeping, okay? Whisper means to talk very softly, like this." She leaned down and whispered in their ears, "I love you very much."

Lily and Max nodded and whispered back, "I love you too, mom." They hugged their mom and gave her a kiss. Then they went back to the photo book and whispered to each other. They were happy and quiet. Their mom smiled and went back to her room. She closed the door and fell asleep.

One day, two little boys were sitting on the steps of their house. It was a dark afternoon and one of the boys said to the other, "I heard our neighbour talking about a ghost". 

The other boy shrugged and said, "I don't believe in ghosts". He paused for a moment and then added, "Let's go explore the dark woods". 

The two boys grabbed their flashlights and ran into the woods. As they walked, the darkness seemed to grow thicker, and the boys started to get scared. All of a sudden, they heard a noise and both of them jumped back! 

The boys stood there, trembling in fear. Then, one of them said with a shrug, "Maybe it was just a ghost".  The other boy agreed, and they ran all the way back home!

Once upon a time, there was a serious car. It was red, shiny, and big. One day, the serious car wanted to go really fast. It wanted to speed down the street.
The car zoomed around the corner. It was going so fast, it almost lost control! But it stayed on the road. The car was going so fast that its lips were flapping in the wind.

Finally, the serious car stopped. Its tire had reached its top speed. The car was really happy. It had had a great time speeding down the street.

The end.

Anna and Ben liked to play on the beach. They made sand castles and dug holes. They watched the waves come and go. Sometimes they found shells and crabs.

One day, they saw a big boat on the water. It was red and white and had a horn. They heard it go "toot toot". They wanted to see it closer. They ran to the edge of the water.

"Wait, Anna, wait!" Ben said. "Mom said we have to be careful. The water can be strong. It can take us away."

Anna did not listen. She was too excited. She ran into the water. She felt the water touch her feet. It was cold and wet. She laughed.

"Come on, Ben, come on!" she said. "It's fun! The boat is near. Maybe we can say hello."

Ben was scared. He did not like the water. He saw the water move. It was getting higher and higher. He knew it was the tide. The tide could be dangerous.

"Anna, come back, come back!" he said. "The tide is coming. It can push us down. We have to yield. We have to go back to the sand."

Anna did not hear him. She was too busy looking at the boat. She waved her arms. She shouted "toot toot". She thought the boat would see her. She did not see the wave behind her. It was big and fast. It was ready to crash.

Ben saw the wave. He was very scared. He ran to Anna. He grabbed her hand. He pulled her out of the water. He saved her.

They fell on the sand. They were wet and cold. They were also safe. The wave passed by. The boat passed by. It did not see them. It did not care.

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They were quiet. They realized they were silly. They should have listened to Mom. They should have been careful. They hugged each other. They said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They never ran into the water again.

Once upon a time, there was a small dark bottle. Inside the bottle lived a tiny creature called a genie. The genie had a special power that granted 3 wishes. One day, a 3 year old child came across the bottle. They peered inside and the genie's magical voice said, "I am the genie of the bottle. What is your name?"

The 3 year old child was very excited and told the genie their name. The genie smiled and said, "So your name is ____, wonderful! I will now grant you three wishes!" The child smiled wide and thought about their wishes. After making three wishes, the genie disappeared. 

The 3 year old child was very happy and thanked the genie for the amazing gifts. After making sure the bottle was safe, the child continued on their way with a hop and a skip in their step.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer and his sheep. The farmer lived on a big farm full of dirt and mud. 
One day, the farmer was looking for his sheep but he could not find them. He looked everywhere for them but he could not see them. He was worried and started to yell.

Suddenly, he heard a loud "baa!" He looked through the mud and saw the sheep! But they were dirty! He had to get them out of the mud.

The farmer yelled at the sheep to try and get them out of the mud. The sheep started jumping and jumping. Finally, the farmer got them out safely. 

The farmer was relieved and he gave the sheep a big hug. He was so happy that the sheep were safe and not hurt. From that day on, the farmer was extra careful when watching his sheep.

Once upon a evening there was a new home. Maria wanted to explore her new home and took some steps in to the garden. It was dark, but the stars were twinkling in the night sky.

Suddenly, Maria heard some noise coming from the tree. She came close to the tree and saw a tiny little bird. "Welcome to my home," said the little bird. Maria was so happy to have a new friend. 

She welcomed the little bird with a smile and offered it some of her food. The little bird was very happy and kept chirping. They spent the evening together, talking about the new home and looking at all the stars in the night sky.

The little bird said goodbye when the evening had ended and Maria thanked the bird for coming to welcome her in her new home.

Once upon a time, there was a bright kid. He loved playing all sorts of sports. 

Whenever his mom and dad would watch a game on the television, he would try and copy all the moves. He was very fast and he could jump high. 

One day, his mom saw him outside playing a sport. "Hey, that's enough for today!" she shouted. But the kid kept playing. 

So his mom ran over, grabbed his hand and said, "No need to run so much! Stop now." The kid listened and stopped running. 

He hugged his mom and said, "Okay, I'll be more careful next time." His mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you understand." 

They both laughed and went inside. The bright kid looked forward to the next time he could play a sport.

Once there was a girl who liked to drive. She would go everywhere in her car. One day, however, she had a problem. Her license was not working! She tried and tried to get it to work, but nothing helped. She was so sad.

The girl asked her mom for help. Her mom said she needed to get a new license. The girl knew this was her only hope. She went to the store and got a new one.

When she got home, she was so excited! Now she could drive again. But she was careful. She knew the license was fragile and she had to be careful not to drop it.

After a few days, the girl quit driving. She realized it wasn't so fun anymore. With the new license, she could now do other fun things in life!

Once there was a bird named Steve. He was very healthy and strong. He wanted to fly higher than any other bird in the sky.

So Steve looked for ways to make himself better. He found a bottle of lotion and rubbed it all over his wings. Then he flapped his wings and flew off into the sky.

Steve flew till he was so high that he could touch the clouds. He looked so small, but he was so proud of himself. He flew higher than anyone before him.

He flew happily around the sky, his wings glistening in the sunlight. He was feeling so good, so healthy, and so strong. He had accomplished his goal, and now he was the highest flying bird in the sky!

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Ann. She was very hopeful and excited but also a little bit nervous about her first day at school.

On the way to school, Ann went past a mysterious shop. She couldn't help but be curious and so she opened the door and went inside.
 
Inside, Ann saw lots of magical things - sparkly gems, feathers and things she'd never seen before. But best of all was the big, blue box in the corner. 

Ann was so excited that she opened the box and inside, there was a beautiful sight! It was a golden object with a handle - it was a polishing wand!

Ann took the wand and began to polish the magical gems and feathers around the shop. She was so busy that she forgot all about going to school! 

When the shopkeeper appeared, he was very pleased with all the hard work Ann had done. He gave her a big smile and thanked her for her help.

Ann went on her way, feeling very proud and happy after her magical day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Ben and Jack. Ben loved to bounce and Jack loved to mix things. One day, they decided to have a day of play. Ben and Jack took turns, Ben bouncing and Jack mixing.  

But while they were playing, they accidentally broke their parents' mixer. Ben and Jack were so scared and they ran away, not knowing what to do. 

A nice lady in the neighbourhood saw that the boys were scared and very sorry. She said to them: "Boys, be careful next time. Sometimes things can break when we are playing so we must be careful."

Ben and Jack looked at each other and nodded. They decided to go back home and clean up the mess they made. 

The boys knew that from then on they were always going to be careful when playing, so nothing like this would happen again. 

Moral of the story: Be careful when playing so you don't make a mess!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was so excited because it was her birthday! All of her friends were there and they had cakes, candy and presents.

But Sarah was feeling sad. She wanted to play with the other kids but she felt too heavy.

"What's wrong Sarah?", her Mom asked.

"I'm too big", she replied.

Her Mom hugged her. "That's ok Sarah. You can still play. You can try to move your body - it will help make you feel lighter," she said with a smile.

Sarah was excited! She started wiggling her arms and legs and soon she was running around and laughing with the other kids. She felt so light and happy.

The party was so much fun and Sarah was thrilled that she was able to join in. She was no longer sad - she was happy and full of excitement!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy said, "Let's have a picnic in the park!" Lily was very happy and said, "Yay! I love picnics!" 

When they got to the park, they found a nice spot to sit and eat. But then, a big bird came and stole their sandwiches! Lily's mommy said, "That bird is so stupid!" 

Lily laughed and said, "Silly bird! You can't have our picnic!" They decided to share some fruit instead and had a great time together. When they were done, Lily said, "Can we come back to the park and have another picnic soon?" Her mommy said, "Of course, we can have picnics whenever we want!"

Once upon a time, Benny was walking through the forest. He looked around and saw all sorts of things. Then suddenly, he spotted a mushroom. It was so big and round and it was a very strange color. He got closer, and then he noticed something. The mushroom was very dirty. Benny started to stare at it. He was so curious and wanted to know more about the mushroom.

He touched it, and the mushroom felt all squishy. He poked it, and the mushroom wobbled. Benny had so much fun discovering the mushroom. He wanted to stay and play longer, but he heard his mom calling him and so he said goodbye.

On his way home, Benny kept thinking about the mushroom. He wondered why it was so dirty and why it felt so squishy. He hoped to come back soon and learn more about the mysterious mushroom.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Sam and Sally. They arrived at a creek. It was a very fun place. The creek was flowing and they could see the sun in the sky.

Sam was curious and wanted to explore. Sally said "Let's go look around and see what we can find!"

They ran up and down the creek bank. They saw rocks and leaves, and they heard birds singing. They crossed a bridge and looked into the water. 

Sam said, "I see a fish! He's so cute!" Sally asked, "What kind of fish do you think it is?"

They watched the fish swim by. Suddenly, Sally said, "Look! I see a turtle swimming over there!" 

They were both so happy. They stayed at the creek for hours until it was time to go. 

Sally said, "What a fun day! Let's come back soon." 
And so, they said goodbye to the creek, until next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals so much! One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a beautiful dove. The dove was white and had pretty feathers. Lily thought the dove was sweet.

Lily wanted to show her mom the dove, so she pointed and said, "Look, mommy! Pretty bird!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, that's a dove. It's very pretty." Lily was so happy to see the dove.

Later that day, Lily went to her friend's house and saw a big TV. Her friend's mom said, "We can display pictures on this TV!" Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she was excited to see pictures. They looked at pictures of animals and Lily saw a picture of a sweet dove. She said, "Look, my mommy and I saw a dove today! It was so pretty!"

One day, a bunny named Bob met a new friend named Tim. Tim was a very unusual bunny because he had a big blue spot on his ear. Bob wanted to introduce Tim to his other friends. They all liked to eat carrots together.

Bob said, "Tim, let's go meet my friends and eat some carrots." Tim was a little scared because he thought the other bunnies might not like his blue spot. But he went with Bob anyway. They found a big pile of carrots to share with their friends.

When they got to the other bunnies, one of them said, "Hey, what's that on your ear, Tim?" Tim felt sad and scared. But then Bob said, "That's his blue spot. It makes him special!" All the bunnies agreed and they all ate carrots together, happy to have a new friend like Tim.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who was very adventurous. One day, he packed his things up, and left home to go on an adventure.

He walked for many days and ended up at a camp. The camp was filled with other adventurous people who were also looking for a new adventure. The boy was so excited to be there!

He explored around the camp and made new friends. They all had a great time playing and having fun together.

One day, the boy decided to go out and look for even more adventure. So, he packed his sack and started walking again. He was excited to see what new adventures he would find!

One day, a black cat named Sam went to play with his friend, a dog named Max. They wanted to go on a trip to the big park. So, they had to pack their toys in a big bag. Sam brought his ball, and Max brought his bone.

On their way to the park, Sam saw a cut on Max's leg. "Oh no, Max! You have a cut on your leg!" said Sam. Max looked at his leg and said, "It's okay, Sam. It doesn't hurt too much. Let's keep going to the park."

When they got to the park, they played with their toys and had a lot of fun. Max forgot about his cut, and Sam helped him feel better. They played until the sun went down, and then they went back home. They were happy they packed their toys and had a great day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a small cub and his name was Ben. Ben was always curious and he wanted to peek around. One day, he decided to peek inside a cave. As he looked into the cave, he saw a lion inside! He was very scared, but the lion was very big and hot.

"Please don't be scared," said the lion. "I won't hurt you. I'm just here to help you." 

Ben was a little bit relieved, but he was still scared. He wanted to run away and hide. 

"I understand," said the lion. "Let me give you some advice. Always think before you peek. If something looks scary then it may be too dangerous to take a look."

The lion got up and vanished into the forest. Ben was very relieved, but also sad that the lion had gone. He thought about what the lion had said and decided that he would always think before he peeked. 

The moral of the story is that it's ok to be curious, but always be careful and think before you peek!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her gems. She had a lot of them, but they were all mixed up and not organized.

One day, Lily's mom came into her room and said, "Lily, we need to seat your gems in a nice box so they don't get lost." Lily was happy and said, "Okay, Mommy!"

Together, they found a pretty box and put all of the gems inside. Lily was so happy that her gems were now organized and safe. She hugged her mommy and said, "Thank you, Mommy!"

Once upon a time there was a man and a girl. The man and girl both loved to laugh.

One day, they wanted to make some dough. So they mixed and stirred to make the dough.

The man cut out the dough and put it in the oven. Then he went outside and waited. 

Soon the man started to get angry because the dough was taking too long to bake! He yelled and shouted and stomped. 

But then, the man heard a laugh. He looked and saw the girl, laughing and smiling. She had taken out the dough from the oven and it was so yummy!

The man was so happy that he started laughing too. They both laughed and laughed and it made them so happy!

Bobby and his Mommy went to the park. Bobby was so excited to go outside and have a picnic! He wanted to bring his toy dog too, so that he could play with it in the park.

Bobby and his Mommy packed their picnic bags and headed to the park. When they arrived, there was a big park guard standing at the gate. 

"Good morning, everyone!" said the park guard. "Welcome to the park!"

"Thank you!" said Bobby's Mommy.

Bobby and his Mommy walked through the gate with their picnic bags. They had a successful picnic in the park and played lots of fun games with Bobby's toy dog. 

When it was time to leave, the park guard said goodbye. 

"Goodbye, everyone!" said the park guard. "Have a wonderful day!"

Bobby and his Mommy waved goodbye and walked away, smiling.  Bobby had a successful day in the park with lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a wild laundry basket. It always wanted to go on an adventure. One day, it decided to take a trip.

It went to the river and enjoyed the sunshine. Then, it heard a noise. It was a bear! The bear was playing in the river and splashing around. The laundry basket tried to scoot away, but the bear saw it.

The bear said, "Little one, why are you so shy? Come sit with me!" So the laundry basket hopped into the river and sat next to the bear. They had lots of fun playing in the river together. 

The laundry basket hopped out of the water and said goodbye to the bear. Then, it headed home feeling very happy. It decided to go on more wild adventures in the future.

One day, in a garden, a lily appeared. It was very yellow and beautiful. All of the other plants were jealous. They wanted to be as beautiful as the lily.

The lily blossomed and grew taller. Soon, it had many petals. It made the garden look so much better.

The birds saw the lily and sang about it. They sang for hours and hours. All of the animals in the garden stopped to listen.

The lily stood tall and proud in its bright yellow. Everyone in the garden admired it. It was a very special lily.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat on the sea. The boat had a big anchor to keep it safe. The boat had a tough captain who always said, "I will never let anything destroy my boat!"

One day, a big storm came and the waves were very high. The boat went up and down and the anchor was not strong enough. The boat started to move towards the rocks. The captain said, "We need to do something or the boat will be destroyed!"

The sailors tried to fix the anchor, but it was too late. The boat crashed into the rocks and it was destroyed. The captain and the sailors were very sad. The captain said, "I should have been more careful with my boat and my anchor."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Nora. She was so excited because she was going to the market that day with her mom. When Nora got to the market, she saw the vendor with all the different kinds of candy. She started to yell with joy and ran over to the vendor. Her mom smiled and told her that she could pick one. Nora thought for a minute and then chose a big, sweet lollipop. She was so happy that she couldn't help but yell even louder. The vendor laughed and said, "what a happy girl!" Nora thanked him for the sweet lollipop, and then went off to explore the market with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help with the dishes. Lily was happy to help, but she was too weak to carry the big dish. 

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, you can rub the dish with this sponge." 

Lily took the sponge and started to rub the dish. She rubbed and rubbed until the dish was clean. 

Lily's mom was proud of her and said, "You did a great job, Lily! Now, let's put the dish away." 

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Mommy!" and they put the clean dish away together.

Once there was a man called Steve who had a truck. He loved his truck very much. Everyday he would take it out and drive around the town.

One day, he had to load something very large and heavy. He was very troubled, because the truck had no sides! He didn't know how he was going to load this large item.

But then he had an idea! He bought some wood and built sides around the back part of his truck. Now he had a big space to load the large item.

He was so happy! After he loaded the item, he drove around town with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to climb. One day, he decided to climb to the top of a mountain to get a better view. When he reached the peak, he saw a lake below him. It looked so inviting, so he decided to climb back down to the lake.

As soon as the boy got to the lake, he noticed a boat on the shore. He asked the boat, "Are you available?" The boat replied, "Yes, I am available for you to use." The boy was so excited! He couldn't wait to jump into the boat and go for a ride on the lake. 

The boy took the boat out on the lake and had a wonderful time. But when he finished his ride, he noticed a sign near the shore. It said, "Take care of the boat; treat it with respect". The boy realized that it was not just available, it had been given to him to use with respect. 

The moral of the story is that when given something, it should be treated with gratitude and respect. We should never take things for granted.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Timmy. Timmy lived in a big ocean with his family and friends. One day, Timmy went for a walk on the beach. He saw a shiny shell and picked it up. Suddenly, he stumbled and fell down.

"Are you okay?" asked a friendly seagull.

"Yes, I'm okay," Timmy said as he stood up and dusted himself off.

"That was a modest stumble," said the seagull with a chuckle.

Timmy smiled and continued his walk on the beach, holding onto his new shell tightly.

Once upon a time, there was a fit bunny. Every day, the bunny would go for a run. After running, the bunny liked to rest. One day, when the bunny stopped to rest, he spotted a strawberry. It was big and red, and it looked yummy.
The bunny was excited! He hopped over to the strawberry and took a big bite. The strawberry was so sweet and delicious! The bunny ate the whole strawberry.
Afterwards, the bunny felt full and happy. He was even more fit after eating the strawberry! He hopped around and then he found a nice grassy spot to rest. The bunny snuggled into the grass and fell asleep. He had a long, restful nap. 
The bunny woke up feeling happy and refreshed. He hopped away and enjoyed the rest of his day!

Once upon a time, there was a humble fisherman. He went out to sea each day, in his little blue boat. He loved nothing more than feeling the cool breeze on his face.

One day, he cast his line and he felt a tug. He pulled hard, and out of the deep dark sea came a beautiful surprise - a pink and orange fish that glowed! It lit up the night sky, like a star. 

The humble fisherman was so happy. He had never seen anything like it before. He held up the glowing fish and named it Lucky, before putting it back in the sea. 

From that day on, the humble fisherman made sure to remember Lucky each time he set off to fish. As long as Lucky kept glowing, the fisherman knew he was safe.

One day Mum and Dad took their daughter, Anna, to the east side of town. Anna was so excited - it was her first time in that part of town.

"Look, Anna," said Mum. "Look at all the pink flowers."

Anna gasped. She had never seen so many flowers in one place. They were so pretty!

Then Dad said, "I want to teach you something, Anna."

"What can you teach me, Daddy?" asked Anna.

"I'm going to teach you which flowers are the prettiest ones," Dad replied.

At first Anna didn't understand, but Dad said, "You have to look carefully and decide which flowers are the prettiest. Can you do that?"

Anna looked carefully at all the pink flowers. After a few moments she said, "I think these pink ones are the prettiest ones, Daddy!"

Mum and Dad smiled. Dad said, "You did a great job, Anna!"

Anna smiled and said, "Can we come back here again soon?"

Mum and Dad nodded and said, "Yes, let's come back soon!" 
 Anna was so happy. She had learned something new and seen something beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big bow in her hair that she loved to wear every day. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and played on the swings. But when she got off the swing, she noticed her bow was missing! She looked everywhere for it but couldn't find it.

Lily was sad because her bow was her favorite. Her mom promised to buy her a new one, but Lily wasn't sure if it would be as pretty or reliable as her old one. She didn't want it to spoil easily like some of her other bows.

The next day, Lily's mom surprised her with a new bow. It was just as pretty as her old one and Lily was so happy! She put it in her hair and played all day without worrying about it spoiling. Lily realized that even though her old bow was gone, she could still find joy in new things.

Once upon a time, there was a pink princess who loved to ride her horse. Her horse was very fast and could speed through the forest. One day, while they were riding, they saw a big fire in the distance. The princess was scared and asked her horse what they should do. 

The horse said, "Don't worry, I can speed us away from the fire." So they rode as fast as they could, and soon they were far away from the fire. The princess was so happy that her horse was so fast and thanked him for keeping her safe. 

From then on, whenever they went for a ride, the princess would tell her horse to speed up and they would race through the forest, feeling the wind in their hair. They were the best of friends and always had fun together.

Once upon a time there was a small bird called Sam. He was very hungry so he flew to the park to search for something to feed on. He saw a square shaped pizza on the grass. He flew down and pecked at it.

Suddenly, a fast moving mouse came running. It took the pizza and ran away. Sam was so angry. He shouted at the mouse, "Why did you take my food?"

The mouse replied, "I am so sorry, but I am very hungry too. Please feed me instead."

Sam thought for a moment and then looked around and saw some seeds on the ground. He picked them up and said, "Here, eat these. Maybe next time we can share?".

The mouse smiled and said, "Thank you". They shared the seeds and then went their separate ways. From then on, every time Sam went to the park, the mouse was there waiting to share with him.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a lot of fog in the air. They cannot see very far.

"Wow, look at the fog!" Sara says. "It is like a big cloud on the ground."

"Let's pretend we are famous explorers," Tom says. "We can go on an adventure in the fog."

"OK, but we need to prepare first," Sara says. "We need a map, a compass, and a flashlight."

They go to Sara's house and find the things they need. They draw a map of their neighborhood on a piece of paper. They put the compass and the flashlight in their backpacks.

"Are you ready?" Tom asks.

"Yes, let's go!" Sara says.

They walk out of the door and into the fog. They follow their map and use their compass to find their way. They see different things in the fog. They see a tree, a car, a dog, and a mailbox.

"Look, there is a big castle!" Tom says, pointing to a house.

"Wow, maybe there is a king or a queen inside," Sara says.

They go closer to the house and knock on the door. A lady opens the door and smiles.

"Hello, who are you?" she asks.

"We are famous explorers," Tom says. "We are on an adventure in the fog."

"How nice," the lady says. "Do you want to come in for some cookies and milk?"

"Yes, please," Sara and Tom say.

They go inside the house and eat some cookies and milk. They tell the lady about their adventure. The lady tells them stories about the house and the people who live there.

They have a lot of fun. They forget about the fog. They make a new friend.

One day, John and his mommy went to the park. It was so huge! John saw a big truck and he asked his mommy what it was doing. His mommy said, "That truck is loading the park with wood chips to cover the ground."

John was so excited so he ran over to the truck and asked the driver if he could see inside. The driver said sure and showed John inside. There were many big, brown bags filled with wood chips. John thought the truck was so cool and he asked the driver how he loaded all the bags into the back of the truck.

The driver explained, "I use a crane to lift the bags and put them into the truck. It's not easy, but it's a lot of fun!" John thanked the driver for showing him the truck and he hurried back over to his mommy.

John said, "Mommy, that truck was so cool! I learned how to load wood chips into the back of the truck with a crane. Can we go to the park more often so I can watch the truck load the wood chips?"

Mommy said, "Of course, John! Let's come back next week and watch the truck load the wood chips again. It will be fun!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack. He was three years old and very curious. One day he had a surprise! He went to get the post, and found a big package on the doormat.

He was so excited that he shouted, "Wow!" He opened it and saw lots of fun, colourful toys. But then he started to slip and fall. The package tumbled down the stairs, and all the toys spilled out and got dirty.

Jack started to cry, but then his mum came in to help. She saw the package rolling down and knew what had happened. She told Jack, "It's ok, don't worry."

She hugged him, and then picked up all the toys. She gave them a quick wash and wiped away all the dirt.

Jack was so pleased. He said, "Thanks mum, for cleaning all my toys. I won't let them slip down the stairs again!"

Once upon a time there was a big elephant who lived in the jungle. He had a trunk that was very impressive! One day the elephant was walking around the jungle when he spotted something shiny in the dirt. He used his trunk to pick it up and hold it.

The elephant was surprised to see it was a golden key. He decided to see what it opened. He used his trunk to look around and eventually found an old chest. He used the key to unlock it and opened the chest.

Inside the chest was the most beautiful thing he had ever seen! It was a crown made of flowers and sparkles. The elephant was so impressed with it that he decided he wanted to wear it.

So the elephant put the crown on his head and walked around the jungle proudly. All of the other animals were so amazed to see the impressive crown he was wearing! From then on, they all thought the elephant was so special, and they all held him in very high regard.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lola who loved playing in the park. She especially loved to wear her unique sweater. It was made of soft, fuzzy material that was warm and snuggly.

One day, one of her friends grabbed her sweater and ran off with it. Lola tried to chase him, but he was too fast. She was very sad.

With great sadness, Lola went home. She asked her parents if they could help her get her sweater back. Her parents said yes, and off they all went in the car.

After a while, they arrived at her friend's house and knocked on the door. Her friend's mom answered and said that he had gone to the park. Lola and her parents drove back to the park.

They searched everywhere but couldn't find her sweater. Just when Lola started to give up hope, she heard a familiar, soft sound nearby. It was her unique sweater! Her friend had hung it on the fence, making sure she would find it later. Lola was so happy.

She hugged her sweater tightly and thanked her parents, before they all returned home. From then on, Lola was extra careful with her unique sweater.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called George. He was three years old and one day he wanted to make a drink. He went to the kitchen and he saw his mom's big, messy freezer. He wanted to get something out of it to make his drink.

He opened the freezer door and saw many different things inside. He saw delicious ice creams and yummy popsicles. He also saw special juice boxes. He quickly grabbed one and put it in the freezer again.

George was so excited to make his drink. He quickly opened the juice box and put it in a cup. Then he put the cup in the microwave to warm it. After a few minutes, the drink was ready.

He took a sip and it was yummy. He had made the perfect drink for himself. He was so proud!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat snacks like cookies and crackers. One day, she asked her mom for a snack, but her mom said no because it was almost dinner time. Lily was sad.

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can test a new snack after dinner. But be careful, it might be harsh."

Lily was excited to try a new snack. After dinner, her mom gave her a piece of fruit to try. Lily took a bite and said, "Yum! This snack is not harsh, it's delicious!"

Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. Maybe we can try more new snacks tomorrow."

Once there was a girl named Lily. Lily felt uncomfortable because she had no friends. One day, a big event was happening in the town. Everyone was going, but Lily was still stuck at home.

Then, a sparkly fairy came out of nowhere. She said "I can restore your happiness!" She waved her magic wand and instantly, Lily was at the event. 

Lily was so excited to be with all the other kids. They played games, ate snacks, and made friends. Lily was so happy that she stayed at the event until it was dark. 

The fairy smiled and said "I'm glad I can restore your happiness". Then the fairy flew away. 

Lily smiled and waved goodbye. She felt so happy that she had so many new friends. She knew the fairy had helped her to be happy again.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have a big box of gems. The gems are shiny and pretty. They have red, blue, green, and yellow gems.

One night, Sara and Ben are getting ready for sleep. They brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. They each pick a gem to keep by their bed. Sara picks a red gem and Ben picks a blue gem. They say good night to their mom and dad and go to their room.

But Ben is not happy. He wants the red gem, not the blue gem. He thinks the red gem is more shiny and pretty. He waits until Sara is asleep. Then he sneaks to her bed and takes the red gem. He puts the blue gem in its place. He goes back to his bed and smiles. He hugs the red gem and falls asleep.

In the morning, Sara wakes up and sees the blue gem by her bed. She is upset. She knows Ben took her red gem. She runs to his bed and sees the red gem in his arms. She tries to take it back, but Ben wakes up and holds it tight.

"Give me back my red gem!" Sara says.

"No, it's mine now!" Ben says.

They start to fight over the gem. They pull and tug and yell. Their mom and dad hear the noise and come to their room. They see Sara and Ben fighting over the gem.

"What's going on here?" their mom says.

"Ben took my red gem!" Sara says.

"No, I didn't! I found it!" Ben says.

Their dad picks up the gem and looks at it. He sees a small sticker on it. The sticker has a letter S on it.

"This is Sara's gem," he says. "It has her initial on it. Ben, you should not take things that are not yours. That's not nice."

Ben feels bad. He knows he did something wrong. He gives the red gem back to Sara. He says he is sorry.

Sara feels happy. She gets her red gem back. She says she forgives Ben. She gives him a hug.

Their mom and dad smile. They tell Sara and Ben to share their gems and play nicely. They give them each a kiss and a hug. They say they love them.

Sara and Ben say they love them too. They put their gems back in the box. They decide to play with them together. They are not upset anymore. They are happy.

Once there lived a little girl named Callie. She was very gifted; she could already count up to 20 at only three years old!

One day, Callie heard her Mommy and Daddy talking about a big surprise. Callie didn't know what it would be, but she was very excited.

The next day, Callie and her parents went on a special picnic. Callie couldn't wait to see what the surprise was!

When the family arrived at the beach, her Daddy showed Callie an oyster. He opened it for her and inside was the most beautiful shell! Callie was so happy that she jumped for joy!

Callie's family enjoyed their picnic and Callie proudly displayed her shell for everyone to see. From then on, Callie never forgot the wonderful surprise her Daddy showed her that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big box. In the box, he had many grapes. He liked to keep them organized. He put the green grapes on one side and the purple grapes on the other side. Tim loved his grapes very much.

One day, Tim's friend Sam came to play. Sam saw the box and asked, "Can I have a grape?" Tim said, "No, I own all these grapes. They are mine." Sam felt sad but he still wanted to play with Tim.

They played with toys and had fun. But Sam still wanted a grape. When Tim was not looking, Sam took a grape from the box. He ate it very fast. Tim saw him and got very mad. He yelled, "You took my grape!" Tim did not want to be friends with Sam anymore. Sam went home feeling sad, and Tim was left alone with his grapes.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore her backyard. One day, she found a beautiful butterfly flying around. 

"Hi butterfly!" said Lily. "What are you doing?"

"I'm looking for a flower to land on," said the butterfly. "I learned that flowers have sweet nectar that I can drink."

"Wow, you're so smart!" said Lily. "I wish I could learn things like you."

"Well, you can!" said the butterfly. "If you explore and ask questions, you'll learn lots of new things. And maybe one day, you'll win a prize for all the things you've learned."

Lily smiled and thanked the butterfly for the advice. She continued to explore and learn new things every day, hoping that one day she would win a prize for all her hard work.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they found a hose and started to play with it. They sprayed water everywhere and laughed. But then, Timmy's friend Billy started to tease him. Billy said that Timmy's shoes were too big and he looked silly. Timmy felt sad and wanted to go home.

But then, Timmy had a creative idea. He picked up the hose and sprayed Billy with water. Billy laughed and they all started to play together again. Timmy realized that sometimes, teasing can hurt someone's feelings, but being creative can make things better. From then on, they had fun playing with the hose and no one teased anyone else. The end.

Once there was a driver. She enjoyed taking long car rides. But one day, she started to feel very restless on her journey. She began to rub her hands together and even her legs, too! But no matter how long she rubbed, she still felt the restlessness inside. 

She kept going, telling herself that the relaxation would soon come, but it still didn't. Then she had an idea. She pulled over to the side and went for a walk in the sunshine. The warmth was so soothing and the birds were singing and she finally felt a little better. 

She kept walking and took in the scenery and felt her restlessness fading away. Feeling peaceful, she made her way back to the car, ready to continue her journey. 

The driver felt so much better now that she had taken those few minutes to rub, walk, and just be. What a difference it made!

Once upon a time there was a black driver. He had a very important job. He would drive his car around and keep people safe when they needed help. Every day he would get into his car and start his journey around the town. He would drive from place to place making sure all the people were ok.

One day, the driver was going for a special drive. There were very important people in the back of the car. He was careful to keep them safe as he weaved his way through the busy streets. He managed to get them to where they needed to go without any trouble.

At the end of the day, the driver looked very tired, but he had done a great job. He had kept the important people safe and had stayed alert during his drive. The people were very thankful and gave the driver a big hug when they thanked him before they left.

The driver smiled and waved goodbye as he drove off. He was already thinking about his next journey, but this time he was convinced that it would be even better.
