While they were waiting for the dress to dry, they played with Timmy's toys. They had so much fun that Lily forgot all about slipping and getting her dress dirty. When the dress was dry, Lily put it back on and she felt happy again. She said, "Thank you, Timmy. You're a good friend."

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with equipment in the park. They have a slide, a swing, a seesaw and a climbing frame. They test the equipment every day. They want to see who is faster, higher, and stronger.

One day, they see a new equipment in the park. It is a big net. It is made of ropes. It looks like a spider web. Tom and Mia are curious. They want to test the net. They run to the net and climb on it.

The net is fun. It is bouncy and wobbly. Tom and Mia laugh and shout. They try to reach the top of the net. They test their balance and strength. They are strong. They can hold on to the ropes.

But then, the net starts to shake. It is not because of Tom and Mia. It is because of a big dog. The dog is chasing a ball. The ball rolls under the net. The dog follows the ball. The dog jumps on the net.

Tom and Mia are scared. The net is not strong enough for the dog. The net makes a loud noise. It breaks. Tom and Mia fall to the ground. They are not hurt. They are just dirty and sad. The dog runs away with the ball.

Tom and Mia look at the broken net. They are sorry. They did not mean to break the equipment. They go to find the park keeper. They want to tell him what happened. They hope he can fix the net. They want to test it again.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big log. They want to walk on it.

"Let's balance on the log," Sara says. "It will be fun."

"OK," Ben says. "But be careful. The log is high and wobbly."

They take turns to balance on the log. They try not to fall off. They laugh and cheer each other.

Sara is very good at balancing. She can walk all the way to the end of the log. Ben is not so good. He wobbles and slips. He falls off the log.

"Ouch!" Ben says. "That hurt."

"I'm sorry, Ben," Sara says. "Are you OK?"

"Yes, I'm OK," Ben says. "But you win. You are better at balancing than me."

Sara smiles. She is happy to win. But she is also a loyal friend. She does not want Ben to feel sad.

"Thank you, Ben," Sara says. "But you are good at other things. You are good at running and jumping and singing. You are my best friend."

Ben smiles too. He is glad to have Sara as his friend. He does not mind losing. He hugs Sara.

"You are my best friend too," Ben says. "Let's play something else."

They leave the log and run to the swings. They play and have fun. They are happy and loyal friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom decided to have a tea party in their garden. They brought out their favorite tea cups and a big pot of tea. Suddenly, it started to rain! 

Lily asked her mom, "What do we do now?" Her mom replied, "Let's move our tea party under the big tree. It will keep us dry." 

When they moved under the tree, they noticed that the rain had spoiled their cookies. "Oh no!" cried Lily. "Our cookies are all wet and mushy now." 

But Lily's mom had an idea. "Let's make a new batch of cookies and enjoy them with our tea once the rain stops." And that's exactly what they did. They had a lovely time together, sipping their tea and enjoying their fresh cookies.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He loved to go out on his boat, so one sunny day, he did just that. The sailor moved his boat around the lake, and all around he could see, the birds flying and the fish swimming. He was having lots of fun.

Suddenly, the wind began to blow. The sailor was so excited! The wind meant that he could spread the big sail and go faster. So he did. He spread the sail out, and soon the boat was sailing fast around the lake.

The sailor clapped with joy. He was having the best time ever! But then, the wind died down. The sailor was impatient for it to come back. He clapped and asked the sky for more wind.

Finally, the wind came back, and the sailor continued to sail around the lake. He was so happy and never wanted the day to end.

Once there was a girl who liked to explore dark places. She was very brave. She decided to explore a nearby cave, so she got a flashlight. She brought the flashlight with her and planned to explore the cave.

But the cave was very dark. She needed more light, so she asked her brother for help. He had a much brighter flashlight, so she took it.

She entered the cave, with the bright flashlight. She shined it all around the cave and saw all sorts of interesting things. But then something stupid happened - she dropped the flashlight and it broke. Now she was very sad because she couldn't explore anymore.

But then she remembered that she still had her first flashlight. She quickly found it and it still worked. She was so happy and she used her first flashlight to finish exploring the cave. It wasn't as bright as the other one, but it finally worked.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Mona and Sam. They were best buddies and always wanted to go on adventures together. One day they decided to explore a wild forest near by.

The forest was full of new and exciting things to discover. As they were walking, they suddenly heard an ugly noise coming from a bush. They were both startled and scared of what it could be. 

Mona grabbed Sam's hand and said, "Let's go find out what it is". Sam said, "No, it might happen something bad!" But Mona was brave, so she said, "Come on! I'm sure it will be ok!" 

They both crept carefully up to the bush and to their surprise, it was just a hurt rabbit! It had a twisted foot and looked very unhappy. 

Sam and Mona quickly helped the rabbit. They filled a box with some soft grass and took it home. The rabbit stayed with them for a week and eventually its foot got better. 

Sam and Mona learned an important lesson from their adventure. They realized that even when things that look wild and ugly, they have the potential to be filled with kindness and love.

Once upon a time, there was a knight called Sir Lancelot. He was brave, strong and very kind. One mild morning, he was taking a walk in the park when he heard a noise. He looked around, but he could not tell what was causing it. Suddenly, a dragon appeared and disturbed the peace. Sir Lancelot was ready to fight and quickly grabbed his sword.

The dragon looked very fierce, but Sir Lancelot didn't give up. He bravely held up his sword and yelled at the dragon: "Leave the park or I'll have to use my sword!"

The dragon looked confused and scared. It seemed so scared that it quickly flew away. Everyone cheered for Sir Lancelot and thanked him for saving the park. From then on he was known for his bravery and mild manner.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very eager to go to space and visit a planet. One day, he asked his mom, "Can we fly to a planet?" His mom replied, "Sure, let's go!"

Timmy and his mom went to the airport and got on a spaceship. The spaceship flew high into the sky and into space. Timmy looked out the window and saw lots of stars and planets. He was so happy!

When they landed on a planet, Timmy saw lots of aliens. He said, "Hi aliens, my name is Timmy. Do you want to play with me?" The aliens said, "Yes, let's play!" Timmy and the aliens played games and had lots of fun.

After a while, Timmy's mom said it was time to go back home. Timmy said goodbye to the aliens and got back on the spaceship. He looked out the window as they flew back to Earth. Timmy was happy because he got to fly to a planet and play with aliens. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty rock. It was big and strong. But one day, something strange happened - the rock started to go. It rolled down the hill, faster and faster.

All the animals were surprised and ran away. Even the birds flew up high into the sky. Everyone was so scared!

But when the rock reached the bottom, nothing happened. It just stopped. So everyone came back and looked at the rock.

The mighty rock still stood tall and strong. Everyone was happy and cheered and hugged each other. The rock had gone, but it still protected them.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a girl named Lily. She loved tea very much. Every day, she would drink tea with her mom and dad. They would sit and laugh together. They were a very happy family.

One day, a big, fearful bird saw Lily's tea. The bird wanted the tea for itself. So, when Lily was not looking, the bird flew down and stole her tea. Lily was very sad. She did not know what to do. Her mom and dad told her not to be sad, but Lily missed her tea.

The next day, Lily saw the bird again. She told the bird that stealing was bad. The bird felt sorry and gave the tea back to Lily. From that day on, the bird never stole again. Lily, her mom, and her dad were happy again. They learned that it was important to be kind and not to steal from others.

Once upon a time, there was a nation of people. They lived together, but they sometimes quarreled with each other. One day a little girl named Alice noticed that the nation was not happy. She wanted them to get along, so she decided to share her special gifts with everyone. 

Alice had a wagon full of toys and snacks. She gave away her favorite things to all of her friends and family. She also spoiled her own little pet puppy with treats. 

The nation of people saw how Alice was spreading joy and smiles, and they realized that they could do the same. Instead of quarreling, they started doing nice things for each other. Soon, the nation was a much better place. 

Alice was happy to see that her simple act of kindness had made a big difference. She was glad that all the people in the nation were now happy and getting along with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She liked to play outside with her dog, Spot. They had fun running and playing in the sun. One day, Lucy saw something unusual in the sky. It was a big, shiny star. She never saw a star like this before.

Lucy believed that the star could talk. So, she asked the star what it was doing there. The star said, "I am here to tell you about a special time." Lucy was very excited to know about this special time. The star told her that the special time was when all the animals could talk and play together.

Lucy wanted to see this special time. The star told her to close her eyes and believe. When she opened her eyes, she saw all the animals talking and playing together. Lucy and Spot joined in the fun too. They played with the animals until it was time to go home. Lucy thanked the star for showing her the special time. From that day, Lucy always believed in the magic of the unusual star.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. They liked to walk in the park. The little girl had a tea set and she liked to have tea parties with her mommy. One day, the mommy said to the little girl, "Let's walk to the store and get some tea." The little girl put on her fit shoes and they walked to the store. They got some tea and went home to have a tea party. They had so much fun!

Once upon a time, there was a man with a big, hairy beard. He loved to design things with his hands. One day, he decided to make an axe. He worked hard on it for many days until it was perfect.

The man was so happy with his axe that he decided to show it to his friend. But on the way, he tripped and fell. The axe flew out of his hands and hit his friend. His friend was hurt very badly and had to go to the hospital.

The man felt very sad and guilty. He realized that he should have been more careful with his axe. From that day on, he never designed anything dangerous again.

One day, in the dark night, a cow happened to be out in the meadow. She was having lots of fun playing. She ran around in the grass and made happy noises. Suddenly, something dark happened. She jumped and looked around to find out what it was. She saw a scary looking shadow! The shadow moved and made a noise. The cow was scared and ran away. She hopped over the fence and ran all the way home. The shadow was gone and the cow was safe. She went back to the meadow the next day and had lots of fun again.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, Nemo saw a shiny purse at the bottom of the sea. He was curious and wanted to know what was inside the purse. So, he got ready and took a deep breath. He dived into the water and swam towards the purse. When he reached the purse, he opened it and found a shiny pearl. Nemo was so happy and swam back to his home with the pearl. From that day on, Nemo would dive into the sea every day, looking for more treasures.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went on a vacation with his family. They went to a big park with lots of trees, flowers, and a big lake. Tim was very happy to play with his ball and run around.

One day, while Tim was playing, he did a stumble on a rock. He fell down and his ball rolled far away. Tim felt a little guilty because he didn't look where he was going. He got up and looked for his ball.

Tim found his ball near a big tree. He was very happy to find it. He hugged the ball and promised to be more careful. Then, he went back to play with his family, having lots of fun on their vacation.

Once upon a time, there was a fat dog named Max. Max loved to walk in the park with his owner, Sarah. One day, Sarah forgot to bring a towel to dry Max after he played in the water fountain.

Max looked at Sarah and said, "Woof woof, I am wet. Can we go home now?"

Sarah replied, "Not yet, Max. We need to walk a little bit more."

As they continued to walk, Max saw a pile of towels on the bench. He ran over and grabbed one with his mouth.

Sarah was surprised and said, "Good boy, Max! That towel will come in handy."

Max wagged his tail and felt proud that he could help. From that day on, Sarah never forgot to bring a towel for Max when they went to the park.

Once in a season, the sun began to glow. It glowed brighter and brighter until it lit up the sky.

"Oh wow!" said a little boy as he saw the sun. "It's so bright!"

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it's a very normal thing. The sun glows every day."

The boy grinned and said, "But it's really really really special today!"

His mom laughed and said, "Yes, it's special today, because the sun glows in all kinds of different colors. Look closely, and you'll see the colors!"

The boy gasped and said, "Really? I can see colors in the sun?" He watched closely, and sure enough, he could see colors like yellow, orange, and red in the sun's glow.

"That's so cool!" the boy said.

His mom smiled and said, "Yes, it sure is. The sun glows in all kinds of colors every single season."

The boy smiled and said, "I love it when the sun glows!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. One day, her mummy gave her a string. Lucy was very happy. She loved to play with the string. She moved it from side to side, making different shapes. Sadly, the string broke. Lucy was sad. She pouted and frowned.

Mummy gave Lucy some glue. She showed Lucy how to use it and also gave her a paintbrush. Together they glued the string back together. When the glue and string were dry, Lucy showed her mummy the new string. It was shiny and fixed.

Lucy was happy again. She thanked her mummy and put the string away safely. Her mummy was pleased that Lucy had fixed her broken string.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim. He loved to go outside and play with his friends. They would run and jump all day.

One day, Tim saw a big ball near his waist. He picked it up and wanted to play with it. He called his friends to come and play with him. They all came running and were very happy.

They played with the ball all day long. Tim would throw it and his friends would catch it. The young friends had so much fun. When it was time to go home, they all said goodbye and went to their houses. Tim was happy he found the ball and could play with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a strong bug named Spike. Spike had a special power. He could glow in the dark! Spike loved to play with his friends at night.

One night, Spike and his friends were playing in the park. A big, mean bird saw them. The bird wanted to catch Spike and his friends. Spike was scared, but he knew he had to help his friends.

Spike used his glow to make a bright light. The bird was scared of the light and flew away. Spike and his friends were safe. They were so happy that Spike was strong and brave. From that day on, they played together every night, and Spike's glow always kept them safe.

Once upon a time there was a big tree by the side of the road. Near the tree lived a little girl called Julia. Every day, Julia wished she could fly up to the branches of the tree and feel the sun's warmth on her face.

One spring day, Julia noticed a few birds nesting in the tree's branches. She was very excited and ran to tell her mom. Her mom said that if Julia was patient, a wish might just come true. 

Sure enough, the next day the wind blew softly and suddenly the little birds began to fly. Julia watched in amazement as the birds flew high into the sky. But then one of the birds flew towards her, almost as if it were coming to say hello! 

The little bird landed on Julia's hand and she could feel its tiny feet tickling her. It was such a magical moment and Julia made a wish that she would be able to fly one day too. 

The little bird flew away and Julia's patience was rewarded when she found a pair of wings at her feet. Julia put on her wings and suddenly she was able to fly! From that moment on, she soared up to the tree's branches every spring and made special wishes.

Once upon a time there was a little duck. It was a happy duck who liked to splash in the pond. Then one day, it saw something shiny on the water - it was a big, ugly print. The print was big and ugly and the duck was scared.

But it didn't stay scared for too long. It remembered how much fun it had splashing in the pond. So it took a deep breath and it bravely jumped into the water. As soon as it did, it made a big splash that made the ugly print go away. It couldn't believe it had been so brave.

The little duck was very happy now. It had been brave and the ugly print was gone. And it could splash whenever it wanted. So the little duck splashed and splashed and splashed in the pond, and it stayed happy forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside near the river. One day, Lily saw a big raft floating down the river. It looked so fun to play on! 

But Lily didn't have a raft of her own. She asked her friend if she could borrow their raft. Her friend said yes and Lily was so happy! 

Lily got on the raft and it was very comfortable. She floated down the river and saw so many pretty things. When she was done, she returned the raft to her friend and said thank you. 

From that day on, Lily loved borrowing things from her friends and going on adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots, but one day he tried a radish. He didn't like it! Benny's friend, a mouse named Molly, disagreed with him. She said radishes were tasty. Benny thought Molly was being silly.

Benny decided to be creative and try the radish in a different way. He chopped it up and put it in a salad with his favorite carrots. To his surprise, he loved it! Benny was happy he tried something new and learned to not disagree with his friend so quickly.

From that day on, Benny and Molly would try new foods together and never disagreed again. They were happy to be friends who could be creative in the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat ice cream with a spoon. One day, she went to the ice cream shop with her mom. 

Lily asked the lady behind the counter, "Can I have a regular scoop of ice cream, please?" The lady smiled and gave her a big scoop of vanilla ice cream on a cone. 

Lily was so happy and started to eat her ice cream with a spoon. Suddenly, she dropped her spoon on the ground. She looked up at her mom and said, "Mommy, can you please raise me up so I can get my spoon?" 

Her mom lifted her up and Lily picked up her spoon. She continued to eat her ice cream with a big smile on her face. "This is the best day ever," she said to her mom.

Anna liked to learn new things. She liked to learn how to read, how to draw, how to sing. She also liked to learn about flowers. She liked to smell them, to touch them, to look at them. She liked all kinds of flowers, but her favorite was the rose. She thought the rose was the most pretty flower in the world.

One day, Anna went to the park with her mom. She saw a big rose bush with many roses. She ran to the rose bush and wanted to pick one. She reached out her hand and grabbed a rose. But she felt a sharp pain in her finger. She cried out loud and let go of the rose. She looked at her finger and saw a drop of blood. She had pricked herself on a thorn.

Her mom came to her and hugged her. She said, "Anna, are you okay? What happened?" Anna showed her mom her finger and said, "I wanted to pick a rose, but it hurt me. Why did it hurt me?" Her mom said, "The rose has thorns to protect itself from animals and people who want to hurt it or take it away. The rose is pretty, but it is also strong. You have to be careful when you touch it. You have to ask before you pick it. You have to respect it."

Anna nodded and said, "I'm sorry, rose. I didn't mean to hurt you. I just wanted to have you. You are so pretty." Her mom said, "It's okay, Anna. The rose will forgive you. But you have to learn from this. You have to learn that not everything that is pretty is easy to have. You have to learn that some things have to stay where they are. You have to learn that you can admire them, but you can't always take them."

Anna said, "I understand, mom. I learned something new today. I learned to be careful and respectful with flowers. I learned that the rose is pretty and strong." Her mom said, "That's good, Anna. I'm proud of you. You are a smart and kind girl. Now let's go and wash your finger and put a band-aid on it." Anna said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you." Her mom said, "I love you too, Anna." They walked away from the rose bush, holding hands and smiling.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a favorite pair of pants. They were blue and had little stars on them. He wore them every day and loved them very much.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. While he was playing, he heard a noise in the bushes. He went to investigate and found a little bird with a broken wing. Timmy knew he had to help the bird, so he picked it up gently and brought it home.

When Timmy got home, he asked his mom for a box to put the bird in. She gave him a little box and Timmy made a cozy bed for the bird with some of his old pants. The bird felt safe and warm in its new little home.

The next day, Timmy went back to the park to play with his friends. He was happy knowing that the little bird was safe and warm in its little bed made of pants. And he knew that he would always be there to help little creatures in need.

Once upon a time, there was a very quiet hoop. Every day, the hoop would sit in the playground, waiting for someone to play with. But no one ever came.

One day, the hoop sighed. â€œWhy am I not getting used?â€ they said.

Just then, a little girl came running into the playground. Her name was Mary. She saw the hoop and her eyes lit up. She picked up the hoop and ran around the playground with it.

Mary said, â€œThis is so much fun! We can play hoop games all day!â€

The hoop gave a happy sigh. They were so glad to finally have someone to play with. From then on, Mary and the hoop would play together in the playground every day.

Once upon a time, there was a furry rabbit named Peep. He lived in a small hut on the top of a hill. Peep was always looking for something special, but he never knew what it was.

One day, he decided to leave his small home and find out. He hopped through a dark forest until he reached a beautiful meadow. In the middle of the meadow, he found the most wonderful thing - peace.

He kneeled down and he felt so happy. He was so excited that he wanted to tell everyone what he had found. For the first time, Peep had gained something really special.

He hopped around the meadow, telling all of his friends what he had found. They were so excited for Peep and his new found peace.

Now Peep lives happily in his small hut, knowing that he has gained something truly special. He enjoys his peace and shows it to everyone who visits his small home.

Once upon a time, a clumsy bear and a gentle rabbit met in a forest. Both were sad, as it was raining. Bear said to Rabbit, "I hurt my friend. Will you help me forgive him? Rabbit thought for a moment and said, "Yes, but it won't be easy."

So, Bear and Rabbit set off together, jumping over puddles and splashing in the rain. They soon reached Bear's friend, who was sad too. Bear said sorry and the friend smiled. Rabbit said, "It takes courage to forgive." 

Bear felt much better and the friend hugged both of them. After a while, the rain stopped, and Bear and Rabbit said goodbye to their friend. They promised to always be there for each other, even when it rained. 

And so, Bear and Rabbit found true friendship, in the rain.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, it was very wet outside. Lucy put on her boots and jumped in the puddles. She was having so much fun!

Lucy's mom took a photo of her playing. She wanted to show Lucy how happy she looked. But Lucy didn't want to leave the puddles. She wanted to play more and more. Her mom said, "Okay, just a little longer."

Finally, Lucy was ready to leave the wet outside. She came in and looked at the photo her mom took. She smiled big and said, "I love the rain!" Lucy and her mom hugged and laughed. They had a great, wet day together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. Jack liked wearing nice clothes and shoes. One day he wanted to wear his special pair of boots for a walk.

He got his boots out of the wardrobe and tried to put them on. But the boots were too tight and Jack couldn't fit them on his feet.

He was very sad but then he remembered that he had a nice new pair of shoes given to him by his aunt. He took the shoes out of the box and tried them on. He was so happy as they fit on his feet perfectly.

Jack put on his shoes and his nice coat and was ready for his walk. He was so proud of his nice shoes and boots and went outside smiling. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go to the park to play with her friends. She asked her mom, "Can we go to the park now?" Her mom said, "Yes, we can go now."

When they arrived at the park, there was a long line for the swings. Lily felt frustrated because she really wanted to swing. She asked her mom, "Why is there a long line?" Her mom explained, "There are many kids who also want to swing. We need to wait our turn."

Lily learned that sometimes we need to wait in line and be patient. She also learned that feeling frustrated is okay, but we should not give up or be mean to others. In the end, Lily had fun playing with her friends and waiting for her turn on the swings.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear named Benny. He loved to eat waffles for breakfast every day. One morning, when Benny woke up, he demanded his waffles right away. But his mom told him to wait a little bit because she was making them fresh.

Benny didn't want to wait, so he went outside to play with his friends. They played tag and hide-and-seek until Benny's mom called him in for breakfast. When Benny saw the waffles, he was so happy! He ate them all up and felt very full.

After breakfast, Benny and his friends went to the park to play some more. They had so much fun together and were very friendly to each other. Benny was grateful for his friends and his yummy waffles.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He had bright happy eyes and loved to explore.

One day, Jack decided to go on an adventure. He climbed to the top of a big hill and looked around. He saw a yummy looking lake of hot cocoa. It was all warm and smelled so good.

Jack bent down and wanted to try the cocoa, but he had to be careful. He wanted to make sure he had just the right balance of sweet and sour. He tasted the cocoa and it was just perfect.

As he enjoyed the cocoa, Jack thought about the balance he had achieved. Sweet and sour. He smiled contentedly, knowing that he had done a good job.

Jack finished his adventure and went home. He told everyone about the balance of sweet and sour he had discovered in the cocoa. Everyone loved the story and was so proud of Jack.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only 3 years old. Every day, Lucy enjoyed going to the park with her parents to play.

One day, after a lot of running around and playing in the park, Lucy began to feel really tired. She decided to sit down and take a nap. 

Her parents started to worry, so they gently woke her up. When Lucy opened her eyes, she started to display serious worry as she saw a big tree in front of her.

Lucy: "Oh no! The tree is going to fall on me!"
Her parents smiled and hugged her.

Mum: "Don't worry Lucy, the tree isn't going anywhere."
Dad: "That's right. Trees don't suddenly move or fall. Everything is ok."

Lucy smiled and hugged her parents. She felt reassured and went back to playing in the park all day.

Jim was sad. He had been playing in the park all day and he was really tired. He sat down on the bench and started to complain. He said that the park was too dirty and he didn't like it.

Suddenly, a message floated down from the sky. It said "Hey Jim, why don't you come to the beach? It's clean and beautiful." Jim was excited and jumped up from the bench.

He ran all the way, but when he arrived at the beach, it was just as dirty as the park had been. Jim was even more angry than before and he started to complain again. He said "This beach is just as dirty as the park!"

But then he heard another message coming down from the sky. It said "Jim, just look around. There is so much beauty everywhere! See, there's a pretty tree, some birds and a nice big ocean. Everywhere you look there is love and beauty, you just have to see it!"

Jim looked around and he saw the beauty everywhere. He smiled and he knew that he had been wrong to complain about the dirty park and beach. From then on, he looked for beauty everywhere.

Once upon a time, there was a horse. He was very heavy. He liked to travel far and wide. Every day, his owners would remind him to stay safe and not wander too far away. 

One day, the horse got so excited despite his heavy legs and he ran off away from his owners. He ran and ran and ran, until he reached a meadow. The grass was so green and soft. He decided to stay a while. 

The owners were worried but they didn't know what happened to the horse. They searched for days and days until one day, they remembered the meadow. They went to the meadow and found the horse grazing peacefully. 

From then on, his owners would remind him to be careful when playing and always stay close. He also reminded himself to always stay close to his owners, so he could continue to enjoy his freedom.

Anna was a very special little girl. She loved to go to school every day, to learn new things. Today, her teacher said something special. She told the class, "today, I'm going to teach you about a special place called a hospital".

Anna was very curious and asked, "what is a hospital?". Her teacher smiled and said, "a hospital is a place where people go when they don't feel well. Doctors and nurses work there to help people get better".

Anna smiled and said, "I want to go to a hospital someday". Her teacher said, "maybe you will. Let's find out".

The next day, Anna and her teacher went to a hospital. It was very big and all of the walls were white. Anna was so excited and wanted to see everything.

In the hospital, she saw lots of doctors and nurses. They were all busy helping patients. Anna learned that hospitals were places to help people get better. She was so happy to have learned something new!

Once upon a time there was a gray mouse. The mouse really wanted to stay in his cozy hole, but he just couldn't stay there forever. He wanted to explore the world! 

The mouse asked his mom if he could go outside. She said "yes, but only if you promise to come back in a few hours." She gave him a permit to go out and explore.

The mouse was thrilled. He had never been allowed to go outside by himself before. He walked and walked, and saw so many interesting things. But he always remembered the promise he had made to his mom, so he eventually came back home.

His mom was very happy to see him back safe and sound. She said "My brave little mouse! You were allowed out today but always remember to abide by my rules and get a permit before you go exploring again!â€ The mouse nodded and snuggled into his cozy hole to stay.

Once there was a large tree in a meadow. It was so tall, it touched the clouds. Every day, the tree would lean against the wind. One day, the wind was especially strong and the tree had to lean very hard. To keep itself from falling, it spread its roots even deeper into the ground. In the end, the result of the tree's efforts was that it was even sturdier and taller than before. The meadow was now filled with its large branches. Everyone who saw the tree was amazed and they knew that it would never fall down.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. One day, Daisy's mommy and daddy took her to a special place. She looked around and saw many different things. She saw people eating, laughing and playing.

Daisy turned to her mommy and said, "What are we doing here?" Her mommy smiled and said, "We are here for a surprise!" Daisy's eyes lit up and she clapped her hands.

Then, Mommy and Daddy opened the door and Daisy saw that it was full of rice! She was so happy! She shouted, "Rice! Rice!" Then, she jumped up and down, clapping her hands.

Mommy and Daddy showed Daisy how to take a handful of rice and put it into her bucket. She did as they said, but she wasn't sure what to do next. But then, Mommy and Daddy had an idea. They showed Daisy how to make a big clear mountain with her rice!

Daisy was so proud of her mountain, and Mommy and Daddy clapped and said how wonderful it was. Daisy smiled and shrugged, glad that she had done something that made everyone happy.

Once, there was a mighty oak tree. Its knobby branches and leaves made it look like a strong king. But one day, something strange happened.

The mighty oak tree started to shake. The leaves rustled and the branches quivered. It was just like the tree had an idea!

"What are you thinking?" asked a curious girl.

The tree only shrugged.

The girl said, "Let's play a game. I'll pick something off the ground and you show me what it is."

The tree shrugged again.

The girl picked up a tiny stone and showed it to the mighty oak.
The tree shook its leaves and branches. It was like the oak wanted to say something!

The girl asked "What is it?"
The tree shook more and said, "I'm a rock!"

The girl clapped and shouted, "You're so clever, mighty oak!" She hugged the trunk and thanked it for the fun game.

The tree nodded, its leaves rustling in the wind. The mighty oak was happy.

Lily was lonely. She had no friends to play with. She liked to look at bugs and flowers, but they did not talk to her. She wished she had someone to talk to and hug.

One day, she saw a spider on a leaf. It had eight legs and many eyes. It was black and shiny. Lily thought it was pretty. She wanted to touch it. She reached out her finger and poked the spider.

The spider did not like that. It felt a sharp pain on its back. It was scared and angry. It turned around and bit Lily's finger. Lily felt a sharp pain on her finger. She cried out loud.

Lily's mom heard her cry. She ran to her and saw the spider and the bite. She picked up Lily and hugged her. She took her inside and put some ice on her finger. She told her not to poke spiders, because they can hurt her.

Lily was sorry. She did not mean to hurt the spider. She just wanted to be its friend. She learned a lesson. She decided to look for other friends who liked to play and talk. She hoped the spider was okay. She was not lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved dressing up in her costume and pretending to be a princess. One day, she wanted to send a letter to her grandma, so she asked her mom to help her mail it. 

But the letter didn't arrive at her grandma's house. Lily was sad and wanted to know why. She asked her mom if they could go check the mailbox again. Her mom said they already checked it, but Lily was persistent and kept asking to go back. 

Finally, they went to the mailbox again and found the letter stuck in the back. Lily was so happy that her letter was finally on its way to her grandma. From that day on, Lily made sure to always double-check the mailbox when she mailed something important.

Tom and Lily are brother and sister. They like to play in the garden. They have a big tree with a swing. They take turns to push each other on the swing.

One day, Mom says, "It is time for breakfast. Come inside and eat your oat." Tom and Lily are eager to eat. They love oat. It is warm and sweet and makes them strong.

They run inside and sit at the table. Mom gives them each a bowl of oat. She says, "Do you want some fruit to go with your oat? I have banana, apple and grape."

Tom says, "I want banana, please." He likes banana. It is yellow and soft and easy to peel.

Lily says, "I want apple, please." She likes apple. It is red and crunchy and juicy.

Mom says, "And what about grape? Do you want some grape, too?"

Tom and Lily look at each other. They have never tried grape before. They are curious. They say, "Yes, please. We want to try grape."

Mom smiles and says, "Okay, then. I will include some grape in your oat. Here you go. Enjoy your breakfast."

Tom and Lily say, "Thank you, Mom." They spoon some oat and fruit into their mouths. They taste the grape. It is purple and round and sweet. They like it. They say, "Mmm, grape is yummy. We like grape."

Mom says, "I'm glad you like it. Grape is good for you. It has vitamins and water and fiber."

Tom and Lily nod and eat more oat and fruit. They are happy. They have a good breakfast. They are ready to play in the garden again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kate. She had two ears and she could hear lots of things. One day, there was a big change -- the noise in her house was different. It was louder and more difficult to ignore.

She was scared and didn't know what to do. She tried to cover her ears with her hands to make the noise softer, but it wasn't enough. Then her mom came in and she showed Kate some funny looking ear muffs. They were brightly coloured and had a soft furry inside. 

Kate put the ear muffs on and she could hardly hear the noise anymore! She was really happy! Now it was easier to play and her ears were safe from loud sounds. 

Kate realised it was sometimes difficult to change, but the ear muffs made her house a quieter and safer place. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy robot. It was his favorite toy. One day, Timmy was playing outside when he saw a big, scary dog. The dog barked at Timmy and he started to shiver.

Timmy learned that even though the robot was just a toy, it was still brave and could protect him. He also learned that sometimes things that seem scary can be harmless. From then on, Timmy always played with his robot by his side, knowing that it would always protect him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had an enormous teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Lily was playing with her teddy bear and accidentally dropped it. It fell on her finger and it hurt a lot. 

Lily's mom came to her and asked, "What happened, sweetie?" 

Lily replied, "My teddy bear fell on my finger and it hurts." 

Mom kissed her finger and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. But remember, we should always be careful with our toys and our fingers." 

Lily learned her lesson and promised to be more careful. From that day on, she always made sure to hold her toys tightly and keep her fingers safe.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who grew big, red radishes. He loved to plant them in his garden every year. One day, he found an ancient seed that he had never seen before. He decided to plant it and see what would happen.

After a few days, a small plant grew from the ancient seed. The farmer took care of it every day, watering it and giving it sunlight. Finally, the plant grew into a big, beautiful radish. The farmer was so happy that he completed his collection of radishes.

He took the ancient radish to the county fair and won a blue ribbon for the biggest and most beautiful radish. The farmer was very proud and he knew that his hard work paid off. From that day on, he always looked for ancient seeds to plant in his garden.

Once upon a time there was a bunny. He wanted to have the most expensive mushroom in the world. It looked so big and yummy! So he hopped over to the store to buy it. But when he looked at the price tag he felt sad. The mushroom was too expensive! The bunny was very sad. He was so angry he threw the expensive mushroom away. 

But then he saw a small wild mushroom near his feet. He picked it up and ate it. It tasted so yummy! The bunny realized that the most expensive things in life aren't always the best things. 

So the bunny learned a lesson that day. He learned that sometimes it's better to look around for something special and free! So be sure to appreciate the little things in life and stop to smell the mushrooms.

Once upon a time there was a smart car that liked to zoom around town. It zoomed fast, faster than any other car on the road. One day, the smart car ran out of oil. Without that special oil, the car couldn't zoom.

Once there was a little girl who loved to try new things. She had a frame that her grandpa had given her. Every day she would spend hours looking at it.

Once upon a time there was a gifted girl named Sally. Sally always loved to watch the birds flutter in her backyard. She especially admired the bright yellow canary that would come to her window every morning.

As Sally was admiring the birds one morning, she noticed something reflecting in the bushes. She ran over to investigate and found something remarkable - a silver watch!

Once there was a girl named Jill. She was three years old. Every day she liked to dress up in her favourite clothes.

Jack was feeling a bit sad. He wanted some wine but he didn't have any. He walked up to a store and asked the shopkeeper, "Do you have any wine?"

The shopkeeper counted out two bottles of wine and handed them to Jack. Jack thanked the shopkeeper and went home.

Lily was a fearful girl. She did not like loud noises, big dogs, or new places. She liked to stay at home with her mom and dad and play with her dolls. But today was her birthday, and her mom and dad had a surprise for her. They said they were going to a party with her friends from school.

Lily did not want to go to a party. She was afraid of the other kids, who might laugh at her or take her toys. She was afraid of the balloons, which might pop and make a loud bang. She was afraid of the cake, which might have nuts or raisins that she did not like. She cried and begged her mom and dad to let her stay at home, but they said no. They said the party would be fun and that she would have a good time.

They put her in the car and drove to the party. Lily hid her face in her mom's lap and hoped the party would be over soon. When they arrived, she saw a big sign that said "Happy Birthday Lily!" and a lot of kids running and playing in the yard. She also saw a big slide, a bounce house, and a clown. She felt even more fearful and clung to her mom's hand.

"Look, Lily, there's your friend Sam!" her dad said, pointing to a boy who waved at her. "He's waiting for you to play with him. Why don't you go and say hi?"

Lily shook her head and buried her face in her mom's shoulder. She did not want to play with Sam or anyone else. She wanted to go home.

"Come on, Lily, don't be shy," her mom said, gently nudging her. "Sam is a nice boy. He has a present for you. See, he's holding a big box with a bow. Maybe it's something you like."

Lily peeked at the box and felt a little curious. She wondered what was inside. She liked presents. Maybe Sam was not so bad after all. She let go of her mom's hand and walked slowly towards Sam.

"Hi, Lily, happy birthday!" Sam said, smiling. "I have a present for you. Do you want to open it?"

Lily nodded and took the box from Sam. She tore off the paper and opened the lid. Inside was a big, fluffy, pink ball. Lily gasped and smiled. She loved balls. She hugged the ball and thanked Sam.

"Do you want to play with me?" Sam asked. "We can roll the ball, or bounce it, or throw it. It's fun!"

Lily nodded again and followed Sam to the yard. They rolled the ball, bounced it, and threw it. They laughed and had fun. Lily forgot about her fears and enjoyed the party. She made new friends, ate cake, and slid down the slide. She even let the clown make her a balloon animal. She was not fearful anymore. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet dog named Max. Max loved to play outside in the yard, but one day he ran away. Lily looked for him everywhere, but she couldn't find him.

John was in his room. He was three years old. He was wearing his warm cap. John got up from his seat and decided to go outside.

Once upon a time there was a little seal named Sandy. She loved to swim in the ocean and explore far away places. One day, while Sandy was exploring the underwater caves, she found a secret room! The door to the room said "open", so she opened it and saw a big golden box inside.

Sarah was very enthusiastic about bath time. She grabbed her favourite rubber duck, her rubber boat and jumped into the bathtub. She quickly filled up the bathtub with water and loved to see the bubbles.

Sara was a princess who loved her crown. She wore it every day and never took it off. She liked how it sparkled and shone on her head. She thought it made her look pretty and special.

One day, she went to play with her friend Ben, who was a prince. They had fun running, jumping, and sliding in the garden. But Sara did not notice that her crown was getting dirty. It had mud, grass, and bugs on it. Ben saw it and said, "Sara, your crown is not clean. It is icky and yucky. You should wash it."

Sara was angry and sad. She said, "No, I don't want to wash it. It is my crown and I like it. It is not icky and yucky. It is pretty and special. You are mean and rude. Go away!" She ran away from Ben and hid behind a tree.

Ben was sorry and sad. He did not mean to hurt Sara. He just wanted to help her. He said, "Sara, please come out. I am not mean and rude. I am your friend. I care about you and your crown. I know it is pretty and special. But it will be more pretty and special if it is clean. It will sparkle and shine more. And it will not have mud, grass, and bugs on it. That is not good for your crown or your head. Please let me help you wash it."

Sara heard Ben and felt sorry and sad too. She realized that he was right. Her crown was not clean. It was icky and yucky. And that was not good for her crown or her head. She came out from behind the tree and said, "Ben, I am sorry. You are not mean and rude. You are my friend. You care about me and my crown. You are right. It will be more pretty and special if it is clean. It will sparkle and shine more. And it will not have mud, grass, and bugs on it. That is good for my crown and my head. Please help me wash it."

Ben smiled and said, "Sara, I am glad. You are my friend. I care about you and your crown. Come on, let's go wash it." They went to the fountain and washed the crown. It became clean and shiny again. Sara put it back on her head and said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. I am happy." Ben said, "You are welcome, Sara. You are a good friend too. I am happy." They hugged and played some more.

The moral of the story is: Don't worry about your things getting dirty. You can always clean them. And don't be angry or rude to your friends who want to help you. They care about you and your things. Be thankful and kind to them. They will make you happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big basket of laundry on their neighbor's porch. The laundry looked soft and colorful. Tom had an idea.

"Let's steal some of the laundry and make a fort!" he said to Lily.

Lily was scared. She knew stealing was bad. But Tom was her brother and she wanted to have fun. So she nodded and followed him.

They ran to the porch and grabbed some clothes. They ran back to their yard and piled them up. They crawled inside and pretended they were in a castle.

But they did not see the neighbor come out of his house. He was a big man with a rough voice. He saw his laundry was gone and he was angry. He followed the trail of clothes to Tom and Lily's yard. He shouted at them.

"Hey, you little thieves! Give me back my laundry! How dare you take what is not yours!"

Tom and Lily were terrified. They came out of the fort and dropped the clothes. They tried to say sorry, but the neighbor did not listen. He grabbed them by their arms and dragged them to their house. He knocked on the door and told their mom what they did.

Their mom was shocked and ashamed. She scolded Tom and Lily and made them apologize to the neighbor. She also made them do extra chores and took away their toys. Tom and Lily cried and wished they had never stolen the laundry.

The moral of the story is: stealing is wrong and it will get you in trouble. You should respect other people's things and be honest.
