Before the girl left, she gave the dog one last squeeze. The dog was a bit sad to see her go. 

But the girl promised she would come back and play with him again. And he could look forward to that.

Once, there was a mum and a dad and their son Danny. Danny was only three and was already full of curiosity. Dad was very busy with his work and mum was keeping the house clean. One day, Danny asked his Dad why he was so busy with work. 

"Dad, why do you work so much?,"Danny asked.

Dad looked at Danny with a smile and said," Because, I have to work and bring home money so that you can get the things you need.

Danny nodded understandingly and forgot all about it after a while.

Soon, it was Danny's birthday and Dad gave Danny a very special present. Danny was so glad. 

"Oh thank you Dad!," Danny said, beaming. Since Dad had been so busy with his work, Danny had been worried he might forget his birthday.

Dad smiled again and said, "See how important work is - it gives us the things we need. But don't forget that the most important thing is spending time with your family." 
 
Danny smiled and nodded, glad to have such a wonderful Dad. 

Moral of the story: Work is important, but it's even more important to spend time with your family.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet little boy who loved to explore the garden. One day, he saw something shiny in the grass. It was a spell. He was so excited. He wanted to take it home.

But when he tried to pick it up, it suddenly vanished. He looked all around for it, but it was gone. He was sad, but he kept exploring the garden.

He went around the corner and saw a rabbit. It was holding the spell in its paws. But before the little boy could take it, the rabbit vanished.

The little boy was so sad! Where had the spell gone? He looked all around, but the spell was gone. The little boy was so quiet. He didn't know what to do.

But then suddenly, the spell reappeared. It flew back into the little boy's hands. He was so happy and ran back home with the spell.

He was never sure what caused the spell to vanish and reappear. But ever since, the little boy kept the spell safe in his pocket and never let it vanish again.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little rabbit named Remy. Remy lived in a small tunnel with his family. He loved to play with his friends, but he was too shy to ask them to play with him.

One sunny day, Remy saw a big carrot near his tunnel. He wanted to share the carrot with his friends, but he was too shy to ask. So, Remy thought of a plan. He would leave the carrot outside his tunnel and wait for his friends to find it.

Remy's friends, a squirrel and a bird, saw the carrot and were very happy. They said, "Wow, look at this big carrot! Let's share it with our friend Remy!" They went to Remy's tunnel and called out, "Remy, come out and share this big carrot with us!"

Remy came out of his tunnel and was so happy to see his friends. They all shared the big carrot and had a wonderful time. From that day on, Remy was not shy anymore. He learned that sharing with friends was fun and it made him very happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and swing. They saw a stream with water that sparkled in the sun. They wanted to go near it and splash.

"Look, Lily, a stream!" Ben said. "Can we go there?"

"Yes, let's go!" Lily said. "But we have to be careful. Mommy said not to go too close to the water."

They ran to the stream and saw some white stones and some fish. They picked up some stones and threw them in the water. They made a big splash and laughed.

"Look, Ben, a white fish!" Lily said. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben said. "It reminds me of the white cat we saw at the pet shop. Do you remember?"

"Yes, I do!" Lily said. "It was so soft and fluffy. I wanted to pet it, but Daddy said no."

They watched the white fish swim away. They heard Mommy calling them.

"Lily, Ben, it's time to go home!" Mommy said. "Come on, let's go!"

"OK, Mommy!" Lily and Ben said. They ran to Mommy and gave her a hug. They told her about the stream and the white fish.

"That sounds like fun!" Mommy said. "But you have to be careful around water, OK?"

"OK, Mommy!" Lily and Ben said. They got in the car and went home. They were happy and tired. They dreamed of the stream and the white fish.

Once upon a time there was a red balloon. It was full of air and loved to fly high in the sky. But one day, it wanted to try something new. So, it decided to twist and turn and go on an escape.

The balloon flew above the tall buildings of the town, twisting and turning and feeling so brave. Suddenly, the balloon noticed a fierce wind blowing - it was getting hard to stay in the air. The balloon twisted and turned, trying to stay up, and it realized the only way to escape was down!

The balloon landed in the park, where a little boy was playing. He saw the red balloon and smiled so much at the sight. He picked up the red balloon and hugged it tight. The balloon had made an amazing escape and found its new best friend!

Once, there was a little girl who loved to play the flute. She would put on her pretty dress and run to the park, her favorite spot to perform.

One day, she was playing her flute, when she heard a strange noise. She saw a pale cat stuck in a bush. She quickly put down her flute and ran to rescue the cat.

The girl stuck her arm in the bush, and the cat jumped out, into her arms. She said to the cat, "Are you ok?" The cat purred and rubbed against her neck.

The little girl was so happy to have rescued the cat. She hugged the cat and thanked it for joining her for a flute performance in the park. The cat meowed and seemed to understand. From then on, the little girl was never alone when she went to play her flute in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Furry. Furry loved to eat beans, but one day he ate too many and got a tummy ache. He decided to take a nap to feel better.

While Furry was sleeping, a big monster came and tried to take his favorite toy. Furry woke up and saw the monster. He was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. Furry stood up and said, "I surrender my toy to you."

The monster was surprised by Furry's bravery and kindness. He gave Furry back his toy and they became friends. From that day on, Furry learned to share his toys and not eat too many beans. The end.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big book on a bench. The book has many pictures and words. Sara and Tom want to read the book.

"Let's look at the book," Sara says. "Maybe it has a good story."

"OK," Tom says. "But we have to be careful. Maybe the book belongs to someone."

They open the book and see a story about a pale girl and a wolf. The girl has a red hat and a basket. The wolf has big teeth and a bad plan. Sara and Tom are scared, but they want to know what happens.

They read the story and see how the wolf tries to trick the girl. He pretends to be her grandma and waits for her in the bed. The girl is not fooled. She sees the wolf's ears, eyes, and teeth. She screams and runs away.

"Wow, that was a scary story," Tom says. "I'm glad the girl was smart and brave."

"Me too," Sara says. "But I feel sorry for the wolf. He must be hungry and lonely."

Sara and Tom close the book and put it back on the bench. They hope the owner will come back soon. They also hope the wolf will find a friend and some food. They do not want to bite anyone. They are nice.

Lily was a nosy girl. She liked to look at other people's things. One day, she saw a diary on her big sister's bed. She wanted to read it. She took the diary and opened it.

"Hey, that's mine!" her big sister, Anna, shouted. She ran into the room and grabbed the diary from Lily. "You can't read my diary, it's private!"

"But I want to know what you write," Lily said. "Why do you hide it?"

"Because it's none of your business," Anna said. "You are too little to understand. Now go away and play with your toys."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not like her big sister. She wanted to make her sorry. She saw a chew toy on the floor. It belonged to their dog, Spot. She had an idea. She took the chew toy and ran to the kitchen. She found some peanut butter and spread it on the chew toy. Then she went back to her sister's room and put the chew toy on the diary.

Soon, Spot smelled the peanut butter. He followed his nose to the diary. He saw the chew toy and licked it. He liked it. He started to chew it. He also chewed the diary. He tore the pages and made a mess.

Anna heard the noise and came back to her room. She saw Spot and the diary. She screamed. "No, Spot, stop! Bad dog! You ruined my diary!"

Lily heard the scream and smiled. She thought it was funny. She said, "Now you know how I feel. Maybe next time you will share with me."

Once upon a time, there was a port full of ships. On one of these ships, was a stubborn captain. He never wanted to pay for the port, he thought it was unfair. So each time he docked his ship, he would refuse to pay.

The port-keeper was very angry, he had to make the captain pay. So, he decided to make a plan. He was going to surprise the captain next time he docked his ship.

Sure enough, the next day, the captain arrived. He refused to pay as usual. But this time, the port-keeper was ready. He had made a big wall at the port. The captain could not get his ship in without paying.

The captain was so angry that he was stuck. He couldn't get his ship in without paying. Finally, after a few hours, he realized he had to pay if he wanted to get back out to sea. So, he finally paid and sailed away.

One day, Larry went to the store. He needed to get some lotion. His mom had told him lotion was a dependable thing to receive.

Larry was very excited. He ran to the lotion aisle and saw all kinds of different lotions. He looked at the bottles and read the directions.

Finally he found one that said it was dependable. He brought it to the register and paid for it. When he got back home, his mom hugged him and said, "Thank you for bringing me the lotion. You are very dependable."

Larry was very proud. He was happy to have received something his mom said was dependable. From then on, Larry always received lotion with a dependable attitude.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Joni. She was 3 years old and the bravest girl in the town. She was very brave and nothing ever frightened her. 

One day, Joni took a train to a far-away station. But when she arrived, she was very frightened. She had never been to a station before, so she had no idea what to do. 

She asked a man standing nearby for help. He laughed and told her that he would take her to her station. He said that he would applaud when she got off. 

So, Joni followed him to the station. When she got off the train, everyone applauded her bravery. Joni smiled proudly, feeling quite pleased with herself. 

From that day on, Joni was not frightened by stations anymore. Whenever she arrived at a station, she remembered how brave she was that day.

Once there was a little furry kitten. She was so tiny and cute that everyone wanted to hold her. One day she became curious and went off to explore. 

Soon, she came to a place with lots of tall grass. She decided to go in and play. Suddenly, she felt something sharp on her paw. It was a cut!

The little kitten was scared, but soon she saw something amazing. It was a big, furry rabbit! He had lots of soft fur and she wanted to snuggle up to him. The bunny saw the kitten's cut and used his paw to rub it gently. Suddenly the cut was all better!

The kitten was so happy and the bunny too. They became the best of friends and played together all the time. Whenever the kitten had a problem, she knew the bunny would always be there to make it better.

Once upon a time there was a boy with a reliable lamp. He liked to squeeze it and hold it tight. It made him feel safe.

The boy liked to carry the lamp with him wherever he went. He would bounce up and down looking at the stars in the sky. He was so happy and he laughed every time he bounced.

One night the boy was bouncing around on the grass outside when he saw a special star. He thought it was so special, so he laughed and said "That star looks really pretty!"

Then, suddenly, he heard some magical words.

"Oh boy, I am the star you are looking at. I will grant you one wish," said the star.

The boy was so excited and he said, "I wish that my lamp was always reliable and never ran out of light do I can show it to my friends!"

And with a sparkle, the lamp started to glow.

The boy was so happy with the wish and he thanked the star for making his wish come true. He hugged his lamp tight and he bounced around with joy! 

The End!

Once upon a time, there was a big, big hole in the ground. It was so big, it was a huge pit. One day, a little birdie fell into the pit and couldn't fly out. The birdie chirped and chirped, hoping someone would hear and reply. 

A little boy was walking by and heard the birdie's chirps. He looked down and saw the birdie in the pit. The boy wanted to help the birdie, but the pit was too deep for him to reach. He ran home to get his dad, who was very tall and could reach the bottom of the pit. 

The dad came back with the boy and they lowered a rope into the pit. The birdie climbed up the rope and flew away happily. The boy and his dad felt good for helping the birdie and went home with smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a helpful dancer named Lily. She loved to dance and show her friends all her fun moves. Lily was always happy and kind to everyone.

One day, Lily met a new friend named Tim. Tim was shy and didn't know how to dance. He said, "Lily, I want to dance like you, but I don't know how." Lily smiled and replied, "Don't worry, Tim! I will show you how to dance."

Lily and Tim spent the whole day dancing together. Lily showed Tim all her moves, and Tim tried his best to copy them. Soon, Tim was dancing just like Lily. They laughed and had so much fun. From that day on, Lily and Tim became best friends, and they danced together every day.

Tom and Sue were hungry. They wanted to eat steak for dinner. They asked their mom to cook steak for them. Mom said yes and went to the kitchen.

Tom and Sue waited in the living room. They saw a big steak on the table. It smelled good. They wanted to eat it now. They did not want to wait for mom.

"Let's eat the steak," Tom said to Sue. "Mom will not know."

"No, we have to wait for mom," Sue said to Tom. "She will be mad if we eat the steak."

But Tom did not listen to Sue. He ran to the table and grabbed the steak. He took a big bite. It was hot and juicy. He was glad.

Sue was scared. She saw mom coming back from the kitchen. She tried to stop Tom. But it was too late. Mom saw Tom eating the steak.

"Tom, what are you doing?" mom yelled. "You are very bad. You did not wait for me. You leave the steak alone. You go to your room. No dessert for you."

Tom was sad. He dropped the steak. He cried. He ran to his room. He was sorry.

Sue was sad too. She did not eat the steak. She did not get dessert either. She wished Tom had listened to her. She wished they had waited for mom. She was not glad.

Once upon a time there was a boy who liked to wander in the woods.
One day he set off, curious and excited to explore the unknown. As he looked around, the boy saw many harmless creatures, all enjoying their day in the sun. 
The boy was careful and stepped lightly, looking around him the whole time.
He stumbled across a meadow with the prettiest flowers he had ever seen. He could have stayed there all day. 
But soon, the wind started to blow and the boy decided it was time to go. He bid farewell to the birds and the butterflies and gracefully wandered back to his home.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She wanted a new blouse to wear to her friend's party. So, she went to the store with her mom. 

Lily saw many blouses, but none of them fit her. She said, "Mom, I can't find a blouse that fits me." 

Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will find a blouse that fits you perfectly." 

Finally, they found a pink blouse that fit Lily perfectly. She was so happy and said, "Mom, I love this blouse! Thank you for helping me find it."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was a very curious three-year-old who liked to explore. One day, she decided to go for a walk in the park.

On her way she saw a big hill. It looked fun, so Jane decided to take a few steps up it. It was easy, so she kept going and soon she was at the top!

Jane was so proud of herself. Just then she heard someone say, "Wow! You made it up here so quickly!"

Jane turned around and saw a tall man wearing a hat. She smiled and said, "Yes, I was going very fast!"

The man laughed and said, "You sure were! Great job!"

Jane thanked him and continued on her way. With a smile on her face, she knew she could do anything if she put her mind to it.

Once upon a time, there was a family. The family had a mom, a dad, and two kids. They loved spending time together and having fun.

One day, they decided to go on a picnic. They packed sandwiches, fruit, and juice. The mom said, "Let's bring a blanket to sit on." The dad said, "That's a perfect idea!"

They drove to a park and found a spot under a big tree. They laid out the blanket and ate their lunch. The kids played and ran around. It was a perfect day with their perfect family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. Joe loved to stay up late and watch his favourite video. One night, Joe stayed up late and he heard something lovely coming from outside. He looked out the window and saw a bright, twinkling light in the sky. Joe was so excited! He ran out to his garden to get a closer look. He saw lots of sparkles in the sky and it filled Joe with happiness. Joe watched as the wonderful colors filled the night sky. Joe felt so lucky to hear and see such a lovely sight. Joe smiled, thanked the stars and went back inside to watch his video.

Once there was a dry fire that no one could solve. It had been burning for days and no one could put it out. Everyone was scared and worried.

One day, a brave little girl named Bessie came up with a solution! She thought if she could find some water, she could put out the fire.

She searched and searched, but she couldn't find enough water to put out the dry fire. In frustration, she sat down and began to cry.

Suddenly, Bessie heard someone behind her. It was a friendly fire truck. The firefighters had been watching and decided to help Bessie solve the problem. They sprayed the fire with gallons and gallons of water, and soon the fire was out. Everyone cheered!

Bessie had solved the dry fire and made everyone proud.

One day, Tom found an enormous jar in his room. He was very excited to see what was inside. He tried to open the jar, but it was very tight. He asked his mom for help. "Mom, can you help me open this jar?" Tom said.

Mom came and helped Tom open the jar. Inside the jar, there were many colorful balls. Tom was very happy to see the balls. He wanted to play with them. He took the balls out of the jar and put them on the floor.

Tom's little sister, Lily, came into the room. She saw the balls on the floor and wanted to play too. Lily tried to peek into the jar to see if there were more balls inside. Tom and Lily played with the balls and had a lot of fun together. They laughed and threw the balls in the air. It was a great day for Tom and Lily.

Once upon a time there was an orange hose. The hose was very long and it snaked through the garden. Every day the hose would sit in the sun, but it would never move.

Suddenly one day a girl came by. She was very curious about the orange hose and she wanted to study it. She looked at the hose very closely and touched it carefully. It felt very cool.

The girl kept studying the hose. She looked very closely at all the details. She noticed that the hose had a lot of strange patterns on it. But she was not sure why the patterns were there.

The girl thought and thought, but she could not figure it out. Finally, she decided to take the hose home with her. She hoped that maybe if she could study it more at home, she could figure out what it was used for.

And so the girl took the orange hose home and continued to study it. She looked at it from every angle and at all the strange patterns on it.

The girl never did figure out why the hose had all those patterns, but she still enjoyed studying it. And every day she could still be found studying the orange hose, thinking about all the mysteries it contained.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very excited to go to the park for the very first time. When she got to the park, Sarah was amazed. She saw lots of special and unique things! Sarah looked around and saw some trees, a playground, and even some ducks playing in the pond.

But what Sarah liked best was the cardboard box. It was lying near the swings and Sarah wanted to have it all to herself. She picked up the box, tucked it under her arm, and carried it to a quiet spot in the park.

Sarah sat down in the box and started imagining all sorts of things. She pretended it was a house and she also pretended it was a car. Then Sarah found some sticks, rocks, and leaves. She began to create things with them inside the box. Sarah made a unique castle, a pond, and even a bridge.

Sarah had the best day at the park. She couldn't wait to go back and visit the cardboard box again.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the beach with her mom and dad. Lily loved the beach because she could play in the sand and find pretty shells. 

One day, Lily saw a crab walking fast on the sand. She ran over to it and said, "Hi Mr. Crab, why are you walking so fast?" The crab replied, "I'm trying to get back to my home in the ocean before the sun sets." 

Lily watched as the crab scurried away, and then she started to feel tired. She yawned and said to her parents, "I think it's time for me to take a nap." They found a shady spot for her to rest, and Lily fell asleep dreaming of the fast crab she had met on the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a polite little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toy cars and eat oats for breakfast. One day, Tim's mom gave him a big bag of oats to share with his friends.

Tim went to the park and saw his friend, Sally. He said, "Sally, do you want to split my oats with me?" Sally smiled and said, "Yes, Tim! I love oats too!" So, they sat down and split the oats into two piles.

As they ate their oats, a small bird came by. The bird looked hungry, so Tim and Sally decided to share some of their oats with the bird. The bird was very happy and flew away. Tim and Sally felt good about sharing and being polite to the bird. They played together all day and went home with big smiles on their faces.

Tim and Mia like to play in the woods. They find a creek with clear water and small fish. They take off their shoes and socks and put their feet in the water. It feels cold and nice.

"Look, Mia, I can catch a fish with my hands!" Tim says. He tries to grab a fish, but it swims away. He tries again and again, but he cannot catch any fish.

Mia laughs. "You are too slow, Tim. The fish are too fast. You need a net or a hook."

Tim does not like it when Mia laughs at him. He feels angry. He wants to catch a fish and show Mia. He looks around and sees a big stick. He thinks it is a good idea. He picks up the stick and swings it in the water. He makes big splashes and waves. He scares the fish away.

"Tim, stop it!" Mia says. "You are being rude. You are making the water dirty. You are hurting the fish. You are ruining our fun."

Tim does not stop. He swings the stick harder and harder. He does not care about Mia or the fish. He only cares about himself.

Suddenly, something appears behind Tim. It is a big frog. It is green and brown and has big eyes. It is angry too. It does not like it when Tim makes noise and mess in its home. It jumps on Tim's back and croaks loudly. It makes Tim drop the stick and scream.

"Help, Mia, help! There is a frog on me! It is biting me! It is slimy and gross!" Tim cries.

Mia sees the frog and laughs. She thinks it is funny. She does not help Tim. She says, "That is what you get, Tim. You are being rude. You are making the frog mad. You should say sorry to the frog and the fish."

Tim is scared and sorry. He says, "Sorry, frog, sorry, fish. I will not be rude again. I will be nice and gentle. Please, frog, get off me."

The frog hears Tim and croaks again. It jumps off Tim and goes back to the water. It swims away with the fish. It is happy.

Tim and Mia put on their shoes and socks and leave the creek. They go back to the woods. They are friends again. They learn a lesson. They will not be rude to the animals. They will be kind and respectful. They will have more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy who lived on a farm. Every day, she would help her mom and dad with the animals and the crops.

One day, her mom said, "Daisy, I need you to carry this corn to the market and sell it." Daisy smiled and said, "Ok!" She was excited, because she had never been to the market before.

Daisy carried the corn and started walking to the market. But, on the way, she met a farmer named Mr. Johnson. He was an ignorant farmer, so he asked Daisy, "Why are you carrying this corn?" 

Daisy smiled and said, "I'm taking it to the market to sell it. I help my parents on the farm." 

The farmer said, "Wow! That's great. I wish I could be like you and help my family too."

Daisy laughed, and said, "You can! I'm sure you know lots of things about farming that I don't!"

Mr. Johnson smiled and said, "You're right! Well, best of luck to you at the market!"

Daisy thanked him and continued walking to the market with the corn. When she arrived, she sold the corn and made a lot of money for her parents. 

The End.

Once there was a family. They were very excited one day because they had a visit. It was a special visit.

Suddenly, a fragile butterfly appeared in the garden. Everyone was amazed. The butterfly moved slowly and softly. They watched it carefully. They wanted it to stay.

But just as quickly as the butterfly had appeared, it flew away. Everyone was sad. But they were also happy to have seen such a beautiful thing.

They knew that they could always have a visit from the butterfly again.

Jake and Lucy were best friends. They liked to play games outside together. Today, they were playing a game of tag.

Suddenly, Jake had an idea. He said, "Let's play a new game. It's called 'Clubhouse'."

Lucy was excited. She said, "Yes, let's play it!"

They went to their secret clubhouse. Jake said, "Let's make some rules." They agreed to be polite and share all their toys. 

Next, Jake said it was time for the game to start. He said, "Let's take turns counting to ten." 

They both paused for a moment as they waited for one of them to start. Then, Lucy turned to Jake and said, "You go first!" 

So, Jake counted to ten slowly and politely. He said, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" 

Then, it was Lucy's turn. She smiled and counted to ten too. They both laughed with happiness.

The game was a success!

Once there was a boy named John. John used to go outside and play with his friends. One day, John and his friends were playing tag. John was always the fastest and he loved the speed.

Suddenly, the sky went dark and it started to rain. John and his friends decided to quit playing and go home.

As John was running home, the rain got heavier and the wind got stronger. John was still running, but the weather was so terrible. He was going too fast and he slipped and fell. He hurt his leg and started to cry.

Johnâ€™s mom heard him crying and came running. She was sad to see that he was hurt. John looked up at her and said, â€œNext time I wonâ€™t quit playing so fast.â€

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Fred. He was only three years old and he loved to have fun.

One day Fred went to the park by himself. When he got there, he saw a big whip. He wanted to try it so he grabbed it and began to swing it around. Suddenly a powerful wind blew and the whip flew away!

Fred was very scared, so he closed his eyes and started to pray. "Please God, help me get the whip back," he said.

Suddenly something amazing happened. Out of nowhere a big bird appeared, grabbed the whip in its beak, and brought it back to Fred.

Fred was so thankful that he gave the bird some delicious treats. He thanked God for answering his prayer and then ran home with a big smile on his face. The end.

John and Sam were two best friends. They were always playing together and it made them very happy. One day, John had a joke to share with Sam. He thought it would be fun to tell his friend. But when he did, Sam didn't laugh. He didn't even smile. John felt uncomfortable.

He asked his friend why he didn't like his joke. Sam said he thought it wasn't funny. John was surprised and a bit sad. He wanted Sam to be happy. So he asked Sam if he had his own joke to share.

Sam's face lit up and he shared his joke. When he finished, both John and Sam laughed. They laughed so much that John's tummy hurt. It made John very happy that his friend was having fun. From then on, John and Sam shared jokes often, and always had so much fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very tiny, but had very big plans. She wanted to separate the dust in her room. Everywhere she looked she saw a dirty, filthy mess.

The little girl grabbed a broom and started to sweep. She used her tiny hands to separate the dust. She moved the dirt around until everything was organised.

After a while, the room was sparkly clean. All the dust was separated into two piles. One neat pile of dark dust, and another one of light dust.

The little girl was overjoyed. She looked around at her clean room and smiled. She could now play happily with no dirty, filthy dust around her.

The end.

Randy and Allen were best friends. Every Tuesday they would play together in the park. They loved to play tag and hide and seek.

Their favorite game was to build towers with wooden blocks. They would have lots of fun stacking the block up high, counting the blocks and knocking them down.

One Tuesday, they wanted to build together, but Randy had an important appointment he had to attend. He was sad to have to separate from Allen and promised to come back afterwards.

Allen said goodbye to Randy and waved until he was out of sight. When he came back, they hugged and laughed as they started building a huge tower. It was the best game ever.

Once there was a little girl called Sam. She was only three years old and she was very hungry. One day, she and her parents went to a beautiful temple.

At the temple, Sam saw lots of people. Everyone was so happy and excited. Sam looked around and saw that the temple had many decorations. A big colorful flag was hung in one corner.

Sam was still hungry, so her parents bought her a delicious snack. She loved it! But the snack made her very thirsty, so her parents bought her a can of drink.

After a while, Sam and her parents left the temple. On the way home, Sam felt much less hungry. She was very happy to own a snack and a can of drink to enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. The wind was blowing hard, making the leaves on the trees rustle and dance. 

Lily noticed that the swings were moving back and forth by themselves. She thought it was scary, but her mom told her not to worry. They went to play on the slide, but Lily couldn't stop thinking about the scary wind. 

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew Lily's hat off her head and it flew away. Lily started to cry, but her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we'll find your hat." They looked all around the park, but they couldn't find it. Just when Lily thought she would never see her hat again, a kind stranger came up to them and gave her back her hat. "No, Sara, that is my car!" Tom says. "I got it for my birthday. It is not yours. Give it to me!"

Sara and Tom start to argue. They both pull the car. They both shout. They are not happy.

Mama hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees Sara and Tom fighting over the car.

"What is going on here?" Mama asks. "Why are you fighting?"

Sara and Tom stop pulling. They both answer Mama.

"This is my car!" Sara says.

"No, this is my car!" Tom says.

Mama looks at the car. She sees a sticker on the bottom. It has a name on it.

"Children, this car is not yours," Mama says. "This car belongs to your cousin Ben. He left it here when he visited last week. He will come back to get it soon. You have to share the car until then."

Sara and Tom feel sorry. They did not know the car was Ben's. They say sorry to each other. They say sorry to Mama.

"Can we still play with the car?" Sara asks.

"Yes, you can, but you have to take turns," Mama says. "And you have to be nice and gentle with the car. It is not yours."

Sara and Tom agree. They decide to play with the car together. They make noises like vroom and beep. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small number of dark clouds in the sky above a group of friends sitting in a park. They thought the clouds were pretty. Suddenly, one of the friends shouted out.

"Look! A dangerous ear!"

Everyone else squinted up at the sky, trying to find the ear. Sure enough, they spotted a large, scary-looking ear floating in the clouds.

"What is that?" asked one of the friends.

"I think it's an ear monster!" another answered.

They all agreed that the ear looked dangerous, so they decided to run away as fast as they could. They kept running until they reached their homes, and never looked back.

The end.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. They find a big bowl of sugar and a furry hat.

"Let's make a snowman!" Lily says. She puts the hat on her head and takes a teaspoon. She scoops some sugar and throws it in the air.

"Wow, look at the snow!" Ben says. He takes another teaspoon and does the same. They laugh and clap their hands.

But then, Mom comes in. She sees the mess and the hat. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She sounds angry.

"We are making a snowman, Mom!" Lily and Ben say.

"That is not snow, that is sugar!" Mom says. "And that is not a hat, that is my furry coat! You are making a big mess!"

Lily and Ben feel sorry. They did not know they were doing something bad.

"We are sorry, Mom," they say. "We will help you clean up."

Mom sighs. She is not angry anymore. She loves her twins.

"OK, thank you," she says. "But next time, please ask me before you use my things. And do not speed with the teaspoons. You could hurt yourself or break something."

Lily and Ben nod. They hug Mom and say they love her. They help her clean up the sugar and the coat. They learn their lesson. They still like to play, but they are more careful.

Once upon a time there was a farmer who lived in a big yellow house in the middle of a field. Every day he would work hard in the field to grow food for his family.

One day, the farmer and his family were sitting outside enjoying the sunshine. Suddenly, the farmer said, "Let's play a game, who wants to spin?"

His little daughter cheered, "Me, me!" She jumped up and grabbed the family's old spinning top. She started spinning it in the sunshine, and it went round and round.

The daughter started to giggle. The spinning top went faster and faster, and she laughed until her tummy hurt. Then she called out, "The spin is so crazy!"

The family all laughed, because they knew the spin was crazy too. The daughter spun the top until the sun went down, and then she went inside with her family and they all laughed and laughed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys when her little brother came in and broke her favorite doll. Lily got very angry and yelled at him, calling him stupid.

Her brother felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to break your doll."

Lily thought about it for a moment and decided to forgive him. She said, "It's okay, I forgive you. But please be more careful next time."

Her brother felt happy and they continued playing together. As they played, Lily began to wonder about how she could make her brother feel even happier. She thought about it for a while and then came up with an idea to give him her favorite toy car.

She said, "Here, you can have this toy car. I hope it makes you happy."

Her brother was very happy and said, "Thank you, Lily. You're the best sister ever!"

From that day on, Lily and her brother played together happily and forgave each other whenever they made mistakes.

Once upon a time, in a peaceful town, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to run and play outside. One day, Tim saw a race in the park. He was excited and wanted to join the race.

Tim went to his friend, Sarah, and said, "Let's start the race!" Sarah smiled and said, "Yes, let's go!" They lined up with the other kids and waited for the race to begin. When they heard the word "Go!", they started running as fast as they could.

Tim and Sarah ran with all their speed, laughing and having fun. They could feel the wind in their hair as they raced to the finish line. In the end, Tim won the race and Sarah came in second. They were both so happy and proud of themselves. They celebrated with their friends and had a great day at the park.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many flowers. They wanted to go up and see.

"Come on, Lila, let's climb the hill!" Tom said.

"No, Tom, I don't want to. It is too high and steep. I am scared." Lila said.

"Don't be scared, Lila. It will be fun. We can see the whole park from there. And maybe we can find some bugs or birds." Tom said.

He took Lila's hand and tried to pull her. But Lila refused. She shook her head and let go of his hand.

"Please, Lila, please. Just try. I will help you. I will hold your hand and we will go slow." Tom said.

He looked at Lila with big eyes and a smile. Lila looked at Tom and then at the hill. She saw the flowers and the sun. She saw a little mist in the air. She thought it looked pretty and soft.

"Okay, Tom, okay. I will try. But you have to be careful. The flowers are delicate. We don't want to hurt them." Lila said.

"Okay, Lila, okay. I will be careful. The flowers are delicate. We will be gentle." Tom said.

They held hands and started to climb the hill. They stepped on the grass and avoided the flowers. They felt the mist on their faces and the sun on their backs. They laughed and talked and sang. They reached the top and looked around. They saw the whole park and the sky. They felt happy and proud. They hugged and cheered.

"We did it, Lila, we did it! We climbed the hill!" Tom said.

"We did it, Tom, we did it! We saw the mist and the flowers!" Lila said.

They sat on the hill and enjoyed the view. They played with the bugs and the birds. They picked some flowers and made a crown. They had a lot of fun. They were glad they tried.

Once there was a naughty little girl. She was very naughty and always misbehaving. One day she do something very naughty. She took her daddyâ€™s tie and put it in the dirt. It began to rot away in the soil.

The little girl felt very bad about what sheâ€™d done, but it was too late. The tie was ruined and couldnâ€™t be fixed.

The little girlâ€™s daddy was very sad. He had worked very hard to buy that tie, and now it was gone. The little girl knew she had done something wrong and she was sorry.

The daddy gave the little girl a big, big hug and said it was alright. He said he still loved her and that she must never do such a naughty thing again.

The little girl was very happy and promised to never do anything naughty again. And with that, the tie was forgotten and the little girl was happy once more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play by the river with her friends. One day, they found a big box with a ribbon on it. Lily's friend, Sarah, said it was a gifted present for them. 

Lily was so happy and curious about the present. She questioned her friends, "What could be inside the box?" They didn't know, so they decided to open it together. 

As they unwrapped the ribbon, they saw a beautiful toy boat. They all took turns playing with it in the river. Lily was so grateful for the gifted present and had so much fun with her friends.

One day, Timmy was playing with his friends in the park. They were running and dancing and having a great time.

Suddenly, they saw a small rabbit through the bushes. It was fragile and timid.

The children squealed in delight and ran towards the rabbit, wanting to play with it.

"Let's celebrate," Timmy said. "Let's give the rabbit a party!"

His friends cheered and clapped their hands.

The children slowly approached the rabbit and made it a special party. They decorated the area with paper streamers, and provided the rabbit with yummy fruit snacks.

The rabbit stayed to enjoy the delicious treats and the children showed their love and respect for the small creature.

At the end of the day, the rabbit hopped away into the bush, feeling happy and safe.

The children hugged each other and celebrated the wonderful moment they had shared.

Once upon a time, there was a river where a little otter lived. The otter was very useful because he could catch fish to eat. One day, a little girl came to the river and saw the otter swimming. She said, "Hello, otter! You appear very happy today."

The otter replied, "Yes, I am happy because I caught a lot of fish today. They are very tasty!"

The little girl smiled and said, "You are such a useful otter. Can you catch some fish for me too?"

The otter agreed and caught some fish for the little girl. She was very happy and said, "Thank you, otter! You are my new friend."

From that day on, the little girl would often visit the river to play with her new friend, the useful otter. They would swim together and catch fish for each other. They had a lot of fun together and were very happy.

Once there was a diamond that was lying on the ground. It was very sparkly and special. One day, a polite rabbit came along and saw the diamond. He wanted it for himself, so he struck the diamond with his paw. 

The diamond started to rise up into the air. It twirled around and around before landing softly in the rabbitâ€™s arms. He was so happy! He thanked the diamond for being so polite and giving him a surprise. 

The rabbit held the diamond close and it started to sparkle. It was so pretty! He took it back to his home and talked to it about his day. 

The rabbit and the diamond were very happy together and they stayed friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain in the forest. It was so high. The animals loved living near the mountain, especially a squirrel family.

One day, the animals noticed something strange. Smoke seemed to be coming from the top of the mountain. It was increasing by the minute.

The animals were worried, so they went up the mountain. On the way up, they saw more and more smoke. It was getting thick in the air.

When they reached the top, they found the cause of the smoke. There was a big fire burning, and it was increasing.

The animals quickly ran back down the mountain, and the fire brigade came soon after. With their help, the fire was put out and the smoke cleared. All the animals were safe and happy.

One day, two friends, John and Jane, wanted to share something.

John had a feeling of an urge to share something but wasn't sure what. Jane saw that John had a need and suggested that they should share an ice cream.

John was excited and they went to the nearby shop. Inside, they could see lots of different ice creams, all of them looking very delicious! They chose two different flavours, which were available in the shop, and shared them together.

John and Jane shared the ice cream with big smiles, happy that they had something to share. They enjoyed the experience and after they finished, they decided they would always share things like this.

Once upon a time, there was a boy with cool skin. He always felt like he didn't belong. He was sad and wanted to be part of something special.

One day he went walking in the woods. There he suddenly saw a magical forest. When he entered the forest, he felt like he belonged. Everything was peaceful and cool. 

The boy stayed there for a while. He felt safe and happy in the cool forest. He made friends with the animals and they played together. He laughed and had lots of fun. 

Every day the boy went back to the forest. He belonged there, like he was a part of it. As his skin got nicer and cooler, the boy knew he found his special place.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved to use to play with his friends. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his car, but he realized that his car was missing! Timmy started to cry because he loved his toy car so much. 

Suddenly, a man came up to Timmy and asked him why he was crying. Timmy told the man that his toy car was gone. The man told Timmy that he saw a thief take it. Timmy was very sad because he didn't know what to do. 

But then, Timmy had an idea. He asked his friends if they wanted to play a game to find the thief and get his toy car back. They all agreed and started to look for the thief. They were very competitive and wanted to win the game. After a few minutes, they found the thief and got Timmy's toy car back! Timmy was so happy that he could use his toy car again.

Anna likes to jog with her dad in the park. She likes to see the trees, the birds and the flowers. Sometimes she sees other people jogging too. They say hello and smile.

One day, Anna sees something shiny in the grass. She stops and picks it up. It is a small fairy. The fairy has wings, a dress and a wand. She is very pretty.

"Hello, little girl," the fairy says. "Thank you for finding me. I was lost and scared."

"Hello, fairy," Anna says. "What is your name?"

"My name is Lily," the fairy says. "I came from the fairy land, but I flew too far and got lost. Can you help me go back?"

Anna nods. She likes to help. She puts Lily in her pocket and runs to her dad. She tells him about the fairy. He is surprised, but he believes her.

"Let's go find the fairy land," he says. "Maybe it is near the big pond. There are many flowers there."

They jog to the pond. They see many colors and smells. They hear a loud sound. It is the sound of bells. They follow the sound and see a big tree. The tree has a door and a sign. The sign says "Fairy Land".

Anna knocks on the door. The door opens. A fairy comes out. She looks like Lily.

"Lily, you are back!" the fairy says. "We were so worried about you. Who are these people?"

"They are my friends," Lily says. "They helped me find my way back. This is Anna and this is her dad. They are very kind."

The fairy smiles. She invites them in. She says they can see the fairy land. Anna and her dad are happy. They jog inside the tree. They see many fairies, animals and toys. They have a lot of fun. They thank Lily and her fairy friends. They say goodbye and jog back to their home. They are very tired, but very happy. They have a new fairy friend.

Marry had a special TV and they were very happy. But one day it stopped working, so Marry's mom and dad said they need to buy a new one.

Marry was very upset, especially because she loved to watch the cartoons on the old TV. But no matter how much she begged, her mom and dad still said they need to get a new one.

But Marry's mom and dad bought a surprise for her. They came home with a new TV for Marry, and when she saw it she was very happy.

Now she could watch her cartoons again, and she didn't need to be upset anymore. She was very happy.

One day, Sam went to the park with Mom and Dad to play. Sam looked around, but he could not see his friends. Suddenly, an earthquake started and everyone was scared.

Mom asked, "What was that?"

Dad said, "It was an earthquake!"

Sam had never experienced an earthquake before. He asked, "What is an earthquake?"
 
Dad said, "An earthquake is when the ground test us to see how strong we are."

Sam was a bit scared, but Dad encouraged him. He said, "It's okay, Sam. Sometimes the ground tests us with new things, but we can stay strong and together."

Mom and Dad held onto Sam and smiled. Sam smiled too. He felt better knowing that Mom and Dad were there with him.  Sam and his family stayed together, and they came out okay.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy whip that he loved to play with. One day, Tim was very sleepy, but he did not want to take a nap.

Tim's mom said, "Tim, you look so sleepy. Please go to bed and take a nap." But Tim did not want to sleep. He wanted to play with his whip. So, he went outside to play.

While playing, Tim heard a loud noise. He was scared. The noise was coming from a big dog. The dog wanted to take Tim's whip away. Tim said, "No, dog! This is my whip!" The dog did not listen and tried to grab the whip from Tim.

Tim ran back to his mom, crying. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you get your whip back." Together, they went to the dog and asked for the whip. The dog gave the whip back to Tim.

After that, Tim was so happy to have his whip back. He thanked his mom and said, "I am sleepy now, mom. I will take a nap." Tim went to bed and had a nice, long sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw shapes with her crayons. One day, she drew a triangle with an orange crayon. Her mommy asked her what she drew, and Lily said, "It's a triangle, mommy! See, it has three sides!" 

Lily's friend, Timmy, came over to play. He saw the drawing and said, "I disagree, Lily. That's not a triangle. Triangles are pointy, and this shape is round." Lily got upset and said, "No, Timmy! It's a triangle! It has three sides!" 

They both got into a little argument, but then they realized it was okay to have different opinions. They decided to draw more shapes together and have fun. In the end, Lily showed Timmy how to draw an orange circle, and they both laughed and played together. The end.

Once upon a time there were two good friends, Annie and Ben. Every day they would find fun things to do together.

One day, Annie and Ben noticed a big, soft loop on the ground.

"Let's play with it," Annie said.

"Okay," Ben said eagerly.

They took turns jumping over it and around it, having a great time.

Then Ben had an idea. He suggested they offer the loop to other friends.

"That's a great plan!" Annie said.

So Annie and Ben ran around to neighbouring farms and offered the loop to their friends.

Everyone was happy to accept the loop and they used it to make funny shapes like circles and squares. 

The friends all loved playing with the soft loop.

Annie and Ben spent the day together, and they were so happy they had something to offer their friends.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Lily and William. They both loved to visit each other, but one day when they were visiting, they started to fight. Lily wanted to play with her cars and William wanted to play with his building blocks.

Lily was not happy and pushed William. William got really mad and started shouting. Suddenly they heard a noise. It was coming from downstairs.

When they went to check it out they saw an open door. They were surprised to see the door open and didn't know what to do. Then they had an idea. They would hide behind the door and try to scare each other. 

They both jumped out with their hands in the air, and they both laughed. They laughed so hard they hugged each other. They had forgotten all about their fight, and they agreed to never fight again and just have fun when they visit each other.

Once upon a time in a big forest there lived a tiny caterpillar. He was so small and fragile that he could barely move around. He had never seen another caterpillar like him.

One day while he was crawling along, he heard a voice. It was a magical voice that said, "Hello, little caterpillar!" The caterpillar was so happy and he spoke back to the voice. The voice told him, "I'm a fairy and I can help you find other caterpillars like you!"

The fairy helped the tiny caterpillar find a big group of caterpillars. There were so many of them! The little caterpillar was so excited he couldn't speak. He made a lot of new friends that day! Every day, the caterpillar and the other caterpillars would gather together to eat and play.

The little caterpillar was so happy to have found his friends. He knew he had to be careful and delicate as he was still so fragile, so he moved around very gently. He made sure to take good care of himself and he had the best time with his new friends.

One day, a little bird was flying in the sky. The blue sky was warm and bright. Suddenly, the little bird saw something bitter. The bitter thing was a shut door.

The little bird flapped it's wings and said, "What is that?" 

The door smiled at the bird. It said, "I'm a shut door. People use me to keep things out." 

The bird thought for a moment. It said, "You look so sad. Why can't you open?"

The door replied, "I'm shut. Nothing can come in, or go out." 

The little bird smiled and said, "Don't be sad. I will come back and visit you soon." 

The door smiled again and said, "Thank you. That would be nice." 

The little bird flew away and the door stayed shut. But the bird came back to visit every day, and the door slowly began to feel less bitter and more happy.

Tim likes to dig in the dirt. He likes to find worms and put them in a jar. He thinks worms are funny and slimy. He wants to show them to his mom and dad.

One day, he digs a big hole in the backyard. He finds many worms and puts them in his jar. He is very happy. He thinks he will surprise his mom and dad with his worms.

But he does not see the dog. The dog is big and hungry. The dog likes to eat worms. The dog sees the jar and thinks it is a snack. The dog runs to the jar and knocks it over. The worms fall out and the dog eats them.

Tim hears a loud noise. He turns around and sees the dog. He sees the jar and the worms. He is very sad. He cries and runs to his mom and dad.

Mom and dad hug him and comfort him. They tell him they are sorry about his worms. They tell him he can dig more worms another day. They tell him they love him. They think he is brave and smart. They give him a cookie and a juice. Tim feels a little better. He thinks he will dig more worms tomorrow. He thinks he will keep them away from the dog. He thinks he will make a sign that says "No dogs allowed". He thinks he will have fun.

Once, there were two friends, Tom and Cat. Tom wanted to show Cat something special. So, he carried her to a secret space.

The space was smelly. Cat wrinkled her nose. She knew it wasn't a nice smell. But Tom was happy. He said they had found a very special place.

They looked around and saw lots of old furniture. Some chairs, a big table and an old cupboard.

Tom told Cat they could pretend these things were from outer space. They could explore and be astronauts.

So, they made rockets by piling the furniture up. They danced around the piles, pretending they were flying.

They had lots of fun pretending and exploring, until it was time for Tom to carry Cat home.

Once upon a time there was an elephant who had a very special secret. Everywhere he went he carried it around with him but no one had any idea what it was until one day he decided to show it to the other animals. 

He spread the news throughout the entire jungle and all the animals gathered around to see it. When he opened the pack he had been carrying, everyone gasped in amazement. Inside it was a brand new hat!

"Where did you get this?" asked one of the monkeys.

The elephant smiled. "Oh, I made it myself. I thought it would look nice on me," he said.

The other animals were really impressed. They wanted to know how he did it so he showed them how to make more hats - and soon the entire jungle was wearing the new hats!

Once upon a time there was a boy named John. He was three years old. One day, John wanted to join a wild pitch game with his friends. But when he got there, he saw that there were lots of other kids playing too. 

John was excited but also a bit scared. He wanted to play but he did not know how. Suddenly, John's friend shouted, "John, join us - let's have some fun!"

John smiled and ran over. Suddenly a big kid stepped in front of him and said, "You can't join. We don't want kids as small as you!"

John was so mad. He yelled, "It's not fair! Everyone should be able to join the wild pitch game!"

John's friend grabbed his arm and nodded. "John knows the rules. He's allowed to play too!"

The big kid grumbled and let John join the game. From then on, John always remembered to stand up for himself and for his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a family of four living in a big city. Alex, the father, was very hardworking. Every day he would take the subway to provide for his family.

One day, the subway stopped working and Alex found himself stuck in the middle of the station. He felt helpless and did not know what to do.

Just then, he heard a small voice say "Don't worry".

Alex looked down and saw an old woman with a warm smile.

She said: "I can help you get to work. Look, I have a cart. You can rest there while I provide a ride down the street".

Alex felt so relieved and happily accepted the offer.

For the rest of the day, he rode the cart to the office and back home. He thanked the old woman for providing him the ride and was relieved to know that his family would not go without food that day.

One day, a big, bossy cat and a little, shy dog were playing near a pond. They saw a net with many fish in it. The cat said, "I want to eat the fish!"

The dog said, "No, we should let them go back to the pond." The cat did not like that idea. The cat tried to slap the dog with its paw, but the dog moved away.

The dog said, "Please don't be mean. Let's be nice to the fish." The cat thought about it and said, "Okay, we can let them go." They opened the net and let the fish swim back to the pond. The cat and dog were happy, and they played together all day.

Once there was a little boy who was very curious. He was always looking to explore new places and always interested to learn something new. One day he found a garden full of flowers and he discovered a rake. He was amazed and happy, so he decided to try it. But he was not careful enough and he accidentally destroyed some delicate flowers.

He was feeling very sad and he started crying; he knew he had done something wrong. But then, the flower fairy appeared! She said that she will heal the flowers and she showed him how to do it with the rake. She was very kind and she showed him the right way to use it.

The little boy was so happy and thankful; he learned a valuable lesson. He thanked the flower fairy from the bottom of his heart for teaching him and for healing the flowers. From then on, the little boy always used the rake carefully and delicately in the garden. He learned a great lesson - never do something without thinking first and don't be careless.

The pale stair was long. Sally wanted to go up it. But she had to delay. It was too high and too far.

Instead she waited and waited. She watched her mommy go up it. Mommy said she'd wait for Sally at the top. Sally wanted to see what was up there.

Finally, Sally decided she'd try the big pale stair. One slow step at a time, she followed her mommy. It was a long way up the stair!

Soon Sally reached the top. She was very proud of herself. She could see everything from up here. Mommy smiled at her. She said, "I am proud of you, Sally."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk and saw a big hill. She wanted to climb to the top, but it was too steep for her little legs.

Suddenly, she saw her friend Jack. Jack was famous for being very strong. She asked Jack if he could lend her a hand to climb the hill. Jack agreed and helped her up the hill.

When they reached the top, Lily was so happy. She saw a beautiful view and felt like a queen. She thanked Jack for his help and promised to lend him her favorite toy next time they played together. From that day on, Lily and Jack were the best of friends and always helped each other out.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat grapes. One day, Timmy saw a grape on the floor and picked it up. He wanted to eat it, but he saw that it was dirty. He didn't want to eat a dirty grape, so he threw it away.

Timmy's mom saw what he did and said, "Timmy, you shouldn't throw away food. It's not nice."

Timmy felt ashamed and said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't mean to waste food."

His mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Timmy. Next time, just lay the grape on a napkin and clean it before you eat it. That way, you won't waste food and you'll still get to enjoy your grapes." 

Timmy learned his lesson and from that day on, he always cleaned his grapes before he ate them. The end.

A bunny named Alex was feeling sad. He wanted to make himself feel better, but he didn't know how. It was getting harder and harder each day.

Then one day, his best friend Sam visited him. "What's wrong?" Sam asked.

"I'm feeling very difficult," Alex said.

"Let's go for a walk," Sam said. "Maybe getting outside will help!"

Alex and Sam hopped through the grass until they reached a nearby playground. They spotted a swing and hopped over to it.

"Let's swing!" Sam said.

They hopped up and down on the swing, going higher and higher until they were both laughing. When they stopped, they hopped over to a nearby stream.

Sam said, "Let's bathe in the stream and make ourselves feel better!"

Alex thought that sounded like a good idea. So, they both hopped into the stream and splashed around. Finally, Alex felt better.

The moral of the story is that doing something fun with a friend can help you feel better whenever you're feeling sad.

Tom is a famous cat. He can sing and dance and make people laugh. He has many friends who like to watch him on TV. But Tom does not like winter. Winter is a cold season. Tom does not like to wear a coat and a hat and a scarf. He likes to be warm and cozy.

One day, Tom has to go to a show in the snow. His friends tell him to put on his coat and his hat and his scarf. But Tom refuses. He says he does not need them. He says he is not cold. He says he is a famous cat and he can do what he wants.

Tom goes to the show without his coat and his hat and his scarf. He sings and dances and makes people laugh. But he also shivers and sneezes and coughs. He feels very cold and sick. He wishes he had listened to his friends.

After the show, Tom goes back to his home. His friends are there. They are worried about him. They give him some soup and some tea and some medicine. They also give him a big hug and a warm blanket. They tell him they love him and they want him to be well.

Tom says he is sorry. He says he was silly and stubborn. He says he will wear his coat and his hat and his scarf next time. He says he is lucky to have such good friends. He says he is a famous cat, but he is also a smart cat. He learns from his mistakes.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mary. Mary was so happy, because she was going to marry her best friend. On the day of the wedding, everyone was so excited.

Mary looked so beautiful in her pretty dress. Her friend was wearing a white suit and he looked so handsome. They looked so happy together. 

When it was time for the reception, everyone enjoyed the party. There was delicious food, and one of the treats was yogurt. It was very smooth and tasted so yummy. 

Mary and her friend loved the yogurt so much, they fed each other. Everyone clapped and cheered for them. Then the music started so that everyone could dance. 

It was the best day ever and Mary and her friend married and were very happy together.

Grandma smiled. "Come on in and find out," she said. So Amy walked into the room and the first thing she saw was a toy gun. It was pink and had sparkles on it.
