The old plane was never seen again, but it will always be remembered. It was a simple plane, but it had served its purpose.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily's mom made her some hot soup for lunch. Lily blew on it to cool it down before she ate it.

Later, Lily went to the park with her friends. They played on the swings and the slide. It was very noisy because there were lots of other kids playing too. When Lily's mom called her to come home, Lily replied, "Okay, Mommy!" and ran over to say goodbye to her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a fierce barrel. The barrel was so fierce, nothing could scare it. One day, a truck drove up and stopped right in front of the barrel. The truck had a very big arm on it. The arm reached out and started to load the barrel onto the truck. The barrel didn't want to go, but the truck arm was too strong.

Once the barrel was loaded onto the truck, the truck drove away. The barrel didn't know where they were going, but they were going very fast.

Soon, they drove to a new place. The barrel saw lots of other barrels, just like him. Before long, the truck arm unloaded the barrel from the truck. The barrel was now with all his barrel friends! They were all so happy to be together. 

The fierce barrel was now safe and sound with all his barrel friends. They had a lot of fun playing together. The end.

Tommy arrived at his room and saw something new. He was curious and went to investigate it.

"Whatâ€™s that Mommy?" asked Tommy.

"Itâ€™s something to help you relax. Itâ€™s called a bed," replied his mom.

"A bed? What does it do?" asked Tommy.

"It lets you take a nap in your bedroom or just lay down and relax," his mom said with a smile.

Tommy got on the bed and laid down. His eyes were heavy, the bed was so comfy. He soon fell into a peaceful sleep.

His mom watched as he slept and thought about how serious he could be sometimes. But when he slept he always looked so relaxed and happy. 
She was glad he had a comfortable bed to relax in.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ann who wanted to help her mom with the laundry. She went to her mom and said, "Can I help with the laundry?" Her mom said, "Yes, that's a good request. Thank you."

So, Ann and her mom went to the laundry room. Inside, it was very noisy. The washer was humming and the dryer was clanging. Ann was a little bit scared, but she knew she had to help. Ann's mom showed her how to put the laundry in the washer.

Then Ann's mom said, "Now your job is to put the clothes in the dryer when the washer is done". So, Ann waited patiently until the little buzzing sound went off. That meant the washer was done.

Ann put the clothes in the dryer and made sure to turn it on and choose the right setting. Then she waited some more and soon the dryer was done too. 

Ann was proud that she had helped with the laundry. She went back to her mom and said, "I helped with the noisy laundry!" Her mom smiled and said, "You did a great job."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mommy and daddy. They had a neighbor named Mrs. Smith. Mrs. Smith was always worried about something.

One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help Mrs. Smith with her groceries. Lily was happy to help. She carried the bags to Mrs. Smith's house and Mrs. Smith was very grateful. Lily gained a new friend that day.

From then on, Lily would visit Mrs. Smith every day. They would talk and play games together. Mrs. Smith was no longer worried because she had a new friend. Lily learned that being kind to others can make them happy and that gaining a new friend is always a good thing.

Once there was a little boy named James. He was very naughty and liked to do naughty things. One day he was walking past a mailbox and saw something sparkly in it. He reached his hand in to get it but he felt a shiver up his spine. He quickly pulled his hand out and ran away.

The next day James went back to the mailbox. He opened it very carefully and saw a baby bird. The bird was shaking and had big eyes, it must have been very scared. Poor little bird!

James offered the bird some food. Then the bird stopped shaking and chirped happily in the sunshine. James played with the bird for the rest of the day.

It was nice that James was nice to the bird, even though he had been naughty the day before!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Flora. She wanted more fun, so she asked her neighbour if she could lend her some. Her neighbour had a lot of fun things, but they were all pink! Flora didn't want to play with pink things, she wanted colourful. Her neighbour said no, she couldn't lend her anything else. Flora was sad.

Then she had an idea. She decided to make her own fun things that were colourful. She got some paper, paint, glue and scissors and began to make her own fun things. She made a house and a car in rainbow colours.

She went to her neighbour's house and asked if she could show her what she had made. Her neighbour was very pleased and said that Flora could lend her the things. So Flora lent her the rainbow house and car and her neighbour gave her lots of fun in return.

They played together for the rest of the day, and from then on shared their fun with each other - no more pink things for Flora!

Once upon a time there was a brilliant mouse. The mouse wanted to help a crack in the house. He hopped in and tried to make it better. He filled it with mud, rocks and twigs. He worked so hard to make it fit. The mouse was very proud of what he did. The crack looked much better and everyone was happy. The mouse had helped a lot and he felt very brilliant.

Once upon a time there was a poor temple. The temple was very old and had many broken pieces. People used to come and pray.

One day, a little girl called Amy came to visit the temple. She looked around and imagined what it must have been like when the temple was first built. She closed her eyes and saw colourful flags and animals roaming around the temple.

Amy wanted to help the poor temple, so she decided to take some of her pocket money and use it to buy some flowers and new flags. She decorated the temple and suddenly it seemed very bright and beautiful.

People started to come to the temple again, and were amazed by the changes. They thanked Amy for her hard work and thanked her for bringing life back to the old temple.

Amy had done a wonderful job and was very proud of herself. She had imagined a better temple and with a little hard work and help from her community, Amy had made her dream come true.

Once upon a time there was a monkey called Molly. She was excited because today was a special day. Molly was going to explore the forest.

Before she left, she reminded herself to be careful. She didn't want to get lost. As she stepped into the forest, Molly noticed that it was full of purple flowers. She was so excited to explore!

Molly spent the morning running around, hopping from branch to branch, and swinging from vines. She even made a few friends along the way.

When Molly got tired, she remembered to use her mind and find her way back home. She looked for purple flowers and followed them until she reached her home safe and sound.

Molly went to bed that night, feeling excited and proud. She had used her mind to explore, and find her way safely back home.

John was scared. He was very scared. It was night time, and night time always made John scared. He was all alone in his bed, but he wasn't scared of the dark. He was scared of the noises he heard. 
He tried to think of happy things. He thought of his mom and dad, he thought of his best friend, but he was still scared. Then he thought of one more thing to help, he hoped. He closed his eyes and hoped with all his might. He hoped and hoped, until he fell asleep. 
John was no longer scared. He was all snug and cozy in his bed. He felt safe, and with that his hope was fulfilled.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who wanted to buy something special. He had a rare barn and wanted to give it an extra sparkle. So he went out to buy the perfect thing.

The farmer searched and searched, but nothing seemed quite right. Then, he stumbled upon something quite unique - a shiny diamond! It was so rare, the farmer knew this was the perfect thing to put in his barn.

The farmer bought the diamond and took it back to his barn. To his surprise, when the diamond was placed in the barn it lit up the entire space â€“ like a never ending twinkle! Everyone who had visited the farm was in awe of this magical sight. The barn had become rarer than ever before!

The farmer was so happy with his purchase. He now had a truly special barn, better than ever before. And so, the farmer and the diamond lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play chess with his big sister, Sue. One day, Tim found a big, bitter apple in the kitchen. He had an idea.

Tim went to Sue and said, "Sue, if I eat this bitter apple, will you play chess with me?" Sue looked at the apple and said, "If you eat it, I will play chess with you." Tim was very happy and took a big bite of the apple. It was very bitter, but he did not refuse to eat it.

After Tim ate the apple, Sue kept her promise and played chess with him. They had a lot of fun, and Tim learned that sometimes, you have to do something you don't like to get what you want.

Tim and Jen were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were spies and hide under the big rug. They had a key that could lock and unlock the door to their secret base.

"Let's lock the door so no one can find us," Tim said. He took the key and turned it in the lock. "Now we are safe and cozy."

Jen nodded and crawled under the rug with him. They giggled and whispered their spy plans. They did not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

After a while, they got hungry and thirsty. They decided to go out and eat. Tim tried to unlock the door, but the key was stuck. He pulled and twisted, but it did not move.

"Help me, Jen," he said. "The key is broken."

Jen tried to help him, but she could not. They pushed and kicked the door, but it did not open. They started to cry and yell for help, but no one heard them.

They felt hot and dizzy under the rug. They wished they had not locked the door. They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they were not spies.

Once there was an earth and the people on it really loved one another. They used to meet together every day and laugh and play. 

One day something terrible happened and it made all the people very sad. Everywhere was full of sadness and tears.

The people decided to try and unite, to come together as one and make things better. So with smiles on their faces and hands together, the people spoke for the first time as one voice.

"Let's be kind to one another," said one.

"Let's spread happiness," said another.

And soon everyone was smiling and the laughter filled the air again. The people had united and brought back happiness to the earth.

One day a little boy named Jack went out for an adventure. On his way he came across a colourful garden full of beans. There were small round beans, tall thin beans, and some long and wiggly beans. He'd never seen such different beans in one place before, and he was so curious.

Jack looked around for a bit then he heard a voice. "Care to come closer and take a peek?" Jack looked around and saw a small, friendly-looking rabbit.

He walked closer and said, "Hello! What kind of beans do you have here?"

The rabbit beckoned him to follow, and soon they were in the middle of the beans. "These are the best beans in town!" The rabbit said with a smile. "Would you dare to pick one and see how it tastes?"

Jack was surprised but he wanted to try it. He spotted a unique-looking bean, different from the others. He picked it, popped it in his mouth and... it was delicious!

The rabbit laughed and said with a twinkle in his eye, "You sure are brave for such a little one, Jack. You now know the secret of my special beans!"

Molly was a little girl who loved to swing. She ran outside every day and hopped onto her swing. She would rock back and forth and fly through the air. While she swung, she made happy sounds like "whee!"

Molly's swing was broken. It had a gear that was loose and needed to be tightened. Molly was very troubled because she could no longer swing.

One day, Molly's mother and father took her to the store to buy a new swing. Molly was so excited, she picked out the brightest colors.

When they got home, Daddy put the swing together and Molly immediately jumped on. She pumped her legs back and forth and was swingin' high in the sky. Molly was so happy, she laughed and shouted "Whee!"

Molly loved her new swing and she enjoyed swinging every day. She had no more troubled times because her new swing brought her so much joy!

One day, a little boy named Tommy went for a walk in the park. He saw an incredible acorn on the ground. Tommy was so excited about the acorn. He wanted to catch it so he picked it up and put it in his pocket. 

He kept walking and soon he found something else - a monster! The monster was huge and had lots of teeth. Tommy was scared, but he knew he had to catch it. He slowly moved closer and then - he jumped and grabbed the monster. 

Tommy was so proud. He had caught something incredible! He showed the monster to his mom. She was so happy and said that he was very brave. 

Tommy was so proud of himself. He kept the acorn in his pocket as a reminder of his brave catch.

Mia and Tom were sitting on a bench in the park. They both had a diary. Mia's diary was as blue as the sky. Tom's diary was red and green.

Mia opened up her diary and started writing in it.

Tom looked over at Mia and said, "What are you writing in your diary?"

Mia smiled and said, "I'm writing about my day."

Tom opened up his diary and said, "Me too!"

The two of them sat and wrote in their diaries for a while. When they were done, they both closed their diaries and put them in their backpacks.

Then, they went back to sitting on the bench, looking up at the blue sky and talking about their day.

John and his mom were walking to the park. As they passed the store, John saw a present in the window. He asked his mom if he could get it. His mom said, "It looks very nice, but is it useful?" John thought for a moment, then said, "Yes, I think it would be useful." So they walked into the store.

Inside, the store was full of colorful presents. John's eyes sparkled as he looked at all of the pretty things. He and his mom searched and searched, until eventually, they found the perfect present.

John was so excited to give his present to his friend. He couldn't wait to see his friend's face when he opened it. John knew it would be a great present!

Joe and Mum were walking around the park. Joe saw a dove resting on a branch and he shouted to Mum, "Look! There's a dove!"

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, Joe! That's a beautiful dove! Let's go and show it to Dad."

Joe and Mum walked over to the dove and Joe was so excited to see it so close. He asked, "What does it smell like?"

Mum laughed and said, "It smells a bit smelly!"

Joe stepped back and laughed too. He asked, "Mum, can I hold the dove in my hands?"

Mum said, "No, Joe. The dove needs to be free. But you can show it in other ways, like clapping and singing to it."

So Joe clapped and sang to the dove. The dove seemed very happy and flew away to find a new place to rest. 

Joe was so amazed and he smiled as he watched the dove fly away gracefully. He turned to Mum and said, "That was so much fun! Can we show the dove again soon?"

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, Joe. Let's go show the dove again soon!"

Lily loved elephants. She had many toys of elephants, and she liked to watch them on TV. She always asked her mom and dad to take her to the zoo, where she could see real elephants. But her mom and dad said no. They said the zoo was too far, too expensive, and too crowded. They said maybe when she was older, they would go to the zoo.

One day, Lily saw a poster on the street. It said there was a circus in town, and it had elephants. Lily was very excited. She ran to her mom and dad and showed them the poster. She begged them to take her to the circus. She said she wanted to see the elephants more than anything. She said she would be very good and do all her chores. She said please, please, please.

Her mom and dad looked at each other. They saw how happy Lily was. They decided to permit her to go to the circus. They said they would buy tickets for the next day. They said they would have a fun family outing. They said they loved Lily very much.

The next day, Lily woke up early. She put on her favorite dress and her elephant necklace. She ate her breakfast and brushed her teeth. She was ready to go to the circus. Her mom and dad drove her to the big tent. They bought popcorn and cotton candy. They found their seats and waited for the show to start.

The show was amazing. Lily saw clowns, acrobats, lions, and horses. She laughed and clapped and cheered. But she was waiting for the elephants. She wanted to see them the most. Finally, the ringmaster announced that the elephants were coming. Lily saw four big gray elephants enter the ring. They had colorful blankets and hats on. They walked in a line and did tricks. Lily was amazed. She thought they were the most beautiful animals in the world.

But then, something went wrong. One of the elephants looked angry. He did not want to do the tricks. He did not like the loud noise and the bright lights. He did not like the whip and the chain. He wanted to be free. He roared and shook his head. He broke the chain and ran out of the ring. He knocked over the chairs and the people. He made a big mess.

Lily was scared. She did not understand why the elephant was angry. She thought he was happy in the circus. She thought he liked to do the tricks. She did not know he was sad and hurt. She cried and hugged her mom and dad. They told her not to worry. They told her they were safe. They told her they would leave the circus and go home.

Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned that elephants are not toys. They are not meant for the circus. They are meant for the wild. She learned that animals have feelings too. They can be happy or sad, or angry. She learned to respect and love them. She still loved elephants, but she did not want to see them in the circus anymore. She wanted to see them in the zoo, or better yet, in their natural home. She hoped the angry elephant would find his way back to his family and friends. She hoped he would be happy again.

Mum pulled her little girl by the hand. They were off to see the shopkeeper. 

The shopkeeper had a smile on his face and said "Hello my little one, what can I do for you?".

Mum said "We would like to buy something tasty!"

The shopkeeper pulled out a jar of yummy coins. Little girl was very excited and pulled out a coin from her pocket.

Mum said "Oh, that coin won't be enough, it's too small."

The shopkeeper said "Let me help you. I'll give you the treats, but in exchange I would like the coin."

Little girl was upset and started crying. Mum hugged her tightly and said "Don't worry, it's ok, we'll find a bigger coin somewhere else."

They said goodbye to the shopkeeper and started walking away. Little girl looked less upset; she knew soon they'd have enough coins to buy something yummy.

Once upon a time there was a tidy family. They had a nice house and were very happy together. But one day something bad happened - they split up! The little girl in the family was very sad and didn't understand why. Her parents didn't explain either. She was sad because she wanted her family to stay together, but they had split. 

The little girl was determined to get her family back together again. She worked hard to make her house tidy, so that she would be a good example for her family. She wanted her family to be happy again.

Every morning she woke up early, to sweep and clean her house. After a few days, she noticed something. Her parents were coming to visit and bringing presents with them! The little girl was so glad that her efforts had worked. After lots of hugs, her family was back together again!

Once there were two brothers. They were joyful and cheerful. They were looking for something fun to do.

The younger brother said, "Let's play a game. We can try to reverse around the room." The older brother thought that was a great idea.

So they both got up and started to spin and twirl in circles. They twirled so fast they were almost blurs. They spun around and around until they felt dizzy.

The younger brother laughed and said, "Let's reverse! I think it would be even funnier!" The older brother nodded, and they took turns running around the room in reverse.

Their laughter filled the room until they collapsed to the ground, giggling. The older brother said, "That was so much fun! Let's do it again!"

And they did, smiling and laughing while they spun and reversed around the room.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her kite. Lily's kite was very special because it had brightly coloured streamers that would blow in the wind. 

One day, Lily took her kite to the park to have fun with it. But as she was getting ready to fly it, it suddenly flew away!

Lily was so sad. She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, my kite flew away!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, sweetheart. We can find the kite and go back to the park to fly it again."

So, Lily and her mom drove back to the park. When they got there, Lily's kite was still flying in the sky!

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "You forgive the kite for flying away and now it can forgive you for letting it go. That's why it stayed."

Lily was so happy! And from then on, whenever Lilly flew her kite, she always remembered to forgive it for occasionally flying away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mom and dad. One day, while playing on the swings, she met a new friend named Max. They played together on the slide and had so much fun. 

After playing for a while, Max told Lily about a prize he had won at a game. Lily was so excited and wanted to see the prize. Max told her it was available at his house and they could go get it together. 

Lily and Max walked to Max's house and his mom gave them the prize. It was a shiny gold medal. Lily was so happy for Max and they decided to share the prize and play together again soon. From that day on, Lily and Max were the best of friends and they always met at the park to play together.

Once upon a time, there was a skeleton named Mr. Bones. He lived in a spooky house in the forest. One day, a little girl named Lily was walking in the forest and she saw the spooky house. She went inside and saw Mr. Bones standing in the corner.

"Hi, Mr. Bones," said Lily. "Why are you standing there all alone?"

"I am deaf," said Mr. Bones. "I cannot hear anything."

"Oh, I'm sorry," said Lily. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, I would like that very much," said Mr. Bones. They played together for a while, and Lily showed Mr. Bones how to dance. He was very happy and they became good friends. From that day on, Mr. Bones never stood alone in the corner again.

One day, Lily and her mom went to visit her grandma. Grandma lived in a big house with a huge garden. Lily loved to play in the garden with the flowers and the birds.

"Look, mom, a butterfly!" Lily said, pointing to a yellow and black one. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is, honey. Do you want to catch it?" mom asked.

Lily nodded and ran after the butterfly. She tried to be gentle, but it flew away. She followed it to a big bush with pink flowers. She saw something white on the flowers. It looked like snow, but it was not cold.

"What is this, mom?" Lily asked, touching the white stuff. It was soft and fine, like powder.

"That is pollen, Lily. The flowers make it to help other flowers grow. The butterfly likes to eat it, too. But be careful, some people are allergic to it. It can make them sneeze or itch," mom explained.

"Oh, I see. I don't want to sneeze or itch. Can I smell the flowers, though?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can. But don't get too close. Just a little sniff," mom said.

Lily smelled the flowers. They smelled sweet and nice. She smiled and said, "I like the flowers, mom. And I like grandma's garden. Can we visit her again soon?"

"Of course, we can, Lily. Grandma loves to see you, too. She has a surprise for you inside. Do you want to go and see?" mom said.

Lily nodded and took mom's hand. They walked to the house, where grandma was waiting for them with a big hug and a cake. Lily was happy. She loved to visit her grandma.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. Emma was curious and liked learning new things. One day, Emma's mommy and daddy said they were going to the airport. Emma was so excited! 

When they got to the airport, Emma couldn't believe all the people and planes. She asked lots of questions and was very curious. Mommy and Daddy promised they would show her around. They took her all over the airport, showing her how planes took off, and how to check in her bags. 

Then, it was time to say goodbye. Emma was sad, but she was happy too because she had a wonderful time. Her mommy and daddy promised to come back next week, and Emma couldn't wait to see them again.

Once upon a time there was a tall tree. One day, a little bird perched on the branch of the tree. The bird had a surprise for the tree. It had a hook!

The little bird said to the tree, "I have a surprise for you!" 
The tree was excited and said, "What is it?"

The little bird smiled and said, "I brought you a hook. Now you can hold things like apples and nuts." 
The tree was delighted and said, "Thank you, little bird!"

The bird smiled and flew away, happy to have surprised the tall tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Hannah. She was 3 years old and she loved to have a massage. 
One day, she asked her mum, "Mum, can I please have a massage?" Her Mum replied, "Yes of course!"

Hannah was so excited. She followed her mum to the massage room. When she arrived, she saw that the massage room was very special and original. There was a big massage table, some soft music and lots of comfy pillows.

Hannah asked, "Can I get on the table, please?" Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, please get comfy".

Hannah lay down on the table, and her mum started to give her a massage. It felt so nice! She felt all her muscles relax, and she was so peaceful. 

When the massage was over, Hannah said, "Thank you Mum for the massage, it was so nice and original"! Her mum smiled and said, "You are very welcome, Hannah".

Molly and her family were sitting in the living room. Her mom and dad were on the couch and Molly was sitting on the floor. They were looking around the room, wondering what to do.

Then, Molly had an idea. She said, "Let's watch TV!" Everyone thought it was a good idea and so they decided to do it.

Molly's family looked around the room until they saw an old TV in the corner. It hadn't been used in a long time, but Molly's mom decided to plug it in and turn it on.

The TV made noises and lights came on. Molly was so excited and ran to the couch with her mom and dad. They all watched the show together and had a lot of fun.

At the end of the night, everyone said they had a great time. They thanked Molly for deciding to watch the old TV.

Once upon a time, there was a little pink bunny. The bunny was famous for being the fastest in the field. One day, the bunny saw a big carrot on the other side of the field. The bunny wanted the carrot so much that it decided to crawl under the fence to get it. 

But as the bunny crawled under the fence, it got stuck. It tried and tried to get free, but it couldn't. Suddenly, a sly fox appeared. The fox saw the bunny and said, "I'll help you get out, but first you have to give me your famous speed." The bunny agreed, and the fox helped it out.

But without its famous speed, the bunny couldn't run away from the fox. The fox caught the bunny and ate it for dinner. And that's why you should never crawl under fences, even if you really want a big carrot.

Once upon a time, there lived a generous rabbit. The rabbit was always so kind to her friends and neighbours. One day, the rabbit was hopping down the path when she spotted a little girl. 

"Hello there! Where are you going?" said the rabbit.

"I want to run in the park," said the little girl.

"Well, you should be careful, but also have lots of fun," said the rabbit. "Would you like me to show you how to speed?"

The little girl nodded.

The generous rabbit hopped alongside the little girl, showing her how to speed. The little girl was delighted! She followed the rabbit's instructions and soon she was faster than ever before. 

In the end, the rabbit's generous teaching paid off and the little girl was able to speed around the park in no time!

Once, there was a very old shape. It was round and had nine sides. It liked to tell stories to the other shapes. 

One day, it told a story about a snake and a tiger. But a square shape didn't like this. It wanted the old shape to tell stories about a snail and a ladybug instead. 

But the old shape didn't want to change its story. So, it kept telling the story about the snake and the tiger. 

The square shape was very angry. It shouted and shouted, but the old shape still wouldn't listen. 

Then another shape stepped in. It was a triangle shape and it was very wise. It explained to the square shape that everyone has different stories to tell. 

The square shape understood and it smiled. Everyone was happy and the old shape carried on telling its story.

Once there was a happy family who did fun things together. One day the family gathered to do something very special and creative. They made a paper bird! It was bright and colourful, and they put it in the middle of the room.

Suddenly the paper bird started to flap its wings and it flew all around the room. Everyone was so surprised! Then, with a twinkle, the paper bird vanished!

Though they were sad to see the paper bird go, the family had lots of fun playing together and being creative. No matter what, they always had each other. And that made them very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, in a big yard, there was a brown tree. The tree had many leaves. The leaves were green, yellow, and red. The wind blew, and the leaves began to fall. They fell to the ground, making a big pile.

A little girl named Mia saw the leaves. She wanted to play with them. Mia ran to the yard and found a rake. She used the rake to make the pile of leaves even bigger. Mia was happy to see the big pile of leaves she made.

Mia jumped into the pile of leaves. She laughed as the leaves flew up in the air. Mia's dog, Max, came to play too. Max jumped in the leaves with Mia. They played and played until they were tired. Then, they lay down in the leaves and looked at the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a duck named Don. He lived in a wide swamp. Every day, Don would bathe in the cool, swampy water. He would take a long bath and enjoy the wetness of the water.

One day Don wanted to go for a really long bathe. He swam to a different part of the swamp and was amazed by how wide it was. He got lost in the vastness of the swamp, but he didn't mind.

Don kept swimming and every day he went further and further. He got further away from his home, but soon he found a small, cozy pond. It was the perfect spot to bathe and have fun.

Don loved his long baths and the space to swim. He enjoyed taking the long, leisurely swims and spending his time in the wide swamp. Don was happy, and the swamp was happy to have him.

Once upon a time, there was a chicken who liked to hide all the time. He liked to hide under the bushes, and behind big rocks. One day, the chicken decided to hide in a scary cave. He was very brave and he didn't realize how fierce the animals in the cave were.

As the chicken walked further and further into the cave, he suddenly heard a loud voice. He looked around and saw a fierce lion, who said, "Why are you here? This is my cave!"
The chicken was scared and started to tremble. He said, "I'm just trying to hide, that's all."

The lion thought for a moment, then he said, "I will hide with you, if you want. I like to hide too." The chicken was so happy, and said yes. The chicken and the lion hid together, deep in the cave. The chicken felt much safer with his new friend.

The chicken and the lion are still hiding in the cave today. They have become very good friends and have lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a horse named Brownie. Brownie lived in a big, red stable with his friends. One day, Brownie was feeling very hungry and he wanted to eat some apples. But he couldn't reach the apples on the tree. 

Then, a helpful boy came along and saw Brownie. The boy knew that Brownie wanted to eat apples, so he went to the tree and picked some apples. He brought the apples to Brownie and Brownie was very happy. 

From that day on, Brownie and the boy became good friends. The boy would often visit Brownie and bring him some apples to eat. Brownie was very grateful to have such a helpful friend.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in a tall tree. He loved to roar loudly every day. One day, he smelled something yummy and followed his nose to find a steak on the ground. 

As he was about to eat the steak, a little bird flew by and said, "That's my dinner! Please don't eat it!" The lion replied, "I'm sorry, but I'm very hungry. I need to eat something." 

The little bird said, "I understand, but please don't eat my dinner. I'm very small and I need it to survive." The lion thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, I won't eat your steak. I'll find something else to eat." 

But as the lion was walking away, he accidentally knocked over a beehive. The bees got angry and stung the lion. He was so hurt that he couldn't move. The little bird came back and said, "I'm sorry you got hurt. Can I help you?" But it was too late. The lion had died from the bee stings. The little bird was very sad and flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toys and his dog, Max. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to visit his grandma. Timmy was so happy because he loved his grandma and he always felt welcome at her house.

When they arrived at grandma's house, she gave Timmy a big hug and said, "Welcome, my sweet boy!" Timmy was so happy to see his grandma and he gave her a big smile. They sat down to have some cookies and milk, but Timmy noticed that his grandma looked sad.

He asked her, "What's wrong, grandma?" She replied, "I'm having a difficult time acting happy today." Timmy didn't understand what that meant, so he asked, "What does 'acting' mean?" His grandma explained that sometimes people pretend to be happy even when they're feeling sad inside.

Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Well, I don't want you to act happy. I want you to be happy for real!" His grandma smiled and gave him a big hug. Timmy felt happy because he knew he had made his grandma feel better.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Ken and John. One day, Ken had an idea. He wanted to test if John could swim out to a brown whale! 

John was very excited and he quickly put on his swimming gear. Ken said, â€œBe careful, John!â€ 

John smiled and said, â€œI can do it!â€ He bravely jumped into the water and started swimming towards the whale. 

After a few minutes, John was close enough to touch the whale. He reached out his hand and carefully patted the whale on its back. 

John called out to Ken, â€œI did it! I tested it and I did it!â€ 

Ken smiled and clapped his hands, proud of his best friendâ€™s courage. They spent the rest of the day playing games by the beach.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a charming jeep. It was red and shiny. Everyone loved the jeep. It would drive around the town, making people smile.

One day, a little boy named Tim saw the jeep. He asked his mom, "Can I ride the jeep, please?" His mom said, "Yes, but be careful." Tim was so happy. He climbed into the jeep and started to drive around the town.

Suddenly, the jeep began to vanish. Tim was scared. He tried to stop the jeep, but it was too late. The jeep was gone, and Tim was sad. The town people were sad too. They all missed the charming jeep. The end.

Once there was a mommy who was mad at her daughter. The mommy was very angry, and she was mad that her daughter had made a mess all over the living room.

The mommy started to yell at the daughter. "How dare you make this mess!" the mommy said. Her voice was very loud and the daughter was scared.

Suddenly, the mommy said that they would go to the ranch. The daughter was confused, because she hadn't heard her mommy say anything about a ranch before.

At the ranch, things were disgusting. There were dirt and bugs everywhere and the daughter felt gross. She wanted to go home, but the mommy said no.

The daughter learned her lesson that day and from then on she was very careful to keep the living room clean.

Lily liked to create things with her crayons and paper. She made pictures of flowers, stars, and animals. One day, she wanted to create something new. She looked at a book and saw a picture of a shrimp. It was pink and had many legs and a long tail. Lily thought it looked funny and cute.

She took a pink crayon and started to draw a shrimp on her paper. She gave it big eyes, a smile, and some dots. She was happy with her creation. She showed it to her mom and said, "Look, mom, I made a shrimp!"

Mom smiled and said, "That's very nice, Lily. What is your shrimp's name?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "His name is Bob. He is a friendly shrimp."

Mom nodded and said, "That's a good name. Do you want to hang your shrimp on the fridge?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, please. I want everyone to see Bob."

Mom helped Lily to hang her shrimp on the fridge with a magnet. Lily was proud of her shrimp. She said, "Bye, Bob. I'll see you later."

But when Lily came back from playing outside, she saw that her shrimp was gone. She looked around and saw her brother, Tom, holding her paper. He had torn it into pieces and was laughing. He said, "Your shrimp is silly and ugly. I don't like it. I made it better."

Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "No, you didn't. You ruined it. That was my shrimp. His name was Bob. He was friendly. You are mean and fierce. Give me back my shrimp."

Tom said, "No, I won't. It's mine now. Go away."

Lily ran to mom and told her what Tom did. Mom was not happy. She said, "Tom, that was not nice. You should not take and destroy Lily's things. You should apologize and make it up to her."

Tom said, "But I don't like her shrimp. It's stupid."

Mom said, "It doesn't matter if you like it or not. It was her creation. She worked hard on it and she loved it. You should respect her feelings and her work. How would you feel if someone did that to your things?"

Tom thought for a while and realized that he would feel bad if someone did that to his things. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I shouldn't have taken and torn your shrimp. Can I help you make a new one?"

Lily said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Yes, you can help me make a new one. Maybe we can make a friend for Bob."

Tom said, "Okay, let's do that. What should we name him?"

Lily said, "How about Tim?"

Tom said, "That sounds good. Let's go get some crayons and paper."

Mom smiled and said, "That's very nice of you, Tom. I'm proud of you. And I'm proud of you, Lily. You are very creative and kind. You both learned a valuable lesson today. You should always treat others the way you want to be treated."

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a very loud mushroom. He liked to polish things all day long. He polished toys, books, and even the chairs. He was very proud of all his polishing. 

One day, he saw a very shiny rock. He picked it up and started to polish it. The mushroom worked hard and polished the rock very well. He was so happy with the job he did.

But then, something peculiar happened. The rock suddenly started to grow larger and larger. It became so big that it was bigger than the mushroom was! The mushroom quickly backed away, frightened.

But then, the very loud mushroom started to laugh. He had found a big mushroom! He ran and started to polish it, just like he polished all the other things. Soon, the mushroom was as shiny as it could be. The loud mushroom was so proud of his new shiny mushroom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She loved exploring, so she decided to go on a trip with her family. She packed her bag with all the necessities, and brought along a sailor to take them away.

The day was sunny as they waved goodbye to their family and friends. The little girl and the sailor hopped into the boat and sailed away. They sailed for hours, passing by palm trees and small islands. 

The little girl was so excited that she wanted to scream, but the sailor told her they had to be quiet while they sailed. They had to be careful of the giant fish that could bite them in the water. 

Finally, after hours of sailing, the little girl and the sailor arrived at a new place. It was far away from their home, and everything was different there. The air was salty and bitter. The little girl didn't know what to do.

The sailor smiled kindly and said, "Let's explore and see what we can find here."

The little girl smiled and nodded, and off they went. Together, they explored the island, having a great adventure. Every day, the little girl was grateful that she had the courage to pack her bags and go on the trip.

Once there was a little girl. She liked playing at the beach. One day she and her mom went to the beach together. When they got there, the girl saw a playful tide. She wanted to go and play in it. 

The playful tide was very special. The girl wanted to belong to the cheerful tide. She walked towards it and the tide seemed to accept her. She enjoyed playing with it. 

The tide tickled her toes, it even gave her rides. The girl laughed and laughed as the playful tide created waves around her. She felt as if she belonged to it and the tide belonged to her. 

The girl and her mom stayed at the beach until the tide got too low. Then they packed up and went home. The little girl never forgot the wonderful time she spent with the playful tide.

Once upon a time, there was a dark rug.

The rug was sat by a river, and one day, the sun was so hot that the rug started to soak.

A little girl came along and saw what was happening. She was so excited that she shouted to her best friend.

"Look! The rug is soaking!"

Her best friend went over to take a closer look. She saw the dark rug soaking up the water.

"It's so cool!" She said.

The two friends laughed together and decided to splash each other and soak their feet in the river. They had so much fun that they stayed until the sun went down. When they were done, the dark rug was completely dry.

The two friends said goodbye and promised to meet up the next day. Since then, the dark rug has stayed dry and the two friends have enjoyed many more days of fun at the river.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy gear. It couldn't do much except share drinks.

One day, it clumsily tried to pour some juice. It spilt it everywhere, but that didn't stop it. It kept trying, splashing the drink all around.

Finally it got it right. It filled up two cups and then took them to two kids. One had big eyes and the other had little eyes. They both smiled and clapped.

The gear felt proud that it could give the children something nice to drink. The two kids thanked the gear with big hugs.

The gear was happy and so were the kids. And they all drank their drinks and had a great time. The End.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Sam and Rhonda. One day, Sam wanted to go to the movies, so she asked Rhonda if she wanted to come. Rhonda eagerly said yes and they went to buy tickets.

When they got to the ticket booth, the clerk said they each had to buy a ticket. Sam gave the clerk some money and said, "One ticket, please." The clerk handed Sam the ticket and Sam gave it to Rhonda. Rhonda looked at her ticket. It had an unknown symbol written on it.

Sam said to Rhonda, "Let's go watch a movie!" When they got to the theater, they each showed the ticket to the man at the door. He smiled and said, "Enjoy your movie!"

So, Sam and Rhonda watched the movie. They laughed, jumped, clapped and cheered during the movie. Even though the movie was unknown, Sam and Rhonda had a lot of fun. They had a great time together. 

The End

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. Sam has many cars and trucks. He is rich. Ben has only one car. He is not rich.

One day, Sam and Ben go to the park. They see a big hill. Sam says, "Let's play on the hill. We can race our cars and trucks down the hill. I will win because I have more cars and trucks than you."

Ben says, "OK, let's play. But I can win too. My car is fast and strong. It has a name. Its name is Red."

Sam says, "A name? That is silly. Cars and trucks don't have names. They are just toys. I have many toys. I don't need to name them."

They go to the top of the hill. They put their cars and trucks on the ground. They say, "Ready, set, go!" They push their cars and trucks down the hill.

Sam's cars and trucks go fast. But they also go wild. They bump into each other. They crash and break. They stop before the end of the hill.

Ben's car goes fast too. But it also goes straight. It does not bump or crash. It reaches the end of the hill. It is the winner.

Ben is happy. He says, "See? Red is the best car. It has a name. It has a friend. It has me."

Sam is sad. He says, "Oh no. My cars and trucks are broken. They are not fun anymore. They are just trash."

Ben says, "Don't be sad, Sam. You can play with Red. Red can share. Red can be your friend too."

Sam says, "Thank you, Ben. Thank you, Red. You are both nice. Can I name one of your trucks?"

Ben says, "Sure, Sam. You can name one of my trucks. What do you want to name it?"

Sam thinks for a moment. He says, "I want to name it Blue. Blue is a good name. Blue is a good color. Blue is a good friend."

Once upon a time there was a nice fairy. She was very small and hid in the garden.

One day when the sun was shining, a little boy named Timmy went to the garden. He saw something sparkling in the grass. Timmy was curious and bent down to take a closer look. 

He said, "Wow! Is that a fairy?"

The fairy blinked and nodded. She said, "Yes, it is me! My name is Rose."

Timmy smiled. He asked Rose, "Do you want to play with me?"

Rose giggled. She said, "Yes, let's have some fun!"

So Timmy and Rose played together in the garden all afternoon. When it was time to go home, Timmy said goodbye and thanked Rose for such a fun day.

The little fairy waved goodbye and said, "You're welcome! I hope to see you again soon!"

Bob was out for a walk in the forest. Suddenly he saw something shiny in the leaves. He bent down to take a closer look. What he found was a berry that was so juicy and yummy looking! He couldn't resist picking it up and eating it.

But the berry was not alone. He looked around and saw many more. Bob was so excited. He gathered as many of these tasty berries as he could and started to put them in his basket.

Suddenly, he heard a voice, "What do you think you're doing?" He looked around and saw a little girl. She was very messy with leaves and dirt all over her clothes. She asked him "Why are you picking my berries?"

Bob replied, "I'm sorry I didn't know they were yours. I just thought I'd find some yummy berries!".

The little girl smiled. "That's ok, I'm happy to share. Just make sure you don't make a mess. Choose the berries carefully."

Bob gave her a big smile. He thanked her and continued to hunt for berries. He picked the biggest and juiciest ones he could find and eventually filled his basket. He had fun and made sure he didn't leave a messy trail. The little girl even gave him an extra berry for being so careful. Bob was happy to have found so many delicious berries, and to have made a new friend.

Once there was a girl called Jane. She was very shy and always preferred to stay alone. As Jane grew, she wanted to make friends but felt too scared to try. One day, she decided to take a chance.

Jane walked up to the group of children and slowly said, "Hi." The children turned to her in surprise.

"What do you want?" asked the tallest boy.

"I was wondering if I could join you," Jane answered.

The children looked at one another and then smiled. "Sure! We'd love it if you'd play with us," said the same tall boy.

Jane smiled, her face turning red. She was so excited to make friends. They played all sorts of games, even with a thermometer that the tall boy had added. And, before she knew it, Jane had made a brand new group of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a fast car named Zoomy. Zoomy loved to race with his friends. One day, Zoomy and his friend, Slowpoke, were talking.

Zoomy said, "I am fast and you are slow. Let's race!"

Slowpoke did not like this idea. Slowpoke said, "No, I disagree. I do not want to race."

Zoomy was sad, but he understood. He knew he needed fuel to race. So, he went to the fuel place to get some.

At the fuel place, Zoomy saw a big truck named Biggie. Biggie was getting fuel too. Zoomy said, "Hi, Biggie! Do you want to race with me?"

Biggie smiled and said, "Sure, Zoomy! Let's race!"

Zoomy and Biggie raced and had lots of fun. Zoomy was happy he found a new friend to race with. And Slowpoke was happy too, because he did not have to race. They all played together and were very good friends.

Tom and Anna are having lunch with Mom and Dad. They have soup and bread and cheese. Tom likes soup, but Anna does not. She makes a face and pushes her bowl away.

"Anna, you have to eat your soup. It is good for you," Mom says.

"I don't like soup. It is hot and wet and yucky," Anna says.

"Look, Anna, you can use your fork to eat the cheese. Cheese is yummy and soft and yellow," Dad says. He shows Anna how to cut the cheese with his fork.

Anna looks at Dad's fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth. She likes Dad's fork. She reaches for it, but Dad stops her.

"No, Anna, this is my fork. You have your own fork. It is smaller and easier for you to hold," Dad says. He gives Anna her fork. It is not as big or shiny as Dad's fork. It has three teeth and a pink handle.

Anna looks at her fork. She does not like her fork. It is small and dull and has a silly color. She throws her fork on the floor and cries.

"Anna, that is not nice. You have to pick up your fork and say sorry," Mom says.

Anna does not want to pick up her fork or say sorry. She is angry and sad. She wants a big fork like Dad's. She thinks it is not fair.

Tom looks at Anna. He feels sorry for her. He likes his sister, even when she is silly. He has an idea. He picks up his fork and gives it to Anna.

"Here, Anna, you can have my fork. It is big and shiny and has four teeth, like Dad's. I don't mind. I can use my spoon to eat my soup," Tom says.

Anna looks at Tom's fork. She is surprised and happy. She takes Tom's fork and smiles.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good brother. I am sorry I was mean," Anna says.

Mom and Dad look at Tom and Anna. They are proud and happy. They hug their children and praise them.

"That was very kind of you, Tom. You are a good sharer. And that was very nice of you, Anna. You are a good apologizer. We love you both very much," Mom and Dad say.

Tom and Anna hug Mom and Dad back. They love them too. They eat their lunch with their forks and spoons. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very excited for her special trip! She had a passport in her hand and was ready to go. 

Before she could go, her mother said to Sarah, "Let's decorate your passport!" 

Sarah smiled and said, "Yes, let's do it!"

She and her mother went to the kitchen and gathered some colorful markers, stickers, and glitter. Then they went to the living room and got to work.

They carefully decorated Sarah's passport with the colorful markers, stickers, and glitter. Sarah loved the way it looked when they were done! 

"Now you are ready for your trip," said her mother. 

Sarah was so excited and couldn't wait. With her decorated passport in her hand, Sarah was off on her special trip!

One day, a sleepy boy named Tim went to play a sport. He liked to play with a ball. His friend, Sam, came to play too.

"Let's play!" yelled Sam. But Tim was too sleepy to play well. Sam got mad and yelled, "You are not good today!"

The sky got dark and it looked like rain. Tim felt bad and wanted to go home. Sam threw the ball one more time. Tim tried to catch it, but he fell down.

In the end, Tim got hurt and went home sad. Sam felt bad too. They should have stopped playing when Tim was sleepy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sun. One day, she saw a big bucket and wanted to fill it with water. She went to the hose and turned it on. The water filled the bucket and she splashed her hands in it. Suddenly, she felt a sharp pain in her thumb. She cried a little bit, but her mom came and hugged her. She felt calm and safe in her mom's arms. From then on, she was more careful when playing with water. The end.

Sam and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a red car. The car is tough. It can go fast and make loud noises.

One day, Sam and Mia want to play with the car. But they cannot find it. They look in their room, in the living room, in the kitchen, but the car is not there. They are sad and confused.

"Where is our car?" Sam asks Mia.

"I don't know. Maybe Mom or Dad took it?" Mia says.

They go to Mom and Dad. They ask them about the car. Mom and Dad shake their heads. They say they did not see the car.

"Maybe it is outside?" Dad says.

Sam and Mia run to the backyard. They look under the tree, behind the swing, in the sandbox, but the car is not there. They are more sad and more confused.

"Where is our car?" Mia asks Sam.

"I don't know. Maybe someone stole it?" Sam says.

They start to cry. They miss their car. They want to play with it.

But then, they hear a familiar noise. It is the car. It is coming from the garage. They run to the garage. They see their car. It is on a shelf. It is next to a big box.

"Look, there is our car!" Sam says.

"How did it get there?" Mia says.

They climb on a stool. They reach for the car. They are happy and relieved.

They see a note on the car. It is from their big brother, Ben. It says:

"Sorry, I borrowed your car for a school project. I forgot to tell you. Here is your car. It is tough. I hope you are not mad. Love, Ben."

Sam and Mia smile. They are not mad. They are glad. They hug their car. They thank Ben. They go to play with their car. They have fun. They love their car. The car is tough. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tony. One day, Tony was walking in the woods when he found a pole leaning against a tree. Tony wanted to play, so he lay down on the ground and grabbed the pole. The pole was very long and open at one end. 

As Tony was playing with the pole, he noticed a hole in the ground. It was open and looked like it was made by the pole. Tony looked inside the hole and saw a snake inside! Tony was scared and tried to run away, but the snake bit his hand. 

Tony screamed and tried to get away, but it was too late. The snakeâ€™s bite was very dangerous and Tony died moments later.

The forest was now very silent. Tonyâ€™s parents never knew what happened to their little boy. They spent many days looking for him, but they never found him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily found a glove on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"What is it?" asked Timmy.

"It's a glove," replied Lily.

"What's a glove?" asked Timmy.

"It's something you wear on your hand to keep it warm," explained Lily.

Timmy looked at the glove and said, "I don't know who it belongs to."

Lily suggested, "Let's discuss what we can do to find the owner."

They went around the neighborhood asking if anyone had lost a glove. After a while, they found a lady who said it was her glove. She was very happy and thanked Lily and Timmy for finding it.

From that day on, Lily and Timmy were known as the "glove detectives" in their neighborhood. They loved helping people find their unknown items.

Tom and Anna are twins. They share a big bed with a blue sheet. But they do not like to share. They always fight for the sheet. They pull and tug and kick and scream.

One night, Mom hears them and comes to their room. She is not happy. She says, "Stop fighting, you two! You are making too much noise. You are driving me crazy!"

Tom and Anna stop and look at Mom. They are scared. They do not want to make Mom crazy. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We just want the sheet."

Mom sighs. She has an idea. She says, "How about we separate the sheet? I can cut it in half. Then you each have your own sheet. No more fighting. OK?"

Tom and Anna think. They like the idea. They nod and say, "OK, Mom. Thank you, Mom."

Mom smiles. She gets scissors and cuts the sheet in half. She gives one half to Tom and one half to Anna. They wrap themselves in their own sheet. They are happy. They say, "Good night, Mom. We love you, Mom."

Mom says, "Good night, Tom. Good night, Anna. I love you, too. Sleep tight. Don't let the bed bugs bite."

Mom turns off the light and leaves. Tom and Anna snuggle in their own sheet. They do not fight anymore. They fall asleep. They dream of happy things.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, he noticed a ladder leaning against his neighbor's house. Timmy wanted to climb the ladder, but he was too scared. 

Later that day, Timmy's neighbor, Mr. Smith, came over to say hello. Mr. Smith was very friendly and always had a smile on his face. Timmy's mom welcomed him inside and they all sat down to have some cookies and milk. 

After they finished their snacks, Mr. Smith said to Timmy, "I have a surprise for you outside." Timmy was very curious and followed Mr. Smith outside. To his surprise, Mr. Smith had set up the ladder for Timmy to climb! Timmy was so happy and climbed all the way to the top. 

From that day on, Timmy and Mr. Smith became good friends. Timmy would often visit Mr. Smith and they would do fun things together like play catch or go for walks. Timmy was grateful for the ladder and for his new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lacy. She was very happy, playful and loved to explore her world. 

Every day, Lacy had lots of fun as she played in her backyard. She always ran around the garden with the sun shining on her back.

One day, when Lacy was playing outside, she heard something in the bushes. She looked around and saw a small furry creature looking back at her. It was a tiny little fox, just like she had seen on TV. She was so excited and shouted, "Mine!"

The fox, who was also very playful, didn't run away and even came closer. Lacy started petting the fox and ever since then, the fox became her best friend. 

From that day onward, Lacy and the fox went on many adventures together, running and playing through the garden and discovering the world around them.

Little did Lacy know that one day, the fox would protect her from danger. But that's a story for another day!

Once upon a time, there was a garden with lots of fruit and vegetables. The little girl who lived in the garden was very polite. Every day, she picked the best looking tomatoes and cucumbers, and then she cooked them. She would mix them together, add a pinch of salt, and then stir the mixture.

The girl loved to eat what she made, and she always shared it with her friends who lived nearby. Sometimes they all cooked together, and they would each bring a different ingredient. One day, the girl's friend brought an inch of ginger root. It smelled delicious, and it tasted really good with the tomatoes and cucumbers.

So from then on, the polite little girl and her friends cooked together and enjoyed their delicious creations. The end.

There was a little girl named Julie. She was only 3 years old. One day she wanted to play with her ball. She ran outside to the garden with it. She was so happy. She ran and ran, kicking her ball further and further away from her.

Suddenly she felt a sharp pain in her ankle. She started to cry. She wanted to go back inside but the pain was too strong. She sat down and cried.

Just then, a yellow bird came to sit on a tree next to her. The bird started to chirp and flew around her. This made Julie stop crying. She looked up at the bird and smiled.

The bird flew away but Julie wasn't sad anymore. She slowly walked back inside, trying to complete her game of ball. When she got back, her mom hugged her and kissed her pain away. Everything was complete again.

Maggie went to the park with her mom. It was a sunny day, but Maggie was feeling miserable. Suddenly she saw a beautiful crystal lying in the grass. She ran over to it and picked it up. It shone in the sunlight and Maggie knew it was special.

Maggie was so happy that she ran back to her mom and showed her the crystal. Her mom smiled and hugged her. Maggie was glad to have the crystal that made her happy.

But then Maggie accidentally dropped the crystal and it broke into many pieces. She started to cry. She felt so sad and miserable. Her mom came over and hugged her tight.

"It is ok", her mom said. Maggie knew that even though the crystal was broken, it had still made her happy for a little time. She dried her eyes, and her mom and her went home. Even though the crystal was broken, Maggie still remembered the wonderful feeling she'd felt when she found it.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Flopsy. Flopsy loved to play outside in the grass and hop around. But one day, Flopsy got very tired and needed to take a nap. So, Flopsy hopped over to a cozy spot under a tree and closed his eyes.

While Flopsy was napping, a butterfly flew by and got caught in a net. The net was hanging from a tree branch and the butterfly couldn't get free. The butterfly felt frustrated and sad.

When Flopsy woke up from his nap, he saw the butterfly in the net and knew he had to help. Flopsy hopped over to the tree and nibbled at the net until the butterfly was free. The butterfly was so happy and thanked Flopsy for his help. From that day on, Flopsy and the butterfly were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear. He didn't like to play, he just liked to be alone. One day, he decided he wanted to try something new. He decided to the swing in the park. 

He hopped onto the swing and pushed off the ground. He whooshed back and forth, feeling happier than before. As he was swinging, he spotted something soar through the sky - it was a missile. 

He got excited and decided to try to grab the missile. He jumped off the swing and ran to the sky, but he was too slow! The missile kept flying higher and higher, until it was out of sight. 

The grumpy bear was sad. He had missed the missile. He shuffled back to the swing, but suddenly felt much happier. Even though he had missed the missile, he realized that the swing was fun. And he never stopped swinging again!

â€œWow. Look at all the bright colors!â€ said Maggie.
