Once, there was a lovely turkey. This turkey had many friends. They all lived on a big farm.

One day, the turkey and a pig had a fight. The pig was sad and the turkey was mad. They did not want to be friends anymore. The turkey did not forgive the pig.

The farmer saw the fight. He was not happy. He wanted all the animals to be friends. But the turkey did not listen. The farmer was very sad.

In the end, the turkey did not have any friends. All the animals stayed away from the turkey. The turkey was sad and alone. The lovely farm was not happy anymore.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a pretty fountain. The water in the fountain went up and down, and many kids loved to play near it. One sunny day, a little boy named Tim and a little girl named Sue were playing by the fountain.

Tim saw a small bird near the fountain that looked sad and helpless. He told Sue, "Look, the bird can't fly. Let's help it!" Sue nodded, and they both went near the bird. They were very gentle and kind to the bird.

Tim and Sue talked to their mom and dad about the bird. They said, "Can we help the bird get better?" Their mom and dad agreed to help. They all took care of the bird together. Soon, the bird was strong and happy again.

One day, the bird flew away, and Tim and Sue were sad. But their mom and dad told them, "You did a good thing. You helped the bird when it needed you." Tim and Sue felt proud and happy.

The moral of the story is to be kind and help others when they need it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to play outside. One day, as she was playing, she saw a stranger. The little girl was scared and wanted to get away, so she started hurrying back to her house.

When she got there, she felt safe. Her mom was there too, and she gave the little girl a big hug. The little girl felt very good. 

The mom asked the little girl about the stranger, but the little girl couldn't describe him. She just said she was scared and hurried away. 

The mom told the little girl she did the right thing, and that she should always hurry home if she ever feels scared around someone she doesn't know. 

The little girl smiled and hugged her mom again. She knew she had done something good. And from then on, she would always remember what her mom told her and hurry home if she ever saw a stranger.

Lily liked to dance. She danced in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. She danced with her doll, her teddy, and her cat. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the kitchen. She danced when she was happy, when she was sad, and when she was bored.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, you have to stop dancing now. It is time to clean your room. Look at all the cloth on the floor. You have to put them in the box."

Lily did not want to stop dancing. She wanted to keep dancing with her cat. She said, "No, mom, I want to dance. Dancing is fun. Cleaning is not fun."

Her mom said, "Lily, you have to be obedient. Cleaning is good. Dancing is good, too, but not all the time. If you clean your room, you can dance later. If you don't clean your room, you can't dance at all."

Lily did not like that. She felt angry. She said, "No, no, no! I don't want to clean. I want to dance. You can't tell me what to do."

Her mom said, "Lily, that is not nice. You have to listen to me. I am your mom. I love you, but I also have to teach you. You have to do what I say. Now, go and clean your room, or you will be in trouble."

Lily knew her mom was serious. She knew she had to do what her mom said, or she would be sad. She did not want to be sad. She wanted to be happy. She wanted her mom to be happy, too. She said, "OK, mom, I will clean my room. But can I dance after I clean?"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily, you can dance after you clean. But you have to clean well. And you have to be quick. Then you can dance as much as you want."

Lily said, "OK, mom, I will do that. I will be obedient. I will clean well. And I will be quick. Then I will dance with you. Can you dance with me, mom?"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily, I can dance with you. I like dancing, too. But first, we have to clean. Come on, let's go and clean your room."

Lily and her mom went to clean her room. They put all the cloth in the box. They made her bed. They threw away the trash. They dusted the shelf. They cleaned her room well. And they were quick.

Then they went to the kitchen. They put on some music. They danced with each other. They danced with the doll, the teddy, and the cat. They danced in the morning, in the afternoon, and at night. They danced when they were happy, when they were sad, and when they were bored. They danced and they laughed. They had fun. They were happy.

Once there was a mighty bear, who lived in a big blue house. Every morning he woke up with a wink and gave the world a mighty smile. 

One day when he was walking in the park, he found a little toy. It was red and looked like a car, but it had no wheels. He thought the car was lonely, so he decided to replace the wheels. 

He searched around the park, and looked underneath the trees, until he found two round rocks. He put the rocks on the car and smiled. Then he gave the car a gentle push and watched it roll away. 

The bear waved goodbye and wiggled his nose. He was proud that he had helped the car, and with a wink of his eye, he smiled and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a litttle girl called Ella. Every night Ella would lay in bed and count the stars in the sky. Ella loved to look up and count how many stars there were.

One night, Ella noticed the stars were not twinkling as bright as they usually did. Ella's worry grew and she wondered why this was.

Suddenly, Ella's mommy appeared beside her bed. Her mommy smiled at Ella and said, "Don't worry Ella, the stars are still available to count." Ella smiled and her worry melted away.

Ella thanked her mommy and with a hug and a kiss, Ella was soon back counting the stars and happily dreaming away.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy was very thin and he always felt hungry. One day, he saw a big hotel and decided to go inside to find some food. When he got inside, he saw a big piece of cheese on a table. He wanted to eat it, but he knew he had to be careful because there were many people around.

Timmy thought of a plan to get the cheese. He climbed up on a chair and jumped onto the table. As he was about to grab the cheese, a cat appeared out of nowhere! Timmy quickly ran away, but he knew he had to try again to succeed.

The next day, Timmy went back to the hotel and saw the cheese again. This time, he waited until the cat was sleeping before he climbed up on the table. He grabbed the cheese and ran away as fast as he could. Timmy succeeded in getting the cheese and he learned that if he tried hard enough, he could achieve anything he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and she was very curious. One day, she asked her mom if she could have some shrimp for dinner. Her mom said no, because it was too expensive. Jane got angry and demanded shrimp. Her mom said no again and Jane started to cry.

Just then, Jane noticed something pink out of the corner of her eye. It was a magical box with a big, pink shrimp inside. Jane wanted the shrimp more than ever and she demanded it. Her mom was hesitant but she finally agreed that Jane could have it.

Jane was so excited! She clapped her hands and laughed. She thanked her mom, grabbed the pink shrimp and ran outside to play. She was so happy to have a special treat. Jane's mom smiled and felt relieved that Jane was content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved animals. One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She saw many animals like lions, monkeys, and elephants. But her favorite animal was the zebra. She loved the black and white stripes on its body.

As she was looking at the zebras, she saw a little boy who looked frightened. She asked him what was wrong. He said he was scared of the lions. Lily told him not to be frightened and that she would protect him. They both gazed at the lions from a safe distance.

After a while, they went to see the zebras again. The little boy said, "Thank you for protecting me. You are very brave." Lily smiled and said, "It's always good to help others. That's what friends do." The little boy smiled and they both continued to gaze at the zebras. From that day on, they became good friends and went to the zoo together every weekend.

Sara and Ben are friends who like to play in the garden. They have a big sunflower that they water every day. The sunflower is very tall and has a bright yellow face.

One day, a lady comes to the garden. She has a basket of seeds and a hat. She smiles at Sara and Ben and says hello.

"Hello, lady," Sara says. "What do you have in your basket?"

"I have some seeds for you," the lady says. "They are sunflower seeds. You can plant them and grow more sunflowers like this one."

"Wow, thank you, lady," Ben says. "We love sunflowers. They are our favorite flowers."

The lady gives them some seeds and shows them how to plant them in the soil. She says they need to water them and give them lots of sun.

"Can we plant them anywhere?" Sara asks.

"Well, you can, but I recommend that you plant them in a regular pattern," the lady says. "That way, they will look nice and neat and you can see them all."

"What is a regular pattern?" Ben asks.

"A regular pattern is when you plant them in a row or a circle or a square," the lady says. "Like this." She draws some shapes in the dirt with her finger.

"Oh, I see," Sara says. "That looks pretty. Let's plant them in a circle around our big sunflower."

"Okay, let's do that," Ben says.

They plant the seeds in a circle and water them. They thank the lady and wave goodbye. They are happy and excited to see their new sunflowers grow. They hope they will be as tall and bright as their big sunflower.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved exploring. She had been playing all afternoon and as the evening sky turned a deep pink, the little girl had gotten really hungry.

So, she asked her mom if she could have something to eat.

"Okay," said mom. "Why don't you guess what's for dinner?"

The little girl smiled and carefully thought about what it could be. "Is it something delicious?" She asked hopefully.

Mom smiled. "Yes, it is something very delicious," she said.

The little girl clapped her hands and was so excited. She had just guessed correctly! As she enjoyed her delicious evening meal, she thought about how wonderful it was that she was able to guess what it was.

John was an impatient boy. He wanted to read a novel, but he couldn't decide which one. He asked his Mom, but she said she couldn't decide for him. Soon John became even more impatient. 

But then an idea popped into his head. He decided to ask his big sister! She was very smart and usually had good ideas. When John asked, she had just the right book. She said it was called The Cat in the Hat. 

John was so excited. He could not believe it! He quickly grabbed the book, and raced to his bedroom to begin reading. He was so happy he had decided to ask his sister.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had an old teddy bear named Teddy that she loved very much. One day, Lily saw a new teddy bear at the store and she wished she could have it. She asked her mommy if they could buy it, but her mommy said they didn't have enough money.

Lily was sad, but she still loved her old Teddy. She played with him every day and took him everywhere she went. One day, while they were playing in the park, a little boy came up to Lily and asked if he could buy Teddy. Lily didn't want to sell her beloved Teddy, but the little boy offered to trade his new teddy bear for old Teddy.

Lily thought about it and realized that she could make a wish come true by trading Teddy for the new teddy bear. So, she agreed to the trade and the little boy was very happy with his new old teddy bear. Lily was happy too, because she now had a new teddy bear that she loved just as much as her old one.

John was in the park with his Mom. He loved the park and he was always looking out for animals. Suddenly, he saw something in the distance - it was a big, green dinosaur! John was so excited so he couldn't help running towards it.

John's Mom yelled after him and warned him to stop. She said to John, "The dinosaur is not available John. You cannot go near it."

John stopped and looked at the dinosaur. He couldn't believe that a real, living dinosaur was right in front of him. He wanted to get closer but he listened to his Mom and stayed where he was. 

John waved goodbye to the dinosaur as he and his Mom left the park. John was happy to have seen a dinosaur and he smiled the whole way home, thinking about his special sighting.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jody. She was three-years-old and very curious. Jody was playing in the living room, and noticed something very interesting. On the shelf, there was something that was very clean. She walked closer and noticed it was a sparkly toy. She stopped and paused for a moment. Then she reached up and carefully took it off the shelf. Jody looked at the toy with excitement, and could not believe her luck. She ran off into the next room and started playing. She smiled at the toy and knew that it would be her new best friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so excited, and she had something very special to do. She went to the shop with her mom. 

The little girl saw something she wanted to buy, it was a rabbit. She asked Mom if she could buy it, and Mom said yes.

The rabbit was so friendly! The little girl was so happy. She hugged it and said, "Hi, Rabbit, I'm your friend."

The rabbit was so happy too. The little girl took it home and she fed it and played with it. The rabbit was so happy to have a new friend.

The little girl and the rabbit became the best of friends. They had so much fun, playing together and cuddling up at night. They were the best of friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat dessert, especially ice cream. One day, her mommy made a nice chocolate cake for her to eat after dinner. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to eat it.

But when it was time for dessert, Lily's little brother spilled his milk all over the cake. Lily's mommy tried to clean it up, but it was too late. Lily was sad and asked her mommy to pause for a moment. She didn't want to eat the cake anymore because it wasn't nice anymore.

Lily's mommy felt bad and tried to make it up to her by giving her some ice cream instead. But Lily was still upset and didn't want anything. She went to bed without eating any dessert. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a thin little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the hot sun. One day, he saw a cactus and wanted to touch it. His mommy signed to him to not touch it, but Timmy didn't listen. He touched the cactus and it hurt him a lot. 

Timmy cried and cried, but his mommy signed that she would make it better. She tried to take out the needles, but it was too hard. Timmy had to go to the hospital. The doctor signed that Timmy had to stay there for a few days. 

Timmy was very sad and missed his mommy and his toys. But then he saw some other kids in the hospital and they played together. They played games and drew pictures. Timmy was happy again. But then, one day, Timmy got very sick and he had to go to sleep forever. His mommy was very sad and missed him very much. The end.

Mommy and baby went for a walk. The grass was green and there were birds in the sky. Baby looked up and smiled.

"Let's relax, baby," said mommy.

Baby kicked her legs and laid her head down in the grass. She felt the sun on her face and listened to the birds. It was very peaceful.

But then baby's head got dirty! She sat up and reached up to her head.

"Oh, no!" said mommy. "Let's go wash that off."

They went back home and mommy put baby in the warm bath. Baby felt the water on her head as she relaxed and smiled.

When baby was clean she felt much better. She laid back and smiled as her mommy dried her off with a warm towel.

"That's much better," said mommy. "Now, let's go and find more birds!"

Once there was a large kitchen. Everything in the kitchen was big. The cabinets were big, the oven was big, and the fridge was also big.

One day, a little boy wanted to help in the kitchen. He wanted to be just like his dad and help prepare dinner. So his mom gave him a big spoon and told him to stir the soup. The little boy was so happy! He was supporting the family by helping in the kitchen.

Soon, the little boy was helping to cook dinner every day. He was becoming an expert in the kitchen. His mom was so proud of him. He was a big helper in the kitchen and the family was thankful for his support.

From then on, the big kitchen was always filled with laughter. The little boy was a big part of that!

Tom is a boy who likes to play with balloons. He has many balloons of different colors and shapes. He likes to blow them up and tie them with strings. He likes to make them bounce and fly in the air.

One day, Tom finds a big yellow balloon in his room. He thinks it is a lemon balloon. He likes lemons because they are sour and make his mouth pucker. He decides to blow up the lemon balloon and see how it tastes. He puts the balloon in his mouth and blows hard.

But the balloon is not a lemon balloon. It is a balloon filled with sour water. When Tom blows hard, the balloon pops and the sour water sprays all over his face. Tom feels a sting in his eyes and a burn in his mouth. He spits out the balloon and screams.

"Ow! Ow! Ow! That hurts! That is not a lemon balloon! That is a bad balloon!" Tom cries.

His mom hears him and runs to his room. She sees him with his face wet and red. She sees the balloon on the floor. She understands what happened. She hugs him and wipes his face with a towel.

"I'm sorry, Tom. That was not a lemon balloon. That was a prank balloon. Someone gave it to me as a joke. I forgot to throw it away. It was not meant for you. It was meant to release sour water and make people laugh. But it was not funny. It was mean. Are you okay?" she asks.

Tom nods. He feels better. He still likes lemons, but he does not like sour water. He does not like prank balloons. He likes his mom. He likes his other balloons. He decides to play with them instead. He picks a blue balloon and ties it with a string. He smiles and releases it in the air. He watches it fly and bounce. He feels happy. He likes balloons.

One day, a mum and her son, Ted, went on a journey. They had a special reason for the journey - a teacher was going to teach Ted all about plants. Mum showed Ted a bright flower. "This flower is alive", the teacher said. Then he showed Ted a dead flower. "This flower is dead," the teacher said. Ted looked very sad. "Don't worry, Ted," the teacher said kindly. "We can teach you all about how to grow plants and you can help them to stay alive." Ted smiled. He knew his journey with his mum and the teacher was filled with possibilities.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red boat. It loved to sail on the water. The boat had a friend, a little blue car. The blue car lived in a garage.

One day, the boat asked the blue car to sail with it. The blue car was scared, but the boat said it would be fun. So, the blue car got on the boat. They sailed together on the water.

The sun was shining, and the blue car felt comfortable on the boat. They laughed and played all day. When the sun went down, they went back to the blue car's garage. The boat and the blue car were happy to be friends.

Lila and Leo are brother and sister. They like to play together in their room. They have many toys and books and games. But today, they want to do something unusual.

"Let's pretend we are animals," says Lila. "I will be a cat and you will be a dog."

"OK," says Leo. "But what will we do?"

"We will lay on the floor and make noises and chase each other," says Lila. "And we will not use our hands, only our paws."

They start to play. Lila lays on the floor and meows. Leo lays on the floor and barks. They crawl and jump and run around the room. They have fun.

But then, they hear a knock on the door. It is their mom.

"What are you doing, my little ones?" she asks.

Mom smiles. She thinks they are very cute and clever.

Mom thinks for a moment. Then she says, "I will be a bird. And I will lay an egg for you."

She lays on the floor and makes a chirping sound. She pretends to lay an egg with a pillow. Lila and Leo are surprised and happy. They hug the pillow and thank mom.

They continue to play as animals. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a cute dog named Spot. Spot loved to eat. His favorite food was sausage. One day, Spot went for a walk in the park with his owner, Sam.

Sam said, "Spot, listen to me. Do not eat anything you find in the park." Spot wagged his tail and kept walking.

While walking, Spot saw a big sausage on the ground. He remembered what Sam said, but he could not resist. He ate the sausage very fast. Suddenly, Spot felt sick. His tummy hurt a lot. Sam was sad and worried.

The bad ending was that Spot had to go to the vet. The vet said, "Spot should have listened to Sam." The moral of the story is to always listen to the people who care about you. They want to keep you safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books and had many of them on her shelf. One day, she wanted to read a new book but couldn't find it on her shelf. She looked and looked but it wasn't there.

Lily became frustrated because she really wanted to read that book. She asked her mom for help, and together they searched for the book. Finally, they found it hiding behind some other books on the shelf.

Lily was so happy that she found her book and became even more excited to read it. She learned that sometimes things can be hard to find, but with a little help and patience, everything can become okay in the end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Benny and Mindy. They were playing together when Benny challenged Mindy to a race. Mindy agreed, but she was hesitant because Benny was much faster than her. 

â€œCome on, I accept you can do it,â€ Benny said in an encouraging voice.

The moral of this story is that everyone should accept and respect each other's efforts, even if they don't win. Helping each other reach our goals and celebrate each other's successes is better than competing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Binky that she loved very much. One day, Lily's mommy said they were going on a trip to the beach. Lily was very excited and asked if Binky could come too. 

Mommy said yes, but they had to pack their bags first. Lily helped pack her clothes and toys, but she was envious of Binky because he didn't have to pack anything. 

When they arrived at the beach, Lily and Binky had so much fun playing in the sand and swimming in the ocean. But when it was time to go home, Lily didn't want to leave. She said to Binky, "I wish we could stay here forever." 

Binky replied, "I know, but we can always come back next year." Lily smiled and hugged Binky tightly. She was happy to have him with her and knew they would have many more adventures together.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play at the beach. They had a big bucket and a small shovel to make sand castles. They also had a ball to throw and catch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard and pick flowers. One day, while she was playing, she found a safe under a big tree.

Tom and Anna liked to play in the kitchen. They liked to open and close the dishwasher and see the shiny plates and cups inside. They also liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with the pots and pans.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her daddy, who was very strong. He would lift her up high and spin her around. One day, Lily and her daddy went on a walk in the woods. They saw many trees and flowers along the way.

Mama and baby were in the car. They were going to the grocery. Mama was tired, but baby was excited. They drove to the grocery and Mama got out of the car with baby. They went into the grocery and baby saw lots of fun things.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird. He had two wings, one on either side.

Mommy was very excited and she said, "Let's unpack!"

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Ben had a small car. They were having fun until Lily saw Ben's car and wanted it.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big cloth in their room. It was soft and colorful and had many shapes on it. They decided to make a tent with the cloth and some chairs.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Larry and Luke. Larry had an idea to act silly. He wanted to find a funny way to surprise Luke.

Once upon a time there were two little friends, Toby and Emily. They were playing in the park together one sunny day. Toby could see the birds in the sky and hear their songs. â€œThey look so happy!â€ he said, â€œI wish I could fly like them.â€

The moral of the story is: we all have special gifts to share with each other, and it's important that we always be kind to one another.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One sunny day, she went to the park with her mom. Lily's mom told her to wear her sunglasses to protect her eyes from the bright sun.

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there lived a girl named Sue. Sue loved to go for walks on the trail near her house. One sunny day, she decided to take her little brother, Tim, with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to help her mommy. One day, her mommy said, â€œWill you help me make squash?â€ The little girl smiled and said, â€œYes!â€

The little girl and her mommy ate the squash together. It was delicious. The little girl was so proud that she could help make it with her mommy.

One day, Josh and his Mommy went to the market. Josh was excited because he liked going to the market. He liked to look at all the delicious fruits and vegetables.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was 3 years old and very curious. She loved exploring the world around her.

One day, she went out into the garden to explore. She saw butterflies flying around and heard birds chirping. But she also saw a strange plant. It had green leaves, small purple flowers and strange smells. The girl was amazed!

She observed carefully and soon realized it was an herb. She thought it was so creative for the plant to smell so nice! She even touched it to feel the soft leaves.

She looked around and found even more herbs in the garden. They all smelled differently and each one was unique. The girl was so excited and enjoyed learning about them. She even asked her parents if she could start her own herb garden.

The girl had so much fun learning and exploring. She was very creative in finding new herbs, and soon her garden was blooming with all sorts of plants.

Once upon a time, in a big round park, there lived a group of animals. They loved to play games with each other. They were competitive, but they also had a lot of fun.

One day, they decided to play a new game called "Squeeze the Round Ball." The animals took turns to squeeze a big round ball as hard as they could. The one who could squeeze the ball the most would win.

The animals were excited and tried their best to squeeze the ball. The strong animals like the bear and the elephant squeezed the ball really hard, but the smaller animals like the squirrel and the rabbit tried their best too. In the end, the bear won the game. All the animals laughed and clapped for the bear. They had a great time playing the game and promised to play more games together in the big round park.

One day, Mom took Jack and Lucy to the beach. Jack and Lucy were so excited, they could not believe it. 

When they were at the beach, Jack and Lucy saw a big, wide way that went right into the ocean.

Jack asked, "Mom, can I go in the water?"

Jack had fun at the beach that day. He found a way to play without going too deep into the ocean.

The End.

Once there was a mom. She had a shop. It was a very big shop. She liked it very much. 

Every day she would go to the shop and raise her things. She had so many things in her shop. She raised them to the sky and sold them.

One day she wanted to raise something special. She got a big piece of cloth. It was very thick. She wanted to make something special.

She cut the cloth and made a beautiful dress. She put the dress in her shop. Everyone liked it very much.

The mom smiled when she saw how happy people were. They liked the dress so she was very proud of herself. She kept raising more things in her shop and she worked hard!

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big cloud in the sky. It is dark and loud.

"Look, Sam, a storm is coming!" Mia says.

"Let's go to the shelter!" Sam says. The shelter is a small house near the park. It is for people who need a place to stay.

They run to the shelter. They knock on the door. A woman opens it. She has a kind face and a big smile.

"Hello, children, do you need help?" she asks.

"Yes, please, can we sit here until the storm is over?" Mia asks.

"Of course, you can. You are very smart to come here. Come in, I have some cookies and milk for you." she says.

She leads them to a cozy room. There are some books and toys on the shelves. She gives them each a plate of cookies and a glass of milk.

"Thank you, you are very nice." Sam says.

"You are very welcome. What are your names?" she asks.

"I am Sam and this is Mia. We are friends." Sam says.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named John. He was very young and full of joy. One day, John was playing in the park when he fell down. He started to cry as he looked up to the sky.

Suddenly, an old man appeared. He was kind and very compassionate. The old man told John, "Don't worry. Everyone falls down sometimes."

John rolled over and looked at the old man. He asked, "Who are you?"

The old man smiled and said, "I am your youth. I never leave your side, even when you fall. Know that I will always be with you."

John smiled, feeling better now. He thanked the old man and the old man disappeared.

John then stood up and went back to playing in the park. He remembered the old man's words, knowing that no matter what, his youth would never leave him. He had found comfort in the old man's compassionate words.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to play a game of catch. Timmy threw the ball to his friend, but it went too high and hit a tree branch. The branch broke and a part of it fell to the ground.

Timmy's friend picked up the broken branch and they both looked at it. It was hot outside and the broken branch felt warm in their hands. They decided to pass it back and forth to each other like a hot potato. They laughed and had so much fun playing with the broken branch.

When it was time for Timmy to go home, he said goodbye to his friend and went inside. His mom asked him how his day was and he told her all about playing catch and passing the hot branch back and forth. She smiled and was happy to hear that he had a fun day. Timmy went to bed that night with a smile on his face, thinking about the fun he had with his friend.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and loved to write. He wrote stories about all sorts of things: animals, food, even the sky.

One day, Joe found a funny looking patch on the ground. It was a black patch and Joe knew he had to write a story about it. He ran and got his notebook, eager to start writing.

Just then, Joe's mom called out to him. She said, "Joe, what are you doing?"

Joe said, "I'm writing a story about this funny black patch!"

Joe's mom smiled. "That sounds really fun," she said.

So Joe went back to the black patch and started writing. He wrote and wrote until he had finished the story. When it was done, he was very proud of what he had written.

The End.

Tim and Sue like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They run and laugh and have fun. But then the sky turns dark and the wind blows hard. It starts to rain.

"Oh no!" Tim says. "Our kite will get wet!"

"Let's bring it back!" Sue says. "Hurry!"

They run to the kite, but it is too high. The wind pulls it away from them. They try to catch it, but they can't. The kite flies over the fence and into the street.

"Stop!" Tim shouts. "That's our kite!"

He runs after the kite, but Sue grabs his hand.

"Wait!" Sue says. "It's not safe! There are cars!"

Tim looks at the street. He sees the cars zooming by. He sees the kite getting smaller and smaller. He feels sad and angry.

"But I want our kite!" he says. "It's ours!"

"I know," Sue says. "But we can't get it now. It's too wet and too far. Maybe we can find it later. Or maybe we can make a new one."

She hugs him and tries to comfort him. He hugs her back and tries to calm down. They are both wet and troubled. They walk back to the park, holding hands. They hope the rain will stop soon. They hope they will see their kite again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a brilliant idea to make a note for his mom. He took a paper and wrote "I love you, Mom" on it. He put the note in a sack and went outside to play.

While he was playing, he saw a squirrel trying to get some nuts from a sack. Timmy thought it would be funny to put his note in the sack and see what the squirrel would do. So, he put the note in the sack and left it there.

Later, when Timmy's mom came home, she saw the sack with the note in it. She read the note and was so happy. She gave Timmy a big hug and said, "You are so brilliant, Timmy! I love you too." From that day on, Timmy always made sure to tell his mom how much he loved her, even if it wasn't in a note in a sack.

Once, there was a rich mechanic who loved to fold things. Every day, he would take something, like paper or cloth, and carefully fold it into all sorts of beautiful shapes.

One day, he went to the park to work on a new project. As he was folding pieces of paper, a three year old child walked up to him and asked: "What are you doing?"

The mechanic smiled and explained what he was doing. The child had many questions and was curious about each shape the mechanic made.

But as the mechanic folded more and more, he accidentally made a crease in one of the pieces of paper. The three year old started to cry and said: "It's all ruined now!".

The mechanic just looked at the little one and said: "It's ok, no matter how much I fold, I can never make something perfect. That's part of being human, isn't it?". The child smiled and nodded.

The mechanic then bent down and offered the little one a new piece of paper. The mechanic showed the child how to fold it, and together they made many new shapes, each of them perfect in their own way.

One day, Mommy wanted to make some soup. She took out a big pot and filled it with water. Then she put some vegetables inside the pot and turned the stove on to heat it. All of a sudden, there was a loud noise that disturbed Mommy.

Lilah asked, "Mommy what was that noise?" 

Mommy replied, "I don't know, sweetie. Let's go look and see if we can find out what it is."

Mommy quickly covered the pot with a lid to keep the mouse inside and then opened the window. The mouse escaped, but Mommy had to make a new pot of soup. Lilah was happy to help her, and they finished making the soup together.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. They see a big swing. They want to swing on it.

Lily and Ben are happy. They have a new friend. They take the penguin to the swing. They swing with it. They have fun. They laugh. They hug the penguin. They name it Pinky.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Adam and Jack. They were both very kind to each other. One day, Jack took Adam to the zoo.

Jack laughed and said, â€œNo, Adam, itâ€™s too dangerous. The fish might get scared and swim away.â€

He said, â€œHey, Adam, why donâ€™t we find you a small toy tank so you can pretend to crawl inside it and play with the fish?â€

Adamâ€™s eyes lit up. He said, â€œYes, letâ€™s do that!â€ 
 
So, Jack and Adam went to the zoo shop and found a small plastic tank with some toy fish inside. Adam was delighted and thanked Jack for being so kind. From that day on, whenever Adam visited the zoo he would remember his friend Jack and his toy tank full of fish.

Tommy liked to look at the sky and wonder what was up there. He saw birds, clouds, and sometimes airplanes. One day, he saw something new. It was a helicopter. It had a big fan on top and a long tail. It made a loud noise and flew very fast.

Tommy wanted to see the helicopter better. He ran after it, but it was too fast. He did not look where he was going. He crossed the street without looking. A car was coming. It honked and stopped. Tommy was scared. He almost got hit by the car.

The driver got out of the car. He was angry. He yelled at Tommy. He said, "You have to be careful, kid! You can't just run across the street like that! You could get hurt or hurt someone else! You have to look both ways and wait for the green light!"

Tommy felt bad. He said, "I'm sorry, sir. I was looking at the helicopter. It was so colorful and cool. I wanted to see it better."

The driver said, "I understand, kid. Helicopters are cool. But they are not worth risking your life. You have to pay attention to what's around you. You have to be safe and smart. That's more important than anything."

Tommy nodded. He said, "You're right, sir. I learned my lesson. I will be more careful next time. Thank you for stopping and not hitting me."

The driver said, "You're welcome, kid. I'm glad you're okay. Now go home and tell your parents what happened. And maybe they can take you to see a helicopter up close someday."

Tommy said, "Okay, sir. Thank you. Goodbye."

Tommy went home and told his parents what happened. They were worried, but they were also proud. They said, "We're glad you're okay, Tommy. And we're glad you learned your lesson. You have to be careful and follow the rules. But we also know you're curious and love to wonder. That's a good thing. Wondering makes you learn and grow. Just don't forget to be safe and smart too."

Tommy hugged his parents. He said, "I love you, Mom and Dad. And I love to wonder. But I will also be safe and smart. And maybe someday, we can see a helicopter together."

The end.

Mama and Daddy took little Daniel to a place far away. Daniel had never seen anything like it before!

The place was so icy, it made Daniel shiver. Everywhere he looked, he saw mineral rocks of different shapes and sizes.

"What is this place, Mama?" Daniel asked, standing close to his parents.

"This is a mine, Daniel," Mama said, bending down and brushing the snow off one of the mineral rocks.

"A mine?" Daniel asked.

"Yes, sweetheart," Daddy said. "Miners work hard to design this mineral into useful things. They also dig for other useful minerals which are found here."

Daniel looked amazed. He had never seen something like this before. All the icy mineral rocks were so fascinating!

"Come, let's explore," Daddy said, taking Daniel's hand in his. Together, Daniel and his family explored the mine. They had a great time!

John and his mom walked into the valley. It was wide and lonely. John asked, "Mom, why is it so quiet here?"

"This valley used to be filled with many animals and plants, but then something happened," his mom said. "Now, we have to restore it."

John nodded. He liked to pick up leaves and twigs. He wanted to help restore the valley too. He looked around and felt so sorry for the valley. 

Suddenly, a tiny mouse popped up from a hole in the ground. It started to scurry away, but John stopped it.

"Don't be afraid," he said. He reached out his hand and gently picked it up. "You can help restore this valley too."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was only three years old.

One day, she asked her mom for something sweet. Her mom said yes and gave her a blueberry muffin. Jane was so happy! She remembered how sweet it tasted and wanted more.

But Jane didn't remember what her mom said. She kept asking for a muffin. Her mom got tired of her requests and said, "No, Jane. No more muffins today."

Jane was sad, but she didn't give up. She kept asking for a muffin and started to cry. Her mom eventually got angry and said, "That's it! No more muffins for you ever again."

Lily was a little girl who liked to dream. She dreamed of big things, like flying in the sky, or having a pony, or being a princess. She dreamed every night when she went to sleep in her bed.

One night, she had a very strange dream. She dreamed that she was in a big house, with many doors. She wanted to see what was behind the doors, so she opened them one by one. She saw many things, like toys, and flowers, and books. She was happy.

But then she opened a door that was very dark. She was scared, but she was curious. She went inside the dark door, and saw a big monster. The monster had sharp teeth, and red eyes, and hairy arms. The monster roared at her, and said, "I am going to eat you!"

Lily screamed, and tried to run away. But the door was locked, and she could not get out. She cried, and wished she was awake. She wished she was in her bed, with her teddy bear, and her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He liked to use his crayons to draw pictures of animals. One Tuesday, Timmy saw an amazing bird outside. It was very colorful and had a long tail. Once there was a curious little girl called Lucy. She was 3 years old and loved to explore the world around her. Every day she would make new discoveries that filled her with joy.

At the end of the day, Lucy thanked the tutor for teaching her something new. She said goodbye and hugged the tutor before the tutor left with a happy wave.

Lucy was so happy with her new knowledge and couldn't wait for the next tutor to come and teach her even more!

The family was looking for the perfect place to park. They drove for a long time until they found a beautiful country. It was so perfect for them.

The family got out of the car and looked around. They saw big trees and tall mountains. Everything was so green and peaceful.

The father parked the car and the family began to explore. They had a picnic in the sun and walked around. Then the dad started a fire and made dinner for everyone.

When the family was done eating, they all sat by the fire together. They watched the stars come out and it was the perfect evening.

The family went back to the car and drove home. They all had a smile on their face and they were excited to come back to the perfect country again.

The ship took lots of pictures of the island. It used its flexible wings to fly up and over the island. It was such a fun day!

At the end of the day, the ship flew back to its home. It had done its job and taken lots of amazing pictures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, she saw a dolphin dive into the water. Lily thought it was very cool.

Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily didn't want to get wet, so she opened her umbrella. It was pink and had lots of polka dots. She thought it was very impressive.

Lily continued to swim and play in the ocean, but she always kept her umbrella close by in case it rained again. She knew that if she ever needed to, she could dive under the water and stay dry with her impressive umbrella.

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play and have fun. But today, they have to stay in their room. Mom and Dad are busy. They have to talk on the cell. The cell is a thing that makes sounds. Mom and Dad use it to talk to other people.

Tim and Jen are bored. They do not want to stay in their room. They want to go outside and see their friends. They want to play with their toys. They want to watch TV. They do not want to listen to Mom and Dad.

They have an idea. They sneak out of their room. They go to the living room. They see the cell on the table. They pick it up. They press some buttons. They hear a voice.

"Hello? Who is this?" the voice says.

But the voice is not happy. The voice is angry. The voice is loud. The voice is Mom's boss.

Mom and Dad hear the voice. They run to the living room. They see Tim and Jen with the cell. They are shocked. They are mad. They take the cell from them. They say sorry to the voice. They hang up.

They look at Tim and Jen. They are not smiling. They are frowning. They are scolding.

"You are in big trouble!" they say. "You should not touch the cell. You should not bother the voice. You should listen to us. You should stay in your room. You should be quiet."

Mom and Dad are still mad. But they are also kind. They love Tim and Jen. They hug them back.

They say, "We know you are bored. But you have to be good. You have to follow the rules. You have to wait a little bit. Then we can play and have fun. OK?"

Tim and Jen nod. They say, "OK."

They go back to their room. They wait a little bit. They listen to Mom and Dad. They are good. They are not bored. They have each other. They are twins. They are happy.
