But then, Lily had an idea. She went over to the children and showed them her camera. They were amazed and wanted to take pictures too. Lily felt happy because she made new friends and they didn't disturb her anymore. From that day on, Lily and her new friends went to the park together to take pictures and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alex. She was only three years old and loved running around outside.

One day, Alex went to the park. She climbed a tree and perched high in the branches. From her vantage point, she looked down and saw something sparkly around the base of the tree. 

Alex carefully climbed down and noticed it was a spirit made of shiny silver stars. The spirit smiled brightly at Alex and said, "Hello, my name is John. I am very, very busy but I wanted to say hi." Alex was so excited to meet the spirit! 

John asked Alex if she wanted to join him on an adventure. She happily agreed, so the two set off. They went for a long walk, then stopped for a nap under a big tree. After a few minutes, the two were up and running again. Alex had the best time spending the day with John!

Once upon a time, there was a family. They had a big vehicle. Every morning, the dad would get in the vehicle and drove off to work.

He drove really well and was always so successful. One day, he came home and shut the door.

The family was so excited - it was the weekend, and they were going to have lots of fun. They jumped into the vehicle and drove off for the day. They had lots of fun, eating yummy food and going on rides.

At the end of the day, the dad shut the door of the vehicle and the family drove back home. They were all so happy and successful.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw a pretty flower. The flower was red and yellow. Lucy wanted to pick the flower, but she did not know how.

A friendly bird saw Lucy. The bird said, "Hi, Lucy! Do you need help?" Lucy said, "Yes, I want to pick the flower, but I can't." The bird said, "I can help you. Let's do it together."

Lucy and the bird worked together. They managed to pick the flower. Lucy was happy. She said, "Thank you, bird!" The bird said, "You're welcome, Lucy! It's a clear day, let's play!" So, Lucy and the bird played in the park all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old. One day, her mommy brought her a surprise. It was a brand new uniform! Lucy was so excited about it. 

The uniform was red and white. It had a big star on the front. Lucy loved it. She put it on and felt very special.

Mommy said, â€œAre you ready to surprise Daddy?â€ Lucy smiled and nodded. 

Daddy was at work. When he saw Lucy he was so surprised. He said "Wow! Look at you. You look so grown-up!" Daddy reached out and gave her a rough hug. 

Mommy and Daddy smiled proudly. Lucy was so happy. She knew that she looked just right in her new uniform.

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden with her friends. They had a club where they would plant pretty flowers and watch them grow.

One day, Lily and her club planted a new flower in the garden. They waited and waited for the flower to grow. They gave it water and lots of love. Soon, the flower started to bloom. It was big and bright, just like the sun.

Lily and her club were so happy to see the flower bloom. They danced and played around the flower all day long. The smart little girl and her friends knew that with love and care, they could make any flower grow. And that's how Lily and her club made their garden even more beautiful.

One day, a little girl was playing in the garden. She felt safe and peaceful, like nothing could hurt her. Suddenly, she heard a sound. It was a shark!

The little girl started to crawl away, but it was too late. The shark was getting closer, ready to attack. The little girl tried to stay quiet and still, hoping the shark would go away, but it didn't work.

The shark came closer and closer, until suddenly it lunged forward and bit the little girl. She screamed in pain as the shark dragged her away.

The little girl never returned, and was never seen again. Her peaceful day in the garden ended in tragedy.

Once there was a little girl. She was so naughty! She did not want to listen to her mommy. One day, her mommy gave her a package. The little girl was so excited! She opened it and saw that it was a toy. She smiled and then began to clap. She was so happy. 

Her mommy was happy too and clapped with her. They were clapping with such joy! Then, the little girl hugged her mommy and they both laughed. 

The mommy then reminded the little girl that she needs to be good and listen to her mommy. The little girl nodded and promised to be good. The mommy hugged her daughter and gave her one more clap for being so happy and naughty!

Once there was a big, fat cat named Sam. Sam was very spoiled and loved to lounge around all day. He loved a good game of chess and often watched people play it in the park.

One afternoon, Sam was strolling around looking for something fun when he spotted a little girl playing with a chess set. It looked like lots of fun. Sam crawled over to get a better look. 

The girl noticed Sam and smiled. "Would you like to play?" she asked.

Sam couldn't believe it! He nodded his head and settled down next to the girl. He watched as she moved her pieces around the board and showed him how to play. 

When the game was over, Sam thanked the girl for the fun time and crawled away. He was so happy that he had a new game to play. 

Sam kept playing chess for many days and always looked forward to those afternoons. He had found the best way to be spoiled!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl called Daisy. Daisy loved her mummy and daddy very much, and she spent every day playing with them.

One day, Daisy went to play in the garden. While she was there, she found a beautiful crystal lying in the grass. It glittered in the sunshine and Daisy thought it was magical. She wanted to keep it for herself.

Daisy put it in her pocket and ran back to the house to show mummy and daddy. But when she got there, she saw that someone had disturbed the living room. Everything was in a mess and her parents were nowhere to be seen.

Poor Daisy started to cry. She was scared and she didn't know what had happened. She was so upset that she dropped the crystal and it made a loud noise when it hit the ground. 

At that moment, the bad robbers returned to the house. The crystal made them angry and they chased Daisy out of the house.

They never saw Daisy again. Her parents were so sad that she was gone. Daisy's chubby little face never returned to the house again.

Once upon a time, there was a oak tree. It was the biggest, strongest tree in the whole forest. Every day, a little girl would go and sit under the tree and look out over the forest.

One day, while the little girl was sitting under the oak tree, something strange happened. As she looked out, she saw a sour-looking man appear from behind the tree. He had a huge bag over his shoulder and it was jingling.

The little girl jumped up and said, "Who are you?"

The man smiled and said, "I'm a traveler and I'm carrying a bag of magical treats. Would you like some?"

The little girl's eyes lit up and she said, "Yes, please!" She eagerly opened the bag and was delighted to find all kinds of sweet and sour treats. She thanked the man and ran off to show her mom what she had found. 

From then on, every time the little girl visited the oak tree, she was sure to look out in the hope that the mysterious traveler would appear again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to spend time outside in nature, playing with the flowers and the birds. She was always so happy and fit, running around and laughing.

One day, Lily went into the forest to play. She wandered deeper and deeper until she got lost. She tried to find her way back but couldn't. She spent hours walking around, getting more and more scared.

As it started to get dark, Lily realized she was lost for good. She tried to find a place to sleep, but it was too cold and scary. She spent the night in the forest, all alone and frightened. The next morning, the rescue team found her, but it was too late. Lily had caught a cold and died in the forest.

Lily was a lively kid who liked to play and talk a lot. She had many toys and books in her room, but she also wanted to see what was outside. One day, she saw a big truck on the street. It was making a loud noise and had bright colors. Lily wanted to go closer and see what it was.

She ran to the door and opened it. She did not listen to her mom, who told her to stay inside. She did not see the car that was coming fast. She only heard a loud honk and a scream.

"Stop, Lily, stop!" her mom shouted. She ran after Lily and grabbed her hand. She pulled her back to the house. She was very scared and angry.

"Lily, you have to listen to me!" her mom said. "You could have been hurt by the car. You have to be careful when you go outside. You have to look and listen before you cross the street."

Lily felt sorry for making her mom worry. She hugged her mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't do it again. I love you, mom."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. I'm glad you're safe. Now, let's go inside and play with your toys. Maybe we can read a book about trucks later."

Lily nodded and smiled. She learned to listen to her mom and to be more careful. She still liked to be lively, but she also liked to be safe.

Billy was feeling gloomy. He stood outside and looked up at the sky. Suddenly he jumped as he heard a noise!

"What was that?" he asked.

"It's just the water jumping up the drain," his mom said.

Billy smiled. He loved to jump! He jumped up and down the street, higher and higher each time. His mom laughed and said, "Look at you go!" Billy beamed with pride.

The sun began to shine and the gloom disappeared. Billy jumped one last time, up into the air and down onto the ground. His mom clapped and hugged him tight.

"You sure do like to jump!" she said.

"Yes!" Billy said with a grin. "Jumping is fun!"

Once upon a time, there was a big boat that sailed the seas. It was filled with oil and the captain wanted to make it smaller. So, he filled the tank with some special liquid and watched it shrink! Soon the big boat became a very small boat and the captain was very happy.

The captain then set off on a journey to a distant land. The sea was rough and the waves were big. But the small boat sailed on, filled with oil.

Finally, the distant land was in sight and the captain felt relieved. But then, something strange happened! As the boat sailed closer to the shore, it began to shrink again! Soon it became so small that the captain could barely fit inside.

The captain was sad that his boat had shrunk again. He decided he would find some new oil to make it big again. So, he sailed off in search of oil, hoping to find some that would make his boat big again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Clara. Clara loved to make things grow. Every day she went to the garden and looked after the plants. She watered, sang and played with them - until all the plants started to bloom.

One day, when she was playing in the garden, she spotted a little seed on the ground. "What is that?" she said. She picked up the seed and blew on it. Suddenly, it started to grow into a beautiful flower. "Wow!" Clara was amazed.

Clara decided to take the flower home with her. She lovingly put the flower into her pocket and started on her way. But then Clara noticed something. Her stomach felt rough. She thought to herself, "maybe I am hungry."

So Clara went to the kitchen and made herself a sandwich. As she ate it, the flower in her pocket began to open. Clara was so excited to see it bloom. "Look at that!" she said.

Once there was a little girl named Ella. She was the most popular girl in school. She loved to play on the balancing beam in the playground. She was so good at balancing that she never had to use her muscles.

One day, all the kids gathered around Ella, asking her to show them what she could do. She smiled and got on the beam. She balanced so well that the kids all applauded.

Ella's teacher came out and told her not to stay on the beam too long. "Sometimes, muscles get tired," he said.

But Ella didn't listen. She stayed on the beam for a really long time. Eventually, her muscles got tired and she fell off. Everyone was very sad. Ella's teacher told her to be careful next time.

But Ella didn't listen and she fell off the beam the next time too. And the next time. The kids in school stopped asking Ella to balance on the beam, since they were afraid something bad might happen. Ella was no longer the most popular girl at school.

Lily was playing with her ball in the park. She liked to kick it and watch it fly. She saw a big tree and wanted to hit it with her ball. She ran and kicked the ball hard. But the ball did not hit the tree. It hit a bird.

The bird fell to the ground. Lily was scared. She ran to the bird and saw that it was not moving. She felt sorry for the bird. She picked it up and hugged it. She wanted to help it.

She ran to her mom and showed her the bird. Her mom was sad too. She said they had to go to the vet. The vet was a person who helped animals. They got in the car and drove to the vet.

The vet looked at the bird. He said it had a broken wing. He said he had to take an x-ray. An x-ray was a picture that showed the bones inside the body. He took the bird to a room and put it on a table. He turned on a machine and took the x-ray.

He came back with the x-ray. He showed it to Lily and her mom. He pointed to the wing. He said there was a crack in the bone. He said he had to fix it. He said he had to put a bandage on the wing. He said the bird would be okay.

Lily was happy. She thanked the vet. She said she was sorry for hitting the bird. She said she would be careful next time. The vet smiled. He said it was an accident. He said he was glad Lily brought the bird to him.

He gave the bird back to Lily. He said she could keep it until it got better. He said she had to feed it and keep it warm. He said she had to be gentle with it. He said he would see them again in a few weeks.

Lily nodded. She held the bird close. She said she would take good care of it. She said she would be its friend. The bird looked at her with its clear eyes. It made a soft sound. Lily smiled. She said she loved the bird.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to walk in the woods and look for animals and plants. One day, they see a big tree with many roots. The roots are thick and twisted and stick out of the ground.

"Wow, look at this tree!" Tom says. "It is so old and strong. I wonder what it knows."

Sue nods. She touches one of the roots gently. "It feels rough and hard. Maybe it has stories to tell."

They sit down next to the tree and listen. They hear the wind in the leaves, the birds in the branches, and the squirrels in the nuts. They think they hear the tree whispering too.

But then, a boy comes along. He is bigger and older than Tom and Sue. He has a stick in his hand. He sees the tree and the roots and laughs.

"What are you doing here, you silly kids?" he says. "This is just a dumb tree. It doesn't know anything. It doesn't talk. It doesn't feel. It is just wood and dirt."

He swings his stick and hits one of the roots. The root cracks and breaks. Tom and Sue gasp. They feel sad and angry.

"Stop it! Stop it!" Tom shouts. "You are hurting the tree. You are ignorant. You don't understand. The tree is alive. It is our friend."

The boy snorts. He doesn't care. He hits another root. The tree shivers and groans.

Sue stands up. She runs to the boy and pushes him. "Go away! Go away!" she cries. "You are mean and bad. You don't belong here. This is our place. This is the tree's place."

The boy stumbles and falls. He drops his stick. He looks at Tom and Sue and the tree. He is scared and confused. He gets up and runs away.

Tom and Sue hug each other. They hug the tree too. They say sorry to the tree. They hope the tree is not too hurt. They hope the tree forgives them.

They stay with the tree for a while. They hear the tree whispering again. They think the tree says thank you. They smile and say you're welcome. They are happy and proud. They are not ignorant. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. He wanted to fly high in the sky. He stretched out his wings, ran and jumped. He flapped his wings and he flew. He flew high and he flew low. He flew over mountains and rivers. 

After a while, he saw a slide. It was very wide and it looked like fun. So the bird flew down and landed near the slide. He ran up to it and started sliding down. He slid fast and he slid slow. He had so much fun sliding down that he kept going up and down.

When he was done, he took one more look at the slide and then he flew away. The little bird was happy. He had a fun time flying and sliding.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. She was three years old, and she wanted to find something special. So she went out on an adventure.

Mary looked under rocks and behind trees, but she couldnâ€™t find anything. Then, she heard a sound in the distance.

She ran to see what it was and saw a tall, clear post. She was happy and jumped up and down.

She ran around the post, eager to find out what was at the top. Sure enough, there was something special waiting for her. She found a big, red balloon tied to the post.

With a big smile, the little girl released the balloon into the air. She watched it soar away until it become a tiny speck in the sky. And so Mary's adventure was over. She went home with a smile and a special memory.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with green and yellow fruits. They are pears. Tom and Anna want to eat some pears.

"Look, Anna, there are so many pears!" Tom says. "Can we get some?"

"Yes, let's try!" Anna says. "But how can we reach them? They are too high."

Tom has an idea. He sees a big stick on the ground. He picks it up and says, "I can use this stick to hit the pears. Then they will fall down and we can eat them."

"Good idea, Tom!" Anna says. "But be careful. Don't hit the bees. They are wild and they can sting you."

Tom nods. He swings the stick and hits a pear. The pear falls down and rolls on the grass. Tom and Anna run to get it. They are happy. They share the pear and eat it. It is sweet and juicy.

"Yum, yum, this pear is good!" Tom says.

"Me too, I like it!" Anna says.

They want more pears. Tom swings the stick again and hits another pear. But this time, he also hits a bee. The bee is angry. It flies out of the tree and buzzes around Tom's head.

"Ow, ow, the bee is after me!" Tom says. He drops the stick and runs away. Anna follows him. They lie down on the grass and cover their heads with their hands. They hope the bee will go away.

"Are you okay, Tom?" Anna asks.

"I think so, Anna. The bee did not sting me. But it scared me." Tom says.

"Me too, Tom. The bee was wild. Maybe we should not hit the pears anymore." Anna says.

"Maybe you are right, Anna. The pears are good, but the bees are bad. Let's play something else." Tom says.

They get up and look for another game. They leave the stick and the pears behind. They are still friends. They are still happy.

Jill and Jack came to the vegetable patch. Jill saw a brilliant cauliflower. She wanted to pick it. But Jack warned her not to.

"We can't pick it" said Jack. "It will make the farmer very sad."

Jill was sad too but she listened to Jack. Then they saw more cauliflowers in the vegetable patch. They were the same size, and just as brilliant.

Jack told Jill, "Let's pick one of these cauliflowers and take it home."

Jill was so happy. She said "Yes, let's do that. But let's leave the other cauliflowers so the farmer can have them too."

Jack smiled. "That's very kind of you Jill. You are so brilliant!"

Once upon a time, there was an orange dancer. She liked to paint. One day, she talked to a friend and said, "I want to paint a picture today of something special."

The friend said,  "What do you want to paint?" 

The orange dancer smiled, "I want to paint a picture of me dancing." 

So the orange dancer set out to find colors to paint with. She found lots of colors including red, blue, yellow, and pink. She also found some orange paint and this made her happy. 

She started to paint her picture. She mixed some of the colors together and used them to make new colors. As she painted she started to dance, and her friend laughed.

When she was done, the orange dancer was very happy with her painting. She said, "This painting is so special. It looks like me dancing." 

Her friend said, "Yes, you are a very special orange dancer.

Once upon a time, there was an obedient boy named Tom. Tom was very good, and he listened to his parents. Tom didn't understand very much about the big world around him. So his parents decided to show him the wonders of the earth.

Tom was very excited, and he couldn't wait to learn more. He saw forests full of trees and streams with fish. He saw mountains and deserts, and fields with animals. He also saw oceans full of water, as far as he could see.

Tom could not believe his eyes. He saw so many amazing things! He felt so small when he looked up into the sky. But he was happy to understand just how big the earth really was.

Tom's parents were happy that Tom had learned something new. Tom was happy too. He had been very obedient, and looked after the earth with care. He was thankful to be part of such a big, wonderful world.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with their toys and run in the park. One day, Tim got a new toy. It was a big truck that made loud noises. Sam wanted to play with it too, but Tim said no. He said it was his toy and he did not want to share.

Sam felt sad and angry. He thought Tim was not a good friend. He saw Tim's puppy sleeping on the grass. He had an idea. He took a stick and poked the puppy. The puppy woke up and barked. It was scared and hurt. Tim heard the noise and ran to his puppy. He saw Sam with the stick. He was very mad. He yelled at Sam and pushed him. He said Sam was a bad boy and he did not want to be his friend anymore.

Sam ran away crying. He felt sorry for what he did. He knew he was wrong. He wanted to say sorry to Tim and his puppy. He waited for a long time. He hoped Tim would come and talk to him. But Tim did not come. He stayed with his puppy and his truck. He was still mad.

Then, Sam saw something. It was a big dog. It was not a friendly dog. It was a dangerous dog. It had sharp teeth and angry eyes. It saw Tim and his puppy. It wanted to hurt them. Sam was scared. He wanted to help Tim and his puppy. He forgot about the truck and the stick. He ran to Tim and shouted. He told him to run away. He threw a rock at the big dog. The big dog growled and chased Sam.

Tim saw the big dog. He saw Sam trying to save him and his puppy. He felt sorry for what he said. He realized Sam was a good friend. He grabbed his puppy and his truck. He ran to Sam. He helped him get away from the big dog. They ran to a safe place. They hugged each other. They said sorry to each other. They forgave each other. They were happy again. They learned to share and to be kind. They played with the truck and the puppy. They were best friends.

Once upon a time there lived two friends, Tommy and Larry. Tommy found a big place. He thought it was the perfect spot to keep things. So every day, Tommy and Larry filled the big place with their treasures.

One day, Larry said, "Let's go somewhere else and find more treasures!" But Tommy said, "No! Let's keep the things here in this big place that I found."

Larry asked, "How will we know if someone else finds it?" Tommy said, "Don't worry, no one will ever find this spot!"

So they kept filling the big place until one day two bad men came. The men were angry and grabbed their treasures. They told Tommy and Larry to stay away or else they would be in trouble.

Tommy was sad. He had been so sure no one else would ever find their spot. He told Larry, "We shouldn't have kept our treasures in one place."

Moral of the story: Don't keep all your treasures in one place; spread them out so they stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat. He had a very special mission. He was sent on a mission to keep a missile safe. 

The cat kept the missile in a big box, so no one could find it. He kept watch, making sure no one took it away. He walked around the box all day, until it was dark. 

One night, a robber tried to take the missile. But the furry cat was ready! He hissed and growled at the robber, and scared him away. The cat kept the missile safe and snug in its box.

The furry cat was so proud. He knew he had done his job well. Everyone praised him and said he was the best furry watch cat they ever had! 

From then on, the cat kept the missile safe and sound. He was the protector of the missileâ€”the furry guardian!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time to come inside. It's getting dark." Lily didn't want to go inside. She wanted to play more.

The next day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, you can play outside, but you must come inside when I say so." Lily was happy her mom permitted her to play outside longer. She played with her friends until the sun went down.

Later that week, Lily's friend told her about a popular game they could play. Lily wanted to play too, but she didn't know how. Her friend said, "It's easy, I'll show you." Lily was excited to learn.

The next day, Lily's friend showed her how to play the popular game. Lily was happy she learned something new. She knew it was true that her friend was a good teacher. From that day on, Lily played the popular game with her friends every day.

John and his mom went to the store. John wanted to buy a notebook. His mom said she would provide him with one. 

"Wow! Thank you, mom!" said John excitedly. 

They walked to the notebooks section and John saw many notebooks. He noticed that one was big and it was dry.

"Mom, can I have the dry big one?" asked John. 

"Yes, you can have it," said his mom. 

They bought the notebook and went home. John was very happy about his new dry notebook. He started writing in it right away.

Tommy liked to swim in the pool. He had a big floaty that looked like a shark. He would pretend he was a shark and splash his sister Lily. Lily did not like that. She would cry and tell Mommy.

One day, Tommy saw a new boy at the pool. His name was Ben. Ben had a floaty that looked like a lawyer. Tommy thought that was funny. He wanted to play with Ben. He swam over to him and said, "Hi, I am Tommy. Do you want to be friends?"

Ben looked at Tommy and said, "No, I don't. I am independent. I don't need friends. Go away, shark boy."

Tommy felt sad. He did not understand why Ben was so mean. He tried to be nice. He said, "But we can have fun together. We can share our floaties. I like your lawyer floaty. It is cool."

Ben did not like that. He got angry. He said, "No, you can't. This is my lawyer floaty. It is mine. You can't touch it. Go away, or I will sue you."

Tommy did not know what sue meant. He thought it was a game. He said, "Okay, let's play sue. How do we play?"

Ben said, "We don't play. I sue you. I tell the lifeguard that you hurt me. Then you get in trouble. Then you have to give me your shark floaty. That is how you play sue."

Tommy did not like that. He said, "That is not a game. That is mean. You are mean. I don't want to play with you."

Ben said, "Too late. I already sued you. Look, there is the lifeguard. He is coming to get you."

Tommy looked and saw the lifeguard. He was big and scary. He had a whistle and a red shirt. He looked angry. He said, "Hey, you, shark boy. Come here. I need to talk to you."

Tommy was scared. He did not know what to do. He wanted to run away. But he could not. He was in the pool. He had to swim. He tried to swim away. But the lifeguard was faster. He caught him. He grabbed him by the arm. He pulled him out of the pool. He said, "You are in big trouble, kid. Ben told me that you hit him and took his lawyer floaty. Is that true?"

Tommy said, "No, no, no. That is not true. He lied. He is mean. He wanted to take my shark floaty. He said he sued me. I don't know what that means. Please, don't be mad at me. Please, let me go."

The lifeguard did not believe him. He said, "Sorry, kid. I have to believe Ben. He is a lawyer. He knows the law. You are a shark. You are dangerous. You have to go to time out. Come with me."

The lifeguard took Tommy to a small room. He locked the door. He said, "You have to stay here until your mommy comes. You have to think about what you did. You have to say sorry to Ben. You have to give him your shark floaty. That is the only way you can get out."

Tommy cried. He did not want to stay in the room. He did not want to say sorry to Ben. He did not want to give him his shark floaty. He wanted his mommy. He wanted to go home. He wanted to swim. He hated Ben. He hated the lifeguard. He hated the pool. He hated the lawyer floaty. He wished he never met Ben. He wished he never saw the lawyer floaty. He wished he never swam. He wished he was a shark. He wished he could bite them. He wished he could be free. But he could not. He was stuck. He was sad. He was alone. The end.

John and his mom had to take their horse to the stable. When they arrived, John saw the stable keeper, Bill. Bill told him that he needed to sort out his horse. John was embarrassed because he had never done this sort of thing before.

John's mom smiled and told him it was okay. She said he could try sorting out the horse. So he tried his best, although it was a bit tricky.

The stable keeper stood back and watched. He kept shaking his head and saying it wasn't good enough. He said that John's sorting skills were not very good.

John was so embarrassed. His face turned red and he started to cry. His mom hugged him and said it was okay. She said he had tried his best.

The stable keeper just laughed and said he was sorry. John and his mom rode away from the stable, feeling embarrassed and sad.

Ben and Lily were friends. They liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big red thing in the park. It had wheels and a horn. They both wanted to play with it.

"Let me have it!" Ben said. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Lily said. "I saw it first!"

They pulled and pushed the thing. They did not share. They made a lot of noise. They were not nice.

A man came to the park. He saw Ben and Lily. He was angry. He said, "That is my thing! I left it here for a minute. You are not allowed to take it!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They let go of the thing. They said, "Sorry, sir. We did not know."

The man took his thing and left. Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt sad. They did not win. They lost a friend.

They said, "We are sorry. We were silly. Can we be friends again?"

They hugged and smiled. They learned to share. They played with other toys. They were happy. They won a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Emmy. Emmy was gifted and curious. She often wondered what it would be like to be something else in the world.

One day, Emmy saw a beetle. She got closer to take a better look.

"Hello there," said Emmy. "I want to be like you, little beetle. Would you show me how it feels to be like you?"

The beetle smiled, and nodded its head. Then, it flew onto the tip of Emmy's finger. Emmy smiled, and the beetle flew away.

Emmy suddenly felt different. She felt like she could fly, and she wanted to see what it was like. Taking a leap of faith, Emmy jumped off the ground and flew around.

Emmy was amazed. Now she knew what it was like to be like the beetle. Every now and again, she still sees the beetle and remembers the special feel of being able to fly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy told her that they were going to have a party at their house. 

Lily was very excited and asked her mommy what she could do to help. Her mommy told her that she could polish the silverware. Lily didn't know what "polish" meant, so her mommy explained that it meant to make something shiny and clean. 

Lily was happy to help and went to find the silverware. She found it in a drawer and started to polish it with a cloth. When she was done, it was very shiny and looked beautiful. 

The day of the party arrived and Lily's house was full of people. Everyone was having a good time and eating yummy food. Lily was happy to see that the silverware she had polished was being used. Her mommy told her that she did a great job and that she was very helpful. 

The party was over and everyone went home. Lily went to bed feeling happy and proud that she had helped make her house look nice for the party. She knew that she was always available to help her mommy and daddy whenever they needed her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, her mommy asked her to get the pan from the shelf. Lily said, "Okay mommy, I will get it for you!" 

When she reached for the pan, her big brother came in and said, "Lily, you are too little to help. Let me do it!" Lily felt sad and didn't like how her brother was being bossy. 

But then her mommy said, "No, Lily can help too. Please let her get the pan." Lily was happy her mommy stood up for her. She got the pan and helped her mommy make pancakes. They all tasted delicious and her brother even said, "Lily, you are a great helper!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to pick flowers in the garden with her mommy. One day, Lily was worried because it started to rain outside. She didn't want her flowers to get wet.

Her mommy told her not to worry and brought her inside. They went to the kitchen and her mommy poured some hot chocolate in a cup for Lily. They sat together and drank the chocolate while listening to the rain. Lily felt happy and warm inside. She realized that sometimes things can be different than what we expect, but it can still be nice.

Anna loves to sing. She sings every day at home, in the car, and at school. She wants to sing on the big stage, like the stars on TV. She asks her mom to take her to the talent show at the park. Mom says yes, and they go.

At the park, there are many people and many kids. Anna sees a big microphone on a stand. She runs to it and grabs it. She wants to sing her favorite song. But a big boy pushes her away. He says, "That's mine! Go away, you little brat!" He takes the microphone and starts to rap.

Anna is sad and angry. She cries and yells, "That's not fair! I want to sing! Give it back!" She tries to pull the microphone from the boy, but he is too strong. He pushes her again, and she falls on the ground. She hurts her knee and her elbow.

Mom sees what happens and runs to Anna. She hugs her and says, "I'm sorry, honey. That boy is very mean. Are you OK?" She looks at her wounds and says, "We need to go home and clean these. Come on, let's go."

Anna is frustrated and disappointed. She doesn't want to go home. She wants to sing on the stage. She says, "No, Mom, please. I want to sing. Please, Mom, please." But Mom says, "No, Anna, we have to go. Maybe another day, OK?" She picks her up and carries her to the car.

Anna cries all the way home. She doesn't understand why the boy was so mean. She doesn't understand why Mom didn't let her sing. She doesn't understand why her dream didn't come true. She thinks, "Maybe I'm not good enough. Maybe I can't sing. Maybe I'm just a little brat." She feels very sad and very bad. She wishes she never went to the park. She wishes she never saw the microphone. She wishes she never tried to stand on the stage.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack was carrying a basket of cherries he had picked from a cherry tree. He said to Jill, "Look at all the nice cherries I have here!" 

Jill was so excited that she asked Jack, "Can I have one?" Jack was a nice friend, so he decided to share some of the cherries with her. He said, "Yes, you can have one." 

Jill happily took a cherry and said thank you. She smiled at Jack and said, "Your cherries are so yummy!" Then Jack said, "Come on, let's go and have some fun!" 

The two friends went off to play. As they walked away, Jack was still carrying the basket of cherries. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big monster. The monster was very tough and strong. He liked to swing on the trees in the forest. One day, the monster saw a little bird's nest. The monster wanted to destroy the nest, but the little bird was still inside. The little bird was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a brave mouse came along. The mouse saw what the monster was trying to do and knew he had to help. The mouse ran up to the monster and bit him on the toe. The monster was so surprised that he fell off the swing and ran away. The little bird was safe and happy in her nest, thanks to the brave mouse.

Once upon a time, there was a baby. The baby was upset because it couldn't find its toy. The baby cried and cried. Then, the baby's big sister came and asked the baby what was wrong. The baby pointed to the toy. The big sister found the toy and gave it back to the baby. The baby stopped crying and smiled. The end.

Once there was a happy little girl named Lucy. She loved to have soup for dinner every night.

One night, her Mommy made her a big bowl of delicious soup. Lucy was so happy that she wanted to thank her Mommy for making her such a tasty dinner. 

So she repeated the words "Thank you, Mommy!" She said the words over and over and over again. 

Mommy smiled and said, "You're welcome my sweet girl!" 

Every night from then on, Lucy asked for her soup, and while she ate it, she repeated "Thank you Mommy" with a big smile on her face. 

And every night, Mommy returned the same loving smile.

Once upon a time, there was an old house. It was so old that it had leaks in the roof when it rained. One day, a little girl saw the leaks and told her mommy. Her mommy replied, "We should fix it soon." 

The little girl wanted to help, so she got her toy hammer and tried to fix the leak herself. But it was too big for her to fix. She asked her mommy for help and her mommy replied, "Let's call a repairman to fix it."

The repairman came and fixed the leak. The little girl was happy that the old house was fixed. She thanked the repairman and he replied, "You're welcome!"

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful girl. She ran all around the park. Her mom saw her running and shouted, "Don't run away! Come here!" The girl ran back to her mom.

Mom said, "Let me tell you something important. Running is good but it is also important to take care of yourself. Eat your meals and drink milk to stay healthy. Will you do that for me?"

The girl nodded and said yes. She hugged her mom and said, "I will take care of myself, Mommy."

Mommy smiled and said, "That's my good girl! Being healthy and taking care of yourself is the most beautiful thing of all!"

At the end, the girl learned that running around is great, but it's also important to take care of herself. After all, being healthy is the most beautiful thing in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a funny little girl named Lily. She liked to play, laugh, and have fun with her friends. Lily was always happy and made everyone around her smile.

One day, Lily went on a walk with her dog, Spot. They walked and walked until they discovered a big tree. Under the tree, they found a wise old owl. The owl had lots of wisdom to share with Lily.

The owl told Lily that being kind and helping others is very important. Lily listened and learned from the owl's wisdom. She decided to be even more kind and helpful to her friends and family. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole who lived in a big hole. One day, the mole went to the store to buy a shiny new toy. When he got there, he saw a toy that he really liked, but it was too expensive for him to buy. 

The mole asked the store owner, "Can you make it cheaper, please?" The store owner replied, "I'm sorry, but this toy is very expensive. I can't make it cheaper." 

The mole felt sad and disappointed. He walked back to his hole and sat down. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was his friend, the bird. The bird said, "Why are you sad, little mole?" The mole explained that he couldn't afford the toy he wanted. 

The bird said, "Don't worry, I can help you. I know how to speak to the store owner and maybe we can make a deal." The mole felt happy and grateful to have such a helpful friend. Together, they went back to the store and the bird spoke to the store owner. In the end, the mole got his shiny new toy at a price he could afford. He was so happy that he thanked the bird and hugged him tightly.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going to the park. Timmy was so happy and promised to be good.

When they got to the park, Timmy saw his friend Billy. Billy wanted to play on the swings, but Timmy wanted to play on the slide. They argued and Timmy's mom got frustrated. She gave them a lecture about sharing and being kind to each other.

After the lecture, Timmy and Billy decided to take turns on the swings and slide. They had so much fun together and promised to always be friends. Timmy's mom was happy they were getting along and they all went home with big smiles on their faces. The end.

The sun was shining and it was time to play. Millie and her brother, Mike, wanted to make a fort. Millie had an idea that they should use the old cable. Mike thought it was a good idea and so they started to build. 

Mike was stretching the cable and tying it tightly, when Millie noticed something. 

"Mike, why is that man being so rude?" she asked. 

Mike looked and saw their neighbor, Mr. Stevens, making angry faces and waving his hands. 

Mike said, "I don't know, Millie. Maybe he doesn't like us using his cable." 

Mr. Stevens walked over and said, "I don't want you kids to spend your time taking a cable that isn't yours." Millie looked up and said, "We were just making a fort. We're sorry." 

Mr. Stevens smiled and said, "That's okay. Just don't take things that don't belong to you. Here, let me help you with that cable."

Millie and Mike thanked Mr. Stevens and they worked together to make an amazing fort. They all had a great time that day.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and pretend she was a princess. One day, Lily's mom said she had to go to the office and couldn't play with her. 

Lily was sad because she wanted to play with her mom. But then she had an idea! She put on her prettiest dress and became a princess. She went to her mom's office and said, "Hello, I am Princess Lily. Can I play with you?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course you can, my pretty princess." They played together and had so much fun. Lily was happy she could be with her mom and still be a princess.

John saw something cute on the other side of the playground. He wanted to know what it was. He ran to the other side and saw a prize. He wanted it! He ran to the prize but then he saw that someone else was coming for it too.

John said to the other person, "I want the prize!"

The other person said, "I want it too!"

John thought for a moment, then he said, "I know. We can both have it. We can share the prize!"

The other person agreed and they shared the prize. They were both happy. John was glad he got to keep a part of the cute prize.

Once upon a time there there was a fierce big cat called Max. He liked to take long walks in the wide forest near his home. One day, Max came across a lake. He stopped and looked around, but he couldn't see anything special. Suddenly, a voice came from the lake.

â€œMax, come here,â€ the voice said.

Max was scared and wanted to leave but he was curious, so he stepped closer. Then, he saw another fierce big cat come out of the lake. The cat said, â€œI am Ty the Water Cat. I live underwater. Come with me, Max.â€

Max didn't know what to do. He was not sure if he should take Ty's advice or not.

He thought for a moment and then he decided to take Ty's advice. He followed him into the lake.

Max was amazed by what he saw. There were lots of colourful fishes, coral reefs, and wonderful underwater plants. Ty showed Max all the amazing underwater things. It was a beautiful place, and Max had a great time.

At the end of the day, Ty said goodbye to Max and Max said goodbye. He took the long journey home with a big smile on his face. From then on, Max visited Ty in the wide lake every week.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Jack and Jill. Jack and Jill loved to match. Every day, they would match rocks, leaves, and sticks. One day, Jack and Jill wanted to match in the harbor. 

Getting to the harbor was a long journey, but they kept on walking until they arrived. When they got to the harbor, it was so miserable. There were no rocks, leaves, or sticks to match. Jack and Jill were so sad.

Suddenly, they spotted a pile of match boxes near the harbor. Jack and Jill were so excited, they grabbed one of the match boxes and began to match the colorful boxes. They played at the harbor all day, matching the pretty match boxes until the sun started to go down. 

That day, Jack and Jill had an amazing time and each went home with a smile. And they promised to come back to the harbor soon and match again.

Once upon a time there was an orange needle called Frank. He had been in the same spot for years and he was getting bored. He wanted to explore, but he didn't know how to.

Then one day, a small 3 year old child saw Frank. The child said "Hello Frank! I'm going to help you explore the world." Frank was so excited!

The child said, "I think we should reverse!" Frank looked confused, but the child explained that it meant going backwards, the opposite of forwards.

So, the child and Frank started reversing. They went up and down, side to side and around in circles. Frank was enjoying his adventure!

After an hour of reversing, the child and Frank stopped. The child said, "Wow, that was a lot of fun! You now know that you can explore by reversing."

Frank thanked the child for his help and then said goodbye. As the child walked away, Frank knew that he would never forget this adventure.

One day a little girl was sad. She was in her bedroom. She felt like she wanted to fly away. So she went on an adventure in her bedroom! She imagined she was a bird, flying around her bedroom. She flapped her arms like wings, and jumped on her bed. Then, she flew down to the floor, happily twirling around and around.

When she felt tired, she flew back to her bed. She curled up in a soft blanket and closed her eyes. In her mind, she was soaring high in the sky, where the birds flew. She felt happy and free.

At the end of her adventure, she snuggled in her bed and felt safe and content. She was no longer sad. She had taken a wonderful flying adventure in her bedroom and it had filled her heart with joy.

Once upon a time there was a very lucky little girl. She had a special pair of sunglasses that she liked to wear every day. One hot day she was walking in the park and she came across a big pile of toffee. She chewed it and it tasted so good, she wanted to chew more.

Suddenly, a big dog came running up to her. He was looking at her sunglasses and he wanted to take them away. 

The little girl said, "No, these are my special sunglasses, I won't let you have them!"

The dog barked and growled. He tried very hard to take the sunglasses away but the little girl held on to them. 

The dog was growing more and more angry. He barked louder and louder. But the girl was lucky. She managed to keep her sunglasses away from the dog. When he realised he couldn't take them, he started to run away.

The little girl looked around and smiled to herself. She was lucky that she managed to keep her sunglasses safe. She was also very happy that she got to enjoy her toffee too!

Once upon a time there was a boy. He liked to watch his toys. One day, he saw a strange figure. He felt a bit guilty and he hid behind his sofa. Then, the figure started to move. He poked his head out and watched. It was his mom! She was moving his toys around the room. The boy was so happy that all he felt was joy--no more guilty feeling! He ran out and hugged his mom. From then on, every time he saw a figure coming in, he knew it was his mom watching him.

So mama and papa set off on their adventure. They walked and walked, until they found the shop. Mama went in and asked for the gold she needed. The man said, â€œNo problem!â€ But when mama looked at the gold, it wasn't shining - it looked very lazy! 

Mama said, â€œIt's not what I need. I need something that will keep shining.â€  The man smiled and said, â€œHere it is. I have real gold right here! This will keep shining no matter what.â€ Mama smiled, too.

They bought the gold and headed back home. Mama was so glad to have found the right gold. Now she could keep it shining in the night sky long after the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old, and she loved peaches. One day she saw a big, red peach in a tree. She wanted to pick it, so she asked her mom.

"Can I pick the red peach, mommy?"

"Yes, Sarah," said her mom. "But don't forget to watch out for the bees!"

Sarah smiled and started heading over to the tree. She was so close to the red peach when she saw a bee! She screamed, turned around and ran away. Unfortunately, she forgot about the red peach and ran home instead.

When she got home, she was so upset that she forgot the peach. She started to cry and asked her mom if they could go back and get the peach.

"No, sweetheart," said her mom. "It's too late now and the peach is probably gone now."

Sarah was sad and angry, but she had to accept that she forgot the peach. She never forgot about that red peach though, and she always wished she could have picked it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lucy. Every day, Lucy liked to spin around in circles and around and around. She would spin until she couldn't spin anymore â€“ until she was so dizzy that she had to lay down on the ground.

One day, Lucy was spinning around and around when she heard a loud noise. She looked up to see the Most Silly Knee ever! The Knee was wearing a fancy hat, and had a big voice. "I want you to spin around me!" it said.

Lucy was scared at first, but then she felt brave. She spun around and around the big silly knee. The Knee laughed and laughed while Lucy spun glitz. Finally, Lucy was so dizzy that she had to stop. "Thank you for spinning," The Knee said. And Lucy smiled and giggled before running off to play.

Once upon a time there lived a little boy named Sam. He was three years old and very happy.

One day his mom was very worried. Sam asked her why she was so worried and she told him she needed to cook dinner for his birthday. 

"Mommy, can I help you cook?" asked Sam. 

"That's a nice idea, Sam," said his mom.

So Sam and his mom went to the kitchen and started cooking his very special birthday dinner. While cooking, Sam made a happy singing noise as he stirred the big pot of noodles. 

When they finished cooking dinner, Sam's mom hugged him and said, "Thank you for helping me cook, Sam! Your help made dinner extra special this year." 

Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mom!" 

Then they both went to the table and ate their tasty dinner together. Sam had the best birthday ever!

Lila and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. Lila liked the giraffes best, because they had long necks and spots. Ben liked the monkeys best, because they made funny noises and jumped around.

Then they came to the ostriches. Ostriches are big birds that cannot fly. They have long legs and feathers, but no arms or hands. Lila and Ben thought they looked funny and silly.

"Look, Ben, that ostrich has a gray head and a black body," Lila said, pointing to one of the ostriches.

"Yeah, and look, that one has a white head and a brown body," Ben said, pointing to another one.

They went closer to the fence to see the ostriches better. One of the ostriches saw them and ran towards them. It opened its big mouth and made a loud noise.

"Rawr!" the ostrich said.

Lila and Ben were scared. They ran back to Mom and Dad, who were watching from a distance.

"Mom, Dad, the ostrich tried to eat us!" Lila cried.

"Shh, Lila, it's okay. The ostrich was just saying hello. It can't hurt you through the fence," Mom said, hugging Lila.

"Are you sure, Mom?" Ben asked, still shaking.

"Yes, Ben, I'm sure. The ostrich is not a bad bird. It's just curious and playful. Maybe it wanted to play with you," Dad said, patting Ben's head.

Lila and Ben looked at the ostrich again. It was still standing near the fence, but it looked less scary now. It blinked its big eyes and tilted its head.

"Hello, ostrich," Lila said, waving her hand.

"Hello, hello," the ostrich said, nodding its head.

Lila and Ben smiled. They decided to give the ostrich a name. They called it Gray-Black, because of its colors. They stayed for a while, talking and playing with Gray-Black. They learned that ostriches can be friendly and fun, if you are nice to them. They also learned that ostriches can shut their mouths, when they want to.

Bob was a very sad boy. He sat in his office and sighed. He was feeling very fragile. Then, something magical happened! A beautiful butterfly flew into his office and began to dance in front of him. Its wings were colourful and sparkled in the sunlight. Bob smiled and suddenly he felt like he could do anything. He got up from his chair and jumped and sprang out of the office. He kept on jumping and springing down the street, feeling very happy. He waved to everyone he saw and everyone smiled back at him. He felt so free and happy he wanted the feeling to last forever.

Once upon a time, there was a player. He was nervous, but he had an important job. He had to repeat the song. It was time for him to begin. He knew he could do it. He had practiced every day. He curved his fingers around the instrument, ready to make the music. He started to play. The notes were slow and gentle. They repeated in an interesting way. As he heard the beautiful notes, his nervousness faded away. He kept playing until the song ended. Everyone clapped, and he was so happy. He did it! He repeated the song.

Once there was a lovely little girl who went for a walk in the park. As she was walking, she looked down and saw a leg in the grass. She was so excited that she stopped to take a closer look. It was a little wooden leg, and she recognized it as the same one that had been on the scarecrow she had seen earlier.

The little girl loved the leg and wanted to take it home. She picked it up, dusting off the dirt, and began her walk back home.

Along the way, she was so happy she was singing and carrying the leg in her hands. People were smiling at her as she cheerfully hummed along.

Finally, she got home and quickly ran inside, beaming with excitement. She immediately showed her mom the lovely leg and explained what she had found. Her mom hugged her and said she was so proud of her forrecognizing its special value.

The little girl kept the leg close to her and cherished it forever. It was a sweet reminder of the lovely day she had spent out in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl, called Tara. She was very restless and wanted to have a big adventure.

One day, she saw something very special - a small triangle in the middle of a garden. She stepped towards it and as she got closer, the triangle started to grow bigger and bigger!

Tara couldn't help but step even closer, until she was right in front of the triangle. By this time, it had grown so big that she could step right inside it.

Suddenly, the triangle started to move and Tara found herself on the most exciting adventure! The triangle took her over hills, rivers and valleys until it finally stopped in a big city.

Tara's restless journey was finally over and she had had the most amazing adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside and exploring the earth. He loved looking at all the green trees and plants. One day, he saw a man setting up a tent in the park.

"Can I help you set up the tent?" Timmy asked the man.

"Sure, that would be great!" the man replied.

Timmy helped the man set up the tent and they talked about how important it is to take care of the earth. The man told Timmy that we need to keep the earth green and clean so that we can continue to enjoy it for years to come.

Timmy learned that even though he was small, he could make a big difference in taking care of the earth. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always pick up litter and recycle. He knew that even small actions could help keep the earth green and beautiful.

Tommy did not like class. He thought it was stupid. He had to sit and listen to the teacher talk and talk. He had to repeat what the teacher said. He did not want to repeat. He wanted to play and have fun.

One day, the teacher said they would learn a new song. She sang the song and asked the class to repeat. Tommy did not repeat. He made a funny noise instead. The teacher was angry. She told Tommy to go to the corner and be quiet. Tommy did not go. He made another funny noise.

The other kids laughed. They thought Tommy was funny. The teacher did not think so. She called the principal. The principal came and took Tommy away. He said Tommy had to go to his office and talk. Tommy did not want to talk. He wanted to play and have fun.

But he could not play and have fun. He had to sit and listen to the principal talk and talk. He had to repeat what the principal said. He did not want to repeat. He wanted to go back to class and make funny noises. But he could not. He was in trouble. He learned that class was not so stupid after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was different from the other kids. He had a special power. He could save people when they were in trouble.

One day, Tim heard a loud noise. It was a big wake from a boat. He saw a little girl in the water. She was scared and needed help. Tim jumped into the water and swam to her. He said, "Don't worry, I will save you!"

Tim grabbed the little girl's hand and pulled her to the shore. The little girl was so happy that Tim saved her. She said, "Thank you for saving me!" Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome! I'm glad I could help."

From that day on, Tim and the little girl became best friends. They played together every day. Tim was happy to be different because he could save people and make new friends.

One day, a truck arrive in a small town. The truck was loaded with mail. The people watched as the truck drove up to the big red mailbox.

The driver stopped the truck and got out. She opened the back of the truck and brought out big bundles of mail. She started to put the mail into the mailbox.

When the mailbox was full, the driver got back into the truck. She waved goodbye to the people and drove away.

Then something amazing happened! The dead mailbox started to move. It jumped down from its spot and went running across the town. Everywhere it went, it dropped letters and packages.

The townspeople ran after it, but the mailbox was too fast. Finally, it jumped into a pond and disappeared.

The people were so surprised, but in the end they were happy. Everyone in the town got their mail.

The little girl was grateful for the win. She had worked so hard and was so happy to finally see the result of her hard work.

She wanted to make it special. So the little girl decided to get some polish and make the win shine brighter than ever before.

So she got her little brush and some red, shiny polish and started polishing away. She took her time and made sure every corner of the win was polished.

When she was done, she stepped back and admired her work. It was even more beautiful than before! She was SO proud and grateful for her win. 

The little girl thanked the win and kept it safe in her room. She would always remember the special moment of polishing her win.

Once there was a duck named Bob. Bob loved to lay in the sun and look up at the clouds. One day he saw an old patch in the pond. It looked like it had been there for a long time. Bob wanted to fix the patch so he could use the pond.

Bob asked his friends to help him patch the pond. They all tried their best, but the patch refused to stay fixed for long. Bob became frustrated as the patch kept coming undone.

Then Bob had an idea. He asked his friends to find something flexible enough to hold the patch in place when it rained. They searched and searched until they found the perfect material.

Bob and his friends were able to patch the pond with the flexible material, and now Bob and all his friends can enjoy the pond on a sunny day. 

The moral of this story is that being flexible and using creativity can help us solve difficult challenges.

Mum and Dad took Jack and Sam to the fun fair. Jack loved the bright colours and wanted to go on the rides. Dad said he needed to be weighed first. He was excited to get on the scales. The scales said he was too light!

Mum had a clever plan. She gave Jack an ice-cream and he weighed enough to go on the rides. Jack was happy he could join in the fun and had an big smile on his face.

The rides at the fun-fair were so fun. Jack and Sam went on them over and over again. They laughed and smiled so much that their faces were very red.

When it was time to go home, Jack was sad. He wanted to stay at the fair a bit longer. Dad said it was time to go, but had a surprise for him. He bought Jack a big bag of ice-cream for the journey home.

The ice-cream was the best part of the day, the sweet flavour made Jack feel very happy. Even the dull car ride home seemed fun with ice-cream in his hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite teddy bear named Mr. Fluffy. One day, Lily was eating a chocolate bar and accidentally got some on Mr. Fluffy's fur. 

"Oh no, Mr. Fluffy is dirty!" Lily exclaimed. 

"Don't worry, we can wipe it off," said Lily's mom. 

Lily's mom got a wet cloth and wiped the chocolate off of Mr. Fluffy's fur. 

"Good as new!" said Lily. 

Later that day, Lily and Mr. Fluffy went outside to play. Mr. Fluffy's tie kept falling off, but Lily was persistent and kept tying it back on. They had so much fun playing together!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Benny decided to hide in the forest. He found a peaceful spot under a big tree.

As Benny was hiding, he noticed his shadow on the ground. He thought it was very funny and started to play with it. But then, Benny got scared because he thought his shadow was a big monster. He ran away and bumped into a tree.

Benny learned that shadows are not scary and that it's important to be brave. He also learned that it's okay to be peaceful and take a break from playing with friends. Benny felt happy and proud of himself for learning these things.

Once there was a rare crane that flew in the sky. It was the most wonderful crane anyone had ever seen! It was so beautiful, people came from all around the world just for a chance to glimpse the crane.

One day, a little boy wanted to catch the crane. So he grabbed his net and set off looking for the crane. Everywhere he went, people said the crane had gone, but he kept looking.

Finally, he found it! He was so excited; he jumped up and down. Then he slowly crept forward, net in hand. Before he knew it, the crane was in his net!

The little boy was so proud of himself. He had caught the rare crane all by himself. He could tell everyone, show them what he had done.

From that day on, the little boy never gave up looking for a rare crane again. He always remembered how special it was to catch one.

Once upon a time there was a bulb. The bulb was very useful. One day a 3 year old noticed the bulb and wondered what it did. He had lots of fun playing with it. He noticed the bulb was very bright when he switched it on, lighting up his room. He soon realised it was useful and played with it every day. He enjoyed seeing how the bulb lit up his room when it was dark. He loved it so much he would talk to it and say, "Hello bulb!" He enjoyed the light and thought it was the best bulb ever. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Emma. She was three years old and loved to play outdoors.

One day, Emma was playing in the garden when she saw something lying in the tall grass. She walked over and saw that it was a cup. Emma picked it up and the cup was thick and heavy. 

When she brought it inside, Emma's mom was busy in the kitchen. She saw the cup and said, "Where did you get this cup, Emma?" Emma replied, "I found it in the garden!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's great. The cup is just what we need. Do you know what this cup is for?"

Emma thought for a moment and then said, "It's for supplying water!"

"That's right," said her mom. "We can put water in it and give it to the flowers in the garden to make sure they stay healthy and happy."

Emma was so proud to have found something useful. From then on she kept an eye out for things that she could supply to make her world a better place.

Once, there was a skeleton who was very fit. He felt amazing every day.

He loved to run, jump and play. He would even prance around his garden.

But one day, the skeleton felt tired and weak. He couldn't run, jump or play.

He was confused. Why did he feel so bad?

The skeleton went to the doctor, who told him he was missing a part of his body. He needed to eat better food to make himself fit again.

So he did. He ate all the right things and soon he felt better. He was fit again and ready to run, jump and play.

The skeleton was so happy! His happily ever after had come to an end.

Jack was a brave 3 year old boy who liked to explore. One day, while he was playing outside, he saw an old door. He had never seen it before. He walked slowly towards it, because he was curious. He grabbed the handle and tried to open it. It was locked! Jack tried harder and harder but could not unlock it. Just then, Jack saw a key on the ground. It was old and rough. He picked it up and put it in the door. He turned it, and the door unlocked. Inside he saw something very special. It was a big dinosaur! Jack was so excited. He petted it and the dinosaur snuggled up close. Jack smiled and they were best friends ever since.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her aunt very much. Her aunt was so lovely and kind to her. Every time her aunt came to visit, they would play games and have fun together.

One day, Lily's aunt had to go away for a long time. Lily felt sad because she would miss her aunt so much. But before she left, her aunt gave her a special present. It was a beautiful necklace with a locket that had a picture of them together.

Lily wore the necklace every day and it reminded her of her lovely aunt. She would talk to the picture in the locket and tell her how much she missed her. And every time she felt sad, she would look at the picture and feel better. Even though her aunt was far away, Lily knew that she would always love her and be there for her.

The little girl had a thick coat on her back. Everywhere she looked there were people trading things. One man traded shoes for coins, another were swapping hats for bread. She watched with wide eyes as the trades were made. 

Soon she was asked to trade too. She was asked to give her coat in exchange for some vegetables. After much thought, she decided to do it. 

As soon as she completed the trade she dreamt of having a thick coat again. She dreamt of a big, warm coat that would keep her safe from the cold. 

The next day she headed back to the market. There she saw a coat hanging outside one of the shops. It was thick and warm just like in her dreams. She traded some of the vegetables she had gotten earlier and the coat was hers. 

The little girl happily walked home wearing her new warm and thick coat.

Once upon a time, there was a successful tool that rocked the world. It was a special machine made by a clever man. With the help of this tool, life became easier for everyone.

Every day, the clever man would put the tool to work. He used it to fix things and to build things. He even used it to cook food. Everyone who saw the tool was amazed by its brilliance.

One day, a young child saw the tool and asked to use it. "Of course!" said the clever man and handed him the tool. The child was so excited and carefully began working with the tool. He whizzed, he whittled, he whistled with delight.

Before long, the child's work was complete. Everyone in the room stared in awe. The tool had been used to make something really special.

When the little boy was done, he smiled proudly. Thanks to the successful tool, the child had rocked everyone's world!

One day, a little girl named Lisa wanted to take a walk to the park. She got dressed and put on her shoes. She could hardly wait to enter the park and explore.

When Lisa entered the park, she was filled with joy. There were bright colors, pretty flowers, and lots of things for her to do. She ran to the playground and began to play.

But then something strange happened. Lisa looked down and noticed her skin was different. It looked red and her arm was hot. Lisa was very upset.

Luckily, her mom saw what was happening and ran over to comfort her. She grabbed a cold cloth, placed it on Lisa's arm, and said everything would be alright.

Slowly, the skin on Lisa's arm stopped feeling hot and soon returned to its normal color. Lisa smiled, thankful that she was alright. She could continue to explore and play in the park without feeling bad. From that day on, Lisa was always sure to have her mom nearby when she entered the park.

Once there was a little boy. He loved to search! One day, he was searching and he heard a funny noise. He looked around, but he couldn't see what it was. He kept searching and then he found it! It was a big orange ball!

He picked it up and looked it all over. He saw that it was filled with water! He couldn't believe it! He wanted to show it to his mom. He held the orange ball tight, and ran off to show it to her.

When he arrived home, his mom was very surprised to see the orange ball full of water! They had lots of fun with it, and searched for more things around their house. They found lots of interesting things! The little boy was so happy.

Lily and Sam are playing in the garden. They have a big pool of water and some toys. They splash and laugh and have fun.

But then the sun comes out and makes the water go away. The pool becomes smaller and smaller. The toys are wet and sticky.

"Oh no!" Lily says. "The water is drying up! What will we do?"

Sam thinks for a moment. He has an idea. He runs to the shed and gets a hose. He turns on the tap and sprays water all over the pool and the toys.

"Yay!" Lily says. "You are so smart, Sam! Now we can play some more!"

But then they hear a loud voice. It is Dad. He is not happy.

"Hey!" Dad says. "What are you doing? You are wasting water and making a mess! Turn off that hose right now!"

Lily and Sam look at each other. They are scared. They turn off the hose and run to Dad.

"Sorry, Dad," Sam says. "We were just playing."

Dad sighs. He is not really angry. He loves his kids. But he wants them to be careful.

"I know, I know," Dad says. "But you have to be more responsible. Water is precious and we have to save it. And you have to clean up your toys and dry them off. Or they will get ruined."

Lily and Sam nod. They understand. They hug Dad and say they are sorry. They promise to be more careful next time.

Dad smiles. He hugs them back and says he loves them. He helps them to clean up the garden and dry the toys. He thinks they are crazy, but he also thinks they are wonderful.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Bobby. He was only three years old and he was very curious. One day Bobby decided to go on an adventure and he picked some oats from the garden to take with him. 

As Bobby traveled through the garden he heard an animal calling out to him. It was a squirrel who had gotten stuck in a tree and he was asking Bobby to help him. 

Bobby decided he should help and he started to come up with a plan. He thought to himself 'Maybe if I throw the oat up to the squirrel he can eat it and have enough strength to get down.' So Bobby threw the oat up high, but it didn't make it to the squirrel.

The squirrel scolded Bobby, telling him he was stupid for not planning his plan better.  Bobby nodded politely and said "Okay, I'll try it again and this time I will make a better plan. 

Bobby carefully decided that this time he would stand on a box and throw the oat up to the squirrel. He tried the plan and it worked perfectly! The squirrel was finally free and thanked Bobby for his help.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play sport with his friends. They would run and kick a ball around. One day, Timmy's friend brought a fake ball to play with. Timmy didn't like the fake ball because it didn't bounce like a real ball. He wanted to slap the fake ball away, but his friend said it was all they had to play with. So, they played with the fake ball and had fun anyway.

Once there was a mighty man who lived in the forest. Every day he used to go fishing in the nearby lake and collect coins. One day he got a dare from his friends to jump off a cliff and swim across the lake. The man thought it was an impossible task, but he was brave and decided to take up the challenge. He took a deep breath and jumped off the cliff into the lake below. With a mighty splash he swam across the lake to the other side. There he found a huge pile of coins lying on the ground. He was so surprised to see a treasure of coins that he jumped out of the lake and ran back home to show his friends the coins. From then on the man never took up a dare without thinking twice.

John was very organized. Every morning he would bring his carpet to school. On the carpet were many special toys. They were kept in a special way so they were easy to find. 
At recess, John would unroll the carpet. All the children would gather around. Everyone loved to play the games. John would organize a game of tag and the children would laugh and giggle as they ran around. 
John would also organize a hide and seek game. Everyone would hide behind the carpet. Then, when the seeker found them, they would all burst into laughter. 
At the end of the day, John would roll up the carpet and take it home, looking forward to the next day when he could bring back his favorite carpet again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to discover what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Lily!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a treasure or a secret cave!"

"OK, Ben!" Lily said. "But be careful. It looks dark and spooky over there."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They heard a loud noise. It was the wind. It was blowing hard and making the trees shake and the leaves fly.

"Wow, look at the wind, Lily!" Ben said. "It's so strong and fast!"

Lily felt scared. She did not like the wind. It made her cold and it made her hair go in her eyes. She wanted to go back to the park.

"Ben, I don't like the wind," Lily said. "Can we go back, please?"

Ben looked at Lily. He saw that she was scared. He wanted to make her feel better.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. "We can go back. But first, let's do something fun. Let's make a kite!"

Ben found a stick and a plastic bag. He tied the bag to the stick with a string. He gave it to Lily.

"Here, Lily," Ben said. "This is a kite. You can hold it and let the wind lift it up. It will fly like a bird!"

Lily took the kite. She felt curious. She wanted to try it.

"Thank you, Ben," Lily said. "How do I make it fly?"

Ben showed her how to hold the string and run with the kite. They ran down the hill, laughing and shouting. The kite flew high in the sky, dancing with the wind.

Lily felt happy. She liked the kite. She liked the wind. She was not scared anymore.

She hugged Ben and said, "You are the best, Ben. You made me discover something new and fun. I love you."

Ben hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best, too. You made me discover something new and sweet."

Once there was a little boy who hated to sing. Every day, his Mom asked him to sing a song and he would cry. He was very worried and didn't want to do it. One day, his Mom brought him a special song. It was bright and sunny, just like a day at the park. 

The little boy was so excited, he could hardly wait. He listened to the song and smiled. His worries were gone and he began to sing! Soon, he was singing and laughing and having so much fun. His Mom was so proud of him.
 
The little boy never hated singing songs anymore. He sang them all the time and enjoyed every minute of it! His Mom was so happy and always praised him for being so brave. He was the best singer in the house!

Once upon a time, there was a big swamp. In the swamp, there lived an elderly frog. The elderly frog had many friends.

One day, the elderly frog saw a little fish. The little fish was sad. The elderly frog asked the little fish, "Why are you sad?" The little fish said, "I want to find a friend."

The elderly frog said, "I will help you." They swam and swam in the swamp. They met a big turtle. The little fish said, "I want to be your friend." The big turtle smiled and said, "Yes, I want to be your friend too."

Now, the little fish was happy. The elderly frog, the little fish, and the big turtle were all friends. They played and had fun in the swamp every day. And they lived happily ever after.
