Raquel ran out of the house, into the big backyard, with a smile on her face. In her hand, she held her yellow ball. She looked up at the sky and saw a kite so high. She wanted to try flying it. 

Raquel asked her mom, "Can I fly the kite?" Mom said, "Let's give it a try." They started walking to the big field. 

When they reached the field, mom showed Raquel how to hold the kite in her palm and with a big push, it was flying in the sky! Raquel couldn't believe how high it had gone. She stared at the kite as it flew around and around.

Mom said, "You did a great job flying it!" Raquel smiled and said, "Can we do it again tomorrow?" Mom laughed and said, "Of course!" 

Raquel was so happy that she had mastered flying the kite. The next day she asked if she could fly it again, and again, and again.

Once upon a time, there was a famous girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She asked her mom if she could borrow her bike, so she could go on a journey.

Her mom said yes and told her, to be careful and not to get lost. She said goodbye and off she went.

The girl peddled all day until she came to a special meeting. It was a meeting of famous people. They were all so excited to see the girl arrive. They all said hello and talked with her.

The girl enjoyed talking with them and was sad when it was time to leave. She thanked them all and said goodbye. Then, she hopped on her bike and pedaled off onto her next adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls in the evening before bedtime. One day, she found a magic potion that made things shrink. She thought it would be fun to try it on her dolls.

Lily poured the potion on her dolls and they started to shrink. She was happy at first, but then she realized that her dolls were too small to play with. She felt uncomfortable and sad.

Lily's mom noticed her daughter was upset and asked her what happened. Lily explained what she did with the potion and how her dolls had shrunk. Her mom tried to help but couldn't fix the dolls.

Lily went to bed that night feeling sad and lonely without her dolls. She learned that sometimes playing with magic can have bad consequences.

Alice was very frustrated. She wanted to play with her friend, Sammy, but he was nowhere to be found. She looked around the playground but Sammy wasn't there. Alice decided to look in the ocean. She tiptoed to the shore and peered over the edge. There was Sammy, hiding in the blue water! He must have been very quiet, because Alice hadn't heard him. 
 
Alice waved to get his attention, and Sammy came out of the water. He had a big smile on his face and was laughing. They jumped in the sand and played a fun game of hide and seek, taking turns hiding and looking for one another. 

When they were tired, they both smiled and looked out at the vast ocean. They were so lucky to be able to find each other among such a big ocean. Sammy and Alice held hands and were thankful for their special friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sally. Sally was young and liked to explore. One day, Sally went to the beach and asked her mum, "What is the tide?" Her mum explained that the tide was the water that comes in and out of the beach. Sally thought this was very funny and said to her mum, "Let's go and play in the tide!"

So they both stepped out into the water. It was beautiful and the sun was shining down. Sally was running around, splashing and playing. She was having so much fun. Eventually they had to leave, but Sally was already planning her next trip to the beach.

Just before they left, Sally asked her mum, "When will the tide come back?" Her mum said, "The tide will come back tomorrow. It's really beautiful so let's come back!" Sally was so excited and couldn't wait for her next adventure.

Timmy had a large dog named Max. Max was always very happy and playful. One day, Max stopped eating and seemed sad. Timmy asked his mom what was wrong, and she said that Max was sick.

Timmy was very worried and wanted to help his dog. They called the veterinarian and made an appointment. The veterinarian gave Max a checkup and said he was going to be OK.

Timmy was so happy, but he still missed Max when he had to go to the vet. He wanted to be there to take care of him. Timmy was so relieved when Max came back home feeling better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain. One day, she went for a walk in the forest to find some herbs for her mommy's dinner. It was raining a lot, and Lily got very wet. 

As she was walking, she saw a big truck driving on the road. The truck was carrying a lot of herbs! Lily was very happy because she knew that the truck would bring the herbs to her mommy's store. 

When Lily got home, she told her mommy about the truck full of herbs. Her mommy was very happy too and thanked Lily for finding out. Later that day, the truck arrived at the store and her mommy was able to buy all the herbs she needed. Lily was proud of herself for helping her mommy and finding the herbs.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their toy jets. They liked to make zooming noises and pretend they were flying in the sky. Sometimes they would strike each other's jets and say "Boom!" or "Crash!"

One day, a big jet flew over the park. It was loud and fast and shiny. Lily and Ben looked up and saw it. They were amazed and excited. They wanted to see it better.

"Let's follow it!" Ben said. He ran after the jet, holding his toy. Lily followed him, but she was worried. She did not want to go too far from the park. She did not want to get lost.

"Ben, wait!" Lily called. "We don't know where it's going. We should go back."

But Ben did not listen. He kept running and running. He wanted to catch the jet. He did not see the road or the cars or the people. He only saw the jet.

Lily ran after him, but she could not keep up. She was scared and tired. She wanted to go back to the park. She wanted to find their mom.

"Ben, stop!" Lily shouted. "We're in trouble. We need to go back."

But Ben did not hear her. He was too far away. He was too busy chasing the jet. He did not see the red light or the big truck. He only saw the jet.

Lily saw the red light and the big truck. She saw Ben running into the road. She screamed and dropped her toy. She wanted to save Ben. She wanted to strike the truck. She wanted to make it stop. But she could not. She was too small and too late. She only saw the jet.

Once upon a time, there was a big aeroplane. It was very messy inside. The aeroplane needed help to organize everything. So, it asked the animals to help clean up.

The nice animals like the dog, the cat, and the bird came to help. They worked together to organize the aeroplane. But there was a rude monkey who did not want to help. He just sat and watched the other animals work.

After the aeroplane was clean and organized, it was time to fly. The nice animals got to ride inside the aeroplane and have fun. The rude monkey was sad because he did not get to ride. The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run really fast, but he also loved to scatter his toys all over the house. His mom would always tell him to pick them up, but he never listened. 

One day, Timmy's mom told him that she had a present for him. Timmy was so excited! He asked his mom what the present was, but she wouldn't tell him. She said he had to pick up all his toys first. 

Timmy didn't want to pick up his toys, so he ran away. His mom was sad because she wanted to give him the present, but Timmy was too busy scattering his toys everywhere. 

Later that day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy showed him all his toys, but his friend accidentally stepped on one and broke it. Timmy got very upset and started crying. His friend said sorry, but Timmy didn't want to forgive him. 

Timmy's mom came in and saw what happened. She told Timmy that it's okay to be upset, but it's important to forgive his friend. She also reminded him that if he had picked up his toys, they wouldn't have gotten broken. Timmy realized his mistake and apologized to his friend. His mom then gave him the present she had been saving, and Timmy was so happy.

One day, a little boy named Jack went for a walk in the forest with his mom. They were having a great time, running and jumping around when Jack noticed a small wooden door in the ground. He went up to it and tugged on the knob. His mom told him to be careful, but he didn't listen. He opened the door and fell inside!

Jack couldn't see anything; it was dark. Suddenly he heard a strange voice. It asked him why he had opened the door. Jack was scared, but he bravely answered that he had wanted to explore. The voice then said that it was the home of a magical shape. It was there to help anyone who came in.

Jack was filled with curiosity and asked the voice what he should do. It told him that he had to follow a path of tasty food that was scattered on the floor. So Jack did as he was told and began to follow the path! Along the way, he found all sorts of shapes including a heart, a star and a triangle.

When he reached the end of the path, he saw a bright light. It was coming from a chest. Inside the chest was a beautiful diamond shaped diamond. Jack eagerly picked it up and ran back out of the door.

Back outside, Jack excitedly showed the diamond to his mom. To his surprise, she scolded him for picking it up without asking permission. She reminded him how important it was

Anna and Ben wanted to make a surprise for their mom. They decided to prepare jelly for her, because she liked it very much. They found a box of jelly powder in the cupboard and a big bowl in the sink. They poured some water in the bowl and added the powder. They stirred it with a spoon until it was all mixed.

Then they had a creative idea. They wanted to make the jelly more fun and colorful. They looked around the kitchen and found some things they could add to the jelly. They found some grapes, some chocolate chips, some cheese, some ketchup, and some salt. They thought these things would make the jelly taste better and look prettier. They put them all in the bowl and stirred them again.

They were very proud of their jelly. They put it in the fridge and waited for it to set. They wanted to give it to their mom when she came home from work. They cleaned up the kitchen and went to play in their room.

When their mom came home, she saw the bowl of jelly in the fridge. She was very happy and thought it was a nice surprise from her kids. She took it out and put it on the table. She called Anna and Ben to come and have some jelly with her. They ran to the kitchen and smiled.

"Mom, we made this jelly for you!" they said. "We were very creative and added some things to make it more fun and colorful!"

Their mom looked at the jelly and saw the grapes, the chocolate chips, the cheese, the ketchup, and the salt. She felt sick and angry. She did not like these things in her jelly. She thought it was a bad joke and not a nice surprise.

"Anna and Ben, this is not jelly, this is a mess!" she shouted. "How could you do this to me? You wasted the jelly powder and the other food. You made a big mess in the kitchen and in the fridge. You are very naughty and not creative at all!"

She threw the bowl of jelly in the trash and sent Anna and Ben to their room. They started to cry and felt very sorry. They did not mean to make their mom mad. They wanted to make her happy. They did not know that their jelly was bad. They thought it was good. They wished they had not made the jelly at all.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle bunny named Lucy. Lucy loved to skip and play with her friends in the sunny meadow. One day, Lucy and her friends decided to watch a movie together.

They found a movie about a big, happy family of animals. Lucy and her friends sat down and watched the movie. They laughed and clapped as the animals on the screen played and had fun together.

When the movie was over, Lucy and her friends went outside to play. They skipped and hopped, just like the animals in the movie. They were all very happy and had a great day together.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toy box. They had many toys of different shapes and colors. Some were soft, some were hard, some made sounds, and some had wheels. But their favorite toys were the gems. The gems were shiny stones that sparkled in the light. They had gems of red, blue, green, yellow, and purple.

One day, Tom and Lily decided to organize their toy box. They wanted to make it neat and tidy. They took out all their toys and put them in piles. They put the soft toys in one pile, the hard toys in another pile, the toys that made sounds in another pile, and the toys that had wheels in another pile. Then they looked at their gems.

"How should we organize our gems?" Tom asked Lily.

"Let's organize them by color," Lily said. "We can make a rainbow with our gems."

"That's a good idea," Tom said. "You start with the red gems, and I'll start with the purple gems. Then we'll meet in the middle with the green gems."

Tom and Lily began to organize their gems by color. They put the red gems in a line, then the orange gems, then the yellow gems, and so on. They made a long and curved rainbow with their gems. They were very happy with their work.

"Look at our gem rainbow!" Lily said. "It's so impressive!"

"It's the most impressive thing I've ever seen!" Tom said. "Let's show it to Mom and Dad."

They ran to find their parents and brought them to their toy box. Mom and Dad were very proud of Tom and Lily. They praised them for organizing their toy box and for making such a beautiful and impressive gem rainbow. They gave them hugs and kisses and told them they were very clever and creative. Tom and Lily smiled and hugged them back. They loved their toy box, their gems, and their parents.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park with their dog, Spot. They liked to run and jump and slide and swing. Spot liked to chase and bark and fetch and roll. They were having a lot of fun.

But then, they saw a big hole in the fence. They were curious. They wanted to see what was on the other side. They told Spot to stay and they crawled through the hole. They found a big field with flowers and trees and birds. They felt happy.

They did not see the sign that said "Beware of the Bull". They did not hear the loud moo that came from behind the bushes. They did not notice the big, angry animal that was running towards them. They were in danger.

Ben and Mia heard Spot's bark. They saw the bull and Spot. They were shocked. They realized they were in trouble. They ran back to the hole. They crawled through and hugged Spot. John had a new toy that he wanted to try out. He asked his Mom if he could play in the park with it. She said yes and he ran outside with his new toy. 

In the park, he saw a fountain that he had never noticed before. He walked up to the fountain and looked closely. He loved it! The sparkling water looked so inviting and the colors and shapes seemed to fit perfectly together. 

John couldn't believe his luck and he immediately asked his Mom if he could accept the fountain as his toy. His Mom smiled and said yes. 

From that day on, John's new toy was the fountain. He would play around it, dipping his hands in the cool water and watching the bubbles float up to the surface. He was so proud of his new toy and thanked his Mom for helping him make it fit in the park.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia was different from other kids because she had magic in her hands. She could reach out her hands and make things happen.

One day, Mia met a sad boy named Sam. Sam was upset because he lost his toy. Mia wanted to help him. She said, "Don't worry, I can help you find your toy with my magic hands." Sam looked at Mia and asked, "Really? How?"

Mia reached out her hands and closed her eyes. She used her magic to find Sam's toy. Suddenly, the toy appeared in front of them. Sam was so happy and said, "Wow, thank you, Mia! Your magic hands are amazing!"

From that day on, Mia and Sam became best friends. They played together every day and had lots of fun. Mia's magic hands always made their playtime more fun and exciting.

Once upon a time, there was a festival. All the people were so excited! Everyone wanted to be successful.

John had a big plan. He wanted to climb to the top of the festival! All day, he looked and planned. He made sure he was very safe.

John worked hard until it was dark. He climbed and climbed until he made it to the top. All the people cheered! John was so happy; he was successful! 

John enjoyed the beautiful view from the top of the festival. He was so proud of himself. He thanked everyone for believing in him. 

John had a wonderful day. He learned that you can do big things if you work hard and believe in yourself.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful fish. The fish swam around having lots of fun. But then a big scary thing came. It was a big green monster and it had big teeth. The monster made a threat to the fish, scaring it away.

The fish was frightened, but it was also brave. It took a deep breath and decided to be brave. The fish started to wave its tail and fins, gracefully back and forth. The monster was so taken aback by the fish's grace that it stopped threatening the fish and swam away.

The fish was so happy and swam around happily again. All of its friends were so happy too. The fish was very proud of itself for being so brave and graceful.

One day, Johnny was driving in his car. He looked out the window and saw a big gray building that said 'jail' on it. Johnny wanted to know what was inside. So he parked his car and got out.

Johnny opened the big door of the jail and looked inside. He saw lots of cells and people inside them. He was surprised! Then he heard a noise. It was a police truck that was coming to load the people into the truck.

Suddenly, Johnny became scared. He didn't want to get loaded into the truck. He quickly ran back to his car. He drove away from the jail as fast as he could!

Johnny was glad he was safe. He had learned his lesson. He learned that he should always be careful and never go too near the gray jail again.

Once upon a time there was a large thumb. The thumb was very insistent and wanted to do something fun. So it decided to go on an adventure.

The thumb hopped and skipped around the garden and soon arrived at the pond. But when it tried to step into the pond, the water was too deep and the thumb was scared. The thumb insisted that it wanted to go deeper, but the water didn't listen.

The thumb started to daydream. It imagined all sorts of things it could do if it only had someone to help it. Suddenly, it spotted a tall, strong frog on a nearby lily pad. The thumb asked the frog to help it go deeper into the water and the frog agreed.

The frog grabbed the thumb with its long, slimy tongue and tugged it into the pond. The thumb was so excited that it could finally explore the deep pool. 

The thumb thanked the frog and went on a grand underwater adventure. It had so much fun finally experiencing the pond that it insisted on visiting again soon!

Lily wanted to play with her scooter. She liked to go fast and make turns. She put on her helmet and went outside. She saw her friend Ben on the sidewalk. He had a ball.

"Hi, Lily," Ben said. "Do you want to play catch with me?"

Lily shook her head. "No, thank you. I want to play with my scooter."

Ben looked sad. He liked to play catch. He asked Lily again. "Please, Lily. It will be fun. You can play with your scooter later."

Lily refused. She did not want to play catch. She wanted to play with her scooter now. She said, "No, Ben. I don't like catch. Catch is boring. Scooter is fun."

Ben felt angry. He did not like Lily's answer. He wanted to make Lily play with him. He had an idea. He saw a lemon on a tree. He picked it and ran to Lily. He squeezed the lemon on Lily's scooter. The juice was sour and sticky.

Lily screamed. She saw her scooter covered in lemon juice. She was very mad. She said, "Ben, you are mean! You ruined my scooter! Go away!"

Ben laughed. He thought it was funny. He said, "Now you have to play with me. Your scooter is bad. Catch is good."

Lily did not think it was funny. She did not want to play with Ben. She wanted to play with her scooter. She ran to her house and told her mom. Her mom was not happy. She said, "Ben, you have to say sorry to Lily. You have to clean her scooter. You have to be nice to your friends."

Ben did not want to say sorry. He did not want to clean the scooter. He did not want to be nice. He refused. He said, "No, I don't. Lily is not my friend. She is mean. She does not play with me."

Lily's mom and Ben's mom talked. They decided that Ben had to go home. He had to learn how to share and be kind. Lily cleaned her scooter with a cloth. She played with her scooter again. She had fun. She hoped that Ben would be a better friend next time.

Once upon a time, there was a high sun in the sky. It was very bright and it shined on everything. One day, the sun made a record in the sky. It was so high that everyone saw it. Everyone was so happy that they clapped and cheered. Even the birds sang a song to celebrate. Everyone agreed that it was the best record ever. They smiled and enjoyed the beautiful sun. 

The sun shone high in the sky for a long time. It made everything happy and bright. Every day, the sun would record something special in the sky. Clouds, rainbows, stars, and more. Everyone loved watching the sun record in the sky.

Every night they would watch the sun go down and they said goodbye to it. They knew that it would come back the next day, and they would see its beautiful record once again. They thanked the sun for making everyday special. The sun was always willing to share its record with everyone. 

The End.

Lily and Tom are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. Lily wants to give the snowman a glove, but she only has one. She looks for the other glove, but she cannot find it.

"Tom, do you have my glove?" she asks.

"No, I have my own gloves. See?" Tom says, showing his hands.

"Maybe we can ask Mom for another glove," Lily says.

They run to the house and knock on the door. Mom opens the door and smiles.

"Hello, my little snowflakes. What do you need?" she asks.

"Mom, can we have another glove for the snowman? We only have one," Lily says.

"Sure, let me see what I have. You can come in and warm up for a bit," Mom says.

She goes to the closet and finds an old glove that she does not use anymore. She gives it to Lily and says, "Here you go. This glove is very helpful. It can keep the snowman's hand warm and cozy."

"Thank you, Mom. You are very helpful too," Lily says.

She hugs Mom and runs back to the snowman with Tom. They put the glove on the snowman's other hand and smile.

"Look, we finished the snowman. He looks very happy," Tom says.

"Yes, he does. And he has two helpful gloves," Lily says.

They clap their hands and dance around the snowman. They are very happy too.

Mary and Jimmy were at the beach. "Let's go sailing!" shouted Jimmy. So they got in the boat, and set out on the sea. 

The water felt cool and nice, and the sun was shining brighter than ever. Soon, the boat started to melt! Mary and Jimmy started to cry.

But then a giant whale came to their rescue! He blew some cool air onto their boat, and soon seemed like it was new again! Mary and Jimmy laughed and smiled.

Suddenly, however, an imp rudely spoke out. He said that Mary and Jimmy should leave the beach immediately. 

But then the whale spoke. "No one can be this rude to my friends Mary and Jimmy," he said. And so the imp flew away. Mary and Jimmy waved goodbye to the friendly whale, and sailed back to the beach to have fun and play.

Once there was a little girl named Sally. She was always friendly to everyone she met. One day, Sally was playing in the park when a rude dog suddenly barked at her. The dog was a threat and Sally was scared.

Sally started to cry and ran away from the nasty dog. She ran to her mother and told her what happened. "Don't worry, sweetheart," her mother said. 

Sally's mother felt bad for the little girl and wanted to help. She knew she had to protect Sally so she took her to the pet store. There she bought a big strong chain that could keep the rude dog away from Sally.

The chain worked and Sally was able to play in the park again without having to suffer from the threat of the rude dog. 

From then on, Sally always enjoyed her time in the park and was never afraid again.

Tom was a king. He had a big crown made of gold and jewels. He liked to wear his crown and sit on his throne. He felt very important and proud.

One day, he had to go to a party with other kings and queens. He wanted to show off his crown and make them jealous. He put on his best clothes and his crown and walked to his carriage.

But on the way, he did not see a stone on the ground. He stumbled and fell. His crown flew off his head and rolled away. He hurt his knee and his nose. He cried out loud.

"Help! Help! Where is my crown?" he shouted.

A girl who was passing by heard him. She saw his crown and picked it up. She ran to him and gave it back.

"Here is your crown, sir. Are you okay?" she asked.

Tom took his crown and looked at it. It was dirty and bent. Some of the jewels were missing. He felt miserable.

"Thank you, but my crown is ruined. It is not shiny and pretty anymore. The other kings and queens will laugh at me. I don't want to go to the party anymore," he said.

The girl felt sorry for him. She smiled and said, "Don't be sad, sir. Your crown is not the most important thing. You are still a king. You have a big heart and a kind voice. You can make people happy and help them. That is what makes you a good king. The other kings and queens will like you for who you are, not for what you wear."

Tom listened to her words. He wiped his tears and smiled back. He realized she was right. He thanked her and hugged her. He put on his crown and got on his carriage. He went to the party and had fun. He made new friends and learned new things. He was happy and proud. He never forgot the girl who helped him. He always remembered to be a good king.

Once upon a time, there was a generous horn. It would snap every time someone walked by. One day, a little boy heard the horn snap and he was curious. He snuck around the corner to see what was making the sound.

When he got closer he saw a old, friendly man. The man was holding the generous horn and playing a cheerful tune. The boy was so excited that he started to dance and clap his hands.

The boy asked the man if he could try the generous horn. The man said, "of course, go ahead". The boy smiled and put the horn up to his lips. He took in a deep breath, and then he snapped.

The sound of the generous horn filled the air. Everyone around stopped and smiled. The boy was so proud that he could make the horn snap.

The man smiled and told the boy, "now you are a part of the band". From that day forward, the boy and the man would play the generous horn loud and proud together.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl named Sue. She loved to explore and play outside. 

One day, Sue was in the backyard when she saw a big ship in the distance. She squealed with excitement and ran over to it.

But when she got closer, the ship ignored her. It just sailed away, leaving Sue confused. She asked her mom why the ship had ignored her.

"Sometimes, ships ignore people," her mom said. "That doesn't make you any less special. Don't worry, soon another ship will come your way."

Sue smiled. She knew her mom was right - and she was excited for the next ship that she'd find!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She wanted to make something special. So she got some copper, which is shiny and smooth. She started to prepare. First she formed it into a bowl. It was an empty bowl. Then she put it in a hot oven to bake.

When it was out of the oven, she looked at it and smiled. It was beautiful. Now it was full of hope and possibilities. She put it aside and went to get some things she will use in the bowl. First she put in some eggs and then some butter. Then she stirred until it all was mixed.

The little girl was so happy. She had made something special and it was ready. She put it in the oven to bake. When it came out, it smelled so yummy. She tasted it and it was delicious!

The little girl was very proud of her special dish. She knew that she had made something amazing with her copper bowl. With it's help she was able to turn empty ingredients into a tasty creation!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved muffins and ate them every day. One day, she went to her favorite bakery to buy a muffin but they were all gone. She felt gloomy and sad.

But then, the baker came out and said, "Don't worry, I will replace the muffins soon." Lily was happy to hear that and waited patiently. Soon, the baker came back with a fresh batch of muffins and gave one to Lily. She was so happy and took a big bite. It was delicious!

From that day on, Lily knew that even if things seemed gloomy, they could always be replaced with something better. And she continued to enjoy her muffins every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a polite cactus. The cactus lived in a big garden with many friends. One day, the cactus met a little bird. The bird was very sad.

The cactus asked the bird, "Why are you sad?" The bird said, "I can't number my friends. I want to know how many friends I have."

The cactus wanted to help the bird. So, the cactus told the bird, "I can help you number your friends. Let's find them together."

They looked around the garden and found all the bird's friends. They counted them one by one. The bird was happy to know the number of friends. The bird thanked the cactus and they became good friends. From that day, they played together in the big garden and had lots of fun.

Once there was a boy called Sam. He was three years old. One day he saw a big stone. He wanted to try and move it. It was very heavy. So he tried and tried but he couldn't move it. He was getting hot and sweaty so he decided to take a break.

Suddenly, he had an idea. He decided to use some of the mild soap that he had at home to try and move the stone. He ran to his house, using all his strength to carry the soap back. He poured it on the stone. The soap made the stone slippery. Sam put both his hands on the stone and with one big push he moved the stone!

He was so happy. He smiled and shouted with joy. He had achieved something he didn't think he could do. Sam felt so proud of himself and his strength. He had tried and it worked!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was a restless girl who always wanted to play. One day, her mom gave her a big piece of candy. Amy was so happy to receive the candy. She played with it and showed it to her friends.

Amy's friends wanted a piece of candy too, but Amy didn't want to share. Her friends were sad and went away. Amy played alone with her candy, but she started to feel lonely.

As the day went on, Amy ate her candy. But she ate it too fast, and her tummy began to hurt. She cried because she was in pain and had no friends to help her. The bad ending is that Amy learned that she should have shared her candy and played with her friends.

Andy was so excited for his first day of school. He put on his backpack and skipped all the way to the classroom. As he walked into the classroom, he heard the teacher say "Welcome! Let's start with a safe game of bounce."

Andy was so excited, he couldn't wait to try. He ran up to the middle of the room and said to the teacher, "Let me try first!"

The teacher smiled and said, "Okay then, Andy. Bounce the ball all the way around the room!"

Andy excitedly started bouncing the ball. He bounced it around all the tables and chairs in the classroom. He bounced it through the door and back around again. Andy felt very safe, even though he was bouncing alone.

When he was done, the teacher smiled and said, "Well done, Andy! You can keep bouncing around the classroom whenever it's safe to play!"

Andy smiled and bounced his way back to his seat. He couldn't wait to come back to school tomorrow!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anne. She wanted a slide, so she asked her mommy if she could have one. 

"Please, Mommy? Can I have a slide?" she asked excitedly. 

Her mommy smiled and told her she would look for one. Soon, Daddy and Mommy took Anne to a store.

"Look, Anne! This slide is very cheap. Can you see it?" asked Daddy.

Anne was so excited! She said yes, it was very cheap. So, Mommy and Daddy bought it for her.

When they got home, Annie quickly ran outside to get the slide. She put it all together and it was ready to go. 

Anne asked, "Can I come on it now?" 

"Yes, of course, Anne," said Mommy.

So, Anne jumped on the slide and went down it many times. She was so happy! 

She thanked Mommy and Daddy and said, "I love my new slide!"

Anna and Ben love to watch cartoons on TV. They sit on the sofa with their snacks and laugh at the funny animals and people. Sometimes they point at the screen and say what they see.

"Look, look, a big red car!" Anna says, pointing at a cartoon about a racing car.

"Vroom, vroom, it goes so fast!" Ben says, making a sound like a car.

They watch the car zoom past the other cars and win the race. They clap their hands and cheer.

"That was a brilliant cartoon!" Anna says.

"Yes, it was!" Ben agrees.

They hear a knock on the door. It is their mom, who has come back from work.

"Hi, kids, how was your day?" she asks, smiling.

"We watched cartoons, mom, they were brilliant!" Anna and Ben say together.

They hug their mom and tell her about the cartoons they watched. She listens and nods.

"I'm glad you had fun, kids. Do you want to help me make dinner?" she asks.

"Yes, please, mom!" Anna and Ben say.

They turn off the TV and follow their mom to the kitchen. They help her wash the vegetables, stir the soup, and set the table. They talk and laugh and enjoy their time together. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved winter. She loved to play in the snow and make snowmen. One day, she was playing outside when she saw her friend Jack.

"Hi Jack!" said Lily.

"Hi Lily!" said Jack. "I don't like winter. It's too cold and the snow is too thick."

Lily felt sad because she wanted Jack to like winter too. "Why don't you try to accept winter, Jack? It can be fun!" she said.

Jack thought about it and decided to give winter another try. He put on his warm coat and went outside to play with Lily. They made a big snowman together and had so much fun. Jack realized that winter wasn't so bad after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hear stories before bed. One night, her mom read her a story about a princess who needed to be saved from a bad dragon.

Lily was scared and asked her mom if the princess was going to be okay. Her mom said, "Don't worry, the prince will save her and they will live happily ever after."

Lily felt better and fell asleep. The next day, she told her friends the story and they all played pretend, pretending to be the prince and saving the princess from the bad dragon. It was a fun day and Lily was happy that everyone was safe.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. But today they have a fight. Lily wants to play with the red car. Ben wants to play with the red car too. They both pull the car and shout.

"Mine!" Lily says.

"No, mine!" Ben says.

They are not happy. They are angry.

Mom sees them and comes to help. She takes the red car and puts it on the shelf. She says, "No more fighting. You need to share and be nice. Why don't you play with something else?"

Lily and Ben look at the shelf. They see a big book with pictures and words. They like the book. Mom says, "This is a sign book. It shows you how to make signs with your hands. You can learn new signs and talk with them. Do you want to try?"

Lily and Ben nod. They want to try. Mom opens the book and shows them a sign. She says, "This is the sign for clean. You rub your hands together like this. Can you do it?"

Lily and Ben do the sign for clean. They rub their hands together. They smile. They like the sign. Mom shows them more signs. They learn the signs for hello, thank you, sorry, and more. They have fun. They forget about the red car. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a very nice park. All the animals and birds lived happily together. There was peace everywhere.

But one day, something terrible happened. Two of the animals had a big fight. They made such a lot of noise that all the other animals got scared and ran away.

The park was soon quiet. Everyone was gone, and there was no peace. The animals were too scared to come back.

The people in the town were very sad. They liked to go to the park and it was important to them. They loved the peace there.

The people thought and thought about what to do. Then someone had a wonderful idea. They decided to give the animals something special. If they shared it, the animals might learn to get along.

So the people got the animals a special treat. As soon as they started to share it, peace came back to the park. Everyone was happy and peace was important again.

Once upon a time, a thin team of four friends went on an adventure. The friends were named John, Daisy, Tom and Lucy. As they travelled and explored, they came across an old chest.

John approached the chest and exclaimed "What's this?" Tom replied, "Let's open it and find out!" Daisy agreed and they all surrounded the chest and opened it together. 

To their surprise, they revealed a secret map! John looked at the map and declared, "Let's follow this path and see where it leads!"

The friends all held hands and followed the map. As they walked, they heard a singing voice. They came closer and revealed a beautiful fairy! The fairy said, ""Hello!" and welcomed the team. She then granted the team a wish.

The team was positively excited and John said, "Let's wish for an adventure!"
The fairy waved her wand and with a twinkle of her eye, their wish was granted. A bubble floated up from the ground, and inside was a surprise that would reveal their exciting new adventure ahead.

Lila and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sometimes they found worms, or ants, or beetles. They put them in a jar and watched them.

One day, they found something different. It was gray and hard and had many legs. It did not move or make any sound. Lila and Ben thought it was dead. They put it in the jar with the other bugs.

That night, Lila and Ben left the jar on the window sill. They went to bed and dreamed of bugs. But the gray thing was not dead. It was sleeping. And when the moon came out, it woke up. It was a firefly. It had a light in its belly that could glow.

The firefly saw the other bugs in the jar. They were scared and sad. They wanted to go out and be free. The firefly felt sorry for them. It used its light to make a hole in the lid of the jar. Then it flew out and helped the other bugs escape.

Lila and Ben woke up in the morning. They looked at the jar. It was empty. They saw a hole in the lid. They wondered what happened. They looked out the window. They saw the firefly and the other bugs flying away. They saw the firefly's light glow in the sun. They smiled and waved goodbye. They learned that some bugs are not dead, but magic.

Once upon a time there was a tall cherry tree. A little girl named Candy wanted to get some of the bright red cherries, but they were very high off the ground. She tried to reach one but it wasn't easy.

Candy's mom came over and asked, "What are you doing?"

"I want to get those cherries," said Candy.

"Well how about we go for a nap first, and when we wake up I'll help you get those cherries," suggested her mom.

So Candy and her mom had a nap. When they woke up, they went to the cherry tree. Candy's mom found a long stick and was able to help Candy pick all the cherries she wanted.

Candy was so happy that she and her mom had gone for a nap, because now she was able to get as many cherries as she wanted. The two of them ate cherries all day until they were full and very happy.

Once there was a boy called Sam. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, he and his friends wanted to go to the park, but they didn't have enough tickets. They tried to be flexible but the ticket-seller wouldn't let them in.

Sam was angry and he started to fight the ticket-seller. His friends tried to calm him down, but he wouldn't listen. Finally, his mum arrived and she scolded him for fighting.

Then the ticket-seller had an idea. He said he would let all of them in if they worked together to clean up the park. Sam, his friends and even his mum agreed to help.

In the end, they all had fun. Everyone worked hard and the park looked super clean. The ticket seller was impressed by their hard work and let them all into the park for free.

From then on, Sam and his friends always worked together and stayed flexible when facing new challenges. They learned that it was possible to get what you want without having to fight.

Once upon a time, there were four brothers who lived together in a big house. They were very happy, but sometimes they argued and it made them sad.

One day, they argued so much that they decided to split into two groups. One group was made up of two brothers and the other group was made up of two brothers.

The two brothers in the first group were strong and tough. The two brothers in the second group were weak and scared.

The two strong brothers started laughing at the two weak brothers. The two weak brothers were very upset.

One of the weak brothers called out, "It's not fair. Just because we're a bit weaker doesn't mean you should make fun of us!"

The two brothers on the other side stopped laughing and said, "Sorry!" They all hugged and made up. From then on, they always stayed together and were very happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden with her mom. They would water the flowers and pick some herbs for dinner. Lily's favorite herb was basil because it smelled so good. 

One day, Lily's mom surprised her with a fancy dress for their tea party. Lily loved the dress and twirled around in it. They enjoyed their tea with some biscuits and talked about their favorite things. 

At the end of the day, Lily hugged her mom and said, "I love you, Mommy." They both smiled and felt happy. Lily went to bed dreaming about their next tea party in the garden.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room. They liked to look at the books on the bookcase. There were many books with pictures and stories. Some books were big and some books were small. Lily wanted to see a book with a princess and a dragon. She saw one on the top shelf. She tried to reach it, but it was too high.

"Ben, can you help me?" she asked her brother. "I want that book."

Ben looked at the book. He wanted it too. He was taller than Lily, but not much. He stretched his arm and his fingers. He almost touched the book, but not quite.

"Sorry, Lily, I can't get it," he said. "It's too high for me too."

Lily was sad. She really wanted that book. She looked around. She saw a chair near the bookcase. She had an idea. She ran to the chair and dragged it to the bookcase. She climbed on the chair and reached for the book. She was happy. She got the book.

"Ha, I got it!" she said. "Now I can see the princess and the dragon."

Ben was not happy. He wanted that book too. He was angry. He ran to the chair and tried to pull the book from Lily's hands. Lily held the book tight. She did not want to share it.

"Let go, Ben, it's mine!" she said. "I got it first!"

"No, let go, Lily, it's mine!" he said. "I saw it first!"

They pulled and pulled. They shouted and shouted. They did not listen to each other. They did not see their mom coming.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. "What are you doing?"

They looked at their mom. They felt scared. They let go of the book. The book fell on the floor.

"We were fighting for the book," Lily said.

"We both wanted the book," Ben said.

Their mom picked up the book. She looked at the cover. She smiled.

"This is a nice book," she said. "It has a princess and a dragon. And it has a lesson. Do you know what the lesson is?"

They shook their heads. They did not know.

"The lesson is that sharing is caring," she said. "If you share the book, you can both enjoy the story. And you can be happy and kind to each other. But if you fight for the book, you can hurt each other and the book. And you can be sad and mean to each other. Which one do you prefer?"

They thought for a moment. They did not like to hurt each other or the book. They did not like to be sad or mean. They liked to enjoy the story. They liked to be happy and kind.

"We prefer to share the book," they said.

"Good," their mom said. "That's a wise choice. Now, why don't you sit on the couch and read the book together? I'll make some cookies for you. And remember, no pinching, no pushing, no shouting. Only reading, listening, and smiling."

They nodded. They said sorry to each other. They hugged each other. They took the book and sat on the couch. They opened the book and looked at the pictures. They read the words and listened to the story. They smiled and laughed. They learned the lesson. They shared the book. They were happy.

The sun was bright and the sky was blue. It was a good day for playing.

John peeked around the corner. He saw something! He couldn't quite figure out what it was, so he snuck closer to take a better look. As he peeked again, he saw a saw. He gasped at the sight of it.

John was scared but he wanted to know what the saw was for. He reached out his hand and grabbed the saw. He was even more scared when he saw it move.

Suddenly, a loud noise startled him. He dropped the saw and ran away. He looked back one last time and saw that the saw had cut a wire. He knew it was a bad sign and ran even faster.

When John got back home he found out that his house had lost power! He knew that the saw that he had touched had caused all the trouble. He was very sad, but he had learned a good lesson: never touch something that you don't know.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a rhinoceros named Rosie. Rosie loved to bounce up and down all day long. She would bounce on the soft grass and make her friends giggle.

One day, Rosie met a little bird who was sad. "Why are you sad, little bird?" Rosie asked. The bird said, "I tried to eat a spicy bug, but it was too hot for me." Rosie thought hard, then she had an idea. "Let's go find a sweet bug for you to eat instead!"

So, Rosie and the little bird went on a hunt for a sweet bug. They looked under leaves and on tree branches. Finally, they found a sweet bug for the little bird to eat. The bird was so happy and thanked Rosie.

From that day on, Rosie and the little bird became best friends. They learned that helping others can make you happy too. And Rosie kept on bouncing, making everyone in the forest laugh and smile.

One day, Mama took her little boy to the park. He felt so glad! Everywhere he looked he saw so many things to explore. He played on the swings and ran around the grass.

When he got tired, Mama brought out a special lunch for him. It was delicious! He ate it all up and was so content.

Before they left, Mama took her boy for a special shower. The water was warm and it felt so nice. He played and splashed and was so happy.

Finally, after he was fed and washed, they said goodbye to the park. Mama was glad she had such a fun day with her little boy. He smiled and held her hand as they walked home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very patient and loved to explore new things. One day, she was out walking with her mom when she noticed something big and wide. She was so excited to see what it was, so they set off to find out.

They soon realised it was a lake, so big and wide that it went on forever. As they stopped to admire its beauty, Lucy noticed a small boat by the side of the lake. She eagerly asked her mom if they could go on a boat ride and was overjoyed when she said yes!

So, with patience and excitement, Lucy and her mom sailed around in the boat for hours. As the day went by, Lucy learned that even when you're patient and take your time, you can discover amazing things and get exciting new experiences.

The moral of the story is that patient is rewarded and being excited for the things you find can help lead to new and adventurous experiences.

Once there was a powerful man who wanted to mix something special. He took a newspaper and cut it into tiny pieces. He then poured the tiny pieces into a bowl, added a few drops of water and stirred them with a spoon.

The man looked into the bowl and could see that it was now mixing like a tornado. He thought it looked very cool and interesting.

The man then took the bowl outside, and using his powerful hands, he tossed the mix high into the sky. It twirled, flew around and sparkled in the sun.

The man smiled - he had made an incredible mix that was so much fun to watch! He knew he would never forget the wonderful mix he had made.

Once upon a time there was a small kid named Bob. Bob lived with his Mom and Dad and he had a lot of toys to play with. One day, Mom and Dad decided to take Bob to the park. 

When they arrived at the park, Bob saw other kids playing and he wanted to join them. But he was a bit scared because they looked bigger and older than him.

So, Dad came up with an idea. He said, "Let's play a game of tag. Bob, why don't you be It?" 

Bob liked the idea and quickly agreed. He started chasing the other kids around and he really enjoyed it. He even managed to tag a few of them.

Soon, it was time for Bob to go home. As he was leaving, one of the kids said, "Hey Bob, you're so bossy. You made all the motions". All the other kids laughed and Bob felt proud. He had made all the decisions and managed to tag almost everyone.

He smiled and it was time for him to go home. He had enjoyed playing at the park and made a lot of new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sugar and always asked her mom for candy. One day, her mom said no and Lily got very mad. She decided to sneak into the kitchen and take some sugar from the cabinet. 

But when she was pouring the sugar into her mouth, she accidentally spilled it all over the floor. Lily was embarrassed because she knew her mom would be angry. She tried to clean it up, but she couldn't get all of the sugar off the floor. 

Later that day, Lily's mom came into the kitchen and saw the mess. She was very upset and told Lily that she regretted letting her have any candy at all. Lily felt very sad and wished she had listened to her mom. From then on, she always asked before taking anything from the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the fields. One day, he saw a big, strong bull in the distance. The bull was very scary and Timmy was afraid. 

But then, Timmy had an idea. He decided to peek at the bull from behind a big rock. He was very careful not to make a sound. To his surprise, the bull was not scary at all. In fact, the bull was very modest and shy. 

From that day on, Timmy visited the bull every day. He would bring him fresh grass and water. The bull was very grateful and they became good friends. Timmy learned that sometimes things that seem scary aren't really that bad.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Gally and Timmy. They both liked admiring different things outside. One day, Gally wanted to do something fun. "Letâ€™s go rowing!" Gally said. 

Timmy was excited and agreed. They started paddling on the water and admiring the nature around them. Gally wanted to see what else was around and decided to go across the river. Timmy, however, thought it was too dangerous and told Gally to turn back. Gally refused, insisting that he wanted to be creative.

Timmy tried to talk some sense into Gally, but he wouldnâ€™t listen. So, against his better judgement, he followed Gally across the river. When they were almost halfway, their boat started rocking and things started going wrong. Gally was too scared to do anything and Timmy had to take charge and row the boat back.

When they safely reached the shore, Gally started to understand the danger of being too curious and seeking the unknown. He thanked his friend Timmy for his bravery and promised never to be too adventurous again. 

The moral of the story is that itâ€™s okay to admire new things, but you must always be mindful and use caution. Donâ€™t be too creative and risk getting into trouble!

One day, Susan the sheep was feeling very lucky. She had been wandering around the village all day, and wanted to see something new. She urged herself to try something different.

On the outskirts of the village, she noticed a small, modern house. She had never seen anything like it before. She stayed very still and watched the house from a distance.

Suddenly, a voice called from inside the house. "Hey there! Come on in, why don't you?"

Susan hesitated for a moment, but then she eagerly went closer. When she arrived at the door, the kindly old lady inside welcomed her with a big smile.

The woman showed Susan around the house, and explained to her about all the modern gadgets inside. Susan had so much fun!

The old lady thanked Susan for visiting and gave her a big hug before she left. Susan left feeling very happy, grateful that she had urged herself to try something new.

Once upon a time there was a fake dragon. He was very sharp and he liked to play with the other animals. He was best friends with the turtle and the two of them were always together. One day the dragon climbed high up into a tree and the turtle tried to follow but couldn't make it up the trunk. The funny dragon called down to his friend and insisted the turtle join him. Finally, the turtle found a way up and the two friends laughed and laughed as they shared the view from their high perch. 

When they returned to the ground, they saw a real dragon! It was big, and very sharp and neither the dragon nor the turtle knew what to do. The dragon put on a brave face and made a fake roar. The real dragon roared back and then flew away.

The dragon and the turtle felt relieved and excited. They decided that they had been brave and made a special pact - they would remain friends forever.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was afraid of monsters. She was so scared of them that she didn't want to go to bed at night. Every day she asked her mom if the monsters were gone and every day her mom said yes.

One night, when the little girl was sleeping, she heard a noise. She was so scared that she jumped out of bed and hid under the bed covers. "Mommy," she whispered. "Are the monsters still here?"

Her mom came into the room, smiled, and said, "No, sweetheart. I'm here to give you a welcome surpriseâ€”it's a crazy surprise!"

The little girl was so excited that she jumped out from under the bed covers and shouted, "Really?!"

Her mom laughed and said, "Yes, really. Now come and see your surprise!"
The little girl was so happy she ran out of the bedroom to see what the surprise was. When she got there, she saw the most amazing thing she'd ever seenâ€”a beautiful toy castle with a surprise inside! She was so surprised, she said, "Wow!"

The little girl was so happy she ran to give her mom a big hug. From that day forward, she was never afraid of monsters again because she knew her mom would always be there to give her a special surprise.

One day, a young girl named Sarah was playing in her backyard. She saw something shiny and started to dig it up. It was a gold crown! Sarah was so excited, she started dancing around in circles.

Suddenly, her neighbor called out from his porch. "What do you have there, Sarah?" 
He could barely contain his surprise when Sarah held up the crown.

The neighbor smiled. He pointed to the crown and said, "That looks like a special crown. It must be a very special treasure. It could be very valuable."

Sarah didn't understand what he meant, so she just smiled and continued to twirl around.

Days passed and Sarah continued to wear the crown proudly. One day when she was visiting her grandmother, the old woman said, "Sarah, I used to be a queen when I was young. That's why you have the crown. You must use it wisely." 

Sarah suddenly realized that the crown was more than just a toy. She carefully put it back in the box and made sure to take special care of it. She knew that one day it would be a reminder of her young queen days.

There once was a very big zoo. In the zoo, there were many animals and birds. One day, two children, John and Jane, went to the zoo. 

John was only three, but he was very brave. He followed Jane down a path and eventually they came to a big elephant. John was amazed.

Jane smiled at John and said, "Do you want to pet it?"

John nodded and with a trembling hand, he put his hand on the elephant's trunk. It was very soft and the elephant made a happy noise. John's face lit up with joy.

John and Jane continued their trip down the path. Everywhere John went, he was in awe of what he saw! At the end of their trip, the two of them had seen the biggest animals they had ever seen!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk by the creek. She saw a frog and said, "Hello frog, are you happy?"

The frog nodded his head and said, "Yes, I am very cheerful today! Would you like to play with me?"

Lily was so happy to have a new friend to play with. They played together by the creek, jumping and splashing in the water. They had so much fun that they didn't even notice the time passing by.

When it was time for Lily to go home, she said goodbye to the frog and promised to come back and play again. As she walked home, she felt cheerful too, knowing she had made a new friend by the creek.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and cuddle with her teddy bear. One day, Lily went to a hotel with her family. The hotel had a big pool and a yummy breakfast.

At the hotel, Lily saw a pretty vase in the lobby. It was very fragile and could break easily. But a bad man came and stole the vase! Lily was very sad and told her parents what happened. They called the police and the bad man was caught.

Lily learned that stealing is wrong and that we should always be careful with fragile things. She was happy to go back home with her family and her teddy bear. The end.

Once there was a little raven who needed help. He was very impatient and did not want to wait. He asked a frog, a fox and a chicken to help him, but they all said no. The raven became angry and flew away feeling sorry for himself.

Eventually he stopped at a pond and saw an old turtle. He asked the turtle if she could help him and the turtle said yes. The little raven was surprised and thanked her.

The turtle was very wise and taught the little raven that patience is a virtue. She explained to him that it was important to wait for help as good things can often take more time than expected.

The little raven was so impressed with the turtle that he decided to be patient in the future. He thanked her again, waved goodbye and flew away with new knowledge. The moral of the story is that patience often brings good rewards.

Sam and Mia are playing in the park. They like to imagine that they are superheroes. Sam wears a red cape and Mia wears a blue mask.

"Look, there is a big tree!" Sam says. "Let's climb it and save the birds!"

"OK, but be careful!" Mia says. "The tree is very high and the branches are thin."

They run to the tree and start to climb. Sam goes first and Mia follows him. They see many birds on the tree. They are singing and flying.

"Hello, birds!" Sam says. "We are here to help you. Do you have a goal?"

One bird looks at Sam and says, "Yes, we do. We want to find a new home. The old one is too small and noisy."

"Where do you want to go?" Mia asks.

"We want to go to the lake. There is more water and food there. But we don't know how to get there. It is far and we are afraid of the big animals."

"Don't worry, we can help you!" Sam says. "We are superheroes. We can fly and protect you. We have a useful idea. Follow us!"

Sam and Mia jump from the tree and spread their arms. They pretend to fly and lead the birds to the lake. The birds follow them and thank them.

"Thank you, superheroes!" the birds say. "You are very kind and brave. You helped us reach our goal. We are happy in our new home."

"You are welcome, birds!" Sam and Mia say. "We are happy to help you. We like to imagine and have fun. Goodbye, birds!"

Sam and Mia wave to the birds and go back to the park. They smile and hug each other. They are proud of their adventure. They imagine more stories and play until it is time to go home.

Tom was a patient boy. He liked to wait for his mom to read him a story before bed. He picked his favorite book, with pictures of animals and colors. He climbed into his bed and hugged his teddy bear.

"Mom, can you read me this book?" he asked, holding up the book.

"Of course, my sweetie," his mom said, sitting next to him. "Let's see, what is this book about?"

She opened the book and started to read. Tom listened carefully and pointed at the animals he knew. He saw a lion, a monkey, a zebra, and a giraffe. He learned some new words, like elephant and hippo.

He yawned and rubbed his eyes. He was feeling sleepy, but he wanted to hear the end of the story.

"Mom, what happens next?" he asked.

"Well, the animals are all friends and they play together in the jungle. They have fun and they help each other. They are happy and they say good night to each other," his mom said, turning the last page.

She closed the book and kissed Tom on the forehead. "Just like we are happy and we say good night to each other, right?"

"Right, mom," Tom said, smiling. "I love you."

"I love you too, my patient boy," his mom said, tucking him in. "Sweet dreams."

She turned off the light and left the room. Tom closed his eyes and cuddled his teddy bear. He thought about the animals and their friends. He yawned again and fell asleep.

Once upon a time there was a driver who was very clever. He drove his car every day and took many different people to different places.

One day, he was driving and he saw something that made him stop. It was a small dog that had appeared from nowhere. The driver was amazed and he asked the dog, "Where did you come from?" 

The dog replied, "I'm lost, please help me!"

The driver was very clever and so he knew just what to do. He leaned out the window and asked the dog, "Do you remember where you live?"

The dog started to bark and the driver followed. Eventually the driver drove the dog back to its home.

The driver was so pleased he felt like a hero. He knew he had done something clever and he felt very proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and she loved to explore the outside world.

One day, Lucy was out in the garden playing. It was a lovely day and Lucy was having a lot of fun. Suddenly, a bug landed on her arm.

"What's this?" asked Lucy, but the bug didn't answer.

Then, a voice from behind her said, "It's a bug, Lucy. Be careful!"

Lucy turned around and saw her mom. Her mom was smiling and trying to warn Lucy about the bug.

"That's ok, Mom," said Lucy. "I like bugs. It's very lovely."

So Lucy and the bug continued playing together. Lucy learned about the bug and it was a wonderful experience.

Lucy was very thankful that her mom was there to warn her about the bug. She loved her mom very much.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a powerful king. The king had a magic wand that could restore things. One day, a big storm came and took away the power from the town. All the people were sad and scared.

The king said, "Don't worry, I can help." He took his magic wand and waved it in the air. With a "whoosh," the power came back to the town. The people were so happy and thanked the king.

The king told the people, "We must always help each other when we can." The people learned that being kind and helpful is what makes someone truly powerful. And from that day on, they all worked together to make their town a better place.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in the cabin in the woods. The cabin was old and small, but it had many toys and books. Ben and Sam had fun with the toys and books.

One day, they heard a loud noise outside. They looked out the window and saw a big truck. The truck was red and shiny. It had a bald man driving it. The bald man got out of the truck and knocked on the door.

"Hello, boys," the bald man said. "I'm sorry to delay your play, but I need to talk to your dad. He asked me to fix the roof of the cabin. It has a hole and it leaks when it rains."

Ben and Sam were curious. They wanted to see the hole and the roof. They asked the bald man if they could help him.

"Sure, you can help me," the bald man said. "But you have to be careful. The roof is high and steep. You have to wear these helmets and gloves. And you have to listen to me and do what I say."

Ben and Sam nodded. They put on the helmets and gloves. They followed the bald man to the ladder. They climbed up the ladder and saw the hole. It was big and dark. The bald man had a hammer and some nails. He showed Ben and Sam how to fix the hole with some wood and tar.

Ben and Sam helped the bald man. They held the wood and the nails. They spread the tar. They hammered the nails. They worked hard and fast. They fixed the hole.

"Good job, boys," the bald man said. "You are very brave and smart. You helped me a lot. Now the roof is good and strong. It won't leak anymore."

Ben and Sam smiled. They were proud and happy. They thanked the bald man. They climbed down the ladder. They ran to the cabin. They told their dad what they did. Their dad hugged them and praised them. He gave them some cookies and milk. They ate the cookies and drank the milk. They went back to the cabin. They played with the toys and books. They had more fun.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy cat. He was always falling into things and getting into all sorts of trouble. One day, he was playing in the grass when his collar suddenly vanished! He was so surprised that he just stayed there looking for it. He searched and searched but he couldn't find it anywhere. Finally, he gave up, feeling sad without his collar.

Just then, a kindly old lady appeared. She said she had seen a little sparkle near the river and thought it might be his collar! She helped the cat down to the river and, sure enough, the collar was there! It had been washed up on the shore and was looking a little bit wet, but otherwise it was good as new.

The cat was so happy he thanked the kind old lady, and went on his way, ready to explore the world again with his cozy collar safely around his neck.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Susie.

One day, Susie wanted to do something fun. So she decided to start singing. She chose a very funny song to sing. She started to dance around and sing. Everyone around her started to laugh and giggle because her singing was so funny.

Susie had so much fun singing and dancing. She kept singing the funny song until she could hardly breathe. After a while, her mommy and daddy came to give her a big, warm hug.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a clever musician. He sailed on a boat in the big blue sea. He was having so much fun! He started to sing and dance and the fish were very happy.

Suddenly, he heard a strange noise. It was a dolphin who loved his music! The dolphin asked the musician to sail with him under the sea. The musician happily agreed and they both sailed happily.

They travelled through the sea, deep and deeper. Finally, they had to go back up again. The musician was sad but the dolphin was happy and thanked him for sailing with him all the way. The musician waved goodbye to the dolphin and sailed back home.

Once there was a lion. He was big and hairy. He wanted to go exploring. He thought and thought about where to go. He decided to go to the jungle. 

He walked through the trees and saw some monkeys. He said hello but they ran away. He was so sad. He kept walking and saw a butterfly. He was so happy. He followed the butterfly for a while. 

The butterfly flew higher and higher. Soon, the lion was so high that he could see the whole jungle. It was so beautiful. He stayed there for a while, watching the trees. Then, he started to walk back home. 

On his way back, he decided to be a better friend. He wanted to make sure that if he ever saw the monkeys again, they wouldn't be scared. 

The lion continued walking and soon he was back home. He was very happy and thought about all of his new friends. He knew he would have many more adventures soon.

Tommy loved to draw with his pencil. He drew cars and planes and houses and animals. He drew on paper and on the wall and on the floor. Sometimes his mom got mad at him for making a mess, but Tommy did not care. He wanted to be an artist.

One day, Tommy found a big, blank canvas in the garage. It was white and smooth and perfect for his pencil. He dragged it to his room and put it on his bed. He climbed on the bed and started to draw. He drew a big sun and a blue sky and a green field. He drew a brown cow and a yellow duck and a pink pig. He was very happy.

"Tommy, what are you doing?" his mom asked, opening the door. She saw the canvas and the pencil and the drawings. She was very angry. "Tommy, this is not your canvas! This is your dad's canvas! He is a painter and he needs this canvas for his work! You ruined it with your filthy pencil!"

Tommy was scared. He did not know the canvas was his dad's. He did not know his dad was a painter. He thought his dad was a doctor. He wanted to say sorry, but he could not find the words.

His mom grabbed the canvas and the pencil and threw them in the trash. She told Tommy to go to the corner and think about what he did. Tommy went to the corner and cried. He felt very bad.

Later, his dad came home. He saw the trash and the canvas and the pencil and the drawings. He was very curious. He took them out and looked at them. He saw the sun and the sky and the field. He saw the cow and the duck and the pig. He smiled. He saw something else. He saw a small, faint signature at the bottom of the canvas. It said "Tommy".

He went to Tommy's room and found him in the corner. He knelt down and hugged him. He told him he was not mad. He told him he liked his drawings. He told him he was proud of him. He told him he was an artist.

Tommy was surprised. He looked at his dad and saw his smile. He smiled back. He felt very happy.

He asked his dad if he could draw with him. His dad said yes. He gave him a new pencil and a new canvas. He told him to stretch his imagination and have fun. Tommy did. He drew with his dad and they had fun. They were both artists.

Once upon a time, there was a big fierce lion. He lived in the jungle and loved to hunt. One day, he found a track of a rabbit. The lion followed the track and found the rabbit's house. 

The rabbit was cooking some carrots when the lion arrived. The lion said, "I'm going to eat you and your carrots!" But the rabbit replied, "Please don't eat me, I'll give you all my carrots!" 

The lion agreed and the rabbit gave him all the carrots. But the lion was still hungry and decided to eat the rabbit anyway. The poor rabbit was eaten by the fierce lion and the jungle was never the same again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who lived in a small house. They were a happy bunch and liked to have fun. One day, mama said, "Let's go to the park!" 

So, they packed a basket and off they went. At the park they met a strange rabbit. He seemed very friendly and he said, "Do you want an invitation to the ball?" 

The family gaped at the rabbit. They had never heard of a ball. Fancy invitations were not something they were used to. But the rabbit seemed kind and mild, so they said yes. 

"When is it?" Papa asked.

The rabbit said, "Tomorrow night. I'll come back here tomorrow and take you to the ball." 

The family was so excited. They couldn't wait to see what the ball would be like!

Once there was a brother who was very cheerful. He loved to laugh and play. One day he wanted to cover himself up so he got his blanket. He spread it out over his head and body and quickly it covered him up. Now he couldn't see anything and it made him laugh. He was having so much fun.

Then his brother saw what he was doing and decided to join in. He got his own blanket and covered himself up too. Now the two of them were both covered up with their blankets. They laughed and giggled as they felt the warmth from the blankets.

After a while, they took off their blankets. The two brothers looked at each other and smiled. The cheerful brother's face was full of joy! They had so much fun being covered up and giggling like little kids.

There was a little girl and she had a cat. The cat was big and grey, and it was very bossy. Every day, it would demand to be petted. The little girl would be very happy to pet her cat, so every day she would give it lots of scratches and belly rubs. The girl's mom didn't like how bossy the cat was and she usually yelled, "Go away!" when it demanded her attention. The little girl would always protect her cat and say, "Leave her alone. She just loves getting lots of rubs." The mom sighed, but she knew the little girl and her cat were best friends!

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls of different sizes and colors. She gave them names and clothes and made them talk to each other. She was very organized. She put her dolls in a big box when she was done playing.

One day, Lily's mom said they had to go to the store. Lily wanted to bring her dolls with her, but mom said no. "You have to remain here with dad," mom said. "We will be back soon. Don't make a mess, okay?"

Lily nodded, but she was sad. She wanted to play with her dolls. She looked at the big box and had an idea. She opened the box and took out all her dolls. She put them on the couch, the table, the floor, and the chairs. She made them have a tea party, a dance, a picnic, and a nap. She had a lot of fun.

But then she heard the door open. Mom and dad were back. Lily saw them and felt scared. She knew she made a mess. She ran to the couch and hid behind a pillow. She hoped mom and dad would not see her.

Mom and dad saw the dolls everywhere. They looked surprised and angry. They looked for Lily. They saw a figure behind the pillow. They walked to the couch and lifted the pillow. They saw Lily's face. She looked sorry.

"Lily, what did you do?" mom asked. "Why did you take out all your dolls? You were supposed to remain here and be good."

Lily did not know what to say. She felt bad. She loved her dolls, but she did not want to make mom and dad mad. She said in a small voice, "I'm sorry, mom. I was bored. I wanted to play with my dolls. I forgot to be organized."

Mom and dad sighed. They were not happy, but they loved Lily. They hugged her and said, "We understand, Lily. But you have to listen to us and follow the rules. Playing with your dolls is fine, but you have to put them back in the box when you are done. Can you do that?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. Yes, dad. I will be organized. I will put my dolls back in the box. I'm sorry I made a mess."

Mom and dad smiled. They said, "That's good, Lily. We forgive you. But first, let's have some cookies and milk. Do you want to share with your dolls?"

Lily smiled too. She said, "Yes, please. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad. I love you. And I love my dolls."

The end.

Lily and Ben went to the farm with Mom and Dad. They wanted to pick pumpkins for Halloween. Mom and Dad gave them each a basket and said, "You can pick any pumpkin you like, but only one. Look for a big, round, orange one."

Lily and Ben ran to the pumpkin patch. They saw many pumpkins, but some were too small, some were too green, and some had holes or spots. They looked and looked, but they could not find the perfect pumpkin.

Then, Lily saw something shiny in the grass. She went closer and saw a gold coin. She picked it up and showed it to Ben. "Look, Ben, I found a treasure!" she said.

Ben was happy for Lily, but he was also sad. He wanted to find a treasure too. He looked around, but he could not see anything shiny. He felt like crying.

Lily saw Ben's face and felt sorry for him. She remembered that Mom and Dad said they could only pick one thing. She thought for a moment, and then she had an idea. She gave the coin to Ben and said, "Here, Ben, you can have the treasure. I don't need it. I already have something better."

Ben looked at Lily and smiled. He took the coin and hugged her. "Thank you, Lily, you are very kind. What do you have that is better than the treasure?" he asked.

Lily pointed to a big, round, orange pumpkin that was hiding behind a scarecrow. "I have this pumpkin. It is the perfect pumpkin for Halloween. And I have you, Ben. You are my best friend. I am very grateful for you."

Ben and Lily carried their pumpkin and their coin to Mom and Dad. They were very happy and proud. Mom and Dad praised them for their good choices and their good hearts. They said, "You are very lucky, Lily and Ben. You have found the best things in the pumpkin patch."

Jack and his Mommy went to the store. They got a cart to put things in. Jack was happy. He was excited to help his Mommy pick up things. 

They picked some apples, pears, and bananas. He thanked his Mommy for them. Then then looked for something else.

Jack saw a toy on the shelf. He asked his Mommy if they could buy it. She said no. Jack was sad. He said sorry.

His Mommy said it was alright. She thanked Jack for being so understanding. They said goodbye and left. 

Jack was happy to have gone shopping with Mommy. And he thanked her again!

Once upon a time, there was a tall giraffe named Jerry. Jerry was very happy because he had strong muscles that helped him run fast and reach high leaves to eat. 

One day, Jerry's friend the monkey lost his banana. The monkey searched high and low but couldn't find it. Jerry offered to help and started to search too. 

They looked in the trees, on the ground, and even in the river. After a while, they found the banana hiding behind a tall rock. The monkey was very happy and thanked Jerry for his help. 

Jerry felt proud of his strong muscles that helped him search for the lost banana. From that day on, Jerry and the monkey were the best of friends and searched for lost things together.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky liked to play in the water with his friends. One day, Ducky and his friends found a big log in the water. They decided to roll the log and see where it would go. They pushed and pushed until the log started to move.
