"Thank you, Sam. You are very kind. This is a very nice gift. I like it a lot. But you know what? I like you more. You are my best friend." She said.

Sam smiled too. He hugged Lila back.

"You are welcome, Lila. You are my best friend too. I am glad you like the truck. But you know what? I like you more. You are very brave. You came from a far country. You miss your country. But you still try to be happy. You are very strong." He said.

Lila and Sam played with the truck. They laughed and talked. They forgot about the big city and the poor country. They were happy. They had each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to dream. She would dream of flying like a bird and swimming with the fish. One night, she had a mysterious dream about a big castle with a dragon guarding it.

The next day, Lily told her best friend, Timmy, about her dream. "I had a dream about a big castle with a dragon," she said. "Wow, that sounds cool!" Timmy replied.

As they were playing in the park, they saw a dog running towards them. Lily got scared and tried to run away, but the dog bit her leg. "Ouch! The dog bit me!" Lily cried.

Timmy quickly ran to get help, and Lily's mom came to take her to the doctor. As they were walking, Lily told her mom about her mysterious dream and how she wished she could fly away from the dog like in her dream.

"Don't worry, Lily. You'll be okay," her mom said, giving her a big hug. "And who knows, maybe one day you'll be able to fly like a bird in your dreams again."

Once upon a time, there was a big fish. He had long fins and big eyes. He liked to swim really fast. One day, the big fish saw a fancy hook. He went to have a closer look. But when he got close, something happened. The hook slapped the big fish on the nose! The fish was so surprised he jumped out of the water. He was so scared of the fancy hook that he decided never to go near it again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to visit her grandma who lived in a big modern house. When she arrived, her grandma was wearing a black dress and a big smile.

"Hello, Lily!" her grandma said. "I'm so happy you came to visit me today."

Lily looked around the house and saw many modern things like a big TV and a shiny new car outside. She was very impressed.

"Grandma, your house is so cool!" Lily said.

"Thank you, dear," her grandma replied. "I like to keep my house modern and stylish."

Lily and her grandma spent the day playing games and eating yummy snacks. When it was time to go home, Lily hugged her grandma and said, "I love visiting you, grandma. Your house is the best!"

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who had a dream to soar. So he built a plane out of plastic. He worked very hard to finish it, and when he was done, he was very happy. He put it on the ground, and climbed in. He was so excited when he got it rolling. He leaned forward and he soared! He felt like he was flying. He flew very high, until he could see the whole town. He was so happy and he smiled the whole way. Finally he touched the ground with his plane and he felt so proud of himself that he had made his dream come true.

Once upon a time there was a girl who had a huge mirror. Every morning she looked in the mirror and she was so happy with what she saw. One morning, the girl was running late and had to delay looking in the mirror. She ran to school without pausing to look at herself.

To her surprise, when she arrived at school, all her classmates said how pretty she looked. She wondered why and then she remembered the huge mirror at her house. She smiled.

When she came home from school, she found the huge mirror waiting for her. She looked at herself in the mirror and she smiled because she could see how wonderful she looked. The girl was happy that she had delayed looking in the mirror but she promised herself that she wouldn't do it again.

Ben and Lily were hungry. They saw a cake on the table. It looked yummy. They wanted to eat it.

"Let's take some cake," Ben said. "Mom is not here. She will not know."

Lily nodded. She took a fork from the drawer. She gave it to Ben. Ben cut a big piece of cake. He put it on a plate. He gave it to Lily. He cut another piece for himself.

They ate the cake. It was sweet and soft. They smiled. They ate more cake. They did not leave any cake.

Then they heard a sound. It was Mom. She came back from the shop. She saw the empty plate. She saw the fork. It was filthy. It had cake and cream on it. She was angry.

"Who ate my cake?" she asked. "It was for Grandma's birthday. She is coming soon."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt bad. They knew they did a wrong thing. They regretted eating the cake.

They said sorry to Mom. But Mom was still angry. She said they had to go to their room. They had to stay there until Grandma came. They could not play or watch TV. They could only think about what they did.

Ben and Lily went to their room. They were sad. They wished they did not eat the cake. They wished they listened to Mom. They wished they had a good ending. But they did not.

Once there was a girl who loved to listen. Everywhere she went she listened to the birds singing and the leaves rustling in the breeze. One day she decided to take a special journey.

She found a boat and paddled out onto the river. As she drifted along, she listened to the water burbling around the boat and the creak of the oars. Suddenly she heard a splash in the water.

It was a big fish! The girl was so excited. She forgot all about her journey and rowed towards the big fish. The fish was bigger than the boat and the girl was amazed. 

The fish was speaking. She looked carefully and listened to what it had to say. The fish told her an important lesson - always listen and never forget. 

The girl learned a valuable lesson that day and she never forgot it. She always remembered to listen and to never forget the lesson the big fish had taught her.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse who lived in a big yellow house. Every day, he would wake up early and take a little walk around the house. He loved to check for any new things that were happening.

One day, the mouse noticed a long green hose lying on the ground. He wanted to play with it, so he ran over to it. He tried to pick it up, but he couldn't because it was so fragile!

He was feeling sad and decided to go get something to eat. Just as he started to walk away, he heard a voice.

"Hello Mr. Mouse!" the voice said. "Do you want to play with my hose?"

The little mouse was so excited that someone was talking to him. He said yes and thanked the voice. The voice belonged to a frog who lived in the pond behind the yellow house.

The mouse and the frog spent the day playing with the long green hose. The mouse was so careful with it, because he knew it was fragile.
 
At the end of the day, the mouse said goodbye to his new friend and went inside his yellow house. He couldn't wait to come back out the next day and play with the hose again.

Mum and Dad were sitting on the sofa. It was very comfortable because it had two big cushions on it. Mum looked up at Dad and said, "Let's watch something on the TV". Dad smiled and nodded.

They both watched the TV for a while. After a few moments, a tall man walked into the room. He was wearing a big hat. Mum and Dad said hello to the tall man.

The tall man showed Mum and Dad something he had brought. It was a big, colourful balloon. Mum and Dad laughed when they saw it. The balloon was very shiny.

The tall man gave the balloon to Mum and Dad. They sat back down on the cushions and watched the balloon float around the room. It was fun to watch the balloon and see where it would go. The balloon was so bright and colourful. 

Mum and Dad watched the balloon for a long time until it finally floated up to the ceiling and couldn't be seen anymore. Mum and Dad smiled and hugged each other. They had a lot of fun watching the balloon.

One day, a clumsy dog named Spot wanted to play with his friends. Spot was not very good at running and jumping, but he loved to try. He asked his mom, "Mom, can you permit me to go play with my friends?"

His mom said, "Yes, Spot, you can go play. Be careful and have fun!"

Spot went to the park where his friends were playing. They were all running and jumping. Spot tried to run and jump too, but he fell down. His friends laughed, but they helped him up. They said, "It's okay, Spot. We all fall sometimes. Let's keep playing!"

Spot felt happy that his friends were kind. They played until the sun went down. When Spot went home, he told his mom about his day. She was proud of him for trying and having fun with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was walking with her mommy and daddy when she saw a big billboard. The billboard had a picture of a yummy ice cream cone on it.

Lily pointed at the billboard and said, "I want ice cream, please!"

Mommy said, "Okay, sweetie. Let's go find an ice cream shop."

Daddy said, "That sounds easy enough. There's one just down the street."

Lily was very happy and they all walked to the ice cream shop together. They got their ice cream cones and sat down to enjoy them. Lily smiled and said, "This is the best day ever!"

Once upon a time there was a lucky girl. Her name was Sarah and she was only three years old. She loved to play in the park, especially in the sand box. One day, while she played, she found a square. She was so excited and she decided to take it home. Sarah managed to carry the square all the way home, which made her very proud. 

Once she got home, she wanted to show her parents, so she ran inside. Her parents were so happy for Sarah and congratulated her for managing to get the square all the way home. Sarah was very happy, she knew she was lucky that day!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Lucy and she was very proud. Every day she would run and play in the sunshine.

One day, Lucy's mum asked Lucy to do something she didn't want to do. Lucy felt very sad and wanted to cry. But she decided she could be brave.

So she took a deep breath and started to do the job. She worked until it was finished. And when it was done she smiled without crying.

Lucy's mum was proud of her and said that she had done a wonderful job. Lucy looked up at the stars, at the big universe and remembered. It was the same way she felt when she was brave and didn't cry.

Lucy learned that it was possible to be brave and strong - even when things were tough. Being brave was something to be proud of in life.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big, shiny ball in the sky. It was the sun. They wanted to touch it, but it was too far and too hot.

"Let's make a ladder with sticks and stones," said Tom. "Then we can climb up and reach the sun."

"OK," said Lily. "But be careful. It is difficult to make a ladder. We need many sticks and stones."

They worked hard to make a ladder. They put sticks and stones on top of each other. But the ladder was not strong. It was wobbly and shaky.

"Look, we are almost there," said Tom. He climbed up the ladder. He wanted to be the first to touch the sun.

But the ladder broke. Tom fell down. He hurt his arm and his leg. He cried.

Lily ran to him. She hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you OK?"

Tom said, "No, I'm not OK. I'm sad and I'm in pain. And I didn't touch the sun."

Lily said, "Tom, you were silly. You can't touch the sun. It is too far and too hot. And you don't need to touch it. You can see it and feel it. It shines for everyone. It gives us light and warmth. It makes us happy."

Tom said, "You are right, Lily. I was silly. I wanted to have something that I can't have. And I didn't think about you. I was selfish. I'm sorry, Lily. Can you forgive me?"

Lily said, "Of course, I can forgive you, Tom. You are my friend. And friends help each other. Come on, let's go home. We can ask our moms to put some ice on your arm and your leg. And we can look at the sun from the window. It is beautiful."

They held hands and walked home. They learned a lesson. They learned that some things are not meant to be touched. And they learned that sharing is better than wanting. They were happy. The sun smiled at them. It shone for everyone.

Lily and Tom are brother and sister. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they find a big yellow box in the corner. They wonder what is inside.

"Can we open it?" Lily asks Tom.

"Let's ask Mom first," Tom says. He runs to the kitchen and finds Mom making lunch. "Mom, can we open the yellow box in the living room?" he asks.

Mom smiles and says, "Sure, you can. That's a special box for our family. It has some things from Grandma and Grandpa. They sent it to us for Christmas."

Tom runs back to Lily and tells her the good news. They open the box and see many things inside. There are books, clothes, toys, and pictures. They are very happy and excited.

"Look, Lily, this is a train set. We can use it to make tracks and tunnels," Tom says.

"Wow, Tom, this is a doll house. We can use it to make rooms and furniture," Lily says.

They take out the train set and the doll house and start to play with them. They have a lot of fun and make up stories. They thank Grandma and Grandpa for the nice gifts. They also thank Mom for letting them open the box. They hug and kiss Mom and tell her they love her. Mom hugs and kisses them back and tells them she loves them too. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sally. She was three years old and loved to write. One day she asked her mom for something special for her to write with. Her mom gave her a big box. Inside the box was a hat and a pen. Sally was so excited! She put on the hat and started to write.

But then Sally realized something strange. The hat was not real! It was fake. So Sally took it off her head and asked her mom, "Why is this hat not real?" 

Her mom replied, "Silly Sally, sometimes things look real but they aren't. That hat is only pretend!" 

Sally smiled and said, "Can I have a real hat?" 

Her mom laughed and said, "Yes! Let's go find you a real hat!" 

So they went off on an adventure to find a real hat. And Sally wrote a story about her experience on her way there. 

The End.

Mia was walking in the forest. She heard something that made her stop and listen. Was it a bird chirping? No, it sounded like whistling. She looked around and saw a strange man. He was holding a spear and looking very sad. 

Mia ran up to him. "Hello!" she said.

The man jumped and looked up. "Oh! I'm so sorry," he said. "I was just walking and the sun was so warm and I was feeling so lonely that I started to whistle." 

"It's OK," said Mia. "I like to whistle too. Will you be my friend?" 

The man smiled. "Yes I would love to be your friend," he said. 

Mia and the man were now best friends. They enjoyed walking in the forest and whistling together. Whenever the man felt sad, Mia would hug him and say, "It's OK. Everything will be alright." 

The man was so happy to have such a wonderful friend. He knew he would never feel alone again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big cooler near a bench. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there are snacks or drinks," Lily said.

"Or toys or books," Ben said.

They ran to the cooler and opened the lid. But they were disappointed. There was only ice and water and some cans.

"What are these?" Lily asked, picking up a can.

Ben shrugged. He did not know. He tried to read the label, but it had too many letters.

"Let's ask that man," he said, pointing to a man sitting on the bench. He looked old and tired.

They walked to the man and showed him the can.

"Excuse me, sir, what is this?" Ben asked.

But the man did not answer. He did not look at them. He did not hear them.

Lily tapped his shoulder. "Hello, sir, can you help us?" she asked.

But the man did not respond. He did not feel them. He was deaf.

Lily and Ben felt sad and confused. They did not know what to do.

They put the can back in the cooler and closed the lid. They decided to leave the man alone.

They went back to their toys and played some more. They hoped the man was happy. They wished they could talk to him.

Once upon a time there was Tom. Tom was a brave little boy who liked to march. Every day he would lay down his toys and march around the garden, singing and playing.

One day, Tom was having a perfect day. He was marching in big circles around the garden when he saw a beautiful butterfly. He stopped and watched it flutter, admiring its colours and grace.

Tom took a deep breath and stretched out his hands. Just as he was ready to catch the butterfly, it flew away. Tom sighed and smiled. "I will never catch one," he said.

Just then, Dad appeared. He smiled and told Tom, "No need to give up. Keep trying and one day you'll catch the perfect butterfly!"

Tom laughed and said, "Okay dad!" He then began to march once more and continued in search of the perfect butterfly.

Gina was on a tour with her family. They flew in an airplane, took a boat, then walked through a spicy forest. While they were walking, Gina started to sniffle, then she sneezed. Her family started to laugh, and her brother asked if the spicy smell made her sneeze. She shook her head and said, "No, I just sneezed from the breeze!" They all laughed and kept walking. The spicy air made them all sneeze, but they enjoyed the tour. They eventually made it back home and had some cold water. It was a very fun day!

Lily liked to print pictures with her crayons. She had many colors and papers. She printed flowers, animals, stars and more. She was very happy with her prints.

One day, she wanted to print a big sun. She found a yellow crayon and a big paper. She started to print a circle and many rays. She wanted to make the sun very bright and hot.

She printed and printed until the paper was full of yellow. She looked at her sun and smiled. She said, "This is the most beautiful sun ever!"

She wanted to show her sun to her mom. She picked up the paper and ran to the kitchen. But she was not careful. She bumped into the table and dropped the paper. The paper fell on the stove, where mom was cooking.

The paper caught fire. Lily screamed. Mom turned around and saw the fire. She quickly grabbed a pot and poured water on the paper. The fire went out, but the paper was burned and wet.

Lily cried. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry! I wanted to show you my sun, but I ruined it!"

Mom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie. I'm glad you're not hurt. But you have to be careful with fire. Fire is very hot and dangerous. It can burn things and hurt people. You should never put paper near fire. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I won't do it again."

Mom said, "I'm proud of you for being honest and sorry. But you don't have to be sad. You can print another sun. And I'm sure it will be beautiful too. Because you are a beautiful and creative girl. And I love you very much."

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom. Thank you for being nice to me."

Mom and Lily hugged and kissed. Then they went to the living room and printed a new sun together. They had fun and learned a lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a snake slithering in the grass. She felt scared and ran to her mommy.

"Mommy, mommy, there's a snake in the garden!" Lily said.

Her mommy came outside and saw the snake too. "Don't worry, Lily. The snake is weak and won't hurt us," her mommy said.

Lily felt better knowing that the snake wasn't going to hurt her. She watched as the snake slowly crawled away. From that day on, Lily always looked out for snakes in the garden.

Once upon a time there was a wild jungle. A family of animals were living in the jungle. Every day they would talk about how wonderful the texture of the jungle was. The warm sun and the soft grass felt nice between their toes.

One day, the animals decided to go on an adventure. They wanted to explore and see what else was out there. As they were walking, they came across a giant hill which felt really bumpy. The animals were curious and decided to climb the hill. As they got closer to the top, they started to mention how exciting the texture of the hill was. It was full of bumps and ridges and they loved it.

At the top of the hill, the animals found a wild river. They jumped in the river and started to swim. The cold water felt so good on their skin. They mentioned how wild it was to be swimming together in the river.

The animals had a great time exploring the wild jungle and playing in the river. They were happy to have ventured out and enjoyed the different textures of the jungle.

Once upon a time there was a new little bunny. Her name was Chloe and she was very excited to explore the world. 

One day she was hopping in the forest when something big happened! The trees began to shake and the ground rumbled. Chloe didn't know what to do, so she crouched down and covered her ears until the shaking stopped. 

When it was all over, Chloe looked around and saw all of the other animals. They were all looking just as scared as she felt. 

Suddenly, a wise old owl spoke up. "My friends," he said. "We just had an earthquake!"

Everyone looked confused. "What is an earthquake?" Chloe asked.

"It is a big shaking that happens sometimes," said the owl. "We all need to be careful when it happens!" 

Chloe thanked the owl for teaching her something new and, after that day, she liked to be extra careful whenever she heard rumbling in the ground.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who loved plants. She planted lots of them in the garden and took time to care for them every day.

One night, a dark storm came and all the plants got wet from the rain. When morning came, Sarah looked in the garden and saw that a dark plant was missing. She gasped and asked her mom, 
"Mommy, why is one of my plants gone?" 
Her mom said sadly, 
"Oh sweetie, sometimes things get lost during a storm. You will have to learn to accept that you lost it."

Sarah was very sad. She realised that if she had taken better care of her plants, maybe some of her plants would not have been lost.

The moral of the story is: When it comes to taking care of special things, it is important to protect and watch over them, so they don't get lost in bad storms.

The sun was shining, and it was a beautiful day. Suddenly, it started to rain. Mary was very sad. All her friends were outside playing, but now they had to go home.

Mary looked out the window and saw a kite. She had never seen one before. She opened the window and the kite flew away.

Mary quickly put on her coat and hat, and ran outside. She looked up into the sky and the kite was still there.

Mary chased the kite, but it was too fast. Every time she got close, it flew away again. Finally, she saw that the kite was available on the ground. She grabbed it, and made it her own.

Mary was so excited. She ran back home and showed everyone her new kite. The rain stopped, and now she could enjoy the beautiful day.

Joe was walking around the lawn. He believed that anything was possible. All of a sudden, he heard a loud noise. Joe was scared.

He ran to his parents and asked, "What was that?"

His mom said, "It was just a dog. Don't be scared."

Joe felt better and decided to go back out to the lawn to play. He jumped on the grass, ran around and threw around a ball. Then he heard another loud noise.

He got scared again and ran back to his parents. He was ashamed of his fear. His dad put an arm around him and said, "Don't worry son. There is nothing to be scared of. You need to believe in yourself and be brave. That's how you become stronger."

Joe nodded his head and ran back out to the lawn. He felt nervous but he knew that he could brave whatever scared him. He played on the lawn until it was dark. From then on, Joe had no fear. He knew that he could believe in him self, even when it got scary.

Once there was a good boy who loved to dream. Every night he would dream about building a big tower. One night, he dreamt he was holding a big bucket of stones. The stones were all different colours and sizes. He was careful to pick up the biggest stones for the bottom of the tower and the smallest for the top.

He kept dreaming and the tower began to get bigger and bigger. He was so excited, he didn't want his dream to end. Eventually, the tower was so tall, it almost touched the stars in the sky.

The good boy felt so proud of his tower, he wanted to keep it forever. But then he woke up, and it was all just a dream. Even though he was disappointed his tower wasn't real, he was still happy with his dream. It was almost like it was real.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big red bike that they shared. Sara liked to ride the bike very fast. She enjoyed the speed and the wind in her hair. Tom liked to ride the bike slowly. He enjoyed the flowers and the birds on the way.

One day, they decided to go to the park on their bike. Sara said, "Let me ride first. I want to go fast and have fun." Tom said, "OK, but be careful. Don't go too fast or you might fall." Sara nodded and got on the bike. She pedaled hard and zoomed away.

Tom waited for his turn. He watched Sara go around the park. She looked happy and excited. But Tom also saw something else. He saw a big hill at the end of the path. He knew that the hill was steep and slippery. He wondered if Sara would see it and stop.

Sara did not see the hill. She was too busy enjoying the speed. She reached the hill and went down. She felt a thrill and a scare. She tried to brake, but it was too late. She lost control of the bike and crashed into a bush.

Tom ran to help her. He saw that Sara was not hurt, but she was dirty and sad. She had scratches on her arms and legs. She had tears in her eyes. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I was too fast and foolish. I ruined our bike and our fun." Tom hugged her and said, "It's OK, Sara. I'm glad you're OK. We can fix the bike and play again. But next time, let's be more careful and slow."

They walked back home with their bike. They were both sleepy and sore. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that speed is not always good. They learned that sometimes, it is better to enjoy the simple things.

Anna and Ben are camping with Mom and Dad. They have a big tent with four beds. Anna and Ben like to play outside the tent. They see many trees, flowers and animals.

One day, they find a black cat near the tent. The cat is hungry and scared. Anna and Ben want to help the cat. They ask Mom and Dad if they can feed the cat.

Mom and Dad say yes, but they tell Anna and Ben to be careful. The cat may scratch or bite. They give Anna and Ben some milk and fish for the cat. Anna and Ben take the milk and fish to the cat.

The cat sees Anna and Ben. The cat meows and comes closer. Anna and Ben put the milk and fish on the ground. The cat smells the food and starts to eat. Anna and Ben watch the cat. They are happy to see the cat eat.

The cat finishes the food and licks its paws. The cat looks at Anna and Ben. The cat rubs its head on Anna's leg. Anna and Ben smile and pet the cat. The cat purrs and closes its eyes.

Anna and Ben say to the cat, "You are a good cat. Do you want to stay with us?" The cat nods and follows Anna and Ben to the tent. Mom and Dad welcome the cat. They say, "You can sleep with Anna and Ben. You are part of our family now." The cat, Anna and Ben snuggle in their beds. They are happy and warm.

Once upon a time, there was a wild bear. He liked to play in the forest with his friends. One day, he found a shiny rock and he wanted to make it shiny more. He went to his friend's lab and asked for help. His friend gave him a cloth and said, "You can polish the rock with this." The bear took the cloth and polished the rock. It became so shiny that he could see his reflection in it. The bear was happy and his friend was proud of him. From that day on, the bear loved to polish shiny things.

Once upon a time, there was a playful rabbit and it had an operation. After the operation, the rabbit felt very tired. So the doctors cleaned it very carefully.

They took a soft and clean cloth and wiped the rabbit's fur. Then they brushed it very softly. Finally, they rubbed the rabbit's fur with the cloth until it was spotless.

Then the doctors put the rabbit back in bed to take a nap. After a few hours, the rabbit felt much better and even more playful than before.

The doctors smiled and said it was a successful operation. The rabbit was so happy that it started hopping around around the hospital room as if nothing had happened.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the shop with her mommy. One day, while they were in the shop, Lily saw a toy she really wanted. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said no.

Lily was sad, but then a nice lady who worked at the shop came over and gave her a thoughtful smile. She said, "Don't worry, maybe you can save up your money and buy the toy next time." Lily felt better and thanked the lady.

As they were leaving the shop, Lily accidentally slapped her mommy's hand. She quickly said sorry and her mommy forgave her. They walked home together, happy and excited for their next trip to the shop.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, he went to the park to catch some butterflies. He saw a yellow one and tried to catch it, but it flew away. Timmy was sad that he didn't catch the yellow butterfly.

The next day, Timmy went to a fishing competition with his dad. Timmy's dad told him that whoever catches the biggest fish wins a trophy. Timmy was so excited and wanted to catch a fish too. He put his fishing line in the water and waited patiently. Suddenly, he felt a tug on his line and started to reel it in. He caught a big yellow fish! Timmy was so happy that he won the trophy for catching the biggest fish.

From that day on, Timmy loved to catch things. He caught butterflies, fish, and even a ball during a game of catch with his friends. Timmy was proud of his trophy and showed it to everyone he met. He knew that catching things was fun and could lead to great rewards.

One day, a little girl was running fast through the park. Her feet felt light and she had a big smile on her face. Suddenly, she tripped and dropped to the ground. Her knee started to hurt. She started crying, but her mom was nearby. She gave her a big hug, and then she helped her up again.

Her mom promised to be more careful next time, and reminded her to not run so fast. The little girl promised to be more careful and keep her speed down. With a smile on her face, she was ready to keep playing.

The next day, the little girl was running again. She was going faster that usual and the ground was slippery. Her foot slipped and she felt herself drop. She hit the ground and it hurt. But then, mom was there. She hugged her and reminded her to always pay attention and keep her speed down.

The little girl was sad, but she learned an important lesson: pay attention and don't run too fast. She was ready to start playing again, this time a little slower.

There was a little girl with dark hair. Her name was Joy. She lived in a big house with her parents. One day, Joy was playing outside in her garden. Suddenly, she felt something on her leg - something pinching her. It was a big, black bug! 

Joy screamed and tried to get away, but the bug kept following her. She tried to run and hide, but it was too quick. 

Joy's parents heard her cries and came running. They used a stick to help her get rid of the bug. After the bug was gone, they hugged Joy and told her everything would be alright. 

When the bug was gone, Joy felt relieved and happy. She went back to playing in the garden, making sure she didn't step on any more bugs.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were walking along the beach. One friend said to the other, "I wish I could belong to a jellyfish." 

They looked around the beach and saw many jellyfish swimming in the clear ocean. Then the first friend ran off towards the jellyfish.

The second friend yelled, "Wait! You can't belong to a jellyfish!" But it was too late, the first friend had already jumped into the ocean and was swimming closer to the jellyfish.

The second friend was worried and ran after the first friend, but he was too slow. The jellyfish began to move away, and the first friend was stuck in the ocean. 

The second friend yelled, "Don't worry! I'm coming to help you!" Together, they swam back to the shore, and the first friend realized that he can't really belong to a jellyfish.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow goat. The goat was very happy and loved to play in the sunshine all day.

One day, the goat felt sad and lonely because she had no friends. So she went looking for someone to play with. But she couldn't find anybody.

Just then, the wind started to blow. It blew and blew until it sent the goat flying. The little yellow goat flew over hills and rivers until she finally saw a group of goats down below.

The yellow goat waved her arms and shouted hello. The other goats waved back. The little goat was so excited that she flew down and joined them.

From that day on, the yellow goat and the other goats were best friends. Whenever the wind blew, they would hug each other and send each other off with a big smile.

Freddy the teddy was feeling very lonely. He wanted a friend to play with. One day he went for a walk and he rolled past a big house.

When he got to the doorstep, he heard a voice.

"Hello? Who's there?" The voice said from behind the door.

Freddy was so surprised. He looked around and saw a big brown curtain was pulled aside. He saw a friendly face waving at him. It was a small girl.

"Hey! I'm Suzy! Who are you?" Suzy asked with a big smile.

"I'm Freddy the teddy" Freddy replied with a smile too.

Suzy brought Freddy inside and they started to play together. They rolled around the house laughing and having fun with each other. 

Freddy was so happy to have a new friend to play with. And every day they opened the big brown curtain and made new adventures together.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. They were Tom and Kate. Tom and Kate liked to play together all the time.

One day, Tom and Kate went for a walk in the park. As they were walking, they came across a club. The club seemed like the most exciting place ever! The only problem was, it was a hairy club. 

Tom and Kate were a little scared. But they decided to be brave and stick together. Very cautiously, they opened the hairy club door! 

Inside, they saw the most amazing things! They saw toys and lots of other friends. 

Tom and Kate were so happy, they could hardly believe it! From that day, they visited the club every single day. They even made it their special place!

James was feeling very naughty. He loved playing tricks on his parents. He slipped out of the house quietly, rushing to get his passport. His parents had told him many times not to take it out of the house, but James thought they were not watching him.

He was so excited to be taking a trip. He ran all the way to the airport, but when he tried to enter the doors, an alarm started ringing. He realized he had forgotten to grab his passport!

James was sad, but he had to be sneaky. He pretended to be a pilot and rushed back home. He snuck into his parents' bedroom and grabbed the passport from the drawer.

Finally, James made it to the airport on time. His parents were very happy to see him, but scolded him for being so naughty. They told him never to do that again. James promised to be good and listened to his parents carefully.

Max and Jenny were playing a game of chess. It was cold outside and their cheeks were pink due to the cold breeze.

"I'll move this piece," said Max, as he moved the pawn across the black and white checkered board.

"Wait," said Jenny, shaking her head, "I don't think that's right!"

Max ignored her and kept playing. He worked his way up to the Kings and Queens as Jenny watched in frustration.

Just when Max was ready to make his next move and win the game, the clock struck twelve.

Jenny smiled, "It's midnight!"

Max suddenly stopped and refused to move anymore. "No, I don't want to go to bed," he said.

Jenny started to laugh. "Max, even kings and queens need to sleep! Come on, it's time to stop now."

But Max was determined not to lose. With a loud grunt, he pushed all of the chess pieces off the board in one swipe.

Jenny frowned, disappointed that her game of chess had ended so poorly. "We'll have to play another game tomorrow," she said, trying to make the best of it.

Max huffed, "No! I'm never playing chess again." And with that, he stormed off to bed in a fit of anger.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake pies with her mother. One day, Lily wanted to make a unique pie. She decided to put lots of different fruits in it. Her mother encouraged her to try new things.

Lily worked hard on the pie, mixing all the fruits together. She put it in the oven and waited for it to bake. When it was done, it smelled delicious. Lily couldn't wait to taste it.

But when she took a bite, she realized something was wrong. The pie was too sour and too sweet at the same time. Lily was disappointed. She had worked so hard on the pie, but it didn't taste good. She felt sad and cried.

Her mother hugged her and told her it was okay to make mistakes. They decided to try making another pie together. This time, they made a simple apple pie, and it turned out delicious. Lily was happy again, and she learned that sometimes it's better to keep things simple.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, Tom brings a new toy to Mia's house. It is a magnet. A magnet can stick to some things, like metal.

Tom and Mia have fun with the magnet. They stick it to Mia's fridge, her spoon, her car, and her bell. They make loud noises and laugh. Mia's mom smiles and says, "Welcome, Tom. I'm glad you came to play."

But after a while, Tom and Mia get tired. They yawn and rub their eyes. They want to take a nap. Mia's mom says, "You can sleep in Mia's room. She has a cozy bed and a soft pillow."

Tom and Mia go to Mia's room. They bring the magnet with them. They put it on Mia's nightstand, next to her lamp. They cuddle under the blanket and close their eyes. They dream of more things to stick with the magnet. They are happy.

Once there was a young girl who loved to play. Every day she would go out and use her imagination to create adventures. One day, she found a heart in her garden and she was filled with joy. She embraced the heart in her hands as she ran outside to show it to her friends.

The little girl and her friends played with the heart all day long. In the morning they ran around it, in the afternoon they skipped over it, and in the evening they sang songs around it. It felt like a magical time and the girl's young heart filled up with happiness.

As the sun began to set, the little girl gently placed the heart back into the garden. She took one last look at it and smiled, knowing that it would keep her happy for many years to come.

Lily liked to eat. She liked to eat apples, bananas, cheese, and bread. She liked to eat with her mom and dad at the table. Sometimes, she liked to eat with her doll, too. She gave her doll a small plate and a spoon.

One day, Lily wanted to eat a cookie. She saw a cookie jar on the kitchen counter. She climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. But the jar was too heavy. It fell on the floor and broke. Cookies and glass were everywhere. Lily was scared and sad.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw Lily and the mess. She was not happy. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You could have hurt yourself. You should not touch the cookie jar. It is not for you."

Lily started to cry. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted a cookie. I was hungry. I didn't mean to break the jar."

Mom hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you are not hurt. But you have to ask me before you eat a cookie. Cookies are not good for you all the time. They are only for sometimes. And you have to be careful with the jar. It is not a toy. It is glass. Glass can cut you."

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, Mom. I'm sorry. Can I help you clean up?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can. But first, let me change your blouse. It is dirty with cookie crumbs and glass. We don't want you to get hurt."

Mom took Lily to her room and gave her a new blouse. It was pink and soft. Lily liked it. She said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you, too, Lily. Now, let's go back to the kitchen and clean up. Then, we can have some fruit for a snack. How does that sound?"

Lily said, "That sounds good, Mom. I like fruit. Fruit is yummy and healthy."

Mom and Lily went back to the kitchen and cleaned up the mess. They threw away the cookies and the glass. They swept the floor and wiped the counter. Then, they washed their hands and sat at the table. Mom gave Lily a bowl of fruit. It had apples, bananas, grapes, and strawberries. Lily ate the fruit and smiled. She said, "This is a good snack, Mom. Thank you."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm proud of you for helping me clean up. You are a good girl."

Lily and Mom ate their fruit and talked. They were happy and peaceful. They forgot about the cookie jar. They only remembered their love.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the garden. Lily had a rubber ball that bounced very high. Ben had a wooden truck that rolled very fast. They liked their toys very much and did not want to share them.

"Can I play with your ball, Lily?" Ben asked.

"No, it is my ball. I value it a lot. You have your truck," Lily said.

"But I want to try your ball. It looks fun. My truck is boring," Ben said.

He tried to grab the ball from Lily, but she held it tight. They started to pull and tug on the ball, making angry noises.

"Stop it, Ben! You are hurting me and my ball!" Lily shouted.

"Let go, Lily! You are being mean and selfish!" Ben shouted back.

Their mother heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting over the ball and frowned.

"What are you doing, children? Why are you not playing nicely?" she asked.

They both stopped and looked at her. They felt ashamed and sorry.

"Lily won't let me play with her ball. She says she values it a lot," Ben said.

"Ben tried to take my ball. He says his truck is boring," Lily said.

Their mother sighed and sat down with them. She took the ball and the truck and held them in her hands.

"Children, I know you love your toys, but they are just things. They are not alive. They are harmless. They cannot feel or think or talk. They are not your friends. They are only for playing," she said.

She gave them back their toys and smiled.

"But you know who are your friends? Each other. You are brother and sister. You are alive. You can feel and think and talk. You can help and hug and laugh. You can value each other more than any toy. Do you understand?" she asked.

They nodded and looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting and hurting each other.

"I'm sorry, Lily. Can I play with your ball for a little while? I will be careful," Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Yes, you can play with my ball. And I will play with your truck. It looks fun," Lily said.

They hugged and smiled. They gave their toys to each other and started to play together. Their mother watched them and felt happy. She valued them more than anything.

Once upon a time, there was a big factory that made yummy candy. The candy was so good that everyone wanted to eat it. One day, the factory stopped making candy and the people were sad. They wanted their candy back!

So, a little girl named Lily decided to help. She went to the factory and rang the doorbell. But no one answered. She rang it again, but still no one came. Lily was determined to help, so she climbed over the fence and went inside.

Inside the factory, Lily saw that the machines had stopped working. She knew she had to fix them. She pressed some buttons and pulled some levers, and soon the machines started working again. The candy started coming out, and everyone was happy again. Lily was a hero!

One sunny day, Betty went outside to play. She saw a cube and she was so excited. She invited her friend Daisy over to play with her. 

Betty and Daisy played for a long time. They built towers with the cube and rolled it around the backyard. Soon, they got a little too excited and accidentally knocked over their tower. 

Betty and Daisy felt a bit guilty. They knew they shouldn't play too hard with the cube. Betty gave Daisy a hug and told her it was OK. Then they cleaned up the cube and put it back in the same place.

At the end of the day, they invited each other over to play again the next day. They both smiled and waved goodbye, feeling happy and much less guilty.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She was very hungry. Her tummy felt funny and all she wanted was something yummy. So she went outside to look for something to eat.

As she walked, the sky grew dark and a storm began. Big rain drops started to fall and thunder clapped in the sky. Amy was scared and started to cry.

But then, she heard a voice from behind, saying "Amy, don't worry". When she looked back, she saw her Mommy. Her Mommy opened her umbrella and said, "Come here, I will squeeze you tight".

Amy felt much better when her Mommy held her. She knew she felt safe and loved in her Mommy's arms.

From that day on, Amy learned that when times were tough and the storm was scary, all she had to do was squeeze her Mommy and she would feel safe. This taught her that love was one of the most important things in life.

Tom and Mia are going to the zoo with their mom. They are very happy and excited. They want to see the lions, the monkeys, and the penguins. Mom has three tickets in her bag. She tells Tom and Mia to hold her hands and be calm.

But when they get to the gate, mom cannot find the tickets. She looks in her bag, in her pockets, in her coat. She says, "Oh no, where are the tickets? We need them to go in."

Tom and Mia are sad and scared. They do not want to miss the zoo. They start to cry. Mom tries to calm them down. She says, "Don't worry, we will find the tickets. Maybe I dropped them somewhere. Let's go back and look."

They walk back to the car. Mom checks the seats, the floor, the trunk. She still cannot find the tickets. She says, "This is strange. I am sure I had them. Maybe someone took them."

Then Tom sees something shiny on the ground. He runs to pick it up. It is a ticket. He says, "Look, mom, I found a ticket! It is shiny and new. Someone polished it."

Mom is surprised and happy. She says, "Good job, Tom! You found a ticket! But where are the other two?"

Then Mia sees something shiny under the car. She crawls to get it. It is another ticket. She says, "Look, mom, I found another ticket! It is shiny and new too. Someone polished it."

Mom is amazed and happy. She says, "Good job, Mia! You found another ticket! But where is the last one?"

Then they hear a voice behind them. It is a man in a uniform. He says, "Hello, are you looking for these?" He holds up the last ticket. He says, "I found them on the ground. They were so shiny and new, I thought someone polished them. They must have fallen out of your bag. Here, take them. Have a nice day at the zoo."

Mom is relieved and grateful. She says, "Thank you, sir. You are very kind and helpful. You saved our day. Come on, Tom and Mia, let's go to the zoo."

Tom and Mia are happy and excited again. They hug the man and thank him. They hold mom's hands and be calm. They go to the zoo and see the lions, the monkeys, and the penguins. They have a lot of fun. They say, "This is the best day ever."

Once upon a time there was a big family. One day they were all together. The little girl in the family was very upset. She was crying and couldn't stop. 

Her uncle noticed and asked her, "What's wrong my little one?"

The little girl said, "I'm sad, uncle. I don't have a toy to play with." 

Her uncle smiled and said, "Don't cry sweetheart. I will offer you something special to make you happy." 

He reached into his pocket and pulled out a small toy car. The little girl's eyes lit up. She quickly hugged her uncle and said, "Thank you uncle! I love it!" 

The uncle was glad that he was able to make his niece happy and give her a special gift. From that day onwards, the little girl no longer felt upset.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sew with her mommy. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a spool of thread. "Here you go, Lily. This is for you," said her mommy. "Can I sew now?" asked Lily. "Yes, you can," replied her mommy.

Lily tried to sew but the thread was too fast for her. "Mommy, I can't get the thread to stay in the needle," said Lily. "Don't worry, Lily. You just need to go slow and steady," said her mommy. "Okay, I'll try again," said Lily.

Lily took her time and finally got the thread through the needle. "Yay, I did it!" exclaimed Lily. "Good job, Lily. You're getting better and better," said her mommy. From that day on, Lily sewed with her mommy every day and got better at it.

Anna and Ben like to play with blocks. They make different buildings with the blocks. Sometimes they make houses, sometimes they make castles, sometimes they make towers.

One day, they decide to have a contest. Who can make the most unusual building with the blocks? They start to build with the blocks. Anna makes a building that looks like a snake. Ben makes a building that looks like a star.

They look at each other's buildings. They are both very unusual. They don't know who wins.

They ask their mom to judge. Mom comes and looks at the buildings. She smiles and says, "Wow, you both did a great job! Your buildings are very unusual and creative. I think you both win!"

Anna and Ben are happy. They hug their mom and each other. They say, "Thank you, mom! We both win!" They share their blocks and play together. They have fun with their unusual buildings.

Once upon a time, there was a pink mouse. The mouse lived in a small house made of cheese. One day, a big cat came to the mouse's house. The mouse was scared and didn't know what to do. The cat wanted to catch the mouse and eat it.

The mouse thought for a moment and then decided to surrender. Surrender means to give up. The mouse gave up and let the cat catch it. But when the cat picked up the mouse, it saw that the mouse was pink. The cat was surprised and thought it looked too cute to eat. So, the cat let the mouse go and they became friends. From that day on, the pink mouse and the big cat played together every day.

Once upon a time there was an intelligent little mouse. He was so fast and clever he could escape from anything. But one day, instead of trying to escape, the mouse just stayed where he was.

Suddenly, an enormous cat appeared in front of him. The cat had terrible sharp claws and a huge mouth! The poor mouse was very scared, but he didn't escape.

Instead, the mouse was brave. He looked the cat in the eye and squeaked, "I won't run away! I'm too smart to do something like that!"

The cat was so surprised by the mouse's bravery that it ran away. From then on, the mouse promised himself that he would never be too brave and never try to escape trouble.

The moral of the story is no matter how clever we are, it's best to always be smart and stay away from trouble.

One day, a boy named Tim found a mysterious drum in his room. He did not know where it came from. The drum was big and had pretty colors on it. Tim thought it was very cool.

Tim asked his mom, "Can I keep the drum?" His mom said, "Yes, but we need to store it in the garage when you are not playing with it." Tim was very happy and played with the drum all day. He made loud and fun sounds with it.

At night, Tim stored the drum in the garage like his mom said. The next day, he found another mysterious drum in his room. He played with both drums and had lots of fun. Tim loved his mysterious drums and took good care of them.

Once upon a time, there was a nut. It was small and round and it rolled around in its tree. But one day, it fell out of the tree and onto the ground. The nut was scared. It did not know what was happening.

Suddenly, it noticed another nut. It had the same size, shape, and color. The first nut was happy and it joined with the other nut. They started to bounce around and have fun.

But then, they noticed something scary. It was a big, scary bug. The two nuts were so scared that they rolled away as quickly as they could. The big bug followed them, but it was too slow and it couldn't catch them.

Finally, the two nuts made it back to their tree. They were so glad and hugged each other. Then, the two nuts went back to their tree and rolled around happily together.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Ali. One day, Ali took a walk in the park near her house. She saw a big tree at the park which was very tall and strong. She also saw a lot of soft green grass. Ali took a walk to the tree. She touched the tree and it felt very soft. She ran her hands along the trunk of the tree. Ali was so happy that she hugged the tree and started to play around it. She enjoyed playing around the soft tree. Then, Ali took a few steps back and looked up the tree. The tree was so tall and it seemed to stretch up into the sky. Ali was amazed by the tall tree and she took a few steps back to admire it. After that, she happily went back home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a huge bear. He was walking around in the woods looking for a friend. He wanted someone to play with.

He came across a little rabbit hopping around. The bear asked the rabbit, â€œDo you want to play with me?â€

The rabbit answered, â€œYes! Letâ€™s play tag!â€

The bear and the rabbit started running and jumping around the woods. The bear was so big and the rabbit was so small that the bear had trouble running around.

Then the rabbit said to the bear, â€œCan you fold your foot? You will be able to run faster!â€ The bear tried and he could move faster and better. 

The bear and the rabbit laughed and continued playing and running around until they were both too tired. They said goodbye and went on their way.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah who loved to sleep. Every night she would snuggle up in her bed, close her eyes and dream wonderful dreams. 

One night was very different, however. Sarah was very sleepy but she couldn't seem to go to bed. She just kept looking out of her bedroom window at the dark night sky. 

Suddenly her mom appeared in the doorway with a calendar in her hand. She said to Sarah, "It's time for bed, sweetheart. Look, you can see the crescent moon on the calendar!" 

Sarah gasped as she spotted the crescent moon in the bottom corner of the calendar. She said to her mom, "I'm so sleepy now. I'll go to sleep now mom." 

Her mom smiled, kissed her on the forehead and said, "Goodnight sweetheart." 

Sarah closed her eyes and went to sleep. She slept soundly throughout the night and dreamt wonderful, wonderful dreams.

One day, a girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a big, scary house. It had a tall door and small windows. Mia was brave, so she went inside the house.

In the house, Mia saw a birdcage. Inside the birdcage, there was a little bird. The bird was sad. It wanted to fly and be free. Mia wanted to help the bird.

Mia opened the birdcage door. The bird flew out and was happy. It was not scary anymore. Mia and the bird were friends. They played and had fun all day.

The sun was shining brightly in the sky. 
In the backyard, a little girl eagerly stepped up to a white line painted on the ground. She smiled as she saw an adorable family of kittens playing nearby. Her eyes sparkled with excitement!

The little girl eagerly stepped closer to the line. The kittens noticed her and ran over to her. 
The little girl was overjoyed and gently bent down to pet the kittens. They were so adorable!

As she stepped back to the line, one of the kittens stepped forward with her. The girl smiled at the little kitten and stepped forward onto the line. They played together for a while and the little girl soon stepped back off the line.

The little girl giggled and waved goodbye to the kittens as she skipped back inside. She'd had such a fun time playing with her new adorable friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Betsy. Betsy loved to hop along the path in the forest. One day, she saw a carrot on the path. Betsy hopped over to the carrot and started to chew. It was so yummy!

Suddenly, Betsy heard a loud growl. It was a big bear! Betsy knew she had to run away, but the path was too easy for the bear to follow. She had to think fast. Then, Betsy remembered the carrot. She quickly hopped back to the carrot and picked it up with her mouth.

As the bear got closer, Betsy threw the carrot as far as she could. The bear ran after it and Betsy hopped away as fast as she could. She was safe! From that day on, Betsy always made sure to watch out for bears on the path.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Red. Red liked to travel to different places. One day, Red's gas was running low and he needed to find a gas station. Red looked and looked, but he couldn't find one. Finally, he saw a sign that said "Gas Here" and he was so happy. 

But when Red got to the gas station, he saw that the road was tough and bumpy. Red was scared, but he knew he had to be brave and drive on the tough road. He made it to the gas pump and filled up his tank. Then, he continued on his journey to new places. 

Red learned that sometimes traveling can be tough, but if you keep going and stay brave, you can make it to where you want to go. And it's important to always make sure you have enough gas for your travels!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sail on her toy boat in the bathtub. One day, she decided to take her boat to the big lake near her house. She put on her favorite dress that her mom said fit her perfectly and went to the lake. 

When she got there, she saw a big stage on the shore. There were people singing and dancing on it. Lily wanted to join them, but she was too shy. She decided to sail her boat around the stage and watch the show from afar. She had so much fun sailing and watching the show that she didn't want to go home. 

As the sun began to set, Lily's mom came to the lake to find her. She saw Lily sailing her boat and watching the show. Lily's mom was so proud of her for being brave and having fun. They went home together, and Lily fell asleep dreaming about sailing and watching the stage show again. The end.

Once upon a time there was an ant who wanted to make everyone laugh. He was very smart and always made jokes. He made the other animals laugh until their bellies hurt.

One day the ant made a silly joke about a squirrel, who didn't think it was funny at all. The squirrel felt very guilty and sad. The ant felt guilty too and apologised to the squirrel.

They both decided to make peace. The ant said he would never make jokes about animals again, and the squirrel said it was ok.

They hugged and laughed, and from then on the ant only made jokes about things that couldn't get hurt. So everyone could have fun and nobody would feel guilty again.

Sam liked to draw. He had many colors and papers. He drew cars, trees, animals and people. He showed his drawings to his mom and dad. They smiled and said they were good.

One day, Sam wanted to draw something new. He saw his dad's pants on the chair. They were blue and had pockets and buttons. Sam thought they looked nice. He took a paper and a black color. He tried to draw the pants.

But it was hard. The pants had many lines and shapes. Sam's drawing looked messy. He was not happy. He showed his drawing to his dad.

"Dad, look. I drew your pants. But they are not good. They are bad."

Dad looked at the drawing. He hugged Sam and said, "No, Sam. They are not bad. They are very good. You tried to draw something new. That is hard. But you did not give up. You are a good drawer. And you can improve. Do you know what improve means?"

Sam shook his head. He did not know.

Dad said, "Improve means to get better. To learn more. To practice. If you want to draw better pants, you can improve. You can look at the pants more. You can draw them again and again. You can ask me or mom for help. You can improve your drawing. And I will be proud of you. Do you know what proud means?"

Sam nodded. He knew.

"Proud means to be happy and to like someone. You make me proud, Sam. You are my son. And you are a good drawer. And you can improve. Do you want to try again?"

Sam smiled. He said, "Yes, dad. I want to try again. I want to improve. I want to make you proud. And I want to draw good pants."

Dad smiled too. He said, "That's great, Sam. Let's go and get more paper and colors. And let's draw together. I will help you. And we will have fun."

Sam and dad went to get more paper and colors. They drew together. They drew pants and other things. They improved their drawings. They had fun. And they were proud.

Once upon a time, there was a strong little boy. He loved to explore his house. One day, he decided to explore the kitchen. He saw a big stove and he wanted to grab it to see how strong he was. 

He gripped the stove tightly with both hands and pulled with all of his might, but he could not move it. He kept pulling and pulling, but it was just too heavy. He started to feel frustrated, but then he thought of a new idea.

The little boy grabbed a chair, put it beside the stove, and climbed up to get a better grip. He tried one last time to grab the stove and this time, he was able to push it across the kitchen floor! He was so happy that he managed to do it, and it made him feel strong and proud. 

The boy smiled and knew that he had explored the kitchen in style!

Today Ann and Toby walked to the park. Ann was very happy. When they arrived, Toby saw a pink bird. He pointed excitedly and said "Look Ann"! 

Ann was also excited to see the pink bird. Ann and Toby watched the little bird fly around. Suddenly, Ann and Toby saw two more pink birds, but these birds were fighting. They were squawking and trying to peck each other. 

Ann was scared and wanted to go home, but Toby was fascinated by the birds. He wanted to stay and watch. Ann said no, they had to leave. So, Ann and Toby turned and started to walk away from the park. 

Ann and Toby talked about the pink birds all the way home. They were both very excited about the fight they saw. Ann and Toby liked the pretty pink birds and still talk about them today.

Tom and Mia went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and giraffes. They liked the animals, but they wanted to see the rhinoceros. The rhinoceros was big and gray, with a horn on its nose.

They walked to the rhinoceros pen, where they saw a sign that said "Do not spray the rhinoceros". Tom and Mia did not know what spray meant. They saw a hose near the fence, and they had an idea. They picked up the hose and turned on the water. They thought it would be fun to spray the rhinoceros.

The rhinoceros did not like the water. It got angry and ran towards the fence. It made a loud noise and shook its horn. Tom and Mia got scared and dropped the hose. The water kept spraying, and it hit the rhinoceros in the face. The rhinoceros sneezed and backed away.

Mom and Dad saw what Tom and Mia did. They were not happy. They ran to the hose and turned off the water. They told Tom and Mia that they were naughty and that they should not spray the rhinoceros. They said that the rhinoceros was weak and sick, and that the water could hurt it. They said that they had to say sorry to the rhinoceros and the zookeeper.

Tom and Mia felt bad. They did not mean to make the rhinoceros angry or sad. They said sorry to the rhinoceros and the zookeeper. The zookeeper was nice and said that it was okay, but that they should be careful and follow the signs. He said that the rhinoceros was getting better, and that he hoped they would come back and see him again. Tom and Mia nodded and smiled. They learned a new word, and they learned to be kind to the animals.

Grandma was having a party. All the kids were so excited! There were balloons and candy and even a clown. Everyone was having so much fun. 

After a while, Grandma brought out some toys. All the kids ran over to see their favorite toys. They all wanted to play with them. 

Suddenly, one of the kids found a toy hammer. He grabbed it and started to destroy all of the other toys. He had so much fun smashing them! 

The kids started to cry, but Grandma was not mad. She just said that it was an important lesson. We should always be careful with our toys and not destroy them. 

The kids all agreed and the party went on. Soon, everyone was excited and playing again. Grandma was glad that the party was happy once more.

Once there was a gifted girl named Sam. She had a special saw in her hands. One day, she went out to the garden with the saw and started playing. Sam saw a tree and decided to make a joke with it. She started sawing the tree, but suddenly the tree said, "Stop it! I don't want to be cut into pieces." Sam laughed and corrected the tree. It wasn't a real saw, it was only a toy saw! Sam was very gifted and she knew it was only a joke. The tree was so happy to hear that it was only a joke. Sam and the tree went on playing together in the garden, laughing and joking around.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved winter and playing in the snow. One day, she went outside to build a snowman. Her mommy said, "Be careful, Lily. Don't get too cold."

Lily replied, "I'm not cold, Mommy. I'm proud of my snowman." She set the carrot nose and the coal eyes on the snowman's face. Suddenly, the wind picked up and it started to snow harder. 

Lily's mommy called her inside, but Lily didn't want to leave her snowman. "Just a little longer, Mommy," she pleaded. But the snow got too heavy and the snowman fell apart. Lily was very sad. She cried and cried until her mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. We can build another snowman tomorrow."

Once upon a time, there was a sack. Inside the sack was some oat, and it was very expensive. Every day, the little sack waited by the phone, hoping someone would call and buy the oat. But no one did. 

One day, a big truck came down the street. The little sack noticed a man walking up the road, carrying oat. He walked up to the sack and said, "Do you want to buy my oat?" 

The little sack was so excited! It wanted the oat, but it didn't have enough money. The man smiled and said, "I'll give you the oat for free if you can carry it all the way home." 

The little sack was delighted! It quickly filled the sack and set off down the road with its new, expensive oat. It was the happiest sack in town!

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She had a special mission; to collect doves. Everyday she would put on her brightly coloured dress and her sparkly shoes and go out collecting. Every morning she would walk to the park and then look to the sky. Then she would spot a dove and try to catch it in her hands.

Today was a sunny day, and the little girl was feeling very sleepy. She found a big tree to sit under as she watched the doves up in the sky. Suddenly she noticed a dove land on a branch close to her. Gently, she reached out to try and catch it. "Coo-Coo!" the dove said.

The little girl was suprised. She had never heard a dove talk before!

"Hi, little dove" the little girl said. "My name's Daisy. And I'm here to collect doves".

"Well, you caught me!" the dove said. "Let's be friends!"

Daisy was so happy. She had found a special friend and could share her dove collecting mission with him.

Together Daisy and her dove friend went on many adventures and caught lots of doves. Every night before bedtime, Daisy would give her doves a big hug before they flew up to the sky.

That was Daisy's life collecting her special doves, and it was just perfect.

Once there was a girl named Mary. Mary was so excited because she was going to the theatre to watch an opera. She put on her favourite dress and was so happy to go. 

When Mary got to the theatre, the lights were shining so brightly. On stage, the performers were singing and playing music. Mary couldn't believe how beautiful their music was and how sweet their singing sounded.

The performers were so talented. They danced and sang on stage. Mary was amazed as she watched them perform the opera. 

At the end of the show, Mary was clapping and shouting, she was so proud of the performers. She was so happy she got to see the opera and she had a sweet smile on her face as she went home.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lilly. Lilly was very excited and enthusiastic about learning spells. She wanted to be a powerful magician like her mother.

One day, Lilly asked her mother if she could learn a special spell. Her mother smiled and said, "Yes, I promise I will teach you a special spell."

Lilly was so happy that she jumped up and down. "When can I start?" she asked.

Her mother said, "Tomorrow, I will teach you the spell. Then you can practice until you have it down." 

Lilly was so excited that she couldn't stop smiling. She said to her mother, "I promise I will practice as hard as I can." 

The next day, Lilly started to learn the spell. She quickly got the hang of it and soon was performing the spell with enthusiasm. 

Lilly was so proud of herself for learning the spell so quickly. She hugged her mother and said, "Thank you for teaching me. I promise I will practice every day so I can be the best magician ever."

And that is the story about how Lilly learned a special spell with enthusiasm and kept her promise to practice every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who lived by the beach. His name was Justin and he liked to go to the beach near his house every day. One day, while Justin was playing in the sand, he spotted a shark in the water. He was scared at first, but then he remembered his dad's words: "Always be brave, Justin." 

He decided to get closer to the shark and showed it his box of sandwiches. To his surprise, the shark was hungry! He shared his sandwiches with the shark and thanked it for not eating him! 

Justin was so excited that he ran back home to tell his family about his unusual friend. From then on, every day Justin would bring food for the shark before going to the beach to play. 

Justin was so happy to have a new friend in the big blue sea. He thanked the shark for being his friend and for teaching him to be brave.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books with her mommy. One day, she was playing outside and fell down and hurt her leg. She cried and her mommy came to help her. "What happened, sweetie?" her mommy asked. "I fell and hurt my leg," Lily said. "Let's go inside and read a book to make you feel better," her mommy said. They went inside and read a little book about a happy puppy. Lily felt much better and her leg didn't hurt anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. Sally went to the woods with her mommy, who was looking for a mysterious statue. Sally loved exploring, so she ran ahead and looked everywhere.

She soon saw the statue in a clearing. It was so tall and shiny, like a giant gold teddy bear. She wanted to touch it.

Sally tugged and tugged, but she couldn't move the statue. â€œHere, Sally! Let me show you!â€ her mom said.

Silly and her mommy pulled really hard, and the statue started to wobble. Finally, it jumped up and Sally giggled with delight. â€œWow! It's so mysterious" she said. 

On the way home, Sally stretched her arms around the statue and dragged it in the sunshine. She already had most of the answers to her questions, but she knew she would find out more during her next adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big bookshelf in her room that was filled with lots of books. One day, Lily's mom took her to the zoo to see all the wild animals. Lily saw lions, tigers, and bears. She was so excited that she couldn't stop saying "wow"! When they got back home, Lily went to her room to pick out a book to read. She looked at her bookshelf and picked out a book about animals. As she read the book, she imagined herself in the wild with all the animals she saw at the zoo.

Once upon a time there was a big, bright moon. It weighed a lot! It was so heavy that it looked like it was going to fall out of the sky. 

One day, a little girl was out in her backyard when she saw the moon. She was very nervous. She had never seen anything so big before. 

The little girl wanted to know how much the moon weighed. She thought it must be more than anything else she had ever carried. 

So she got some scales and carefully placed the moon on top. Everyone watched as the needle on the scales moved until it settled on the biggest number the little girl had ever seen! 

The moon had weighed a lot more then anyone had expected! The little girl realized how special the moon was and she smiled. She wished she could always see the moon from her backyard.

One day a little girl was very worried. She could see her dad working with a long cable. She watched as he plugged it into the wall and secured it, but it was all a bit confusing. She didn't understand why they needed it.

The little girl was beginning to feel upset, so she went to find her mom. But mom was busy talking on the phone and didn't seem to hear the little girl's question.

Suddenly, a loud voice called out from the other room. It was the little girl's dad! He was asking Mom to help him with the cable. The little girl ran to the room to see what was happening.

Mom and Dad were discussing how best to plug the cable in. Mom was helping Dad to make sure it was secure, but the little girl could tell that Mom was worried too.

They eventually finished and it became clear that the cable was for the internet! The little girl was relieved, and so were Mom and Dad. They all gave each other a big hug and the little girl smiled. No more worrying!

Once upon a time, two friends wanted to unite. One day, they decided to play hockey. They never played before, so everything was unknown. They tried their very best and laughed together.

By the end of the day, they were very good at hockey! They could even practice together. The friends were so happy they united by playing hockey, and they decided to play every day. Every day, they discovered something new and had a wonderfully fun time.

The friends could always rely on hockey to unite them and make them happy. Whenever they felt sad, they knew they just had to pull out their hockey sticks and have a game to make everything better. The friends had fun and were united by hockey.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was a restless bunny who loved to play all day long. One day, Benny was playing in the garden when he saw a big, bouncy ball.

Benny hopped over to the ball and said, "Hi there! Can I play with you?"

The ball replied, "Of course! Let's bounce together."

Benny and the ball bounced and bounced, having so much fun. Suddenly, Benny saw a beautiful spring flower and said, "Wow, that flower is so pretty. I want to rest by it."

The ball said, "Sure, let's go rest by the spring flower."

Benny and the ball rested by the spring flower, feeling happy and content. From that day on, Benny and the ball were the best of friends, bouncing and playing together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore nature. One day, she found a small cell on the ground. It was a cheap phone, but she was happy to have found it.

Lily showed the phone to her mom and asked if she could keep it. Her mom said yes, but warned her not to disturb anyone by calling them. Lily promised not to.

Later that day, Lily's friend came over to play. They were having so much fun until Lily's phone rang. It was a wrong number and it disturbed their playtime. Lily apologized to her friend and turned off the phone. From that day on, Lily made sure to only use her phone when it was necessary and not to disturb anyone.

Once upon a time, there was a big oak tree. It was very tall and had many branches. The oak tree was very independent and didn't need anyone else to stand up straight. 

One day, a group of animals came by the oak tree. They were looking for a place to rest and play. The oak tree was happy to share its branches with them. 

But soon, the animals started to fight and argue. They wanted to split up and go their separate ways. The oak tree tried to stop them, but they didn't listen. 

Later that day, a big storm came. The wind was so strong that it split the oak tree in half. The animals were scared and sad. They realized that they should have stayed together and listened to the oak tree. From then on, they promised to always stick together and be friends.

Tom and Mia liked to play in the park. They saw a big tree with many branches. The tree was very old and had many holes. Tom and Mia wanted to make a house in the tree.

They found some wood and some rope. They tied the wood to the branches with the rope. They made a floor and a wall and a door. They were very happy with their house.

"Look, Mia, we have a house in the tree!" Tom said. "We can pretend we are birds or squirrels or pirates!"

"Yes, Tom, this is fun!" Mia said. "But we need a roof. What if it rains?"

They looked around for more wood and rope. They saw a man with a big hat and a long beard. He was sitting on a bench. He had a book and a stick. The book and the stick looked very old.

"Hello, children," the man said. "What are you doing?"

"We are making a house in the tree," Tom said. "But we need a roof. Do you have any wood or rope?"

The man smiled. He opened his book and showed them a picture. The picture was of a tree with a house. The house had a roof made of leaves.

"This is an ancient house," the man said. "People used to live in trees like this a long time ago. They used leaves to make roofs. You can do the same. There are many leaves on the ground. You can tie them together with your rope."

Tom and Mia thanked the man. They liked his book and his stick. They picked up some leaves and tied them together. They made a roof for their house. They invited the man to come and see their house. The man was very proud of them. He gave them his book and his stick as a gift.

"Thank you, sir," Tom and Mia said. "You are very kind. We like your ancient book and your ancient stick. They are very special."

The man hugged them. He said goodbye and left. Tom and Mia played in their house for a long time. They read the book and pretended to be ancient people. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little bear named Bubba. Bubba liked to play with his friends in the forest. One day, Bubba and his friends were playing hide and seek when they heard a loud shout. They all got scared and ran to hide behind a big tree.
