It was Bubba's friend, Bobby the rabbit. Bobby was shouting because he found a book about history. Bubba and his friends were curious, so they went to see the book. Bobby showed them the pictures and told them stories about the past. 

Bubba and his friends were amazed by what they learned. They all thanked Bobby for sharing the book with them. From that day on, Bubba and his friends would often shout to each other, "Let's go learn more about history!" and they would spend their days reading and exploring the world around them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lisa. She loved to play with her toys and eat her favorite fruit, the peach. One day, she found a big, fake peach in her toy box. She thought it was funny and showed it to her mom.

"Look, Mom! I found a fake peach in my toys!" Lisa said, laughing. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a fun toy! Let's put it in a special place so you won't lose it."

Lisa and her mom decided to put the fake peach in a small box. They put the box on a shelf in Lisa's room. Before they left the room, Lisa's mom showed her how to lock the box to keep it safe. Lisa was very happy to have a special place for her fake peach.

Every day, Lisa would unlock the box, take out the fake peach, and play with it. She would pretend it was real and share it with her toys during tea parties. At the end of the day, she would lock the box again to keep her fake peach safe. Lisa loved her fake peach very much and was glad she could keep it in a special place.

Tom and Lily liked to play near the station. They saw big trains and cars and people. They liked the noise and the colors. Sometimes they found things on the ground, like cans and coins and papers. They liked to lift them and look at them.

One day, they saw a big box near the station. It was brown and had a red sign on it. They did not know what the sign meant. They thought it was a picture of a flower. They wanted to see what was in the box. They ran to the box and tried to lift it.

But the box was not harmless. It was a bomb. It had a timer and a wire. When Tom and Lily lifted the box, they moved the wire. The bomb made a loud beep and then a big boom. The box exploded and hurt Tom and Lily and the station and the people. There was fire and smoke and noise and pain.

Tom and Lily did not play near the station anymore. They did not play at all. They were gone. The people were sad and angry. They said Tom and Lily should not have touched the box. They said the box was dangerous and had a warning sign. They said Tom and Lily should have listened and learned.

The moral of the story is: Do not touch things that you do not know. They might be harmful and hurt you and others. Listen to the signs and the people who know better. Be careful and safe when you play.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to play mailman and mailwoman. They put on their dad's old bathrobes and made some letters out of paper. They also found a big cardboard box and wrote "mail" on it.

They took turns to deliver the letters to different rooms in the house. They knocked on the doors and said "mail for you!" and gave the letters to their mom, dad, and baby brother. They had a lot of fun and felt very important.

But then, they made a mistake. They delivered a letter to the bathroom, where their dad was taking a shower. They did not know that he was there, because the door was not locked. They opened the door and said "mail for you!" and threw the letter inside.

Their dad was very angry. He shouted "what are you doing? Get out of here!" and grabbed a towel. He was wet and soapy and did not want anyone to see him. He chased Ben and Lily out of the bathroom and slammed the door.

Ben and Lily were scared and sorry. They ran to their mom and hugged her. They said "we are sorry, we did not know dad was in the bathroom. We were just playing mailman and mailwoman."

Their mom said "it's okay, I know you did not mean to upset your dad. But you should always knock before you enter a room, especially the bathroom. And you should not throw things at people, especially wet things. That is not nice."

Ben and Lily said "we understand, mom. We will not do it again. We love you and dad."

Their mom said "we love you too, sweeties. Now, why don't you go and play something else? Maybe you can be doctors and nurses, or firefighters and police officers, or teachers and students."

Ben and Lily said "okay, mom. That sounds fun. Can we keep the bathrobes?"

Their mom said "sure, you can keep the bathrobes. But only for playing, not for delivering mail."

Once upon a time, there was a young boy called John. John had a missile which he loved very much. One day, John decided to take it outside and throw it in the sky. He kept throwing the missile up into the air, and he enjoyed watching it go higher and higher. 

One day the sky was very cold and John decided to keep throwing his missile. But this time the missile flew too high, and it got lost in the cold sky. John was sad, but then he heard something. It was a noise from the sky - and it was his missile coming back! 

John ran forward and caught the missile, and he kept on throwing it up in the sky. The missile made him happy, and he smiled as he kept throwing it in the cold sky. 

The end.

One day, a wild animal walked into the forest. He was very hungry and began to look for something to eat. He found a big pile of food and began to feed on it. The animal ate the whole meal and felt much better. He was so happy he ran into the woods, showing off the wild moves he had learned.

The next day the animal came back to the same spot to find the same big pile of food. He looked around and realized that he had been fed by a kind person. He felt so grateful and could not believe his luck.

The kind person came out of the woods every day and fed the wild animal. He taught the animal how to hunt and find his own food too. The animal was so happy and thanked the kind person for helping him.

From then on, the wild animal was fed every day and enjoyed living in the woods. He looked forward to the kind person coming to feed him. And he remembered the lesson to be always kind to others.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. He flew around and loved singing each day. One day, he found a big cage with a door wide open. He hopped inside and he was so happy! The little bird was proud.

The bird told the other animals in the forest about the big cage. Everyone wanted to see it. So all the animals crowded around and saw the cage. The little bird told them that he was living in the cage and they were all very surprised.

But soon, it was time to leave. The little bird felt so sad because he couldn't take the cage with him. His friends said goodbye and left.

Now the little bird had a home. He was so proud of it! He sang loud and happy each day in his new and special home. The cage made him so happy. He had a safe and cozy place to live in and he was so very thankful.

One day, Joe and his dad drove to the park. Joe had a lot of fun. He saw a dry bush and wanted to explore it. He looked around and saw some money shining in the sun! His dad said he could keep it.

Joe was so excited. He and his dad drove home. Joe asked his dad what he could do with the money. His dad said he should save it for something special.

So Joe put the money in a dry box and kept it safe. Every day he would count his money and watch it grow. Soon, Joe had enough money to buy a toy from the store. He was so excited!

Joe and his dad drove to the store. He bought the toy and felt happy. Joe loved his toy and never forgot the day he found money in the dry bush.

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was three years old and liked to do new things.

One day, Lucy wanted to go for a walk in the park. She put on her shoes and went outside. In the park, she saw a tree with lots of birds. She smiled and watched them fly around.

Lucy then saw a dog and she wanted to play. She smiled at the dog but the dog barked really loudly. It was a bit too noisy for Lucy so she decided to continue her walk.

She passed a pond full of ducks and wanted to feed them. She put her hand in her pocket and pulled out some bread. The ducks were very happy and came close to her. She used the bread to feed the ducks and they made noisy quacks. Lucy smiled and laughed at the ducks.

When she finished the walk, she was very tired but also very happy. She loved all of the things she saw in the park and can't wait to go back again!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in his backyard. He liked to run around and jump up and down. One day, he found a thin stick on the ground.

Timmy's mom called out to him, "Timmy, it's time to come inside for lunch!" But Timmy didn't want to go inside. He wanted to play with his stick. "Mom, can I bury my stick in the backyard?" he asked.

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Timmy. You can bury your stick in the backyard." So Timmy dug a little hole and buried his stick. He was very happy.

Later, Timmy's friend came over to play. "What did you do today?" his friend asked. "I buried my stick in the backyard!" Timmy replied excitedly. His friend thought that was really cool and they went to go dig it up together.

Ben and Mia liked to play near the lake. They saw many things in the water, like fish, ducks, and boats. One day, they saw something unusual. It was a kayak. A kayak was a long and thin boat that you could sit in and move with a stick.

"Look, Mia, a kayak!" Ben said. "Let's go and find it!"

They ran to the shore and saw the kayak on the sand. It was blue and white, with a hole in the middle. They touched it and felt that it was hard and smooth.

"Can we sit in it?" Mia asked.

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. It might tip over," Ben said.

They climbed into the kayak, one by one. They felt excited and curious. They pretended to move the stick and make waves. They laughed and had fun.

But then, they heard a voice.

"Hey, kids, what are you doing with my kayak?" It was a man. He was wearing a wet suit and a helmet. He looked angry and surprised.

Ben and Mia felt scared and sorry. They jumped out of the kayak and ran away.

"Sorry, mister, we just wanted to play!" they shouted.

They learned that they should not touch things that did not belong to them. They also learned that a kayak was an unusual boat.

Once upon a time, there was a nice van. It was big and blue. One day, the van went for a drive. It drove fast down the road. 

Suddenly, a man yelled at the van. The van stopped and the man got in. He said, "Can you take me to the store?" The van said, "Yes, I can!" 

So, the van drove the man to the store. He bought some nice things and then the van took him back home. The man said, "Thank you, van. You are so nice!" And the van felt happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very adventurous and loved exploring the world around her.

One day, she decided to go for a walk around the park. She soon came across a big river and wanted to try and cross it. She spotted a bridge, but it looked very secret and seemed like no one had been there before.

Lucy felt brave and decided to go anyway. She lay down on the bridge and carefully inched her way across. As she was almost to the other side, she suddenly heard a noise. It was a big bear, who had woken up and noticed Lucy on his bridge.

The little girl was too scared to move and the bear just stood and looked at her. Then Lucy remembered her mum's advice: if ever you feel scared, ask for help. So she asked the bear for help.

The bear asked Lucy what she needed help with and Lucy explained that she was trying to get to the other side of the river but was too scared to move. The bear came over and lay down on the bridge, inviting Lucy to climb up on to his shoulder.

The bear walked over the bridge, with Lucy balanced on his shoulder. When they reached the other side, he put Lucy down and gave her a big hug. He then waved goodbye and Lucy continued on her adventurous journey.

Billy was sitting in his classroom. All the other kids had hair on their heads, but Billy was bald. Suddenly, he heard a loud roar. He started to feel scared. He looked around, but he couldn't see who was roaring.

He slowly stood up and walked around the classroom. As he looked around, he saw a big lion! It was standing in the corner of the classroom and roaring again.

Billy wasn't sure what to do. He was very brave, so he slowly walked up to the lion. He and the lion looked at each other for a few minutes.

Then, the lion smiled. It stopped roaring and licked Billy's face. Billy laughed and hugged the lion. He pet it and then ran back to his seat.

After that, the lion stayed in the classroom for the rest of the day. It followed Billy around and even helped him with his work. Everyone in the classroom was happy and surprised that the lion was so nice.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. Anna was very enthusiastic and always excited to try new things. One day, Anna's parents took her to the ocean. She had never seen the ocean before; she was so excited! Anna ran around and explored the beach, feeling the waves brush against her feet. She even saw a few fish swimming in the crystal clear water. Anna was so happy and excited to be near the ocean, it felt like a magical place full of adventure. She couldn't wait to come back again soon!

Once upon a time there was a small boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He decided to take a boat out to sea. After a few hours, the boat sailed onto a big, beautiful island.

The island was so nice that the boy wanted to explore it. He jumped out of the boat into the water and started to swim towards the island. There was a mild breeze that kept him cool as he swam.

The boy arrived on the shore of the island. He looked around and noticed a small hut. He stood up and walked towards it. When he arrived, he heard a voice say, "Hello! Who are you?"

The boy was surprised. He looked around and saw an old man standing nearby. The old man said, "I'm the island's caretaker. My name is John. What's your name?"

The boy smiled and said his name. Then he asked if he could explore the island. John said to him, "Of course you can. Just be careful - some of the island can be a bit wild. I'll stay here and make sure you're safe."

So the boy explored the island with John. They walked around the beach and swam in the mild ocean. Then, when it was time to go back, the boy thanked John for showing him the island and waved goodbye.

The boy sailed back to the shore with lots of great memories of the island. He

Once there was a house. It was a big house with a purple roof. One day, the roof started to leak. A repairman was called to fix the roof. He came with his tools. The repairman worked hard, but it was easy to repair the roof because it was not a big problem. After he was done, the roof looked as good as new. It was still purple, but no more water was leaking. Everyone in the house was very happy.

Jane was a poor little girl. Her family did not have much money and her old home was quite small. She lived with her mom and dad in one room. 

One day, Jane saw that the window in their room was open. She was excited and ran over, wanting to see what was outside. When Jane saw the street below, she decided to slide down the window. 

Her mom shouted at her to stop, but Jane would not listen. She kept going further and further down the window. Her mom was so worried because Jane was going to get hurt. 

Suddenly, her dad's strong hands pulled Jane up from the window! He explained that she could not do this because it was so dangerous. Poor Jane had to stay inside the room but she promised to not slide down the window ever again.

One sunny morning, Kate went to the park with her mom. It was so exciting for Kate! She saw the trees and the grass and all the beautiful flowers. Her mom pointed to a bright blue jewel up in the sky. It was a big, shiny star! 

Kate was so happy she ran toward it. But as they got closer, they found out it was just a big tree. It had a bright blue jewel hanging in it that sparkled in the sun. 

Kateâ€™s mom was frightened. She didnâ€™t want Kate to get too close. She pointed to a big bear. The bear was very scary. He was standing tall and looking right at them. 

Kate was frightened too. Her mom quickly grabbed her hand and ran away together. They looked back and saw the big bear was still pointing to the jewel in the big tree. That was the end of their adventure to the park.

Molly and Joe were best friends. Every day they did fun things together. One day they decided to build a castle.

Molly brought a pile of blocks and Joe brought a box of stamps. They found a tall table and started building.

Molly said, "Let's make the walls thick!" She put two blocks on top of each other. Joe said, "You're right - it needs to be strong!" He put two more on top.

They made the sides and the top of the castle. Then Molly said, "Now let's put some stamps on the walls to make it look pretty!" Joe smiled and said, "Great idea!"

They put lots of stamps on the walls, and it was soon looking very nice. Joe said, "Now it looks like a real castle!"

Molly and Joe smiled at each other. They had built a wonderful castle.

Terry was very sad. He had been feeling terrible all week. No matter how hard he tried to not feel so sad, he just couldn't stop. He couldn't help it and he started to cry.

Big tears streamed down his face, one after the other. Nothing he did made him feel better. He kept on crying and crying, until he felt like he had no more tears left.

Finally, after a while, Terry's mom came into the room. She hugged him tight and whispered softly: "It's ok to be sad, we all have bad weeks sometimes". Terry looked up at her, sniffed and said: "Yes, it was a terrible week". 

"Come on, let's go and get some ice-cream. That always makes me feel better", said Terry's mom. Just like that, Terry's tears dried up and he smiled. 

The two of them headed off together to get some delicious ice-cream. Terry knew that everything would be ok really soon.

Jane was a foolish girl. She drove her car to the store. She needed a mop. She drove and drove until she saw the store. She pulled up next to it and went in. She looked around until she saw a mop. She smiled and bought it. She drove back home with the mop. Jane was proud of herself. She had gotten a mop, and she didn't even get lost!

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. But Ben was not careful. He ran too fast and fell down. He hurt his knee and it was bleeding.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "It hurts!"

Lily ran to him and hugged him. "Don't cry, Ben. I will help you." She said. She looked around and saw a lady with a bag. She ran to the lady and asked, "Please, can you give me a bandage for my friend? He has a boo-boo."

The lady smiled and said, "Of course, dear. Here you go." She gave Lily a bandage and some wipes. She said, "You are a good friend. You need to clean the wound first and then put the bandage on it. It will make it feel better."

Lily thanked the lady and ran back to Ben. She cleaned his knee and put the bandage on it. She said, "There, Ben. You are brave. The bandage will make it heal."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are kind. The bandage is nice. It has stars on it."

Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Ben. Do you want to play some more?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, but let's be careful. I don't want to fall again."

Lily agreed and said, "Me too. Let's go to the swings. They are fun."

They held hands and walked to the swings. They had fun and laughed. They learned to be careful and to help each other. They were happy.

One day, a little girl named Amy was playing with her red brick. She liked to build towers with her bricks. She was trying to make a very tall tower, but it kept falling down. Amy felt frustrated.

Amy's big brother Tom saw her and asked, "What's wrong, Amy?" She told him, "I want to make a tall tower, but it keeps falling." Tom wanted to help his sister, so he had an idea. "Let's save the tower with a strong base," he said.

Tom and Amy worked together to make the tower. They put many bricks at the bottom to make the strong base. Then, they carefully added more bricks to make the tower taller and taller. Finally, the tower was very tall and did not fall down. Amy was so happy, and she thanked Tom for his help. They played with the brick tower all day and had lots of fun.

Once there was an ostrich that wanted to perform. He had never done it before, but he was brave and hopeful. So he prepared for a big show and he was almost ready.

Suddenly, the stage became empty. There were no people, no music and no audience. The ostrich felt sad and confused. He was ready to perform, why was there no one there to watch him? 

The ostrich was so sad that he wanted to forget about it, so he ran away and never wanted to perform again. He was so disappointed that he never wanted to do it again, and he was left all alone in the empty stage.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear fancy clothes and play dress-up. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new dress that was very fashionable. Lily was so happy and she wore it all day.

But then, when Lily was playing outside, she accidentally broke a flower pot. She felt sad and scared that her mom would be mad. She went inside and told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said it was okay, accidents happen.

Lily realized that even though her dress was fancy and fashionable, it didn't matter as much as her mom's love and kindness. From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to be careful and honest, even if it means breaking something.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite rag doll that she carried everywhere. The doll was very fragile, so she had to be careful not to drop her.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. While they were playing, Lily saw a little boy crying. She went to him and asked, "Why are you sad?" The boy answered, "I lost my toy." 

Lily wanted to help the boy find his toy, so she asked him, "What does it look like?" The boy described his toy and Lily looked around. Suddenly, she saw something on the ground. It was the boy's toy! 

Lily picked it up and gave it to the boy. He was so happy and said, "Thank you!" Lily smiled and hugged her rag doll tightly. She was happy too because she helped someone.

Once upon a time, in a distant land, there was a big hedge. A little boy named Tim wanted to see what was on the other side of the hedge. He thought it must be something very fun and exciting. So, Tim decided to try to climb over the hedge.

Tim tried and tried, but he could not reach the top of the hedge. A friendly bird saw Tim and said, "Hi, Tim! What are you doing?" Tim replied, "I want to see what's on the other side of the hedge. Can you help me?" The bird agreed to help Tim and carried him up and over the hedge.

When they got to the other side, Tim saw that it was just a big field with nothing fun or exciting. Tim was very sad and started to cry. The bird tried to cheer him up, but Tim was too sad to smile. In the end, Tim learned that sometimes, what we think is exciting is not always as fun as we imagine.

One day, there was a little girl who went to the beach. She saw something thin, floating in the water. Curiosity filled her eyes. She reached out her hand and touched it. It was a jellyfish! She watched as it started to move, graceful and slow. She decided she wanted to play with it.

Suddenly, the jellyfish disappeared. The little girl was very confused. Where did it go? She looked around and around, but she couldn't see it anywhere. It had just vanished.

The little girl was sad. She wanted to see the jellyfish again. She waited for a long time, but nothing happened. The jellyfish had disappeared into thin air.

The little girl never forgot about the jellyfish. She made sure to be extra careful at the beach, just in case it came back to say hello.

Max was feeling very sad. He had been looking forward to going to the park all week, but now the rain was pouring down outside.

But then Max had an idea! He remembered that his mom had told him once that he could go to the park even if it was raining. All he had to do was climb!

So Max climbed onto his bed and then up onto his momâ€™s bed. From there, it was easy to climb down from the window above the front door and make it to the park.

Max smiled as he ran through the rain. The park was just as fun as it always was, even in the rain! He laughed as he played hide and seek and swung on the swings.

Max left the park feeling much happier than when he had arrived. Climbing to the park had been a great idea and it had put a smile on his face!

Once upon a time, there was a naughty monkey in a jungle. He liked to have fun and not have a plan. One day, he was bored and wanted something to do. So, he organized a party in the jungle. He invited all the animals in the jungle and they came to the party. Everyone had so much fun, dancing and singing. The monkey was very happy that he could organize a party. Everyone was very happy! The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was very restless and wanted something to do. So he decided to go to the park. When he arrived at the park, he saw a big, round, sausage. It was big enough for him to hug. So he grabbed it tight and hugged it. He smiled, feeling happy that he had something to hug.

He hugged it so much until he was tired. When he was tired, he sat down. He felt cozy with the sausage by his side. He closed his eyes and felt very peaceful. He fell asleep with the sausage still in his arms.

When he woke up, the sausage was still there. He smiled and gave the sausage one final hug before he went home.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy mole who lived in a big field. He was a very clumsy mole, and he was always tripping over his feet.

One day, the mole's best friend, a squirrel, came over for a visit. The mole was excited and asked his friend, "What should we do?"

The squirrel answered, "Let's cover things with leaves!"

The mole thought it was a great idea, so they spent the day covering things like rocks, trees, and even a hole in the ground with colorful leaves. 

When they were done, the mole was tired and said, "This is fun! Let's do it again!" 

The squirrel laughed and said, "Sure, let's do it tomorrow!"

The End.

Lily liked to work with her mom. Mom worked at a store that sold socks. Lily helped mom put the socks in piles by color and size. Lily thought socks were fun and pretty.

One day, a girl came to the store with her dad. The girl saw Lily and said, "Hi, I'm Anna. Do you work here too?" Lily nodded and smiled. Anna said, "Can I help you? I like socks too." Lily said, "Sure, you can help me. We can be friends."

Lily and Anna worked together for a while. They found socks that matched their dresses. They found socks that had stars and hearts on them. They found socks that were soft and warm. They had a lot of fun.

Mom saw Lily and Anna and was happy. She said, "You two are very good workers. And very good friends. Do you want a treat?" Lily and Anna said, "Yes, please!" Mom gave them each a cookie and a juice. They thanked mom and shared their treats.

Lily and Anna became popular at the store. Everyone liked them and their socks. They worked and played together every week. They were very happy.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They like to find stones and make shapes with them. Sara finds a big stone that looks like a heart. She shows it to Ben and says, "Look, I found a heart stone. It is for you, Ben."

Ben smiles and says, "Thank you, Sara. It is a nice stone. I like it." He puts the stone in his pocket and gives Sara a hug.

They keep playing until it is time to go home. Sara's mom calls her and says, "Sara, we have to leave now. It is getting late. Say goodbye to Ben."

Sara says goodbye to Ben and runs to her mom. She is sad to leave her friend, but she knows she will see him again. She says, "Mom, can we come back to the park tomorrow? I like to play with Ben and the stones."

Her mom says, "Maybe, Sara. It depends on the weather and if we are not too busy. But I am glad you had fun today. You are a good friend to Ben."

Sara nods and gets in the car. She looks out the window and sees Ben waving at her. He takes out the heart stone and holds it up. He says, "Bye, Sara. I will keep the stone safe. It is a special stone. You are a special friend."

Sara waves back and smiles. She feels happy and warm. She thinks, "Ben is a special friend too. I hope we can play again soon."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park, especially when the moon was shining bright in the sky. One night, as she was playing with her toys, she saw a mysterious shadow lurking behind a tree.

Lily felt scared and didn't know what to do. She tried to ignore the shadow and continued to play, but then she heard a loud noise. Suddenly, a big branch from the tree fell down and almost hit her!

Lily realized that the mysterious shadow was actually a big, scary monster that was trying to hurt her. She quickly ran away and hid behind a rock. She knew that she had to be careful and stay away from the monster.

The next day, Lily went back to the park with her mom. She showed her mom where the monster was hiding and her mom called the park rangers to come and take care of it. Lily was happy that she was safe and could play in the park again under the beautiful moon.

Lila and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big truck with many boxes. The truck driver is loading the boxes on the truck. He puts them on his shoulder and walks to the truck.

Lila and Ben are curious. They want to know what is in the boxes. They sneak behind the truck driver and look at the boxes. The boxes have unknown words on them. Lila and Ben do not understand the words.

The truck driver does not see Lila and Ben. He finishes loading the boxes on the truck. He gets in the truck and drives away. Lila and Ben are sad. They wanted to see what was in the boxes.

They go back to the playground and play with their toys. They forget about the unknown boxes. They have fun with their friends. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old man. Every day he would ignore the people around him and be angry with everyone. One day he went to the market, and saw a big and delicious potato. He couldn't resist it and took the potato without asking.

The potato seller saw it and was very angry. He ran to the man and shouted at him. The man refused to admit that he had taken the potato and acted like he didn't know what was going on.

The potato seller was so mad that he decided the man had to be punished. He took the man to the police station, where the police said that the man had to pay a fine.

The man was so sad because he didn't have enough money to pay the fine. But he was also very wise and knew that if he learned his lesson, he would never do something like this again. The potato seller saw this, and decided to forgive him and let him go.

The man was very happy and thanked the potato seller. From then on the man was nice and friendly to other people, and never acted grumpy again. He learned his lesson, and never took anything without asking first.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl called Sarah. She loved looking up at the sky and gazing at the sunshine. Every day at 3 o'clock, Sarah would stand outside and look up towards the sun.

One afternoon, as she was gazing at the yellow sunshine, she saw a shiny, yellow balloon floating by. Sarah gasped in delight and jumped up and down in excitement!

"Mummy, mummy!" She called out, "Come look what I saw!" 

Mummy ran outside to see the balloon. "Oh Sarah, it's so beautiful!" 

"Let's get it!" said Sarah.

Mummy smiled and said, "Let's see if we can get it!"

Together, they reached up to the sky and grabbed the yellow balloon. Sarah hugged it tightly and laughed with joy as the sunshine showered down on them.

The End!

The sun was shining brightly and the wind was blowing. Two kids were playing in the backyard. They had a large tent and were trying to build it together.

"Hurry up!" The young girl yelled.
The young boy laughed. "We can't build this tent all by ourselves!"

The little girl smiled and said, "You don't have to yell at me. Let's just keep going."

The two kids worked hard on the tent, but it didn't seem like they'd ever finish it. Suddenly, the boy stopped and stared at the sky. "What's wrong?" The little girl asked.

The boy pointed to the clouds in the sky. "We better hurry. It looks like it's going to rain soon." The girl's eyes widened and she started working faster. 

Sure enough, the sky got darker and darker and the wind started to howl. The kids ran towards the tent and managed to finish it just in time. Then, they both got inside and waited. 

Outside, the rain pounded and the winds blew. The tent swayed and the children held on tight. The storm raged on and the children were serious. 

The children were relieved when the storm passed. They had made it through thanks to their tent.  They hugged each other and smiled. "Let's never yell at each other again, okay?" the little girl said with a big smile.

Sara was a girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a bear. She played with them every day in her room. She made them talk to each other and have fun.

One day, Sara was playing with her bear. She pretended that he was her friend and they went to the park. She said, "Hello, bear. Do you want to go on the slide?" The bear nodded and said, "Yes, Sara. I like the slide. It is fast and fun." Sara smiled and took the bear to the slide. She put him on the top and pushed him down. The bear laughed and said, "Whee! That was fun. Thank you, Sara."

Sara and the bear played on the slide for a long time. They also played on the swings, the seesaw and the sandbox. They had a lot of fun. But soon, Sara felt tired. She yawned and said, "I am sleepy, bear. Let's go home." The bear yawned too and said, "Me too, Sara. Let's go home and take a nap."

Sara and the bear walked back to her room. They saw that Sara's mom was waiting for them. She said, "Hello, Sara. Hello, bear. Did you have fun at the park?" Sara nodded and said, "Yes, mom. We had fun. But we are sleepy now. Can we take a nap?" Sara's mom smiled and said, "Of course, Sara. You can take a nap. But first, you need to wash your hands and face. You are dirty and smelly from playing." Sara said, "Okay, mom. I will wash my hands and face. But what about the bear? He is dirty and smelly too." Sara's mom said, "Don't worry, Sara. I will wash the bear for you. He needs a bath too. Then he will be clean and soft again."

Sara and the bear washed their hands and face. Then Sara's mom took the bear and put him in the sink. She used soap and water to wash him. She rinsed him and dried him with a towel. She gave him back to Sara and said, "Here you go, Sara. Your bear is clean and soft now. He smells good too." Sara hugged the bear and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I love you and I love the bear." Sara's mom said, "I love you too, Sara. And I love the bear too. Now, let's go to your bed and take a nap. You need to rest after playing so much." Sara and the bear said, "Okay, mom. Let's go to bed and take a nap." They followed Sara's mom to the bed. They snuggled under the blanket and closed their eyes. They fell asleep and dreamed of the park. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a farmer named Tom. Tom loved to perform amazing tricks. One day, Tom was in the forest performing some of his best tricks. It was a foggy morning, and a nice mist was everywhere.

Suddenly, Tom saw a big empty hole on the ground. He was so puzzled! He had never seen an empty hole like this before! He looked around, but there was no one around.

Tom decided to jump in the empty hole. He jumped in and noticed a little house. He knocked on the door and the door opened. A little girl peeked out.

The little girl asked Tom, "What are you doing here?"
Tom replied, "I am performing some tricks and I saw this empty hole here so I thought I should take a look inside."

The little girl smiled, "My name is Lilly, and I was just playing in the mist, but I got lost. Can you help me get back home?"

Tom held out his hand and said, "Let's go, Lilly!" Together, Tom and Lilly walked out of the hole and back home in the mist. They waved goodbye and went their separate ways.

Once upon a time there was a happy rhythm. It was a fancy rhythm and it lived inside a music box. Every day the music box would open and the fancy rhythm would jump out and dance around the room. Everyone who watched it loved the amazing show!

One day, the music box suddenly stopped. It was too quiet! The people in the room were sad because they missed the happy rhythm.

But then, someone had an idea! She told the people to order the rhythm to come back. So they called out to the rhythm, and sure enough it heard them. The rhythm began to dance again, and everyone was so happy.

It was the best day ever! The people clapped along to the fancy rhythm and watched in awe as it danced around the room. From that day on, they never forgot to order the rhythm to come back whenever it stopped.

Josh was a three year old with a pocket full of wild dreams. He loved to swing high and far on the swing set. But today, something big was happening. Josh's dad was talking to him and his mom about going to a different city. Josh was excited and scared at the same time. 

He grabbed his pocket full of wild dreams and swung high and far on the swing set. As he rocked back and forth, he imagined his new home and all the exciting places to explore. When he reached the peak of his swinging, it was almost like he could touch the stars.

Josh's dad smiled as he saw his son swinging on the swing set. Now, no matter where Josh and his family moved, he would always have his pocket full of wild dreams to carry with him.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very independent. She liked to do everything by herself.

One day Lucy was in the garden. She started to jump and hop around. She was having lots of fun, springing around in the grass.

Next she heard the telephone ringing. She was very excited. She had never heard a telephone before. She wanted to see who was on the phone.

She ran into the house and saw her Mum talking into the phone. Lucy wanted to talk to the person on the phone too. She was very independent and wanted to do it all by herself.

She picked up the telephone and listened to the voice on the other end. Even though she couldn't understand the person on the phone, she felt very proud that she had answered the telephone all by herself.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who had a pet monkey. She loved her pet very much. Every day she would take him for a walk to the park.

One day, when the girl was walking with her pet, she spotted a banana tree. She was so excited! She quickly grabbed her pet and ran to the tree.

Unfortunately, the monkey was too big to reach the bananas. The little girl was so frustrated. She started to cry.

The girl's pet monkey saw how upset she was. He took her hand in his and smiled at her. The girl smiled back and wiped her tears away.

The monkey hopped up the tree and began to pick the bananas. The little girl waited eagerly at the bottom of the tree. She hoped and hoped that the monkey would find some bananas.

Finally, the monkey came back down and gave the girl a bunch of ripe, juicy bananas. The little girl was so happy! She thanked her pet monkey and happily went home with her bananas.

Once upon a time, there was a bright glass box. Inside it was a special delivery that was mysterious and exciting! One day, a little girl named Lisa was walking by and saw the box. She was so fascinated by it! She wanted to open it and find out what was inside.

Lisa tried to open the lid, but it was stuck tight. She decided to give it a little push. Suddenly, the lid flew open and out came a big, bright ball. It rolled across the floor and came to a stop near Lisa's feet. She looked inside and saw the special delivery.

Lisa was so happy and ran to show her mom. She showed her the bright glass box and the special delivery. Lisa's mom smiled and said, "That's a special delivery from the sky. It's a gift from the clouds and they delivered it just for you!" 

Lisa smiled and hugged her mom. They spent the rest of the day playing with the special delivery and it was the best day ever.

Once upon a time there was a great whale who lived deep in the sea. Every day it would step down to the shore and peek out of the water. It saw everything on the beach and decided to take a look.

The whale stepped out of the ocean on its two big fins. It was so tall that it was almost touching the sky! Everyone on the beach stopped what they were doing and ran to the whale.

The children giggled and stepped closer to the whale to get a better look. They asked it questions and the great whale answered by splashing around in the water.

When the sun began to set, the whale stepped back into the sea and disappeared. Everyone waved goodbye and thanked the whale for its visit. They walked away happy and smiling, wishing the great whale a safe journey.

Molly was excited. She had been waiting all afternoon for her mom to come home from work. As soon as she heard the door open, Molly clapped her little hands and ran to greet her.

"Molly, I have a surprise for you!" said Mommy, pulling out a cup of yogurt. She opened it up and the aroma filled their kitchen. Molly's eyes lit up. But then Mommy said "But you can not have it just yet! You must wait until after dinner". Molly groaned, but Mommy was firm.

At dinner, Molly was so hungry that she ate quickly. When she finished, Mommy said "Now it's time for your surprise!" She smiled and gave Molly the yogurt.

Molly dug in and it was delicious. She ate until the cup was empty. Then Mommy said, "Do you remember why I asked you to wait until after dinner?". Molly shook her head. Mommy said: "It's because the yogurt was too cold and harsh for your tummy. If you had eaten it too early, it could have made you feel bad!"

Molly nodded, understanding the lesson. She smiled and clapped for her mommy for being so wise.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a small town with his mom and dad. One day, Timmy and his dad went for a walk and saw a big billboard. The billboard was so high that Timmy had to look up to see it.

"Dad, what's that big sign?" Timmy asked.

"That's a billboard, Timmy. It's where people sell things by showing them to others," his dad replied.

Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "I want to sell something too!"

So, Timmy and his dad went home and made some lemonade. They put up a sign that said "Lemonade for sale" and waited for people to come. Soon, a lady stopped by and bought a cup of lemonade. Timmy was so happy that he sold something on his own billboard.

Once there was a little girl named Jo. Jo liked to run in the park. One day, she ran over to a pear tree. She saw a pear on the ground. The pear was cold. Jo picked it up and took a big bite. It tasted so sweet! Jo smiled and ran over to a bench to sit and eat her yummy pear. 

Then she heard something. It was a little bee buzzing around the pear tree. Jo watched the bee as it flew around the tree. Then it flew away. Jo smiled and starting running again. 

Jo ran all around the park. She explored all the paths and found new places to play. She even saw a pond with some fishes in it and a big hill that she could run up and down. But then it started to get cold, so Jo ran home. 

When she arrived home, Jo's mom was waiting for her with a warm hug. Jo smiled and showed her mom what she had found in the park - a cold pear. Even though it was a bit squishy from her running, it was still sweet and juicy. Jo and her mom shared the pear and Jo enjoyed the last bites.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who dreamed of seeing lightning. He was so excited that he mentioned it to his mom.

His mom said that she would take him to a place to see lightning that very night. She took him to a big, expensive house to watch the storm. The boy was amazed. 

Bright flashes of lightning lit up the sky and it was so beautiful! His mom was so happy to see his excitement. They stayed in the expensive house and watched the lightning until it was time to go home.

The next day, the boy mentioned the lightning to all his friends. He told them how awesome and cool it was to watch. His friends were jealous that he got to see the bright lightning. 

The boy was so happy to have seen the lightning. He talked about it all the time!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. Sally was very careful when she did things. One day while she was playing outside, Sally spotted a strange powder. Sally's mommy had taught her to be careful, so she knew that she couldn't touch it.

Sally went back inside and asked her mommy what it was. Her mommy told her that it was a special kind of powder, and she needed to be very careful. Her mommy grabbed a special cloth and some gloves, then went outside to remove the powder.

Sally watched as her mommy carefully removed the powder using the cloth. Once all of the powder was gone, her mommy threw away the cloth, much to Sally's relief.

Sally smiled as she watched her mommy clean up the powder. She was so happy that her mommy was so careful. She knew that, with her mommy around, she would always be safe.

Once upon a time there was a bunny. His name was Tom. Tom was a very nice bunny, but he wasn't very good at fixing things.

One day Tom tried to repair a broken chair, but he was having a lot of trouble. Then, he saw an avocado on the floor.

Tom thought, "Maybe I can use the avocado to repair the chair!"

He picked up the avocado and put it on the broken chair. Then he put a crazy hat on top of the avocado.

Tom said, "There, it's fixed!"

The next morning, Tom came back to the chair and saw that it was still broken. He said, "I think I need someone else to help me repair this chair."

So, Tom asked his best friend, a bear called Dave, if he could help repair the chair. Dave said, "Yes, of course I will help you repair the chair."

Dave used some glue and pieces of wood to repair the chair. When the chair was fixed, Tom said, "Thank you Dave!"

Tom's chair was repaired and everyone was very happy. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Jack. Sam liked to fight and Jack liked to itch. One day, the sky was gloomy and Sam wanted to fight. Jack was itchy and he didn't want to fight. Sam said he would take an itch break and fight first.

Jack and Sam started to fight in the grass. Sam was bigger but Jack was faster. Sam was throwing punches like a robot. Jack was trying to dodge and run away. But Sam was too fast for him! 

Jack was getting scared, so he started shaking. Suddenly, his whole body started to itch. He knew if he scratched his itches, Sam would get the upper hand in the fight. So, Jack kept moving and tried to ignore the itches. 

At last, Sam got tired and stopped fighting. Jack was relieved - he had won! Although he was itchy all over, he was happy to have won the fight. He and Sam hugged and they decided they wouldn't fight again any time soon.

Once upon a time, there was a big, squishy jello. It was green and it liked to play. One day it wanted to explore, so it decided to go underground. It stretched itself across the ground and snuggled down into a hole.

The jello found it was quite tight and hard down there. But it kept squeezing between the rocks and gravel. It kept feeling around until it bumped into something. Its eyes opened wide in surprise.

It was another squishy jello. It was blue and the same size as the first one. The first jello was so excited and they squeezed each other in a big hug.

They decided to explore together and after a while they found a big, warm cave. They made a cozy home and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a long cactus. She was full of spines, which made her very prickly. She wanted to explore the world around her, but she was stuck in the same spot. 

Then one day, a big heavy door closed and locked in front of her. She was sad, because she couldn't get out to explore. She thought she would be lonely and bored forever. 

But one day, she heard a funny noise! It was a key turning in the lock! The door opened, and a little girl walked in. She wanted to pick up the cactus and take her out to explore. 

The cactus was so excited! Finally, she was able to explore with her new friend. Together, they had lots of fun. 

The cactus learned that being locked up doesn't mean you can't explore the world. It just means you need someone to unlock the door!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy who loved to explore the world. She would wander around looking at the different things she could see and touch. One day, Daisy was searching around her garden when suddenly she found a curious thing. It was a furry, small creature that she had never seen before!

Daisy picked up the creature and looked closely at it. It was her first time touching a furry animal and it felt strange to her. She asked her mom, "Mama, what is this?"

Her mother replied, "It's a baby rabbit, Daisy. Its name is Thumb and it looks very lost!"

Daisy was so happy that she wanted to keep the little rabbit. She asked her mother, "Please mama, can I keep Thumb?"

Her mother shook her head, and sadly said, "No, Daisy. Thumb needs to go home. We don't know where his home is, so we must take him to the animal shelter instead."

Daisy felt ashamed, but she knew it was the right thing to do. She hugged Thumb tightly and said goodbye as they drove away to the animal shelter. There, a nice lady helped reunite Thumb with his family.

Daisy and her family felt relieved and happy. They all waved goodbye to Thumb as he hopped away with his family, back to his home.

One day, a little girl saw a bottle in the park. She was so curious. She ran up to it and saw it was filled with pretty stones. She couldn't believe her eyes, they were so adorable.

The little girl asked her mom, â€œMommy, what is this?â€ Her mom said, â€œThat is a bottle filled with rocks. Do you want to count them?â€

The girl eagerly nodded her head yes and started counting the rocks. She delightedly said, â€œOne, two, three, four!â€ with each pebble she counted.

After she finished counting, she held the bottle up to the sky. The sun shone through it and lit up the colorful rocks. The little girl smiled. She had a beautiful bottle of rocks and she loved counting them.

Once upon a time, there were two races; one was mighty and strong while the other was small and weak. Neither race wanted to be separated from the other. 

The mighty race wanted to stay together and help the small race become stronger. But the small race kept wanting to leave, as they were scared of being too weak.

One day, the two races faced each other in a big race. They both wanted to win but neither wanted to separate. The tiny races ran fast and the mighty race ran powerfully. 

The race was so close that it was impossible to tell who had won. In the end, they came to a happy agreement where they would stay together and never be separated. 

The small race helped the mighty race reach their goals, and the mighty race helped the small race feel stronger and more confident. From then on, they never separated and always worked together happily.

There was a little figure walking in the park. He was feeling hurt and very alone. He saw a big tree close by and decided to go and sit under it. He was hoping to feel better. But as he sat, he started crying.

Then suddenly, he heard a voice from the tree saying, â€œCome here and I will close you in my armsâ€. He looked up and the tree had turned into a big, friendly figure. He walked over to the figure and it hugged him close.

The figure said, â€œYou donâ€™t need to feel so hurt because I am here to help youâ€. The little figure could feel the warmth of the figures hug and started to feel much better. 

The figure gave him one more hug and said, â€œGo now, my friend and donâ€™t feel so alone. I will always be here if you ever need meâ€. 

The figure waved goodbye as the little figure walked away with a big smile on his face. He was no longer feeling so hurt and alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little fox who was very tired, so he decided to take a nap. He scurried off to the cave where he thought it was the best place to sleep. Once the fox arrived, he sat down and closed his eyes, letting out a big yawn. 

He was just starting to drift off when he heard a deep rumble. In fear, he quickly opened his eyes and saw that it was a friendly bear. The bear was licking his lips and looking very hungry.

The bear asked the fox, â€œHave you seen something delicious? I am starving.â€ The fox thought of his lunch that was packed in his pocket. He knew that it was important to be kind, so he decided to share with the bear. The fox offered his lunch to the bear and the bear gratefully accepted.

The fox and the bear ate together. The bear thanked the fox for being so kind and invited him to explore the cave. The fox was excited to explore the cave but he needed to stay alert, so he took a few moments to wake up. He stretched and yawned, feeling very refreshed.

The fox and the bear had lots of fun exploring and the fox learnt a valuable lesson, that kindness makes the world a better place. The fox was thankful for the delicious meal and the moment he shared with the bear.

Once there was a young boy named Tom. Tom didn't have much. He only had a few clothes and a small amount of money. 

Tom's neighbor had lots of luxury. She lived in a big house and had lots of expensive things. Tom wanted to have those things too. 

One day Tom asked his neighbor why she had so much luxury while he had so little. She said that she worked hard to get it and that Tom should do the same. Tom hated the idea of working hard and he said that he didn't want to. 

Tom tried to find shortcuts to get luxury but it seemed that nothing he did worked. Everything was slow and nothing changed. 

Tom eventually realized that he had to work hard if he wanted to get what he wanted in life. He started to do the hard work and soon he found success. Tom had all the luxury he desired and he was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Cat. Cat was going to a fancy birthday party, so she needed to dress up. She found the perfect outfit with a special patch. Cat took her patch and pinned it onto her party dress.

But when Cat stepped outside, it started to rain. The rain made the patch wet and it started to fall off. Cat got so angry and said, "Oh no! My patch!"

Just then, Cat's best friend Polly came by. Polly saw Cat's angry face and said, "Don't worry, Cat. I have another patch that'll fit perfectly!"

Polly pinned the patch to Cat's dress and they both smiled. Cat was so happy and said, "Thank you, Polly! Now I'm all dressed up and ready to go to the party!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was very adventurous and liked trying new things every day. She was always exploring and finding new places to go.

One day, Jane was playing in her home when she stumbled upon an old armchair. She was curious and decided to take a seat. It was very comfy and she thought it was perfect for her. 

Jane jumped out of the armchair and ran to her mom. She said, "Mommy, look! Is this chair mine to keep?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can keep it! It will be here if you ever want to relax and read a book or just take a little nap."

Jane was so happy! She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for taking care of me, Mommy!" 

Janie now loves to relax in her armchair and explore the world around her. She feels safe and secure knowing that her mom cares for her and will always be there for her.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Sam. He was three years old. One day, he decided to make something special. He fetched a bowl and spoon from the kitchen. Then he took some jelly and began to load the jelly into the bowl. Sam liked his jelly extra spicy so he added a lot of extra spice. It was soon ready! Sam grabbed a spoon and tried some of the jelly. It was so good! Sam smiled and ate all the jelly. He had made a delicious snack using jelly and spices. The end.

Once upon a time there was a small bag. It was very special because it was made out of bright colors and it sparkled in the sunlight.

One lovely morning, the bag went out for a walk. But on its way, it got trapped in a deep puddle! Poor bag!

It tried and tried to get out, but it couldn't. So the bag had to suffer in the muddy water. After a long time, the sun went down and night came. 

But luckily, at the very last moment, a nice little girl saw the bag and saved it! She pulled it out of the deep puddle and took it home.

The bag was very happy to be away from the puddle and be back in the warm and bright house. 

The little girl took care of the bag and they became best friends. Whenever the girl went out to play, she always brought the bag with her!

Ginger was a young rabbit who lived in the meadow with her family. Every day she hopped around looking for delicious carrots and playing with her brothers and sisters.

Today, Ginger was feeling brave. Everywhere around her she saw tall trees made of lumber. She had never touched them before and she was curious.

Ginger hopped carefully towards one of the trees. She wished and hoped that it would talk to her. She touched it and said, "Hello, tree". 

Suddenly, a voice said: "Hello, Ginger. What do you want?". Ginger was so surprised that she jumped back.

Ginger asked, "Can you help me? I want to build a treehouse". 
The tree replied, "Yes, I can help you. But, you must be careful and take care of our meadow".

Ginger smiled and said, "Thank you!". She got to work with the lumber and eventually built a beautiful treehouse for her and her family.

From then on, Ginger would visit the tree every day. She would talk to it, share her stories and also get advice. Together they hoped that the meadow would be happy and healthy. 

The End.

Anna loves books. She likes to look at the pictures and listen to the stories. She has many books, but her favorite is the one about the bird who can fly. The bird is adventurous. He flies to many places and sees many things.

One day, Anna wants to fly like the bird. She puts on her red cape and runs outside. She jumps and flaps her arms, but she does not fly. She tries again and again, but she only falls. She feels sad.

Then, she hears a voice. "Hello, little girl. Do you want to fly?" She looks up and sees the bird from her book. He is real and he is talking to her. He is colorful and bright.

"Yes, I do!" Anna says. "But I don't know how."

The bird smiles. "I can teach you. Come with me. We can have an adventure."

Anna is surprised and happy. She holds the bird's wing and he lifts her up. They fly together in the sky. They see the clouds, the trees, the flowers, and the animals. They fly over the mountains, the rivers, the fields, and the sea. They fly high and low, fast and slow, and have fun.

Anna is amazed. She feels like she is in her book. She thanks the bird for the adventure. The bird says he is glad to have a friend. He gives her a feather and says goodbye. He flies away.

Anna runs back to her house. She hugs her book and her feather. She tells her mom and dad about her adventure. They smile and hug her. They say she has a big imagination. Anna smiles too. She knows she has a big book.

One day, there was a little boy who wanted to go and play outside. He looked out the window and saw a sunny day. He couldn't guess what it was like outside but he knew it was warm. He went outside and found a tree with lots of shade. He felt so comfortable in the shade that he fell asleep. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was his dad, telling him to be careful in the shade. The little boy was being careless and he had almost fallen asleep. His dad laughed and the little boy laughed too. That day, the little boy learnt to be careful so he wouldn't get hurt in the shade.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to drink milk. She thought it was the best thing ever! One day she was walking around looking for something special. After a while she came across a bottle of luxury milk. It looked so yummy and delicious, she couldn't resist. So, she opened the bottle, put it to her lips and started drinking. But it was too strong and it hurt her throat. She started to cry and put the bottle down. She never drank anything like that again.

One day Jack and Sally were on an adventure. They had to save the land from the mean dragon. All of a sudden they saw the dragon flying in the sky! Jack said "We have to save the land from the dragon!" Sally was scared but she knew what to do - she had to get some food to distract the mean dragon.

So Jack and Sally ran to the store and got lots of broccoli. When they got back, they put the broccoli in a basket and held it up in the sky. The dragon saw the broccoli and flew down to get it. Jack and Sally were both very brave!

The dragon was so big and strong, but Sally was delicate and gentle. She talked to the dragon in a soft and kind voice, and she offered him the broccoli. The dragon took a bite of the broccoli and he got so full that he fell asleep.

Jack and Sally had saved the land from the mean dragon! They were so happy that they hugged each other and cheered. They had done it! Jack and Sally were heroes!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bob and Jane. They were very close and liked to play together. One day, they were playing in the dark woods. Bob suddenly stumbled upon a funny-looking rock, and he asked Jane to come take a look.

When Jane saw the rock, she said, "This is the start of something special!" Bob agreed, and they decided to unite the funny-looking rock with the trees around it. 

Jane said, "Let's make a campfire. That way, we can stay warm in the dark woods." 

Bob and Jane got together the twigs and pieces of wood and put them around the rock. Then, Bob looked in his pocket and found a big, red match. He struck the match and the campfire came to life!

Bob and Jane laughed and shared stories by the campfire that night. They were happy to be so united in the dark woods. The start of this wonderful adventure will not be forgotten.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy truck that he loved to play with. One day, his friend Johnny came over to play. Johnny saw Timmy's truck and said, "Can I play with your truck, Timmy?" Timmy thought for a moment and then replied, "No, it's mine." Johnny looked sad and his face turned pale. 

Timmy saw that Johnny was sad, so he said, "You can play with it too, Johnny." Johnny's face lit up with happiness and he replied, "Thank you, Timmy!" They played with the truck together and had a lot of fun. From that day on, Timmy and Johnny shared their toys and played together every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown dog. His name was Jack. Jack loved to play games with his friends. One day, Jack's friends said, "Let's play catch!" 

Jack was so excited. He grabbed his yellow ball and ran outside. Then he threw it up in the air. 

His friends tried to catch it. One of them caught it with his nose! It was so funny. Even Jack laughed.

Then the friends threw the ball again and again. They had lots of fun playing catch. 

At the end of the day, Jack was so tired, but he was very happy. He went inside and slept with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a big garden with lots of flowers. One flower was very special, it was an orange flower that was about to bloom. A little girl named Lily loved to play in the garden and she loved the orange flower. She would visit it every day and talk to it.

One day, Lily saw a boy walking towards the flower with a pin in his hand. She knew he wanted to pick the flower, so she ran to stop him. The boy didn't listen and picked the flower with the pin. Lily was very sad and cried a lot.

The next day, Lily went back to the garden and saw that the orange flower was gone. She asked the gardener what happened to it and he told her that the flower had died because someone had picked it. Lily was very upset and wished she could have stopped the boy from picking the flower with the pin.

Tom and Mia liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big ship. The ship had wheels, a sail, and a flag. They pretended to sail the ship on the floor, on the bed, and on the couch.

One day, their mom said, "It is time to store your toys. We have to go to the park soon." Tom and Mia did not want to stop playing. They said, "But mom, we are having fun. Can we play a little more?"

Mom said, "No, you have to store your toys now. You can play with them later. If you store them, they will be safe and clean. If you leave them out, they might get lost or broken."

Tom and Mia were sad, but they knew mom was right. They started to put their toys in a big box. They put their cars, their dolls, their blocks, and their books. But when they came to the ship, they hesitated. They loved the ship so much. They did not want to store it.

They learn that it is better to be kind than to be mean. They also learn that animals are fun and loyal. They promise to treat them well. They have a good time at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big house with many rooms. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help feed the cat. Lily was happy to help and gave the cat some food.

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to go up to the attic to find some old toys. Lily was a bit worried because she had never been up there before. But she bravely climbed up the stairs and found some really cool toys.

Lily was so happy to have helped her mom and feed the cat. She played with her new toys all day and couldn't wait to help again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she looked up and saw the big, round moon in the sky. She wanted to touch it, but she knew she couldn't. 

Suddenly, she heard a little bird chirping. The bird was hurt and couldn't fly. Lily felt helpless and didn't know what to do. 

She decided to pick up the bird and walk to her mommy's house. Her mommy knew just what to do to help the little bird. They put a bandage on its wing and gave it some water to drink. 

The next night, Lily looked up at the moon again and smiled. She knew that even though she couldn't touch it, she could still help the little bird.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to do lots of fun things. One day, Sarah heard a noise coming from the kitchen. She hurried to see what was happening and saw her mommy shaking a big calendar.

"Mommy, why are you shaking the calendar?" Sarah asked.

Mommy smiled and said, "I'm shaking the calendar because it's time to turn the page and start a new month."

Sarah was very excited. She helped her mommy flip the page to reveal a brand new month.

"It's very quiet in here," Sarah said.

Mommy nodded. "Yes, it is quiet. It's the beginning of a new month and time to start afresh. Let's go have some fun."

They quickly changed into their warm sweaters and snuck out of the house. As they walked, Sarah noticed all the trees shaking in the wind and she smiled.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She was very lucky to have a loop that her mom had given her.

Every day Jane liked to go outside and spin her loop around in circles. Then, when she was tired, she would just rest for a few minutes with her loop.

One day, Jane was outside spinning her loop when something magical happened. The loop began to glow and Jane could actually feel it spinning her up, up, up into the air!

She was so lucky that she was able to fly around in the sky, until she got tired and it was time for her to rest. Jane was so happy that she had a loop that could help her fly into the air!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons. One day, he went to the kitchen to get a snack. His mom was cutting an apple with a big knife. Timmy thought the knife was scary, so he stayed far away.

After he ate his snack, Timmy wanted to play with his blocks. He counted the number of blocks he had and stacked them up high. But then his sister came in and knocked them down. Timmy thought that was rude and got mad.

Timmy's mom came back into the room and saw that Timmy was upset. She asked him what was wrong and he said, "Sissy cut my blocks down and that was rude." His mom hugged him and said, "I'm sorry that happened. Let's build a bigger tower together." And so they did, and Timmy was happy again. The end.

Sam and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Sam had a lot of cars and trucks, and Lily had a lot of dolls and animals. They liked to share their toys and make up stories.

One day, Sam had an urge to build a big tower with his blocks. He asked Lily to help him. "Lily, do you want to build a tower with me?" he said.

Lily nodded. "Yes, Sam, that sounds fun. How high do you want to make it?"

Sam thought for a moment. "Very high, like the sky. We need a lot of blocks. Can we use some of your blocks too?"

Lily agreed. "Sure, Sam, we can use some of my blocks. But we have to be organized. We have to sort the blocks by color and size. That way, we can find the ones we need."

Sam and Lily started to sort the blocks. They made piles of red, blue, yellow, and green blocks. They also made piles of big, medium, and small blocks. They worked together and talked to each other.

"Look, Lily, I have a big red block. This can be the base of the tower," Sam said.

"Good idea, Sam. I have a medium blue block. This can go on top of the red block," Lily said.

They continued to supply each other with blocks and stack them on the tower. They made the tower higher and higher, until it reached the ceiling. They were very proud of their tower.

"Wow, Sam, we did it! We made the highest tower ever!" Lily exclaimed.

"Yes, Lily, we did it! We are the best builders!" Sam cheered.

They hugged each other and smiled. They had fun building the tower, and they were happy to share their toys and their urge.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lila. She was three years old and very charming.
Every day she would go for a walk with her mom and her dad. They would take her to the park and let her explore different kinds of places.

One day, Lila noticed a big book in the park. It was a dictionary. She was so excited that she asked her parents if she could have it. Her parents said yes, so Lila was very happy.

Lila took the dictionary home and started reading through it. She was excited to gain new words and knowledge! She was learning so many things and found the dictionary very interesting.

Every day Lila would read the dictionary and gain new knowledge. She even started to remember some of the words she learned. She was getting smarter every day.

Lila was so proud of her dictionary. She loved it and found it so charming. The dictionary taught her a lot of new things and she was very thankful for it.

This is the story of how Lila gained knowledge from her charming dictionary.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to run really fast in his yard. One day, Timmy's dad bought him a new toy car. It was very expensive and Timmy loved it so much. He wanted to race his toy car in the yard. 

Timmy's friend, Sarah, came over to play. She saw Timmy's new toy car and wanted to race too. Timmy said, "Okay, let's race!" They started racing their toy cars in the yard. Timmy's car was faster than Sarah's car. Timmy was very happy that he won the race. 

After the race, Timmy and Sarah played with their toy cars together. They had a lot of fun. Timmy was happy to have a friend to play with in his yard.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Max and Sam. They both smiled at each other. Max said to Sam, "Let's have a race!"

Sam said, "Yes, but only if I get a prize. I want a orange prize."

Max smiled and said, "Okay, if you win, you will get an orange prize."

They both ran as fast as they could. Max used all his might and finished first. Sam was very close behind.

Max smiled and reached for the orange prize. He held it out to Sam and said, "Here you go, you won!"

Sam smiled and hugged Max. Then he hugged the orange prize too and said, "Thank you!"

Sam and Lily were playing in the tent in the backyard. It was dark outside, but they had a flashlight to see. They liked to pretend they were explorers in a jungle.

"Look, Sam, I found a treasure!" Lily said, holding up a shiny necklace. "It is very attractive. It has many colors and sparkles."

"Wow, Lily, that is a great treasure!" Sam said. "Where did you find it?"

"I found it in the old box under the table. Maybe it was Mommy's or Grandma's. Can I keep it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can keep it. But you should wrap it in something to protect it. Maybe in this cloth." Sam said, handing Lily a piece of fabric.

"Good idea, Sam. Thank you." Lily said, wrapping the necklace carefully. "Now it is safe and cozy. I will show it to Mommy and Daddy later."

They put the wrapped necklace in their backpack and continued to play with the flashlight. They made shadows on the tent wall and told stories. They had a lot of fun in the tent. They were happy explorers.

Tom and Ben are brothers. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many toys with motors. Motors make the toys go fast and make noise.

One day, Tom and Ben are playing in their room. Tom has a big red truck with a motor. Ben has a small blue car with a motor. They race their toys on the floor.

"Look, my truck is faster than your car!" Tom says. He makes his truck go vroom vroom.

"No, my car is faster than your truck!" Ben says. He makes his car go beep beep.

They keep racing and arguing. They do not see their dog, Spot, come into the room. Spot is hungry. He sees the toys with motors. He thinks they are food. He runs to the toys and grabs them with his mouth.

"Hey, stop! That's my truck!" Tom shouts. He tries to get his truck from Spot.

"Hey, stop! That's my car!" Ben shouts. He tries to get his car from Spot.

But Spot does not listen. He runs away with the toys. He bites the motors. The motors break. The toys stop working. Spot spits them out. He does not like the taste.

Tom and Ben are sad. They look at their broken toys. They cry.

"Spot is a bad dog!" Tom says.

"Spot is a stupid dog!" Ben says.

They hug each other. They are sorry for fighting. They decide to share their other toys. They hope Spot will not eat them.

One day, a famous bear was walking through the woods. He saw a log that looked very inviting and he decided to sit on it. He was so comfortable that he decided to take a nap.

As he dozed off, a squirrel saw the bear sitting on the log. He started running around the woods, shouting to all his friends, â€œThereâ€™s a famous bear sitting on a log!â€

Soon, many other animals had gathered around the bear. They all stood and watched, in awe of the famous bear who had come to visit them.

The bear woke up, feeling very surprised and happy to be surrounded by all of the animals. He smiled and said hello to everyone, and then he hopped off the log and went on his way. The animals all waved goodbye, very happy to have been able to meet the famous bear.

Once there was a deer who lived in the woods. She was the original deer, so all the other deer looked up to her. One day, she noticed something strange in the woods. It was a big, moving thing that made a loud noise. She wasn't scared, she was curious. 

She followed the thing to a big open space. She noticed that it had shiny wheels and that it was turning around in circles. She watched as it reversed and went back the way it came. As she watched this strange thing, she realized that it was an original toy car! 

She admired the toy car, but she wasn't sure why it was so special. She decided to reverse and head back to the woods, but the toy car followed her! The toy car beeped and whirred and kept following her all the way back to her home in the woods. 

The deer was so happy that the car wanted to be her friend. She never knew something so original could be so much fun! From then on, they were the best of friends and they would play together in the woods every day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a tall tree. The tree was so high that it almost touched the sky. Many birds lived on this tree. Two little birds, named Tim and Kim, lived there too.

One day, Tim found a big, juicy worm. Kim saw it and said, "Can we share the worm, Tim?" Tim thought for a moment and said, "Yes, we can share it." So, they both ate the worm and felt very happy.

After that, Tim gave Kim a big wink. Kim winked back. They knew that sharing made them happy. From that day on, they always shared everything they found. All the other birds saw this and started to share too.

Soon, the whole tree was full of happy birds, all sharing and caring for each other. The tree became the happiest place in the town.

The moral of the story is that sharing makes everyone happy.

Once there were two sisters, Sue and Rose. One day, they were having a picnic in the park. Rose was very excited, but Sue thought it was boring. She said, "Picnics are not fun! I don't want to stay here."

Rose said, "Why don't you try speaking to someone? Maybe you will make a new friend."

So Sue slowly walked across the park and then she saw a girl playing all alone. She smiled and said, "Hi, my name is Sue! Would you like to be my friend?"

The girl smiled and said, "Yes!" 

They talked for a long time and both of them enjoyed the picnic a lot.

The moral of the story is to speak to others and you will find lots of friendship and fun. Don't be afraid to reach out and talk to new people. Otherwise, life can be very boring!

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to climb the big oak tree. It had many branches and leaves. They felt like birds in the sky.

One day, they saw a small bird on a branch. It was hurt. It had a broken wing. Sara and Ben wanted to help the bird. They climbed up to the branch.

"Hello, bird," Sara said. "We are here to help you. Don't be scared."

The bird was scared. It tried to fly away, but it could not. It made a loud noise. Sara and Ben were gentle. They wrapped the bird in a soft cloth. They climbed down the tree.

"Let's take the bird to the vet," Ben said. "The vet can make the bird better."

They ran to the vet. They yelled for help. The vet heard them. He came out of his office. He saw the bird.

"Good job, Sara and Ben," the vet said. "You are very helpful. You saved the bird's life. Come in, I will fix the bird's wing."

Sara and Ben smiled. They followed the vet. They were happy. They helped the bird. They were good friends.

John took a snack and went to the park. He was very excited to get there and he ran through the park gates. He saw a big slide, and he quickly went down it three times. He was having lots of fun!
