Lily and Emma played together all day. They shared their clothes and their toys. They told each other stories and secrets. Lily was very happy. She thanked her mom for the surprise. She said, "I love Emma. She is the best doll ever. She is like me."

Sam liked to measure things with his ruler. He measured his toys, his books, his bed, and even his cat. He wanted to know how big everything was. One day, he decided to measure his mom. He asked her to lie down on the couch and he started to measure her feet, her legs, her arms, and her head. His mom smiled and said, "This feels like a nice massage, Sam. Thank you."

Sam was happy that his mom liked his measuring. He wanted to measure her hair too, but it was too long for his ruler. He looked around and saw his dad's scissors on the table. He thought, "Maybe I can cut some of her hair and measure it." He grabbed the scissors and ran to the couch.

His mom did not see him coming. She closed her eyes and enjoyed the massage. She did not hear the snip, snip, snip of the scissors. She did not feel the hair falling on her face. She did not know that Sam was cutting her hair very short.

When Sam finished, he was proud of his work. He measured the hair he cut and said, "Wow, mom, your hair was very long. Now it is very short. Look, I measured it for you." He showed her the ruler and the hair.

His mom opened her eyes and screamed. She saw her hair on the couch and on the floor. She saw her son holding the scissors and the ruler. She saw her reflection in the mirror and saw how short her hair was. She was very angry and very sad. She said, "Sam, what did you do? You ruined my hair. This is very bad. This is very scary. Go to your room right now."

Sam was confused and scared. He did not understand why his mom was so mad. He did not mean to hurt her. He just wanted to measure her hair. He dropped the scissors and the ruler and ran to his room. He cried and wished he never measured his mom. He wished he never saw the scissors. He wished he could make his mom happy again.

Tom and Sue are twins. They like to play with their cars and trucks. One day, they wake up early and go to the living room. They see a big box with a bow on it.

"Wow, what is that?" Tom asks.

"Maybe it is a present for us!" Sue says.

They run to the box and open it. Inside, they find a new toy train set. It has a black engine, a red caboose, and many cars. It also has tracks, bridges, and tunnels.

"Yay, a train!" Tom and Sue shout.

They take out the train and set it up on the floor. They turn on the engine and watch it go around the tracks. They make choo-choo noises and pretend to be the conductor and the passengers.

They have a lot of fun with the train. But then, Tom has an idea. He wants to make the train go faster and faster. He turns the knob on the controller all the way up.

"Look, Sue, the train is so fast!" Tom says.

But Sue is worried. She sees the train wobble and shake on the tracks. She thinks it will fall off.

"Tom, slow down the train! It will wreck!" Sue says.

But Tom does not listen. He likes to see the train zoom and zoom. He does not see the curve ahead. The train goes too fast and flies off the tracks. It crashes into the wall and breaks into pieces.

"Oh no, the train!" Tom and Sue cry.

They run to the wreck and see the black engine, the red caboose, and the cars all smashed and bent. They feel sad and sorry. They wish they had been more careful.

They hear their mom and dad come downstairs. They see the mess on the floor and the broken train.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

"We were playing with the train and it wrecked," Tom says.

"We are sorry, Mom and Dad," Sue says.

Mom and Dad look at Tom and Sue. They see their sad faces and their tears. They hug them and say,

"It's okay, Tom and Sue. We know you did not mean to break the train. We are glad you are not hurt. But next time, you have to be more careful and listen to each other. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom and Dad," Tom and Sue say.

They help Mom and Dad clean up the wreck. They hope they can fix the train someday. They learn a lesson about playing safely and nicely.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help wash the dishes. Timmy didn't want to because he thought it was a bad job. 

"Timmy, please help me wash the dishes," said Timmy's mom.

"I don't want to. It's a bad job," replied Timmy.

"It's not a bad job. It's an important job. We need clean dishes to eat off of," explained Timmy's mom.

Timmy thought about it and decided to help his mom wash the dishes. He realized it wasn't such a bad job after all.

There was a game that the children liked to play. But it was dangerous. All the kids knew they had to be careful.

One day the game changed. It no longer looked like it used to. That made everyone scared. They worried something bad might happen.

But when the children tried it, they saw that the game was still fun. They laughed and had a great time.

The game was still dangerous, but everyone was careful. They made sure that nothing bad would happen.

At the end of the day they all agreed that the game was different, but it was still fun. They were glad that it had changed.

One day, Little Bear and his Mommy went for a visit. She took him to a place he had never seen before. It was an icy place with lots of snow. As they walked around, Little Bear heard some music. It came from something his Mommy called a radio. It made Little Bear smile. 

When Little Bear asked his Mommy about it, she said it was called a radio and that it played music. 

Little Bear said, "Can I make music with it too?"

Mommy said, "Yes, Little Bear, you can make your own music too. Let's try it together."

So Little Bear and Mommy made music together with the radio. Little Bear was so happy. It was an amazing visit!

Ben and Mia were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many different objects, like cars, dolls, blocks, and books. They liked to make up stories and pretend with their objects.

"Look, I made a castle with my blocks!" Mia said, showing Ben her creation. "It has a princess and a dragon and a knight!"

"That's cool, Mia!" Ben said. "Can I play with your dragon?"

"OK, but be careful. He is very fierce and can breathe fire!" Mia said, handing Ben the dragon.

Ben took the dragon and made it fly around the castle. He made roaring noises and pretended the dragon was attacking the knight. "Rrrr! I am the dragon and I will burn your castle!" he said.

"Hey, stop that!" Mia said, getting upset. "You are ruining my story! The dragon is nice and the knight is his friend!"

"No, the dragon is mean and the knight is his enemy!" Ben said, not listening to Mia.

They started to argue and pull the dragon from each other. The dragon's tail snapped off and they both gasped.

"Look what you did!" Mia said, crying. "You broke my dragon! He was my favorite object!"

"I'm sorry, Mia!" Ben said, feeling bad. "I didn't mean to break him! Can we fix him?"

They looked at the dragon's tail and tried to put it back on, but it didn't work. They felt sad and angry.

Then, Ben had an idea. He ran to his room and came back with some tape and a feather. He taped the feather to the dragon's tail and showed it to Mia.

"Look, Mia! I solved the problem! I made a new tail for your dragon! It is original and pretty!" he said, hoping Mia would like it.

Mia looked at the dragon and smiled. She liked the new tail. It was different and fun. She hugged Ben and thanked him.

"Thank you, Ben! You are a good brother! I like your new tail for my dragon! It is original and pretty!" she said, feeling happy.

They hugged the dragon and played with him again. They made up a new story where the dragon had a magic feather tail that could do amazing things. They had fun and forgot their fight. They were friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers was very tired because he had been running and playing all day. He decided to take a nap in the sun. 

While Whiskers was sleeping, a bird came and left a message for him. The message said that there was a mouse in the garden. Whiskers woke up and saw the message. He got up and went to the garden to catch the mouse.

When he got there, he saw that the mouse was already gone. Whiskers started to frown because he really wanted to catch the mouse. He went back home and went back to sleep.

Once upon a time there was a little puppy called Patch. He lived in the forest with his mom and dad. 

Today Patch was very excited â€” he was going to the post office to mail a letter to his friend!

Mom and Patch walked through the beautiful landscape until they arrived at the post office. Patch was alert and looked around at the shiny stamps, colourful envelopes and postcards. 

Dad smiled and said "What letter will you be mailing today patch?" 

Patch replied with a grin "I'm sending my friend a letter telling him how much I love to play in the forest!"

So Patch put his letter in the mailbox and waved goodbye. He made sure to keep an eye out for when his letter was delivered.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle. The castle was very old and made of soft, sandy stones. Every day, the sun would shine on the castle and the stones would slowly melt even more.

But one day, something special happened. The castle remained in one piece, despite the hot sunlight and melting stones. Inside the castle, there was a very patient wizard who had cast a special spell to keep the castle from melting away.

The wizard made sure to keep the spell strong, so that his castle would stay safe and strong for many years to come. The wizard was very happy with his castle and wanted to share it with everyone. So, he opened the castle door and invited all the children to come play and explore!

The children had so much fun running around the castle and pretending to be kings and queens. They were so happy that the wizard was so patient, and that his castle had not melted away.

Frank the frog was very troubled. His fountain had broken and he was sure no one could fix it.

One day Frank's best friend Sam the snail came to visit him. Sam asked, "What's wrong Frank?"

Frank said sadly, "My fountain is broken and I can't fix it." 

But Sam had a plan! He said, "If you come with me I might know someone who can help you fix your fountain."

So Frank and Sam went out into the woods, looking for help. And soon they found Snail Bob!

Snail Bob smiled at Frank and said, "Don't worry, with a bit of hard work we can get your fountain running again."

Frank was overjoyed! He and Snail Bob got to work and soon he had a beautiful working fountain.

Frank was so happy and relieved, and he thanked Snail Bob for his help. From then on, Frank and Sam made sure to visit Snail Bob to say thank you.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was rich and the other wasn't. One day, they decided to have a race. The rich one had a triangle and the other one had a long stick. They both put their objects on the floor, ready to race.

"Ready, set, go!" shouted the rich friend. Both of them started to speed across the room. The triangle whizzed faster than the other one, because it was so light. The rich friend won the race, but it was fun for both of them.

When they finished, the poor friend said, "That was fun! But I think I'll stick to using my stick from now on!" The rich friend replied, "That's a good idea!"

The two friends laughed and enjoyed the race. It was a fun time for both of them. They enjoyed playing together and running as fast as they could!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was eager to explore the sea. So one day, she went to a beach with her dad. When she got there, she was amazed at what she saw. There was so much to explore! She wanted to observe it all.

First, they saw a lot of colorful fish swimming around. Lucy was so excited! She wanted to get closer, so her dad took out a net and they tried to catch one. But they were too quick!

Next, they saw a shark. It had a big nose and sharp teeth. Lucy was a bit scared, but she wanted to observe it. So she grabbed her dad's hand and they watched it swim around. They were so fascinated!

Finally, they said goodbye and went home. Lucy loved exploring the sea and she couldn't wait to go back and observe more. She was so eager to learn more about the ocean and its animals.

Once upon a time, in a gloomy forest, there was a little fairy named Lily. She had many friends, but her best friend was a big, kind bear named Ben. They played together every day and were very happy.

One day, Lily and Ben found a lost kitten. The kitten was very sad and scared. Lily said, "We should help the kitten find its home." Ben agreed, and they decided to look for the kitten's family together.

As they searched, they met other animals who wanted to help. They all worked together, and soon they found the kitten's family. The kitten was so happy to be home! Lily, Ben, and their new friends learned that when you help others, you make the world a better place.

One day, a boy named Tim wanted to watch his favorite cartoon. He went to the living room and saw the TV was empty. He was sad because he could not find his cartoon.

Tim's mom came in and said, "Why are you sad, Tim?" Tim told her about the empty TV. His mom said, "Let's sort this out." She took the remote and pressed some buttons.

Soon, Tim's favorite cartoon appeared on the TV. He was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mom!" They sat together and watched the cartoon with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat cheese. One day, he saw a big, clear piece of cheese on the table. He wanted it so badly, but he couldn't reach it.

Suddenly, a big, friendly cat named Mittens walked by. "Can you help me, Mittens?" asked Timmy. "I want that cheese, but it's too high."

Mittens smiled and said, "Sure, I can pass it to you." Mittens reached up and grabbed the cheese. She passed it down to Timmy, who was so happy he could hardly believe it. From that day on, Timmy and Mittens were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was looking for something special. She looked around the room, but nothing seemed right. She wanted to choose something that was special and that would make her happy.

Then she spotted a shiny rail. It was so big and so beautiful. â€œI choose the rail!â€ she said to her mom. But her mom said, â€œThat rail is too expensive. We canâ€™t afford it.â€

The little girl said, â€œPlease, Mommy. I really want it.â€ So her mom said, â€œOk, if it will make you happy.â€ They bought the expensive rail and brought it home.

The little girl was so happy. She put her toys on the rail and now her room was even more special. She hugged her mom and said, â€œThank you, Mommy. I love my new rail!â€

One day, Emma was very excited for something special. She grabbed a big box of crayons with every color imaginable! She was so excited she could hardly wait.

Emma had a reliable friend who was always willing to help, so she asked for help to open the box of crayons. Together, they opened the box and all the colors were just as bright and vivid as she had imagined.

With her crayons in hand, Emma couldn't wait to start drawing. She wanted to draw a beautiful rainbow with all of the colors of the crayons. So, she started drawing and the colors were so perfect!

When Emma was finished, she was amazed by her art and so proud of herself. She excitedly showed her mom and dad and they thought it was the most beautiful picture they had ever seen. 

Emma was so proud of her work and it excited her to create something that was so beautiful with her crayons!

Once there was a modest baby who lived in a house with her Mum and Dad. So very young was she that she did not understand many words. But she did understand the words love and together.

One day her parents took her out for a walk to the park. On their way, they saw a bird in a tree. They asked the baby if she understood what the bird was singing.

The baby replied, "no, I don't understand it".

Her parents said, "that's OK, one day you will understand."

So the family continued on their happy walk to the park and enjoyed the sunshine, the trees and the music of the birds.

The baby felt so loved, and she knew her family was special. She understood love, and that was enough.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every week. They had a big ball that they could roll to each other. They had fun with the ball.

One day, a big dog came to the park. The dog saw the ball and ran to get it. Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want the dog to take their ball. They shouted at the dog.

"Go away, dog! That is our ball!" Lily said.

"Leave us alone, dog! We want to play!" Ben said.

But the dog did not listen. The dog grabbed the ball with its mouth and ran away. Lily and Ben were upset. They lost their ball. They did not know what to do.

They ran to Lily's mom, who was sitting on a bench. They told her what happened. Lily's mom hugged them and said,

"I'm sorry, kids. That was a bad dog. But don't worry, we can get you a new ball. Maybe we can find the dog and get your ball back. Come on, let's go look for it."

Lily and Ben felt a little better. They hoped they could find their ball. They followed Lily's mom and looked for the dog. They wanted to play with their ball again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore the world around her. One day, she found a pretty ribbon and decided to tie it in her hair. She made a promise to herself to always wear it.

One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest. She saw a butterfly and ran after it, but she got lost. She didn't know how to get back home. She remembered her promise to wear the ribbon, but it was gone. She started to cry.

Hours passed and it started to get dark. No one came to find her. Lily was very scared and didn't know what to do. She wished she had never left her home. Finally, she fell asleep on the ground. The next morning, the rescue team found her, but it was too late. Lily had died from the cold.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mom and dad. One day, they went to a picnic and her mom served her a sandwich. The bread was soft and the filling had a funny taste. Lily liked it anyway.

After lunch, they played on the swings and the slide. Lily loved the texture of the slide - it was smooth and shiny. When they were done playing, they went home and Lily took a nap. She dreamed of funny animals and soft blankets.

When she woke up, her mom served her some milk and cookies. The cookies had a crunchy texture and made her laugh because they were shaped like little animals. Lily had so much fun playing and eating that day. She couldn't wait to go back to the park again!

Once upon a time, there was a powerful bicycle. One day, the bicycle appeared near the park.

A little girl, three years old, saw the bicycle. She asked her mommy, "What's that?"

"That's a bicycle," answered Mommy.

The little girl said, "Wow, it's so big and powerful!" She walked up to the bicycle and tried to ride it. The bicycle was too big for her, but she was determined to ride it.

Mommy said, "It's too big for you, but I can get you a little bike that you can ride."

The little girl was so excited! She couldn't wait to get her own bike. "Yes please, Mommy," she said.

The next day, they went to the store and bought a little bike for the little girl. She was so happy to have her own bike, and she rode it all around the park. She was so happy, and she thought the powerful bicycle was the coolest thing ever.

Once there was a large building with a dark sky above it and a bright moon. Anna was walking around the building with her big brother, Jack, who was smiling a lot.

Suddenly, they heard a growling sound coming from the large, dark forest. "What's that sound?" asked Anna. Jack just smiled and said, "Let's find out!"

The two walked cautiously, Anna holding tightly onto Jack's hand into the darkness of the forest. As they got closer, Anna could see a large, fierce bear standing before them. The bear was growling angrily and blocking their way.

Jack looked very scared but he still managed to smile and said, "We should turn around and go back". Anna smiled and nodded, and they both ran quickly out of the forest.

The two were very relieved to be out of the dark forest and away from the large bear. They gave each other a big hug and smiled, happy that they were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a mule. The mule was big and strong, but also very dirty. The farmer wanted to give the mule a bath, but he couldn't catch him because the mule was always running away.

One day, the farmer found a key and he knew it could unlock something special. He searched and searched until he found a clean and shiny barn. He put the mule inside and locked the door. The mule was scared at first, but then he saw the fresh hay and clean water. He was very happy!

After a good bath, the mule was no longer filthy. He was now clean and beautiful. The farmer was very happy too, because he had a clean mule to help him with his work. From that day on, the mule always went to the clean barn and he never ran away again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a famous key. It was a magical key and everyone wanted it. It could give the holder the ability to do amazing things. But no one knew where it was.

One day, a little girl named Lucy found the key. She picked it up and held it out in front of her. She knew it was special. Suddenly, all the adults around her started to ignore her. No one wanted her to have the key.

But Lucy was brave and she ran away with the key. She kept running until she was safe. When she stopped, Lucy looked at the key in her hand and smiled. She knew she was the only one who could use the key now.

Dave was a shy little boy. He kept a special notebook under his bed. Inside the notebook he wrote down all the things he wanted to remember. 

One day, Dave heard his parents mention that they were going to the beach. He excitedly wrote it inside his notebook. 

When his parents asked Dave what he wanted to do, he kidly said the beach. His parents were so surprised and asked how he knew. Dave shiedly pulled out his notebook and showed it to them. 

His parents smiled and admired his notebook. They were so proud that he was thinking ahead and writing important things down.

From that day on, Dave made sure to keep his notebook organized. He even mentioned things to his parents that they should remember to write down in his notebook.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was so brave and strong. One day, she wanted to solve a problem. She had to figure out how to stay safe when the ocean was rough.

So she thought really hard. She decided to paddle her boat away from the rough sea. She used both her hands and kicked her feet. The little girl paddled away until the sea became calm.

When the little girl looked behind, she could see the rough sea in the distance. She was so relieved to have solved the problem and stay safe.

The little girl smiled with satisfaction. From then on, she knew she could solve her own problems.

Once upon a time there was a green pear tree. It grew tall and proud in the sun and rain. One day, a little girl decided to pick one of the pears from the tree. She reached up and plucked the pear from the branch. 

Feeling happy, she held the green pear in her hand. She took a bite, but what she tasted was sour. She made a funny face and shrugged her shoulders. 

The little girl didn't understand why the pear was so sour. She shrugged her shoulders again and decided to try a different one. She reached up, chose one more pear and took a bite. This time it was sweet and juicy. 

The little girl smiled, and to this day she always takes a extra bite to make sure she's choosing the sweetest pear.

Once there was a chubby little boy who was very excited. His mom was giving him a present and he couldn't wait to see what it was. His mom said, "Close your eyes!" and the little boy did. She asked him, "Can you guess what it is?" The boy shook his head and pointed to the present. His mom laughed and said, "Yes, that's the present!" He opened his eyes and reached for it with his little hands. He ripped off the wrapping and was so excited to see what it was. It was a fun toy car! The little boy smiled and started racing it around the room. His mom smiled and said, "Isn't that a fun present?" The little boy nodded and kept playing. He was so happy to have such a fun present.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who had an obedient goat. He loved taking care of the goat, feeding it its favourite vegetables and playing with him in the garden.

Every day, the little boy would take the goat outside for a walk. He would carry the goat along with him, as the goat was too small to walk on its own. On the way, they would pass by fields and trees, where the goat could smell the fresh grass and listen to the birds chirping. It was very peaceful and the little boy enjoyed taking his goat for a walk.

One day, while they were walking, the little boy saw a homeless man sitting on the side of the road. The man was hungry, so the little boy took a carrot out of his pocket and gave it to the man. The man thanked him and said that the little boy was very kind.

From then on, the little boy always kept a few carrots in his pocket whenever he took his goat for a walk. Whenever he saw someone that was in need, he would give them a carrot from his pocket.

The little boy was very happy, knowing that his obedient goat was always by his side.

Ben and Lily are brother and sister. They like to play together. Sometimes they play with toys, sometimes they play with books, sometimes they play with puzzles.

One day, they want to play with TV. TV is big and shiny. It has many colors and sounds. Ben and Lily like to watch TV.

But Mom says, "No, TV is not for playing. TV is for watching. You can watch TV for a little time, but then you have to play with something else."

Ben and Lily are sad. They want to play with TV more. They ask Mom, "Why can't we play with TV? TV is fun. TV is nice."

Mom says, "TV is fun and nice, but TV is not good for you if you watch too much. TV can make your eyes tired and your brain sleepy. You need to play with other things that make your eyes happy and your brain smart. Like toys, books, puzzles, or outside."

Ben and Lily think about it. They like to make their eyes happy and their brain smart. They say, "OK, Mom. We will watch TV for a little time, and then we will play with other things."

Mom smiles and says, "Good. I love you, Ben and Lily. You are good children."

Ben and Lily watch TV for a little time. They see animals and songs and stories. They laugh and clap and sing. Then they turn off TV and go to play with other things. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He loved to laugh, he laughed all the time. 
Jack had a well in his town. Every day, the people in the town would come together around the well to talk and play. 
One day, Jack noticed something was not right. The water in the well didn't look the same. It was black and smelly- it looked terrible! But everyone just laughed and kept playing.

The next day Jack woke up to find the well had disappeared. The townspeople were very upset. They asked Jack why he had not said anything about the water being terrible the day before. 

Jack had noticed something was wrong, but he thought it would just go away. He had wanted to keep everyone laughing and he was sorry he hadn't said something sooner. 

The townspeople realized Jack had only wanted to keep them happy and they forgave him. They knew Jack would never let something terrible pass by again. Everyone laughed and they all lived happily ever after.

Once there were two friends: Anna and Bill. Anna had an unknown history and Bill wanted to learn about it. 

One day, Bill asked Anna, "Can you tell me about your history? I would like to know more." 
Anna smiled and said, "Yes of course!"

Anna then opened a book and began to tell Bill about the numbers that made up her history. She told him about all the different numbers that had been with her since she was born.

Bill looked surprised and asked, "Are you sure all those numbers are connected to your history?"

Anna nodded and said, "Yes, all those numbers have been part of my history for a very long time. That's why it's so special." 

Bill smiled and said, "That's amazing. Your history must be very important." 

Anna nodded and said, "It is. It's a history filled with unknowns, but I'm happy to share it with you."

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had long hair that shone in the sun. One day, she went outside to play and felt glad because it was a beautiful day. Suddenly, she saw a butterfly and tried to catch it with her hand. But, she missed and accidentally struck her head on a tree. Ouch! She rubbed her head and felt sad. Her hair was messy, but she was glad she didn't hurt the butterfly.

Once there was a young boy named Jim. He was playing outside on a beautiful day. He was admiring all the colourful things around him. Then he noticed a heavy sack by the side of the road. He wondered what was inside the sack.

He went over to take a closer look. He was so excited when he saw lots of toys inside the sack. All of the toys were different shapes and sizes. They were so brightly coloured andJim couldn't help but admire them.

He picked up one of the toys and it was very heavy. It was too heavy for Jim to carry. But he was determined to bring it home with him. So he pushed and pulled until the sack was rolling behind him.

Finally, Jim made it back home with the heavy sack of toys. He was so happy with the treasures he had found. Jim spent the rest of the day playing with all the wonderful toys. He knew he would always appreciate and admire the special memories it brought.

Lola and her mum were walking along the beach. Suddenly, Lola stared at an orange image in the sand. It looked like an orange butterfly! She bent down and touched it gently with her finger. Suddenly, it moved! It was a real orange butterfly, fluttering its wings. Lola smiled and watched in wonder as the butterfly flew away.

The next day, Lola took her bucket to the beach again. She wanted to find another orange butterfly and said a silent prayer that she would see one. This time, Lola stared at the sand for a long time, but she couldn't find an orange butterfly. She was a bit sad and started to walk away when suddenly, she spotted something bright in a nearby bush.

It was the orange butterfly! Lola couldn't believe her eyes and quietly moved closer. She stared in wonder as the beautiful butterfly flew around the bush. Suddenly, the butterfly flew away. Lola smiled and ran home to tell her Mum all about it.

Harry was feeling very excited. A big box had just arrived in his room and he wanted to peek inside. He rushed to the box, and noticed a big, red button on the top.

Harry said: "What could be inside? Let's find out". 

He put his finger on the button and pressed down. To his surprise, the box opened and revealed something amazing!

Inside he found a toy robot with lights and noises. Harry couldn't believe it. He said: "Wow, what an amazing toy!"

He grabbed the robot and had lots of fun playing with it. Everywhere he went, people stopped to peek and admire his new toy. It was an amazing day!

Once upon a time, there was a monkey. The monkey liked to eat bananas. One day, the monkey went for a jog in the jungle. The monkey saw a big, fine banana tree. The monkey climbed up the tree and ate some bananas. The monkey was happy and went home. The end.

Jake and his mom were walking in the park one day. Jake saw a thin, shiny object and asked his mom what it was. 

"It's a razor," said his mom.

Jake was curious and asked if he could hold it. 
"No, Jake," his mom said. "Razors are dangerous. We need to leave it there and keep walking."

But Jake did not want to yield. He wiggled out of his mom's grasp and ran over to the razor. He picked it up and it felt cool and smooth in his hands. He wanted to see if he could open it.

He tried and tried, but the razor was not yielding. His mom saw what he was doing and ran over to him.

"That's enough, Jake," she said, taking the razor away. "When I said no, that meant no. You need to learn to listen to me."

Jake nodded and said ok. He knew he had to yield this time.

But Jake was still curious about the razor and he asked his mom what it was for. 
"It's for shaving," she said. "But you're much too young for that, so it's best to just leave it alone."

Jake agreed and smiled. He was happy to have seen such an interesting object, even if he couldn't open it. He knew that he had to yield this time

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Susie. She liked playing outside with her green friends who lived near her house. Susie and her friends liked to go on adventures and play together, but one day something strange happened.

Susie's friends started to hate her because they said she was different. Susie was sad and didn't know why they would say such things.

The next day, Susie decided to take her friends on an adventure. She brought her green backpack and guided them all through the forest. They played games, laughed and had fun. Susie was happy that things were back to normal.

At the end of the day, Susie's friends said they were sorry for being mean and that they would never hate her again. Susie thanked her friends and gave them each a big hug. From then on, she was part of their group and would always start off their new adventures with a smile.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved music. He loved to hear music of all kinds, but especially the sound of the violin. Every day he would pretend to be playing the violin with a fake one he had made.

One day, the boy was sitting in his room and he heard a noise outside. He opened his window to see what it was. To his surprise, he saw a real violin player!

The boy got very excited and asked the violin player if he could play too. The violin player said yes, so the boy grabbed his fake violin and began to play. He made some silly sounds but then suddenly, he was playing music. Everyone was so impressed, they started to clap and talk about him.

The boy was so happy he continued playing until it was time to go home. From that day on, the boy was known as the fake violin player and he was the happiest he had ever been!

Sammy was a happy little boy. Every day he would go outside and jog around the park with his mom. One day when they were jogging, Sammy noticed a jar. 

"Mom, what's that?" Sammy asked.

"That's a jar," his mom replied.

"Can I have it?" Sammy said.

"No," his mom replied. "It looks too expensive."

But Sammy didn't give up. He kept jogging until they had gone around the park three more times. Finally, Sammy's mom said yes to the jar.

They went over to take a closer look and Sammy saw it was filled with pennies. He was so excited and thanked his mom for the jar. He couldn't wait to get home and count all of the coins.

For Sammy, it was the most expensive jar in the world.

One day, a little girl named Jane was out playing in the park. She was having so much fun until she heard a noise coming from behind a tree. Jane was a bit scared, so she moved closer to take a look. When she peeked around the tree, she saw a stranger.

Jane had never seen this stranger before. He was tall and dark. Jane didn't know what to do. She slowly moved closer to get a better look. Suddenly, the stranger saw her, and she ran away.

Jane ran as fast as she could. After a few minutes, she stopped and caught her breath. She looked back, but she couldn't see the stranger anymore. Jane was happy because she felt safe again.

From that day forward, Jane was very curious about the unknown stranger she had discovered in the park. She wanted to find out what he was doing there, but the mystery remained unsolved.

Once there was a little girl named Roberta. She was 3 years old and very cute.

Every day, Roberta would go outside and kick her new soccer ball. She loved to kick it so hard that it would go flying across the yard. It made her very happy.

One day, her mommy called her inside for a special meal. On the table was a beautiful yellow cake with lots of pretty flowers on it. Roberta was so excited and gave her mom a big hug.

After eating the cake, Roberta went back out to the backyard. She hugged her soccer ball and started to kick it again. It was a beautiful day for playing outside, and Roberta had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. Joe liked to play games. He was very good at them and his friends often asked him to join. He usually liked to win.

One day Joe found an old, strange game in a box. It looked like fun, so he asked his friends to join. Everyone played the game, but Joe just couldn't win. He kept trying but it was too hard.

After a while, Joe noticed something really disgusting in the box. It was slimy and green and it smelled terrible. He went running to tell his friends - they were so scared they all ran away! Joe was left alone and never got to win the game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious about the world around her. One day, Lily's mommy took her to a tutor to learn new things. The tutor was very nice and taught Lily how to sing a song. Lily loved singing and practiced every day.

One day, Lily's mommy took her to a park. There, they met a group of children who were singing and dancing. Lily was very excited and joined them. She sang the song she learned from her tutor and the other children clapped and cheered.

From that day on, Lily loved singing even more. She told her mommy that she wanted to become a famous singer one day. Her mommy smiled and said that with practice and hard work, she could achieve anything she wanted. Lily was very happy and continued to sing every day.

One morning, a nice little girl was playing in the park. She was running around, having a lot of fun. Suddenly, she saw something appear. It was a giant foot! She was very surprised and she asked herself if it belonged to someone. She waited and waited but nobody appeared.

The little girl decided that she had to investigate. She walked up to the big foot and touched it. It felt soft and nice. She began to imagine who it could have belonged to? Was it a giant? Or maybe a monster?

Then, after a few moments, a man appeared. He had lovely blue eyes and a friendly smile. The little girl was very relieved and she realised that the foot belonged to the man. They became friends and the man showed the little girl how to build castles in the sand with her feet.

They had a lot of fun together and the girl was very sad when the man had to go. But the nice man promised to come back the next day and they could play together again. The little girl was very happy and she ran off to tell her mommy all about her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on vacations with her family. One day, Lily's mom told her they couldn't go on vacation because they didn't have enough money. Lily was sad, but she understood.

Lily's dad worked hard every day, but they still couldn't afford a vacation. One day, Lily saw her dad cutting the grass in their yard. She asked if she could help, and her dad said yes. Lily worked hard and helped her dad finish cutting the grass.

After they finished, Lily's dad gave her some money for doing such a good job. Lily was so happy! She realized that working hard can help you get what you want, even if it's not a vacation. That was a harsh lesson, but Lily learned that hard work can pay off in the end.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to walk on the beach. They liked to look for shells and stones and crabs. One day, they saw something big and round and gray on the sand. It was an oyster.

"Look, Sue, an oyster!" Tom said. "Maybe it has a pearl inside."

"Can we open it?" Sue asked.

"I don't know. It looks very old and hard. Maybe it is ancient. Maybe it was here before the people and the houses and the cars."

Tom and Sue tried to open the oyster with their hands, but it was too strong. They tried to use a stick, but it was too soft. They tried to use a rock, but it was too heavy.

"Ouch!" Tom said. "I hurt my finger."

"Me too," Sue said. "This oyster is too tough. Let's leave it alone."

They walked away from the oyster and looked for something else to play with. They found a starfish and a sandcastle and a kite. They had fun on the beach and forgot about the oyster.

But the oyster did not forget them. It was happy that they did not break it. It was happy that it still had its pearl. It was happy that it was ancient and wise. It smiled and closed its shell.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys. But they do not have many toys. Mama says toys are cheap, but money is not. Mama works hard to get money for food and clothes.

One day, Sara and Ben see a big toy store. They see many toys in the window. They see dolls, cars, balls, books, and puzzles. They want to go inside and look at the toys. But Mama says no. She says they have to go home and do their homework.

Sara and Ben are sad. They do not want to go home. They want to play with the toys. They see a big red ball on a shelf. It looks fun and soft. Sara says to Ben, "I want that ball. Do you want it too?" Ben nods. He says, "Yes, I want it. But how can we get it?"

Sara thinks. She sees a stool near the shelf. She says, "I have an idea. You stand on the stool. I will reach for the ball. Then we can run away with the ball." Ben says, "OK. Let's do it. But we have to be quick and quiet."

Sara and Ben wait for Mama to look away. Then they run to the stool and the shelf. Ben climbs on the stool. Sara reaches for the ball. But the ball is too high. She cannot get it. She tries again and again. She stretches her arm. She jumps. She pushes the stool. But the ball does not move.

Suddenly, they hear a loud voice. It is the store man. He says, "Hey, you two! What are you doing? Stop that! You cannot take that ball. It is not yours. It is mine. You have to pay for it." Sara and Ben are scared. They drop the stool and the ball. They turn and see Mama. She is angry. She says, "Sara and Ben, how could you? You are naughty. You do not steal. You do not lie. You do not run away. You come with me. Now."

Sara and Ben are sorry. They cry. They say, "We are sorry, Mama. We are sorry, store man. We just wanted to play with the ball. We did not mean to be bad. Please forgive us." Mama says, "I love you, Sara and Ben. But you have to learn. You have to be good. You have to listen. You have to respect. You have to say thank you. You have to say sorry. You have to work hard. Then you can have nice things. But not cheap things. Cheap things are not good. They break. They hurt. They make you sad. You do not want cheap things. You want good things. Right?" Sara and Ben nod. They say, "Right, Mama. We want good things. We do not want cheap things. We want to be good. We want to make you happy. We want to say thank you. Thank you, Mama. Thank you, store man. We are sorry. We will not do it again." Mama hugs Sara and Ben. She says, "I am glad you understand. I am proud of you. Now let's go home and do your homework. Then we can play with your toys. The toys you have. The toys you love. The toys that are good. OK?" Sara and Ben say, "OK, Mama. We love you. We love our toys. We love our home. Let's go." They hold Mama's hand and walk away. The store man smiles and waves. He says, "Bye, Sara and Ben. Be good. Come back another day. Maybe I will have a ball for you. A good ball. A ball you can afford. A ball you can enjoy. A ball you can share. How about that?" Sara and Ben smile and wave. They say, "Thank you, store man. That sounds nice. Maybe we will. Bye." They leave the store and go home. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They reached for the ball, but they turned away from the cheap. They chose the good. The end.

The bell rang loudly. Trudy the happy girl heard it and smiled. She loved ringing the red bell. 

Trudy was very fond of plants. She was very careful with them too. She watered them every day and talked to them.

One morning, Trudy saw a careless boy near her plants. He was picking the flowers off her pretty plants. Trudy asked, "Why are you doing that?"

The careless boy shrugged and said, "I'm just having fun." 

Trudy shook her head. She said, "My plants are very special to me. Please don't pick them again."

The boy was sorry for his careless mistake. He promised he would never pick Trudy's plants again. Trudy smiled and rang the bell.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to collect nuts and make big piles of them. One day, Nutty found a very big nut that was too heavy for him to carry. He asked his friend, a humble mouse named Mickey, for help. Mickey was happy to help Nutty and together they carried the big nut to Nutty's pile. 

As they were putting the nut on the pile, Nutty realized that he had too many nuts and his pile was getting too big. He asked Mickey if he wanted some nuts to take back to his home. Mickey was very happy and thanked Nutty for his kindness. 

From that day on, Nutty and Mickey would often share their nuts and make big piles together. They were very happy and humble friends. The end.

Once there was a girl. She liked to run. She ran everywhere. She ran outside and inside. One day she was running inside the house and she was being silly. 

Her mom heard her and said, "Why are you running inside?"

The girl said, "I'm having fun!"

Mom smiled, "That's nice, but it's time to stop and eat dinner!"

So the girl stopped running and ate dinner. That night she went to bed and dreamed about running around the world. 

The next day she was back to running around again, having fun and being silly.

One day, there was a little girl who really wanted a trumpet. She asked her mom for one, but her mom refused. The little girl was very sad. 

She decided to look around her house to see if she could find something to play with. And then she spotted it! She found a yummy banana in the kitchen. She snatched it up and pretended it was a trumpet.

She started playing her pretend trumpet, blowing into the banana like it was a real trumpet. She had so much fun making music with her yummy banana. 

The mom heard the music and came to check it out. She was so impressed with what the little girl had made and refused to interrupt the fun. Instead, she smiled and said "Yes, that sounds like a real trumpet!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Joy. She was very brave and wise.

Every day, Joy would visit the beach. She loved playing in the sand and watching the tide.

One day, Joy decided to do something brave. She wanted to dive in the sea! She looked into the waves and wondered how deep they were. Then, she held her breath, closed her eyes and dived into the tide.

Joy loved the feel of the cool water. She swam around and had a wonderful time. She was so glad that she had listened to her wise heart and taken the plunge! 

When Joy came out of the water, she felt even braver and wiser. She beamed with joy and knew that she could do anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she found a black rock outside. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. "Mommy, look at this rock!" she said. "It's black and shiny!" 

Lily's mom examined the rock and said, "It's very pretty, Lily. Where did you find it?" 

"I found it outside," Lily replied. 

"Well, it's important to be careful when picking up rocks," her mom said. "Sometimes they can be sharp or dangerous. I'll give you a little lecture about it later." 

Lily nodded and put the rock in her pocket. She was excited to show her dad when he came home from work. "Daddy, look what I found!" she said, pulling the black rock out of her pocket. 

Her dad examined the rock and said, "Wow, that's really cool, Lily. It looks like it could be from outer space!" 

Lily smiled and felt proud of her special black rock. She decided to keep it in her room where she could look at it every day.

Once upon a time there was a poor boy. He was very tired and had no friends. He walked down the street, dragging his feet with every step and feeling sad. 

One day he saw a wink in the sky. The boy wondered what it was. He looked up and smiled.

"Maybe something good will happen to me," he said. 

He kept walking and walking, and soon he came upon an old man. The old man smiled at the boy and asked him if he wanted to come to his house. 

The boy followed the old man, but soon he started to feel very bad. He felt like he was not able to move and something was wrong. 

At last they reached the old man's house and the boy started to suffer. He screamed and tried to run away, but the old man had locked the door. 

The poor boy was never seen again. No one knew what happened to him and he was never freed. He suffers to this day and his exhausted body never gets any rest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park with her friend Timmy. They played on the swings and slides, but then Lily saw some ice on the ground.

"Look, Timmy! Ice!" she said.

Timmy looked at the ice and said, "I think it's too cold to touch."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Maybe we can make it flexible if we warm it up."

So, they took the ice and held it in their hands. After a while, the ice started to melt and become flexible. They had so much fun bending and stretching the ice.

As they played, Lily's mom called out, "Time to go home, Lily!"

Lily and Timmy said goodbye and ran off, happy and excited about their new discovery of how to make ice flexible.

Sara liked to whistle. She whistled when she woke up, when she ate, when she played, and when she went to bed. She whistled loud and happy. She whistled songs and sounds. She whistled all the time.

But her brother Ben did not like her whistling. He said it was too noisy and annoying. He said it hurt his ears and head. He said it made him mad. He asked her to stop whistling many times. But Sara did not stop. She was persistent. She liked to whistle too much.

One day, Ben had an idea. He went to the kitchen and opened a can of tuna. He knew Sara did not like tuna. She said it smelled bad and tasted worse. She said it made her sick. He took the can of tuna and hid it under her bed. He thought it would make her stop whistling.

But he was wrong. Sara did not notice the tuna under her bed. She whistled as usual. She whistled when she woke up, when she ate, when she played, and when she went to bed. She whistled loud and happy. She whistled songs and sounds. She whistled all the time.

The next day, Ben was surprised. He smelled something bad in Sara's room. He looked under her bed and saw the can of tuna. It was open and rotten. It was full of flies and worms. It was gross and stinky. He felt sick and sorry. He realized his idea was bad and mean. He took the can of tuna and threw it away. He went to Sara and said, "I'm sorry, Sara. I put tuna under your bed. I wanted you to stop whistling. But I was wrong. You can whistle if you want. I don't mind."

Sara smiled and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Ben. I'm sorry, too. I know you don't like my whistling. But I like it. It makes me happy. Can we be friends?"

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, we can be friends. And maybe you can teach me how to whistle. It sounds fun."

Sara was happy. She said, "Sure, I can teach you. It's easy. You just have to blow air through your lips. Like this." She whistled a tune.

Ben tried to whistle. He blew air through his lips. But he only made a funny noise. He laughed. Sara laughed. They laughed and whistled together. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a zebra called Max. He was very competitive and liked to show off his stripes. Every morning Max would stretch and show off.

One day, a giraffe came along and saw Max stretching. 'You are very competitive,' said the giraffe. 'I can help you to stretch even better,' she said.

Max was very excited and couldn't wait for the giraffe's help. He watched carefully as the giraffe showed him some new stretches. They stretched their legs, toes and arms.

Max loved being competitive and he enjoyed showing off his stretches. Everyone was very proud of him and Max was the happiest zebra in the whole world.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She had a big basket of apples and was so excited to give them away as presents.

Anna set off on her journey and soon arrived at her best friend's house. Her friend was very surprised to see her and her basket of apples. 

"Thank you for the apples, Anna!" said her friend.

"You're welcome!" said Anna and she handed over the basket with a big smile. 

Anna and her friend had a great time playing with the apples. They counted them, rolled them, smelled them and even tasted a few. 

Anna suddenly realised that she had to go, so she gathered up the last few apples and said goodbye to her friend. 

"Thank you for coming Anna," her friend said.

"You're welcome!" said Anna happily, with a big wave.

Anna was a bit worried on the way home, but she felt better when she saw her house. She put the last few apples in her basket and said a big thank you. 

Anna was so happy she had been able to give her friends such a lovely surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to build structures with his toy blocks. One day, Tim built a big structure that he was very proud of. He wanted to show his friend, Sam.

But then, Sam came over and accidentally knocked down Tim's structure. Tim was very sad and said, "Please be careful, Sam! My structure is dead now." Sam felt bad and wanted to make Tim happy again.

So, Sam said, "Please, let me help you build a new structure, Tim." Together, they built an even bigger and better structure than before. Tim was happy again, and they played with the new structure all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play and have fun all day long. One day, Benny was hopping through the forest when he saw a big oak tree. Benny thought the oak tree was very important because it was so big and strong.

Benny wanted to show off his speed to the oak tree, so he started hopping as fast as he could around the tree. But as he was hopping, he accidentally bumped into another animal and hurt them. Benny felt very bad and realized that it was not important to show off his speed.

From that day on, Benny learned that it was more important to be kind and careful than to be fast. And every time he passed by the big oak tree, he remembered the lesson he learned and felt happy knowing he was doing the right thing.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing in her backyard. She saw a bird flying in the sky and said, "Look, Mommy! A bird!" 

Her mommy replied, "Yes, Lily. Birds are good animals. They can fly high in the sky and sing beautiful songs." 

Lily asked, "Can we watch the bird together?" 

Mommy said, "Of course, we can watch the bird together. But did you know that there are many more things to watch in the universe? The universe is very big and has many stars and planets." 

Lily looked up at the sky and said, "Wow! The universe is so pretty. I want to watch it every day with you, Mommy." 

Mommy smiled and said, "I would love that, Lily. Watching the universe with you is one of my favorite things to do."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to bake cookies with her mom. One day, Lily's mom put on a modern apron with bright colors and asked Lily to help her mix the cookie dough.

Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, Mama!" She loved helping her mom in the kitchen. As they mixed the dough, Lily's mom said, "You are such a good helper, Lily. You are going to be a great baker one day!"

Lily smiled and said, "I love baking with you, Mama." They finished making the dough and put it in the oven to bake. As they waited for the cookies to be done, Lily's mom asked, "What kind of cookies do you want to make next time?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Chocolate chip cookies, please!" Her mom nodded and said, "Sounds good to me!" They hugged each other and waited for the cookies to finish baking. When they were done, they enjoyed eating their delicious cookies together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Ben. He was so restless that he could hardly sit still.

One day, Ben's mom brought him to the park. She said he could play for as long as he wanted.

So he ran and jumped and had lots of fun! When it got too dark, Ben's mom said it was time to go.

But Ben was not done having fun and he didn't want to go. He pleaded with his mom to stay a bit longer.

"Mom, please!" Ben said.

His mom smiled and said, "If you pass this test, I will give you a special reward. All you need to do is sit still for one minute without moving."

Ben quickly agreed, and he sat still and quiet for the whole minute. When it was over, his mom gave him a big hug and a special reward.

Ben was so happy and proud of himself. He had passed the test, and he was rewarded with love. From then on, Ben never felt so restless again.

Once upon a time there was a lion, and he was troubled. He needed someone to help him, because he was feeling scared and alone.

One day, a brave little mouse arrived at the lion's den. The mouse asked the lion, "Why are you so troubled? Can I help you?"

The lion roared with sadness, "I'm so scared and alone. I don't know what to do."

The little mouse smiled and said, "Let's start a journey together. We can help each other, and I'm sure we'll find a way to be brave again."

The lion roared with happiness and asked the mouse, "Will you be my friend?"

The little mouse nodded. "Yes, I'll be your friend!"

And with that, the lion and the mouse started their journey together, never feeling scared or alone again!

Once upon a time, there was a big muffin. It was the biggest muffin anyone had ever seen! All the animals gathered around it and sniffed the delicious smell. They were so excited to eat it, but then something unexpected happened.

 Suddenly, the big muffin started to glow. A magical white light shined all around it, healing everything it touched. The animals were so amazed! 

The animals had all different types of hurts and bruises. But as the light touched them, they were made all better. Their scratches and bumps went away and they felt all healed up!  

The animals danced and cheered in joy. They thanked the big muffin for its healing magic and shared it with all the other creatures in the forest. 

The big muffin had brightened up everyone's day! It was the best ever, for sure.

Once upon a time, there was a clever bear who loved to raise logs. He was so strong and brave. Every day he would take a big log and raise it up high. He loved how it made him feel brave and powerful! 

But one day, while he was busy raising logs, a fox appeared. The fox couldn't believe how strong the bear was and asked him, "how do you raise logs so well? It's amazing!" The bear smiled and said, "It's easy, I just use my strong muscles." The fox was so impressed that he decided to try and raise logs as well. 

The fox tried with all his might and was almost able to raise the log, but it was just too heavy. The bear saw the fox's hard work and knew the fox was clever and could do it with just a little more practice. So, he encouraged the fox to keep trying and before long, the fox was raising logs like a pro! 

The bear and the fox became such good friends and every day they would meet in the forest and raise logs together. They were so happy and had so much fun that they stayed friends forever!

Once there was a girl named Mabel. She was only three years old and loved playing with her friends.

One day, Mabel went to the store with her mom. Inside, her mom bought a carton of oats for breakfast. But on the way home, Mabel got very nervous. She forgot to bring the oats.

So Mabel went back to the store. She asked her mom to help her find the oats. And when they found the oats, they both hugged each other.

Mabel was so happy! She never wanted to forget the oats again. And so, she made sure to always remember them, each time they went shopping.

Once upon a time there was a jolly hunter. He went out into the forest, looking for animals to hunt.

He was walking and walking and walking until he came upon a surprise! It was a bear! The hunter stopped and was so surprised to see it.

He carefully grabbed his bow and arrow and aimed. He shot the arrow and the bear ran away. The hunter was happy and now he could bring the animals home to share with his family and friends.

The hunter was feeling jolly after his successful hunt. As he started to walk away, he heard a noise! He looked behind him and saw an even bigger surprise! It was a lion!

The hunter was so amazed and quickly ran away. He couldn't believe that he had seen two different animals on the same hunt. What a jolly hunter he was!

Once there was a rich farmer. He had lots of money, but he didn't have many staff to help him with his land. One day the rich farmer had a plan.

He thought about his land and the staff he needed to make it work. Then the farmer set a plan in motion. He did lots of work, and soon he had the staff he needed.

The staff worked really hard. They were able to grow enough food to sell, and the farmer became even richer. Everyone was happy and the land was beautiful.

The rich farmer and his staff got lots of money. Everyone was glad that the farmer had thought of such a great plan.

Tom and Lily were very excited to go on a tour of the zoo with their mom and dad. They wanted to see the lions, the monkeys, the elephants and the penguins. They held their parents' hands and followed the guide who told them about the animals.

But when they reached the bear enclosure, Tom saw a big red balloon that someone had left on a bench. He let go of his dad's hand and ran to get the balloon. He did not listen to his dad who called him to come back. He wanted to play with the balloon.

Lily saw what Tom did and felt scared. She did not want to lose her brother or get in trouble. She shouted to Tom, "Tom, come back! The bears are dangerous! You have to be obedient!"

But Tom did not hear her. He was too busy blowing the balloon and making it bigger and bigger. He did not see the bear that was watching him from behind the fence. The bear was hungry and curious. It wanted to see what the balloon was.

The bear reached out its paw and tried to grab the balloon. But the balloon was too far away. The bear growled and roared. It made a loud noise that scared Tom. He dropped the balloon and turned around. He saw the bear and screamed.

His mom and dad heard him and ran to him. They hugged him and took him away from the fence. They were angry and worried. They told him he was very naughty and he could have been hurt. They said he had to say sorry to Lily and the guide and the other people on the tour.

Tom felt bad. He realized he had made a mistake. He said sorry to everyone and promised to be obedient. He did not want to play with balloons anymore. He wanted to see the rest of the animals and be safe. He held his dad's hand and did not let go. Lily held his other hand and smiled. She was glad he was okay. They finished the tour and learned a lot. They had fun, but they also remembered to be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy box that was empty. One day, she asked her mom, "Can we open the toy store?" Her mom said, "We don't have a toy store, honey." Lily replied, "No, not the store. The toy box." 

So, her mom opened the toy box and they found some old toys. Lily was happy and played with them. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love playing with my toys." Her mom replied, "You're welcome, sweetie. Anytime you want to play, just ask me to open the toy box." 

Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom." Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too, Lily. It's always a good time to play with you." And they spent the rest of the day playing together with the toys.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Rose. Rose had a big brother named Ben. Ben loved playing with Rose and teaching her new things. One day, Ben told Rose he wanted to show her something special.

He handed Rose a tube and explained that it was full of something he liked to eat. He said it was bitter but promised his little sister it would be yummy. Rose was hesitant but decided to give it a try.

Rose took a bite of what was inside the tube and scrunched up her nose. It was too bitter for her and so she quickly left it there on the ground.

Ben smiled, understanding why Rose did not like the tube's contents. He walked over and picked up the tube, "That's okay Rose, maybe it's just not your thing," he said. He then took a big bite of the tube's contents and said with a grin, "See, it's not so bad!"

Rose smiled and laughed. Despite the bitterness, Ben still loved this strange snack. That's one of the things that made her big brother so special.

Alice was a 3 year old girl who lived in a small house with her mom. Every day she would put on her shoes and go with mom to the park.

Alice always had a lot of fun at the park. She would often find something different, like the soap bubbles her mom made with her hands.

"Look at the bubbles mom!" said Alice.

Her mom smiled. "It's amazing what soap can do! It can make all sorts of different things, like bubbles or a beautiful painting."

Alice looked around the park. She imagined what was possible with soap. "I think I can make a big castle," she said.

Her mom gave her a hug. "I'll support you. Let's go get some soap and have some fun."

Alice smiled. She was excited to see what she could create with soap. The day was full of surprises.

One day, a girl named Sophie went to the beach with her mum. They gazed at the bright shining sea for a long time, it was beautiful! 

Sophie was having so much fun building sand castles. She made them big and tall. Suddenly, a stupid seagull came and knocked down her castle. Sophie was so mad, she shouted and jumped around.

Mum said it was time to go home. But Sophie wanted to stay! She gazed out at the sea, with its shimmering waves. She wanted to stay and play here forever. 

Mum said they had to go back but promised they could come back another day. Sophie smiled and they walked back, dreaming of their next beach visit.

Max and his Mum went to the cafe. Max was very excited. He saw the special food they had - a big plate of waffles. He wanted to try some.

Mum said they could. Max was so happy. The waffle was served in front of him. It was warm and tasted sweet. Max was so grateful.

He said thank you to the waiter for serving him the waffle. They both enjoyed their food. Before leaving the cafe, Max said thank you again. The waiter said you're welcome. 

Max was very happy. He loved eating the waffle and felt grateful to the waiter for serving it to him.

The sky was dark and it started to rain. But little Sarah wasn't scared. She couldn't wait to go outside and splash in the puddles!

Sarah put on her raincoat and headed out. Suddenly, she heard a honking sound and saw a goose. It was flapping its wings and moving its neck. Sarah was very scared and wanted to run away.

But then her mom said it was ok â€“ the goose was just saying hello. So Sarah stayed and waved back. She even tried to talk to it!

After a while, Sarah was no longer scared. She and the goose played together in the rain until the sun came back out.

The sun shone down from above, glinting off the river below. A small duck was swimming and splashing in the water. Suddenly, the duck saw something else - a little fish swimming along in a zigzag motion. It looked so happy, the duck couldn't help but think it was fun.

The duck wanted to join in so it started to swim with the fish, zigzagging this way and that. It was the best game ever! Suddenly, the fish ducked down into a deep part of the river, and the duck followed it.

Together they plunged down into the river and went for a bath. The duck and fish swam in circles, playing and splashing around, making the water go sparkly. The water felt cool and soft on the duck's feathers, so it stuck around and kept swimming until it was too tired to keep going.

Finally, they finished and swam to the shallows. The duck was happy to be out of the water, as it had been a bit boring at times. But the duck was also sad to have said goodbye to its new friend. Still, the duck felt refreshed and happy and it was ready for its next adventure!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to sit under a big tree near his house. One day, while he was sitting, he saw a girl named Sue. Sue was very careful with her toys.

Tim and Sue became friends and decided to play together. They had many toys, like cars and dolls. They thought it would be fun to trade their toys with each other. Tim gave Sue a red car, and Sue gave Tim a pretty doll.

They played for hours, being careful not to break their new toys. They were so happy that they decided to trade toys every week. Tim and Sue learned that sharing and being careful with their things made them the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Jim. He was three years old and loved to speed around! 
One day, Jim was playing outside and saw a green school. He became fascinated with it. He asked his mom if he could go inside, and she said yes.

So Jim grabbed his bike and began to speed towards the school. When he arrived he was in awe of how green the school was. He even saw some trees and grass outside. He couldn't believe it! 

Jim explored the school, looking at all the classrooms and the playground. Everywhere he looked was green. Then he came across a big playground. He jumped onto the swing and started to swing as fast as he could, speeding around and around. 

Jim had so much fun playing at the green school, and raced home on his bike when it was time. 
He couldn't wait to come back again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat. He ate regular food like apples and bananas. He also liked to play with his toy switch. The switch was red and blue, and it made him happy.

One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He took his switch with him. They played on the swings and the slide. Tim got hungry and wanted to eat. His mom gave him a regular sandwich. Tim ate it all up.

After eating, Tim and his mom went home. Tim played with his switch again. It was a fun day at the park. Tim was happy because he got to eat and play with his switch. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a busy rabbit. His name was Bounce. Bounce was always running around. He was always very busy.

One day, Bounce wanted to get some grapes. He hopped off to the grocery store. He was so busy that he forgot to bring any money with him.

Bounce looked around the store. He saw a big jar of grapes. He was so excited! He wanted to snap them up right away.

Bounce asked the shopkeeper, "Can I have some grapes, please?"

The shopkeeper said, "I'm sorry, Bounce, you need to pay for them first."

Bounce was very sad. He had no money. He wanted to snap up those grapes so badly! He went outside and cried.

Just then, his friend Rabbit came along. Rabbit had heard what had happened. He said, "Don't worry, Bounce. I have enough money for the grapes. Let's go back inside and snap them up!"

Bounce was so happy. He and Rabbit hopped back into the store and bought all the grapes. They were so happy to have the grapes that they munched a few right away. Yum!

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big leather ball that their dad gave them. They liked to kick the ball, throw the ball, and roll the ball.

One day, their mom said, "It's time for your nap, Sara and Ben. You need to rest and grow." Sara and Ben did not want to nap. They wanted to play with their leather ball. They said, "No, mom, we are not tired. We want to play more."

Their mom was polite and patient. She said, "I know you love your ball, but you also need to sleep. How about this? You can take your ball with you to your bed, and I will read you a story. Then you can nap with your ball."

Sara and Ben thought about it. They liked stories, and they liked their ball. They agreed to go to their bed with their ball. Their mom read them a story about a brave lion who also liked to nap. Sara and Ben listened to the story and cuddled with their ball. Soon, they fell asleep.

Their mom smiled and kissed them. She was proud of them for being polite and listening to her. She knew they would wake up happy and ready to play again. She also knew they learned a lesson: napping is good for you and your ball.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jacky. She was three years old and very excited about her new big girl job - serving. Every morning Jacky woke up early and checked to see that her body was ready to serve.

One day, Jacky's mother said to her, "Jacky, today you will be helping to serve food in the garden. Are you ready?"

Jacky was so happy that she shouted, "Yes, Mommy. I'm ready to serve!"

Jacky put on her bright blue dress and checked once more to make sure her body was ready. She looked in the mirror and said, "Yep, I'm ready!"

Jacky got to the garden and started helping to serve delicious treats. She felt so proud that she was helping to serve. 

At the end of the day, Jacky said farewell to the guests with a big smile on her face, proud to have served in the garden.

Sara liked to play with her teddy bear. She called him Brownie, because he was brown and soft. She always took him with her to bed, and squeezed him tight when she was scared or sad.

One day, Sara's mom said they had to move to a new house. Sara was not happy. She did not want to leave her room, her friends, and her toys. She packed Brownie in a big box, and hugged him goodbye.

In the new house, Sara felt lonely and lost. She did not know anyone, and the rooms were cold and empty. She missed Brownie a lot. She asked her mom where he was, but her mom said they had many boxes, and she did not know which one had Brownie.

Sara looked for Brownie in every box, but she could not find him. She cried and cried, and wished she could squeeze him again. She felt very poor without her teddy bear.

One night, Sara heard a soft sound from under her bed. She looked, and saw a brown furry thing. She reached for it, and felt a familiar pattern. It was Brownie! He had fallen out of the box, and hidden under the bed. Sara was so happy, she pulled him out and squeezed him hard. She kissed him and said, "I love you, Brownie. You are my best friend. I am not poor anymore." She smiled, and fell asleep with Brownie in her arms.

Once upon a time, there was a young prince who wanted to go on an adventure. He decided the best way to start his adventure was to march. He marched and marched and marched. He went through a big forest, over a tall mountain and through a wide sea. Everywhere he went, the young prince found a way to have adventures. 

He went on a hot air balloon ride and saw a giant rainbow in the sky. He stopped to help a friendly squirrel find some nuts. He even had a picnic with a group of butterflies. Everywhere the young prince marched, he had wonderful adventures. 

As the day grew to night, the young prince marched back home. He thought of all the amazing things he saw, and was happy and content. He was also ready to go on another adventure the next day. So, the young prince continued to march his way through life, looking for new adventures every day.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to make some food. They saw a box of macaroni and cheese in the cupboard. They liked macaroni and cheese.

They put some water in a big pot and turned on the stove. They waited for the water to boil. Then they poured the macaroni in the pot. They stirred the macaroni with a big spoon.

They looked at the cheese packet. It was yellow and powdery. They opened it and smelled it. It smelled bad. Very bad. They made a face.

"Yuck! This cheese is bad!" Lily said.

"Let's throw it away and use some other cheese," Tom said.

They found some cheese slices in the fridge. They tore them into small pieces and put them in a bowl. They put the bowl in the microwave and pressed some buttons. The cheese melted and became gooey.

They drained the macaroni and put it back in the pot. They poured the melted cheese over the macaroni. They stirred it well. It looked yummy.

They scooped some macaroni and cheese into two plates. They sat at the table and ate. They smiled.

"This is good!" Lily said.

"Much better than the bad cheese!" Tom said.

They finished their food and licked their spoons. They were happy. They had made some food. They liked macaroni and cheese.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly crystal. It was all alone in a dark cave. The crystal wanted to be pretty, but it was too scared to leave the cave. 

One day, an explorer saw the crystal in the cave and decided to taste it. The explorer licked the crystal and it tasted sweet! He was so happy about his discovery that he took the crystal home with him.

Once he got home, the explorer looked closely at the crystal. It sparkled and shone in the sunlight! The explorer knew the crystal was meant to be beautiful.

The explorer kept the crystal safe, and soon, the ugly crystal had become a beautiful crystal. It was now too valuable to stay in the explorer's home and he decided to take it to market.

When the crystal reached the market, everyone was amazed by its beauty. People admired the crystal and paid lots of money for it.

The ugly crystal was now a beautiful and valuable crystal, thanks to the explorer!

Lily and Ben were playing knights and dragons in the garden. Lily had a wooden sword and a cardboard shield. Ben had a green scarf and a plastic horn. They ran around the trees and bushes, pretending to fight and roar.

Lily saw a big rock and climbed on top of it. She waved her sword and shouted, "I am the mighty knight! I will defeat the dragon and win the victory!" Ben ran towards her and blew his horn. He said, "You cannot stop me! I am the fiercest dragon in the land!"

They pretended to clash and wrestle on the rock. Lily tried to hit Ben with her sword, but he dodged and bit her shield. Ben tried to knock Lily off the rock, but she held on and kicked his horn. They laughed and giggled as they played.

Then they heard their mom calling them for lunch. They stopped and looked at each other. They said, "Who won the game?" They thought for a moment. Then they smiled and said, "We both did! We had fun and we are friends!"

They jumped off the rock and ran to the house. They hugged and said, "You are a mighty knight and you are a fierce dragon!" They washed their hands and sat down to eat. They told their mom about their adventure and asked if they could play again after lunch. Their mom said, "Yes, you can. I am proud of you both!"
