"Where do you come from?" asked the small fish.

"I come from a place far away," answered the large fish. "I take a bath in the tide every day. Do you do the same?"

The small fish nodded. "It feels nice to bathe in the warm tide," he said.

The larger fish smiled. "Yes, it's very nice indeed," he said. "It makes me feel independent and free. I'm glad to meet you, small fish."

The small fish smiled in return. From that day on, they enjoyed swimming and bathing in the tide together.

Molly had a view of the sea from outside her house. Each day she liked to look out and watch the waves, feeling like she was part of it.

One day, Molly decided she wanted to do something creative with the view. She went to fetch the paper and some markers from inside the house.

She sat down with the paper and started to draw a picture of the view. Then she carefully folded it three times and gave it to her daddy.

Daddy was so happy with her creative work and smiled as he opened it. He said that it was the most beautiful view in the world! Molly was super proud of herself and hugged Daddy - she was so very pleased.

Once there was a shy pick. He liked to put things in his pocket. One day he saw something shiny on the ground. He wanted to put it in his pocket but was too shy to pick it up.

Suddenly a voice called out to him, "Go ahead and pick it up! It's yours!"

The pick looked up and saw an owl who was friendly and kind. So he reached down and put his small, shy hand on the shiny object. He pulled it out of the dirt and put it safely in his pocket.

"Thank you!" he said to the owl with a smile on his face "I was too shy to pick it up!"

The owl smiled and said, "That's ok! We are all shy sometimes!" The pick nodded and thanked him again before walking away with the shiny object in his pocket.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big chocolate cake to share with her friends. But when she tried to cut it, the cake split into two pieces. Lily was sad because she wanted to give her friends big slices of cake.

Her friends said they could stay and wait for her to fix the cake. Lily was happy they were patient with her. She tried to put the two pieces back together, but it didn't work. Then she had an idea. She took the two pieces and put them on top of each other, making a tall cake. Her friends were amazed and happy to have a big slice of cake. They all had a fun time together.

Jack enjoyed exploring the park very early in the morning. Every morning, he put on his favourite red shirt and ran out the door. Today Jack was excited to see the birds gathering early in the sun.

He stopped to look at a squirrel with a big bushy tail. It was so cute! From behind him, Jack heard a voice.

"Good morning, Jack," said the voice. He turned around and saw his friend Sarah. 

'Hi Sarah," said Jack, smiling. 

"Isn't it a hot morning?" asked Sarah.

"Yes! I don't want to miss it," said Jack.

They spent the morning walking and playing together. They chased each other around the trees and laughed and had so much fun. Jack smiled as he looked up at the hot sun.

Jack was sad when it was time to go home. He already missed the morning at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a crab who lived in a big, wide ocean. He wanted to explore and see all the different parts of the ocean!

The crab was urged to leave his home and explore. He was a very careful little crab, so he started slowly. He wanted to look around and take it one step at a time.

He looked in nooks and crevices and found all kinds of things! He found bright and colourful coral, and lots of friendly fish! He was having so much fun, exploring all the different parts of the ocean.

Soon, he had seen so many things. He was so happy, he started to do a crab dance! He was so careful when exploring, and he made lots of new friends!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. Tom liked to go fast. He enjoyed running and playing so he would speed around everywhere.

One day Tom decided he wanted to build something. He looked around and discovered a box filled with bricks. The bricks were red, blue and yellow and Tom thought they looked really interesting.

Tom was delighted. He quickly started to stack the bricks and before long he had built a tower. He was so proud!

Tom stepped back and admired his work. Then he put his foot down, took a deep breath and speed off round the garden. He laughed with delight.

The end!

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But today they want to do something new. They want to crawl under the bed.

"Come on, Ben, let's crawl under the bed. Maybe we can find something fun," Lily says.

"OK, Lily, let's go. But be careful. It is dark and dusty under the bed," Ben says.

They crawl under the bed. They see some old shoes, a ball, a hat and a sock. The sock is blue and has a hole. Lily picks up the sock.

"Look, Ben, I found a sock. It is not a good sock. It has a hole. But maybe it is useful for something," Lily says.

"What can you do with a holey sock, Lily? It is not good for your feet. It is not good for anything," Ben says.

Lily thinks for a moment. Then she has an idea. She puts the sock on her hand. She makes the sock talk.

"Hello, Ben. I am a sock puppet. I am not a holey sock. I am a funny sock. I can make you laugh," Lily says with a funny voice.

Ben laughs. He thinks Lily is clever. He wants to play with the sock puppet too. He looks for another sock under the bed.

"Hello, Lily. I am another sock puppet. I am not a funny sock. I am a silly sock. I can make you giggle," Ben says with a silly voice.

Lily giggles. She thinks Ben is funny. She plays with the silly sock too. They have fun with their sock puppets. They forget they are under the bed. They are happy. They are twins.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was called Jack and the other was called David. Jack loved basketballs and David loved playing basketball.

Every day Jack and David would meet in the park. Jack would proudly show David his new basketball. It was round and red and very expensive.

One day, David whispered to Jack. He said he had something to show him. David took out a key and said he could open the secret basketball court just for them. Jack was so excited that he smiled from ear to ear.

Jack and David ran to the secret basketball court. They spent the entire day playing with their basketballs. They laughed, giggled and had lots of fun.

At the end of the day, Jack whispered to David that this was the best day ever.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big cake on the table. It smelled good and looked yummy. They wanted to eat some.

"Can we have some cake, please?" Lily asked Mom.

"Not now, sweetie. The cake is for later. It is Grandma's birthday cake. We have to wait for Grandma to come," Mom said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They went back to playing. But they still looked at the cake. It had pink frosting and sprinkles. They wished they could have a bite.

Tom had an idea. He whispered to Lily. "Let's push the chair to the table. Then we can climb up and get some cake. Mom won't see us. She is busy in the other room."

Lily thought for a moment. She was scared. What if Mom found out? What if they made a mess? What if they got in trouble? But she also wanted some cake. It looked so good.

"OK, let's do it. But be quiet and quick," she said.

They pushed the chair to the table. They climbed up. They reached for the cake. They took a big chunk each. They smiled. They ate the cake. It was delicious.

But then they heard a noise. It was Mom. She was coming back to the kitchen. She saw them on the chair. She saw the cake. She saw their faces. She was angry.

"Lily and Tom! What have you done? You ruined the cake! You were naughty! You have to say sorry to Grandma! And no more cake for you today!" she shouted.

Lily and Tom felt bad. They knew they did wrong. They got down from the chair. They said sorry to Mom. They said sorry to Grandma. They hugged them. They learned their lesson. They never pushed the chair to the cake again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Max and Ben. They were very happy and they always played together. 

One day, they wanted to perform a very special show. Max thought it would be fun to make a sandwich to share with the audience during the show. So they raced to the kitchen to make one.

But they soon got very frustrated because they couldn't figure out how to make the sandwich. Max kept putting way too much pepper on it and Ben kept messing up the cheese. 

Finally, after a few tries, they managed to make a delicious sandwich together. Everyone was very happy, Max and Ben performed a wonderful show and everyone was treated to a yummy sandwich!

Once upon a time, there was a little prince. He lived in a big castle. The prince loved to talk to everyone he met. He wanted to learn new things.

One day, the prince was walking in the castle gardens. He heard a noise coming from a big open door. He was curious and walked inside. In the doorway, he saw a little mouse. The mouse was squeaking and talking.

The prince was very excited. He bent down to talk to the mouse. 'Hello there! What is your name?' he asked.

The little mouse squeaked and said, 'I am Max. What is your name?'.

The prince told Max his name and said, 'Would you like to become my friend?' 

Max giggled and said, 'Yes! I would love to be your friend'. 

The prince and Max talked and talked. They talked about their days, the castle, and their adventures. They even sang silly songs together! 

The prince and Max became best friends. They played in the castle gardens and talked all day. 

The End.

Jimmy was new in town and he wanted to make friends. He saw a group of children playing and decided to join them. When Jimmy asked if he could join, the group said yes. But he didn't fit in. Everyone stared at him, and he felt uncomfortable. He tried hard to be part of the group, but it didn't work. He asked the group if everything was okay, but they just kept looking at him.

Jimmy started to feel very sad. He asked if he could still stay in the group, but the kids said no. They said he was too different and made the group uncomfortable. So, Jimmy left the group and started to walk away. He felt sad and alone.

Jimmy kept his head down and walked home. He wished he hadn't asked to join the group. He didn't feel like he belonged.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom said to her, "Lily, it's time for your nap. You need to sleep so you can have lots of energy to play later."

Lily didn't want to take a nap, but her mom insisted. So, Lily got into her bed and closed her eyes. She tried to sleep, but she couldn't. She heard a noise outside her window that sounded unusual.

Lily got out of bed and went to her window to see what was making the noise. She saw a bird sitting on a branch, singing a beautiful song. Lily thought it was so pretty that she forgot all about taking a nap.

When Lily's mom came to check on her, she saw that Lily was still awake. "Lily, why aren't you sleeping?" she asked.

Lily told her mom about the bird and how it was making an unusual noise. Her mom smiled and said, "Well, sometimes it's okay to skip a nap for something special like that." And with that, Lily went outside to play with the bird.

Once there was a boy. His name was Sam. He had a very special purple blanket. Every night Sam would wrap his blanket around himself and he would feel peaceful and happy.

One evening, Sam was snuggling up in his blanket as usual, when he noticed something strange. His blanket was glowing! Sam jumped in surprise.

"What is happening?" he said.

Suddenly, a magical fairy appeared in front of him. "Hello Sam" said the fairy.

Sam was speechless.

"I wanted to thank you," said the fairy. "Throughout your life, you have been so kind. I have come to give you a very special present: your blanket will now be magical!"

Sam felt so grateful. "Thank you!" he said.

The fairy smiled. "Enjoy your magical purple blanket," she said. Then she flew away.

From then on, the blanket kept Sam so safe, warm and peaceful. Sam was so thankful for his special gift.

Once there was a man who had a job. Every day he went to the job and worked until it was finished.

One day his job was to run. He started running but then he felt something hurt in his foot. He had to stop.

He sat down and rubbed his foot to make the hurt go away. Then he got back up and started running again. But every time he took a step his foot hurt. He had to stop again.

Suddenly he saw a friend walking towards him. The friend had a big bag. The man asked his friend what was in the bag and the friend said there was a special kind of belt in the bag.

The man put on the belt and it made the hurt go away. He was so excited he jumped up and started running. He finished his job and he was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very independent. She liked to do things all on her own. One day, she went to the airport. She felt very grown-up and even though she was a little scared, she was excited too. 

When she arrived at the airport, she saw many airplanes. She saw people talking, running and carrying suitcases. She said hello and waved to the people she saw. 

Before she knew it, she was saying goodbye to her mom and dad. She hugged them and said that she would be back soon. She thanked them for bringing her to the airport and she thanked the people who waved goodbye as she got on the plane. 

The little girl was so proud of herself for being so independent. She could not wait to tell her friends about her adventure to the airport.

One day, two siblings, Bill and Jill, had a lot of fun playing together. They played with their toys and tried out some new games. But then, they realized they had made a mistake.

They looked around and noticed they had made a mess with lots of junk everywhere. As the mess got bigger, the two siblings started to argue. Bill wanted to keep playing and said the junk was part of the game. Jill wanted to tidy up.

The two disagreed and decided to find a way to settle it. Suddenly, they heard a sound coming from the junk. It was kind of unusual, but both of them were curious, so they looked inside.

Surprisingly, they found a tiny creature living inside the junk. The creature told them that if they worked together to clean up, it would give them a reward.

The siblings agreed and tidied up the room. After they finished, the creature gave them a surprise, an unusual grant-phone. They were so pleased and never fought again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally who loved adventure. One day she heard a bell ringing far away and she wondered what it could be. She decided to go and find out.

Sally was excited and a little bit scared as she ventured away from home, but she kept going until she came to a big house with a big bell in the garden. Her heart raced as she approached the bell and saw that it was much bigger than she had thought.

Sally reached out and asked the bell, "What are you doing here?"

The bell replied, "I am here to announce the arrival of a new adventure!"

Sally was thrilled and couldn't wait to start her newest adventure! With a smile on her face, she waved goodbye to the bell and took off on her new journey with a heart full of excitement.

Once upon a time there was a little girl in a clean crib. Every night her mother would pass her a story book and read to her until she fell asleep. Then the little girl would dream about adventures and playing with her friends.

When morning came, the little girl would get out of bed and go play. She loved to visit the beach, collect shells and make castles in the sand. Sometimes she would even pass by a playground and swing on the swings.

At the end of the day, when the sun had gone to sleep, the little girl would go home to her clean crib. After eating a yummy dinner and giving her mom a hug, she would curl up in her comfy crib and be ready for the next day's adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because her family was going on vacation to the beach. She loved playing in the sand and swimming in the ocean.

The day before they left, Lily's mom asked her to help pack her suitcase. She picked out her favorite little dress and some matching sandals. "These will be perfect for the beach," said Lily.

When they arrived at the beach, Lily ran straight to the sand and started building a sandcastle. Suddenly, she saw a little boy who was also building a sandcastle. "Do you want to play together?" asked Lily. The little boy nodded and they started playing together.

As they were playing, the little boy's mom came over and said, "Thank you for playing with my son. He's been feeling a little lonely on this vacation." Lily smiled and said, "No problem! We're having so much fun together." From that day on, Lily and the little boy played together every day on their vacation, and they became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big water bottle that she loved to carry with her everywhere. One day, she noticed that her water bottle was very heavy and she couldn't carry it anymore. 

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, my water bottle is too heavy. Can you help me carry it?" 

Her mom replied, "Lily, you don't need to carry such a heavy water bottle. You can drink from a smaller one that is easier for you to carry." 

Lily understood what her mom said and went to get a smaller water bottle. As she was pouring water into the new bottle, she noticed that her old water bottle had a leak. She told her mom about it and her mom said, "Lily, it's important to take care of our things. We need to fix the leak so we don't waste water." 

Lily learned that it's important to take care of her things and to only carry what she needs.

Lily was a thoughtful girl who liked to ask questions. She always raised her hand in class when she wanted to say something. One day, she learned about eyes and how they help us see. She was very curious about how eyes work.

She raised her hand and asked her teacher, "How do we see colors with our eyes?" The teacher smiled and explained that our eyes have tiny parts called cones that can sense different colors of light. She showed Lily a picture of a rainbow and pointed to the colors.

Lily nodded and looked at the picture. She raised her hand again and asked, "How do we see shapes with our eyes?" The teacher said that our eyes also have tiny parts called rods that can sense light and dark. She showed Lily a picture of a circle and a square and said that our eyes can tell the difference between them.

Lily smiled and looked at the picture. She raised her hand one more time and asked, "How do we see dreams with our eyes?" The teacher laughed and said that dreams are not really seen with our eyes, but with our minds. She said that when we sleep, our minds make up stories and images that we can remember when we wake up.

Lily was amazed and said, "Wow, our eyes and our minds are very smart!" The teacher agreed and said, "Yes, they are, and so are you, Lily. You are a very thoughtful and curious girl." Lily felt happy and proud. She thanked her teacher and gave her a hug. She couldn't wait to go home and tell her mom and dad about what she learned.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. Sally had two ears on either side of her head, but one of her ears was bigger and rounder than the other. This made her ear rare. 

One day, Sally was playing in the backyard when she heard something rustling in the bushes. "Who's there?" Sally shouted. 

"It's me," answered a voice from within the bushes. "My name is Red Bird!"

Sally was surprised to find a talking bird in her backyard. Red Bird asked Sally, "Do you want to play with me?"

Sally smiled and said, "Yes!"

The two of them played many different games together. They played tag, hide and seek, and they talked and laughed. Eventually, it was time for Sally to go home. 

As Sally walked away, Red Bird said sadly, "Goodbye Sally. I will miss you." 

Sally turned around and smiled. "I will miss you too," she said. And with that, Sally waved goodbye and went home.

There was once a mighty knight. He wore a shiny metal armour and carried a huge sword. He rode a strong horse and was always very brave.

One day, the knight went on a journey. He felt the hot heat of the day, so he took off his armour and rode faster. But then he saw something that made him frown.

It was a dragon! The dragon had glossy scales and breathed fire. The knight knew he wouldn't be able to defeat the dragon on his own. He then thought of a plan.

He reached for his knight's shield and held it up against the dragon's fiery breath. The shield protected the knight from the heat of the dragon's flames.

The brave knight then brandished his sword. He was successful and the dragon flew away. The knight was so proud of his mighty victory!

One day, a farmer and his wife went to the market to sell their eggs and milk. They were glad because they worked hard and had many animals on their farm. They loved each other very much and always kissed before they left the house.

At the market, they met a man who said he wanted to buy all their eggs and milk. He said he would pay them a lot of money and give them a big bag of candy. The farmer and his wife were happy and agreed to sell him their eggs and milk. They did not know that the man was bad and wanted to trick them.

The man gave them a big bag of candy, but it was not real candy. It was rocks wrapped in shiny paper. He took their eggs and milk and ran away. The farmer and his wife opened the bag and saw the rocks. They were sad and angry. They had no money and no food for their animals.

They went back to their farm, but they found that their animals were gone. The bad man had come to their farm and stolen their animals while they were at the market. He had left a note that said: "Thank you for the eggs, milk and animals. I hope you enjoy your candy. Ha ha ha!"

The farmer and his wife cried and hugged each other. They had nothing left. They wished they had never met the bad man. They wished they had never gone to the market. They wished they had stayed at home and kissed.

Once there was a playful little boy named Patrick. He loved to play games and go on adventures every day. One day he was playing tag with his friends in the park when suddenly the sky went dark and it started to rain. 

Patrick began to worry and said to his friends, "What shall we do now?" His friends replied, "Let's run home before we get too wet."

So they ran back to Patrick's house and when they got there they saw that the lights were on. His mom was in the kitchen making dinner. Patrick was so relieved that he ran up to her and hugged her. 

His mom said, "Surprise! I'm having a magical dinner for us tonight." Patrick was so excited that he could barely contain himself!

The dinner was delicious and afterwards the kids decided to go play a board game. Patrick wanted to play the game so badly that he accidentally knocked the pieces off the table. Everyone gasped but then his mom said, "It's okay Patrick, don't worry. We can set it up again." 

When the game was set up, Patrick started to play and he was so happy. Suddenly, something scary happened. A hand came out of the board game and it started to strike at Patrick. He screamed and backed up quickly. 

His mom said, "It's okay Patrick, it's just a nightmare. Nightmares can't hurt you." 

Patrick

Once upon a time, there was a child who loved making things. This child had a box of things to play with, which included clay. It was large, red clay. 

One day, the child got an idea. He took some of the large clay and rolled it into a ball. He then flattened the clay so it was thin. It looked like a pizza! The child smiled and used his hands to make a little house out of the clay.

He carefully added tiny pieces to the big clay house. He added a door, windows, a roof and even a chimney! It looked so cool.

The child was so proud of his clay house. He had lots of fun including making it!

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play in the garden. They saw many flowers, bugs and birds there. One day, they found a small plant with green leaves and a nice smell. Lila said, "This is a herb. My mom uses herbs to cook. She says they are good for you." Tom said, "Can we pick some and take them home?" Lila said, "No, we can't. If we pick them, they will die. We have to support them and let them grow."

They decided to water the herb and make a fence around it with sticks. They came back every day to check on it and talk to it. They named it Herb. Herb grew bigger and stronger and had more leaves. Lila and Tom were happy and proud of their herb.

One day, they saw a rabbit near the fence. The rabbit was hungry and wanted to eat the herb. Lila and Tom ran to the fence and shouted, "Go away, rabbit! This is our herb. You can't have it." The rabbit was scared and ran away. Lila and Tom hugged each other and said, "We saved Herb. We are good friends to Herb and to each other."

The moral of the story is: We should support and protect the things we care about and share them with our friends.

Tim and Mia like to play in the park. They run and jump and laugh. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to climb the tree.

"Can we climb the tree, please?" Tim asks Mia.

"Yes, let's climb the tree. It looks fun and cool," Mia says.

They hold hands and walk to the tree. They find a low branch and pull themselves up. They climb higher and higher. They feel the wind and the sun on their faces. They see the birds and the clouds. They are happy.

"Look, I can see our house from here!" Tim shouts.

"Wow, me too! And I can see the slide and the swings!" Mia shouts.

They wave to each other and smile. They are proud of themselves. They are brave and strong. They love the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and he was always very happy.

One day, Joe wanted to go on a big adventure. He decided to take a trip to the tip. Joe was so excited, but he was a little worried too. He was scared that the trip might be a bit boring.

So Joe decided to ask his mum for help. His mum gave him a big bag full of fun toys and she showed him the best way to get to the tip.

When Joe arrived, he was delighted to see so many fun things. There were old toys to play with and piles of cards to make. Joe played there all day and forgot all about his worries. It was the best day of his life!

Mary was a girl who loved to soar. She loved to run, jump and feel the warm breeze on her cheeks. Every day she would go outside, run and jump until she could no longer see the ground.

One day, Mary was in the park and saw a big shiny train. It was so colorful, and she wanted to feel the wind on her face. So Mary ran up the hill and joined the train. She was so excited to soar on the train.

The train took Mary around the park and she could feel the warm air going past her. She did not feel like she was running, but more like she was flying! She waved to the other people at the park, and they waved back.

When the train stopped, Mary hopped off and ran all the way home. From that day on, Mary felt like she could soar anywhere.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Timmy. Timmy was three years old.

One day Timmy went outside to play. He saw a big hill and decided to climb it. He was so happy to get to the top!

But then Timmy saw a creek. The creek was so deep, he thought he could never cross it. But then he noticed a log. Timmy decided to climb along the log. He was careful not to fall in the creek.

At last Timmy made it across the creek! When he looked back, he felt very successful. He had climbed the hill and crossed the creek. He was so proud of himself.

Timmy smiled and said, " I did it! I'm the best climber ever!"

Once upon a time there was a girl who was ugly. She was sad all the time. Her friends noticed and one day asked her why she was so unhappy. She said she felt ugly.

Her friends said they could help. They gave her some makeup and showed her how to use it. She put it on and looked in the mirror. She smiled because she looked so much better!

She kept using the makeup every day and felt much happier. She was no longer ugly, she looked beautiful! But one day she ran out of makeup. She felt ugly again and she needed more. 

So she went back to her friends for help and asked if they could get her some more makeup. Her friends said yes and made her some more. She put it on and felt happy again!

From then on, the girl never felt ugly again. She knew she could always get more makeup if she needed it, and she lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl. She wanted to go on an adventure and so she decided to march through the forest. As she marched, she kept her eyes open for something special.

Soon, she found something amazing - a big tasty pick! She was so excited and quickly picked it up. She hugged the pick tightly and kept marching.

She followed her nose and found a field full of very tasty strawberries. She couldn't believe her luck! She happily picked the strawberries, filling her basket with them.

After a long time of marching and picking, the girl got very tired. But she had a basket full of tasty strawberries and was very happy. She marched back home, holding the pick tightly.

The girl hugged her pick and the basket of strawberries together. She knew she had been on a great adventure. From then on, she remembered to always keep her eyes open for something special, just like her march through the forest!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to paint. Her mommy gave her a new paint set. Lily was very happy. She knew something yummy was coming.

One day, Lily painted a big cake. It was a yummy cake with pink and blue. She showed her mommy. Her mommy smiled and said, "Wait until tomorrow." Lily was excited.

The next day, Lily saw a big box. She opened it. Inside was a real yummy cake! It looked just like her paint. Her mommy replaced the paint with a real cake. Lily and her mommy laughed and ate the yummy cake. They were very happy.

One sunny day, a pretty boat was on the water. The boat was red and blue. A girl named Lily and her dog, Spot, were on the boat. They liked to play and have fun together.

Lily saw a big fish jump out of the water. She said, "Wow, Spot! Did you see that big fish?" Spot barked and wagged his tail. They both laughed and clapped their hands.

Lily picked up a hose and started to spray water. She sprayed the water on the boat and on Spot. Spot jumped and barked, trying to catch the water. They played and sprayed water until the sun went down. Then, they went home, happy and wet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her pink scarf everywhere she went. One day, Lily was playing with her friends when she accidentally broke her friend's toy. Her friend was very sad and started to cry.

Lily felt bad and said, "I'm sorry I broke your toy. Please forgive me." 

Her friend stopped crying and smiled. "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you," she said cheerfully. 

Lily was so happy that her friend forgave her. She gave her friend a big hug and they continued playing together. From that day on, Lily made sure to be careful with her friend's toys and they remained cheerful friends.

Dave was very sad because his treehouse had fallen down. Tears rolled down his cheeks and he felt lost. 

His mom came over and hugged him. She said, "It's okay to be sad, Dave. We will start building a new one soon." 

Dave was excited at this idea and he quickly wiped away his tears. He said, "Yay! I can't wait to get going!" 

But later that night, Dave looked out his window and saw the dark sky. He started to regret wanting to build a new treehouse. It would take lots of work and he wasn't sure he could do it. 

Dave's mom saw him looking out the window. She said, "What's wrong, Dave?"

He said, "I am scared. I want to make a new treehouse, but it will take a long time. I regret bringing it up." 

His mom smiled and said, "Come, Dave. We can do it together. Building a treehouse will be so much fun!" 

Dave smiled and felt better. He was excited to start the project with his mom!

Once there was a boy who was walking to the park. He was so excited because he had a lollipop in his pocket. On the way he saw a little bird in a tree. The boy wanted to give it a lollipop, so he took aim and shoot. But it missed, and the bird flew away.

Then the boy went to the park. He found a swing and sat on it. He took a big lick of his lollipop and suddenly, he started to shoot it. The lollipop flew into the sky, and it looked so magical! But then he saw something bad.

A mean man was shooting at a rabbit with a gun. He was so stupid. The boy got so angry. He wanted to stop the man, so he shouted and told him to stop. The man didn't listen, and he kept shooting.

The boy was really scared, but then he had a great idea. He quickly ran over, grabbed the man's gun, and threw the lollipop at him. He hit the man, and the man stopped shooting. Thankfully, the rabbit was safe!

Tim and Liz liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of toys in their room. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a scale. It had a round thing that could spin and show numbers. Tim and Liz did not know what the numbers meant, but they liked to spin the round thing.

They took the scale to the living room and put it on the floor. They took turns to stand on the scale and spin the round thing. They laughed when the numbers changed. They did not see their mom come in. She was worried when she saw them playing with the scale. She knew the scale was not a toy. It was a special scale that their dad used for his work. It was very expensive and delicate.

She shouted at Tim and Liz to stop playing with the scale. She ran to the scale and tried to take it away from them. But Tim and Liz did not want to give up their toy. They pulled the scale from their mom. They pulled too hard. The scale broke. The round thing fell off and the numbers stopped. The scale was ruined.

Their mom was very angry and sad. She scolded Tim and Liz for breaking the scale. She told them they had to go to their room and stay there. She said they had to pay for the scale with their allowance. She said they had no more toys to play with. Tim and Liz cried. They were sorry for breaking the scale. They wished they had not played with it. They wished they had listened to their mom. They had no fun. They had a bad day.

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was 3 years old and loved playing with mixers. One day, Mia's mum called her into the kitchen. When she arrived, she saw a huge, clean mixer on the counter. 

"Look, Mia," said her mum. "This mixer is for you!" 

Mia's eyes lit up with excitement and she gave her mum a big hug. "Thank you, mum," she replied.

Mia and her mum played together all day with the mixer. They made fruit smoothies, delicious cakes and all kinds of tasty treats. They laughed and had so much fun!

When it was time to go, Mia gave her mum a big hug and said cheerfully,"Goodbye! See you tomorrow!"

Mia's mum smiled and gently replied, "Goodbye, sweetheart. I'll see you then!"

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with blocks. They made many buildings with their blocks, like houses, towers, and castles. They were very proud of their buildings and showed them to their mom and dad.

One day, a new boy came to their playgroup. His name was Max and he had big teeth. He saw Ben and Lily's buildings and wanted to play with them too. But he did not ask nicely. He just grabbed some blocks and started to eat them.

"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted. "Those are our blocks! You can't eat them!"

"Yes, I can!" Max said. "They are yummy and crunchy. And I am hungry!"

Lily was scared of Max and his big teeth. She ran to their mom and told her what Max was doing. Mom came over and saw Max eating the blocks.

"Max, that is not nice. You can't eat other people's toys. And blocks are not food. They can hurt your teeth and your tummy. You need to say sorry to Ben and Lily and give them back their blocks."

Max looked at mom and felt ashamed. He realized he was being rude and mean. He spit out the blocks and said sorry to Ben and Lily.

"I'm sorry, Ben and Lily. I was wrong to eat your blocks. Can I play with you?"

Ben and Lily were kind and forgiving. They said yes and showed Max how to make buildings with the blocks. They taught him how to share and cooperate. Max learned how to play nicely and made new friends.

The moral of the story is: Don't eat other people's toys. Be polite and respectful. And you will have more fun and friends.

Once upon a time there was a crab named Bob. He lived in a big rock by the sea. One day, Bob was walking along the beach and he saw a little girl playing. The girl looked very happy, so Bob decided to greet her.

Bob said, "Hello!" 
The girl smiled and said, "Hi there!" 

Bob asked, "What are you doing?" 
The girl said, "I'm looking for seashells. They are so pretty, and sweet too!" 

Then Bob said, "I know of a place that has lots of seashells, right near my rock home. Would you like to come and see?" 
The girl was very excited, so she said, "Yes please!" 

So Bob and the girl went to Bob's rock home. Sure enough, the beach was full of pretty and sweet seashells. The girl picked up all the shells she could see and thanked Bob for finding them. 

Bob said, "You're welcome! I'm glad you're happy." 
The girl smiled and gave Bob a big hug. 

They said goodbye and the girl ran off, clutching her shell collection close to her heart. Bob watched her go, feeling a great sense of joy. He was glad he could help make someone so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Yesterday, she went to the store with her mom. She saw a toy she really wanted, but her mom said they didn't have enough money to buy it. 

As they were leaving the store, they met a kind old man who gifted Lily a shiny coin. Lily was so happy and thanked the man.

One night, a little girl was scared and decided to go look for her favorite toy. She grabbed her flashlight and turned it on. The bright light illuminated the dark room. She couldn't find her toy anywhere! She started to get confused and couldn't figure out where it was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat yummy food, but one day she noticed that the fridge was empty. So, she went to the store with her mommy to buy some food. Once upon a time there was a pig. She was tired after a long day and wanted to lay down her head. She wandered over to the grassy field, where she saw a folder. It looked very filthy, so she decided to clean it up.

The pig got to work and slowly she got the folder nice and clean. She smiled and her spirits lifted. She lay the folder down in the grass and curled up for a nap.

Soon, a little bird flew down and saw the folder. It was intrigued and started chirping cheerfully. The pig woke up with a smile. She watched as the bird hopped onto the folder and played around with it. It even sang a merry tune!

The pig watched with happiness as the bird played and sang until it was time for them to go home. The pig said goodbye to the bird and picked up the now clean folder and headed off with a smile.

Sammy was feeling hungry and he wanted something to eat. He went to the kitchen where he saw his mom holding a long, hard celery.

"What are you doing with the celery, Mommy?" asked Sammy.

"I am going to make a snack for you," she said with a smile.

Mommy opened the fridge and came out with some cheese. She cut it into small pieces and put them on the celery. She then gave it to Sammy. 

"Thank you, Mommy!" he said happily. 

He held the celery and took a big bite. He smiled as he chewed. The celery was crunchy and the cheese was soft and delicious. 

"Yum!" yelled Sammy. 

He ate the whole celery and asked for more. Mommy was happy to see him enjoying the snack.

Once upon a time, there was a wise man who loved mysteries. He touched many strange things as he searched for answers. One day, he touched a big rock in the woods and a loud noise came out. The man was scared, so he ran away.

The wise man kept searching, but soon he forgot all about the big rock. He spent weeks searching for new mysteries. He thought he was so clever, but soon he found out he was wrong.

One day, he touched something he shouldn't have touched. It was too late, because all the mysterious things in his life had gone. He looked around, but he couldn't find anymore mysteries. He had touched one too many and it was a bad mistake.

The wise man was sad and lonely, knowing he would never find the mysteries he wanted. He had never felt so foolish in all his life. But there is a lesson in this story: never touch the things that are mysterious!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was an adventurous boy who liked to play outside. One day, Tim found an axe in his yard. He didn't know what it was for, but he thought it looked fun.

Tim saw a big tree close to his house. He wanted to try the axe on the tree. As he walked to the tree, his friend Sue came over. "What are you doing?" Sue asked. "I found this axe and want to try it on the tree," Tim said. Sue thought it was a bad idea, but Tim didn't listen.

Tim started to cut the tree with the axe. But he didn't know how to use it, and he hurt himself. Tim cried and his mom came running. She took the axe away and said, "You should never play with things you don't know about." Tim learned that being too adventurous can be dangerous, and it's important to listen to others when they try to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, he went outside to play with his friend, Sally.

Sally said, "I want to win this race!" Timmy replied, "I don't mind if you win, as long as we have fun." They started racing their toy cars down the hill. Sally's car was faster, and she won the race.

Timmy felt a little bitter about losing, but Sally said, "Don't worry, we can race again and again. Winning is not important, having fun with our friends is." Timmy smiled and agreed, and they continued to play together happily.

Once upon a time there was an original earth full of bows. No one knew how or why! Every day, people would find peculiar bows that seemed to sprout out of the earth. 

The bows seemed to have special powers. Every time someone touched one, they would start to glow. Some people thought the bows were magical! 

One day, a three-year-old child discovered a bow. She touched it and immediately felt a great power. She then began to bow to the earth, thanking it for the original bow.  

The little girl's bows were seen by every one in the land. Word of the magical bows quickly spread. Everyone was in awe of the little girl and the mysterious bows. 

To this day, the original earth still looks up to the little girl and her bows. Whenever a new bow appears, people are reminded of the power the little girl and the earth hold.

One day, a girl named Sue had to take a test called an exam. She was very scared. Her mom told her, "Don't worry, just mix all the things you learned and do your best." Sue thought that was a good idea. She would try to mix everything she learned to do well on the exam.

On the day of the exam, Sue saw her friend Tom. He was sad because he didn't study. He said, "Sue, I don't know what to do. I didn't study and now the exam will be very hard." Sue told Tom, "Just try to mix everything you remember and you might do okay."

During the exam, Sue tried to mix all her learning. She saw a question with thick lines. She remembered her mom said thick lines are big. So she knew the answer. Tom tried to mix his learning too, but it was hard because he didn't study.

After the exam, Sue and Tom talked. Sue said, "I did my best to mix all my learning. I think I did okay." Tom said, "I tried to mix my learning too, but it was hard. Next time, I will study like you."

Sue and Tom learned that it is important to study and mix their learning. They promised to help each other study for the next exam. They knew they could do it if they worked together.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were racing. Ben had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They had fun together.

But then Ben's car stopped moving. He tried to push it, but it did not work. He was sad and angry. He looked at Lily's car and saw that it was still moving. He wanted her car.

He said to Lily, "Give me your car. My car is broken. You have a good car. I want it."

Lily said, "No, Ben. This is my car. You have your own car. You cannot take my car. That is rude."

Ben did not listen. He grabbed Lily's car and pulled it away from her. Lily cried and tried to get it back. They fought over the car.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw Ben and Lily fighting. She was not happy. She said, "Ben, Lily, what are you doing? Why are you fighting over a toy car?"

Ben said, "Mom, my car is broken. I want Lily's car. She has a good car."

Mom said, "Ben, that is not nice. You cannot take Lily's car without asking. That is rude. You have to share and be kind. Maybe your car is not broken. Maybe it just needs a new battery."

Mom took Ben's car and opened the back. She took out the old battery and put in a new one. She closed the back and gave the car to Ben. She said, "Here, Ben. Try your car now. Maybe it will work."

Ben pushed the car and it started moving. He was happy. He said, "Wow, Mom. You fixed my car. Thank you, Mom. You are smart."

Mom said, "You're welcome, Ben. I'm glad your car works. But you still have to say sorry to Lily. You hurt her feelings when you took her car. That was rude."

Ben looked at Lily. She was still crying and holding her car. He felt bad. He said, "Sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should not have taken your car. Can we be friends again?"

Lily looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She said, "Okay, Ben. I forgive you. We can be friends again. Do you want to play with me?"

Ben said, "Yes, Lily. I want to play with you. Can I show you my car? It has a new battery. It is fast."

Lily said, "Sure, Ben. You can show me your car. I will show you my car too. It is blue. It is pretty."

Ben and Lily smiled and hugged. They played with their cars again. They made noises and pretended they were racing. They had fun together.

Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them. She said, "Good job, Ben and Lily. You are good kids. You learned how to share and be kind. I love you both."

Once upon a time, two friends were playing together. Suddenly, one of them saw something strange. It was an iron! The other friend had never seen anything like it before. She asked her friend what it was and he had to explain. He said it was a tool used to keep clothes flat.

The friend was a bit scared because she had never seen anything like the iron before. But her friend was explaining about it and soon she felt better. He showed her how he used the iron and she was excited to learn about it.

At the end of the day, both friends were happy. They had learned something new, and the iron no longer scared them.

Jimmy was walking through the park when suddenly he saw a beautiful rainbow. He had never seen one before. But then he noticed someone was frowning at the rainbow. Jimmy wondered why they didn't look happy.

He asked the person why they were so unhappy. The person said they were ignorant and did not understand how beautiful the rainbow was. Jimmy smiled. He knew the person needed help understanding the beauty of a rainbow.

He taught the person about rainbows, explaining that all the colors came from the water in the sky. The person started to smile and thanked Jimmy for his help.

Jimmy was so happy he had changed someone's frown into a smile by teaching them about rainbows. He knew that everyone should be able to enjoy the beauty of a rainbow, no matter how ignorant they might be.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around in the springtime, when the flowers would bloom and the sun would shine. One day, Benny found a shiny rock that glowed in the sunlight. He thought it was magic!

Benny wanted to keep his shiny rock safe, so he put it in his tidy burrow. But every night, the rock would glow so bright that it kept Benny awake! He tried to cover it with a blanket, but it still shone through. Finally, Benny realized that the rock was meant to be shared with everyone. So he took it outside and showed it to his friends, who were all amazed by its glow.

From then on, Benny and his friends would gather around the rock every night and tell stories under its magical glow. And Benny's burrow stayed tidy, because he had learned that sharing is better than keeping things all to yourself. The end.

Once upon a time there was a very elderly tutor. She was kind and friendly and always served her students in the best way possible. She was known for her patience, even when her students made mistakes.

One day, the elderly tutor had a new student, a 3 year old child. The child was very eager to learn and the elderly tutor was excited to teach her. They spent many hours together, learning and exploring.

But one day, the elderly tutor decided to give the child a very difficult task. The child struggled and soon became frustrated. Finally, the child said, "I can't do it!" and ran away.

The elderly tutor was disappointed. She tried to help the child, but she had been too hard. The child learned an important lesson that day - that it's important to be patient, no matter how difficult a task is.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and saw a big sack on the ground. She asked her mommy, "What's in the sack?"

"I don't know, let's go see," said her mommy.

When they got closer, they saw that the sack was full of toys! Lily was so happy and grateful. She said, "Mommy, can I play with the toys?"

"Of course, you can," said her mommy.

Lily played with the toys for hours and had so much fun. When it was time to go home, she said, "Thank you, mommy. I'm grateful for the toys in the sack."

"You're welcome, sweetie," said her mommy. "I'm glad you had fun."

Once there was a little girl named Clara. She was three years old and she loved the season of summer. One day, Clara wanted to try something spicy. She begged her mother to get her something spicy to eat.

Eventually, her mother decided to buy her some spiced chips. Clara was so excited she began to cry out of joy. She couldn't wait to eat them.

Clara didn't realize just how spicy the chips were. When she ate one, her eyes became very watery and her nose started to run. She began to cry and cry. She asked her mother for some milk but it was too late. Her mouth was burning and her stomach was in pain.

Clara learned a hard lesson that day. Never try something too spicy!

One day, Mommy and Eric, a 3 year old, decided to bake a cake. Eric was so excited! He could hardly wait.

They went to the backyard and found the perfect spot. It was in the sunshine and was very lively.

Mommy and Eric gathered the ingredients they needed. Then they carefully measured everything out. Eric had so much fun stirring the mixture together.

When it was all ready, they popped it in the oven. Eric watched to see what would happen next.

Soon, the cake was ready to be eaten! It tasted delicious. Eric couldn't wait to show his family. It was the best cake ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie was only three years old and she loved furry things! One day, she went for a walk in her garden and stumbled across a cup. She picked it up and gave it a cuddle as it was so furry and soft.

Suddenly, Sophie sneezed! She had never sneezed before, so she was a bit scared. She looked around to see if anyone else had heard her, but no one else was in the garden.

Just then, Sophie heard a little voice say, "Bless you, Sophie!" She looked around to see who it was, and she could just make out a tiny furry creature in the tree.

"Who are you?" asked Sophie.

The furry creature said, "I'm your garden fairy! I heard your sneeze and wanted to say bless you!" 

Sophie was so excited to meet a fairy that she asked if she could keep the cup she was cuddling. The fairy said of course, and gave her a little wink before flying away.

Sophie was so happy with her furry cup and she kept it forever as a reminder of her magical garden.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful fisherman. Every day, he managed to catch lots of fish. He would take the fish home and share them with his family. 

One day, the fisherman got a very special surprise. When he arrived home, he found a little lost puppy waiting for him outside his door. The puppy was so cute and cuddly! 

He took the puppy in and made it part of his family. The puppy was grateful and wanted to repay the fisherman for his thoughtful kindness. 

So every morning, the puppy managed to help the fisherman catch more fish. With little puppy's help, the fisherman was able to catch more fish than ever before. 

They all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly octopus named Ollie. Ollie loved to swim in the deep blue sea. One day, Ollie met a little fish named Finn.

"Hello, Finn! Do you want to swim with me?" asked Ollie.

"Yes, please!" replied Finn.

So, Ollie and Finn swam together and had lots of fun. Suddenly, they saw a big shark coming towards them!

"Oh no! What are we going to do?" cried Finn.

"Don't worry, I'll protect you. I'm an expert at swimming away from sharks," said Ollie.

And with that, Ollie used his eight tentacles to swim as fast as he could, carrying Finn on his back. They swam and swam until they were safe from the shark.

"Thank you, Ollie. You're the best swimmer ever!" said Finn.

Ollie smiled and replied, "No problem, Finn. That's what friends are for."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to mail a letter for her. Timmy was so excited to help his mom that he ran to the mailbox as fast as he could.

But when Timmy got to the mailbox, he realized that the letter was enormous and wouldn't fit inside. Timmy didn't know what to do, so he asked his neighbor, Mr. Smith, for help. Mr. Smith told Timmy that he could take the letter to the post office instead.

Timmy was worried that he would get in trouble for not being able to mail the letter, but Mr. Smith reassured him that it was okay to ask for help when you need it. Timmy learned that it's important to ask for help when you're feeling stuck and that it's okay to make mistakes. From that day on, Timmy always asked for help when he needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Rose who loved to make tasty treats. One day, Rose made some yummy cookies and left them on the table. Lily wanted to eat them all, but her mom said she could only have one. Lily tried to resist eating more, but she couldn't help herself. She ate all the cookies when her mom wasn't looking.

Later that day, Lily started to feel sick. Her tummy hurt and she felt very tired. Her mom took her to the hospital, but it was too late. Lily had eaten too many cookies and her body couldn't handle it. She passed away, leaving her sister Rose and her family very sad. From that day on, Rose never made tasty treats again because it reminded her of her sister.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to help their dad, who was a farmer. They liked to feed the chickens, milk the cows, and pick the apples. But they also liked to be playful and have fun.

One day, they decided to mix some things in a big bowl. They took some flour, some eggs, some milk, and some sugar from the kitchen. They also took some apples from the basket. They poured and cracked and stirred and chopped. They made a big mess, but they did not care.

They wanted to surprise their dad with a cake. They put the bowl in the oven and waited. They smelled something good. They hoped their dad would like it.

When their dad came home, he saw the twins smiling and the oven on. He asked, "What are you two doing?"

"We made you a cake, dad!" Ben and Lily said.

"A cake? For me?" their dad said. He opened the oven and took out the bowl. He saw a brown and lumpy thing. He was not sure what it was.

He smiled and said, "Thank you, my playful twins. You are very sweet. But next time, let's use a recipe, okay?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They hugged their dad and said, "We love you, dad!"

They all laughed and ate the cake. It was not very good, but they did not mind. They were happy.

Mother and Suzie were walking through the park. Suzie had on her red coat, and she was smiling. It was cold out, but Suzie didn't mind.

Suddenly, Mommy said, "Oh look Suzie! Strawberries!" Suzie saw a bush full of big, juicy strawberries. She wanted to pick one, so she did. It was so sweet and juicy!

Next, Mommy said, "Let's have an icy treat!" So they went to a shop and got icy ice cream. Suzie got strawberry ice cream. It was so cool and yummy!

When they finished their treat, Suzie and Mommy went back home. Suzie was so happy because she got to eat a strawberry and wear her red coat!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys when her mom called her for lunch. Lily didn't want to stop playing, so she ignored her mom and continued playing. 

Her mom called her again, but Lily still didn't want to stop playing. So her mom came up the stairs and saw Lily playing. She was angry and told Lily that she was being rude. Lily felt sorry and started to cry. 

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay to play, but you need to listen when someone calls you. It's important to be polite." Lily nodded and wiped her tears. She hugged her mom back and said, "I'm sorry, Mommy." 

From that day on, Lily always listened to her mom and was polite. She learned that it's important to be respectful to others. And whenever she did something good, her mom would clap and cheer for her.

Once, there was a small and very special pumpkin. He had the gift of being able to spin! He was so proud of himself. All the other vegetables and fruits were amazed by his talent.

One day, a big and mean cabbage came along and said to the pumpkin, "You are nothing special, you can't do anything other than spin. That's nothing impressive!"

The pumpkin felt embarrassed and embarrassed. He wanted to prove the cabbage wrong, so he decided to learn some more skills to show he was not just a simple spinning pumpkin. He learned to roll and jump, twirl and bump!

At last, the mean cabbage was silenced and the other vegetables and fruits praised the pumpkin for his hard work.

The moral of the story is that hard work can bring great rewards and no one should ever put you down because of your gifts.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was only three years old.

One day, Sarah was playing with her rag when she heard a noise. A noise she had never heard before. She got scared and stopped playing.

Slowly, she peeked around the corner of the room. She saw an animal. He looked so modest and gentle. Sarah knew she did not have to be afraid.

The animal started to move toward her, and Sarah's fear disappeared. She stretched out her hands and showed the animal her rag. The animal came to her and started to play with the rag too.

Sarah and the animal were having so much fun playing together. But soon it was time to go. Sarah said goodbye to her new friend and stopped playing. She waved as the animal left and she was filled with happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to play with her toys every day. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new toy. It was a big box filled with all sorts of equipment. Lily opened the box and saw lots of different things inside. She recognized some of the toys, but others were new to her.

Lily started to play with the equipment and had so much fun. She found a soft ball, a little car, and some blocks. She also found a mild toy that made funny noises. Lily played with the equipment all day long and didn't want to stop. She was so happy to have new toys to play with. From that day on, Lily played with her equipment every day and loved it.

Tom and Sue are twins. They like to play with their toys and talk to each other. Sometimes they repeat what the other one says, like a game.

One day, they find a big balloon in the closet. It is red and shiny. They want to blow it up and make it bigger. They take turns to blow air into the balloon. They think it is fun.

But then, Tom feels a pain in his tummy. He has too much gas from blowing the balloon. He burps loudly and says, "Ouch, my tummy hurts!"

Sue hears him and says, "Ouch, my tummy hurts!" She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is in pain. She thinks it is part of the game.

Tom says, "No, Sue, it is not a game. I need help. I need Mommy." He repeats what he says, hoping she will understand.

Sue hears him and says, "No, Sue, it is not a game. I need help. I need Mommy." She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is serious. She thinks he is still playing.

Tom gets angry and says, "Stop repeating me, Sue! You are not helpful. You are silly!" He repeats what he says, trying to make her stop.

Sue hears him and says, "Stop repeating me, Sue! You are not helpful. You are silly!" She repeats what he says, but she does not know he is angry. She thinks he is joking.

Tom cries and says, "Mommy, Mommy, where are you?" He repeats what he says, looking for their mother.

Sue hears him and says, "Mommy, Mommy, where are you?" She repeats what he says, following him.

Then, Mommy comes and sees them. She sees the balloon and the tears. She hugs them and says, "What is wrong, my darlings?"

Tom says, "Mommy, I have gas. It hurts. Sue repeats me. She is not helpful. She is silly." He repeats what he says, pointing at Sue.

Sue says, "Mommy, I have gas. It hurts. Sue repeats me. She is not helpful. She is silly." She repeats what he says, pointing at herself.

Mommy smiles and says, "Oh, my darlings, you are both helpful and silly. You have gas because you blew the balloon too much. It is not good for your tummy. Next time, blow less and share more. And don't repeat each other when someone is in pain. Repeat only when someone is happy or funny. Do you understand?"

Tom and Sue nod and say, "Yes, Mommy, we understand." They repeat what she says, but this time they mean it. They hug Mommy and say, "We love you, Mommy." They repeat what they say, but this time they are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Mike. He liked to play with the lumber from his dad's shed. Every day he would use the regular saw to cut up the lumber and make it into different shapes.

One day, while Mike was playing, his dad noticed and came to talk to him.

"Mike, what are you doing now?" his dad said.

Mike replied, "I'm playing with the lumber, Dad!"

His dad said, "But Mike, that's dangerous! You could get hurt with the saw. There are also other ways to play with the lumber, like building a fort or a house."

Mike looked down, feeling guilty. Then his dad continued, "Let me show you something that can help you play with lumber without the saw."

Mike's dad gathered up some sticks from the lumber pile and put them in a bowl. Then he added some hot water and some drops of food coloring. With a smile, he said, "Mike, watch closely and you'll see something special."

After a few minutes, the sticks began to melt in the bowl. Mike was amazed! He asked his dad, "What happened?"
