One day, Jack was walking in the park. He saw a colorful grape hanging from a tree. He felt excited and wanted to have it. He quickly picked it up and began to eat it. Suddenly, he felt scared. He heard a loud voice from behind him. It was a park keeper. 

"That grape belongs to everyone," the park keeper said. "You can't take it without asking."

Jack felt disappointed. He apologized and put the grape back on the tree. From that day, he learned to asked for permission before taking something.

Moral of the story: Always ask before taking something.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and cuddle with her stuffed animals. One day, Lily's mom went to the store to buy some stuff for dinner. Lily asked her mom to buy her favorite snack, but her mom said it wasn't available at the store.

Lily felt sad and started to sneeze. She sneezed so much that her nose turned red and she couldn't stop. She tried to play with her toys, but she couldn't focus because of her sneezes. Lily's mom came back from the store and saw her daughter sneezing. She knew something was wrong and asked Lily what happened.

Lily told her mom that her favorite snack wasn't available at the store. Her mom hugged her and said they could make something else for snack time. Lily stopped sneezing and felt happy again. From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes things aren't available, but there are always other options to make us happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl who had a funny smell coming from her. It made her feel sad and troubled. One day, she asked her mom to help her.

Her mom had an idea. She took the little girl on a surprise visit. They drove to a special store and bought a sweet-smelling perfume.

When they got home, the little girl was so happy! She put some of the perfume on the troubled areas and felt much better.

The little girl was so excited. She put a little extra scent on her neck and wrists and started to feel very special. She thanked her mom for taking her on the special visit and for helping her smell nice again. They hugged and smiled and went off together to play. 

The end.

One day, a little boy had gone out to explore the forest near his house. As he walked through the trees, he noticed a raven high up in a tree. The boy was curious and wanted to reach up for it, so he stretched his arm out and tried, but it was too far away.

The next day, the boy was determined to try again. He ran to the same tree and once again, he tried to reach for the raven, but it was out of reach. Just as he was about to give up, a voice spoke, asking the boy why he wanted the raven. The boy replied he was curious about it.

The mysterious voice explained that the raven was not for the ignorant, but only for those who were patient and brave. With that, the voice showed the boy a way to reach the raven. The little boy was amazed and slowly, carefully, he reached up with his arm and finally touched the raven.

The patience and bravery of the little boy had paid off. From that day forward, the little boy never gave up - he kept reaching until he found success!

Tom was a small boy who liked to play with his toy train. He had a big track that went around his room and he made noises like a real train. He loved his train very much and took good care of it.

One day, Tom's mom said they had to go to grandma's house for Christmas. Tom was happy to see grandma, but he was sad to leave his train. He asked his mom if he could take his train with him, but she said no. She said there was not enough room in the car and he could play with it when they came back.

Tom was very sad, but he did what his mom said. He packed his clothes and his teddy bear and got in the car. He looked out the window and saw the snow and the trees and the houses. He wondered if Santa would find him at grandma's house and bring him a present.

When they got to grandma's house, Tom hugged her and said hello. She was very happy to see him and gave him a big kiss. She said she had a surprise for him in the living room. Tom followed her and saw a big Christmas tree with lights and ornaments and a star on top. Under the tree, there were many boxes wrapped in colorful paper and ribbons.

Tom looked at the boxes and saw one that had his name on it. It was a big box, bigger than him. He was very curious and excited. He asked his mom and grandma if he could open it. They said yes, but he had to be careful. Tom tore the paper and opened the box. Inside, he saw something that made him gasp.

It was his toy train! His mom and grandma had brought it with them and hid it in the box. They wanted to surprise him and make him happy. Tom was so happy that he cried and laughed and hugged them. He thanked them and said it was the best present ever. He took his train out of the box and set it up on the floor. He played with it all day and all night. He did not care about the other presents or the coal in his stocking. He only cared about his train and his mom and grandma who loved him.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight. His name was Sir Lancelot.
One day, Sir Lancelot went on a great adventure. He came to a mysterious cave, but he was brave and he went inside. When he went inside the cave, something incredible happened.

When Sir Lancelot saw what was hidden in the cave, he couldn't believe it. He saw a huge spear!

He took the spear and held it up in the air. The spear glowed with an incredible light. He knew that this must be a magical spear, so he decided to call it the Spear of Wonder.

When he held the Spear of Wonder up in the air, something incredible happened. All around him, there was a sparkle of light. He realised that the Spear of Wonder had revealed a secret to him.

He knew he was now a very special knight with a very special power! Sir Lancelot was so happy and he thanked the Spear of Wonder for letting him know this incredible secret. He never forgot the Spear of Wonder, and everyone always remembered the hero with the magical powers.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little seed, who was looking for a place to grow. The seed tried to find a place but there was nowhere to go.

The seed asked the fridge: "Can I please grow here?" The fridge was surprised. It replied: "But I am so cold, I don't think you can grow here."

The seed thought for a moment and then said: "I will try anyway."

So the seed planted itself deep inside the fridge and it started to grow and grow. Soon, the seed had grown into a beautiful flower!

The flower looked out of the fridge, and saw the sunlight in the sky. It smiled and was so happy that it had found a place to be, despite the cold temperature.

The moral of the story is to never give up, even if the conditions seem difficult. If you stay strong and brave, then you can always find a way to make something beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. While playing, she saw her friend Timmy. Timmy said, "Hi Lily! Can you bring a message to my mom?"

Lily was happy to help. Timmy gave her a note and said, "Please give this to my mom. It's important." Lily ran to Timmy's house and knocked on the door. Timmy's mom answered and Lily gave her the note.

But Lily was embarrassed because she had a little accident on the way. She spilled her juice on her shirt! Timmy's mom said, "Don't be embarrassed, accidents happen. Thank you for bringing the message." Lily smiled and ran back to the park to play with Timmy.

Once upon a time, there was a witch named Sally. She was very famous because she could do magic. One day, Sally decided to prepare a special potion. She needed some special ingredients like frog legs and spider webs. She went to the forest to collect them.

While Sally was collecting the ingredients, she met a little girl named Lily. Lily was lost in the forest and was scared. Sally helped her find her way back home. Lily was very happy and thanked Sally. She told everyone about the kind witch who helped her.

Sally felt good that she could help someone. She finished preparing her potion and it turned out to be the best one she had ever made. From that day on, Sally became even more famous for her kind heart and her magical potions.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy. They saw a big slide and Lily wanted to go on it. But she was scared. 

Her mommy said, "Don't worry, I'll be right here to help you." So, Lily climbed up the ladder and went down the slide. It was so much fun! 

After playing for a while, they went to have a picnic. Lily's mommy gave her a sandwich in a tube. Lily was confused, "Why is my sandwich in a tube?" 

Mommy explained, "It's like a straw, but for food. It keeps your sandwich fresh and yummy." Lily thought it was helpful and touched the tube. It was cold and smooth. 

They finished their picnic and went home, happy and full. Lily couldn't wait to go back to the park and play on the slide again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl and she liked to go on adventures. She had a wagon that she used to carry all her things on her trips. Today she was going on a very special mission. She needed to hurry and get started.

As she was walking along, she came upon something very unusual. It was a cart filled with toys, sticks and leaves. As she was looking at the cart, she saw an old man. He said to her, "You must be in a hurry, little girl. I will help you. I will pull your wagon and get you to your destination faster."

The girl was so happy. She thanked the old man. The old man said, "There's no need to thank me. I like helping people reach their destinations faster. Hurry now, little girl!"

The old man pulled the girl's wagon as she smiled with joy. They traveled together and soon she had reached her destination. She thanked the old man again and were soon on their way. The little girl never forgot the nice old man and her unusual experience.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog called Spot. Spot wanted to explore, so he opened the front door and ran outside. He trotted across the street to a big bridge. He walked all the way to the end and looked around. He could see the river below!

Spot was so excited, he wanted to jump off the bridge and play in the water. He was just about to leap when a kind voice said, 
"Where are you going my friend?" Spot turned around and saw a friendly frog.

"I am going to play in the river!" Spot said, wagging his tail.

The frog smiled at Spot and said, "Be careful Spot, the water can be deep!"

Spot thanked the friendly frog, before padding back across the bridge. He was very loyal, so he decided to follow the Frog's advice and play somewhere safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big factory. The factory made toys for kids to play with. One day, a little girl named Lily went to visit the factory. She saw a man who was very rude. He didn't smile or say hello to her.

Lily wanted to see how the toys were made. She asked the man if she could see inside. But the man said, "No, go away." Lily was sad and walked away. 

Later, Lily saw a sign that said "Toy Factory Tour". She asked her mom if they could go on the tour. Her mom said yes. When they got to the factory, the same rude man was there. But this time, he was smiling and said, "Welcome to the tour!" 

Lily was happy to see how the toys were made. At the end of the tour, the man gave her a toy to take home. Lily was happy and said, "Thank you!" The man smiled and said, "You're welcome." And then he closed the door of the factory.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in the jungle. He had a big mane and sharp teeth. One day, he met a little girl who was walking in the jungle. The lion said, "Hello, little girl. What are you doing here?"

The little girl replied, "I am looking for a fountain. Do you know where it is?"

The lion said, "Yes, I do. It's over there. But be careful, the water is very cold and it might make you dizzy."

The little girl said, "Thank you, Mr. Lion. You are very kind." And she went to the fountain. She drank some water and then she heard a loud roar. She turned around and saw the lion. He was roaring because he was happy to see her again. The little girl smiled and said, "You are my friend, Mr. Lion." And they played together in the jungle.

Once there was a cute little mouse called Mark. Mark loved to do lots of fun things.

Mark then saw a crack in the floor. He got closer and closer to investigate.

Mark couldn't believe it. He was so happy! He tried to pull the cheese out, but he was too small.

Once upon a time, there was a popular girl named Lily. She had a pretty veil that she loved to wear. Lily was very good at tying her veil. She would tie it around her head to look like a princess.

One day, Lily went to play with her friends. She wore her veil and tied it just right. Her friends thought her veil was very pretty. They wanted to learn how to tie a veil too.

Lily showed her friends how to tie a veil. They all practiced and got better at it. Soon, all the girls were wearing veils and tying them just like Lily. They were all very happy and had lots of fun playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. But one day, the sunshine went away and it became very dark and cloudy. Lily felt sad because she couldn't play outside anymore.

Lily decided to make her own sunshine. She got some paper and crayons and drew a big yellow sun. She taped it to her window and it made her room feel warm and bright. But when she went outside, it was still dark and cloudy.

Lily realized she couldn't make the real sunshine come back. She felt poor because she couldn't do anything about it. But then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. It was beautiful and made her feel happy again. Even though the sunshine was gone, she knew there were still good things in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cozy bed with a soft blanket and a comfortable pillow. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help her hang up new curtains in her room. Lily was excited to help and handed her mom the curtain rods. 

As they hung up the curtains, Lily's mom asked her, "Do you believe these curtains will make your room look pretty?" Lily nodded her head and replied, "Yes, I believe they will!" 

Later that night, Lily snuggled into her bed and looked at her new curtains. She felt so happy and comfortable in her room. She said to herself, "I love my new curtains, they make my room look so pretty!" 

Lily's mom came in to say goodnight and asked her, "Do you feel comfortable in your bed?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I feel very comfortable. Thank you for my new curtains, Mommy!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was just three years old and loved to explore and go on adventures. 

One day, Lucy decided to go exploring into the forest near her home. She was so excited to see all the trees and animals she might find. But as she started walking through the forest, things didn't seem quite right. She heard strange sounds and was beginning to get scared. 

Suddenly Lucy saw a ghost! She was very frightened and ran away as fast as she could. Lucy was sure she heard the ghost chasing after her. She ran out of the forest and back to her home. 

When she got home, Lucy was so frustrated. She told her mom about the ghost she'd seen, but her mom just smiled and told her that ghosts weren't real. 

Lucy felt better after talking to her mom, and she decided she would still explore the forest. Just this time, she would take her mom with her.

Once upon a time there was a lucky thumb. Every day it would go out and explore the world around it. One day it found a pool of water so it decided to soak in it. The thumb felt so happy and content. It kept soaking and giving itself a massage with the warm water. Every day the thumb kept coming back. All of the other thumbs from the neighbourhood were so jealous of this lucky thumb and wanted to come soak too! Eventually the other thumbs joined in and all of the thumbs had a big soak together. They laughed and smiled as the water bubbled and glowed. They stayed there for hours and had a wonderful time. It was the best day ever!

Andy was envious of his older brother, who had lots of toys. He decided to go outside to find something special. He walked around the garden, looking for something exciting.

He came across some strange soil. It looked like it was sparkling in the sunlight. He touched it and it was so cold, that he started to shiver! He was sure this must be something special. 

He dug around the soil and found something shiny. It was the most beautiful stone he had ever seen! He was so happy, he hugged it close and he ran straight home with it.

His brother was so envious when he saw what Andy had found, he wanted it for himself. But Andy just hugged it tighter and said, "This is my special stone and it will stay with me!" 

Andy took his stone inside and kept it safe and warm. He knew it was special and he was so happy he found it.

One day, a man had to push his wife. She was very angry and screamed. He tried to explain why he was doing it, but she did not listen. He had to push his wife so that he could save her from the bad man. The bad man was running towards them, and the man knew he had to push her away so she would be safe. The man was scared, but he was brave and he pushed his wife away from the bad man.

She landed on the ground and she looked very scared. But when she saw that the bad man had give up, and left, she was very grateful. She hugged the man and thanked him for saving her. The man was very relieved that his wife was safe, and he was grateful that he had been brave enough to push her away. They both knew that his brave push had saved them.

Once there was a little boy namedJon. He was only three years old and he loved having fun. One day, he asked his mom if he could have a candle. His mom said no, but Jon insisted. He wanted a candle to play with.

His mom tried to explain why he could not have a candle, but Jon just kept insisting, until she agreed. So his mom bought him a special candle and put it on the table.

Jon was so excited and instantly took the candle to his bedroom. He tried to light it, but it wouldn't light. He was sad, so his mom showed him how to light it, but still it wouldn't light.

Jon's mom saw that he was getting spoiled, so she lit the candle for him. Jon was so delighted that he hugged his mom and thanked her.

From then on, Jon was happy with his candle and played with it every day. He was never too far away from it, and it still works to this day.

Tom had a coin that he liked very much. It was shiny and round and had a picture of a lion on it. He found it in the park one day and he was very happy. He wanted to own the coin and keep it in his pocket.

But some of the other kids in his class also liked the coin. They wanted to see it and touch it and play with it. They asked Tom to share the coin with them, but Tom said no. He did not want to share his coin. He wanted to own it all by himself.

This made the other kids sad and angry. They did not want to be friends with Tom anymore. They said he was mean and selfish and greedy. They played with other toys and games and left Tom alone. Tom had his coin, but he had no friends. He was not popular at all.

Tom felt lonely and bored. He looked at his coin and wondered why it made him so unhappy. He realized that owning the coin was not as fun as sharing it. He decided to change his mind and be nice to the other kids.

He went to the other kids and said he was sorry. He said he would share his coin with them and let them see it and touch it and play with it. He said he wanted to be friends with them and have fun with them. The other kids were surprised and happy. They forgave Tom and welcomed him back. They took turns with the coin and enjoyed it together. Tom had his coin, but he also had friends. He was popular and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird named Ted. Ted loved to soar in the sky and show off his beautiful wings that were covered in colourful patterns.

Every morning, Ted would rise up high into the air and admire the world below him. One day, when Ted was soarin g high, he heard a loud, noisy noise. He looked around and saw a plane nearby. Ted was so scared of the noise that he quickly flew away. 

The plane followed behind him and the noise grew louder and louder. Eventually, Ted was so tired that he couldn't fly anymore, and he was about to give up. Just as he was about to land, he heard someone calling out to him: "Don't be scared, Ted! I'm sorry that I made so much noise!"

The voice belonged to a friendly pilot who had seen Ted's beautiful wings and decided to fly alongside him. They flew side by side until they reached the highest clouds and Ted was amazed by the views. From then on, Ted and the friendly pilot became good friends. Every morning they would soar together and Ted was no longer scared of the noisy plane.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved ice-cream so much. One day, he saw an ancient ice-cream truck. The truck was very old and slow, but it had a big sign that said "Ice-Cream".

Tim went to the truck and said, "Hi, can I have ice-cream, please?" The ice-cream man looked at him and said, "Sure, little boy. Here you go." Tim took the ice-cream and started to eat it. But it did not taste good at all. It tasted very bad.

Tim screamed, "Yuck! This ice-cream is bad!" The ice-cream man just laughed and said, "I am sorry, little boy. The ice-cream is too old." Tim was very sad and walked away. He did not get to enjoy his ice-cream that day.

Minnie was a three year old girl who loved to explore. One day, she decided to investigate an old house in the woods. As she started to look around, she noticed a message written on the door - it said "tough times ahead". Minnie was confused by this, but she knew it was something important.

She kept exploring and soon she heard a man's voice. He was talking about something called a "message". Minnie had no idea what he meant and she walked up to him to ask. He explained to her that a message was a way to tell someone about something important.

Minnie was still a bit confused but the man reassured her and said, "Whenever you miss someone, you can send them a message." He showed her how to write a message and soon Minnie was on her way with a note in her pocket.

When she got home, she shared the note with her family who hugged her tight and said: "We always miss you when you're away". Minnie smiled, feeling extra special and safe. She had learned an important lesson - tough times can be made better with a simple message.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was always polite and kind to everyone. One day, he went to the park with his mom. At the park, he saw two toys: a red ball and a blue truck. Tim had to choose which toy to play with.

Tim asked his mom, "Mom, can I play with the red ball or the blue truck?" His mom smiled and said, "You can choose one toy to play with, Tim." Tim thought for a moment and chose the red ball.

While Tim was playing with the red ball, a little girl came over. She had a question. "Can I play with your blue truck?" she asked. Tim remembered to be polite and said, "I am sorry, but I chose the red ball. I don't have the blue truck."

The little girl looked sad. Tim wanted to make her happy, so he gave her the red ball to play with. They played together and became good friends. The moral of the story is to be polite and share with others, and you will make friends.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have lunch in a bag. They sit on a bench and eat.

"Look, Ben, I have a sandwich with cheese and ham. Do you want some?" Anna says.

"No, thank you, Anna. I have a banana and a cookie. Do you want some?" Ben says.

"Yes, please, Ben. I like bananas and cookies. They are sweet and soft." Anna says.

They share their lunch and talk. They see a bird on a tree. They see a dog on a leash. They see a flower on the grass.

"Anna, can I hold your hand?" Ben says.

"Sure, Ben. Why do you want to hold my hand?" Anna says.

"Because you are my friend. And because you are pale. You need some sun." Ben says.

Anna laughs. She is pale because she has blond hair and blue eyes. Ben is tan because he has brown hair and brown eyes.

"I don't need sun, Ben. I like being pale. But I like holding your hand, too. Because you are my friend." Anna says.

They hold hands and smile. They finish their lunch and play some more. They are happy.

Once there was a boy who wanted to meet someone new. One day, he saw a wire lying on the ground. It was dull and gray, so it did not look very fun. But the boy was curious, so he picked it up. 

He wrapped the wire around a nearby tree and took the other end in his hand. All of a sudden, the wire lit up with bright colors. The boy was amazed. 

Just then, a friendly, old man strolled by. He saw the boy with the wire and smiled.

The boy asked the man, "What is this?" The man said, "This is a magic wire. It can help you meet people."

The boy was very excited. He said goodbye to the man and thanked him. The man said, "You are very welcome!"

The boy ran off with the magic wire in search of adventure, looking forward to all of the people he would meet.

Once upon a time, there was a brave turtle. She was very small, but full of courage. One day, she decided to explore the big world and find new things.

She started to crawl very slowly. After a while, she saw a small hole under the ground. She wondered what she will find there. She got very excited and started to crawl into the hole.

Once she got in she saw the most amazing thing: thousands of brightly coloured stones and sparkly crystals! She was so excited that she couldn't move.

Suddenly, a small mouse said: "Why hello there little turtle! What are you doing here?". The turtle was so surprised, but she answered: "I'm looking for amazing things!". The mouse smiled: "Well, look no further. You're in the most amazing place!".

The turtle smiled and started to play with the stones and crystals. She forgot about the time, until it got dark and she decided to crawl back home.

The turtle was very happy. She found an amazing place she never knew existed before. Whenever she felt sad, she remembered that magical place she'd seen and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a baby named Timmy. Timmy was scared of the dark and always cried when it was time to go to bed. His mom would sing him lullabies and give him a teddy bear, but Timmy still felt scared.

One day, Timmy's mom told him a story about a little bird who was scared of flying. The bird wanted to stay in its nest forever because it was too scary to fly. But one day, the bird decided to try and fly. It flapped its wings and soared through the sky. The bird felt so happy and free!

Timmy thought about the little bird and decided to be brave like it. He closed his eyes and took a deep breath. He imagined himself soaring through the sky like the little bird. Slowly, Timmy started to settle down and fall asleep. From that night on, Timmy wasn't scared of the dark anymore. He learned that sometimes things can be scary, but if you try your best, you can overcome your fears.

Kate was a little girl who liked to dress up. She had a lot of fancy clothes and really liked picking out the perfect outfit of the day. One day she and her family went out to take a special picture at a park. 

Her mom asked Kate to dress in her favorite clothes. Kate took out her best dress and put it on. She was very proud of how she looked.

When they got to the park, they set up a big camera. They placed Kate in front and took her picture. Kate posed like she was a movie star.

After the picture was taken, everyone was very proud of how well Kate looked. She was so proud too. They all felt very happy to have this special picture. It was a picture to remember!

Lily was sad. She had a bad dream and woke up crying. She wanted her mommy and daddy, but they were not in their room. She felt scared and alone.

She walked to the kitchen, hoping to find them. She saw a plate of waffles on the table. They smelled good and looked yummy. She wondered who made them. She heard a voice behind her.

"Hi, Lily. Are you hungry?" It was her big brother, Sam. He was holding a glass of milk. He smiled at her.

Lily ran to him and hugged him. "Sam, I had a bad dream. I want mommy and daddy. Where are they?" she asked.

Sam hugged her back and comforted her. "It's okay, Lily. Mommy and daddy went to the store. They will be back soon. They made waffles for us before they left. They love us very much. Do you want some waffles? They are warm and sweet."

Lily nodded. She liked waffles. She liked Sam too. He was nice and brave. He helped her feel better. He gave her a glass of milk and a fork. They sat at the table and ate the waffles together. They talked and laughed. Lily forgot about her bad dream. She felt happy and safe. She thanked Sam for being her brother. He thanked her for being his sister. They hugged again. They waited for mommy and daddy to come home. They knew they were a family.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play together. One day, they saw their dad reading a newspaper on the sofa. They were curious about what he was looking at.

"Dad, what is that?" Ben asked, pointing at the newspaper.

"It's a newspaper, Ben. It has stories and pictures about what is happening in the world," Dad said.

"Can we see?" Lily asked, climbing on the sofa next to Dad.

"Sure, but be careful. It's expensive and I don't want you to tear it," Dad said, handing them the newspaper.

Ben and Lily stared at the newspaper. They saw words and letters they did not know. They saw pictures of people and places they did not recognize. They saw numbers and colors and shapes.

"What is this?" Ben asked, pointing at a picture of a big building.

"That's a skyscraper, Ben. It's a very tall building where people work and live," Dad said.

"Wow, it's so high!" Ben said.

"And what is this?" Lily asked, pointing at a picture of a shiny car.

"That's a sports car, Lily. It's a very fast and expensive car that some people like to drive," Dad said.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said.

Ben and Lily stared at the newspaper for a long time. They asked Dad many questions and learned many new things. They liked the newspaper, but they liked Dad more. They gave him a big hug and a kiss.

"Thank you, Dad, for showing us the newspaper. We love you," they said.

"I love you too, Ben and Lily. You are my best stories," Dad said, smiling.

Once there was a man who was very intelligent. He wanted to make something special with a lime. He told the lemon, "Please come here, I need some help!" The lime was very polite and said, "Yes sir, of course!" 

The man said, "I need you to help me make some juice. Will you please squeeze yourself?" The lime was a little worried, but he said, "Yes sir, I can do it!" 

The man put the lime in a juicer and quickly the juice started to flow. The man smiled as he tasted the lime juice. He was so pleased with how well it turned out. 

The man said to the lime, "Thank you for your help! You are a very intelligent lime." The lime was very happy and said, "You're welcome!"

One day, there was a busy mouse. It was looking for something to eat. It looked in all the corners but it couldn't find anything. Suddenly, it saw a thing that made it very happy. It was cheese! 

The mouse was so excited that it quickly ran up to the cheese. It sniffed it with its tiny nose to make sure it was safe. The mouse grabbed the cheese with its little paws and ran away with it. 

After it had eaten some of the cheese, the mouse started to feel full and sleepy. So it found a safe, quiet spot and fell asleep. When it woke up, it was feeling better and very full. 

The mouse was very happy that it had found the cheese. It was just what it had been looking for!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. They played on the swings and the slide. Lily loved to swing high in the sky.

Suddenly, Lily's mommy saw a wire on the ground. She said, "Lily, we need to leave now. There is a wire on the ground and it's not clean." 

Lily asked, "What is a wire?" 

"It's a thin, long thing made of metal," her mommy replied. 

Lily said, "Oh, we don't want to touch that. Let's go home and play with my toys." 

So, they left the park and went home to play with Lily's toys. They had a fun day together.

Sara and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They want to make a cake for Mom. They have a big bowl, some flour, some eggs, some milk and some sugar. They also have a spoon to stir.

"Tom, can you stir the flour and the eggs?" Sara asks.

"OK, Sara, I can stir," Tom says. He takes the spoon and stirs the flour and the eggs. He stirs and stirs until they are mixed.

"Good job, Tom! Now we need to add the milk and the sugar," Sara says. She pours the milk and the sugar into the bowl. "Can you stir some more, Tom?"

"OK, Sara, I can stir some more," Tom says. He stirs and stirs until the milk and the sugar are mixed with the flour and the eggs. He stirs and stirs until the batter is smooth.

"Wow, Tom, you are a good stirrer!" Sara says. "Now we need to put the batter in the pan and bake the cake."

"OK, Sara, let's do that," Tom says. They pour the batter in the pan and put the pan in the oven. They set the timer and wait for the cake to be done.

While they wait, they see a letter on the table. It is from Grandma. Sara picks up the letter and opens it. She reads it out loud to Tom.

"Dear Sara and Tom, I miss you very much. I hope you are having fun and being good. I sent you a nice surprise in the mail. It should arrive soon. I love you. Grandma."

"Wow, Sara, Grandma is so nice!" Tom says. "I wonder what the surprise is."

"Me too, Tom. Maybe it is a toy or a book or a candy," Sara says. "I love Grandma."

"I love Grandma too," Tom says. They hug each other and smile.

Then they hear the timer beep. The cake is done. They take it out of the oven and let it cool. They decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. They write "We love you, Mom" on the cake with a squeeze bottle.

They are very proud of their cake. They can't wait to show it to Mom and share it with her. They know Mom will love it. They know Mom is nice. They love Mom.

One day, a little fish named Fin was swimming in the sea. He saw a big scale on the ground. Fin was very careful not to touch it. He knew it could be sharp.

A big fish came by and saw the scale too. He wanted to take it away from Fin. The big fish tried to grab the scale, but Fin was fast. Fin swam away and said "No, you can't have it!" The big fish was not happy. He tried again and again to take the scale from Fin.

Fin was smart. He knew he had to be careful and not let the big fish take the scale. He swam around in circles and the big fish got tired. Fin would repeat this trick over and over. The big fish could not catch Fin or the scale. In the end, the big fish gave up and swam away. Fin was happy and kept the scale safe.

Once upon a time there was a shy little boy. He lived in a village by the sea. One day he saw something strange in the sky, it was an airplane! He had never seen an airplane before. He kept watching and then more airplanes came and they had welcome flags flying. They dropped presents from the sky and the people in the village were so happy! 

The little boy wanted to know what was going on. He asked his Grandpa, who told him that the airplanes were welcoming the end of the war. The war was over and now everyone would be safe. 
The boy was very excited, the war was over and his village was safe. He hugged his Grandpa and hugged all the other people in his village. From that day forward, the village was a place of peace and happiness.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to be soldiers and march around the house. They put on their hats and boots and grabbed some sticks for guns. They marched up and down the stairs, making loud noises.

"Bang! Bang! You're dead!" Tom shouted at Lily.

"No, I'm not! You missed me!" Lily shouted back.

They marched into their bedroom and saw a big closet. They thought it would be a good place to hide from the enemy. They opened the door and went inside. The closet was dark and full of clothes and toys. They felt around for a switch, but they could not find one.

"Tom, I'm scared. It's too dark in here," Lily said.

"Don't be scared, Lily. We're soldiers. We're brave," Tom said.

But he was scared too. He wanted to get out of the closet. He pushed the door, but it did not move. He pushed harder, but it still did not move. He banged on the door, but no one heard him.

"Tom, the door is stuck. We can't get out," Lily cried.

"Help! Help! Someone help us!" Tom cried.

But no one came. Their mom and dad were not home. They had gone to the store to buy some food. They were poor and did not have much money. They did not have a phone or a neighbor to call. They did not know when they would be back.

Tom and Lily were trapped in the closet. They were hungry and thirsty and cold. They hugged each other and cried. They wished they had not played pretend. They wished they had stayed out of the closet. They wished someone would find them. But no one did.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they decided to put on a show for their moms and dads. They used a big box as a stage and some old clothes as costumes.

Lily was a princess and Ben was a knight. They acted out a story they made up. The princess was locked in a tower by a mean dragon. The knight had to rescue her with his sword and shield. He also had a secret weapon: a peanut.

The dragon was allergic to peanuts. When the knight threw the peanut at the dragon, the dragon sneezed and ran away. The knight climbed the tower and freed the princess. They hugged and danced happily.

Their moms and dads watched the show and smiled. They were very proud of Lily and Ben. When the show was over, they clapped their hands and cheered. They applauded loudly.

Lily and Ben bowed and thanked their audience. They were very happy. They shared the peanut as a snack. They agreed that it was the best show ever.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - a kitten and a puppy. They were playing in the park together when the puppy stopped suddenly. He said to the kitten, "Look, do you see this perfect tree?" The kitten looked up and saw a tall tree with leaves of many colours. He nodded his head. He agreed with the puppy, the tree was perfect.

The puppy then jumped and said in a loud voice, "Let's climb the tree!" The kitten starred at the puppy and shook his head. He had never climbed a tree before and didn't think it was a good idea. But then, the puppy smiled and said, "It's be fun! I'll show you how." So, the two friends started climbing the tree together.

It was hard work, but with the puppy's help, the kitten made it to the top of the tree. He was so proud of himself and looked out over the park. He turned to the puppy and smiled. Then, they both nodded their heads in agreement - it was the perfect view.

Lily and Mom went to the grocery to buy food. Lily liked the grocery. There were many things to see and touch. Mom gave Lily a list of things to find. Lily had to find milk, eggs, bread, and apples.

Lily found the milk and put it in the cart. She found the eggs and put them in the cart. She found the bread and put it in the cart. She looked for the apples, but she could not see them. She walked around the grocery, but she still could not see them. She saw a big picture of a famous man on a box. He had a big smile and a funny hat. Lily liked the picture. She wanted to see it better. She left the cart and went to the picture.

Mom did not see Lily leave the cart. She thought Lily was still with her. She pushed the cart to the checkout. She paid for the food and put it in bags. She looked for Lily, but she could not see her. She called her name, but she did not answer. Mom was scared. She had lost Lily.

Lily was happy. She was looking at the picture of the famous man. She did not hear Mom call her name. She did not see Mom leave the grocery. She did not know she was lost. She saw a nice lady who worked at the grocery. The lady asked her if she was lost. Lily said no. She said she was looking at the picture. The lady smiled and said the picture was of a famous chef. He made yummy food. Lily said she liked yummy food. The lady asked her if she knew where her mom was. Lily said no. She said she left the cart to see the picture. The lady said they had to find her mom. She took Lily by the hand and walked to the front of the grocery.

Mom was crying. She had looked everywhere for Lily, but she could not find her. She asked the people who worked at the grocery, but they did not see her. She asked the other shoppers, but they did not see her. She was afraid Lily was gone. She saw a policeman who came to help her. She told him what Lily looked like and what she was wearing. The policeman said he would find her.

The lady and Lily walked to the front of the grocery. They saw Mom and the policeman. They saw the cart with the food. Lily saw Mom and ran to her. Mom saw Lily and hugged her. She was so happy. She thanked the lady and the policeman. She said she was sorry for losing Lily. Lily said she was sorry for leaving the cart. She said she wanted to see the picture of the famous chef. Mom said she understood. She said she was glad Lily was safe. She said they could go home and make yummy food with the food they bought. Lily said yes. She said she loved Mom. Mom said she loved Lily. They smiled and left the grocery.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Sarah. She wanted a pet, so one day she decided to go search for a pony. It was an open field, with lots of green grass and sunshine. She looked around and what did she see but a beautiful, small pony. She ran up to it and it was so friendly. Sarah was so happy. She hugged the pony and they became best friends. Every day they would go on a search together to find yummy carrots, apples, and hay. Sarah was so proud of her pony and they would play together everyday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she never liked to tidy them up. One day, her mom asked her to please tidy up her toys, but Lily didn't want to.

Later that day, Lily fell off her bike and hurt her arm. Her mom took her to the hospital for an x-ray. The doctor said that Lily's arm was broken and she needed a cast.

Lily was sad because she couldn't play with her toys while wearing the cast. She wished she had listened to her mom and kept her toys tidy. From then on, Lily always made sure to tidy up her toys so she wouldn't get hurt again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a chimney. The chimney was always tidy and neat. Every day, the chimney permitted a little boy named Billy to take a nap inside the chimney. One day, the chimney said to Billy, "Why don't you go outside and play in the sunshine?"

Billy said, "But I like taking naps here in the chimney. It's so cozy and warm."

The chimney smiled and said, "It's nice to take naps here, but don't you want to go outside and play for a while? There's so much to do out there!"

Billy thought about it for a moment, then said, "Okay, I guess I'll go outside and play!" He waved goodbye to the chimney and went out to play in the sunshine. He had so much fun, and when he was done, he came back to the chimney, all tired and happy.

The chimney smiled, and said, "See, I told you it would be fun! Come back anytime, Billy. I'm always happy to permit you to take a nap here."

And they both lived happily ever after.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the kitchen. They have a big bowl, a spoon, and some flour. They want to make a cake.

"Let's stir the flour," Anna says. She holds the spoon and moves it around the bowl. The flour makes a cloud of white dust.

"Stir, stir, stir," Ben says. He helps Anna with the spoon. They laugh and cough.

Mom comes in the kitchen. She sees the mess. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" she asks. She looks at the bowl, the spoon, and the flour.

"We are making a cake," Anna says.

"A cake?" Mom says. "Do you know how to make a cake?"

Anna and Ben shake their heads. They do not know.

Mom smiles. She has an idea.

"Let's make a quiz," she says. "I will ask you some questions. If you answer right, you can help me make a real cake. If you answer wrong, you have to clean up the mess. Do you want to play?"

Anna and Ben nod. They want to play.

"OK," Mom says. "First question: What do you need to add to the flour to make a cake?"

Anna and Ben think hard. They remember what they saw in the book.

"Eggs!" they say together.

"Very good," Mom says. "You are right. You can add some eggs to the bowl. Next question: What do you need to make the cake sweet?"

Anna and Ben think again. They remember what they like to eat.

"Sugar!" they say together.

"Very good," Mom says. "You are right. You can add some sugar to the bowl. Last question: How long do you need to bake the cake in the oven?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They do not know. They guess.

"Five minutes?" Anna says.

"Ten minutes?" Ben says.

Mom shakes her head. She says, "No, that is too short. You need to bake the cake for a long time. Maybe thirty minutes or more. You are wrong. You have to clean up the mess."

Anna and Ben make a sad face. They do not like to clean up.

"Can we still have some cake?" they ask.

Mom nods. She says, "Yes, you can have some cake. But only after you clean up. And only if you say please and thank you."

Anna and Ben say, "Please and thank you." They start to clean up. They hope the cake will be yummy. They are still friends.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Judy. Judy was three years old and she loved mittens. One day she was in the park with her Mum when she saw the most magical mitten she had ever seen. It was bright purple with golden sparkles. Judy wanted to get it so she asked her Mum: "Mummy, can I have that mitten?". 

"No Judy, I'm sorry. We don't have enough money to buy it," said Mum. 

"But I want it so much," said Judy and she started to cry. Then from behind them, a voice said: "It's alright. I can give it to you for free". Judy turned around and saw an old lady smiling at her. Judy was so happy.

"Thank you! Thank you so much!" said Judy as the old lady handed her the mitten and Judy put it on right away. 

It fit perfectly and Judy couldn't have been happier. She pressed a button on the mitten and suddenly something amazing happened. Judy's mitten began to snap. Judy couldn't believe it. She had a magic mitten and she was so grateful that the old lady had made it available to her. 

From that day on, Judy wore her magical mitten everywhere. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She had a notebook that she loved very much. The notebook was blue and had many pages.

One day, Lily wanted to complete her notebook by drawing a big, happy sun. She took her yellow crayon and started to draw. She made a big circle and then added lines all around it.

When she was done, Lily showed her mommy the picture. Her mommy smiled and said, "Wow, what a pretty sun!" Lily felt happy and proud that she completed her notebook with a beautiful drawing.

Tom and Lily were best friends. They liked to play in the garden and look for bugs. One day, they saw a big, orange carrot in the dirt. They wanted to dig it out and eat it.

"Can I have the shovel?" Tom asked Lily.

"OK, I will lend it to you. But you have to share the carrot with me," Lily said.

Tom nodded and took the shovel. He dug and dug until he pulled out the carrot. It was amazing. It was bigger than his hand and very bright.

"Wow, look at this carrot!" Tom said. "It is so big and pretty!"

He broke the carrot in half and gave one piece to Lily. They both took a bite and smiled. The carrot was sweet and crunchy.

"Thank you for lending me the shovel, Lily. And thank you for sharing the carrot with me," Tom said.

"You're welcome, Tom. You are a good friend," Lily said.

They hugged and ate the rest of the carrot. They were happy and full. They decided to plant the carrot tops in the dirt and hope for more amazing carrots.

Lily loved to bounce on her big red ball. She bounced up and down, left and right, and all around the garden. She bounced so high that she could see the birds and the clouds. She bounced so fast that she felt the wind in her hair. She bounced so much that she laughed and giggled.

One day, her friend Max came to play. He saw Lily bouncing on her ball and he wanted to try. He asked Lily if he could bounce too. Lily said yes, but she made him promise to be careful. She said, "This is my ball and I love it. You can bounce, but you have to give it back to me when we are done. Promise?"

Max nodded and said, "I promise. I will be careful and I will give it back to you." He took the ball from Lily and started to bounce. He bounced up and down, left and right, and all around the garden. He bounced so high that he could see the birds and the clouds. He bounced so fast that he felt the wind in his hair. He bounced so much that he laughed and giggled.

But then, something bad happened. Max bounced too hard and the ball popped. It made a loud noise and the air came out. The ball became flat and sad. Max stopped bouncing and looked at the ball. He felt sorry and scared. He said, "Oh no, I broke your ball. I'm sorry, Lily. I broke my promise."

Lily heard the noise and came running. She saw Max and the ball. She felt angry and sad. She said, "You broke my ball. You broke your promise. You are not my friend." She started to cry and ran away.

Max felt bad and wanted to make Lily happy again. He said, "Wait, Lily. Don't go. I'm sorry, I'm sorry. I will get you a new ball. A bigger and better ball. A brilliant ball. Please, be my friend again."

Lily stopped and turned around. She looked at Max and the ball. She thought for a moment. She said, "You will get me a new ball? A brilliant ball?"

Max nodded and said, "Yes, I will. I promise. I will get you a brilliant ball. A ball that is red and shiny and bouncy. A ball that you will love. Please, be my friend again."

Lily smiled and said, "OK, I will. But you have to keep your promise. You have to get me a brilliant ball. And you have to be careful with it. Promise?"

Max smiled and said, "I promise. I will get you a brilliant ball. And I will be careful with it. Promise."

They hugged and said, "We are friends again."

They went inside and had some juice and cookies. They talked and played and laughed. They waited for the new ball. The brilliant ball. The ball that would make them bounce again.

Once upon a time there was a cute little rabbit. The rabbit lived in a village and was always very happy. One day, the sun was shining brightly and the rabbit thought it was the perfect day to go outside and explore. 

The rabbit went hopping around and soon arrived at the village market. The market was full of all sorts of new and interesting things! The rabbit saw something shiny and decided it was the perfect thing to take home. 

The rabbit asked the market seller for the shiny object. The seller said he was happy to order it for the cute creature! And so the rabbit bought the shiny object. 

The rabbit was so happy, it ran home and showed its family the bought item. All the rabbit's family were happy and thanked the sun for all its wonderful gifts. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max had a flea on his back that made him very itchy. One day, Max met a wise old owl who said, "If you spin around three times, the flea will fall off." Max tried it and it worked! He was so happy and grateful to the owl.

Later that day, Max saw his friend, a cat named Bella, who was crying. "What's wrong, Bella?" asked Max. "I lost my favorite toy mouse," said Bella. "Don't worry, I'll help you find it," said Max, who was always dependable.

They searched everywhere but couldn't find the toy mouse. Just when they were about to give up, Max remembered what the wise old owl had told him. He spun around three times and suddenly, there was the toy mouse! Bella was so happy and grateful to Max.

The moral of the story is that sometimes, the answer to our problems is right in front of us, we just need to spin around and look at things in a different way. And it's always good to be dependable and help our friends when they need us.

One day, Mike saw an amazing thing in the sky. It looked like a never ending universe! He wanted to pick it, because it looked harmless and peaceful. 

He stretched his arm out to try and grab it, but it was much too far away. He tried jumping, but he still couldn't reach it. 

Mike was a bit sad, but then he had an idea! He started to pick a bunch of flowers and made a ladder out of them. He climbed the ladder and saw that it was even more beautiful up close than he had imagined. 

He reached out to pick a star but as he did, it twinkled and flew away! Mike laughed and thought it was magical. In the end, he couldn't pick the universe, but he had a wonderful day looking at it from his flower ladder.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who decided to go for a walk. He went down a path, and all of a sudden he found something. It was a pile of leaves! The little boy decided to sort them into different piles.

He sat down and started to sort the leaves. After a while he started to get really tired, but he kept on sorting. Suddenly, he thought he heard something coming down the path. He stopped sorting, and tried to listen carefully to see what it was.

It was a big, mean, wolf! The wolf was heading right for him! The little boy didn't know what to do, so he tried to build a little wall around himself with the leaves he had been sorting before. But that didn't stop the wolf!

The wolf ate the little boy up! That was the end of the little boy, and the leaves were left lying on the path.

Once there was a little girl called Lily. Lily didn't have much, but she was very happy. One day, Lily wanted to go shopping for something special. She asked her mommy for some money, so she could buy something nice. 
Mommy said, â€œLily, you should look for something cheap, okay?â€ 
Lily said, â€œOkay, Mommy, I will.â€ 
So, Lily went to a shop. She looked around until she saw something she liked. It was a big, white egg. The egg was very cheap. 
Lily said, â€œMommy, can I please buy this egg? It's so cheap!â€ 
Mommy said, â€œYes, Lily, you can come buy the egg!â€ 
Lily was so happy. She took the egg home with her and kissed it. She said, â€œThank you, Mommy!â€ 
It was the best egg ever!

Tim liked to collect stamps. He had many stamps from different places. He put them in a big book. He showed his book to his friends at school. They liked his stamps too. Tim was popular.

One day, a new boy came to school. His name was Sam. He had a big backpack. Tim wanted to be friends with him. He went to Sam and said hello.

"Hello, I am Tim. What is your name?" Tim asked.

"Hello, I am Sam. I am new here." Sam said.

"Do you like stamps?" Tim asked.

"Yes, I do. I have many stamps too. Do you want to see?" Sam asked.

"Yes, please." Tim said.

Sam opened his backpack and took out a big book. He opened it and showed Tim his stamps. Tim was amazed. Sam had many stamps that Tim had never seen before. They were colorful and shiny and had pictures of animals and cars and flowers.

"Wow, your stamps are very nice. Where did you get them?" Tim asked.

"My dad works at the post office. He gives me stamps from different countries. He says stamps are like little windows to the world." Sam said.

"That is cool. Can I have one?" Tim asked.

"Sure, you can have one. Which one do you like?" Sam asked.

Tim looked at the stamps and chose one. It had a picture of a panda. He liked pandas. They were cute and fluffy.

"I like this one. Thank you, Sam." Tim said.

"You are welcome, Tim. Do you want to be my friend?" Sam asked.

"Yes, I do. You are very nice. Do you want to see my stamps?" Tim asked.

"Yes, I do. Let's go to the table and share our stamps." Sam said.

Tim and Sam went to the table and showed each other their stamps. They talked and laughed and traded some stamps. They became good friends. They liked stamps and each other. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who wanted to fly. So she decided to make a missile. She used all the parts she could find, but there was still one part missing - a big red button. She searched high and low, up and down for the last part, but she couldn't find it.

One day, she arrived home and saw a tiny red button on the floor. She picked it up and exclaimed, "This must be the missing part! Now I can make my missile fly."

The little girl quickly put the piece into the machine and stepped back. With a loud roar, the missile began to move. The little girl was so excited and shouted "It's flying! Look, I'm flying!" 

Suddenly her mom came running in. "What's going on here?" She asked.

The little girl turned to her mom and smiled. "I made my missile fly with that little red button!" 

The mom smiled back. "Good job, sweetie. Now let's get you out of that missile before you miss out on any more fun!"

Once upon a time there was a girl who was very curious. Every day she wanted to know more. One day the girl heard about a secret. It was a mysterious secret and she had to find out more.

The girl asked around but nobody would tell her what it was about. She was very frustrated. She knew that it must be something very special!

One day she bumped into her old friend who was always teasing her. He said he knew the secret but he wouldn't tell her unless she did something special. The girl was mad but agreed.

So she gave him all her candy and money, but still the boy wouldn't answer. He just kept on teasing her. In the end she was very sad and the secret remained a mystery.

Once there was a little girl who loved to draw. One day, her pen broke. She was very sad.

Her mom said, "Don't worry. We will repair it." So they went to the shop and they bought a new pen.

The girl wanted to show everyone her pictures. So her mom helped her to print them. They came out looking very different and the girl was very proud.

She thanked her mom for helping her to repair her pen and for printing the pictures. They both laughed and smiled.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. One day Tom went outside and saw a bright, red fire truck parked in the driveway. Tom's eyes lit up and he ran up to the truck, shouting with excitement.

Tom asked his mum if they could get inside. She laughed and opened the door. Tom jumped in and sat down in the special driver's seat. He grabbed the steering wheel and started pushing the pedals. He drove back and forth around the house, pretending he was a real fireman.

Tom drove until he was tired. He then asked his mum to take him to the fair. She agreed, and soon they were off. At the fair, Tom got to ride lots of rides, eat ice-cream and fill up buckets with water from a special fountain.

Tom raced back to the fire truck. He got inside and started pushing the pedals. Soon he was driving back to the house, going as fast as he could. Everyone laughed as they watched him, with a huge smile on his face.

The happy little boy had had a very fair day.

Once there was a humble girl who loved to read. But she didn't have any books. So, she decided to make her own. She got a map and some crayons. She marked roads, rivers, and cities on the map. Then she wrote stories to go with them.

Her stories were all about adventure and exploration. The girl couldn't stop reading her own stories. She would take her map everywhere and every day she would learn something new.

The girl was so excited that she wanted to share her stories with everyone. So, she gathered all of her friends to read the stories too. They all had so much fun!

From then on, the humble girl always kept her map with her. Wherever her adventures took her, the map was sure to come along.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, she was playing with her favorite toy car when she heard a loud sneeze. She looked around and saw her friend Max coming towards her.

"Hi Max," said Lily. "Are you okay? You sneezed very loudly."

"I'm okay," said Max. "I just have a cold."

"Oh no," said Lily. "I hope you feel better soon."

While they were playing, they saw a thief trying to steal Lily's toy car. Max was very impatient and wanted to catch the thief right away. So, he ran after the thief and caught him. They got the toy car back and went home happily.

Once there was a little boy who was always very serious. His mummy wanted to show him to have fun, so she gave him some gum. He held it in his hands, and thought carefully about what to do.

Then, he had an idea. He took out a ruler and decided to measure his gum. First, he measured its length. Then, he measured its width. He measured it very carefully.

When he had finished, he looked at his measurements with pride. Now his gum was well measured, he decided it was time to have a chew. So, he put it in his mouth and enjoyed a delicious snack. Yum!

Once there was a delicate sun. It was so bright and round. Every day it would rise and turn in the sky.

One day, a little girl named Addy looked at the sun. She smiled and said "Sun, you are so pretty". But then something strange happened! 

The sun heard Addy and it started to turn extra fast in the sky. It turned and turned and it started to laugh. Addy was so surprised!

The sun said to Addy â€œI am so happy when you look at me. Thank you for being my friend!â€.

Addy was so happy and she hugged the sun. She said â€œSun, I love you!â€.

From that moment on, Addy and the sun were best friends. Every day the sun would delicately turn in the sky, and Addy would be by its side, smiling.

Once upon a time, Tom the bear was walking through the forest. He was looking for something special and exciting, but he hadn't seen anything yet.

Suddenly, Tom saw a spark in the distance. He got closer and closer until he realized it was a flame!

The flame was bright and warm. He wondered what he should do.

Tom looked around and noticed there were many other furry animals in the forest. He decided to invite them to join him and the flame.

Tom said, "Come, friends! Join me around this warm flame!"

There were two hairy squirrels eager to cuddle up together and keep warm. There were two rabbits who were so excited to join the group. A friendly fox even joined in.

They all snuggled together and stayed warm around the flame that night. They had so much fun playing and telling stories around the fire.

Tom smiled and said, "Thanks for coming to my flame party, friends!"

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big green apple on a tree. Lily wanted to eat it, but Ben wanted to throw it.

"Give me the apple, Lily. I want to play with it," Ben said.

"No, Ben. It is my apple. I want to eat it. It is yummy," Lily said.

They pulled the apple from each other. The apple broke in half. They both dropped the pieces.

"Oh no! We destroyed the apple!" Lily cried.

A bird flew down and picked up one piece. A squirrel ran and took the other piece.

"Look, Lily. The bird and the squirrel are happy. They like the apple," Ben said.

"Maybe they are hungry. Maybe we can share with them," Lily said.

They smiled and waved at the bird and the squirrel. They went to find more apples to share.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient land. It had been kept secret and no one knew what was inside.

One day, a brave child called Joey decided to explore the land. She packed her bag then went on an adventure. Joey walked and walked until she arrived at the ancient land.

She looked around but it all seemed quiet. Then, suddenly, something began to move. Joey was scared but then she was amazed when a beautiful bird flew out of the land!

The bird revealed a secret. Inside the ancient land were trees, flowers and all kinds of animals. Joey was so excited. She told her friends about this amazing discovery!

Once upon a time, there was a kind bunny named Benny. Benny loved to race with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny's friend, a turtle named Timmy, asked him for help. "Can you serve me some carrots? I'm very hungry," said Timmy. Benny happily gave Timmy some carrots to eat.

Later that day, Benny and Timmy were racing when they saw a snail who was struggling to cross a big rock. Timmy remembered how Benny had served him earlier and said, "Let's help the snail cross the rock." Benny agreed and they both helped the snail. 

After the race, Benny and Timmy were very happy. They realized that helping others made them feel good inside. They learned that being kind and helpful to others is important. From that day on, Benny and Timmy always looked for ways to serve and help others.

Once upon a time, there was a big, old house with a tall chimney. The chimney was very ancient and had been there for a long time. One day, a bird flew into the chimney and got stuck inside. The bird was very scared and didn't know what to do.

Luckily, a kind man came to help the bird. He climbed up the roof and carefully released the bird from the chimney. The bird was very happy and flew away into the blue sky. The man felt proud of himself for helping the little bird and went back inside the house with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a girl who had a tooth that was wiggly. She was very embarrassed. She did not want to show anyone else her wiggly tooth.

One day, the girl went to the park with her mom and dad. There was a slippery slide at the park and the girl wanted to go down it. Her mom said no.

So instead, the girl came up with a plan. She would crawl down the slide! She took off her shoes, went to the top of the slide and started crawling down.

The girl was so excited to be having so much fun. At the bottom of the slide she heard a loud CRUNCH! She looked at her mouth and the wiggly tooth had fallen out!

The girl was embarrassed but also happy because she had finally gotten rid of her wiggly tooth. The girl's parents were very proud of her for being brave and trying something new.

Once there was a girl called Katie. She was 3 years old. One day, she wanted to take a nice cross - it was bright and colourful, and she thought it was very pretty.

So, she went outside and found a cross. She took it and hugged it tight. She was very happy to have her own nice cross.

Katie took her cross to the garden and played with it. She made a game where she pretended to be an explorer looking for a hidden treasure. She pretended to take her nice cross with her on her adventure - just like all the brave explorers did.

Katie played for a long time until it was time to go back inside. She took her cross and hugged it one last time. She felt very happy and excited to keep playing the next day with her special cross.

Once there was a little girl named Lily who loved the rug in her bedroom. She could cuddle up on the rug and feel safe. On this special day, Lily couldn't find her rug. She looked everywhere in her room, but she couldn't see it! She started to tremble, feeling scared and confused.

Suddenly, Lily heard a voice coming from beneath her bed. It said "Here I am, Lily! I'm hiding under your bed!". Lily crawled onto her bed and looked over the edge, and she spotted her rug tucked away in a hidden corner.

Lily smiled and said "Oh rug, why did you hide from me?". The rug replied by saying "I was feeling lonely and thought maybe if I hid, you'd come and find me. Now I'm happy you're here!".

Lily smiled even wider and said "I'll never let you be lonely again rug!". Then she stretched out on top of the rug and cuddled into it. Suddenly, the rug didn't feel lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there was a dog named Rhythm. Rhythm was a very happy dog. He loved to play and dance all day long. His favorite thing to do was to tap his feet to the sound of the music playing in the town square.

One day, while Rhythm was dancing, he saw a little bird stuck in a tree. The bird was scared and couldn't fly away. Rhythm wanted to help, so he barked very loud to call his friend, Kitty the cat.

Kitty came running and asked, "What's wrong, Rhythm?" Rhythm pointed to the bird and said, "We need to rescue the bird. Can you help?" Kitty nodded and climbed up the tree. She carefully picked up the bird and brought it down to the ground.

The little bird was so happy to be free. It flapped its wings and sang a beautiful song. Rhythm and Kitty danced to the music, and they all became the best of friends. From that day on, they played and danced together every day, making the busy little town even happier.

Once upon a time there was a cute little girl. Every day she would love to play and sing her favorite song. Her song was so catchy! Every day she would repeat her song over and over again, until it was almost dark. 

One day, the little girl was walking around and singing her song when she met a big mean monster. He was so ugly and he growled at the little girl. He asked her to stop singing her song, but the little girl refused. 

The monster got very angry and he grabbed the little girl. She was so scared that she started to cry. But the monster didn't care, he just held the girl tightly and refused to let her go. 

The little girl never sang her song again. The monster kept her trapped and made sure that she never sang again. So the little girl never shared her cute song with the world again.  This is why you should always be careful who you meet when you are out and about in the world.

Once there was a boy named John. He was three years old and loved to explore the world around him. One day, he decided to take a walk in the woods.

John stepped carefully along the path, keeping an eye out for any interesting things he could explore. Suddenly he heard a song coming from deep in the woods. He stopped to listen.

"That sounds like a nice song," he said to himself.

He stepped cautiously towards the sound. He pushed aside the branches of a bush and saw a bird singing. The bird was tweeting a happy tune.

John was so happy that he began to dance and sing along to the bird's song. He got so carried away that he stepped right into a muddy puddle. Now his shoes were dirty.

He laughed at himself as he stepped away from the puddle. He continued his walk through the woods, feeling happy and content. As he walked, he hummed the bird's song to himself.

Once upon a time there was a small flag. The flag wanted to surprise something, so it started to flutter. It moved up and down, but it wasn't fast enough. So it thought of a plan. It asked two birds to help it. 

The birds were happy to help and flapped their wings quickly. The small flag flew high and far. It was so excited and it waved to the sky. Everywhere it went, it brought a surprise. 

The small flag was now the most famous flag in the world. It made many people happy. So it kept flying until it was tired. Then it rested on a tall tree with a smile.

Once upon a time, there were two friends; Sam and Emily. Sam and Emily decided to go on an adventure. They came across a big, bossy tree. Sam and Emily saw that the tree was offering a mystery! They both got excited and couldn't wait to see what the tree had to offer. 

The tree asked them to help her pick apples. She was very bossy and made sure they did the job just right. After they finished picking the apples, the tree finally revealed the mystery. It was a special surprise for both Sam and Emily. The tree had given them two bags full of toys! 

Sam and Emily couldn't believe it. They thanked the tree and ran off with their toys. They spent the rest of the day playing with the toys and laughed and smiled the entire time. The mystery was solved!

Once upon a time, there was a mouse. He was very brave and liked to go on adventures. One day, the mouse set out to explore a hidden cave. He took a few steps inside and noticed that the cave was dark and scary. He called out, "Hello? Is anyone there?" 

Suddenly, a voice answered back, "I'm here!" The mouse looked around and saw a bigger mouse in the shadows. The bigger mouse said, ""Go away or I'll bite you!" 

The brave mouse was scared and started to run away. But on his way out, he heard a roar. He quickly looked and saw a big cat. The cat said, "you shouldn't be here, little mouse. You will be my dinner!"

The mouse tried to run away, but it was too late. The cat quickly pounced and caught him. The mouse was never seen again. The moral of this story is that things that are hidden can be dangerous and it's important to be careful.

One time, Mommy and Daddy made a promise. They said, "We will always take care of you and keep you safe." That night, a cop came to their house. He looked so weird! But Mommy and Daddy weren't scared. They said, "We made a promise to take care of our child." 

The cop nodded. He said, "We have to make sure you keep your promise, so I'm going to stay here with you." And he did! He stayed with them all night, watching over them. Mommy and Daddy were so happy. 

The next morning, the cop said goodbye and thanked them for keeping their promise. Mommy and Daddy smiled and hugged their child. They were so happy that they kept their promise. 

From then on, they knew they would always keep their promises. And they knew they could count on the cop to help them keep their promises, too.

Sam was a three-year-old girl who lived in a big city. Each day she would wake up, looking out of her window at the tall buildings. When she looked out one day, she saw something wonderful - a huge colourful train. She watched as the train went along the rail, and passed her window. Sam was so excited that she just had to get closer.

So the next day, Sam and her family went to the rail station. Sam loved everything she saw - the machinery, the tracks, and the unique-looking train. She felt so small and excited standing near the rail. 

Suddenly, the train started to move. It moved slowly at first, but quickly gained momentum. Sam found herself running along the rail, with the train still ahead of her. It felt wild and exhilarating!

Soon, Sam and the train reached the city centre. Sam waved goodbye to the train as it left the station. She had had a unique and wonderful experience, and knew she would never forget it.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Grace. She was three years old and liked to dress up in fancy clothes.

One day, Grace put on a beautiful dress. As she looked in the mirror, she felt so happy.

But when she saw her friend, she felt envious. Her friend was wearing a party dress, too. It was more sparkly than Grace's. She wished she had a dress like that.

So, Grace took a deep breath and closed her eyes. She said a little prayer. She asked God to give her a dress like her friend's.

The next day, Grace was very excited. She opened her wardrobe and saw a beautiful dress in there. It was just like her friend's!

Grace smiled and thanked God for his kindness. From then on, she thanked him every day for all the blessings in her life.

Mary was nervous, her heart trembled like thunder in her chest. She looked at the icy mask in her hand, it looked scary but she had to wear it. She took a deep breath and put it on her face. It was cold against her skin and made her shiver.

Mary walked out of her bedroom and down the hallway. Her mouth felt dry and her legs felt weak, but she kept moving. Suddenly a big, loud noise made her tremble. Her brother had jumped out from behind a corner and scared her. She let out a gasp and laughed a little.

Finally Mary reached the end of the hallway and opened the door. Outside the sky was dark and clouds filled the sky. She took a deep breath. She could feel the icy wind against her face and knew that it was going to be a cold day. She grabbed the mask in her hands and started walking, trembling a bit with every step.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird with a dull wing. He wanted to fly high in the sky with his friends, but he couldn't because of his wing. One day, he met a kind girl who set his wing straight. 

The little bird was so happy that he could finally fly again. He flapped his wings and soared into the sky. He saw all the beautiful trees and flowers below him. 

From that day on, the little bird and the girl became great friends. They would play together and have fun. The little bird was grateful for the girl who set his wing and helped him fly again.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Carla who loved to catch bugs. She would catch all kinds of creepy crawly bugs in the garden. One day she noticed a bright blue bug and she decided she wanted to catch it. She ran around and around the garden but the bug was too fast! She chased the bug until she was all out of breath.

Suddenly, a big white napkin landed on the blue bug! Carla cautiously picked the napkin up and carefully opened it; and there it was, a beautiful blue bug! She was so excited! 

Carla sat in the garden to enjoy her catch. But soon, she realized that it wasn't as exciting as she thought it was going to be. She looked around for something else to do but all she could find was an old, boring tree.

Carla approached the tree and asked, "Hey, tree. Do you have anything fun to do?"

The tree said, "I may not look like it, but I'm full of surprises. Come and take a closer look and see what you can catch!" 

Carla was delighted and soon she was collecting leaves and petals, she made herself a colourful crown, and she even caught a butterfly! She had a great time exploring the tree and the garden with her new found treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old dog. His name was Spot. He lived in a very nice house with some kind people. 

Every morning, the people would get out of bed and give Spot some breakfast. He usually got a big bowl of food, and then he'd move around and play with the people. 

One morning, the people had something special for Spot. It was a big, yummy cake. Spot loved cake, and he wanted to move closer to the people so he could get closer to the cake. But the people said, "No, Spot. This cake is for us. You can't have any!"

Spot was very sad. He looked up at the people and whined. The people saw how sad Spot was, and then they realised that Spot was a wise old dog and he deserved something special, too. So they moved the cake a little closer to Spot and said, "Ok, you can have just one piece."

Spot was so happy! He moved closer to the cake, wagged his tail, and slowly ate the cake. When he was done, Spot gave the people lots of licks and thanked them with a big, happy bark!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was very excited because his grandpa had given him a big whistle. Jack loved to blow on the whistle and it made a loud sound.  

One day, Jack and his dad went for a walk in the woods. It was the wildest place Jack had ever seen with lots of trees and bugs. As his dad watched him, Jack blew his whistle as loud as he could. Suddenly, an animal popped out of the bushes. It was a fox! 

The fox jumped around in circles and started to do tricks. Whenever Jack blew on his whistle, the fox did a new trick. His dad laughed and clapped his hands.
