Jack was so excited and he wanted to do something nice for the fox. He dug his hand into his pocket and found a tip that his grandpa gave him. He threw the tip to the fox and the fox quickly caught it. 

The fox thanked Jack by wagging his tail, then hopped into the woods. Jack and his dad waved goodbye as the fox disappeared into the wild.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play in their room with their toys. But sometimes they fought over the toys. One day, Ben wanted to play with the big truck, but Sam had it. Ben tried to take it from Sam, but Sam was stronger. He pushed Ben away and said, "No, it's mine!"

Ben was angry. He looked around the room and saw a cloth. He had an idea. He grabbed the cloth and ran to the door. He locked the door with the cloth. He said, "Ha, ha, now you can't get out!"

Sam was scared. He banged on the door and shouted, "Let me out, Ben! Let me out!" But Ben did not listen. He laughed and played with the truck. He thought he was smart.

But he did not know that Mom was coming. She heard the noise and went to the room. She tried to open the door, but it was locked. She asked, "What's going on in there? Who locked the door?"

Ben heard Mom's voice and felt sorry. He realized he was mean to Sam. He said, "I did, Mom. I'm sorry. I locked the door with a cloth."

Mom said, "That was not nice, Ben. You should not lock your brother in the room. You should share your toys. Now, take the cloth off the door and open it."

Ben did what Mom said. He took the cloth off the door and opened it. He saw Sam crying. He said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I was wrong. Do you want to play with the truck?"

Sam nodded and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Ben. I forgive you. Can we play together?"

Ben said, "Yes, we can. I love you, Sam."

They hugged and played with the truck. Mom was happy. She said, "That's better. I'm proud of you, boys. Now, be nice to each other."

Once upon a time, there was a shy little fish who lived in the big blue sea. One day, the fish saw a big shark swimming nearby. The fish was scared and tried to swim away, but the shark followed it.

The fish saw a boat and thought it could hide there. The boat was loading things onto it, so the fish swam inside to hide. But the boat was actually going to take the things to a faraway land, and the fish was trapped.

The shark followed the boat, and when it got to the faraway land, it ate the little fish. The end.

Mum was cooking dinner. She got a big knife and cut up some spaghetti. She put it into some boiling water. Bruno watched her seriously.

Mum put some butter and cheese on the spaghetti. Bruno wanted to help. She gave him a spoon and he stirred the spaghetti. It was fun!

Once it was ready, Mum took it off the heat. She put the spaghetti onto a plate and brought it to the table. Bruno was so excited!

Mum said it was time to eat. Bruno smiled and grabbed his fork. He had the first bite and it was delicious! He could hardly wait to have more. 

Mum smiled and said serious, "Let's enjoy this spaghetti".

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She knew just how to make the sun shine.

The little girl went outside and there were big puddles everywhere. She felt anxious but she was excited too. She took a big step and jumped right into the biggest puddle.

She covered the puddle with happy steps and squeals of joy. The sun came out and it warmed her all over. She smiled and felt safe and happy.

The little girl kept dancing and jumping until the puddle was all covered up. Now she could play in the sunshine for ever. She smiled and was no longer anxious.

Once upon a time there lived a boy named Jack. He was curious to explore the world around him. One day he decided to take a walk in the forest. While walking, he saw a large whip! Jack wondered what it was and was so curious that he decided to take it.

When Jack brought the whip back home, his mom saw him and asked him where he got it. Jack told his mom he found it in the forest. His mom said "I think it is better if you remain here with me, Jack!"

Jack was disappointed and started to cry. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Jack! We can go back to the forest tomorrow and leave it back where it was".

Jack was so excited and couldn't wait to go back to the forest the next day. He grabbed his mom's hand and said, "Let's go, Mom!". So the next day, Jack and his mom went back to the forest and found the same spot where Jack had found the whip. They left it there, and Jack smiled happily, knowing that he had done the right thing.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Fred. Fred loved to hop and play with his friends. One day, Fred saw an attractive red blanket on the grass. It was a picnic! He hopped over to take a closer look.

At the picnic, there were many yummy foods like apples, cheese, and bread. Fred's tummy rumbled. He wanted to eat some food too. But there was a big, mean bird at the picnic. The bird said, "No, Fred! You can't have any food. This is my picnic!"

Fred felt sad and hungry. He hopped back to his friends and told them about the mean bird. His friends wanted to help. They all hopped together to the picnic. There were so many frogs hopping that the bird got scared and flew away.

Now, Fred and his friends could enjoy the picnic. They shared the yummy food and had a great time. From that day on, they knew that together they could face any problem. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little boy named James who loved to zoom. Everywhere he went, he zoomed. He zoomed around his house, around the yard and even around school. He thought it was so much fun!

One day, James was zooming around his yard when he felt a sharp pain in his leg. He fell down and started to cry. He didn't want to move. His mom and dad came right away and asked what had happened.

James told them that he had zoomed and felt pain in his leg. They took him to the doctor. The doctor said that James had strained a muscle while zooming and gave him some healthy medicine to make it all better.

Soon, James was feeling healthy again. He promised himself he'd go slower next time he zoomed around. He wanted to stay healthy and have fun. And that's exactly what he did!

Once upon a time, there was a very selfish boy who loved to scare his friends. One day, he brought a gas mask to school and he wanted to scare everyone. He even put on the gas mask himself and then tried to scare his friends.

His friends were scared and became angry. One of them said, "Why are you so selfish?"

The boy realized that it wasn't nice to scare his friends. He told them, "I'm sorry. I won't do this again."

His friends were happy and then all of them played together in the playground. They all had a lot of fun and the boy now knows better than to scare his friends.

Once upon a time there was a powerful warrior who had a special spear. He was strong and brave and used the spear to protect his kingdom.

One day, he found an old magical wand and decided to mix the wand with his special spear. He waved the wand over the spear and said some special words.

Suddenly, lightning crackled and smoke filled the air. When the smoke cleared, the warrior was amazed to see that his spear had changed. It was even more powerful and shone in the light.

The warrior was so pleased with his new powerful spear. He thanked the magical wand, and promised to use it to protect his kingdom forever.

Once upon a time, there was a big bus. Every day, it was busy taking people to their destinations. One day, it drove to a big town.

When the bus arrived, a little girl came out. Her name was Lola. She had been on an adventure and was making her way back home.

As she walked, she met an old woman. "Good morning child," said the old woman. "What brings you here?

Lola smiled and replied, "I am returning from a very long journey. I went to a magical place and had so many adventures! I even heard a story about a beautiful princess!"

The old woman smiled and said, "That sounds like a wonderful experience. I am sure you enjoyed it."

Lola nodded in agreement, then said goodbye to the old woman and continued her journey. Over the next few days, she made her way back home, remembering the busy days on the bus and the magical stories she had heard.

Lily and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big box on the table. It had a shiny paper and a bow.

"Let's open it!" Lily said. She grabbed a knife from the drawer.

"No, no, no!" Tom said. "That is not for us. That is for Mommy. And the knife is sharp. It can hurt you."

"But I want to see what is inside. Maybe it is a toy or a book or a cake." Lily said. She tried to cut the paper with the knife.

Tom ran to the door and called for Mommy. "Mommy, Mommy, come quick! Lily has a knife and she is opening your box!"

Mommy came into the kitchen and saw Lily with the knife and the box. She was angry and scared. She took the knife from Lily and put it away. She looked at the box and saw a hole in the paper.

"Oh, Lily, what have you done? This is a very special gift from Grandma. She made it for me. It is a scarf. She wrapped it with love and care. And you ruined it with the knife." Mommy said.

Lily felt bad. She did not mean to make Mommy sad. She saw the scarf in the box. It was red and blue and green. It had flowers and stars and hearts. It was very pretty. But it was also very smelly.

"Mommy, why is the scarf smelly?" Lily asked.

Mommy sniffed the scarf and made a face. "Oh, no. The scarf is smelly because Grandma has a cat. And the cat likes to sleep on the scarf. And the cat is not very clean. He has fleas and dirt and hair. And he pees on the scarf. That is why it is smelly." Mommy said.

Lily and Tom made a face too. They did not like the smelly scarf. They did not want to touch it or wear it.

"Mommy, can we throw away the smelly scarf?" Lily asked.

Mommy thought for a moment. She loved Grandma and she knew Grandma loved her. She did not want to hurt Grandma's feelings. But she also did not want to keep the smelly scarf.

"Maybe we can wash the smelly scarf and make it clean and nice. And then we can wrap it again and send it back to Grandma. And we can say thank you and we love you. And we can ask her to make us a new scarf without the cat." Mommy said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They liked that idea. They helped Mommy wash the smelly scarf and dry it and wrap it. They wrote a card for Grandma and put it in the box. They hoped Grandma would understand and not be mad. They also hoped Grandma would make them a new scarf that was not smelly.

Once, there was a girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old. Every day she asked her mom if they could go out to the park. Today, mommy said yes. 

When they got to the park, Lucy saw two friends playing on the swing. "Can I swing too?" asked Lucy.

The two boys lent Lucy the swing so she could play too. She had so much fun!

Then, Lucy wanted to have some fun in the sand. She lent her mom a little bucket and filled it up with sand. But she needed something else too.

"Mommy, can I have some salt?" asked Lucy.

Mommy smiled. She knew that Lucy wanted to make sand castles. She lent Lucy some salt and Lucy carefully sprinkled it on the sand. Suddenly, the sand became so solid that it didn't move.

"Wow, now my sandcastle looks so fragile!" exclaimed Lucy.

Mommy smiled. She was so proud of her daughter.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. Their names were Max and Molly. 

Max and Molly were both very silly. They loved having fun together, and giggled all the time.

One day, they decided to go outside to play. But when they were outside, they heard some strange noises. Max asked Molly "what is that sound?"

Molly said "listen, Max. It's the sound of lightning. Can you hear it? Listen closely."

Max listened very carefully. Sure enough, he heard the lightning, which was loud and funny. 

Max was so excited that he started jumping around and giggling. Molly also laughed and said "you're so silly, Max!" 

The two best friends enjoyed listening to the thunder and lightning all night, until it was time to go to bed.

One day, Max went to the zoo. He was very enthusiastic to see all the animals. He saw lots of animals: lions, tigers, monkeys, bears, and zebras. He was so excited when he saw the zebra and he wanted to take it home. 

His mom said, â€œWe can't take it home Max, but feel free to look at it from outside its cage.â€ Max nodded and walked over to the zebra's enclosure. He looked at it and smiled. The zebra had black and white stripes and a long tail. 

Max waved at the zebra and said, â€œHi, I'm Max!â€ The zebra waved its tail and ran around in circles. Max laughed and waved goodbye. He was so happy to have seen the zebra, he couldn't stop smiling. 

Max and his mom waved goodbye and went home, with Max telling everyone about the enthusiastic zebra.

Once upon a time, there was a furry bunny named Bob. Bob loved to play in the hay. One day, he went to the hay field to play with his friends.

Bob's mom said, "Don't forget to come home before dark, Bob!" Bob said, "Okay, Mom!" and hopped away to play. He played with his friends all day. They made a big hay castle. They had so much fun!

As the sun went down, Bob remembered what his mom said. He hopped back home before it got dark. When he got home, his mom was happy. She said, "Good job, Bob! You didn't forget!" They had a big hug and went to bed.

One day, John wanted to go slide. He ran off to the playground with his diary.

At first he wasn't sure which slide to go down. He looked around and noticed the ordinary slide. He decided to give it a try and climbed up the ladder. Once up, he happily sat down and then slid down and around the curves.

John laughed as the wind rushed past his face. He slid all the way to the bottom and jumped off the slide.

He opened his diary and wrote about how much fun he had sliding down the ordinary slide. He knew he'd come back to the playground soon to go down the slide again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went for a walk in the park with her mom. Suddenly, she saw a little boy playing with a pipe. "Mommy, who is he?" asked Lily. "I don't know, let's go introduce ourselves," replied her mom.

"Hi, my name is Lily, what's your name?" asked Lily. "My name is Timmy, nice to meet you," said the little boy. "That's a lovely pipe you have there, can I play with it too?" asked Lily. "Sure, let's play together," said Timmy. They played together and had lots of fun.

After a while, it was time to go home. "Goodbye, Timmy. It was nice to meet you and play with your lovely pipe," said Lily. "Goodbye, Lily. Let's play again soon," said Timmy. Lily and her mom walked home, happy to have made a new friend.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big yellow building. It has many windows and doors. They wonder what is inside.

"Let's go and look," Ben says. He runs to the building. Anna follows him.

They find a door that is open. They go inside. It is dark and quiet. They see many things. There are chairs, tables, books, and toys. They also see a big bed.

"Wow, this is a nice place," Anna says. She goes to the bed. She lies on it. It is soft and warm. She feels sleepy.

"Anna, come on, let's play," Ben says. He picks up a toy car. He makes it go vroom vroom on the floor.

"No, I want to lie here," Anna says. She closes her eyes. She likes the bed.

"Anna, we have to go," Ben says. He hears a noise. He looks at the door. He sees a woman. She is wearing a yellow dress. She looks angry.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" the woman says. She walks to the bed. She sees Anna.

Ben is scared. He drops the toy car. He runs to Anna. He shakes her.

"Anna, wake up, we have to go," he says. He pulls her hand.

Anna opens her eyes. She sees the woman. She is scared too.

"Sorry, we were just playing," she says. She jumps off the bed. She follows Ben.

They run to the door. They go outside. They run to the park. They do not look back.

They do not like the yellow building anymore.

Once upon a time there was a big exam. It was hard for some of the kids, but not for Susie. She was going to pass it easily!

Susie studied hard for the exam. Every day she printed out notes so she could learn them. Slowly and steadily, she was learning more and more.

On the day of the exam, Susie felt soft and calm. She carefully printed her answers and smiled when she was done. She knew she had done well.

When the results came out, Susie was very proud. She had gotten the highest marks in the class! Everyone was so proud of her. They cheered and hugged her, and Susie was the happiest girl in the world!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was an adorable dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his red ball. He would run, jump, and roll with his ball all day long.

One day, Spot found a band of friends. They were all different animals: a cat, a bird, and a rabbit. They played together every day, and they had so much fun. They would chase each other, hide, and find new things to play with.

But one day, they found a big, brown apple under a tree. The apple was not good to eat, it was old and starting to rot. The animals did not want to play with the apple, so they left it alone. Instead, they found a big, green leaf to play with. They all took turns jumping on the leaf and laughing. And so, Spot and his band of friends had fun every day, and they were very happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with a big ball. They bounce the ball to each other. Sometimes the ball goes too high or too far. Then they run to get it.

One day, they find a bunch of grapes on the table. They are purple and shiny. Anna and Ben want to eat them. They each take one grape and put it in their mouth. They are sweet and juicy.

"Let's play with the grapes!" Ben says. He throws a grape in the air and tries to catch it with his mouth. He misses and the grape falls on the floor.

Anna laughs. She tries to do the same. She throws a grape in the air and opens her mouth. But the grape bounces off her nose and lands on the sofa.

"It's difficult to catch the grapes!" Anna says.

They try again and again. But they can't catch any grapes. The grapes bounce everywhere. Some bounce on the table, some bounce on the chairs, some bounce on the windows.

Soon, there are no more grapes on the bunch. Anna and Ben look around. They see grapes all over the room. They also see their mom coming in.

"Uh-oh," they say.

Lily and Tom were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and bridges with the colorful blocks. They were having fun and making noises.

But then, their big brother Sam came in. He was bored and wanted to play too. He saw the blocks and had a bad idea. He decided to destroy what Lily and Tom had built. He kicked and smashed and threw the blocks everywhere. He laughed and said, "This is more fun!"

Lily and Tom were very sad and angry. They saw their blocks broken and scattered. They cried and shouted, "Stop it, Sam! You are mean and naughty! You ruined our game!"

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and the tears. She was not happy with Sam. She scolded him and said, "Sam, what did you do? You should not destroy your siblings' toys. You should be kind and share. Go to your room and think about what you did."

She hugged Lily and Tom and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. Don't worry, we can fix the blocks and play again. You did a good job building. I'm proud of you." She helped them pick up the blocks and put them in a box. She gave them some cookies and milk and said, "Let's go to the couch and read a story. That will make you feel better."

Lily and Tom nodded and smiled. They followed Mom to the couch and snuggled with her. They felt comfortable and safe. They listened to Mom's voice and looked at the pictures. They forgot about Sam and the blocks. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a bright bus. The bus was full of happy people, all wearing big smiles. One of the people on the bus was a little boy. He had bright eyes and bushy hair. He always smiled and was very friendly.

As the bus drove around, the boy looked out the window. He saw lots of interesting things: cars, trees, and birds. His face lit up, and he smiled. He was having lots of fun on the bus ride.

When the bus reached its destination, the boy got off. He waved goodbye to everyone on the bus and still had a big smile on his face. He waved and waved until the bus drove away. Then the little boy walked happily home, his face still filled with a bright smile.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the zoo with her mommy. They saw many animals like lions, tigers, and monkeys. But Lily's favorite animal was the hippo. She loved how big and round it was.

One day, Lily and her mommy went to see the hippo again. But when they got there, they saw a surprise! The hippo had a big cake in front of it. Lily was so happy and surprised. The hippo was celebrating its birthday!

Lily's mommy asked if she wanted to try the cake, but Lily said no. She thought the cake looked bitter. Instead, they sang "Happy Birthday" to the hippo and watched it eat the cake. It was a fun and surprising day at the zoo.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient owl. The owl lived alone in the forest and it liked to measure things. Every day, it measured the trees and the animals. It counted the leaves and measured the rocks. One day, it measured a butterfly and the butterfly flew away. The owl kept on measuring things, each one carefully. 

Then one day, it found something amazing! It was a tiny castle made of twigs and leaves. It was so small, the owl had to use a feather to measure it. When the owl opened the door, a group of animals came out. They were so surprised to see the owl measuring their castle. 

The animals asked the owl to measure them too. So the owl flew around them, counting and measuring as it went. When it was done, everyone cheered. They thanked the owl for coming and measuring the castle, and they asked it to come back soon. 

The ancient owl was so happy. It had found a special place in the forest, and it had made some new friends. From then on, the owl measured everything with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved pieces, so one day she decided to go and pick some pieces in the hot sun. She looked around, but she could not find any pieces. She was feeling sad.

Just then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. She followed the rainbow and it led her to a little house. When she opened the door, she saw a big pile of pieces. Daisy was so happy! She trusted the rainbow and it led her to pieces. 

She spent the day happily playing with the pieces. She had fun building castles and towers with them. When Daisy was finished, she was happy and warm from playing in the hot sun. 

She never forgot the day that the rainbow showed her the pieces. She learned to trust. And she liked to remember that special day.

Once there was a rich man who lived in a very big house. He had many friends who came to visit him often and they would always sit around his big network of tables and chairs.

One day he had a special visitor, a little 3 year old girl. She was amazed at how nice his house was.

"Wow, what a beautiful house!" she said.

The rich man smiled. "Thank you!" he replied.

The girl looked around and noticed something moving under the tables. She pointed to it and asked "What is that?"

The rich man said "That is a big puppy, he loves to lie down under the tables".

The girl was so excited and ran to pet the puppy.

The rich man looked at her with a big smile and said "I am so glad you like my big network of friends and family here in the house".

The little girl was so happy and gave the rich man a big hug. From that day on, the little girl and the rich man were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Emily. She was only three years old and she loved to explore the world around her. One day, Emily was in the living room and she saw a big seat. She did not know what the seat was for, so she asked her mom.

"Mom, what is this seat for?" Emily inquired.

"It is for you, Emily! You can sit in it to watch your favorite cartoon," her mom explained.

Emily was so excited and ran over to the seat. She jumped into the seat and started to watch her favorite cartoon. She had so much fun and sat in the seat for a whole zero minutes! After that, Emily said goodbye to the seat and went to do something else. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big race in the forest. All the animals were very excited to join. The rabbit, the fox, and the bear were very competitive. They all wanted to win the race.

As they were running, the rabbit suddenly felt something strange in his chest. He stopped and told the other animals, "My chest hurts. It's hard to breathe." The fox said, "Maybe you just need to take a break." But the bear said, "No, we need to keep going. We can't stop now."

The rabbit tried to keep up, but he couldn't. He fell behind and the other animals didn't notice. Suddenly, he fell to the ground and couldn't move. The other animals eventually realized he was missing and went back to look for him. But it was too late. The rabbit had squeezed too hard and his chest couldn't take it. He was gone forever. The other animals were very sad and learned an important lesson to always take care of each other.

Mandy and Jack were best friends. Every day they would go out to play and explore the world. Today they decided to go to the forest. 

As they walked down the path they began to see all sorts of things. They saw a tree with a squirrel on it. They saw a butterfly fluttering around some flowers. Then suddenly, they saw something sparkly. It was a mine!

Mandy quickly raced over and picked it up. She was so excited she wanted to keep it.

Jack was tired and getting sleepy. "Let's attach it to your bag so we can keep it safe. That way, if we get too tired we can take it home with us," he said.

Mandy smiled and agreed. She quickly attach the mine to her bag. Then they continued their journey. 

Little did they know, the mine contained some pretty rare and precious stones. They had struck gold! But they still oblivious to this, they continued on. 

By the end of the day they were both feeling very sleepy. They got back to Mandy's house and quickly discovered the treasure within the mine. 

They both squealed with excitement! They had found a mine filled with precious gems. What a wonderful and exciting day they had.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annie. She was only three years old but she was full of energy and liked to explore. One day, she was walking in the forest and came across a clearing. In the middle of the clearing was an arrow. 
 Annie was nosy and wanted to take a closer look. She walked up to the arrow and suddenly a voice shouted at her from behind, â€œBe careful not to touch it!â€ Annie jumped back in fright and saw an old man.  
 
The old man said, â€œMy name is Wilbur and I was just minding my own business when I saw you walking towards the arrow. I was worried that you may get injured, so I shouted.â€
