Once upon a time, there was a big octopus. He lived in the deep blue sea. He had a friend, a reliable fish. They played together every day.

One day, the octopus and the fish found a big jug. They wanted to pour water on their friends for fun. But they couldn't agree on who would pour the water. The octopus said, "I want to pour the water!" The fish said, "No, I want to pour the water!" They were not happy.

Then, the octopus had an idea. He said, "Let's both pour the water!" The fish liked the idea. They picked up the big jug together and poured water on all their friends. Everyone laughed and had fun. The octopus and the fish were happy again. They learned to share and play together. And they lived happily ever after.

Mommy was so excited to take Lily to the park. They hopped in the car, and drove to the park. When they got there, Lily squealed with excitement, and ran around the park. They took out some snacks, and shared them with the ducks! 

Lily wanted to explore the playground, so Mommy followed her from slide to slide. Suddenly, she watched Lily jump into a big drain, filled with dark water. Lily's face lit up, but Mommy shouted "No!", and she looked very scared. 

Mommy quickly ran to pull her out, but she regretted not watching Lily closer. They had a strong hug, and Mommy explained why this was dangerous. Lily nodded her head, and said "Okay". 

After that, Mommy made sure to always keep her close, and keep an eye out for dangers. They had more fun, and left the park with lots of smiles!

Once upon a time, there was a little train. The train was chugging along when it saw a station. The train wanted to stop at the station, so it slowed down and came to a stop. 

At the station, there was a tough-looking conductor. The conductor helped the train pass through the station safely. The train was happy to have passed the station with the conductor's help. 

As the train continued on its journey, it passed many more stations. Each time, the conductor helped the train pass through safely. The train was grateful for the conductor's help and knew it couldn't have done it without him.

One day, a boy named Tim went with his mom to get on the subway. Tim was very excited. He had never been on the subway before. His mom told him that the ride might be a bit rough, but not to worry.

As they waited, Tim saw a big, red ball on the ground. He picked it up and wanted to keep it. His mom said they could take it with them. When the subway came, they got on and found a seat. Tim held the ball tight.

The subway started to move and it was a little rough, just like his mom said. Tim's ball rolled out of his hands and went far away. A nice man found the ball and gave it back to Tim. Tim was very happy and learned that even when things get rough, everything can be okay in the end.

Once upon a time there was a boy named John. He wanted to take a ride in a helicopter. So one day, he asked his mommy, â€œCan I please take a ride in a helicopter?â€ His mommy said, â€œI donâ€™t know, John. That costs a lot of money.â€ 

But John was very persistent. Every day he asked and every day his mom said no. One day, his mommy had had enough. She said, â€œAll right, John. Iâ€™ll see if we can find a way to make it happen.â€

John was so excited. After a few days, they found a way to take the helicopter ride. John put on his best shirt and they went to the airport. Soon, they hopped in the helicopter and took off. 

John was so happy. The wind whipped through his hair and the clouds marbled in the sky. He smiled and laughed the whole time he was in the helicopter. 

The day ended with a happy little boy and a proud mommy. John learned that day that being persistent pays off.

One day, a boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went to the park. They saw many kids playing. Tim and Spot were very glad. They wanted to play too.

Tim saw a big box with many medals inside. The medals were all mixed up. Tim said, "Let's sort the medals, Spot!" Spot barked, and they started to sort the medals by their colors: red, blue, and yellow.

After they sorted the medals, a girl named Sue came over. She said, "Thank you for sorting the medals, Tim and Spot!" Tim and Spot were very happy to help. They all played together and had a fun day at the park.

Once there was a girl who was very nervous but she wanted to study hard. She looked at the sky and saw a beautiful rainbow. She knew that if she tried really hard she could get better at studying.

So, every day she set aside time to study and she was soon learning more and more each day. She was so proud of herself that she looked up at the rainbow and smiled.

But one day the rain clouds came and blocked out the rainbow. She was so disappointed that the rainbow was gone. But then she remembered her studying and she stayed focused.

The rain stopped and when the sun came out, the girl looked up and saw the most beautiful rainbow in the sky. She was so happy that she had kept studying even when it was raining.

She felt so proud of herself and she learned a very important lesson that day - with hard work and determination, you can do anything!

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big cage with a bird inside. The bird was blue and yellow and had a long tail. It looked very sad.

"Hello, bird," Lily said. "Why are you in the cage?"

The bird did not answer. It only made a soft noise.

"Maybe he wants to fly," Ben said. "Let's help him."

Lily and Ben looked around. They did not see anyone who owned the cage. They decided to open the door and let the bird out. They thought they were doing a good thing.

But when they opened the door, the bird did not fly away. It flew to Lily's shoulder and bit her ear. Lily screamed and tried to shake the bird off. The bird was not sad. It was angry and mean.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "Get him off me!"

Ben ran to help Lily. He grabbed the bird and threw it back in the cage. He slammed the door and locked it. He was scared and sorry.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.

Lily touched her ear. It was red and sore. She was hurt and mad.

"No, I'm not okay," Lily said. "That was a bad bird. He tricked us. He was not adorable. He was evil."

Lily and Ben learned a lesson. They learned that they should not touch things that do not belong to them. They also learned that they should not trust strangers. They did not recognize the bird's true nature. They almost did not escape from his bite. They ran away from the park and never played with the bird again.

Once there was a little girl. She loved to explore. Whenever she found something new she would test it. One day, she found a pepper. She hadn't seen one before. She sniffed it. It smelled funny. But she was brave. She decided to take a bite.

It was spicy! The little girl was so surprised! It was not at all what she expected. She was patient. She tried it again. It was still spicy, but not as bad. She liked it.

The little girl was so proud of herself for testing the pepper. She learned that trying new things could be okay. She also found out that it was important to be patient. She enjoyed the pepper with dinner that night and everyone was proud.

Once there was Bob, who was very pale and had a mop. He was going to introduce the mop to his friends.

Bob went to his best friend's house, but when he arrived, his best friend Tom already had a mop. Bob was jealous because Tom's mop was bigger and newer than his.

Bob said, â€œWhy don't you introduce me to your mop?â€

Tom replied, â€œI don't think that's a very good idea. My mop is much better than yours and I don't want to make you feel bad.â€

Bob sighed and said, â€œI understand, but I still want to show off my mop. Can I at least introduce it to some of your other friends?â€

Tom smiled and said, â€œOf course, that's fine. Let's go!â€ 

So Bob proudly introduced his mop to Tom's friends, and everyone was so impressed with how well it worked! Bob was happy and his pale face glowed with joy. 
 
From then on, Bob and Tom shared the same mop happily ever after.

John was a very adventurous three year old. He loved exploring and meeting new animals and plants. One day, John went for a walk in the woods near his house. As he was walking, he saw a big rubber ball. He wanted to take it home with him and play but as soon he reached out to grab it, he noticed something was off. 

John quickly realized he wasn't alone. There was a big bear in the distance. John started to tremble. He knew a bear could be dangerous and he didn't move a muscle. The bear slowly looked at John and then it slowly moved away.

John was relieved and kept his eyes on the bear until it disappeared. Then he quickly grabbed the rubber ball and ran home as fast as he could. He was so happy he found such an interesting toy!

Lily and Max were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sometimes they found worms, snails or beetles. They put them in a jar and watched them.

"Look, Lily, I found a big worm!" Max said, holding up his jar.

"Wow, that's a long one!" Lily said. "Can I see?"

Max gave her the jar and she looked at the worm. It was brown and slimy and wriggled in the dirt.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a car horn. They looked up and saw a red car in front of their house. A man and a woman got out of the car. They had bags and suitcases.

"Who are they?" Max asked.

"I don't know," Lily said.

They ran to the house and saw their mom and dad at the door. The man and the woman hugged them and smiled.

"Lily, Max, these are your aunt and uncle. They came to visit us for a week," their mom said.

"Hi, kids, we are so happy to see you!" their aunt said.

"Hello, we brought you some presents!" their uncle said.

Lily and Max felt shy. They did not know their aunt and uncle. They did not want to share their toys or their room with them. They wanted to play in the garden with their bugs.

They felt frustrated. They did not like this visit. They wished their aunt and uncle would disappear.

Once there was a cool cat named Lefty who loved to drop things. Whenever he had a chance, he would drop his favourite toy mouse onto the ground. One day, Lefty was walking around the garden with his toy mouse when he heard a voice.

"What are you doing, Lefty?" said the voice. Lefty looked around, but he couldn't see where the voice was coming from. He saw a cool bluebird which was chirping from a nearby tree.

"Are you talking to me, bird?" Lefty asked. The bluebird flapped its wings before saying, "Yes, I was wondering why you keep dropping your toy mouse."

"I like to drop it because it's fun," said Lefty. The bluebird smiled before telling him, "Well, why don't you try dropping me instead? It could be even more fun!"

Lefty was very excited and he said, "Yes! You can join the game!" He picked up the bluebird and dropped it safely in the grass. The bluebird smiled and said, "That was so much fun!"

Lefty was very happy and he played drop with the cool bluebird until the sun set.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight who wanted to explore a far away valley. The knight was a bit scared of the dark, but wanted to be brave so he decided to dare himself to go.

On the way to the valley, he saw a beautiful stream and a delicate flower. After he enjoyed his view, he continued walking and cheering himself on, being brave.

Suddenly, he saw the entrance to the valley and realized he had made it! He was overjoyed with excitement and ran to explore the valley.

He felt the warm sun and heard the noise of the animals nearby. He felt so free and happy that he was daring himself by exploring the unknown!

Jimmy was searching for something special to watch on tv. He wanted to find a good film. He asked his dad to help him find something available.

They looked and looked, but they couldn't find anything fun. Jimmy was starting to lose hope. Then suddenly, something caught his attention. It was a cartoon that was available!

Jimmy was so excited. He ran over to the tv and turned it on. There were lots of bright colors and fun sounds. He watched the whole movie and couldn't stop smiling.

When it finished, Jimmy searched for something else. He wanted to see what else was available. He watched several other films and was kept entertained the whole day. 

Jimmy's dad was so happy to see his son enjoying himself. He was glad he was able to help him find the perfect film.

Once there was a kid who liked to explore the world. Every day they would go outside to see what they could find. 

One day, as the kid was walking through the woods, they discovered an old, rusty tricycle. It looked a bit wobbly, but the kid thought it was useful, so they decided to climb on it and take it for a spin. 

But, as the kid tried to ride the rusty tricycle, it suddenly started to wobble and fall apart. The kid quickly jumped off and the tricycle clattered to the ground. The kid was sad, but then they looked around and noticed something sparkling in the dust. 

It turns out that, when the rusty tricycle fell apart, it had revealed a sparkly golden key! The kid was so excited. They knew that this key must open something really special. It was so useful!

The kid took their special key and went home, never forgetting their magical discovery that day.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Jane had a very special summer. She was so spoiled and happy every day that she could not help but laugh.

On the last day of summer, her mother asked her to clean up her room. Jane was so happy that she started jumping, screaming and laughing.

"Now, now, Jane. Cleaning your room is not fun and games," said her mother."You must behave." But Jane refused to listen.

So her mother took away her favourite toy. Jane started to cry and shouted "No! Give it back!"

Her mother refused and said, "If you don't learn to listen and be responsible, you won't have another summer like this one."

Jane looked outside and all the fun summer activities she would be missing out on. She started to cry harder and all the laughter she had shared throughout the summer disappeared.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She was three years old.

One day, Lily got a dictionary from the library. She was so excited to see what was inside! She opened it up and started reading. But after a few pages, Lily was feeling bored.

So, she decided to rest for a while. She lay down on the floor and closed her eyes. After a few minutes, Lily was feeling much better.

When she opened the dictionary again, Lily noticed that it was still a bit boring. But she was determined to keep reading. This time, she read much slower and tried to take in all the words.

Finally, the dictionary wasn't boring anymore. Lily was excited to learn all the new words!

Once upon a time there was a man with a big mustache. He wanted to be successful and have lots of fun. He decided to try to unlock something but he didn't know what.

One day he went to an old castle and he saw a big lock on the biggest door. He knew he could unlock it. So he took out a big key and put it into the lock. With a loud click, it unlocked!

The man was so happy and he opened the door. Inside he found a secret treasure. He was very successful and he celebrated and smiled with his big mustache.

He was so glad he unlocked the door and now he was very rich. He thanked his mustache for helping him be successful.

Lily and Max were at the park with their mom. They saw a big stage with many people on it. Mom said they were going to watch a show. Lily and Max were excited. They liked shows.

The show started. There was music and lights. The people on the stage wore colorful clothes. They did a dance. Lily and Max clapped their hands. They liked the dance. They wanted to dance too.

"Can we dance, mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can dance here," mom said. She pointed to a grassy area near the stage. "But don't go too far, okay?"

"Okay, mom," Lily and Max said. They ran to the grassy area. They started to dance. They copied the moves of the people on the stage. They spun and jumped and twirled. They had fun.

Then, they saw a man with a big camera. He came to the grassy area. He pointed the camera at Lily and Max. He smiled and said, "Hello, kids. You are very good dancers. Can I take a picture of you?"

Lily and Max felt uncomfortable. They did not know the man. They did not want him to take their picture. They stopped dancing. They looked at mom.

"Mom, who is he?" Max asked.

"He is a reporter. He works for a newspaper. He wants to write a story about the show and the dancers," mom said. She walked to the man. She said, "Hello, sir. These are my children. They are shy. They don't want to be in the picture."

The man nodded. He said, "I understand. They are very cute. Maybe they can wave at me instead?"

Lily and Max looked at each other. They decided to wave at the man. They raised their hands and waved. The man waved back. He said, "Thank you, kids. You are very nice. Have a good day."

He left. Lily and Max felt better. They went back to dancing. They enjoyed the show. They were happy.

One day, two friends, Tom and Joe, were playing in their backyard. Tom said to Joe, "Let's have a race!"
Joe was excited and he said "Yes, a race!"

Tom and Joe started running around their backyard. Tom was running fast and Joe was running slow. 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. They looked around and saw a deaf dog running from the neighbour's yard. It was heading straight for the fence! 

Tom said, "Come on Joe, let's help the dog!" They ran over and grabbed the dog's collar. They pulled it back to the neighbour's yard, and the dog stopped barking. 

The neighbour said thank you, and then asked Tom and Joe if they wanted to join the dog in a race. 

Tom said, "That sounds like fun! Let's do it!" 

Joe was a bit scared, but Tom held his hand and they both started to run. They ran together, laughing and enjoying being part of the race. 

In the end, they were both winners. Tom and Joe hugged each other and then ran back to the house to tell their families about the race.

The sun was bright and warm when the little girl stepped outside. She had her favorite brush in her hands. Her mom had looked at her with a twinkle in her eye and said, "Today is the day you start brushing your own hair!"

The little girl was excited to give it a try. She used the brush to try and make her hair look nice. But it was very hard and she soon started to weep. Tears ran down her cheeks and she felt so frustrated.

Just then her big sister stepped in. She noticed the tears and asked what was wrong. The little girl explained how hard the brush was and how she couldn't make her hair look nice. Her sister smiled and said, "I know just the thing! Hold this brush and I'll do the brushing."

The big sister was so bossy but she knew what she was doing. She brushed the little girl's hair until it was soft and shiny. The little girl smiled and gave her big sister a big hug. "You can do the brushing now, anytime," the big sister said.

The little girl felt so much better! She picked up her brush and said, "Thank you, I think I can do this now!" With a happy little skip, she knew she could do anything with the help of her big sister.

Once upon a time there was a special star in the sky. It was different from the other stars. It shone by itself and was very independent.

Every night, the star thanked the sky for being so wonderful. It thanked the trees for being green and the animals for being happy and content.

One night, the star saw a small child looking up at it. The star was very excited. It thanked the child for taking the time to look at it.

The child smiled and waved to the star. Then the star said thank you again and shone even brighter.

That night, something magical happened. The star suddenly descended from the sky and landed right on the childâ€™s head. The star thanked the child one last time before it twinkled and flew away.

The child closed its eyes and wished upon the star.  From that day on, the star shined brighter and brighter, and the child was able to live happily ever after.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to observe things. They observed birds, flowers, stars, and people. Sometimes they had different opinions about what they observed.

One day, they observed a big dog in the park. Ben thought the dog was scary and loud. He said, "I don't like that dog. He barks too much and he has sharp teeth. He might bite us."

Lily thought the dog was friendly and cute. She said, "I like that dog. He is just saying hello and he has a soft fur. He might want to play with us."

They argued for a while, until their mom came and said, "Stop arguing, please. You can have different opinions, but you should respect each other. The dog is not scary or friendly. He is just a dog. He has his own personality and feelings. Maybe he is happy or sad or bored or curious. You should be humble and try to understand him, not judge him."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for arguing. They said, "Sorry, mom. You are right. We should be humble and try to understand the dog, not judge him."

They went closer to the dog and observed him more carefully. They saw that he had a collar with a name tag. It said, "Rex". They also saw that he had a wagging tail and a smiling face. He looked like he wanted some attention and affection.

They asked their mom if they could pet him. She said, "Yes, but be gentle and ask his owner first. He might be shy or nervous around strangers."

They found his owner, a nice lady, and asked her if they could pet Rex. She said, "Sure, he loves kids. He is very gentle and sweet. He is also very smart and observant. He can do some tricks, if you want to see."

They said, "Yes, please. We would love to see his tricks."

They watched as Rex did some tricks, like sit, roll over, shake, and speak. They clapped and cheered and gave him some treats. They also petted him and told him he was a good boy.

They learned that Rex was not scary or friendly. He was just Rex. He had his own personality and feelings. He was also very smart and observant. He could do some tricks, but he also liked to be loved and cared for.

They thanked the lady and Rex for the fun time. They said, "Bye, Rex. You are a great dog. We hope to see you again."

They went back to their mom and said, "Mom, we learned something today. We learned to be humble and try to understand things, not judge them. We also learned that Rex is a great dog. He is very smart and observant. He can do some tricks, but he also likes to be loved and cared for."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "I'm proud of you, Ben and Lily. You are very smart and observant, too. You can do some tricks, but you also like to be loved and cared for. You are also humble and respectful. You have good opinions, but you also listen to others. You are great kids. I love you very much."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy was very spoiled and loved getting her way. One day Lucy wanted a toy, but her mom said she couldn't have it. Lucy got angry and started to act out. She threw things around and screamed. Her mom told her to stop but Lucy wouldn't listen. She kept acting bad.

Finally her mom said that she was going to timeout. She made Lucy stand in the corner and said she couldn't move until she was calm. Lucy was so mad that she tried to run away but as she tried to take a step, she fell.

She started to cry, feeling really scared and sad. Lucy's mom came to give her a hug and told her it was ok to feel scared. Finally, Lucy calmed down so mom said it was ok to get up.

Lucy realized it was better to be nice than to act spoiled and bad. She promised never to act like that again and from that day on, she was a very nice and obedient little girl.

One day, Mom was looking for an empty note. She split it in two and wrote something on one side. Then she gave the note to her three year old daughter. The little girl was surprised to see the note split in two pieces. She looked at it carefully and smiled. 

Then the little girl took the note and split it in two again. She handed one half of it back to Mom. Mom was amazed! The little girl said, "I can split the note just like you did!" 

Mom gave her daughter a big hug and said, "You're such a clever girl!" 

The little girl was so happy. She knew that empty notes could be split in two. Now she was even more excited to show her friends.

Jimmy was swinging in the playground. He loved being high up in the air and how it made him feel so light. His friends were there too and everyone was having a great time.

Suddenly, Jimmy heard a loud noise. He stopped swinging and looked around. He saw a jar lying on the ground near the swing. He ran to it and picked it up. The jar had a gentle pattern, with blue and yellow flowers.

Jimmy brought the jar closer to his eyes and saw a ladybug crawling around inside. It was really tiny. He smiled and called his friends.

"Look what I found!" he said. 

His friends gathered around him and all looked at the little lady bug. They oohed and ahhed and said it was so cute.

Then the lady bug stopped and Jimmy decided to set it free. He opened the jar's lid and gently turned it upside down. The lady bug hopped out and flew off into the sky, free to explore its new world.

Jimmy smiled and watched until it was out of sight. Then he went back to swing with his friends. That had been an exciting find and he couldn't wait to tell his mom about it when he got home!

The sun was shining in the sky and Jenny was feeling so excited. She was waiting with her Mom at the station for the train to arrive. Suddenly they heard the sound of the train coming and Jenny started to feel very anxious. 

"It's almost here, Jenny," said Mom. 

They waited at the station and soon the train arrived. They got on the big train and it slowly started moving. After a while they arrived at their destination, another station.

When they got off the train, Jenny was surprised to see someone she hadn't seen in a very long time - her Grandma! Mom and Grandma were hugging and crying together and Jenny was so happy to see Grandma.

"It's so nice to meet you again, Grandma," said Jenny. Grandma smiled and gave Jenny a big hug. Jenny was so glad that she and Mom had come to the station to meet Grandma. Even though she had been feeling anxious before the train arrived, Jenny was very happy now.

Once upon a time there was a furry animal who lived on a small island far away. The furry animal was always worrying and never looked very happy. One day, the furry animal wanted to go on an adventure. 

The furry animal sailed away from the island to explore the world. After many weeks, the furry animal found a new, bigger island with lots of things to explore. The furry animal was so excited and thought it would be the perfect place to explore. 

Unfortunately, when the furry animal got to the new island they saw a big scary monster. The furry animal was so scared and began worrying again. They did not know what to do.

Suddenly, the furry animal remembered something from their old island. It was a special tool! The furry animal knew that the tool could help them scare away the monster and keep them safe. The furry animal ran back to their old island, got the special tool and returned to the new island. Then, the furry animal scared away the scary monster and felt safe again! 

The furry animal was relieved and thankful for the special tool. From then on, the furry animal never worried and explored the new island with no fear. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. One day, he went to the beach with his mom and dad. Tim was very alert and excited to play in the sand and water. He took his favorite towel with him, which had a big red fish on it.

While playing, Tim started to complain that he was hot and tired. His mom told him to rest on his towel under the big umbrella. But Tim didn't listen and kept playing in the sun.

After some time, Tim felt very sick. He went to his towel and lay down, but it was too late. Tim had a sunburn and felt very bad. If only he had listened to his mom and rested earlier, he would have been okay.

Once upon a time, there was a big white bull. He lived on a farm with many other animals. The bull was very strong and liked to play with his friends.

One day, the bull wanted to test how strong he was. He asked his friend, the horse, "Do you want to play a game with me?" The horse said, "Yes, I want to play with you!"

So, the bull and the horse played a game. They pushed each other to see who was stronger. The bull was very strong, but the horse was strong too. They played and played until they were both tired. In the end, they both laughed and had fun.

The white bull and the horse became very good friends. They played together every day and helped each other when they needed it. The other animals on the farm liked to watch them play and have fun. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big, hairy dog with a bandage on its leg. The dog looked sad and lonely.

"Can we pet the dog?" Lily asked Tom.

"I don't know. Maybe it is hurt or angry," Tom said.

They walked closer to the dog and saw that it had a name tag. It said "Rex".

"Hello, Rex. Are you okay?" Lily said softly.

The dog wagged its tail and licked Lily's hand. It seemed friendly and happy.

"Can we play with you, Rex?" Tom asked.

The dog barked and nodded. It wanted to play with them.

Tom and Lily threw a ball for Rex and ran with him. They had a lot of fun. Rex was very fast and strong.

"Rex, you are a good dog. Do you have a home?" Lily asked.

The dog looked sad and shook his head. He had no home.

Tom and Lily felt sorry for Rex. They wanted to help him.

"Rex, do you want to come with us? We can be your friends. We can include you in our family," Tom said.

The dog looked surprised and happy. He wagged his tail and licked Tom's face. He wanted to go with them.

Tom and Lily took Rex to their house. They showed him to their mom and dad. They told them how they met Rex and how he had no home.

Mom and dad smiled and hugged Rex. They said he was a brave and sweet dog. They said they would take him to the vet and find him a new bandage. They said they would adopt him and make him part of their family.

Tom and Lily were very happy. They had a new friend and a new pet. Rex was very happy too. He had a new home and a new family. He was no longer sad and lonely. He was loved and included.

Once upon a time, there was a creative little girl. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. On a particularly sunny day, the girl decided to play outside. She was so excited to experience the warmth of the sun. As she began playing, she noticed a giant umbrella in the sky with a smiley face on it. She had never seen anything quite like it before!

The girl wondered if the umbrella was there for her. She carefully walked beneath the umbrella and found it blocked the sun's rays. She smiled and danced beneath the umbrella, enjoying the shade it provided.
 
At the end of the day, the girl was sad when it started raining. But then she noticed that the umbrella was still there, blocking the rain. She was so happy; the umbrella was there to protect her the whole time! She smiled and continued to play with her toys until it was time to go home.

From then on, the girl always remembered that if she was ever feeling down, she only had to look up at the sky and find her smiley umbrella watching over her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Dave. Dave loved to play. He played every day. One day, Dave was playing in the park. He saw a big ash tree. He thought it was very impressive. He wanted to see what it felt like, so he put both his hands around it and squeezed. Dave said, "Wow! It's so squishy!"

Suddenly, an old wise man appeared from the tree. He said, "Greetings, young Dave. Your hug was so impressive. Do you want to know a magical secret?"

Dave was very excited. He nodded eagerly. The man said, "If you close your eyes and squeeze the tree again, magic will come!"

Dave couldn't believe it. So he closed his eyes and squeezed again. Suddenly, with a sparkle and a poof, a silver unicorn appeared! Dave couldn't believe his eyes.

The wise man said, "You see, magical things can happen if you believe." And with that, the unicorn galloped away into the night. Dave was amazed and couldn't wait to tell his friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Let's race to the slide!" Ben says. "Who is faster?"

"Me!" Lily says. "I am very fit. I can run and jump and climb."

They run to the slide. Ben is ahead. He is fast. Lily tries to catch up. She is fit. She runs and jumps and climbs.

They reach the slide. Ben goes first. He slides down with speed. He laughs. He is happy.

Lily goes next. She slides down with speed. She laughs. She is happy.

They see each other at the bottom. They smile. They hug.

"We are both fast and fit!" Lily says.

"Yes, we are!" Ben says. "And we are both fun!"

They go to the slide again. They slide down with speed. They laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a drum. The drum was big and red. Tim thought it was easy to play the drum. He hit the drum with a stick and it made a loud noise. Tim was happy.

Tim wanted to show his friend, Lily. He went to her house and said, "Look at my drum!" Lily liked the drum too. She said, "Can I try?" Tim said, "Yes, it's easy!" Lily hit the drum and it was very loud. They laughed and played the drum together.

Tim and Lily played the drum all day. They did not mention the drum to their moms and dads. They wanted to keep it a secret. But, the drum was too loud. Their moms and dads heard the noise and came to see. They all laughed and played the drum together. It was a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to decorate her room with pretty things. One day, she found a shiny copper penny on the ground. She picked it up and thought it was very pretty. She decided to decorate her room with it. 

Lily took the copper penny and put it on her shelf. She looked at it every day and loved how it sparkled in the sunlight. She also liked to touch it because it felt cool and smooth. 

Lily was a slow decorator, but she always made sure everything looked just right. She added more things to her room, like a colorful rug and some bright pillows. When she was finished, her room looked like a rainbow. She was so happy with how it turned out. 

From that day on, Lily loved to decorate with shiny things like copper. She would always take her time and make sure everything was perfect. And every time she saw her copper penny, she smiled and felt proud of her slow and steady decorating skills.

Once there was a little girl who was 3 years old. Her name was Sally. One day Sally went to the park with her mom. As they walked around the park, Sally saw somebody who was trying to wrap something in a blanket.

Sally asked her mom, â€œWhat are they doing?â€

Her mom smiled and said, â€œThat person is wrapping a present.â€ Sally's eyes lit up and she got so excited. She wanted to wrap something too.

So her mom went to the store and bought a few boxes, some wrapping paper, a pair of scissors and a tape measure. When they got home, her mom showed Sally how to wrap the present.

First, Sally measured the box with the tape measure, then she cut the paper with the scissors to make sure it fit. After that, she used the tape to stick the wrapping paper to the box.

Sally was so proud when she finished that she couldn't help but smile. When she showed her mom the present, her mom smiled back and gave her a big hug.

But then Sally started to feel something else. She felt hurt. She realized that her mum wasn't going to be able to wrap a present every day. So with a happy smile, she hugged her mom tighter and said, â€œIt's okay mom, I can wrap presents all by myself.â€

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sam. She was very brave and she liked to help others.
One day, Sam saw a cat in a tree. The cat had climbed up but he was stuck and meowing helplessly.
Sam knew that she had to help and so she asked her dad for a ladder. Her dad quickly brought one and Sam set up the ladder and carefully climbed up to the top of the tree.

When she reached the top, she gently scooped up the pale cat and carried it back down the ladder. The cat was very glad to be safe, and purred happily.

Then Sam took the cat to the kitchen and gave him a big meal from the tap. The cat was so pleased with the nice food and fresh water that he purred even louder.

Sam was very proud of her rescue and the cat never moved from the house ever again. They became best friends from that day forward.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. He would run around in the grass and jump up and down. One day, he went to the playground with his mommy. He saw a big slide and wanted to play on it.

Timmy climbed up the ladder to the top of the slide. He felt very happy and excited. But then, he looked down and saw that the ground was very distant. Suddenly, he felt scared and wanted to go back down. But it was too late. He slipped and fell down from the slide.

Timmy was very hurt and had to go to the hospital. He learned that it's important to be careful when playing on the playground. From that day on, he never went on the big slide again.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends called Tom and Jim. Every morning they would rush to the park together and have lots of fun.

Every day they would play catch with a ball, or look at the sky and pick out shapes in the clouds. But today something was different.

Tom's dad had taken him to the art gallery the day before and he had seen the most incredible picture. 

He asked Jim if they could go back to the art gallery the next morning, forgetting that his dad had only brought him there once. Jim was confused, but he said okay anyway.

The next morning they both rushed to the art gallery, so excited to see Tom's incredible picture. But when they got there, the picture was gone. 

All that was left were two frames that were empty. Tom was very sad, but Jim smiled and said, "I'm sure we will find it again one day".

Tom smiled too and the two of them rushed off to the park to play. They knew that wherever it was, the incredible picture was waiting for them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys and have fun with her friends. One day, Lily's mom asked her to go to the store and buy some soap. Lily was excited to help her mom, so she put the soap in her bag and started to carry it home.

On her way back, Lily saw a little bird that had hurt its wing. She felt sad for the bird and wanted to help it. Lily remembered that her mom had told her that being flexible and kind is important. So, she gently picked up the bird and carried it home with her.

When she got home, Lily's mom was happy to see that she had bought the soap and was proud of her for helping the little bird. Lily learned that being kind and flexible is important and can make a difference in the world.

One morning, Tim and his mom went to the park. They saw a big tree with a cat in it. The cat was very high up and needed help to get down. Tim wanted to help the cat, so he asked his mom if they could remove the cat from the tree and make it safe.

Tim's mom found a long stick. She used the stick to reach the cat in the tree. The cat was scared, but Tim's mom was very careful. She slowly removed the cat from the tree. The cat was now safe in her arms.

Tim and his mom took the cat home. They gave it some food and water. The cat was happy and safe with Tim and his mom. They played with the cat all day and had lots of fun. Tim was glad that they could help the cat and make it safe.

Sam was a brave knight. He wore a big helmet and carried a shining shield. He was looking for a quest to complete.

Suddenly, he saw a dragon! "Roar!" the dragon growled. Sam was a bit scared but lifted his shield and faced the dragon.

The dragon said, "I challenge you to a race! If you win, I will give you a prize!" Sam was excited, so he agreed.

The race began and Sam started running as fast as he could. But the racing made him feel uncomfortable. The dragon was running faster!

Just then, Sam had an idea. He threw his shield in front of the dragon. The dragon had to stop and Sam won the race!

He cheerfully said, "I won! Now what is my prize?"

The dragon said, "You get to keep your shield". Sam was happy and thanked the dragon. He went home, with his shield in tow, feeling brave.

Once there was a wild lady who lived in a big forest. One day, she went to explore the forest and came across a big cave. When she peered inside, she saw a tiny bear cub. The bear cub saw her and started to yell. She was startled and stepped back. The cub kept yelling and she thought it was so funny! She started to laugh and the cub yelled even louder. She kept laughing, and the cub kept yelling. Everyone in the forest heard the bear cub's wild yells and came to investigate. They all had a great time listening to the cub's wild yelling. The lady was so proud of her new little cub and would bring him with her whenever she explored the forest. Everyone would always hear the cub's wild yells as they strolled along.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. Molly was only three years old and she was eager to learn. One day, her parents took her to the gas station. She watched as they filled the car's tank with gas. Suddenly, Molly started to smell something strange. She asked her parents what the smell was and they said it was the gas. 

Molly was very curious, so she asked them why the gas smelt funny. Her parents explained that the gas was special and that it made their car go faster. 

So Molly decided to learn all she could about gas. She asked her parents to teach her. They showed her how the gas flowed through the pipes, and how it was put into the car's tank. 

Molly was very proud of what she had learned and she knew it was very important. When her parents said it was time to go, Molly gave the gas station a big hug. She was sorry to leave and promised herself she would learn more about gas the next time.

Once upon a time there was a wise veil who lived in a big tree. Every day the veil would count all the leaves in the tree and tell everyone how many there were.

One day a little bird flew down to the veil and said, "Good day wise veil. Can you number the leaves for me? I cannot count that high." 

The veil smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can! There are 836 leaves on this tree. Can you say that number?" 

The little bird tried very hard and finally said, "eight three six" with a happy voice.

The veil was very proud of the little bird and said, "Well done! You are wise for your age!" 

The bird thanked the veil for its help and flew away happily. From then on, the veil counted all the leaves every day with a smile on its face.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tom. He was a very adventurous boy, who liked to explore the outdoors.

One day Tom went outside to find some fun. He went looking around the trees and soon found an acorn. It was shiny and brown, and Tom thought it was special.

Tom was excited to show the acorn to his friends. He ran over to them and showed them the acorn. They were very excited to see it and gave Tom lots of hugs.

Tom and his friends decided to take the acorn on an adventure. They made up a story with the acorn as their hero. They pretended the acorn could do all sorts of amazing things like fly and move rocks.

Tom and his friends had a great time on their acorn adventure. They learned a lot, laughed a lot, and had fun. At the end of the day, Tom put the acorn in a special place to remind him of their adventurous day.

Once there was a girl. Her name was Sue. Sue was three years old. She loved playing dress-up. Sometimes she used weird clothes she found in her Mom's closet.

One day Sue was playing in her bedroom when she found a pillow. She had never seen it before. It was weird.

Sue hugged it. Then, she decided to test the pillow. She asked her Mom, "Mom, can I test the pillow?" Her Mom said, "Sure!"

So Sue tested the pillow. She jumped and bounced and sometimes landed on it with her feet. The pillow was really fun. She kept testing it until it was time for dinner.

Sue decided to keep the pillow and keep testing it. She loved it!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to nap in the warm sun. One day, Max saw a big cat napping in his spot. Max felt jealous. He wanted his spot back.

Max went to the cat and said, "Please, can I have my spot back?" The cat looked at Max and said, "No, I like this spot." Max felt sad, but he went to find a new place to nap.

In his new spot, Max felt an itch. He tried to scratch it, but it was hard. Max thought about the cat in his old spot. He thought the cat might be itchy too. Max went back to the cat and said, "I can help you if you have an itch." The cat smiled and said, "Thank you, Max." They both napped in the sun, happy and itch-free.

Once upon a time there was a fluffy puppy. The puppy was very soft and had a gentle texture. He loved to run and play in the park. One day, while playing, he hurt his paw. He yelped in pain and his puppy friends ran to see what was wrong.

The puppy tried to speak but he only whimpered and whined. His friends couldn't understand what he was trying to say. But then, one of his friends took a close look and saw that his paw was red and swollen.

The other puppy told the hurt puppy that it was time to go to the veterinarian so he could feel better. The hurt puppy was very scared but he knew his friend was right.

Once at the vet, the doctor gave the hurt puppy a gentle pat and some soothing medicine. The puppy soon felt better and was soon back to running and playing in the park. He learned an important lesson - if you ever get hurt, speak up and tell your friends so you can get help.

Tim and Mia liked to go to the lake with their mom and dad. They liked to swim and splash and play with the fish and the ducks. Sometimes they found shiny rocks or pretty shells on the shore.

One day, they saw a big boat on the lake. It was red and white and had a loud horn. Tim and Mia wanted to see it up close. They asked their mom and dad if they could go near it.

"Okay, but be careful," their mom said. "And don't remove your life jackets. The water is deep and the boat is fast."

Tim and Mia nodded and ran to the water. They swam towards the boat, but it was far away. They tried to wave and shout, but the boat did not see them or hear them. The boat was moving closer and closer to them.

"Tim, Mia, come back!" their dad yelled. "The boat is too big and too noisy. It might hurt you!"

Tim and Mia heard their dad and turned around. They saw the boat was very close to them. They saw the big propeller that made the water swirl and bubble. They were scared and wanted to go back to their mom and dad.

But then they saw something else. They saw a playful dolphin jumping out of the water. It was gray and shiny and had a friendly smile. It looked at Tim and Mia and made a funny sound.

"Wow, a dolphin!" Tim said.

"Hi, dolphin!" Mia said.

The dolphin came closer to Tim and Mia. It nudged them with its nose and pushed them away from the boat. It helped them swim back to the shore, where their mom and dad were waiting for them.

"Thank you, dolphin!" Tim and Mia said.

The dolphin waved its tail and made another funny sound. Then it swam away, back to the lake.

Tim and Mia hugged their mom and dad. They were happy and safe. They had seen a big boat and a playful dolphin. They had had a big adventure.

Mama was very happy. She was going to a party. She wanted to decorate the house. She got her brush and some paint and started to paint the walls. She was so excited. 

When Papa saw the walls, he was very angry. He said it was not a good idea. Mama was sad. She started to cry. 

But then, everyone at the party said the house was beautiful. They praised Mama for her decorations. She was so happy. Everyone clapped and celebrated. 

Mama hugged Papa and thanked him for helping her. The party was a great success!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mommy went for a drive on a bumpy road. Lily was scared because the car was shaking a lot. She held her mommy's hand tightly and closed her eyes. 

After a while, they arrived at a farm. There, they saw a cow that was suffering. Lily felt sad for the cow and asked her mommy why it was making noise. Her mommy explained that the cow was in pain and needed help. They went to find the farmer and told him about the cow. The farmer thanked them and said he would take care of it. 

Lily felt happy that they could help the cow. On the way back home, the road was still bumpy, but she wasn't scared anymore. She was proud of herself for being brave and helping the cow.

Tom and Mia were excited to play with the new scissors. They liked to cut paper and make shapes. They did not listen to Mom when she said scissors were sharp and they should be careful.

"Look, I made a star!" Tom said, showing Mia his paper.

"I made a heart!" Mia said, showing Tom her paper.

They wanted to make more shapes. They looked around for more paper. They saw Mom's magazine on the table. They thought it had pretty pictures. They took the magazine and started to cut it.

Mom heard the sound of scissors and came to see what they were doing. She was angry when she saw the magazine. She shouted at Tom and Mia.

"Stop! What are you doing? You are ruining my magazine! Give me those scissors right now!"

Tom and Mia were scared of Mom. They tried to hide the scissors behind their backs. But they were not careful. The scissors slipped and cut Tom's face. Tom screamed in pain. He saw blood on his hand. He started to cry.

Mia saw Tom's face. She was shocked and sorry. She dropped the scissors and hugged Tom. She started to cry too.

Mom saw Tom's face. She was worried and sorry. She dropped the magazine and ran to Tom. She took a cloth and pressed it on his face. She called Dad and said they had to go to the hospital.

Tom and Mia learned a hard lesson. They should never play with scissors. They should always listen to Mom. They should not cut things that are not theirs. They should be careful with their faces. They were not excited anymore. They were sad and sorry.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Anna and Ben. They were playing together in the park. Anna was beginning to get tired, so she sat down and said, "I am too weak to act." Ben looked over at her and said, "Don't worry! I've got an idea." He opened his bag and showed her his calendar. "If you put a mark on this calendar each day that you act," said Ben, "then you won't feel so weak any more." Anna smiled and said, "Let's try it!" 

So they started putting a mark on the calendar each day. And little by little, Anna got stronger and stronger. After a few weeks, she was able to act with ease! Ben and Anna were so happy, they hugged each other and danced around the park.

The End.

Once there was a man walking down the street. He had a very hard frown on his face. He was very sad about something. When he passed a small girl, she smiled at him. But the man didn't smile back. He kept walking with his hard frown.

Then, he saw an ice cream store. It was filled with bright colors and tasty smells. All of a sudden his hard frown melted away. His face lit up with a big smile because he remembered the happy times he had eating ice cream with his family. 

He entered the shop and ordered his favorite treat. As he walked out of the store the man was no longer frowning. He was smiling and feeling much better now. The small girl watched him go and smiled too.

Once upon a time, in a big, dark house, there lived a stubborn little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around the house. One day, while playing, she heard a loud roar coming from the basement. Lily was scared but also very curious.

She went down the stairs to see what made the roar. In the basement, she saw a big, white ghost! The ghost said, "Boo! I am the ghost of this house. Leave now or I will scare you more!" Lily was very brave and said, "No, I live here too. We can be friends and play together."

The ghost didn't want to be friends at first, but Lily was very stubborn. She kept asking the ghost to play with her. Finally, the ghost agreed and they played together all day long. The ghost wasn't scary anymore, and they both had lots of fun. From that day on, Lily and the ghost became best friends, and the house was never scary again.

Sam woke up in the morning. His mommy was making breakfast. Sam was excited. He saw a tray of eggs and bacon on the table. He jumped out of bed and ran over to it. 

"Mommy, can I have a piece of bacon?" Sam asked. 

"Yes, you can!" Mommy said.

Sam took a piece of bacon and started eating it. He was so excited. But then the bacon fell into the glass of milk. Sam looked very sad.

"Oh, no! My bacon is wet!" he said. 

Mommy laughed. She gave Sam a napkin and said, "Let's try this again, okay? I have some fresh bacon here, just for you!"

Sam smiled and grabbed the fresh, dry bacon. He ate it in one bite and said, "Yummy!"

Once upon a time, there was a big fat cat named Whiskers. Whiskers loved going to the theater with his friends. They would watch movies and eat popcorn together. One day, Whiskers saw a little mouse all alone. Whiskers felt sad for the mouse and wanted to hug him. But when Whiskers tried to hug the mouse, the mouse ran away.

Whiskers felt sad because he wanted to be friends with the mouse. So, he decided to follow the mouse. The mouse led Whiskers to a trap. Whiskers got stuck in the trap and couldn't get out. He was scared and alone. He wished he had never followed the mouse.

The next day, Whiskers' friends went to the theater without him. They wondered where Whiskers was. They looked for him everywhere, but they couldn't find him. They never saw Whiskers again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the pool with her friends. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big lemon tree and wanted to taste a lemon. Her mom picked a lemon and let her try it. Lily made a face and said, "This is sour!" Her dad laughed and said, "Yes, lemons are sour. Do you like it?" Lily shook her head and said, "No, I don't like it." Her mom said, "That's okay, everyone has different tastes. What do you want to eat for lunch?" Lily said, "I want a sandwich, please!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a big smile and two thumbs. One day, Lily spun around and around until she got dizzy. She fell down and her thumb hurt. Her mom gave her a kiss and a band-aid, and Lily felt better. From then on, Lily was careful not to spin too much and make herself dizzy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy.

Lucy was three years old and she loved to play. One day, she was playing in the garden when she got a surprise.

A fine, white letter fell from the sky. Lucy was amazed. She picked up the letter and opened it. Inside there was a smooth stone.

Suddenly, Lucy started to sneeze. She put the letter down and went inside. Soon, the sneezes stopped.

She looked out of the window and saw a magnificent rainbow in the sky. Then she knew - the stone was a gift from the rainbow.

Lucy smiled and held the stone tight. She was the luckiest three year old in the world!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved taking pictures with his camera. He would take pictures of his toys, his friends, and even his food! 

One day, Timmy's mom reminded him that he had a big competition coming up at his school. Timmy was very excited to show off his picture-taking skills. 

At the competition, Timmy saw all of his friends with their cameras too. He felt a little nervous because they all looked very competitive. 

But Timmy didn't give up. He took pictures of everything he could find - the flowers, the trees, and even the bugs! When the competition was over, the judges looked at all of the pictures and announced the winner. 

It was Timmy! He was so happy and proud of himself. He knew that he had worked hard and it had paid off. From then on, Timmy continued to take pictures and always remembered the day he won the competition.

Once upon a time a wise owl had to deal with a problem. Everywhere he looked, things seemed to be breaking. He wanted to find a solution to make all the broken things work again.

He thought and thought but he could not come up with a plan. Suddenly he had an idea. He suggested that he use a laser. He flew off to get one.

When he came back, he carefully used the laser and all the broken things worked! He was very happy. He told all the other animals about his wise suggestion and soon everyone knew that a laser could be used to fix broken things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old. 

The little girl had an armchair of her own. It was thin and very comfortable. She used to spend hours just sitting in it.

One day, the little girl asked her mum, "Mum, what is the best thing about my armchair?" 

Mum replied, "Well honey, it's special because it's yours! You own it and it's just for you".

The little girl smiled and nodded. She was so happy to have her own armchair. From then on, she loved that armchair more than anything else.

Once upon a time, there was a big gate. It was very tall and made of metal. One day, some kids came to the gate and wanted to go inside. But the gate was closed and they couldn't get in. So, they decided to organize a plan to open the gate. 

They looked for a key, but they couldn't find one. Then, they saw a famous person walking by. They asked him if he knew how to open the gate. The famous person said yes and helped them open the gate. 

The kids were so happy that they could go inside. They thanked the famous person and organized a party to celebrate. They played games, ate cake and had so much fun. From that day on, the gate was always open for everyone to come in and play.

Once upon a time there was a nice man who had a smart hat. He wanted to sell his hat so he could buy more things. He went to the market and saw lots of people. He asked everyone if they wanted to buy his hat.

Everyone said no until he saw a little girl. The girl was wearing a dress with lots of bows. She saw the man's hat and said that it looked very nice. She asked the nice man how much it cost and he said a dollar.

The girl thought it was a good deal so she bought the hat. The nice man was very happy. He gave the little girl the hat and thanked her for buying it. The little girl put on the hat and it made her look very smart.

The nice man waved goodbye to the little girl and went home. He was very happy that he was able to sell his hat.
