Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved to march around the jungle and stomp her big feet. One day, Ellie saw a bottle of red wine on the ground. She picked it up with her trunk and took a big sniff. It smelled so good!

But Ellie remembered that wine was not good for her. It was only for humans. She didn't want to be selfish and keep it all to herself. So, she marched over to her friend, a monkey named Max, and gave him the bottle of wine as a gift. Max was so happy and thanked Ellie for being such a good friend. From that day on, Ellie and Max marched through the jungle together, enjoying each other's company and having lots of fun adventures.

Once there was a little boy. His name was Jack. He was three years old.

One day, Jack's mom said it was time for a bath. Jack was nervous. He had never been in a pit before. But it was time to bathe.

So Jack grabbed a bucket and filled it with water. He filled a big bowl too. Then he dipped his feet in the water. It was cold! Jack hopped back out and put a towel around himself.

Next, Jack got into the pit. He felt a little bit scared, so he closed his eyes and counted to three. Then he opened them again. That was better!

Jack got into the pit and dunked himself in the cold water. He splashed around and had so much fun! He washed his face and body and then got out of the pit.

Jack dried himself off, feeling clean and happy. He had gone in the pit, and now he could say he had taken a real bath!

Once upon a time there was a black cat named Pit. Pit was a very curious cat. One day, Pit decided he wanted to explore a big black pit he had seen in the yard. 

Pit's mommy saw him walking towards the pit and shouted, "No, Pit! Don't go in there!" 

But Pit was already standing at the edge of the pit, so he looked up and said, "What is down there?" 

His mommy replied, "It's a big, deep, dark pit. I don't want you to go down there, so please don't." 

But Pit couldn't help himself. He wanted to know what was down there. So he put one paw in and then another and soon he was down in the pit. It was very dark inside, so he felt around. Soon, he found a big black mouse! 

Pit was so excited that he quickly put the mouse in his pocket and climbed back out of the pit. He raced home to show his mommy the mouse. 

His mommy was so pleased with what Pit had done that she gave him a hug and said, "That was very brave of you to go in the pit, Pit!"

Today, Emily and Mommy were very excited. They were going to decorate the living room together.

Mommy said, "Let's get started, Emily. What color do you want to use?" Emily smiled and said, "Gray." So Mommy got out the gray paint and a brush.

They painted the walls with the gray paint. Mommy said it was looking very beautiful.

Then they got out the small decorations. Emily chose a few stars to decorate the wall. Mommy hung them up with tape. After they were finished, they looked around. Everything was special and gray.

Mommy said, "Look how beautiful the living room looks. You did a great job decorating, Emily!" Emily smiled and said, "I like it."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a big present to give to his friend, but he didn't know how to wrap it. His mommy helped him wrap it with pretty paper and a bow.

When Timmy went to give his friend the present, he forgot his friend's name. He felt very sorry and embarrassed. But his friend was happy to see Timmy and loved the present.

Timmy learned that it's important to remember people's names and to wrap presents nicely. He felt happy and proud that he made his friend smile. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and write in her notebook. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she found a notebook on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it belonged to her friend, Timmy. 

Lily went to Timmy and said, "Look what I found! Is this your notebook?" Timmy was happy and said, "Yes, thank you Lily! You are so thoughtful." Lily smiled and felt happy that she could help her friend. 

Later that day, Lily received a note from Timmy. It said, "Thank you for finding my notebook. You are the best friend ever!" Lily was so happy that she danced around her room. She knew that being kind and thoughtful to others was important.

Mia had a birthday. She was very excited. She wanted to see what was inside the present. But it was hard to open. She tried hard to open the package. Finally it opened. She saw a blue bike! She was so happy she jumped up and down. She ran to show her mom and dad. They said it was the best birthday present ever. Mia went outside and rode her bike. She had so much fun. She said it was the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He liked to play games with his friends. They were very competitive and always wanted to win. One day, they decided to have a race to see who was the fastest.

The old man tried his best, but he was very slow. His friends all ran ahead of him. But then, something magical happened. The old man's granddaughter came to watch the race. She ran up to him and gave him a big kiss on the cheek.

Suddenly, the old man felt like he could run faster than ever before. He started to catch up with his friends. They were all amazed at how fast he was going. In the end, the old man won the race! His friends were happy for him and they all hugged and laughed together.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Her parents spoiled her a lot, so she loved to have lots of fun.

One day, Sarah's parents bought her a shiny trumpet. She was so excited! She valued her new toy and loved to make it squeak.

Whenever Sarah took her trumpet outside, the birds flew away when they heard the sound. Sarah laughed and kept playing.

One day, Sarah shared her trumpet with her friends. They had so much fun taking turns playing the trumpet.

Sarah's parents were so proud of her and her new instrument. They loved seeing her happy and valued all the joy she found in music.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah loved to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, her mommy gave her a useful apron to wear. Sarah was happy and put it on.

Mommy asked Sarah to open the fridge and take out some eggs. Sarah opened the fridge and found the eggs. She carefully carried them to the counter, but one fell on the floor. Mommy said it was okay and helped her clean it up.

Then, mommy showed Sarah how to crack the eggs and put them in a bowl. Sarah was very careful and did a great job. Mommy was proud of her little helper. They made yummy scrambled eggs together and enjoyed them for breakfast. The end.

Once there was a tiger who liked to go for walks. He had a beautiful orange coat and his mind was always full of ideas and fun. One day he went for a walk in the wild and heard some birds singing. He was charmed by the sound and stopped to take a closer look. He loved how peaceful it was and he wanted to keep listening. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud roar and he realised it was coming from a much bigger tiger. He was scared, but the other tiger just wanted to play! He crawled closer and the two of them had so much fun. They chased each other around, pouncing and growling. 

After they had their fill, they both lay down in the sun and just enjoyed being together. The smaller tiger was so happy that he met the bigger, more charming tiger. They stayed friends and went for walks together, always enjoying the beauty of the wild. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish little bean. It wanted to have some fun and be sprayed with water. So, it ran towards the garden hose and jumped in front of it. Suddenly, the water came out and sprayed all over the silly little bean. It got so wet and laughed with joy. After a while, the bean was all dried up, but it had enjoyed its adventure. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Maria. She was a very busy girl who liked to build things. She had built a swing, a castle, and a boat.

One day she decided to build a tower very high in the sky. She was excited to start the tower but it was hard for her to do it alone.

When she asked her mom for help her mom said, "I'm sorry honey, I can't help you right now." She was sad but knew she had to try anyway. 

So she decided to work hard and start building the tower all by herself. She used blocks and boards to build the tower higher and higher. But it still wasn't as tall as she wanted it to be.

Eventually, Maria asked her mom for help one more time and this time she said yes. With her mom's help, they were able to finish the tower together. It was much higher than Maria thought it would be and she was so proud!

Mum was very excited. She had a secret that she was going to unpack and show to everyone in the house. She asked Jimmy to close his eyes while she unpacked her secret. Then she asked him to open his eyes. 

Jimmyâ€™s face lit up with a big smile. He saw a shiny, smooth, toy train. It was the best train he had ever seen. Mum said it was a special train just for him. 

Jimmy was so happy he couldnâ€™t stop smiling. He began to play with his new toy train, unpacking and repacking the secret surprise that Mum had given him. He had so much fun with the train and was so thankful for his special present.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play pretend with his friends in the forest. They would pretend to be pirates and sail on a big ship.

One day, Benny and his friends found a beautiful harbor by the river. They decided to pretend that they were pirates and sail their ship to the harbor. They were very excited to explore the new place.

As they got closer to the harbor, they saw a big boat with a flag that had a skull on it. Benny's friends were scared and wanted to turn back, but Benny was brave and said they should keep going. When they got to the harbor, they saw that the boat belonged to some friendly pirates who invited them to join in the fun.

Benny and his friends had a great time playing with the pirates and exploring the harbor. They even found some treasure! From that day on, they would often go back to the harbor to play pretend with their new pirate friends.

Susie was very excited today. She was going to see a big machine. When Susie arrived, she was amazed by how big it was.

'Wow, it is so big!' said Susie. 

Mommy smiled. 'It is very good,' said Mommy.

Suddenly, something went wrong with the machine. It started to make loud noises. Everyone around the machine started to panic. 

Susie was scared and started to cry.

But Mommy was calm. She held Susie's hand and said, 'It's okay. We will get this machine fixed, and it will be working again soon.'

Mommy was right. After a few minutes, someone changed a few things on the machine and it was good again. 

Susie was relieved and happy. 'Yay!' She said. 'Let's go home!' 

Mommy smiled and they walked away, hand-in-hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma was three years old and very playful. She liked to run and jump around.

One night, Emma was worried. She was worried that she hadn't gotten enough exercise that day. She wanted to go outside and play, but it was very dark outside. So instead, Emma hopped around and jumped on the couch.

The next morning, Emma was very sorry. She had heard her mum saying she needed to get more exercise. So she decided to try something new. She went outside and played in the grass and ran around the flowers. It was so much fun!

Emma was very happy. All her worries were gone and she was excited to get more exercise. Now she was always sure to get outside and move around as much as she could.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very grumpy. She had to make her bed every morning. She would grab her sheet and set it on the bed. But today her sheet wouldn't stay in place. She kept trying and trying but it kept sliding off. Finally, she threw it down grumpily. She asked her mom for help. Her mom set the sheet on the bed and finally it stayed put. The grumpy little girl was very happy. She hopped into bed and quickly fell asleep. The end.

The little girl was standing on the side of the road, watching all the people and bright flags in the parade. She was so excited and wanted to join in. Suddenly, she saw a group of children in the parade wearing cool hats, dancing and singing.

"I want to join!" the little girl shouted happily.

One of the adults in the parade saw the little girl and gave her a big smile. "Come on" he said, diving into the parade, "Come join the fun!"

The little girl followed him and started to dance with the other children. Everyone was laughing and having a great time.

But soon the little girl became frustrated. She couldn't keep up with the other children, and they were all having more fun than her. But then one of the adults came over and said:

"Come on, let's show them how to dive in this parade."

With a big smile, the little girl followed the adult and started to dance and sing. Soon, she was singing and dancing just like the other children, and everyone was having a great time. The little girl was happy and no longer frustrated.

Once upon a time there was a package. It was a big package and the package passed down the street. Everyone was scared when they looked at the package because it looked scary to them.

Then one day a boy saw the package. His name was Jake and he was three years old. He wasn't scared when he saw the package. Instead, he got very excited and he wanted to get the package.

So Jake ran over and grabbed the package. He opened it up and found a surprise inside. It was a puppy! Jake hugged the puppy and was very happy.

He showed the puppy to all his friends and everyone was excited for him. The puppy was scared at first, but it soon started to like all the new people. Now Jake and his puppy are best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny, dirty acorn. He lived in a big, green forest. Every day he would pass the same big trees and all the other little animals. 

One day, the acorn wanted to explore. So he started going in the opposite direction. After a few steps, he noticed something shiny. It was a much bigger acorn! He was bigger and cleaner than the tiny, dirty acorn. 

The tiny acorn was excited, so he passed the big acorn and started running in circles around him. He wanted to show the big acorn that he was just as fast and strong. 

For the rest of the afternoon, the two acorns played together and passed each other back and forth. They both had lots of fun. The big acorn even taught the tiny acorn a few tricks! 

At the end of the day, the acorns had to part ways and said their goodbyes. The tiny, dirty acorn said he would never forget all the fun they had together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, she drew a picture of a dark forest with lots of trees. She used her green pastel to color the leaves and her brown pastel to color the trunks. 

As she finished her drawing, Lily noticed a bunny hopping by. She stared at the bunny for a while and then decided to draw it too. She used her pink pastel to color the bunny's ears and her white pastel to color its fluffy tail. 

Lily was very happy with her drawing and showed it to her mom. Her mom loved it too and hung it on the fridge for everyone to see. From that day on, Lily loved to draw animals and nature with her pastel crayons.

Once upon a time there was a boy who thought he was very clever. He was always trying to escape doing his chores. One day his mommy asked him to clean his bedroom. The boy was very ignorant and refused to do it.

Mommy told him if he didn't clean his bedroom he would have to stay in it all day. The boy still didn't move. So Mommy said he would have to wear a hat shaped like a cleaning brush on his head until he did. That made the boy angry and he quickly cleaned his room.

When he was finished Mommy took the hat off his head and said, "Now you see how nice it is to finish what you have to do!" The boy nodded with a smile, he had learned his lesson. From that day onwards he was more careful about cleaning. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cat named Mittens who had very soft fur. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we are going to have guests over for dinner tonight. Can you help me prepare the table?"

Lily said, "Yes, Mommy! I will help you." She ran to the table and put the plates and cups on it. Then, she went to her room to get her modest dress to wear for dinner.

While Lily was getting ready, Mittens came into her room. Lily said, "Mittens, you have such pretty fur. Let me brush it for you." Mittens purred happily as Lily brushed her fur.

When the guests arrived, Lily helped her mom bring the food to the table. Everyone sat down and enjoyed the delicious meal. After dinner, Lily's mom said, "Thank you for helping me prepare for dinner, Lily. You are such a great helper!" Lily smiled and felt proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a Huge spaghetti that stretched from one mountain to the other. Two little children, Jack and Jane, were standing by the spaghetti. 

"Let's twist it!" said Jane. 

"We can't," said Jack. "It's too Huge."

Jane kept insisting, but Jack refused. 

Suddenly, an old lady came walking by. She had a kind face and she was wearing a shawl. "What are you trying to do?" she asked the children. 

"We want to twist the Huge spaghetti," said Jane.

The old lady smiled and shook her head. "It's too Huge for you to twist. But if you work together and never give up, you can do it," she said.

Jack and Jane worked very hard, and eventually they managed to twist the Huge spaghetti. As they enjoyed the view of their accomplishment, the old lady smiled.

The moral of the story is to never give up! No matter how Huge the task may seem, if you work together you can accomplish anything.

Once upon a time there was an ordinary barber. He cut people's hair and made them feel happy. Every day he watched people come and go from his shop. One day a little boy walked into the shop. He was only three years old and his hair was very messy.

He sat on the barber's chair and the barber started to cut his hair. His little eyes watched as the barber snipped away. When the barber was finished, the little boy's hair looked neat and tidy. He was very pleased and thanked the barber.

The barber watched as the little boy skipped out of the shop. He smiled to himself and thought, "That's why I love being an ordinary barber."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Millie. She was 3-years-old and very curious. One day, Millie sneaked away and went to explore a nearby bush. Millie forgot about the time and soon her mom called her back home. Millie was embarrassed because she had been gone so long. 

When Millie got home, her mom decided to cook them a special dinner. She made Millie a yummy bowl of spaghetti and meatballs. Millie ate every bite and was so happy. 

Millie never ever snuck away to explore another bush again. She was just too embarrassed. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a class. In this class there was a group of kids. They liked to play together and have fun. One thing they did not like was their teacher. She was very mean, and always said mean things. She even made them do disgusting things.

One day they decided they wanted to make a plan. They wanted to make the teacher include them in something fun. So they came up with an idea. They decided to hide in the classroom and steal all the teacher's books. When the teacher came back she was very angry!

The kids laughed and said the teacher needed to include them more. They said if she did, the things she made them do wouldn't be so disgusting. The teacher looked at them and thought for a moment.

The next day the teacher came to class with a smile on her face. She said that her plan was to include the kids in her next lesson. They were very happy and played together until it was time to start the lesson. 

The lesson turned out to be some of the most fun they had ever had in class. It was so much better than doing disgusting things! From then on, the teacher always made sure to include the kids in everything.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lucy. She loved to play in the park. One day when she was there, she saw a slide. She smiled and went over to it. 

Lucy said, "I am going to slide down this slide!" She climbed up to the top of the slide. It was big and it was clear like glass. She put her hands in the air and then slid down. She screamed as she went faster and faster. 

At the bottom, Lucy saw a big bowl of water. She asked, "Should I drink this water?" 

But then she saw a sign. It said, "Sliding is fun but drinking is not allowed." Lucy smiled and said, "Okay, I won't drink the water." 

Lucy went down the slide again. And then she went home, happy and thirsty.

Ben and Lily were twins. They liked to play and have fun. But they did not like to share. They wanted to have their own things.

One day, it was their birthday. Mom and Dad gave them a big present. They put it on the table and said, "This is for both of you. You have to open it together and share it."

Ben and Lily were curious. They ran to the table and tore the paper. Inside the box, they saw something disgusting. It was a big cake with worms and bugs on it. They screamed and jumped back.

"Yuck! What is this?" Ben said.

"This is not a present. This is a prank!" Lily said.

Mom and Dad laughed. They said, "We are sorry. We wanted to make a joke. This is not your real present. Your real present is in the closet. Go and see."

Ben and Lily were angry. They did not like the joke. They did not want to see the present in the closet. They said, "No, thank you. We do not want your present. We do not trust you."

Mom and Dad felt bad. They said, "Please, give us a chance. We promise, this is a good present. You will like it. It is something you both wanted."

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They were still mad, but they were also curious. They decided to give Mom and Dad a chance. They went to the closet and opened the door. Inside, they saw two bikes. One was blue and one was pink. They had bells and baskets and stickers. They were beautiful.

Ben and Lily smiled. They said, "Wow! These are our presents? We love them! Thank you, Mom and Dad!"

Mom and Dad hugged them. They said, "You are welcome. We are sorry for the cake. We hope you forgive us. We love you very much."

Ben and Lily forgave them. They said, "We love you too. But next time, please do not give us disgusting cakes. They are not funny. They are gross."

Mom and Dad agreed. They said, "OK, no more disgusting cakes. Only yummy ones. Now, let's go outside and ride your bikes. Happy birthday, Ben and Lily!"

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little cat called Fluffy. One day, Fluffy was wandering around when she noticed something shiny. It was a pattern of lines on the ground. She had never seen anything like it before and couldn't help but have a closer look. She started to stir the lines with her paw.

When she stirred, something magical happened. Suddenly, the lines began to move around and turn into shapes and colours. Fluffy couldn't believe her eyes!

Soon, the shapes and colours began to move. They started to form a beautiful dance and soon a story emerged. Fluffy watched in wonder as the shapes danced around and told their magical story.

When the story was over, Fluffy knew she had to find out what the pattern was. She went home and asked everyone she knew, but no one could answer her.

Until one day, her nosy friend George found out about the magical pattern. He said it was called a mandala. Fluffy was so excited to learn about her new discovery and couldn't wait to show it to her friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane had a friend named Joe who was very selfish. Every time Joe would come over to play, he would take all of Jane's toys without asking and leave her nothing to play with.

This made Jane very sad, so she would weep. But she was too scared to tell Joe how she felt.

One day Joe came over with a new toy: it was a spike. He showed it off to Jane and then took away all of her toys again. Jane stared down at the ground and her eyes filled with tears.

Joe saw this and started to feel a little bit guilty. He offered Jane the spike so they could both play together. Jane smiled and hugged it tight.

Joe saw that Jane was happy, and felt much better. From then on, Joe was a lot less selfish and they both had lots of fun playing together!

One day, a dull comet was flying through the sky. The comet was not shiny and bright like the other comets. It was sad because it wanted to be pretty too.

Then, a little bird saw the comet and wanted to help. The bird did not want the comet to be sad. So, the bird found some pretty things to put on the comet. The bird found shiny stars and put them on the comet. The comet was very happy.

But, the other comets did not like it. They said the bird was trying to spoil the comet. The comet did not care. It was happy with its new shiny stars. The bird and the comet became friends and played together in the sky.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jill. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad.

One day, Jill saw a key in the hall. She asked her dad what it was for.
"That key unlocks the door to the backyard," her dad said.

Jill was excited! She grabbed the key, put it in the lock and turned it. It worked! She opened the door to the backyard.

When she stepped outside, Jill was met with a sweet surprise. There were flowers, butterflies and a special playground just for her! Jill was so happy. She ran around, playing with the flowers and butterflies, and trying out all the fun things in the playground.

"This is the best backyard ever!" Jill said. Her dad smiled and gave her a big hug.

The end.

Once upon a time, in a big house, there lived a little girl. She was only three years old, but very determined and strong. She loved playing games. Each day, she would set up a game and have fun with her friends.

One day, when the little girl was playing a game, she noticed something strange. Her friends were all so weak and tired, so she decided to help them out. She asked them all to sit in a big circle and then started to count. One, two, three, four. She counted in a funny voice, and her friends all laughed.

The little girl soon found that counting made the game much more fun. She began to create new games involving counting. She would get her friends to count the stars in the sky, or the petals on a flower. Counting brought them all together and made them stronger.

The little girl found that counting was a powerful tool. It made her friends happy, it made them laugh, and it made them feel better. Whenever her friends were feeling weak, she would get them together and count. It always cheered them up. 

That's the power of counting. It can make even the weakest people feel strong.

Lila liked to make things with string. She had many colors of string in her box. She could make bracelets, necklaces, and pictures with string. She liked to show her things to her friends and family.

One day, she had an idea. She wanted to make something unusual with string. She took a long piece of green string and tied it to a stick. Then she took a short piece of red string and tied it to the green string. She made a loop with the red string. She had made a string bow.

She found a thin piece of wood and made it sharp at both ends. She tied a yellow string to it. She had made a string arrow. She was very proud of her string bow and arrow.

She went to the garden and looked for a target. She saw a big pumpkin. She put the arrow on the bow and pulled the string. She let go of the string and the arrow flew. It hit the pumpkin with a thud.

Lila was very happy. She had hit the pumpkin with her string arrow. She ran to the pumpkin and picked up her arrow. She saw her mom and dad watching her from the window. They smiled and clapped their hands. They applauded her for her unusual string bow and arrow. Lila waved at them and smiled. She felt very good. She loved to make things with string.

Lily and Ben like to visit the park with Mom. They like to play on the swings, slide and sandbox. They also like to look for twigs and leaves on the ground. They make pretend houses and boats with them.

One day, they see a big pile of twigs near a tree. They run to it and start to take some. They do not see the sign that says "Do not touch". They do not hear Mom calling them to come back.

The pile of twigs is not just twigs. It is a nest for bees. The bees do not like Lily and Ben taking their twigs. They get angry and fly out of the nest. They buzz very loud and sting Lily and Ben all over.

Lily and Ben scream and cry. They drop the twigs and run to Mom. Mom hugs them and takes them to the car. She drives them to the doctor. The doctor gives them medicine and bandages. He says they will be okay, but they have to stay home for a few days.

Lily and Ben are very sad. They do not like bees. They do not like twigs. They do not want to visit the park again. They wish they had listened to Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to mix juice for her friends. One day, she had a great idea. She wanted to have a juice party!

She invited all her friends to her house. When they arrived, she showed them all the different juices she had. There was red juice, yellow juice, and even green juice! Lily was very generous and wanted to share everything with her friends.

"Let's mix the juices together!" said Lily. Her friends loved the idea. They took turns mixing the juices in a big bowl. The juice became a beautiful rainbow color. Everyone was so happy and they enjoyed the tasty rainbow juice together.

Lily liked to read books. She had many books with pictures and words. She could read some words by herself, and some words she asked her mom or dad to help her.

One day, she found a new book in her room. It was a big book with a shiny cover. It had a picture of a circle on it. Lily wondered what the book was about. She opened it and saw many circles inside. Some circles were big, some were small, some were red, some were blue, some were dotted, some were striped.

Lily started to read the words under the circles. She read: "This is a circle. A circle is round. A circle has no corners. A circle can roll. A circle can spin. A circle can be a ball, a wheel, a cookie, or a ring."

Lily liked the book. She thought circles were fun and interesting. She wanted to show the book to her friend Max. She called him on the phone and said: "Hi, Max. I have a new book. It is about circles. Do you want to see it?"

Max said: "Sure, Lily. I like circles too. They are not ordinary. They are special. Can I come to your house and read the book with you?"

Lily said: "Yes, Max. Come to my house. We can read the book and play with circles. We can make circles with paper, with clay, with string, or with anything we want."

Max said: "OK, Lily. I will come soon. I am excited to read the book and play with circles. See you later."

Lily said: "Bye, Max. See you later."

Lily put the book on the table and waited for Max. She was happy to have a new book and a good friend. She thought circles were not ordinary. They were amazing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big power, she could run very fast! One day, Lily was playing outside when she saw a little bird that was suffering. The bird had hurt its wing and couldn't fly anymore. 

Lily was very careful and picked up the bird gently. She brought it to her mommy who knew how to take care of hurt animals. Her mommy gave the bird some medicine and a bandage for its wing. 

Lily was so happy that she could help the little bird feel better. She knew that even though she was small, she had the power to make a difference. From that day on, Lily was always careful when playing outside, making sure to watch out for any animals that might be suffering.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing tag when she saw a man walking towards them. He had a big bag with him.

Lily's mommy had told her to be careful around strangers, so she ran to her mommy to tell her about the man. Her mommy thanked her for being so smart and told her to stay close to her.

Later that day, Lily and her mommy went to the store to buy some oil for cooking. The bottle was very rough and bumpy, but Lily liked how it felt in her hands. When they got home, Lily helped her mommy cook dinner. She had to kneel on a chair to reach the stove, but she was very careful not to spill the oil.

As they sat down to eat, Lily's mommy told her how proud she was of her for being so smart and careful earlier. Lily smiled and felt happy. She knew she had done the right thing.

Sam and Lily were playing soccer in the park. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they would pass the ball to each other and try to score a goal.

"Pass me the ball, Lily!" Sam shouted. He was near the goal and wanted to try a shot.

Lily kicked the ball hard to Sam. But the ball was too fast and went over his head. It landed near a big tree, where a boy was sitting and reading a book.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Sam said. He ran to the tree and tried to get the ball back. But the boy did not let him. He held the ball in his arms and said, "No, this is my ball now. I found it."

"That's not fair!" Lily said. She ran to the tree too and tried to help Sam. "You did not find it, you took it. Give it back to us!"

The boy shook his head and said, "No, this is a brilliant ball. It is shiny and round and bouncy. I like it. It is mine."

Sam and Lily did not know what to do. They wanted their ball back, but the boy was bigger and stronger than them. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They both kneeled on the ground and pretended to cry. They made loud and sad noises. They said, "Please, please, give us our ball back. We love our ball. It is our favorite toy. We have nothing else to play with. Please, please, don't be mean."

The boy heard them and felt sorry for them. He did not like to see them cry. He said, "OK, OK, stop crying. Here, take your ball back. But you have to let me play with you. I have no friends to play with. Please, please, don't be mean."

Sam and Lily stopped crying and smiled. They said, "OK, OK, you can play with us. But you have to be nice and share the ball. We can all have fun together. Please, please, don't be mean."

The boy nodded and smiled too. He gave them the ball back and joined them. They all kicked the ball and ran after it. Sometimes they would pass the ball to each other and try to score a goal. They had a brilliant time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside, but today it was raining. His mom told him to stay inside, but Timmy was bored. So, he put on his raincoat and went outside to play.

Timmy ran around and jumped in puddles. He didn't realize that the ground was getting very wet. He saw a slide and decided to climb up. When he got to the top, he slipped and fell. He hit his head and started to cry.

His mom heard him and came outside. She saw that Timmy was hurt and took him to the hospital. The doctor said that Timmy had a bad injury and needed to stay in the hospital for a long time. Timmy wished he had stayed inside and sat on the couch. Now he knew that he should always listen to his mom and stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big, scary lion. He had a big, strong roar that could be heard from far away. One day, he met a little girl who was missing a tooth. She was scared of the lion, but he said, "Don't be scared, little one. I won't hurt you." The little girl was surprised that the lion could talk, but she felt better. 

The lion asked the little girl if she wanted to play a game. The little girl said, "Yes, please!" The lion said, "Let's play hide and seek. I'll count to ten and you hide." The little girl ran off to hide behind a tree. The lion counted, "One, two, three..." and then he heard a giggling sound. He found the little girl and said, "I found you! You're yummy, just like my favorite food." 

The little girl giggled and said, "I'm not food, silly lion. I'm a person." The lion felt embarrassed and said, "I'm sorry. I won't eat you. Let's be friends instead." The little girl smiled and said, "Okay, let's be friends." From that day on, the lion and the little girl played together every day.

Tommy was playing in the garden. It was a beautiful mild day and there were many animals in the garden. He saw a cage with some small creatures in it. They were sorting themselves into two groups. He was curious and wanted to get closer. He stepped closer and suddenly one of them flew out of the cage. He was scared and ran away.

The small creature tried to fly away but its wings were too weak. It ran away but couldnâ€™t get very far. Tommy followed it and saw that it was trying to get back into the cage. He tried to catch it but it was too quick. It was almost back in the cage when Tommy finally grabbed it.

Tommy put the creature back in the cage and watched as it reunited with its friends. He felt sorry that it had caused so much trouble but also happy that they were all safe again. He watched them sort themselves into two different groups before going off to play. Tommy smiled, feeling satisfied that he had helped solve the problem.

One day, Sam and Sue had a plan. They wanted to go on vacation. So, Sam and Sue packed their bags and got ready to go.

"Where should we go?" asked Sue.

"Let's go to the beach!" said Sam, excitedly.

"Let's be patient!" replied Sue. "We need to make sure we have everything with us before we go. Have you got your bathing suit?"

Sam checked his bag. "Yes, I've got it!"

So, Sam and Sue patiently made their plan and packed their bags. Finally, they were ready.

"Are you ready for our vacation?" asked Sue excitedly.

"Yes!" said Sam, and off they went.

Once upon a time, there was a young rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to run and play with his friends every day of the week. One day, Benny's friends wanted to race to see who was the fastest. Benny was so excited that he started to zoom ahead of everyone else. But then, he realized that he had left his friends behind.

Benny felt sad because he had forgotten that it was important to be kind and wait for his friends. So, Benny decided to slow down and wait for his friends to catch up. When they all crossed the finish line together, they all felt happy and proud of each other.

Benny learned an important lesson that day. It's not about being the fastest or the best, but it's about having fun with your friends and being kind to others. From that day on, Benny made sure to always wait for his friends and have fun together every week.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle. In the jungle, there was a leopard. The leopard was very playful. He liked to run and jump and play with his friends. 

One day, the leopard saw a friend far away. He wanted to say hello. So he lifted his paw and waved it in the air. The friend saw the leopard and waved back. 

The leopard was happy. He ran over to his friend and they played together. They ran and jumped and had fun. The leopard was very happy to have such a good friend.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy cowboy named Timmy. Timmy had a shiny pistol that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy was playing with his pistol when he accidentally dropped it. The pistol went off and a loud noise scared Timmy.

Timmy's friend, a brave horse named Sparky, heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. Timmy told Sparky that he was scared and that he needed help. Sparky knew just what to do. He ran to get the sheriff to save Timmy.

The sheriff came quickly and saw that Timmy was okay, but he scolded him for playing with his pistol. Timmy promised to be more careful and thanked Sparky and the sheriff for saving him. From that day on, Timmy never played with his pistol again.

Once upon a time, there was an oven. Every day, the oven wanted to fit all of its food inside. But, sadly, the oven couldn't! Every time it tried, the food wouldn't fit. Then, one day, a little girl came by. She looked at the oven and said, "let me help you". 

The little girl tried to help the oven. She moved the food around and made it fit. The oven was so happy that it could hold all of its food! But then, something went wrong. The food started to smoke! The oven was so upset. 

The little girl was sad, too. She didn't want the oven to feel upset, so she thought of something. She took out the food and put it in a special box. Now, the oven had enough space to fit in all its food. The oven was so happy that it smiled! The little girl put the food back in the oven and hugged it. Now the oven was no longer upset.

Once upon a time, there was a big comet in the night sky. It was so impressive that everyone stopped to stare. Two curious kids, John and Anna, were admiring it.

John: "Can we go closer to it, Anna? Let's go outside and see it!"
Anna: "No, John! It's too dark!"

But John didn't want to give up. He kept asking until Anna finally said yes. So they went outside and stood near the comet, quietly admiring its beautiful colors. After a few minutes, they sat down and relaxed, looking at the starry sky and smiling.

John: "This is so relaxing, isn't it, Anna?"
Anna: "Yes! The comet is really impressive! Let's come back here next time and relax." 

And that's exactly what they did! Every night, John and Anna would look at the comet and relax together. Every time it was more beautiful and impressive than before.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to visit his grandma's house because she always had yummy cookies. One day, Timmy saw a cop car parked outside his grandma's house. He asked his grandma why the cop was there, and she said the cop was just visiting to check on her. Timmy thought it was cool that a cop would visit his grandma. After the cop left, Timmy and his grandma enjoyed their cookies together. The end.

The boy had many questions. He wondered what an airport was. He asked his mum what the strange place was and why they were heading there. His mum smiled and explained that an airport was a special place where people fly around the world in big colourful planes. She said that they were going to the airport to go on a holiday.

The boy was excited! He liked flying on planes, and he liked discovering new places so he couldn't wait to get to the airport.

At the airport, he was amazed. It was big, bright and busy. He turned to his mum and wondered out loud. He asked if they were allowed to fly. His mum laughed and said yes of course! He was going to fly to the beach!

The boy was so happy. He couldn't believe that he was going to fly in the sky. The boy stayed close to his mum and watched in awe. He watched people check in their bags and thought of creative ways to use their luggage. 

When the plane took off, the boy felt so excited. He waved goodbye to the airport and looked forward to all of the new adventures that his holiday would bring!

Once upon a time, there was a big, happy family. The mom cooked a delicious dinner for everyone to eat. The dad went to check the mail and found a letter from their grandparents. They were excited to read it together.

After dinner, the family went to the living room. The dad displayed the letter on the table for everyone to see. The kids were happy to see the letter from their grandparents. They read it together and talked about how much they missed them.

The family was grateful for the letter and the delicious dinner. They hugged each other and went to bed with happy hearts. The end.

Once upon a time there was a mom and her son. His name was Jack. One morning they were in the kitchen together.

"Do you want to have cereal for breakfast?" Mom asked.

"Yes, please," Jack said. He was very excited!

Mom took a box of cereal out of the cupboard and let Jack pour it into his bowl. He was so clever! He could do it all on his own.

Then Mom added some milk so the cereal was all nice and creamy.

"Yum!" said Jack. He ate every last bite of his cereal. 

"You're such a clever boy!" Mom said, giving Jack a big hug. "Let's do it again tomorrow!"

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. Lily loved to go to the store with her mom. One day, her mom bought her a new toy. Lily was very happy and played with it all day.

But then, Lily did something she wasn't supposed to do. She broke her mom's vase. Her mom was very angry and said she would have to punish Lily. Lily felt very sad and knew she shouldn't have broken the vase. 

The next day, Lily went back to the store with her mom. She saw a new toy that she really wanted, but she remembered how she had been punished the day before. She decided to be good and not ask for the toy. Her mom was proud of her and bought her a treat for being so well-behaved. From then on, Lily always tried to be good and not get punished.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jody. She was very shy and loved to skip. One day she was skipping along when she saw a word on the ground. It said â€œrunâ€. Jody wasnâ€™t sure what it meant, so she asked her mom, â€œWhat does â€˜runâ€™ mean?â€

Her mom smiled. â€œIt means that you can move quickly. Do you want to try it?â€

Jody thought for a minute and then nodded. She tried running and it was fun! She was still shy so she was careful not to run too fast. But she kept on running and soon she was skipping and running at the same time. 

Jody smiled. She had found a new way to skip! From then on whenever she saw a word on the ground, she stopped to think of what it might mean.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear named Benny. Benny had a big chest and he loved to show it off to his friends. His friends always admired his chest and thought it was the biggest and strongest chest in the forest.

One day, Benny met a little rabbit named Rosie. Rosie was very patient and kind. Benny admired her patience and wanted to be her friend. They played together and had lots of fun.

But one day, Benny got stuck in a trap and couldn't get out. His big chest was too big to fit through the trap. Rosie remembered how patient Benny had been with her and knew she had to help him. She found a way to free Benny from the trap and they became even better friends.

From that day on, Benny admired Rosie's kindness and patience. He realized that having a big chest wasn't as important as having a good friend like Rosie.

The boy's friends wanted to stand on top of the volcano. They said it would be a fun adventure. The boy knew it was not a good idea to be so careless. But all his friends wanted to do it, so he followed them and they climbed the volcano.

At first, they were having a lot of fun together. But then suddenly, an earthquake happened and the ground started shaking violently. The boy was too scared to move and he knew it was dangerous to stand there. But his friends were careless and kept playing.

Then, a big part of the volcano broke off and fell in the boy's direction. He was standing in the way, so he couldn't escape. The rock hit him and he was hurt badly. The boy's friends ran away, scared and shocked.

The boy was taken to the hospital, but it was too late. He had suffered too much damage and he died. His friends were very sad and regretted not being more careful. If only they had listened to the boy, his death could have been prevented. But it was too late.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who loved to eat shrimp. They were famous in their village for how much shrimp they could eat. One day, they found only one shrimp left and they both wanted it. They began to quarrel, shouting and pushing each other. Suddenly, the shrimp fell on the ground and a dog ate it. The two friends were sad and went home without eating any shrimp. From that day on, they never quarreled again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Patrick and Sally. They were both feeling lucky because it was almost time to celebrate.

"Let's get some wine," suggested Patrick.

"Great idea!" laughed Sally.

Patrick and Sally went to the store to buy some wine. They each chose one bottle that was just right for their celebration.

When they got back home, they each opened their bottle of wine and poured some into two glasses.

"Cheers to us," said Patrick happily.

Sally smiled and clinked her glass with Patrick's.

They drank their wine and celebrated the rest of the day.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small baby rabbit. He was hopping through the forest one day when he saw a beautiful billboard. It shined brightly in the sun and the baby rabbit wanted it for himself.

He hopped up to it carefully and started to steal it. He carried it all the way back to his home and proudly put it in his burrow. He thought it was the prettiest thing ever and was very happy.

But when he was sleeping, a big grouchy bear came by and saw the billboard. The bear was angry because someone had stolen it and he wanted it back.

The bear growled loudly and stomped over to the baby rabbit's burrow. He grabbed the billboard from the baby rabbit and took it back to the forest where it belonged.

The baby rabbit was very upset but knew that the grouchy bear was right. He shouldn't have stolen the billboard, even if it was very small.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and look for bugs. Lily had a jar with a lid. She put some dirt and grass in it. She wanted to catch a bug and keep it in the jar.

"Look, Ben, I found a worm!" Lily said. She picked up the worm and put it in the jar. She closed the lid. "Now I have a pet worm!"

Ben looked at the jar. He saw the worm wriggling inside. He wanted to touch it. He asked Lily, "Can I hold the jar?"

Lily nodded. She gave the jar to Ben. Ben held the jar and watched the worm. He smiled. He liked the worm too.

They heard their mom calling them. "Lily, Ben, time for lunch!" Mom said. She was in the house. The house was distant from the garden.

Lily and Ben ran to the house. They were hungry. They forgot the jar in the garden. They forgot the worm in the jar.

The worm was alone in the jar. It did not like the jar. It wanted to go back to the dirt. It pushed against the lid. The lid was loose. The worm pushed harder. The lid fell off. The worm crawled out of the jar. It went back to the dirt. It was happy.

One day Mummy and Daddy took Little John for a walk. He was curious about everything he saw, which made Mummy and Daddy smile. 

Little John saw a giant tree with a hole in it. Daddy said the hole was a home for a small creature called a woodpecker, who had made the hole. Little John was amazed!

Then Little John saw a problem - a little bird was stuck in the tree! Its tail was caught on a branch. Daddy called the bird Polly and said, â€œwe need to solve this problemâ€.

So Daddy put his arms around the tree and pulled very hard. He pulled so hard, the little bird was eventually freed. Daddy felt very proud and hugged Mummy with a big smile on his face. 

Little John asked Daddy how he had solved the problem. Daddy said, â€œI used all my strength in my waist and arms and that is how I made the bird free!" Little John was glad the problem was solved and hugged Daddy too.

Today Jim started the day off feeling very excited. His mom had a surprise for him. She took him outside and showed him a big pool! The water was blue and sparkly. 

Jim jumped in and had so much fun. He swam around and splashed in the water. Eventually, Jim got a little too wet. His mom decided it was time to get out of the pool. 

Mom brought Jim inside and gave him a pair of fresh clothes from his closet. Jim put them on and sat down in the kitchen. Jim's mom started to cut the wet clothes with some scissors. 

Jim watched his mom cut the wet clothes int o small pieces. He asked if he could cut too. Mom said yes, and Jim was very happy with his surprise. He and his mom laughed and laughed while they cut the wet clothes. 

When they were finished, Mom told Jim to put on his new dry clothes and gave him a hug. Jim thanked his mom for the fun day. He was so glad to have such a special surprise.

Anna loved to sail with her dad. They had a small boat with a white sail and a red flag. They sailed on the lake when the sun was bright and the wind was good. Anna liked to feel the wind in her hair and the water on her face.

One day, they saw a big boat with a blue sail and a gold flag. It was very pretty and shiny. Anna wanted to see it closer. She asked her dad if they could sail near it. Her dad said yes, but they had to be careful and not get too close.

They sailed near the big boat and saw that it had many people on it. They wore fancy clothes and hats. Some of them had velvet coats and dresses. Velvet was a soft and smooth fabric that Anna liked to touch. She wondered how it felt to wear velvet.

But then, a thick cloud came and covered the sun. The wind became strong and the water became rough. The big boat started to rock and sway. The people on it looked scared and shouted. Anna and her dad heard them say that the big boat was too heavy and could sink.

Anna and her dad quickly turned their small boat and sailed away from the big boat. They sailed back to the shore and tied their boat to a tree. They were safe and happy. Anna hugged her dad and said that she liked their small boat better than the big boat. Her dad smiled and said that he liked it too. They went home and had some hot chocolate.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went for a walk in the woods and found a shiny stone. The stone was so pretty, it made her happy. She held the stone up to the light and it began to glow. 

Lily was amazed by the way the stone glowed in the light. She decided to keep it in her pocket so she could show her mommy and daddy. As she walked home, she felt the stone in her pocket and smiled. 

When she got home, she ran up to her mommy and daddy and showed them the stone. They both said it was very pretty and they liked the way it glowed in the light. Lily was so happy that she found the stone and that her mommy and daddy liked it too. She decided to keep it forever and ever.

Lila was a restless girl who liked to explore. She always wondered what was behind every door and under every bed. One day, she found a big chamber in the basement of her house. It was dark and dusty, and full of old things.

"Wow, look at all this stuff!" Lila said to herself. She saw a chest, a lamp, a mirror, and a book. She opened the chest and found a dress, a hat, and a necklace. She put them on and looked at herself in the mirror. She felt like a princess.

She picked up the lamp and rubbed it. Nothing happened. She rubbed it harder. Still nothing. She shook it and heard a clink. She opened the lamp and saw a coin. She was happy. She put the coin in her pocket and looked at the book. It had a lock on it. She wondered what was inside.

She tried to open the book with the coin, but it did not work. She tried to break the lock with the lamp, but it did not work. She tried to pry it open with her fingers, but it did not work. She got angry and threw the book on the floor. It made a loud noise.

Suddenly, she heard footsteps on the stairs. It was her mom. She was coming to check on her. Lila was scared. She knew she was not supposed to be in the chamber. She quickly took off the dress, the hat, and the necklace, and put them back in the chest. She hid behind the chest and hoped her mom would not see her.

Her mom entered the chamber and saw the mess. She saw the lamp, the mirror, and the book on the floor. She saw the coin on the table. She saw the chest open. She knew Lila was there. She looked around and found her behind the chest.

"Lila, what are you doing here?" her mom asked. She was not happy. She was angry.

Lila did not answer. She looked down and felt sorry.

"Lila, you know you are not allowed to be in this chamber. This is where I keep my old things. They are not toys. They are precious to me. You could have broken them or lost them. You could have hurt yourself. You have been very naughty. You have to apologize and clean up this mess. And you have to give me back the coin. It is not yours. It is a special coin that my grandma gave me. It is very old and very valuable. Do you understand?" her mom said.

Lila nodded. She said sorry. She gave back the coin. She helped her mom clean up the mess. She learned her lesson. She learned to respect other people's things. She learned to be careful and not be so restless. She learned to wonder with her eyes, not with her hands.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Tom. He was very naughty and loved to have adventures. He often wanted to escape from his parents who chased him when he was naughty.

One day, he decided to try and escape them. He decided to make a fake plan. He wanted to spend the day roaming around in the park and running away from his parents. So, he pretended to go to bed but instead, he crept out of the house and ran to the park.

Tom spent the whole day playing and running around. He thought it was so much fun! He pretended to be an explorer and imagined he could escape from the park and explore the world.

Eventually, the evening came and Tom's parents had finally found him. Tom was quite sad to say goodbye to his pretend adventures but he was also glad to be back home. His parents gave him a hug and he knew that they would never let him escape again.

One day, Jack and his sister were playing in the rain. They kept running around and having fun with the water. Jack smiled as he watched his sister twirl in the puddles.

Then, Jack saw that his sister got very wet and was starting to shiver. He wanted to keep her warm, so he ran inside and brought her a big, fluffy towel. His sister thanked him and dried herself off.

Once she was warm and dry again, Jack and his sister sat on the porch and watched the rain keep falling. They giggled when a big splash hit them, then turned around and ran inside.

Jack and his sister had a very fun time that day. His sister said it reminded her of when they used to play together in the rain when they were much younger.

Jack smiled. He loved to keep his sister happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big oak tree. The oak tree stood tall in the middle of a pretty forest. Many animals lived near the oak tree and liked to play around it.

One day, a little squirrel wanted to build a new home. The squirrel found a nice spot on a branch of the oak tree. The squirrel was very happy and started to build its new home with leaves and sticks.

As the squirrel was building, it accidentally dropped a stick on a bird's nest below. The bird was upset and the squirrel felt sorry. The squirrel said "I am sorry" to the bird. The bird forgave the squirrel and they became friends. They both lived happily in the big oak tree.

Once upon a time, there was a deer in the forest. He was a very nice deer, but he was kind of scared. One day, he went to explore the woods and he noticed a scary noise. It was getting louder and louder. He could see a big shape in the trees. The deer was so scared he wanted to run away. Then, out of the trees came a big bear! It was roaring and growling and its teeth were very sharp. The deer was so scared he didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, the bear started to pull the deer closer and closer. The deer was so frightened he thought he was going to die. Just then, a little rabbit came out of the forest and started to hop around the bear. It was making funny noises and pulling on the bear's fur. The bear was so surprised, he let go of the deer and ran away. The deer was so happy he had been saved!

The little rabbit saved the deer and showed him a safe place to sleep. It was very nice. The deer thanked the rabbit and they became friends. They walked through the forest together and had lots of fun. The deer learned that even if something looks scary, it doesn't always mean it will hurt you. And he was so glad the little rabbit had been there to save him.

Anna and Ben liked to play in the garden. They had a big tent that they could hide in. They pretended it was a castle or a spaceship or a cave.

One day, they heard a loud noise from the tent. It sounded like a roar. They looked at each other and felt frightened. What was in the tent?

They crept closer to the tent and peeked inside. They saw a big, furry, brown thing. It had sharp teeth and claws. It was a bear!

"Hello, little ones," the bear said. "Don't be scared. I'm not going to hurt you. I'm just looking for a place to sleep."

Anna and Ben were surprised. The bear could talk! They felt less frightened and more curious.

"Where did you come from?" Anna asked.

"I came from the forest," the bear said. "I was looking for food, but I got lost. I saw your tent and thought it was a cozy den. I hope you don't mind."

Ben shook his head. "We don't mind. You can stay in our tent. But how did you fit inside? You're so big!"

The bear smiled. "I have a secret. I can grow and shrink as I please. Watch this." He closed his eyes and made a wish. He became smaller and smaller until he was the size of a teddy bear.

Anna and Ben gasped. They thought it was amazing. They invited the bear to play with them. They had fun with their new friend. They forgot to be frightened. They were happy.

One day, Tom was very eager. He did not know why, but he wanted to find out.

He asked his mum, â€œWhat is my surprise?â€

She smiled and said, â€œLetâ€™s go and see!â€

Tom and his mum went outside. They walked together until they came to a park. In the park, Tom could see a big tree with lots of colourful balloons around it.

Tom was so excited and ran to the tree. He had the best surprise ever! A puppy was sitting underneath the tree, just for him!

Tom was so happy. He hugged the puppy and named it Coco.

Tom was eager for many more surprises like this one!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary. Mary had a special request, she wanted to go to the church. Every Sunday she would ask her mom if she could go but her mom said no.

Today was different. Her mom said she could go! Mary was so excited. She was allowed to go with her uncle. They walked together through the streets, looking for the church.

Finally they reached it! The church was big and organized. There was a special bell they rang when they arrived. Mary smiled. She was happy to be in the church.

They went inside and there were lots of other people. Mary liked how everyone was so organized and she liked the music they sang.

When it was time to go, Mary said goodbye to everyone. She felt happy and content. Mary had reached her special goal.

Once there was a man who was very miserable. He had no friends, and he always felt sad. One day, he went to the store to buy some food. He saw a judge in the store.

The judge was very kind and said, "Hello, why are you so miserable?" The man told the judge his story. He said he was all alone and had no one to talk to.

The judge said, "I'm here now. Let's be friends!" The man was so happy to have a friend. The judge invited the man to have dinner in his house. The man was even happier. He was no longer lonely and miserable. They were very good friends and would often go to the store together.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go on a wild adventure. So he asked his mom, "Can I please go out into the wild?"

His mom said, "Yes, you may go, but be careful!" So the little boy set off into the wild world and he saw so many wonderful animals. 

He walked and walked until he came to a clearing where there was a wild animal. The animal was a big and hairy boar. He was very hungry and the little boy asked, "Will you give me some of your meat?" 

The boar said, "Yes, I shall leave some of my wild meat for you." So the little boy was very happy and picked up the wild meat off the ground. 

He continued his journey, happy to have found a piece of wild meat on his wild journey.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat. The boat was blue and it liked to float on the water. One day, the sun was very hot and the water began to dry up. The boat was sad because it could not float anymore.

A bird saw the boat and asked, "Why are you sad, little boat?" The boat said, "The water is dry and I cannot float. I miss the water." The bird wanted to help the boat, so it thought of an easy plan.

The bird told the boat, "I will find more water for you. Then you can float again!" The boat was happy and thanked the bird. The bird flew away and soon found a big pond. It came back and told the boat about the pond.

Together, the bird and the boat went to the big pond. The boat was able to float again and it was very happy. The bird and the boat played together in the water all day long. And they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was playing in her garden and found something very special, a pin! It was a beautiful pin with lots of sparkly colours. She was so excited and wanted to keep it forever, so she put it in her pocket.

Later that day, the little girl wanted to show her pin to her friends, but when she looked inside her pocket, it was gone! She was very sad, so she search everywhere but still could not find it.

The next morning she awoke and went back outside to look for the pin again. As she was searching, she heard a gentle voice. The voice said, "Stay here and you will find it." The little girl stayed and sure enough, there it was, her beautiful pin! She was so happy and knew that the voice was right. 

From then on, she would always listen to the voice when she was looking for something special.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. Their names were Lily and Winnie. They both had birthdays coming up, and they wanted to celebrate together!

Lily asked Winnie to come to her birthday party. Winnie was so excited, and they made all kinds of plans.

Unfortunately, Winnie got sick and had to delay her arrival. Lily was disappointed, but she was still happy for Winnie.

The day of the birthday party arrived, but Winnie was still sick. Lily was very sad, but she knew it was more useful for Winnie to rest instead of coming to the party.

The moral of this story is to remember the importance of taking care of yourself and your friends when needed. It is more useful than any birthday party.

Sara liked to play with her toy animals. She had many of them: a lion, a bear, a monkey, a bird, and more. She kept them in a big cage that her dad made for her. She was very organized and put each animal in its own place.

One day, she wanted to play with her bird. She opened the cage and reached for it. But the bird was scared and flew away. Sara was sad and ran after it. She saw it land on a tree outside her window.

"Come back, bird, come back!" she cried. "You are my friend, I want to play with you!"

But the bird did not listen. It liked the tree and the sky. It did not want to go back to the cage.

Sara was very angry. She grabbed the cage and threw it on the floor. She started to tear it apart. She broke the bars, the door, the roof. She made a big mess.

Her dad heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. He saw Sara and the broken cage. He was not happy.

"Sara, what did you do?" he asked. "Why did you tear the cage? That was not nice. You hurt your toy animals and made a big mess."

Sara looked at her dad. She felt sorry. She did not mean to be bad. She just wanted her bird back.

"I'm sorry, dad," she said. "I was mad. The bird flew away and did not come back. I love the bird. I miss the bird."

Her dad hugged her. He understood. He loved the bird too. He said, "I know, Sara, I know. But tearing the cage was not the answer. The bird is free now. Maybe it will come back someday. But we have to respect its choice. And we have to take care of our other toy animals. They are your friends too. Can you help me fix the cage and clean the mess?"

Sara nodded. She said, "Yes, dad, I can. I'm sorry. I will be more careful next time."

They worked together to fix the cage and clean the mess. They put the toy animals back in their places. Sara gave them each a hug and a kiss. She was still sad about the bird, but she was also happy to have her dad and her other toy animals. She was organized again.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to visit the sea. They liked to watch the big boats and the small fish. They also liked to play with the sand and the shells.

One day, they saw a shiny thing in the water. It was an anchor. It was very big and heavy. Lily and Ben wanted to touch it.

"Let's go and see the anchor," Lily said.

"But it is too deep," Ben said. "We can't swim there."

Lily was brave. She said, "We can use this rope. It is long and strong. We can tie it to the anchor and pull it out."

Ben was scared. He said, "No, Lily, it is too hard. We might get hurt. And what if the boat comes back and wants the anchor?"

Lily did not listen. She took the rope and ran to the water. She threw the rope over the anchor and tried to pull it out. But the anchor was too heavy. Lily could not move it. She pulled and pulled, but the rope only got tighter around her hand.

"Help, Ben, help!" Lily cried. "The rope is hurting me. I can't get free."

Ben heard Lily's cry. He was scared, but he was also brave. He ran to the water and saw Lily's hand. He took a knife from his pocket and cut the rope. He freed Lily's hand and hugged her.

"Are you okay, Lily?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben, I'm okay. Thank you for saving me. You are very brave," Lily said.

They ran back to the shore and told their mom what happened. Their mom was angry and worried. She scolded them for being foolish and careless. She also hugged them and kissed them. She was glad they were safe.

She said, "Lily and Ben, you are brave, but you are also silly. You should never play with things that are not yours. And you should never go near the water without me. The sea is beautiful, but it is also dangerous. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, mom, we understand. We are sorry. We love you."

They learned their lesson. They never played with the anchor again. They still liked to visit the sea, but they always stayed with their mom. They also always said hello to the boat and the fish. They were happy and careful.

Once upon a time, there was a very important train. It was going so fast, it could travel from one end of the track to the other in no time at all.

One day, a bad monster made a big threat. He said if the train didn't stop, he would do something terrible. So the train driver quickly made the train stop.

Then the train driver did something amazing. He made the train reverse! The monster was so surprised and scared, he ran away.

The train continued its journey and everyone was so happy to see it go. From that day on, the train driver was very important and everyone thanked him for having the courage to make the train reverse and save them from the bad monster's threat.

Once upon a time there was a poor goose. She lived alone in a small pond. Every day she would look for food, but she never seemed to find enough. One day she was feeling very hungry. She decided to go for a walk, hoping to find something to eat. As she was walking, she came to a hill. The top of the hill was closed, so the goose couldn't go any further. She was so disappointed. She turned around and started to go back home. Suddenly, she heard a noise. It was a farmer with lots of food. She asked him if she could have some, and the farmer was very kind. He gave the poor goose some food and she was very happy. She thanked him and said goodbye. The goose could now go back home with a full belly, happy and content.

One day, Mommy and Johnny went to the park. They saw a tall grass and Mommy decided to cook it. Johnny was so excited and watched as Mommy picked the grass. 

Mommy found a mysterious pot and put the grass in it. Then she added a few unknown ingredients. Johnny stared in amazement as it smelled so good. 

Mommy lit the fire and stirred the pot. She continued to stir and stir until the grass was cooked. Johnny was so excited!
 
Mommy served the tasty grass for dinner and both Mommy and Johnny loved it. They laughed and smiled as they enjoyed their yummy dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a seal. He lived by the beach and loved playing in the ocean all day. One day, a big, selfish wave came and tried to sweep the seal away.

The Seal called out to the wave, "Please stay away from me!"
But the big, selfish wave ignored the Seal's plea and kept pushing him further away from the beach.

The Seal eventually managed to stay near the shore by swimming very hard. He was very tired, but he was happy he was back home.

The Seal warned the wave, "You must be more careful and less selfish when you play with others!"

The wave tried to listen, but it was hard because it was so big and strong. The wave promised to try its best to be more careful and finally the Seal was satisfied. 

From then on, the Seal and the wave played together near the beach. The wave learnt to be less selfish and the Seal learnt that it was important to stand up for himself.

One day, Jane wanted to go on a ride. She got into her daddy's big, red car. It was so big that it looked like it would never fit in the tiny garage. But somehow, it got in and the garage door closed. 

 Jane and her dad drove to a bright park. When they got there, they saw a tall slide. Jane screamed with delight! She put on her helmet and raced over to the slide. "Whee!" she yelled as she rode down. 

Her dad watched, smiling. When she was done, he said, "Let's go find a shelter for lunch." Jane nodded eagerly. They walked until they found a nice, sun-filled spot beneath a big tree. Dad put out a blanket and Jane munched on her lunch. 

After lunch, Dad said, "Let's go for another ride!" Jane clapped her hands and raced off to find another slide. She could hardly wait to go down it!

Once upon a time, there was a big yellow bird. He was so sad and felt so gloomy. He wanted to find some friends to make him feel better. He flew around looking in many places but he could not find any.

Then one day he came across a group of birds. They all had different colors and looked very happy. He asked if he could join them. They happily said yes and included the yellow bird.

He was so excited to have some friends! They all played and sang together. The yellow bird was very happy and the gloominess was gone.

He was part of the group and had lots of fun. He found out how much better it was to have friends than to be sad and lonely.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. Amy liked to dream. Her dreams would take her to different lands. One night, Amy had a dream about a magical line.

In her dream, the line was helpful. It showed her all sorts of wonderful things. She saw the strangest creatures and all kinds of incredible places she had never seen before.

Soon, the dream was over and Amy woke up. She couldn't remember the dream, but she felt happy.

The next day, Amy was playing in the park with her friends. She noticed a long line of ants walking around.

She smiled and said to her friends, "I had a dream about helpful lines like this!"

Her friends laughed and nodded. They knew that Amy liked to dream, and that was a truly magical dream.

Once there was a mechanic who was very tidy. He cleaned up his tools and kept his garage in order. He worked hard every day.

One day a car came into his garage. It was broken, so the mechanic worked very hard to repair it. He tinkered and tightened and checked it all over.

When the car was fixed the mechanic smiled. He loved seeing the car drive off, working perfectly.

He went inside and had dinner with his family. They all hugged him and said they loved him. The mechanic smiled and thanked them. He knew that his hard work meant something to them. 

The mechanic worked hard but he also enjoyed it. He loved helping people, and he loved feeling proud of how tidy his garage was. It made him happy to help people and make things nice and neat. 

The mechanic was very happy and he knew that he had found the right job for him.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was only three years old. Jane liked to play in the garden, with the sun shinning in her hair and the flowers around her.

One day, Jane's mother called her inside. She said "Jane, I want to remind you of something. It's very important". 

Jane replied "What is it, mummy?"

"Never ever go near the old barn in the back of our house. There is a whip inside, and it is very dangerous".

Jane was worried, but her mother told her "Don't worry. I'll remind you every day to make sure you don't forget".

And every day Jane heard her mother's words in her head. She never forgot about the old whip in the barn.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big bush with many blueberries. They are hungry and want to eat some.

"Look, Mia, blueberries!" Tom says. He picks some and puts them in his mouth. He chews and chews. They are sweet and juicy.

"Can I have some, Tom?" Mia asks. She likes blueberries too. Tom nods and gives her some. She chews and chews. They are sour and wet.

"Yuck, Tom, these are not good!" Mia says. She spits them out. They are green and moldy.

"Sorry, Mia, I did not see!" Tom says. He looks at his blueberries. They are also green and moldy. He spits them out too. They are gross.

"Let's go, Tom, these are bad blueberries!" Mia says. She grabs Tom's hand and runs away. They look for another bush with good blueberries. They are careful and check them before they chew. They find some that are ripe and blue. They are happy and eat them. They are yummy and good.
