The rabbit looked up, and it saw that the mouth belonged to a giant. The giant was so tall that it went up to the sky. It waved and smiled at the rabbit before walking away. The rabbit waved goodbye and hopped back into the field.

The rabbit told all the other animals in the field about the giant. They were so excited and couldn't wait to meet the giant. So the next day, the animals all joined together for an adventure. They ran and hopped until they found the giant. 

The giant was very friendly and welcomed the animals. They played hide and seek and ate delicious snacks. The animals had so much fun that they stayed for days! 

When it was time for the animals to go home, the giant made them promise to come back soon. The animals said goodbye to the giant and went back to their field. They will remember the day they met the giant forever.

The sun was shining brightly and little Jack was so excited. He went to school and saw the big blackboard in the classroom. The green chalk made interesting shapes on it that he wanted to try.

He asked his teacher, "Can I draw on the blackboard?"

"Of course!" she said.

Jack grabbed the green chalk and started to make funny shapes. Every time he finished one, he would look up and laugh. This made his teacher and the other kids smile.

After a while, he put down the chalk and said, "I'm tired".

His teacher said, "That's ok, Jack. You can relax while I write something on the blackboard."

Jack smiled and lay down on the floor. The sun was shining on his face and it felt so nice. He closed his eyes and relaxed. The feeling was wonderful.

One day, a young girl named Betty wanted to go explore outside. She put on her shoes, grabbed her favorite teddy bear, and set off to find something exciting. 

Betty walked and walked until she stumbled upon an unusual stone. It was big, round, and sparkly. She had never seen a stone like this before! She decided to stay with the stone and see what it did.

Betty spent the whole day playing with the stone. She threw it in the air, put it in her pocket, and even gave it a hug. Then the sun began to go down and it was time to go home. 

Betty said goodbye to the stone and ran to her house. From that day on, she always stayed near the unusual stone whenever she went exploring - because it was her special friend.

Mia and John were best friends and they loved to explore. Today they decided to go on an adventure. Mia wore her favourite dress and John put on his trainers. 

John grabbed Mia's hand and they went outside. On their way, they spotted a band playing on the street corner. "Let's go watch!" said John excitedly.

Mia loved the band and their music. She couldn't help but dance with the crowd. John watched her and laughed. 

Soon the music stopped and the band started packing up. John had an adventurous idea. He went over and asked if he could grab a drumstick from the band. The band was happy to share and let John have a drumstick. 

John and Mia beamed with joy. They had the most exciting adventure today!

Once upon a time, a little girl went to find a cave. She knew the cave was very far away and the path was difficult. She kept walking until she got to the cave. Once she arrived, she noticed something was attached to the cave. She looked closer and saw a pink flower! She thought it was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She decided to attach her own flower to the cave. She was very proud of her work. From that day forward, she wanted to go back to the cave every day. The cave became a special place to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the forest. One day, she found a beautiful dragon who was lost. "Are you lost?" Lily asked the dragon. "Yes, I belong in the mountains," the dragon replied. 

Lily wanted to help the dragon find its way home, so she decided to go on an adventure with the dragon. They walked and walked until they finally found the mountains. But when they got there, they saw that the charming castle where the dragon lived was being attacked by mean knights. 

Lily and the dragon knew they had to save the castle. "We have to help!" Lily said. The dragon breathed fire and scared away the knights. The king of the castle was very grateful and said, "You both belong in this castle now. You are both very brave and charming." Lily and the dragon were very happy to have found a new home and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Spirit. Spirit was a very obedient bird who always listened to his mom and dad. One day, Spirit's mom told him it was time to learn how to fly.

"Okay, Mom," Spirit said, and they went outside. Spirit's mom showed him how to flap his wings and jump into the air. Spirit tried and tried, but he could not fly. He was sad, but he did not give up.

Finally, after many tries, Spirit was able to fly. He was so happy and proud of himself. His mom and dad were happy too. They all flew together in the sky, laughing and singing.

The moral of the story is to never give up and always listen to your mom and dad.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a cool toy car that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy wanted to take his toy car outside to play with it in the park. But his mom said he couldn't because they didn't have a license for it.

Timmy was sad and didn't understand why they needed a license for his toy car. He wanted to take it with him to show his friends. So, he decided to sneak it out of the house when his mom wasn't looking.

As he was walking down the street, his toy car suddenly stopped moving. Timmy didn't know what was wrong with it. He tried to fix it, but it wouldn't move. Then, a police officer came by and asked Timmy where his license was for the toy car. Timmy didn't have one and the police officer took the toy car away.

Timmy learned that it's important to have a license for things that move, even if they are just toys. He also learned that it's not cool to sneak things out of the house without asking permission.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy loved to explore the world around her. One day she decided to go on an adventure. She stepped outside and saw a diamond, glimmering in the sun. She knew she wanted to explore it, so she took a step forward.

But then she paused. Supremely helpless, she was unsure of what to do. She had never seen such a beautiful stone before and it scared her!

Suddenly, a lovable, furry friend came hopping up beside Daisy. It was her pet bunny who was ready to explore with her. With her friend by her side, Daisy felt brave again. She smiled, slowly approached the diamond and touched it.

The light from the diamond sparkled around her as they explored the beautiful gem together. Daisy felt so lucky to have a friend like her pet bunny, as together they went on many more adventures!

The next day, Lily's dad came to the garden with a pair of scissors. He started to cut the hedge and make it smaller. Lily was so happy! She could now see her friends on the other side. She ran to them and they played together. They played until the sun went down and it was time to go home.

When Lily came back to her garden the next day, she noticed that the hedge had changed again! This time, it was not tall and bushy, but it was in the shape of a heart. Lily was so surprised and happy. She thought to herself, "This is not the original hedge, but it's even better!" From that day on, Lily loved her garden even more and was always excited to see what surprises it had in store for her.

Once upon a time, there was a parade. Everyone was wearing comfortable clothes and were happy. They all had something to attach to their outfit. Some had balloons, others had ribbons, and some had flags. Everyone was having a great time.

The parade slowly made its way through the town. Everyone was smiling and waving, and the parade music was very loud and happy. Everyone felt so comfortable and excited.

The parade finally ended, and everyone cheered. They all said goodbye to their friends, hugged each other, and thanked the parade leader for organizing such a wonderful event. Everyone was so comfortable and content.

They all went away feeling very happy, knowing that they had been part of a great parade. And from now on, each time they saw a parade, they would remember how wonderful and comfortable it was.

One year, a boy was admiring a beautiful rainbow. He had never seen one before and he was so amazed! He wanted to get closer, but he was scared. He was nervous that he might get wet or even see a monster!

Then he heard a voice. It was kind and friendly, and it said "Don't be scared, it's just me!" He looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. Then suddenly, he heard the voice again. It was coming from the rainbow!

The friendly voice explained that the rainbow was made of colors that mixed together to create something beautiful. The little boy smiled and admired the rainbow even more.

He looked at it until it started to get dark, then he waved goodbye and ran home. He knew he would remember this happy day for the rest of his life!

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Joe and Lizzy. They loved to play in the garden every day.

One day, Lizzy saw something bright in the corner of the garden. It was a pan. She went over to pick it up and asked Joe: "Let's play a game with this pan!" 

The two friends then took turns to spread things onto the pan. They spread sand, leaves and stones. 

The pan was so full that it spilled all over the ground. Joe and Lizzy laughed and clapped when the things spread everywhere. 

Then they had an idea. They spread the things back into the pan with their hands.

The sun shone brightly and Joe and Lizzy thought it was so much fun to spread things on the pan. They played this game until the sun went down. 

It was the best game ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go outside to run and jump. One day, her mom gave her a math book to practice. Lily didn't like math, so she tore the book into pieces. 

When her mom saw what happened, she was very sad. She explained to Lily that tearing the book was not fair to her, because now she couldn't learn math. Lily felt bad and promised to never tear a book again.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and fair to others, even if we don't like something. We should always try our best and not give up, even if it's hard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to work. One day, she decided to help her mommy in the kitchen. She took a modest dish and filled it with water. Then, she found a sponge and started to wash the dishes. She worked so hard and scrubbed until her hands hurt. But she was so proud of her work that she smiled the whole time. 

When she finished washing the dishes, she took the dish to the counter and wiped it off. After that, she put the dish away. Lily was very excited to be able to help her mommy with working.

The next day, Lily wanted to help even more. This time, she brought a modest dish of food to the table. Her mommy smiled and praised Lily for being so kind and helpful. Lily was so happy to work and help her family.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy and their daughter. The daughter was only three years old. She was happy and loved to explore.

One day, the mommy and daddy brought their daughter to the store. There were lots of things to look at and the daughter wanted to explore everywhere. The mommy and daddy said it was better to crawl so she wouldn't hurt herself.

The daughter smiled and started to crawl around the store. She looked at everything and thought it was so much fun.

After a little while, the daughter came across a toy. It was a teddy bear. Its eyes were shiny and they sparkled in the light. The mommy and daddy smiled. It was cheap so they let their daughter keep it.

The daughter hugged the bear tight. â€œThank youâ€, she said with glee. She was so happy she wanted to crawl all the way home.

Once there was a young girl called Anna. Anna loved to explore the beach. Whenever she went, her mommy and daddy would come too. They would always teach her about the wonders of the beach.

One day, Anna and her mommy and daddy went to the beach. It was a beautiful day and the sun was shining brightly. Together, they explored the sand and the sea. Anna was fascinated by the seagulls flying in the sky, and the fish swimming in the sea. 

Mommy and Daddy showed Anna how to play games in the sand. They taught her how to make sandcastles and how to find shells. Anna was so happy and spent the whole day playing in the sand.

At the end of the day, they all went home feeling very happy and tired. From now on, every time Anna thinks of the beach, she will remember the wonderful day she spent there with her mommy and daddy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and lived in a house with a big fence. The fence was very long and it surrounded their big backyard. 

One day, the little girl asked her mom if she could help her mix something in the kitchen. The mom said yes and they went to the kitchen. 

The little girl watched closely as her mom got a bowl and spoon. Then her mom put some milk and flour in the bowl and started mixing! The little girl watched for a long time as the milk and flour mixed together. 

Finally the mom said that it was done! They looked at the mixture and it was thick and gooey. The mom smiled and told the little girl that she had made something special. 

The little girl was so happy and proud! She couldn't help but smile as she watched the mom cook the gooey mixture on the stove. 

They ate the mixture for dinner, and it was delicious! The little girl was so proud that she helped mix the ingredients. She went to bed that night feeling very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a charming girl named Emmie. She was three years old and had lots of lovely toys. One day, she decided she wanted a pillow for her bed, so she asked her mummy for one. Mummy said yes and bought Emmie a special pillow with a pattern of flowers on it. 

When Emmie saw it, she said "thank you!" with a big smile. She loved her new pillow and hugged it tight. Every night, Emmie would cuddle her pillow and wake up with a smile. She felt so cozy and comfortable snuggling her pillow. 

Mummy was really happy to make Emmie so happy with her little gift. She thought it was so charming to see Emmie so excited about her new pillow. 

Whenever Emmie would look at her pillow, she would say "thank you" to mummy and give her a big hug. She was so happy to have her new pillow, and Mummy was happy to have made her so happy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a delicate butterfly friend named Winky. Winky was special because every time she would wink, magic would happen.

One day, Sue wanted to understand how Winky's magic worked. So, she asked her friend, "Winky, how do you do magic when you wink?" Winky just smiled and winked at Sue. Suddenly, a big, yummy cake appeared in front of them.

Sue was so happy! She now understood that Winky's magic was a secret. They both ate the cake and played together all day. And every time Winky winked, something fun would happen.

Ben and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, but they liked the monkeys best. The monkeys were funny and smart. They jumped and swung on the trees. They made noises and faces. Ben and Lily wanted to play with the monkeys.

"Can we go inside the cage, Mom?" Ben asked.

"No, Ben, you can't. The monkeys are not pets. They might bite or scratch you. You can watch them from here," Mom said.

"But they look so friendly, Mom. Please, please, please," Lily begged.

"No, Lily, you can't either. The cage is locked and the zookeeper is not here. You have to follow the rules," Dad said.

Ben and Lily were sad and angry. They did not listen to Mom and Dad. They waited until they were not looking. They found a hole in the fence. They crawled through the hole. They ran to the cage. They saw a door that was open. They went inside the cage. They tried to play with the monkeys.

The monkeys did not like Ben and Lily. They did not want them in their home. They felt scared and angry. They started to scream and throw things. They bit and scratched Ben and Lily. Ben and Lily cried and screamed. They wanted to get out of the cage. But the door was closed. They were trapped.

Mom and Dad heard the noise. They saw Ben and Lily in the cage. They were shocked and scared. They called for help. The zookeeper came. He opened the door. He took Ben and Lily out of the cage. He scolded them. He said they were naughty and foolish. He said they could have been hurt badly. He said they had to leave the zoo.

Mom and Dad were very mad and sad. They took Ben and Lily to the car. They drove them home. They did not talk to them. They put them in their rooms. They said they were grounded. They said they could not play with anything. They said they had to think about what they did.

Ben and Lily were very sorry and sad. They had cuts and bruises. They had no fun. They had no friends. They wished they had listened to Mom and Dad. They wished they had not played with the monkeys. They learned their lesson. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing with her toys on the couch. Suddenly, her dog Spot started to run around the room. Lily felt glad because she loved when Spot was happy. 

Lily decided to join in on the fun and started to run around too. Spot chased after her and they both laughed and giggled. 

After a while, they both got tired and plopped back down on the couch. Lily snuggled up with Spot and felt glad that she had such a fun playmate. 

From that day on, Lily would often run and play with Spot on the couch. They both loved spending time together and it always made Lily glad.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a big box. The box was empty. A little boy named Tim wanted to find something to put in the box. He started to search his room.

Tim looked under his bed and found a soft toy. He pushed the toy into the box. Next, he searched in his closet and found a ball. He pushed the ball into the box too. Tim was happy to see his box filling up.

After a while, the box was full. Tim felt proud of his search. He showed his mom and dad the full box. They smiled and clapped. Tim had turned the empty box into a box filled with fun things.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy piano. It was shiny, white and smooth. It just begged to be tickled and played! Everyone wanted a turn on that piano.

There were two siblings who were always fighting over it. The older brother would tease his little sister, saying he would only let her play if she played a certain song. She would huff and puff, but eventually she'd figure it out and play it perfectly! Then he'd cheer, 'You did it!'.

At other times, the brother would tell his little sister that only he knew how to play the piano. She could try, of course, but he was the only one with the talent. Then he'd play his fingers across the keys of the fancy piano, showing off his skill.

The little sister might pout, but eventually she'd join in, playing a song as brilliant as her brother's. They'd pause, then laugh and clap each other's hands. In the end, no one ever tired of playing the fancy piano, and it brought the brother and sister closer together each day.

One day, Tom was feeling adventurous. He wanted to explore. So he decided to follow a candle. Tom was a bit stubborn and he didn't take no for an answer. He went up and down the stairs, around corners, further and further and deeper and deeper into the dark. He kept walking, his candle showing him the way. 

Soon, Tom came across a mysterious door. He tried to open it but it wouldn't budge. 

"What is behind this door?" he asked himself out loud. But he didn't see a way in.

Then, a deep voice came out of the darkness. "You'll never get through this door if you are too stubborn. If you comply with what I ask, the door shall open," the voice said.

Tom was scared but he was determined. He nodded and the voice continued, "For this door to open, you must bring me a flower."

Tom was relieved. This was an easy task. He quickly ran to the garden and grabbed a flower. As he was about to bring it back, he heard heavy footsteps behind him. Tom was scared, but he ran back to the mysterious door with the flower in his hand. 

The door opened immediately and Tom could see that he had followed the candle to find the entrance to a secret cave! Tom was ecstatic and quickly ran in. 

Tom had followed a candle and beat his stubbornness

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who were all friends. One day, the bunny asked the bear, â€œHey friend, what do you want to do today?â€ The bear replied gently, â€œLetâ€™s watch a peaceful firework show!â€ The bunny smiled and said, â€œLetâ€™s go!â€

So they hopped and ran until they reached the best spot to see the firework show. â€œOh wow!â€ the bunny shouted when all the colorful firework lit up the night sky. It was so pretty!

The bear smiled, wrapped his arms around his friend, and said, â€œIsnâ€™t it beautiful?â€ The bunny nodded and replied, â€œItâ€™s so peaceful!â€ The animals watched the firework show until the sky turned dark again. They said goodbye and went home, their hearts feeling full and happy.

Once there was a little boy called Jack, he was three and very excited. Jack had packed his bag, he was ready to go camping.

Jack and his mom jumped into the car, they drove off and soon arrived at the cabin.

Mom smiled at Jack and said: "We're here at last! You must be so excited".

Jack nodded, looking around at the cabin. It looked so cozy, he couldn't wait to explore.

Mom said, "Shall we get started?"

Jack grinned and said, "Yes, let's go!"

So Mom and Jack went out and explored the woods. Jack found all sorts of interesting things, like fluffy rabbits and huge trees.

The day went by so quickly and soon it was time to head back to the cabin. Jack was exhausted, but also very happy; he had seen so many wonderful things.

The next morning, Jack and his mom packed up their bags, they were ready to go home. They said their goodbyes to the cabin and set off in the car.

The journey home felt so much shorter, Jack and his mom were back home before they knew it.

Jack gave the cabin one last look and said, "Bye cabin, I'll miss you!"

And with that, the camping trip came to an end.

Once upon a time there was an old woman. She wanted to get some water from a nearby stream, so she took an empty jug with her. She was walking through the forest, but it was getting dark. Suddenly, a dangerous animal appeared in front of her!

The animal growled and said, "Give me your jug or I will attack you!"

The poor old woman was scared but she bravely replied, "No! Please don`t hurt me!"

The animal stormed closer and demanded once more, "I said give me the jug!"

The old woman quickly grabbed the jug and put it in front of the animal. It happily picked up the jug and ran away.

The old woman was relieved, but then she realized that she had no jug and she'd have to go home without any water. Luckily, there were plenty of other jugs at home.

The old woman learned her lesson. The forest was dangerous, and it was not safe to wander around there at night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to move. She could jump, twirl, and even run very fast. One day, she wanted to explore, so she decided to move into a mysterious forest. As she moved closer and closer, a thick mist blanketed the trees. 

The little girl was scared, but she kept moving. Suddenly, something moved in the mist. She wasn't sure what it was, so she called out, "Hello?" 

From out of the mist came a reliable voice saying, "It's okay. Don't be afraid. I'm here to help you." 

The little girl felt better and followed the reliable voice. As she moved closer, a friendly fox appeared. The fox had moved in the mist to protect the little girl. The fox said, "Welcome to the forest. I'm here to help you explore and stay safe." 

The little girl smiled. With the fox's help, she moved around the forest with no fear. Together, they made the most of their adventure.

Billy was at the park with his Mom and Dad. He saw lots of junk on the ground. As he looked around in wonder, his Dad said, "Let's pick up this junk."

Billy said, "But why? It's just junk."

His Mom said, "It's important to stay kind to others and the world. By cleaning up this junk, we can remain helpful to others."

Billy slowly began to pick up the pieces of junk laying around. He looked at them for a moment and then threw them away into the garbage. He asked his Dad, "Why do we still have junk?"

His Dad said, "Unfortunately, not everyone is kind. Some people think it's ok to just leave their junk lying around."

Billy rubbed his chin in thought. He asked, "Can we make it so there's no more junk?"

His Dad smiled and said, "No, but we can remain kind and help out wherever we can."

Billy smiled and said, "Ok, let's help then!" 

Mom and Dad were proud to see that Billy understood the importance of remaining kind and helping out. Together, they continued to pick up the junk around the park.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with shapes. They have a box of shapes. They have circles, squares, triangles and stars.

One day, they want to make a picture with shapes. They have paper and glue. They look at the box of shapes. Tom sees a triangle. He likes triangles. He says, "I want this triangle. It is yellow and big."

Mia sees the triangle too. She likes triangles too. She says, "I want this triangle too. It is yellow and big."

Tom and Mia both want the same triangle. They start to pull the triangle. They are not happy. They are angry.

Lily is their teacher. She sees Tom and Mia. She says, "What is wrong, Tom and Mia? Why are you angry?"

Tom and Mia say, "We both want this triangle. It is yellow and big. We like triangles."

Lily says, "I see. Triangles are nice. But you have many shapes. You have circles, squares, stars and more triangles. Why don't you share the shapes? You can make a picture together. You can use the yellow and big triangle and other shapes too. Sharing is kind. Kind friends are happy friends."

Tom and Mia think. They say, "You are right, Lily. Sharing is kind. We can make a picture together. We can use the yellow and big triangle and other shapes too. We are sorry. We are kind friends. We are happy friends."

Tom and Mia smile. They hug. They share the shapes. They make a picture together. They use the yellow and big triangle and other shapes too. Their picture is beautiful. They are proud. They show their picture to Lily. Lily says, "Wow, Tom and Mia. Your picture is beautiful. You are kind friends. You are happy friends. I am proud of you."

One day, a little girl named Rose was playing in the park. She saw a grumpy man with a camera. "What's that?" asked Rose.

"It's a camera," said the man.

"Can I look?" asked Rose.

The man smiled. "Sure!" he said. He showed Rose how to load the camera with a film.

Rose was excited. "I can take pictures!" she said.

The grumpy man laughed. "Yes, you can," he said.

Rose thanked him and then ran over to a nearby tree. She held the camera up and snapped a few pictures of the tree.

The grumpy man watched her happily. "You are a very talented photographer," he said.

Rose beamed. "Thank you!" she said. Then she ran away to take more pictures. She was so proud of the grumpy man for teaching her how to load the camera.

One day, Mark was walking in the park. He was walking with his Mom and he was having a lot of fun. Suddenly, Mark stumbled on something. He looked down and saw that it was a dry stick. He tried to pick it up but it broke in two. He started to cry.

Mom reached down and wiped away Mark's tears. She said, "Don't worry, Mark. I can help you make a mark on the ground with the stick so you'll remember it."

Mark smiled. He took a piece of the stick and placed it in the ground. He made a big circle with it, just like Mom asked.

But then, something strange happened. The wind started to blow and the dry stick started to roll across the ground. It was heading right towards the pond! If it got in the pond, Mark would never find it again!

Mark ran and grabbed the stick just in time. He hugged it and said, "You never left me, dry stick!" He smiled and placed it back in the ground, making sure it stayed put. From that day on, he always remembered the mark he made in the park.

Billy was a very obedient 3 year old boy. He loved playing in the park with his friends, but his favorite thing to do was playing the piano. Every morning, Billy would wake up and immediately go to the piano. His mom always had to yell for him to come eat breakfast.

Billy was becoming very good at the piano. He could even play some songs all by himself. His mom was very proud of him. She often clapped and cheered when he would perform.

One day, Billy was playing in the living room. He had been practicing the same song over and over again. His mom had gone to the store and left him home alone. Suddenly, the door opened and Billy's mom walked in. She was so surprised to see Billy playing the piano. She quickly ran over to him, shouting his name and pointing to the door. She had told him not to be alone in the living room.

Billy quickly ran out of the room to go back to his bedroom. His mom looked after him for a few moments, but then went back to the store. Billy was relieved he had been so obedient. He knew his mom was very proud of him.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named James and Lily. They often went on adventures together every day. One evening, they decided to go collecting.

James excitedly grabbed a bucket, while Lily picked up her net. "Where should we go to collect things?" asked James.

Lily thought deeply before she answered, "Let's go to the ancient forest."

James smiled broadly. "That's a wonderful idea!" he exclaimed.

They walked to the ancient forest and quietly looked for things to collect. Suddenly, Lily spotted something glimmering in the corner. She ran over and carefully picked it up - it was an ancient coin!

James happily put it into the bucket. Lily and James continued collecting things until it began to get dark. James felt tired, so he suggested they have a nap under a tree.

Lily nodded in agreement and they both snuggled up together. As they drifted off to sleep, they smiled - they had learnt a valuable lesson: you can make sure you have the most wonderful adventures if you have the right company.

Sara and Ben were very happy. They were going on a holiday with Mum and Dad. They packed their bags with toys and clothes. They went to the big place where the planes fly.

Mum and Dad had to weigh their bags. They put them on a big scale. The scale said how heavy the bags were. Mum and Dad had to pay money for the bags. Sara and Ben did not have to weigh their bags. They were small and light.

They got on the plane. The plane was very big and loud. Sara and Ben sat by the window. They saw the clouds and the birds. They ate some snacks and played some games. They were very excited.

But then the plane hit some bad air. The plane shook and bounced. Sara and Ben felt scared. They held Mum and Dad's hands. Mum and Dad said it was OK. They said it was just a little bump.

The plane landed in a new place. It was very cold and white. Sara and Ben saw snow and ice. They wore their warm coats and hats. They got off the plane. They felt a bitter wind on their faces. They shivered and hugged Mum and Dad.

They got in a car. The car took them to a nice house. The house had a fire and a tree. The tree had lights and balls. Sara and Ben smiled. They said it was a beautiful holiday. They forgot about the bad air and the bitter wind. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, Lily looked out the window and saw that the weather was very cloudy. She wondered if it was going to rain. Lily put on her raincoat and boots and went outside to play.

As she was playing, Lily saw a snail crawling on the ground. She was curious and wanted to touch it, but her mom had told her to never touch snails. Lily didn't listen and picked up the snail. Suddenly, the snail squirted slimy goo all over her hand.

Lily learned her lesson and realized that sometimes it's better to listen to the advice of others. She also wondered if the snail was trying to protect itself from her curiosity. From then on, Lily was more careful and respectful of the creatures she encountered outside.

Lily and Ben went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things in the sea, like fish, crabs and shells. But they did not like jellyfish. Jellyfish were disgusting. They were slimy and stingy and made Lily and Ben cry.

One day, they saw a big jellyfish on the shore. It was purple and pink and had long tentacles. Lily and Ben wanted to poke it with a stick, but Mom and Dad said no. They said jellyfish were alive and needed water to breathe. They said they should help the jellyfish go back to the sea.

Lily and Ben did not understand. Why should they help something so disgusting? They asked Mom and Dad.

Mom and Dad said, "Jellyfish are part of nature, just like us. They have a place and a purpose in the sea. They are not bad, they are just different. And sometimes, they need help, just like us. If we help them, we improve the world a little bit. And maybe, they will help us too, someday."

Lily and Ben thought about it. They did not want to be stingy or slimy, but they did not want to be mean either. They decided to give the jellyfish a chance. They took a bucket and filled it with water. They carefully scooped the jellyfish into the bucket and carried it to the water. They gently poured the jellyfish back into the sea. They watched it swim away, waving its tentacles.

Lily and Ben felt good. They had helped the jellyfish. They had improved the world a little bit. And maybe, they had made a new friend. They smiled and hugged Mom and Dad. They said, "Thank you for teaching us. We love you. And we love the sea. And maybe, we love jellyfish too."

Once upon a time there was a lively fairy who loved to fly around the garden. She fluttered from flower to flower, spinning and twirling.

But one day, the fairy noticed something new in the garden. She paused for a moment, hovering in the air to get a better look. 

It was a butterfly! Its wings sparkled in the sunshine and it flew up and down, spinning around and around.

The fairy watched the butterfly for a while and then flew off. She flew over the flowers and the trees, chasing after the butterfly. They played tag in the sky and it was lots of fun. 

Then, when the fairy was too tired to fly anymore, she paused and landed on a flower. She smiled, feeling happy and content, before flying off to bed.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the lake with their moms. The lake is big and blue. It has fish and ducks.

Anna and Ben see a boat. The boat is red and white. It has a sail and a wheel. They want to ride the boat. They ask their moms.

"Can we ride the boat, please?" Anna says.

"Can we, can we?" Ben says.

Their moms look at the boat. They look at Anna and Ben. They nod.

"Okay, you can ride the boat. But be careful and stay close," Anna's mom says.

"Listen to the man who drives the boat. He is dependable. He knows the lake well," Ben's mom says.

Anna and Ben are happy. They run to the boat. They put on life jackets. They climb on the boat. The man who drives the boat smiles. He starts the boat. The boat moves on the lake.

Anna and Ben sit on the boat. They look at the water. They look at the sky. They see clouds and birds. They feel the wind and the sun. They are having fun.

"Look, a duck!" Anna points.

"Quack, quack!" Ben says.

They laugh. They wave to the duck. The duck swims away.

"Let's play a game," Anna says.

"What game?" Ben asks.

"Who can see more things on the lake. The one who sees more things wins," Anna says.

"Okay, let's play. I go first. I see a fish," Ben says.

"I see a flower," Anna says.

"I see a rock," Ben says.

"I see a leaf," Anna says.

They take turns. They see many things on the lake. They count them. They are both good at the game. They are both smart.

"Who wins?" Ben asks.

"I don't know. We see the same things," Anna says.

"Maybe we both win," Ben says.

"Maybe we do," Anna says.

They smile. They hug. They are both happy. They are both winners. They are both friends.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom asked her to bring a jug of water from the well. Lily happily went to the well, but the jug was too heavy for her to carry.

Just then, a wise old man came by and asked Lily if she needed help. She said yes, and the old man showed her how to attach a rope to the jug and carry it on her back. Lily was so happy that she could help her mom.

Later that day, Lily's little brother wanted to play with her favorite toy. She didn't want to share, but then she remembered the wise old man's words: "When you help others, good things will come back to you." So, she decided to share her toy with her brother.

In the end, Lily realized that being kind and helpful to others makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, a bald dad was cooking dinner at his house. He stood in the kitchen and cooked the dinner with a big smile on his face.

He cooked some vegetables in the pan, and some meat in the oven. Meanwhile, the back fence of the house was looking a bit old.

So Dad decided to cook dinner first, and then he would fix the fence. He quickly finished cooking dinner and then got to work on the fence. He took some wood and some tools and mended the old fence.

When he finished, the fence was strong and Dad was happy. He had a good dinner and a nice fence â€“ he was very pleased.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Tom. Tom was three years old and he was very curious about the world. One day, Tom heard his mommy talking about something called a "dream". Tom asked his mommy, "Mommy, what is a dream?" 

His mommy smiled and said, "A dream is something we all have inside us. It is like a wish that can come true. It's something to believe in and something special."

Tom thought long and hard before he spoke. He asked his mommy, "Mommy, can I have a dream to believe in?"

His mommy nodded and said, "Yes, of course you can have a dream. All you have to do is be brave and not be fearful. Then, you will be able to name your dream. What will you name yours?" 

Tom thought for a moment and then he said, "I want to name my dream adventure!" 

His mommy smiled and said, "That's a wonderful dream! Now, you must believe in it and never give up. I know you can do it!" 

Tom smiled at his mommy and said, "Thank you, mommy! I believe in my dream adventure!"

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice every day. One day, her mom made a big pot of rice for dinner. Lily was so happy and ate a lot of rice. 

After dinner, Lily went to bed. But she heard some noisy sounds outside her window. She looked out and saw a big, scary monster. The monster was crying and asking for help.

"Oh no, Jimmy," Mommy said, "It's too dark outside. Let's just take a look at the shadows for now".
Jimmy said, "Okay, Mommy. Let's see how our shadows look like."
Mommy and Jimmy watched their shadows stretch across the path. They were long and thin like two dark lines in the night. 
Jimmy said, "Mommy, look, I can make my shadow go on a walk. It's so fun!"
Mommy smiled at Jimmy and said, "Let your shadow go on a walk. I'm sure it will have so much fun!" 
Jimmy smiled and with a little skip and a jump, his shadow went on its way. What fun they had that night!

Tom is a boy who likes to play with cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. He thinks he has the best cars in the world.

One day, he goes to the park with his mom. He sees another boy playing with a big red car. The car has lights and sounds and can move by itself. Tom wants the car very much. He goes to the boy and says, "Give me your car. I need it."

The boy says, "No, this is my car. You can't have it. Go away."

Tom gets angry and tries to grab the car. The boy pushes him away and shouts, "Stop it! You are mean and rude. Go play with your own cars."

Tom falls on the ground and starts to cry. His mom hears him and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the car and the boy and understands what happened. She says to Tom, "Tom, you can't take other people's things. That is not nice. You have to ask and share. How would you feel if someone took your cars?"

Tom feels embarrassed and sorry. He realizes he was wrong. He says to the boy, "I'm sorry. I was selfish and greedy. Your car is very cool, but it is yours. Can we be friends and play together?"

The boy smiles and says, "It's okay. I forgive you. Yes, we can be friends and play together. You can try my car if you want."

Tom and the boy become friends and play with their cars. They have fun and learn to respect and share. Tom's mom is proud of him and gives him a hug. She says, "Tom, you did a good thing. You said sorry and made a new friend. That is what matters, not the car. You have a big heart."

Tom feels happy and hugs his mom. He says, "Thank you, mom. I love you. You are right. The car is not important. The friend is important."

Once upon a time, there was a lazy bear who loved to sleep all day. He had lots of blocks to play with, but he never wanted to stand up and build something with them. One day, a hardworking ant came by and saw the lazy bear just sleeping and not playing with his blocks.

The ant said, "Mr. Bear, why don't you stand up and build something with your blocks? It's so much fun!" But the lazy bear just grumbled and went back to sleep.

The ant decided to build something with the blocks all by herself. She built a tall tower that reached up to the sky. When the lazy bear woke up and saw the tower, he felt bad that he had been too lazy to play with his blocks. From that day on, he stood up and built something new with his blocks every day. The moral of the story is that it's important to stand up and do things, even if they seem hard or boring at first.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to collect music. She had many CDs with songs that made her happy. One day, Amy found a new CD in a store. It had a picture of a big drum on it. She thought it would be fun to listen to.

Amy took the CD home and put it in her CD player. She said to her mom, "I think this music will be loud and fun!" Her mom smiled and said, "Let's see!" They both waited to hear the music. The CD started to play, and it was very loud! The drums went boom, boom, boom!

Amy and her mom laughed and danced to the loud music. They had so much fun. The CD with the big drum became Amy's favorite. She was happy that she collected it. And from that day on, Amy and her mom always danced to the loud drum music together.

Once there was a little girl called Sally. Sally loved building things and playing in the garden. As the snow started to fall and the nights were getting dark and cold, Sally thought of the perfect way to spend her time. She got a box of her things and began to build a camp!

Sally used a blanket to make a roof and logs for the walls. She put a rug in the middle for the floor. She added some of her favourite things around the camp to make it cozy, like a pillow, a lamp and some pretty stones, too.

The camp was all finished now! Sally was so happy and it was so cozy in the camp that she invited her friends over to play. Even though it was cold outside, the camp was warm and everyone had a great time.

Sally learnt something that day - that you don't need much to build something amazing!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived on a farm with her mom and dad. One day, Lily and her mom went to the barn to collect eggs from the chickens. The eggs were heavy, but Lily tried to carry them all by herself.

Suddenly, a gust of wind came and scattered the eggs all over the barn. Lily's mom saw what happened and said, "Oh no! The eggs are all over the place now. Let's clean them up together." So, Lily and her mom worked together to pick up all the scattered eggs.

After they finished cleaning, Lily's mom said, "Good job, Lily! You helped me so much. Let's go inside and have some eggs for breakfast." Lily smiled and said, "Yay! I love eggs!"

John and his mum were on holiday. It was very interesting! They went to the beach and saw the big waves. John wanted to go swimming, but his mum warned him not go too close. 

They saw two seagulls chasing each other in the sky and then stopped to look at some funny looking crabs. John could see them dig in the sand and when one found something good to eat, it made him smile. 

John and his mum walked a little further, and John was excited when he saw a big boat. His mum warned him not to go near the water, as it was too dangerous. But John enjoyed the view and the warm weather. 

They stayed on holiday for a few more days, and John's mum taught him about safety at the beach. He remembered what she said, and he had a really interesting time!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside, but she always forgot to put lotion on her skin. One day, her mommy reminded her to put lotion on her arms and legs before going outside to play. Lily didn't want to, but she knew it was important.

As she was playing, she saw a butterfly and chased after it. She was so excited that she didn't notice a big tree root in her way. She tripped and twisted her ankle. She cried out in pain and her mommy ran outside to help her.

Her mommy was anxious and called the doctor. The doctor said that Lily's ankle was broken and she needed to stay in bed for a while. Lily was sad that she couldn't play outside anymore, but she knew she had to listen to the doctor.

Days passed and Lily's ankle started to feel better. She was so happy that she could finally go outside and play again. But when she went outside, she saw that the butterfly she had chased before was now dead. She felt sad and wished she had been more careful.

Billy was a curious three year old. He liked going for a jog in the park every day. One day, he was jogging around the lake, when he spotted something strange. It was a big net, all tangled up. He went closer to take a look.

Billy was curious about the net and he accidentally stepped in it. He stumbled, but then felt something soft. Something fluffy was in the net! Billy was puzzled and decided to untangle the net.

When he opened the net, he found out it was full of little birds. They were scared and flapping their wings. Billy smiled and slowly freed all the birds from the net. They were grateful and happily flew away.

Billy finished his jog and went home, feeling proud that he had helped the birds. He wouldn't forget his curious adventure.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

But then they saw a big cat with spots on its fur. It was a leopard. The leopard was hungry and looking for food. It saw Tom and Lily and their ball. It wanted to eat them.

"Look, Lily, a big cat!" Tom said. "It is incredible!"

"No, Tom, it is not a cat, it is a leopard!" Lily said. "It is dangerous! We have to run!"

But it was too late. The leopard was faster than them. It jumped on Tom and bit him. Tom screamed and dropped the ball. Lily was scared and tried to run away. But the leopard saw her and chased her. It caught her and bit her too. Lily screamed and cried.

The leopard ate Tom and Lily and their ball. It was full and happy. It left the park and went back to the forest. Nobody saw what happened. Nobody helped Tom and Lily. They were gone. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted dog named Spot. Spot could do many fun tricks. He could show people how he could jump very high and run very fast. Spot had many friends who liked to watch him play.

One day, Spot met a new friend named Tim. Tim asked, "Can you show me your fun tricks?" Spot said, "Yes, I can!" So, Spot showed Tim how he could jump high and run fast. Tim was very happy to see Spot's tricks.

But then, Spot saw a big car coming fast. Spot wanted to show Tim how brave he was. So, Spot ran towards the car to show he was not scared. But the car hit Spot, and he got hurt. Tim was sad, and everyone missed the gifted dog who had so much fun to share.

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was three years old and very happy. She loved going to the beach and splashing in the sea.

One day she went to the beach with her mom and dad. She ran very fast to the shore and started to make big waves. She was so excited that she started to yell with joy!

Suddenly she saw something moving in the distance. It was another girl who was waving to her. Lucy was so surprised to see another person on the beach that she started to yell even louder.

Both girls waved to each other. The other girl was doing a very hard wave, much harder than Lucy's. But that didn't stop Lucy, she kept on waving and yelling with excitement.

Soon they started to play games in the sand. As they laughed and played, they were both yelling and waving to each other. They had so much fun! 

At the end of the day, both girls went back home, still yelling and waving goodbye to each other. From then on, Lucy loved going to the beach and saying hello with a big happy wave.

Once upon a time there was a baby named Carl. He wanted to do something special and fun, so he decided to crawl. He started crawling slowly, learning new things with every step. He was feeling brave and confident, and he was determined to reach his goal.

He kept crawling and crawling, until all of a sudden he had a surprise! He had reached his goal - a beautiful, new playground! He explored the playground, finding slides and swings, and lots of exciting things to try out.

He kept exploring until he was tired, but he was very happy. Carl had achieved his goal and had a new place to play, and that made him very proud. The end.

Mom and Dad love Jack very much. They love to kiss his little lips. Jack loves to give kisses too, but with a different lip. His top lip is bigger than his bottom lip. 

Jack has one lip like mom and one lip like dad. Sometimes he squishes them together and smiles. 

Mom and Dad love Jack's different lip so they give him lots of kisses. Jack always smiles and gives kisses back. 

Mom and Dad love Jack and his different lips! He loves them too!

Once upon a time there was a family. Every day the family did regular things. The dad worked and the mom cleaned the house. The kids played and laughed - it was a happy family. 

One morning, the mom and dad went to work. But when the kids woke up and started to yawn, they realised something was wrong. There was no breakfast on the table! 

The kids were very sad and confused. Suddenly, they heard a voice coming from the kitchen. It was the regular babysitter. She had got up late and them missed her bus. She had not been able to get the family breakfast before she left. 

The kids were mad at the regular babysitter. But, after a lot of talking, the kids agreed to forgive her - she hadn't meant for this to happen. So, the family all hugged each other and laughed. 

From that day on, the family made sure to wake up earlier - so that they could all eat breakfast together. 

The End.

Tom had a big hole in his pocket. He liked his pocket. He put his toy car in his pocket. He put his candy in his pocket. He put his rock in his pocket. But one day, his pocket ripped. His toy car fell out. His candy fell out. His rock fell out. Tom was sad.

He went to his mom. He showed her his pocket. He said, "Mom, can you repair my pocket? I want my pocket back."

Mom looked at his pocket. She said, "Oh, Tom, your pocket is very bad. I can try to repair it, but I need a needle and a thread. Can you help me find them?"

Tom nodded. He and mom looked for a needle and a thread. They found them in a box. Mom took the needle and the thread. She said, "Tom, can you hold your pocket for me? I will sew it with the needle and the thread. Be careful, the needle is sharp."

Tom held his pocket. Mom sewed it with the needle and the thread. She made small stitches. She closed the hole. She said, "There, Tom, your pocket is repaired. Now you can put your things in it again. But don't put too many things, or it will rip again."

Tom smiled. He thanked his mom. He said, "Mom, you are the best. You repaired my pocket. I love you." He hugged his mom. He put his toy car in his pocket. He put his candy in his pocket. He put his rock in his pocket. He was happy. He ran outside to play. He saw the sun. It was light and warm. He said, "Today is a good day."

Once upon a time there was a big blue bird. The bird was very gentle and liked to stand on the tallest tree in the forest. One day, a strong wind came and knocked the bird to the ground. The bird was scared and did not know what to do.

But then, a big gentle bear came by. The bear saw the bird on the ground and stood next to it. The bear comforted the bird and said "It's alright little blue bird. You can stand up and fly again." With the bear's help, the bird slowly stood up and flapped its wings. The bear smiled and then ran away.

The bird showed its gratitude by flying circles around the bear. Every now and then, the bird and the bear stand next to each other and look up at the sky together.

Once there was a little boy. His name was Tim. Tim wanted to get a rich field.

One day, while walking, Tim saw a field. It was very big and green and it looked very rich. So he decided to get it.

Tim went up to the field and knocked on the door. He waited for someone to answer and he heard a voice from inside.

"Who's there?" the voice asked.

Tim replied, "It's me, Tim. Can I have your field?"

The voice said, "Yes, you can get it. But first, you have to bring me something special." 

Tim knew this would be a challenge. He thought and thought, and finally he remembered that he had a basket of apples in his bag. So he took out the apples and offered them to the field owner. 

The field owner was very pleased. He smiled and said, "Yes, you can get the field. It's now yours!"

So Tim got the rich field and was very happy. He ran around the field, laughing and twirling in joy. He had finally achieved his dream.

Tim and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like monkeys, elephants, and giraffes. Tim liked the animals, but Lily did not. She complained a lot.

"I'm bored. I'm hungry. I'm tired. I want to go home," she said.

"Shh, Lily. Be nice. We are almost done. Look, there is the tiger. He is big and orange and black. He is very cool," Tim said.

Lily looked at the tiger. He was lying on a rock, licking his paw. He did not look cool to her. He looked weird.

"Why is he so weird? Why does he have stripes? Why does he lick himself? Why does he not play with us?" she asked.

Tim rolled his eyes. He was tired of Lily's questions. He wanted to enjoy the zoo.

"He is not weird. He is a tiger. He has stripes to hide in the grass. He licks himself to clean his fur. He does not play with us because he is not a pet. He is a wild animal. He can be dangerous," he explained.

Lily did not listen. She thought the tiger was boring. She wanted to make him more fun. She had an idea. She picked up a stick and threw it at the tiger. She hoped he would chase it like a dog.

The tiger did not chase the stick. He did not like being hit by it. He was angry. He roared loudly and jumped off the rock. He ran towards the fence that separated him from the children. He looked fierce and hungry.

Tim and Lily were scared. They screamed and ran away. Mom and Dad heard them and came to see what was wrong. They saw the tiger and grabbed their children. They ran to the exit.

The zookeeper heard the commotion and came to calm the tiger. He saw the stick and guessed what happened. He shook his head and sighed.

"Some kids never learn. They should not complain about the animals. They should respect them," he said.

Bruce was an incredibly brilliant three year old. He was playing with his friends in the garden and they were having a lot of fun. They were playing a game but Bruce started to feel like something wasn't quite right.

He asked his friend, "Do you trust your sauce?" His friend shrugged and said, "Sure, it's tasty and I always eat it." Bruce thought for a moment, then asked, "Do you think it's always reliable?"

His friend replied, "Yes, it's always been brilliant and hasn't let me down. I think it's reliable." That was enough for Bruce and he decided to trust the sauce.

He made a choice to keep playing the game and have fun, trusting the sauce would always be reliable. Together with his friend, they finished the game happily.

Once upon a time there was a man who had a wife. One day, the man wanted to go on a trip. He asked his wife to come with him, but she said no. The man felt guilty for wanting to go without her. He thought about it for a long time and decided to lead his wife on the journey instead. 

When they arrived at their destination, they both had a wonderful time. They explored the area and looked at all the amazing sights. They were very happy to be together. 

The man was happy he had decided to lead his wife on this journey. He knew that he did the right thing, and he was no longer feeling guilty. From then on, they decided to make more trips together. They were so happy to be together that each journey was even more special than the last.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the land near his house. He would run around and laugh with his friends. 

One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help decorate the house for a party. Timmy was excited to help and started putting up balloons and streamers. However, his older sister was being very bossy and telling him what to do. Timmy didn't like it, but he didn't want to make her mad, so he did what she said. 

After they finished decorating, they went outside to play again. But while they were playing, they heard a loud crash. They turned around and saw that the decorations they had put up had fallen down and made a big mess. Timmy's mom was very upset and she scolded them for not doing a good job. 

Timmy felt very sad because he had tried his best, but his sister had been too bossy. He wished he had stood up for himself and done things his own way. From that day on, Timmy learned to be more confident and not let others be bossy to him.

One day, Mary saw an ugly rainbow in the sky. She smiled and said, "Wow!" She wanted to mark the rainbow so she found some bright, colourful paper and markers.

When she was done, she ran outside with the paper and markers and held them up to the sky. She wanted to mark the rainbow so she waved her arm around in circles, making a big, colourful circle.

But then it started to rain. Mary was so disappointed! She wanted to show everyone her beautiful rainbow.

But then, something wonderful happened! A rainbow appeared in the sky! It was so bright and beautiful! Mary quickly ran outside and started to mark the rainbow again. She waved her arm around in circles and made a pretty, colourful circle all around the rainbow.

When she was done, Mary smiled and said, "That's the best ugly rainbow I ever saw!"

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars and dolls. But sometimes they quarrel. They quarrel when they want the same toy or when they do not share or when they are tired.

One day, they quarrel a lot. Anna wants the red car and Ben wants the red car too. They pull and tug and shout. Their voices are loud and angry. They do not listen to each other. They do not have fun.

Mom sees them quarrel. She is not happy. She says, "Anna and Ben, stop quarreling. You are friends. You can play nicely. You can take turns or trade or play together. You can use your voices to say sorry and thank you and please. You can be playful and kind."

Anna and Ben hear Mom. They feel sorry. They say sorry to each other. They hug and smile. They decide to trade the red car for the blue car. They decide to play together. They build a big tower with the blocks. They make the cars zoom and beep. They make the dolls talk and laugh. Their voices are soft and happy. They have fun.

Mom sees them play. She is happy. She says, "Anna and Ben, I am proud of you. You are good friends. You can play nicely. You can use your voices to be polite and friendly. You can be playful and kind."

Once there was a little girl named Emma. She had a red hose and liked to shoot it in the air. She would make funny shapes and designs with it. One day she was having so much fun shooting her hose that she didn't notice a weird man standing behind her.

Suddenly the weird man yelled at her. "Stop shooting that hose!" he shouted. Emma was so scared she dropped her hose and ran away as fast as she could.

She hid behind a tree and looked for the man. But he was gone. Emma was so relieved. She picked up her hose and smiled. From then on she kept a look out before she started playing with her hose again.

Jack found a large table in the living room. He ran over and grabbed one of the chairs. He was so excited, he started jumping up and down. He pushed the chair and climbed up onto the table. Jack couldn't believe how big it was! He looked all around him and started to spin around on the large table. 

Jack was having so much fun, he didn't realize how fast he was going until he lost his balance and fell off the table! He was so surprised, he started to cry. But when he saw his mom look over and smile, he knew he would be ok.

His mom came over, grabbed him up in her arms and said, "That was fun, wasn't it? I'm glad you had such a good time." Jack smiled and said, "Yes!" He knew he would have lots more fun on the table again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to paint. One day, she wanted to paint a picture of her favorite sock. But when she went to get it, she found that it was filthy! 

Lily said, "Oh no! My sock is dirty. I can't paint it now." 

Her mom heard her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can wash it and then you can paint it." 

Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mommy!" After they washed the sock, Lily painted a beautiful picture of it. She was so proud of herself and showed it to everyone she knew. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was 3 years old and loved playing outside with his friends.

One day, Jack and his friends had a big fight. At first, Jack was brave and tried to sort things out. But soon, he became embarrassed and his cheeks turned red. 

Jack's friends could see how sad he looked, so they decided to forgive him and stop fighting. Jack smiled and said "Thank you, I'm happy we solved this without a fight."

Everyone smiled and ran off to play. From that day on, Jack was excited to go out and play with his friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mary. Mary had a file that she would keep all of her important things in. She kept it in a special spot in her room and knew exactly where it was.

One day, she was looking through the file and noticed that one of her important pieces of paper was missing. She started to get angry.

Mary went to her mom and said in a loud voice, "Mom! My file is missing something."

Her mom said in a calm voice, "Mary, let's look for it together. I'm sure we'll find it!"

So the two of them looked around for the missing paper. After searching for a few minutes, Mary found her paper inside her file. She had put it in there but forgotten about it.

Mary smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom. You helped me find it!"

Her mom smiled back and said, "You're welcome, Mary. I'm glad we found it!"

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread, so they asked their mom for some.

"Here you go, boys. But be careful, don't go too close to the water. There might be an alligator hiding there," their mom said.

Ben and Sam nodded and ran to the pond. They threw some bread to the ducks and fish, who came to eat. They were having fun, but soon they ran out of bread.

"Let's go back to mom and get more bread," Sam said.

"No, I want to stay here. Look, there is a big log in the water. Maybe we can stand on it and see more ducks and fish," Ben said.

He pointed to a long, brown thing in the water. Sam thought it looked like a log, too. He followed Ben to the edge of the pond.

"Be careful, Ben. Don't drop in the water. It might be hot," Sam said.

Ben laughed. "Don't be silly, Sam. The water is not hot. It is cool and nice. Watch me, I can stand on the log."

He stepped on the log, but it was not a log. It was an alligator. The alligator opened its big mouth and snapped at Ben. Ben screamed and jumped back. He dropped his hat in the water.

"Help, help! It's an alligator!" Ben cried.

Sam was scared, too. He ran to their mom and told her what happened. Their mom came to the pond and saw the alligator. She grabbed Ben and hugged him.

"Are you okay, Ben? You are very lucky. The alligator could have hurt you. You should have listened to me and stayed away from the water," she said.

Ben was sorry. He realized he was wrong. He hugged his mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. I won't go near the water again."

Sam hugged his brother and said, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I should have stopped you. I'm glad you are safe."

Their mom smiled and said, "It's okay, boys. I'm glad you are safe, too. Let's go home and have some ice cream. But remember, always be careful and listen to your mom."

Ben and Sam learned their lesson. They never went near the water again. They also never saw their hat again. The alligator kept it as a souvenir.

Amy was very excited about painting. She grabbed all of her art supplies and ran to the backyard. She found a patch of ground and spread her painting materials out. Amy had a brilliant idea - a rainbow! 

First, Amy painted the sky yellow. Then, she painted the ground green. She added some pink clouds and a bright orange sun. 

After adding lots of colors, she stood back to inspect her work. It was beautiful! Amy looked up into the sky and smiled at the rainbow she had painted. 

"What do you think?" She asked her dad. 

"It's brilliant," he replied. "You painted a wonderful rainbow." 

Amy was so proud of her work. She jumped for joy and went in for dinner, still smiling about her brilliant painting.

Once upon a time, Timmy had a special sack. It was thin and brown, but it was filled with lots of special treasures. Every day, Timmy would take his sack with him on his adventures. 

Today, Timmy wanted to find the tallest tree he could see. He tied his sack to his belt and began to climb. He reached the top and smiled. He could see so far! 

Suddenly, Timmy heard a noise. It was loud and close by. He looked around and saw a little mouse. Timmy wanted to catch it, so he reached out his thumb. The mouse was too quick. But it left behind its tail in Timmy's thin brown sack. 

Timmy smiled. He had a new treasure - one he would keep in his sack for a very long time. 


End of Story.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room. They had many toys, but they liked to pretend with the big fan. They took turns to be the wind and blow on each other.

"Ben, you be the wind now. I want to feel the breeze," Lily said.

"OK, Lily. But you have to close your eyes and guess what I blow on you," Ben said.

He looked around and saw a banana peel on the floor. He picked it up and held it behind the fan. He turned the fan on and aimed it at Lily.

Lily felt something wet and slimy on her face. She opened her eyes and screamed.

"Ben, what is this? It is disgusting!" she cried.

She saw the banana peel and threw it away. She ran to the couch and wiped her face with a pillow.

"Ben, that was not nice. That was mean. Why did you do that?" she asked.

Ben laughed and said, "It was a joke, Lily. It was funny. Don't you like jokes?"

Lily frowned and said, "No, Ben. That was not a joke. That was gross. You made me dirty and smelly. You have to say sorry."

Ben stopped laughing and said, "Sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to make you sad. I just wanted to play. Can we still be friends?"

Lily looked at him and said, "Only if you promise to never do that again. And you have to help me clean the mess. And you have to give me a hug."

Ben nodded and said, "OK, Lily. I promise. I will help you clean. And I will give you a hug. You are my best friend."

They hugged and said, "We are sorry. We are friends."

They decided to play something else with the fan. They discussed what they could do. They agreed to make paper planes and fly them with the fan. They had fun and forgot about the banana peel.

Sam and Mia like to go to the park with Mom. They run and play on the swings and slides. They see many green things in the park. Green grass, green trees, green frogs. They like green.

One day, they see a big truck in the park. It is not green. It is red and yellow and blue. It has a big arm that moves up and down. It makes a loud noise. Sam and Mia are curious. They want to see what the truck is doing.

Mom says, "Be careful. The truck is in motion. It can hurt you if you get too close." She holds their hands and walks with them to the truck. They see a man in the truck. He is wearing a hard hat and a bright vest. He smiles and waves at them.

He says, "Hello, kids. I am working in the park. I am digging a hole for a new fountain. Do you want to see?" He shows them the hole and the water pipes. He says, "The fountain will make the park more beautiful. It will spray water in the air. It will have lights and colors. Do you like fountains?"

Sam and Mia nod. They like fountains. They say, "Thank you, mister. You are making the park nice." The man says, "You are welcome, kids. Enjoy the park. But remember, stay away from the truck when it is in motion. It is dangerous." He goes back to his work.

Sam and Mia go back to their play. They have fun in the park. They look forward to seeing the new fountain. They think it will be green. They like green.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl. She wanted to see if she could do things that were tough, so her mum dared her. One day she decided to take the dare and baked a cake. Everyone was so surprised at how good it was and said it was incredible.

But the brave girl didn't want to stop there. She wanted to do something else that was tough, so her mum dared her again. This time she decided to take the dare to tell the truth. The brave girl was scared but she found the courage to speak the truth.

Everyone was so impressed at the brave girl's courage. They said she was incredible for telling the truth even though it was so scary. Everyone cheered for the brave girl and praised her for being so courageous.

The brave girl was so happy to face her fears and take the dares. She was proud of herself that she had the courage to do two incredible things.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play with swords. They had wooden swords that they made from sticks. They pretended to be knights and fight bad guys.

One day, they saw a big sword in a shed. It was shiny and sharp. Tom wanted to play with it. He said to Sam, "Look, a real sword! Let's take it and have fun!"

Sam was scared. He said, "No, Tom, that is not a toy. That is a dangerous thing. It can hurt us or someone else. We should leave it alone."

But Tom did not listen. He said, "Don't be a baby, Sam. It is just a sword. I know how to use it. Come on, let's go!"

He took the sword and ran out of the shed. Sam followed him, but he was not happy. He wanted to talk to Tom and make him stop.

They came to a field where they saw some cows. Tom said, "Look, Sam, some bad guys! Let's fight them with our swords!"

He ran towards the cows and swung the sword. The cows were scared and angry. They mooed and kicked. One of them hit Tom with its horn. Tom fell down and dropped the sword. The sword cut his arm. He cried out loud.

Sam ran to help him. He saw blood on Tom's arm. He was very worried. He said, "Tom, Tom, are you okay? I told you not to play with the sword. It is not a toy. It is a dangerous thing. Now you are hurt. We need to get help."

He looked around and saw a farmer. He waved and shouted, "Help, help, my friend is hurt! He played with a sword and cut his arm!"

The farmer came and saw what happened. He was angry and sad. He said, "What were you doing with my sword? That is not a toy. That is a tool for work. You could have killed yourself or the cows. You are very foolish and naughty. Come with me, I will take you to your parents. They need to know what you did."

He took Tom and Sam to their parents. Tom's parents were shocked and upset. They took him to the doctor. The doctor cleaned and bandaged his wound. He said, "You are lucky, Tom. You could have lost your arm or your life. You should never play with swords or other dangerous things. They are not toys. They can hurt you or someone else. You should listen to your friend and your parents. They know what is best for you."

Tom felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I am sorry, Sam. I am sorry, mom and dad. I am sorry, doctor. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. I will never play with swords again. I will only play with safe toys. I hope you can forgive me."

Sam said, "I forgive you, Tom. You are still my friend. But you need to be more careful and smart. You need to think before you act. You need to talk to people who care about you. They can help you make good choices. That is how you can be happy and safe."

The moral of the story is: Do not play with dangerous things. They are not toys. They can hurt you or someone else. Listen to your friend and your parents. They know what is best for you. Talk to them and ask for help. They can help you make good choices. That is how you can be happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl. She was just three years old and very tidy. Every day, she would clean up her room and make sure everything was in its place. One day, she was cleaning her room when she saw something shiny. She picked it up and saw it was a penny!

The girl nodded, and put the penny in her drawer. Then, she shut the drawer tightly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play in the big green field behind her house. One day, she saw a shiny red ball in the field. It was so attractive that she ran towards it and picked it up.

But then, Lily heard a loud growl coming from the bushes. She saw a big, scary dog coming towards her. She regretted going into the field alone. She tried to run away, but the dog chased after her.

Lily's parents heard her scream and ran to the field. They saw the dog attacking Lily and tried to save her, but it was too late. Lily was hurt badly and had to be taken to the hospital. From that day on, Lily regretted going into the field alone and promised to always listen to her parents.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to prepare food for his family. One day, he wanted to make a big meal for everyone. He set the table with plates, cups, and forks. He was very excited.

While Tim was cooking, he found a tough piece of meat. He tried to cut it, but it was too hard. He was sad and didn't know what to do. He thought his family wouldn't like the meal.

Tim's mom saw him feeling sad. She came to help him. She showed him how to cook the tough meat so it would be soft and yummy. They cooked together and had a great time. In the end, the family loved the meal and they all had a happy dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Bert who felt very uncomfortable. He was always stressed, so he decided to find a way to relax. He went to the store and bought a mineral bath. 

Bert drew himself a nice bath and sprinkled the mineral into the water. He stepped in and the hot water felt really nice. He relaxed his muscles and slowly breathed in and out. He felt much better after taking his mineral bath.

The next day, Bert felt a lot less uncomfortable. Whenever he needed to relax, he knew he always could take a mineral bath. He always felt peaceful and happy afterwards.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Dave and Lisa. They were both very little and loved to play together. One day, Lisa got too close to Dave's special toy and he was mad.

"Give it back," Dave shouted.

Lisa shook her head and clutched it to her neck.

"No," she said, holding tight.

Dave and Lisa began to fight, each one wanting the toy for themselves. They scowled at each other and tugged, but neither one was willing to let go.

Suddenly, their mom walked into the room. She saw the fight and quickly separated the two.

"Calm down, you two," she said, giving them a hug.

Dave and Lisa both sighed. They were a bit embarrassed, but also grateful that Mom had stepped in to stop the fight.

"It's ok," she said, giving each of them a kiss. "Why don't you play together and share the toy?"

Dave and Lisa smiled. It was a great idea! They both hugged Mom, thankful that she had stopped their fight. Then they played together and shared the toy, happy to be friends again.

Once there was a little lamb who was very frightened. He had never seen a velvet before, and he was scared of its softness. Every day long he heard the loud voices of the shepherd and his dog, and he grew even more frightened.

One day, the shepherd shouted to the little lamb, "Come here, little one!" The little lamb was so scared that he didn't move. But the shepherd said again, "Don't be scared, I will send you to a safe place!"
 
The little lamb still didn't move, so the shepherd said gently, "Trust me, I will send you to a nice place where you can find velvet and make new friends!"

The little lamb was still frightened but he decided to trust the shepherd. So, the shepherd sent him to a lovely meadow. When the little lamb reached there, he couldn't believe his eyes. Everywhere he looked, he saw velvet. He realized that the shepherd had sent him to a safe place.

The moral of this story is that when things seem uncertain, it's best to trust your elders. They will always send you to a safe place.

Once upon a time, there were two little boys in the town. One of them was Jack, who was three years old. He went to the dock early every morning with his father. Today, dad had given Jack an important task.

Sam was out on a walk. He was enjoying the sunshine, when he saw something on the ground. He stopped to look, and saw a stamp! It had a picture of a small animal on it.
