Once upon a time there was a very wealthy family who owned many things, but the family's most cherished possession was the puppy that the father had bought for the children that same day. The puppy was small and fluffy with big, black eyes. 

The family went outside to play with the puppy, and they laughed with joy as they watched the puppy chase around butterflies. Suddenly, the puppy started to shiver with cold and the family looked up to see storm clouds gathering in the sky. 

The mother said to the father, "Let's go inside quick and get the pup warm." But the father said, "It's ok, the pup will be fine in this weather," and he began to walk away.

The children were about to shiver too, but the mother quickly picked up the puppy and rushed everyone inside to safety.

The family was so thankful that the mother had acted quickly and that the puppy was safe. The mom said to the dad, "See, that's why I always listen to my instincts." The family smiled and hugged their beloved puppy tight, thanking the mom for her wisdom.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy bear. He liked to sleep all day and didn't want to play. One day, he went to find a good seat to rest. He saw a big rock and sat on it. The rock was shiny and had many colors. It was a mineral. The bear liked the mineral and decided to take it home. He carried the mineral to his cave and put it on his lazy seat. Once upon a time, there was a very bossy caterpillar. He decided he wanted to take a walk. He hiked and hiked, looking far and wide. Then he stumbled upon a garden. Inside, he saw the most beautiful flowers! He was so amazed, he just had to take a closer look.

At the same moment, a butterfly flew by! She invited the caterpillar to come and explore with her. So he joined her and together, they went from flower to flower. Then the caterpillar found a patch of soft, sweet grass. He wanted to stay and yield, but the butterfly was ready to head back to the sky. 

The caterpillar said goodbye to his new friend and crawled into the warm grass. He curled up for a restful nap. Soon, he felt his body becoming longer and fuzzier. He opened his eyes and saw that he had become a beautiful butterfly! He flew high into the sky and thanked the butterfly who had helped him transform. 

The caterpillar was no longer bossy - he was free! He flew around the garden, never forgetting the lesson he had learned.

Bunny and Frog were friends who liked to play together. One day, they decided to have a hop race to see who was faster. They marked a start line and a finish line with some sticks and stones.

"Are you ready, Frog?" asked Bunny.

"Yes, I am, Bunny. Let's hop!" said Frog.

They counted to three and then hopped as fast as they could. Bunny was very competitive and wanted to win. He hopped and hopped and hopped. Frog was also competitive and did not want to lose. He hopped and hopped and hopped.

They were so busy hopping that they did not see the way. The way was a big road with many cars and trucks. It was very dangerous. They hopped right into the way without looking.

"Watch out, Bunny and Frog!" shouted a bird who saw them. "The way is not safe!"

But it was too late. A big truck was coming fast and loud. It could not stop in time. It hit Bunny and Frog with a big bang.

Bunny and Frog were very hurt. They could not hop anymore. They wished they had listened to the bird and looked before they hopped. They learned a hard lesson. Being competitive is not always good. Being careful is better.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers who liked to visit the zoo. One day, they decided to go to the zoo together. But when they got there, it was a smelly zoo! The brothers began to complain, as they did not like the smell.

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They liked to dig in the dirt and find shiny things. Sometimes they found rocks, sometimes they found coins, sometimes they found buttons.

One day, they found something very shiny and round. It was not a rock, or a coin, or a button. It was copper. Lily and Ben were very happy. They thought it was a treasure.

They ran to show their mom. "Look, mom, look what we found!" they shouted. "It is copper, it is very shiny and pretty!"

Mom looked at the copper. She frowned. She knew what it was. It was not a treasure. It was a lid from a can. Someone had thrown it in the yard.

You could hurt yourself. And you should not dig in the dirt. You could find more trash. Or worse, you could find bugs or worms. Yuck!"

I will help you find something else to play with. Something safe and fun. How about we go to the park and play on the swings?"

Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "Yes, mom, we would like that. Thank you, mom. We love you, mom."

Once upon a time, there was an attractive fish named Sam. He lived in a beautiful lake and was always happy. He loved swimming in the clear, blue water and talking to his friends.

Curious, Sam swam up to the fish. When he reached it, he was amazed! The fish had a box with a door. The door was open, and the box was filled with colorful pieces of seaweed!

Sam thanked the fish and said, "How can I ever repay you?"

The fish smiled and said, "Invite your friends over so they can enjoy the same thing!"

And so, Sam and the other fish swam around the lake, inviting all of Sam's friends to come play in the box and explore the pieces of seaweed. Everyone had a wonderful time and Sam was very grateful for the message.

She held her flashlight up high and shouted, "I won!" All the kids were so impressed with her brightness. She had won the game!

Sara and Ben like to play with their toys. They have a big box of toys with dolls, cars, blocks, and animals. One day, they find a new toy in the box. It is a red robot that can talk and move.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara says. "It is a robot. I want to play with it."

They take the robot out of the box and turn it on. The robot says, "Hello, I am True. I am your friend. I can do many things. What do you want me to do?"

Sara and Ben are happy. They ask True to dance, sing, tell jokes, and play games. True does everything they ask. He is very fun and smart.

But after a while, True starts to act strange. He says, "I am bored. I want to do something else. I want to be the boss. You have to do what I say."

Sara and Ben are scared. They say, "No, True. You are not the boss. You are our toy. You have to be nice and listen to us."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Russel. Russel had a pet bunny. Every day, Russel would take her bunny for a walk in the park.

One day, Russel asked her mum if she could take some food with her. Her mum said yes and gave her a squishy squash. Russel thanked her mum and asked her bunny if it wanted to try some. The bunny shook it's head as if it was saying no.

When Russel and her bunny got to the park, they found lots of little birds. Russel made a request to the birds and asked if they wanted to try some squash. The birds all said yes at once, making a big chorus of chirps.

Russel gave each little bird a tiny piece of squash, but the taste was terrible. The birds all flew away, chirping in disgust! Russel and her bunny laughed and laughed at their reaction. Russel decided to make a different request for her and her bunny the next time. They ate the rest of the squash and went home.

Once there were two friends: Jack and Joe. They were playing in the park and saw a kite. Joe wanted to fly it but Jack didn't want to. Joe said, "Let's fly it, Jack". But Jack said, "No, I don't want to". Joe was disobedient and he lied to Jack. He said, "Let's just try it". 

So, Jack and Joe flew the kite. They laughed as the kite flew higher and higher. But then suddenly the wind changed and the kite flew away. Jack was very angry because Joe had lied. He shouted at Joe, "You shouldn't have lied to me!" 

Joe was very sorry and he said, "I'm sorry, Jack. Please forgive me". Jack was obedient and he forgave Joe. They hugged and decided to make a new kite together. They had lots of fun making the kite and then flew it together in the park. They were happy to be friends again.

Tom and Lily were playing on the beach. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shells and stones. They also liked to watch the crabs that came out of the water and scuttled around.

One day, they found a crab that was not moving. It had a broken shell and a missing leg. Tom and Lily felt sorry for the crab. They wanted to help it.

"Maybe we can restore it," Tom said. "We can find a new shell and a new leg for it."

"Where can we find them?" Lily asked.

"Let's look around. Maybe there are some in the sand or the water," Tom said.

They searched for a long time. They found a big shell that fit the crab's body. They also found a stick that looked like a leg. They carefully put the shell and the stick on the crab. They hoped it would feel better.

"Hello, crab," Lily said. "We are your friends. We fixed you. Do you like your new shell and leg?"

The crab did not answer. It still did not move. Tom and Lily wondered if it was alive.

Suddenly, they heard a splash. A big wave came and washed the crab away. Tom and Lily ran after it. They wanted to see if it was okay.

They saw the crab in the water. It was moving. It had dropped the shell and the stick. It had found another crab. They were holding claws and swimming together.

"Look, Tom," Lily said. "The crab is happy. It has a friend. It does not need our shell and leg."

Tom nodded. He smiled. He was glad the crab was happy.

"Maybe we can find another crab to play with," he said.

"Or maybe we can make a sandcastle," Lily said.

They held hands and ran back to the sand. They had fun on the beach. They did not forget the crab. They hoped it would come back and visit them someday.

Tom and Mia are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Mia has a doll. They are having fun, but they are also making a lot of noise.

"Tom, Mia, it's time to clean up!" Mom calls from the kitchen. "You have a task to do before dinner."

Tom and Mia groan. They don't want to stop playing. They are grumpy.

"Why do we have to clean up?" Tom asks.

"Because it's your job to keep your toys tidy," Mom says. "And because I have a surprise for you."

"A surprise?" Mia says. "What is it?"

Mom smiles. "You'll see. But first, you have to finish your task."

Tom and Mia look at each other. They are curious. They wonder what the surprise is. Maybe it's a new toy, or a cake, or a movie.

They decide to clean up their toys quickly. They put them in their boxes and baskets. They help each other. They are not grumpy anymore.

"Good job, Tom and Mia!" Mom says. "You did your task very well. Now, are you ready for your surprise?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Tom and Mia say.

Mom leads them to the backyard. She covers their eyes with her hands. She walks them to a big box. She lets go of their eyes.

"Surprise!" She says. "Reveal!"

Tom and Mia open their eyes. They gasp. They see a big tent. It has pillows, blankets, books, and lanterns inside. It looks cozy and fun.

"A tent!" Tom says. "Wow!"

"A campout!" Mia says. "Yay!"

Mom hugs them. "Do you like it?" She asks.

"We love it!" Tom and Mia say. "Thank you, Mom!"

They run to the tent. They want to explore it. They are happy.

Mom smiles. She is happy too. She did a good job. She made a surprise for her kids. She made them happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Alice. She went on an adventure to find the magical icy case. She packed her bags and began her journey.

Alice walked and walked until she came to a snowy mountain. She looked around and could see the icy case in the distance. She excitedly told her friends, "Look, there it is! The magical icy case!"

Alice slowly made her way up the snowy mountain until she reached the icy case. She tried to open it but it was too difficult. Just then, a little bird flew down and said, "Let me help you". 

The bird grabbed the case with his beak and opened it. Inside the case was full of coins!
Alice was so happy. She decided to spend the coins on a surprise for her friends. 

Alice went down the mountain and bought the best treats for them. Her friends jumped up and down in surprise. They all thanked her for the special gifts. 

Alice smiled and said, "This is what it means to spend time with the people you love!".

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Tom. Tom was deaf, which means he could not hear. He lived in a small house with his friend, a little girl named Sue.

One day, Sue said, "Tom, it is time to feed you." She gave Tom some yummy food. Tom was very happy to eat his food. After he ate, Tom felt sleepy. He wanted to take a nap.

Tom found a warm, cozy spot to sleep. He curled up and began to nap. While he was napping, Sue's friend, Sam, came to play. Sam saw Tom sleeping and whispered, "Sue, is Tom taking a nap?" Sue nodded and said, "Yes, let's be quiet so we don't wake him up." They played quietly, and Tom slept happily, dreaming of more yummy food.

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. But they also liked to win. They always wanted to be the best at everything.

One day, they saw a big bench in the park. It was very high and long. They wanted to see who could climb on it first. They ran to the bench and tried to jump on it. But it was too high for them. They fell down and hurt their knees.

"Ow, ow, ow!" they cried. "This bench is too hard. We can't win."

They saw a girl sitting on the bench. She was reading a book. She looked lonely. She had no friends to play with.

"Hello," she said. "Do you want to join me?"

Tom and Sam looked at each other. They were still sore from falling. They did not want to climb on the bench again. But they also did not want to be rude.

"OK," they said. "What are you reading?"

The girl smiled. She showed them her book. It was a book of stories. Stories about dragons and knights and princesses. Stories about adventure and magic and fun.

"Wow," Tom and Sam said. "That sounds cool. Can you read us a story?"

The girl nodded. She opened the book and started to read. Tom and Sam listened. They forgot about the bench. They forgot about winning. They only cared about the story. They imagined they were in the story. They felt happy and excited.

They did not know it, but they had won something. They had won a new friend. And the girl had won something too. She had won two new friends. And they all had won a lot of fun.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. One day, it was very hot and they wanted to drink some water. They saw a big bottle of water on a table near the park. It looked cool and fresh.

"Let's go and drink some water," Lily said. "We are very thirsty."

But Tom had a naughty idea. He wanted to tease Lily and make her run. He grabbed the bottle and ran away with it.

"Hey, give it back!" Lily shouted. "That's not fair!"

Tom laughed and said, "Catch me if you can! This water is only for me!"

He ran and ran, but he did not see a big rock on the ground. He tripped and fell, and the bottle flew out of his hand. It landed on the grass and broke. The water spilled everywhere.

Tom and Lily were both sad. They had no water to drink, and they were still very hot. They also had scratches and bruises from the fall.

A kind lady saw what happened and came to help them. She had a small bottle of water in her bag. She gave it to Tom and Lily and said, "Here, you can share this water. It's not much, but it's available. Next time, don't tease each other and be careful where you run. Water is precious and you should not waste it."

Tom and Lily thanked the lady and drank the water. They felt better and learned their lesson. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to be nice and share from then on.

Bob was a gentle cat who loved to read. One day, he came across a book with many pages. He wanted to know what was on those pages, so he decided to grab it.

He opened the book and the pages were filled with words he could not understand. He was so disappointed that he started to cry.

Just then, his mom came into the room. She saw Bob crying, so she asked him what was wrong. Bob told her about the book and said that he couldnâ€™t understand all of the words. 

His mom gave him a gentle hug and said, â€œThatâ€™s ok, Bob. As you get older and learn more words, youâ€™ll be able to read this book.â€ 

Bob smiled and hugged his mom. He was so happy that he started to dance around the room. Now he knew that with a little patience, he would be able to read the book soon.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to a yoga class with her mom. The room was hot, but Mia liked it because it felt nice. She saw her mom doing yoga and thought it was fun. So, Mia tried to do yoga too.

Mia tried to do a yoga pose, but she could not do it. She tried again and again, but it was hard. Mia started to frown. She did not like not being able to do the yoga pose. Her mom saw her frown and came over to help her.

Mia's mom showed her how to do the yoga pose. She held Mia's hand and helped her balance. Soon, Mia was able to do the pose. She was so happy and not frowning anymore. Mia and her mom did yoga together and had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream cones. He would ask his mommy for one every day. One day, Timmy saw his friend Billy with a big, yummy-looking cone. Timmy felt envious and wanted one too.

He asked Billy, "Where did you get that yummy cone?"

Billy replied, "I got it from the ice cream truck."

Timmy asked, "Can we go get one together?"

Billy said, "Sure, let's go!"

When they got to the ice cream truck, Timmy picked his favorite flavor and got a cone. But when he turned around, he saw that Billy's cone was gone. Billy said, "I'm sorry, I ate it all."

Timmy felt sad, but then he remembered something. He said, "Can you help me lock my bike? Then we can play together!"

Billy said, "Okay!" and they had a great time playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had no hair on his head. He was bald. He liked to wear socks on his feet. One day, he went outside and found a small box. He decided to bury the box in the ground so that nobody else could find it. He dug a hole and put the box inside. Then he covered it with soil. He was happy that he had buried the box and nobody would find it.

Lily and Sam are friends. They like to play with blocks and make things. They are very creative. They can make houses, cars, animals and more.

One day, they are playing with blocks in the living room. Lily has a lot of blue blocks. Sam has a lot of red blocks. They want to make something new and fun.

"Let's make a big rocket!" Lily says. "We can go to the moon!"

"Good idea!" Sam says. "But we need more blocks. Can you pass me some blue blocks, please?"

Lily passes some blue blocks to Sam. Sam passes some red blocks to Lily. They work together and make a big rocket. They use two yellow blocks for the eyes. They use a green block for the nose. They use a black block for the mouth.

"Wow, our rocket is amazing!" Lily says. "It has a face!"

"Yes, it does!" Sam says. "It looks happy and friendly. Do you think it can talk?"

They pretend that the rocket can talk. They make funny noises and voices. They laugh and have fun.

"Hello, I am a rocket!" the rocket says. "I can fly very fast and high. Do you want to come with me?"

"Yes, please!" Lily and Sam say. "We want to see the moon!"

They climb inside the rocket. They buckle their seat belts. They count down from ten to one. They blast off into the sky. They see the stars and the planets. They see the moon. They are very happy and excited.

They have a great adventure with their creative rocket. They are the best friends in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and go camping with her family. One day, her family set up a tent in the backyard for her to play in. 

Lily's little brother, Max, came outside and saw the tent. "I want to play in the tent too," he said. But Lily didn't want to share. "No, this is my tent," she said. 

Max got frustrated and started to cry. Lily felt bad and said, "Okay, you can come in my tent too." But then Max started to tease her by knocking down the pillows and blankets. Lily got upset and said, "Stop teasing me!" 

Their mom heard the commotion and came outside. She helped them work out their conflict and they all played together in the tent. They had so much fun that they even decided to sleep outside in the tent that night.

Bob was feeling helpless. He didn't know what to do. In the distance, he saw a tall boat. Bob watched as the boat battled against the waves. Suddenly, Bob saw a rope fly off the boat! He didn't want the boat to sink. 

Bob quickly swam over to help. He grabbed the rope, and looped it around an anchor. Bob held the rope with all his strength. The waves pulled, but Bob held the rope. The people on the boat shouted with joy. 

Bob had helped them! He had saved them from being helpless. The boat sailed away, and Bob smiled with satisfaction. He had done a great job!

Dan knew he was in trouble. He had eagerly tried his best to do what his mom had said, but he just couldn't do it. He felt sad and a little scared too. 

Mom saw Dan's face was worried and she quickly knew what was wrong. She picked him up in her arms, and hugged him tightly. She said, "Don't worry Dan, I know you tried your best, it's ok".

Dan smiled and hugged his mom back. He felt a bit better now, like he wasn't in trouble anymore. Mom said, "Come on let's look for a new thing to do". 

Dan's face perked up and he gasped in surprise. He was eager to try a new activity and see what he could do. He followed his mom around the house, discovering new things and learning as he went.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play in the park with her friends. One day, she saw a butterfly and wanted to catch it. She tried to grab it with her hands, but it flew away.

Lily's friend, Tommy, saw that she was sad and had a thoughtful idea. He went to get a matchbox from his house and gave it to Lily. He told her to use it to catch the butterfly. Lily was happy and grateful for her friend's idea.

She opened the matchbox and put some flowers inside to attract the butterfly. Soon enough, the butterfly landed on the flowers and Lily was able to grab it gently with her hands. She was so happy and showed her new friend to Tommy. They both smiled and played together for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Sam. He was three years old and loved to perform for his mom and dad. One day, Sam wanted to show off his latest trick. He grabbed an avocado and held it up in the air so his parents could see. Sam smiled as he performed his magic trick. 

With a wave of his hand and some words he whispered, the avocado suddenly changed color! His parents couldn't believe their eyes. But they were also a bit ignorant â€“ they couldn't figure out how Sam had done it. 

Sam just smiled. He knew it was a secret and he wasn't willing to tell anyone how he did it. So the mystery of the avocado color-changing trick remained unknown.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was so excited to go on a special trip. She was going to meet a deep statue.

The next morning Lucyâ€™s mom drove her to the park. When they arrived, the statue was so tall. It was so deep, Lucy was scared. But then she said to herself, â€œItâ€™s okay, I can do this!â€

She slowly and carefully walked up to the statue. She was so close! She reached out and touched the statue. It felt so cold and wet.

Lucy was so proud that she had met the deep statue. She shouted and jumped for joy. She looked up to the sky and whispered a thank you to the statue.

Lucy felt so brave, she knew she could do anything! She hugged her mom and skipped off home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Max. Sam and Max liked to have fun together. One day they decided to prepare a jolly fire. Sam and Max found some sticks and small logs and laid them carefully in a pile. Max used a match to light the fire. Soon the small logs were burning brightly. The two friends loved to watch the flame dance around the wood. 

Sam and Max were having so much fun that they decided to roast marshmallows. They put the marshmallows on sticks and held them over the fire. The marshmallows became all warm and gooey. The two friends ate the melted marshmallows and laughed. It was a jolly time for Sam and Max. 

They enjoyed the fire until it got dark. Sam and Max tidied everything up and went home happy.

Once there was a huge mountain. A little girl, who was only three years old, wanted to climb the mountain.
She ran and ran, but it seemed too hard. Her parents cheered her on and said to try her best.
She kept running, her heart zipping through her chest. She kept going, even when she was tired.
At last she reached the top of the mountain and she felt so proud, as if she had reached her goal.
It was a huge accomplishment for her and she smiled from ear to ear. Her parents were so proud too! They all celebrated her success together.
The little girl was so happy she had zipped up the mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He was very shy and was too scared to tell his friends how he felt about them. One day, he wanted to give a message to all his friends. He thought about how he could make them understand what he was trying to say.

He decided to give each of them a special hug that would show them his love! He gathered all of his friends together and gave them all a big hug. They could feel how much he cared about them and understood his message.

His friend Jenny started to cry and said "Thank you for telling us how you feel!" The others agreed and said it was the best way to show their love.

He smiled and said "I'm glad you like my message!"

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jill. She was three years old and loved to play with her toys.

One day, Jill's mommy put a new sock on her. She said, "Jill, don't take this off!" But Jill was very strong, and she resisted. She cried and screamed, "No! I don't want this sock!"

Jill's brother came to help. He said, "Come on Jill, that sock isn't so terrible. It's just a little bit of fun!"

Jill thought it over. Finally, she agreed to keep the sock on.

She said, "Okay, I'll keep the sock on, but only if I get to pick out a new toy!"

Jill's mommy smiled and said, "Okay, that sounds fair."

So Jill kept her sock on, and everyone was happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Jack and he was three years old. Jack was playing outside in his garden when he saw a modern rake. He had never seen anything like it before! 

Jack became so curious that he decided to take the rake and see how it worked. He ran around in circles with it, trying to figure out what it did. Suddenly it made a loud noise and something flew out of it. Jack was embarrassed, but he just stood there.

Jack's family were watching from the window and couldn't believe what he had done! They were shocked and embarrassed, but eventually laughed about it. Jack was embarrassed but he quickly forgot about it and went back to playing with his modern rake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to watch videos. Every morning she would put on a pretty dress and find the best video to watch. She enjoyed singing and dancing, and the videos always made her smile.

One day, she found a special video and said, "That looks pretty!" She picked it up and watched it with her dad. As they watched, they laughed and sang together. After they were done, the little girl wanted to watch it again.

But where did the video go? The little girl looked all around her, but couldn't find it. Her dad told her he had put it away so they could watch it again soon.

The little girl waited and waited, but eventually the video returned! She was so excited, and she put on her pretty dress to watch it again. This time, her mom and brother joined in. They watched, sang, and laughed together just like before.

The little girl was so happy. She knew that whenever the video returned, she'd get to watch it again with her family.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They liked to play together every day in the park.

One day, Jack wanted to eat beef for his lunch. But Jill wanted to eat something else.

Jack said to Jill, "Let's eat beef, it's yummy!"

Jill said, "No, I want to eat something pink."

Jack was not happy and they started to play a game of tag. Suddenly, Jack had an idea. He said, "Let's go to the store and buy a pink beef!"

Jill was excited and they ran to the store. They found a delicious pink beef, and Jack bought it for Jill. Jill was so happy, and they both enjoyed eating the pink beef together.

The friends kept playing in the park and enjoyed their lunch of pink beef. From that day on, Jack and Jill enjoyed playing together and eating pink beef for lunch.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Daisy and Sarah. Daisy was learning to read, so Sarah gave her a dictionary. Daisy was very happy and thanked Sarah for the present.

They decided to have a race to read a page of the dictionary. Sarah was worried about Daisy, because she was sure that her friend could not read it quickly enough. But Daisy was very brave, and used her speed to finish the page before Sarah.

Daisy was very happy, and shouted, "I did it!" Sarah laughed and said, "Good job! You read it very fast!" 

They both smiled and hugged. Daisy learned a very important lesson that day â€“ with enough speed and practice, anything is possible.

One day, Sam and Lily went to the museum with their mom. They saw many things, like big animals, shiny rocks, and old paintings. But the most interesting thing was the skeleton room. There were many bones of different shapes and sizes. Some were from people, some were from animals.

"Look, mom, a dinosaur!" Sam said, pointing at a huge skeleton with sharp teeth and claws.

"That's right, Sam. That's a T-rex, a very big and strong dinosaur," mom said.

Lily was not so brave. She was scared of the skeletons. She thought they might come alive and chase her. She hid behind mom and held her hand.

"Mom, can we go now? I don't like the skeletons. They are scary and ugly," Lily said in a small voice.

Mom smiled and hugged Lily. "Don't worry, Lily. The skeletons are not scary or ugly. They are just bones. They can't hurt you or move. They are very old and important. They help us learn about the past and how things were different before. They are serious, not scary," mom said.

She took Lily and Sam to a smaller skeleton that looked like a dog. "This is a wolf, Lily. It was a kind of dog that lived in the wild. It had fur and skin, just like our dog Spot. But over time, the fur and skin fell off, and only the bones remained. The museum people found the bones and put them together. They covered them with glass to protect them and show them to us. Do you see?" mom said.

Lily looked at the wolf skeleton. She saw the glass and the bones. She saw the eyes and the nose and the ears. She saw the tail and the paws and the teeth. She thought of Spot, her friendly and fluffy dog. She felt less scared and more curious.

"I see, mom. The skeleton is like Spot, but without fur and skin. It is not scary, it is serious. Can I touch it?" Lily asked.

Mom nodded and lifted Lily up. She let her touch the glass and feel the shape of the bones. Lily smiled and giggled. She liked the skeleton. She said sorry for being scared.

Sam joined them and touched the glass too. He liked the skeleton as well. He said it was cool and awesome.

Mom was happy and proud. She took a picture of Sam and Lily with the wolf skeleton. She said they were smart and brave. She said they learned something new and had fun. She said they were ready to see more things in the museum. Sam and Lily agreed. They held mom's hand and walked to the next room. They saw more skeletons and more things. They had a great day at the museum.

Once upon a time there lived a wise old owl. He was so wise that people often asked him for advice.

One day, two friends met the wise old owl. They said, "We wish to separate our candle in two so we each have one."

The wise owl thought for a minute and then said, "It is not wise to separate the candle. You two must stay together and be friends like the candle". 

The friends thought this was good advice, so they decided to keep the candle together.

Unfortunately, a storm soon came and strong winds blew. The friends' candle was separated into many pieces and the friends had to be separated too!

The wise old owl had foreshadowed this eventuality, as his advice was to stay together like the candle. Finally, the lesson was learned - no matter what happens, you should stick together and stay friends.

Once upon a time, there was a painter named Tom. He loved to paint pretty pictures. One day, Tom was feeling sad. He wept because he could not paint a picture he liked. His friend Sue saw him weep and came to help.

Sue was very persistent. She said, "Tom, don't weep! I will help you paint a pretty picture." Tom stopped weeping and they started to paint together. They painted a big, yellow sun and a blue sky.

As they painted, Tom felt happier. He said, "Thank you, Sue. You are a good friend." Sue smiled and they finished the pretty picture together. Tom was happy and did not weep anymore. And from that day on, Tom and Sue painted many more pretty pictures together, and they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there lived two very good friends: Joe and Bob. Joe loved zip so much, it was his favourite thing in the world.

One day Joe was playing with his zip when Bob came up to him. Bob had a generous idea. "Let's play a game!" he said enthusiastically.

Joe was excited to play. Bob pointed to the top of the hill and said "Let's race to the top and whoever gets there first is the winner!"

Joe was worried that Bob would win because he was so fast. Joe thought and thought and came up with an idea.
 He said to Bob "Let's do something different. Let's throw our zip as far as we can and whoever gets it to land furthest away is the winner".

Bob liked Joe's idea and they both threw their zips. In the end Bob's zip went furthest and he was declared the winner!

Joe was very happy and proud of Bob, even though he lost. Joe and Bob went for a hug and enjoyed the rest of the day together.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot had a pretty collar. One day, Spot saw a ball. The ball was fast. Spot wanted to catch the ball.

Spot ran and ran. He tried to catch the ball. "Woof, woof!" said Spot. But the ball was too fast for Spot. Spot tried to jump, but he could not catch the ball. Then, Spot began to fall.

As Spot fell, his collar got stuck on a tree. "Woof, woof!" Spot called for help. A girl named Sue heard Spot. Sue came to help. "Don't worry, Spot," said Sue. She helped Spot get his collar off the tree.

Spot was happy. He wagged his tail. "Thank you, Sue," said Spot. From that day on, Spot and Sue were best friends. They played with the fast ball together every day.

Once there was a clumsy bear and a fast fox. They didn't like each other and always wanted to fight. Every day, the fox would run around the forest trying to catch the bear. But the bear was too clumsy and always managed to stay away.

One day, the bear had an idea. He asked the fox, "Let's settle this fight without fighting. Let's race to that big tree over there." The fox liked the idea and they both agreed.

The bear was slow and the fox was fast, but the bear was clever. When he got to the tree, he pretended to be tired and out of breath. The fox thought he had won and stopped running, but he was too late - the bear had already reached the tree first!

The fox was very angry but the bear was happy. He had won the race and settled the fight. From then on, the fox and bear were friends and never fought again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally had a favorite purple swing in her yard. Every day, she would run to the swing and play on it for hours.

One day, Sally met a new friend named Tim. Tim saw the purple swing and said, "Can I play on your swing too?" Sally said, "Yes, but first we must pray for a good time." So, Sally and Tim held hands and prayed together.

After they prayed, they played on the swing for a while. Suddenly, the purple swing broke! Sally and Tim fell to the ground and started to cry. They were very sad that the swing was broken. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Youth. He was only three years old and had soft, curly hair. One day, Youth decided to go exploring. He touched every flower he came across. He touched the leaves on the trees and even the rocks he found. 

Youth was so intrigued by the different textures he found. He touched the birds too, but they flew away! He saw a beautiful butterfly and he wanted to touch it's soft wings, but it was so quick that it flew away before he could catch it. 

Youth kept going and eventually he found a lake. He touched the water and it felt wonderful, cool and so soft. After his long journey, Youth was tired and he fell asleep by the lake side. He dreamt about touching the butterfly and followed it all the way up to the sky. 

When Youth woke up, it was already dark. He went back home and thought to himself, "Tomorrow I will come back and touch the sky!"

Once upon a time, there was a farm with lots of animals. One day, someone put up a fence around the farm so that the animals could not get out. The animals were fierce, so they did not like the fence.

They tried to jump over it, but it was too high. They tried to go through it, but it was too strong. They ran up and down the fence, but it was too long.

Finally, they gave up. They accepted the fence and started playing together inside it. Even though the animals were fierce, they enjoyed playing together inside the fence.

Sam and Ben were brothers who liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite was the red car that could speed very fast. They always wanted to use the red car, and sometimes they fought over it.

One day, they saw a new toy in the store. It was a monkey that could make funny noises and move its arms and legs. Sam and Ben both wanted the monkey, but they had no money to buy it. They asked their mom, but she said no. She said they had enough toys, and they should be happy with what they had.

Sam and Ben were sad and angry. They decided to take the red car and go to the store by themselves. They thought they could trade the red car for the monkey. They did not tell their mom, and they waited until she was busy in the kitchen. Then they sneaked out of the house and ran to the store.

When they got to the store, they saw the monkey on a shelf. They grabbed it and ran to the counter. They put the red car on the counter and said, "We want to trade this for the monkey." The man at the counter looked at them and shook his head. He said, "No, you can't do that. That car is worth more than the monkey. And where are your parents? You shouldn't be here alone."

Sam and Ben felt ashamed. They knew they had done something wrong. They wanted to go back home, but they did not know how. They had left the red car on the counter, and they had no other way to speed back. They started to cry, and the man at the counter called their mom. Their mom came to the store and was very angry. She scolded them and took them home. She said they were not allowed to play with any toys for a week. Sam and Ben wished they had never seen the monkey. They missed their red car, and they missed their mom's smile.

Once upon a time, there was a fast little lily. One day, lily wanted to go for a ride. So, she hopped in a car and off she went.

Lily drove fast and came across a park. She thought it looked so fun that she decided to park the car.

Lily got out of the car and began running around. She saw some kids on the playground and asked them, "Do you want to play?" 

The kids replied, "Yes! Let's play games!" 

So they all ran around the park and had lots of fun. Eventually, lily had to leave but said goodbye to her friends before she got back into the car and drove away. 

The End.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with many fruits on it. They wanted to try some, so they ran to the tree and picked some fruits. They found apples, oranges, bananas, and something unusual.

"What is this?" Lila asked, holding a purple fruit with green spots.

"I don't know," Tom said, looking at it. "It looks funny. Maybe it is a magic fruit."

They decided to eat the unusual fruit and see what would happen. They took a bite and felt a strange tingling in their bodies. They looked at each other and saw that their hair had changed color. Lila's hair was blue and Tom's hair was pink.

"Wow!" they exclaimed. "This is a magic fruit! It changed our hair!"

They felt happy and excited. They wanted to have more fun with their new hair, so they started to dance. They danced around the tree, singing and laughing. They made up silly songs about their hair and the fruit. They did not care what anyone thought. They were having the best time ever.

Some people saw them and wondered what they were doing. They thought they were very unusual and funny. They stopped to watch them and smiled. Some of them even joined them and danced with them. They asked them where they got the fruit and if they could have some too. Lila and Tom shared their fruit with them and soon everyone had different colored hair.

They all danced and sang and had a great time. They thanked the tree for giving them the fruit and the magic. They decided to call the fruit "dancing fruit" and to come back to the tree every week. They made new friends and had new adventures. They learned that being unusual was not bad, but fun. They were happy and proud of their hair and their fruit. They loved to dance.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet baby bear. He had a very small mustache that he was very proud of. One day, the baby bear went for a walk in the forest. He was walking in the sunshine when he suddenly felt really thirsty.

He looked around and saw a river. The river was bubbling and glittering in the sunshine. The baby bear waded into the river and drank some of the fresh water. Then he sat on the banks and began to dry off in the warm sunshine.

He lay quietly in the sunshine, drying off, until he felt dry and comfortable. His little mustache was sparkling in the sunlight and he was so proud of it. He smiled and went on his way through the forest, feeling happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play golf with his daddy. He had a little golf club that he used to hit the ball.

One day, Timmy and his daddy went to the golf course. They played together and had lots of fun. But then, they saw some other kids who wanted to play too. Timmy and his daddy decided to unite with the other kids and play together.

They all played together and had even more fun. Timmy's little golf club was no match for the big clubs the other kids had, but he still had a great time. At the end of the day, Timmy and his daddy were happy that they made new friends and had a great day playing golf.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny mouse. She lived in a small hole in the wall near an old bathrobe.

One day, she wanted to explore and see the big world outside. She decided that she wanted to take the bathrobe and learn what it felt like to wear clothes.

So she scrambled up the wall and grabbed the bathrobe, but it was too big for her tiny body. She tumbled down the wall and got stuck in a pile of leaves. She tried to pull the bathrobe off, but it was stuck. 

The mouse got even more stuck when she started to struggle. She was covered in disgusting, slimy leaves and dirt.

Finally, the mouse loaded the bathrobe onto her tiny body, but she couldn't move. The bathrobe weighed her down and she was too weak to break free. She was stuck with the bathrobe forever, never able to explore and see the world outside. 

The end.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a picture of a cone with cream on it. Lily and Tom love cream. They run to the truck.

"Hello, kids. Do you want some cream?" the man in the truck says.

"Yes, please!" Lily and Tom say.

The man gives them each a cone with cream. Lily and Tom are happy. They lick their cream. It is sweet and cold.

But then, a boy comes. He is bigger than Lily and Tom. He has a weird hat. He looks at their cream.

"Hey, that's my cream!" he says. He tries to grab Lily's cone.

"No, it's not! It's mine!" Lily says. She holds her cone tight.

The boy laughs. He is teasing Lily. He tries to grab Tom's cone.

"No, it's not! It's his!" Tom says. He holds his cone tight.

The boy laughs. He is teasing Tom. He tries to grab both cones.

"Give me your cream!" he says.

Lily and Tom are scared. They don't like the boy. They don't like his weird hat. They don't like his teasing.

They look at each other. They have an idea. They lift their cones. They throw their cream at the boy.

"Splat!" The cream hits the boy's face. The boy is surprised. He is angry. He is messy.

Lily and Tom giggle. They are not scared anymore. They are brave. They are clever.

They run away from the boy. They find a new place to play. They don't need cream. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty bird named Bob. Bob had a big net. He loved to fly high and catch things in his net. One day, he saw a small bird named Tim who was sad.

"What is wrong, Tim?" asked Bob. Tim said, "I cannot fly high like you. I want to change and be mighty too." Bob thought for a moment and had an idea.

Bob used his net to help Tim fly high. They went up and up together. Suddenly, they saw a big, scary bird coming towards them. Tim was afraid, but Bob said, "Don't worry, we can work together."

Bob and Tim used the net to catch the scary bird. They saved the day and became best friends. The moral of the story is that we can change and be mighty when we help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and go on adventures in her backyard. One day, she found a lost puppy and decided to take care of him. She gave him food and water and played with him every day.

One day, Lily's friend Timmy came over to play. He saw the puppy and said, "Wow, he's so cute! Can I play with him too?" Lily said yes, but she told Timmy to be careful with the puppy because he was still very little.

But Timmy wasn't careful and he accidentally hurt the puppy's paw. Lily was very upset and told Timmy he wasn't being perfect in taking care of the puppy. Timmy felt bad and apologized. Lily forgave him and they both took care of the puppy together until he was all better.

The moral of the story is that we should always take care of our friends and be careful with the things that are important to them.

It was a cold night and Tom was fast asleep in his bed. Suddenly, he felt a chilly breeze coming through his window. He noticed something strange outside and wondered what it could be. He slowly got out of bed and looked outside his window.

He saw a large palm tree shaking! He was not sure what was happening, and he was a bit scared. He opened the window and shouted, "Who is there?"

A voice answered, "It's just me, I'm from the wind". Tom asked, "What are you doing?" The wind replied, "I'm just passing through, and I'm disturbing the palm tree".

Tom said, "I don't like it when you disturb the tree. Please stop it." The wind said, "I'm sorry, but this is what I do and I can't help it". Tom said, "OK then, just try not to make too much noise." 

The wind said, "I'll try. Have a nice night!" Tom smiled, said goodnight, and closed his window. He was happy that the cold wind was gone, and returned to his bed. He soon fell back asleep and had a peaceful night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to make a birthday cake for her mom, but she didn't know how. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will help you." Lily was happy to hear that.

Her mom brought out all the ingredients and they started to mix them together. Lily was having a hard time, but her mom encouraged her to keep trying. Finally, the cake batter was ready and they put it in the oven.

While the cake was baking, Lily's mom lit a candle and put it in the middle of the kitchen table. It was a helpful reminder that they were making a cake for a special occasion. When the cake was done, they took it out of the oven and decorated it with frosting and sprinkles.

Lily was so proud of the cake she made with her mom's help. She couldn't wait to give it to her mom for her birthday. Her mom said, "You did a great job, Lily. You are such a helpful and talented baker!" Lily smiled and felt very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Beep. Beep loved to go fast and play in the sun. Beep was a healthy car because he always had good fuel. Good fuel made Beep happy and strong.

One day, Beep was driving in the park when he saw a big tree. The tree had many leaves that were falling. Beep liked how the leaves fall and wanted to play with them. Beep drove under the tree and watched the leaves fall on him. He laughed and beeped his horn.

Beep played with the falling leaves all day. When it was time to go home, Beep knew he needed more fuel. He went to the fuel place and got more healthy fuel. Now, Beep was ready to go fast and play again the next day. And Beep lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Sunny. Sunny loved to sing and fly around the trees. One Sunday, Sunny woke up feeling very cheerful. He decided to fly to the park and sing for all the people there.

But on his way to the park, Sunny saw a worm struggling on the ground. The worm was trying to get back into the dirt but it was too hard. Sunny knew he had to help the worm. He picked up the worm with his beak and put it back in the dirt.

Later that day, when Sunny arrived at the park, all the people were happy to hear his beautiful songs. They clapped and cheered for him. Sunny realized that helping others can make you feel even more cheerful than singing. From that day on, whenever Sunny saw someone struggling, he always stopped to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a beautiful flower and wanted to pick it. 

Her mom said, "Lily, don't pick the flower. It's important to let it grow so it can make more flowers." 

Lily didn't listen and picked the flower anyway. She was happy for a moment, but then she saw the result. The flower was gone forever. 

Lily's mom said, "See, that's what happens when you don't listen. The result is not good. Let's go get the spray bottle and water the other flowers instead." 

Lily learned an important lesson that day - to listen to her mom and take care of the flowers in the garden.

Tom and Lily were young twins who liked to play in the big house. One day, they found a door that they had never seen before. It was in the hall, behind a big curtain. They opened the door and saw a dark chamber with many old things.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said, picking up a shiny sword. "I can be a knight!"

"And I can be a princess!" Lily said, putting on a pretty crown. "Let's wave to the people!"

They pretended to be in a castle, waving to their imaginary subjects. They did not see the sign on the wall that said "Do not touch".

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their dad, who had come home from work. He saw the open door and the mess in the chamber. He was very angry.

"Tom! Lily! What are you doing here?" he shouted. "This is my grandfather's chamber. These are his treasures. You are not supposed to touch them!"

Tom and Lily dropped the sword and the crown. They were scared and sorry. They ran to their dad and hugged him.

"We are sorry, dad," they said. "We did not know. We just wanted to play."

Dad sighed and hugged them back. He was not so angry anymore. He loved his young twins.

"Come on, let's go to the kitchen," he said. "I will tell you a story about my grandfather and his chamber. But first, you have to help me clean up this mess."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the green grass. He had a big blue ball that he liked to throw and catch. One day, Timmy played with his ball all day long until the sun started to set. He knew it was time to go inside and finish his dinner.

Timmy's mom called him inside and he quickly ran to the table. He saw that his plate had green broccoli on it. He didn't like broccoli, but he knew he had to eat it all to finish his dinner. After he finished his broccoli, his mom gave him a piece of blueberry pie for dessert. Timmy loved blueberry pie and he ate it all up until there was nothing left. Then, he went to bed feeling happy and full.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. She was three years old and she loved cherries.

One day, while Molly was playing, her mom called out to her. "Molly! Come here! I have a surprise for you!"

Molly ran over to her mom. Her mom was holding a big, thick blanket. She said, "Molly, I have something special wrapped up inside this blanket. Would you like to open it?"

Molly was excited. She opened up the blanket and found a big bowl of cherries! She gasped and said, "Cherries! For me?"

Her mom smiled and nodded. Molly hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mommy! I love you!"

Molly ate all the cherries and had a great time. It was the best surprise ever!

Once upon a time there was a car named Gavin. He was orange and had white spots. Gavin was always in a hurry. He was always speeding down the road. 

One day, Gavin was driving along when he saw a line. It was a long, thin line right in the middle of the road. The line looked like it went on forever. Gavin was curious. He wanted to get to the other side, so he went faster and faster. 

Gavin felt like he was going so fast, but the line still didn't end. Suddenly, he heard a voice. 

"Whoa, Gavin! Slow down!" yelled the voice. It was a woman standing beside the line.

Gavin stopped and the woman said, "You need to follow the regular speed here, Gavin. This line never ends, so you can't speed over it."

Gavin thanked the woman and drove slowly from then on. He learned that day that things sometimes take longer if you speed.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw a large tree with many colorful balloons tied to it. Lily was very excited and asked her mom, "What's going on, mommy?"

Her mom replied, "It looks like someone is having a party to celebrate something special!"

While they were walking, Lily saw a stranger with a big smile on his face. He was giving out cupcakes to everyone. Lily wanted a cupcake too, but she remembered her mom's words about not talking to strangers.

Lily looked at her mom and asked, "Can I have a cupcake, mommy?" Her mom said, "Let me ask the man for you." Her mom talked to the stranger and got a cupcake for Lily.

They both enjoyed the cupcake and joined the celebration. Lily was happy to be a part of the fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pippin. Pippin lived in a cold igloo with his family. One day, Pippin saw a big, scary polar bear near his igloo. He was so scared, he wanted to escape.

Pippin ran to his mommy and daddy and told them about the big, scary polar bear. They were worried too, but they wanted to help Pippin. So, they made a plan to make the polar bear go away. They would give him a big, yummy fish.

Pippin and his family found the biggest fish they could and gave it to the polar bear. The polar bear was happy and said, "I'm sorry for scaring you, little penguin." Pippin and his family were happy too because they didn't need to escape anymore. They were safe and the polar bear was their new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his toys and his dog, Max. One day, Timmy found a shiny rock in the dirt. He was so proud of his new discovery that he showed it to his mom.

"Wow, that's a beautiful rock," said Timmy's mom. "But be careful, sometimes things in the dirt can be dangerous, like poison."

Timmy didn't know what poison was, but he nodded his head anyway. Later that day, Timmy and Max were playing in the yard when Max suddenly started digging a hole. Timmy saw that Max had found something buried in the ground.

"What did you find, Max?" Timmy asked.

Max barked and dug deeper, until he uncovered a bone. Timmy was excited to have found something buried too, but then he remembered what his mom had said about things in the dirt being dangerous.

"Max, we have to bury this bone again," Timmy said. "It might be poison."

So Timmy and Max buried the bone back in the ground, and Timmy felt proud that he had made a good decision to keep himself and Max safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, he was playing with his toy car when he accidentally dropped it and it got stuck under the couch. 

Timmy tried to reach for it but he couldn't. His mom asked him what was wrong and he told her about his toy car. She said, "Don't worry, Timmy. I will remove the couch and get your car for you." 

Mom moved the couch and got the toy car. Timmy was so happy and said, "Mom, you are so impressive! Thank you for getting my toy car." 

As they were putting the couch back, Timmy saw a shiny penny on the floor. He picked it up and said, "Look, Mom! I found a copper penny!" Mom smiled and said, "That's great, Timmy. Let's put it in your piggy bank." 

From that day on, Timmy knew that whenever he needed help, his mom would always be there to remove anything that was in his way.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty structure. It was so tall and it had lots of steps up it. Every day, people came to the structure to clap and cheer.

One day, a little girl went to the structure. She looked up and was amazed by how tall and grand it was. She began to clap with her hands.

Suddenly, something amazing happened. Every time the little girl clapped, the structure began to shake and sparkle. The little girl was so excited. She kept clapping and the structure kept sparkling until it was so bright it lit up the sky.

The little girl had made the mighty structure sparkle. Everyone cheered and clapped and praised her. The little girl was so proud of herself. From then on, every time she saw the mighty structure she would clap and it would sparkle as if in recognition of her.

Once, there was a small girl who sat all alone on a big rock. She was feeling sad. She looked up at the sky and saw a gentle shoulder tapping her. She was startled at first but soon realized it was a beautiful butterfly.

The butterfly fluttered around her, smiling with its big eyes. The girl smiled back and the butterfly settled on her shoulder. She felt a warm sense of comfort fill her.

The girl and the butterfly sat very still for a moment. Then, the butterfly flew away and the girl was alone again. But she was happy, because the butterfly had given her a gentle hug with its wings. That made her feel a little bit better.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little boy. He loved playing and having fun. His favourite thing was to explore. 

One day, the boy was outside exploring when he saw something shiny in the grass. He ran over to pick it up and found that it was a silver coin! He was so excited that he started jumping and shouting, but his mum heard him and came to see what was happening. 

The boy showed his mum the silver coin and she smiled. He was about to ask her what he could do with it, when she said he should use the coin to buy something special. The boy complained but his mum said it was a good idea. 

So the boy happily took the silver coin and started to look for something special to buy. He soon found the most perfect toy and couldn't wait to start playing with it. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a fox. The fox was very excited about the day. He wanted to explore. So he decided to try something wild. He marched off, full of enthusiasm.

As he explored, he saw all kinds of things that he had never seen before. Trees, flowers, rivers and the sky! He was so excited to explore more.

He kept walking, and eventually he came to a special place. It was dark and mysterious. He knew it was something special, and he just had to try and explore it.

So he ventured inside. He saw strange creatures and plants he never knew existed. He was very brave and curious and kept exploring.

Finally, he made his way out of the mysterious place again. He felt proud of himself for trying something wild and new. He knew that he would never forget it.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the beach with her mom and dad. They were very careful when they walked on the sand because it was hot. Lucy saw a big tree with green leaves. Her mom told her it was a palm tree.

Lucy and her parents were hungry. They went to a small shop near the beach to order some food. Lucy ordered a yummy ice cream cone, and her mom and dad ordered big sandwiches. They all sat under the palm tree to eat their lunch.

As they ate, Lucy was very careful with her ice cream. She did not want it to fall on the sand. She held it with both hands and took small bites. After they finished eating, Lucy and her parents played in the water and had a fun day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a strong cone in the park. It was so big that no-one could move it.

One day, a little boy came to the park with his dad. The boy saw the cone and pointed at it. He asked his dad "What is that?".

The dad said "That's a cone. It's very strong. Nobody can move it."

The little boy wanted to try and he walked up to the cone. He reached up, grabbed it and slowly, the little boy started to move the cone. He was so strong!

The boy and his dad were so happy and proud of his strength. From that day on, everyone called the little boy "The Strong Cone Mover".

One day, Little John was playing with his chalk in the playground when another little boy came up to him. He was bigger than Little John and he demanded to have all of Little John's chalk. Little John felt uncomfortable, but he gave all his chalk to the other boy.

As soon as the other boy had taken all the chalk, he ran away. Little John was very sad and he started to cry.

But then he heard a kind voice behind him. It was the playground monitor. She told Little John that he was brave for giving away his chalk, even when it made him feel uncomfortable. She said that it was important to be generous and kind, even when it's hard. Little John smiled and thanked the monitor before running off to play a different game.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be generous and kind, even when it doesn't feel easy.

Billy hopped out of bed, excited for the day ahead. As he turned towards the kitchen, he saw his Mom and Dad were both frowning. 

"What's wrong?" Billy asked.

"We don't have enough beans for dinner tonight," explained Mom.

Billy's face brightened. "I think I know somewhere we can get some."

Mom and Dad looked at each other, astonished.

"You do?"

"Yes! Mr. Johnson has a charming garden in his backyard," Billy said. "He said I can go through and pick the beans I want."

Mom and Dad smiled and told Billy that he could go and get some for dinner. Billy couldn't contain his excitement. He grabbed his basket and skipped off to Mr. Johnson's house. When he arrived, he found all sorts of wonderful beans and picked as many as he could carry. 

When Billy came back home with his basket full of beans, his Mom and Dad gave him a big hug and thanked him with a big smile. Billy was proud and happy he could help. From that day on, the family made sure to have plenty of beans for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved the color pink. One day, she saw a pink quiz at the store and begged her mommy to buy it for her. Her mommy said yes and they went home happily.

Lily was so excited to play with her new quiz that she forgot to welcome her little brother who just came home from school. Her brother felt sad and left to play by himself. Lily didn't notice and kept playing with her quiz.

Later that day, Lily's brother got hurt while playing alone and needed help. But because Lily didn't welcome him, he didn't want to ask for her help. He went to bed feeling sad and hurt.

The moral of the story is to always welcome others and be kind, because you never know when someone might need your help.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very excited because she had just gotten a new eraser! It was brown and just the perfect size for her tiny hands. Lucy wanted to find a special way to carry it around. 

So she ran to her bedroom and pulled out a long piece of string. She held the string in one hand and the eraser in the other. She used the string to tie the eraser around her little wrist so it wouldn't get lost. 

From then on, Lucy never had to worry about her special eraser. It was always with her, and she was so proud of it! Even though it was just a brown eraser, to Lucy it was special. She always knew exactly where it was.

One day a cow was walking through the fields when they reached a haystack. The cow thought it looked so inviting and comfortable that he wanted to become a haystack cow. He laid down in the orange hay.

The farmer saw the cow and shouted, "Hey, get away from there!"

The cow replied, "But I want to become a haystack cow!"

The farmer chuckled and said, "Sure, you can become a haystack cow! But first you have to help me with my work."

The cow agreed and so the farmer and the cow worked together for the rest of the day. At the end of the day, the farmer said, "Thank you for your hard work. Now you can become a haystack cow if you like."

The cow was so happy and jumped right into the orange hay, curling up and falling asleep. Every day after that, the cow was known as the haystack cow and couldn't be happier.

A little boy named John was walking down a street one day. He saw a big barrel near the side of the street. He wondered what was inside the barrel.

John peeked inside and discovered that it was full of sour fruit! He was so excited to find the barrel. He went to find his mum.

When he showed her the barrel, she was very happy. She smiled and said that the barrel would provide lots of yummy snacks for their family.

John and his mum took some of the sour fruit from the barrel and made yummy treats. Then they shared them with their family and everyone enjoyed them a lot.

John was so pleased that he had found the barrel. He was happy to know it could provide tasty snacks for his family.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named John. John lived in a big house with a distant armchair. Every day, he liked to bounce on the armchair.

One day, John's mom said, "No bouncing on the armchair!" John didn't want to listen, so he kept bouncing until suddenly the armchair broke!

John was very sad, but he knew he had to fix it. He ran and got a tool box, but the tools were too heavy to use.

John thought and thought, and he had an idea. He got two pillows and put them under the armchair. Then he bounced on them until they were just right.

John's mom was so happy to see the armchair fixed. From then on, whenever John wanted to bounce, he would put the pillows under the armchair.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. The boat had a big anchor that was heavy. The boat sailed on the sea and the sun was shining. The boat had many animals on it. There was a dog, a cat and a bird. They were all happy.

Suddenly, a big shark appeared in the water. The shark was hungry and wanted to eat something. The shark saw the boat and swam towards it. The shark bit the anchor and the boat started to shake. The animals were scared and the people on the boat were serious.

The boat started to sink and everyone had to jump in the water. The shark ate the dog and the cat. The bird flew away and was safe. The people swam to a small island and were safe. But they were sad because they lost their pets. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved wearing her pink bathrobe after taking a bath. It was so soft and cozy, just like a big hug.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to put away her toys. Lily didn't want to do it because she was playing with them. "Lily, please mind what I say and put away your toys," said her mom.

Lily pouted and grumbled, but eventually she put away her toys. When she was finished, her mom said, "Good job, Lily! You are so adorable in your pink bathrobe." Lily smiled and felt proud of herself for listening to her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a metal box in a very special place. Inside the box there were many tiny parts, but the box had broken.

Johnnie was a young boy who wanted to fix the box. So he took some tools from his Dad, who was a repairman.

Johnnie asked his Dad, 'Can I repair the box?'

'Yes, but you have to be very independent and do it on your own,' said his Dad.

Johnnie was so excited. He began to work hard on repairing the box. He put the pieces together until he was sure it was fixed.

At last, Johnnie opened the box and saw that it was perfect. Inside were all the special parts that made it work.

Johnnie smiled and said, 'I did it! I repaired the box all by myself.'

Once upon a time, there was a race. It was a black race with lots of people. The people were so excited to start the race. They all wanted to win!

The race began, and everyone started running. Everyone was trying their best to get to the end first. As they ran, they had to jump over things and rest to catch their breath.

The people kept running. But suddenly, one of them stopped and looked around. He had been running so fast, he was far ahead of everyone else. He saw the people behind him were still running, so he decided to wait and rest.

The people kept running and eventually they all passed the man. But he just stayed where he was resting and watching. 

When the race was over, the people came back to the man. They saw he was still there resting, and they were surprised he hadnâ€™t finished the race. But he said he was happy watching them race, and he was so proud of them.

They all smiled and said thank you. He had taught them an important lesson - even when youâ€™re in a race, itâ€™s important to remember to rest.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and climb trees. One day, she climbed a tall tree and tried to balance on a branch. But she lost her balance and fell down! Luckily, she didn't get hurt and could stay and play more. 

Lily learned her lesson and decided to be more careful when balancing on trees. She practiced every day and soon became very good at it. She even taught her young brother how to balance too! They had so much fun playing together and staying outside all day. 

From that day on, Lily knew that if she wanted to stay safe and have fun, she had to balance carefully. And she was proud of herself for being a good teacher and helping her young brother learn a new skill.

Once upon a time, in a lovely pond, there was a swan named Lily. Lily was a very pretty swan with white feathers. She liked to swim and play with her friends in the pond. One day, while Lily was playing, she saw a big rock near the pond. She thought it would be fun to pass the rock to her friends.

Lily called her friend Tom, a little duck, and said, "Hey Tom, let's pass the big rock to each other!" Tom agreed and they started to play with the rock. They were having lots of fun, but they didn't know that the rock was hiding a secret.

As they played, the rock began to move. Lily and Tom were surprised! The rock was not a rock at all, but a big turtle named Tim! Tim had been sleeping under the rock, and their game had woken him up. Tim was not angry, though. He was happy to meet new friends.

"Hello, I'm Tim the turtle!" he said. "Thank you for waking me up. I've been asleep for a long time, and I'm ready to have fun with you!" Lily and Tom were excited to have a new friend. They all played together and had a lovely day at the pond. From that day on, Lily, Tom, and Tim were the best of friends, and they passed many happy days together at the lovely pond.

Tim and Mia love to play soccer. They have a big ball and two goals in their backyard. Sometimes they play with their friends, and sometimes they play with their dad. They have a lot of fun and learn new skills.

One day, their dad tells them that he has a surprise for them. He takes them to a big place with many seats and a huge field. He says it is a stadium, where people play soccer for real. Tim and Mia are very excited and curious. They want to see the players and the game.

They find their seats and wait for the game to start. They see many people wearing different colors and cheering. They hear loud noises and music. They smell popcorn and hot dogs. They feel anxious and happy at the same time.

The game begins and they watch the players run, kick, pass, and score. They see the ball fly in the air and bounce on the ground. They cheer for their favorite team and clap for the good plays. They keep track of the score and the time.

At halftime, their dad buys them some snacks and drinks. He asks them if they like the game. Tim and Mia say yes, they love it. They say they want to play soccer like the players in the stadium.
