But then she spotted a big slide. She entered the slide, excited to have some fun. She smiled as she went around and around, faster and faster. After that, she entered the sandbox, giggling as she played. She found some friends and together they made beautiful sandcastles.

The little girl was no longer sad. She had so much fun that she forgot all about why she was feeling sad in the first place. Her day at the park on Tuesday had been the best.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and sing all day long. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and saw a big gray cloud in the sky. It was very big and made her feel sad.

Suddenly, a bird came and started singing a beautiful song. Lily clapped her hands and the bird flew away. But then, she saw a lot of waste on the ground. She knew it was bad for the earth, so she picked it up and threw it in the trash can.

After that, Lily felt happy again and continued to dance and sing. She learned that even though there can be sad things in the world, she can still make it better by doing small things like picking up waste and clapping for happy moments. The end.

Once upon a time there was a box. It was a very special box, and it was made of wood. It was a trunk.

The trunk belonged to a little boy. His name was Max. Max was three years old.

One day, his mummy said to him, "Max, let's unpack the trunk!" Max was very excited. He opened it up.

But when he opened it, he couldn't believe it. Inside the trunk was fake stuff. There were fake cars, fake animals and even fake outfits. 

Max was not very happy. His mummy laughed. She said, "It's just pretend! Let's have some fun and make believe." 

Max smiled. He and his mummy played with the fake stuff all day. They imagined they were driving in the fake cars and wearing the fake outfits. It was so much fun!

A curious girl called Mia went for a walk. She walked happily down a wooded path. Suddenly, Mia heard a noise. She turned around and saw a little tea pot. Mia was very curious. She walked up to the tea pot and said hello. The tea pot didn't answer. Mia tapped it gently and she heard a buzzing from inside. Suddenly, the tea pot came to life! Mia was so excited. The tea pot asked her if she would like some tea. Mia said yes and the tea pot poured her a warm cup of tea. Mia drank the tea and thanked the tea pot for being so kind. Then she waved goodbye and continued her walk. Mia smiled to herself in amazement - she had just shared a cup of tea with a magical tea pot!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat fruits, but she didn't know what to eat next. Her mom recommended that she try a lime. 

Lily had never tried a lime before, but she was excited to try something new. She went to the store with her mom and picked out a lime. It was small and green, but it had a brown stem. 

When they got home, Lily's mom cut the lime into small pieces. Lily took a bite and made a funny face. The lime was sour, but she liked it! She ate the rest of the lime and asked her mom to buy more. 

From that day on, Lily loved limes. She recommended them to all of her friends and even brought some to school to share. Everyone loved them, even though they were sour and had brown stems.

Once there was a grumpy man who lived in a town by the beach. Every night, the most beautiful sunset lit up the sky and was just too stunning to be true. The man wanted the sunset to be his own and every night he would try to steal it.

One night, he stayed up to watch the sunset. He waited and waited and when the sun was about to disappear he ran to catch it. But, as soon he tried to catch it, the sky turned dark and the man was very upset.

Just then, he heard a small voice behind him. He turned around and saw a small 3 year old girl standing in the sand. The man asked the girl, "Why did you stop me from taking the sunset?". The girl replied, "Because no one can steal the sunsets that are to be shared with everyone". The man smiled and agreed with what the girl said. 

The man thanked the little girl and they both watched the beautiful sunset together. From that day onwards they became friends and watched the beautiful sunset together every night.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was cool because he had a red hat that he always wore. One day, Timmy was walking in the forest when he stumbled on a rock. He fell down and hurt his knee.

Suddenly, he saw a pistol on the ground. "Wow, this is so cool!" he said to himself. He picked it up and started playing with it. "Bang bang!" he shouted.

But then, a bad man appeared and took the pistol from Timmy. Timmy was scared and ran away. He learned that playing with guns is not cool and can be dangerous.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to catch butterflies. They ran around the garden with their nets, trying to catch the colorful butterflies.

Lily's friend, Timmy, started to worry that they wouldn't catch any butterflies. But Lily told him not to worry, and they kept trying. Suddenly, Lily saw a butterfly with bright blue wings. She ran after it and caught it in her net! She was so happy and excited.

After they finished playing, Lily's mom made them some tasty snacks. They had sandwiches with cheese and ham, and some juicy watermelon. Lily was happy that she caught a butterfly and got to eat something tasty. She went to bed that night with a big smile on her face.

Mama and Emmy were off together on a march in the park. Emmy held Mama's hand as they walked together. They laughed and talked, and the sun shone on them warmly.

"Look at these flowers, Emmy," said Mama, pointing at some bright yellow blossoms. 

Emmy smiled happily and looked. "They're so pretty," she said. 

"Maybe we can pick some and take them home to Mama," Mama said. 

So they stopped together to pick the flowers. Mama showed Emmy how to hold each stem gently and then they had a whole bunch of them. 

On their way back home, Mama stopped to buy some delicious ice cream. 

"Mama, can I have some too?" Emmy asked. 

Mama smiled and said, "Of course Emmy! Ice cream is a nice reminder of our march in the park." 

Emmy smiled and ate her ice cream. It was so delicious! 

When they got home, Emmy gave her bunch of bright yellow flowers to Mama with a big hug. Mama smiled and said, "This is the best reminder of our fun march in the park today." 

Emmy was happy, and knew that this would be a day she would always remember.

Bob and his mom were walking in the park on a Sunday. Bob was being very curious, looking at everything around him. He saw a tree that had a funny twist in it. He asked his mom about the twist, and she said it had been there a long time. "Sometimes nature twists things in unusual ways!" she said.

Bob walked on, still curious about the twist. He saw a squirrel twisting its body around the bend of the tree trunk. Bob laughed and said "That squirrel is making funny twists!" His mom smiled, and they kept walking until it was time to go home.

Every Sunday, Bob and his mom would go back to the park. Bob loved to see the twist in the tree, and he was always looking for things that had been twisted by nature. He thought it was so exciting and always made sure to visit the twist every Sunday.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Kelly. She was three years old. Her mommy and daddy took her to the park one day in the winter. 

When Kelly arrived, she was so excited! She saw big snowflakes falling from the sky and all around her there was snow. She said, "Look mommy, it's so perfect!" 

Kelly and her mommy went to the top of the hill. They made a snowman with the perfect round snowballs. They put a hat on him and a scarf around his neck. Kelly was so happy!

Then, Kelly and her mommy went to the slide. Kelly said, "Slide is my favourite!" She laughed and giggled as she went down the snowy hill. 

Evening started to come and it was time to go home. Kelly said, "Mommy, this was the perfect winter day. I enjoy it so much!" 

Everyone smiled and they went home happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big city with her mom and dad. One day, Lily and her family went to the park. Lily played on the swings and went down the slide. But after a while, she got tired and wanted to go home.

"I'm tired," said Lily to her mom.

"Okay, let's go home," said her mom.

As they walked back to their apartment, Lily saw a big building that she didn't like.

"I hate that building," said Lily to her dad.

"Why do you hate it?" asked her dad.

"It's too big and scary," said Lily.

Her dad smiled and said, "Don't worry, we don't have to go there. Let's go home and rest."

Once upon a time, there was a pilot named Max. Max was flying his plane when he noticed a bird flying low. Max felt alert and hoped the bird wouldn't hit his plane. "Hello birdie," said Max. "Please fly high so we don't crash." The bird flew up and Max felt relieved. "Thank you birdie," said Max. "You're a good listener." Max continued to fly his plane, feeling happy and safe.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a gun in the park. It is big and black and shiny.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom says. He picks up the gun and holds it in his hands.

"Be careful, Tom. That is not a toy. That is a gun. It can hurt you," Sam says. He is scared of the gun.

"No, it is a toy. See, it makes a loud noise. Bang! Bang!" Tom says. He pulls the trigger and the gun makes a loud noise. He laughs and raises the gun in the air.

"Stop, Tom, stop! That is not funny. That is bad. You can hurt someone with the gun. Put it down, please," Sam says. He tries to take the gun from Tom.

But Tom does not listen. He runs away with the gun. He sees a friendly dog in the park. The dog is brown and fluffy and has a red collar. The dog barks and wags its tail. It wants to play with Tom.

"Hi, doggy. Do you want to play with me?" Tom says. He raises the gun and points it at the dog.

"Tom, no! Don't do that! That is not nice. That is mean. The dog is friendly. He does not want to play with the gun. He wants to play with a ball or a stick. Leave the dog alone," Sam says. He runs after Tom and the dog.

But Tom does not listen. He pulls the trigger and the gun makes a loud noise. The dog yelps and falls down. He does not move. He does not bark. He does not wag his tail.

Tom is shocked. He drops the gun and runs to the dog. He touches the dog and sees blood. He starts to cry.

"Doggy, doggy, wake up. I am sorry. I did not mean to hurt you. Please, wake up," Tom says. He hugs the dog and cries.

Sam is sad and angry. He picks up the gun and throws it away. He goes to Tom and the dog. He hugs Tom and tries to comfort him.

"Tom, I am sorry. You made a big mistake. You should not have played with the gun. The gun is dangerous. The gun is not a toy. The gun can kill. You killed the dog. The dog is dead. He will not wake up. He will not play with you. He will not be your friend," Sam says. He cries with Tom.

They stay with the dog until a man comes. The man is the owner of the dog. He sees the gun and the dog and the boys. He is very angry and sad. He calls the police and the ambulance. He takes the dog away. He does not talk to the boys.

The police and the ambulance come. They talk to the boys. They ask them many questions. They take them to the hospital and to the police station. They call their parents. They are in big trouble.

Tom and Sam are sorry. They learn a hard lesson. They never play with guns again. They never forget the friendly dog. They never stop being friends.

One day, Johnny was playing outside with his ball. He saw a clown walking around. He was excited to catch the clown.
Johnny quickly ran up to the clown, but it was too fast. It moved away each time he got close. Johnny kept running around it and trying to catch it.
Eventually, Johnny got exhausted. He plopped down on the ground and watched the clown.

The clown had a smelly aroma. It smelled almost like garbage. Johnny made a face, but he still thought the clown was funny. 

The clown saw Johnny and asked, "Do you want to catch me?" Johnny smiled and shook his head.

The clown ran away with a big smile on its face. Johnny laughed and said, "I almost caught the clown!" He went back to playing with his ball.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the post office with her mommy. She saw a lady putting stamps on envelopes. Lily asked her mommy, "What is that lady doing?" Her mommy replied, "She is putting stamps on the envelopes so they can be sent to their friends."

Lily was very curious and asked the lady, "Can I help you put stamps on the envelopes?" The lady smiled and said, "Sure, you can help me put stamps on the envelopes." Lily was so proud of herself for helping.

After they finished putting stamps on all the envelopes, the lady gave Lily a sticker as a reward. Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, I had so much fun helping you put stamps on the envelopes!" Her mommy smiled and said, "I'm proud of you for being such a good helper."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Elsie. She was a brave and extraordinary girl who loved to explore. 

One day, Elsie was exploring in the woods near her home when she heard some news. The news said that a scary monster was coming to town! Elsie wanted to see the monster for herself, but her mom was scared and didn't want her to go. 

Elsie insisted, but her mom said no. Her mom explained that the monster was dangerous and she didn't want Elsie to get hurt. Elsie still wanted to go, but her mom said no once more. 

Elsie kept insisting, but her mom said no again. Finally, Elsie agreed to stay home and decided to explore in her own backyard instead. She knew it wouldn't be as exciting as exploring in the woods, but at least she was safe. 

And so, Elsie stayed safe and happy. She never did get to see the scary monster, but she was content knowing that she made the right decision.

Once upon a time there lived a brave knight. He lived in a big castle and his job was to protect the people. He was very loyal and always ready to help. 

One day he found out that his friend, the King, was in trouble. It seemed that the King's enemies were trying to steal his prized pizza. It was very special because it had lots of yummy toppings and it smelt so good. The brave knight was determined to save the pizza. 

So the knight got on his big white horse and rode off to protect the King's pizza. As he travelled through the forest, he saw lots of scary things. He was so brave that he didn't even flinch. All the animals admired him for his courage. 

Finally, the knight arrived at the castle and confronted the enemies. With just one slice of his impressive sword, he scared them away. The King was so thankful that he rewarded the brave knight with a big piece of pizza. 

The brave knight had successfully protected the King's pizza. Everyone in the castle was so proud of him. He was truly a knight to be admired.

Once upon a time, there was a sad tiger who lived in the jungle. He used to be so happy and show his bright stripes to everyone, but not anymore. One day, he found his friend, a zebra. The zebra was so excited to see the tiger and said, â€œLetâ€™s race!â€ The tiger was unsure as he had not been happy for a long time, but the zebra was insistent.

Finally, after much convincing and persuading, the tiger decided to race the zebra. When he started running, the tiger realised how much fun it was. His belly was filled with happiness and his stripes were shining brightly! After the race was over, the tiger was so excited that he won and hugged the zebra.

The moral of the story is: if we try hard and never give up, even when things seem sad and difficult, we will be rewarded with happiness.

Molly was a brave girl. She wanted to explore a big house but it was locked. Molly looked around for the key, but couldn't find it. She was about to give up when suddenly she had an idea.

Molly bravely decided to dare herself to go inside. She took a deep breath and walked up to the door. The door was tall and old and very pale.

Molly was scared, but she forced herself to reach out and open the door. It opened with a loud creak and Molly walked inside.

Molly was amazed by all she saw inside the house. She explored room after room, each more fascinating than the last. Eventually, Molly found the key to the lock and went home with a satisfied grin.

The little boy wanted to play with the stamps. He saw them in his mommy's drawer and he wanted them. His mommy said "No, we need to keep the stamps here to prevent them from being lost". The little boy started to cry. His mommy knew he was very sad, so she said she would give him one of the stamps every day if he was regular about it. He agreed, and every day his mommy would give him just one stamp to play with. He was so happy and always made sure to be regular about getting his stamp each day. His mommy was happy he was learning to be responsible and taking care of his special stamps.

Once upon a time, there was a big boat. The boat had a big anchor. One day, the boat went to the sea to play. The boat was not careful. It went too fast.

The boat saw a big rock in the water. The boat needed to stop. The boat dropped the anchor to stop. The anchor made a big splash in the water. The boat was scared.

But the anchor did not work. The boat hit the big rock. It made a big hole in the boat. The boat could not play in the sea anymore. The boat was very sad.

Lily and Ben wanted to decorate their room for Halloween. They had many things to make it scary and fun. They had pumpkins, spiders, bats, and ghosts. They also had costumes to wear.

Lily wanted to be a witch. She had a black dress, a hat, and a broom. Ben wanted to be a superhero. He had a red suit, a cape, and a mask. They helped each other put on their costumes.

"Wow, you look incredible, Lily!" Ben said. "You are a very good witch."

"Thank you, Ben. You look incredible, too. You are a very strong superhero." Lily said.

They were ready to decorate their room. They hung the spiders and bats on the walls. They put the pumpkins and ghosts on the floor. They turned off the lights and used a flashlight to make shadows.

They were very happy with their room. They invited their mom and dad to see it. Mom and dad were very surprised and proud.

"What a spooky and fun room you have, Lily and Ben!" Mom said. "You did a great job decorating it."

"And what amazing costumes you have, Lily and Ben!" Dad said. "You are very creative and brave."

Lily and Ben smiled and hugged their mom and dad. They had a lot of fun decorating their room and dressing up for Halloween. They were very excited to go trick-or-treating later.

Kelly and her mommy went on a walk into the valley. The sun shone brightly in the sky.

"Look, Mommy," said Kelly. "The sun is so bright."

"Yes," said Mommy. "Let's have a look around and see what else we can find in this valley."

They both looked around. Kelly saw butterflies flying in the air, some birds singing in the trees and bright flowers growing in a garden.

"It is so creative here," said Kelly. 

"Yes, it's beautiful," said Mommy.

They walked for a while until they came to a pond. The sun was shining on the water and it looked like the pond was made of glitter.

"It's so pretty," said Kelly. "The sun is making it shine like gold!"

"Yes, it's like a magical place," said Mommy.

They stayed and watched the pond until they couldn't see the sun anymore. Then they went home and Kelly went to bed, dreaming of the beautiful valley they had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy and his friend Billy went to a big event in the park. There were lots of games and prizes to win.

Timmy and Billy played a game where they had to shoot a basketball into a hoop. Billy was very good, but Timmy was weak and couldn't make the ball go in. Timmy felt sad because he really wanted to win a prize.

Suddenly, a big boy came and started to push Timmy. "Move out of the way, weakling!" he said. Billy stood up for Timmy and said, "That's not nice! We're all here to have fun and play games."

The big boy realized he was wrong and said sorry. Timmy and Billy continued to play games and have fun. The moral of the story is that it's important to stand up for your friends and be kind to others, even if they are not as strong as you.

Andy and his mom were walking in the park. Mom had a small bag with money in it. Andy was very excited. 

"Where are we going?" Andy asked. 

"We are gonna buy something special," Mom said with a nod.

They came to a distant place, far away from the park. It was a big store. Andy knew it was the toy store. He clapped his hands in joy. 

Mom opened her bag and got out some money. She gave it to the woman at the desk, who nodded in return. Then she took Andy in the back room. 

There were so many toys for Andy to choose from. 

After a few minutes of inspection, he decided to buy a robot. It was shiny and made of metal.

Mom nodded in approval. She took out the money and gave it to the woman at the desk. The woman smiled and handed the robot to Andy. 

He smiled and hugged his new toy tight. Mom and Andy walked back to the park, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a big house. Inside the house, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane wanted to paint the house so it would look nice and clean. She ran to the shed and found her hammer.

Jane carefully used her hammer to open the paint pot. Then, she dipped her brush into the paint and started to paint the walls of the house. She painted slowly and carefully, making sure to go all the way to the edges.

When she had finished one wall, she slowly moved on to the next. Before long, the whole house was painted! Jane was very proud of herself. She had painted her house to make it look clean and pretty.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a heart full of love and kindness. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She met a boy named Timmy who was crying. Lily asked him, "Why are you crying, Timmy?" 

Timmy said, "I miss my toy car. It's my favorite." 

Lily felt sad for Timmy and said, "Don't worry, we'll find your toy car together." 

They looked for the toy car and finally found it under a tree. Timmy was happy and hugged Lily. Lily felt a mild happiness in her heart. 

The moral of the story is that helping others can make us feel good inside.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play together. They have many toys in their room. Some toys are big and strong. Some toys are small and fragile. Fragile means they can break easily.

One day, Ben and Mia are bored. They want to do something new. They see a book on the shelf. The book has numbers and shapes. The book is called math. Math is what big kids learn at school.

"Let's do math!" Ben says. He takes the book and opens it. He sees a page with a long snake. The snake has numbers on its body. The book says: "Stretch the snake and count the numbers."

"Wow, that looks fun!" Mia says. She wants to try too. She grabs the other end of the book and pulls it. Ben and Mia stretch the book as much as they can. They count the numbers on the snake. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!" they say together.

But the book is fragile. It is not meant to be stretched. The book rips in the middle. The snake breaks into two pieces. Ben and Mia are shocked. They hear a loud voice. It is their mom.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She sees the broken book. She is angry. "That is my math book. It is not a toy. It is fragile. You should not stretch it. You should be careful with books. They are for reading, not for tearing."

Ben and Mia are sorry. They did not know. They say: "We are sorry, Mom. We wanted to do math. We did not mean to break your book. Can you fix it?"

Mom sighs. She is not happy, but she is not mad anymore. She says: "I can try to fix it. But you have to promise me something. Next time, if you want to do math, ask me first. I can show you how to do math without breaking books. Math can be fun, but you have to respect the books. They are fragile, but they are also valuable. They have many things to teach you."

Ben and Mia nod. They say: "We promise, Mom. We will ask you next time. We will respect the books. We want to learn math. We want to be smart like you."

Mom smiles. She hugs them. She says: "I love you, Ben and Mia. You are smart and curious. You can learn math and many other things. But you have to be gentle and careful. Fragile things can break, but they can also be beautiful and useful."

Once upon a time there was a poor family. The family did not have a lot of money. But they had a lot of love.

One day, the family wanted to build a swing in the garden. The swing needed something strong so it could hang from the tree. They found some metal and decided to use it.

The family worked together and the dad and mum helped the little girl. They all worked really hard. They drilled the metal into the tree and hung the swing.

The swing was a great success. All the family were happy and excited. They played together on the swing until sundown.

The family was glad to have helped each other to make something special.

Tommy loved to climb. He climbed on chairs, on tables, on sofas, on beds. He climbed everywhere he could. His mom always told him to be careful and not to climb on things that could fall or break. But Tommy did not listen. He wanted to climb higher and higher.

One day, Tommy saw a big red button on the wall. It was very high, above a shelf. He wondered what it did. He wanted to press it. He climbed on a chair, then on a table, then on a shelf. He reached for the button. He was almost there.

"Tommy, no!" his mom shouted. She saw him climbing on the shelf. She ran to him. "That button is not for you. It is for the fire alarm. If you press it, it will make a loud noise and the firemen will come. You will be in big trouble."

Tommy did not understand. He thought the button was a toy. He wanted to see what it did. He did not want to be obedient. He pressed the button.

BEEP! BEEP! BEEP! The button made a loud noise. Tommy was scared. He let go of the button and fell off the shelf. He hurt his arm and his leg. He cried.

His mom picked him up and hugged him. She was angry and worried. She checked his arm and his leg. They were not broken, but they had bruises. She put a band-aid on them. She told him he was very naughty and he had to say sorry.

Tommy said sorry. He was sorry for pressing the button. He was sorry for hurting himself. He was sorry for making his mom upset. He learned his lesson. He did not want to climb on things that could fall or break anymore. He wanted to be obedient. He wanted to make his mom happy.

Tom and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food with pots and pans. They also liked to wash the dishes in the sink with soap and water.

"Look, I made a cake!" Tom said, holding up a plate with some bread and jam. "Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Mia said, smiling. She took a bite and said, "Mmm, yummy!"

Tom was happy. He liked to share with his sister. He wanted to make her something else. He looked around and saw a can of beans. He thought beans were useful. They could make soup or salad or pie.

He opened the can with a can opener and poured the beans into a pot. He added some water and salt and stirred with a spoon. He put the pot on the stove and turned on the fire.

"Tom, what are you doing?" Mia asked, curious.

"I'm making bean soup!" Tom said, proud. "Do you want some?"

"No, thank you!" Mia said, making a face. She did not like beans. She thought they were yucky.

Tom did not care. He thought his soup was good. He waited for it to boil. He did not know he had to watch the pot. He went to get some bowls and spoons.

But the pot was too full. The soup bubbled and spilled over. It made a mess on the stove and the floor. It also made a loud noise.

Tom and Mia heard the noise and ran to the kitchen. They saw the soup everywhere. They were scared. They thought they were in trouble.

They started to cry. They did not know what to do.

Mom heard the noise and the crying. She came to the kitchen. She saw the soup everywhere. She was not happy. She was angry.

"Tom, Mia, what did you do?" Mom asked, stern.

"We were playing chefs!" Tom said, sobbing. "I made bean soup!"

"But you made a big mess!" Mom said, frowning. "You should not play with the stove and the fire. It is dangerous. You could get hurt. And you wasted the beans. They are not for playing. They are for eating."

"We're sorry, Mom!" Mia said, sniffling. "We did not mean to make a mess. We did not know the soup would spill."

Mom sighed. She was not angry anymore. She was glad they were not hurt. She hugged them and said, "It's okay. I know you were trying to have fun. But you have to be careful and listen to the rules. The kitchen is not a playground. The stove and the fire are not toys. The beans are not useful for making soup. They are useful for making other things."

"Like what?" Tom asked, curious.

"Like bean burgers or bean dip or bean brownies!" Mom said, smiling. "Do you want to help me make some?"

"Yes, please!" Tom and Mia said, smiling too.

They dried their tears and helped Mom clean up the mess. Then they helped her make some bean burgers and bean dip and bean brownies. They learned how to use the beans in a useful way. They also learned how to use the kitchen in a safe way. They had fun and they ate well. They did not cry anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a car. The car was old and rusty. One day it got so rusty that it rot. The car was sad and angry. 

The car said to a nearby tree, "This is so stupid! I don't want to rot!" 

The tree said, "But that's how cars get when they're old. You need to accept it."

The car replied, "No! I wish I could still drive around like I used to."

The tree shook its leaves sadly. "I know. But life isn't always fair. You will just have to rot and accept your fate."

And that's how the car learned to accept its fate and rot away in peace.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Bob. Bob liked to fly high in the sky. He felt happy and free when he flew. One day, he saw a comb on the ground. It was easy to see because it was very big.

Bob wanted to show the comb to his friend, Sue. So, he picked it up with his beak and flew to Sue's nest. Sue was a bird too. Bob said, "Look, Sue! I found a big comb!" Sue looked at the comb and said, "Wow, that's big! Let's play with it!"

Bob and Sue played with the comb all day. They took turns flying and carrying the comb. They had lots of fun. But then, the comb got stuck in a tree. Bob and Sue tried to get it out, but it was not easy. They pushed and pulled, but the comb would not move.

Bob and Sue were very sad. They could not play with the comb anymore. They had to say goodbye to the comb and fly away. The comb stayed stuck in the tree, and Bob and Sue never saw it again.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lilly. Lilly was a very wealthy girl. She lived in a big white house with her mommy and daddy. Every day she would go out to the garden and pick fresh rice for dinner.

One day, Lilly ran to the garden to finish gathering the rice. She was so happy when she was done, she had finished all the rice. She wanted to share it with everybody in her family.

The next day, she shared the rice with her mommy and daddy and they all enjoyed it. From that day on, Lilly and her family had a delicious dinner of rice every night. 

Lilly loved to pick the rice for her family. She was so proud of her work when she was done. Lilly was the happiest and wealthiest girl around. And she was reminded of it every time she ate her dinner.

One Sunday, a big red dog named Max went for a walk with his friend, a little girl named Lily. They walked and played in the park. Max saw a cat and wanted to play with it. The cat did not want to play with Max and ran away. Max felt sad.

"Max, don't be sad," said Lily. "We can still play together." They played catch and had fun. But then, Max felt a big sneeze coming. "Achoo!" Max sneezed so hard that he blew some leaves off a tree.

"Oh no! I did not want to do that," said Max. The tree was sad because it lost its leaves. Lily had an idea to fix the problem. "Let's pick up the leaves and put them back on the tree," she said.

Max and Lily worked together to put the leaves back on the tree. The tree was happy again. Max, Lily, and the tree played together for the rest of the day. They all had a fun Sunday together.

Once there was a worm who lived in the garden. He was a very persistent worm and would always try to get things done no matter what. One day, he noticed two garden bugs quarelling. He didn't like it. He wanted them to get along and be friends.

He wiggled over to the quarreling bugs and tried to reason with them. "Friends don't quarrel," he said. The bugs looked at him, not understanding the meaning of his words. The worm could see they didn't understand so he tried another way.

He reached out and gave the bugs a gentle hug. He held them tightly in his arms and said, "Friends hug." This time the bugs got the message and hugged each other back. They stopped quarrelling and became friends from that day forward.

The persistent little worm had accomplished his goal, and he was proud. He wiggled off, happy that he had helped the two bugs get along.

John wanted to draw a picture, so he told his mom he needed some paper. She handed him a big piece of white paper, and he sat down to draw. Suddenly, a gorilla appeared in the window! It had an ugly face and was scowling. 

John was scared and started to cry. His mom quickly wiped away his tears and told him not to worry. She said she would get rid of the gorilla. She grabbed a broom from the kitchen, held it high above her head, and chased the gorilla away. 

John felt safe and smiled. He thanked his mom and quickly went back to his drawing. He knew that his mom would always protect him and keep him safe.

Once upon a time, there was a family who liked to play a game. Mom, Dad and their two children, Sarah and John, liked it. It was a hard game, but they kept playing it. 

One day, Sarah and John weren't behaving very nicely. Mom and Dad said they had to stop playing the game if they didn't behave. Sarah and John stopped talking and began to be quieter. 

Mom and Dad were very happy. They continued to play the game and they were very careful to be good. Sarah and John followed the rules of the game and tried very hard to be good. 

Finally, they finished the game. Everyone cheered and clapped and gave each other a big hug. Mom and Dad said they had all done a wonderful job and behaved very well. The family was so proud of themselves. 

They decided to play the game again soon, because it was so much fun. They promised to always behave and have a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to eat apples and would pick them from the tree in her backyard. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and got lost. She didn't know which way to go. 

Lily saw a man walking by and asked him for help. He was compassionate and gave her a compass to help her find her way back home. Lily followed the compass and guessed which way to go. After a while, she found her way back home and was happy to eat her apples again. 

From that day on, Lily always carried a compass with her whenever she went for a walk in the forest. She knew that if she ever got lost again, she could use it to find her way back home.

Once, there was a lucky lady. She was walking through the forest when she heard a loud sound. She came to a clearing and saw a bush shaking. She walked closer and saw a baby bird in the bush, its wings had broken!

Right away, the lucky lady knew what to do. She carefully picked up the baby bird, and she took it home with her. There, she fed it and gave it a warm, cozy bed.

Soon, the baby bird was feeling much better. Its wings were healed and it was able to fly! The lucky lady opened her window and the bird flew away.

The lady felt so happy and lucky. She knew she had saved the bird's life.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Sally. Tom had a very creative idea for the day. He was going to make a turkey. 

Tom said to Sally, "Would you like to help me make a turkey?" Sally agreed and the two of them started gathering the things they needed. 

Tom asked Sally, "What do you think we need for a turkey?" 

Sally replied, "We need some feathers and some glue." So Tom and Sally got some feathers and glue, and set off on their creative mission. 

Tom said, "We need to make a turkey shape". So they got to work cutting the feathers and gluing them to the paper. 

When they were done, they stepped back and admired their work. 

"It looks so good," said Sally. 

"Let's show everybody," said Tom. 

So they ran off to show all of their friends their turkey. Everyone was impressed by their creative work and allowed them to keep it! 

The two friends had so much fun making the turkey and were so happy that all their friends allowed them to keep it. They decided to make a different turkey every week, and each one was more creative than the last!

Billy and Joe were best friends. They loved to play together. 
One day, Billy asked Joe if he wanted to go sliding. Joe was so excited that he couldn't wait!

They ran to the hall, and Billy said, "Look! Our slide is so cool!" 
Joe smiled and said, "Let's go!"

The two boys then grabbed their plastic slide, and quickly slid down the hall. They laughed and clapped as they went down.

When they reached the bottom, Joe said, "That was the best slide ever! Can we do it again?"

Billy smiled and said, "Of course! Let's go!"

It was a beautiful day and the sun was shining. Little Anna was out playing in the garden with her dolls. She ran and laughed and played, happy and content.

Suddenly, she remembered: she had forgotten to water her pine tree! She quickly put down her dolls and ran to the pine tree with the watering can.

"I'm sorry, Pine Tree!" she said. "I forgot to water you today!"
Anna carefully poured water over the roots of the tree and was happy to see it drinking eagerly.

"There, now you'll be nice and healthy", she said, patting the trunk of the tree.

Anna stood back and admired the beautiful pine tree, happy and content again.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom loved to sleep all day long. He did not like to play with his friends. His friends would run and jump, but Tom just wanted to nap in the sun.

One day, Tom found a trumpet. He did not know what it was, so he took it home. Tom tried to play the trumpet, but he was not very good. He made loud and funny sounds. His friends heard the noise and came to see what was going on.

Tom's friends laughed at the funny sounds. They wanted to play too! So, they all took turns playing the trumpet. Tom was not lazy anymore. He loved to play the trumpet with his friends. They played and laughed together every day. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy city. In this city, there lived a family - Mom, Dad and Baby. This family was very happy and excited as they had just moved to this city.

"Welcome to this city, Baby," said Mom.

"It looks so nice," said Dad.

The family started exploring the city. Everywhere they looked, they saw neat stores, nice houses, and gardens filled with flowers.

"I like this place," said Baby.

After a few weeks, the family had settled in the city. Mom and Dad got jobs, Baby went to school and before they knew it, they had turned this new city into their home.

The family was so happy to have settled in the city. Everywhere they went they saw other people who had made this city their home. Each day was filled with smiles and laughter.

The family felt so lucky to have made this wealthy city their new home. They looked forward to many years of happiness living in this city.

Once there was a girl called Amelia. She wanted to find a pet alligator to keep her company. So, she asked her mom if she could have one. Her mother said it was a bad idea, but Amelia was very attractive, and her mom eventually said yes!

Amelia was so excited. She ran out and bought the alligator from the pet store. When she got home, alligator was so happy and she named it Gator.

Gator was so cute and playful. Amelia played with him every day. She loved to take him for walks and she even taught him some tricks. Everyone she showed Gator to thought he was very attractive. 

One day, when Amelia and Gator were out for a walk, some kids asked Amelia about her alligator. Amelia was so proud and she proudly told them all about Gator. She asked them if they wanted to pet him and they all said yes!

Once there was a nosy little box. It was very curious and always wanted to know what was inside of things. One day it saw a huge scale. The scale was very big and had two sides. The nosy box wanted to see what it was for so with a small creaky voice it said 'Hey scale, what are you for?' The scale chuckled and said 'I can weigh things!' The nosy box was excited and thought of all of the things it wanted to weigh. First it tried weighing a teddy bear, but it was too small. Then it tried weighing a big ball, but that was too big. The nosy box was stuck, it didn't know what to weigh! Until it thought of the perfect thing - Candy! The nosy box collected all of the candy it had and put it on the scale. It was so happy to see that the scale could weigh it! From then on, the nosy box was always having fun weighing things.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish who lived in the sea. It was a restless fish, always on the go. One day, the little fish was swimming past a reef. It had never seen this reef before, and the little fish was curious. So, the little fish decided to ask some other fish what it was. A grouper fish answered the little fish and said that the reef was a special kind of coral. The coral provided homes for all the other fish in the sea. The little fish was so excited! It decided to keep exploring the reef and learning more about all its new friends. The reef provided an endless adventure, but the little fish was never too restless - it was happy to take its time and learn something new every day.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food for their dolls and stuffed animals. Lila had a big box of paper and scissors and glue. She wanted to make wraps for her doll, like the ones she saw on TV. Ben had a jar of red sauce and a spoon. He wanted to make spicy food for his teddy bear, like the ones his dad liked.

Lila cut a big piece of paper and folded it like a wrap. She put some pretend cheese and lettuce and tomato inside. She glued the edges together and gave it to her doll. "Here you go, Molly. This is a yummy wrap. You will love it," she said. Ben saw what Lila did and wanted to copy her. He cut a piece of paper and folded it like a wrap. He opened the jar of red sauce and poured some inside. He did not know that the sauce was very spicy and hot. He glued the edges together and gave it to his teddy bear. "Here you go, Ted. This is a spicy wrap. You will love it," he said.

Lila and Ben were happy with their wraps. They decided to try them too. They each took a big bite of their own wrap. Lila smiled and said, "Mmm, this is good. Molly likes it too." Ben screamed and said, "Ow, ow, ow! This is bad. Ted does not like it. It burns my mouth!" He dropped the wrap and ran to the kitchen. He looked for water or milk to drink. He did not see the clock on the wall. He did not know that it was almost time for dinner.

Mom and Dad came home from work. They smelled the red sauce in the living room. They saw the paper and glue and scissors on the floor. They saw the half-eaten wraps on the table. They saw Lila and her doll smiling. They saw Ben and his teddy bear crying. They were not happy. They said, "Lila and Ben, what did you do? You made a big mess. You wasted the paper and the glue and the sauce. You ruined your toys and your appetites. You did not listen to us. We told you not to play with scissors and glue and sauce. We told you to wait for dinner. You are in big trouble. You have to clean up everything. You have to go to bed early. You have to say sorry to each other and to us."

Lila and Ben felt sad and sorry. They did not mean to make a mess. They did not mean to waste the things. They did not mean to hurt each other. They did not mean to disobey their parents. They said, "We are sorry, Mom and Dad. We were just playing. We wanted to make wraps. We did not know the sauce was spicy. We did not know it was time for dinner. We will clean up everything. We will go to bed early. We will be good next time."

Mom and Dad hugged Lila and Ben. They said, "We love you, Lila and Ben. We know you were just playing. We know you did not know the sauce was spicy. We know you did not know it was time for dinner. We are glad you are sorry. We are glad you will clean up everything. We are glad you will go to bed early. We are glad you will be good next time. But you have to be more careful and more respectful. You have to follow the rules and the directions. You have to be safe and smart. You have to be kind and polite. You have to be better chefs and better children."

Lila and Ben nodded and said, "We will, Mom and Dad. We will be more careful and more respectful. We will follow the rules and the directions. We will be safe and smart. We will be kind and polite. We will be better chefs and better children." They cleaned up everything. They went to bed early. They hugged their toys and each other. They said good night and fell asleep. They dreamed of wraps and sauce and time and love. They hoped to have a better day tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a creative little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy plane. He would fly it all around his room and make fun sounds like "zoom" and "whoosh".

One day, Tim's plane got stuck in a tree. He felt sad and didn't know how to get it down. Tim thought and thought, and then he had a creative idea! He would use a long stick to separate the plane from the tree.

Tim found a long stick and carefully poked the plane. The plane wiggled and wobbled, and then it fell down from the tree. Tim was so happy to have his plane back. He played with it all day long and promised to be more careful next time. And that's the end of the story about Tim and his creative idea to separate his plane from the tree.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. Today, they are excited. They want to see the big slide.

"Come on, Lily!" Tom says. "Hurry, hurry! The slide is fun!"

Lily runs after Tom. She is happy. She likes the slide too. But she sees something else. She sees a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a red collar.

"Look, Tom!" Lily says. "A dog! What is its name?"

Tom stops. He looks at the dog. He likes dogs. He wants to pet it. He walks to the dog. He says, "Hello, dog. You are cute. Can I touch you?"

The dog wags its tail. It likes Tom. It licks his face. Tom laughs. He says, "You are friendly. Do you want to play?"

The dog barks. It wants to play. It runs to the slide. It climbs up. It slides down. Tom and Lily are surprised. They clap their hands. They say, "Wow, dog! You are smart. You can slide!"

The dog barks again. It runs to Tom and Lily. It wants them to slide with it. Tom and Lily smile. They say, "Okay, dog. We will slide with you. You are fun. You are our new friend."

Sam was a curious little three-year-old, who loved going on adventures. One day, while walking outside, he noticed a big, gloomy looking door. A chill ran down his spine, but his curiosity was stronger. He tip-toed closer, and peeked inside.

Suddenly, he saw something strange. It was big and white, and had funny long arms and strange long fingers. Sam was a bit scared, until it spoke.

"Don't be afraid," said the skeleton. "My name is Skeleton. I live in this dark, gloomy room, and I'm looking for a friend to play with - someone like you!"

Sam was so excited. "I'll be your friend," he said, shouting and jumping up and down. He couldn't believe he was playing with a skeleton. 

Since then, Sam and Skeleton have been the best of friends. They play every day, and Sam tells him about all his adventures outside. Skeleton loves hearing about them, and since then, his room isn't so gloomy anymore.

Once there was a girl named Jill. She liked to go to the park with her mom. On one sunny day she put on her pants. They were fake pants because her mom had made them for her.

Her mom laughed and said, "That's enough running Jill, why don't you go play on the swings?" Jill said, "Okay!" and went over to the swings. She pretended to be a bird and flew around in circles.

Mark is a boy who likes to draw. He has many colors and papers to make pictures. He draws cars, animals, houses and flowers. He is very happy when he draws.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who was very sad. Her toys were all broken and the things she loved to do weren't fun anymore. Every day she would walk around trying to find something to play with and no one could help her.

The young girl was so thankful for her mom and for staying at home. She was never so happy in her life!

The girl smiled and set the mouse back on the ground. Then, she waved her hands in a big circle and did the same special dance in reverse. The mouse's gray fur returned to its original luster and the little mouse scampered away, grateful for the gift given to her by the little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a yellow bird named Sunny. Sunny loved to fly high in the sky. One day, Sunny saw a race in the park. The race was for all the birds to see who could fly the fastest.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with toys. Lily has a doll and Max has a motorcycle. They share their toys and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He liked to travel. He went to many places and saw different things. One day he wanted to try something new. He decided to travel to a spicy place.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a lot of toys. Ben and Mia run to the truck.

Ben and Mia run to the bench. They want to play with their toys. But then, they see something unusual. On the bench, there is a big teddy bear. The teddy bear has a tag. The tag says, "This is mine. Do not touch."

"Who left this here?" Ben wonders.

"I don't know. Maybe someone forgot it," Mia says.

Ben and Mia look at the teddy bear. They think it is cute. They want to touch it. But they remember the tag. They are scared. They do not want to make someone angry.

"Maybe we should leave it alone," Ben says.

"Maybe we should find the owner," Mia says.

Ben and Mia look around. They do not see anyone. They do not know what to do. They are confused. They hold their toys. They wait.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they found a big tunnel near the park. They wanted to see what was inside, so they decided to test it.

They walked into the tunnel, holding hands. It was dark and cold, but they were not scared. They saw some shiny things on the walls and some funny noises. They thought it was fun.

But then, they heard a loud roar. It was a big bear, and it was angry. It saw Tom and Lily and ran towards them. They were very scared and tried to run away, but the tunnel was too long and the bear was too fast.

The bear caught them and bit them. It hurt a lot and they cried. They wished they never went into the tunnel. They wished they stayed in the park, where it was lovely and safe. But it was too late. The bear ate them up. The end.

Rose was a clumsy 3 year old girl. One day she was playing on the beach when the tide started to come in. She was so busy exploring that she didn't notice the water creeping up towards her.

Just as the tide began to cover her toes, Rose's mom waved to her from the shore. She told her to come back so they could go home. Rose was upset that she had to leave because she valued the fun she was having.

As she walked back to her mom, Rose suddenly felt a wave splash her ankles. She was laughing and smiling because she liked the feeling of the water. Rose knew she had to be careful and value the condition of the sea.

When she reached her mom, Rose said goodbye to the ocean and the warm sand. Even though she was clumsy, Rose enjoyed her time by the beach and valued the experience.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She walked into the garden with her mom and saw a huge pumpkin. She got very excited and wanted it. Her mom said that it was too big and they had to leave it there.

Lucy started to complain, saying it was unfair. She wanted that pumpkin, no matter what. 

Her mom smiled and told her that if she found an even bigger pumpkin, the one she wanted was hers.

Lucy was determined. She looked around the garden and found one that was far bigger. She smiled, thrilled that she had found the bigger pumpkin. 

Her mom was a little envious of Lucy finding a bigger one. She said that she was very proud of her, and that she could have the pumpkin.

Lucy was so happy and hugged her mom with a big smile on her face. She gleefully skipped to the pumpkin and dragged it home with her mom's help.

Sophie and Jack were two friends who loved playing together. But one day, they started to quarrel and soon an argument started. 

Sophie cried and said, "Why are you making me upset?"

Jack replied, "You broke your promise!"

Sophie was very sorry and she said, "I'm sorry. I promise I won't do it again."

Jack also said sorry and they hugged each other. They both realised that it was better to talk it out than to quarrel. From then on, they decided to always keep their promises and never quarrel.

Pete and his mom were in the kitchen. Pete's mom had a bowl full of dough on the counter. "We are going to make cookies, Pete," she said.

Pete touched the dough. It felt rough between his fingers. He didn't like the feeling. "Mom, can we make the dough smooth?" he asked.

His mom smiled. "Yes, Pete. We can use the rolling pin to make the dough smooth. That will improve it."

Pete helped his mom roll out the dough. Together their efforts made the dough nice and smooth.

"We did it!" said Pete happily.

His mom laughed. "Now, let's make some cookies!"

One day, Mrs. Cat had something interesting to study. She found an avocado that was ready to eat! She was so happy because she hadn't eaten an avocado for a long time.

Mrs. Cat studied the avocado carefully and smelled it. It smelled so good! She decided to cut it in half and eat it. Mrs. Cat was feeling guilty because she didn't want to share it with her friends.

So Mrs. Cat ate the whole avocado and enjoyed it very much. She felt a little guilty, but she was so happy that she had eaten it all. When it was gone she felt guilty again, so she decided she would share next time!

Jill had a motor. It went vroom, vroom very loud. She liked it a lot.

One day, her mom said, "Let's take your motor to the park." Jill smiled.

At the park, they had a big hill. It was soft and green. Jill's mom said, "Let's go down the hill."

So they did! Jill felt the wind in her hair and laughed. She was so happy.

Finally, they got to the bottom of the hill. Jill felt brave and strong. She said, "Mom, let's do it again!" And so they did!

Molly and Jake had their birthday parties at the same time. They were both turning three years old and had invited all their friends over to celebrate. The party was a blast and everyone had a lot of fun. 

At the party, Molly noticed how envious Jake was of her special bouncy castle. She wanted to make Jake feel better, so she asked if anyone wanted to come and play with her in the bouncy castle. All of the kids eagerly said yes and went to play with Molly. 

To remind Jake of all the fun they had had, Molly gave each of her friends a small toy from the bouncy castle as a party favor. All the kids loved the tokens and thanked Molly. 

Jake smiled and thanked Molly too. He was happy that Molly had remembered him and had been so sweet to share the bouncy castle with her friends. He was definitely having the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little mouse who lived in a cozy hole in the wall. One day, he decided to go outside to meet new friends. As he was walking, he saw a big cat who wanted to eat him. The mouse ran as fast as he could and found a friendly bird. 

The bird saw that the mouse had a big stitch on his tail and offered to help him. She used her beak to carefully remove the stitch and the mouse felt much better. The mouse and the bird became good friends and played together every day. 

From then on, the mouse was no longer alone and he was very happy. He learned that it was important to be brave and to meet new friends, even if you are poor.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat blueberries. One day, she went for a walk in the forest and found an ancient tree. The tree was very big and had lots of branches. Lily climbed up the tree and found lots of blueberries. She picked them all and put them in her basket. 

Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily was getting wet, so she used her basket to cover her head. She climbed down the tree and ran home. When she got home, she made a blueberry pie with all the blueberries she had picked. It was delicious! From that day on, Lily went back to the ancient tree every week to pick more blueberries and make more pies.

Tom was a mechanic who liked to fix cars. He had a big garage with many tools and parts. He worked hard every day and helped many people with their car problems.

One day, a lady came to his garage with a red car. She said her car was making a loud noise and asked Tom to check it. Tom opened the hood of the car and saw a broken belt. He told the lady he could fix it, but it would cost some money. The lady said she did not have much money and asked Tom to lower the price. Tom said no, he had to charge the fair amount for his work.

The lady was angry and said Tom was greedy and mean. She said she would find another mechanic who would do it for less. She drove away in her noisy car, leaving Tom feeling bitter and sad.

The next day, Tom heard a loud crash outside his garage. He ran out and saw the red car smashed into a tree. The lady was hurt and bleeding. Tom called for help and ran to the lady. He asked her what happened. She said her car broke down and she lost control. She said she was sorry for being rude to Tom and wished she had listened to him.

Tom felt sorry for the lady and helped her until the ambulance came. He told her he forgave her and hoped she would get better soon. He learned that being bitter and angry did not help anyone. He decided to be more kind and patient with his customers, even if they were not nice to him. He realized that being a good mechanic was not only about fixing cars, but also about caring for people.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their new rug. The rug has many colors and shapes. They can make pretend roads and houses on the rug.

One day, Tom wants to whistle. He tries to blow air from his mouth, but he cannot make a sound. He sees Sam whistling and he gets angry. He says, "Stop whistling! You are too loud! I want to whistle too!"

Sam says, "I can whistle because I am older. You are too young. You need to practice more. Whistling is fun!"

Tom does not like what Sam says. He thinks Sam is mean. He grabs the rug and pulls it. Sam holds the other end of the rug and pulls it back. They start to fight over the rug. They make a lot of noise.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Tom and Sam fighting over the rug. She says, "Stop fighting! You are both naughty! You need to share the rug and play nicely. Whistling is not a problem, but fighting is. Say sorry to each other and hug."

Tom and Sam feel sorry for what they did. They say sorry to each other and hug. They also say sorry to Mom and hug her. They decide to share the rug and play nicely. They take turns whistling and listening. They have fun with their new rug.

Once upon a time, there was a cabin in the woods. It was a very old cabin, but Jack liked it. He was a little boy who lived alone in the cabin with his puppy.

One day, Jack was very confused; he could smell something strange. It wasn't his puppy's food, it was something else. So, he followed his nose and went to the back of the cabin.

When Jack got to the back of the cabin, he saw smoke! The cabin had caught fire. It was burning so fast; he couldn't do anything to put it out.

Jack tried to run into the cabin, but it was already too late. He shouted out to his puppy, but it was too scared to come out. He cried, "My puppy's still inside! Help me!"

But no one came. Jack was alone, confused and scared. His cabin burned to the ground until nothing remained. Jack and his puppy were both gone forever.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lisa wanted to find a rainbow. She excitedly asked her mom if they could go look for one. Her mom mentioned that it was dangerous to go out without an umbrella because of the rain. Lisa thought for a moment and then smiled. She remembered that she had seen a big rainbow in the sky the last time it had rained. 

The next time it rained, Lisa eagerly waited for the rainbow to appear. Sure enough, the sky began to light up and a rainbow formed! It was so beautiful, with all its different colors stretching across the sky. Lisa was mesmerized.

Suddenly, the weather got too rough and the wind started blowing hard. Lisa's mom shouted to her that it was dangerous and they had to go inside. Lisa didn't want to leave, but her mom said it was time to go. And so, Lisa looked at the rainbow one last time and ran inside.

There were two friends, Jack and James, who liked to play together. Every Sunday they went to the park together. One Sunday, Jack was feeling a bit lonely because James didn't appear. He waited and waited, but he still didn't show up. 

Jack was angry and started to walk home by himself. Suddenly, James appeared from behind the trees, carrying a big balloon for Jack! Jack was so happy and he gave his friend a big hug. 

But when he asked why he was late, James said it was because he had found the balloon first and he wanted it for himself. Jack thought this was selfish, but he was happy that his friend had still shared the balloon with him. He and James laughed as they continued to play in the park.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to travel. One day she went on a journey with her family. First they went on the road in their car. The road was so long and the scenery was so pretty!

Eventually they arrived at their destination. The little girl was so excited! Everywhere she looked she saw friendly faces. Everyone was so nice!

The little girl and her family kept on traveling until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to all their new friends, waved to everyone and started off on the road again. 

As they drove along, the little girl thought about all the fun she had on her journey. She had made so many new friends and felt very happy. The sunset in the background only made the journey even more special. 

Finally they arrived home safely. The little girl was sad to be back, but she was also content after such a fun travel adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She wanted to go on an adventure and so she packed a bag with her favourite things. She got ready and set off on a trip.

Along the way, she found a cave. It was dark so she lit a candle and its light made the cave walls glow. Lucy was so excited! The cave was full of secret treasures and wonderful things. She found long strings of colourful beads and tasty spices that were spicy. 

Before long, the cave started to get dark again. Lucy was scared so she decided to take some of the beads and the spices home with her in her bag. 

When Lucy got home, she showed her mum the treasures she had found. The light from the beads made their home look beautiful - just like the cave had before!

The end.

Once upon a time there was an old man who loved woodwork. Every day he would go to the forest to collect lumber. One day, he made a request to the forest. He said "Please give me some lumber to make a chair!"

Suddenly, a giant tree started shaking. Everyone was surprised! Out of the tree, an old, wise owl appeared and said, "If you make me a chair with the lumber, I will give you as much as you need."

The old man was so happy. He thanked the owl and went to get the lumber. He soon made a beautiful chair out of the lumber.

The old man went back to the tree and showed it to the owl. The owl thanked the old man and said, "Now I have a comfy place to sleep and see the stars at night."

The old man and the owl were so happy. The old man thanked the owl for his generosity and went home with a big smile on his face!

Once upon a time there was a helpless truck. It was stuck at the bottom of a steep hill. The truck tried and tried to get back up the hill, but nothing it did made any difference. 

Suddenly, the truck saw a big number leaning against the hill. It decided to lean on it too. Little by little, the truck was able to lean on the number and inch its way up the hill.

The truck was very relieved. Before long, it had made it to the top of the hill and drove away happily. From then on, the truck leaned on the number whenever it needed a helping hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park with her friends. One day, she saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She climbed up the ladder and slid down the slide. It was so much fun!

The next day, Lily went to her classroom. Her teacher showed her a new toy. It was a flexible ball that could stretch and bounce. Lily loved it and showed it to her friend, Tom.

Tom said, "Wow, that's so cool! Can I play with it too?"

Lily replied, "Sure, let's play together!" They played with the flexible ball and had so much fun. They laughed and giggled in the classroom all day long.

Jill was walking in the park when she saw a big hill. She wanted to jump up the hill. She ran and jumped as high as she could, but she couldn't get to the top. She tried a few more times, but still couldn't reach the top. She was getting tired, so she sat down.

Then, she had an idea. She started to walk up the hill, one step at a time. It was easy, and she was making steady progress. Soon, she reached the top of the hill and she was so happy. She stood at the top and looked all around. She could even see far away.

Jill was so proud of herself. She had worked hard and made it to the top of the hill. She jumped up and down in celebration. She knew she could do anything if she tried hard enough.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant boy named Bobby. Bobby loved to explore and have adventures. One day Bobby got an exciting idea. He wanted to see what the inside of a jail was like. So Bobby set off on his adventure to find a real jail. 

Unfortunately Bobby soon came to a big delay. It was a river he had to cross to get to the jail but there was no bridge. Bobby thought and thought about what he should do, but nothing seemed to work. Then he had an idea. He made a boat out of some wooden planks and sailed across the river.

Soon enough Bobby reached the jail. He was so excited to explore! He couldn't believe his brilliant idea had worked so well! Bobby wandered around the jail, peeking in all the rooms. He even said hello to the prisoners. Everyone was so happy to meet him.

Finally after lots of exploring, Bobby decided it was time to go home. He said goodbye to everyone and made his way back across the river in his boat. Bobby had such an exciting adventure that day and he was so proud of himself for being so brilliant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to talk and play with her friends, but one day she met a boy who spoke a different language. Lily didn't understand what the boy was saying and felt sad because she couldn't talk to him.

Lily's mommy told her that everyone speaks a different language, but that doesn't mean they can't be friends. Lily didn't want to be stupid, so she decided to learn the boy's language. She practiced every day and soon she could understand him.

One day, Lily and the boy were playing when another kid came up and said mean things about the boy's language. Lily stood up for her friend and told the mean kid that it's not stupid to speak a different language. The mean kid felt bad and apologized.

From that day on, Lily and her friend played together every day, and Lily felt proud that she could understand his language. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jenny and John. They always played together. 
One day, they were playing and Jenny said, "I want to try something". 
John asked, "What is that?" 
Jenny smiled, held up her hand and said, "Let's do a zip!" 
John knew his friend was asking him to kiss her, so he said, "OK".
John leaned in and kissed Jenny on the cheek. 
Jenny was so happy! She smiled and said, "Thank you."
But suddenly, John felt a bit embarrassed and he said, "Sorry". 
Jenny laughed and said, "It's alright. That was fun!" 
They hugged each other and Jenny said, "Let's do it again!" 
John couldn't help but smile and the two friends kissed again.

Once there was a wise old lady. One day she went outside her house and saw a board lying in the grass. She seemed to think it was a special board. She took it inside and put it in the corner of her living room.

The next day when the old lady awoke, the board seemed to be glowing. She was so excited. She picked up the board and walked outside. She shouted, "This board is magical!"

The old lady soon found out what the board could do. When she held it up high and sang, wonderful music seemed to play from it. The old lady was so happy and sang all day.

The old lady was wise and she knew it was important to share this special board with others. So she decided to let all the kids in the neighbourhood play with the board. They sang and danced to the magical music. Soon everyone was having fun!

The old lady and the kids smiled at each other. It seemed like the magical board brought them all together. They shared many stories and laughed a lot. It was a happy day!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Millie. Millie loved playing outside in the sun, and she often went to the beach to explore the shore.

Today, Millie went to the beach to look around. She was so excited that she wanted to take a big dive into the ocean. But when she looked down into the water, it looked so quiet. Millie was scared of the deep water, so she held her hands tight and couldn't move.

Suddenly, she saw her mom coming. "Why don't you go for a dive?" her mom said. Millie shook her head, scared of what might happen. "Come on sweetheart," her mom said. "It's ok to be scared, but you can try it. I'll be watching you."

Millie thought about it and slowly stepped into the water. She felt the warm water on her feet, but she was still frightened. She took a deep breath, then shouted, "I'm going for a dive!"

She gathered all her courage and jumped into the deep water. She felt scared at first, but soon the fear was replaced by a feeling of joy. Millie was so happy that she had been brave enough to go for a dive. She floated in the water and waved her hands in the air.

The sun was setting and the beach had become quiet. Millie knew that it was time to go home, but she was

Lily and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a man selling balloons of many colors. Lily wanted a pink balloon and Ben wanted a blue one. Mom gave them some money and they ran to the man.

"Can we have a balloon, please?" Lily asked.

"Sure, here you go. One pink and one blue balloon for you," the man said. He tied the balloons to their wrists and smiled.

"Thank you!" Lily and Ben said. They were very happy with their balloons. They waved them in the air and ran around the park.

But then, Ben saw a huge slide. He wanted to go on it. He forgot about his balloon and ran to the slide. He climbed up the ladder and slid down. He had fun, but when he looked at his wrist, he saw that his balloon was gone. He had dropped it when he climbed the ladder. He felt sad and cried.

"Ben, what's wrong?" Lily asked. She saw him crying and ran to him.

"I lost my balloon. I dropped it when I went on the slide. I can't find it," Ben said.

"Oh, Ben, I'm sorry. That's too bad. Do you want to share my balloon with me?" Lily asked. She held out her pink balloon to him.

"Really? You would share your balloon with me?" Ben asked.

"Of course. You are my brother and I love you. We can both play with the pink balloon. It's okay if it's not blue," Lily said.

Ben smiled and hugged Lily. He took the pink balloon and thanked her. They played with the balloon together and had fun. Mom saw them and was proud of them.

The moral of the story is: It's good to share with others, especially when they are sad. Balloons are fun, but they can fly away. Family and friends are more important.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swing on the playground. One day, she saw her friend Billy cutting a piece of paper with scissors. 

"Hi Billy! What are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I'm making a paper airplane," replied Billy.

Lily watched as Billy cut the paper. Suddenly, he accidentally cut his finger because he was being careless. 

"Ouch!" cried Billy.

Lily ran to get help from the teacher. The teacher put a bandage on Billy's finger and told him to be more careful next time. From that day on, Lily and Billy always made sure to be extra careful when using scissors. And they continued to swing on the playground every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Blue. Blue liked to fly high in the sky and feel the wind in her feathers. One day, Blue saw a beautiful blouse hanging on a clothesline. She wanted to fly down and take a closer look, but there was a big, mean cat guarding it. Blue was scared and felt miserable.

Blue didn't want to give up on the blouse, so she came up with a plan. She flew up high and then dove down towards the cat, causing it to run away in fear. Blue quickly grabbed the blouse and flew back up to the safety of the sky. She felt happy and proud of herself for being brave and successful in her mission.

From that day on, Blue flew around with the blouse in her beak, showing it off to all her bird friends. They were all impressed and congratulated her on her bravery. Blue felt happy and content knowing that she had overcome her fear and accomplished her goal.

Once upon a time, there was a big boy who had a watch. The watch was very special because it made him feel like he could do anything.

One day, the boy wanted to try and do something special, so he used his watch to try and succeed. He worked very hard, and soon he had a plan.

He thought his plan was very clever, but it wasn't working very well. He tried and he tried, but the plan still didn't work. The boy was very sad and sour.

But then, something amazing happened. Suddenly, his plan started to work, and he was really happy. He had done it - he had finally succeeded!

The boy was so proud of himself, and he kept his watch close to him as a reminder of what he had achieved. He had worked so hard and he was so happy that he had succeeded.
