Once upon a time, there was a band. This band liked to organize and do fun things. They liked to sing, dance, and play.

One day the band wanted to get organized. So they did. The band leader was careful and told them what to do. Everyone worked together to get organized.

Everyone was careful to do the right thing. They practiced their dances, sang together, and played their instruments. They all worked together to get organized.

The band was ready. They were so organized. They were ready to show everyone their neat and organized band. Everyone in the band was so proud. They were ready to put on a show and be the best band ever!

Lily and Ben love to play with their toy train. They have a big track with hills and bridges and tunnels. They make the train go fast and slow and make noises like choo-choo and beep-beep.

One day, Lily and Ben have a fight. Lily wants to make the train go fast, but Ben wants to make it go slow. They pull and tug at the train and shout at each other.

"Let go, Lily! It's my turn to make it slow!" Ben says.

"No, Ben! It's my turn to make it fast!" Lily says.

They are so angry that they don't see their dog, Spot, coming. Spot likes to bite things. He sees the train and thinks it is a bone. He jumps and bites the train. He breaks it in half.

Lily and Ben stop fighting. They look at the train and cry. They are very sad. They hug each other and say sorry.

"Spot, bad dog! You bit our train!" Lily says.

"Spot, no bite! You made our train broken!" Ben says.

Spot looks at them and wags his tail. He doesn't understand why they are mad. He thinks he was playing. He licks their faces and tries to make them happy.

Lily and Ben smile. They forgive Spot. They decide to share their toys and play nicely. They find some glue and fix their train. They make it go fast and slow and make noises like choo-choo and beep-beep. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a princess named Daisy. Daisy was very tidy, and loved to keep her room clean and neat. One day, she had a big problem-- her favourite coin was stuck in the drain! She asked her mom for help, but mom said she couldn't help. Daisy's mom said, "Your coin is too far down the drain. We have to prevent it from going any further." 

Daisy was sad and asked her mom, "What can I do?"
Mom thought for a moment, then she had an idea. She said, "You can get some sticky tape and put it over the drain. That will prevent the coin from going down."

Daisy got up right away and gathered some tape. She carefully put it over the drain so it was all secure. Then she reached down the drain and grabbed her precious coin!

Daisy was so happy and thanked her mom for her help. Her tidy room was complete again. The princess and her coin lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park every day with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends decided to go on an adventure. They walked and walked until they found a beautiful landscape with trees and flowers.

Lily's friend, Timmy, said, "This place is perfect for a picnic!" So, they all sat down and had a yummy lunch. After they finished eating, they played games and had fun.

Suddenly, the sky turned dark and it started to rain. Everyone was sad because they didn't want to leave the beautiful landscape. But then, Lily had an idea. She said, "Let's build a fort with the blankets we brought for the picnic!" They all helped to build the fort and soon they were all settled inside, cozy and dry. Lily's idea saved the day and they all had a great time in the end.

One day, Jenny was looking out of her window when she saw something red in the sky. She ran outside to take a closer look and saw a beautiful red bird. She was amazed at how pretty it was and admired it for a few minutes.

The bird suddenly flew down to the ground and landed in a small pocket. Jenny carefully approached it. She opened her pocket and the bird hopped straight inside. She was so excited and smiled to herself. 

Jenny took the bird to the park and admired it as it flew around in the bright sunshine. Every time it came back to the pocket, she couldn't stop smiling. 

At the end of the day, Jenny carefully carried the bird home. She gave it some food and watched it explore its new home. She always felt happy when she admired the bird in its bright red feathers.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to sleep. She yawned every morning, for she was so tired. Every day, she dreamed of a beautiful soft image. It was so calm and peaceful.

One day, she decided to try to find this image. She went looking all around the house, but couldn't seem to find it. She yawned, so sleepy that she could barely keep her eyes open. But she was determined to find the image! 

So she searched high and low. Finally, she fell asleep in her bed. And guess what she saw when she woke up? All around her bed there was a soft image just like she had imagined! The little girl smiled, for she could finally look at the image she had been dreaming of. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Hannah. She was three years old, and she loved to play with her toys. One day, her mom said she had something special for her.

Hannah was so excited! Her mom showed her a new uniform and said she was going to join a rich school. Hannah was excited, but then the mom said there was a delay.

At first, Hannah was worried no one would play with her? But then her mom said the delay was just for a few days. In the meantime, she could play with her friends, just like always.

Finally, the delay was over and Hannah was ready to go to school. All dressed up in her new uniform, she said goodbye to her mom with a big smile on her face.

Hannah had a great time at her new rich school. She met lots of new friends and enjoyed playing with them every day. From then on, she wore her new uniform with pride and thanked her mom for giving her this fantastic opportunity. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a smart little boy named Seth. He had a lamp which was his best friend. 

One day, Seth noticed that the lamp was making funny noises and that its bulb was flickering. He asked his mom, "What's wrong with my lamp?"
She explained, "I think the bulb needs to be changed. That's why it's making those strange sounds." 

Seth didn't know what to do so he decided to lock the lamp. He thought that maybe that would make it stop making the noises and make the bulb stop flickering. But Seth didn't realize that by locking the lamp he had made it worse.

The bulbe was working more than it should and soon it overheated and made a loud popping noise. Smoke came out of the lamp and the bulb had cracked.

Seth was so sad that he had locked the lamp. He had wanted to help it, but instead he had made it worse. He had to throw the lamp away and get a new one which made him feel very sad. 

The moral of the story is: never lock something when you don't know what you're doing, or the results can be very bad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and see all the pretty flowers. One day, she saw a mysterious box on the sidewalk. She wondered what was inside. 

Lily decided to trade her favorite toy for the mysterious box. When she opened it, she saw a beautiful necklace with a shiny diamond. She was so happy! 

But then, Lily realized that the necklace belonged to her neighbor. She felt bad for trading for something that wasn't hers. So, she went to her neighbor and gave back the necklace. Her neighbor was happy and gave Lily a big hug. 

From that day on, Lily learned that it's not good to trade for things that don't belong to you. She continued to see all the pretty flowers outside and played with her favorite toy.

Alice was playing in the sandpit when she noticed something strange. There was a figure in the sand that seemed to be trying to talk to her. Alice went closer and saw that it was a little girl. The girl was deaf and didn't have any friends. Alice smiled and offered a hand. The two held hands and Alice noticed that the girl was smiling too. They became best friends and Alice even learnt some sign language from her. When the bell rung, they said goodbye and Alice promised to come back again the next day.

Sam likes to bounce. He has a big ball that he can bounce on the grass. He also has a small ball that he can bounce on the floor. But his favorite thing to bounce is a tube.

A tube is a long and round thing that has air inside. Sam's dad gave him a tube that is red and blue. Sam can blow air into the tube to make it bigger or let air out to make it smaller. He can also twist the tube to make different shapes.

One day, Sam decided to bounce his tube on the bed. He put the tube on the bed and jumped on it. The tube bounced up and down with him. It was fun. But then, the tube bounced too high and hit the lamp. The lamp fell down and broke. Sam heard a loud noise and saw glass on the floor.

Sam was scared. He knew he did a bad thing. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. His mom was not happy. She told him to never bounce his tube on the bed again. She also told him to be careful with the glass and to help her clean it up.

Sam felt sorry. He said he was sorry to his mom and to his dad. He helped them clean the glass and fix the lamp. He also hugged his tube and said he was sorry to it. He promised to only bounce his tube on the grass or on the floor. His mom and dad forgave him. They told him they still loved him and that he was a good boy. Sam was happy. He still liked to bounce, but he learned to bounce safely.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a big cube in his toy box. It was red and shiny. He picked it up and it was heavy. Timmy wondered how much it weighed. 

Later that day, Timmy's mom made him a sandwich for lunch. But when he took a bite, he made a face. The sandwich tasted bad! Timmy didn't like it at all. 

After lunch, Timmy went back to playing with his toys. He decided to weigh the cube with his toy scale. It was very heavy! Timmy was surprised. He played with the cube for a while longer, but then he got bored. He put it back in his toy box and went to play outside.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved animals and wanted to go on a safari. He was very hungry and wanted to eat something before he went. He asked his mom for a snack.

His mom gave him a banana and mentioned that he would see lots of animals on the safari. Timmy was excited and ate his banana quickly. He went on the safari with his family and saw many animals like lions, zebras, and elephants. Timmy was very happy and couldn't wait to go on another safari.

Lily was a big girl who liked to do things by herself. She was independent and did not need help from anyone. One day, she wanted to make a cake for her mom's birthday. She found a recipe book and some ingredients in the kitchen. She did not ask her dad or her brother for help, because she thought she knew everything.

She mixed the flour, the eggs, the sugar, and the butter in a big bowl. She poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. She did not check the time or the temperature, because she thought she was smart. She went to play with her toys and waited for the cake to be ready.

After a while, she smelled something burning. She ran to the kitchen and saw smoke coming out of the oven. She opened the door and saw a black and hard cake. She was scared and sad. She did not know what to do. She heard her dad and her brother coming home. She did not want them to see her mistake. She grabbed a towel and covered the cake with it. She hoped they would not notice.

"Hi, Lily, what are you doing?" her dad asked as he entered the kitchen.

"Nothing, dad, just playing," Lily said, trying to act normal.

"What's that smell?" her brother asked, sniffing the air.

"Nothing, brother, just the oven," Lily said, lying.

They looked at her and saw the towel on the counter. They were curious and lifted the towel. They saw the burnt cake and gasped.

"Lily, what is this?" her dad asked, surprised.

Lily felt ashamed and started to cry. She told them the truth. She said she wanted to make a cake for mom, but she did not ask for help, and she did not follow the recipe, and she ruined everything.

Her dad and her brother hugged her and comforted her. They told her they were proud of her for trying, but they also told her she should have asked for help. They said baking a cake was not easy, and they could have helped her if she had told them. They said it was okay to make mistakes, but it was not okay to hide them. They said they loved her no matter what.

Lily learned a lesson that day. She learned that being independent was good, but being honest and asking for help was better. She learned that covering her mistakes did not make them go away, but only made them worse. She learned that silence was not always golden, but sometimes it was better to speak up and admit her faults. She apologized to her dad and her brother, and they forgave her. They decided to make a new cake together, and they had fun. They surprised their mom with the cake, and she was happy. Lily was happy too, and she thanked her dad and her brother for their help. She realized that sometimes, two or three heads were better than one.

Billy was a curious toddler. He wanted to try all kinds of things. One day he stepped out of the house and he was greeted by a delicious smell. He followed the smell and came to a riverbank. On the river bank he saw a lady with a big pot, stirring something with a huge spoon. 

Billy walked up to her.

"What are you cooking?" he asked.

"I'm making jam!" the lady smiled.
"Can I have a taste?"

The lady nodded and scooped up some of the thick mixture with her spoon. She showed it to Billy. He put his mouth to the spoon and the taste was so sweet.

"Mmmm," said Billy. "Can I have more please?".

The lady smiled, and gave him more of her delicious jam.

Billy went back home with a smile on his face, tummy full of sweet jam!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jake. Jake was always a very cheerful and careless kid. One day, Jake went on an adventure with his family. They went to a far away landscape.

The landscape was so beautiful! Jake couldn't believe his eyes. Everywhere he looked, there were lush fields of green and pretty blue skies. But Jake's favorite part of the landscape was the big lake.

"Let's go swimming!" Jake said, a bit too casually. Everyone started to laugh, because they knew Jake couldn't swim! But Jake didn't know why they were laughing, until his dad began to joke. His dad said, "Maybe it's too late to learn now... you should've started earlier!"

Jake just smiled, even though he didn't understand the joke. He just continued to admire the beautiful landscape and had a lot of fun.

One day, a fox was wandering through the forest. The fox moved quickly and gracefully, her playful spirit showing in her every step. All of a sudden, she saw a small rabbit ahead. The rabbit immediately seemed scared and ran away.

The fox was surprised, for she had no intention of scaring away the rabbit. She wanted to make friends!
The fox chased after the rabbit and called out, "Don't be scared! I just want to be your friend."

The rabbit stopped and looked back. It crept back slowly, not sure if it could trust the fox.

The fox declared firmly, "I won't ever hurt you. I promise!"

The rabbit hesitated, but felt that it could trust the fox. They became friends and played together all day.

The moral of the story is that if you are kind and trustworthy, you will make good friends.

Molly got up early one morning. It was still very dark outside but she was filled with excitement. She went to the window and opened it. The mild morning air filled her room and a bright sun was just beginning to appear on the horizon.

Molly could hear chirping birds, and the fresh smell of grass and flowers filled the air. She stood there for a moment and smiled. Then she quickly put on her shoes and ran outside to explore.

Molly ran around the garden, picking flowers, chasing butterflies and catching bugs. After an hour of play, Molly was tired. She nestled herself in a warm spot underneath a big tree and rested.

The sun began to warm the ground and lulled Molly to sleep. When she woke up, it was late afternoon. Molly felt refreshed and happy after her mid-morning nap. She smiled and ran inside to tell her mom all about her adventure.

It was a sunny day and John and his mom were going on a cottage holiday. The cottage was hidden in a beautiful forest and they were excited to stay there. As they were out walking one day in the forest, John and mom saw a cozy log cabin. It looked like the perfect spot to explore so they decided to take a closer look. 

John ran up to the door and noticed it was locked. "Mom, can we open it?". 

"No," she said. "You know it's not polite to just open someone's door. Besides, it looks like it's been many years since anyone was here. It's best if we leave it alone."
 
John still wanted to know what was inside so he pleaded with mom. John became very sill, until he started to cry.

His mom finally gave in and said, "Alright, but be careful". She grabbed a large tree branch, used it to pry open the cabin door, and it split in half! 

John was so happy. He rushed inside to explore. However, as soon as he stepped inside he began to hear strange creaking and cracking noises. He quickly ran back to his mom, scared. 

"John, look up," said mom. To their horror, the cabin was starting to split apart! They ran away fast, but sadly, the cabin was completely destroyed.

John and his mom had to leave

Once upon a time there was a jolly avocado named John. John was always eager to learn new things, but he never seemed to have time. One day, he decided to take a break from all of his learning and have some fun.

He plucked a ripe avocado from one of the tall trees nearby and started to play with it. He laughed as he rolled it back and forth, like a ball.

John was so focused on his play that he didn't notice at first, but he was actually learning something too. He was becoming more expert at recognizing ripe avocados. All of that practice was making him ever jollier.

Eventually, John found a whole day to dedicate to his learning. He was really excited and made sure the ripe avocado was fed and watered while he was gone. When he came back, he was filled with knowledge.

John and the avocado shared many jolly days together afterwards, laughing, playing and learning.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys. One day, she found a bottle of lotion in her mom's room. The bottle was open.

Lily put some lotion on her hands. She rubbed her hands together and something magical happened. Her hands started to vanish! Lily was surprised and a little scared.

She ran to her mom and showed her the vanishing hands. Her mom knew what to do. She took the open bottle of lotion and put some on Lily's hands again. Just like that, Lily's hands were back! They hugged each other and laughed. From that day on, Lily knew that the open bottle of lotion was magical.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she was in her bed with her favorite blanket. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and got scared. She wanted to call her mom, but she was too scared to move. 

Then, Lily saw her mom come into the room and she smiled at her. Her mom gave her a big hug and tucked her in with her cozy blanket. Lily felt safe and warm with her mom and blanket. She smiled and fell asleep, knowing her mom was there to protect her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Alice. She was three years old and very obedient. 
One day, her parents took her to the beach. As they strolled along the shore, Alice spotted something shiny in the sand. She ran over to a spot and started to dig. 
She pulled out a silver key! She jumped up and down and shouted, "I've found a key!". 
Her parents laughed and asked her what she thought the key unlocked. 
Alice considered this and frowned. She then smiled and said, "Maybe it unlocks an adventure!" 
Her parents smiled and hugged her. They then all started out together, determined to discover the secret of the silver key.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, they decided to play on a big board. Timmy was very excited because he had never played on a board before.

As they played, Timmy noticed that one of his friends would always peek when they were hiding. Timmy didn't think that was fair, so he told his friend that it wasn't nice to peek. His friend apologized and promised not to peek again.

The game continued and Timmy's friend didn't peek anymore. Timmy felt mighty proud of himself for standing up for what was right. From that day on, they all played fair and had a great time on the board. The moral of the story is that it's important to play fair and be honest with your friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Squeaky. Squeaky loved to play with his friend, Tiny the bird. One day, they found an interesting acorn. It was big and shiny. They both wanted the acorn, but there was only one.

Squeaky and Tiny did not know what to do. They both wanted the acorn very much. They thought and thought. Then, they had an idea. They would share the acorn. Squeaky would keep it in the morning, and Tiny would keep it at night.

Squeaky and Tiny were happy with their plan. They hugged each other and played together with the interesting acorn. They learned that sharing made them both happy. And they stayed best friends forever.

Once there was an oak tree. It was very strong, but the days had been so dry that the tree started to look weak.

One day, a little bird was sitting on its branches. The bird was so small and happy. She looked at the tree and said "you will be strong again". The little bird wanted the tree to be strong and hopeful.

The bird hopped down from the tree, and as she was flying away, she said "don't give up! Hope!"

The little bird made the tree smile. With a little hope, the tree started to get stronger. The days were still dry, but the tree continued to hope.

Soon enough, the rains came and the tree was strong again. Everywhere the bird went, she spread the message to hope. 

The little bird reminded the tree that hope can make anything possible, no matter how dry the days may seem.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and write in her journal. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean her room. 

Lily said, "But mom, my room is already tidy!" 

Her mom replied, "I know, but can you please step on the toys and put them away?" 

Lily giggled and said, "Okay, mom!" She stepped on the toys and put them away in their proper place. 

After she was done, Lily went back to her journal and drew a picture of her clean and tidy room. She showed her mom and said, "Look, mom! My room is so pretty now!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Good job, Lily! Your room looks great!"

Once upon a time there was an ordinary dragon. He lived alone in a cave. Every night, he flew around the forest looking for food.

One day, while flying around the forest, he saw something shiny in a tree. He chose to keep it, so he flew back to his cave and put it away safely.

The next morning, the dragon was surprised to find that the shiny object was actually an egg. He decided to keep the egg and take care of it.

Suddenly one day, a small baby dragon hatched from the egg. The ordinary dragon kept the baby dragon safe and protected him from danger.

The ordinary dragon and the baby dragon were now best friends. They flew together, ate together and kept each other safe. They were happy together and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the wild with her friends. One day, Lily's mom went to the store and forgot her phone at home. When she came back, she realized she needed her phone to call her friend. 

Lily saw her mom looking for her phone and asked, "Mommy, what's wrong?" Her mom said, "I need my phone to call my friend, but I can't find it." Lily remembered seeing her mom's phone on the table earlier, so she ran inside and grabbed it for her.

Her mom was so happy and said, "Thank you, Lily! You're so helpful!" Lily felt proud of herself for being able to help her mom. They both went outside to play in the wild with Lily's friends. They had so much fun playing and laughing together. From that day on, Lily always made sure to keep an eye out for her mom's phone.

Mama and Papa were very happy because they had a new baby. Mama took care of the baby and Papa got food for him.

One day, Mama asked Papa, "What should we give the baby for breakfast?"

Papa said, "Let's give him some cereal. It's reliable and it will fit his little tummy."

Mama smiled and said, "That's a great idea. We can give him cereal every morning and he'll be so happy!"

So, from then on, the baby had cereal for breakfast every morning. He liked it so much that he always asked for more.

Mama smiled and said, "It looks like the cereal fits him just right!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the woods near his house. One day, he found a shiny rock that looked amazing. He picked it up and put it in his pocket.

As he walked deeper into the woods, he heard a loud noise. It sounded like someone was yelling. Timmy followed the sound until he came to a clearing. There, he saw a man with a laser gun! The man yelled at Timmy to leave, but Timmy didn't want to go.

Suddenly, Timmy remembered the shiny rock in his pocket. He took it out and aimed it at the man with the laser gun. The rock shot out a beam of light that hit the man's gun. The gun exploded and the man ran away. Timmy was safe and happy that he had found such an amazing rock.

Anna and Ben are twins. They live on a farm with their mom and dad. They like to play with the animals and help with the chores. But they hate the winter. It is too cold and icy. They cannot go outside and have fun.

One day, mom and dad have to go to town. They tell Anna and Ben to stay inside and be good. They say they will be back soon. Anna and Ben nod, but they are bored. They look out the window and see the barn. The barn is big and red. It has hay and tools and a loft. Anna and Ben think it would be fun to explore the barn.

They put on their coats and boots and sneak out of the house. They run to the barn and open the door. It is dark and dusty inside. They see a ladder that leads to the loft. They climb up the ladder and find a pile of hay. They jump on the hay and laugh. They think they are very clever.

But they do not see the hole in the roof. The hole lets in the icy wind and snow. The snow falls on the hay and makes it wet and cold. Anna and Ben start to shiver and sneeze. They want to go back to the house, but they are afraid. They hear mom and dad's car coming. They think they are in trouble.

Mom and dad enter the barn and see Anna and Ben in the loft. They are angry and worried. They call their names and tell them to come down. Anna and Ben climb down the ladder and apologize. They say they were bored and curious. They say they are sorry and cold.

Mom and dad hug them and take them to the house. They give them hot chocolate and blankets. They tell them they love them, but they also scold them. They tell them they should never go to the barn without permission. They tell them the barn is dangerous and icy. They tell them they could have been hurt or sick. They tell them they should listen and obey.

Anna and Ben nod and say they understand. They say they will never do it again. They say they learned their lesson. They say they hate the barn and the winter. They say they love mom and dad and the house. They say they are sorry and thankful. They hug mom and dad and smile. They are happy and warm.

One day, a prince was playing in the garden with his ball. He saw a big bird in the sky. The bird was hungry and wanted to eat the ball. The prince was scared and ran to his mother.

"Mommy, mommy, help me! The bird wants to take my ball!" he cried.

His mother hugged him and said, "Don't worry, my dear. I will protect you and your ball. The bird can't hurt you."

She took a stick and waved it at the bird. The bird was afraid and flew away. The prince was happy and thanked his mother.

"Thank you, mommy. You are brave and kind. I love you," he said.

His mother smiled and said, "I love you too, my prince. You are my precious son. Now, let's go inside and have some cookies."

They went inside and ate some cookies. The prince shared his cookies with his mother. He was sorry for the bird. He hoped the bird would find some food somewhere else. He wished the bird would be his friend. He said a little prayer for the bird. He was a good prince.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a friend named Tom who was a pupil in her school. One day, Lily and Tom went to the park to play. It was very warm outside and they were having fun on the swings.

Suddenly, Tom realized that he had left his favorite toy at home. He said to Lily, "I need to return home to get my toy." 

Lily said, "I can come with you!" 

So, they both went back to Tom's house to get his toy. They found it and then returned to the park to play some more. They had a great time together and felt happy and warm inside. The end.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little girl who loved to play with her friends. One day, she found a big roll of tape in her room. She excitedly unwound it from all the way across the room and around the corner, like a big, colorful caterpillar. Her friends cheered with glee!

The little girl and her friends had so much fun as they stuck the tape all over the room. They made a talk bridge and decorated the walls with lots of colorful designs.

At last, their fun had to come to an end. The little girl collected all the tape together, wound it up nice and neat, and put it back on the shelf. It was a perfect day, made even more perfect by her lovely friends.

Once upon a time, there was a bird with a mysterious sound. Everytime it would play and make its sound, the little animals around would smile. They all enjoyed the mysterious sound of the bird. 

One day, a little rabbit wanted to know where the mysterious sound was coming from. He asked all the other animals, but nobody knew. Determined to find out, the bunny ventured deeper into the forest. 

Finally, the curious bunny found the mysterious bird. The bird had a broken wing and was unable to fly. The little bunny felt really sad. He then decided to help the bird and took it to the vet. 

After a few weeks, the bird was all healed and was free to fly once again. And so, every time the bird flew, the same mysterious sound played, making all the animals around smile. 

The bunny taught us a very special lesson. We should always help others in need. Even if we don't know them, a little kindness can go a long way!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went out to play even though it was raining. She didn't have an umbrella, so she got all wet.

Lily's mom saw her and said, "Oh no, Lily! You're all wet! You'll catch a cold and suffer."

Lily replied, "I don't hurt, Mommy. I just got wet. Can I still play outside?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily. You have to come inside and dry off. You don't want to suffer from being sick." So, Lily went inside and changed into dry clothes. She felt much better and was happy to play inside with her toys.

Anna loved to play the violin, but she was very shy. She did not like to play in front of other people, only in her room. She had a big violin recital at school, and she was very scared.

"Anna, you can do it," her mom said. "You play so well, and you have practiced a lot. Just relax and enjoy the music."

"But mom, what if I make a mistake? What if they laugh at me?" Anna said.

"No one will laugh at you, Anna. They will be happy to hear you play. And if you make a mistake, it's okay. Everyone makes mistakes sometimes. The important thing is to keep going and have fun."

Anna nodded, but she was still nervous. She put on her dress and carried her violin case to the car. Her mom drove her to the school, where she met her teacher and her classmates. They all went to the stage, where they saw a lot of chairs and a big curtain.

"Are you ready, Anna?" her teacher asked.

Anna took a deep breath and nodded. She opened her violin case and took out her violin and bow. She followed her teacher to the front of the stage, where a microphone was waiting for her.

"Hello, everyone," her teacher said. "Welcome to our violin recital. We have some very talented students who will play for you today. Our first performer is Anna. She will play 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star'. Please give her a big applause."

The curtain opened, and Anna saw a lot of faces looking at her. She felt her heart beat fast and her hands shake. She wanted to run away, but she remembered what her mom said. She lifted her violin to her chin and placed her bow on the strings. She closed her eyes and thought of the stars in the sky. She started to play.

At first, she played very softly and slowly, but as she played, she felt more confident and happy. She forgot about the people and the microphone. She only heard the music in her ears and felt the vibration in her fingers. She played faster and louder, and added some variations to the melody. She felt like she was flying with the stars.

She finished the song and opened her eyes. She heard a loud applause and saw a lot of smiles. She smiled back and bowed. She felt proud and happy. She had done it. She had played the violin in front of everyone. She had released her fear and shared her joy. She looked for her mom in the crowd and saw her waving and clapping. She waved back and ran to hug her.

"Mom, I did it! I played the violin!" she said.

"Yes, you did, Anna. And you played beautifully. I'm so proud of you. You are amazing," her mom said.

"Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love the violin," Anna said.

"I love you too, Anna. And I love your music," her mom said.

John and Mary were on holiday together at the beach. They wanted to have some fun so they borrowed a small boat. The sea was so hot in the sun and the water was very blue.

John and Mary spent the whole day together in the boat. They played and talked and could even see some fishes. They even stopped to have a picnic in the middle of the sea.

When the day was over, they returned the boat to the people who had lent it to them. John and Mary were both happy that they had had such a great day. They waved goodbye and thanked the people for lending them the boat. 

John and Mary went back to the beach, tired and very happy. They had enjoyed being so close to the sea and being on the boat together. They knew they would always remember this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride her bike through the park. One sunny day, Lily saw a big pile of wood. She wanted to ride over it, but it was too high. So, she got off her bike and climbed up the wood. When she got to the top, she looked around and saw that the park was very quiet. It was nice to be up high and see everything. After a while, Lily climbed back down and rode her bike home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pip. Pip lived with his family in a cold place called Antarctica. Pip loved to eat fish and swim in the icy water.

One day, Pip's mommy took him to a store. There, they saw a big, expensive toy. Pip wanted it very much, but his mommy said they couldn't buy it. She told Pip that sometimes we have to be patient and wait for things to grow.

Pip didn't understand what his mommy meant by "grow", but he knew that he wanted to be patient and wait. So, he went back to his home and played with his friends. As he played, he grew bigger and stronger. And one day, when he was all grown up, he found a shiny toy just like the one he saw in the store. He realized that sometimes the things we want can grow if we wait and work hard.

Once there was a plane that liked to spin in the sky. It was really fun and interesting!
One day, while it was spinning around, it saw a little bird on the ground. 
"Hey little bird," said the plane, "Do you want to join me and spin together?" 
The bird replied, "Oh yes! That sounds like lots of fun!"
So the plane and the bird began to spin together around the sky.
They went faster and faster and laughed in delight. They spun so much that they turned the whole sky into a rainbow! 
When their spinning was done, the plane winked at the bird and flew away. The bird smiled and said, "That was so playful and interesting!" 

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big cable on the ground. It was black and thick.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a snake," Tom said.

They walked closer to the cable. They wanted to touch it. But then they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, kids, get away from there! That cable is dangerous. It has electricity inside," the voice said.

They looked up and saw a man. He was wearing a yellow hat and a blue shirt. He had a tool in his hand. He was working on a pole.

"Sorry, mister," Tom said.

"We didn't know," Lily said.

The man smiled. He was not angry. He was nice.

"It's okay. I'm glad you are safe. My name is Ben. I'm an electrician. I fix the wires that make the lights work," he said.

He showed them his tool. It was a plier. He explained how he used it to cut and connect the wires.

Tom and Lily were curious. They asked him many questions. He answered them patiently. He taught them some words. They learned about volts, amps and ohms.

They liked Ben. He was smart and friendly. They wanted to be his friends.

"Can we meet you again?" Tom asked.

"Sure. I work here every week. You can come and say hello. But remember, always stay away from the cables. They can hurt you," Ben said.

He gave them each a sticker. It had a picture of a light bulb and a smiley face. It said "Be bright, be safe".

Tom and Lily were happy. They thanked Ben and waved goodbye. They ran back to their parents. They showed them their stickers. They told them about Ben and the cable.

Their parents were proud. They praised them for being careful and polite. They said they could come back to the park and meet Ben again.

Tom and Lily smiled. They had a fun day. They learned something new. They made a new friend. They were not embarrassed. They were brave.

Tim and Mia are playing with their toy cars in the living room. They like to make them zoom on the carpet and pretend they are racing. Tim has a red car and Mia has a blue car. They take turns to say who is faster.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom! My car is powerful! It can go very fast!" Tim says.

"No, no, no! My car is more powerful! It can go faster and jump over things!" Mia says.

They zoom their cars near the sofa and see a big pillow. They decide to use it as a ramp and make their cars fly in the air.

"Watch this! My car can fly very high!" Tim says. He zooms his car on the pillow and makes it fly over the sofa. He is very happy.

"Wow! That was cool! But I can do better!" Mia says. She zooms her car on the pillow and makes it fly over the sofa too. But she zooms too hard and her car flies out of the window.

"Oh no! My car!" Mia cries. She runs to the window and sees her car on the grass outside. She is very sad.

"Don't cry, Mia! I can help you!" Tim says. He runs to his room and puts on his superhero pants. They are green and have a big star on them. He thinks they make him powerful. He runs back to the living room and says to Mia:

"Look, Mia! I have superhero pants! I can save your car! Follow me!"

He runs outside and zooms to the grass. He picks up Mia's car and gives it to her. She smiles and hugs him.

"Thank you, Tim! You are a superhero! You are very powerful and kind!" Mia says.

"You're welcome, Mia! You are my friend! And your car is very powerful too!" Tim says.

They hug and laugh. They go back to the living room and play with their cars again. They zoom them on the carpet and the pillow and have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a wide chicken. He was pecking around in the meadow looking for something yummy to eat. Suddenly, he heard a loud shout. It was coming from the farmer! He was walking around in his big boots, looking for his chicken. The wide chicken was so scared that he started running away. He couldn't find anywhere to hide!

The wide chicken was running faster and faster, until he reached a nice big tree. He hid behind the trunk, but he was still so scared. He could still hear the farmer shouting and looking for him. But then suddenly, a big brown rabbit came hopping over to the wide chicken. The rabbit said in a friendly voice, "Come with me and I'll help you".

The wide chicken and the big brown rabbit ran together through the meadow until they reached a small pond. The wide chicken jumped into the pond, and he stayed quiet and still. The farmer didn't hear a sound, so he went away disappointed.

The wide chicken was so relieved and happy to be safe. He hopped out of the pond and said goodbye to his new friend, the grand old bunny. From that day onwards, the wide chicken and the big brown rabbit were the best of friends!

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma. She was very messy. She had lots of clothes, but they were all messy too.

One day Emma wanted to wear one of her dresses, but it was too big. She wanted it to be smaller.

She took her dress outside and tried to shrink it. She put the dress in the sun and the dress started to get smaller and smaller.

Soon, Emma's dress fit her perfectly. She was very happy. She could wear the dress to the party.

But other things were shrinking too - all of Emma's messy clothes! So, she had lots of very small clothes but no clothes for the party. Oh dear.

Sara held her lily tight. She had found it while she was out in the garden. It had been morning and the sun was out, but it was starting to rain.

The lily was so beautiful. Its petals were bright and smelled so nice. But then, something disgusting happened. A big bug came crawling onto it!

Sara was scared, but she held the lily tight. She was not going to let the bug take it away. She started to cry, but the rain washed it away.

Finally, Sara was happy again. She hugged the lily and took it home. Now, she could look at it whenever she wanted!

John and his mom walked through the park. They stopped to find a pot. It was shiny and sweet. They wanted to attach it to their garden.

John found some string and his mom found some glue. They attached the string to the pot and the glue made it stick. 

John was so happy that he danced around with joy. His mom laughed as he ran circles around her. 

John took the pot home and his mom planted some sweet-smelling flowers inside it. Now the garden smelled so fresh and sweet. 

John and his mom both looked at the pot and smiled. They had made a beautiful garden together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She liked to wear a yellow hat whenever she went outside. Sarah needed a new hat because her old hat was too small.

One day, Sarah went to the shop with her mummy. As soon as she arrived, she saw a beautiful yellow hat.

â€œMummy,â€ said Sarah excitedly. â€œI need that hat!â€

Mummy smiled. â€œYes,â€ she said. â€œThat yellow hat looks perfect for you.â€

They bought the hat and Sarah wore it straight away. She was so happy! She thanked her mummy for the new hat.

Sarah wore her new yellow hat everywhere. Now she had exactly what she needed.

Once upon a time, a mommy and a daddy took their little girl for a ride in their car. They wanted to go to the park and see the swans. The little girl was so happy to see the swans swimming in the pond. They were so pretty with their white feathers.

After watching the swans for a while, the family got back in their car to go home. The little girl loved how the car could drive so fast. She felt like she was flying! Her mommy and daddy told her they had a modern car that could go really fast.

The little girl was so tired from all the fun at the park that she fell asleep in the car. When she woke up, she was back home in her own bed. She dreamed about the swans and the fast car all night long. The end.

One day Alfie was walking through the park. He wanted to stop and play. Everywhere he looked he saw children playing, but they did not seem friendly. They were all staring at him in an unfriendly way. Alfie felt scared and sad.

He kept walking until he saw a large event taking place. There were lots of people and children there and Alfie heard laughter and music coming from the event. Alfie walked closer and saw people dancing and playing games. Everyone was smiling and friendly.

Alfie walked closer and joined in the fun. Everyone was so welcoming and friendly that Alfie soon forgot his fear. He laughed and laughed and made lots of new friends at the event.

The day soon came to an end but Alfie had had a great time. When he walked back through the park, all the children were staring at him, but this time Alfie was not scared. He had made lots of new friends, and now he was ready to face anything!

Bella was a modest bunny who liked to hop and play in the meadow. She had many friends, like Milo the mouse, Lily the lamb and Fido the fox. They always had fun together, sharing carrots, grass and berries.

One day, a new bunny came to the meadow. His name was Zane, and he was not modest at all. He was big and loud and bossy. He said he was the best at everything, and he wanted all the food and toys for himself. He made fun of Bella and her friends, and chased them away from their favorite spots.

Bella and her friends were sad and scared. They did not know what to do. They tried to be nice to Zane, but he was mean to them. They tried to avoid Zane, but he followed them. They tried to stand up to Zane, but he was too strong and fast.

One day, Zane found a new toy in the meadow. It was a shiny ball with a zigzag pattern on it. He grabbed it and ran away, laughing. He did not care that it belonged to someone else. He thought it was the coolest toy ever, and he wanted to keep it for himself.

He played with the ball for a while, bouncing it and rolling it and throwing it. He did not notice that the ball had a hole in it, and that something was coming out of it. It was pepper, and it made Zane sneeze.

Zane sneezed so hard that he dropped the ball. He sneezed again and again, and he could not stop. He felt his nose tickle and his eyes water. He could not see or hear or smell anything. He was miserable.

Bella and her friends heard Zane sneezing. They were curious and worried. They went to see what was wrong. They saw Zane lying on the ground, surrounded by pepper and the ball. They realized that the ball was not a toy, but a trap. Someone had put pepper in it to catch Zane.

Bella and her friends felt sorry for Zane. They knew he was not nice, but they did not want him to suffer. They decided to help him. They brought him some water and some flowers and some honey. They cleaned his nose and his eyes and his fur. They spoke to him softly and kindly.

Zane was surprised and grateful. He had never been treated so well by anyone. He realized that he had been wrong to be mean and greedy and selfish. He apologized to Bella and her friends, and asked them to forgive him. He promised to be more modest and friendly and generous.

Bella and her friends forgave Zane, and welcomed him to their group. They shared their food and toys with him, and invited him to play with them. Zane was happy and thankful. He learned to be a good bunny, and he made new friends. He never played with the zigzag ball again. He gave it back to its owner, who was a sneaky skunk.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived with her mom and dad in a big house with a garden. One day, Lily's mom cooked some meat for dinner. Lily didn't like the meat because it was too dry. She said to her mom, "Mommy, this meat is too dry. Can you make it juicy?" Her mom said, "Sure, let me put some sauce on it."

After dinner, Lily went to play outside. She saw her neighbor, Mrs. Johnson, walking her dog. The dog was acting crazy and barking loudly. Lily asked Mrs. Johnson, "Why is your dog acting crazy?" Mrs. Johnson said, "He's just excited to go for a walk. He loves to run around and play."

Lily went back inside and told her mom about the crazy dog. Her mom said, "Maybe we should get a dog too." Lily said, "Yes, and we can feed him juicy meat so he won't be dry like the one we had for dinner." Her mom laughed and said, "That's a good idea. Let's go to the pet store tomorrow and see if we can find a dog."

One day, a little boy named Tim was playing outside. He was running and jumping, but he was also very careless. He didn't look where he was going. Tim's mom called out, "Tim, be careful! You might fall and hurt yourself!"

But Tim didn't listen to his mom. He kept playing and running around. Suddenly, he tripped and fell. "Ouch!" he cried. His knee was hurt and dirty. Tim's mom came over and said, "Oh no, Tim! Your knee is hurt. Let's go inside and wash it."

Tim and his mom went inside the house. His mom tried to wash his knee, but Tim didn't want her to touch it. "No, Mom! It hurts!" he cried. His mom said, "Tim, if we don't wash your knee, it will get worse." But Tim still didn't listen. He ran away from his mom and hid under his bed. 

Days went by, and Tim's knee got worse. It was red and swollen. His mom was sad and worried. She told Tim, "I wish you had let me wash your knee. Now we have to go see the doctor." Tim felt bad for not listening to his mom. He learned that being careless can lead to bad things.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there was a big book called a dictionary. The dictionary lived in a small house with a kind girl named Sue. Sue loved to read the dictionary and learn new words every day.

One day, Sue had to go to the store and asked the dictionary to mind her baby brother, Tim. The dictionary was a little scared but wanted to help. So, when Sue left, the dictionary sat next to Tim and watched him play with his toys.

Tim was a happy baby, and he liked the dictionary. He laughed and clapped his hands as he played. The dictionary felt proud that it could help Sue and mind Tim. When Sue came back, she was very happy to see that her baby brother was safe and the dictionary had done a good job. From that day on, Sue and the dictionary were the best of friends, and they always helped each other.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Lily saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. She knew that it was going to rain soon. So, she ran back home to her mom.

"Mom, it will rain soon. Can we make pasta for dinner?" Lily asked. Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can make pasta. Let's make it together."

They made pasta and waited for the rain. When the rain started, it was very cold. Lily and her mom sat by the window and ate their warm pasta. They watched the rain fall and listened to the sound it made. Lily started to shiver because it was so cold outside.

"Mom, I'm cold," Lily said. Her mom hugged her tight and said, "Don't worry, my sweet girl. We are warm inside, and we have our pasta to keep us happy."

The rain stopped, and the sun came out again. Lily and her mom were happy that they had their pasta and each other to keep warm. They knew that they could always find warmth and love with each other, even on the coldest days.

Anna and Ben went to the store with Mom. They liked to help Mom get groceries. Anna pushed the big cart. Ben put things in the cart. Mom said what things they needed.

Anna saw a dull green ball. She wanted the ball. She took it from the shelf and put it in the cart. Ben saw a bright red car. He wanted the car. He took it from the shelf and put it in the cart. Mom did not see the ball and the car.

They went to the cashier. The cashier scanned the groceries. She saw the ball and the car. She said, "Do you want these toys?" Mom looked surprised. She said, "No, we don't need these toys. Put them back, please."

Anna and Ben felt sad. They did not want to put the toys back. They liked the toys. They cried and whined. Mom said, "Stop crying. You have enough toys at home. We only buy groceries here."

Anna and Ben stopped crying. They pushed the cart with Mom. They put the groceries in the car. They went home. They played with their old toys. They forgot about the ball and the car. They had fun.

Once there was a very shy 3 year old named Andy. He liked to play with his many teddy bears, but he wasn't sure what to do when he was outside. One day, Andy's mom took him to the park. 

Andy was scared and didn't want to join the other kids. His mom said, "Come on, Andy. You will learn something here, and it will be fun too!" 

At first, Andy was hesitant, but eventually, he gathered his courage and went to the playground. He felt a bit dull there, but he soon found out that he could make new friends. In addition, he was able to learn all kinds of things in the park.

Each day, Andy spent time in the park with his new friends. He learned how to climb up a tall slide, prices of different things he saw, how to swing with grace, and more. 

When it was time to leave, Andy was sad. He thanked his mom and said, "I want to come to the park everyday. It was really fun to learn so many things here!"

Once there was a boy named Dave. He was 3 years old and loved to play pretend. He always dreamed of receiving something special. 

One day, he received a crazy thing in the mail. It was so colourful and sparkly that he couldn't even imagine what it was. To find out, he decided to open the package.

He was so excited that he ran to show his family. Inside the package, he discovered a toy robot! It had big eyes, lots of buttons and buzzed when he pressed them. Dave was amazed and couldn't wait to play with his new toy!

He spent the whole day playing with his robot. His family had never seen him so happy before. They couldn't believe how crazy the thing was that Dave had received in the mail. It was definitely the best gift ever!

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl named Leticia. She lived on a farm with her mom and dad. One day, Leticia had a big idea. She wanted to go outside and examine the farm.

Her mom said, "No, Leticia, it is too dangerous." But Leticia said it was a brave thing to do and so her mom let her go.

Leticia went outside and examined the farm. She looked high and low for any danger. Finally, she saw something that looked dangerous. It was a giant spider! But Leticia was brave and wasn't afraid. She carefully examined it and then let it go.

After her examination, Leticia went back inside and told her parents all that she had seen. She was very brave and her parents were proud.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly hotel. It was big and made of bricks. Inside it was really dark and everyone seemed scared.

One day, a brave girl came to visit the hotel. The girl didn't seem scared. She went inside and started exploring. Everywhere she looked, it seemed strange and spooky.

Then the girl saw a room filled with sunshine. It seemed so nice and warm. She knew she wanted to stay there. So she stayed in the hotel.

Each morning, the girl woke up and felt excited. She could watch the sun rise over the ugly hotel. Even though it was ugly outside, the girl seemed happy inside.

The girl liked staying in the hotel. She liked pretending it was her own special place. Even though the hotel was ugly, it was the only one she had. And the girl seemed happy there.

Once upon a time, there was a restless robot. The robot couldn't sit still and kept moving around. One day, the robot met a little girl. 

"Hello, little robot. Why are you moving so much?" asked the little girl.

"I don't know. I can't sit still. I feel restless," replied the robot.

The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "Why don't you sit down next to me? Maybe that will help you feel better."

So, the robot sat down next to the little girl and they talked and played together. The robot felt much better and learned that sometimes all you need is to sit down and spend time with a friend.

Once upon a time there was a monster. He was so big and strong that he could move mountains. But he was also very naughty.

One day, he took all the laundry from the village and put it in his pocket. Everyone was mad!

The people tried to find the laundry, but it had vanished. Nobody could find it.

The monster was angry. He thought he had been very clever. He was so proud!

But then the people had a good idea. They asked a wizard to help them find the laundry. After a while, it reappeared in the monster's pocket. Everyone was so happy!

The village was happy and the monster was not so proud anymore!

John and his dad were walking in the woods. They stopped near a campfire. There, they saw a gentle man, seated on a rock and yawning. 

John's dad smiled and asked him, â€œWhy are you so tired?â€ 

The man sat up and said, â€œI was looking for firewood and it took me a long time to collect." 

John's dad nodded and said, â€œThat must have been tiring. Can I help you finish the job?â€ 

The man nodded. He and John's dad worked together, collecting more firewood.

While they worked, John stayed near the campfire, watching. Suddenly, a gust of wind blew some sparks on the ground! 

John was scared, but the man stayed calm. He smiled at John and spoke gently, â€œIt's alright, John. Let's blow the fire out so it doesn't spread.â€

John and the man worked together to put out the fire. 

John felt glad to have helped the man. He yawned and said goodbye before walking away with his dad.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with a ball. They pass the ball to each other and try to score a goal. But there is a guard in front of the goal. The guard is a big dog. The dog does not like the ball. He barks and runs after the ball.

One day, Tom and Sam find a new ball. The ball is very small and shiny. It makes a funny sound when they shake it. They want to play with the new ball. But the guard is still there. He sees the new ball and wants it too. He barks louder and runs faster.

Tom and Sam are scared of the guard. They run away from him. They look for a place to hide the new ball. They see a hole in the wall. The hole is very small and dark. They think the guard cannot fit in the hole. They pass the new ball to each other and try to put it in the hole.

But the guard is smarter than they think. He sees them pass the new ball. He jumps and catches the new ball in his mouth. He is very happy. He runs away with the new ball. He does not care about the hole.

Tom and Sam are sad. They lose the new ball. They look at the hole. They see something shiny in the hole. It is the old ball. The old ball is too big to fit in the hole. The guard cannot get it. Tom and Sam smile. They take the old ball and play with it. They forget about the new ball. They are friends again.

Tommy wanted to go to the city. He asked his mom, "Can I go to the city?"

Mom said, "Not today. It's too far away."

Today, Tommy was going to do something special. He wanted to fix something unusual. So, he went outside and started to look around his yard. Under a bush, he found something unusual - an old toy car.

Tommy was excited. He wanted to fix it and make it better. He asked his mom, "Can I fix this car?"

Mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can fix it. Let's get some tools first."

So, Tommy and his mom went to get the tools they needed. With his mom's help, Tommy fixed the car. He was very proud of his work.

When it was all done, Tommy said, "I did it! Now I'm ready to go to the city!"

Mom smiled and said, "Let's go!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play with her toys and eat candy. One day, Lily went to the store with her mommy. They walked around and looked at all the things in the store. 

Suddenly, Lily saw a boy who was being very naughty. He was throwing things and making a mess. Lily's mommy told her to stay away from the naughty boy. 

When they were done shopping, Lily and her mommy went to the exit. They saw a man who was wearing a big bow tie. Lily thought it looked funny and she laughed. Then, they went home and had some ice cream. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but it was raining outside. She asked her mom if she could go outside and play.

Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Lily, but I can't permit you to play outside in the rain. You might get sick."

Lily was sad, but she understood. She went to the window and looked outside. She saw a wise owl perched on the roof of her neighbor's house. She asked her mom, "Mom, why is the owl on the roof?"

Her mom said, "The owl likes to sit on the roof because it's high up and he can see everything around him."

Lily thought that was very interesting. She watched the owl for a while, then went to play with her toys inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who loved to sing. Every morning, he would fly to the wheat field and sing a beautiful song. The wheat was tall and golden, and the bird loved to hop from stalk to stalk.

One day, the little bird noticed that some of the wheat was looking thin and sickly. He was worried that the wheat wouldn't grow strong and healthy. So, he sang his most beautiful song to the wheat, hoping it would make them feel better.

To his surprise, the wheat started to grow taller and stronger! The little bird was so happy that his singing had helped the wheat. From then on, he made sure to visit the wheat field every day and sing his songs to keep the wheat healthy and strong.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day, she decided to go on a journey. She put her knapsack on and started out on the path.

As she travelled, Lucy noticed a big pile of salt. She was so excited! She started to fill her knapsack with the salt. Suddenly, she heard a scary noise. 

Lucy quickly turned around and saw a giant dragon! She was so scared. The dragon said, "What are you doing with my salt?"

Lucy was so afraid. She said in a tiny voice, "I was just taking some salt to bring back home."

The dragon looked at her and smiled. He said, "You can take it. Just make sure to be careful."

So, Lucy filled her knapsack with the salt and thanked the dragon. She waved goodbye and ran all the way home. She was so glad to have her adventure and so grateful that the dragon was kind!

Once upon a time, there was a helpless crab who wanted to swim in the sea. She looked around and couldn't find a way to get to the water. Suddenly, she heard a voice. 

"Come here, little crab. I can help you," said the voice. The crab looked around and saw a beautiful white duck.

"Jump on my back and we'll swim to the sea together," said the duck. The crab was so happy and jumped on the duck's back. Together, they swam off to the sea.

The crab laughed as she watched the waves and felt the warm sun on her back. She knew she was safe and that the duck would look after her.

The duck and the crab swam for hours until they reached the shore. The crab thanked the duck and hopped back onto the sand.

From then on, the crab would always look back fondly on the day she had taken a ride on the beautiful duck's back and gone swimming in the sea.

Anna and Ben are playing in the snow. They make a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They give him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They are very happy.

"Let's sing a song for our snowman!" Anna says. "Maybe he will come alive!"

"Okay!" Ben says. "What song do you know?"

Anna thinks for a moment. She remembers a song her mommy taught her. She starts to sing:

"Frosty the snowman, was a jolly happy soul,
With a corn cob pipe and a button nose, and two eyes made of coal.
Frosty the snowman, is a fairy tale they say,
He was made of snow but the children know, how he came to life one day."

Ben joins in the song. They sing louder and louder. They hope their snowman will hear them.

Suddenly, they hear a voice behind them. It is deep and friendly.

"Hello, children!" the voice says. "Thank you for singing that lovely song!"

Anna and Ben turn around. They can't believe their eyes. Their snowman is smiling at them. He has come alive!

"Wow!" Anna says. "You can talk!"

"Of course I can!" the snowman says. "You gave me life with your song and your love. My name is Frosty. What are yours?"

"I'm Anna and this is Ben!" Anna says. "We are so happy to meet you, Frosty!"

"Me too!" Frosty says. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Anna and Ben say. They hug Frosty and laugh.

They have a lot of fun playing in the icy snow. They reveal their secrets and their dreams to Frosty. He tells them stories and jokes. They are the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a kind lady named Mrs. Smith. She loved to bake cookies and share them with her friends. One day, she saw a little girl crying on the street. Mrs. Smith stepped closer and asked, "What's wrong, dear?"

The little girl said, "I lost my mommy and I don't know where to go." Mrs. Smith smiled and said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find your mommy." Mrs. Smith held the little girl's hand and walked with her around the neighborhood. They asked people if they had seen the little girl's mommy, but no one had.

Mrs. Smith was very compassionate and didn't want the little girl to be scared. She said, "Let's go to my house and have some cookies while we wait for your mommy to find us." The little girl smiled and followed Mrs. Smith to her house. They had cookies and milk together and talked about their favorite things.

Finally, the little girl's mommy found them and they were reunited. The little girl hugged Mrs. Smith and said, "Thank you for being so kind and helping me. You are a very compassionate lady." Mrs. Smith smiled and said, "It was my pleasure. I'm happy you found your mommy." From that day on, Mrs. Smith and the little girl became good friends and would often have cookies together.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to splash in the puddles and make mud pies. Lily had a red bucket and Ben had a blue one. They filled their buckets with water and mud and carried them to the sandbox.

"Look at my pie!" Lily said. "It is big and round and wet."

"Mine is bigger and rounder and wetter!" Ben said. He poured some water on his pie and made it soak.

Lily wanted to make her pie wetter too. She reached for Ben's bucket, but he pulled it away.

"No, this is my water!" Ben said. He was stubborn and did not want to share.

Lily was angry. She grabbed her bucket and threw it at Ben. The water and mud flew out of the bucket and hit Ben in the face and chest. He was soaked and dirty.

"Hey, stop that!" Ben shouted. He wiped his eyes and saw Lily laughing. He picked up his bucket and threw it back at her. The water and mud hit Lily in the hair and dress. She was soaked and dirty too.

They both stopped and looked at each other. They were wet and muddy and silly. They started to giggle.

"Sorry, Lily," Ben said. "You can have some of my water."

"Sorry, Ben," Lily said. "You can have some of my mud."

They hugged and shared their buckets. They made more pies and decorated them with stones and leaves. They had fun in the garden.

When they were done, they ran to the house. They wanted to show their pies to Mom and Dad. But they forgot to check their pockets. They had put some stones and leaves in their pockets and they were still wet and muddy. When they got to the house, they left a trail of water and mud behind them.

Mom and Dad saw the mess and shook their heads. They were not happy. They told Lily and Ben to go to the bathroom and take off their clothes. They had to soak them in the tub and wash them. They also had to wash their faces and hands and hair.

Lily and Ben did what Mom and Dad said. They were sorry for making a mess. They hoped Mom and Dad would still like their pies. They were proud of their pies. They were big and round and wet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and would spend hours playing in the garden. One day, she found a tiny seed and decided to plant it in the soil. She watered it every day and waited patiently for it to grow.

One morning, she woke up to find a beautiful flower had bloomed. It had bright colors and a lovely fragrance. "Wow, it's so pretty!" she said with a smile.

Her mother, who was watching her, said, "It's the rhythm of nature. Everything grows in its own time."

Lily felt humble and grateful for the beautiful flower she had grown. She knew that with love and patience, anything could bloom.

Once upon a time there was a loyal dog named Fido. Fido loved his owner very much and he always listened to what his owner said.

Every day Fido waited for his owner to come home from work and when he did Fido was always so excited to see him. One day, when his owner came home from work, he had a special surprise for Fido. He gave him a yummy cookie!

Fido was so happy he ate the cookie right up. He wagged his tail and licked his owner's face. His owner laughed and said, "Fido, don't forget to shut the door!"

Fido quickly ran to the door and shut it. Then he came back to Where his owner was and waited to get another cookie. His owner smiled and gave him a good pat on the head.

Fido was a very loyal dog and he was always happy when he was with his owner.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play in the park with their ball. One day, they see an elderly cat sitting on a bench. The cat is black and white and has a collar with a bell.

"Look, a cat!" Tom says. He runs to the cat and tries to pet it. The cat hisses and scratches Tom's hand. Tom cries and runs back to Sam.

"Bad cat!" Sam says. He is angry at the cat for hurting his brother. He picks up the ball and kicks it hard at the cat. The ball hits the cat on the head and makes a loud noise. The cat meows and jumps off the bench.

"Hey, stop that!" a voice says. It is an elderly lady who owns the cat. She walks to the bench and picks up the cat. She glares at Sam and Tom. "You should not kick my cat! He is old and sick. He does not like strangers. You should be nice to animals!"

Sam and Tom feel sorry for the cat and the lady. They did not know the cat was old and sick. They did not mean to hurt him.

"We are sorry, lady," Sam says. "We did not know. We like animals. We have a dog at home. He is friendly and likes to play."

The lady softens her look. She sees that Sam and Tom are not bad boys. They just made a mistake.

"It's okay, boys," she says. "But you should be careful with your ball. You could hurt someone or something. And you should always ask before you pet a cat. Some cats are shy or scared. They need time to trust you."

Sam and Tom nod. They understand. They apologize again to the lady and the cat. They promise to be more careful and respectful. The lady smiles and thanks them. She walks away with the cat in her arms. The cat looks at Sam and Tom and purrs. Sam and Tom wave goodbye and go back to playing with their ball. They are happy and have learned a lesson.

Max was a 3 year old who took lots of things from his friends. He wanted to borrow them, but he was never sure when he was supposed to give them back. One day, Max saw a little figure in his neighbour's window. It looked so pretty and Max wanted it for himself. He asked his neighbour if he could borrow it, and the neighbour said yes.

But when they got home, Max saw the figure was broken! It was all rough and jagged. Max had to face his neighbour and tell him what happened to the figure he borrowed. Lily and Mom went to the mall. Lily liked the mall. She saw many toys and clothes and books. She wanted to touch everything. Mom said, "No, Lily, you have to stay with me. The mall is big and busy. You can get lost or hurt."

But Lily did not listen. She saw a gray cat in a pet shop. She loved cats. She ran to the cat and said, "Hello, kitty, you are so cute. Can I pet you?" She opened the cage and took the cat out. The cat was scared and angry. It scratched Lily's face and ran away.

Lily cried. She was in pain and she was sorry. She looked for Mom, but she could not see her. She saw many people and things, but not Mom. She felt alone and scared. She wanted Mom to protect her.

Mom heard Lily's cry. She was worried and angry. She ran to the pet shop and saw Lily's face. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You are hurt and you are naughty. You did not stay with me. You made the cat run away. You are in trouble."

She took Lily to the nurse. The nurse cleaned Lily's face and put a bandage on it. She said, "Lily, you have to be careful and listen to your mom. The cat was not your friend. It was wild and scared. You have to respect animals and their homes."

Lily was sad. She said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, nurse. I'm sorry, cat. I just wanted to play. I love you, Mom. Please don't be mad at me."

Mom hugged Lily. She said, "I love you, too, Lily. But you have to learn from your mistake. You have to obey me and stay with me. I want to protect you and keep you safe. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I will be good. Can we go home now?"

Mom said, "Yes, Lily. We can go home now. But you have to say sorry to the pet shop owner and pay for the cat's cage. And you have to be more careful next time."

Lily said, "OK, Mom. I will say sorry and pay. And I will be more careful. I don't want to get hurt or lose you again."

They left the mall. Lily was still sad and sore. She did not like the mall anymore. She learned a hard lesson. She wished she had listened to Mom. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a wide field. In the middle of that wide field stood a tall tree with branches so strong and tall.

One day, a mommy said to her little 3 year old, "I am going to test you and see how much sugar you know." So the little one looked up at the tall tree and said, "The tree has lots of sugar?"

"No, no," said the mommy, smling. "Let me show you what I mean." She brought out a bag of white sweet powder and said, "This is sugar. Taste it!"

The little one put a pinch of the powder on her tongue and smiled. "It's sweet!" she exclaimed.

The mommy laughed. "That's right, sweetie. That is the sugar I was talking about. And I am so proud of you for testing yourself and finding out. You are so smart!"

The little one smiled happily and gave the mommy a big hug. All was good in the wide field.

One day, a thoughtful goose wanted to lead the other animals in a game. She clucked loudly and flapped her wings to get their attention. "Let's play!" she said.

The animals followed the goose as they headed out on their adventure. The rabbit hopped, the pig snorted, and the dog barked. They followed the thoughtful goose through the thick forest and around the pond.

The goose led them to a field of green grass. At the far end of the field was a bright rainbow. All the animals stopped to admire the beautiful sight.

Suddenly, a fox stepped forward, "I have an idea! Let's have a race to the rainbow!" The animals all cheered and lined up at the edge of the field.

The thoughtful goose counted down, "1, 2, 3, GO!" and the animals were off. The fox was fast, but the thoughtful goose was faster! Soon she was first to the rainbow.

The animals all gathered around the goose to hear what she had to say. "You were all so brave and fast," she said. "I am so proud of you. Now, let's all go get some ice cream!"

The animals all shouted with delight. The thoughtful goose had lead them on an exciting adventure, and now it was justly rewarded with ice cream.

Mama had made some delicious pies. She asked Tim to help her get them out of the oven. Tim was only three years old, but he was very eager and excited to help. 

He carefully lifted the pies out and put them on the counter. Mama said, "They look delicious - Why don't you eat one, Tim!" Tim happily agreed and he ate the pie in no time.

Just then, they heard the doorbell ringing. Mama opened the door and a little girl from the neighbourhood was standing outside.

Mama said, "Hi there! Come on in." 

The little girl said, "Hi, I thought I heard Tim singing. Could we play together?"

Mama said, "Yes of course! He's been so restless all day; playing will be good for him."

So, the two little kids played together for the rest of the day. They laughed and laughed, and had so much fun playing together. Mama was happy to see them having a great time.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah and she liked to explore. One day, Sarah decided to go for an adventure.

She started walking in the park and soon she saw a pretty swan. The swan was swimming and making noisy sounds. Sarah thought it was so funny and she wanted to be friends.

She slowly walked towards the swan and said "hello!" but the swan didn't reply. She tried again, this time waving her hands, but the swan still didn't answer.

Sarah didn't give up and she decided to sing a song for the swan. After she finished singing, the swan started to make soft cooing sounds and it slowly came closer to Sarah.

That was the start of a beautiful friendship between Sarah and the swan. They became best friends and Sarah always liked to go to the park to hang out with her noisy swan.

Tommy loves rockets. He has many rockets in his room. He plays with them every day. He makes them fly and zoom and blast off. He pretends he is an astronaut.

One day, Tommy gets a new rocket for his birthday. It is big and shiny and red. It has a button that makes it light up and make noises. Tommy is very happy. He says, "Thank you, Mommy and Daddy! This is the best rocket ever!"

He runs to his room to play with his new rocket. He puts it on his bed and presses the button. The rocket lights up and makes noises. Tommy smiles and claps. He says, "Wow, this is so cool!"

But then, something bad happens. The rocket falls off the bed and hits the floor. It breaks into pieces. The light and the noise stop. Tommy is very sad. He says, "Oh no, my new rocket! It is broken!"

He picks up the pieces and tries to fix them. But he can't. He starts to cry. He says, "I want my new rocket back! It was so fun!"

Mommy and Daddy hear Tommy cry. They come to his room and see the broken rocket. They hug Tommy and say, "We are sorry, Tommy. Your new rocket was an accident. It is not your fault."

They help Tommy clean up the pieces. They say, "We can get you another rocket, Tommy. Or maybe you can play with your other rockets. You have many rockets, Tommy. You are still an astronaut."

Tommy stops crying. He says, "Thank you, Mommy and Daddy. You are right. I have many rockets. I am still an astronaut."

He smiles and hugs them. He says, "I love you, Mommy and Daddy. And I love rockets."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was only three years old, but he was very bright.

â€œMom, look at that bird!â€ he said.
