One day Spike was walking and she saw a gray bird. She wanted to find out more about it so she decided to follow it. The bird was so fast and it soon flew away. Spike was upset but then she had an idea.

Spike decided to make a look-out point. She built a tower with some sticks and put it in a tree with a view of the sky. She sat inside and waited to see the gray bird.

After a while, the gray bird returned and flew around the tower so Spike could see it better. She was so delighted and waved at it with a big smile. Spike had decided to make a new friend!

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play dress-up with their mom's clothes. One day, they find a big suit in the closet. It is black and has many buttons. Lily and Tom want to try it on.

They take turns putting on the suit. It is very heavy and long. It covers their feet and hands. They laugh and pretend to be grown-ups. They walk around the room and say, "Hello, I am a boss. I have a lot of work to do."

Then they hear their mom calling them. "Lily, Tom, it's time to eat. Come to the kitchen, please." They run to the door, but the suit is too heavy. They fall down and get tangled in the suit. They can't get up.

"Help, help!" they cry. "We are stuck in the suit!"

Their mom comes to the room and sees them. She smiles and helps them out of the suit. She says, "You two are very funny. But you should not play with my suit. It is not for children. It is for work."

She hugs them and takes them to the kitchen. She has made their favorite food: macaroni and cheese. Lily and Tom are hungry. They forget about the suit and eat their food. They say, "Thank you, mom. You are the best."

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She wanted to find something special, so she looked everywhere. She looked in her garden, but nothing was there. Then she looked in the park. Suddenly she saw something shining on the ground! She bent down and picked it up. It was a golden star! Sarah was so happy.

She wanted to find out what the reward was, so she asked her Mom. Mom said that the reward was a tasty treat! Sarah was so excited. She went to the kitchen and Mom gave her a yummy ice cream. It was so tasty!

Sarah was so happy that she found a special reward. She was sure that she wouldn't forget this day, and she was now ever so lucky to have such a tasty treat.

A little girl named Mary was playing outside on a Tuesday. Her parents had warned her not to play with fire, but Mary was feeling brave and wanted to prove that she could be responsible.

Mary found a yellow stick and dragged it over to her campfire. She touched the stick to the fire and it began to burn. Mary was so excited she clapped her hands.

But then Mary's parents arrived. Mary felt ashamed and scared. She knew she had made a mistake.

Mary's father said, "Mary, fire can be very dangerous. We told you to be careful." He hugged her and said, "We love you, and we want you to stay safe. Remember, it's always good to be careful with fire."

Mary was very sorry and promised never to play with fire again. She learned that it's important to always listen to her parents and stay safe.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys, but sometimes they fight. One day, they have a big fight over a red car. Tom says it is his car, and Lily says it is her car. They pull and push the car, and they yell at each other.

"Give me the car!" Tom says.

"No, it is mine!" Lily says.

They repeat the same words over and over. They do not listen to each other. They do not share. They make a lot of noise.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She sees Tom and Lily fighting over the car. She is angry. She takes the car away from them. She says they have to say sorry and play nicely, or they will not get the car back.

Tom and Lily are sad. They do not want to lose the car. They look at each other. They say sorry. They hug. They ask Mom to give them the car back. Mom smiles. She gives them the car back. She says they have to take turns and share. She says they have to be kind and gentle.

Tom and Lily nod. They agree. They take turns and share the car. They are kind and gentle. They play happily. They have fun. They feel good. They have victory. They have peace.

Once upon a time, there was a thin chest. It had a secret written on it that only certain people could see.

One day, Jack saw the chest. He was a curious 3-year-old and he wanted to know what the secret was. He didn't know how to open it so he went looking for help.

He found a wise wizard who said that he could open the chest if Jack promised to sign a special document. Jack was afraid of signing something he didn't understand, but the wizard promised that it was nothing bad so he signed the document.

The wizard opened the chest, revealing a bag of gold coins. Jack was so excited that he started jumping up and down. 

Suddenly, the wizard cast a spell and the gold coins turned into thin air! Jack was devastated as he realized that he had been tricked. He had signed away all his rights to anything in the chest! 
 
The wizard had set him up! The secret on the chest had been a warning that only careful people could open it. And Jack had been too curious and naive to notice.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the lively park with her friends. One day, they decided to enter the big castle that they saw in the distance. They were very excited and ran towards the castle. When they got there, they saw a sign that said, "Welcome to the Castle of Dreams." They were amazed and couldn't wait to explore inside. They saw many beautiful things and had a lot of fun. They even got to meet the queen of the castle and she asked for their names. Lily was very happy to tell her name and they all had a great time together.

Lily and Ben were very happy. They were going to the city with Mom and Dad. They had never seen the city before. They wanted to see the big buildings, the cars, the people, and the park.

"Are we there yet?" Lily asked.

"Soon, sweetie," Mom said. "Look, you can see the city from here. Do you see the green park in the middle?"

Lily and Ben looked out the window. They saw the city. It was very big and shiny. They saw the green park. It had trees and grass and flowers. They saw a big pond with ducks and swans.

"Wow!" Ben said. "Can we go to the park, please?"

"Of course," Dad said. "That's where we're going. I have a surprise for you there."

Lily and Ben wondered what the surprise was. They were very excited. They hoped it was something fun.

They arrived at the park. Dad parked the car. Mom took out a basket. They walked to a nice spot under a tree. They spread a blanket on the grass. They had a picnic. They ate sandwiches, cookies, and fruit. They drank juice. They were very happy.

"Are you ready for your surprise?" Dad asked.

"Yes, yes, yes!" Lily and Ben said.

Dad smiled. He reached into the basket. He took out two boxes. He gave one to Lily and one to Ben.

"Open them," he said.

Lily and Ben opened the boxes. They gasped. Inside each box was a toy. Lily received a doll. Ben received a car. They were the toys they had wished for.

"Thank you, thank you, thank you!" Lily and Ben said. They hugged Mom and Dad.

"You're welcome, sweeties," Mom and Dad said. "We're glad you like them. We love you very much."

Lily and Ben played with their toys. They had a lot of fun. They also fed the ducks and swans. They ran and laughed. They had a wonderful day at the park. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy's family was very wealthy and had a big house with lots of seats. Timmy loved to sit on the soft, fluffy seats and watch TV all day.

One day, Timmy's mom asked him, "Are you tired, Timmy?" Timmy replied with a big yawn, "Yes, Mommy. I am very tired." 

His mom said, "Well, why don't you take a nap on the seat?" Timmy agreed and laid down on one of the seats. He closed his eyes and soon fell asleep.

When he woke up, he saw his mom sitting next to him. She asked, "Did you have a good nap, Timmy?" Timmy replied with a smile, "Yes, Mommy. I feel much better now." 

From that day on, Timmy took naps on the seats whenever he felt tired. He loved his comfy seats and his mom's caring words.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures with her mom and dad. One day, they went for a drive in the car. Dad had a special paper called a license that allowed him to drive the car. 

As they drove down the road, Lily saw something unusual on the side of the street. It was a big, purple balloon! She asked her mom and dad if they could stop and get it. Dad pulled over and got out of the car. He tried to grab the balloon, but it suddenly disappeared! 

Lily was sad that she couldn't have the balloon, but she was also confused. Where did it go? Mom and dad explained that sometimes things can disappear and we don't know where they go. They continued on their drive, but Lily couldn't stop thinking about the unusual disappearing balloon.

Once upon a time, there was a woman who lived in a big, original house. Every day, the woman would go for a walk in the park and enjoy the quiet and the sunshine.

One day, as the woman was walking in the park, she heard an odd noise. She was curious and went over to investigate. When she arrived, she saw a little mouse being disturbed by a big cat. The woman was sad and tried to find a way to help the mouse.

Suddenly, she had an idea. She carefully approached the mouse with a cup, and offered it some food. The mouse happily jumped into the cup and the woman quickly sealed it.

The woman couldn't bear to leave the mouse, so she took it home with her. She let the mouse out of the cup and it quickly ran away. The woman smiled and said, "I'm glad I was able to help and make things better."
 
From that day on, it became a tradition for the woman to feed the wildlife in the park. She was thankful that she was able to save the original mouse and make a difference.

Once there was an island. On the island lived a family. They were a happy, curious family. Every day they would explore the island and find something new and exciting.

One day, when the family went for a walk around the island, they noticed something very strange. There was a big rock where nothing had been before. They decided to take a closer look, and when they did they saw it was full of crystals! They were so excited they decided to take some home.

But as they arrived back, they started to complain. The crystals were not as beautiful as they had expected. They were dark and ugly, and the family was disappointed.

The family's joy soon turned to anger as they realised that their neighbours must have taken them from their island. The family argued for a long time about what to do with the crystals and the neighbours, but they could not agree.

The conflict stayed unresolved and the family continued to complain and be angry. Their bad feelings remained and their island was never the same.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very rich and had lots of toys to play with. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny came over to play with him. Johnny saw Timmy's toys and wanted to play with them too. Timmy didn't want Johnny to play with his toys because he was afraid Johnny would break them.

Johnny said, "Timmy, can I please play with your toys? I promise I won't break them."

Timmy replied, "No, I don't want you to poke my toys and make them itch."

Johnny felt sad because he really wanted to play with Timmy's toys. But then, Johnny had an idea. He said, "Timmy, I have my own toys at home. Let's go to my house and play with my toys instead!"

Timmy thought about it and agreed. They went to Johnny's house and had lots of fun playing with Johnny's toys together. Timmy realized that sharing his toys with his friend was much more fun than keeping them all to himself.

Once upon a time there was a happy girl. She loved picking things. One day she saw a pretty rose in her garden. The girl was so excited that she bent down to pick it. The rose was so beautiful that it made the girl even more happy. She took the rose inside and showed it to her mom. Her mom smiled and told her that she had picked a very special rose. The girl was so proud and she went around the house showing everyone her special rose. Everyone was very happy for her. And since then the little girl always liked to pick roses in her garden. The end.

One day, a small girl was walking in the woods. She saw a hut perched atop a grassy hill. She climbed up the hill to take a look inside the hut.

She saw a rabbit sitting in the corner of the hut. The rabbit wasn't happy, and the little girl knew she had done something to make the rabbit feel bad.

She asked the rabbit what was wrong and he told her that she had said a mean word the day before. He was very hurt and didn't know what to do.

The little girl told him that she was sorry and that she would forgive him. She realized that words could be difficult to take back. She gave the rabbit a big hug and told him that everything would be okay.

The rabbit was so happy and they spent the rest of the day playing together in the hut. The little girl learned that it was important to forgive and to be kind to others.

Once upon a time, there was a kind rabbit named Benny. Benny was very compassionate and always helped his friends. One day, Benny and his friends took a photo together to remember their fun day. Benny made a silly joke and they all laughed. 

Later, Benny went to find some carrots for his friends. He used his nose like a compass to find the way. Suddenly, he saw a squirrel who was lost. Benny felt sad for the squirrel and decided to help him find his way home. They walked and walked until they found the squirrel's home. The squirrel was very happy and thanked Benny for his kindness. From that day on, Benny and the squirrel became good friends.

Once, there was a little bear. He was a curious one. He wanted to try new things.

One day, the little bear saw a laser. He immediately wanted to act. He asked the laser owner, "Can I act with the laser?"

The laser owner said, "Yes, it is okay but remember to be careful. You will get wet while doing that."

The little bear was so excited that he immediately ran close to the laser. But as soon as he did, his foot stepped on a wet spot. He slipped and fell in the water. He was scared and started to cry.

The laser owner came to comfort him. He said, "Remember, you must be careful when you act. You must always be aware of the environment around you to prevent any accidents."

The little bear understood the message and dried himself off. He was much more careful the next time he acted with the laser.

Moral of the story: It is important to be careful when trying new things. We must always be aware of our environment to keep ourselves safe.

Ben and Jen are twins. They like to play with matches. They find a box of matches in the kitchen. They sneak out to the backyard. They want to make a fire.

But Grandpa sees them. Grandpa is elderly. He walks slowly with a stick. He loves Ben and Jen. He does not want them to get hurt. He shouts, "Stop! Matches are dangerous! Give them to me!"

Ben and Jen are scared. They drop the matches. They run to Grandpa. They hug him. They say, "Sorry, Grandpa. We did not know. We wanted to have fun."

Grandpa is kind. He says, "It's okay. I forgive you. But you must never play with matches again. They can burn you and the house. They are not toys. They are tools. Only grown-ups can use them safely."

Ben and Jen nod. They say, "We understand, Grandpa. We will not play with matches again. We will play with something else. Can you play with us?"

Grandpa smiles. He says, "Of course. I love to play with you. What do you want to play?"

Ben and Jen think. They say, "How about we play unite? We can make a big circle with our arms. We can sing a song. We can be happy."

Grandpa likes the idea. He says, "That sounds like a good game. Let's play unite. We are a family. We are a match."

They hold hands. They make a big circle. They sing a song. They are happy. They play unite.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they found a bow and arrow in the park. Timmy's friend, Billy, showed him how to use it. Timmy aimed the arrow and shot it into the sky. It went up and up until they couldn't see it anymore.

After playing for a while, Timmy's mom called him inside for lunch. She served him a big sandwich with cheese and ham. Timmy was very hungry and ate it all up. He felt cheerful and happy after his meal.

Later that day, Timmy and his friends went back to the park. They found the arrow and decided to try shooting it again. This time, Timmy hit a target they made out of cardboard. They all cheered and clapped for him. Timmy felt proud of himself and had a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She had a smart cat named Whiskers who was very good at solving puzzles. One day, Lily found a square puzzle and asked Whiskers to help her solve it. 

Whiskers was an intelligent cat and he quickly figured out how to put the puzzle pieces together. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Whiskers! You are so smart!" 

Whiskers purred and said, "Please don't mention it, Lily. I'm always happy to help you." From that day on, Lily and Whiskers solved many puzzles together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was an old clock. It was very big and it had a shiny face. Every day, the clock would tick-tock and tell the time. The clock lived in a big house with many other things. One day, the sun came out and shone on the clock. The clock sparkled and glowed in the sunlight. The clock was very happy to shine in the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went for a walk and found a big rock. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a big rock!" she said.

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a nice rock, Lily. Let's bring it home and mark it with a special sticker."

Lily was happy and put the rock in her pocket. As they walked home, Lily saw a bird with a troubled wing. "Mommy, the birdie is hurt. Can we help it?" she asked.

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. Let's bring the birdie to the vet and see if they can fix its wing." They brought the birdie to the vet and the vet fixed its wing. The birdie was happy and flew away.

Lily was happy too. She had found a rock and helped a birdie all in one day.

Once upon a time there was a whale. He was big and strong and his skin was tough. But the whale had a secret. He was very sad. He didn't know why he felt that way, he was just lonely.

One day a small fish swam up to him. She said, â€œWhatâ€™s wrong big whale?â€ The whale replied â€œI am sad because no one cares about me.â€ 

The little fish said, â€œDonâ€™t worry! I care about you! I will always be here for you. I will be your friend.â€

The whale was very happy! He thanked the little fish for being so kind. Then the two of them had a long swim together. They laughed and joked the whole time. 

Even when the harsh sea storms came, the whale and the little fish stayed together. They knew that no matter what, they would always care for each other.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play with stickers. They had many stickers of different shapes and colors. They liked to attach them to their books, their toys, and their clothes. Sometimes they shared their stickers, and sometimes they wanted to keep them for themselves.

One day, Ben found a new sticker in his drawer. It was a big, shiny star with a smiley face. He was very happy and wanted to show it to Lily. He ran to her house and knocked on the door. Lily opened the door and saw the sticker. She liked it very much and wanted to have it too.

"Can I have your sticker, Ben?" she asked.

"No, Lily, this is my sticker. I found it in my drawer. It is very special and I want to keep it," Ben said.

"But I like it too, Ben. It is so pretty and happy. Please, can I have it?" Lily begged.

"No, Lily, you have many stickers already. You cannot have my sticker. Go away," Ben said.

Lily felt very sad and angry. She was jealous of Ben and his sticker. She thought he was not a good friend. She wanted to make him feel bad too. She had an idea. She ran to her room and got her scissors. She came back to Ben and said, "If I cannot have your sticker, you cannot have it either." She grabbed the sticker from Ben's hand and cut it in half with the scissors.

Ben was shocked and hurt. He saw his sticker, his favorite sticker, torn in two pieces. He started to cry. He said, "Lily, why did you do that? That was very mean and bad. You ruined my sticker. You are not my friend anymore."

Lily felt sorry and ashamed. She saw Ben's tears and heard his words. She realized she had made a big mistake. She said, "Ben, I am sorry. I was jealous of your sticker and I wanted to have it. But I should not have cut it. That was very wrong and rude. I am sorry. Can you forgive me?"

Ben looked at Lily and saw her face. She looked sad and sorry too. He remembered they were friends and they liked to play with stickers. He said, "Lily, I forgive you. But you should not be jealous of what I have. You have many stickers too. And you should not cut things that are not yours. That is not nice. We should share and be kind."

Lily nodded and hugged Ben. She said, "You are right, Ben. I should not be jealous or mean. We should share and be kind. I am sorry. Can we still be friends?"

Ben smiled and hugged Lily back. He said, "Yes, Lily, we can still be friends. And we can still play with stickers. Look, we can attach the two pieces of my sticker together and make a new sticker. It will have a spot in the middle, but it will still be shiny and happy. And it will remind us of our friendship."

Lily and Ben attached the two pieces of the sticker together and put it on their book. They were happy and proud of their new sticker. They learned a lesson that day. They learned not to be jealous of what others have, but to be grateful for what they have. They learned not to hurt others, but to help them. They learned to share and be kind. And they learned that friendship is more valuable than any sticker.

Anna and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They have some pots and spoons and pretend to cook. Anna says, "I will make soup for you, Ben. You are hungry." Ben nods and smiles.

Anna fills a pot with water from the tap. She adds some salt and pepper and stirs. She looks for something else to put in the soup. She sees a big bag of flour on the counter. She thinks flour will make the soup thick and yummy. She opens the bag and pours some flour into the pot.

The flour makes the water cloudy and sticky. Anna stirs harder, but the soup does not look good. She says, "Oh no, this is not soup. This is glue." Ben laughs and says, "Glue is not for eating, Anna. Glue is for sticking things."

Anna does not want to waste the glue. She thinks of something to do with it. She says, "I know, Ben. We can make a picture with the glue. We can stick some paper and crayons on the wall." Ben thinks this is a fun idea. He says, "Yes, let's do that, Anna. We can make a big picture."

They take the pot of glue and some paper and crayons. They go to the wall and start to stick things. They make a picture of a house, a tree, a sun and a bird. They use a lot of glue and paper and crayons. They are very happy with their picture.

But they do not see that the glue is dripping from the wall. It drips on the floor and on the table and on the chairs. It drips into the drain and clogs it. It drips on the door and makes it stick. It drips on the window and makes it hard to see.

Soon, the kitchen is full of glue. Anna and Ben are stuck to the wall. They cannot move. They say, "Help, help, we are stuck. We need someone to feed us. We are hungry."

Mom comes home and sees the mess. She is very angry. She says, "What have you done, Anna and Ben? You have made a big mess. You have wasted the flour and the water and the paper and the crayons. You have clogged the drain and stuck the door and the window. You have ruined the kitchen."

She opens the door with a lot of force. She pulls Anna and Ben from the wall. She cleans the glue from the floor and the table and the chairs. She cleans the drain and the window. She takes the picture from the wall and throws it away.

She says, "You are very naughty, Anna and Ben. You have to learn to play nicely and not make a mess. You have to say sorry and help me clean. You have to eat your real soup and not your glue soup."

Anna and Ben say sorry and help Mom clean. They eat their real soup and feel sorry for their glue soup. They promise to not play with flour and water again. They hug Mom and say, "We love you, Mom. You are the best." Mom hugs them back and says, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. You are my sweeties."

Anna was an adventurous girl who liked to explore new places. She had a white cat named Snowy who followed her everywhere. One day, Anna saw a big hill behind her house. She wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.

"Can I go to the hill, Mommy?" Anna asked.

Mommy looked at the hill and frowned. "It is too far and too high, Anna. You might get lost or hurt. You can play in the yard, but not on the hill."

Anna was sad. She really wanted to see the hill. She looked at Snowy and whispered, "Do you want to go to the hill, Snowy?"

Snowy meowed and nodded. He was adventurous too.

Anna waited until Mommy was busy in the kitchen. Then she grabbed her backpack and put Snowy inside. She sneaked out of the house and ran to the hill. She did not allow Mommy to stop her.

Anna and Snowy climbed the hill. It was hard and steep, but they did not give up. They reached the top and looked around. They saw a big lake, a forest, and a rainbow. They were amazed and happy.

"Wow, Snowy, look at this!" Anna said.

"Meow, meow, meow!" Snowy said.

They decided to go down and explore the lake. They did not know that Mommy had seen them from the window and was following them. She was worried and angry.

"Anna, Snowy, come back here right now!" Mommy shouted.

Anna and Snowy heard Mommy and turned around. They saw her running towards them. They were scared and sorry.

"Mommy, we are sorry. We just wanted to see the hill. It is so beautiful here." Anna said.

Mommy reached them and hugged them. She was relieved and glad. "I know, Anna, but you should not go without telling me. It is dangerous and rude. You could have been hurt or lost. I love you and I want you to be safe and happy. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded and said, "I understand, Mommy. I love you too. I am sorry for making you worry."

Snowy meowed and rubbed his head against Mommy's leg. He was sorry too.

Mommy smiled and said, "It's okay, Anna, Snowy. I forgive you. But next time, you have to ask me first. And maybe we can go to the hill together, okay?"

Anna and Snowy agreed. They said goodbye to the hill and the lake and the rainbow. They followed Mommy back to the house. They learned their lesson and promised to be more careful and respectful. They were still adventurous, but they also allowed Mommy to guide them.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally. She was three years old and liked to take naps. One day, Sally was walking with her mom when they saw an old, rock house. 

Sally's mom said, "Wow, look at that rock house. It looks very old."

Sally smiled and said, "I want to go in."

Her mom laughed and said, "No, that house looks very silly and stupid. We can't go in there."

But Sally was very determined and said, "Please, Mommy. I can nap in the rock house."

Her mom thought for a moment and said, "Ok, but if you are going to nap there, you must be very careful."

So, Sally went into the rock house and laid down. She was very sleepy, but before she could take her nap, a big spider came out of the corner. Sally screamed, but then the spider waved at her with all its legs. 

Sally smiled and said, "Hi, spider. I'm not scared of you, so you can be my nap friend." 

The spider waved again, and Sally closed her eyes and fell into a deep, comfortable nap.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man who had lots of money. He lived in a big house and owned many fancy things. He was very wealthy. One day, he decided to take a walk in the park. As he walked, he saw a little boy who looked sad. The rich man asked the boy what was wrong. The boy said he wanted a toy, but his family didn't have enough money to buy it. The rich man felt bad for the boy and decided to pass him some money to buy the toy. The little boy was so happy and thanked the rich man. The rich man realized that luxury wasn't as important as helping others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted a red waffle for breakfast, but her mom said they didn't have any. Lily felt sad and started to cry. 

Her mom tried to make her feel better by offering her pancakes, but Lily still wanted a red waffle. She stomped her feet and yelled, "I want a red waffle!"

Her mom thought for a moment and then said, "I have an idea! Let's make our own red waffles!" Lily's face lit up with excitement and they went to the kitchen to make the waffles together. 

They mixed the batter, added red food coloring, and cooked the waffles until they were crispy and delicious. Lily was so happy that she got her red waffle and she hugged her mom tightly. From that day on, they made red waffles every weekend and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug named Benny. Benny loved to crawl around in the grass and play with his bug friends. One day, Benny saw something shiny in the sky. It was a missile! Benny didn't know what a missile was, but he knew it didn't look friendly.

Benny ran to his friend, Ladybug. "Ladybug, there's a shiny thing in the sky and I don't like it," Benny said. "It's a missile," Ladybug said, "and it's coming towards us. We need to hide." Benny and Ladybug crawled under a leaf to hide from the missile.

After a while, they peeked out and saw that the missile had gone away. "Phew, that was close," Benny said. "I'm glad we're safe." "Me too," Ladybug said. "But we need to be careful. There are ignorant creatures out there who might not care about our safety." Benny nodded, knowing that he needed to be more careful in the future.

Kevin was sad as he watched his brother play. He had wanted to play but he had to do math instead.
He sighed and looked at the paper with all the black numbers. He knew he had to do it but he didn't want to.
Just then his brother came over and said, "What's wrong Kevin?"
Kevin replied, "I don't want to do math. It's too hard."
His brother smiled and said, "Don't worry Kevin. You'll get it done. Just take it one step at a time."

Kevin smiled back and felt a little better. He started to do the math and all of a sudden he understood it and it didn't seem so hard. He felt proud and happy.

When his brother found out, he smiled and said, "I told you so! See, math isn't so bad!" But Kevin just shook his head and said, "I wished I hadn't wasted so much time. I should have just trusted you."

Kevin always regretted not listening to his brother more often. He had learnt that math wasn't as bad as it seemed and would never forget that lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy gave her a package to examine. It was a big, brown package with a silly smiley face on it.

Lily was so excited to open the package, but she didn't know how. She asked her mommy, "Can you help me open it, please?"

Her mommy said, "Sure, let's see what's inside!" They carefully opened the package together.

Inside the package, there was a silly toy that made Lily laugh. She hugged her mommy and said, "Thank you for the package, mommy. I love it!"

Once upon a time, there was a big, intelligent cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to play with her toy mouse and eat tuna for dinner. One day, Mittens saw a little bird outside her window. She meowed and said, "Hello birdie, do you want to play with me?"

The bird chirped and said, "No, thank you. I am afraid you might eat me since you are a cat."

Mittens replied, "Don't worry, I promise I won't eat you. I just want to be your friend."

The bird thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I will be your friend. But you have to promise to release me if I ever get scared."

Mittens agreed and they became friends. They played together and shared tuna for dinner. Mittens kept her promise and never tried to eat the bird. They had lots of fun together and lived happily ever after.

Nina was a chubby three year old girl with a big, bright smile. She loved going on walks with her parents in the park. One day, Nina asked her mom if they could do something more exciting than walking. Her mom said, "Sure, let's go for a jog!" 

So Nina and her mom put on their trainers and started to run around the park. Nina really enjoyed it and laughed as she ran. Each time she passed by a tree, she patted it as she jogged past. 

When they finished their jog, Nina thanked her mom for taking her on the run. She was so happy to have gone jogging and couldn't wait to do it again.

Once there was a mom and a boy. The boy asked his mom to listen to some jazz. She said, "ok".

The boy put on the jazz and it made him happy. He started to dance around the room. He was so light and the music was so good.

But then something happened. His mom said it was too loud and asked him to separate from the music. The boy didn't want to, so he said no. His mom got mad and said he had to separate from the music now. The boy was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then it happened. His mom made him separate from the music. The boy was alone and felt terrible. He tried to play the music again, but his mom told him he had to stop.

The boy was so sad. He wanted to listen to the jazz and dance, but his mom said no. He knew he had to separate from the music and never listen to it again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play in the park with his friends. One day, Spot's owner asked him to deliver a bone to his friend's dog. Spot was very excited to help and ran as fast as he could to deliver the bone.

On the way, Spot heard a loud noise coming from a construction site. It was very nosy and scared him a little. But Spot was a brave dog and continued on his way to deliver the bone.

Finally, Spot arrived at his friend's house and delivered the bone. His friend was very happy and thanked Spot with a wag of his tail. Spot felt proud of himself for being such a good helper. And even though he was a little scared of the nosy noise, he knew he could always be brave and help his friends.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide on the big slide. It was fun and fast. They took turns to go down the slide and laugh.

But then they saw a man with a big box. He put the box on a bench and went away. Anna and Ben were curious. They went to the bench and looked at the box. It smelled good. They opened the box and saw pizza. It had cheese and pepperoni and sauce. They were hungry.

"Let's take a slice," Anna said. "The man won't notice."

Ben nodded. He liked pizza. They each took a slice and bit into it. It was warm and yummy. They ate the whole slice and licked their fingers.

But then they heard a voice. It was the man. He came back to the bench and saw the open box. He looked angry.

"Hey, who ate my pizza?" he shouted. "That was my lunch!"

Anna and Ben felt guilty. They knew they did something bad. They ran away from the bench and hid behind the slide. They hoped the man would not find them. They were sorry they took his pizza. They decided not to do it again.

John was excited. He was going to design something cool! He thought really hard about what he should make. Then it hit him - a cooler! He set to work and drew the plans for his cooler.

John was very careful when it came to cutting the pieces for his cooler. He made sure to measure them very accurately so that they would fit together perfectly. He was careful not to make any mistakes.

When it was time to put it all together, John was thrilled with the result. His cooler was a perfect size and he was so proud of himself for his hard work. He couldn't wait to show it to all of his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a blue cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with her friends in the park. One day, Kitty saw a big ball near a tree. She wanted to grab the ball and play with it.

Kitty ran to the ball and said, "Ball, let's play together!" The ball did not say anything. So, Kitty grabbed the ball and started to play. But, the ball was not happy. It was sad because it belonged to a little boy named Timmy.

Timmy saw Kitty playing with his ball and started to cry. He walked up to Kitty and said, "Kitty, that's my ball. Give it back, please!" Kitty did not want to give the ball back. She liked it too much. So, she grabbed Timmy's ear and ran away.

Timmy was very sad and hurt. His ear was red and he did not have his ball. Kitty did not care. She kept playing with the ball, but deep down she knew she did something bad. In the end, Kitty lost all her friends because they did not want to play with a mean cat.

Tim was feeling very nervous. He didn't like to talk in front of big crowds. Everyone was watching him and he felt scared. He just wanted to be alone and hide.

But Tim couldn't hide. He heard his mom calling him to talk in front of the crowd. He was so afraid that he started to cry. But he didn't want to look silly in front of everyone, so he wiped his tears away and slowly stepped forward.

He was shocked to see all the junk in the room. There were all sorts of broken toys and trash strewn about. He realized it was a junkyard, and he felt even more nervous. He wanted to go back home, but his mom was encouraging him forward.

Timmy had an idea. He took the rake and used it to make a lot of noise. The man stopped printing and looked at Timmy. Timmy smiled and said, "Thank you for stopping the noise. Now I can play in the leaves." The man smiled back and said, "You're welcome. Have fun!" Timmy was happy and jumped in the leaves. He loved how the light shined through the leaves.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Tweety. Tweety had a friend named Daffy, who also had wings like Tweety. One day, Tweety and Daffy were flying in the sky, looking for some food to eat.

Suddenly, they saw an orange fruit hanging from a tree. Tweety said, "I want to eat that orange fruit." But Daffy disagreed, saying "No, I want to eat something else." 

Tweety decided to listen to Daffy and they flew away to find another fruit. As they were flying, they saw a big tree with lots of fruits. They were happy and started to eat the fruits. Tweety said to Daffy, "I'm glad we didn't eat that orange fruit. These fruits are much better!" 

From that day on, Tweety and Daffy always agreed on what to eat and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a teacher who wanted to help others. He wanted to teach them to do lots of things. He gave them tools to make things. One day, he showed them how to use fire. He showed how to light a match and how to put wood on the fire. He showed how to keep the fire burning.

The children watched with wide eyes as the flames reached up and danced. They were amazed by the heat and the light. The teacher said that the fire was useful for many things. He said it could help them cook food, light their way in the dark and keep them warm.

The teacher was very pleased with what he had taught them. The children had learned a valuable lesson and they felt happy. They thanked the teacher and then they went home. From then on, they could light a fire whenever they wanted, and they would always remember the useful lesson he had taught them.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a girl named Lucy. She loved to wear her favorite blouse. It was red with little flowers on it. One day, she saw a boy with an unknown toy. It looked like so much fun! Lucy wanted to play with the toy too.

Lucy asked the boy if she could play with his toy. The boy said no, but Lucy did not listen. She tried to push the boy to get the toy. The boy got very sad and started to cry. Lucy's mom saw what happened and came to help.

Lucy's mom told her that pushing is not nice. She said, "We should always be kind to others and share our toys." Lucy felt bad for making the boy cry. She said sorry to the boy and gave him a hug. From that day on, Lucy always remembered to be kind and share her toys. And they all played happily together.

Tom and Lily are playing in the garden. They have a big box and some paper. They want to make a surprise for Mom.

"Let's wrap the box with paper and put a bow on it," says Tom. "Mom will think it is a present."

"Good idea," says Lily. "But what will we put inside the box?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He sees a frog hopping near the pond. He runs and catches it. "How about this?" he says, holding the frog.

Lily screams. "No, Tom, no! Mom does not like frogs. They are slimy and hoppy. She will be scared."

Tom laughs. "But it will be funny. Come on, Lily, help me put the frog in the box."

Lily shakes her head. "No, Tom, no. I will not help you. That is not nice. Mom will be sad."

Tom shrugs. He does not listen to Lily. He puts the frog in the box and closes the lid. He wraps the box with paper and puts a bow on it. He is very proud of his surprise.

He carries the box to the porch. He sees Mom coming from the kitchen. He hides the box behind his back. "Hi, Mom," he says. "I have something for you."

Mom smiles. She loves Tom and Lily. She thinks they are smart and sweet. She wonders what they have made for her. "What is it, Tom?" she asks.

Tom gives her the box. "It is a present, Mom. Open it and see."

Mom takes the box. She feels something moving inside. She hears a croak. She is curious. She opens the lid.

The frog jumps out of the box and lands on Mom's face. Mom screams. She drops the box and the frog. She runs into the house.

Tom laughs. He thinks it is funny. Lily cries. She thinks it is not funny.

Mom comes back from the house. She is angry. She sees Tom and Lily. She sees the box and the frog. She knows what Tom has done.

"Tom, that was not a nice surprise. That was a mean trick. You scared me and made me sad. You need a time out. Go to your room and lock the door. And don't come out until I say so."

Tom stops laughing. He feels sorry. He knows he has been bad. He goes to his room and locks the door. He wishes he had listened to Lily.

Lily goes to Mom. She hugs her. She says she is sorry. She says she loves her.

Mom hugs Lily. She says she loves her too. She says she is not mad at her. She says she is smart and sweet.

They go to the kitchen. They make some cookies. They share them with Tom when he comes out of his room. They say they are sorry. They say they love him.

They are a happy family again. They do not play with frogs anymore.

Once upon a time, there were three friends. One was called Joe, one was called Sara, and the other was called Tom.

One Wednesday, Joe and Sara looked at Tom with big eyes as he told them he was going to marry someone. "Who?" asked Sara. "Her name is Lucy," replied Tom.

Joe and Sara were so happy! Lucy was so kind and brilliant. They were sure that it was a perfect match. The three friends all hugged and said goodbye, so Tom could go and live with his new family.

Joe and Sara went to see the wedding. They were so excited! On the day of the wedding, everyone looked so happy and beautiful. Joe and Sara's eyes twinkled as the minister said, "You are now married!" 

The night ended with music and dancing. Joe, Sara and Tom all hugged each other and thanked their lucky stars for such a brilliant day.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy puppy. The grumpy puppy did not like anyone. No one had ever been nice to the puppy and it made the puppy sad.

The puppy didn't know what to do, so it wandered around town all day long. One day the puppy bumped into a kind and caring little girl. The girl looked down at the grumpy puppy and said, "Hi there little pup! What's your name?"

The puppy looked up and said, "I don't have a name." The little girl smiled and said, "Well, I will call you Snowball. How does that sound?"

Snowball liked the sound of its new name. The little girl reached out her hand to Snowball and said, "Come on, you can come home with me."

The grumpy puppy was so happy! The little girl took Snowball home and looked after it every day. She gave Snowball cuddles, took it for walks, and fed it the best food. Now Snowball was no longer grumpy!

The little girl and Snowball were best friends. Everywhere they went, people could tell they cared for each other. It was a truly special bond.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. Every day Mia went for a walk with her mom. One day, Mia and her mom were walking when they saw two dogs fighting. Mia was scared and hid behind her mom. "It's okay, Mia," said her mom, "Those two dogs are just fighting." 

Mia looked at the dogs and saw one was white and the other was brown. She wanted to help. "Mom, what can I do?" She asked. 

Her mom said, "We can do something to help the dogs. Let's make a clear saltwater solution." Mia was excited. She grabbed the bowl and filled it with water, while her mom added some salt. Mia stirred it until it was all mixed up. 

The mom poured the clear salt water between the two dogs. It helped stop the fight. Mia smiled and hugged her mom. It was a happy ending!

Joseph found a battery on the ground in the park. He picked it up and brought it home.

When he got home, he showed his mom and dad what he had found. "What can I do with this battery?" Joseph asked. 

"We can use it to power something," said mom.

Joseph thought for a moment but he couldn't stay what he wanted to power. His parents smiled at each other. 

"Let's put it in this toy car," said dad. "Then your car can stay moving all day!" 

They put the battery in the toy car. 
Joseph and his parents stepped outside and the car started moving. It was hot outside, but the car kept going! 

Joseph was so excited that he jumped up and down in the park. His parents laughed and joined in. 

The battery kept going and going until it was almost dark outside. Then they took the battery out and brought it back inside. 

Joseph put the battery away and went to bed. He couldn't wait until tomorrow to put the battery back in the toy car and play with it again.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old.

One day, Lucy saw a butterfly flutter past her. It was very slow and the colours were very pretty. Lucy laughed and joked about chasing the butterfly.

She ran after it, but the butterfly was too fast. She stopped to rest and noticed some butter on the ground. "I can make a joke with this butter," thought Lucy.

She laughed as she put the butter on her nose and pretended to be a butterfly. She moved around very slowly, just like a real butterfly. Everyone who saw laughed and joked with her. Everyone had so much fun that day!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a bald head and loved to play with his silver toy car. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. Timmy ran around and played on the swings and slides, but he got tired. His mom told him to relax on a bench while she got him a snack. Timmy sat down on the bench and looked at his silver toy car. He felt happy and relaxed as he played with it. After his snack, Timmy went back to playing and had a fun day at the park. The end.

One day, a small boy called Sam found a kite in the park. He was so happy to see it! He ran to get it and started to fly it.

Suddenly, an old man came over and told him, "Stop! You're disturbing me!" Sam was so scared.

The old man had a very gentle voice. He said, "This kite belongs to me. I lost it a long time ago." Sam was sorry to hear this and apologised to the old man.

The old man was very compassionate. He said, "I'm happy that you found it. Do you want to keep the kite? You can fly it whenever you want". 

Sam was overjoyed that the old man was so kind. He thanked him a hundred times and flew away with the kite. He had a wonderful time in the park, flying his kite with a compassionate old man.

Molly and her daddy were having a picnic. Molly loved being in the park. Daddy had laid down a red and white blanket and Molly was munching on a delicious apple.

Suddenly there was a loud noise. "What was that?" Molly asked.

Daddy smiled. "It was just a gentle squeak," he said. "It's coming from the file."

Molly craned her neck around in surprise. She saw a big box-shaped file, its lid left ajar.

"What's inside the file?" Molly asked curiously.

"Just some papers," said Daddy. "But it's important to keep them still so that they don't disturb anyone."

Molly nodded in understanding. "So, we have to be gentle with the file?" she asked.

"Yes, exactly," Daddy said with a smile.

Molly carefully closed the file, then she and her daddy settled back down on their picnic blanket to finish their lunch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside and picking flowers. One day, Lily fell and hurt her arm. It hurt so much that she had to go to the hospital. 

At the hospital, Lily met a kind nurse named Sarah. Sarah had a white uniform and a big smile. She helped Lily feel better and gave her a lollipop. 

Lily's mommy was worried and asked the doctor if Lily would be okay. The doctor said that Lily's arm was broken, but it would heal soon. This news revealed that Lily would have to wear a cast for a little while. 

Lily was sad because she couldn't play outside with her friends. But her mommy and daddy bought her a new coloring book to keep her busy. Lily was happy again and drew lots of pictures of flowers.

Once upon a time, there was a big clown. He was very tall and had bright colors all over his face. When the clown walked around town, everybody got super excited. 

One day, a three year old child saw the clown walking on the street. He ran up to the clown and asked, "What are you doing here?" 

The clown smiled and said, "I'm coming to make you smile and laugh." 

The little kid's eyes lit up. He said, "Yay! You are going to make me excited?" 

The clown nodded and said, "Yes, I'm here to make you happy!" 

The little kid cheered and ran off to tell everyone that the big clown was in town. All the kids in town soon got very excited. 

The clown hugged each and every one of the kids and put on a show that made them laugh and smile for the rest of the day. The big clown made all the kids in town excited. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a pot. It was a very bright pot that glistened in the sunlight. The pot wanted friends but was very worried about being alone. He wished he could find someone who shared his love for the sun.

One day, the pot spotted a bright butterfly fluttering around the garden. The pot's worries melted away as the butterfly flew closer and closer. Finally, the butterfly landed on the pot's side and they became friends.

The butterfly and the pot shared many adventures in the bright sun. They jumped over streams, laughed in the breeze and swirled in circles around the garden. The pot never worried anymore, because he knew his friend the butterfly was always there to keep him company in the bright garden.

Once there was a poor little girl named Mary. Mary loved to kick around circles in the dirt. One day, Mary went to the park, kicked the circles around for a while, and got very tired. She decided to take a nap.

While Mary was sleeping, a beautiful fairy flew down from the sky and she said, "What a beautiful little girl! Here, I will give you a special present." She waved her magic wand and a big circle appeared.

Mary woke up, saw the big circle and asked, "What is this?"

The fairy said, "It's a magic circle. It will give you whatever you want. All you have to do is to kick the circle three times, and something special will happen." 

So Mary kicked the big circle three times, closed her eyes and when she opened them again, she was filled with joy! The magic circle had given her a bag of money, a beautiful house and a pet dog.

Mary looked up to the sky and thanked the fairy from the bottom of her heart. Now Mary was no longer poor, and she could enjoy kicking circles in the park for hours and hours!

Once upon a time there was a green copper car. This car was special because it could drive really fast. It was so fast that it felt like it was flying. Everyone wanted to drive it.

One day, a little boy got to ride in the green copper car. He was so happy. He said 'Wheeee!' as the car sped down the street. He laughed and clapped his hands as the wind blew through his hair.

The car went faster and faster. Soon it was going so fast that it felt like they were in outer space. The little boy was so amazed. He felt like he was in a dream.

Finally, the green copper car stopped and the little boy said 'again, again'. The car was so much fun! The little boy and the green copper car were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful rainbow. It shone in the sky each day, stretching from one side of the horizon to the other.

One day, the rainbow faded away and the sky was grey. Everyone was sad and the birds stopped singing.

But then the rain came and washed away the grey clouds. After the rain stopped, a new rainbow appeared. Everyone was so happy to see it return.

The rainbow was so bright and vivid, with all its colors available to everyone. The birds chirped and the sun shone.

The rainbow stayed in the sky all day and it lit up everyone's heart with happiness. Everyone knew that the rainbow would always return to brighten up the sky.

Once there was a girl named Minnie. She lived in her home with her mommy and daddy. But Minnie was feeling very anxious because her mommy and daddy had to separate. Minnie didn't understand what was happening, so she asked Mommy and Daddy why they had to separate.

Mommy and Daddy said that things weren't working out between them and it was time for them to go their own ways. Minnie was really sad because she loved them both so much.

The next day, Mommy and Daddy packed up their things and moved away from Minnie's home. Minnie was so sad. But then she ran to the window and waved at them. She knew that even though they had to separate, they would always love her no matter what.

Once upon a time there was a lonely turkey. He wanted a friend, but all of the other animals were scared of him because he was so big.

One day, the turkey had an idea! He would slide down a hill and the other animals would come out and watch him.

So the turkey ran to the top of the hill and then he started sliding down the hill.

The other animals were so amazed! They watched the turkey slide down the hill and started to clap and cheer for the turkey.

The turkey was so happy! He loved being cheered by the other animals and it made him feel less lonely.

From that day on, the turkey slides down the hill every day as all the other animals cheer him on and they all became friends.

Once there was a bunny who loved to hop. He liked hopping all around, especially in the sunshine. One day, while he was hopping, he saw a harmless pear nearby. He had never seen one before, so he hopped over to take a closer look.

He stood up on his hind legs and sniffed the pear. It smelled sweet and yummy. He wanted to take a bite, but he was a little bit scared. He called out to his friend, a bird named Chirpy, who was sitting near by in a tree.

"Chirpy, do you think this pear is harmless?" the bunny asked.

"Yes, I think it is!" Chirpy said. "You should take a bite!"

So the bunny hopped over to the pear and took a big bite. It was the best thing he had ever tasted! He hopped in circles, as he was so happy.

After that day, the bunny hopped over to that pear tree every day. It always had new, delicious pears to try. He felt so lucky to have such a harmless and tasty snack.

One day there was a persistent little girl named Molly. She wanted to find anything that was inside the refrigerator. She knew it was a big white box with a cold inside! But no matter how hard she tried, she just couldn't open it.

So Molly was very persistent and kept trying. She pushed, pulled, and even tried giving the refrigerator a big hug. But nothing seemed to work.

Finally, Molly's mom came to the rescue. She opened the refrigerator and showed Molly what was inside. Molly was very excited to see a bag of yummy apples and lots of cold milk.

Molly learned a valuable lesson that day. If you're persistent enough, you can do anything. And that's the story of Molly and the refrigerator!

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to look at the stars at night. They had a big window in their room where they could see the sky. Sometimes they saw a shooting star and made a wish.

One night, they saw a very bright star that was bigger than the others. They wondered what it was and wanted to know more. They asked their mom, who was reading a book in the living room.

"Mom, mom, what is that big star?" they said, running to her.

"That is not a star, my loves. That is the moon. It is very far away, but sometimes it looks bigger and brighter. It is called a full moon," mom explained.

"Wow, the moon is so pretty. Can we go there?" Lily asked.

"No, we cannot go there. It is too far and too cold. But we can look at it and enjoy its light," mom said.

"Can we touch it?" Tom asked.

"No, we cannot touch it. It is too high and too hard. But we can imagine how it feels and what it is made of," mom said.

Lily and Tom were very curious and had many questions. They kept asking mom about the moon and the stars. Mom was very patient and answered them as best as she could. She was happy to see them interested in the sky.

But soon it was time for bed. Mom told them to brush their teeth and put on their pajamas. Lily and Tom did not want to stop looking at the moon. They begged mom to let them stay up a little longer.

"Please, mom, please. Just five more minutes. We want to see the moon," they said.

"Sorry, my loves, but you have to go to bed now. It is late and you need to sleep. The moon will be there tomorrow night, too. And maybe you will see a shooting star and make a wish," mom said.

Lily and Tom were not happy. They did not want to miss the moon. They started to scream and cry. They threw a tantrum and kicked their feet.

"Stop, stop, stop. That is enough. You are being very naughty and rude. You have to listen to mom and do as I say. Go to bed now, or you will be in trouble," mom said, sternly.

Lily and Tom realized they had gone too far. They saw mom's angry face and heard her loud voice. They felt scared and sorry. They stopped screaming and crying. They said sorry to mom and gave her a hug.

"Sorry, mom. We love you. We love the moon, too. But we love you more," they said.

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She was not angry anymore. She was glad they apologized and calmed down. She kissed them good night and tucked them in.

"Good night, my loves. I love you, too. I love the moon, too. But I love you more," she said.

She turned off the light and left the room. Lily and Tom closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of the moon and the stars. And they hoped to see a shooting star and make a wish.

Once upon a time there was a ship. The ship provided a home for the people and animals on board. One day the ship sailed upon a dangerous ocean. There were storms and high waves which made it hard to stay safe. 

The ship couldn't provide everything the passengers and animals needed. They were so hungry and thirsty. They looked for land but it was hard to find. 

At last the ship came to some islands, and the people and animals were able to get the food and drink they needed. There were some dangerous places, but the people and animals stayed safe by following the captain's instructions. 

The people and animals were so thankful to the ship for providing them a safe home. They were all happy to be safe and to have enough food and drink.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play at the beach. They make sand castles and look for shells. Sometimes they go into the water, but not too far. They hold hands and jump over the waves.

One day, they see a big wave coming. It is bigger than the others. Tom is scared. He wants to go back to the sand. Lily is brave. She wants to stay in the water. She thinks the wave is fun.

"Come on, Tom, let's jump over the wave!" Lily says.

"No, Lily, let's go back! The wave is too big!" Tom says.

They pull each other, but they cannot agree. The wave is getting closer. They have to decide. They separate their hands and go different ways. Tom runs to the sand. Lily stays in the water.

The wave reaches Lily. It is not as big as it looked. It is gentle and soft. It lifts Lily up and down. Lily laughs and enjoys the ride. She feels the water on her skin and in her hair. She sees Tom on the sand. He looks sad and lonely.

"Lily, Lily, come back!" Tom shouts. He misses his sister. He is sorry he left her.

Lily hears Tom. She wants to go back to him. She waits for the wave to go away. Then she swims to the shore. She runs to Tom and hugs him.

"I'm sorry, Tom, I should have listened to you. The wave was not so fun without you." Lily says.

"I'm sorry, Lily, I should have stayed with you. The sand was not so fun without you." Tom says.

They smile and forgive each other. They are happy to be together again. They go back to the water and play with the waves. They hold hands and jump over them. They are twins and they are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a prince who was very brave and kind. One day, he left his kingdom to go on an adventure. As the prince walked in the light of day, he heard a voice that said â€œHello!â€

The prince looked around, but he didnâ€™t see anyone. Then he saw a small fairy peeking out from behind a tree. The prince was very surprised!

â€œWhat is your name?â€ asked the prince.

â€œMy name is Glimmer,â€ said the fairy. â€œWill you play with me?â€
