There was a girl who loved dolls. She always wanted to have them around. One day, she decided to go to the store and grab a new one. When she saw a beautiful independent doll, she was so excited! She quickly grabbed it and brought it home.

When she got home, she put the doll in her room. She loved it and played with it all the time. She hugged it and gave it lots of cuddles. She even talked to it like it was a real person.

The girl was always happy that she got such an independent doll. She was proud that her doll could stand up against all the other dolls. She felt very special when she had it around. She was so glad she grabbed it from the store.

Once there was a man and a woman. They went to the store to get some things. They saw a coffee shop and they decided to stop. The man and woman paused and looked around. The shop was hidden, because it was tucked away from the busy street.

The woman said she was thirsty, so the man went in to get a coffee for her. He came out with two cups of coffee. They both took a sip of the hot drink.

The woman said she liked the coffee and thanked the man. They smiled and paused again. They enjoyed the quiet moment together. The man and woman got up, finished their coffee and went on with their day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play chess with his grandpa. One day, Timmy's grandpa got very sick and had to go to the hospital. Timmy was very sad and missed playing chess with his grandpa.

But one day, Timmy's grandpa got better and his sickness started to heal. Timmy was very happy and went to visit his grandpa at the hospital. They played a game of chess and Timmy won! His grandpa was so proud of him.

From that day on, Timmy played chess with his grandpa every time he visited him at the hospital. And even though they were both very happy, they never forgot how sad they were when grandpa was sick.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Puddles. Puddles was always cold because he lived in an icy place. One day, Puddles went for a walk and saw a big iceberg. He imagined what it would be like to climb to the top of it.

As Puddles was walking back home, he saw a friendly seal named Sammy. Sammy winked at Puddles and said, "I have a surprise for you tomorrow!" Puddles was so excited that he couldn't sleep that night.

The next day, Sammy took Puddles to the top of the iceberg he had imagined climbing. Puddles was so happy that he gave Sammy a big hug. From that day on, Puddles and Sammy were the best of friends and they went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a mum and her little girl. The mum and the girl went on a walk together. The mum had a sweet treat in her pocket. It was a chunk of chocolate!

As they walked along, the girl saw a big balcony, she wanted to explore it. So the mum said yes and they climbed the stairs to the balcony. It looked over a big garden.

But then the mum saw something, it was a big patch of mud. The mum was worried, she wanted her little girl to stay safe. So mum said, I'll lead you away from the mud. The girl was sad, she wanted to play in the mud.

But mum said: come, let me lead you to a nice and safe place. The girl followed her mum and together they found a comfy spot. The girl was happy finally.

The mum then took out the piece of chocolate and gave it to the girl. The girl was so happy and grateful, she thanked her mum and enjoyed her special treat.

The mum was happy too, she felt good knowing that she had taken care of her little girl and given her something that made her so much joy.

One day, little black Timmy and his mom were walking in the park. Timmy wanted to run and play, but his mom said he needed to wait. He asked her why, and she explained that in the park, it's important to respect everyone else's opinion. 

Timmy noticed a big bully demanding that everyone else should do what he thought was right. Timmy's mom got angry and told him she wouldn't let him do that. 

Timmy went up to the bully and said: "Why don't you respect the opinion of others?" 

The bully laughed and said that his opinion was the only one that mattered. He demanded that everyone should do what he said. 

Timmy told the bully that it's important to respect everyone else's opinion. He said that everyone is allowed their own opinion, but no one should demand that others should do something. 

The bully was embarrassed and said he was sorry. He thanked Timmy for teaching him such a valuable lesson and for standing up for what was right. 

This story teaches us an important lesson - we should respect the opinion of others, and no one should demand that others should do something. Respect is what makes our world a better place.

One day Mommy, Daddy and Sarah went out to the beach. Sarah was very excited to find shells. She started looking up and down the beach and found some very interesting ones. Mommy asked Sarah which shell she thought was the most special. Sarah picked up a shiny white shell and said, "This one! Look at it shine!"

Daddy was very proud of Sarah and said, "You found a beautiful shell! Good job!"

Sarah smiled and said, "I'm going to keep it forever."

Mommy smiled and said, "I'm sure it will make you very happy each time you look at it." 

Sarah nodded and looked at the beautiful shell with a big grin on her face. She was so proud to have found such a special shell. She was sure it would always make her feel happy.

Once upon a time, there was a parrot named Sid. He was a brave parrot who wanted to learn to fly. Every day, he hopped from branch to branch of a nearby tree.

Sid's friend, a clever owl, said, "Sid, why don't you try to fly?" Sid was scared but the owl encouraged him to try. So, the parrot made a brave leap and tried to soar. But he fell to the ground.

The owl said, "Don't be afraid, Sid. You can do it. Just be patient. You will fly up high one day." Sid was sad but determined.

So each day, the owl encouraged Sid and kept telling him he could do it. Finally, on a sunny morning, Sid spread out his wings and flew away.

Sid thanked his friend the owl for being so patient and encouraging. Now, Sid is flying higher than ever. And every time he passes by, he says hello to his owl friend down below.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Hannah. She wanted to go on an adventure. So she gathered some friends and they planned to visit a special place. 

They got on a boat and sailed across the sea. After a long journey, they reached a wonderful island. It was full of treasures! They were so excited.

As they explored the island, they spotted a soft, furry treasure. It was a small bunny! They were very happy and took the bunny back to their boat. 

The bunny hopped around the boat, and the friends had lots of fun playing with it. Then the bunny went to sleep.

At the end of their visit, the friends said goodbye to their furry treasure and sailed away. They were grateful for the adventure and looked forward to their next visit.

Once there was a package. It was very attractive and hung from the wall. Inside the package was a mysterious gift.

Every day, a little girl would come to the package and try to open it. It didn't matter how hard she tried, it was too hard to open.

One day, the package spoke to the little girl. It said, "I have a special surprise inside for you. Hang me at a safe place and the surprise will be revealed."

The little girl was so excited that she found the perfect spot and hung the package there. Then, she stepped back and opened the package. Inside was a beautiful toy doll! The little girl was so happy that she hugged the package and thanked it for the wonderful surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who loved to eat bananas. He ate so many bananas every day that he became very big and strong. But one day, the monkey saw a sign that said "Beware of the banana peel!" The monkey was worried that he might slip and fall on a banana peel, so he decided to prevent this from happening by being very careful.

But one day, the monkey was walking on a path and he saw a banana peel on the ground. He tried to avoid it, but he slipped and fell down. The monkey hurt himself very badly and couldn't move. He was very sad and worried that he might never be able to eat bananas again.

The other animals in the forest tried to help the monkey, but it was too late. The monkey had hurt himself too badly and he passed away. All the animals were very sad and missed the monkey. They decided to prevent this from happening again by always being careful and watching out for banana peels.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn umbrella. He did not like to move around too much and would usually just stay in one place, even when the wind blew.

One day, the umbrella felt a little bored, so he decided to try something new. He stretched his arms wide and flew up into the sky! He soared around and around, feeling free and happy.

However, the wind was getting stronger and stronger and soon the umbrella found it hard to stay up in the sky. He tried really hard to stay above the clouds but eventually he had to come down.

The stubborn umbrella landed on the ground, feeling disappointed and tired. His arms were sore from all of the stretching and he was very tired. He decided that he had had enough stretching for today and that he would stay on the ground.

The wind eventually died down and the tired umbrella lay there, resting until he had enough energy to move again. He would never forget his fun adventure in the sky and he promised himself that he would try stretching and flying again soon.

Ben and Lily were playing in the living room. They liked to jump on the couch and pretend it was a boat. They had a furry toy dog that they took turns holding. The toy dog was soft and brown and had a squeaky nose.

"Let me have the dog, Lily!" Ben said. He tried to grab the toy from his sister, but she held on tight.

"No, it's my turn, Ben!" Lily said. She hugged the toy dog and stuck out her tongue.

Ben was angry. He wanted the toy dog very much. He thought of a way to make Lily give it to him. He leaned over and bit her arm hard.

"Ow! Ben, that hurts!" Lily cried. She dropped the toy dog and rubbed her arm. It had a red mark where Ben bit her.

Ben smiled and picked up the toy dog. He squeezed its nose and made it squeak. He thought he had won.

But then he heard a loud voice behind him.

"Ben, what did you do?" It was Mom. She had seen everything. She looked very mad.

Ben turned around and saw Mom's face. He felt scared. He knew he had done something bad. He wished he had not bitten Lily.

Mom took the toy dog from Ben and gave it back to Lily. She hugged Lily and said sorry. She told Ben to go to his room and think about what he had done. She said he could not play with the toy dog or the couch for a long time.

Ben walked to his room with his head down. He felt sad and sorry. He had lost his toy, his couch, and his sister. He had bitten more than he could chew.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely girl. She was sad, because she didn't have anyone to talk to. Suddenly, she noticed a whisper coming from the tree in her backyard. She listened carefully, and heard a voice. It said, "Come closer. I want to tell you a secret". Slowly, the girl approached the tree. 

The voice spoke again. It asked, "Do you like desserts?" The girl was surprised. She nodded her head and answered, "Yes, I do!". The voice laughed, and said, "Good! I have a special one that is just for you". The girl's eyes lit up, and she held out her hand. 

The voice seemed to hesitate, as if it was thinking of something. Then, suddenly, the voice said, "Look in the sky". She looked up, and saw a dull glimmer in the night sky. It twinkled and sparkled, and suddenly the sky lit up with colors. The girl couldn't believe her eyes! There was a beautiful dessert in the sky. 

The girl thanked the voice, and said goodbye. She grabbed the dessert and ate it. It tasted sweet and delicious. From then on, she was never lonely again. She would occasionally hear the voice again, and they would talk and share secrets.

Lily and Sam were playing in the backyard. They saw an elderly lady walking on the sidewalk. She had a big bag of mail in her hand. She looked tired and sad.

"Hello, lady," Lily said. "Do you need help with your mail?"

The lady smiled and nodded. "That's very kind of you, dear. I have to mail these letters to my family. They live far away and I miss them very much."

Lily and Sam took some letters from the bag and ran to the mailbox. They put the letters inside and closed the lid. They ran back to the lady and gave her a hug.

"Thank you, children," the lady said. "You made my day brighter. What are your names?"

"I'm Lily and this is Sam," Lily said. "We live in that house over there. Do you want to come and play with us?"

The lady looked at the house and saw a cut on the window. She frowned and asked, "What happened to your window?"

Lily and Sam looked at each other and lowered their heads. They had broken the window with a ball yesterday. Their mom was very angry and said they had to pay for it.

"We're sorry, lady," Sam said. "We were playing with our ball and it went too fast and hit the window. It made a big cut and a loud noise. We didn't mean to do it."

The lady touched their heads and said, "It's okay, children. Accidents happen. But you have to be careful and listen to your mom. She loves you and wants you to be safe."

Lily and Sam nodded and said, "We love our mom too. And we love you, lady. You're very nice and sweet. Can you be our friend?"

The lady smiled and said, "Of course, I can be your friend. And you can call me Grandma. I don't have any grandchildren of my own, but I would love to have you as mine."

Lily and Sam cheered and hugged the lady again. They took her hand and led her to their house. They introduced her to their mom and asked if they could play with her. Their mom said yes and thanked the lady for her help. The lady said she was happy to help and to meet them. They all went inside and had a good time. They played, talked, and laughed. They became good friends and called each other Grandma, Lily, and Sam.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable little girl. Every day, she would go to the garden to poke around in the dirt. One day, however, she saw something sparkly! She walked closer and saw a beautiful, shimmering veil! She was so excited, but she was scared, too. She poked it to make sure it was real. The veil was soft and strong and made the little girl feel calm. 

The little girl took the veil home and could not wait to show her family. When she arrived, her parents were very excited, too. They had a special use for the veil--they said it was for her wedding one day. 

The little girl held onto the veil for many years. She always knew she would be dependable and someday find someone she could trust to marry. Someday she would dress up in her special veil and celebrate her happiest day.

Sara liked to play in the attic. She found many old things there. Some were toys, some were clothes, some were books. She liked to display them on the floor and pretend they were hers.

One day, she found a big box in the corner. She opened it and saw a doll. The doll had long hair, a pretty dress and shiny shoes. Sara was happy. She took the doll out and hugged it. She wanted to display it with her other things.

But the doll was not nice. It had a mean face and sharp teeth. It bit Sara's arm and made her cry. Sara was scared and hurt. She threw the doll back in the box and ran away. She did not want to play in the attic anymore.

She went to her mom and showed her the bite. Her mom was worried and angry. She asked Sara where she got the bite. Sara told her about the doll in the attic. Her mom did not believe her. She thought Sara was lying.

She took Sara to the attic and opened the box. She wanted to see the doll. But the box was empty. There was no doll. Sara was confused and uncomfortable. She did not know where the doll went. She hoped it would not come back.

One day, Emily was sitting in her room. She was feeling calm. She picked up a piece of paper and a pencil. She wanted to write something on the paper.

Emily began to write. She wrote some lines on the paper, then she wrote a cloud in the sky. Emily smiled, she was very happy.

The cloud was big and fluffy, it made a beautiful shape. Emily felt peaceful when she looked at it. After some time, the cloud started to move away.

Emily kept writing. She wrote more clouds in the sky. They were different sizes and shapes. Emily was amazed by the beauty of them.

When Emily finished writing, she felt calm and happy. She looked at the clouds she had drawn and all the wonderful shapes they made. It was the best day ever!

Lily loved her dog, Spot. Spot was a big, brown dog who liked to run and play. But one day, Spot got sick. He did not want to eat or drink. He only wanted to sleep. Lily was very sad and worried.

She asked her mom, "What is wrong with Spot? Can we help him?"

Her mom said, "We need to take Spot to the veterinarian. The veterinarian is a person who helps sick animals. Maybe the veterinarian can make Spot feel better."

Lily and her mom put Spot in the car and drove to the veterinarian's office. The office was very organized. There were many cages with different animals inside. There were also many shelves with books and tools. The veterinarian came out and greeted them.

"Hello, I am Dr. Lee. What is your dog's name?" the veterinarian asked.

"His name is Spot. He is sick. He does not eat or drink. He only sleeps," Lily said.

The veterinarian nodded and said, "Let's take a look at him. I need to check his ears, his eyes, his nose, and his heart. You can stay with him and hold his paw. He might be scared, but I will be gentle."

Lily and her mom followed the veterinarian to a room. The veterinarian examined Spot and gave him some medicine. He told them that Spot had a fever and an infection. He said that Spot needed to rest and drink a lot of water. He said that Spot would feel better soon.

Lily was relieved and happy. She hugged the veterinarian and said, "Thank you, Dr. Lee. You are very nice. You helped Spot."

The veterinarian smiled and said, "You are very welcome, Lily. You are a good friend to Spot. He is lucky to have you. Take good care of him and bring him back for a check-up next week."

Lily and her mom thanked the veterinarian again and took Spot home. Spot was still tired, but he wagged his tail and licked Lily's face. Lily gave him some water and a soft blanket. She stayed with him and read him a story. She hoped that Spot would get well soon. She loved him very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to paint pictures with her mommy. One day, they went to the park to paint. Lily picked up her paintbrush and painted a pretty flower. 

Suddenly, Lily's mommy said, "Oh no! I left our picnic basket at home. We don't have any snacks." 

Lily said, "That's okay mommy. We can eat the ugly apples from the tree." 

Mommy smiled and said, "You're right, Lily. The apples may not look pretty, but they will still taste good." 

Lily and her mommy had a fun day painting and eating apples. They learned that sometimes things that look ugly can still be good.

Jack went to the beach with his mom. He couldn't wait to explore! His mom said, "Let's test the water. Is it too cold?" Jack was excited and waded in the water. It was just the right temperature!

Soon, Jack saw something shiny in the sand. He ran over to pick it up. It was a big, fancy oyster! "Wow Mom, look at this oyster! Can I keep it?" His mom smiled and said yes. 

Jack held the oyster in his hands and asked, "Can I open it?" His mom nodded. She said, "It's okay to try, but be careful!" Jack carefully pried the oyster open and found a shining pearl inside. He exclaimed, "Mom, look! I found a pearl in this fancy oyster!" His Mom smiled, "Wow, that was a fun test!"

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with blocks and make towers. One day, they find a new box of blocks. The blocks have symbols on them. Some have stars, some have circles, some have squares.

"Look, Tom, these blocks are different!" Lily says. "They have symbols. What do they mean?"

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe they are a code. Maybe we can use them to send messages," Tom says.

They start to build towers with the blocks. They try to make patterns with the symbols. They have fun.

But then, Lily's mom comes. She says it is time to go home. She says they have to clean up the blocks.

"Can we leave them like this, mom?" Lily asks. "We are making a code. We want to finish it."

"No, Lily, you have to be obedient. You have to put the blocks back in the box. You can play with them another day," Lily's mom says.

Lily and Tom are sad. They like their code. They don't want to break their towers.

But they are obedient. They listen to Lily's mom. They put the blocks back in the box. They say goodbye to each other.

"Maybe we can play with the blocks again tomorrow," Tom says.

"Maybe we can find out what the symbols mean," Lily says.

They smile. They are still friends. They still like to play with blocks.

Once upon a time there was a troubled boy. He was so sad he couldn't think of anything that could make him feel better. He sat outside and looked around him sadly.

Suddenly he heard music. He looked up and saw a group of people dancing. They were happy, and the boy couldn't help but smile.

The boy laughed and began to dance too. He moved his feet around in circles and jumped up and down. He felt much better.

But soon there was a loud noise and the boy stopped to listen. A big animal was making angry noises and coming closer and closer. The boy was scared and ran away as fast as he could.

The animal seemed to follow him though, and the boy ran harder and harder. He didn't know what was happening! The boy tried to remember what his mommy had taught him: in tough times, just keep dancing.

So the boy started to dance. He moved his feet around in circles and jumped up and down. The animal stopped to watch the boy's silly dance. And after a few moments it walked away, just like that! 

The boy was no longer scared. He was relieved and he laughed as he danced. He was sure he had faced the threat.

Mary and her mom were in the kitchen for dinner. Mary had a napkin in her hand and she dangled it in the air.

"What are you doing, Mary?" her mom asked, smiling.

Mary grinned and replied, "I'm playing with the napkin."

"Oh, let me see!" her mom said.

Mary handed the napkin to her mom and she hung it on her finger. It looked funny hanging there.

"It looks like a hairy little monster!" her mom laughed.

They both laughed and hugged each other. Mary hugged the napkin and hung it on her finger again. She giggled when she pretended it was talking. Mary and her mom were having so much fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her dog Spot. One day, while they were playing, Spot ran away.

Lily looked for Spot everywhere, but couldn't find him. She was very sad and started to cry. Suddenly, she saw an orange cat in the backyard. The cat looked hungry, so Lily gave him some food.

While she was feeding the cat, she heard a bark. It was Spot! He had been chasing the cat. Lily was so happy to see Spot again. She gave him a big hug and they played together. From that day on, Lily always made sure to feed the cat and watch out for Spot when they played outside.

Jack was feeling very frustrated because he had not been able to spin. His mom and dad had told him he was not ready yet and he wasn't allowed to spin.

One day Jack saw a jet flying in the sky. He was so excited. Jack wanted to go up in the sky to spin just like the jet. 

He climbed up on a hill and started spinning. He twirled around and around faster and faster until he could no longer stand up. He started to fall and got hurt.

Jack was so frustrated. He knew he shouldn't have tried to spin like the jet. He was too little. His mama and daddy were right. He felt sad and couldn't stop crying.

Tommy was excited. His mom bought him a new gray sweater. He couldn't wait to put it on. 

Tommy lay it on the bed and pulled it over his head. It fit perfectly. He loved the way it felt so soft and warm. 

Tommy ran outside in his new gray sweater. He felt so happy and proud. His friends saw it and said, "Wow Tommy, your gray sweater looks so cool!"

Tommy smiled and ran around with his friends. They had so much fun playing and their gray sweaters kept them warm when the sun went down. 

Tommy lay the sweater across the chair when he went to bed. He dreamed of all the fun he had in his new gray sweater that day.

Once there was a girl who liked to eat spicy food! Every day she would go to a restaurant and order something with lots of spicy flavors. One day, she noticed something different about the food that she ordered. There was a small print on the side of it!

The girl was very interested in the print, so she decided to remove it. She started to slowly peel the print away and was surprised by what she found underneath!

It was a message! The message said that if she ate the spicy food, she would feel more energy and become more active. The girl was very happy to hear this and decided to finish eating all the spicy food.

After she finished, the girl felt much better and she was able to do all the things she wanted to do! She was very happy that she had removed the print and found the message underneath.

Once there was a bald sailor. He loved being out on the water and was brave and strong. One day, he was alone in his boat, when a giant wave came and rocked it hard. He knew he needed to close the boat quickly before the wave could make it sink.

He screamed as he pulled and pushed on the latch. Finally, it snapped closed, and the wave bumped the boat, but it stayed safe.

The bald sailor smiled. He was so happy that he was able to close the boat quickly and stay safe. He knew how to handle the seas. He would continue to be a brave and strong sailor.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy fell down and hurt his knee. He cried and cried because it hurt so much. 

His mommy came over and picked him up. She hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. It's okay. I'm here to comfort you." She gave him a snack, a yummy apple, to make him feel better. 

After a little while, Timmy's knee started to feel normal again. He smiled and went back to playing with his toys. He was happy because his mommy was there to make him feel better.

Max was three years old and he loved being outside. He liked to play on the swings and run around in the garden. One day, he was playing when he saw a napkin lying on the ground. He picked it up and took it home. 

Max was so excited to show his mom what he had found. He wanted to surprise her, so he hid the napkin under his shirt. When he got home, he ran straight to his mom. He proudly showed her the napkin and she was impressed.

But then she said something that made Max feel stupid. She told Max that he had made a promise to not pick up any rubbish outside. She said he had broken his promise.

Max was sad. He had really wanted to surprise his mom with the napkin, but it had ended in disappointment. He knew he should keep his promises.

Tim and Sue were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big cross on the grass. It was shiny and had jewels on it.

"Wow, look at that!" Tim said. "It is so pretty. I hope we can have it."

"Me too," Sue said. "Maybe it is a gift for us. Let's go and take it."

They ran to the cross and picked it up. It was heavy and cold. They smiled and hugged each other.

But then, a man came out of the bushes. He was angry and scary. He had a big stick in his hand.

"Hey, you little thieves!" he shouted. "That is my cross. Give it back to me or I will hit you!"

Tim and Sue were afraid. They dropped the cross and tried to run away. But the man was faster. He caught them and hit them with his stick. He hurt them a lot. He took the cross and left them on the ground.

Tim and Sue cried and cried. They wished they had not taken the cross. They wished they had listened to their moms and dads. They were not grateful for what they had. They were sorry and sad.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play together. One day, they find a big bottle of shampoo in the bathroom. The shampoo is colorful. It has red, blue, green, and yellow stripes.

"Look, Tom, this shampoo is like a rainbow!" Sara says. "Let's play with it!"

Tom nods. He thinks the shampoo is pretty. They open the bottle and squeeze some shampoo on their hands. They rub the shampoo on their hair, their faces, their clothes, and the walls. They laugh and make bubbles.

But then, Mom comes in. She sees the mess. She is angry. She says, "Sara and Tom, what have you done? This shampoo is not for playing. It is for washing your hair. You have wasted the shampoo and made a big mess. You have to clean up and say sorry."

Sara and Tom feel bad. They know they did something wrong. They say sorry to Mom. They help her clean up the bathroom. They wash their hair with water. They learn their lesson. They do not play with shampoo again. They only use it when they need to wash their hair. They understand that shampoo is not a toy. It is a useful thing.

Lily liked to play with her dad's microscope. She wanted to see the tiny things that he looked at. One day, when dad was not home, she took the microscope from his desk and put it on the floor. She turned the knob and looked through the eye-piece.

"Wow!" she said. "I can see a bug! It has many legs and a long tail. It is moving very fast!"

She tried to catch the bug with her hand, but it was too small. She got an idea. She took a glass jar and put it over the microscope. She hoped the bug would go inside the jar.

She waited for a while, but the bug did not move. She got bored. She picked up the jar and shook it. She wanted to make the bug move.

"Stop!" a voice said. "You are hurting me!"

Lily was surprised. She looked at the jar and saw the bug talking to her. It had a tiny mouth and eyes.

"Who are you?" Lily asked.

"I am a microbe," the bug said. "I live in the microscope. You are not supposed to shake me. It makes me dizzy and sick."

"I am sorry," Lily said. "I did not know you could talk. I just wanted to play with you."

"Well, you can't play with me like that," the microbe said. "You are too big and rough. You are a tall girl. I am a small microbe. We are very different."

"Can we be friends?" Lily asked.

"Maybe," the microbe said. "But you have to be gentle and careful. And you have to put me back in the microscope. That is my home."

"OK," Lily said. "I will do that. But can I look at you sometimes?"

"Sure," the microbe said. "But only with your dad's permission. He knows how to use the microscope. He is a smart man."

"OK," Lily said. "Thank you for talking to me. You are a nice microbe."

"You are welcome," the microbe said. "You are a curious girl."

Lily smiled. She put the jar back on the microscope and lifted the lid. She saw the microbe wave at her. She waved back. She put the microscope back on the desk and ran to her room. She wanted to tell her dad about her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat. The cat was naughty and did not like to behave. She would often run away and explore outside.

One day, the cat started to explore near a drain. But it wasn't just any drain. It was a big drain and it suddenly opened, trapping the cat inside!

The poor cat was so scared. She screamed and mewed for help but no one could hear her. She was stuck!

Finally, a neighbor heard the cat's cries and called for help. But by the time the rescuers got there, it was too late. The cat had already drowned in the drain.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim wanted to build something special for his mom's birthday. He thought and thought about what to make. Then, he had an idea! He would build a big present for her.

Tim was worried. He didn't know if he could build the present all by himself. He asked his dad for help. Together, they found some big boxes, pretty paper, and a big bow. They worked together to make the present look nice.

When Tim's mom saw the present, she was so happy! She gave Tim a big hug and thanked him for the special gift. Tim felt proud that he could build something so nice for his mom. And he was no longer worried.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who had a goal. She wanted to go to the top of the mountain and see what was there. But the mountain was very high, and the path was long.

The girl began to climb and soon the sun went down. When it was dark, the girl stopped walking. She was tired and she was cold.

The girl began to weep. She was far away from her home and she was stuck. She didn't know what to do.

Then, after a while, the girl saw a light. It was coming from a big house at the top of the mountain. The girl walked towards the house and when she got there, she saw a kind woman. She gave the girl some food to eat and a warm bed to sleep in.

The kind woman said, "You can stay here tonight and then tomorrow you can keep climbing and reach your goal".

From that day, the girl never stopped believing in her goal. She kept climbing and she eventually reached the top of the mountain. And there, she saw the most beautiful view.

She was glad she stayed strong and never gave up. She was proud of her long journey and all she had accomplished.

Once upon a time, there were two small boys, Jack and Sam. They were playing with furniture in their room. Then Sam found a big, long string. He held it and said "Let's tie this string around the furniture!"

Jack said "That's stupid! We can't tie it around the furniture".

But Sam didn't listen. He said "I know what I'm doing", and he started tying the string around the furniture.

Jack was getting angry, but he didn't know what else to do. He said "Stop! This is not a good idea".

But Sam kept tying the string until he was done.

Finally, Jack said "See, I told you it was a stupid idea". 

But it was too late. The string was tied around the furniture and there was no way to untie it.

The two boys had to learn their lesson that not all ideas work out.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who opened the door to the outside. He was so excited to go out and play when he heard a strange buzzing sound. He looked around and saw a weird little creature. It was a mosquito! The boy wanted to catch it, so he tried to grab it but it kept flying away. He ran after it and followed it around the yard, trying to catch it. The mosquito was too fast, though and it flew away. The little boy was so disappointed but he also thought it was kind of funny. He laughed and went back inside. He never forgot the weird little mosquito that he tried to catch.

Once upon a time there was a sack. In the sack there was a welcome. It was a friendly welcome.

"Who is there?" asked the sack.
"It's me, your friend," replied the welcome.

The sack was so happy to have a friendly visitor. She opened to let the welcome inside.

The welcome was so excited to be inside. She thanked the sack and said, "This will be a very fun visit!"

The sack smiled and nodded in agreement. They spent the day playing and having lots of fun.

At the end of the day the welcome said her goodbyes and promised to come again soon.

The sack was very sad to see her friend go, but was happy because they made such wonderful memories together. And with this, the sack knew she had something special that she could always welcome back.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big mop in his house. He decided to play with it. Tim held the mop and started to march around the house. He marched up and down the halls, and he had so much fun.

As Tim marched, he met his friend, Sam. Sam asked, "What are you doing with the mop?" Tim said, "I'm marching with it, come and join me!" So, Sam found another mop and they both marched together. They were happy and laughed as they marched.

Soon, Tim and Sam felt cold. They stopped marching and went inside to warm up. Tim's mom saw them and said, "You two did a great job cleaning the floors with your mops while you were marching!" Tim and Sam smiled, happy to help. They learned that playing and helping can be fun at the same time.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little bird. It had pretty feathers and sang a sweet song. One day, the bird saw a big, juicy worm and tried to catch it. But the bird didn't see the big, bad cat sneaking up behind it.

The cat pounced and caught the bird in its sharp claws. The bird tried to fly away, but the cat was too strong. The bird's brain told it to keep trying, but it was too late.

The cat ate the bird and all the other animals in the forest were sad. They didn't want to make any noise, but they knew the bird deserved to be applauded for its beautiful singing. But now, there was nothing left to applaud.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to go to the theater. She asked her mom if she could go, but mom said no. The little girl was sad, but mom promised her a special surprise.

The next day, the little girl woke up early in the morning and mom took her to the theater. The little girl was so excited! The theater was so quiet and cozy.

They went inside and the little girl saw fairies, princes and princesses dancing on the stage. She smiled and laughed as she watched the show. 

At the end of the show, mom gave the little girl a special present. She was so happy and thanked her mom for the surprise. 

From then on, the little girl always remembered momâ€™s special promise to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie. She went to the mall with her mom and dad. When they got there, Susie saw a fake toy and shouted, "I want it!"

Her mom said, "No, Susie. It's fake. We need to get a real one."

Susie didn't like that and started to shout even louder, "I WANT IT!"

Her dad laughed and said, "Let's go find the real one!" 

So they all went off to find the real toy. Susie found it very quickly and shouted, "I found it!"

"That's great, Susie! Let's get it!," said her mom, and off they went to check out. 

When they got home, Susie was very happy. She smiled and hugged her new toy and said, "I love it! Thank you, Mom and Dad!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and singing songs. One day, she saw a trumpet in her toy box. She was so excited to try it out!

Lily picked up the trumpet and blew into it. It made a loud noise that made her giggle. Her mom heard the noise and came to see what was happening. "Wow, Lily! You're playing the trumpet!" her mom said.

Lily smiled and replied, "Yes, I'm trying to play it. It's so much fun!" Her mom was happy to see Lily so excited and they both danced to the music Lily made with her trumpet. From that day on, Lily played her trumpet every day and she became very good at it.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to travel and see new things. One day, they find a big train at the station. The train has many cars and a loud whistle. Tom and Sam want to ride the train.

They ask the man in the blue hat. He is the train driver. He says, "Do you have tickets?" Tom and Sam shake their heads. They do not have tickets. The train driver says, "Sorry, you cannot ride the train without tickets. But you can watch the train go."

Tom and Sam are sad. They want to ride the train. They go to the end of the station. They see the train start to move. The train makes a lot of smoke. The smoke is thick and black. It fills the air.
