He stayed there and waited until the sound stopped.

When the noise from the emergency finally ended, Toby crawled out from under the rock. He felt glad to be back to normal.

He heard a voice. It belonged to his best friend, a mouse named Marty.

"Hey, Toby. Did you hear that loud noise? What was it?" the mouse asked.

"It was an emergency," Toby replied. "But now it's all over and we can go back to living our normal life." 

Marty smiled and said, "Yes, we can!" 

Toby and Marty wandered off together, happy to be reunited and safe from the emergency.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw her neighbor, Mr. Smith, getting into his kayak. 

"Hello, Mr. Smith! Where are you going?" asked Lily.

"I'm going for a paddle in the lake," replied Mr. Smith.

Lily watched as Mr. Smith paddled away. She started to worry that he might fall out of his kayak. 

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean up the kitchen. When she opened the fridge, she saw that it was empty. 

"Mama, we need to go to the store. The fridge is empty!" said Lily.

So, they went to the store and bought some food. Lily was happy that the fridge was no longer empty.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she saw a peach tree in her neighbor's yard. She wanted to taste a peach, so she went to ask her neighbor if she could have one. Her neighbor said yes and told her to gather as many as she wanted.

Lily was excited and gathered a lot of peaches. She ate one and it was so juicy and delicious. But then she saw a squirrel who looked confused. The squirrel had been gathering nuts and acorns for the winter, but Lily had taken all the peaches from the tree. She didn't realize that she had taken away the squirrel's food.

As winter approached, the squirrel couldn't find enough food to survive. Lily felt very bad and realized that she should have only taken a few peaches instead of all of them. She learned that it's important to think about others and not just ourselves. The story has a sad ending because the squirrel didn't have enough food and couldn't survive the winter. The moral of the story is to be kind and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, Nemo saw a piece of gum floating in the water. He thought it looked yummy, but his mom told him not to eat it because it was bad for him.

Nemo was feeling adventurous and wanted to explore the wild ocean. He decided to dive deep down to see what he could find. As he swam deeper, he saw all kinds of colorful fish and plants. He even saw a big, scary shark! Nemo quickly swam away and made it back to his home safely.

From that day on, Nemo learned that it's important to listen to his mom and not eat things that aren't good for him. He also realized that the ocean can be a wild and exciting place, but it's important to be careful and stay safe.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play with their toys in the park. One day, they find a big box. They open the box and see many shiny things inside. They see a cell, a watch, a necklace, and a ring.

"Wow, look at these!" Sam says. He picks up the cell and presses some buttons. "This is fun!"

"I want the cell too!" Mia says. She tries to grab the cell from Sam. "Give it to me!"

"No, it's mine!" Sam says. He holds the cell tight. "You can have the watch!"

"I don't want the watch, I want the cell!" Mia says. She pulls the cell hard. "Let go!"

They both pull the cell and fight. The cell breaks in half. They hear a loud beep. They see a red light on the cell.

"Oh no, what did we do?" Sam says. He drops the cell. "Is it broken?"

"I don't know, maybe it's a bomb!" Mia says. She runs away. "Help, help!"

A man comes to the park. He sees the box and the cell. He is angry. He is a spy. The cell is his. It is a dependable cell. He needs the cell to talk to his boss. He sees Sam and Mia.

"Hey, you kids, what did you do to my cell?" he says. He runs after them. "Give it back to me!"

Sam and Mia are scared. They run to their moms. They tell them what happened. Their moms hug them and take them home. They say they are sorry. They learn not to touch things that are not theirs. They hope the spy will not find them. They hope the cell will not explode.

Little Jack was worried about his new tooth. It had been very difficult to manage and was hurting a lot. He went to his mum for help.

"Mum, my tooth is so difficult! It hurts a lot," Jack said.

"Oh, sweetheart, let me take a look," his mum replied. She looked at Jack's tooth and noticed it was very loose.

"It looks like it might be loose," she said. "We need to see the dentist, so he can help manage it."

Jack was scared and didn't know what the dentist would do. He was scared he would make it worse.

"It's okay, Jack," his mum said, seeing the worry on his face. "The dentist will make it better. He will help manage your tooth so it stops hurting."

Jack still felt scared, but he knew he had to go to the dentist. With his mum's help, he would manage the difficult tooth.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her colorful cubes. One day, Lily's mom came into her room and saw all of her cubes scattered on the floor. 

"Lily, we need to organize your cubes," said her mom.

"What does organize mean?" asked Lily.

"It means to put things in their proper place," replied her mom.

Lily and her mom started to put the cubes in a neat pile. "Look, now they're all in order!" exclaimed Lily. 

After they finished organizing, Lily's mom said, "Let's have a snack. I made some delicious cookies." 

Lily's eyes lit up with excitement as she munched on the tasty treats. "These cookies are so yummy!" she exclaimed. 

From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her cubes organized and enjoyed delicious snacks with her mom.

Sam had a watch that he liked very much. It was blue and shiny and it made a tick-tock sound. He wore it every day and showed it to his friends. He felt mighty with his watch.

One day, a man came to his house. He had a big bag full of toys and books. He said he wanted to sell them to Sam and his mom. He saw Sam's watch and said, "What a nice watch you have! Do you want to trade it for something in my bag?"

Sam looked at the bag and saw many things that he wanted. He saw a red car, a yellow ball, a green dinosaur, a brown bear, and a big book with pictures. He thought they were all very fun and cool. He said, "Yes, I want to trade my watch for something in your bag. What can I have?"

The man smiled and said, "You can have anything you want, but only one thing. Choose wisely, because you can't change your mind later." He opened the bag and let Sam see all the things inside.

Sam thought hard. He liked his watch, but he also liked the toys and books. He wanted to have them all, but he knew he had to pick one. He looked at the red car, the yellow ball, the green dinosaur, the brown bear, and the big book. He wondered which one he would play with the most. He wondered which one would make him feel mighty.

He decided to trade his watch for the big book. He liked books because they had stories and pictures that he could look at and read. He thought the book would make him learn new things and have new adventures. He said, "I want the big book, please."

The man nodded and said, "Okay, here you go. Give me your watch and take the book. It's a fair trade." He took Sam's watch and gave him the book. He said, "Thank you, Sam. Enjoy your book. Goodbye." He left with his bag and Sam's watch.

Sam opened the book and saw many pages with words and drawings. He felt happy and excited. He said, "Mom, look at my book! It's so big and nice! Can you read it to me?"

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, Sam. I'm glad you like your book. It looks very interesting. Let's sit down and read it together." She hugged him and said, "You are a mighty boy, Sam. You made a good choice."

Once there was a girl called Joy. Joy was three years old. She loved to explore and adventure. One day, Joy decided to explore a chamber she hadn't seen before. As Joy entered the chamber, she noticed everything had a purple tint. She looked around in wonder. In the corner of the chamber Joy noticed a box. She walked closer and slowly opened the box. Inside, Joy found a purple stuffed animal. She moved closer to it and picked it up. Joy hugged the purple stuffed animal and decided to accept it as her friend. She named it Purpley. Joy and Purpley explored the chamber together and had a lot of fun. Joy loved her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a good cat named Tom. Tom had a big pen with lots of ink. He loved to draw with his pen. He would draw all day and all night.

One day, Tom saw a little bird who needed help. The bird was lost and could not find its way home. Tom wanted to care for the bird. So, he took the bird to his house and gave it food and water.

Tom had an idea. He used his ink and pen to draw a map for the bird. The map showed the bird how to get back to its nest. The bird was very happy and thanked Tom. Tom felt good because he helped the bird. They became the best of friends.

Timmy was cool. He liked to wear his cool clothes, no matter what. Today, he had on his favorite red shirt and blue pants.

Timmy wanted adventure. He wanted to feel the wind in his hair and the sun on his face. He wanted to find something new and exciting.

Looking around Timmy spotted a bull. It was a big and strong bull. He was wearing a bell around his neck, and it jingled as he walked. Curiosity overcame Timmy, and he walked over to the bull.

The bull stood still and let Timmy pet him. Timmy was amazed and filled with awe. He had found something new and cool!

After a few moments, the bull started to walk away, and Timmy followed him until he got to the farmer's stable. He said his goodbyes and ran back home with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sally. She liked to play with her doll named Lucy. One day, Sally met a boy named Tom. Tom had a toy car. They played together and had fun.

Sally said to Tom, "I want to marry you." Tom said, "OK, let's marry." They played a game where they pretended to be married. They had a big party with their toys.

But then, a bad dog came. The dog took Lucy and the toy car. Sally and Tom said, "No, bad dog!" They chased the dog and got their toys back. They were happy and played together again.

Once there was a family who took a trip to the river. The dad had a bright idea; they would all march to the river. The kids were excited to march, so they all ran quickly on the path. 

The mom noticed something strange ahead on their path. It was a big dark cloud! The dark cloud was growing bigger and bigger. The mom was worried and she knew they had to hurry. So they marched faster to the river. 

When they finally getting close to the river, the dark cloud started to rain. The family was getting soaked and they ran as fast as they could to the river. 

Once they got to the river, they couldn't believe their eyes! The river was overflowing and it was impossible to cross. The kids were so very ashamed. They thought they would never even get close to the river. 

But then, the dad had an idea. He took out a rope and tied it to a nearby tree. Everyone grabbed the rope and held on tight. As the dad moved the rope back and forth, the family crossed the river. The kids couldn't believe it! 

The family was so happy that they all made it safely to the other side. The dad had saved them from the rain and the river! They were proud and grateful and marched back home, all safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mom gave her a calendar to hang on her bedroom wall. Lily thought the calendar was pretty.

The next day, Lily went outside to play with her friends. They were having fun playing tag when they saw a scary dog. The dog was barking and growling, and it looked like it wanted to bite them. Lily remembered the calendar on her wall and knew what to do.

She ran back to her house and grabbed the calendar off her wall. She ran back to her friends and held the calendar up like a shield. The dog came running towards them, but Lily kicked the calendar at the dog. The calendar hit the dog, and it ran away yelping.

Lily and her friends were safe, and they all cheered for Lily's quick thinking. From that day on, Lily knew that her calendar was more than just pretty â€“ it could also be used to protect her from scary things.

Once upon a time, there was a little, red train. The train was very sad and miserable. It could not go fast like the other trains. It wanted to be fast and strong, but it was slow and weak.

One day, a kind, old man saw the sad train. He said, "Do not be sad, little train. I can help you." The old man worked hard to fix the train. He put new steam inside the train. The train started to feel better.

After the old man fixed the train, it was not miserable anymore. It could go fast like the other trains. The train said, "Thank you, kind old man!" The train was now very happy and went on many fun trips.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to color with her green crayon. One day, she wanted to color a picture of a frog, but it was very difficult for her to draw the frog's legs. She kept trying, but she couldn't get it right. Then, her big brother came to help her. He showed her how to mark the frog's legs with the crayon, and it looked perfect! Lily was so happy and proud of her picture. From then on, she knew that even difficult things can be done with a little help.

Kasey was walking in the park. The sun was shining and the birds were chirping. Suddenly, Kasey heard a loud roar. He started to panic. He looked around but couldn't figure out what it was. Then he saw it! It was a powerful lion. Kasey was scared. He felt his heart beat faster. He wanted to run away but he couldn't. It felt like his feet were stuck. The lion looked like it was coming closer. Kasey knew he had to do something! He took a deep breath and yelled loudly. The lion was surprised and stopped. Kasey felt relieved. He was safe. He had faced his fear and now he felt powerful!

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. He had a long trunk and big ears. One day, he saw a little mouse and wondered if he could be friends with him. The mouse was scared of the big elephant and ran away. The elephant felt sad and wanted to lift the little mouse up to show him he was friendly. The mouse saw the elephant's kind eyes and realized he was not scary at all. They became friends and played together every day. The big elephant was happy to have found a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a reliable boy who lived on a farm. He was so reliable that the farmer put him in charge of feeding the animals every day.

One day, the boy was feeling curious. He had heard stories about toilets, but he had never seen one before. He wondered what it was like, so he set off to find one.

On his way, he saw a big house in the distance. He knew he had to be brave to find out what a toilet looked like, so he shrugged and went closer.

The door of the house was unlocked. He went in, but it was dark, so he couldn't see what the toilet was like. He felt scared, but he was so reliable he wanted to go further. He reached for the light switch and suddenly, the toilet lit up!

It was beautiful. He was so happy he had been brave enough to find out. One day, he would make a reliable toilet of his own.

Once upon a time there was a fairy. She lived in a beautiful, smooth palace. One day, she decided to go on an adventure. She flew out the window and went high, high up in the sky.

The fairy saw a cloud and asked it, "Where am I going?" The cloud answered, "You will find out soon!"

The fairy said goodbye and continued flying. She saw a bird and asked it, "Will you help me find my way?" The bird answered, "Yes, follow me!" 

The fairy asked the bird many questions, and the bird answered each one. Finally, the fairy found her way back home. She thanked the bird and flew inside her smooth palace. 

The fairy was happy to be back and went to bed. She had such a great adventure and now knew the answer to her questions!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. Tom liked to play outside but sometimes he got tired and wanted to rest. One day, Tom was sitting in his garden and saw something he wanted - a nice, red stamp. It was beautiful and Tom knew he needed it.

So Tom asked his mum, â€œMummy, I need that red stamp!â€ But his mum shook her head and said, â€œNo, Tom. You donâ€™t need it. We already have enough stamps.â€

So Tom kept asking and eventually his mum said, â€œYou can borrow a stamp from your friend. Thatâ€™s much nicer than taking something you donâ€™t need.â€

So Tom went to his friendâ€™s house and asked if he could borrow a stamp. His friend said yes and gave Tom a nice, red stamp.

Tom was so happy and learnt a lesson - itâ€™s better to ask and share than to take something you donâ€™t need.

Martha was an enthusiastic three-year-old. She loved to observe the world around her. One day, she saw a candle burning brightly. It's warm, orange flame filled her with delight. She was determined to find out what it was. She asked her Mom, and was told it was a special point of light, called a candle. Martha observed the candle carefully, admiring its flame and its soft scent. She asked her Mom to teach her how to light it. To her surprise, her Mom said it was a grown-up task, and she'd have to wait until she was a bit older. For now, she could bask in the lovely soft glow of the candle's light. Martha smiled, content for now to simply observe the beautiful candle.

Quincy was a little girl. She was three years old and loved to explore the world. She especially loved visiting new places. 
One day, her mommy and daddy took her to a big park. Quincy was so excited to see all the new sights and sounds. She loved looking at all the trees and animals. 

As Quincy was exploring the park, she suddenly saw something sparkle. She ran over to it and found a shiny penny on the ground. She was so lucky to find it! 

Quincy picked up the penny and put it in her pocket. She knew that she must have become very lucky to find a penny like that. 

Quincy decided to take the penny home. She told her mommy and daddy all about the penny and they helped her keep it safe in a special jar. 

Quincy now alway brings her lucky penny with her every time she goes for a walk or to the park. She knows that if she's ever feeling a bit down, she can look at the penny and it will make her feel better. It has certainly become a special pass for her!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color. One day, she decided she wanted to create something new. She took out her crayons and drew a big round sun in the sky. It was so easy for her to do! 

As she was drawing, her little brother came over to see what she was doing. He asked if he could help, and Lily said yes. Together, they created a beautiful picture of a garden full of flowers and butterflies. 

Their mommy came in and saw what they had created. She was so proud of them! She put their picture up on the fridge for everyone to see. From that day on, Lily and her brother loved to create new things together.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful king. The king had a big seat. He loved to sit on his seat all day. The king had many friends. His best friend was a little girl named Sue.

One day, Sue wanted to write a letter to the king. She took a paper and a pen. She wrote, "Dear King, I love you. You are my best friend. Love, Sue." She was very happy with her letter.

Sue gave the letter to the king. The king read the letter and smiled. He was so happy to have a friend like Sue. They played together all day. Sue and the king were the best of friends. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there were two bears. They were best friends and loved to play together. One day, the two friends were walking in the forest when they noticed a basket full of apples. 

The first bear said, "Let's take the apples and share them."

But the second bear wasn't sure. He didn't want to share the apples. He wanted them all for himself. He pinched one of the apples and said, "You can't have one! They are all mine!"

The first bear was jealous. He wanted an apple too. He pinched one of the apples and said to his friend, "You have to share. We can both eat an apple."

The second bear smiled. He knew that his best friend was right. He was happy to share the apples. They each ate an apple and had a wonderful time. The end.

Once upon a time there was a special price. Everyone wanted it, but no one would ever find it. Until one day, a calm little girl walked through the forest. As she looked around she spotted the price. She picked it up and couldn't believe her eyes! Suddenly, it began to disappear. She was so surprised! The price kept fading away until it was gone.

The little girl was so sad. She had found the special price, but now it was gone. She looked around the forest, but it was nowhere to be seen. She sat down and thought about the amazing price. Suddenly, it came back! She was so excited, she had found the price once again.

The little girl picked up the price and hugged it close. She was so happy that she didn't want it to disappear again. She promised to take very good care of it. The little girl had a special bond with the price and it stayed with her calm and happy. Forever.

It was a beautiful day and Timmy was thrilled to go outside. He came across a maze and the walls were yellow. Timmy felt excited because it was his first time seeing a maze. He started to explore it and noticed there was something special about the maze. 

"Daddy, what is this?" said Timmy as he looked up at his dad.

"It's a maze, son. See this wall?" Daddy gently pointed at the yellow wall. "You have to cover the maze to finish it."

Timmy was excited to cover the maze and he ran to the first yellow wall. He carefully followed the wall and made his way to the next wall. He went around and around the maze, until he got to the end. 

"Look, Daddy, I did it!" Timmy shouted with joy.

"That is amazing, Timmy" replied Daddy. "You have covered the entire maze and finished it!"

Timmy smiled and felt proud of himself for completing the maze. He was so happy he had gone outside that day.

Jake had a regular bicycle. It was red and it was his own. He would ride it every day. He rode it to school and to the park. In the park, he liked to ride it up and down the big hill. 

Sometimes his dad would come along with him. They would both go riding together. His dad's bicycle was green. They would go really fast and it was a lot of fun.

When the weather was nice, Jake would ride his bicycle for hours. He would go to lots of different places. He loved feeling the wind in his hair and hearing the sound of the wheels on the road.

One day, a blue bicycle passed Jake on the road. He thought it looked like so much fun. He wanted his own blue bicycle but he knew it would have to wait. He knew that if he was patient, soon he could own a blue bicycle too.

Mummy and Daddy took Liz to the park. It was very sunny and the sky was a bright blue. Liz liked the sunshine so much.

First, she saw the big playground. There were swings and slides, so she picked the swing to play on. It was brilliant! She was swinging so high up into the space. She was even higher than the birds. It felt like she was flying!

Then, Liz went over to the sandpit. She picked up a shovel and filled up a bucket with sand. She loved feeling the sand and watching it move between her fingers. It was so cool!

But soon, it was getting dark and it was time to go home. Liz was so sad. But they told her they would come back soon and she could play again!

One day, a little girl went to the park with her mom. She saw a soldier sitting on a bench. The soldier was wearing a green uniform and had a big backpack. The little girl was curious and went to talk to him.

"Hello, soldier! What are you doing here?" asked the little girl.

"I'm taking a break from my job. I'm a soldier and I have to be careful when I'm working," replied the soldier.

The little girl was impressed. She asked the soldier if he liked to read books. The soldier said yes and showed her a book he had in his backpack. They read the book together and had a nice time. The little girl thanked the soldier and went back to play with her mom.

Lily and Ben love to play with their toy instruments. Lily has a small drum and Ben has a tiny guitar. They pretend to be musicians and make loud noises. Sometimes they sing along, too.

One day, they decide to play in the garden. They find a huge tree with many leaves. They think it is a good place to make music. They sit under the tree and start to play. They are very happy.

But then, they hear a loud roar. They look up and see a big lion on the tree. The lion is angry and hungry. He wants to eat them. Lily and Ben are very scared. They drop their instruments and run away.

"Help! Help!" they shout.

Their mom hears them and comes out. She sees the lion and grabs a big blanket. She throws the blanket over the lion and covers him. The lion is confused and can't see. He stops roaring and tries to get out.

"Go away, lion!" mom says. "You can't eat my children!"

She takes Lily and Ben by the hand and runs inside the house. She locks the door and hugs them.

"Are you okay, my loves?" she asks.

"Yes, mom, we are okay," Lily and Ben say. "Thank you for saving us!"

They are very grateful and proud of their mom. They tell her about their music and their instruments. Mom smiles and says they are very brave and creative.

"Maybe we can play music together later," she says. "But first, let's have some cookies and milk."

Lily and Ben agree. They love their mom and their music. They forget about the lion and the huge tree. They are very happy.

Once, there was a squirrel who loved to sing. Every day, he would gather up his friends and sing. He sang all kinds of different songs, some happy and some sad. All of his songs were so different, but they all sounded like a wonderful melody. 

One day, he heard another squirrel singing and he thought it sounded familiar. He listened closer and realised it was a song he had sung before! He was so excited that he ran over to the other squirrel and started singing with him. 

Soon, all the squirrels were singing together. It was so beautiful! The trees were shaking with the sound of the squirrels' singing and the birds were chirping along. All the animals in the forest were so happy. 

The squirrels sang for hours, until the sun went down in the sky. They said farewell to each other and the squirrel went back to his home, feeling so excited that he had made some new friends. From that day on, all the squirrels would sing together and it felt so special.

Johnny was walking in the park. He saw a big worm on the ground. Johnny wanted to pick it up, but his mom yelled at him.

"Johnny, don't touch that worm!" said his mom.

Johnny didn't listen. He picked up the worm, and put it in his pocket. His mom scolded him and told him to put the worm back on the ground.

"No," said Johnny. "I want to keep it."

His mom was starting to get angry. "Johnny," she said, "I recommend that you put that worm back on the ground. It's not safe to keep it."

Johnny thought about it for a moment. But then he said, "No, I want to keep the worm."

His mom was getting frustrated. "Johnny, please put it down. It's not safe to keep it," she said again.

But Johnny refused to listen. In the end, his mom had to take the worm out of his pocket, and put it back on the ground. Johnny watched as the big worm disappeared into the tall grass.

Once there was a great sand beach. It was the biggest sand beach in the world and people came from all over to explore it.

Every day the kids loved to play in the sand. They built giant sand castles and tried to dig to the bottom of the sea. 

When the day was done, the sun would go down and the sand would dry up. The kids would go home with their sandy clothes and big smiles. 

The sand beach at night was beautiful and mysterious. Nobody knew what was hidden beneath the dry sand. 

One day, the kids decided to explore the beach at night and dig in the dry sand. When they did, they found a great treasure! They jumped up and down in excitement, thrilled with their great discovery. 

From then on, the kids visited the sand beach every night and dried more of the sand looking for more treasure. It was a great adventure for them, and they had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma. Emma was very obedient. One morning, Emma went into her classroom. As she entered, she saw her teacher sat at the desk. Emma said â€œHello teacherâ€ and smiled. The teacher smiled back and said, â€œHello Emma, it's nice to see you.â€

Emma walked over to the desk and put her bag down. She had some pencils in her bag.

The teacher said, â€œEmma, I want you to be obedient and write your name on the whiteboard.â€ Emma nodded and started to write her name carefully.

When she had finished, the teacher said, â€œWell done, Emma. You have been very obedient. You can sit back down at the desk now.â€ Emma smiled and went back to her desk. She was proud of herself for being obedient. She was happy to be in her classroom.

Once upon a time, there was a giant. He was very big and strong, but he was also very sad. His heart was broken because he had no friends to play with. One day, he saw a little girl walking in the forest. She was so small and cute! The giant wanted to kiss her, but he was afraid she would be scared of him. 

The little girl saw the giant and she was scared at first, but then she saw that he was sad. She asked him why he was sad and he told her that he had no friends. The little girl felt sorry for the giant and she gave him a big kiss on the cheek. The giant was so happy! He had never felt so loved before. 

From that day on, the little girl visited the giant every day. They played together and had lots of fun. The giant's heart was no longer broken because he had a friend. The little girl was happy too because she had a giant friend who loved her very much. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful girl named Stella. Stella was so excited because today was different. It was her very first time seeing a television!

When Stella saw the television, it seemed to glow like a bright star. She was amazed by the beautiful colors and shapes that glided across the screen.

Stella wanted to explore the television more, so she walked closer and pressed the buttons on the remote. Suddenly, the screen lit up brighter than before and began playing a wonderful show. 

Stella was mesmerized by the images and sounds coming from the television. She watched for hours, her eyes full of wonder and delight. 

When it was time to go, Stella waved goodbye to the television, grateful for the beautiful new experience.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy who had a baby. The baby was very curious and always asked lots of questions. One day, the baby saw strange noises coming from outside. He wanted to know what was happening and asked his mommy, "What is that?"

Mommy smiled and said, "That is the hose. It is making mysterious noises." The baby thought this was fascinating and wanted to go outside and explore.

So, the mommy and baby went outside together and the baby saw a big, long hose making mysterious noises. He walked around it, amazed, and asked his mommy, "What is it?"

Mommy smiled and said, "It's a hose. It helps give us water." The baby was so excited and he touched and held the hose. He had a lot of fun exploring the mysterious hose.

Once upon a time, there was a group of friends. They were playing hide and seek in the park. It was getting dark outside and they knew it was time to end the game.

One of the friends said, "I want to play more. Can we play one more time?" 

The other friends said, "No, it's too dark and we need to go home. We can play again tomorrow."

The friend who wanted to play more felt sad, but knew it was time to end the game. They all said goodbye and went home. The end.

One day, a big mosquito came to a little town. It was not nice. It wanted to bite everyone. The people in the town did not like the mosquito. They wanted to prevent it from biting them.

A smart girl named Lily had an idea. She told everyone to use a special cream. The cream would make the mosquito not want to bite them. Everyone put the cream on their arms and legs. They hoped it would stop the mosquito.

The mosquito tried to bite the people, but it did not like the cream. It flew away, sad and hungry. The people in the town were happy. They stopped the mosquito and no one was dead. They thanked Lily for her smart idea.

Tommy was very happy today. He was going to a meeting with his mommy and daddy. The meeting was at a big place with many books and toys. Tommy liked books and toys very much.

He put on his blue shirt and his blue shoes. He liked blue. It was his favorite color. He also took his blue teddy bear with him. He called him Bluey. Bluey was his best friend.

Mommy and daddy drove the car to the big place. Tommy looked out the window and saw many things. He saw trees and flowers and birds and dogs. He pointed at them and said their names. Mommy and daddy smiled and said good job.

They arrived at the big place and went inside. There were many people there. Some were big and some were small. Some had blue shirts and some had other colors. Tommy saw a lady with a blue dress. She smiled and said hello. She said she was the teacher. She said she was going to help Tommy learn new things.

Tommy was a little scared. He did not know the lady or the other people. He held Bluey tight and looked at mommy and daddy. They said it was okay. They said they were going to stay with him. They said they were proud of him.

Tommy felt better. He said hello to the lady and the other people. He showed them Bluey and said he was his best friend. They said he was very cute and soft. They asked him if he wanted to play with them. Tommy nodded and smiled. He liked to play.

He went to a table with many books and toys. He saw a book with a blue cover. He picked it up and opened it. It had pictures of animals and words. He tried to read them. He remembered some of them from mommy and daddy. He said them out loud. The lady and the other people clapped and cheered. Tommy felt happy. He liked the meeting. He liked the big place. He liked the lady and the other people. He liked to learn new things. He liked blue.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and pick flowers. One day, she found a green caterpillar crawling on a leaf. She picked it up and put it in a jar to take home.

At home, Lily made a tidy little home for the caterpillar in a box with leaves and twigs. She whispered to the caterpillar, "You're going to be a beautiful butterfly one day." 

Days went by and Lily watched as the caterpillar grew bigger and bigger. Then one day, the caterpillar spun a cocoon around itself and went to sleep. Lily waited patiently, and one day, the cocoon began to shake and wiggle. Out came a beautiful butterfly with green wings. Lily was so happy she whispered, "I knew you would be beautiful!"

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She loved books very much! One day Sarah was walking through the park and she found a special book lying on the ground. It looked very nice. She picked it up and opened it. 

Inside the book were pictures of all kinds of animals. Sarah smiled and hugged the book tight. But then she saw something that made her cry. There was a sad face on one of the pictures. Sarah started to weep. 

Just then a little bird appeared. It was very pretty and had a nice song. The bird flew over to Sarah and looked at the book. It sang a happy song and pointed at the sad face. 

Sarah smiled and the bird flew away. She looked at the book and the sad face was now happy. Sarah hugged the book and skipped away. She was so happy to have found a nice book.

Lily and Max were squirrels who lived in a big tree. They liked to play and run and jump on the branches. One day, they found a shiny acorn on the ground. It was brown and smooth and hard.

"Wow, look at this acorn!" Lily said. "It is so pretty. I want to keep it."

"No, I want to keep it!" Max said. "I saw it first. It is mine."

They both grabbed the acorn and pulled and tugged. They did not want to share. They did not listen to each other. They started to fight.

"Stop it, stop it!" Mama squirrel said. She came out of the tree and saw them. She was not happy. "Why are you fighting over an acorn? You have many acorns in the tree. You should be kind and share."

"But Mama, this acorn is special. It is shiny and smooth and hard. We both want it." Lily and Max said.

Mama squirrel shook her head. She took the acorn from them and held it up. "Do you know what this acorn is?" she asked.

Lily and Max looked at the acorn. They did not know.

"This acorn is a seed. A seed can grow into a new tree. But it needs water and soil and sun and time. It needs to be patient. If you plant this acorn in the ground and take care of it, one day it will sprout and grow and become a big tree. Then you will have more branches to play on and more acorns to eat. But if you keep this acorn and fight over it, it will not grow. It will stay small and hard and lonely. What do you think is better?"

Lily and Max thought about it. They looked at the acorn. They looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting. They did not want to be selfish. They wanted to be kind and share.

"Mama, we are sorry. We do not want to keep the acorn. We want to plant it and grow a new tree. Can we do that?" Lily and Max said.

Mama squirrel smiled. She was proud of them. "Yes, you can. That is a very good idea. Come on, let's find a good spot to plant the acorn. And remember, you have to be patient. It will take a long time for the acorn to grow. But it will be worth it."

Lily and Max nodded. They followed Mama squirrel and carried the acorn. They found a good spot and dug a hole. They put the acorn in the hole and covered it with soil. They watered it and gave it a kiss. They said goodbye to the acorn and thanked it for being a seed. They hoped it would grow into a big tree.

Then they ran back to their tree and hugged each other. They were happy. They learned to share and to be patient. They learned that seeds are special and can make new life. They learned that acorns are not just for keeping. They are for growing.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to jump and play with her friends. One day, she met a new friend named Bob. Bob was a soft and cuddly dog who also liked to jump and play.

Sue and Bob were playing in the park when they saw a big piece of beef on the ground. Sue said, "Bob, let's share the beef and eat it together." But Bob wanted the beef all to himself. Sue felt sad and told Bob, "We should share, so we can both be happy."

Bob thought about it and realized Sue was right. He said, "Sue, you are right. Sharing is good." So, they shared the beef and ate it together. They had a great time and continued to jump and play in the park.

From that day on, Sue and Bob always shared their things with each other and their friends. They learned that sharing made them happier and brought them closer together. The moral of the story is: sharing is caring and it brings happiness to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to help her mommy in the kitchen. One day, her mommy gave her an apron to wear. It was pink and had a picture of a cupcake on it. Lily loved it!

They were making cookies for a party that night. Lily wanted to decorate the cookies with sprinkles. She put lots of sprinkles on each one. When they were done, they looked so pretty. 

Later, at the party, Lily saw a lady who was deaf. She couldn't hear the music or the people talking. Lily felt sad for her. She gave her a cookie and smiled. The lady smiled back and hugged Lily. It made her feel happy inside.

Once upon a time, there was a pale horse named Lily. Lily lived on a big farm with other horses. She liked to play with her friends and keep them happy.

One day, Lily saw a small bird with a hurt wing. The bird could not fly. Lily wanted to help the bird. She let the bird sit on her back and took it to her friends. Together, they found a way to make the bird's wing better.

The bird was very happy and thanked Lily and her friends. The other horses learned that it is good to keep helping others, even if they are not like you. From that day on, all the horses on the farm were kind to everyone they met. And they all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were playing outside after dinner. They liked to look at the sky and find stars. They had a book with pictures of stars and their names. They tried to match the stars they saw with the book.

"Look, Lily, I found a big star!" Tom said, pointing at the sky. "It is bright and yellow. It is the sun star!"

Lily looked at the star and smiled. "Yes, Tom, you are right. It is the sun star. But it is not a star like the others. It is much closer and bigger. That is why it is so bright."

Tom nodded. He wanted to learn more about the stars. He opened the book and turned the pages. He saw a star that looked like a circle with five points. It was blue and shiny. He liked it very much.

"Lily, look at this star!" Tom said, showing her the book. "It is perfect! It has five points and it is blue. It is the star of wishes. Do you know what wishes are?"

Lily nodded. She knew what wishes were. They were things you wanted very much. She had many wishes. She wished for a new doll, a bike, a cake, and a hug from Mommy.

"Tom, I know what wishes are. They are things you want very much. I have many wishes. Do you have wishes too?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had some wishes too. He wished for a rocket, a dinosaur, a ball, and a kiss from Daddy.

"Yes, Lily, I have wishes too. But how do we make our wishes come true?"

Lily remembered what Mommy had told her. She had to close her eyes, think of her wish, and blow a kiss to the star of wishes.

"Tom, I know how to make our wishes come true. We have to close our eyes, think of our wish, and blow a kiss to the star of wishes. Do you want to try?"

Tom nodded. He wanted to try. He closed his eyes, thought of his wish, and blew a kiss to the star of wishes. He opened his eyes and smiled.

"Lily, I did it! I made a wish! Did you make a wish too?"

Lily nodded. She did it too. She closed her eyes, thought of her wish, and blew a kiss to the star of wishes. She opened her eyes and smiled.

"Tom, I did it too! I made a wish! I hope our wishes come true!"

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They were happy. They looked at the sky and saw the star of wishes twinkling. They hoped their wishes would come true.

But they did not see the bird that was flying by. The bird saw the book with the star of wishes. The bird liked shiny things. The bird swooped down and grabbed the book with its beak. The bird flew away with the book.

Tom and Lily did not notice. They were too busy looking at the star of wishes. They did not see the book flying away. They did not see the bird wiping its beak with the book. They did not see the star of wishes fading away. They did not see their wishes disappearing. They only saw each other and smiled. They thought they had made the perfect wish.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jack. She was playing in the park one day and saw a billboard. She asked her mom, "What's that?" Her mom replied, "That is a billboard." Jack had never seen one before and was curious. She asked her mom, "What does it do?"

Her mom answered, "Well, people can put messages on it and display them for others to see." Jack was excited, and asked, "Can I put something on it?" Her mom nodded and replied, "Yes, but it has to be open first."

So they went up to the billboard and her mom opened the boards. Then, her mom and Jack put messages on the billboard. Jack drew a picture and wrote "I love my mom" on the billboard. Her mom wrote "My daughter is the best!" on the billboard. Everyone in the park was delighted!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was a cheerful girl who loved to play outside. One day, Lily's mom asked her if she wanted to go to the park. Lily was very excited and said yes.

As they were walking to the park, Lily saw a big dog. She wanted to pet the dog, but her mom told her not to. Lily refused to listen and went to pet the dog. The dog bit her and she felt a lot of pain.

After that, Lily learned to listen to her mom and not to refuse her advice. She also learned that sometimes things that seem fun can be dangerous. From that day on, she always made sure to ask her mom before doing anything risky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance all day long. One day, Lily found a note on the ground. It said "Meet me at the park at 3 o'clock". Lily was worried because she didn't know who wrote the note.

Lily went to the park at 3 o'clock and saw a boy sitting on a bench. She asked him, "Did you write the note?" The boy said, "Yes, I did. My name is Max and I wanted to be your friend." Lily was happy to hear that and they played together all day long.

From that day on, Lily and Max played together every day. They sang and danced together and had lots of fun. Lily was no longer worried because she had made a new friend named Max.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named John. John was healthy and strong. He loved to go exploring. One day John decided to go to the park.

As he was walking in the park, he stumbled on a big pile of leaves. He got very excited as he kept exploring. He stumbled again and saw something shiny. It was a little wake! John was so happy.

He took the wake and showed it to his mom. His mom said that it was very special and it showed how healthy he was. Then she said he needed to go to bed, as he had to get up early the next morning to go to school.

John put the wake under his pillow and went to bed. He had lots of sweet dreams. In the morning, he remembered the exciting adventure he had with the little wake he found in the park. He smiled, feeling healthy and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to sing and fly around with his bird friends. One day, Tweet heard a loud noise and saw a big, scary cat. Tweet was frightened and flew away quickly.

Later, Tweet saw the cat again and thought to himself, "Maybe the cat is not so scary after all. I should go say hello." But when Tweet got closer, the cat grabbed him and ate him up. 

The moral of the story is that we should not judge others based on their appearance or our first impression of them. And when we hear something that scares us, it's important to trust our instincts and stay away from danger.

One day, a big dog named Max was in the park. Max saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was lost and sad. Max wanted to help Tim. Max walked up to Tim and wagged his tail. Max felt comfortable with Tim.

Max said, "I will lead you home, Tim." Tim was in shock. He did not know dogs could talk. Tim said, "Thank you, Max. I am scared." Max smiled and said, "Do not be scared. I will help you."

Max led Tim through the park. They walked and walked until they saw Tim's house. Tim was happy to be home. He hugged Max and said, "You are the best dog ever!" Max wagged his tail and felt proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the zoo with his mommy and daddy. They saw lions, tigers, and bears! Oh my! 

One day, Timmy woke up feeling very dull. He didn't want to go to the zoo. But his mommy and daddy said they would buy him a big ice cream if he went. That made Timmy happy! 

At the zoo, Timmy saw a big elephant. It was so big and strong! Timmy loved watching the elephant eat peanuts. He was happy he woke up and went to the zoo.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Timmy. Timmy was very thin and loved to fly in the sky. One day, Timmy saw a rabbit who was jogging in the field. Timmy thought it would be fun to jog with the rabbit, so he flew down and joined him. They jogged and jogged until they were tired. 

After they rested, Timmy asked the rabbit if he wanted to fly with him. The rabbit was surprised but excited to try. Timmy helped the rabbit fly by holding onto him with his talons. They flew high in the sky and saw the world from a different view. 

The rabbit was so happy and thanked Timmy for the wonderful experience. From that day on, Timmy and the rabbit became good friends and would often jog and fly together.

Sam was a gifted boy who liked to play soccer. He could kick the ball very hard and fast. He wanted to be the best player on his team. He did not like to share the ball or pass to his friends. He wanted to score all the goals by himself.

One day, he had a soccer game against another team. He kicked the ball a lot, but he did not score. The other team had good players who worked together. They passed the ball and helped each other. They scored many goals and won the game.

Sam was sad and angry. He blamed his friends for losing the game. He said they were not good enough. He said he was the only gifted one. His friends did not like what he said. They felt hurt and angry too. They did not want to play with him anymore.

Sam's coach saw what happened. He talked to Sam and told him a story. He said that once there was a big tree that had many roots. The roots were strong and deep. They helped the tree grow and stay up. The tree was proud of its roots and thanked them every day. But one day, the tree saw a flower that had only one root. The flower was beautiful and colorful. The tree wanted to be like the flower. It did not like its roots anymore. It said they were ugly and boring. It said it was the only gifted one. The roots felt hurt and angry. They did not want to help the tree anymore. They stopped giving it water and food. The tree became weak and dry. It could not stand up. It fell down and died.

The coach asked Sam if he understood the story. Sam nodded. He realized he was like the tree. He realized he needed his friends like the tree needed its roots. He realized he was not the only gifted one. He realized he was wrong to be selfish and mean. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He went to his friends and said he was sorry. He said he wanted to play with them again. He said he wanted to share the ball and pass to them. He said he wanted to work together and have fun. His friends forgave him and hugged him. They were happy to be friends again.

Sam learned a lesson that day. He learned that being gifted is not enough. He learned that being kind and humble is more important. He learned that friends are more valuable than goals. He learned that teamwork makes the dream work.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went to her garden to plant some flowers. She dug a hole in the soil and put a seed in it. 

Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time for your nap." Lily said, "But I want to watch my flower grow." Her mom said, "Your flower will grow slow. You can watch it when you wake up from your nap." 

Lily went inside and took a nap. When she woke up, she ran outside to see her flower. The flower had grown big and tall! Lily was so happy. She said, "Thank you, Mommy, for telling me to take a nap. Now my flower is big and beautiful!"

Mummy and Daddy had a special surprise for the little girl. They unpacked a big box and out came a little puppy. The little girl was so happy she clapped her hands and jumped up and down. 

Mummy and Daddy said they had another surprise. They went to the kitchen and came back with a big bag of beef. The little girl laughed and ran to get a bowl to put the beef in. 

The puppy loved the beef so much he ate it all up. The little girl was so happy that she gave the puppy a big hug. The puppy licked her face and they spent the whole day playing together. 

Mummy and Daddy were very happy too and knew that the little girl and the puppy would be best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to explore. One day, he decided to go on a special adventure and explore a spooky forest. He was brave, but as he walked through the trees, he started to shiver.

The little boy kept walking and soon he came to a big, dark cave. There were strange noises coming from the cave, and the boy was so scared that he put his hands over his ears. Suddenly, he heard a gentle tapping coming from inside the cave.

The little boy was curious, so he walked inside and looked around. Suddenly, he saw a pale little creature in the corner of the cave. It was a tiny mouse, tapping away at the walls of the cave with its tiny feet.

The little boy smiled and slowly approached the mouse. He stretched out his hand and the mouse crawled onto his palm. Carefully, the little boy took the mouse outside the cave and set it free. They both thanked each other and waved goodbye.

The little boy was no longer scared. He'd made a new furry friend, and nothing in the spooky forest could scare him!

One day the sky was grey. It was starting to rain. It was so silly!

The rain started to pitter-patter on the ground. The trees were dripping with water. All the people outside ran for cover.

Nancy was watching from her bedroom window. She saw the funny sight of people running away from the rain. It made her giggle.

But she didn't mind the rain too much. She ran outside and twirled under the raindrops. It felt so cool and refreshing.

The rain eventually stopped and the sun came out. Everything was so sparkly and colourful. What a silly sight! Nancy smiled, happy to be outside again.

Navy was a big dog who loved to play. He had black fur and brown eyes. He lived with a family who gave him food and hugs. Navy liked his family very much.

One day, Navy saw a small cat in the garden. The cat was white and fluffy. Navy wanted to chase the cat and make it run. He barked and ran towards the cat. The cat was scared and hissed.

"Stop, Navy!" a voice said. It was the voice of Anna, Navy's friend. Anna was a little girl who lived in the house. She was three years old and had blonde hair and blue eyes. She loved Navy and the cat. "The cat is not a toy. The cat is my pet. Her name is Snowy. She is nice. You have to be nice to her, too."

Navy stopped and looked at Anna. He wagged his tail and licked her face. He was sorry for scaring the cat. He wanted to be a good dog and make Anna happy.

"Good boy, Navy!" Anna said. She petted him and smiled. "You are a very obedient dog. I love you, Navy. And I love Snowy, too. Can you be friends with Snowy?"

Navy nodded and sniffed the cat. The cat sniffed him back and purred. Navy and Snowy decided to be friends. They played together in the garden with Anna. Navy was happy. He had two friends who loved him. He loved them, too.

Jimmy was playing outside with his friends when they found a big rock. They were excited and quickly put it in the middle of the lawn. They all tried to balance it up so it wouldn't wobble. Jimmy was very organized and tried to see if he could make the rock stay upright on just one spike. It took some trial and error, but he eventually figured it out and the rock was balanced! His friends cheered and celebrated, jumping around and giving Jimmy high-fives. The rock was balanced, and everyone was happy!

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to go kayaking. He had a red kayak that he loved very much. One day, he went kayaking on the river and his kayak hit a rock. The kayak got a big hole and the man was upset. 

But then, the man remembered that he knew how to repair things. He took his kayak to his workshop and got to work. He used some glue and some tape to fix the hole. It took some time, but finally, the kayak was good as new! 

The man was very happy that he could repair his kayak. He went back to the river and went kayaking again. This time, he was very careful and didn't hit any rocks. He had a great time on the river with his newly repaired kayak.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They enjoy the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They are playful and happy.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and furry. It has a long tail and sharp teeth. The dog runs to Anna and Ben. It barks and growls. Anna and Ben are scared. They try to run away, but the dog is faster.

"Help, help!" Anna and Ben cry. "Go away, bad dog!"

But the dog does not go away. It jumps on Anna and Ben. It bites them hard. Anna and Ben scream and cry. They bleed and hurt.

No one hears them. No one helps them. The dog is hungry and angry. It eats Anna and Ben. They are gone.

The dog is full and happy. It enjoys the world. It is playful and bad.

Once upon a time, there was a rare little girl named Milly. She was just three years old, but Milly was already special because she could wink. Every morning before she got out of bed, Milly would practice winking in front of the mirror. 

One day, Milly asked her mom, "Can I record myself winking today?" Her mom replied, "Sure, why not?"

So Milly set up her camera and recorded her winking. After she was done, she watched the recording and smiled. Every time she watched it, Milly felt proud and special. 

Milly knew she was rare and her winking was special. Now that she had the recording, she can enjoy her winking whenever she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a careless hippo called Henry. He loved to write and did it every day. One day, Henry found a very special book. He wrote his name on the cover and opened it carefully. Inside, he discovered hundreds of blank pages. He was so excited and started to write stories on the pages. He wrote about his favourite things, like eating watermelon and playing in the lake. He wrote about his best friends too.

Henry wrote so many stories, he didn't have time to play. But one day, he decided to take a break. He put the special book away and went to play with his friends. Suddenly, it started to rain. Henry and his friends ran back to his house to stay dry.

But it was too late. The special book was ruined. Henry was so sad and felt very careless. He wished he had taken more care of the book. But no matter how much he wanted to, Henry couldn't change what had happened. 

But Henry still had his stories. He remembered all of the stories he had written in the special book. And with the help of his friends, he quickly put them all back in the book.

Despite what had happened, Henry was still proud of his book and all of the stories he had written them. He cherished the book, and never wrote carelessly again.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's big brother came in and started to tease him. Timmy didn't like that and started to cry. 

His mom came in and saw what was happening. She told Timmy's big brother to stop teasing him and to be nice. Timmy's big brother said sorry and gave Timmy a bottle of water to make him feel better. 

Timmy drank the water and felt much better. He smiled and went back to playing with his toy cars. From then on, Timmy's big brother didn't tease him anymore and they played together happily. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was hungry, so he asked his mom to make him a sandwich. His mom said yes and went to the kitchen. Tim was excited to eat his sandwich.

In the kitchen, Tim's mom cut the sandwich into two pieces. She put something new inside the sandwich. She thought Tim would like it. But she did not know that Tim did not like this new thing. Tim saw his mom put the new thing in his sandwich, and he felt a little scared.

When Tim took a bite of the sandwich, he made a terrible face. The sandwich tasted very bad. Tim did not want to eat it. He told his mom that he did not like the new thing. Tim's mom felt sad, and they did not have any more food to make a new sandwich. Tim went to bed hungry that night.

Lily and Ben are twins. They share a room and a bed. Every morning, they wake up when the sun comes in the window. They like to play and talk before they get up.

One morning, they hear a loud noise outside. It sounds like a big truck. They jump out of bed and run to the window. They see a big yellow truck with a long arm. The truck is picking up the trash cans and dumping them in the back.

"Wow!" Lily says. "Look at the truck! It is so big and strong!"

"Shh!" Ben says. "Don't shout! You will wake up Mom and Dad!"

But Lily is too excited. She shouts again. "Look, look! The truck is moving to the next house! It is so fast and noisy!"

Ben covers his ears. He does not like the noise. He likes quiet and ordinary mornings. He wishes the truck would go away.

But Mom and Dad hear Lily's shouts. They wake up and come to the room. They see Lily and Ben at the window. They smile and hug them.

"Good morning, sweeties!" Mom says. "What are you looking at?"

"A big yellow truck!" Lily says. "It is picking up the trash! It is so cool!"

"A big yellow truck?" Dad says. "That is not very ordinary. That is a special truck. It is called a garbage truck. It helps us keep our street clean and tidy."

Lily and Ben nod. They learn a new word. Garbage truck. They like the garbage truck. They think it is fun and interesting. They watch it until it goes away. Then they get ready for breakfast. They have an ordinary but happy day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play together every day. One day, Timmy found a toy that he really liked. Tommy also liked the toy, but Timmy didn't want to share it. Tommy started to worry that Timmy didn't want to be friends anymore.

Tommy asked Timmy, "Can I play with your toy too?" Timmy thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, we can share it." Tommy was happy and they played with the toy together.

After they finished playing, Timmy said to Tommy, "I'm sorry I didn't want to share before. I learned that it's important to share with my friends." Tommy smiled and said, "It's okay. It's rare to find such a good friend like you." They hugged and continued to play together happily ever after. The moral of the story is that sharing is caring and it's important to be a good friend.

Once there was a compassionate policeman. He loved to talk to everyone. He always had a smile ready for anyone he met.

One day, a little girl came to the police station. She was very scared and had been crying. She was all alone.

The policeman knelt down and asked her what was wrong. The little girl told him about a mean man that had taken her seat on the bus.

The policeman felt sorry for the little girl. He was so gentle and compassionate. He told her he would help her get her seat back.

The policeman called a few of his friends and together they went to the bus station. They approached the man who had taken the girl's seat and demanded that he give it back to her.

The mean man muttered something but finally he got up and moved to the back of the bus, so the little girl could have her seat back. The little girl was so happy and she thanked the policeman and his friends. The policeman smiled and went back to the police station with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Pam. She was very shy and never liked to be around a lot of people.

So each day, Pam would take a walk in a special place, a field near her home. Every day when she walked in this field, she'd take a sack with her.

One day, as Pam was walking in the field, she heard something strange. It was like a horn calling out - faint noises coming from a far distance. After a while, Pam recognised the sound; it was her pet donkey, Jack.

Pam was very excited - she had been looking for Jack since the morning! She quickened her pace and soon she could see him, running and jumping in the meadow. She ran towards him and hugged him.

"You're finally here!" Pam said, relieved and happy. "Where have you been? You fit quite well in this field!"

Jack smiled and looked content. Pam was sure that from now on, this would be his favorite spot in the world!

"Once upon a time, there was a popular playground. It had all kinds of exciting things to explore. One of the most popular things was the swing. It was big and colorful, and kids could swing very high in it. Some kids even pretended they were flying!

One day, a boy named Max saw something very strange in the playground. It was a weapon! He had never seen one before and was curious. He slowly walked closer and saw that it looked like a sword. The sword was sparkling in the sun.

Max was scared and quickly ran back to the swing. He started to swing very fast and high. Every time Max swung, he felt safe. He had fun swinging and soon forgot about the weapon.

The end."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy car, but one day, the battery died. Timmy was sad because he couldn't play with his toy car anymore. 

His mom saw that Timmy was sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told his mom that the battery in his toy car was dead. His mom said she could help and went to prepare a new battery for Timmy's toy car. 

Timmy was so happy when his mom gave him the new battery. He put it in his toy car and it worked perfectly! Timmy realized that his mom was very useful and always knew how to make things better. From that day on, Timmy knew that whenever he had a problem, his mom could help him.

Once upon a time, there was a group of young animals who lived in the forest. There were bunnies, squirrels, and birds. They liked to play games and have fun together.

One day, while they were playing hide-and-seek, one of the bunnies disappeared. They looked everywhere but couldn't find him. They were worried and sad.

Suddenly, the bunny appeared again! He had just been hiding really well. The group was so happy to see him again and they continued playing together. From that day on, the bunny made sure not to disappear for too long.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was very lonely and felt like he had no one else in the world. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the forest.

As he walked, he heard a noise. He thought it was strange and cautiously walked towards the sound. Then he saw a big, furry animal.

"Hello!" said the animal. "My name is Puppy and I am very hungry. Can you help me find something to eat?"

The boy felt a little scared, but he knew Puppy was just looking for a meal. He smiled and said, "Yes, I can get you something to eat."

The boy and Puppy went to a nearby house. The boy knocked on the door and asked the lady if she had anything for them to eat.

The lady was kind and gave them both a delicious meal. Puppy ate every bite and thanked the boy for helping him find it. The boy thanked the lady for the meal. 

They both went back to the forest and the boy said goodbye to Puppy. He couldn't believe how kind the lady was and how tasty the meal was. He smiled and waved goodbye to Puppy as he walked away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with yarn and make colorful bracelets. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She brought her yarn with her to make bracelets.

While playing, Lily saw a boy crying. She asked him what was wrong. The boy said he lost his favorite toy. Lily felt sad for the boy and wanted to help. She remembered she had some rough yarn in her bag. She gave it to the boy and told him to use it to make a bracelet for himself.

The boy was so happy and stopped crying. He thanked Lily and they became friends. Lily learned that helping others can make them feel better and make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to hop around in the forest. One day, he saw a big, shiny bike with pedals. He wanted to ride it, but he didn't know how. He asked his friend, a wise old owl, for help. The owl told him to practice and record his progress every day.

The little bunny practiced every day, and soon he was able to ride the bike with ease. He felt very intelligent and proud of himself. But then he saw a little bird who couldn't fly because one of its wings was broken. The bunny realized that being intelligent and skilled was not enough if he didn't use it to help others.

So, he offered to help the little bird by giving him a ride on his bike. The little bird was very happy, and the bunny felt even happier for helping someone in need. From that day on, the bunny learned that being kind and helpful is just as important as being intelligent and skilled.

Once upon a time, there was a baby who lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. They loved him very much and wanted him to be very happy.

The baby slept in a special crib. Every night his mommy and daddy would cuddle him and give him lots of hugs and kisses until he was all snuggly and warm in his crib.

But one night, something strange happened. The baby felt very troubled, and he was so sad. His mommy and daddy could tell something was wrong and they hugged him tight.

It was time for the baby to go to bed, so his mommy and daddy put him in his crib. But before they left, they hugged and kissed him one more time. As they hugged, the baby's troubles seemed to separate from him.

When the mommy and daddy said goodnight, the baby was happy and content. He was safe, and he knew that his mommy and daddy were always there for him.

Once upon a time, there was a big fun fair in the park. A little girl named Lily and her dog, Bo, went to the fair. They saw a game where you could win a prize. Lily wanted to play the game, but she didn't know how. Bo looked at the game and wagged his tail.

A kind man saw Lily and said, "Do you want to play? I can help you." Lily was happy and said, "Yes, please!" The man told Lily to throw the ball and try to hit the bottles. Lily threw the ball and knocked down all the bottles. The man smiled and said, "Great job! You win a prize."

Lily looked at the prizes and saw a big, fluffy bear. She wanted the bear, but she was too small to reach it. Bo saw the bear too and wanted to help Lily. He jumped up and grabbed the bear with his mouth. Lily was so happy and hugged Bo. They went home with their new friend, the big fluffy bear, and had a great day at the fun fair.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to go for walks with his owner, Lily. Lily always put Spot on his leash before they went outside. Spot liked to sniff around and explore the world. One day, Lily took Spot to a popular park where lots of other dogs were playing. Spot was excited to meet new friends. 

Lily sat down on a bench and gave Spot a treat. Spot sniffed the treat and then took a bite. He loved the taste! Suddenly, Spot saw a squirrel and tried to run after it. But his leash stopped him. Spot barked and pulled, but he couldn't get free. Lily laughed and gave him a pat on the head. "Silly Spot," she said. "You can't chase every squirrel you see!"

Once upon a time there was a cute little girl named Daisy. Daisy had a glove that she liked to play with. She used to mix everything with it. She mixed sand and dirt and even food. One day, Daisy tried to mix mud and water with her glove. It didn't work very well, because it was too sloppy. Daisy got mad and threw the glove into the mud. She started to cry, because it was her favorite glove.

But then something amazing happened! A little frog hopped out of the mud and gave her the glove back. It was all cleaned off and looked like new. Daisy was so happy! She hugged the frog and thanked him for cleaning her glove.

And from then on, Daisy was always careful when she mixed things with her glove. She always made sure it was clean, and she still plays with it today.

Once there was a mommy and a little baby. The baby was very small and pretty. One day, the mommy said to the baby, "Let's have a massage." 
 The baby was so excited. The mommy rubbed her back and arms with gentle strokes. The baby felt so happy and cozy. 
 
After the massage was finished, the mommy smiled and said, "Now time for a kiss!"
The baby smiled and said, "Yes please!" So the mommy kissed the baby on the forehead. 

The baby said, "That was so pretty, I love you mommy!" 
The mommy smiled and said, "I love you too."

Ravi was a young boy of three and he loved to draw. One day he wanted to make a colorful picture, but he soon realized he had forgotten to bring his eraser. He began to worry as his mother had always told him to make sure he had all the materials he needed for his art. 

He went to his neighbor, Mrs. Graham, and asked her if she had an eraser he could borrow. Mrs. Graham had a kind and compassionate look in her eye and she said yes. 

Ravi thanked her and was excited to start drawing. But when he did, he realized that the eraser was not all he had thought it would be. It was too hard, and it tore up all his pictures and erased too much. 

Ravi began to worry again. He went back to Mrs. Graham and told her what had happened. Unfortunately, there was nothing she could do to help.

Ravi went home feeling sad and dejected. He was so worried about what his mother would say when she saw all the drawings ruined. He wished he had been more careful in the first place.

Ben and Mia liked to play with magnets. They had many magnets of different shapes and colors. They liked to stick them on the fridge, on the door, on the table. They liked to see how the magnets pulled or pushed each other.

One day, they found a new magnet in their toy box. It was a ring magnet. It was shiny and silver. It looked very modern. Ben and Mia wondered what it could do.

"Let's try it on the fridge," Ben said.

"OK," Mia agreed.

They ran to the kitchen and put the ring magnet on the fridge. It stuck very well. They tried to pull it off, but it was hard.

"Wow, this is a strong magnet," Ben said.

"Maybe it can stick to other things too," Mia said.

They looked around the room and saw a phone on the counter. It was their mom's phone. It was also shiny and silver. It looked very modern too.

"Let's try it on the phone," Mia said.

"OK," Ben agreed.

They took the ring magnet and put it on the phone. It stuck very well too. They tried to pull it off, but it was harder.

"Wow, this is a very strong magnet," Mia said.

But then, something strange happened. The phone started to make a loud noise. It was ringing. Ben and Mia were scared. They did not know what to do.

"Mom, mom, help!" they shouted.

Their mom came running from the living room. She saw the phone and the magnet. She looked angry.

"Ben, Mia, what have you done?" she asked.

She took the phone and the magnet. She tried to separate them, but it was very hard. She had to use a lot of force. She finally managed to pull them apart.

She looked at the phone and saw that it was broken. The screen was cracked. The buttons were stuck. The sound was distorted.

She looked at Ben and Mia and said, "This was a very bad idea. You should never put magnets on phones. Magnets can damage phones. Phones are not toys. They are important and expensive. You have to be careful and respectful with them. Do you understand?"

Ben and Mia nodded. They felt sorry and ashamed. They did not mean to break the phone. They did not know that magnets could hurt phones. They just wanted to play and have fun.

They said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not know. We will not do it again. We love you."

Their mom sighed. She was still angry, but she also loved them. She said, "I love you too. But you have to be more responsible and sensible. You have to learn from your mistakes. And you have to help me fix the phone. Come on, let's go to the store and see what we can do."

Once upon a time, there was a new ship. The ship sailed across the big blue sea. It was strong and shiny and always kept safe.

One day, the ship got into deep trouble. It was surrounded by big, mean monsters. The monsters wanted to take the ship from the nice people on board.

The captain and his crew knew they had to protect the ship. They worked together to come up with a plan. First, the crew made a big wall around the ship. Then, they put up a strong shield to protect it.

Finally, the monsters went away. The ship was safe! Everyone was so happy. They had worked hard to protect the new ship.

Once upon a time there was a family who had a very hot day. The mother said to the father, "It's so hot, can you help and get me a fan?"

The father said, "Yes, I will help you." He went outside and searched for a fan. After a while he found one, it was quite old but he thought it would do the job.

He took it home and plugged it in. It started to work but it made a very hard noise. The mother said, "Oh dear, the fan is a bit hard."

The father said, "Not to worry. I can help you." So he worked very hard fixing the fan until it was perfect. The noisy stopped and the house was cool and comfortable.

The family was so happy with the fan. They thanked the father for his help. Moral of the story: It's always a good thing to help.

Once, there was a little girl named Ami. Ami wanted to learn, but she wasn't sure how. Then, one day, her mommy brought home a surprise. It was a tutor - someone just for Ami!

Ami was scared at first. But the more time she spent with the tutor, the safer she felt. She learned all sorts of things, like how to do math and how to read!

She was so excited that her secret skills were beginning to reveal themselves. On the very last day of Ami's tutoring, she earned a special diploma. It had something written on it: "Ami is a smart kid!"

Ami showed her diploma to everybody. She felt proud and safe - she had new, amazing things to show the world now!

Jen and Ben had a dog named Spot. Spot was unique. He had black and white spots all over his fur. He liked to run and play and chase balls. Jen and Ben loved Spot very much.

One day, Jen and Ben wanted to take Spot to the park. They had a new leash for him. It was red and shiny and had a bell on it. Jen and Ben thought it was very pretty. They hoped Spot would like it too.

They put the leash on Spot and went outside. Spot was excited. He saw a lot of things to sniff and explore. He pulled on the leash and made the bell ring. Jen and Ben laughed and followed him.

But when they got to the park, they saw a problem. There was a big sign that said: "No dogs allowed". Jen and Ben were sad. They wanted to play with Spot in the park. They looked around and saw a lot of people and children and bikes and swings. They did not see any other dogs.

They wondered what to do. They did not want to break the rule. They did not want to make Spot unhappy. They did not want to go back home. They wished they could find a place where Spot could fit in.

Then they saw it. Across the street, there was a pet store. It had a big window with a lot of animals inside. There were cats and birds and fish and hamsters and rabbits. And there were also dogs. They were all different sizes and colors and shapes. They looked happy and friendly.
