Jack and Jill were best friends. They always played together. One day they disagreed. Jack wanted to go outside to play, but Jill wanted to stay inside. They both got frustrated.

Jack's mom heard the disagreement. She put on the alarm to let them know it was time for lunch. They were both confused. They didn't know what the alarm was for.

Jack's mom explained that the alarm was for lunch. She said they could decide what to do later, but now it was time to eat.

Jack and Jill disagreed about lunch too. Jack wanted a sandwich, but Jill wanted macaroni and cheese. Jack's mom said they could both have what they wanted.

Jack and Jill were still confused, but they started to calm down. They both agreed on lunch and went to eat. They still disagreed sometimes, but they learned that it was OK to have different ideas.

Anna and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, slide and swing. They liked to see the birds, the flowers and the clouds. They had a lot of fun.

One day, it was very hot and sunny. Anna and Ben did not bring any water or hats. They felt thirsty and tired. They looked for some shade, but they could not find any. All the trees were very small and had no leaves. All the benches were in the sun. They wished they had listened to their mom, who told them to bring water and hats.

They saw a big tent in the corner of the park. It looked cool and dark inside. They ran to the tent and went in. They hoped to find some water and some shade. But they did not find what they wanted. They found a lot of scary things. They found a snake, a spider, a bat and a skull. They screamed and ran out of the tent. They were very scared.

They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a wide blanket. She hugged them and gave them some water and some hats. She told them that the tent was for a Halloween party. She told them that the snake, the spider, the bat and the skull were not real. They were just toys. She told them that they should not go into places they did not know. They should always ask before they enter.

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They regretted going into the tent. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to their mom and thanked her for the water and the hats. They decided to play on the wide blanket, under the shade of an umbrella. They felt safe and happy. They still liked to play in the park, but they also liked to listen to their mom.

Once there was a brave girl named Lucy. She loved to go to the popular station. At the station, Lucy saw a small bird. She wanted to help the bird get home.

She decided to take the bird outside. She held the bird very carefully as she walked around the station. Soon, the bird found its way home.

Lucy was happy that she could help the bird. But something else made Lucy happy too. She had forgiven herself for being scared.

Lucy was so glad that she had found the courage to forgive. She learned that it is good to forgive, even when it is hard. Lucy will always remember to forgive.

Jerry was happy to see the horse. He ran as fast as he could just to get closer. When he saw the horse, he was filled with excitement. He knew he wanted to ride it. So Jerry ran to the horse and yelled "Hi, horse!" 

The horse seemed to understand him, and Jerry thought that was silly. He took the bridle and started to load the horse. Just when he finished, he heard his mom calling him.

"Jerry! Come home right now!" 

But Jerry was so excited that he wanted to get on the horse. He thought that his mom didn't understand how much he wanted to ride the horse. He started to cry, but his mom was very serious and told him to get down.

Jerry started to feel sad, but he got down. He was very disappointed because his dream of riding the horse had disappeared. He went home feeling silly. He knew that he was not allowed to load horses without permission.

Once upon a time there was a brave bear. He wanted to explore the world. He looked around, but all he saw was a cold landscape.

The bear was feeling a bit sad he didn't have anywhere to go. So he decided to make a request. He asked the wind to take him somewhere new.

The wind heard his request and became very excited. It picked up the bear and blew him all around the world. 

The bear got to see so many exciting places. He saw mountains and canyons, sandy beachs and icy glaciers. Every place he went was so different and exciting.

Finally, the wind brought him back home. The bear thanked the wind for his adventure and ran off into the cold landscape. He was so happy to be home.

Once upon a time there was a cheerful little girl. Her favorite thing to do was to rest in her chair. Every morning, she would wake up, sit down in her chair, and close her eyes. With the bright sunlight shining through her window, she felt very happy and content. 

She would spend the whole day in her chair, reading books, playing with her toys and daydreaming. She loved the feeling of resting in her chair. It felt so warm and comfy! 

At night, the little girl would say goodnight in her chair, giving it a big hug. She was so grateful for the chair, and how happy it made her feel. She knew that as long as she had her chair to rest in, she would always be cheerful. And so, the little girl and her chair lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. Tom has a big truck and Lily has a doll. Tom likes to make loud noises with his truck and zoom it around the floor. Lily likes to brush her doll's hair and dress her up.

"Tom, can I play with your truck?" Lily asks. She thinks the truck looks fun and shiny.

"No, it's mine!" Tom says. He does not want to share his truck. He thinks the doll is boring and ugly.

"Please, Tom, just for a little bit?" Lily begs. She tries to reach for the truck, but Tom pulls it away.

"Go away, Lily!" Tom shouts. He pinches Lily's arm hard. Lily cries out in pain and drops her doll.

"Ow, Tom, that hurts!" Lily says. She feels a big ouch on her arm. She is angry and sad.

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to hurt you," Tom says. He feels bad for pinching Lily. He sees a red mark on her arm. He remembers that Mommy told him not to pinch.

He gives Lily his truck and picks up her doll. He sees a zip on the doll's dress. He tries to open it, but it is stuck. He pulls harder, but the zip does not move. He breaks the zip and tears the dress.

"Oh no, Tom, what did you do?" Lily says. She sees her doll's dress ruined. She is more angry and sad.

"Sorry, Lily, I didn't mean to break it," Tom says. He feels worse for breaking Lily's doll. He remembers that Mommy told him to be gentle.

He hugs Lily and says, "I'm sorry, Lily, I'm a bad brother. I love you."

Lily hugs Tom back and says, "I'm sorry, Tom, I'm a bad sister. I love you."

They wipe their tears and smile. They decide to play together and share their toys. They find a dry cloth and wrap it around the doll's dress. They pretend the cloth is a cape and the doll is a superhero. They have fun and laugh. Mommy comes in and sees them happy. She is proud of them. She gives them a big hug and a kiss. She says, "You are good children. I love you."

Once there was a little girl. She was playing in the park. She saw a big, tall tree with clusters of fruit hanging from it. She ran over to it.

The little girl picked some of the fruit and bit into them. They were sour! She made a sour face, it was very yucky. 

"This is terrible," she said.

Just then, an old man came walking over. She smiled at him and said, "This fruit is sour!"

The old man chuckled. "Well, that's because you've been picking the wrong type of fruit," he said. "What you need to do is reverse and climb to the top of the tree!"

So, the little girl decided to try it. She slowly walked backwards, and then she climbed, reaching up toward the highest branches. She found some sweet, juicy fruit, and she picked it and ate it.

It was delicious! She thanked the old man for his help, and then ran off to tell her friends about her adventure.

Tom liked to play with his toy iron. It was orange and shiny and made a funny noise when he pressed a button. He liked to pretend he was ironing his clothes like his mom. He had a small board and some old shirts and pants to iron.

One day, his friend Lily came over to play. She saw his toy iron and wanted to play with it too. She asked Tom if she could have a turn. Tom said no, it was his iron and he did not want to share. Lily got angry and tried to grab the iron from Tom. They both pulled and pushed and shouted.

Tom's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Tom and Lily fighting over the toy iron. She was not happy. She told them to stop and said they had to share. She said Tom could play with the iron for five more minutes, then he had to return it to Lily. She said Lily could play with another toy until then.

Tom did not like this. He wanted to keep the iron for himself. He thought it was not fair. He pouted and said he did not want to play with Lily anymore. He turned away from her and ironed his clothes very fast.

Lily felt sad. She wanted to play with Tom and the iron. She did not understand why Tom was so mean. She looked around and saw a toy truck on the floor. She picked it up and started to roll it on the carpet. She made a vroom-vroom sound and smiled.

Tom heard Lily's sound and looked at her. He saw her playing with the truck and having fun. He felt a little sorry. He realized he was being selfish. He decided to be nice and share. He finished ironing his clothes and put them on the board. He took the iron and walked over to Lily. He said he was sorry and asked if she wanted to play with the iron. He said he would play with the truck.

Lily was surprised and happy. She said thank you and took the iron. She said she was sorry too and asked if he wanted to play with the truck. She said they could take turns. Tom nodded and smiled. He took the truck and rolled it on the carpet. He made a vroom-vroom sound and laughed.

Tom's mom saw them playing nicely and smiled. She was proud of them. She said they were good friends and gave them a hug. She said they could have a snack and watch a cartoon. Tom and Lily agreed and followed her to the kitchen. They held their toys and each other's hand. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a kind man. He wanted to have a parade. So he went out and rang the bell. All of his friends heard the bell and came running. They had all kinds of fun things for the parade. They had flags and candy and balloons! Everyone was in the parade, even the animals! The parade was so much fun. They laughed and sang and danced all day. When the parade was over, the kind man thanked everyone for coming. They all said goodbye and wished him well. That was the best parade ever!

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play and sing. One day, they find a big hat and a long scarf in Mom's closet. They put them on and pretend to be opera singers.

"Hello, I am Sara, the best opera singer in the world!" Sara says in a loud voice.

"And I am Ben, the most handsome opera singer in the world!" Ben says in a loud voice.

They start to sing a song they make up. They sing very high and very low. They sing very fast and very slow. They sing very loud and very soft. They make funny faces and gestures.

Mom hears them and comes to see what they are doing. She sees them in the hat and the scarf, singing their silly song. She smiles and claps her hands.

"Bravo, bravo, you are wonderful opera singers!" Mom says in a kind voice.

Sara and Ben stop singing and bow. They are happy that Mom likes their show. They run to hug her and say thank you.

Mom is compassionate. She loves Sara and Ben very much. She laughs with them and tells them they are very creative and funny. She says they can keep the hat and the scarf and play opera anytime they want. Sara and Ben are very happy. They love Mom very much. They laugh with her and tell her they love her too.

Once upon a time there was a unique elephant called Ella. Ella was a special elephant because she had the loudest trumpet and the longest trunk!

One day, Ella found herself in trouble. She had been walking with her friends around the jungle when she slipped into a deep hole. Ella was very scared and called out for help.

Just then, she heard a voice. There was a brave elephant called Bruce who was nearby. Bruce was so kind that he had come to rescue Ella.

Bruce: "Don't worry Ella, I'm here to help!"

Ella was so relieved to hear Bruce's voice. He carefully pulled her out of the deep hole and Ella thanked him for rescuing her. From then on, Ella and Bruce were best friends and always looked out for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she was playing with her toy car when her mom came in and said, "Lily, it's time to clean up your toys." 

Lily didn't want to stop playing, but she knew she had to listen to her mom. So, she turned off her toy car and started putting away all of her toys. As she was cleaning, she found a puzzle that she had never finished before. She thought it would be interesting to try and finish it, so she asked her mom if she could keep playing for a little longer.

Her mom said yes, and Lily started working on the puzzle. It was really hard, but she didn't give up. After a while, she finally finished it! She was so happy with the result and showed her mom. 

Her mom was proud of her for not giving up and finishing the puzzle. She told Lily that sometimes things might be hard, but if she keeps trying, she can accomplish anything. Lily learned that it's important to never give up and to always try her best.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park, but her mom always told her to be careful and not to pick up stones she didn't know. One day, Lily saw a shiny stone that she had never seen before. She wanted to pick it up and take it home, but she remembered what her mom had said and asked for permission first.

Her mom permitted her to pick up the stone, but warned her to be careful because it was unknown and could be dangerous. Lily picked up the stone and brought it home. She showed it to her dad, who told her that it was a rare gemstone and very valuable. 

Lily was very happy that she had found the stone, but she also learned an important lesson. She realized that it was important to always ask for permission and not to take things that were unknown or could be dangerous. From that day on, Lily always asked for permission before doing anything, and she never picked up unknown stones again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard and talk to the birds. One day, she saw a lemon tree and picked a lemon from it. She squeezed it and made lemonade. It was sour but she liked it.

One day, Lily's friend came over and saw her drinking lemonade. She said, "Wow, that's fancy!" Lily didn't know what "fancy" meant but she knew it was a nice word. She felt happy.

Lily learned that sometimes it's good to try new things, even if they are sour. And it's nice to learn new words and know what they mean.

Mummy was anxious. She couldn't find her special dress. She looked in her wardrobe, but it wasn't there.

"Please help, Daddy," she said.

Daddy smiled and reached into the wardrobe. He pulled out a toolbox and a brush.

Mummy's eyes lit up. "You can restore it?" she asked.

Daddy nodded. He worked carefully and when he was finished, the dress was shiny and beautiful.

Mummy smiled. She hugged Daddy and said, "Thank you, Daddy. You always make things better."

Once upon a time, there was a smart monkey who lived on an island. The monkey liked to slide down the trees and play with his friends. One day, the monkey saw a banana on the other side of the island. He wanted to get it, but he didn't know how to get there. 

The monkey thought and thought, and then he had an idea. He would slide down a big hill to get to the banana! So, he climbed up the hill and started to slide down. It was so much fun! When he got to the bottom, he found the banana and ate it all up. He was very happy and proud of himself for being so smart. 

From that day on, the monkey would slide down the hill whenever he wanted to go to the other side of the island. His friends thought he was very clever for coming up with such a fun way to travel. And the monkey was just happy to have his banana and his fun slides. The end.

Lily and Ben were brother and sister. They liked to play outside in the sun. One day, they found a big box in the yard. They decided to make it their shelter. They put some blankets and pillows inside. They also drew some pictures on the box with crayons.

But their dog, Spot, did not like the box. He wanted to play with Lily and Ben. He barked and scratched at the box. He made it filthy with his paws. He tore some of the blankets and pillows. He also ate some of the crayons.

Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They told Spot to go away. They tried to fix their shelter. But it was too hard. They needed some help. They asked their mom to support them. Their mom was kind and smart. She gave them some tape and scissors. She helped them cut and stick the box. She also gave them some new blankets and pillows. She told them to share their shelter with Spot. She said he was lonely and wanted to be their friend.

Lily and Ben listened to their mom. They made some space for Spot in their shelter. They also gave him some toys and treats. They invited him to join their play. Spot was happy and wagged his tail. He licked their faces and cuddled with them. He stopped barking and scratching. He was a good dog.

Lily and Ben were happy too. They had a nice shelter and a nice dog. They thanked their mom for her support. They hugged and kissed her. They also hugged and kissed Spot. They had a lot of fun in their shelter. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time, there was a festival with lots of fun things happening. There were lots of games for children to play and goodies to munch on.

The best part was when everyone joined together to freeze. Everyone stopped what they were doing and stood still like a statue! It was so funny, everyone looked like a frozen bunch of robots! After a minute, all the children cheered and started playing again.

That night, they all had a delicious festival feast. They ate, sang, and danced. It was supposed to be the best day ever.

But when it was time to go home, everyone was sad. They wanted to keep on freezing and playing together. Soon, they all waved goodbye and promised to have lots more fun together again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who went on a great adventure. She had a special passport just for this trip and she was very excited. She packed her suitcase and hopped on the bus to her destination.

When she boarded the bus, the driver looked at her passport and started to poke at it with his finger. She felt a bit guilty but she remembered why she was here and kept going.

At the end of the journey, the girl had a stamp in her passport. She was so proud that she had made it all the way here. Every time she looked at her stamped passport, she remembered her great adventure and smiled.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved flowers. Every day she went outside to look for them. One day, the little girl saw a beautiful flower. She was so excited! She reached out and tried to touch it. 

Suddenly, a terrible noise filled the air. It was so loud that the little girl was scared. Then, a big dog appeared. He wanted to get the flower too! 

The little girl tried to reach for the flower, but the dog got there first. The girl was so sad. She didn't know what to do. 

Luckily, the girlâ€™s mom saw what happened. She gave the little girl another flower. It was just as beautiful as the one the girl wanted. The little girl was so happy. She thanked her mom, and embraced the flower like it was a treasure.

Once upon a time there was an animal called Sammy the Sloth. Sammy was very lazy and he always wanted to take the easy way out. One day Sammy had to cover something in his order (the way his house and furniture was laid out). He thought that if he made it quick, he could be done with the job faster. He rushed through the job and when he was done, he realized that he had made a big mess. 

Sammy felt sad and embarrassed. That's when his mom came in the room and said, "Sammy, it's ok. I'm glad you tried so hard, but I want to remind you that you need to take your time while doing your work and do it right the first time. That way you won't be so rushed and your work will be better!"

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy had a big drum. He loved to bang it loud, but his mom said it was too noisy. One day, Timmy decided to stir up some fun by playing his drum outside. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat jelly all day long. Her mom told her, "Lily, you need to eat more vegetables to grow big and strong." But Lily didn't listen.

The moral of the story is that eating healthy foods helps you grow big and strong. Plus, it's important to listen to your friends when they give you good advice. And when you eat quietly, you can enjoy your food and have a happy tummy.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big shiny thing in the grass. They run to it and pick it up. It is a diamond!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very restless and always wanted to do something fun. One day, she saw her friend Max outside and she invited him to play.

Mia had a friend named Tim. Tim was troubled because he couldn't build a structure like Mia. He tried and tried, but his structure always fell down. Mia saw Tim was sad and wanted to help him.

Mia showed Tim how to build a strong structure by putting the blocks together in a special way. Tim tried it and his structure stood tall and strong, just like Mia's. They were both very happy. This story shows that if we help our friends, we can make them happy and we can be happy too.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run, but their favorite thing was to rock on the big horse. The big horse was made of wood and had a spring under it. It could go up and down and side to side when they pushed with their feet.

One day, they went to the park with their mom. She said they could rock on the big horse for a little while, but then they had to go to a lecture. A lecture was when a grown-up talked for a long time and they had to sit still and listen. Tim and Jen did not like lectures. They thought they were boring and hard.

They rocked on the big horse as fast as they could. They pretended they were cowboys and cowgirls, riding in the wild. They laughed and shouted and had fun. They did not want to stop. They did not hear their mom calling them. They did not see the big dog running towards them.

The big dog was black and hairy. It had sharp teeth and a loud bark. It liked to chase things that moved. It saw Tim and Jen rocking on the big horse and thought they were toys. It ran to them and jumped on the horse. It bit the horse's ear and pulled it hard.

Tim and Jen screamed. They were scared and hurt. The big dog was too strong and heavy. They could not rock the horse anymore. They felt helpless. They wished their mom would come and save them. But their mom was far away. She was at the lecture. She did not know what was happening. She did not hear their screams. She did not see the big dog. She did not help them.

Sara likes to go to the library with her mom. She can see many books with pictures and words. She can pick some books to take home and read with mom. She likes to find books about animals, colors, and shapes.

One day, Sara and mom go to the library, but it is very busy. Many people are there, and many books are gone. Sara looks for books about animals, but she cannot find any. She looks for books about colors, but she cannot find any. She looks for books about shapes, but she cannot find any. She feels sad and mad.

Mom sees Sara is sad and mad. She hugs Sara and says, "I know you want to find books, but today the library is very busy. Maybe the books you want are not available. That means someone else has them, or they are in another place. But we can still find some books to read. Let's look for books about something else. Maybe we can find books about cars, or stars, or flowers. What do you think?"

Sara thinks for a moment. She likes cars, and stars, and flowers. She nods and says, "OK, mom. Let's look for books about cars, or stars, or flowers." Mom smiles and says, "Good. Let's go and see what we can find." They hold hands and walk to another shelf. Sara sees a book with a big car on the cover. She picks it up and says, "Look, mom. A car book. Can we take this one?" Mom says, "Yes, we can. That looks like a fun book. Do you see any other books you like?" Sara looks around and sees a book with a star on the cover. She picks it up and says, "Look, mom. A star book. Can we take this one too?" Mom says, "Yes, we can. That looks like a nice book. You are very good at finding books, Sara." Sara feels happy and proud.

They go to the counter and check out the books. They say thank you to the librarian and goodbye to the library. They go to the car and drive home. Sara holds the books on her lap and says, "Mom, I like the library. Even when the books I want are not available, I can find other books to read. The library has many books, and they all seem interesting." Mom says, "I'm glad you like the library, Sara. I like it too. And I like reading books with you. You are a smart and curious girl. I love you, Sara." Sara says, "I love you too, mom." They hug and smile. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a kid called Milly. She was three years old and very smart. One day her mommy told her she needed to go to university and become very organized. Milly wasn't sure what that meant, so she asked her mommy.

Mommy said university was a special place where people go to learn things. But Milly just wanted to play and have fun.

Milly said, â€œI don't want to go. It doesn't seem fun at all.â€ 

Mommy said, â€œIt will be fun once you get used to it. You'll learn lots of new things and it will make you very organized."

Milly thought for a moment and then agreed to go. She started off at the university and it all seemed a bit strange and overwhelming at first, but soon she was having lots of fun and learning new things. As she got more organized, she felt proud of herself. 

Now Milly loves going to university and enjoys learning new things. Mommy is proud of her daughter and the way she is so organized.

Once there was a sailor who had an important job. He needed to measure how heavy different things were. 

One day, he was weighing an apple. A little boy came up to him and said, 'What are you doing?' 

The sailor replied, 'I'm weighing the apple.'

The little boy looked very serious. He asked, 'Why do you need to weigh it?'

The sailor smiled and explained, 'I'm measuring its weight. That way I can tell if it is heavy or light.'

The little boy was amazed. 'Wow!' he said. 'That's so cool!'

The sailor smiled again. 'Yes, it is. But it's also very important. Now let's weigh this apple!'

Once upon a time, there was a family of four. Mom, Dad, and two little ones. Mom and Dad wanted to take their two little ones on an adventure. 

So, the four of them packed up their things and visited a beautiful beach. They had never seen anything so wonderful before! The sand was soft and the water was blue. 

The two little ones and their parents played in the sand and looked for shells in the water. They ran back and forth, and had lots of fun. 

When it was time to go, they were a little bit sad to leave, but they took lots of beautiful memories with them. 

The family visited the beach again and again and it always felt like a special place. They loved it!

Once there was a mommy and a toddler. The toddler wanted to try to do yoga with mommy. So they tried it together.

The toddler tried to touch his toes, but he could not do it. He felt frustrated. Mommy said, "Stretch your legs, sweetheart. You can do it!"

The little one tried again and he actually got his toes to touch. He felt proud and happy, but it still seemed like a long way for him to do yoga. The mommy held his hand and said, "Let's take it slow, and practice often."

The toddler and mommy kept practicing yoga and soon, the little one could do long stretches. He smiled and told mommy, "Look what I can do now!"

The moral of the story is that practice and patience can help us do anything, even if it seems too hard or too long in the beginning.

Once upon a time, there was a silly clown. He had a big red nose and wore a colorful hat. One day, he went to a party and brought his pen with him. He wanted to draw funny pictures for the kids.

When the clown started to draw, the kids clapped their hands. They loved the silly pictures he made. The clown felt happy and continued to draw more pictures. The kids clapped louder and louder each time he finished a drawing.

At the end of the party, the clown thanked the kids for clapping and gave each of them a silly drawing as a gift. The kids were so happy and thanked the clown for making their day so much fun. From that day on, the clown knew that drawing with his pen and making silly pictures was his favorite thing to do.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big saw in the shed. They wanted to use it to cut some wood and make a house.

"Look, Lily, I can cut this log with the saw!" Tom said. He held the saw with both hands and tried to move it back and forth.

"Be careful, Tom, the saw is sharp and heavy!" Lily said. She watched Tom struggle with the saw.

Tom did not listen to Lily. He thought he was strong and clever. He pushed the saw harder and faster. But he did not see a stone on the ground. He stumbled on the stone and fell down. The saw slipped from his hands and landed on his leg. He cried out in pain.

Lily ran to Tom and saw the blood on his leg. She was scared and sorry. She ran to the house and called their mom. Mom came quickly and took Tom to the hospital. She bandaged his leg and gave him a hug.

"Tom, you were very naughty and foolish. You should not play with the saw. It is not a toy. It is a tool for grown-ups. You could have hurt yourself or Lily very badly. You are lucky it was not worse." Mom said.

Tom felt ashamed and sad. He said sorry to Mom and Lily. He learned his lesson. He never played with the saw again. He realized that it was not useful for him, but dangerous. He decided to play with safer things, like blocks and balls. He also listened to Lily more, because she was his sister and she cared for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat pears because they were soft and yummy. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a big, juicy pear to eat. Lily was so happy that she shouted, "Yay, thank you mommy!" 

As Lily was eating her pear, she noticed a little bird outside her window. The bird was chirping loudly and Lily wanted to say hello. So, she shouted, "Hello little birdie!" The bird chirped back and Lily giggled with joy.

After finishing her pear, Lily went outside to play. She saw her friends and shouted, "Hey guys, come play with me!" They all ran over and played together until it was time for dinner. Lily went home with a happy heart and a full tummy, thinking about how much she loved soft pears and playing with her friends.

Once there was a robot who loved to joke. He was always making funny jokes and everyone would laugh and have fun. One day, the robot decided to tell a really spicy joke. He found the perfect spicy joke and told it to everyone. Everyone laughed so hard, and the robot felt so happy. He loved making jokes, especially when people liked them. 

The robot kept telling jokes and everyone kept laughing. He was so excited by how much everyone enjoyed his jokes, he decided to tell a spicy joke every day. The robot couldn't wait to tell more funny and spicy jokes. 

So every day, the robot made sure to tell funny and spicy jokes. Everyone was so delighted by the jokes, the robot felt like the happiest robot around and he continued to tell jokes for everyone else to enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who had big hair. Her hair was so long, it came down to her waist. Everyday, she would mix it up, tying it into bunches, braids and ponytails. But one day, something strange happened â€“ the girl was too confused to mix her hair!

She tried and tried to mix her hair, but it just wouldn't work. The more she tried, the more confused she became. She started to panic and cry, until, suddenly, she had a brilliant idea!

She would ask all her friends to come, and together they would sort out her huge mane. Her friends jumped at the chance to help and soon, they were mixing her hair into all sorts of styles! Everyone was amazed at the beautiful hairdos they had created and the little girl was so happy.

From then on, she never felt confused about mixing her hair, because she knew her friends were always there to help her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to play with her hoop in the open yard. One sunny day, Mia saw her friends playing with their hoops too. They were all having so much fun.

Mia had an idea. She thought they could all scatter their hoops on the ground and see who could jump in and out of them the fastest. Her friends thought it was a great idea. They all took turns and laughed as they jumped in and out of the hoops.

At the end of the game, Mia's friend, Tim, was the fastest. All the kids cheered for him. They learned that playing together and sharing ideas made their games even more fun. From that day on, they always played together in the open yard, and they were all very happy.

Mommy was getting supper ready. She was very organized. She was filling up the plates. She was using a teaspoon to put nice food on each plate.

Baby wanted a teaspoon too. He wanted to help. Baby asked, but mommy refused. She said he was too little. "No, Baby," she said, "You have to wait until you're bigger."

Baby was sad. He wanted to help. But mommy said no. So Baby had to wait until later. He watched while mommy filled the plates and put them on the table. Soon it was time to eat. 

Baby was glad. Maybe now he could help mommy. He asked and this time she said yes! Baby was so happy. He was able to use the teaspoon to help mommy at the table. 

He was very proud! He helped fill up everyone's plates. He was happy that mommy let him help. Baby was an organized helper!

Once upon a time there was a creative little girl. She loved exploring and tasting new things. One day, when she was exploring in the garden, she stumbled upon a lung. She was curious about it and wanted to taste it. She quickly put it in her mouth and took a bite!

It tasted strange and the little girl quickly took it out of her mouth and spat it out. She decided that this wasn't something she wanted to taste again! She quickly continued exploring in the garden, in search of something else to taste. 

Finally she found a delicious, juicy fruit, ripe and ready to eat! She quickly popped it in her mouth and closed her eyes. It tasted sweet and juicy, and the little girl was so happy. She was glad that she had been creative enough to find the fruit and taste it!

Tom and Jen are friends who like to play on the farm. They like to run, jump, and climb on the hay, the fence, and the tractor. One day, they see a big barn with a high roof. They want to see what is inside.

"Let's go in the barn," Tom says. "Maybe we can find some animals or toys."

"OK, but be careful," Jen says. "The barn is old and dark. We might get hurt or lost."

They open the door and walk in. They see some cows, some pigs, and some chickens. They also see some ropes, some ladders, and some boxes. They start to explore and have fun.

"I bet I can climb higher than you," Tom says. He is competitive and likes to win. He sees a rope hanging from the roof. He grabs it and starts to pull himself up.

"Be careful, Tom," Jen says. "The rope might break. You might fall."

"I'm not scared," Tom says. "I can do it. Watch me."

He tries to climb higher and higher. He is almost at the roof. He feels proud and happy. He looks down at Jen and smiles.

"See, I told you I can do it," he says.

But then, the rope snaps. Tom screams. He falls down, down, down. He hits the floor hard. He feels pain and fear. He cries.

Jen runs to him. She is scared and sad. She sees blood and bruises. She tries to help him. She calls for help.

"Tom, Tom, are you OK?" she says.

But Tom does not answer. He does not move. He does not breathe. He is gone.

One day, a fine helicopter was flying in the sky. It was a big and pretty helicopter. The helicopter was very good at helping people.

The helicopter saw a little girl named Lucy. Lucy was lost and did not know how to go home. The helicopter wanted to help Lucy. It came down and said, "Lucy, I can provide help. I can take you home."

Lucy was happy and said, "Thank you, helicopter!" She got in the helicopter and they went up in the sky. They flew over the trees and houses. Soon, they found Lucy's home.

Lucy was very happy to be home. She said, "Thank you, fine helicopter, for providing help!" The helicopter was happy it could help Lucy. It flew away, ready to help more people.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in the park. One day, she went to the park with her mom and they saw a big sign that said, "Lost Lion". Lily asked her mom what it meant and her mom explained that a lion had run away and people were searching for it.

As they walked around the park, Lily saw a big, heavy rock and asked her mom if they could lift it up to see if the lion was hiding underneath. Her mom said no and reminded her that lions are dangerous and they should stay away from them.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar and saw the lion coming towards them! Lily's mom quickly picked her up and ran away. They found some people who were searching for the lion and told them where they saw it. The people were able to find the lion and take it back to its home at the zoo.

After they were safe, Lily's mom told her that they should always listen to the signs and not try to search for dangerous animals on their own. Lily nodded and promised to be careful in the future.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. They have a lot of fun making noises with their cars, dolls and blocks. They zoom, beep, bang and chatter as they pretend to be drivers, doctors and builders.

But their mom is working in the kitchen. She has a big headache and needs some quiet. She comes to the living room and says, "Anna, Ben, please stop making so much noise. You are hurting my head. Can you play something else?"

Anna and Ben look at their mom. They see that she is not happy. They love their mom and do not want to make her sad. They say, "Sorry, mom. We did not know you had a headache. We will play something else."

They put away their noisy toys and pick up some books. They sit on the couch and read quietly. They look at the pictures and say the words softly. They learn about animals, colors and shapes.

Their mom comes back to the living room. She sees that Anna and Ben are reading. She smiles and says, "Thank you, Anna, Ben. You are very good and kind. I feel better now. Do you want to read with me?"

Anna and Ben nod and hug their mom. They say, "Yes, mom. We love you. We love reading with you." They snuggle on the couch and read together. They are happy and quiet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to go to the beach. She loved to play in the sand and splash around in the water. One day she decided to try something new - she wanted to try to surf!

She got onto her board and tried to catch a wave, but it was harder than she thought. Finally, she managed to catch a big wave, but she fell off and started to cry. Her mom saw her and tried to comfort her, but the little girl was very upset.

However, the girl didn't give up. She kept trying and trying until she finally managed to surf the wave all the way to shore. When she reached the shore, she couldn't help but smile. It was so much fun! She was so happy, she jumped and shouted with joy. Everyone watched her, thinking she was so crazy.

And that's how the little girl learned to surf. She had lots of fun and still loves to go to the beach, where she can show off her surfing skills.

Once upon a time there was a queen who was very lovely. She lived in a big palace with lots of people. One day, two children went to visit. They were very excited and wanted to see the queen.

When they arrived, the queen said, â€œWelcome! I am so happy to meet you. What would you like to do?â€

The children smiled and said, â€œWe want to see you!â€ The queen smiled and said, â€œYes, of course you can.â€

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise coming from outside. The queen looked worried and said, â€œI am afraid I have to go now. It was nice to meet you!â€

The children were disappointed, but they said goodbye and waved as the queen left. They never saw the queen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant. The ant loved to crawl around and explore the world. One day, the ant saw a big, juicy cherry on the ground. The ant wanted to eat the cherry, but a rude bird was sitting on top of it. The bird wouldn't let the ant have any of the cherry. 

The ant thought and thought about how to get the cherry. Finally, the ant had an idea. The ant crawled up the bird's leg and tickled it. The bird laughed so hard that it fell off the cherry and the ant was able to enjoy a delicious snack. From that day on, the ant knew that even when things seem impossible, there is always a way to get what you want.

A mummy and her little girl called Sarah were getting ready to go on a trip. Sarah watched as her mummy packed a big sack with lots of things.

"What's in that sack, Mummy?" asked Sarah.

Mummy replied, "It's full of lots of fun things that we can take with us on our trip."

Sarah asked, "Can I take my dolly?"

Mummy replied, "Yes of course, but you will have to pack it into the sack yourself."

Sarah was excited and put her dolly safely into the big sack. She looked up at her mummy and smiled.

On the trip, Sarah met lots of friendly people and things she had not seen before. She was having a wonderful time. 

When it was time to go home, Sarah remembered that she had put her dolly in the sack and so she checked to make sure it was still there. It was! 

Mummy said to her, "Isn't it nice when things are packed up neatly and safely?"

Sarah nodded and smiled.

The moral of the story is to be careful to always pack up things neatly and safely, which helps us to take care of our possessions.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly mouse. He lived in a deep, dark wood. One day he was freezing cold. He had never felt this cold before. So he decided to go in search of warmth.

The mouse travelled far and wide. He looked for a warm and cozy place to rest. Soon he came across a house. He peeked through the windows and it looked warm. So he decided to enter the house.

Inside the house, it was nice and warm. The elderly mouse was very happy. He found a cozy corner and he snuggled up in it. He felt safe and content. 

The mouse was so happy that he even began to dance. As he was dancing, the homeowner suddenly arrived and saw the mouse. He was worried at first, but then he realized how cute and joyful the elderly mouse was. He could not bring himself to frighten away such a little one. 

So, instead, the homeowner opened the window and let the mouse just be free and warm. The elderly mouse thanked the homeowner and scampered away, never forgetting the warmth of that house.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy bunny named Benny. Benny was her favorite toy and she loved him very much. One day, Lily and her mommy went to a big building with lots of floors. They went inside the elevator and went up, up, up to the very top floor.

When they got out of the elevator, they saw a boy crying. Lily asked him why he was sad. The boy said he lost his teddy bear and didn't know where it was. Lily felt bad for him and said, "Don't worry, we'll help you find your teddy bear. Where does it belong?"

The boy said he thought he left it in the elevator. So they went back down, down, down in the elevator. When they got to the bottom, they saw the teddy bear sitting on the floor. The boy was so happy to find his teddy bear and said, "Thank you so much! You guys are the best!" Lily smiled and felt happy too. She knew how it felt to lose something she loved, like when her mommy accidentally spoiled her milk.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who was very selfish. She wasn't very nice to anyone who she didn't like. One day, she heard a story from the King. The story was about a magical necklace that could shrink anyone who put it on.

The selfish princess was curious, so she asked the King if she could try it out. He said yes, and she sneakily put on the necklace.

Suddenly, she began to shrink. The King was very surprised and told her to take it off quickly. But she didn't want to listen, she was too excited about being small.

The King begged and pleaded with her, but the selfish princess just laughed and kept shrinking. Finally, the King had had enough. He used his magic to make her shrink even more, until she was so small no one could see her.

The King sent out an announcement to the whole kingdom that anyone who could find the selfish princess would get a special prize. But no one ever found her. The selfish princess was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a special cage. It was very original and special. One day, a little girl decided she wanted to take it with her on an adventure. So she packed it very carefully in her suitcase. 

The girl was so excited for her adventure that she couldn't wait. She made sure the cage was safe and sound so she could bring it back home. 

When the adventure was over, the girl was tired but happy. She opened her suitcase and found the original cage was still there! She was delighted and couldn't wait to show it off to everyone.

The little girl was so pleased that she had been able to take the cage with her and wasn't worried anymore. Her adventure was now complete and the cage was back home with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little monkey named Bongo who lived in the jungle. Bongo loved to swing from tree to tree and play with his friends. One day, Bongo saw an adorable baby bird who had fallen out of its nest. Bongo wanted to help the baby bird.

"Hello, little bird," said Bongo. "What's wrong?"

"I fell out of my nest," said the baby bird. "I can't fly yet."

"Don't worry," said Bongo. "I will help you." Bongo picked up the baby bird and sprang up to the nest. The mama bird was very happy to see her baby back in the nest.

"Thank you, Bongo," said the mama bird. "You are very kind."

Bongo smiled and swung off to play with his friends. He was happy to have helped the adorable baby bird.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. Timmy loved Sundays because that was the day he got to play with his friends at the park. One Sunday, Timmy went to the park and saw his friend, Billy. But Billy didn't look cheerful. 

"Hi Billy, what's wrong?" asked Timmy.

"I lost my ball," said Billy, sadly. "I can't play without it."

"Don't worry, I'll help you find it," said Timmy, determined to help his friend. They looked all over the park, but they couldn't find the ball. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was thunder! 

"Oh no, it's going to strike us!" cried Billy, scared.

"Don't worry, we'll be safe under this tree," said Timmy, pointing to a big tree. They huddled under the tree and waited for the storm to pass. When it was over, they looked up and saw the sun shining again. 

"Thanks for helping me, Timmy," said Billy, with a big smile. "You're a good friend."

"I'm just happy to help," said Timmy, also smiling. They continued to play at the park, cheerful and happy once again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Mark. Mark was three years old, and he loved his mommy very much. One day, Mark and his mommy went to the park. 

At the park, Mark noticed a big berry tree. He wondered what would happen if he touched it. He asked his mommy, "Can I touch it?"

His mommy said, "No, Mark. It's hard to stay away from things that are tempting." So Mark smiled and waved to the berry tree. 

The next day, Mark saw some other kids trying to get the berries off the tree. But they had a hard time doing it. Mark remembered what his mommy said and decided to stay away, even though the berries looked very delicious. 

This is an important lesson, to stay away from tempting things even though they may look fun. What we should remember is that if something looks too hard, it's best to just stay away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom asked her to set the table for dinner. Lily got a plate for everyone and spread the napkins on them. She was very successful in setting the table all by herself.

As they sat down to eat, Lily's mom asked her to pass the butter. Lily tried to spread the butter on her bread, but it was too hard. Her mom showed her how to soften the butter and spread it easily. From that day on, Lily was able to spread butter on her bread all by herself.

Lily was proud of herself for being successful in setting the table and spreading the butter. She felt like a big girl and couldn't wait to help her mom in the kitchen again.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to visit her grandma. When she got there, her grandma gave her a big hug and said, "Hello, Lily! You are so polite."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, grandma!" Then, her grandma showed her how to do the lock on the front door. "You have to turn the key like this," she said, as she demonstrated.

Lily watched carefully and then tried it herself. She did it perfectly! "I did it, grandma!" she exclaimed. Her grandma smiled and said, "You are such a smart girl, Lily." And they spent the rest of the day playing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat yummy cookies every day. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. While playing, Timmy fell and hurt his eyes. He couldn't see anything anymore!

Timmy's parents took him to the doctor. The doctor said that Timmy's sight was damaged and he needed a special medicine to restore it. Timmy took the medicine and waited. After a few days, Timmy's sight was restored! He could see everything again, including his yummy cookies. Timmy was very happy and grateful to the doctor.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big bird in a tree. The bird has a shiny thing in its beak.

"Look, Lily, the bird has a ring!" Ben says. "I want the ring. It is pretty."

"No, Ben, the ring is not for us. It is the bird's. The bird needs it for its life. Maybe it is a gift for its mate. We should not take it," Lily says.

But Ben does not listen. He climbs the tree to get the ring. The bird sees him and gets angry. It flies at him and pecks his face. Ben screams and falls down. He hurts his head and his arm.

Lily runs to him and cries. She calls for help. A man comes and sees Ben. He calls an ambulance. The ambulance takes Ben to the hospital. Lily is very sad. She wishes Ben had listened to her. She hopes he will be okay. But he is not. He has a big wound on his head. He does not wake up. He dies. Lily loses her friend. She is very sorry. She learns a hard lesson. She should not keep things that are not hers. She should respect other lives.

Once there was a little girl named Alicia who was always asking questions. She wanted to know about the world around her and often asked her mom for answers. One day, she asked her mom why the sky was blue. Her mom told her it is because of the sunlight reflecting off the oceans.

Alicia became curious and wanted to know more. She asked her mom to help her search for the answers. So they looked in books, magazines and on the internet - but all the answers were too hard for Alicia to understand.

Alicia became troubled. No matter how hard they searched, they could not find an answer she could understand.

Then one day, her mom asked Alicia to look around her and suggested that the best answers are sometimes right in front of us. Alicia looked out the window and saw a bright blue sky. Suddenly, she knew why the sky was blue.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream and always got a cone when she went to the ice cream shop. One day, she was walking in the park and saw a cone on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it was not smooth, but instead it was bumpy and dirty.

Lily wanted to bury the cone so nobody would see it and step on it. She found a spot under a tree and dug a little hole with her hands. She put the cone in the hole and covered it with dirt.

As she walked away, she felt happy that she did something good for the park. She learned that even small actions, like burying a cone, can make a big difference. It's important to take care of our environment and keep it clean for everyone to enjoy.

One day, Jack went out to play in the garden. He was very excited to explore. He looked around and saw a wide field. He ran through it and saw a carrot! He was so excited to find it. He bent down to pick it up. It was so big and juicy. Jack smiled and held it up to show his parents. He ran back to tell them that he had found a big carrot. They were so proud of him.

Jack wanted to bring the carrot back to the garden. He had big plans for it. He wanted to put the carrot in the wide garden bed to grow. He carefully placed it in the soil, covered it up and watered it. Then he sat back to watch it grow.

Each day, Jack went back to the garden to check on his carrot. He watched as it grew bigger and bigger. He smiled and was so happy that he had found such a big carrot. Eventually, Jack was able to pick the carrot and take it home to eat. It was sweet and delicious. Jack was so proud of himself for having found such a special carrot.

Ben is a farmer. He has a big farm with many animals. He likes to feed the cows, the pigs, the sheep and the chickens. He also likes to grow corn, carrots, apples and pumpkins.

One day, Ben has to go to the town. He has to sell some of his food and buy some things for his farm. He takes his truck and drives on the road. He is happy to go to the town.

But on the way, he sees a big problem. There is a lot of water on the road. It rained a lot last night and the road is flooded. Ben cannot drive his truck through the water. He has to stop and wait. He is sad and worried. He does not want to delay his trip to the town.

Then he sees a big boat. It is a famous boat. It is the boat of the mayor. The mayor is the boss of the town. He is very nice and helps people. He sees Ben and his truck. He waves to him and says hello.

"Hello, Ben! I see you have a problem. Do you need some help?" the mayor says.

"Yes, please. I have to go to the town, but the road is flooded. Can you take me and my food on your boat?" Ben says.

"Of course, I can. Come on board, Ben. I have some space for you and your food. I am also going to the town. We can go together." the mayor says.

Ben is very happy. He thanks the mayor and puts his food on the boat. He gets on the boat and sits next to the mayor. The boat starts to move on the water. Ben sees the animals and the plants on his farm. He waves to them and says goodbye.

He is not sad and worried anymore. He is excited and grateful. He does not mind the delay. He is happy to go to the town with the mayor on his famous boat.

Once there was a little girl who was very curious. She loved to explore her house and see all the fun things in it. On day she opened a drawer in the kitchen and found it was very dirty. It was filthy! She took out a cloth and started to add some water to it. She then rubbed the cloth over the drawer and soon it was sparkly clean.

The little girl looked inside the now clean drawer and found lots of treasures - old buttons, sparkly beads and colorful felt pieces. She was so excited. She started to add the beads to the buttons to make jewelry. With the felt she made a special hat for her teddy bear.

The little girl was very happy with the fun things she found in the drawer. She decided to use the drawers from now on to store all her special treasures.

Once upon a time there was a family who lived by the sea. Every day they would take long walks by the shore and listen to the waves.
One day, the family decided to make a picnic by the sea. They made rice, salad and a spicy sauce. Everyone loved the sauce, especially the little girl. 
She ate it all up and insisted she wanted more. Her dad went to make the same sauce, but he just couldn't get the same taste. The little girl insisted that they go to the sea to get more of the spicy seasoning. 
So they followed the little girl and went searching for the spice. When they got to the sea, they didn't find any spices. Instead, they found a giant seahorse!
The seahorse asked for help as he had lost his way. The family agreed to help him and as a reward for their kindness, the seahorse gifted them a spicy sprinkle that tasted just like the one from the picnic. The little girl was very happy and ran back to the picnic. 
Everybody enjoyed the spicy sprinkle from the sea. 
The End.

Mum and Dad were at the beach with their three-year-old daughter. They wanted to show her something exciting.

"Look!" said Dad, pointing out to the sea. "An octopus!"

The little girl jumped with excitement. She had never seen one before.

The octopus had lots of arms and it was a clear, bright day.

Mum looked at it and smiled. "Do you know what? Octopuses are very clever. And they like to joke!"

Mum and Dad laughed, then Dad said, "Let's find out if it can joke too!"

He waved his hands and shouted, "Hey octopus! Tell us a joke!"

The octopus splashed its arms against the water and made silly noises.

The little girl giggled. "That octopus was telling you a joke!"

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bobby. He was loyal to his family and always played sports with them. He was the best of all the animals at sport.

One day Bobby decided to rise up early in the morning and surprise his family with a game of sport. He went off to find a perfect spot for the game. But when he came to it, he found that the spot was too small for all the animals! Bobby was so disappointed.

Bobby thought and thought about what to do and he decided to build a bigger field. With lots of determination, he worked hard for many days, picking stones, collecting soil, and planting grass. Finally, the field was ready and he invited everyone to the big game.

All the animals gathered at the field and cheered for Bobby, the loyal bear. Bobby was so proud and the game was so much fun. From that day on, they all rose up early in the morning to play sports with Bobby!

Tommy did not like meat. He thought it was disgusting. It smelled bad and tasted worse. He did not want to eat it for dinner.

But his mom said he had to eat some meat or he would not get any dessert. She put a big piece of meat on his plate. Tommy felt sad and angry.

He looked around the room. He saw his dog, Spot, under the table. He had an idea. He picked up his fork and pretended to eat the meat. But he did not put it in his mouth. He removed it from his plate and threw it under the table. Spot was happy. He ate the meat in one bite.

Tommy smiled. He thought he was clever. He asked his mom for dessert. But his mom was not fooled. She saw what he did. She was not happy. She said he had to eat another piece of meat or he would get no dessert and go to bed early.

Tommy felt sad and angry again. He did not like meat. He thought it was disgusting. He wished he had a different dinner.

Once there was a small village full of people and animals. But the village was so dull. Nothing ever happened there. All the animals and people were bored.

One day, a mysterious carriage rolled into the village. Everyone was so excited and they all stopped to look at it. Inside the carriage was a zebra with a very special power - it could zip!

The zebra used its special zip power to make the village much more fun. Suddenly the streets were full of exciting activities and bright colours! Everybody was thrilled and started to cheer. 

The zebra left the village with a big smile on its face. But it left something behind â€“ the feeling of excitement and happiness that it had brought to the village. From then on, the village was always cheerful and full of life.

Mummy was walking in the park with her little girl. Suddenly, the little girl saw a snake! She was scared and started to complain to mummy. But mummy said, "Don't worry, it's ok, the snake won't hurt us". Just then, an open door appeared near the snake. On the other side of the door was a big garden full of nice flowers and pretty birds. The little girl pointed to the door and said, "Let's go there, mummy!". Mummy said, "OK, lets go!" So the little girl and mummy opened the door and went through together. Inside the garden, there were no more snakes, only pretty things to look at. The little girl said, "I'm so glad we came here, it's much nicer!". And mummy smiled, happy to have made her daughter happy.

Once upon a time, there was a kitty named Mittens. Mittens had a paw that was different from her other paws. It was a little bit smaller, but that didn't stop her from playing and having fun with her friends.

One day, Mittens and her friends decided to decorate their treehouse. Mittens wanted everything to be perfect, so she carefully placed the decorations on the treehouse. Her friends helped too, and soon the treehouse looked beautiful.

Mittens was very happy with how the treehouse turned out. She looked at her paw and realized that even though it was different, it was still perfect for her. Mittens and her friends spent the rest of the day playing in their newly decorated treehouse, and they all had a paw-some time!

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Mia. Mia loved to bake. She often went to her kitchen to mix and stir ingredients for her tasty treats. 

One day, when she was in the kitchen, Mia found a big book. It was a novel, and Mia was so excited. She decided to sit down and read it.
 
But when Mia tried to read the book, the words sounded strange. She couldn't understand what they meant. Mia became deaf. She couldn't hear a thing.

Mia was so sad. She wondered if there was a way that she could hear the stories in the novel. Then, she had an idea. She grabbed her mixer, and mixed a bit of flour, sugar and milk. She put the dough in an oven and baked a jolly cake. 

When Mia took the cake out of the oven, she heard music and noise. Mia smiled as she ate her cake. She knew that as long as she kept baking, she would never have to be deaf again.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and watch TV. One day, they see a famous man on TV. He is a singer. He has a big hat and a shiny coat. He sings very loud and makes funny faces.

"Wow, he is so cool!" Ben says. "I want to be like him. What is his name?"

"I don't know," Lily says. "Maybe we can ask Mommy. She knows a lot of names."

They run to the kitchen, where Mommy is making lunch. They point to the TV and ask, "Mommy, who is that man? He is famous. He sings very loud and makes funny faces."

Mommy looks at the TV and smiles. "That man is Elton John. He is a very famous singer. He has a lot of songs and fans. Do you like his music?"

"Yes, we do!" Lily and Ben say. "He is so cool! Can we have his hat and coat?"

Mommy laughs. "No, you can't have his hat and coat. They are his. But you can pretend to be him. You can use your own hats and coats and sing with him."

Lily and Ben are happy. They run to their room and find their hats and coats. They put them on and go back to the TV. They sing with Elton John and make funny faces. They have a lot of fun.

But soon, Lily feels something in her tummy. She needs to go to the bathroom. She tells Ben, "Ben, I need to go to the bathroom. Can you pause the TV?"

Ben says, "No, I can't. The TV is not a video. It is live. If I pause it, we will miss the song. You have to wait."

Lily says, "But I can't wait. I really need to go to the bathroom. Please, Ben, pause the TV."

Ben says, "No, I won't. You have to wait. The song is almost over. It is the best part."

Lily says, "No, it is not. The best part is when I go to the bathroom. I don't want to have an accident. Please, Ben, pause the TV."

Ben says, "No, I don't. You have to wait. The song is over. Now, he is talking. He is saying his name. Listen, he is saying his name."

Lily says, "I don't care about his name. I care about the bathroom. Please, Ben, pause the TV."

Ben says, "No, I can't. He is saying his name. His name is Elton John. Elton John. Elton John."

Lily says, "I don't care about Elton John. I care about the bathroom. Please, Ben, pause the TV."

But Ben doesn't listen. He keeps saying, "Elton John. Elton John. Elton John."

Lily can't wait any longer. She runs to the bathroom. But she is too late. She has an accident. She feels wet and sad. She cries.

Mommy hears her cry. She comes to the bathroom. She sees Lily. She sees the accident. She says, "Oh, Lily, what happened? Why didn't you go to the bathroom sooner?"

Lily says, "I tried, Mommy, I tried. But Ben wouldn't pause the TV. He wanted to hear the name. The name of the famous man. The name of Elton John."

Mommy says, "Oh, Ben, that was not nice. You should have paused the TV. You should have let Lily go to the bathroom. The name of Elton John is not more important than the bathroom. The bathroom is more important than anything."

She hugs Lily and cleans her up. She changes her clothes and gives her a kiss. She says, "It's okay, Lily. It's not your fault. Accidents happen. Next time, you can go to the bathroom whenever you need to. And next time, Ben will pause the TV for you. Right, Ben?"

Ben feels sorry. He sees Lily. He sees Mommy. He says, "Yes, Mommy. I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong. I should have paused the TV. I should have let you go to the bathroom. The name of Elton John is not more important than the bathroom. The bathroom is more important than anything."

He hugs Lily and says, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you. You are more important than anything. Even more important than Elton John."

Lily smiles and says, "I love you too, Ben. You are more important than anything. Even more important than Elton John."

They hug and kiss. They say, "

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Bob. Bob had a very loyal friend, a dog named Skip. Skip and Bob would go on adventures every day.

One day, Bob said to Skip, "Let's go on a special adventure!" Bob grabbed his backpack and filled it with things he might need. Skip and Bob set off on their adventure. 

When they came to a river they needed to cross, Bob knew just what to do. He took a long zip out of his backpack and wrapped it around them. It was like he was giving them a big hug. 

Skip and Bob held onto the zip and together they crossed the river. And when they came to the other side, they were happy to still be together. They had faced a challenge, but they had stayed loyal to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was feeling sick and her mommy gave her some medicine to make her feel better. The medicine tasted sweet, like candy.

Lily's mommy said, "Take this medicine and you will feel better soon." Lily took the medicine and said, "Thank you, mommy."

Lily's daddy came into the room and said, "Look outside, the sun is shining so bright today!" Lily looked outside and saw the sun shining in the sky. She smiled and said, "The sun is shining, it's so pretty!" 

Lily's mommy said, "Yes, it's a beautiful day. Now take a nap and you will feel even better when you wake up." Lily closed her eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of the sweet medicine and the shining sun.

Ben likes to play with his toys. He has many toys, but his favorite is a big truck. He likes to make the truck go fast and loud. He likes to pretend the truck can destroy anything.

One day, Ben finds a book on the shelf. It is a story book with many pictures. Ben does not know how to read, but he likes to look at the pictures. He sees a picture of a dragon. The dragon is big and scary. It has fire in its mouth. It can destroy anything.

Ben wants to play with the dragon. He takes the book and the truck to his room. He puts the book on the floor. He makes the truck go fast and loud. He makes the truck hit the book. He wants to destroy the book. He thinks it is fun.

But Mom does not think it is fun. She hears the noise and comes to Ben's room. She sees the book and the truck. She sees the torn pages and the broken spine. She is angry and sad. She says, "Ben, what did you do? This was a special book. It was a hidden story. It was a gift from your grandma. She loved this story. She wanted you to love it too. You destroyed it. That is not nice. That is not how we treat books."

Ben feels bad. He did not know the book was special. He did not know the book was a hidden story. He did not know the book was a gift. He says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I did not mean to destroy it. I just wanted to play with the dragon. I like dragons. They can destroy anything."

Mom sighs. She hugs Ben. She says, "I know you like dragons, Ben. But books are not toys. Books are stories. Stories are precious. They can make us happy and sad. They can make us learn and dream. They can make us imagine. You can play with dragons in your imagination. But you cannot destroy stories. Stories are for sharing and caring. Do you understand?"

Ben nods. He says, "I understand, Mom. I'm sorry. I will not destroy stories again. I will be careful with books. Can you read me the story of the dragon? Maybe I will like it too."

Mom smiles. She says, "Of course, Ben. I will read you the story of the dragon. Maybe you will like it too. Maybe you will find another hidden story in the book. Maybe you will make your own story with the truck and the dragon. But remember, stories are for sharing and caring. Not for destroying."

Sam was a little boy who loved mail. Every morning he waited excitedly for the mailman to come. Today was extra special because Sam was very nervous. He was sure this would be the day he got his new novel in the mail.

He opened the door and sure enough, there it was. A big, shiny package with his name on it. He knew it had to be the book he wanted. He gave the mailman a big hug and then ran back inside.

He tore open the box and inside was the novel he'd been wanting for so long. He opened the cover and the first page said, "Welcome to a new adventure!" Sam smiled and couldn't wait to start reading.

He finished the novel late into the night. And when he flipped to the last page, he smiled and said, "I can't wait to get more mail!"

George was a little boy. He wanted to borrow a hose. But it was very gloomy outside. Everything was grey like the sky. 

He went to his neighbor, Mrs. Smith. He knocked on the door and asked politely, â€œCan I borrow your hose?â€ 

Mrs. Smith smiled at him. She said, â€œYes, you can borrow my hose! Here you go.â€ 

George was very happy. He thanked Mrs. Smith and gave her a big hug. He was so excited to have a hose that he could use. He took it outside and began to play with it. He laughed and giggled as the water went this way and that. 

He had so much fun with the hose, and he was sad when it was time for him to bring it back to Mrs. Smith. But he knew he could borrow it again someday.

Jack was feeling excited. He was about to perform in his very first show. The stage was full of lights and the audience was very lively. Everyone was looking forward to seeing him perform.

Jack was feeling very nervous, but he tried to remember his practice. But as he looked around the stage, he noticed some strange spices. It was pepper! He had never seen this before, and he was intrigued on how it could be used in the show.

He could not contain his excitement, so he decided to use the pepper to perform a new trick. He would make the audience laugh with a ticklish pepper shaker. Everyone loved the trick, but Jack kept putting too much pepper in it! They were getting more and more overwhelmed as the pepper filled the air.

Jack knew something was wrong when the audience stopped laughing. Instead, everyone was coughing and eyes were watering. He had made a mistake using the pepper, and he had made the audience really uncomfortable. 

When the show was over, Jack felt really embarrassed. He didn't understand why he hadn't just stuck to his original plan. He had been so excited about the rich smell of pepper and he had let it ruin everything. Jack learned a valuable lesson that day. His attempt to try something new had backfired and he was left feeling embarrassed by his mistake.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He was very generous and kind. He loved to share his food with everyone in the jungle. One day, a little girl came to the jungle to play. She saw the lion and said, "Hi, Mr. Lion! Can I play with you?"

The lion replied, "Sure, little girl. Let's play together!" They played all day long and had lots of fun. At the end of the day, the little girl said, "Thank you for playing with me, Mr. Lion. I had a great time."

The lion replied, "You're welcome, little girl. I had fun too." Then the little girl said, "I want to spend more time with you, Mr. Lion. Can I come back tomorrow?"

The lion said, "Of course, little girl. I would love to play with you again." But the next day, the little girl didn't come back. The lion waited and waited, but she never showed up. He was very sad and lonely. He realized that he had been too generous and kind to the little girl, and she had taken advantage of him. From that day on, the lion decided to be more careful about who he spent his time with.

Once upon a time there were two friends named George and Lola. They both loved eating yummy food and going to new places. One day, they walked to a new restaurant and opened the door. Inside they saw a furry cat. The cat spoke to them in a soft voice. She said "Welcome, I'm Mia the cat. Would you like to try my delicious food?"

George and Lola smiled at each other, and then said yes together. Mia the cat led them to a table and pointed at the menu. George and Lola chose to have pizza with cheese, olives and tomatoes. Mia said she was going to the kitchen to bring them their food.

Meanwhile, George and Lola talked and laughed together as they waited for the food. A few minutes later, Mia returned with pizza and two plates. Yum! George and Lola were so excited that they couldn't wait to eat. It tasted so good that they asked for more. Mia was happy to bring them more tasty food.

When they finished eating, George and Lola thanked Mia for their delicious meal. She smiled at them and said "you're welcome. Come back anytime!" They waved goodbye and left the restaurant, still talking and laughing together.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy cat. The cat was not happy and meowed all day long. One day, the cat looked up at the sky and saw the sun setting. The sky was orange and pink. The cat watched as the sun settled down and the sky turned dark. Suddenly, the cat felt happy and stopped meowing. The cat settled down and fell asleep under the stars. From that day on, the cat was never grumpy again.

Molly was very excited. Her mom had invited her to the classroom. When they got there, she saw a big blackboard on the wall. It was white and shiny, like a clean piece of paper. All around were children laughing, smiling and playing.

Molly wanted to join them but she didn't know what to do. Then, her mom said, "Let's try something fun." She took out a white chalk and wrote something on the blackboard. She invited Molly to come closer and look.

Molly saw that her mom had drawn a picture of a big white bear! She smiled and clapped her hands. Her mom had made a game for her.

She got to take turns with her friends, erasing a small part of the white bear and then replacing it with a different color. Soon the big white bear was rainbow colored and the classroom was filled with laughter and joy. Molly was so happy and couldn't wait to do it all again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Timmy found a blue rock while he was playing outside. He thought it was very pretty because blue was his favorite color.

Timmy decided to hide the blue rock in a rare spot so that no one could find it. He looked all around the yard and finally found the perfect spot. He dug a little hole and put the blue rock inside. Timmy was very proud of himself for finding such a good hiding spot.

Later, when Timmy's friends came over to play, he told them about the blue rock he had found and how he hid it in a rare spot. They all searched for a long time, but no one could find the blue rock. Timmy was happy that he had found something special and was able to keep it safe in his rare hiding spot.

Once upon a time there was a lazy pipe. He didn't like to move very much and so spent most of his days sleeping.

One day, he was awoken by a voice. It was a number! The number said, "Hey pipe! Wake up! Let's go exploring!". The pipe sighed and replied, "No thanks. I'm too lazy to move." 

But the number was persistent. He said, "Come on, pipe! Moving will make you feel better, I promise!"

The pipe thought about it for a minute, and then decided to give it a try. So, he moved his long body around and even danced a bit. He was surprised to find that he actually enjoyed it!

So, from then on the lazy pipe and the number went on many fun adventures. No matter what, the pipe was always happy to go exploring with his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved the beach. She wanted to go to the beach every day, but her mom said no. One day, when it was getting dark outside, Mom said yes! The little girl was so excited, she ran to get her beach bag.

The little girl and her mom drove to the beach. When they arrived, it was dark. The little girl couldn't see the beach, but she could hear the waves. She thought it must be a magic beach.

The little girl and her mom walked to the beach. It was so dark, the little girl could only see a few stars in the sky. She thought that made the beach even more magical. 

The little girl stayed at the beach until it was very late. When it was time to go, the little girl said goodbye to the magical beach. She said she would come back soon and think about the beach every day.

Mia and Mama were in the kitchen. Mama was putting a calendar on the wall. Mia asked Mama what it was. Mama said it was a calendar to help them remember special days. Mia thought it was easy to understand. 

Mama asked Mia if she wanted to help with the calendar. Mia said yes and they both started placing stickers on it. Mia thought it was fun to put them on. Then they noticed a tear on the calendar.
