Mama asked Mia what made the tear. Mia said she didn't know. She saw a drawer open and thought maybe something from the drawer made the tear. Mama looked inside the drawer and saw a pair of scissors. 

Mia said she might have used the scissors without meaning to destroy the calendar. Mama hugged Mia and said it was okay. Mama said there was an easy way to fix it. Together they mended the tear. Then Mia and Mama high-fived each other.

Once there was a boy called Jack. He was only 3 years old and loved nothing more than playing with his toys. One day he decided that he wanted to sort out his toys. He took one of his trays and put all of his harmless toys on it. He carefully arranged the toys so that he knew where each one went. 

After he finished sorting them out, he was so pleased with what he had done. He smiled and clapped his hands. Then he ran off to find more toys to sort out. He wanted to try sorting out more complex toys too!

The next day Jack was back sorting out toys. This time he had found some colourful beads. He picked them up from the tray and put them in different piles according to the colour. When he finished sorting the beads he felt very proud of himself.

Jack was so happy he could sort out his toys! Now he could find them quickly and easily. He knew it was all his hard work that made it so. He ran off to go find something else to sort.

One day, a small cat went for a walk. The cat saw a big rock. The cat wanted to cover the rock with leaves. So, the cat started to work. 

The cat saw a dog walk by. The dog said, "I can help you." But the cat said, "No, I can do it." The dog left and went down the pass. The cat felt helpless but kept working.

The cat covered the rock with leaves. It was getting dark. The cat was very tired. The dog came back and said, "I told you I could help." The cat was sad and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to drink juice from a big cup. One day, Timmy drank too much juice and his stomach got very hard. He didn't feel good, but he didn't want to stop drinking juice.

The next day, Timmy's stomach hurt even more. He cried and cried, but his mommy couldn't make it better. Timmy had to go to the hospital. The doctors said Timmy had to stop drinking so much juice.

Timmy was sad that he couldn't drink as much juice anymore, but he knew it was important to take care of his stomach. From that day on, Timmy only drank a little bit of juice at a time.

Once upon a time, a dolphin was in the sea. She was gentle and she liked to stir. She moved around the water, using her fins to stir up the ocean. She would twist her body and splash around. 

On the shore, the little boy was watching the dolphin. He was three years old and he always loved dolphins. He was so excited to see the dolphin stirring up the sea. The dolphin seemed to be dancing, flipping through the water with grace.

Then, abruptly, she stopped. The little boy was anxious and curious. He was wondering what happened. He couldn't wait to get closer to the dolphin.

But then, the dolphin started moving again. Closer and closer to the shore, she came. The little boy was happy and clapping. When the dolphin finally reached the shore, the little boy was able to touch her gentle back. He looked into her eyes and smiled. The dolphin was stirring the sea, but it was all the more fun now that the little boy was a part of it!

Once upon a time, there was a big doll. She was very pretty, with golden curls and bright buttons for eyes. The doll had many friends, and was always having fun.

One day, the doll was outside playing hide-and-seek with all of her friends. They had been playing for a while when the doll noticed something strange. Her friends had suddenly disappeared!

The doll began to worry. Where had her friends gone? She looked all over, but could not find them. Suddenly, she felt scared and alone.

Then, the doll heard a laugh coming from behind a big tree. There were her friends! They had found a spot to keep playing and forgotten to tell the doll. 

The doll was relieved and excited to join them. She never worried again when playing with her friends.

Once upon a time there lived a girl called Emma. One day, Emma got an invite to the a birthday party. She was very excited. She quickly put on a pretty dress and rushed to the party.

When she got there it was very big. She couldn't believe it! It was enormous. Everything was so colourful and there were so many people there.

The party had lots of fun things to do. Everyone was eating cake and playing games. But Emma couldn't join in. Her tooth was very sore and it caused her pain. She tried to cope but it was too much and she started to cry.

Everyone was so kind and wanted to help her. They got some ice cream and put it on her tooth. It was cold but it felt better. Soon, she was able to join in with the party and she had lots of fun.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big pole with wires on top. Tom wanted to climb the pole. He said, "Look, Lily, I can be powerful like a superhero. I can touch the wires and make sparks."

Lily was scared. She said, "No, Tom, don't do that. The pole is dangerous. The wires have electricity. Electricity can hurt you. It can make you fall and cry."

Tom did not listen. He ran to the pole and started to climb. He reached for the wires. He felt a shock. He screamed and let go. He fell to the ground. He was hurt and crying.

Lily ran to Tom. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay? You should not climb the pole. It is not a toy. It is for the lights and the phones. You should be careful and listen to me."

Tom was sorry too. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. You were right. The pole is not powerful. It is scary. I will not climb it again. I will listen to you. You are my friend."

Once upon a time, there was a busy boy named Jack. He loved adventure, so he decided to go fishing. He grabbed a raft and started paddling out to the middle of the lake.

When he arrived, he cast his line out in the cool water and waited. He felt a pinch on the end of the line! Quickly, he pulled in the line, and there was a big, shiny fish. He cheered in delight!

Jack looked around, and there were ten other rafts with other busy fishermen. They were all trying to catch the biggest fish. Jack had his big prize, so he decided to paddle back to shore.

He was so proud of his big catch! When Jack got home, he told everyone about his adventure and the big fish he had caught. He went fishing every day after that. What a lucky little boy!

Once, there was a very important bell. Everyday, the bell would ring loudly. Everyone in the village heard the bell. It was a sign that something special was happening.

One day, the bell rang and everyone gathered around the village square. The mayor of the village said that today was a special day. He included everyone in a special game. Everyone was so excited and happy.

The mayor said to stay very quiet and to all close their eyes when the bell rang again. Everyone followed the mayorâ€™s instructions and the bell rang again. When the bell stopped ringing, everyone opened their eyes and the mayor held up a big box full of surprises!

Everyone who was included was so happy. They all laughed and cheered for the surprises. From then on, the bell was very important to the village. It was always a sign that something special was happening and that everyone was included in it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden, where she had a pretty flower bed. One day, she saw a big bug crawling on her flowers. She knew that bugs can sometimes be harmful to the flowers, so she decided to protect them. She gently shooed the bug away and made sure her flowers were safe. 

Later that day, Lily's mom gave her a glass of juice. But Lily didn't want to drink it all and left some in the glass. Her mom explained that wasting food and drinks is not good, and we should always try to finish what we have. Lily understood and promised to not waste anything again. 

From that day on, Lily made sure to protect her flowers and not waste anything. She felt proud of herself for being a good girl.

Once upon a time there was a small boy. He had a big dream but he felt so small. Everyday he would look at the nearby mountain and see a scale. The scale looked so tall and strong and seemed like it would never move.

One day the boy decided he was going to fight the scale. He took a deep breath, clenched his fists and started running uphill. With each step he felt stronger and more courageous.

As he reached the top of the mountain, he leaped onto the scale. He held on tight and kicked with all his might. Suddenly, the scale began to move! 

The boy cheered and shouted with joy. He had fought the scale and won! From that day onwards, the boy dreamt bigger and bigger dreams. He was no longer small and vulnerable. He was brave and strong.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily wanted to play with her friend's toy. She asked her mommy if she could borrow it. Her mommy said it was okay, as long as she remembered to give it back.

Lily went to her friend's house and asked if she could borrow the toy. Her friend was kind and said yes. Lily was very happy and played with the toy for a long time. When it was time to go home, Lily remembered to give the toy back to her friend.

As Lily walked home, she saw a big wall. She thought it was very tall and wondered what was on the other side. But she knew she couldn't climb it, so she just walked along it until she got home. When she got home, she told her mommy and daddy about the wall and they thought it was very interesting.

One day, Joe and his mommy went to the park. Joe saw a pretty lady wearing a skirt. He thought it was so silly and wanted one too.

So Joe asked his mom if he could get one. She thought it was a great idea and took him to the store. Joe picked out the silliest skirt he could find. It was bright yellow with purple polka dots.

When they got home, Joe put on the skirt right away. He felt silly but happy. His mommy smiled and said, "Welcome to the world of fashion, Joe!" 

Joe laughed and spun around, loving the way that the skirt swooshed around him. He couldn't wait to show his friends at the park the next day.

Lily and Max are best friends. They like to play in the park with their toys. Lily has a yellow ball and Max has a blue car. They share their toys and have fun.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. The dog is loud and fast. It runs after Lily and Max and tries to take their toys. Lily and Max are scared. They drop their toys and run away.

"Help, help!" they cry. "The dog is bad!"

Mama and Papa hear them. They come to the park and see the dog. They shout at the dog and make it go away. They pick up the toys and give them back to Lily and Max.

"Are you okay, my loves?" Mama asks.

"Yes, Mama, we are okay," Lily says.

"Thank you, Mama, thank you, Papa," Max says.

Mama and Papa hug Lily and Max. They are happy and safe.

"Let's go home now," Papa says.

"Yes, let's go home," Lily and Max agree.

They hold hands and walk home. Home is warm and cozy. They have milk and cookies and tell Mama and Papa about their day. They hug each other and say good night. They sleep well and dream of the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brown notebook that she loved to draw in. One day, Lily promised her mom that she would clean up her toys before dinner.

But Lily got distracted and forgot to clean up her toys. When her mom asked if she had kept her promise, Lily felt bad and sad. She remembered her brown notebook and how she would feel if someone broke a promise to her.

So, Lily quickly cleaned up her toys and apologized to her mom for forgetting. Her mom forgave her and Lily felt happy again. She learned that it's important to keep your promises and that it feels good to do the right thing.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. Sara opened the cupboard and saw a big cake. It was chocolate with pink frosting and sprinkles. Sara admired the cake. It looked incredible.

"Wow, look at this cake!" Sara said to Ben. "It is so pretty and big. I want to eat it."

Ben came over and saw the cake too. He admired the cake as well. It smelled incredible.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said. "Let's have a slice. Mom won't mind."

Sara and Ben took a knife and cut a big piece of cake. They put it on a plate and shared it. They ate it with their fingers and made a mess. The cake was incredible. It was sweet and soft and melted in their mouths.

They were so happy and full. They did not hear Mom coming into the kitchen. Mom saw the cake and the plate and the mess. She was not happy.

"Sara and Ben, what have you done?" Mom said. "That cake was for Grandma's birthday. You were not supposed to touch it."

Sara and Ben felt bad. They did not know the cake was for Grandma. They loved Grandma and wanted to make her happy.

"We're sorry, Mom," Sara and Ben said. "We admired the cake and wanted to try it. It was incredible."

Mom sighed. She was angry, but she also loved Sara and Ben. She knew they did not mean to ruin the cake.

"It's okay, my loves," Mom said. "But you have to ask before you take something from the cupboard. And you have to clean up your mess. And you have to help me make a new cake for Grandma. Can you do that?"

Sara and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry again. They hugged Mom and helped her clean up. They also helped her make a new cake for Grandma. It was vanilla with blue frosting and stars. It was incredible too. Sara and Ben admired the cake and hoped Grandma would like it. They learned their lesson and did not touch the cake until Grandma came. Grandma was happy and gave them a big kiss. She said the cake was incredible and so were they.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy loved to play football. He had a red ball that he kicked around his yard every day. One day, it started to rain. Timmy ran inside and watched the raindrops fall from his window. He thought the rain looked like little tears from the sky.

Timmy's mom made him a delicious snack of peanut butter and jelly. He ate it while he watched the rain. After the rain stopped, Timmy went back outside to play with his football. The grass was wet and squishy, but he didn't mind. He kicked the ball through the puddles and pretended he was playing in the World Cup.

From that day on, Timmy loved playing football in the rain. He said it made the grass taste even more delicious.

Once there was a boy named Tom. Tom was three years old and loved to explore. One day Tom's mommy said they were going to see a volcano. Tom was so excited!

When they arrived, Tom and his mommy looked up at the volcano. It was huge and empty. Tom was so amazed he couldn't believe it was real.

Tom and his mommy walked around the volcano and looked at the different rocks. Tom could see the birds flying around and far away the sun was setting. Tom clapped his hands and shouted with joy.

Tom and his mommy continued looking around. They could see the smoke come out of the volcano. It was exciting and Tom laughed.

On their way home, Tom waved goodbye to the empty volcano and thanked it for the wonderful day. He knew he'd always remember this amazing sight.

Mia was building lots of different shapes with blocks. She had built a big circle and a square and lots of different shapes! Daddy came in to join her and asked what she had built.

"I've made a circle and a square," explained Mia. "I'm going to make a cube next!"

Mia started to lay out the blocks in a cube shape. Daddy sat down and watched her build. After a while, the cube was finished!

"Look Daddy, I made a cube!" exclaimed Mia.

"That's great Mia," said Daddy.

"That cube looks really fit," he said.

Mia smiled and she was really proud of her cube. Then she started to make another cube. This one was even more fit!

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jane. She was very curious and enjoyed new adventures. She wanted to explore the world and all the different places she could visit.

One day she decided to go down to the river. When she arrived, something unusual happened. There was an old man sitting by the river. He was wearing a big hat and he smiled at her.

Jane sat down beside him and he asked her if she wanted to go on an adventure. Jane smiled and nodded her head. She was so excited. 

The old man took her on a boat ride down the river. Along the way, they saw lots of animals and plants. They even saw some fish jumping in and out of the water. It was like nothing Jane had ever seen before.

When they reached the end of the river, the old man looked at Jane and smiled. She knew it was time to say goodbye. With one last nod of her head, she said goodbye and headed back home. 

It had been a very unusual adventure, but Jane loved every minute of it.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to go for walks with his owner, Sarah. One day, Sarah put a leash on Max and they went for a walk. Max was glad to be outside.

As they walked, Max saw a cat sitting on a fence. Max stopped and stared at the cat. "Woof woof!" Max barked. The cat ran away.

Sarah laughed and said, "Max, you scared the cat! Let's keep walking." Max wagged his tail and they continued their walk.

Soon, they met another dog named Bella. Bella was also on a walk with her owner. Max and Bella sniffed each other and wagged their tails. Sarah and Bella's owner chatted for a bit before they said goodbye.

Max and Sarah continued their walk, and Max was glad to be outside with his owner.

Once upon a time there was a little dancer. She was very brave, but she was also a bit nervous. Every day she practised hard to make her dancing better.

One day, her mum said she could go see a show. It was a special show just for dancers. The little dancer was so excited! She couldn't wait to go.

On the night of the show, her mum let her dress up in a special outfit. It was a sparkly dress and shiny shoes. She was almost ready to go!

When they arrived at the theatre, the little dancer was even more nervous. She was standing in front of lots of people and she wasn't sure if she could do it. But she was brave and took her first step.

Soon the little dancer found herself enjoying the show. It was even better than she had imagined! She danced and twirled with the rest of the dancers. She was so happy!

At the end of the show, the audience clapped and cheered. The little dancer smiled and waved. She was so proud of what she had achieved.

Once there was a bad monster who wanted to destroy everything. He saw a print and wanted to destroy it. He tried to tear it, but it wouldn't break. He tried to pull it, but he couldn't take it away. He was so angry! Then a big hero came along and saw the monster trying to destroy the print. The hero shouted loudly, which made the monster scared. The monster ran away, and the hero saved the print from being destroyed. Everyone was so happy that the print was safe, and the monster was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was 3 years old and very curious. Every day, she liked to explore her world and figure out what was what.

One day, she was in the living room with her daddy. He was doing something with a tape measure. The little girl asked what he was doing and he said he was measuring the room.

The little girl asked if she could help. Daddy said yes and showed her what he was doing. She used the soft tape measure and measured the room with Daddy. She loved using the tape measure and seeing the numbers it made.

When they were done, the little girl and Daddy laughed and hugged. They were so proud that they had measured the room together. Daddy gave the little girl a big kiss and said she was a very good helper. She smiled and was happy that she had helped Daddy.

Lily and Max were playing in the yard. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they kicked it too hard and it went over the fence. Then they had to ask the neighbor, Mr. Brown, to give it back.

One day, they saw a shiny thing on the ground. It was a screw. Lily picked it up and showed it to Max. "Look, a screw!" she said. "What is it for?"

"I don't know," Max said. "Maybe it fell from a car or a bike. Let's keep it. It's cool."

They put the screw in their pocket and went back to kicking the ball. They did not see Mr. Brown watching them from his window. He looked angry. He had been fixing his lawnmower and he needed that screw.

The next time they kicked the ball over the fence, they ran to the gate and called Mr. Brown. "Mr. Brown, can we have our ball back, please?" they asked.

Mr. Brown came out with the ball in his hand. He looked at them and said, "Sure, you can have your ball back. But first, you have to give me something back. Something that belongs to me. Something that you took from my yard."

Lily and Max looked at each other. They did not know what he meant. They had not taken anything from his yard. They only played with their ball. They felt scared.

"What do you want, Mr. Brown?" Lily asked.

Mr. Brown pointed at their pocket. "I want my screw back. The one you found on the ground. The one that I need to fix my lawnmower. The one that you stole from me."

Lily and Max gasped. They remembered the screw. They did not know it was his. They did not mean to steal it. They took it out of their pocket and gave it to him. "We're sorry, Mr. Brown," they said. "We didn't know it was yours. We thought it was just a regular screw. We won't take anything from your yard again."

Mr. Brown took the screw and nodded. He gave them their ball back. "Thank you, kids," he said. "Now you know. Don't take things that are not yours. And don't kick the ball so hard. It might break something."

Lily and Max nodded. They said thank you and ran back to their yard. They decided to play something else. They did not want to make Mr. Brown angry again. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite pillow that was black and soft. She loved to cuddle with it every night before she went to bed. 

One day, Lily's little brother, Max, wanted to play with her pillow. But Lily didn't want to share it because it was her favorite. Max got upset and started to cry. 

Lily felt bad for making her brother cry, so she decided to supply him with his own pillow. She found a fluffy white pillow and gave it to Max. He was so happy and hugged it tightly. 

Lily learned that it's important to share and be kind to others. From that day on, she always made sure to supply her brother with anything he needed. And they both slept soundly with their own pillows every night.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy bird and her young babies. They lived in a nest in a tall tree. One day, a big storm came and the wind was very strong. The mommy bird had to raise her wings to keep her babies warm and safe. She was very calm even though she was scared.

After the storm, the mommy bird and her young babies were very happy because they were okay. The mommy bird knew she had to teach her young babies how to fly so they could be ready for the next storm. She showed them how to raise their wings and fly high in the sky.

The young babies were very excited to fly and explore the world. They were also very calm because they knew their mommy was always there to help them. From that day on, the mommy bird and her young babies flew together and had many adventures.

Timmy was very excited. His mum and dad had bought him a special bell for his bedroom. It was a big brass bell with a long, shiny handle. Whenever Timmy wanted to call his mum or dad, he just had to ring the bell.

One day, his mum said, "It's time for your exam!" Timmy's eyes grew wide. He was a bit scared. He wasn't sure what an exam was.

"But why?" he asked.

His mum smiled. "It's just for fun," she said. "It's a silly game that we can play."

Timmy looked at his mum and dad with big, hopeful eyes.

"It's okay," his dad said. "You can ring the bell if you get stuck or need help. When you're finished, we'll all ring the bell together. Isn't that a good idea?"

Timmy nodded. He took a deep breath and started the exam. He was worried at first, but soon he was having fun. Whenever he got stuck, he'd ring the bell and get help from mum or dad.

When he finished the exam, he and his parents rang the bell together. It was the best exam that Timmy had ever taken!

One day, a good dog named Max went for a walk. He saw a big tree and leaned on it. He felt happy and wagged his tail.

Max saw a cop and his car. The cop leaned on the car and smiled at Max. Max knew the cop was nice and wanted to help people.

Later, Max saw a cat stuck in the tree he leaned on before. He barked to call the cop. The cop came and helped the cat down. Max and the cop were both happy they could help the cat. The cat was safe, and they all became good friends.

Tom was a man who liked to work on his car. He had a big car that made loud noises when he drove it. He had many tools that he used to fix his car. He was happy when his car worked well.

One day, Tom wanted to go for a drive. He put on his hat and his coat and went to his car. He tried to start his car, but it did not work. He tried again and again, but nothing happened. He was very angry and sad. He said, "Why does my car not work? I need to go for a drive!"

He got out of his car and opened the hood. He looked inside and saw a lot of wires and parts. He did not know what was wrong. He took his tools and tried to fix his car. He hit and twisted and pulled and pushed, but nothing changed. He was very frustrated and tired. He said, "This is too hard! I do not know how to fix my car!"

He threw his tools on the ground and sat on the hood. He sighed and looked at the sky. He wished he had a friend who could help him. He wished he had a new car that worked well. He wished he could go for a drive.

But he had no friend, no new car, and no drive. He had only his broken car, his tools, and his hat and coat. He was very lonely and unhappy. He said, "This is the worst day ever! I hate my car!"

He stayed on the hood and sighed. He did not see the big truck that was coming down the road. He did not hear the loud horn that warned him. He did not feel the crash that smashed his car and him. He did not know that he was dead. He had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park and saw a big green dragon. It was different from any dragon she had ever seen before.

"Hello, dragon," said Lily. "Why are you here?"

"I'm here to find a spring," said the dragon. "I'm very thirsty."

Lily knew where the spring was and offered to show the dragon. But when they got there, they found out that the spring was dry. The dragon was very sad.

"Don't worry," said Lily. "We can find water somewhere else."

They searched and searched until they found a pond. The dragon drank the water and felt much better. "Thank you, Lily," said the dragon. "You're a great friend."

From that day on, Lily and the dragon played together every day at the park. They had lots of fun and were happy to have each other as friends.

Gwen and her mom had a very special project. They were going to decorate together! Gwen was so excited and tapped the paintbrush on the ground.

First, Gwen's mom gave her a special seal. It was for sticking on the paper. Gwen put it in the center of the paper.

Then, Gwen painted around the seal with bright colors. She made a rainbow and a happy sun!

Finally, Gwen's mom opened up a box of glitter. They sprinkled it all around the seal. Now it was decorated and sparkly! Gwen clapped her hands together in excitement.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Ben. He was 3 years old, and one day he decided to go on an adventure. He walked outside and he started running around the garden. All of a sudden, he saw a flag poking out of the ground. He was very excited! 

Ben ran over to the flag and pulled it out of the ground. He saw that it was red and white. He waved it around and shouted, "This is my flag!"

Ben's mom heard him, and came out of the house. She said, "What are you doing?"

Ben said, "I found a flag and I'm using it for my adventure!"

His mom smiled and said, "That's very exciting! But you need to be careful. The flag is very old and the fabric is a bit bitter."

Ben smiled and said, "Ok mom. I'll be careful!"

So Ben continued his adventure with his new flag, always remembering to be gentle with it because it was old and a bit bitter.

Molly was a little girl who loved to guess things. She would guess what color the sky was, what kind of animal would appear next, and even what shape the clouds were.

One day, her mommy gave her a special surprise. It was a new crib! Molly was so excited! She couldn't believe it! The crib was so colorful. It was pink and blue and green, and it had lots of stars and moons all over it- just like a starry night sky.

Molly loved to play in her new crib. She would guess the colors of the stars and the clouds. She would make up stories about the moon and the stars flying around in the sky.

Molly was so happy in her new crib. It was the perfect place for her to play and use her guessing skills. From that day on, she always loved to guess things - and have lots of fun in her colorful crib!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Every day, her mommy would ask her to test her knowledge by asking her some questions.

One day, Mommy asked, â€œJane, what is round, green and juicy?â€ Jane thought hard and then said, â€œA pear!â€ Her mommy was very proud.

The next day, Mommy asked her another question. She said, â€œJane, how can you tell if something is rich?â€ Jane thought for a while and then said, â€œIt looks happy and shiny!â€ Mommy smiled and said, â€œThatâ€™s correct!â€

Every day, Mommy would test Jane and Jane kept getting smarter and smarter. They would spend the evenings talking about the questions and the answers. It became a fun game for them and Jane would always be happy when she got the right answer.

Eventually, Jane became very knowledgeable, thanks to all the tests Mommy gave her. But even more important than that is the special bond that Jane and Mommy shared through the tests, which gave them both lots of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a robot toy that he loved to play with. One day, Timmy and his sister Sarah were playing hide and seek. Timmy decided to hide his robot so Sarah wouldn't find it. He put the robot in a box and covered it with a blanket. 

Sarah looked everywhere for Timmy's robot, but she couldn't find it. She asked Timmy where it was, but he said he didn't know. Sarah was getting upset because she really wanted to play with the robot too. 

Timmy realized that he was being selfish and decided to show Sarah where he hid the robot. He carefully uncovered the box and showed Sarah the robot. She was so happy and thanked Timmy for being kind and sharing his toy. From that day on, they played with the robot together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a cheerful mama and she was looking for her baby. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find her little one.

Mama walked into the living room and saw the roof was open. Under the roof she heard a baby yell. She thought to herself, "my baby must be up there".

Mama looked up and saw her cheerful baby playing in the roof. She smiled at the sight and yelled, "come down here!"

But it was too late - the baby was already too far in the roof. Mama didn't know what to do, so she started to cry.

She yelled one more time in desperation, "come down right now!" But the baby didn't listen and the roof started to fall.

The roof crashed to the ground and the mama's happy baby was gone. Mama was so sad and cried in grief.

The baby never came back, leaving the mama sad and brokenhearted. The roof was a reminder of the cheerful kid she once had, but would never have again.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day she went for a walk in the woods.

Deep in the woods, Sarah saw something sparkling in the grass. It looked like a diamond. She bent down and picked it up. It was very tough, so she could not break it.

Suddenly, a giant appeared in front of her. He said, "That is my diamond! Give it back to me!"

Sarah was scared, but she didn't want to give the diamond away. She sat down in the grass and hugged the diamond with both arms.

The giant pointed at her and said, "You are brave. You can keep the diamond. But be careful. It is very tough and can hurt you."

Sarah thanked the giant and put the diamond in her pocket. From then on, she kept the diamond very safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and talking to her stuffed animals. One day, she went to visit her grandma's house. Grandma had a big, old clock that chimed every hour. Lily was fascinated by it.

As they were eating lunch, Lily asked, "Grandma, what's inside the clock?" 

"Well, it's a bunch of gears and springs that make it work," replied Grandma.

Lily thought about this for a moment and then asked, "Does it weigh a lot?"

"Yes, it's pretty heavy," said Grandma.

That night, Lily was sleeping in the guest room when she heard a strange noise. She looked up and saw a ghost floating in the air! The ghost was persistent and wouldn't go away. 

Lily was scared and ran to her grandma's room. "Grandma, there's a ghost in my room!" she cried.

Grandma went to investigate and found that the old clock had stopped working. She knew just what to do. She fixed the clock and the ghost disappeared. From then on, Lily loved the clock even more and would always ask, "Grandma, can we weigh the clock again?"

Sarah was feeling worried. She sat on her porch and looked outside at the warm sun. She was sure that summer was coming soon, but she was worried about something else.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was her best friend, Joe! He was running to her house and smiling from ear to ear.

"Joe," Sarah said. "What are you so happy about?"

Joe took a deep breath and said proudly, "I have a surprise for you - something I have been planning all season!"

Sarah was even more curious now. What could it be?

Joe only smiled and said, "You'll find out soon."

Confused, Sarah watched as Joe pulled out a big box. When he opened it up, she was filled with joy - inside was a big teddy bear!

Joe said with a big grin, "This is for you. I wanted to give you a hug that would last all season!"

Sarah was so happy and she hugged her teddy bear tightly. She knew that Joe was the best friend she could ever have.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jane and John. They decided to go on an adventure and explore the park near their home. As they walked, Jane noticed a rare flower growing in the grass. She wanted to pick it, but before she could, John warned her not to. He said that nearby was a very special cross and it was important that the flower stay there.

Jane was scared and started to panic. She wanted to leave the park and go home. But then suddenly the sky lit up as a bright rainbow appeared in the clouds. The cross began to glow and Jane noticed that it was a magical cross that had some kind of special power. She was no longer scared and she and John stayed there to admire the view.

They watched until the rainbow slowly disappeared. As it did, the cross stopped glowing and Jane realized how very rare and special it was. She thanked John for warning her not to pick the flower and they went home. 

The end.

Milly was very excited. She had waited for this day for so long and was happy it was finally here.

She was standing at the door, ready to go outside. Milly opened it and saw the beautiful brown tree. It had so many leaves, and they were all waving in the wind - it was wonderful!

Milly ran to the tree and jumped up. She could touch it now! She wanted to take one of the leaves, so she reached up and plucked one gently.

Suddenly, the leaf started to wink! Milly gasped - it was amazing. She dared it to keep winking, and it did! Milly was so excited that she ran back inside to tell her mom.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They also liked to eat dessert after dinner, but their mom said they had to finish their vegetables first. Sometimes they did not like the vegetables, but they wanted the dessert.

One day, mom made a big cake with chocolate and cherries. It looked so yummy that Anna and Ben were anxious to eat it. But mom put some broccoli on their plates and said they had to eat it before they could have cake.

Anna did not like broccoli at all. She made a face and pushed it away. Ben liked broccoli a little bit, but he liked cake more. He saw that Anna did not want to eat her broccoli, and he had an idea.

"Anna, do you want to trade?" he asked. "I will eat your broccoli if you give me some of your cake."

Anna thought about it. She did not want to eat broccoli, but she also did not want to give up her cake. She liked cake a lot. She looked at Ben and saw that he was smiling. He liked cake a lot too.

"No, thank you," she said. "I will eat my broccoli and keep my cake. You eat your broccoli and keep your cake too. Mom said we have to value what we have and share with others. Maybe we can share some cake with dad later."

Ben was disappointed, but he knew that Anna was right. He ate his broccoli and waited for his cake. He hoped that dad would not eat too much cake, because he still wanted a big slice. He also hoped that Anna would be happy with her cake, because he loved his sister. He was glad that they played together and ate dessert together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the sun. But one day, it was too hot to play outside. So, Lily decided to rest in the shade of a big tree. She closed her eyes and took a nap.

When she woke up, she saw her friends playing a game. They were trying to win a race. Lily got up and joined the race. She ran as fast as she could and she won! She was very happy.

After the race, Lily was tired and hot again. So, she went back to the shade of the big tree and rested some more. She felt much better after her rest.

Ben likes to play with his rocket. He made it from a big box and some paper. He paints it red and blue and puts stickers on it. He pretends he is an astronaut and flies to the moon.

One day, Ben wants to show his rocket to his friend Sam. He tries to lift his rocket, but it is too heavy. He cannot carry it by himself. He needs help. He asks his mom to help him, but she is busy. He asks his dad to help him, but he is at work. He asks his sister to help him, but she is too small.

Ben is sad. He thinks he cannot take his rocket to Sam's house. He sits on the floor and cries. Then he hears a knock on the door. It is Sam! He came to play with Ben. He sees Ben's rocket and says, "Wow, that is a cool rocket! Can we play with it?"

Ben smiles and says, "Yes, we can play with it, but it is very heavy. We need to work together to lift it." Sam nods and says, "OK, let's do it!" They both grab one side of the rocket and lift it up. They are strong together. They take the rocket outside and have fun flying to the moon. Ben is happy. He has a good friend and a good rocket.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Lily and Pete. They were very excited, for today was something special.

Lily and Pete were going to the zoo! As they walked in, they saw so many animals in all shapes and sizes. Some made noise, others moved very quickly and some were in cages.

Lily and Pete first saw the tigers. They were big and had orange stripes. Standing close by was a tall cage.

Lily asked Pete "What's in the cage?" Pete smiled and said "It's a smelly skunk. It needs our support, so we should help it".

Lily and Pete took turns to give the skunk water and food. By the time they were done, the skunk was happy and wrinkled its nose in thanks. Lily and Pete smiled and waved goodbye.

The day had been so much fun and as they left, they said they can't wait to come back soon.

Once there was a hairy pot. It wanted to succeed but it didn't know how. Every day it tried its best but nothing seemed to work.

One day it decided to go for a walk and see what it could discover. As it walked, it saw a butterfly. The butterfly fluttered its wings and flew away.

The pot felt inspired by this! It decided to try something new. It used its hairy legs to climb up a tree and it made it to the top. It had succeeded!

The pot was so proud and happy. It jumped down from the tree and went back home to tell its family and friends about its success. From that day onward, the hairy pot was known as the successful pot.

Once, there was a dad and his little girl. She asked him a question, 'Daddy, will my toy always stay the same?' 

The dad smiled. 'Yes, it will stay the same until you want to change it.'

She thought, then said, 'But Daddy, I want to change it.'

The Dad smiled again. He said, 'Well, I know a place to buy a very cheap new toy, let's go.'

Together, they went to a shop and the little girl looked at all the different toys. There were dolls and animals, cars and dragons. She touched them all and turned this way and that.

Finally, she found a toy she liked. She pointed and said, 'This one please Daddy!'

The dad laughed and said, 'Looks like you found a new toy that you want to change too.' 

The little girl was so happy. She hugged her Daddy and said, 'Yes, I can change it.' 

Together they went home, with a new toy that the little girl could change however she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was very obedient and always listened to his owner, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and Spot went for a walk in the park. Suddenly, Spot saw a little bird in trouble. The bird had fallen from its nest and couldn't fly. Spot knew he had to rescue the bird quickly.

"Quick, Lily! Come see the bird," Spot barked. Lily came over and saw the bird. "Oh no! We have to help it," she said. Spot carefully picked up the bird in his mouth and brought it back to its nest. The bird's family was so happy to see their baby bird safe and sound.

"Good job, Spot! You are such a brave and helpful dog," Lily said. Spot wagged his tail happily. From that day on, Spot and Lily were known as the heroes of the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went swimming in the pool with her mom. After swimming, her mom let her dry off with a soft towel. But Lily didn't like the towel because it was too bitter. She asked her mom for a different towel, but her mom said they only had one. 

Lily was sad and didn't want to use the bitter towel. But then she had an idea! She asked her mom if they could put the towel in the dryer to make it warm and cozy. Her mom thought it was a great idea, so they put the towel in the dryer. 

When the towel was warm and cozy, Lily wrapped it around herself and felt much better. She was happy that she didn't have to use the bitter towel anymore. From that day on, Lily always asked her mom to put the towel in the dryer after swimming so it would be nice and warm.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. While they were playing, Lily saw a bird with a broken wing. She felt very sad for the bird and wanted to help it. Her mommy and daddy told her that they couldn't fix the bird's wing, but they could comfort it by giving it some food and water.

Later that day, Lily's mommy took a picture of her playing with her daddy on her camera. Lily loved seeing the pictures of herself and her family. But when she looked at the camera, she saw an unknown face in the background. It scared her a little bit, but her mommy explained that it was just a stranger who happened to be walking by. Lily felt better knowing that it wasn't anything to be afraid of.

After a fun day at the park, Lily went to bed feeling happy that she could comfort the bird and that her mommy explained the unknown face in the picture. She fell asleep with a smile on her face, dreaming of all the adventures she would have with her family.

Tom and Lily are hungry. They want to eat some cheese. They go to the kitchen and open the refrigerator. They see a big block of cheese on the top shelf.

"Wow, look at the cheese!" Tom says. "Let's get it!"

Tom tries to reach the cheese, but he is too short. He jumps and stretches, but he cannot touch it. Lily has an idea. She finds a chair and pushes it to the refrigerator. She climbs on the chair and grabs the cheese.

"Good job, Lily!" Tom says. "Now we can eat the cheese!"

But Lily is not fast. She holds the cheese with both hands and walks down the chair very slow. She does not want to drop the cheese. Tom is impatient. He wants the cheese now.

"Hurry up, Lily!" Tom says. "I am hungry!"

Lily does not listen. She keeps walking slow. She is almost on the floor when she hears a loud noise. She turns around and sees Mom.

"What are you doing, kids?" Mom asks. "Why do you have the cheese?"

Tom and Lily are scared. They know they are in trouble. They drop the cheese and run to Mom.

"Sorry, Mom!" Tom says. "We were hungry!"

"Please, Mom!" Lily says. "Don't be mad!"

Mom is not happy. She picks up the cheese and puts it back in the refrigerator. She looks at Tom and Lily.

"Next time, you have to ask me before you take something from the refrigerator," Mom says. "And you have to be careful with the chair. You could have fallen and hurt yourself."

Tom and Lily nod. They say sorry again. Mom hugs them and smiles.

"It's okay, kids," Mom says. "I love you. But now you have to wait for lunch. Come, let's go to the living room and read a book."

Tom and Sue were friends. They liked to play in the woods. One day, they saw a big cave. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go in the cave," Tom said. "Maybe we can find some treasure."

"No, Tom, that is foolish," Sue said. "The cave is dark and scary. There might be bears or snakes or spiders. We should go back."

But Tom did not listen. He ran into the cave. Sue followed him. She did not want him to get lost or hurt.

They walked deeper and deeper into the cave. It was cold and wet and quiet. They could not see anything. They only had a small flashlight.

"Tom, I don't like this," Sue said. "Let's go back. Please."

But Tom did not listen. He saw something shiny in the corner. He thought it was gold. He ran to get it.

But it was not gold. It was a trap. A big net fell on Tom and Sue. They were stuck. They could not move.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. "Someone help us!"

But no one heard them. They were too far away.

They heard a loud roar. It was a bear. The bear lived in the cave. He was hungry. He smelled Tom and Sue. He came to eat them.

The bear saw the net. He thought it was a gift. He thought someone had served him a tasty snack. He licked his lips. He opened his mouth.

Tom and Sue were very scared. They wished they had never gone into the cave. They wished they had listened to Sue. They were very foolish. They said sorry to each other.

But it was too late. The bear was ready to bite. He was very happy. He thanked whoever had served him. He said:

"Yum, yum, yum!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the park with her mommy and saw a huge statue of a lion. "Wow, that lion is big!" said Lily. "Yes, it's very big," replied her mommy. 

Lily wanted to touch the lion's nose, but she was too scared. "Mommy, can I ask the lion if it's okay to touch its nose?" she said. "Well, statues can't talk, but you can pretend it said yes," said her mommy. 

So Lily pretended to ask the lion if she could touch its nose. "Mr. Lion, can I touch your nose?" she said. And she pretended the lion said yes. She was very happy and touched the lion's nose gently. "That was fun!" she said. And she skipped away with her mommy, happy to have made friends with the lion statue.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. Sally loved to draw with her yellow pencil. One day, Sally went to the park to draw pictures of the flowers and trees. She sat on a bench and started to draw. 

Suddenly, a boy walked up to Sally and said, "What are you drawing?" Sally said, "I'm drawing a flower. Look!" The boy looked and said, "Wow, that's pretty!" Sally smiled and said, "Thank you. Do you like my yellow pencil?" The boy said, "Yes, it's very bright." 

Sally and the boy talked for a little while longer and then said goodbye. Sally continued to draw her pictures with her yellow pencil and was very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Mittens. Mittens loved to sleep all day and not do much else. One day, Mittens' owner wanted to clean the house, so she asked Mittens to help her remove the toys from the floor. Mittens didn't want to help and just kept sleeping.

The owner became upset and said, "Mittens, you need to help me remove the toys or else we won't have peace in the house." Mittens didn't understand what peace meant but knew that his owner was not happy. So, he slowly got up and started to remove the toys from the floor.

After they finished cleaning, Mittens felt proud of himself for helping. His owner thanked him and gave him a treat. From then on, Mittens realized that helping out made his owner happy and brought peace to the house.

Max was by himself with nothing to do on a foggy day. He saw a flash of grey near the fence and he ran over to take a closer look. It was a kitten! He stroked the kitten's soft fur and immediately fell in love. Max said to the kitten: "I'm Max, what's your name?"

The kitten replied, "I'm Sam. Let's be friends!"

Max was so excited and he smiled with glee. He asked Sam if he wanted to come home and play with him. Sam nodded his head, so Max opened the gate and took him home.

They had lots of fun! Max showed Sam all the best hiding places, the softest spots to nap and the tastiest food. Max took his new friend out for a walk in the park. He kept a tight hold on Sam's paw, so he wouldn't get lost. They shared lots of love and laughter, and had lots of fun together every day. Max was very happy to have met Sam.

Once upon a time, there lived a restless elephant who loved to go on adventures. 
One day, the elephant decided to explore a most magical place. He curiously walked and eventually heard clapping and cheering. Excited, he pushed through the trees and found a bright meadow.

In the meadow, the elephant saw all of the animals clapping and smiling. Even the trees were swaying, enjoying the show. Then, thunder shook the air and the animals applauded louder! 

The elephant looked around and saw a beautiful rainbow floating in the sky. He knew then that he had found the most amazing thing - a rainbow show! All of the animals cheered and applauded some more. 

The elephant was so happy to be there and he joined in the fun by shaking his trunk and stomping his feet. The animals were so excited that they applauded every time the elephant stomped. The thunder was even louder now!

The elephant felt so brave and proud that he cheered, too! He clapped and clapped until his trunk was tired. 

Finally, the magical show was over. The elephant thanked the rainbow for the show and the animals waved goodbye. As the elephant walked away, he knew that the adventure was one that he would never forget.

James was walking on a sunny day with his mother and saw a small plant in the grass. He asked his mother why the plant was there.

His mother said, "This is a very special plant. We need to study it."

James asked, "What does studying mean?"

His mother explained, "Studying means looking very closely at the plant, noticing all its features and details, thinking about them and learning from them."

James said, "That sounds dull."

His mother said, "It can be, but it can also be very interesting. That's why it's important to study things like this plant. We can learn more about the world and how plants work."

James smiled and said, "Alright, I'll study the plant!" And he did. He looked at it very closely and thought about what he saw until he had learned a lot about the plant.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl called Mandy. Mandy loved to play and explore and one day, she found a pair of scissors. She thought they were so cool and was so cheerful! 

As Mandy was exploring, she came to a yummy looking stream. She saw how clear and still the water was and wanted to take a drink. She bent down, cupped her hands and scooped up a nice drink. 

Mandy was so thirsty, she gulped and gulped until she was all done. She went back to playing and was having the best day ever! She brought her scissors and kept finding new, exciting things to do. 

Mandy was so cheerful, she even caught a fish with her scissors. She was so proud of herself and went home to tell her mom. Her mom was so proud of her and gave Mandy a big hug. 

And that was the end of Mandy's exciting day!

Anna loved to swim in the pool with her big sister, Lily. They played games, splashed water, and laughed a lot. Anna wanted to be like Lily, who could swim very fast and dive under the water. Lily taught Anna how to kick her legs and move her arms, and how to hold her breath.

One day, Lily had to go to school, and Anna was sad. She wanted to swim with Lily, not stay at home with Mom. Mom said, "Anna, you can swim later, when Lily comes back. Now, let's do some fun things together. We can read a book, or draw a picture, or play with your toys."

Anna did not listen to Mom. She was angry and bored. She did not want to do any fun things. She wanted to swim. She sneaked out of the house, and ran to the pool. She jumped in, and tried to swim like Lily. But she forgot to hold her breath, and swallowed some water. She coughed and cried, and felt scared. She wanted Mom and Lily.

Mom heard Anna's cry, and ran to the pool. She saw Anna in the water, and quickly pulled her out. She hugged Anna, and said, "Anna, are you okay? What were you doing? You know you can't swim alone. You could have been hurt. You made me very worried."

Anna felt sorry. She said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I wanted to swim with Lily. I wanted to be like her. I forgot to hold her breath. I was silly."

Mom said, "Anna, I understand. You love Lily, and you want to learn from her. But you have to be careful, and listen to me. Swimming is fun, but it can also be dangerous. You have to wait for Lily, or for me, or for someone else who can help you. You have to follow the rules, and be safe. Do you understand?"

Anna nodded. She said, "Yes, Mom. I understand. I will wait for Lily, or for you, or for someone else. I will follow the rules, and be safe. I'm sorry I made you worried. I love you, Mom."

Mom said, "I love you too, Anna. And I'm proud of you for trying to swim. You are learning, and you will get better. But you have to be patient, and practice. And you have to remember what Lily taught you. She is a good sister, and she loves you too."

Anna smiled. She said, "Yes, Mom. I will remember what Lily taught me. She is a good sister, and I love her too. Can we swim together later, when she comes back?"

Mom said, "Of course, Anna. We can swim together later, when she comes back. But first, let's go inside, and get dry, and clean. You are very wet, and very messy."

Anna laughed. She said, "Yes, Mom. I am very wet, and very messy. But I am also very happy."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the value of listening to parents, being careful, and learning from others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very cold. She was standing outside and it was very bright, with the sun shining in the sky. Then, she remembered that she had a warm coat in her closet. She quickly ran inside and put it on. She felt much better and the cold feeling went away. Then she went outside and enjoyed a beautiful, bright day. She smiled and remembered how happy she felt wearing her warm coat. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny. He had a very nice and cozy bed, which he loved to lay on. One day, he thought he would make it even better. So he went looking for something to do it.

He found some nice soft strips of cloth. He got to lay down the strips on the bed, one by one. It made his bed feel extra comfy.

He lay on the bed and it felt good. He hopped and jumped and the bed was so soft. He felt so happy.

The bunny decided he wanted to lay on the bed every day. He knew it would be a good place to take a nap or just to relax. And that's just what he did. He lay down and felt so nice and comfortable.

The bunny knows that he has a good bed. He is so glad he found the strips of cloth to make it even better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw pictures with her crayons. One day, she went to her mom and said, "Mom, I want more crayons. Can we go to the store and get some?"

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily. Let's go to the store and get some new crayons for you."

When they got to the store, Lily found a big box of crayons with lots of colors. She was so happy and said, "Mom, I want this box of crayons. Can we get it?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. You were successful in finding the crayons you wanted. Let's go home and draw some pictures." And they went home and drew lots of pictures with Lily's new crayons.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the sand near the sea. They made castles and bridges and tunnels with their buckets and shovels. One day, they saw something strange in the water. It was an octopus!

"Look, look!" Ben shouted. "An octopus! It has eight legs and a big head!"

Mia was scared. She hid behind Ben and said, "Is it friendly? Will it hurt us?"

Ben was curious. He wanted to touch the octopus. He walked closer to the water and reached out his hand. The octopus saw Ben and squirted water at him. Ben got wet and cold. He ran back to Mia and said, "It's not friendly! It's mean!"

Mia laughed. She thought it was funny that Ben got wet. She said, "It's not mean, Ben. It's just playing. Maybe it wants to be our friend."

Ben was not happy. He did not like the water. He said, "No, it doesn't. It's harsh. It doesn't like us. Let's go away."

Mia felt sorry for Ben. She gave him a hug and said, "OK, let's go. But maybe we can come back another day and play with the octopus. Maybe it will be nice then."

Ben nodded. He dried his face and said, "Maybe. But I don't want to get wet again."

They took their buckets and shovels and walked away from the sea. The octopus watched them go and waved its legs. It was lonely. It wished they would stay and play.

Once upon a time, there was a lively dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his board. He would run, jump, and flip the board in the air. One day, Spot saw a big cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was not nice.

Spot said, "Fluffy, let's play with my board." Fluffy looked at Spot and said, "No, I don't want to play with you." Spot was sad, but he still wanted to play. So, he asked Fluffy again, "Please, let's play with my board."

Fluffy got mad and said, "I told you, no!" Fluffy jumped on Spot's board and broke it. Spot cried and went home. He did not have his board to play with anymore.

Once upon a time there was a pretty girl called Jane. Jane was very kind and generous. One day, she went for a walk in the woods. As she was walking, something strange caught her eye. It was a pale veil covering a bush. Jane was so curious and so she approached the veil. She reached out to touch it, but something stopped her. It was an old lady.

The old lady smiled at Jane. She explained that the veil was very special. It contained a powerful magic that only the bravest people could use. Jane was interested and excited. The old lady told Jane that if she was brave, she could try wearing the veil.

Jane was scared, but she wanted to try it. She placed the veil on her head and closed her eyes. She waited for something to happen, but nothing did. Suddenly, she felt a strange energy around her. When she opened her eyes, the woods around her were glowing. Jane was amazed!

The old lady explained that the veil contained a deep and powerful magic that only those brave enough to wear it could use. Jane was so happy. She thanked the old lady and went on her way. From that day on, Jane wore the pale veil with pride and courage.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and pick flowers. One day, she found a stick and decided to play with it. She twirled it around and pretended it was a magic wand.

Lily's mommy told her that if she believed in herself, she could do anything. Lily believed her mommy and continued to play with the stick. Suddenly, a butterfly flew by and landed on the stick. Lily was so happy and peaceful watching the butterfly.

After a while, Lily decided to go back inside and show her mommy the stick with the butterfly on it. Her mommy was so proud of her and told her that she could do anything she believed in. From that day on, Lily believed in herself and knew that anything was possible.

Once upon a time, a lady went for a walk in the rain. She forgot her umbrella and got very wet. Suddenly, she saw a big bird with colorful feathers. The bird flew up high and then down fast, striking the ground with its strong feet. The lady was amazed and watched the bird fly away. She went home and told her friends about the bird that struck the ground. They were all surprised and wished they could see the bird too.

Jojo was home alone and felt very bored. He looked around for something exciting. He saw a radio on the table. His eyes lit up! He grabbed the radio and turned it on. Jojo heard a lot of noise coming from it. He couldn't understand what it was saying. 

He looked around for something to help him make sense of it. Suddenly, he saw an old man in the garden talking to his mom. He asked the old man what the noise was. The old man smiled and said it was music. Jojo laughed in excitement! 

He listened to the music for a while and it made him feel very happy. But the music sounded a bit bitter. Jojo looked around again, and he saw a bottle of lemonade. He grabbed it and took a sip. Jojo smiled as the sweet taste of lemonade filled his mouth. 

The music was no longer bitter to him. Jojo was now so happy he was dancing and singing along to the music. What a day!

Lily and Tom were playing with their crayons. They liked to draw pictures of animals and flowers. Lily wanted to draw a rainbow, but she did not have all the colors. She only had red, yellow, green and blue.

"Tom, can I have your purple crayon?" she asked.

"No, I need it for my dinosaur," Tom said.

"But I want to complete my rainbow," Lily said.

"Sorry, you have to wait," Tom said.

Lily was sad. She looked out the window and saw a big black cloud. It was going to rain soon. She wished she could see a real rainbow in the sky.

Suddenly, she heard a loud boom. It was thunder. She saw a flash of light. It was lightning. She was scared. She ran to Tom and hugged him.

"Tom, I'm scared of the thunder and lightning," she said.

"Don't worry, Lily, I'm here," Tom said.

He gave her his purple crayon. "Here, you can have it. Complete your rainbow."

Lily smiled. She took the crayon and finished her rainbow. She thanked Tom and gave him a kiss.

They looked out the window again. The rain had stopped. The sun was shining. And in the sky, they saw a beautiful rainbow. It had all the colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.

"Look, Tom, a rainbow!" Lily said.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Tom said.

They clapped their hands and cheered. They were happy. They had made a rainbow and seen a rainbow. They had shared and cared. They were good friends.

Anna loves to write. She writes stories about dancers, fairies, and animals. She writes with crayons, pencils, and stickers. She writes on paper, books, and walls. She writes every day, even when her mom says no.

One day, Anna goes to a dance class with her friend Lily. Lily is a good dancer. She can jump, spin, and twirl. She wears a pink tutu and a shiny crown. She likes to show off her moves to everyone. Anna likes to watch Lily, but she is too shy to dance. She sits in a corner and writes a story about a dancer who is modest and kind.

Lily sees Anna writing and gets curious. She goes to Anna and snatches her story. She reads it out loud and laughs. She says Anna's story is silly and boring. She says Anna can't dance and can't write. She tears Anna's story and throws it away. Anna feels sad and angry. She wants her story back.

Anna stands up and runs to Lily. She pushes Lily and grabs her crown. She says Lily is mean and rude. She says Lily can't read and can't write. She breaks Lily's crown and throws it away. Lily feels sad and angry. She wants her crown back.

The teacher sees Anna and Lily fighting and stops them. She scolds them and makes them sit apart. She says they are both wrong and rude. She says they should respect each other and their things. She says they should apologize and share. She gives them new paper and crayons and tells them to write a new story together. Anna and Lily look at each other and feel sorry. They say sorry and hug. They sit together and write a new story about two dancers who are modest and kind. They write with crayons, pencils, and stickers. They write on paper, books, and walls. They write every day, even when their mom says no.

Gracie was out in the garden on a sunny day. She felt so happy to be able to run around and feel the sunshine on her skin.

Suddenly, she noticed that under the tree there was a big patch of shade and she decided to go and see it.

When she arrived, she saw that it was even bigger than she had thought. It felt so delicate, like she was being wrapped in a bubble of protection.

Gracie could not believe it. She shouted out loud, "This shade feels so amazing, who knew shade could be so nice?"

Suddenly, a voice said, "That's right Gracie, shade can be a beautiful place to be!"

Gracie looked around and saw her mother standing there. She was smiling down at Gracie with love in her eyes.

Gracie smiled back and said, "Thank you, Mama!" and went back to playing in the shade.

Mamma and Baby lay together in the grass. Baby looked up and saw the clouds in the sky and giggled. Mamma hummed a lovely song and all of a sudden the song became louder and louder. Mamma was singing an old lullaby, it made Baby feel so happy and peaceful. As the song continued, Mamma and Baby looked up to the sky and saw a brightly coloured butterfly. It floated gracefully through the air and Mamma smiled. Baby pointed up at the butterfly and said "Look Mamma, it's so lovely!" The butterfly flew away and Mamma hugged Baby tightly. It was a perfect day and Baby was so happy. They lay in the grass until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily saw a weird comet in the sky. She asked her mom, "What is that?" Her mom said, "That's a comet. It's like a big rock that flies in space." 

Lily said, "Wow! Can we go see it?" Her mom said, "No, we can't. It's too far away." 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "But I want to see it up close." Her mom said, "I know, but we don't have the supplies to go to space." 

Lily said, "Oh, okay. Maybe one day we can go see it together." Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, maybe one day we can."

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny loved to hop around in the fields and eat wheat. One day, Benny got lost and couldn't find his way back home. He felt scared and sad. 

Suddenly, he saw a kind farmer who noticed Benny was lost. The farmer took Benny home and gave him some yummy carrots to eat. Benny was so grateful to the farmer for helping him. 

From that day on, Benny visited the farmer every day to say thank you and hop around in the fields. He loved his new friend and was happy to have someone who cared for him.

Lily and Ben were playing with a big ball in the park. They liked to kick the ball and run after it. Sometimes they threw the ball to each other and caught it.

One time, Ben threw the ball too hard and it went over the fence. Lily and Ben ran to the fence and looked for the ball. They saw the ball on the other side, near a big tree. But the fence was too high and they could not climb over it.

"Let's go around the fence and get the ball," Lily said.

"OK," Ben said. They ran along the fence until they found a gate. The gate had a rope with a knot on it. Lily and Ben tried to open the gate, but the knot was too tight.

"Maybe we can break the knot," Ben said. He pulled the rope with all his might, but the knot did not break. He pulled harder and harder, but the knot only got tighter.

"Ouch!" Ben said. He hurt his hand on the rope. He let go of the rope and rubbed his hand.

Lily saw that Ben was sad and hurt. She hugged him and said, "It's OK, Ben. We can find another ball. Or we can play something else. You are my friend and I want you to be happy."

Ben smiled and hugged Lily back. He felt warm and cozy in her arms. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my friend too and you are very kind. I don't need the ball. I just need you."

They walked away from the gate, holding hands. They decided to play tag instead. They laughed and ran and had fun. They forgot about the ball and the knot. They only remembered their friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a lot of toys, but he wanted more. He saw a toy in his friend's house and he wanted it too. Timmy thought of a plan to get the toy. He invited his friend to his house and while his friend was playing, Timmy stole the toy and hid it in his room. 

The next day, Timmy's friend came to his house and asked where his toy was. Timmy felt ashamed and lied that he didn't know. His friend left sadly. Timmy felt bad and wanted to return the toy, but he was scared. 

Days passed and Timmy couldn't stop thinking about what he did. He realized that taking someone's toy without permission is wrong. He wanted to apologize and return the toy. But it was too late, his friend never came back to his house again. Timmy learned that being honest and kind is more important than having more toys.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved candy, especially green candy. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big bag of green candy. Timmy was so happy that he poured all the candy on the floor. 

Timmy's mom was not happy with him because he made a mess. Timmy quickly picked up all the green candy and put them back in the bag. He promised his mom that he would be more careful next time. 

From that day on, Timmy only ate a few green candies at a time so he wouldn't make a mess again. He enjoyed his green candy and was happy that he had learned to be careful. The end.

Once upon a time there was an adventurous olive. He lived in a very special garden and could almost see the sky from his spot. Every day he was daring. Sometimes he'd dare to go higher, sometimes he'd dare to go lower. 

One day he decided to go on an even bigger adventure. He packed a small bag and began his journey. He crossed the meadow to the forest. Everywhere he looked he saw so many exciting things. He could smell the wood and the flowers.

He went up and down mountains and hills. He even swam across a big river. He was very brave and he kept daring. 

In the end, he was able to come back safely to the garden. He had seen so many wonderful things and was filled with joy. Everywhere he went people heard about the adventures of the brave olive.

Once upon a time there was a chicken. He was a very good chicken and he liked to tell stories. One day he was out in the yard and he saw a little boy. The chicken said hello to the boy and asked him if he liked stories. The boy said yes. So the chicken told him a story. The story was about a princess who went on an adventure and found a magical door. The door opened to a wonderful garden full of fruits and flowers. The boy was amazed and he wanted to hear more stories from the chicken. He asked the chicken to come back soon. The chicken said he would and flew away. The boy was happy and smiled. The chicken was a very good storyteller!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, Timmy went on an adventure in the woods with his blue flashlight. He walked and walked until he found a big ice cream cone. Timmy was so excited to eat it, but it was too cold outside and the ice cream started to melt. 

Suddenly, a mean bear appeared and growled at Timmy. "Give me your flashlight!" the bear demanded. Timmy was scared and didn't want to give up his favorite toy. But the bear was very big and Timmy was very small. So, he gave the bear his blue flashlight. 

Timmy was sad and started to cry. He wished he had never gone on his adventure. He walked back home without his flashlight and without his ice cream. When he got home, his mom asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her everything that had happened. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We can buy you a new flashlight. But always remember to be careful when you're outside."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. It was summer and she loved to play outside. She would wander around in her backyard and pick flowers.

One day, Lily saw her neighbor, Mr. Brown, sitting on his porch looking sad. She went over to him and asked, "Why are you sad, Mr. Brown?"

Mr. Brown replied, "I lost my dog and I can't find him. He used to wander around in the summer with me."

Lily felt sad too and decided to help Mr. Brown find his dog. They wandered around the neighborhood together, calling out the dog's name. Finally, they found the dog and Mr. Brown was so happy that he started to cry. Lily felt happy too, knowing that she helped someone.

Once upon a time there was an old man who liked limes very much. Every day he would go to the store and buy the biggest and juiciest limes he could find. One day, he saw a lime that was even bigger and more juicy than the ones he normally bought! He was so excited and he grabbed it right away.

When he got home, he was worried that the lime was too big for him to eat. So, he had an idea. He decided to reverse the lime! He put it in the blender and mixed it around until it was very small and smooth.

The old man was very competitive so he wanted to make sure he did the best job possible. He added lots of sugar and mixed it some more. Finally, he put the mixture in the refrigerator so it would be nice and cool.

When he tried it, it was the most delicious lime he had ever tasted!  He shared it with all his friends and family, and they loved it too. From then on, the old man would always reverse his limes when he wanted to enjoy the juiciest and sweetest lime possible.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to go for walks with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went to a big park and saw a big statue. It was very nice and shiny. Lily asked her mommy and daddy what the statue was for. They explained that it was to remember someone who did something very important a long time ago. Lily thought that was very cool and wanted to learn more about the person. From that day on, Lily loved going to the park to see the nice statue and remember the important person.

Jim was on a mission to find something special. He wanted something hot, cheap and easy to fix. So he hopped on his bike and rode around town, looking for the perfect thing.

He stopped at a market, where he saw lots of hot items. But everything was either too expensive or too hard to fix! He was getting frustrated and was just about to give up.

But then he spotted something in the corner. It was a small thing, but it was hot and cheap. And it looked like he might be able to fix it.

Jim smiled and got to work. After a few minutes of careful tinkering, it was fixed. He had found just what he was looking for! He was so proud of himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a red box. Inside the red box was a pair of scissors. She liked the scissors a lot. Every day, she would take them outside and sit in the grass and play with them.

The scissors grew very big in the grass. Soon they were bigger than the red box. Every day, the scissors grew and grew until they were big enough to use to cut the grass.

The little girl had so much fun playing with the scissors and cutting the grass. She liked the feeling of being tough and strong, like grown-ups.

The little girl learned a valuable lesson - when you work hard and grow, you can do amazing things.

Tom and Lily liked to play hide and seek in the big park. They took turns to count and look for each other. One day, they found a new place to hide. It was a small hut with a door and a window. They thought it was a good spot to stay hidden.

Tom went inside the hut and Lily counted to ten. She looked around the park, but she could not see Tom. She ran to the hut and tried to open the door. But the door was shut. She pushed and pulled, but it did not move. She called Tom's name, but he did not answer. She was scared.

Tom was also scared. He heard Lily call him, but he could not open the door. He felt a weight on his chest. He looked up and saw a big box on the door. He did not know how it got there. He tried to move it, but it was too heavy. He shouted for help, but no one heard him.

Lily and Tom cried and cried. They thought they would never get out. They wished they had not hidden in the hut. They missed their mom and dad. They hoped someone would find them soon.

Then they heard a voice. It was a man. He was a gardener. He worked in the park. He saw the hut and the box. He wondered what was inside. He lifted the box and opened the door. He saw Tom and Lily. They were very happy to see him. He was very surprised to see them.

He asked them what they were doing in the hut. They told him they were playing hide and seek. They said they did not know about the box. They said they were sorry. He said it was okay. He said he was glad he found them. He said he would take them to their mom and dad. He said they should not hide in the hut again. They said they would not. They thanked him and hugged him. They learned a lesson. They never played hide and seek in the hut again.

John was three years old and he loved playing outside. One day he was out exploring and he saw a yellow ball. He was so excited he ran over to it. 

John shouted, "It's a yellow ball! I want to play with it!"

He picked it up, but oh no! It was broken. He started to cry. 

Then he heard a voice from above. It was his mom. 

She said, "John, don't cry. Let me help you." She took the yellow ball and held it tightly in her hand. 

John watched as she blew on it three times. Then mom said, "Now try it again." 

John was amazed! The yellow ball worked perfectly! He was so happy that he started to repeat, "Thank you mom, thank you." 

His mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, now go play!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing games with his daddy. They played all kinds of games together like hide and seek, tag, and catch. Timmy's daddy was very competitive and always wanted to win.
