The hairy goose ran around the yard, playing with the people's children. The children giggled as the goose chased them around. She made the people laugh too.

The goose was happy to remain with her new family. She ate delicious food and took long naps in the sun. This went on for many years. 

The children eventually grew up and moved away. The hairy goose remained in this beautiful place, but she never forgot her new family. She still remembers the time they shared together and she is grateful to have had such wonderful memories.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the bakery with her mommy to get pastries. One day, Lily was so excited to go to the bakery because she wanted to order a chocolate croissant. 

When they got to the bakery, Lily saw all the delicious pastries in the window. She pointed to the chocolate croissant and said, "I want that one, please!" Her mommy helped her order the pastry and Lily was very happy. 

She sat down at a table with her mommy and took a big bite of the chocolate croissant. It was so yummy! Lily was so excited that she wanted to order another one, but her mommy said she could only have one. Lily was still happy because she got to have her favorite pastry. The end.

Once there was a little boy named John. John was three years old and loved to explore the world. One day, John decided to test the drawer in his bedroom. He opened the drawer and looked inside. It was disgusting. All the drawer had was old, moldy food and cobwebs. John quickly closed the drawer and looked around his room to find something else to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little boy called Jimmy. Jimmy loved to play pretend. One day, he went on a pretend adventure with his best friend. They had to find a big jewel!

They needed to find a good place to look for the jewel, so they went looking in the garden. As they looked around, Jimmy's friend saw a big yellow jewel. Jimmy wanted the jewel too, but his friend said it was his.

Jimmy was upset. He really needed the jewel, but his friend wouldn't let him have it. He got so mad that he grabbed the jewel, but his friend started crying. He was so sad!

Jimmy felt bad and gave the jewel back to his friend. He said he didn't need the jewel, he just wanted them to share it. His friend was so happy that they hugged and made up. They shared the jewel and had lots of fun.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but they have one favorite toy. It is a big gray elephant. The elephant is soft and has a long nose. The twins call him Elly.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with Elly at the same time. They both grab his nose and pull. Elly makes a loud noise. He does not like it. Anna and Ben struggle. They do not want to share.

"Elly is mine!" Anna says.

"No, Elly is mine!" Ben says.

They pull harder. Elly makes a louder noise. He does not like it more.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees Anna and Ben struggle. She sees Elly make noise. She is not happy.

"Anna and Ben, stop!" Mom says. "You are hurting Elly. He is not happy. You have to share. Elly is for both of you."

Anna and Ben look at Mom. They look at Elly. They see his sad eyes. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, Elly," Anna says.

"Sorry, Elly," Ben says.

They let go of his nose. They hug him. Elly makes a happy noise. He likes it.

Mom smiles. She hugs Anna and Ben. She hugs Elly.

"Good job, Anna and Ben," Mom says. "You are very kind. Elly is a famous elephant. He is famous for being soft and nice. He is famous for having two friends who love him."

Sam was a barber who liked to cut hair. He had a shop in the town where many people came to see him. He was very good at his job and he was very wealthy. He had a big house, a nice car and many toys.

One day, a big truck came to the town. It was very loud and very fast. It did not stop for anyone or anything. It did not yield to the cars, the bikes or the people. It made a lot of noise and a lot of dust.

Sam was on his way to his shop when he saw the truck. He was scared and angry. He wanted to tell the truck to stop and be nice. He ran after the truck and shouted at it. But the truck did not hear him or see him. It kept going and going.

Sam was so busy chasing the truck that he did not see the red light. He did not see the car that was coming from the other side. He did not see the crash that was about to happen. He did not see the end of his story.

Joe was a cool boy who loved to play. He wanted to drive the ambulance, so he did! It was so much fun! Suddenly, the sirens started and Joe started to worry. He felt sad and he regretted what he had done.

Joe started to cry as the ambulance drove him away to the hospital. He had made a mistake, and he knew it. He was really frightened, but the nice nurse and doctor made him feel better. 

They gave him a yummy treat and a bandage when he was all done. Joe knew he had learnt his lesson and he would never do it again. He felt relieved, and he thought that being cool was not always what it seemed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was so very careful. One day she went outside to play and she found a caterpillar! She was so excited!

The girl carefully put the caterpillar in her pocket so she could take him home. She stopped and said to the caterpillar, "Let's go home," and the caterpillar smiled.

When they arrived, she put the caterpillar in her garden and said, "You can stay here and have lots of adventures." The caterpillar nodded.

The girl gave the caterpillar a hug and said, "Be careful and remember to stay safe." She watched as the caterpillar crawled away, feeling sure he would have a wonderful time in her garden.

It was a sunny day and two friends, Lucy and Max, were out for a walk. They got to the street where there was lots of traffic. 

"Look Max!" Lucy said. "All the cars make noise!"

Max nodded and looked at the traffic. It was strong.

"Let's go to the park," Lucy said.

The two friends walked to the park together. When they got there, they saw a weak tree.

"Let's make the tree stronger," Lucy said. 

Max smiled and ran to get some soil and water. With lots of care and patience, Max and Lucy made the tree strong again.

They were happy and laughed together. The weak tree was now strong and standing tall.

"We did it!" they said together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and stuffed animals. One day, she was playing outside when she saw a big monster. The monster was very grumpy and scary.

Lily ran inside and told her mommy about the monster. "Mommy, there's a monster outside and he's very grumpy!" she said. Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll take care of it."

Her mommy went outside and saw the monster. She started to rock back and forth on her feet and said, "Hello, Mr. Monster. Why are you so grumpy?" The monster replied, "I'm grumpy because I'm lost and can't find my way home."

Lily's mommy helped the monster find his way home and he wasn't grumpy anymore. Lily was happy that the monster was gone and she could play outside again. From that day on, Lily knew that even monsters could be nice if you help them.

Anna loves music. She likes to sing and dance and play with her toy piano. She wants to be a music teacher when she grows up. She is very enthusiastic about music.

Every day, Anna works hard to learn new songs and sounds. She listens to her mom and dad and her music teacher. She practices with her piano and her voice. She is very happy when she makes music.

One day, Anna has a big surprise. Her music teacher invites her to perform in a concert. She is very excited and nervous. She wants to do her best. She works harder than ever to prepare for the concert.

On the day of the concert, Anna wears a beautiful dress and a big smile. She goes on the stage with her music teacher and her friends. She sees her mom and dad in the audience. They are very proud of her. She plays her piano and sings her song. She hears the applause and the cheers. She feels very happy. She loves music.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went on a ride in a taxi. The taxi was very heavy and made a loud noise. Lily didn't like it and started to scream.

The taxi driver asked, "Why are you screaming, little girl?"

Lily replied, "The taxi is too heavy and it's making a loud noise."

The taxi driver said, "Don't worry, we'll be there soon." And Lily stopped screaming. When they arrived at their destination, Lily thanked the taxi driver and said, "Bye-bye, heavy taxi!"

Once upon a time, there was a strong deer. The deer lived in the woods with its friends. Every night, the deer would wander around and look for food. Then, one day, the deer decided to settle in a new part of the woods.

The strong deer found lots of yummy plants and tall trees. He settled there and made a home for himself. He ran and played in the woods and even made new friends.

The strong deer was happy and felt safe. He had found the perfect place to settle and live. Every day he ate yummy plants and played with his new friends.

He lived there for a very long time and was very happy and content. He found a perfect home and he had lots of friends. The strong deer was very happy in his new home.

Rose and her dad were in the garage. Rose was very upset because she had to leave soon.

"I don't want to leave, Daddy," Rose said.

"I know, but we have to go," her dad said. "Look, I'll bring you something special when I come back."

Rose smiled but tears still ran down her cheeks. Her dad hugged her tight and then he put her in the car. Rose waved goodbye as they drove away.

When her dad came back, he had a big surprise. He opened the garage door and a puppy was sitting there! Rose's eyes lit up and she hugged the puppy tight. She knew it was time to leave, but this time she was excited!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, she decided to hide in a big box in her backyard. She thought it was the perfect hiding spot because it was hidden behind some bushes.

As she sat in the box, she started to feel funny. She couldn't breathe very well and her chest felt tight. She called out to her friends, "Help! I can't get any oxygen in here!" Her friends heard her and quickly ran to get her out of the box.

Lily learned an important lesson that day. She realized that sometimes things that seem like a good idea can be dangerous. From then on, she made sure to always play in safe places where she could get plenty of oxygen.

Anna liked to play with her dollhouse. It was a modest house, with only four rooms and a roof. But Anna loved it very much. She liked to move the dolls and the furniture around and make up stories.

One day, she found a new toy in her room. It was a big knob that could make sounds and lights. Anna was curious. She wanted to attach the knob to her dollhouse. She thought it would make her house more fun and pretty.

She looked for a place to put the knob. She tried the roof, but it was too steep. She tried the door, but it was too small. She tried the window, but it was too high. She was frustrated. She wanted to attach the knob to her dollhouse, but she could not find a good place.

Then she had an idea. She saw a hole in the wall of her dollhouse. It was where the chimney used to be, but it had fallen off. Anna thought the hole was perfect for the knob. She pushed the knob into the hole and twisted it. It fit!

She was happy. She pressed the knob and it made a loud beep. She pressed it again and it made a bright flash. She pressed it again and again, and it made different sounds and lights. She laughed and clapped. She had attached the knob to her dollhouse, and it was the best thing ever.

Jack was an ordinary little boy. He loved to climb. Every day, he would find something to climb on - a tree, a fence, or even the sofa.

Today, it was his bed he wanted to climb. The mattress was big and soft, so it was lots of fun cause he could jump up and down on it.

When he got to the top, he shouted with glee! He was so excited that he jumped off the mattress and ran around the room. He laughed and laughed, having a great time.

After a while, Jack decided to climb back onto the mattress. It was nice and comfy. He snuggled up and soon fell into a deep sleep. 

When he woke up, Jack still had a big smile on his face. He remembered all the fun he had climbing onto his mattress. He knew he would have to do it again soon!

Tom and Lily went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. But their favorite was the seal show. They liked how the seals could act and do tricks with balls and hoops.

"Look, Mom, the seal is acting like a clown!" Lily said, pointing at a seal that wore a funny hat and made noises.

"Yes, dear, he is very funny. And smart, too. He can follow the trainer's commands," Mom said.

Tom wanted to see the seal up close. He saw a dark tunnel behind the pool where the seals were. He thought maybe the seals lived there. He left his seat and walked towards the tunnel.

"Tom, where are you going?" Mom asked, but Tom did not hear her. He was curious about the tunnel.

He entered the tunnel and it was very dark. He could not see anything. He heard a splash and a loud bark. He felt something wet and furry touch his leg. He screamed.

"Help! Help! There is a seal in here!" Tom cried.

Mom, Dad, and Lily heard Tom's scream. They ran to the tunnel and saw a sign that said "Do not enter. Staff only." They were worried.

"Tom, are you okay?" Dad shouted.

A zookeeper came and turned on the light. He saw Tom and the seal. The seal was friendly and playful. He had followed Tom into the tunnel because he liked him.

"Sorry, folks, this tunnel is not for visitors. It's where we keep the extra balls and hoops for the show. And this seal is Bob. He is the star of the show. He likes to act and make friends," the zookeeper said.

Tom was scared at first, but then he saw that Bob was not mean. He was just curious and happy. He smiled and petted Bob.

"Hi, Bob. You are a good seal. You can act very well," Tom said.

Bob barked and wagged his tail. He gave Tom a kiss on the cheek.

Mom, Dad, and Lily were relieved and amused. They thanked the zookeeper and took Tom back to their seat. They watched the rest of the show and clapped for Bob and the other seals.

Tom learned a lesson. He should not go to places where he is not supposed to. But he also made a new friend. He liked Bob the seal. He hoped to see him again.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate flower. Its beauty filled the meadow with lovely colors and smells. One day, a small bird flew by and landed on the flower.

The bird asked, â€œWhat is your value?â€

The flower replied, â€œMy value is my beauty. I bring life and joy to this place.â€

The bird fluttered its wings, spread them wide and said, â€œI recognize you and your value. Your beauty, life and calmness all make this meadow better.â€ 

The flower felt happy and smiled. It was nice to be recognized.

Once upon a time, there was a fat motor. The motor belonged to a little girl named Grace. Grace loved her motor very much and liked taking it for a ride. 

Whenever Grace wanted to go for a ride, she would say "Please motor, will you take me for a ride?". And the motor would always say yes. 

So off they would go. Grace and the motor would rumble away. When they were out of the driveway, Grace would say "Faster, faster!" and the motor would go faster and faster and faster! 

Grace and the motor would ride around the block many times and explore all the roads. When they were done, Grace and the motor would always return home. And boy were they tired!

But Grace always said "Thank you motor, for taking me on such a great ride!". And the motor would say "you're welcome". 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Molly. Molly loved to explore, she wanted to see as much of the world as she could. One day she decided to get a map. She found the prettiest map ever with all the places she wanted to explore coloured in fun colours.

Molly got very excited, she showed it to her friends and they all wanted to go explore the world with her. Her best friend, Lucy, was really bossy and she said they could only go if they all went together. Molly didn't want to be bossed around but she hoped she could convince Lucy to change her mind.

Molly sat down with her map and Lucy came to have a look. â€œLetâ€™s go to this place!â€ Molly said, pointing to a place on the map. Lucy shook her head and said no. She wanted to go to a completely different place on the map.

Molly held her breath, this was her chance. She had to be brave and try to change Lucy's mind. â€œPleaseâ€ Molly said softly, with a polite smile. To her surprise Lucy thought about it for a moment and then said â€œokayâ€. 

Molly was so happy and the two of them went on to explore the world together. All thanks to a little bit of hoping!

Once upon a time there was an attractive wall. It was a special wall because it was very important to the people who lived nearby. The wall was so valuable to them that they decided to take extra care of it. Every day people would come to the wall to make sure it was in good condition.

One day, when some of the people were looking at the wall, they noticed a big hole in it. They were so sad because the wall was very important to them and were worried about how to fix it.

The people got together and decided that they would all work together to fix the wall. All the people from the village worked hard to help fix the wall and soon it was looking just as attractive as before. Everyone was very happy because the wall was valuable to them.

The people now take extra care of the wall to make sure they never have to fix it again. Every day they look at the wall and value it for how special it is.

Ben and Lily were friends who liked to play with trains. They had many trains of different colors and sizes. They liked to make a big station with tracks and bridges and tunnels. They shared their trains and had fun.

One day, Ben saw a new train in Lily's room. It was shiny and red and had a loud whistle. Ben wanted to play with it very much. He asked Lily, "Can you lend me your new train? I will give it back soon."

Lily said, "No, Ben. This is my new train. My mom gave it to me for being healthy and eating my vegetables. You have many trains already. You can play with them."

Ben was angry and sad. He did not like Lily's answer. He thought Lily was mean and selfish. He waited until Lily was not looking and took her new train. He ran to his room and hid it under his bed.

Lily looked for her new train and could not find it. She asked Ben, "Ben, have you seen my new train? I left it on the table."

Ben lied and said, "No, Lily. I have not seen your new train. Maybe you lost it or someone else took it."

Lily was sad and cried. She loved her new train and wanted it back. She asked her mom for help. Her mom came and asked Ben, "Ben, do you know where Lily's new train is?"

Ben was scared and said, "Yes, mom. I took it. I wanted to play with it. I'm sorry."

His mom was angry and said, "Ben, that was very wrong and bad. You should not take things that are not yours. You should ask and respect your friends. You should be honest and not lie. You have to give back Lily's new train and say sorry to her."

Ben felt ashamed and sorry. He gave back Lily's new train and said sorry to Lily. Lily was still sad and hurt. She did not want to play with Ben anymore. She said, "Ben, you are not my friend. You are mean and selfish. You broke my trust. Go away."

Ben lost his friend and his train. He learned a hard lesson. He wished he had been nice and fair.

The moral of the story is: Do not take things that are not yours. Be honest and respectful. Share and care.

Sara was a spoiled girl. She had many toys and clothes, but she never shared or said thank you. She did not like to clean her room or help her mom. She only wanted to play and watch TV.

One day, Sara's mom told her they were going to have a party for her birthday. Sara was very happy. She wanted a big cake, balloons, and presents. She told her mom to invite all her friends and buy her a new dress.

But Sara's mom had a plan. She said, "Sara, you can have a party, but first you have to clean your room. It is very messy and dirty. You have to put away your toys, make your bed, and throw away the trash. If you don't clean your room, you can't have a party."

Sara was very angry. She did not want to clean her room. She thought it was boring and hard. She said, "No, I won't clean my room. You can't make me. I want a party now!"

Sara's mom said, "Sara, you are being very rude and selfish. You have to learn to be responsible and respectful. If you don't clean your room, you will have no party, no cake, no balloons, and no presents. You will stay in your room all day and think about your behavior."

Sara did not believe her mom. She thought her mom was bluffing. She said, "Fine, I don't care. I don't need a party. I have enough toys and clothes. I will play and watch TV in my room. You are a mean mom."

Sara's mom said, "Okay, Sara, you have made your choice. I hope you will change your mind and clean your room. But if you don't, you will miss your party and your friends. I will go and prepare everything for the party. You have one hour to clean your room."

Sara's mom left the room and closed the door. Sara was alone in her messy and dirty room. She looked around and saw her toys, clothes, and trash. She felt a little sad and lonely. She wondered if her mom was really going to have a party without her. She wondered if her friends would come and have fun without her. She wondered if she was being a spoiled girl.

She thought for a while and then decided to clean her room. She said to herself, "Maybe mom is right. Maybe I should be more responsible and respectful. Maybe I should clean my room and say sorry to mom. Maybe I can still have a party and enjoy my birthday."

She got up and started to clean her room. She put away her toys, made her bed, and threw away the trash. She worked hard and fast. She wanted to finish before the hour was up. She wanted to show her mom that she could be a good girl.

She finished cleaning her room and looked around. She felt proud and happy. She saw her room was neat and tidy. She said to herself, "I did it! I cleaned my room! It looks so nice and cozy. I hope mom will be proud of me too. I hope I can still have a party and celebrate my birthday."

She opened the door and ran to find her mom. She saw her mom in the living room, with a big cake, balloons, and presents. She saw her friends waiting for her, with smiles and hugs. She saw her mom looking at her, with love and joy.

She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I was a spoiled girl. I cleaned my room. I want to be a good girl. I love you, mom."

Her mom hugged her and said, "Sara, I'm so proud of you. You did a great job. You are a good girl. I love you too, Sara. Happy birthday, Sara."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. Thank you for the party. Thank you for the cake, balloons, and presents. Thank you for being my mom."

She joined her friends and had a wonderful party. She shared and said thank you. She had fun and learned a lesson. She was a happy girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to make a cake for her mommy's birthday. She went to the store with her daddy to buy some ingredients. She picked some green apples and pale eggs to prepare the cake. 

When they got home, Lily started to mix the ingredients together. She poured the pale eggs into a bowl and added some flour and sugar. She cut the green apples into little pieces and mixed them in too. She put the batter into a pan and put it in the oven to bake. 

After a while, the cake was ready! Lily took it out of the oven and let it cool down. She put some frosting on top and wrote "Happy Birthday Mommy" with green icing. Her mommy loved the cake and was very happy. Lily felt proud that she could prepare a special treat for her mommy's special day.

Lily was a spoiled girl who always got what she wanted. She had many toys, but she never shared them with anyone. She liked to play alone in her room and make a mess.

One day, her mother told her to clean up her toys and come downstairs for lunch. Lily did not listen. She said, "No, I want to play more. You are mean and boring."

Her mother was angry and said, "Lily, if you don't clean up your toys and come downstairs, I will take them away. That is your last chance."

Lily did not care. She said, "You can't take my toys. They are mine. I will scream and cry if you do."

Her mother sighed and said, "Okay, Lily, you leave me no choice. You have become a very naughty girl. You are a threat to yourself and your toys. I will take them away and give them to someone who will appreciate them."

She went upstairs and started to collect Lily's toys in a big bag. Lily saw her and started to scream and cry. She ran to her mother and tried to grab her toys back. She said, "No, no, no, please don't take my toys. I love them. I will be good. I will clean up. I will share. Please, please, please."

But it was too late. Her mother had already taken the bag and left the room. Lily was left alone with no toys and no fun. She realized that she had been a spoiled girl and that she had lost her toys because of her bad behavior. She felt very sad and sorry. She wished she had listened to her mother and been a good girl.

Mum and Dad took their little girl, Lily, to the park. She was so excited! She ran around and played on the swings and the slides, and she sang out loud as she ran.

Mum said to Lily, "That was so much fun. Did you enjoy it?"

Lily smiled and nodded. 

After a while, Lily started to feel tired. She looked at Mum and Dad and said, "I tired. Can I take a nap?"

Mum said, "Yes, of course."

So Lily and Mum and Dad went back home and Lily lay down on her bed for a nap. Mum said, "Sleep tight, my little one."

Lily felt very calm and soon fell asleep. She had the most wonderful dream and when she woke up she started singing again. 

When Mum and Dad heard her singing they knew Lily was feeling happy and rested.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a purple butterfly flying around. She ran to catch it, but it flew away. 

Lily saw her friend Jack playing on the swings. She rushed over to him and said, "Jack, did you see the purple butterfly?" Jack shook his head and said, "No, I didn't see it." 

Lily was sad that she couldn't catch the butterfly. Jack saw her sad face and said, "Don't worry, let's play on the wide slide together!" Lily's face lit up and she rushed to the slide with Jack. They had so much fun sliding down together. 

As they were playing, the purple butterfly flew by again. Lily and Jack rushed to catch it together. This time, they caught it and watched it fly away happily. Lily and Jack hugged each other and said, "We make a great team!"

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. They saw a pigeon on the grass. It was brown and white and had a shiny neck.

"Look, a pigeon!" Tom said. "Let's feed it some bread."

They ran to the pigeon with some bread in their hands. The pigeon was scared and flew away.

"Come back, pigeon!" Lily said. "We want to be your friends."

They followed the pigeon to a big tree. The pigeon landed on a branch. Tom and Lily tried to climb the tree, but it was too high.

"Please, pigeon, come down!" Tom said. "We have bread for you."

The pigeon looked at them with its small black eyes. It made a soft sound.

"Co-coo, co-coo," the pigeon said.

Lily smiled. She thought the pigeon was talking to them.

"Hello, pigeon," she said. "We are Tom and Lily. We are gentle. We won't hurt you."

The pigeon tilted its head. It seemed curious.

"Co-coo, co-coo," the pigeon said again.

Tom and Lily broke some bread and threw it to the pigeon. The pigeon flew down and ate the bread. It came closer to them.

"Can we pet you, pigeon?" Lily asked.

The pigeon nodded. It let them touch its feathers. They were soft and warm.

"Wow, you are so nice, pigeon," Tom said. "Can we be your friends?"

The pigeon nodded again. It made a happy sound.

"Co-coo, co-coo," the pigeon said.

Tom and Lily hugged the pigeon. They were very happy. They had a new friend.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a big dog. It barked and ran to them. It wanted to chase the pigeon.

"Go away, dog!" Tom said. "Leave our pigeon alone!"

The dog did not listen. It jumped and snapped at the pigeon. The pigeon was scared and flew away.

"Come back, pigeon!" Lily said. "Don't go!"

But the pigeon was gone. Tom and Lily could not see it. They were very sad. They started to cry.

"Where is our pigeon?" Tom said. "We miss it."

"Me too," Lily said. "It was our friend."

They hugged each other and cried. They hoped the pigeon was safe. They hoped they would see it again.

Jason was very excited. He was going on a family vacation to the mountains! When they arrived, his mommy suggested they explore the area and find a cabin to stay in. 

They took a long walk, looking around at all the beautiful scenery. Finally, they found the perfect cabin. It was an attractive wooden cottage, surrounded by trees and a river. The family decided this was the place they wanted to stay. 

Jason was so happy with the cabin. He ran around and played in the backyard while his parents unpacked. He could not wait to explore the area with his family. 

The family had a lot of fun and enjoyed their stay. Jason was sad when it was time to leave, but he was excited for the next time he could come back to his familyâ€™s attractive cabin.

One day, Lily and her parent went to the park. There were many flowers and trees and birds. Lily wanted to wander and see them all. She saw a big pond with ducks and fish. She ran to the pond and threw some bread to the ducks. The ducks came closer and quacked. Lily laughed and clapped.

But her parent did not see her. Her parent was looking for her and calling her name. Her parent was worried and scared. Her parent asked other people if they saw Lily. No one saw her.

Lily did not hear her parent. She was too busy with the ducks. She wanted to touch them and play with them. She leaned over the pond and reached out her hand. But she slipped and fell into the water. The water was cold and dirty. Lily cried and splashed.

The ducks flew away. They did not like the noise and the splash. Lily was alone and wet and scared. She wanted her parent.

Her parent heard her cry. Her parent ran to the pond and saw her. Her parent jumped into the water and grabbed her. Her parent hugged her and said, "Lily, I found you! I was so worried! Why did you wander away from me?"

Lily sobbed and said, "I'm sorry, parent. I wanted to see the ducks. They were pretty and funny. But they flew away and I fell in. I'm sorry, parent. I'm cold and dirty."

Her parent said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm glad you're safe. But you have to listen to me. You can't wander away from me. You have to stay close to me. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "I understand, parent. I love you, parent."

Her parent said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's go home and get clean."

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emma. Emma was very happy but she was also very naughty. One day she came across an avocado tree in her garden. She was full of excitement and wanted to pick the delicious fruit, so she started to climb the tree.

At the top, Emma shouted, "Look, I've picked an avocado!" But then she heard a loud noise - someone was shutting the garden gate. It was her mum. Mum said, "Emma, you know you should not climb the tree. It's not safe." 

Emma was very sad, but she understood why mum said what she did. She apologised and took careful steps to come down from the tree. Emma decided that next time she would be more careful and not climb the tree.

Moral: You can be happy and have fun, but it's important to be safe too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Abbie who was feeling very troubled. She was thinking about how she wished her life would be different. Then one day, something special happened.

Abbie saw a magical rainbow in the sky. She was filled with joy and ran towards it. As she got closer, a beautiful fairy appeared. The fairy told Abbie that if she wished hard enough, then her wish would come true.

Abbie was filled with hope and she closed her eyes and wished with all her might. Suddenly, she felt a strange feeling wash over her. When Abbie opened her eyes, the fairy was gone, but a beautiful white dove floated in the sky.

The dove flew through the sky and then it stopped and hovered over Abbie's head. Abbie looked around and saw a glimmering rainbow waterfall nearby. Abbie knew that if she surrendered to the event that was happening, then her wish would come true.

So Abbie surrendered to the event and let the rainbow waterfall wash over her. Suddenly, Abbie felt a sense of peace wash over her and all her troubles disappeared.

Abbie smiled and knew that her wish had come true. TheEnd.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, Timmy's mommy took him on a subway ride to the park. The subway was very noisy and Timmy covered his ears.

When they got to the park, Timmy saw a big ball and wanted to throw it. His mommy threw the ball to him and he threw it back. They played catch for a while until it was time to go home. Timmy was very tired from all the playing and fell asleep on the subway ride back. 

When they got home, Timmy's mommy tucked him into bed and he dreamt of throwing the ball in the park again. The end.

Harry was walking in the open fields with his mom. They passed a big barn and mom said "Let's go in!" 
But Harry didn't want to. He was too embarrassed. His mom told him everyone gets embarrassed sometimes, and it was okay. She hugged him and they went inside the barn. 

Inside the barn they saw pigs, cows, and chickens. Harry was so excited! He got to pet the animals and even help feed them. Soon, he forgot his embarrassment and was having so much fun. 

Mom and Harry walked around the barn for hours, exploring everything. It was the best day ever! Harry was so excited that the barn was open, and glad that he didn't let his embarrassment stop him from having a wonderful time.

Sara was going to be a princess for the party. She had a pink dress, a shiny crown and a long veil. She felt very attractive and happy.

She went to the living room, where her friends were waiting. They all had different costumes. There was a pirate, a fairy, a clown and a lion.

"Wow, Sara, you look so pretty!" said the fairy.

"Thank you, you look very nice too!" said Sara.

"Can I try your veil?" asked the pirate.

Sara thought for a moment. She liked her veil, but she also wanted to be kind. She decided to choose to share.

"Okay, you can try it, but be careful. It is very delicate," she said.

She gave the veil to the pirate, who put it on his head. He looked very funny, and everyone laughed.

"Thank you, Sara, this is fun!" he said.

"You're welcome, but can I have it back soon? I want to wear it for the games," she said.

"Of course, here you go," he said, and gave it back to her.

Sara put the veil on again, and smiled. She was happy to have such good friends. They all played together, and had a wonderful time.

Once upon a time there was a modern pool. All the people in the town wanted to go swimming there! One day a brave girl came to the pool. She wanted to resist the temptation to swim, but it was too hard! She sat by the side of the pool, dreaming about how great it would be to dive in.

Finally, the girl could not resist the temptation anymore. She slowly stepped into the water. She felt so free and wonderful! She splashed and laughed and played for a long time. She made so many friends in the pool.

When the day was done, the girl was sad. She wanted to stay in the modern pool forever. But her mom said it was time to go home. The girl said goodbye to all her new friends and reluctantly left the pool.

But she was sure to comeback soon. She had resisted the temptation once, but it wouldnâ€™t be long before she went swimming again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons on his modern TV. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a present. It was a big, shiny present with a pretty wrap on it. 

Timmy was so excited to open the present, but when he did, he didn't like what was inside. It was a shirt that he didn't like. Timmy's mom asked him why he didn't like the shirt, and Timmy just shrugged his shoulders. 

Later that day, Timmy saw a homeless man on the street who didn't have any clothes to wear. Timmy remembered the shirt his mom gave him and realized that he could give it to the homeless man. Timmy felt happy that he could help someone in need and learned that sometimes things may not seem important, but they can be helpful to others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, Lily's best friend Emily passed by her house to play. They went to the park to play hide and seek. Lily found a great hiding spot behind a big tree, but Emily couldn't find her. Emily started to complain that Lily was hiding too well. 

After a while, Lily got tired of hiding and wanted to play something else. She came out of her hiding spot and told Emily that they should play tag instead. Emily agreed and they had a lot of fun running around the park. They played until the sun started to set and it was time to go home. 

When they got back to Lily's house, Emily's mom was waiting for her. She asked Emily if she had fun playing with Lily. Emily smiled and said yes, but she also complained that Lily was too good at hiding. Lily's mom overheard and laughed, saying that Lily had always been good at hiding. The girls said goodbye and promised to play again soon.

Once there were two friends. They wanted to improve their house. One of the friends had a leak in the roof. The other friend was friendly and said they would help. They set to work fixing the leak. They worked hard with their tools and soon the leak was gone. The two friends were very happy. They were glad they improved their house. They were also very proud of their hard work. They hugged each other and knew they would stay friends forever.

Once there was a fat cat. She had a special crystal. Every day she would proudly display it in her house.

One day, a friend came over. The cat shared the crystal with her friend. Later that day, the friend returned with something special to provide the cat.

When the friend opened the box, there was a beautiful, sparkly, crystal ball inside. The cat was so excited! She had never seen such a special crystal before.

The cat knew this crystal was the best thing she would ever own. She patiently waited and eventually after much anticipation, the crystal provide her with a secret message. The message said, "Crystals have magical powers."

The cat took such joy in owning the crystal. She would often look into it and watch it's sparkles. She believed that the crystal could create a magical world.

One day she noticed a crystal tear. She was so upset and started to cry. Soon she realized that the crystal was providing comfort for her. It seemed to understand her grief and provide her with comfort and joy.

The fat cat was thankful for the crystal's magical powers. She never knew what secrets it would provide her, but she trusted its mysterious ways.

Once upon a time, there was a panda named Pandy. Pandy was very cute and cuddly, but sometimes things were difficult for him. One day, Pandy's friend gave him a big bell to ring. Pandy was so happy and he rang the bell all day long. Everyone in the forest could hear the sound. It was so loud! 

At night, Pandy went to bed with his bell. He was so tired from ringing it all day. But suddenly, he heard a strange noise. It was a difficult noise to describe. Pandy was scared, so he rang his bell as loud as he could. His friends heard the sound and came to help him. They found out that the noise was just a little bird trying to find its way home. 

From that day on, Pandy always had his bell with him. He loved ringing it, but he also knew that it could help him when things were difficult. And he was very happy to have such good friends who would always come to his aid.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. They had a toy phone that could record their voices. They liked to pretend they were talking to each other or to other people.

One day, they decided to play a prank on Lily's big sister, Mia. They hid the toy phone under Mia's bed and recorded a scary message. They said, "Hello, Mia. We are the monsters under your bed. We are going to get you when you sleep. Boo!"

They giggled and ran away, leaving the toy phone on. They waited for Mia to come home and hear the message. They thought it would be very funny.

But Mia did not come home that day. She had to stay at the hospital because she was sick. Lily and Ben did not know that. They got bored and went to play with other toys.

That night, Lily's mom came to her room and told her the bad news. Mia had a fever and had to stay at the hospital for a long time. Lily felt very sad and scared. She wanted to see her sister and hug her.

She went to her bed and tried to sleep. But then she heard a voice under her bed. It was the toy phone. It said, "Hello, Mia. We are the monsters under your bed. We are going to get you when you sleep. Boo!"

Lily screamed and cried. She thought the monsters were real and they had come for her. She did not remember that it was her and Ben who recorded the message. She called for her mom, but her mom did not hear her. She was too busy talking to the doctor on the phone.

Lily felt very alone and afraid. She wished she had not played the prank on Mia. She wished she had been a humble and kind sister. She wished Mia was there to protect her. But she was not. She had left her alone with the monsters.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, they were playing hide-and-seek when a big, white fog came rolling in. Timmy and his friends couldn't see each other anymore, and they were scared. But then, Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's hold hands so we don't get lost in the fog!" 

Timmy's friends thought that was a great idea, and they all held hands tightly. They walked slowly and carefully through the fog, and eventually, they found their way out. Timmy felt proud that he had helped his friends gain confidence in the scary fog. 

After that day, Timmy's friends started calling him "Timmy the Wise" because he knew what to do in a scary situation. Timmy was happy that he could help his friends, and he didn't feel ignorant anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a beautiful fountain. It had brilliant colors and sparkled in the sun.

Lily was so excited to see the fountain that she ran towards it. But she accidentally fell in! She was scared and started to cry for help.

Luckily, a kind man heard her cries and came to rescue her. He pulled her out of the fountain and asked if she was okay. Lily was very grateful and said thank you.

But then, something bad happened. The man's dog ran away and got hit by a car. Lily was very sad and cried. The man was sad too and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I couldn't rescue my dog."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his bike with a big wheel in the front. He rode it every day and felt very happy. One day, Timmy saw a girl crying because she didn't have a bike. Timmy felt bad for her and decided to give her his bike. 

The girl was very happy and rode the bike away. Timmy felt proud that he could help someone. But then, he realized he had no bike to ride anymore. He felt sad and ashamed that he gave away his bike. He wished he could keep it. 

Timmy never saw the girl or his bike again. He was very sad and missed his bike every day. He learned that it's important to help others, but sometimes it's okay to keep things that make us happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved her notebook. She took it with her everywhere - to school, to the park, the store. One day, she was having a lot of fun at the playground when she noticed a high tower nearby. She wanted to climb to the top! So, she took her notebook and began her ascent.

The tower was very tall and with each step, she appeared to be getting closer to the top. "If I can make it to the top, I can be the bravest girl in the world," she thought to herself. When she reached the top, she realized she was stuck and couldn't resist the urge to look down. 

Suddenly, a voice spoke out from below. "Don't worry little girl," it said. "I will help you come down safely." It was a policeman who had noticed her climbing the high tower. He climbed right up the tower and helped her down. 

The little girl thanked the policeman and ran all the way home with her notebook. She had resisted the urge to look down and conquered the high tower. She was proud of herself and very happy.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to hop. They hopped on the grass, on the sand, on the rocks. They hopped fast and slow, high and low, far and near. They had fun hopping together.

One day, they saw a sign that said: Hop Race. Win a big toy. They wanted to join the race and win the toy. They went to the start line and waited for the sound. They were nervous. They hoped they could hop well.

The sound came and they started to hop. They hopped as fast as they could. They passed other kids who hopped too. They saw the finish line and the big toy. They hopped harder and harder.

Lily and Ben reached the finish line at the same time. They looked at each other and smiled. They had both won the race. They had both won the toy. They were happy. They hugged and said:

"We did it! We hopped well! We are good friends!"

They shared the toy and played with it. They hopped some more. They had fun hopping together.

Anna loved to draw with her crayons. She liked to make pictures of her family, her friends, and her toys. She had many colors to choose from, and she enjoyed mixing them to create new ones.

One day, she decided to draw a picture of a rainbow. She took out her red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple crayons, and started to make a big arc on her paper. She was very careful to make the colors look bright and pretty.

Her mom came to see what she was doing. She saw the rainbow and smiled. She said, "Wow, Anna, that is an incredible rainbow! You are very good at drawing. I love how you used all the colors."

Anna felt happy and proud. She smiled back at her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You always encourage me to try new things. I like to draw because it makes me feel happy."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm glad you feel happy, Anna. Drawing is a wonderful way to express yourself. You have a lot of talent and imagination. I can't wait to see what you will draw next."

Once upon a time, there was a stable. It was big and strong and made out of wood. Some horses lived inside the stable and they were very happy. One day, a little boy wanted to visit the horses. He saw a big slide outside the stable and he wanted to slide down.

The boy went down the slide. It was so much fun! He had a big smile on his face as he slid down. When he got to the bottom he raced to the stable. He went inside and saw the horses.

The horses looked very unique. They were different colours and different sizes. The boy was so happy to meet the horses. He was so excited that he wanted to slide some more! So he ran back to the slide and went down again.

The boy would go to the stable every day. He would slide down the slide and play with the horses. He realized that the stable was a very special place. It was unique and it made him happy.

Sandy was a happy little girl. She liked to raise her arms and spin around. One day, Sandy decided to find a new game to play. She went outside and saw a big pipe in the garden. She asked her mom if she could use it. Her mom said yes, she could play with it, but she had to raise it carefully.

Sandy was so excited as she lugged the big pipe around. Once she found a spot, she began to raise the pipe up and down. It was heavy, but Sandy was strong and had no trouble. She fit it into the ground and started to dig. Sandy had made a pipe swing!

She kept raising it and pushing it until it fit just right. Sandy was so proud of her work. She sat on the pipe and pushed herself back and forth, back and forth. She giggled in delight as the sun shone down on her.

Sandy was so proud of her pipe swing. She kept it fit for a long time and loved playing with it every day. She thanked her mom for letting her find a new game to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and jump on the floor. One day, Lily's mom bought her a big chocolate cake. Lily was very happy and wanted to eat it all by herself.

But then, Lily's brother Jack came in and said, "Can I have some cake too?" Lily didn't want to share her cake and said, "No, it's all mine!" Jack got sad and said, "That's not fair, Lily. You always spoil everything."

Lily felt bad and decided to share her cake with Jack. They both ate the cake and had a fun time together. But then, they accidentally dropped some crumbs on the floor. Their mom came in and said, "Oh no, you made a mess on the floor!" Lily and Jack quickly cleaned up the crumbs and apologized.

Later that day, Lily's cat Fluffy got sick and died. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. Jack came in and hugged Lily, saying, "I'm sorry about Fluffy. But don't worry, he's not really dead. He's just in cat heaven now." Lily felt a little better and hugged Jack back.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty dresses and always picked the white ones. One day, she went to the park to play with her friend, Timmy. Timmy was wearing a green shirt and blue shorts.

Lily mentioned to Timmy, "I love your shirt, but I wish it was white like my dress." 

Timmy replied, "I like my style. I don't want to wear white like you all the time." 

Lily felt sad because she wanted to match with her friend. They started to argue about their clothes. Suddenly, a butterfly flew by and landed on Timmy's shoulder. Lily forgot about the argument and they both laughed as they watched the butterfly fly away. They realized that it was more important to have fun together than to worry about the color of their clothes. From that day on, they played together happily, no matter what they were wearing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to visit her grandma in the cabin in the woods. Grandma had a big pot of soup on the stove and she asked Lily to help her pour it into bowls. 

Lily thought the soup looked weird because it had lots of vegetables in it. "Grandma, why does the soup look weird?" she asked. "That's because it's healthy and good for us," replied grandma. 

After they finished eating, they went outside to play. Lily saw a squirrel and tried to catch it, but it ran away. "Oh no, the squirrel is gone," she said. "Don't worry, Lily. There are lots of other animals in the woods to play with," said grandma. 

Lily had so much fun at the cabin with her grandma that she didn't want to leave. "Can we come back and play again soon?" she asked. "Of course, my dear. Anytime you want," said grandma with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to brush her hair every day. One day, her mom gave her a pretty new brush. Lily was so happy and she said, "I accept this brush, thank you!" 

Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the park. They saw a big box that was closed. Lily's mom said, "Let's open the box and see what's inside!" Lily was excited and helped her mom open the box. Inside, they found a cute little puppy! 

Lily was so happy to see the puppy. She wanted to take it home with her. Her mom said, "We have to ask the owner if we can keep it." The owner said yes, and Lily was overjoyed. She said, "I accept this puppy as my new friend!" From that day on, Lily and her new puppy played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annabelle. She was a three-year-old and she was full of joy and wonder. One day, Annabelle's mom asked her to count the snowflakes outside the window. Annabelle wanted to do something else, but she knew her mom asked for good reason. 

Annabelle dashed to the window and began to count, but she soon realized that the snowflakes were too fast for her. She asked her mom if she could count something else and her mom agreed as long as it was normal. So Annabelle started counting the birds in a nearby tree. 

Just then a large gust of wind blew the birds away and Annabelle became very upset. She cried out, "Mom, how can I finish counting if the birds won't stay still?" Annabelle's mom hugged her and told her, "That is the nature of winter, Annabelle. But we can still admire the beauty of the snowflakes." 

Annabelle couldn't help but smile. She went outside to enjoy the winter wonderland and showed her mom what she had counted - 54 snowflakes dancing in the air.

Once there were two friends named Jake and Sophie. They were both very strong, but one day Jake ran into trouble. He was sad, so Sophie said â€œLet me help.â€

They separated and Sophie looked for a way to make Jake happy. She gathered many things together then made a plan to surprise Jake.

When Sophie found him, she raced up and called â€œLook what I brought!â€ Jake was so happy that he hugged her tightly. 

From then on, Sophie and Jake were the best of friends. They helped each other out and never let trouble separate them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mommy and daddy. They always went to the same park, and Lily loved playing on the slide.

One day, Lily saw a boy at the park. He had a toy car that was incredible. Lily wanted to play with the car, but she was too shy to say anything to the boy.

The next time they went to the park, Lily saw the boy again. This time, he was playing on the slide. Lily wanted to play on the slide too, but there were too many big kids on it. She was sad and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, the boy with the incredible car came up to her and said, "Do you want to play on the slide with me?" Lily was so happy and they had a great time playing together. From that day on, they were best friends and played together every time they went to the park.

Once upon a time there was a strong man. He loved to listen to his radio. Every day he would turn it on to listen to music and he was always very happy. But one day he was in for a surprise.

When he turned on the radio, something special came out! Instead of music, a loud voice said, "TADA! Surprise!"

The man was so amazed. He had never heard of a radio that could speak. He wanted to know more about it, so he asked the voice, "Who are you?"

The voice replied, "I'm the Magic Radio! I'm here to make your day even better!"

The man asked the Magic Radio to play his favorite song and it did. From that day on, every time the man turned on his radio, he would get a big surprise. The Magic Radio made his day better and stronger than ever before.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to run in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a fancy rake in his neighbor's yard. He asked his neighbor if he could use the rake to help clean up the leaves in his own yard. His neighbor said yes, and Timmy was very happy. Timmy ran back to his yard with the fancy rake and started to clean up the leaves. He worked very hard and soon his yard was all clean. Timmy was proud of himself and ran back to his neighbor's yard to return the fancy rake. The neighbor was happy to see that Timmy had done a good job and thanked him. Timmy felt very happy and ran back to his house to tell his parents about his day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to go upstairs and get her favorite book. 

Lily went upstairs, but she couldn't find the book. She looked and looked, but it wasn't there. Just then, her daddy came upstairs and asked her what she was doing. 

"I can't find mommy's book," Lily said. 

"That's an easy problem to solve," her daddy said with a smile. "Let's look together." 

They searched the whole room, and finally, her daddy found the book. "Great job, Daddy!" Lily said, giving him a big kiss on the cheek.

Once upon a time, there was a little parrot. The parrot was very gray. The parrot was happy and wanted to find someone to feed it.

One day, the parrot ran across a little girl. The girl had a big smile on her face. She was excited to see the parrot. She walked over and said, "Hello, parrot." She held out some food and fed it to the parrot. 

The parrot was happy to have someone to feed it. Every day, the girl would feed the parrot. The parrot always looked forward to the girl coming around and feeding it. 

The girl and parrot became very good friends. They played together and the parrot was very grateful for the food it received. The girl was glad to have the parrot as a friend and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little girl. She loved to watch things. One day, she saw something really interesting--a piece of paper floating in the wind. She watched it go up and down, up and down as it flew through the sky. She wanted to follow it, so she ran after it. 

But the paper was too fast, and the little girl could not catch it. Suddenly, an idea came to her! She picked up some of her own pieces of paper, and threw them up into the air. Then she watched the air fill with lots of lovely paper--all flying around, like a magical dance. 

The girl laughed and laughed, and suddenly she realized something--she loved watching all the paper fly in the sky. From that day onwards, she watched the paper fly every day, until the little girl grew up. 

And that's how the lovely little girl discovered how much she loved watching the paper fly!

Once there was a beetle. She was very small and liked to find hidden things. Every day she looked for something new to find. One day she went on a long journey to find a special hidden prize.

On her way, she didn't know what she would see. She looked high and low, but she couldn't see anything. She was getting very tired until finally she found it! It was a hidden treat.

But when she got there, she was so surprised. She knew it was something amazing, because it was so special. She couldn't believe it was all for her. She was so happy, she wanted to share it with everybody.

Now her friends all know about her special hidden treat. She is so pleased to have found it, and she is happy to share it with everyone.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Bella. She was three years old. 
She was walking up the hill to her home. She was feeling very busy. She was thinking about all the things she had to do when she got home. 
When Bella reached the top of the hill, she looked around. She smiled when she saw her home. It was a bright and happy house. She felt happy when she saw it. 
Bella trusted her home. She knew she would have a good time there. She was excited to go inside. She wanted to play and have fun. 
When Bella finally opened the door, she was so happy to be home. The house was filled with love and trust. It was the perfect place for Bella to be.

Jenny and her mom were walking in the park one day. Suddenly they noticed a raven on a nearby tree. Jenny asked her mom who the little black bird was. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a raven."

Jenny smiled and nodded her head in agreement. "Oh, look how tidy it is!" she said as it fluffed up its feathers.

The raven seemed to be enjoying the warm day. It cocked its head this way and that, trying to catch sounds of the forest.

Then it took off in the air and flew away. Jenny watched it and waved goodbye. She smiled and said, "Goodbye, Mr. Raven!"

Her mom put her arm around Jenny and said, "Let's go get some ice cream. Doesn't that sound nice?"

Jenny's eyes lit up and she nodded her head, saying, "Yes!". She seemed very eager to get some ice cream. 

So off they went, happy to enjoy the day together.

Once upon a time there were two little boys Matt and Sam. They were playing in the park one day with a football, trying to see who could kick it the furthest. Matt was getting frustrated because Sam was winning. Suddenly, Sam peeked and noticed an elderly man walking towards them. He was deaf, but Matt and Sam didn't know this. 

The man called out to them and waved his hand, but Matt and Sam didn't reply. "Why aren't they talking to me?" the man thought. He started to walk away, feeling lonely and sad.

Suddenly, Sam shouted out "Hi!" and the man turned around. Matt and Sam asked the man to join them in their game and he smiled. They had a lot of fun together and Matt ended up winning in the end.

The boys were happy and the old man was overjoyed. From this experience, Matt and Sam learnt an important lesson: it doesn't matter who wins or loses, it's important to always be kind and inclusive.

Lucy was 3 years old and she loved to play outside. She loved to run and jump and explore. One day, Lucy wanted to try something new. She decided to climb as high as she could. She went over to the enormous tree and started to climb. Soon, she was all the way up to her knee. Lucy had decided to go higher, but suddenly she felt very scared. She didn't know what to do. She thought for a moment. Then, Lucy decided to go back down the tree and try something else. Lucy was happy that she had decided to be brave and try something new, even though she was a little scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because her grandma was coming to visit her. Lily loved her grandma very much because she always brought her a special treat. 

Lily's mom helped her put on her favorite crown and they waited for grandma to arrive. Finally, they heard a knock on the door. Lily ran to open it and gave her grandma a big hug. 

During their visit, grandma told Lily a story about a princess who wore a beautiful crown. Lily loved the story so much that she asked if she could wear a crown like that too.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved music and he wanted to play the violin. His mom said she would bring him to the music store to get one. Tim was so happy!

Lily liked to design things with her crayons and paper. She made houses, flowers, animals and people. She was very good at drawing. One day, she wanted to design a figure of her best friend, Mia. She took a big paper and a blue crayon and started to draw.

Sara and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a long, pink rag that she liked to pretend was a scarf. Ben had a big, blue truck that he liked to drive around. They were having fun until Ben saw Sara's rag and wanted it.

Sara and Ben went to their rooms, crying and sulking. They wished they had listened to Mom and not fought over the rag. They realized they had lost their toy and their friend. They felt lonely and sorry.
