Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kate. She loved to play games with her friends. One day she had a great idea. She was going to store the goal in an unusual place.

Kate found a big box in the corner of her bedroom. She went to her mom to get permission to store the goal in the box.

Kate's mom said, "I think it's a great plan. But why do you want to store the goal in the box?"

Kate said, "Because it will be our secret goal and nobody else will know about it. We can practice and play our game together." 

Kate's mom smiled and said, "Alright, go ahead and store the goal in the box. But remember, be sure to be bossy and keep the box closed tight."

Kate said, "Yes, Mom! I'll be sure to keep it closed tight."

So Kate stored the goal in the box and her friends gathered around to practice their game. They played happily for hours and when it was time to stop, they all helped store the goal in the box. They had a great time and would look forward to playing the game again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Tom. He loved to go on walks in the forest. One day, he found a stick on the ground. He picked it up and started to play with it. 

Suddenly, he heard a little girl's voice. "Excuse me, can you help me?" she said. Tom turned around and saw a little girl with tears in her eyes. "What's wrong?" he asked. 

"I fell down and got mud on my dress," she said. "Can you help me wipe it off?" Tom took out a handkerchief from his pocket and wiped the mud off the girl's dress. "There you go, all clean!" he said. 

"Thank you so much!" the little girl said. "Can I play with your stick?" Tom smiled and gave her the stick. "Of course you can," he said. The little girl smiled and ran off to play with the stick. Tom continued his walk in the forest, happy to have helped someone in need.

Once upon a time there was a tough village. In the village lived two friends. They were both small and had fluffy hair.

One day the friends decided to go on an adventure. So they chose a nice spot and began to play. As they played, they heard a strange whispering sound.

They decided to look for the source of the sound. After a while, they found it. It was a magical tree! 

The tree whispered, "You are brave. I can grant you a wish." The two friends were so excited. 

One of the friends said, "I wish for peace in our village." The other friend said, "I wish for a safe home for everyone." 

The magical tree nodded and said, "You are tough. Your wishes will be granted!" 

The two friends thanked the tree and ran off to tell the people of their village about the magical tree. From then on, the village was peaceful and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. He loved gum. One day, he found a thin piece of gum on the ground. He thought it was very special. He put the gum in his pocket to save it for later.

Tom went to play with his friend, Sam. They played a game where they had to escape from a pretend monster. They ran and hid, but the monster always found them. Tom felt scared, but he remembered his special gum. He thought it could help them win the game.

Tom took out the thin gum and shared it with Sam. They both chewed the gum and started to run from the monster again. But this time, they did not escape. The gum made them feel sick and slow. The monster caught them, and they lost the game. Tom and Sam were very sad. They learned never to pick up gum from the ground again.

Once upon a time there was an old grumpy lady. She went for a walk to the pond each day. Everyday she would gulp down a drink from the pond.

One day she didn't notice that the pond was dirty. She still took the drink, but it made her feel sick. She got very grumpy and angry.

The old lady continued to drink from the pond everyday, even though she knew it was dirty. She got sicker and sicker. Her grumpiness kept growing too.

The old lady felt worse and worse each day. Eventually, she was too weak and grumpy to do anything. She fell down and didn't get back up. The old lady died because she drank the dirty water from the pond.

Once upon a time there was a fisherman. He was deep in the ocean. One day, he wanted to taste something special.

So he threw his net into the water. He pulled it back up and there was something in it! He opened it and saw a delicious-looking fish. He grabbed it and took a bite.

He thought it was yummy! He smiled and threw his net back into the deep ocean. He kept fishing and he always tasted something delicious. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind farmer named Sandy. He had a big farm with lots of animals on it.

One sunny day, Sandy went outside to take care of the animals. He brought some hay with him to give to them to eat. He said, "I have some fresh hay for you! Who would like some?"

The animals on the farm were very excited. One of them, a big purple cow, ran over to Sandy and said, "Moo! Moo! I love hay!"

Sandy smiled and gave the purple cow some hay. 

"Thank you for the hay, Sandy," said the cow.

Sandy said, "You're welcome. It's nice to see you so happy."

The cow was very pleased and went to enjoy her meal. Sandy went on giving hay to the other animals. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was an old temple in a big city. The temple was very big and many people liked to visit it. But some people didn't like each other and they fought a lot. They didn't know how to be friends.

One day, a wise person came to the temple and told the people to unite. They didn't understand what "unite" meant, but the wise person explained that it meant to come together and be friends. 

The people listened and started to talk to each other. They realized that they were all the same, even though they looked different. They became friends and the temple was a happy place again. The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind to everyone and to unite with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on adventures with her mom. One day, they went to the park to have a picnic. Lily's mom packed a bag with sandwiches, fruits, and juice.

While they were eating, a squirrel came over to their picnic blanket. The squirrel had a hairy tail and Lily thought it was so cute. "Mommy, look at the squirrel's hairy tail!" she said. 

Lily's mom reminded her to not get too close to the squirrel and to be careful. "Okay mommy, I won't forget," Lily replied. They finished their picnic and went home, happy and full.

Once upon a time, there was a poor man who lived in a small house. He didn't have much, but he was happy. One day, he decided to sack some of the ceiling in his house so he could have more room. He worked hard all day and when he was done, he was very proud of his work. There was now a lot more space in his house, and he could now fit a few more things in!

The next day, the poor man invited his friends over to see his new sack in the ceiling. When they arrived, they were amazed at how big the space was! They thought it was brilliant and congratulated him on his hard work.

The poor man was overjoyed and proudly showed off his sack in the ceiling to everyone who visited. From that day on, his house never felt so spacious and he was very pleased!

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy farmer. He worked and worked, but it seemed like he never got anything for it. One day he had an idea - sale all his wares in the market! So, the next day he got up early and loaded his wagon with goods to sell. But he was so grumpy that not many people wanted to buy from him. Then, just as he was about to give up, he had a genius idea - sell his wares for a reward! People now had a reason to buy from him, and he sold all his wares! Everyone was so pleased, and the farmer was no longer so grumpy. He had learned the value of the reward, and he was happy to have sold his wares. The end.

Charlie was excited to see the parade that was coming down his street. He ran to his bedroom window, and looked outside. He saw bright colors and heard music coming from the street below. He jumped up with excitement, and ran to his mom. "Mommy, please let me go to the parade," he asked.

His mom smiled and said, "Okay Charlie, but you have to stay with me the whole time, okay?" Charlie smiled in agreement. He quickly put on his shoes and ran outside. As he walked down the street he could feel the excitement build up.

As the parade got closer, Charlie realized that it was not just colorful floats and music, but that it smelled smelly too. He started to giggle, and mommy patted him on the back. "What's so funny, sweetheart?" 

Charlie looked up and said, "Mommy, it smells like poo!" She erupted in laughter and replied, "Oh, Charlie! It could be worse, but don't worry, the parade will be over soon". 

Sure enough, after a few more minutes the parade was over, and all of the smelly things had passed. Charlie was glad that he was able to see the parade and to realize that it was smelly, but it was still fun all the same.

Once upon a time, there was a lady who loved to wear purple. She had a big purple hat and a purple dress. One day, she went to the park to have a picnic. She brought a purple blanket and some purple grapes to eat.

While she was eating, a bee flew by and she sneezed. The bee flew into her nose! The lady tried to get the bee out by blowing her nose, but it wouldn't come out. She started to feel scared and sad.

Just then, a kind little girl saw the lady and asked what was wrong. The lady explained what happened and the little girl had an idea. She told the lady to try smelling some flowers to make her sneeze again. The lady tried it and the bee flew out! The lady was so happy and grateful to the little girl. They became friends and had a purple-themed picnic together. The end.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to run and play in the park, but one day she noticed something was wrong. 

Every time Lucy blinked, her eyes hurt. She rubbed them but the feeling didn't go away.

Then she remembered something her mommy told her. She said: "Whenever something is wrong, ask God for help". So Lucy closed her eyes and prayed.

Suddenly, her eyes felt better. She opened her eyes and saw that the sun had gone behind the clouds. The sun's harsh rays had been hurting her eyes.

God had answered her prayer and made her eyes feel better. Lucy was so thankful and promised to be more careful in the future. 

She had learned an important lesson. Whenever something is wrong, never forget to ask for help from God.

Once, there was a nice turtle named Tom. Tom was always very polite to everyone. One day, he was walking through a grassy park. Suddenly, he began to sneeze. His nose felt tickly! He sneezed and sneezed.

Tom noticed a little bunny nearby. It had a soft skin that was brown and white. The bunny looked at Tom with a curious face.

"Why are you sneezing?" asked the bunny.

Tom laughed and said, â€œMy nose feels tickly! Can you help me?â€

The bunny thought for a moment, then said, â€œGo pick some leaves.â€

Tom did, and he rubbed the leaves on his nose and cheeks. And guess what? It worked! The tickle went away, and Tom felt better.

He smiled at the bunny and thanked her.

â€œYou are very polite,â€ said the bunny. â€œThank you for trying my suggestion.â€

Tom smiled, happy that he could help. Then, he waved goodbye and hopped away.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to draw pictures. One day, he drew a silly picture of a cat. The cat had a big, stupid smile on its face. Tim laughed and showed the picture to his friend, Sam.

Sam looked at the picture and said, "That's a funny cat! It looks so stupid!" They both laughed and decided to draw more silly pictures together. They drew dogs, birds, and even a big sack.

Then, Tim had an idea. "Let's play a game with the sack!" he said. Sam agreed, and they took the big sack outside. They took turns putting the silly pictures inside the sack and then pulling one out. They would then act like the silly animal in the picture.

Tim and Sam laughed and played with the silly pictures and the big sack all day. They had so much fun being silly together. And from that day on, they always played and drew silly pictures with their big sack.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy he loved very much. It was a toy knife. He played with it all day long. He liked to pretend he was a big, strong hero with his toy knife.

One day, Tim found a real knife in the kitchen. He thought it looked just like his toy knife. He wanted to play with it, but he remembered what his mom had told him. She said real knives are not for playing. They can hurt people.

Tim put the real knife back and went to find his toy knife. He played with it and had lots of fun. He was glad he listened to his mom. The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents because they know what is best for you.

Once upon a time there was a bear. He was a nice bear and wanted to be fair. He wanted to give everyone the same.

The bear had an idea, he wanted to take a stick and attach something special to the end. He found some beautiful ribbons, cut them into small pieces and attached one piece to the end of the stick. 

He called his friends and they all lined up. The bear handed out the stick with the ribbon attached to the end and he said, "This is so that everyone gets the same and it will be fair." 

The bear's friends were so happy, they hugged the bear and thanked him for being so kind. From that day onwards, everyone was happy and fair.

Once there was a little girl who was very smart. She loved to wear pretty things - especially her favorite scarf. It was bright red with pink stripes, and she liked how it made her look.

She liked to wear the scarf to school, but when the weather got cold it was hard to stay warm. One day, the little girl had an idea. She ran to her room and grabbed her favorite blanket. Then she used it to cover her scarf.

She looked so smart and she felt so warm! She stayed warm all day and still looked nice, even though it was cold outside. Everyone was so impressed with the little girl's idea.

She kept using her blanket to cover her scarf when it got cold, and everyone enjoyed seeing her cute outfit every day. She was so happy that she had found a way to stay warm and look so smart!

Sara and Ben are friends who like to play in the park. They see a big tree with many acorns on the ground. Sara picks up an acorn and says, "Look, Ben, this is an acorn. It is from the tree. It is brown and hard."

Ben picks up another acorn and says, "No, Sara, this is not an acorn. It is a ball. It is gray and soft."

Sara and Ben start to argue. They do not agree on what the acorns are. They show each other their acorns and say, "This is an acorn!" and "This is a ball!"

A squirrel comes by and sees the acorns. He is hungry and wants to eat them. He runs to Sara and Ben and says, "Excuse me, can I have your acorns? They are not balls. They are food for me. I need to store them for winter."

Sara and Ben are surprised. They look at the squirrel and then at each other. They realize that they were both wrong. The acorns are not balls or from the tree. They are food for the squirrel.

They say to the squirrel, "We are sorry, Mr. Squirrel. We did not know that the acorns are food for you. You can have them. We will find something else to play with."

The squirrel says, "Thank you, Sara and Ben. You are very kind. Next time, you can study the acorns with me. I can teach you many things about them. They are very interesting."

Sara and Ben smile and nod. They give the acorns to the squirrel and watch him bury them in the ground. They learn something new and make a new friend. They decide to study the acorns with the squirrel next time they come to the park.

Once upon a time there was a baby. She was very happy and loved to laugh and play. One day, the baby's parents were worried that she was lost. They searched everywhere but couldn't find her. Then, they remembered that the baby had been playing in the backyard. Sure enough, she was there, laughing and playing. Her parents were so happy to have found her safe and sound. From that day on, they remembered to always check the backyard first when they were worried!

The bear went out to play one day. He was so happy and he wanted to dance. He twirled around and around in the sun.

He came to a big hole and looked inside. The bottom of the hole was wet. He could see some stones and leaves lying inside it.

He wanted to dance there too. He stepped inside the hole and did a funny dance. He spun around and around, and splashed the wet ground.

He laughed and laughed until he was tired. He left the hole and felt all happy. He knew he had found a fun place for his dancing.

One day, Lila was outside playing in the dirt when something caught her eye. She saw a pattern of tiny circles and wiggly lines in the dirt. She was so excited that she ran to find her dad to show him.

"Dad! Dad!" she cried. "Look what I found!"

Her dad looked at the pattern and smiled.

"What is it?" he asked.

"I don't know," Lila said, "but I think it is something special!"

Her dad grabbed a stick and started to trace the pattern. Eventually, the pattern revealed itself to be a picture of a flower. Lila was so happy!

"Look at what I found!" she said, grinning.

But the more she looked at it, the more frustrated she became.

"Why is it so complicated?" she asked.

Her dad smiled and said, "Sometimes things just take time to figure out, sweetheart. That's what makes them special."

One summer day, Jack was walking his puppy around the park. Suddenly, Jack heard a loud splash nearby. He quickly ran over to where he heard the noise from and saw that it was a baby duck! The duck had fallen in the lake and was having trouble swimming.

Jack carefully scooped up the duck and returned it safely to the shoreline. He then hugged the duck tightly and said, â€œYou were so brave! Letâ€™s never do this again, okay?â€ The little duck nodded in agreement.

Jack then took the duck home with him so he could give it a warm, safe place to stay. He fed the duck some bread, then snuggled it in a blanket to make sure it stayed nice and cozy.

Jack smiled and said, â€œI rescued you today, little duck. You are safe now.â€ The little duck smiled back and nodded in agreement. Jack had saved the day!

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Blue. Blue loved to soar high in the sky and feel the wind in his feathers. One day, Blue saw a basket on the ground. Inside the basket, there were some yummy berries. Blue wanted to eat the berries, but he couldn't reach them.

Just then, a little girl named Lily saw Blue and the basket. "Oh no, poor birdie!" she said. "You must be cold without any berries to eat." Blue chirped sadly in agreement. "Don't worry," said Lily, "I'll help you get the berries." She picked up the basket and held it up high. Blue flew up and plucked a berry from the basket. "Yum!" he chirped happily.

"Would you like some berries too?" asked Lily. "Yes, please!" said Blue. Together, they shared the berries and became the best of friends. From that day on, Blue knew that whenever he needed help, Lily would be there to lend a hand. And they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a nice temple. People would visit the temple to raise their hands in prayer. Everyone was very happy when they visited the temple.

One day, an old man named Willy went to visit the temple. He was so happy when he was there, he raised his hands in the air and smiled.

After a while, Willy decided to stay at the temple. He could hear the people saying nice things and it made him feel so content.

So, every day Willy would go to the temple and raise his hands in prayer. He would stay there until the sun went down. Willy always felt peaceful inside the temple, it made him feel so nice.

The end.

Once there was a little boy who had a pretty red wagon. He liked to take it everywhere he went and feel the wind on his face as it pulled him along. One day, the little boy was having a wild adventure and his wagon rolled further away from him than it ever had before. He called out, but the little wagon had gone too far. The little boy was so sad. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find it. He had lost his wagon!

For days, the little boy searched and asked around but without luck. He was so upset he couldn't enjoy the wild outdoor adventures anymore.

One day, he was walking along a street and he heard something strange - it was the sound of his little red wagon! The little boy raced towards the sound and there, to his surprise and delight, was his wagon! He was so happy he had found his wagon. He hugged it tightly and never let it out of his sight again.

Once there was an elderly man who loved sailing. He had an old, yellow sailboat that he took out every weekend. One day, he sailed out and the weather was perfect. But then the wind started to pick up, and his sailboat was no match for the storm. The elderly man had to repair it before he could sail back home.

So he took out some tools and started to patch up the holes in the sail. He worked all day, putting pieces of cloth together and mending the sail. Finally, by the time night fell, the sailboat was ready again.

The elderly man was so happy to have repaired his sailboat, and he was ready to head back home. He leapt into the boat and along with the wind, he sailed back home. The elderly man was so grateful that he could again sail his beloved sailboat.

Once upon a time, there were two little brothers, Mark and Tom. Every day, Mark and Tom played together happily. One day, Mark wanted to mix a special potion. He asked Tom to help him. But Tom was worried about the potion, so he said no.

Mark was sad, but he still wanted to mix the potion. So he decided to go ahead and mix it all by himself. He took some water, some leaves and a few other things.

The potion smelled strong and strange. Suddenly, a bright light surrounded Mark and the room. When the light disappeared, Mark had vanished!

Tom was so scared that he ran away. He looked for an exit and managed to escape.

The moral of this story is that one should be thoughtful and think before doing something. Just because something is fun or exciting doesn't mean it's a good idea. Sometimes it brings bad consequences.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside, especially on cold days. He would run around and jump in the leaves, feeling the wind on his face.

One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big, warm coat to wear. It was so cozy! Timmy put it on and ran outside to play. He felt so warm and happy.

But as the sun started to go down, Timmy began to shiver. He was so cold! That's when he remembered the uniform his dad wore when he went to work. It was warm and thick, just like his coat. Timmy wished he had a uniform too.

The next day, Timmy's mom surprised him with a uniform of his own. It was a humble uniform, but Timmy didn't care. He was so happy to have something warm to wear on cold days. From that day on, Timmy wore his uniform whenever he played outside, and he never shivered again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. She was three years old and each day she liked to explore the world around her. 

One day Mia found a special switch in her garden. She was so fascinated! She wanted to know what this switch did so she decided to press it. 

The switch made a funny noise and suddenly water poured from the sky! Mia was so excited - it was like a blessing from the heavens! She knew she could use the water to make her garden grow. She sent a grateful thank you up to the sky. 

Mia ran around in the rain, laughing and splashing around until she was soaked. Then she went inside and played some games while the water stopped pouring. 

Mia was so happy. She had discovered something wonderful with the help of her special switch!

Harry the little boy wanted to climb the mountain. So, he asked his mom to join him. 
First, they took a big, long walk. Harry saw the big green mountain. Then, it started to rain and the ground got wet. But Harry wanted to keep going.

So, they bravely climbed the mountain. The path was slippery and wet. Harry was a bit scared, but he was brave. He kept going.

At the top of the mountain, they had the best view! They could see for miles and miles. The rain had stopped and the sky was bright blue. Harry was so happy!

Mom and Harry joined hands. They danced on the top of the mountain, under the blue sky. It was the best adventure!

Once there was a little girl called Lola who loved to joke around. She was always laughing and making jokes, and her friends loved it. One day Lola was at school and had to wear a uniform. Her teacher was very strict, and she thought he had a harsh look on his face.

Lola wanted to make him smile, so she decided to tell him a joke. She waited until the teacher was in a good mood, and then she said the joke. But the teacher didn't laugh. Lola was sad, and knew that her joke wasn't funny.

But then something amazing happened. Her teacher smiled and laughed, and Lola was so happy. Everyone was laughing and having a good time. Lola was proud of herself for making the teacher laugh and for making everyone else happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a big green bull. He lived in a nice field with many green trees. The green bull had a lot of animal friends. They would play together all day long.

One day, the green bull wanted to talk to his friends. He walked up to a small cat and said, "Hello, cat! Let's talk and play together." The cat was happy and they talked and played all day.

The green bull and the cat had so much fun talking and playing. They became the best of friends. From that day on, the green bull always talked to his friends, and they all had a great time together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She had a big, red ball and a brilliant blue glove. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends.

Sally saw her friend Tim and said, "Let's play catch with my ball and glove!" Tim agreed, and they started to play. But then, Sally's ball went too far and got stuck in a tree. Sally and Tim paused and looked at the tree, thinking about how to get the ball back.

A tall man saw them and asked, "Do you need help?" Tim said, "Yes, please! Our ball is stuck." The man used a long stick to get the ball out of the tree. Sally and Tim thanked the man and went back to playing.

The moral of the story is to always ask for help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there lived a small, fearful mouse in a cozy little house. One night, the mouse saw something glowing through the window. It was so bright and warm. It made the mouse feel curious and brave.

The mouse opened the window and saw a cocoa tree full of bright, twinkling lights. He crept closer and saw the lights were stars. The mouse was amazed!

Suddenly, he heard a kind voice call out to him, "Do you want to come and play with me?" The mouse thought it was the stars speaking. He was afraid, but also wanted to play. He said, "Yes!"

The mouse hopped out the window and the stars twinkled brighter. The mouse knew he was safe and wanted to stay with the stars forever. He welcomed their warm glow and the sweet smell of cocoa in the air.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and liked playing with her toys.

One day, Lucy found a white box in her garden. She was curious and opened it. Inside was a beautiful, peaceful bird. It was so calm and gentle. Lucy got to understand that the bird wanted her to take care of it.

Lucy said, "Hello, Birdy! Can I play with you?"

The bird nodded and said, "Yes, you can play with me. I will be your friend."

Lucy was so happy and excited. She took the bird inside her house and fed it. From that day on, Lucy and Birdy were best friends. They would play together in the garden and always have fun. 

Lucy understood that Birdy was the best friend she could ever have.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved being outdoors. She loved learning about all of the different plants and animals and especially playing in the summer sunshine.

One day, she went out for a walk and spotted a peach tree. She was so excited to see all of the peaches growing on it.

Without hesitation, she ran up to the tree and looked around. She spotted a little peach at the very top, so she decided to see if she could reach it.

She stretched her arms up, but she just couldn't get it. Feeling discouraged, she walked away.

Just then, an kind old voice spoke to the girl. "Why don't you ask the peach if you can have it?"

The little girl was surprised. She turned around to see an old lady smiling at her.

The girl thought for a minute and then asked the peach if it was ok for her to take it.

To her surprise, the peach said yes!

The little girl was so excited. She quickly plucked the peach off the tree, thanked the kind old lady, and ran home with her little peach.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Spot found a smelly old sock in the yard. He liked the sock very much and played with it all day.

As the days went by, Spot noticed that the sock began to become even more smelly. He didn't care because he still loved to play with it. Spot's friends, the cat and the bird, didn't like the smelly sock. They told him to throw it away, but Spot didn't want to.

A whole year went by, and the sock was now very, very smelly. Spot's friends could not play with him anymore because of the smell. Spot felt sad and lonely. One day, he decided to throw the smelly sock away. His friends were happy, and they all played together again. From that day on, Spot never played with smelly things again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who wanted to go on an adventure. They all wanted to go rafting so they searched around for a cheap raft.

Finally, they found exactly what they were looking for. It was a big raft, and it was very cheap.

The family was so excited and stopped work early that day to prepare for the adventure. On the day of the adventure, the family finished packing early, got the raft ready and jumped into it.

The family sailed their raft for hours and hours, enjoying the beautiful scenery and singing together. Suddenly, the raft hit a big rock and the raft began to leak. 

The family tried their best to repair the raft but it was too late. The raft started to sink and the family had to get out. 

The father said sadly, "We won't be able to finish our adventure today". The mother cried, "Our cheap raft ruined our trip!" The family was very disappointed and had to go home.

Tom and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. They saw a big truck with a ladder and a hose. It was red and shiny. They heard a loud noise.

"What is that?" Mia asked.

"It is a fire truck," Tom said. "They help when there is fire."

They ran to the truck and saw some men in yellow suits. They had helmets and boots. They looked busy and strong.

"Hello, kids," one of the men said. "Do you like our truck?"

"Yes, it is very nice," Tom said.

"Can we see inside?" Mia asked.

"Sure, but be careful," the man said. "It is not a toy. It is a tool."

He lifted them up and showed them the seats, the buttons and the radio. Tom and Mia were amazed. They saw a lot of things they did not recognize.

"What is this?" Tom pointed to a metal box.

"That is a fire extinguisher," the man said. "It sprays foam to put out small fires."

"And what is this?" Mia pointed to a shiny thing.

"That is a spark plug," the man said. "It makes a spark to start the engine."

The man explained more things to them. Tom and Mia learned a lot. They thanked the man and got down.

"That was fun," Mia said.

"Yes, it was," Tom said. "But it must be difficult to be a fireman."

They waved goodbye to the men and the truck. They went back to their game. They pretended to be firemen and put out fires with their water bottles. They had a great day.

Once there was a very cute cat. It was always very quiet and never caused any trouble. But one day the Cat had an idea. It wanted to go for a march!

The Cat asked its best friend, Dog, to come along. But Dog disagreed.

"I don't think it's very smart to go for a march," Dog said.

But the Cat was determined and said, "Oh come on! It will be fun! Please come with me!"

Finally, Dog couldn't resist any longer and agreed to join the Cat on the march. They set off on their adventure, and it was even more fun than the Cat had imagined. They marched around the neighborhood, meowing and barking all the way.

From then on, Lily loved to draw pictures of all the weird birds she saw.

Mom and Dad were in the kitchen discussing something. Mom said, "Today is a special day. We have a surprise for you!" John was a little three-year-old and he was excited. He asked, "What surprise?" 

Mom smiled and said, "We're going to the store to pick a prize for you!" Dad said, "Let's go now. If we hurry, we can get there before it closes."

John clapped his hands and jumped up and down. He said, "Can we buy a toy?" Mom said, "Of course we can! You can pick an old or new one, whatever you like!" 

John couldn't believe it. He ran out the door, shouting, "Let's go! I want my prize!" He was so thrilled by the surprise that he forgot to put on his shoes. But Mom and Dad just laughed and chased after him.

Tom is a curious cat. He likes to explore new places and find new things. One day, he sees a big box in the living room. He wonders what is inside. He jumps on the box and sniffs it. He hears a soft sound. He scratches the box and makes a hole. He peeks inside.

He sees a small ball of fur. It is a puppy. The puppy is scared and shakes. Tom feels sorry for the puppy. He says, "Hello, little fur. I am Tom. Do not be afraid. I am your friend." The puppy looks at Tom and wags his tail. He says, "Hello, Tom. I am Max. I am glad you are my friend. I was lonely in the box."

Tom and Max become friends. They play together and share their toys. They cuddle and nap together. They hope to stay together forever. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a helpless king. One day, he wanted to go for a drive. So, he got into his car and drove to the park. He parked his car in the park, then he got out and looked around. He saw some flowers and trees. He saw some children playing, and he waved to them. The children waved back to the king and smiled. The king was so happy to see all the happy faces. He had a great time in the park, and then he drove back home in his car. The end.

Anna and Ben were playing outside in the sun. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw a big bush with red flowers. They wanted to smell the flowers and touch them.

"Let's go to the bush, Ben!" Anna said.

"OK, Anna!" Ben said.

They ran to the bush and bent down to smell the flowers. They smelled sweet and nice. They smiled and reached out to touch the flowers.

But the bush was not nice. It had sharp thorns that hurt their fingers. They cried out and pulled back their hands. They saw blood on their fingers and felt pain.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Anna said.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben said.

They were sad and scared. They wanted to go home and get a hug and a band-aid. They looked for their mom and dad, but they did not see them. They were alone in the park.

Then they heard a loud noise. It was thunder. They looked up and saw dark clouds. They felt drops of water on their faces. It was rain.

The rain was cold and wet. It made them shiver and sneeze. It made their clothes and hair and shoes wet. It made their wounds sting and burn. It made them more sad and scared.

They wanted the rain to stop. They wanted the sun to come back. They wanted their mom and dad to come and get them. They wanted the bush to go away.

But the rain did not stop. The sun did not come back. Their mom and dad did not come and get them. The bush did not go away.

They were stuck in the park with the rain and the bush and the pain. They were not grateful. They were unhappy. They wished they never went to the bush. They wished they never played outside. They wished they stayed home. They wished they listened to their mom and dad.

The end.

Jack was very tired. He had played all day with his friends and wanted to go to sleep. He was in the living room in front of the fan, so it would be cool when he went to bed. He sat down and looked at the fan, his eyes drooping. Suddenly, he let out a big yawn.

The fan continued to spin, and Jack watched it. He was very curious, as he had never seen a fan before. He wondered how fast it moved and if it liked being in the room.

As he watched, Jack's brother came in the room. He had a big smile on his face. His brother was very competitive and he loved to win. He said that he wanted to have a race with the fan.

Jack thought this was a great idea! He was so excited that he almost forgot to yawn again. He watched as they both prepared to race. When they were ready, his brother said, "Go!" and they chased each other around the living room.

The fan was very fast, but Jack's brother was able to beat it. When he was finished, Jack was very proud of him. They both laughed and agreed to race again tomorrow. Jack yawned one last time before finally going to sleep.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little hut. In this hut, a man would sell incredible things. People from all over would come to see what he had.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the hut. He wanted to buy something incredible for his mom's birthday. The man showed Tim many things, but Tim wanted something very special.

Finally, the man showed Tim a beautiful flower that would never die. Tim knew this was the perfect gift for his mom. He bought the flower and gave it to his mom. She loved it and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a smart little bird called Tilly. One day Tilly was flying over a green hill when she saw a little bunny hopping around. She flew down to get a closer look at the bunny and noticed that it was looking sad.

Tilly asked the bunny, â€œWhy are you so sad?â€

The bunny replied, â€œIâ€™m trying to get to the top of the hill but itâ€™s too steep and Iâ€™m too small.â€

Tilly thought for a moment and then had a suggestion. â€œI think I have a way for you to get to the top. Hop on my back and I will fly you to the top.â€

The bunny happily hopped on Tilly's back. Tilly flew up to the top of the hill, and the bunny hopped off her back. The bunny thanked Tilly for her help and said goodbye.

Tilly smiled and flew off, feeling proud of herself for helping the bunny with her smart suggestion.

Once upon a time there was a modern cone. It was an amazing cone, for it could stay wherever it wanted! At first, it stayed at the playground with the other kids. It was great fun to play with them.

One day, the cone decided to stay somewhere else. So it went off to explore the world. Everywhere it went it saw lots of exciting things. So many places to stay and explore!

Soon it was getting late, so the cone decided it was time to stay in one place for the night. It found a comfortable spot at the top of a hill and settled down for the night. In no time, it was fast asleep. 

In the morning the cone awoke, feeling rested and happy. It waved goodbye to the hill and set off again to explore the world. 

The modern cone has been on its adventurous journey ever since. It loves seeing the new places it can stay in, and can always find somewhere comfortable to get a good night's sleep!

Once there was a brave bunny who always wanted to hop higher and higher. He hopped over a large log and kept on going until he came to a tall, green hill. The bunny felt an urge to reach the top of the hill, so he hopped as fast as he could. He hopped, and hopped, and hopped some more until he reached the very peak of the hill. Then his hopped ever so slowly back down the hill until he reached the bottom. He had done it! He felt so proud and happy at what he had achieved. He knew that if he set his mind to it, he could do anything. He hopped off again into the distance, ready for his next adventure.

Once upon a time there was a mighty cold mountain in the middle of a quiet forest. Every morning the birds would sing and the sun would shine bright.

One day, a curious little boy decided to climb the mountain to see what was on the other side. He packed some sandwiches and a bottle of water and began his journey.

As he climbed higher and higher, the air became colder and colder. But the little boy kept on walking.

Finally, he reached the top and looked on the other side of the mountain. What he saw amazed him - it was a paradise full of wondrous things!

The little boy smiled and admired the view. Then he remembered that he had left his bag at the bottom of the mountain, so he quickly climbed down to grab it before setting off to explore the magical land. He was sure he was going to have a mighty cold adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She loved to bake with her mom. One day, they decided to make toast together. Jane was very excited.

Jane and her mom took the bread and put it in the oven. They waited and waited. The toast was ready, and Jane took it out of the oven. The toast was a little bitter, but Jane didn't mind.

Jane shared the toast with her friends. They all liked it, even though it was bitter. They all had fun eating the toast and playing together. Jane was happy she baked with her mom.

Dave was a creative three-year-old boy who was always on the move. One day, he went to his dad's office. He looked around and noticed all the interesting things in the room. He started to roll around the office, having fun exploring the big room. Then he rolled to the big desk and saw a jar of pens and paper. He started to roll the pens around on the desk, feeling creative.

Suddenly, the door to the office opened and Dave's daddy shouted, "What are you doing?" Dave just looked scared. His dad said, "You must not roll here, this is my office now go to your room!" Dave started to cry and rolled to his bedroom.

That day, Dave felt horrible. He did something naughty and got in trouble. He realized he should not have rolled around the office.

One day, there was a yellow bull. He was very happy and running through the field. He turned around and around and around. Suddenly, he stopped and saw a big tree. He looked up, and he saw a bright yellow apple! He galloped to it, and tried to reach it. But it was too high. He turned around and around and around, looking for something to help him. He saw a big rock and turned it over. He smiled - there was a yellow ladder under the rock! He climbed the ladder and grabbed the apple. He was so happy!  He turned back to ground and ate his yummy yellow apple. Then he trotted away into the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, she found a bird with a broken wing. Lily felt sad for the bird and wanted to help it. She took the bird home and gave it some water and seeds to eat.

Her nosy neighbor, Mrs. Brown, saw Lily taking care of the bird and asked what was going on. Lily told her about the bird's broken wing and how she was trying to help it. Mrs. Brown said that Lily was very kind and that she should be careful not to spoil the bird too much.

Lily didn't understand what Mrs. Brown meant by "spoil", but she knew that she wanted to help the bird. She decided to write a word on a piece of paper that said "get well soon" and put it next to the bird's cage. The bird chirped happily when it saw the word and Lily knew that she had done something good.

Once upon a time, there was a big ball. It was red and round like an apple. The ball could roll and bounce. One day, a little girl found the ball and she wanted to play with it. She rolled the ball down a hill and it went very fast. But yet, she caught it before it rolled away. 

The little girl was very happy to have the ball. She played with it every day. One day, a rich man saw the little girl playing with the ball. He wanted to buy the ball from her. But the little girl loved the ball too much to sell it. She said no to the rich man and kept playing with her ball. 

From that day on, the little girl was very happy to have her ball. She would roll it, bounce it, and play with it all day long. And yet, she never forgot how much she loved her ball.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Anna was playing in her garden. To her surprise, she found a large heavy fur. Anna didn't know what the furry thing was. She was excited, and wanted to pick it up and bring it inside.

But then she noticed something moving inside the fur. She knew that whatever it was, it didn't belong in her house. So she politely refused to take it with her.

Anna looked closer at the fur and noticed that two little eyes were looking at her. It was a tiny, baby fox!

Anna was scared and didn't want to hurt the baby. So she told him to go back home, and refused to take him inside.

The fox seemed sad, but he understood. He thanked Anna for being so kind and understanding and showed her his outstanding fur before he left.

Anna waved goodbye to the fox and thanked him for showing her his beautiful fur. She then went back inside, very happy and proud of herself for refusing to take the baby fox with her.

Once there was a gifted little boy. He loved to ride on his bike. One day, he rode to a park to explore.

The sun was shining and he could feel the breeze. As he rode, he heard a sound. It was a sweet, tinkling sound. He followed the sound and saw a pond.

The little boy was so excited. He saw that there were bugs and birds, swimming and flying all around. He raced around the pond, feeling free and happy.

The sound of the bugs and birds was music to his ears. He rode so fast, that he thought he could fly. He had a wonderful day, and soon went back home, full of joy.

Sandy was in the yard with her brother, Rain. He wanted to play a game, but Sandy wasn't sure.

â€œLetâ€™s play in the yard,â€ Rain said, â€œItâ€™ll be cool!â€

But Sandy disagreed. She wanted to go to the park.

â€œLetâ€™s go to the park. Itâ€™s more fun!â€ Sandy said.

Rain shook his head. â€œNo, the park is too far away. We can stay in the yard.â€

Sandy still disagreed. How could they be cool in the yard?

Then, a thought occurred to Sandy.

â€œLetâ€™s hide in the yard,â€ she said excitedly, â€œItâ€™ll be really cool!â€

Rain grinned and jumped up and down.

â€œYes! Letâ€™s hide!â€ He said. 

Sandy smiled. She was glad that she and Rain could agree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy guitar, but the string on it was broken. She asked her mommy to fix it, but mommy said she would have to do it herself.

Lily struggled to tie the string back together, but it kept coming undone. She was starting to get frustrated when her big brother came in and saw what she was doing. He asked if she needed help, and Lily said yes.

Together, they worked on the string and finally got it fixed. Lily was so happy and thanked her brother for his help. Her mommy saw what they had done and said it was a fair and kind thing to help each other out. The moral of the story is that sometimes we need help, and it's okay to ask for it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite skirt every day. It was a pretty pink skirt with sparkly stars on it. 

One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. Her friend Emily was wearing a beautiful skirt too. Lily felt jealous because Emily's skirt was even prettier than hers. 

"Your skirt is so pretty, Emily," Lily said. "I wish I had a skirt like that." 

Emily smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. Maybe we can trade skirts for a little while so we can both feel happy." 

Lily felt happy again and they traded skirts. They both felt happy and pretty in their new skirts. From that day on, Lily learned that sharing and kindness can make everyone feel good.

Once upon a time, there was a bad creature. He was always mean to the other creatures. But one day, something changed. A kind creature saw the bad creature and began to talk with him. She was so compassionate, and she offered him a cookie. He was very happy, and he decided to join her in playing with the other creatures. 

The other creatures were very surprised to see the bad creature playing with them. They were wary of him at first, but the kind creature showed them how to be compassionate too. Soon, they were all having fun together. The bad creature was so happy that he ate all the cookies!

The other creatures were happy to see the bad creature joining them. Every day, they all played together and the bad creature stopped being so mean. He had learned what it was like to be friendly, and he was happy to be a part of the group. 

Living with compassion made the creatures happy, and they all lived happily ever after!

Once there was a pink shape. It was a nice shape and it kept growing. Every day the shape increased.

One day, a boy saw the shape and tried to touch it. The shape got angry and said, "Don't touch me!" The boy was scared and ran.

The boy told his mom what had happened. His mom said, "Maybe you should have been more friendly. Even though the shape was scary, it didn't mean you had to be scared too."

The next day, the shape had increased even more. The boy was curious, so he decided to try again. This time, he said, "Hi. I'm very sorry for being scared yesterday. Can I look at you?"

But before the shape could reply, it started to grow bigger and bigger until it was too big for the boy to handle. He ran away, scared.

Moral: Be friendly even to those who appear scary.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toys. But they did not like to organize their toys when they were done. They left them all over the floor and made a big mess.

One day, their mom said, "Lily and Tom, you have to organize your toys before dinner. We are having turkey and you don't want to miss it."

"But mom, we don't want to organize our toys. We want to play more," Lily and Tom said.

Mom said, "If you don't organize your toys, you will not get any turkey. Turkey is yummy and good for you. And you have to be wise and listen to me."

Lily and Tom did not want to miss the turkey. They liked turkey very much. But they did not want to organize their toys either. They looked at each other and had an idea.

They decided to hide their toys under the bed and under the sofa. They thought mom would not see them and they could have turkey. They were very sneaky.

But mom was very wise too. She saw the toys under the bed and under the sofa. She said, "Lily and Tom, you did not organize your toys. You hid them. That is not nice. Now you have to organize your toys and say sorry. And you will not get any turkey until you do."

Lily and Tom felt bad. They realized they were not wise. They said sorry to mom and organized their toys. They hoped mom would still give them some turkey. They learned their lesson.

Jill was very excited. She was going to take a ride in a big car. She hopped in and Daddy started driving. 

The car was going very fast. She could feel the wind in her hair and she was smiling. 

Jill's Daddy made a turn and drove into a big office. He pulled up and stopped. 

"This is it," Daddy said. "Let's go in and say hello to your uncle."

Jill and her Daddy went into the office. Everyone was talking very loud and it was very noisy. She could see that her uncle didn't look very happy when he saw them. 

"Uncle Jack, it's been so long," said Daddy. 

Jack didn't answer. He just stared at them. Finally he said, "Jill, you can't stay here. You have to go home now." 

So Jill and her Daddy drove away. Jill was sad and disappointed. She cried all the way home. The ride home was not nearly as fun as the ride there.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a note on the ground. It was a pretty note with a big red heart on it. Tim was a nosy boy, so he wanted to know who the note was for. He asked his friend, Sue, "Do you know who this note is for?"

Sue said, "I don't know, but let's show it to our teacher, Miss Jane." They went to Miss Jane and showed her the note. Miss Jane smiled and said, "This note is for the new girl, Lily. She is shy and needs a friend."

Tim and Sue went to Lily and gave her the note. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you for giving me the note. I am happy to be your friend." They all played together and had lots of fun.

The moral of the story is: Being nosy can sometimes help you make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. He loved to play in the garden and eat carrots. One day, Benny saw a carrot that was too high for him to reach. He tried to jump, but he couldn't get it.

Then, Benny saw a piece of string on the ground. He had an idea! He tied one end of the string to the carrot and the other end to a stick. He pulled the stick and the carrot came down. Benny was so happy and ate the carrot.

Later that day, Benny saw a playful squirrel. The squirrel wanted to play with Benny, but Benny was too busy eating carrots. The next day, Benny saw the playful squirrel again. This time, Benny put down his carrots and played with the squirrel. They had so much fun together! From that day on, Benny and the playful squirrel were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play in the mud and roll around in the dirt. He was a very happy dog, but sometimes he would get very dirty.

One day, Spot was playing outside and found a big pile of mud. He jumped in the mud and rolled around, getting very smelly. Then, Spot went back to the house to show his family how much fun he had. But when he got home, his family did not like the smell.

Spot's family told him that he needed to take a bath. Spot did not like baths, but he knew he had to get clean. He felt regret for getting so smelly. Spot took a bath and was clean again. From that day on, Spot tried to stay clean and not get too smelly.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jimmy. He was very hungry and he wanted to eat something tasty. He looked around him and he saw some powder. He poked it and it felt strange. Suddenly, the powder started to rise up into the air! It floated around Jimmy, like a magical cloud. He laughed and laughed as it twirled around him. 

Jimmy was curious and he put out his hand to touch the powder. It felt a little bit like snow or cotton candy. Jimmy smiled and he wished he could taste it. As the powder fell back down to the ground, Jimmy felt a rumbling in his tummy. His tummy was still hungry! 

Jimmy looked around him and he saw a basket in the corner. Inside was full of delicious treats. He was so excited! He reached in and grabbed a big handful of treats. He quickly ate them up and he smiled. Now he was very full and no longer hungry! 

Jimmy thanked the magical powder for giving him the treats. He lay down in the grass and he fell asleep with a smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a wild potato who wanted to get married. He searched everywhere, but he couldn't find a partner.
One day, he found a lonely bird who could be the perfect partner. The potato asked the bird, "Will you marry me?" The bird said yes and they were married.

After the wedding, the bird and the potato would go for walks and have fun together. They would jump in puddles and play in the grass. Sometimes, they would fool around in the garden and get very messy.

The bird and potato were very happy together. They would tell each other jokes and dance around the garden like wild things. Every day, they became closer and felt more and more love for each other.

The bird and potato were married for a long time and all of their friends and family were happy for them. They lived happily ever after, still as wild and happy as ever before.

Lily and Ben like to play with their toys in the living room. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books and more. But sometimes they make a big mess and Mom is not happy.

One day, Mom says, "Lily and Ben, you need to organize your toys. Put them in the boxes and on the shelves. Then you can have a snack."

Lily and Ben nod and start to organize their toys. Lily puts the dolls in a pink box and the books on a shelf. Ben puts the cars in a blue box and the blocks on another shelf. They work hard and fast.

But then they see an orange chair in the corner. It is a new chair that Mom bought for them. It is soft and cozy and has a picture of a lion on it.

"Wow, look at the orange chair!" Lily says. "It is so pretty and fun!"

"Can we sit on it?" Ben asks.

"Sure, let's try it!" Lily says.

They run to the orange chair and climb on it. They hug the lion and giggle. They forget about organizing their toys.

Mom comes back and sees the orange chair. She also sees the toys on the floor.

"Lily and Ben, what are you doing?" Mom asks. "You did not organize your toys. You only played on the orange chair."

Lily and Ben look at Mom. They feel sorry.

"We are sorry, Mom," Lily says. "We like the orange chair so much. It is our favorite toy."

Mom smiles. She understands. She likes the orange chair too.

"It is okay, Lily and Ben," Mom says. "The orange chair is very nice. But you still need to organize your toys. How about we do it together? Then we can have a snack and sit on the orange chair."

Lily and Ben agree. They get off the orange chair and help Mom organize their toys. They put them in the boxes and on the shelves. They make the living room neat and tidy.

Then they have a snack and sit on the orange chair. They hug the lion and Mom. They are happy.

Once there was a girl who wanted a new thing. She saw a very expensive thing in a shop and she wanted it very much. But her mom said she needed to mind the money, and so the girl went home without it.

The girl was sad, but she found a new thing to play with. It was a pretty yellow ball, even though it was not as nice as the expensive thing. But the girl still liked it and began to play in the sun.

The girl's mom saw how happy she was and noticed how much she wanted the expensive thing. So the next day, the girl and her mom went back to the shop. The mom said they could buy the thing and they did!

The girl was so excited, and she hugged her mom to say thank you. The girl played with the thing all day long, and she was very pleased with the special present.

Once upon a time there was a blue spoon. It was special because it always made everyone laugh.

One day the spoon was feeling embarrassed. It was embarrassed because it had slipped out of someone's hand. Everyone on the table had watched it fall and laughed.

The spoon looked up and saw the kindest person at the table. He was the one who never laughed at the spoon. The spoon asked the kind man, "Why don't you laugh when I slip?"

The kind man smiled. He said softly, "I don't laugh at you. I laugh with you, because I'm happy when you're happy." 

The spoon felt happy and no longer embarrassed. He continued to bring joy to everyone around him and was never embarrassed again!

Once upon a time there was a small dog named Spot. Spot was a funny dog and he was always looking for something to do. 

One day Spot found a bone outside in the yard. He was so excited! He dug around it with his paws and tried to pull it out of the dirt.

But then Spot heard his owner's voice. "Spot! You need to leave that bone alone! It doesn't belong to you," his owner said in a loud, clear voice.

Spot was sad and disappointed. He wanted to keep the bone. But he knew he had to listen to his owner. "I need to put it back in the ground," Spot said to himself. 

So reluctantly, Spot put the bone back into the dirt. Even though it was hard, Spot knew he had to be a good dog and obey his owner.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. Her name was Emily. She liked popcorn. 
One day it was very cold outside, so icy! Emily decided to go for a walk. As she walked, she found some delicious popcorn! She was very happy! 
She picked up the popcorn from the icy ground. Then, Emily and the popcorn parted. She ate the popcorn as she continued to walk. 
She felt much warmer with the yummy popcorn in her tummy. She kept walking until she got home. 
Emily was very satisfied. Eating the popcorn made the cold and icy day much better!

Once upon a time, there was a small boy who liked to play in the garden. One day, he decided it was time to go on his first adventure. He packed his bag with lots of things he thought he may need. 

On the way, he had to climb a big hill. It was heavy, but he was determined and so he kept going. After a while, he made it to the top. The view was beautiful! He was so glad he had come on his adventure.

At the bottom of the hill, he stopped to take a break. He had a snack and thought about the things he had seen. He was so proud of himself. He knew everyone would have a different opinion, but he was sure he had a great adventure. 

The boy was ready to go home, so he packed up and started walking back down the hill. He was feeling tired, but happy that he had a wonderful day filled with many new experiences.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Betsy. Betsy loved to taste sweet things. Every day she had a new delicious task to do. She would try and find the most unique treats.

One day, she thought she had found the best taste yet. It was a red lollipop. She knew that it would be extra special. She took the lollipop and tasted it.

But the lollipop was not sweet at all, it was sour! Betsy was so shocked she almost started crying. She had wasted it all. She really wanted it to be sweet.

Sadly, she never found the special treat she was looking for and she had to go without that unique taste. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved playing with a special sack. It was big, brown and smooth. One day, she decided to go for a walk with her sack. 

When Sarah got to the park, her eyes lit up. She looked around and noticed that it was full of flowers, green grass and trees. She started to twirl around with her sack, then suddenly stopped and picked something up. 

It was a white bottle of milk. She opened the bottle and took a sip. It was delicious! Sarah was so happy that she started to dance around with her sack, smiling and laughing. 

After a while, a friendly neighbour saw Sarah and walked over to her.
"What have you got in your smooth sack, Sarah?" asked the neighbour. Sarah grinned and said, "Milk!" Her neighbour smiled and both of them started to laugh. 

Sarah hugged her sack tight and said, "I love my sack, it's full of milk and fun!" 

The End.

Tim and Kim like to play in the garden. They have a big jar with a lid. They catch bugs and put them in the jar. They want to see how big the bugs are.

One day, they find a cricket in the grass. It is green and brown and has long legs. It makes a loud noise with its wings. Tim and Kim are excited. They want to measure the cricket.

They put the cricket in the jar and close the lid. They get a ruler and a pencil. They draw a line on the jar with the pencil. They say, "This is how long the cricket is."

They look at the ruler. They see the numbers on the ruler. They try to count the numbers. They say, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. The cricket is seven long."

They are happy. They have measured the cricket. They open the lid and let the cricket go. The cricket jumps away and makes a loud noise. Tim and Kim say, "Bye, cricket. You are very noisy and very long."

Once upon a time there was a very stubborn little girl. Every day she would have lots of fun playing with her toys and her friends. But this day the little girl had something extra special in her sack. She hugged it tightly as she walked around her garden, looking around for a special place to keep it.

"I want to keep my mystery package safe and sound," she said.

Just then, her mum came around the corner. "What do you have in there?" she asked.

The little girl held on tightly to the sack and said, "It's a surprise, but I want to keep it here because it's special". 

Mum smiled and said, "Well if you're sure, I suppose it'll be OK to keep it here".

The little girl's face lit up. She found the perfect spot and put her sack down. "I won't let anyone take it," she said very firmly.

Mum laughed. "You can be very stubborn when you want to be, can't you?"

The little girl smiled proudly and said, "Yes I can. I'm going to keep my mystery package safe and sound".

And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a factory. It was full of people who were busy doing normal things. 
One day, a worker slipped on the floor. This made him scared so he quickly got up again.

He looked around to see if anyone had noticed. But everyone was still busy doing normal things, so no one had noticed the worker slip. 

The worker was very happy, so he decided to take a break. He went for a walk around the factory and stopped to have a snack. 

When he came back, he was more careful not to slip again. He made sure he was walking on the floor properly. 

And that is the story of the worker who slipped in the factory, but still managed to stay normal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a big piece of paper to decorate. Lily was so excited! She grabbed her crayons and started to draw. 

Suddenly, Lily's big brother, Jack, came into the room. "Wow, Lily! That's a really clever drawing!" he said. Lily smiled and continued to color. 

As Lily was finishing up her drawing, she looked out the window and saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky. "Look, Jack! A rainbow!" she exclaimed. Jack ran over to the window and saw the rainbow too. 

After Lily was done decorating her paper, she showed it to her mommy. "Wow, Lily! That's such a beautiful picture!" her mommy said. Lily felt so happy and proud of her clever artwork.

Once upon a time, there was a castle that belonged to a Compassionate King. The King was very kind and he loved to joke and make his people laugh. 

Every day, the King would make funny jokes as he walked around his castle. The people in the castle thought the King was very funny and they laughed and smiled when he joked. 

One day, the King found a special bucket filled with soap bubbles. He showed it to all of the people in the castle and they laughed and joked as they blew the bubbles. 

The King would often make jokes while they played with the bubbles. Even when they got tired the King would still joke and make them laugh. 

Soon, the King's castle was filled with happy faces and laughter. Everyone was happy and smiling because of the King's kind jokes.

Once upon a time, there was a big park with a tall statue in the middle. The statue was very pale and looked like a giant. Kids loved to play around it and take pictures with it. One day, a bird flew into the park and disturbed the statue. It flew around it and landed on its head. The kids giggled and pointed at the bird. The bird then flew away and the statue went back to being still and pale. The kids continued to play and have fun in the park.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. But sometimes they had a fight over who got to play with what. One day, they both wanted to play with the same train. They pulled and pushed and shouted at each other.

"Mine!" Lily said.

"No, mine!" Ben said.

They fought so hard that they broke the train. The wheels came off and the smokestack snapped. They both felt sad and sorry. They looked at the broken train and then at each other.

"Can we fix it?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Ben said.

They decided to try. They found some glue and tape and put the train back together. It was not perfect, but it was better than before. They smiled and hugged each other.

"Sorry for being spoiled," Lily said.

"Me too," Ben said.

They agreed to share the train and take turns. They played nicely and had fun. They learned that fighting was not good and fixing was better. They were happy twins.

Once upon a time, there was a little car who loved to drive. He was light and fast. He had a big test today. He wanted to show everyone how good he was at driving.

On the day of the test, the little car woke up early. He felt happy and ready. He drove to the test place. There were many other cars there. They all wanted to pass the test too.

The little car did his best in the test. He drove fast, but he was also safe. When the test was over, the little car was very proud. He passed the test and showed everyone how good he could drive.

Once upon a time, there was a big cow named Betsy. Betsy loved to eat grass and play with her friends in the meadow. One day, Betsy overheard some of the other cows teasing her about her big size. "You're as big as a house, Betsy!" they laughed.

Betsy felt sad and started to avoid her friends. She didn't want to be teased anymore. One day, a kind little girl named Lily came to visit the farm. Lily saw that Betsy was feeling down and asked her what was wrong. Betsy told Lily about the harsh words the other cows had said to her.

Lily knew just what to do. She brought Betsy some delicious beef from her family's farm and told her how special and strong she was. From that day on, Betsy felt better about herself and didn't let the teasing get to her anymore. She even made some new friends who liked her just the way she was.

Once upon a time, there was a green hospital. Inside, there was a small bunny. Every day, the bunny sat in the hospital and waited. He waited for someone to come and help him. But no one ever came. 

One day, something bad happened. A big badger appeared. He wanted to prevent the bunny from leaving the hospital. So, he put up a big wall so that the bunny couldn't get away. 

The bunny was sad. He wanted to get out of the hospital and find a better place to live. However, he couldn't do anything. He had to stay in the hospital forever. 

The bunny was very sad and he never got out of the hospital. No matter how hard he tried, the badger had prevented him from leaving.

Once there was a family who wanted to eat. The mommy said "I need to serve something fast!" Daddy said, "I know, how about chicken?" Mommy said, "That's a great idea!"

So Daddy went to the kitchen. He opened the refrigerator and took out the chicken. Then he cut it up so it would cook fast.

Mommy put the chicken in the oven and set the timer. She said, "It'll be ready soon!"

After a few minutes, the timer went "ding!" The chicken was ready! Daddy took it out and served it to the family.

Everybody ate the chicken so fast! They all said "Yummy!" They were so happy that Mommy and Daddy served them something so tasty and fast.

There was a girl who was feeling very uncomfortable. She was walking near a church and she saw some people who looked very happy. She wanted to feel happy too so she went inside the church.

An old man saw her and said hello. He came over to her and he asked her why she was feeling so uncomfortable. She quietly told him about her troubles. 

The old man offered her a hug and told her that everything was going to be okay. She felt very comforted and, soon, she was smiling and enjoying being inside the church. 

The old man was very kind and he stayed with her until she was feeling much better. The girl thanked him and said goodbye. 

The old man told her that she was always welcome in the church if she ever felt uncomfortable again. The girl was so grateful and she was happy to know she had somewhere to go if she needed comfort.

Tim and Sue like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but they want more. They see a big store with many toys in the window. They ask their mom to take them there.

Mom says no. She says they have enough toys, and they need to save money. She says they should play with their toys at home, and be happy and healthy. Tim and Sue are not happy. They are angry and sad.

One day, they sneak out of the house. They run to the store with the toys. They see a big sign that says "Sale". They think they can get many toys for cheap. They go inside the store.

They see many toys they like. They grab them and put them in a big bag. They do not pay for them. They think they are smart and lucky. They run out of the store with the bag.

But they are not smart and lucky. They are bad and foolish. A man sees them and shouts. He is the store owner. He is angry and sad. He runs after them and catches them. He calls the police. He says they are thieves. He says they have to go to jail.

Tim and Sue are scared and sorry. They cry and beg. They say they are sorry and they want to go home. They say they do not want the toys anymore. They say they want their mom.

But it is too late. The police come and take them away. They say they have to go to court. They say they have to learn a lesson. They say they have to pay for the toys and for the trouble.

Tim and Sue have no toys, no money, and no mom. They have increased their problems. They have decreased their happiness. They have hurt their health. They have a bad ending.

Tom and Anna went to the circus with their mom and dad. They saw many animals and people doing tricks. They liked the circus very much. But they did not like the clowns. The clowns had big noses, big shoes, and big smiles. They made loud noises and jokes. Tom and Anna thought the clowns were scary.

One clown saw Tom and Anna sitting in the front row. He decided to joke with them. He walked up to them and said, "Hello, little ones! Do you want to see a magic trick?" Tom and Anna shook their heads. They wanted the clown to go away. But the clown did not listen. He took out a big red balloon and blew it up. Then he twisted it into a shape of a dog. He said, "Look, it's a balloon dog! Do you like it?" Tom and Anna did not answer. They were afraid of the balloon dog.

The clown smiled and said, "Don't be scared. It's just a joke. Here, you can have it." He handed the balloon dog to Tom. Tom did not want to touch it. He was sure it would pop and make a loud noise. He tried to push it away. But the clown did not let go. He said, "Come on, take it. It's a gift." He pushed the balloon dog into Tom's hands. Tom felt the balloon dog squirm and squeak. He screamed and threw it away. The balloon dog flew into the air and landed on a big cage. The cage had a sign that said, "Danger! Lion!"

The lion inside the cage saw the balloon dog. He thought it was a real dog. He roared and jumped at it. He bit the balloon dog and popped it. The loud noise scared the lion. He roared again and shook the cage. The cage door opened and the lion ran out. He chased the clown who had made the balloon dog. The clown ran away, screaming. He dropped his big shoes and big nose. He looked very silly and scared.

Tom and Anna saw the lion and the clown. They were not scared anymore. They thought it was funny. They laughed and clapped. They learned that jokes can backfire and that clowns are not so scary after all. They enjoyed the rest of the circus. They also learned to be polite and say no thank you when they don't want something.

Once upon a time there was an oyster. The oyster was gray and it lived in the ocean. Every day the oyster moved around the ocean, looking for food. One day the oyster moved into a really sunny part of the ocean. The oyster loved the sunshine and it moved around in the sun, feeling happy and warm. Then suddenly, a big wave came and moved the oyster away. The wave moved the oyster to a different part of the ocean. The oyster was sad without the sun, but it kept on moving around and looking for food. The oyster kept moving until it finally found another sunny place to stay in. The oyster was so happy, and it moved around in the sunny part of the ocean, feeling wonderful. The End.

Once there was a yummy dog. He loved to run around the park and play fetch. One day he found a yummy bone in the grass. He happily picked it up and sunk his teeth into it. But then something happened. It started to rot. He quickly dropped it and ran away. 

The dog was so sad and wondered why the bone had rotted. He decided to go back and search for a new yummy bone. He found one and sniffed it to make sure it wasn't rotten. It smelled delicious. He ran around the park with it, enjoying every second. 

The dog was very happy when he finally reached home and showed his owners the bone. They both said "yummy" and gave the dog a pat on the head. He chewed and enjoyed his yummy bone until he fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big sister named Sarah who liked to tease him. One day, Timmy was playing with his toys when Sarah came in and took one of his favorite toys. She started to tease him and wouldn't give it back. Timmy felt sad and didn't know what to do.

He went to his mom and told her what happened. His mom talked to Sarah and told her that teasing wasn't nice. Sarah said sorry and gave Timmy back his toy. Timmy felt happy again. Later, they went outside to play. Timmy saw a big number 0 on a distant sign. He didn't know what it meant, but he thought it looked cool. Sarah explained that it meant "zero" and that it was a number that meant nothing. Timmy thought that was funny and they laughed together. The end.

Once upon a time there was a successful man. He loved to listen. He listened to the world around him and he heard many amazing things. One day he was listening to the birds in the sky and he heard their songs. 

The man held his head up high and closed his eyes. Then he heard something even more amazing. He heard the whole universe. Time seemed to stop and the man listened. He heard the sounds of creation and felt the energy of the universe.

The man had a successful journey that day. He was so amazed by the universe and all the countless wonders. He kept listening to the universe and his life changed for the better. 

The man shared his story with others, telling them to listen carefully and to appreciate the beauty of the universe. By doing this, he found success and happiness. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny rocks and pretty flowers. One day, she met a boy named Timmy who was carrying a big dictionary.

"What are you doing with that big book?" Lily asked.

"I'm trying to learn new words," Timmy replied.

Lily thought it was foolish to carry such a heavy book around, but she didn't say anything. As they walked, they saw a beautiful butterfly. Lily wanted to catch it, but she didn't know how.

"Maybe the dictionary can help us," Timmy suggested.

Lily looked up the word "butterfly" and found out how to catch it. She was so happy and grateful to have the dictionary. From that day on, Lily and Timmy became good friends and collected many more things together.

Once upon a time, there was a bear who was very upset. He didn't know what to do to feel better.

So, he decided to make some tea. He boiled the water and put a teabag in. Then, he poured the tea into a cup and stirred it.

The bear wanted to feel better, so he tried something else. He took some of the tea and rubbed it on his fur. It made him feel nice and warm.

After a while, the bear realised that the tea had made him feel better. He was no longer upset and could enjoy the rest of his day.
