Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new vest to wear. It was pink and had flowers on it. Lily loved it and wanted to wear it every day.

But one day, Lily's vest got smelly because she wore it for too long without washing it. Her mom taught her that it's important to wash clothes so they don't get smelly. From then on, Lily made sure to wash her vest and all her clothes regularly. And she continued to wear her pretty pink vest to the park with her friends. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Marge. Marge was 3 years old and very clever. She loved to learn.

Every day Marge mother would add new tasks for Marge to complete. One day, Marge's mother added a special task - an exam!

Marge was very excited. She studied hard for the exam and learnt lots of new and useful things.

On the day of the exam Marge was feeling a bit nervous. But she used all the useful things she had learnt and did very well in the exam.

Marge was very proud of herself and her mother was very proud too! Marge had done something very special that day - she had added an exam to her list of accomplishments!

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom. But one day, mom says they have to go home early. Sara and Ben are upset. They do not want to leave the park.

They see a big red bus. The bus is going to the zoo. Sara and Ben love the zoo. They want to see the animals. They have a plan. They run to the bus and get on. They do not tell mom. They escape.

Mom sees the bus leave. She is scared. She does not see Sara and Ben. She calls their names. She looks everywhere. She cries. She does not know what to do.

The bus arrives at the zoo. Sara and Ben are happy. They jump off the bus. They run to the cages. They see the lions, the monkeys, the elephants. They laugh and clap.

But the zoo is not safe. The animals are not friendly. They are hungry and angry. They roar and growl. They break the cages. They run out. They chase Sara and Ben.

Sara and Ben are scared. They scream. They try to run away. But they are too slow. The animals catch them. They bite them. They hurt them. Sara and Ben are sorry. They wish they had listened to mom. They wish they had stayed in the park. But it is too late. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two caterpillars. One was fast and the other was slow. The fast caterpillar always laughed at the slow caterpillar and said that it was no good. The slow caterpillar was very sad and full of hate. Then one day, a wise bug came and said to the fast caterpillar: "You must not hate the slow one like that. He may be slow, but he is still very useful. We must appreciate everyone!" The fast caterpillar realized that he was wrong and apologized to the slow one. He welcomed the slow caterpillar to work together with him and be friends. 

This story teaches us that we should not hate each other just because someone is different. We should all appreciate and help each other.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Adam. He wanted to go on an adventure. So, he got in his car and drove off. After a while, he came to a big rail track. He thought it looked like fun and decided to take a ride.

Adam saw a fast train coming down the track. He waved to the train driver and the driver waved back. Soon, the train slowed to a stop. Adam asked the driver, "Can I ride?"

The driver said, "Of course! Hop aboard and come along." 

Adam grinned, climbed onto the train, and they took off. The train flew past fields and forests, chugging and whistling as it went. Adam sang and clapped his hands as he watched the scenery. 

After a while, the train stopped. It was time for the driver to go home. Adam thanked the driver for the fun ride and hopped off. He waved to the driver as the train drove away, then wandered back to his car. 

That night, Adam told his mom all about his adventure. He said that he couldn't wait to return to the rail and take another fast ride.

Once upon a time, in a big, big forest, there was a small, small rabbit. The rabbit had a soft, soft voice. It was not tough. The rabbit liked to play with its friends. They jumped and ran all day long.

One day, the rabbit saw a big, big wolf. The wolf had a tough, tough voice. The rabbit was scared. It hid behind a tree. The wolf looked for the rabbit. It wanted to play, too.

The rabbit tried to run away. It was very fast. But the wolf was faster. The wolf caught the rabbit. The rabbit started to weep. Its soft, soft voice could not help it. The wolf did not want to play. The rabbit was gone.

Once upon a time, there lived a magic rabbit. The rabbit had a special box with a powerful secret inside. The rabbit wanted to share the secret but it needed to be unpacked first. So it hopped over to a 3 year old and said, "I need help!" 

The 3 year old was excited to help and so the two started to unpack the box. As they opened each flap, the 3 year old gasped in delight. Inside was a beautiful colourful garden with tiny butterflies, flowers and other amazing things.

The rabbit explained that this was magic and that it could be used to make wishes come true. The 3 year old couldn't believe it and they carefully unpacked even more of the box.

Eventually, the 3 year old found a special wand. It was so powerful that the 3 year old's wish came true as soon as they said it out loud. Of course, the 3 year old was super happy and thanked the rabbit for all of the magic! The rabbit hopped away, leaving the 3 year old with the secret of the powerful box.

Ben likes to play in the sand near the sea. He makes big castles and holes with his bucket and spade. Sometimes he sees fish and crabs in the water. He wants to see an octopus, but they are very shy and hide.

One day, he sees a big rock with a hole in it. He thinks maybe an octopus lives there. He gets his bucket and fills it with water. He brings it to the rock and pours it in the hole. He hopes the octopus will come out and say hello.

He waits and waits, but nothing happens. He is sad and thinks maybe the octopus is not home. He is about to go back to his castle, when he sees something move in the water. It is an octopus! It has eight long arms and a round head. It is purple and green and has spots. It looks at Ben with big eyes.

Ben is very happy and surprised. He says hello to the octopus and asks if it wants to play. The octopus nods and smiles. It is a clever octopus. It can make shapes and patterns with its arms. It can change its color and size. It can squirt water and make bubbles. Ben and the octopus have a lot of fun together.

They play until the sun goes down and the sea gets dark. Ben says goodbye to the octopus and thanks it for being his friend. The octopus says goodbye and thanks Ben for bringing water to its home. It waves with its arms and goes back to its hole. Ben goes back to his castle and tells his mom and dad about his new friend. They are proud of him for being brave and kind. Ben dreams of the octopus and hopes to see it again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were very cute. One day, they decided to climb a mountain. The mountain was so big and tall, they both got scared. But they wanted to try and fix it.

They worked together to find some stones and sticks to help them build up the mountain higher and higher. They worked hard and soon the mountain had lots of stones covering it.

The two friends were so proud of themselves for fixing the mountain. They looked at it and smiled. Now they could stand on the top of the mountain and look out over the world.

They were so happy they had fixed the mountain together and they hugged each other. They had lots of fun climbing and fixing the mountain. They never forgot their big adventure together!

Mia and Jack were best friends. They liked to do everything together. One day, Mia and Jack decided to spend the day in the park. It was an icy day, but they were excited to play.

They found a pile of junk by the pond, so they ran over to it. Mia and Jack started to look through it.

They found a toy boat and an old ball. They made a path of rocks across the pond and put the boat in it. They watched as the boat drifted away. Then they kicked the ball back and forth until they got tired.

Before they left, they decided to spend some time watching the ducks swim in the pond. It was so fun to watch the ducks and to see the icy water glisten in the sunlight.

Mia and Jack had such a great day, and were happy that they got to spend it together.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to climb the big hill and look at the view. They could see the trees, the flowers, the birds and the sky. They felt happy and free.

One day, they saw a new thing on the hill. It was a big, red slide. It looked fun and shiny. Anna and Ben wanted to try it. They ran to the slide and waited for their turn.

Anna went first. She climbed the ladder and sat on the slide. She looked down and saw how high she was. She felt scared and started to tremble. She wanted to go back, but there were other kids behind her. She closed her eyes and slid down.

Ben saw Anna slide down. He thought she looked brave and fast. He wanted to be like her. He climbed the ladder and sat on the slide. He looked down and saw how far he could go. He felt excited and smiled. He opened his eyes and slid down.

Anna and Ben met at the bottom of the slide. They hugged and laughed. They felt proud and happy. They liked the slide. It was a good fit for them. They decided to go again and again. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and chase butterflies. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly with tight wings fluttering around her garden. She ran after it, but it flew away.

Lily went inside to tell her mom about the butterfly. Her mom said, "Maybe the butterfly will come back tomorrow."

The next day, Lily went outside to play and saw the same butterfly again. This time, she tried to catch it, but it flew away again. She went inside to tell her mom, and her mom said, "Maybe the butterfly is playing a joke on you."

The next day, Lily went outside and saw the butterfly again. She remembered what her mom said about the butterfly playing a joke on her. So, she stood still and waited. The butterfly landed on her finger, and Lily laughed. She realized her mom was right, and the butterfly was just playing a joke on her. From that day on, Lily and the butterfly played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a kid named Joe. Joe was three years old and was very polite. One day, he wanted to open the cup he found on the ground. When he opened it, he saw something shiny inside. 

He took it out and asked his mummy, "What is this?"

Mummy looked at it and said, "It is a coin, Joe. It looks like a penny. You can keep it and show it to your friends."

Joe was so excited and thought, "This is great! Now I can buy some ice cream!" 

He quickly put the coin inside the cup, closed it and ran off to get his ice cream.

The End.

Tom and Mia like to play with their toy boats. They have a big tub of water in the garden, and they pretend it is the sea. They make waves with their hands, and they sail their boats across the water.

One day, they decide to make a port for their boats. They find some rocks and sticks, and they pile them up on one side of the tub. They leave a gap for their boats to go in and out. They are very proud of their port.

They take turns to pick a boat and sail it to the port. They make noises like horns and engines, and they say hello to each other. They have fun docking and undocking their boats.

But then, Tom picks a boat that is too big for the port. He tries to squeeze it in, but it gets stuck. He pushes and pulls, but it does not move. He gets angry and frustrated.

Mia tries to help him, but she slips on a wet rock. She falls into the water, and splashes Tom. They both get wet and cold. They start to cry.

Mum hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the mess and the tears, and she sighs. She picks them up and wraps them in towels. She takes them inside and gives them hot chocolate. She tells them to be careful and gentle with their toys.

Tom and Mia feel sorry and hug each other. They say they are sorry to Mum and to their boats. They also feel dizzy from the spinning water. They decide to rest and read a book. They promise to play nicely with their port tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went on an adventure with her best friend, Teddy the bear. They went on a walk in the forest, and Lily asked Teddy if he wanted to search for treasure.

Teddy was very intelligent and knew just where to look. They walked through the trees and over the rocks until they found a shiny diamond. Lily was so happy, and she thanked Teddy for being so smart. But then, they heard a loud noise coming from behind them.

It was a big, scary dragon! Teddy knew they had to run away fast. They ran and ran until they were safe at home. Lily hugged Teddy and said, "You're my hero, Teddy. You're so intelligent and you saved us from the dragon." Teddy smiled and hugged her back, happy to have helped his best friend.

Once upon a time, there was a big forest with many trees. A man went into the forest with his axe to cut down some trees. He swung his axe and chopped down many trees. But he accidentally hit a bird's nest and broke it. The baby birds fell out and got hurt. The man felt very bad and asked the mother bird to forgive him.

The mother bird was very angry at first, but she saw that the man was sorry. She decided to forgive him. The man was very happy and grateful. He promised to be more careful next time. He also realized that the forest was a great place and he should take care of it. So he stopped cutting down trees and started planting new ones. The forest became even greater than before.

Once upon a time, there was a toy. It was a perfect brick. Although it was small and plain, it was very special. Suddenly, a magical bird arrived in front of the brick. It waved its wings, and the brick began to move! It started to fly around the room.

When the tiny brick flew outside, it was amazed by the new world. Everything seemed so big and wonderful. The little brick wanted to explore a bit more and flew around the garden. Suddenly, the perfect little brick found a big red wall. And so it landed on it and stayed there.

The brick was so happy with its discovery that it decided to stay there forever. Its new home was the most perfect place in the world. From then on, the little brick was always happy whenever it arrived home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play golf with his dad. They would go to the park and use their clubs to hit the little ball. Timmy's club was thick and blue, and he liked it a lot.

One day, Timmy and his dad went to the park to play golf. They saw a rabbit hopping around on the grass. Timmy wanted to pet the rabbit, but his dad said no. "We can't use our clubs on the rabbit, it's not nice," said his dad.

Timmy was sad, but he understood. He knew it was important to be kind to animals. So, he put down his thick blue club and watched the rabbit hop away. Even though he didn't get to pet it, he still had fun playing golf with his dad. The end.

Lily liked to read books. She had many books on her bookshelf in her room. She liked to look at the pictures and make up stories in her head.

One day, she wanted to read a new book. She saw a big book on the top of the bookshelf. She wanted to get it, but it was too high for her. She got a chair and climbed on it. She reached for the book, but it was heavy and rough.

Her mom saw her and said, "Lily, be careful! That book is not for you. It is for grown-ups. It has hard words and no pictures. And it is too heavy for you. You might fall and hurt yourself. Come down from the chair and I will help you find a nice book for you."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She wanted the big book. She pulled it hard, but it did not move. She pulled harder, but then the bookshelf shook. The books started to fall. Lily was scared. She let go of the book and tried to get off the chair, but it was too late. The bookshelf tipped over and fell on her and the chair. Lily cried out loud.

Her mom ran to her and lifted the bookshelf off her. She hugged her and said, "Lily, are you okay? I told you to be careful. You should have listened to me. I was trying to warn you. You could have been hurt very badly. You are lucky you only have a few scratches. Next time, please do what I say. I love you and I want you to be safe."

Lily was sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I was wrong. I should have listened to you. You love me and you know what is best for me. I don't want the big book anymore. I want a nice book for me. Can you help me find one?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. I'm glad you are okay. Let's clean up this mess and then we can read a nice book together. How about this one? It has cute animals and fun rhymes. Do you like it?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, mom. I like it. Thank you for helping me. I love you, mom."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lily. Now let's read and have some fun."

Becky was going on a trip and took her suitcases out to pack her clothes. She was so excited! She packed her bed sheets and a towel. She heard a loud noise in the bathroom and went to check.

She opened the door to find her little brother, Ben, playing with the shower. He was pretending to take a shower but was really just splashing around.

Becky smiled and said, "Ben, why are you playing in the shower?"

Ben replied, "I'm deaf! I thought I heard thunder, but it was just the shower!"

Becky laughed and said, "No! That was just the shower. Come on, let's see if we can find you something else to play with." 

The two of then went off to look for some toys for Ben to play with. Becky had to finish packing but was happy that she got to spend a little bit of time with her brother.

Once there was a three year old boy who was very successful. Everywhere he went, people said he was the best! But while everyone else was impressed, the boy was not. He hated all the walks he had to do. People kept telling him to go out and explore, but the boy wanted to stay inside. 

One day, the boy finally decided he wanted to take a walk. He wanted to have an adventure. He walked and walked and walked, until he got to a big park. It looked so exciting! He ran around and had a lot of fun. But then, while the boy was jumping around, he tripped and he fell. 

The boy was so sad. He tried to get up, but he could not. He hated being hurt so badly. He cried and cried, and finally he started to make his way back home. With each step, he felt worse and worse.

The boy had his adventure, but it did not turn out to be very successful. He was so sad and tired when he got back home. He learned that life sometimes didnâ€™t turn out the way you hoped.

Once there was a little boy. He loved to drive his toy car. He would take it to the road every day. He loved to explore the mysterious road. 

One day something strange happened. He drove his car down the road and saw something in the distance. It was a big, mysterious house! He was so excited and drove closer. 

But as he got closer, the house started to look dark and scary. He was a little scared but he drove closer to find out more. Soon he was outside the house, looking around.

Everything was so mysterious. He wanted to find out more but he was too scared to go inside the house. He decided to drive away and tell his mommy and daddy all about the mysterious house. 

That was the end of his adventure but he never forgot the mysterious house he found on the road.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big stick on the ground. Anna likes the stick. She picks it up and says, "This is my stick. It is beautiful. It is brown and long and smooth."

Ben wants the stick too. He says, "No, it is my stick. Give it to me. I saw it first. It is beautiful. It is brown and long and smooth."

Anna and Ben start to pull the stick. They both demand the stick. They are not happy. They are angry and loud.

Mom hears them. She comes to them and says, "Stop, stop. What are you doing? Why are you fighting over a stick? There are many sticks in the park. You can share the stick or find another stick. Be nice to each other. You are friends."

Anna and Ben listen to Mom. They feel sorry. They say, "Sorry, sorry. We are friends. We can share the stick or find another stick. We do not want to fight. We want to play."

Mom smiles. She says, "Good, good. I am proud of you. You are kind and smart. You can play with the stick or find another stick. But remember, the stick is not yours. It belongs to the park. You have to leave it here when we go home."

Anna and Ben nod. They say, "OK, OK. We understand. The stick is not ours. It belongs to the park. We will leave it here when we go home."

They hug Mom. They hug each other. They play with the stick or find another stick. They are happy. They are friends. The stick is beautiful. It is brown and long and smooth.

Once upon a time, there was a big, fancy house. It had a big, fancy window and a big, fancy door. 

One day, Johnny and his mommy were outside the house, admiring the window. Johnny's mommy said, "Johnny, how do you think we could reach the window?"

Johnny noticed a ladder, standing against the house. He pointed at it and said, "Look mommy, there's a ladder!" 

So Johnny's mommy got the ladder and Johnny helped her to stand it up against the house. Then, Johnny climbed the ladder all the way to the window. 

From the top of the ladder, Johnny could wave to all the people inside the house. Everyone in the house was so excited, especially when Johnny shouted out, "I can see you!" 

Johnny and his mommy had a lot of fun. The fancy window stood tall, and their smiles were even higher.

One day, a little chicken went for a walk. It saw a tidy house with a big door. The chicken wanted to go inside and see who lived there. It knocked on the door and a kind voice said, "Who is it?"

The chicken replied, "I am a little chicken. Can I come in?" The voice said, "Yes, come in, little chicken." The chicken went inside and saw a nice lady. The lady was very kind to the chicken and they became friends.

They played all day and had fun. The chicken helped the lady keep her house tidy. They picked up toys and put them away. The lady said, "Thank you, little chicken, for helping me keep my house tidy."

At the end of the day, the chicken said, "I have to go home now. Thank you for being my friend and letting me help you." The lady replied, "You are welcome, little chicken. You can come back anytime."

The moral of the story is that being helpful and kind can make new friends and bring happiness to others.

Once there was a boy who liked to keep tight snacks. One day, his mom said it was time to grill the snacks. So, the boy went outside and started up the grill. It was hot and the boy quickly kept the snacks inside. He put the lid down tight to keep the heat in and the snacks started to cook. 

He sat and watched them cook. When they were done, he took them off the grill and put them on a plate. They smelled so good and tasted even better! The boy enjoyed the tight snacks and thanked his mom for helping him make them.

Once upon a time, two dogs named Spike and Mutt were happily playing together in a park. All was nice and lively. Suddenly, they saw an old wreck at the corner of the park. They both wanted to explore it, but Spike wanted to go in first. Mutt was mad and argued with Spike. They kept arguing until the started to fight!

It was a very noisy fight with lots of barking and growling. Then, the dogs heard a loud noise. It was the same noise from the wreck. The doors of the wreck opened wide and a car drove out of it! 

The car came straight towards the dogs. They were so scared that they quickly stopped fighting and ran away. They ran as fast as they up a hill, until they got to safety.

Since that day, Spike and Mutt have never argued again. They still play together in the park and the old wreck sits there, to remind them of the day they almost got into a lively fight.

One day, a cheerful little girl called Lucy was looking through her microscope. All of a sudden, a big bug popped up and scared her! She screamed and jumped back. Lucy was so scared she ran to her mom. Her mom hugged her, and told her it was okay.

Then, Lucy remembered how much she liked looking through her microscope to find bugs. She felt brave and wanted to try again. So, she grabbed her microscope and looked through it.

This time, she saw a friendly ladybug! It was so small, she could barely see it through the microscope. Lucy smiled and told the ladybug hello. Soon, Lucy was looking at bugs through her microscope every day. 

She was never scared anymore!

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. Timmy loved pastries, especially the ones his mom made. One day, Timmy's mom made a big pastry that was too heavy for her to carry. So, Timmy decided to help his mom and carried the pastry to the kitchen table. Timmy was so strong and flexible that he didn't even drop the pastry! Timmy's mom was so proud of him and gave him a big hug. From that day on, Timmy knew he could always help his mom carry heavy things.

Once upon a time, there was a big river. A boy wanted to cross the river, but he didn't know how. He went to his friend and asked, "Can you help me cross the river?" His friend said, "Let's make a raft!"

They went to the forest and found a big tree. They cut the tree and made a big raft. The boy said, "Wow, this is a big raft!" His friend said, "Yes, it is. Now let's start crossing the river."

They got on the raft and started to paddle. The water was cold and the wind was strong, but they didn't give up. Finally, they reached the other side of the river. The boy said, "Thank you for helping me cross the river." His friend said, "No problem, we did it together!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who found a shiny coin while walking in the park. He was so excited to have found the coin that he ran home to tell his mum. He showed her the coin and it made her smile. 

The little boy thought he would use the coin to buy something special, so he put it in his pocket. He decided to go back to the park to surprise his mum with something special.

In the park, he found a harsh-looking man selling bright, colourful balloons. He thought they would be the perfect surprise for his mum. He bought the balloons with his coin and took them home. 

His mum was so surprised when she saw the balloons that she was speechless. The little boy had found the perfect surprise for his mum and the coin had made it all possible.

Lily and Max were eager to play in the attic. They liked to find old things and pretend they were treasures. They asked their mom if they could go up the stairs.

"Okay, but be careful and don't make a mess," mom said. "And come down for lunch soon."

Lily and Max nodded and ran up the stairs. They opened the door and saw a big box. They opened the box and found many clothes. They saw hats, coats, dresses, and shoes. They decided to try them on and play dress-up.

"I will become a princess," Lily said. She put on a pink dress and a shiny crown. She looked in a mirror and smiled.

"I will become a pirate," Max said. He put on a black coat and a hat with a feather. He found a wooden sword and a map. He looked in a mirror and made a scary face.

They played for a long time, pretending they were in a castle and a ship. They had fun and forgot about lunch. They heard mom calling them from downstairs.

"Lily, Max, come down, it's time to eat," mom said.

Lily and Max took off the clothes and put them back in the box. They closed the door and went down the stairs.

"Did you have fun in the attic?" mom asked.

"Yes, we did," Lily and Max said. "We became a princess and a pirate."

Mom smiled and gave them a hug. She was happy they used their imagination. She gave them a sandwich and a glass of milk. They ate and told her about their adventure. They were eager to play in the attic again.

Once there was a little girl who wanted a present for her birthday. She asked her mom for it but her mom said no. The little girl was embarrassed.

The girl waited a whole year and then her birthday came again. She asked her mom again and this time her mom said yes! The little girl was very happy and she got an awesome gift.

But it was too late. The present had rotted and it was ruined. The little girl was embarrassed that she had waited a whole year to get the present. She knew she should have asked her mom earlier!

Once upon a time, Sarah and Timmy went to the mall. They were so excited to see all the toys and candy in the stores. Sarah wanted a pink doll and Timmy wanted a blue truck. 

As they walked around, Timmy accidentally dropped his truck and it broke into two parts. He started to cry because he loved that truck so much. Sarah saw how sad he was and said, "Don't worry, we can ask the store worker if they have another one." 

The store worker was very nice and gave Timmy a new truck. It was a little rough around the edges, but Timmy didn't mind. He was so happy to have a new truck to play with. Sarah and Timmy left the mall with big smiles on their faces, happy to have each other and their new toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to collect stones. She had a big jar filled with all kinds of stones. One day, she found a very shiny new stone and she was very happy.

Lily showed the new stone to her friend, Tommy. "Look, Tommy! I found a new stone!" she said. "Wow, that's so cool!" Tommy replied.

But then, Lily accidentally dropped the new stone and it broke into many pieces. She was very sad and cried. "I wish I could change what happened," she said.

Tommy tried to make her feel better. "Don't worry, Lily. We can find more stones together," he said. But Lily didn't want to collect stones anymore. She went home feeling very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but one day he saw a missile in the sky. It made him feel scared and he ran inside to tell his mom. His mom explained to him that sometimes things can be scary, but it's important to stay calm and ask for help.

Later that day, it started to rain. Timmy loved the rain because he could splash in puddles and play with his umbrella. But the rain was also wild, and it made him think about the missile again. He remembered what his mom said and stayed calm.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to feel scared sometimes, but we should always ask for help and stay calm. And even when things seem wild, we can still enjoy the simple things like playing in the rain.

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their faces.

"Hello, doggy!" Lily says. "What is your name?"

The dog barks. He does not have a name. He is lost. He is hungry and cold.

"Can we help you, doggy?" Max asks. "Do you want to come with us?"

The dog nods. He follows Lily and Max to their home. They give him some water and some food. They share their meal with him. The dog is happy. He eats and drinks. He feels warm and full.

"Thank you, Lily and Max," the dog says. "You are very kind. Can I stay with you?"

Lily and Max look at each other. They smile. They like the dog. They want to keep him.

"Of course, you can stay with us," Lily says. "We will be your family. We will give you a name. How about Spot?"

The dog barks. He likes his name. He likes his new family. He gives Lily and Max a big kiss. They hug him and kiss him back.

They are all happy. They are all friends. They are all warm.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a big tree with fruit on it. The fruit was hidden behind the green leaves. Tim wanted to get the fruit, but he was too small to reach it.

He saw a tall girl named Lisa playing nearby. Tim asked her, "Can you help me get the fruit?" Lisa replied, "Yes, I will help you." She reached up high and got the fruit for Tim.

But then, a mean dog came and tried to take the fruit from Tim. Tim was scared and didn't know what to do. Lisa said, "Don't worry, I will help you." She picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. The dog ran away, and Tim was safe. Tim and Lisa shared the fruit and became good friends.

Molly was a polite cow who lived on a big ranch. Every evening she would follow the farmer around the ranch and help him with his work. Molly was a hard working cow and she was very proud of herself.

One evening the farmer was too busy to do his work, so Molly decided to spoil herself. She went off to the other side of the ranch and found a big patch of clover. Molly munched on the clover until it was all gone.

When Molly returned, the farmer was very surprised. He was happy that Molly had take the time to spoil herself and he gave her an extra special pat. From then on, Molly made sure to spoil herself once in a while.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Paul. He lived in a navy house with his mom and dad.

Paul really liked to play dress up. He had some fancy clothes and love to wear them. He also had a dusty-blue navy coat which he thought was very special.

One day, Paul went shopping with his mom. But he didn't know that she was buying a special present for him. It was a navy hat with sparkles that made it look very fancy.

When Paul saw the hat, he was so excited! He tried it on and it was perfect! He wanted to wear it every day and never take it off. So he kept it on for a whole week.

Sadly, one day he lost his navy hat. He was very sad and started to miss his fancy hat. But his mom found it in the park and gave it back to him - so he was very pleased.

Paul never lost his navy hat again and he still wears it every day when he goes outside to play. Every time he sees his hat, he smiles because he never wants to miss it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She had a very special job. Jane's job was to be a purple protector. She was responsible for keeping the world a pretty purple color.

One day, as Jane was walking along, she noticed something strange. There were buildings and houses turning grey! Jane was very worried.

Then, she had an idea. She smiled and nodded her head. She grabbed some big purple paint and started to paint the grey walls. 

Soon, everyone saw the colorful purple walls, and they cheered for Jane. Everyone was impressed by her special job, and they were very grateful.

Jane smiled and nodded her head again. Her job was done!

Once upon a time, there was a band. It was made up of three people who played music together. One day, the band made a plan. They wanted to help their friends. So the band started rocking together. 

Then, a friendly voice said, "Hey, I can help! I know a lot about music!" 
It was a 3 year old child. The band was excited to hear it and said, "Yes please! We would love your help!" 

The 3 year old child got to work. He showed them different music and instruments. He showed them how to rock even harder. Everyone was so surprised and happy with the 3 year old's help. 

After the band was done, they thanked the 3 year old for all his help. Everyone was very proud of what they had done together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to visit her grandma, who always made her feel welcome. Grandma had a big garden with lots of flowers and vegetables. Lily loved to help her grandma water the plants and pick the ripe tomatoes.

One day, Lily saw a butterfly fluttering around the flowers. She wanted to catch it, so she tried to pinch it with her fingers. But the butterfly flew away too fast. Lily felt embarrassed that she couldn't catch it.

Later, when it was time to go home, Lily gave her grandma a big hug and said thank you for a fun day. She couldn't wait to come back and help again.

Once upon a time there was a bright, sparkly girl. She loved to dance all around the garden. She would twirl and leap, her arms spinning in the air.

One night, she heard a noise coming from the rocks. She stopped to listen. It was a big, deep beat from a strange instrument.

The girl followed the sound until she came across a big, strong man. He had an axe in one hand and was singing and dancing and tapping his axe on the rocks.

The girl watched in awe as the man danced and played the axe. She loved the bright, happy sound that it made.

The man smiled and gestured for her to join him. She ran towards him and together they danced and played the axe under the bright, twinkling stars.

Rupert was feeling very nervous. He had to go to the doctors for an x-ray. Rupert had never had an x-ray before and he was scared.

The doctor took Rupert in the room for the x-ray.

"Close your eyes and count to ten," said the doctor. Rupert closed his eyes, started counting and the doctor took the x-ray.

After the x-ray, the doctor showed Rupert the picture of his body. It was an amazing sight!

The doctor put the x-ray in a sack and gave it to Rupert so he could take it home.

Rupert was happy that the x-ray was over and he could go home. He held the sack tightly all the way home.

One day, a little girl called Lucy went to the park with her mum. She saw a big, long rail and she was so excited. She said to her mum, "Can I pick the rail?" Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, sure you can".

So Lucy went to pick the rail. She was so happy and smiley. But then she got stuck. The rail was too big and heavy for little Lucy.

She was feeling helpless. She started to cry and said to her mum, "I can't pick it! Please help me!". Her mum came over and said, "Don't worry, it's ok". She showed Lucy how to get the rail up and soon enough, Lucy was able to pick it up.

Lucy was so proud of herself! She proudly showed her mum and shouted, "I picked it!". They both laughed and her mum said, "Yes you did! Well done".

Once upon a time there were two friends, Susan and Jack. Jack was very wealthy, he owned lots of toys and could do anything he wanted.

Susan on the other hand did not own very many possessions and needed to do a job to have money.

One day they went to the zoo, and while they were there Jack insisted on buying a toy for Susan. He wanted to show her that having lots of possessions did not make him any better than her.

The moral of the story is that having wealth does not guarantee happiness and it is more important to be generous with your money, and to share your wealth with others.

Anna and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together every day. They had many toys and dolls, but they also liked to dress up. They had a big box of clothes and hats and shoes.

One day, they wanted to dress up as princesses. They opened the box and looked for the prettiest clothes. Anna found a pink skirt with flowers. She put it on and said, "Look, I am a princess!"

Lily saw the skirt and said, "No, I want that skirt! It is mine!" She tried to take it from Anna.

Anna and Lily started to disagree. They pulled the skirt and shouted at each other. They were not happy.

Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw them fighting over the skirt. She said, "Stop, girls! Why are you disagreeing? You have many other clothes to choose from. You can share the skirt and take turns. Or you can find another skirt that you both like. That is what wise friends do."

Anna and Lily looked at their mom. They felt sorry for being mean to each other. They said, "Sorry, mom. Sorry, friend." They hugged and made up.

They decided to share the skirt and find another one that was purple and sparkly. They put on their skirts and crowns and said, "Look, we are princesses!"

They smiled and played happily. They were wise friends.

Lily loved to watch the veterinarian work. She liked to see how he helped the animals that were sick or hurt. He had many tools and medicines that he used to make them feel better. He was very kind and gentle with the animals, and they trusted him.

One day, Lily went to the veterinarian's office with her mom and her dog, Max. Max had a cut on his paw from playing in the park. He was limping and whining. Lily was worried about him. She hugged him and told him it would be okay.

The veterinarian came to see them and smiled. He said, "Hello, Lily. Hello, Max. What happened to your paw, buddy?" He looked at the cut and cleaned it with a soft cloth. He said, "This is not too bad. I just need to put a bandage on it and give you some medicine to prevent infection. You'll be fine in a few days."

He wrapped Max's paw with a white bandage and gave him a treat. He also gave Lily a sticker that said, "I'm a useful helper." He said, "Thank you, Lily, for being a useful helper. You helped Max by being calm and brave. You also helped me by watching and learning. Do you like to watch me work?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. I want to be a veterinarian when I grow up. I want to help animals like you do."

The veterinarian smiled and said, "That's wonderful, Lily. You have a good heart and a curious mind. I'm sure you'll be a great veterinarian someday. But for now, you can keep watching and asking questions. And don't forget to take good care of Max. He needs your love and attention."

Lily smiled and said, "I will. Thank you, veterinarian. You're the best."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Lily and Teddy went to the park to play. They went on the slide, the swings and the seesaw. They had so much fun!

Suddenly, Lily's friend came to the park. Her name was Sarah. She wanted to play with Lily and Teddy. But Lily got angry and didn't want to share Teddy with Sarah. Sarah tried to talk to Lily, but Lily didn't listen. She turned away and kept playing with Teddy.

Sarah felt sad and went away. Lily didn't care. She played with Teddy until it was time to go home. But when she got home, she realized that Teddy was gone. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find him. Lily was so sad and wished she had shared Teddy with Sarah.

Tom and Anna were brother and sister. They liked to play outside, but they did not like winter. Winter was cold and wet and gray. They wanted summer to come back, with sun and flowers and ice cream.

One day, their mom said, "Let's go to the park and have some fun. Winter can be fun too, if you accept it and look for the good things."

Tom and Anna did not want to go, but they followed their mom. At the park, they saw a big hill with snow. Their mom gave them a sled and said, "Try it, it's fun to slide down the hill."

Tom and Anna were scared, but they decided to try. They sat on the sled and pushed off. They went fast and felt the wind on their faces. They laughed and screamed and felt happy. They went up and down the hill many times, until they were tired and cold.

Their mom said, "Let's go home and have some hot chocolate. You did great, you accepted winter and had fun. Sometimes, you have to try new things and see the good in them."

Tom and Anna agreed. They hugged their mom and said, "Thank you, mom. You are right, winter can be fun too. We learned something new today."

The moral value of the story is: Accepting what you cannot change and finding the good in it can make you happier and wiser.

Once upon a time, there was a regular boy named Tim. Tim loved to eat blueberries. One day, he went to the park with his mom to pick some blueberries.

In the park, Tim saw a little girl named Sue. Sue was very sad and started to cry. Tim asked, "Why do you cry, Sue?"

Sue said, "I lost my blueberries and now I have none to eat." Tim wanted to help Sue, so he gave her some of his blueberries. Sue stopped crying and said, "Thank you, Tim!"

They both ate blueberries together and became good friends. Tim and Sue played at the park and had lots of fun. They went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys but he didn't have a hammer. One day, he saw his friend Billy playing with a hammer. Timmy asked, "Can I play with your hammer, Billy?" Billy said, "Sure, but be careful because it's very strong."

Timmy took the hammer and started to play with it. He hit the ground and the hammer bounced back. Timmy was surprised because he thought it would break. Billy said, "It's flexible, so it doesn't break easily." Timmy was happy to hear that.

After a while, Timmy said, "I think this hammer belongs to you, Billy. I should give it back." Billy smiled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. You're a good friend." Timmy was happy to have made a new friend and to have learned about flexible hammers. The end.

Mum was urging baby to come to dinner. Baby wanted to keep playing, but Mum said it was time. So, Baby reluctantly agreed and came to the dining table. 

When Baby arrived, there was a big plate of steaming food on the table. It smelled so good! But, Baby did not want to eat it because it looked too hot. Mum said she did not have to eat it, and went to fetch something else from the fridge. 

When Mum returned, she had a bright blue bowl in her hands. She gave it to Baby and said it was something special. Baby opened the bowl, and found it was filled with cold, sweet strawberries. Much better than the hot dinner! Baby was so happy and ate them all up. 

Mum was so pleased that Baby liked the strawberries and urged her to finish them. With a big smile, Baby eagerly ate the last one. Dinner was served and everyone enjoyed it.

Once upon a time there was a factory that made fake toys. The toys looked real, but they were not. One day a little girl named Jacky came to the factory. She saw a big box that was rolling around. Jacky opened the box, and there was an old rusty toy car inside! 

Jacky picked up the car with a big smile and said, "Cool!" She pushed the car around the factory, then decided to take it home.

On the way home, one of the tires of the car fell off. Jacky looked sad, and so she stopped at a store to buy another tire. She looked at all the tires, but none of them fit her toy car. 

But then, Jacky saw a tire that was shaped like a bubble! She asked the shopkeeper, "Is this tire real?" 

The shopkeeper smiled and said, "No, it's just a fake tire. But it will fit perfectly on your toy car! Take it home and have fun rolling around the house!" 

Jacky was so happy. She thanked the shopkeeper and took the fake tire home. She quickly put it on her toy car, and off she went rolling around the house!

Once upon a time, there was a big dog named Max. Max was very kind and liked to share his toys with other dogs. He was a generous dog. One day, Max heard some news on the TV. The news said that there was a lost puppy in the park. Max decided to go and look for the puppy. When he got to the park, he saw many dogs. They were all staring at him. Max didn't care. He just wanted to find the lost puppy. After a while, Max found the puppy and brought him back to his owner. The owner was very happy and gave Max a big hug. From that day on, Max became a hero in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to watch animals at the zoo. One day, he saw a big tiger with orange stripes. The tiger looked very strong and Timmy was scared, but also excited.

Timmy's mom was very rich and she bought him a toy tiger to play with at home. Timmy loved his toy tiger and played with it every day. He even slept with it at night.

But one night, Timmy left his toy tiger outside in the yard. A real tiger came and saw the toy tiger. The real tiger thought it was a real tiger too and attacked it. Timmy was very sad when he saw his toy tiger torn apart. He learned that it's not safe to leave toys outside and that real tigers are very dangerous.

Once upon a time, there was a patient neck living in a forest. This neck had a very big problem - it could not supply food for itself. 

The neck was feeling very sad and worried. But then, one day, three very kind fairies flew into the forest. They said they wanted to help supply food for the neck.

The fairies worked hard, and soon the neck had enough food. With a full stomach, the neck was very happy. 

The fairies were so thankful that they had helped the patient neck. They said goodbye and flew away - waving goodbye as they went. 

The neck was happy with its new food supply. It was content to stay in the forest, with enough food to last it a very long time.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful girl named Sue. Sue loved to play outside. She would run, jump, and swing on the swings.

One day, Sue saw a little bird. The bird had a hurt wing. Sue wanted to help the bird. She took the bird to her bed to keep it warm and safe.

Sue took care of the bird every day. She gave it food and water. Soon, the bird felt better. It could fly again! The bird was so happy. Sue felt happy too, because she was helpful.

It was time to celebrate! The family was so excited as they got on the subway. It felt like they were going to a distant place. As they went on the subway, everyone laughed and talked about all the fun they would have.

When they arrived at their destination, their eyes lit up. They saw a big park full of tall trees and colorful flowers. There were swings and slides everywhere and the kids were so excited. 

The family spent the day playing and laughing. They went on rides, ate cotton candy and built sandcastles. Everyone had a lot of fun and was so happy to spend quality time with each other. 

Towards the end of the day, the family gathered around for a group hug. They were so thankful for the special day and for the time they got to celebrate together. They smiled, hugged and laughed as the sun began to set in the distant sky. 

The family made so many memories that they would never forget. They said goodbye to the park and happily got back on the subway back home.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He was going to a new school. Tim was nervous. His mom said, "At school, you will meet new friends." 

One day, Tim saw a girl playing with tape. He wanted to play too. Tim walked to the girl and said, "Hi, I am Tim." He introduced himself. The girl said, "Hi, I am Sue. Let's play."

Tim and Sue played with the tape. They made a big ball. They had fun. Tim was not nervous anymore. He was happy. His mom was right.

Lila and her mom went to the park. Lila saw a big round thing that she could sit on and spin. She ran to it and climbed on. She asked her mom to push her.

"Mom, push me! Push me!" she said.

"Okay, Lila, but not too fast. You might get dizzy," her mom said.

Lila liked to spin. She felt the wind on her face and the sun on her hair. She laughed and waved her arms. She saw other kids playing on the swings and the slide. She wanted to play with them too.

"Mom, can I go play with them?" she asked.

"Sure, Lila, but be polite. Say hello and ask if you can join them," her mom said.

Lila nodded. She got off the round thing and ran to the swings. She saw a girl with curly hair and a blue dress. She smiled and said, "Hi, I'm Lila. Can I swing with you?"

The girl smiled back and said, "Hi, I'm Mia. Yes, you can swing with me. Do you want to go high?"

Lila nodded again. She sat on the swing next to Mia. Mia's mom pushed them both. They swung high and low. They had fun.

Lila's mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of her daughter. She was polite and friendly. She liked to spin and swing. She was happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a toy boat. He wanted to sail it in the water. Tim was very patient. He waited for his mom to help him. They went to the park with the boat.

In the park, there was a small pond. Tim put the boat in the water. It started to sail. But then, the boat got stuck in a lock. Tim was sad. He did not know how to get the boat out.

Tim's mom had an idea. She found a long stick. She used the stick to push the boat out of the lock. The boat started to sail again. Tim was happy. He knew that being patient helped him have fun with his boat.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play together. One day, they go to the church with their moms. The church is big and old. It is cold inside.

Lily and Tom sit on a bench. They see a man with a guitar. He sings a song. Lily likes the song. She claps her hands. Tom does not like the song. He covers his ears.

"Tom, why do you cover your ears?" Lily asks.

"I don't like the song. It is loud and boring," Tom says.

"But I like the song. It is nice and happy," Lily says.

They look at each other. They are not happy.

Lily has an idea. She has a candy in her pocket. She offers it to Tom.

"Tom, do you want a candy? It is sweet and yummy," Lily says.

Tom looks at the candy. He likes candy. He smiles.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend," Tom says.

He takes the candy. He shares it with Lily. They eat the candy. They are happy.

They listen to the song. They sing along. They have fun. Their moms are proud of them.

Once upon a time, there was a mouse named Bert. He was very clever, but he was still learning new things every day. One day, he came across a disgusting old piece of cheese. He had never seen cheese before, so he wanted to learn more about it.

Bert sniffed the cheese and then licked it. He quickly realized it was really nasty. He made a funny face and backed away. He knew he did not like the cheese at all!

After that, Bert continued to explore and he soon came across a pile of delicious looking crumbs. He quickly munched up the yummy crumbs and realized he had learned a new lesson about food. Now, he knew not to eat anything that looks disgusting!

Once upon a time, there was a small duck. He had a big sailboat. The duck loved to sail around the lake in his boat.

One day, the duck was out sailing when it started to rain. He quickly paddled back to shore, but the rain kept coming down.

The duck was so wet that he couldn't get the sailboat. Then he heard a voice. It was loud and friendly.

"Hey duck! I can help you, if you want", said the voice.

The duck looked around and saw an old man. He was deaf, so he shouted when he spoke. The old man had a big box of cream.

"I'm making ice cream with this cream. Would you like some?"

"Yes please!" said the duck.

So the old man scooped the creamy ice cream into a cone, and the duck ate it up. He was so happy!

Once the duck was full, the old man helped him put the sailboat back onto the lake. The old man waved goodbye as the duck began to sail away.

The duck sailed around the lake, feeling happy and free. He was so glad he had met the old man!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends went to a new place in the park. It was a big hill with a powerful tree at the top. 

Lily's friend, Emily, said, "Let's climb the hill and see the tree!" 

Lily was scared, but she didn't want to be left out. So, she climbed the hill with her friends. When they got to the top, they saw the powerful tree. 

But then, Lily slipped and fell down the hill. She suffered a big boo-boo on her leg and had to go to the hospital. She learned that it's important to listen to your feelings and not do things that scare you.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a lovely dress with many colors. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she noticed that her dress had a button missing. She regretted not checking her dress before leaving home.

Lily's friends tried to help her find the button, but they couldn't find it. Lily was sad because she loved her dress very much. Suddenly, her mom came to the park and saw that Lily was upset. She asked what was wrong and Lily told her about the missing button.

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can fix it together." They went home and found a new button that matched the other ones. Lily was happy again and regretted not checking her dress before leaving home. From that day on, she always checked her clothes before leaving the house.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly around in circles and play with his birdie friends. One day, Tweety saw a big, nosy cat watching him from afar. Tweety didn't like the cat because he looked scary and made his feathers tremble. 

Tweety's mommy warned him to stay away from the cat, but Tweety was curious. He flew closer and closer to the cat, thinking he could make friends with him. But the cat was not friendly. Suddenly, the cat pounced on Tweety and gobbled him up in one big bite. 

Tweety's friends searched for him, but he was nowhere to be found. They were sad and missed him very much. They realized that Tweety should have listened to his mommy and stayed away from the nosy cat. From that day on, Tweety's friends never flew too close to the cat and always remembered their friend who flew too close and lost his life.

Once there was a little boy called Tim. He loved playing with his toy recorder. He had it with him wherever he went. One day, he decided to go on a picnic with his parents. He saw a cloth on the floor and wondered what he could do with it. With a bit of help from his parents, he decided to record a message on his recorder. He spoke clearly and said, "Hello. This is Tim. I'm at a picnic with my family." He was so proud of himself when he heard his own voice recorded on the recorder. From then on, he carried around his recorder and the cloth everywhere he went. He had lots of fun creating new messages and recording them. The little cloth was his favourite toy now.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. Sophie was three years old. She was a very happy girl who loved to explore the world around her. One day, Sophie found an old newspaper in her garden. She was so excited and decided to take a closer look.

When she picked it up, the newspaper felt rough and harsh. She had never seen a newspaper before and didn't understand what it was. Although it felt strange, she was curious and wanted to explore it further. With each page that Sophie turned, she found something new and exciting. She felt amazed and proud of her discovery.

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew across the garden, and the newspaper flew away. Sophie felt a bit sad but still proud of her new discovery. She learned that a newspaper is filled with words and pictures. Sophie now knew more than she did before. She never forgot the harsh feeling of the newspaper as she held it in her hands.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to choose pretty things. One day, she saw a cane in the shop and it was smooth and sparkly. It looked so pretty that the little girl decided to choose the cane for her very own. She swirled and twirled with her new cane and showed her friends. Everyone loved the smooth cane and wanted one just like it. With her special cane, the little girl knew that she had made the best choice ever!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a tall tree. The tree had many pretty leaves. A little boy named Tom liked to play near the tree. One day, Tom saw a nice vest hanging on a branch of the tree. He wanted to wear the vest.

Tom tried to pick the vest from the tree, but it was too high. He asked his friend, Sam, to help him. Sam was taller than Tom, but he still could not reach the vest. They needed to think of a new way to get the vest.

Tom and Sam worked together to make a long stick. They used the stick to pick the vest from the tree. They were so happy! Tom and Sam learned that when they work together, they can do anything. This is the story of the tall tree, the pretty vest, and the two friends who learned to help each other.

Once there was a truck. He was very grumpy because he couldn't help anyone. Every day he drove around, just looking at all the people that he wanted to help, but he couldn't.

One day he stopped at a playground and he saw a little girl having trouble. The truck tried to help out but he was too big and it made the little girl scared.

The truck was so sad he almost started to cry. Then he heard someone say, "Don't be sad truck. I can help you."

The truck looked up and saw the little girl. Even though she was very small, she was determined to help. So the truck and the little girl figured out a way for the truck to help the playground.

The truck was so happy, he even forgot how grumpy he was before. The little girl said, "See truck, you can help people if you just try." 
The truck agreed and said, "Thank you for helping me help others."

The city was a peaceful place, with everyone content and happy. But then, something started to disturb the peace and harmony of the citizens lives. A selfish man moved into the city and thought only of himself, taking what he wanted without regard for others.

He stole food and hoarded money, wanting more and more. He was very greedy, and the people in the city didn't like it. The citizens tried to reason with him, and convince him to share, but he remained stubborn and selfish.

Finally, the people decided to take matters into their own hands. They formed a group and made a plan: each person in the group gave a little bit of what they had, then group together and confront the selfish man. 

Sure enough, it worked. The citizens bravely reminded him of the valuable lesson that if you give a little, everyone can be happy. The man was shamed by their wisdom, and soon enough, the city was peaceful again.

Mia was only 3, but she was very brave. One day, she was feeling really dizzy and didn't know what to do. Her mom saw her and said, "What's wrong Mia?" Mia pointed to her head and said, "I feel dizzy."

Her mom thought for a moment and then said, "I have just the thing to make you feel better." She went to the cabinet and came back with a little pill. Mia looked at it doubtfully. "What is this?" she asked.

"It's medicine," her mom explained. "But don't worry, it will make you feel better soon." Mia still wasn't sure, so her mom said, "You can try it just this once and see if it works. Then you'll know if medicine is something that can help you when you don't feel well."

Mia looked at the pill and then nodded. She took it from her mom and swallowed it down. And sure enough, after a few minutes she started to feel better!

Mia was glad that her mom had pointed her to medicine when she was feeling dizzy. From then on, she knew to always turn to medicine to help her feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to a big museum with her mommy and daddy. They saw many things like big dinosaurs and shiny rocks. 

Suddenly, Lily saw a boy who looked very frightened. He was scared of the big dinosaur. So, Lily went to him and said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" The boy said his name was Timmy. Lily introduced herself to Timmy and they became friends.

Lily showed Timmy around the museum and they had lots of fun. They saw paintings and sculptures and even a big whale! Timmy wasn't frightened anymore because he had a new friend to explore the museum with. They had a great time together and promised to come back to the museum again soon.

One day, the little girl wanted to go outside and play. She saw a high tree and wanted to climb it. She asked her mom to bring her closer to the tree. Mom brought her a ladder and she started to climb it. But not too long after, the little girl started to feel an itch on her foot. She looked down to see what it was and found that there were small ants on the ladder. She quickly asked her mom to bring her down. She ran around in the garden, playing and feeling happy. She was glad her mom had brought her the ladder to climb the high tree!

Tim and Sue like to play in the garden. They have a small house made of wood and a big tree with a swing. One day, they find a shiny thing under the tree. It is a knife. They do not know what it is for.

"Look, Sue, a shiny thing!" Tim says. He picks up the knife and holds it in his hand. He feels the edge. It is sharp. He cuts a leaf with it. "Wow, this is fun!" he says.

"Let me try, Tim!" Sue says. She wants to hold the knife too. She grabs it from Tim. But she is not careful. She cuts her finger with it. She cries. "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts!" she says.

Tim is scared. He sees blood on Sue's finger. He does not like blood. He drops the knife. He runs to the house. He calls for Mom. "Mom, Mom, Sue is hurt!" he says.

Mom comes out of the house. She sees Sue crying and holding her finger. She sees the knife on the ground. She is angry. She picks up the knife and puts it in her pocket. She takes Sue to the house. She washes her finger and puts a band-aid on it. She hugs her and says, "It's okay, Sue. It will get better soon. But you should never play with knives. They are dangerous. They can hurt you and others. Do you understand?"

Sue nods. She is sorry. She says, "I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't know. It was a shiny thing. It was interesting."

Mom says, "I know, Sue. But some things are not for children. They are for grown-ups. You have to be careful and listen to me. I love you, Sue."

Sue says, "I love you too, Mom."

Mom says, "Now, where did you find this knife? We have to return it to its owner. It does not belong to us."

Tim says, "We found it under the tree, Mom. Maybe it fell from the sky."

Mom says, "Maybe. Or maybe someone left it there by mistake. We have to find out. Come on, let's go and ask the neighbors. Maybe they know who it belongs to."

Tim and Sue follow Mom. They leave the garden. They go to the neighbors. They hope they can return the knife and say sorry. They hope they can find out why it is shiny and sharp. They hope they can learn something interesting.

Once upon a time there was a wise bear who was part of a team. 

One day the bear was walking around with his team when he saw something scary. He stopped and said to his team, "I see something that looks scary. What should we do?" 

The team huddled together and discussed how to handle the scary thing. After a few minutes, the wise bear stepped forward and said, "I think we should just run away - fast."

So the team ran away as fast as they could. They ran until they were far away from the scary thing. 

The wise bear was proud of the team. He reassured them that the scary thing was far away now, but to always be careful in the future. 

The team thanked the wise bear for his advice and continued on their way. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick berries. One day, she went to the forest to pick some berries. She saw a big bush with many red berries on it. They seemed so delicious!

Lily started to pick the berries, but soon she realized that she couldn't carry them all. She needed help! She shouted, "Can someone help me pick these berries?" Suddenly, a little squirrel appeared. "I can help you," said the squirrel. "I am very organized when it comes to picking berries."

The squirrel showed Lily how to pick the berries quickly and put them in a basket. They worked together and soon had a big basket full of juicy berries. "Thank you for helping me," said Lily. "You're welcome," said the squirrel. "It was fun picking berries with you!" From that day on, Lily and the squirrel were good friends and they often went berry picking together.

Once upon a time, there was a daddy and his daughter. They were going to the park. The daughter was very excited to play on the swing. "Daddy, are you ready to push me?" she asked. "Yes, I am ready," said the daddy.

The daughter played on the swing and counted how many times she went back and forth. "One, two, three," she counted. The daddy pushed her higher and higher. "Four, five, six," she counted.

Suddenly, the swing broke and the daughter fell off. She hurt herself badly. The daddy felt very sad and wished he had checked the swing before letting his daughter play on it. From that day on, he always made sure everything was safe before letting his daughter play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she pretended to be a doctor and her teddy bear was her patient. She checked his ear to make sure he was okay.

But then, she accidentally broke her mom's favorite vase while playing. Lily felt guilty and knew she had to tell her mom. She pretended that her teddy bear broke it, but her mom knew it was really Lily.

Lily learned that pretending can be fun, but it's important to always tell the truth and not feel guilty.

Once upon a time, there was a big building. It was very tall and had lots of windows. One day, a monster came and wanted to destroy the building. The monster was very mean and had big teeth. He hit the building with his big hands, but it was very strong and didn't break.

Then, the monster got an idea. He went to get some tools to destroy the building. He got a hammer and a saw. He hit the building with the hammer and cut it with the saw. But the building was very thick and didn't break.

Finally, the monster gave up and went away. The building was still there, standing tall and strong. The people who lived inside were very happy that their home was safe. They knew that their building was very strong and could not be destroyed.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty stable. The stable was home to lots of animals, like cows and chickens. Every day, the farmer would feed them and care for them. 

One day, the farmer had an idea. He wanted to see what would happen if he let them all out of the stable. So, he opened the doors and released all the animals. 

The cows ran and jumped in the fresh grass. The chickens clucked and flapped their wings. Everyone was so happy they were free! 

The farmer watched and smiled. He saw that the animals were content and safe. After a while, the farmer put them back in the pretty stable. But from then on, he released them from the stable every few days so they could get some fresh air and exercise. 

From then on, the animals were always happy and content. They loved being able to explore the big, wide world.

Lily liked to dance. She danced in the morning, in the afternoon, and in the night. She danced with her doll, with her cat, and with her mom. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the park. She was happy when she danced.

One day, she saw a new plant in the garden. It had green leaves and red flowers. It was very pretty. Lily wanted to dance with the plant. She ran to the plant and hugged it. She said, "Hello, plant. Do you want to dance with me?"

The plant did not say anything. It did not like to be hugged. It did not like to dance. It liked to stay still and grow. It was angry with Lily. It shook its leaves and dropped its flowers. It made Lily dirty. Lily was sad. She let go of the plant and cried.

Mom heard Lily cry. She came to the garden and saw what happened. She said, "Lily, why did you hug the plant? The plant does not like to be hugged. The plant likes to be watered and cared for. You made the plant unhappy and yourself dirty. You should say sorry to the plant and wash yourself."

Lily nodded. She said, "I'm sorry, plant. I did not know you did not like to dance. I wanted to be your friend. I will water you and care for you. I will not hug you again." She gave the plant a gentle pat and went to wash herself.

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good, Lily. You learned a lesson today. Not everyone likes to dance like you. You should respect their feelings and choices. You can still be friends with them, but you have to be kind and gentle. Then you will be happy and they will be happy too."

One day, a fast rabbit and a slow turtle wanted to have a race. They told all their friends, who were excited to watch. The rabbit was sure he would win, but the turtle was polite and said, "Good luck, rabbit!"

As the race started, the rabbit ran so fast that he was soon very far ahead of the turtle. The turtle kept going, slow and steady. The rabbit saw that he was winning, so he decided to pause and take a nap under a big tree. He thought he had plenty of time to rest and still win the race.

While the rabbit slept, the turtle kept moving. He passed the sleeping rabbit, but the rabbit did not wake up. The turtle reached the finish line, and all the animal friends cheered. The rabbit woke up and saw that the turtle had won. The rabbit learned that being polite and never giving up can lead to a big surprise.

One day, Mommy and Daddy went to the shop to buy some things. They left Anna and Ben at home with Grandma. Grandma said, "Be good, children. I will make some coffee and then we can play a game."

But Anna and Ben did not want to be good. They wanted to be naughty. They ran around the house and made a lot of noise. They knocked over a vase and broke it. They drew on the wall with crayons. They spilled juice on the sofa.

Grandma heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the mess and was very angry. She said, "What have you done, children? This is very naughty. You have to say sorry and help me clean up."

Anna and Ben felt bad. They said, "Sorry, Grandma. We were bored and wanted to have fun. We did not mean to make a mess."

Grandma said, "I understand, children. But you have to be careful and respectful. You can have fun without being naughty. Now, help me clean up and then we can have some coffee and cookies. And maybe we can play a game after that."

Anna and Ben nodded. They helped Grandma clean up the mess. They said, "Thank you, Grandma. We love you."

Grandma smiled. She said, "I love you too, children. You are good children. Sometimes you just seem to forget."

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very popular. Her name was Bella. She was always happy and friendly and everyone loved her.

One day, Bella was feeling a bit tired, so she decided to relax. She lay down on the couch and imagined she was at the beach. The warm sun was shining and she could feel the sand beneath her toes.

It was time for Bella to have a snack so she made a sandwich. It was yummy - it had her favorite fillings inside. She enjoyed it so much that she made another one!

After eating her sandwiches, Bella felt much better. She was relaxed and ready to carry on with her day.

Once upon a time, there was a messy garden. In the garden, there was a small boy named Tim and his friend, a talking rake. Tim and the talking rake loved to play together, but the garden was so messy that they could not have fun.

One day, Tim said to the talking rake, "Let's heal the messy garden and make it clean and pretty." The talking rake agreed and they started to work together. They picked up leaves and trash, and soon the garden was looking better.

But as they were working, a big wind came and blew all the leaves and trash back into the garden. Tim and the talking rake were sad. They tried to clean the garden again, but the wind kept making it messy. In the end, the garden stayed messy and Tim and the talking rake could not play happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She liked to follow her mom everywhere. One day, Lucy and her mom went to the park. They saw a big, scary dog. Lucy was scared.

"Mom, I am scared of the scary dog," Lucy said. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lucy. Just stay close to me and follow me."

Lucy and her mom walked away from the scary dog. They found a small cell on the ground. Inside the cell, there was a pretty butterfly. Lucy wanted to help the butterfly. She opened the cell and let the butterfly go free.

"Mom, I helped the butterfly!" Lucy said. Her mom smiled and said, "Good job, Lucy! You were very brave."

The moral of the story is to always follow your mom and be brave, even when you are scared.

Once there was a kitten named Tom. Tom loved to go on adventures. Today, he wanted to visit the forest. So, he went!

When Tom arrived in the forest, he met an old lion. The lion had big eyes. He was very bossy. 

Tom was scared. He didn't know what to do. 

The lion said, "What are you doing here?"

Tom said, "I wanted to explore the forest."

The lion replied, "You need oil for your journey." 

At first, Tom didn't know what the lion meant. But then the lion gave him a bottle of oil. 

Tom said, "Thank you very much!" He filled his pockets with the oil and went off to continue his adventure. 

Tom had a lot of fun exploring the forest with his oil. And he never forgot how kind the old lion was.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to climb trees. One day, Jack saw a big tree in the park and he wanted to climb it. But his mom said, "No, Jack. That tree is too tall and dangerous."

Jack was sad and went to play with his drum. He played his drum very gently, but he was still sad. Suddenly, he heard a little bird chirping. The bird said, "Jack, don't be sad. I can help you climb the tree."

Jack was surprised and asked, "How can you help me?"

The bird replied, "I can fly to the top of the tree and show you the way. But you have to promise to be gentle with the tree and not hurt it."

Jack promised and the bird flew to the top of the tree. Jack followed the bird's path and climbed safely to the top. From there, he saw a beautiful view of the park.

Jack learned that sometimes it's okay to take risks, but it's important to be gentle and respectful to nature.

Anna and Ben like to play in the kitchen. They pretend to cook and wash dishes. One day, they find a big green apple on the table. Anna wants to eat it, but Ben has an idea.

"Let's put the apple in the sink and see what happens," he says.

"Why?" Anna asks.

"Maybe it will float or sink or make bubbles," Ben says.

They fill the sink with water and drop the apple in. The apple sinks to the bottom. Anna and Ben are surprised.

"Look, the apple is under the water," Anna says.

"Maybe it is too heavy to float," Ben says.

They try to reach the apple with their hands, but the water is too deep. They look for a spoon or a fork, but they cannot find any.

"Mom, can you help us?" Anna calls.

Mom comes to the kitchen and sees the apple in the sink. She smiles and shakes her head.

"What are you doing, kids?" she asks.

"We wanted to see what the apple would do in the water," Ben says.

"Well, it looks like it remains in the sink," Mom says.

She drains the water and takes out the apple. She wipes it with a towel and cuts it into pieces.

"Here, you can share the apple now," she says.

Anna and Ben are happy. They thank Mom and eat the apple. They think it is very sweet and juicy. They decide to play with something else next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved playing with her rubber ball. She would bounce it up and down and all around. One day, Lily accidentally threw the ball too hard and it bounced into the neighbor's yard. 

Lily was worried because she knew her neighbor's dog was not delicate and might chew up her rubber ball. She asked her mom for help and they both went to the neighbor's house to ask for the ball back.

The neighbor was very kind and gave the ball back to Lily. She learned that it's always better to ask for help when you're worried about something. And also, she learned that it's important to take care of delicate things like her rubber ball.
