Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she saw her friend, Timmy, spraying water from a bottle. Lily asked, "Can I spray too?"

Timmy said, "Sure, let's spray the flowers!" They sprayed the flowers and had fun. Suddenly, they heard a bell ringing. It was time to go home. 

Lily's mom asked, "Did you have fun today, Lily?" Lily replied, "Yes, we sprayed the flowers and heard a bell." Her mom smiled and said, "I'm glad you had an organized playtime with your friends."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved rockets! He had a big collection of them in his room. But his room was very messy, and his mom told him he needed to clean it up.

Timmy didn't want to clean his room. He wanted to play with his rockets. So he told his mom, "I don't want to clean my room. I want to play with my rockets."

His mom said, "Timmy, it's important to keep your room clean. You can play with your rockets after you clean up."

Timmy thought about it and decided to collect all of his rockets and put them in a special box. Then he cleaned up his messy room. When he was finished, he felt proud of himself for doing a good job.

The moral of the story is that it's important to keep your things organized and clean. When you collect your things, it's easier to find them and you can enjoy them more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat pears. One day, she went to the market with her mommy and saw a big basket of pears. She was so happy and asked her mommy to buy some for her. Her mommy said yes and bought a big, juicy pear for her.

As Lily was eating her pear, she saw a man kneel down in front of her. He looked worried and asked her mommy for help. He lost his wallet and couldn't find it anywhere. Lily's mommy asked her if she saw anything and Lily said no, but she wanted to help the man. She asked him where he lost it and they all looked for it together.

After a while, they found the wallet and gave it back to the man. He was so happy and thanked them. Lily felt proud that she could help someone and finished her pear with a big smile on her face.

One cold morning, Mommy saw John. She offered him a present. It was a shiny new bicycle and it was all for him. John was very excited. He said â€œWhee!â€ The bicycle had two pedals. Mommy showed John how to put his feet on the pedals. Then he pushed down hard, and he was riding the bike! John felt like a big boy as he rode around. He went faster and faster and he laughed the whole time. Mommy was so proud of him. She hugged him and told him he was getting very good at riding his bike. John smiled and thanked Mommy. He loved his bike and he rode it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a nice girl called Kelly. She had lots of toys and she really liked to create things with them. One day, Kelly wanted to create something new and special. She searched everywhere for something special, until she found four colorful boxes.

Kelly knew that she had something special in those boxes, so she opened them and out came lots of different musical instruments! She was so excited and started playing around with all of the musical instruments. Then Kelly started to create some new musical noises and soon it sounded like a brand new kind of music.

Kelly smiled and called her music "jazz". She was so proud of her creations, and it sounded so cool. Everyone around her danced and sang along with Kelly's new creation. Everyone said that her jazz was the best and it made them so happy.

Kelly smiled and felt so proud that her jazz was liked by so many people. She looked around and saw how happy everyone was. Kelly knew that this day was one she would never forget.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He went for a walk in the woods and saw a snake. The snake was not moving, it was dead. Timmy felt sad for the snake and wanted to bury it.

He went to his mommy and requested her help. Together, they found a nice spot and dug a small hole. They put the snake inside and covered it with dirt. Timmy felt better knowing the snake had a proper resting place.

From that day on, Timmy always remembered to be kind to animals, even if they were scary like snakes. He knew they deserved respect, even if they were dead.

Once upon a time, there was a nice girl. Her name was Anna. One day, Anna decided to go exploring in the woods.

As she walked, it began to get very hot. She felt the heat from the sun on her back. Anna walked and walked until she found a special spot.

As Anna looked around the special spot, the ground began to move and shake and reveal an exciting surprise. It was a lovely pond that sparkled in the sunlight. Anna smiled and was happy to have found such a nice, special place.

Anna cooled off in the pond and had a fun time. She went back home feeling happy and refreshed. Anna was glad to have discovered her special spot!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She always wore a pink dress and loved to play with her dolls. One day, Lily was walking in the park with her mom when a stranger came up to them. The stranger had a friendly smile, but Lily's mom told her to be careful around strangers.

Later that day, Lily suggested to her mom that they have a tea party with her dolls. Her mom thought it was a great idea and they set up a little table with tea cups and cookies. They had so much fun together.

As the sun started to set, Lily's mom reminded her about the stranger they saw earlier. Lily nodded and said she remembered. She was glad she had her mom to keep her safe. Lily went to bed that night feeling happy and loved.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat something yummy. They saw a big jug on the table. It had milk inside.

"Can we have some milk, please?" Lily asked Mom.

"Sure, but you have to share," Mom said. She gave them two cups and a spoon. "You can also have some cereal if you like."

Lily and Tom poured some milk into their cups. They added some cereal and stirred it. They took a sip and smiled. It was sweet and crunchy.

"This is good!" Tom said.

"I like it too!" Lily said.

They ate their cereal and milk until their tummies were full. They felt comfortable and happy. They thanked Mom and gave her a hug.

"Can we play now?" Lily asked.

"Of course, but first you have to wash your cups and spoon," Mom said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They took their cups and spoon to the sink. They rinsed them with water and soap. They dried them with a towel. They put them back on the table.

"Good job, Lily and Tom!" Mom said. "You are very helpful and polite."

Lily and Tom smiled. They ran to their room to play with their toys. They had a fun day.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play in the farm. They had many animals to see and pet, but their favorite was Molly, the mule. Molly was very friendly and gentle, and she let the twins ride on her back sometimes.

One day, Sara and Tom saw a big basket of purple grapes in the barn. They loved grapes and wanted to eat some, but they knew they had to ask their mom first. They ran to the house to find her, but she was busy making lunch. "Mom, can we have some grapes?" they asked. "Not now, my dears," she said. "You can have some after lunch, but don't touch the basket. Those grapes are for the market."

Sara and Tom nodded and ran back to the barn. They wanted to play with Molly, but they also wanted to eat some grapes. They looked at the basket and saw how juicy and sweet the grapes looked. "Maybe we can have just one," Sara said. "Mom won't notice." Tom agreed and they reached for the basket. But Molly saw them and shook her head. She knew they were not supposed to touch the grapes. She made a loud noise and kicked the basket away. The grapes spilled all over the floor and some of them got squashed.

Sara and Tom were scared and angry. They thought Molly was mean and rude. They yelled at her and threw some grapes at her. Molly felt sad and hurt. She did not understand why they were mad at her. She only wanted to help them. She turned away and walked to the corner of the barn.

Soon, their mom came to the barn and saw the mess. She was very upset and asked what happened. Sara and Tom tried to lie and said Molly did it. But their mom did not believe them. She saw the grape juice on their hands and mouths. She knew they were the ones who touched the basket. She scolded them and told them to clean up the barn. She also told them they could not ride Molly for a week.

Sara and Tom felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had been wrong and unfair to Molly. They cried and said they were sorry to their mom and to Molly. They hugged Molly and gave her some carrots. Molly forgave them and licked their faces. She was happy to have them as friends again.

The moral of the story is: Don't be greedy and dishonest. Listen to your mom and respect your animals. They are your friends and they care for you.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went outside to play. He saw a tiny insect on the ground and wanted to pick it up. But the insect was scared and flew away. Timmy felt sad.

Suddenly, a big bee flew near Timmy. He was scared and started to cry. His mom came outside and saw him crying. She hugged him and said, "It's okay, Timmy. Let's go inside and calm down."

Timmy felt better and his mom let him watch his favorite cartoon. He forgot about the insect and the bee and was happy again. The end.

Clara and her mom were at the park. Clara was playing with her toys while Mom sat on a bench and watched.
"Look, Mom!" Clara said excitedly, pointing at a pile of yarn in the grass.
Mom smiled. "Oh, that's nice, Clara."
But then, Clara noticed an odd smell rising up from the yarn. She wrinkled her nose.
"It smells bad, Mom," she said.
"Yes, that's probably because it's been in the sun too long," Mom answered.
Clara kept thinking about the smelly yarn, so she let out a big yawn.
Mom looked over with a stern face. "Clara, no one wants to breathe in the smelly air from that yarn. Let's move away, okay?"
"Okay, Mom," Clara said.
So Clara and Mom went to a new spot in the park, far away from the smelly yarn. Clara happily started to play with her toys again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She went for a walk in the park with her mommy. As she went for a walk she saw some soil. The soil was dark and soft to the touch. She wanted to pick up some of the soil, but mommy said no. The little girl was embarrassed. 

Suddenly she saw a puppy. She squealed with joy and ran towards it. The puppy was chasing a ball, it was so much fun to watch! The puppy stopped and looked up at the little girl. The little girl smiled and the puppy jumped up and licked her face. The little girl giggled with joy.

The little girl and Mommy kept walking and saw some ducks swimming in a pond. They were so bright and beautiful. The little girl wanted to get closer, but Mommy said it was too dangerous. The little girl was embarrassed again. But she was still happy to have seen the ducks. 

The little girl and Mommy went home after a lovely walk in the park. The little girl went to bed, dreaming of the soil, puppy and ducks she had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who loved to hop. One day, he hopped to a big tree where all the animals were meeting. They were meeting to see who could hop the farthest.

The bunny was worried because he had never hopped in front of so many animals before. He saw a wise old owl sitting on a branch. The owl was the judge of the hopping game. The bunny asked the owl, "Can I hop too?"

The owl said, "Yes, little bunny, you can hop too." So, the bunny hopped as far as he could. All the animals clapped and cheered. The wise old owl, the judge, said, "You did a great job, little bunny! You hopped very far."

The bunny was very happy and not worried anymore. He knew that he could hop far and make new friends. From that day on, the bunny hopped and played with all the animals under the big tree. They all had lots of fun together.

Jack was a sleepy little boy. He yawned and stretched, ready for a nap.
Jack's mom called him to the living room. He saw a tall man wearing a funny hat.
"This is the doctor," said Mom.
Jack frowned. He didn't like doctors.
"Don't be scared," said the doctor with a fake smile. "I'm here to help you take a nap."
Jack relaxed a little. The doctor gave him a special medicine that tasted bubbly and sweet. Then Jack lay down and closed his eyes.

When he woke up, he felt happy and refreshed. The doctor had helped him take a good nap. From now on, Jack was never scared of the doctor again.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a big mill. He used to send his grains to the mill to make flour. The mill was very big and had a lot of stones inside. The farmer was very honest and always paid the miller on time. One day, the farmer sent his grains to the mill, but the miller was not there. So, the farmer waited patiently until the miller came back. When the miller arrived, he apologized for being late and promised to be more careful next time. The farmer was happy and thanked the miller for his honesty.

Once upon a time, there was a big guard dog named Max. Max lived in a small house with his best friend, a little girl named Lily. They loved to play together all day long. Max would run and jump, and Lily would laugh and clap her hands.

One day, they saw a pretty bird with green feathers sitting on a branch. Max and Lily were envious of the bird because it could fly high in the sky. They wished they could fly too. The bird saw them and flew down to say hello. "Hi, I'm Bella the bird," she said. "Would you like to play with me?"

Max, Lily, and Bella played together all day. They ran, jumped, and even tried to fly like Bella. They had so much fun, but soon they got very tired. Max, Lily, and Bella decided it was time to rest. They lay down under a big tree, and the soft grass felt nice. As they rested, Max, Lily, and Bella talked about their day and all the fun they had. They knew they would be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna.  Anna wanted to go on an adventure, so she searched around her house to find something to do. Suddenly, Anna spotted something outside that was very unusual. It was a big, red blob of ice! Anna was so excited! She had never seen anything like this before.

Anna ran outside to take a closer look. It was so bright and sparkly in the sun. She reached out her hand to touch it, and it felt cold and crunchy like snow.  Anna was so amazed that she began to search the ground to find more ice like it.

Anna eventually found two more big chunks of red ice scattered around her backyard. She was very excited and she couldn't wait to show her mom and dad. She carefully picked up the pieces and brought them inside. 

Anna's mom and dad were so surprised! They couldn't believe that she had found these in her backyard. They thanked her for her discovery and put the ice in the freezer so it could stay cold. 

Anna was very happy that she went on an adventure and found these special pieces of red ice. She vowed to go on more adventures and explore even more surprises in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was playing with her toys in the living room. She heard her parent talking in the kitchen. They seemed to be talking about something important. Lily wanted to know what they were saying, but she stayed and played with her toys.

One day, Lily found a cookie jar on the kitchen table. The cookie jar was full of yummy cookies. Lily's parent told her she could only have one cookie. But when her parent went to the other room, Lily took two cookies. She felt guilty for taking more than she was allowed.

Later that day, Lily's parent found out that there were fewer cookies in the jar than there should be. They looked at Lily and asked her if she took more than one cookie. Lily felt guilty and told the truth about taking two cookies. Her parent smiled and said it was okay, but she should always ask before taking more. Lily learned her lesson and always asked her parent before taking more cookies from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going on a trip to the beach. Timmy was very excited to play in the sand and water.

When they arrived at the beach, Timmy started to build a sandcastle. Suddenly, he noticed something strange. There was a mystery object buried in the sand. Timmy's mom told him not to touch it, but Timmy was too curious. He dug and dug until he uncovered a shiny treasure chest.

Inside the chest, Timmy found a note that said, "Beware of the tired pirate." Timmy didn't understand what it meant, but he knew it was important. Later that day, Timmy and his mom went for a swim. As they were playing in the water, Timmy saw a man in a pirate hat watching them from the shore. Timmy remembered the note and told his mom. They quickly went back to their hotel room, feeling safe and sound.

Once upon a time there was a new truck. It was very special. Every day something new and interesting happened with it.

One day, the truck was driving in the forest. All of a sudden, it heard a noise. It was coming from the bushes. The truck stopped to see what it was.

Suddenly, a bunny hopped out! The bunny was so excited to see the new truck. It hopped up and down, wanting to explore.

So, the truck invited the bunny to go for a ride. The bunny hopped right up and they drove away together.

The truck and bunny drove all around, having lots of fun. They were laughing and playing until they were too tired and had to go home.

The truck and bunny said goodbye. The new truck drove away and the bunny hopped away. What a fun day it had been for the new truck!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and have fun. One day, her mommy took her to the zoo to see the animals. Lily was so excited to see all the different animals. 

They saw lions, tigers, and bears. They even saw a rare bird with colorful feathers. Lily loved watching the animals, but she started to get hungry. Her mommy took out a sandwich and fed it to her. 

After she finished eating, they went to the playground where Lily had more fun. She went down the slide and played on the swings. She had such a great day at the zoo with her mommy.

Once upon a time there was a cat who loved to pretend. He had a great time pretending to be all sorts of animals, like a lion and a bunny. 

One day, the cat spotted a little three year old boy in the park and decided to have some fun. He pretended to be an elephant and started swaying about. The little boy was so surprised and amazed, he couldn't believe his eyes!

The little boy asked, â€œWhat are you doing?â€ The cat replied with a big smile on its face, â€œI am pretending to be an elephant!â€ 

The little boy smiled and asked, â€œCan I play with you?" The cat said, â€œOf course, letâ€™s pretend to be a great team of elephants together!â€ 

The two laughed and had a great time pretending to be two elephants. Every day they would meet in the park and explore their wild imaginations. 

The cat was so happy to have a friend and they were great friends ever since.

Once upon a time there was a crow who was different to all the others. His feathers were black and he was always hot. The other birds laughed at him and made fun of him.

The crow was so sad and he didn't want to fly around with the others. He just wanted someone to understand him.

One day he met a frog who was different to the others in the pond too. He was hotter than all the other frogs. The two of them were so happy to be together and they talked for hours. The crow finally felt he had someone to understand him.

The moral of this story is that in life we are all different but we can all get along if we just stick together and understand each other.

Once there was a little girl named Jen. She lived in a white house and she loved to play outside in summer. One day, Jen was walking in her garden when she saw something special in the sky. It was a bright, white lightning! 

Jen was so excited and wanted to own it. She ran inside the house and said to her mother, "Mommy, look at the beautiful lightning!" Her mom smiled and said, "Oh, you should go and catch it." 

Jen grabbed her snow boots and ran out in the garden. She jumped and hit the lightning with her hands. But it was too fast and too high for her to reach. Jen was so sad. 

But then a magical thing happened. Suddenly, from the sky, an icy lightning came down to Jen. She smiled and grabbed it with her little hands. Now she owned the icly lightning! 

Jen was so happy and jumped around with her new friend. She would keep the lightning with her forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry, so she went to a restaurant with her mommy. They sat down and a nice lady gave them a menu to choose from. 

Lily looked at the menu, but she didn't know what to choose. "Mommy, what's good?" she asked. "The spaghetti is very tasty," her mommy said. "I want spaghetti!" Lily said with a big smile.

After they finished eating, Lily's mommy said it was time to leave. "But I want to stay and eat more," Lily said. "We can't, we don't have enough money. The spaghetti was very rich," her mommy explained. Lily didn't understand why they had to leave, but she knew they had to go home.

Lila and Ben are playing in the farm. They see a big gray bull in the field. The bull has horns and a ring in his nose. He looks angry.

"Let's go closer and say hello to the bull," Ben says. He likes animals.

"No, Ben, that's not a good idea. The bull might hurt us. He is not friendly like the cows," Lila says. She is scared of the bull.

But Ben does not listen to Lila. He runs to the fence and climbs over it. He walks towards the bull. He wants to touch him.

"Ben, come back! You are in danger!" Lila shouts. She follows him and tries to pull him away.

The bull sees Ben and Lila. He snorts and lowers his head. He charges at them. He is very fast.

Lila and Ben are very afraid. They run back to the fence. But the bull is faster. He is almost on them.

Lila remembers what her dad told her. If a bull chases you, you have to kneel down and stay still. Maybe he will think you are a rock and leave you alone.

Lila kneels down and covers her head with her arms. She hopes the bull will not see her.

Ben sees Lila kneel down. He does not understand why she does that. He thinks she is giving up. He keeps running to the fence. He thinks he can make it.

But he is wrong. The bull catches up with him. He hits him with his horns. He tosses him in the air. He makes him fly.

Ben screams. He is hurt. He falls to the ground. He does not move.

Lila sees what happens to Ben. She cries. She is very sad. She wishes she could help him.

The bull sees Lila. He does not care about her. He thinks she is a rock. He walks away. He goes back to his grass.

Lila gets up. She runs to Ben. She hugs him. She calls for help.

Dad hears Lila's cries. He comes to the field. He sees Ben and Lila. He sees the bull. He understands what happened.

He is very angry at the bull. He is very worried about Ben. He is very proud of Lila.

He picks up Ben and carries him to the car. He takes him to the doctor. He hopes he will be okay.

He tells Lila she is very brave. She did the right thing. She saved her life.

He tells her he loves her. He hugs her. He takes her home.

He tells her they will never go near the bull again. He tells her the bull is very bad. He tells her he will find a new home for him.

Lila nods. She agrees. She does not like the bull. She likes Ben.

She hopes he will get better soon. She wants to play with him again. She loves him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress that she loved to wear. One day, Lily's mom told her it was time to get ready for a party. Lily tried to put on her dress, but it didn't fit. She was sad and said, "My dress doesn't fit, Mommy."

Her mom said, "Don't worry, we will find you a new dress." They went to the store and found a beautiful dress that was graceful and fit perfectly. Lily was so happy and said, "I love my new dress, Mommy!"

At the party, Lily was dancing and having fun when she accidentally bumped into her friend, Timmy. Timmy's lip started to bleed and he started to cry. Lily felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. Let me help you." She got a band-aid and put it on Timmy's lip. Timmy smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend."

Jimmy was a 3-year-old with a lot of energy. He always wanted to be doing something! One day, his mom took him to the beach to get some fresh air and cool down.

Jimmy was so excited to get out of the hot sun and into the colder water. But when he got there, he saw something terrible - it was a big cooler filled with fish!

Jimmy was so disgusted - why did it have to be there? So, he turned to his mom and said "Mommy, I hate that cooler!"

His mom smiled and said, "Why don't you go explore the beach and I'll be here if you need me."

So, Jimmy ran off to look at the interesting things. But no matter where he looked, he could see the terrible cooler. Eventually, he had to accept it. Then Jimmy had a great time at the beach playing in the waves and the sand. 

When it was time to leave, Jimmy said "Bye cooler!" and then he and his mom went home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. Anna was very excited to learn something new. She wanted to learn how to use a fork.

One day, her mommy showed her how to pick up the fork. Anna was so happy and she smiled brightly. She practiced picking up the fork while walking around the kitchen.

But then, something strange happened! Anna started to feel a bit dizzy, as if the room were spinning around her. She bent down and put her head on the table.

Anna's mommy was worried. She rubbed Anna's back, and gave her something to drink. Soon Anna felt better and she was finally able to pick up the fork again.

Anna was so proud of herself for learning how to use a fork! She had felt a bit dizzy, but was very happy she now knew how to do it. She was one step closer to being a big girl.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. One morning, Lucy asked her mom for a glass of tea. Her mom said yes, and kindly lent Lucy a cup for her tea.

Meanwhile, Lucy's older brother, Tom, was feeling very thirsty. He asked his mom for some tea too.
Tom's mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can have some tea. But you'll have to lend me your cup first".

Tom thought that it was a bad idea. He didn't want to share his cup with anyone. He wanted to keep it all to himself. But Tom's mum was very kind and he decided to lend his cup. 

So Lucy and Tom both had a nice, warm cup of tea. They both enjoyed it very much and thanked their mum for being so kind. 

And that's the story of how Lucy and Tom learnt to lend, drink tea and be kind to others!

Once upon a time, there was a little orange cat named Mimi. Mimi had a long tail that she loved to play with. One day, Mimi was walking in the park when she saw a little girl.

"Hello, little girl," said Mimi.

"Hi, kitty," said the little girl. "Your tail is so long!"

"Yes, it is," said Mimi. "Do you understand why cats have long tails?"

"No, why?" asked the little girl.

"Well," said Mimi, "we use our tails to help us balance when we climb and jump."

"Oh, I see," said the little girl. "Can I pet your tail?"

"Of course!" said Mimi, and the little girl gently petted her soft orange tail.

Lily loves to wear her cow dress. It is black and white, like a cow, and has a pink bow on the front. She thinks it is adorable. She wears it every day, even when it is hot or cold.

One day, Lily goes to the farm with her mom and dad. She sees many animals, like pigs, chickens, and horses. But her favorite is the cow. She runs to the fence and says hello to the cow.

"Moo!" says the cow. It looks at Lily and her dress. It thinks she is adorable too.

"Can I pet you?" asks Lily. She reaches out her hand and touches the cow's nose. It is soft and wet.

"Sure, you can pet me," says the cow. "You are very nice and friendly. And I like your dress. It looks like me."

"Thank you," says Lily. "You are very nice and friendly too. And I like your fur. It is black and white, like my dress."

Lily and the cow become friends. They talk and play for a long time. Lily is very happy. She loves her cow dress and her new friend.

Max was a dependable kid who loved to explore. One day, as he was walking in the park, he saw something shiny. Max was curious and he wanted to take a closer look, so he carefully walked over to it. 

It turned out to be a velvet pillow! It was so soft and was shining like gold! Max was excited and he quickly picked it up and hugged it close to his chest. He looked around but nobody was there to claim the pillow.

Max decided to take the pillow home with him. Every day he would cuddle with his pillow as he watched the sun rise, and he knew that he could always depend on it. Max was so happy to have a soft, shiny companion to share his days with. He smiled as he realized how lucky he was to find such an amazing velvet pillow!

Once upon a time there was a famous balloon. It was big, round and sparkly and it floated in the sky. Its beautiful colours made it stand out from all the other balloons.

One windy day, the balloon got caught in a tree. It couldn't free itself and was stuck.

"Oh no," thought the balloon. "What should I do?"

Just then, a little boy came by. He noticed the balloon and said, "Don't worry, I can help you!"

He went to his garden shed, and came back with a long cable. He grabbed hold of the balloon and carefully attached the cable to it.

"There," the boy said, "now you're free to fly again."

The balloon thanked the boy and floated away. He waved goodbye and watched the balloon go higher and higher until it disappeared into the clouds. The boy smiled as he knew that he'd made the famous balloon very happy.

Max wanted to find something to do. He looked all over the room and he saw something that made him smile. He saw a big, bouncy ball! He went over to it and he grabbed it, then he started to bounce it around all over the place. He bounced it on the floor, then he bounced it off of the walls and he bounced it even off the ceiling!

Max was so excited as he bounced around. Then he saw something else that made him smile even bigger. It was a delicious, sweet muffin! There was a plate full of muffins and they looked so delicious.

Max ran over to the plate and grabbed one of the muffins and started munching away. It was so good. He was so glad that the muffin was available for him.

After he finished his muffin, he started bouncing his ball around again. He was so happy that he had something fun to do. He kept bouncing and bouncing until it was time for him to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little animal. The animal was very frightened. It was lost in the big woods.

One day, it found a small house. Inside the house, there was a man who liked to fix things. The frightened animal went to the man for help.

The man saw the frightened animal and wanted to help. He gave the animal food and a warm place to sleep. The man also fixed a map to help the animal find its way home. The animal was no longer frightened and was very happy. They both became good friends.

There was a lazy Wednesday. On this Wednesday a small boy named John was feeling very sad. His pet frog had suffered a fall and was hurt. John had to take his frog to the vet.

John and his mommy drove to the vet in the car. On the way, John asked his mom about suffering. He wanted to know why his frog was suffering. Mommy told him that sometimes animals get hurt, but it usually doesn't hurt too much.

When they arrived at the vet, John was a bit scared. But his mom was there with him, so he didn't feel too scared. The vet checked his frog and said it would be okay.

John was so happy to hear this news. His frog didn't have to suffer anymore. From now on, John would be more careful with his pet frog. He learned an important lesson that day.

Tommy was terrible at sawing wood. Every time he tried to make something with saw, it never looked quite right. He wanted to improve his sawing skills. So he asked Papa to help.

Papa showed Tommy how to carefully hold the saw and make the right shapes. Tommy practiced every day, and soon he was sawing much better.

Tommy was so proud of himself for improving. He started to make lots of different things with his saw. He made wooden dolls and toys. He made little tables and chairs. All his friends and family said how much better his sawing had become.

When Tommy saw what he had created with his saw, he knew that  he had improved a lot. It made him feel really happy. He knew he had worked really hard and now everything he made with his saw looked great!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to run and play all day long. But when it was time for bed, he would get very restless. He would toss and turn and couldn't fall asleep. 

One night, Tim's mom came into his room and saw that he was still awake. She told him to try and rest and that she would be back soon. Tim tried to close his eyes and relax, but he couldn't stop thinking about all the fun things he did that day. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud snap! He looked down and saw that his sock had come off. He reached down to put it back on and felt much more comfortable. He closed his eyes again and before he knew it, he was fast asleep. From that day on, Tim made sure his socks were snug before going to bed.

Once there was a bunny. His name was Pete and he loved to bounce. He would bounce everywhere. No matter what, he always found a way to bounce. 

One day, Pete decided to visit his friend, Bob. When he arrived, Pete bounced up to the door and knocked. But there was no answer. So Pete bounced to the window, looked inside and saw that Bob was very sad.

Pete asked Bob, "Why are you so sad?"

Bob replied, "I don't know why. I just feel sad today."

Pete knew exactly what he had to do. He thought for a moment and then said, "Let's go bounce! That always makes me feel better!" 

So off they went, Pete and Bob, bouncing and jumping. And before long, Bob began to smile and laugh. His sadness had gone away!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very curious and always wanted to explore. 

One day, Lucy found a birdcage outside her house. She went over to pick it up and it felt hard in her hands. Lucy was excited and wanted to see what was inside. 

She opened up the birdcage and discovered a small bird inside. The bird started to chirp and it made Lucy smile. She wanted to keep the birdcage and the bird with her. 

Lucy took the birdcage inside the house and put it on the window sill. She made sure to give the bird lots of food, water and love. 

Every day, Lucy would go play with the bird and discover new things about it. She was very happy and so was the little bird.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, she accidentally dropped her mom's phone and it broke. Her mom got very angry and Lily felt sad.

Lily's mom said, "Why did you break my phone? You need to be more careful!" Lily said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't mean to. Please forgive me."

Lily's mom was still angry but she knew that Lily didn't mean to break the phone. After a while, she said, "Okay, Lily. I forgive you. But please be more careful next time." 

Lily was happy that her mom forgave her. She hugged her mom and promised to be more careful. Even though Lily was sometimes stubborn, she always tried to do the right thing.

One day, a boy named Jack wanted to play hockey. He put on his helmet and skated out onto the ice. He had never skated before, but he was determined to learn.

Jack had to practice a lot but he was so determined that he gained his skills quickly. Soon enough, he was playing hockey like a pro.

Jack's friends thought it was very unusual for him to know how to play so well. They had never seen anyone learn so fast before. Every day Jack continued to gain more skills, and soon enough he became the best player on the team.

He was so proud that he had gained all these skills. No matter how hard things got, he never gave up! He finally did something that was unusual and that made him happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the snow. She put on her coat, hat, and mittens. But when she came back inside, she noticed that one of her mittens was missing. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She felt sad and regretted not being more careful with her things.

A few days later, Lily's mom found the missing mitten. It was in the backyard, buried under a pile of snow. Lily was happy to have her mitten back, but she realized that she should take better care of her things. She didn't want to lose anything else. She learned a mysterious lesson that day. If she took care of her things, they would take care of her.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Ruby went out to play in the garden. She saw a beautiful pool in the corner and was so excited! She ran to the edge of the pool and wanted to get into the water. She wanted to be as independent as she could, so she carefully put her feet in the pool and stepped in. 

But suddenly, the pool began to tremble. The water started to splash everywhere and Ruby became scared. She didn't know what was happening.

Ruby quickly took a few steps back and called out for help. Meanwhile, her brother Jack came running. He saw what was happening and shouted: "Get out! Get out there quickly!"

But Ruby was scared of the trembling pool and didn't move. Jack ran up to the pool and tried to help her, but it was too late. In a matter of seconds, the swimming pool collapsed and sucked Ruby in. 

Jack was extremely scared and started to cry. Ruby never got out of the pool and Jack never saw her again.

Mama and Jack were very excited. They had just moved into a new house. Jack was only three so he couldn't help much, but he watched as Mama unpacked all their boxes. He saw clothes and toys, books and games. When Mama asked him what he was most excited about, he smiled and said, "I'm excited to make friends here!"

But when they opened up one of the boxes, he saw something strange - it was a stiff, white jacket. Jack was confused. "What is this thing?" he asked. 

Mama smiled sadly. "It's a cold jacket," she said. 

Jack frowned. "Why's it here?" he asked.

Mama looked at Jack with deep sadness in her eyes. She told him that the jacket had belonged to Daddy, but he had moved on to a better place. She hugged Jack and said, "It's okay to be sad, but Daddy is always with us in our hearts." 

Jack looked at the cold jacket and made a silent promise that he would never forget Daddy. He knew that no matter where he moved, he would always remember.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who was very hungry. She went to a restaurant with her mom and dad. The waiter gave them a menu to choose what they wanted to eat. Lily saw a picture of a big burger and fries, and her tummy growled.

But when the waiter came back, he teased Lily and said, "Are you sure you can eat all of that?" Lily felt embarrassed and sad. She whispered to her mom, "I don't like that man, he's mean." Her mom told her not to worry and ordered the burger for her.

When the food arrived, Lily was so happy and took a big bite. She smiled and said, "This is yummy!" Her dad asked her, "Do you want to share some with me?" Lily shook her head and said, "No way, I'm too hungry!"

Once there was a boy named Billy who was three years old. He really liked to clap his hands. 

One day, he found a spoon in his backyard. It was very shiny and looked like it was brand new. So, he decided to take it inside and show it to his parents. 

Things took a turn for the worse when he saw it was really dirty when he brought it inside. He tried to clean it with a cloth, but it only made it dirtier. 

His parents were not happy at all and scolded him. Billy was very sad and started to cry. He realised he should have left the spoon in the backyard. He promised himself never to take dirty things in the house again.

Joe wanted to be a soldier. He had a long uniform and a special hat. He was so proud of his uniform. Every day, he would do the same thing.

First, he would stand up tall and straight, like a soldier. Then, he marched around the house, giving orders to his dolls. They had to do what Joe said. After that, he practiced shooting with his toy gun. He could already shoot very far.

Joe's Mom saw how proud he was and she thought he looked very handsome in his uniform. Joe loved going outside with his uniform on, too. Everyone smiled and waved when they saw him. They thought he was so cute.

He would do this every day until it was time to go to bed. After that, he folded up his long uniform and put it away. Then he was ready to have sweet dreams.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Jenny was playing with her toy chest. She loved to make matching games with her jewels and trinkets. She carefully lined up all the prettiest jewels in a row, looking anxiously at each one. Suddenly, a special pair of matching jewels caught her eye.

"Mommy," Jenny said, "look at these two matching jewels!"

Her mom smiled. "Aren't those two beautiful! You have really matched them up nicely!"

Jenny proudly smiled. She had worked hard to find this perfect pair of jewels. She was so happy that her mom had noticed her efforts. From then on, she enjoyed playing matching games even more.

Once, there was a little girl called Jill. She went on a winter day to a meadow beside a mountain. The meadow was filled with long grass and wildflowers.

In the center of the meadow, Jill noticed a sparkling crystal. It was a beautiful crystal and she wanted to take it home.

Jill asked her mom if she could keep the crystal. Mom said, "Yes, but first you must bury it in the ground".

Jill dug a small hole in the ground with her hands. It was easy enough to do. Jill put the crystal in the hole and buried it with earth.

Shortly afterwards, Jill saw a rainbow in the sky! Mom told her that this was a sign of good luck. Then they went home, happy and content.

John loved to ride. He loved the way the wind felt on his face, the way the bike seemed to move beneath him like a wild animal. He was an independent rider, not afraid of anything. Everywhere he went he saw a new landscape.

One day, John decided he wanted to explore. He grabbed his bike and rode as far as his legs could take him. He was surrounded by rolling hills, trees, and bright blue skies. He felt free and alive as he rode.

As he rode, he made up stories about the places he visited. He imagined that the trees were tall enough to touch the clouds and that the dirt was as soft as velvet. He thought the setting sun was god and the mountains were their stands. 

Finally, John stopped and looked around. He'd ridden so far that it had started to get dark. But John didn't feel afraid, he was proud of how independent he'd been. He decided right then that he'd always remember that day, and the magical landscape he'd discovered.

Molly and her best friend Lucy had lots of fun together. They liked to play outside and have tea parties. 

One day, Lucy and Molly went outside to play. Lucy had an idea, she said, "Let's play a game of tease!" Molly laughed and agreed.

They ran around the garden, teasing each other. It was so much fun! Eventually, they got tired and stopped.

Molly and Lucy went inside and heard some yummy jazz music playing. They both grinned, because they loved the music. 

Molly and Lucy danced together and the yummy jazz music made it even more fun. Molly and Lucy had a great time together.

Once there was a small ant who lived in the warm garden. He had many friends there, but he was all alone today. As he was walking through the garden, the ant came across a tear on the ground. He was curious to find out who had put it there. He asked his friends but no one had seen it.

So the ant decided to explore. He looked for footprints, but all he found was a warm, damp patch on the ground. Suddenly he heard a voice, "Can you help me?"

The ant quickly turned around and saw a small girl, crying. She said, "I dropped something special in the garden and now I can't find it. Could you help me look for it?"

The ant was happy to help and he quickly set off searching. Soon enough, he found the warm object the girl had dropped. He took it back to her and she was so grateful. She gave the ant a big hug and thanked him before picking up the object and running off, with a smile on her face.

The ant watched her go and then happily made his way back home. It was nice to know that kindness can help in even the smallest of ways.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. They saw a big pond with many ducks. Lily wanted to feed the ducks some bread, but Tom wanted to tease them. He ran after the ducks and shouted, "Quack, quack, you are silly ducks!"

One duck did not like Tom's teasing. It was a big, white duck with a red beak. It was the leader of the ducks. It swam to the edge of the pond and bit Tom's leg. Tom cried out, "Ow, ow, that hurts! Go away, you mean duck!"

Lily ran to Tom and hugged him. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. The duck was angry because you teased him. He wanted to be nice to you, but you were not nice to him. You should say sorry to the duck."

Tom looked at the duck and saw that it was still watching him. He felt bad for teasing the duck. He said, "I'm sorry, duck. I was wrong to tease you. You are not silly, you are smart and beautiful. Can we be friends?"

The duck nodded and quacked softly. It came closer to Tom and Lily and let them pet its feathers. It shared some bread with them and showed them its nest. It had many eggs and ducklings. It was a rich duck with a big family. Tom and Lily smiled and thanked the duck. They learned to be kind to the ducks and not to tease them. They became friends with the duck and visited him often. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat breakfast at the table with her family every morning. One day, something strange happened. Her mom put a big bowl of cereal on the table, but Lily couldn't hear the milk splashing into the bowl. She was deaf! 

Lily was sad because she couldn't hear her family talking or the birds singing outside. But her family loved her just the same and they learned how to communicate with her using sign language. They even learned how to make breakfast without making too much noise so Lily could enjoy it too. 

One day, Lily got a special device that helped her hear again. She was so happy! She could hear her family's voices and the birds singing. She could even hear the milk splashing into her cereal bowl. From then on, Lily could enjoy breakfast at the table with her family just like before.

Once there was a boy named Nick. One day, Nick mentioned to his mum that he wanted to watch a film. His mum said it was too cold to sit inside and watch a film. So Nick decided to go for a walk in the cold. 

Nick loved the cold and he soon forgot about the film. He spent hours playing in the garden and his mom was worried he might catch a cold. She was relieved when he came back inside. 

But then Nick noticed he was feeling really ill. He started coughing, and when his mum looked closely, she saw he was very pale. She took him to the hospital where the doctor said Nick had a nasty cold. Unfortunately, the doctor said Nick had to stay in the hospital until he got better. 

And so, Nick sadly ended up in the hospital instead of watching a film with his mum on a cold day.

Anna liked mints very much. She liked how they made her mouth feel cold and fresh. She had a jar of mints on her shelf, but she was not allowed to eat them all the time. Mommy said too many mints would make her teeth hurt.

One day, Anna saw the jar of mints on her shelf and wanted one very badly. She looked around and saw that Mommy was busy in the kitchen. She thought she could get one mint without Mommy knowing. She climbed on her bed and reached for the jar. But she was too clumsy and knocked the jar over. The jar fell on the floor and broke. Mints rolled everywhere.

"Oh no!" Anna cried. She heard Mommy coming. She tried to pick up the mints and the broken jar, but it was too late. Mommy saw the mess and was very angry.

"Anna, what did you do?" Mommy asked.

"I'm sorry, Mommy. I wanted a mint, but I was clumsy and dropped the jar," Anna said.

Mommy sighed. She was not happy, but she was not mean. She hugged Anna and said, "I know you like mints, but you have to ask me first. And you have to be careful with glass jars. They can hurt you if they break. Now let's clean up this mess together."

Anna nodded. She felt bad for being clumsy and sneaky. She helped Mommy clean up the mints and the jar. She learned her lesson. She decided to wait for Mommy to give her a mint next time. She hoped Mommy would still love her. Mommy smiled and gave her a kiss. She said, "I love you, Anna. But no more mints today, okay?"

Anna smiled back. She said, "Okay, Mommy. I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because it was her birthday. Her mommy and daddy told her they had a surprise for her.

Lily's mommy made a cake that looked like a castle, but it was fake. It was made of paper and had no yummy cake inside. Lily was sad that she couldn't eat the cake. 

But then, her mommy and daddy brought out a real cake with candles on it. Lily blew out the candles and her mommy and daddy fed her a big slice of cake. It was the best birthday ever!

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a big teddy bear, a yellow ball, and a red car. She liked to make them talk and have fun together. One day, she decided to have a tea party with her toys. She got a small table and some cups and plates from her mom. She filled the cups with water and pretended it was tea. She gave some to her teddy bear, some to her ball, and some to her car.

She said, "Here you go, friends. This is tasty tea. Drink it and be happy." She drank some of her tea and smiled. She felt something tickle her nose. She looked and saw a small ant on her nose. She was scared and said, "Oh no! An ant! Go away, ant! You are not my friend. You are not invited to my tea party. You are not tasty. You are yucky."

She tried to blow the ant off her nose, but it did not work. The ant crawled on her nose and made her sneeze. She sneezed so hard that her water spilled on the table and on her toys. She was sad and said, "Oh no! My tea! My toys! They are wet and messy. I need to get a towel and clean them. I need to get a new tea. I need to get rid of this ant."

She ran to her mom and asked for a towel and some more water. Her mom saw the ant on her nose and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will help you. Let me get the ant off your nose. It will not hurt you. It is just looking for food. Maybe it likes your tea. But you are right, it is not tasty. It is yucky." She gently picked the ant off Lily's nose and put it outside. She gave Lily a towel and some more water. She said, "There you go, Lily. Now you can go back to your tea party. But be careful, there might be more ants around. They like sweet things. Maybe you can share some of your tea with them. They are not your friends, but they are not your enemies either. They are just animals."

Lily said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I will be careful. I will share some of my tea with the ants. But not too much. I want to save some for my toys. They are my friends. They are tasty. They are not yucky." She hugged her mom and went back to her tea party. She cleaned her toys and her table. She poured some of her tea on the ground for the ants. She said, "Here you go, ants. This is tasty tea. Drink it and be happy. But please, stay away from my nose. It is not tasty. It is not yucky. It is mine." She drank some of her tea and smiled. She had a good tea party.

One day, Timmy went to the beach by himself. He was feeling lonely. When he got there, he noticed the sand all around. It was so soft and golden. Especially the sand near the shore which was glimmering in the sun. 

He had his bucket with him and he started to collect shells and small rocks. After a while, he heard a voice behind him. 

"What do you observe?" said the voice.

Timmy turned around and saw a small crab. He smiled and said, "I can see the sand. It's so beautiful and sparkly". 

The crab replied, "Yes, the sand is amazing. I like the sand too". 

And then Timmy continued to explore the beach. He was no longer lonely and he enjoyed his time there observing the sand and everything else around.

Once upon a time there was a pigeon. She was a special pigeon because she was purple all over! She lived in a park, and every day she would take walks around the grass and eat bugs. 

One day she saw a very sad little girl crying on a bench in the park. The little girl had been at the park for hours but no one was coming to get her. The purple pigeon was so kind that she flew up to the bench to see what was wrong.

The little girl told the pigeon that her mommy had gone away and she didn't know how to find her. Suddenly the pigeon had a brilliant idea. She knew a way to help the little girl find her mommy. She could fly around the city and look for her! 

So the pigeon said goodbye and flew off into the sky. After hours of searching she spotted the little girl's mommy in the distance. She quickly flew back to the park and told the little girl the news.

The little girl was so excited and quickly ran to find her mommy. The purple pigeon had used her wings to support the little girl and brought them back together again.

Once there was a girl named Sally. She loved to explore and play in the mud. One day, while playing in the mud, she found a old, leather bag. It was a bit messy, so she decided to clean it up.

Sally worked hard to make the bag look nice, and soon it became shiny and bright. She was really proud of herself, and decided to wear it around town.

When she wore the bag, people smiled and waved at her. Everywhere she went people said how beautiful her bag was. She even made some friends who had similar bags. Soon, everyone wanted to be like Sally and have a leather bag.

Sally smiled and was really happy. She made a new and special thing out of something that was once messy.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who promised to always be together. They were so happy, but one day something scary happened. They met a monster!

The monster was big and loud, and he asked the two friends to leave their happy place. But the two best friends promised each other to stay brave.

Suddenly, a nice big bird flew down from the sky. He promised to help them. He made funny sounds and faces at the monster, and the monster ran away!

The two friends hugged the nice big bird and thanked him for saving them. They promised to always remember how kind and brave the bird was and to always stay together.

Honey was very excited. She was outside with Mommy and Daddy who had a big surprise for her. Suddenly, a funny looking bike appeared. It had two wheels and one seat and a funny round thing on the front. Honey climbed on and Daddy told her to grab the funny round thing, which was the pedal. She tried to push it and the bike started moving forward. Honey was so delighted; she couldn't believe she was riding a bike. 

Mommy and Daddy took her to the ice cream parlor for a delicious treat. Honey had a bubble gum flavored ice cream and was amazed how yummy it was. She gobbled it up, just in time to ride her bike home. Honey was so proud of herself for riding her bike and for eating her delicious ice-cream. As she pedaled back home with Mommy and Daddy following close behind, Honey smiled from ear to ear.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found an interesting bug crawling on the ground. 

"Mommy, look at this bug!" Timmy said excitedly. 

"That's a cool bug, Timmy," replied his mom. "But be careful, it might bite you." 

Timmy continued to watch the bug crawl around until it finally completed its journey and flew away. 

Later that day, Timmy's dad came home from work and went to shave with his razor. Timmy watched curiously as his dad shaved his face. 

"Daddy, what's that thing you're using?" Timmy asked. 

"It's called a razor, Timmy," replied his dad. "It helps me shave my beard." 

Timmy thought the razor was interesting too and couldn't wait to grow up and shave like his dad.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toy trains on the floor. They liked to make them go fast and make noises. Lily had a red train and Tom had a blue train. They also had a big tunnel that they could put their trains through.

"Look, my train is faster than yours!" Lily said to Tom. She made her train zoom past his train and into the tunnel.

"No, my train is faster!" Tom said. He tried to catch up with Lily's train, but the tunnel was too small for both trains. He pushed his train harder and harder, but it got stuck.

"Hey, stop it! You are making my train stop too!" Lily said. She pulled her train back, but Tom's train was in the way. She could see steam coming out of both trains. They were getting hot and angry.

"Move your train! You are selfish! You want the tunnel all for yourself!" Tom said. He pulled his train too, but it did not move. He started to cry.

Lily felt sorry for Tom. She did not want to make him cry. She thought for a moment. She had an idea.

"Tom, I'm sorry. I don't want to be selfish. We can share the tunnel. How about we take turns? You can go first, then I can go, then you can go again, and so on. OK?" Lily said.

Tom stopped crying. He looked at Lily. He thought she was nice. He nodded.

"OK, Lily. Thank you. We can share. You are a good friend." Tom said.

They smiled at each other. They took turns to put their trains through the tunnel. They made noises and had fun. They did not see the steam anymore. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to look up at the sky and see the bright stars shining. One night, she saw a shooting star and made a wish. She wished for a puppy to play with.

The next day, Lily went to the park and saw a little puppy all alone. She cared for the puppy and took it home to keep it safe. The puppy was so happy to have a new friend.

Lily and the puppy played together every day and at night, they would look up at the bright stars and make wishes. They were the best of friends and always took care of each other.

Mummy had a jolly smile on her face when she put the violin in little Jack's hands. He held it carefully and looked up at Mummy, wondering what he was meant to do. She nodded and said, "Go ahead and play!"

Little Jack put the violin to his shoulder and willed himself to make a sound. After a few seconds the room was filled with a beautiful musical melody. Mummy's jolly smile grew even wider and soon she was tapping her feet along with the music.

Little Jack looked up, his eyes sparkling with joy. He put the bow up and down, faster and faster, as if he was trying to make all the music out of the world. The violin was singing and Mummy was singing and they were both laughing and smiling.

Little Jack put the violin down, still smiling. He felt so proud - he had made something so beautiful. And he knew that with a little bit more practice, he would be able to master the violin!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw pictures with her crayons. One day, Lily's little brother came into her room and started to take her toys without asking. Lily said "stop" and her brother stopped taking her toys.

Later that day, Lily went to her drawer to get her favorite toy, but it was gone! She looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She felt envious of her brother because she thought he took it. But then, her brother came in with her toy and said he was sorry for taking it without asking. Lily forgave him and they played together happily.

Ben and Lily wanted to play in the attic. They liked the old toys and books there. But Mom said no. She said the attic was dusty and dark. She said they could get hurt or lost.

Ben and Lily did not listen. They had a plan. When Mom was busy, they sneaked up the stairs. They opened the door to the attic. They saw a big box. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Ben said.

"OK!" Lily said.

They lifted the lid. But they did not see toys or books. They saw a big spider. It was hairy and scary. It jumped out of the box. It landed on Ben's head.

"Help!" Ben screamed.

"Help!" Lily screamed.

Mom heard them. She ran up the stairs. She saw the spider. She grabbed a broom. She swept the spider away. She hugged Ben and Lily.

"Are you OK?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom," Ben and Lily said.

"You were very foolish," Mom said. "You should not go to the attic without me. You could have been hurt. You should listen to me."

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben and Lily said.

Mom was not angry. She was glad they were safe. She took them downstairs. She gave them cookies and milk. She told them a story. Ben and Lily learned their lesson. They did not go to the attic again. They played with their toys and books in their room. They were happy.

Once there was a zip. It was long and white, like a thread. It was rough to the touch. One day, the zip blinked. It saw a red bird fly across the sky. It was so beautiful. 

The zip was excited and blinked again. This time it saw a big elephant walking across the field. It was so big and strong. The zip was amazed and winked once more.

This time it saw a big caterpillar crawling up a tree. It was colourful and slimy. The zip stared in wonder at all these creatures. It was a truly magical day. 

The zip blinked one last time and it was back in its place. But it had a new feeling. It was so excited to see all the wonderful animals around it. It would never forget the magical afternoon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going for walks in the forest with her mommy. One day, they found a big, red mushroom. Lily thought it looked funny and she started to laugh.

"Mommy, look at this mushroom! It's so big and red!" Lily said.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's a mushroom. But be careful, some mushrooms can be spicy and make you sick."

Lily listened carefully and promised to never eat a mushroom without her mommy's permission. From that day on, every time they went for a walk in the forest, Lily would look for mushrooms and they would both laugh at the silly ones they found.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to search for treasure in her backyard. One day, she found a box that was very old and ancient. She opened it and found a beautiful necklace inside.

Lily put the necklace around her waist and felt like a princess. But soon, she realized that the necklace was cursed. It made her feel sick and dizzy. She tried to take it off, but it wouldn't come off.

Lily's parents took her to the hospital, but the doctors couldn't help her. The cursed necklace stayed around her waist forever. Lily learned that sometimes, treasure can be dangerous and it's important to be careful when searching for it.

Once upon a time, there was a tall fireman. He was very nice, and he loved to help people. He had a special job he had to do.

One day, he drove away in his fire truck with lots of sirens and noise. Everyone watched him go as he drove off. Little did they know, this fireman was about to save someone's life.

A few days later, it was very hot outside. Suddenly, the fireman returned with his truck to the same spot he left from. He was carrying a small bundle in his arms. He had saved a small baby from a burning building.

The people looked on in amazement. The tall fireman had done something amazing, and everyone was very proud of him. He had used his mind to help save the baby! 

From that day on, everyone said that the tall fireman was like a superhero. He will always be a hero that they mind and they will never forget his brave act!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to wear a big red hat. He wore it every day. Spot's hat was his favorite thing in the whole world.

One day, Spot's family had a big dinner. They had yummy food like apples, bananas, and cookies. Spot wanted to be a part of the dinner too. So, he put on his big red hat and sat down at the table. He looked very funny wearing his hat at the table.

But Spot was being naughty. Dogs should not sit at the table. Spot's family told him to get down. Spot felt sad, but he knew he had to listen. He went to his bed and took off his big red hat. Even though he was naughty, Spot still loved his hat and his family.

Once upon a time, there was an owl who lived in a large tree. The owl flew around the forest gracefully, and one day he saw two raccoons talking by the tree. They seemed to be discussing something very important.

The owl was curious, so he flew closer to listen. The raccoons explained that they wanted to find food before it got dark outside. The owl had a perfect idea to help. He said that he knew where there were some tasty berries.

The raccoons were so excited. They thanked the owl for his help and started to pick the fruit. The owl watched gracefully from a nearby tree as the raccoons happily ate the berries.

As the sun went down, the owl flew back to his tree and went to sleep. He felt very proud to have been able to help his new friends.

Sara and Tom were playing with their crayons and paper. They liked to draw many things, like flowers, cars, and animals. Sara had a blue crayon and Tom had a red one.

"Look, I made a big fish!" Sara said, showing her paper to Tom.

"That's nice, but I made a faster car!" Tom said, holding his paper up.

They kept drawing and talking, until Sara noticed something strange. Her blue crayon was getting smaller and smaller. She looked at Tom's red crayon and saw that it was also shrinking.

"Hey, what's happening to our crayons?" Sara asked, worried.

"I don't know, maybe they are magic crayons!" Tom said, excited.

They watched as their crayons became tiny bits of ink on their paper. Then, the ink started to fade and vanish. Soon, their paper was white again, with no trace of their drawings.

"Where did our drawings go?" Sara cried, sad.

"They vanished, like magic!" Tom said, amazed.

They looked around and saw a grumpy cat sitting on the table. The cat had a smug smile and some blue and red ink on its fur.

"Did you do this, cat?" Sara asked, angry.

"Meow!" the cat said, and jumped off the table, running away.

Sara and Tom chased the cat, but it was too fast and clever. They could not catch it or get their drawings back.

They were very sad and mad at the cat. They decided to get new crayons and paper, and draw something else. But they also decided to keep an eye on the cat, in case it tried to ruin their drawings again.

Once there was a big tree. Everyday it grew and grew. One day, a silly bird hopped onto the tree. The bird was looking for something shiny to wear. 

The bird said, "I'm looking for something to make me look fancy!" She added, "Do you know where I can find something glimmering?" 

The tree thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, follow me! I can help you find it." 

The bird followed the tree and soon they found a sparkling spell on the ground. The bird cheered and said, "This is perfect! Now I'm the prettiest bird around!" 

The bird thanked the tree and flew away. The tree just smiled and kept growing.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with puzzles. He had a big shelf with many boxes on it. Each box had a puzzle inside. One day, Timmy wanted to play with a puzzle, but he couldn't find the right box. He looked and looked, but the shelf was not clear. 

Timmy decided to match the puzzle pieces he found on the floor to the boxes on the shelf. He worked hard and finally found the right box. He opened it and started to play. Timmy was happy because he had found the puzzle he wanted to play with. From that day on, he made sure to put the puzzles back on the shelf so it would stay clear and he could easily match the pieces to the right box. The end.

Once there was a man and a boy walking to the park. The man was whistling a happy tune as they went.

The boy asked his dad, "What are you doing?"

The father replied, "I'm whistling to make us both happy." 

The boy smiled and thought it was fun. 

When they arrived at the park, it was very clean. The boy said, "Look dad, it's so clean and shiny!" 

The man said, "Yes, that's because someone gave the park a tip and it was cleaned up." 

The boy was amazed. He wanted to whistle now, too. 

So, the man and the boy both started whistling and they were both so happy. 

They both giggled and kept whistling until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little dog named Max. Max had a toy bone that he loved to play with all day. One day, Max was playing with his toy bone when he heard a noise outside. He ran to the window and saw a big cat. Max knew that he had to be brave and protect his toy bone.

Max went outside to face the big cat. The big cat saw Max's toy bone and wanted it too. They both started to pull on the bone with their mouths, but Max didn't want to surrender his favorite toy. Max pulled harder and harder, but the big cat was very strong. Max started to feel tired and worried that he might lose his toy bone.

Then, Max had an idea. He let go of the toy bone with his mouth and quickly grabbed it with his front leg. The big cat was surprised and didn't know what to do. Max used his leg to hold the toy bone and ran back inside his house. The big cat couldn't catch Max, and he saved his toy bone. Max learned that sometimes, being smart is better than being strong. And from that day on, Max never had to worry about surrendering his toy bone again.

Once upon a time, there was a much-loved puppy called Pip. Pip was a curious and adventurous pup and loved to travel. One day, Pip set off on a special journey. He traveled far and wide, until he came upon a beautiful fountain.

The fountain was surrounded by butterflies and other animals who were amazed by its bubbling water. Pip was thirsty so he took a big drink and then looked around. He noticed a little mouse with sad eyes. The mouse explained that it was lost, and did not know the way home.

Pip felt sorry for the mouse and decided to help him. He filled his bowl with water from the fountain and asked the friendly animals around him if they knew the way back to the little mouse's home. They all gave directions and then watched as Pip and the mouse set off together.

After a long journey, the mouse finally reached its home. As the mouse ran off to safety, the animals cheered for Pip who had been so compassionate. The tiny pup had taught them a valuable lesson about the power of friendship. From that day on, Pip was remembered as the pup who traveled far and wide, believing in the kindness of others.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved to wave. He waved to the sun, he waved to the birdies and he waved to his mommy and daddy. One day he wanted to be even better at waving. So, he went to the garden to practice.

The boy waved his arms all around. He waved them high and low. He waved them to the left and he waved them to the right. He became very competitive.

After a while he got tired. He reached up as high as he could and thenâ€¦ he fell down. There were lots of yummy leaves all around and he had a lot of fun. But then it became time to go home. 

The boy said goodbye to the leaves and he waved again. He waved to the sky, the trees and his mommy and daddy. As he got ready to go home, he smiled because he knew he was the best waver in town.

Tommy was walking through the park one day. Suddenly, he spotted a long banana on a tree. He shouted with joy, "I want that banana!" Tommy stretched his arms as far as he could, but he couldn't reach it. 

So Tommy shouted for help. Suddenly, a big friendly bear appeared. The bear said, "I can get that banana for you!" Tommy nodded, and the bear reached up and grabbed the banana. 

The bear handed the banana to Tommy and said, "Here you go! I hope you enjoy it." Tommy thanked the bear and took a big bite of the banana. It was delicious! He shouted with happiness, "Yummy!" 

The bear smiled and said, "You're welcome. Have a good day!" Tommy waved goodbye and continued walking through the park with the long banana in his hand.

Once upon a time, there was a warm nation. In this nation, there was a tiny boy who was three years old. He had never been anywhere else, but he was always curious to learn more.

Every day he would spend some time looking up at the sky, wondering what the world was like. He wondered how many people were in the world, and what would it be like to meet them. 

As he grew older, he kept wondering about the world and all of its many wonders. He also wanted to know what secrets the world was hiding.

One day, his parents took him on a trip to a different nation. He was so excited to explore! Everywhere he looked, he saw new and exciting things. He learned about different cultures and cuisines.

The little boy was so happy during his trip that he could hardly contain himself. He could not wait to go home and tell everyone about all the interesting things he had seen and learned. 

Since his trip, the little boy never stopped wondering what was out there in the world. He was always eager to learn as much as he could, no matter how old he got.

Once there was a little girl named Paige. She loved to bounce. She could bounce on the trampoline, the bed and even the couch.

So one day she found an old umbrella in the attic. She picked it up and went outside. Paige was careful. She knew the umbrella looked fragile. 

Paige was ready to bounce with the umbrella. She threw it up in the air with a big smile. But when the umbrella landed back down, it got stuck in a big tree. Paige tried to get it back, but it was too high for her to reach. 

Paige called for help. Her mom heard her and rushed outside. "Oh Paige!", Mom said when she saw the umbrella stuck in the tree. She found a ladder, climbed up and carefully got the umbrella. "Be careful, Paige," she said. "This umbrella is fragile."

Then Mom and Paige took the umbrella inside and fixed it up. Now Paige can bounce with the umbrella again! What fun!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big ear that he liked to wiggle. One day, Timmy went to the store to sell some toys. He wanted to buy a new toy that was reliable and would make him happy. 

At the store, Timmy met a nice man who wanted to buy his toys. The man said he was reliable and would always be fair. Timmy was happy because he could sell his toys and buy a new one. 

As Timmy left the store, he wiggled his big ear and smiled. He was excited to play with his new toy and knew he could always trust the reliable man at the store. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a baby who was eager to try all kinds of things. Whenever she saw something new, she was full of curiosity and wanted to give it a try.

One day, the baby went out to play with her family. She quickly ran away from them, excited to explore this new place. As she increased the distance between her and her family, she found a tall tree with lots of fruits. At once, she wanted to try them.

But unfortunately, the baby was too small to reach the fruits and no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't get them. Her eagerness to try the fruits was so strong that she started to cry.

Luckily, her family noticed her and her father came to help her. He brought a ladder and placed it against the tree. With his help, she could reach the fruits and satisfied her eagerness to try them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, when she was playing, she saw a skeleton on the ground. She was scared and ran to her mommy.

Her mommy came and saw the skeleton too. She explained to Lily that it was just a pretend skeleton for Halloween. Lily was still scared, so her mommy offered to hold her hand and walk with her past the skeleton.

Lily felt better with her mommy by her side. They walked past the skeleton and continued to play in the park. Later that day, Lily told her friends about the skeleton and how her mommy helped her not be scared. Her friends thought it was very brave of her and offered to play a fun game of tag together. Lily was happy again and had a great day with her friends.

Sad Pete was walking down the road. He was feeling very lonely, and he wished he had a friend. Suddenly, he heard a whistle coming from behind a bush. Pete peeked around the bush and saw a big, yellow bird. The bird smiled and said, "Hello! Would you like to be friends?" Pete's face lit up and he said yes.

The bird dove into the sky and sang a song. It was the happiest Pete had ever felt. They became best friends and did everything together.

But one day, Pete had to leave. He was feeling so sad that he was leaving his friend that he decided not to say goodbye. As Pete walked away, he looked back. He was filled with regret for not saying goodbye.

Pete never saw the bird again, but he never forgot the happy moments they shared together. He always thought back on that day with sadness, and remembered the sound of the bird's happy whistle.

Once a 3 year old girl named Lucy walking down the street with her dad. She saw a vendor who was selling toys. Lucy asked her dad if she could have one of the toys. Her dad replied no, as they didn't have money to buy the toys.

Seeing the vendor being sad, Lucy decided to comfort him. She said, "Don't worry, you can be successful if you work hard." 
The vendor thanked Lucy for her kind words and smiled. He then shared a piece of wisdom with her. He said, "You must always try to do your best, even if it is hard. If you do that, you can achieve anything."

Hearing this, Lucy was so pleased. She told the vendor that she would always remember to do her best. Lucy realised the importance of helping others and remember the valuable lesson she learned. She was glad that she was able to comfort the vendor. 

The moral of the story is that helping others can bring joy to you, and by always doing your best, you can be successful.

Once upon a time, there was a small butterfly. He loved to fly around in the sunshine and have fun. But one day, a big wind started to blow and he had to resist it. He tried his hardest to stay in the air, but it was too strong. He tumbled and tumbled until he was too tired.

He landed on a big leaf and there he saw a small ant walking by. The butterfly asked the ant for help. The ant smiled and said 'Follow me, I can help you'. He led the butterfly back to his home, which was inside a big tree. It was cozy and warm, and the butterfly felt safe.

The ant told the butterfly to wait. He soon returned with some butter, which he spread on the leaf. The butterfly thanked the ant and began to eat the butter. The butter gave him energy and strength, so he spread his wings and fluttered away, feeling much better.
