Once upon a time, there was a rich girl who lived in a big house all by herself. Every day she would walk around her house and remember things. One day, she found a magnet in the garden. She was so excited and put the magnet in her pocket. 

The next day, she decided to take the magnet to a special store. When she entered, she saw lots of amazing things. She asked the shopkeeper what she could do with the magnet. 

The shopkeeper said, "You can make wonderful things with it! With the help of this magnet, you can make things stick together and make magical things!"

The girl was so happy and thanked the shopkeeper. She left the store with the magnet and remembered what the shopkeeper said. From that day, she was always making wonderful things with her magnet.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with clay. They made different shapes and animals with the clay. They had fun and laughed a lot.

One day, they found a big jar of salt in the kitchen. They thought it would be nice to add some salt to their clay. They poured some salt on their clay and mixed it well. The salt made the clay sparkle and crunch.

"Wow, this is so pretty and cool!" Lily said.

"Can I have some salt for my clay too?" Ben asked.

Lily looked at the jar of salt. There was not much left. She wanted to keep it for herself. She said, "No, this is my salt. You can't have any."

Ben felt sad and angry. He said, "That's not fair. You have to share. Sharing is good."

Lily shook her head. She said, "No, this is mine. Go away."

Ben was hurt. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He took his clay and left.

Lily played with her salted clay alone. She made a big star and a moon. But she did not feel happy. She felt lonely and bored. She missed Ben and his clay animals. She wished she had shared the salt with him.

She looked at the jar of salt again. There was still some left. She had an idea. She took the jar and ran after Ben. She found him sitting on a bench, playing with his soft clay.

"Ben, I'm sorry. I was mean and selfish. Do you want some salt for your clay?" Lily said.

Ben looked at her. He saw the jar of salt and the star and the moon. He smiled. He said, "Yes, thank you. That's very kind of you. Do you want to play with my clay too?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, please. I like your clay animals. They are so cute and soft."

They hugged and made up. They shared the salt and the clay. They made more shapes and animals together. They had fun and laughed a lot.

They learned that sharing is good. Sharing makes things more beautiful and fun. Sharing makes friends happy.

Once there was a tall boy named Max. He loved to wander around his home village.

One day, Max found a strange sign near a bush. He had never seen it before. Max decided to wander around and see what would happen.

Max followed the sign for a long way. He saw some houses, a lake, and even some cows!

Finally, Max reached the end of the sign. He found a big park with lots of trees and a playground. Max was very happy and he decided to stay and play all day.

Max had a wonderful time exploring the park. He made some new friends and played lots of games. The time flew by and before he knew it, it was getting dark.

Max thanked the sign for leading him to the park and then wandered home. He was tired but he had a huge smile on his face. He had had the best day ever!

Once upon a time there was a wide festival. All the people there were so happy and excited to be together. They played games and sang songs. 
At the end of the festival all the children got to watch a special show. It had bright lights and loud music and it was so much fun.
When the show finished all the children cheered with excitement. They ran around, hugged their friends and said goodbye. 
Finally it was time to go home. Everyone left with smiles on their faces and joy in their hearts. It had been the best day ever!

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they quarrel over their toys. They want the same toy or they do not want to share.

One day, they find a big blanket in the closet. It is smooth and soft. They both want to use it for their games. Lily wants to make a tent with the blanket. Max wants to make a cape with the blanket. They pull the blanket from each other.

"Let go of the blanket! It is mine!" Lily says.

"No, it is mine! I saw it first!" Max says.

They quarrel and quarrel. They make a lot of noise. Mom hears them from the kitchen. She comes to their room. She sees them fighting over the blanket.

"Stop quarreling, Lily and Max! You are making a mess!" Mom says. "Why don't you play nicely with the blanket? You can take turns or use it together."

Lily and Max look at Mom. They feel sorry. They do not want to make Mom angry. They let go of the blanket.

"Sorry, Mom. Sorry, Lily. Sorry, Max." They say.

Mom smiles. She helps them to fold the blanket. She gives them a hug.

"Why don't you make a tent and a cape with the blanket? You can both use it for your games." Mom says.

Lily and Max like Mom's idea. They thank Mom. They use the blanket to make a tent and a cape. They play happily with the blanket. They do not quarrel anymore. They share and have fun.

One day, Billy was outdoors with his bow and arrow. Suddenly, he noticed a wealthy man across town. He wanted to impress the man, so he thought of a great plan. 

He decided to tie the bow string to his arrow. He grabbed a rope and stood ready to shoot. He shot his arrow as far as he could, watching as it flew across town. 

Billy ran over to meet the man, and the man said, "My, my! What an impressive shot! Did you do that?"

Billy smiled proudly and said, "Sure did! It was all me!" The man laughed and said, "Well, looks like you're quite a successful one!" 

Billy smiled knowing he had made the wealthy man proud. He decided he wanted to tie his bow and arrows every day from then on.

Once upon a time there was a brown bear. His name was Ted. One week Ted noticed that his house was all broken. He was so sad. He wanted to fix it all but he didn't know how. 

So he started to ask his friends.

One day Ted asked his friend, â€œDo you know how to fix my house?â€

His friend said, â€œI sure do. I can help you fix it in just one week.â€

Ted was so happy! He said, â€œThank you so much! Letâ€™s get started right away.â€

His friend brought all the tools they needed and they spent the whole week fixing the house. In the end, Tedâ€™s house was all shiny and new, just like it was before. 

Ted was so happy! He gave his friend a big hug.

The End.

One day, Mommy and Daddy took a trip to the big city. Everything was so big and new! Then they went to the giant building and Daddy got a license. The license made him look so happy and tidy.

On the way back home, they drove past a huge pond. Mommy looked over and shouted, "Look, a pond!" Daddy told her to stop the car, so she did.

Mommy asked Daddy why he stopped the car. He said that he wanted to soak his feet in the pond. So he rolled up his pants and jumped into the pond! He was so happy. Everyone was laughing.

Suddenly, a big bird came swooping down and landed near Daddy. Daddy gave the bird a big hug and the bird gave him a big smile. Daddy thanked the bird and they said goodbye.

They drove away with big smiles on their faces. Mommy and Daddy were so happy that Daddy got to soak his feet in the pond. It was the best day ever!

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play outside in the sun. They run, jump, and laugh. They have fun.

But one day, the sun is very hot. Ben and Mia feel tired and thirsty. They look for some shade to rest. They see a big tree with blue flowers. They run to the tree.

"Let's sleep under the tree," Ben says. "It is cool and pretty."

"Yes, let's sleep," Mia agrees. "But first, let's smell the flowers. They smell nice."

They pick some flowers and smell them. They smile. They lie down under the tree. They close their eyes.

But then, they hear a loud noise. They open their eyes. They see a big bee. The bee is angry. The bee wants the flowers. The bee buzzes and flies around them.

"Go away, bee!" Ben shouts. "These are our flowers!"

"No, they are mine!" the bee says. "I made them. You took them. Give them back!"

The bee tries to sting Ben and Mia. Ben and Mia are scared. They jump up and run away. They drop the flowers. They cry.

They run to their mom. Their mom hugs them and gives them water. She tells them to be careful with bees. She tells them to share the flowers. She tells them to say sorry to the bee.

Ben and Mia nod. They feel sorry. They go back to the tree. They see the bee. The bee is calm. The bee has the flowers.

"Sorry, bee," Ben says. "We did not know. We like your flowers. They are blue and nice."

"Sorry, bee," Mia says. "We did not mean to make you angry. We wanted to smell your flowers. They smell good."

The bee nods. The bee is happy. The bee likes Ben and Mia. The bee says, "It's okay. You can have some flowers. But not all. We can share. They are blue and good."

Ben and Mia smile. They thank the bee. They take some flowers. They give some to the bee. They make friends.

They go back to their mom. They show her the flowers. They tell her the story. Their mom is proud. She says, "You are good kids. You learned a lesson. You can sleep now. It is nap time."

Ben and Mia nod. They are sleepy. They lie down with their mom. They close their eyes. They sleep. They dream of blue flowers and bees. They are happy.

The little boy was so excited. He was about to meet his aunt for the first time! His mom and dad had helped him get dressed for the special day. He picked out his most impressive outfit, with a big blue bow-tie.

He eagerly opened the door when he heard the doorbell. He was so happy to see his aunt standing behind the door. His aunt had a very big smile.

The little boy asked her, â€œWhat did you bring me?â€ His aunt laughed and pulled out a big, wrapped box.

The little boy carefully unwrapped the box. Inside of it, he found a big toy truck. He shouted, â€œCool! Can I remove all of the parts?â€

His aunt replied, â€œYes, you can. Be careful though! Those parts are very important.â€

The little boy continued to play with his toy truck all day, assembling and disassembling the impressive truck. He had so much fun, and his aunt enjoyed watching him play.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. One day, he saw a tasty bone. Spot wanted the bone very much.

Spot ran to get the bone, but he could not find it. He looked and looked, but he could not see it. Then, he realized it was in a big room. Spot went through the door to get the bone.

Inside the room, Spot saw many things. He saw a ball, a toy, and the tasty bone. Spot played with the ball and the toy. Then, he ate the tasty bone. After eating the bone, Spot found the exit and went back home. He was a happy dog.

Tim and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together every day. They had a loyal dog named Spot, who followed them everywhere. Spot was very smart and could do many tricks.

One day, Tim and Lily decided to play hide and seek in the park. Tim was the seeker and Lily was the hider. Lily ran to find a good hiding place. She saw a big toilet near the playground. She thought it was a funny place to hide. She went inside and closed the door.

Tim counted to ten and then started to look for Lily. He looked behind the trees, under the benches, and in the swings. He could not find her. He asked Spot to help him. Spot sniffed the air and wagged his tail. He ran to the toilet and barked.

Tim followed Spot and saw the toilet. He knocked on the door and said, "Lily, are you in there? I found you!"

Lily opened the door and smiled. She said, "You are very good at finding me, Tim. And Spot is very helpful. He is a loyal friend."

Tim and Lily hugged and laughed. They thanked Spot and gave him a treat. They decided to play another game. They had a lot of fun in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she needed to go to the toilet. She went to the bathroom and closed the door behind her. The toilet was very modest, with a small sink and a white toilet bowl. 

Suddenly, Lily heard a strange noise outside the bathroom door. She wondered who or what could be making that noise. She felt a little scared, but she knew she had to be brave. 

Then, she heard a knock on the door. She asked, "Who's there?" A voice answered, "It's me, your big brother." Lily felt relieved and opened the door. Her brother entered the bathroom and said, "I just wanted to make sure you were okay." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you for taking care of me." 

From that day on, Lily knew that she could always count on her brother to be there for her when she needed him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and had a pink bag. She always took it with her everywhere she went. One day, she took her bag to school.

Her teacher said, "Today we are going to study." The little girl was excited. She opened her pink bag and got out her books, pencils and crayons.

But then her teacher said something which made the little girl very angry. She screamed, "No, I don't want to study!"

The teacher tried to be patient. She said, "Why are you so angry? We can learn lots of exciting new things if we study."

The little girl thought about this for a moment. Then she smiled and said, "Okay, let's study!" And with her pink bag in tow, she went off to learn all the wonderful things that can be discovered through studying.

Once there was an egg. It was small, round and white. One day, the egg decided to lay down on the ground. It wanted to see what would happen. Suddenly, it began to crack open. Out popped a baby chick. She was so small and fluffy.

The baby chick looked around. She saw shapes all around her. She didn't know what they were, so she decided to explore them. She pecked at the shapes and tugged at them with her beak. 

After a while, the chick saw something different. This shape was smart. It was square and it had edges! The chick had never seen anything like it before. She kept playing with it and soon enough, she knew how to build something with it.

The baby chick had made a castle! Using the smart shapes, she made a tall castle with a pointy top. The chick was so proud of her work. She thought of herself as smart too!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very excited because today was her birthday. She woke up early and ran to her mom and dad's room to wake them up. "It's my birthday!" she shouted.

Her mom and dad smiled and gave her a big hug. "Happy birthday, Lily!" they said. "What do you want to do today?"

"I want to go to the park and play on the swings," said Lily. "And I want to eat cake!"

So, they went to the park and played on the swings. It was very hot outside, and Lily was getting tired. She whispered to her mom, "Can we go home now? I'm thirsty."

But on the way home, they got into a car accident. Lily's mom and dad were hurt very badly, and they had to go to the hospital. Lily was very scared and didn't know what to do. She whispered to herself, "I wish this wasn't happening on my birthday."

Once there was a gray alligator and he was always on display for everyone to see. He loved when people came to look at him and he would watch them from his favorite spot in the pond.

He was always very quiet and still, like a statue. He did this so he wouldn't scare the people away. He just wanted them to look at him for a little bit. He was so proud of how gray and shiny he was.

One day he noticed something different in his pond. He saw a bright yellow fish swimming around the pond and he was so excited to have a new friend. The yellow fish thought the alligator was so cool and they played together all day under the sun.

The alligator was so happy that he now had a friend to show off to everyone. He would sway his head back and forth so everyone knew he had a new friend and they were having lots of fun.

The yellow fish and the gray alligator became great friends and they spent many days together on display, showing everyone the wonderful friendship they had.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She liked to play outside in the sun. One day, she found a pretty, cheap toy in the park. It was a small, red ball. Lucy was very happy and played with the ball all day.

Soon, Lucy started to feel an itch on her arm. She scratched it, but the itch did not go away. It got worse and worse. Lucy did not know what to do. She did not want to stop playing with her new toy.

After a while, Lucy realized that the cheap toy was making her itch. She was sad because she liked the toy, but she knew she had to let it go. The moral of the story is that sometimes things that seem nice can be bad for us, and we have to let them go.

Once upon a time there was a big pink scare. It was so scary that all the children in the village were scared. Little Jane was so brave, she decided to go and find the scare. 

So she went into the forest and very soon she found the scare! It was a pink monster with lots of eyes. Jane was a bit scared but she didn't run away. 

She took some rubs out of her pocket and started to rub the monster.  The monster was so happy and suddenly it wasn't scary anymore. 

The monster said thank you and vanished. Jane laughed, pleased that she wasn't scared any more. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a yellow doll that she loved very much. One day, Lily was playing with her doll outside when her brother came over.

"Can I play with your doll?" asked Lily's brother.

Lily thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, but be careful. She's my favorite."

Her brother took the doll and started to play with it, but he wasn't being careful. Suddenly, the doll's arm came off!

Lily was very upset. "You broke my doll!" she cried.

"I'm sorry," said her brother. "Let me try to fix it."

He took the broken part and tried to put it back on. After a few minutes, he was able to fix the doll's arm.

"Thank you for fixing my doll," said Lily. "I'm glad she's not broken anymore."

From that day on, Lily's brother was more careful when playing with her toys. And Lily learned that it's okay to share her things, as long as people are careful with them.

Once upon a time, a naughty bird called Toby was walking around the forest. He saw a beautiful feather in the grass. He picked it up and admired how it shone in the sun.

Suddenly, Toby heard a voice. It was a rabbit, who said "Hey, that feather is mine! Don't take it." Toby was a bit scared, but he trusted the rabbit. He explained that he was admiring the feather and would give it back.

"I can trust you, can't I?", asked the rabbit. Toby nodded happily and gave it back.

The rabbit smiled and told Toby "Thank you for trusting me. As a reward, here is a special feather just for you."

Toby was so excited about the new feather. He thanked the rabbit before running off to show his friends. From that day on, Toby trusted others and was always kind to them!

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw some pretty flowers and wanted to pick them. They ran to the flowers and broke some off.

"Look, Lily, I have a red one and a yellow one!" Ben said.

"I have a pink one and a purple one!" Lily said. "Let's put them in a vase!"

They went inside the house and looked for a vase. They found one on the table. It was big and blue and had water in it.

"Can we use this vase, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, you can, but be careful not to spill the water. It is wet and it can make a mess." Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded and took the vase. They put their flowers in it and smiled. They had made a beautiful bouquet.

"Mom, look at our flowers! We supply them for you!" Lily said.

"They are lovely, thank you! You are very sweet and thoughtful." Mom said. She hugged them and kissed them. "Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. You must be hungry after playing in the garden."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, she wanted to make a picture for her mommy. So, she took a piece of paper and started drawing.

After she finished, Lily wanted to make a copy of her picture. She asked her daddy if he could help her. He took the picture and put it on a machine that made a print. Lily was so happy to see a copy of her picture!

Later that day, Lily's little brother tried to cut his apple with a weak knife. He couldn't do it, so Lily's mommy helped him. She used a strong knife to cut the apple into small pieces. Everyone enjoyed the apple slices and had a great day together. The end.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Susie and Wayne. They both loved to visit the beach. They raced down the white sand, chasing each other and laughing. The sand felt soft and warm. Susie picked up a delicate, fragile seashell and held it carefully in her palm. 

Wayne was brave and daring. He ran right into the waves and started splashing around. Susie watched him, but she was too timid to join him in the sea. She stayed on the shore and continued to find more delicate shells. 

Soon, the sun started to set and Susie and Wayne had to go home. They hugged goodbye and waved to each other before leaving. Susie thought about their visit at the beach; it was a sunny, special day!

Once upon a time there was a boy who liked to play in the garden. He liked to find hidden spaces around the house where he could make a little den of special things. One day, he made a den in a corner of the garden and put some of his favourite toys inside. 

But when he went to get a drink, his little brother found the den and started playing with his toys. The boy asked his brother to leave the den alone but he ignored him and continued to play. The boy was getting very angry, so he marched up to his brother and shouted in a very rough voice, "Hey! That's my space. I asked you to leave it alone!" 

But his brother just laughed and ignored him again. So the boy decided to take matters into his own hands and chased his brother away from the den. When it was finally just for him, the boy was glad that he had stuck up for himself and he enjoyed playing in his little den by himself.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign in the park. The sign says: "Start of treasure hunt. Find the clues and win a prize. Only for rich kids."

Tom and Lily want to play the treasure hunt. But they are not rich. They have no money. They have old clothes and toys. They feel sad.

"Can we play, please?" Tom asks the man with the sign.

The man looks at them and laughs. "No, you can't. This is for rich kids only. You are too poor. Go away."

Tom and Lily are angry. They think the man is mean. They want to show him they are smart and brave. They decide to sneak behind the sign and follow the clues.

They find the first clue under a bench. It says: "Go to the big tree with the red swing." They run to the tree and find the second clue. It says: "Look under the bridge with the ducks." They go to the bridge and find the third clue. It says: "Go to the fountain with the coins."

They are close to the end. They are happy. They think they can win the prize. They run to the fountain and look for the last clue. But they see the man with the sign. He is angry. He sees them and shouts.

"Hey, you! What are you doing? You are cheating! You are not rich! You are not allowed to play! Give me the clues!"

Tom and Lily are scared. They hold the clues and run away. They see a big box near the fountain. It has a lock and a key. They think it is the prize. They use the key and open the box. Inside, they see a lot of books and toys. They are happy. They think they are rich.

They take some books and toys and run away. They leave the box open. They hear the man with the sign scream.

"Hey, you! Come back! You stole my prize! You are bad kids!"

Tom and Lily laugh. They think they are good kids. They think they are smart and brave. They think they are rich. They go home and share the books and toys with their friends. They have fun. They are happy. The end.

Mia and Ben are playing in the park. They like to look at the birds and count their wings. Mia can count to five, and Ben can count to three.

"Look, Ben, a big bird!" Mia says, pointing to the sky. "How many wings does it have?"

Ben looks up and sees a black bird with a long tail. He tries to count its wings, but it is flying too fast.

"One, two, umm..." Ben says, scratching his head.

"Two, silly!" Mia says, laughing. "All birds have two wings. But this bird has a long tail, too. Maybe it helps it fly."

The bird makes a loud noise and flies lower. It is a crow, and it is looking for food. It sees Mia and Ben's sandwiches on the bench. It is hungry and alert.

"Hey, that's our lunch!" Mia says, seeing the crow. She runs to the bench and waves her arms. "Go away, bird! Shoo, shoo!"

The crow is not scared of Mia. It lands on the bench and grabs a sandwich with its beak. It flies away with its prize, making more noise.

"Bad bird!" Ben says, running after Mia. He is angry and sad. He wanted to eat his sandwich.

Mia hugs Ben and tries to cheer him up. She still has her sandwich, and she decides to share it with him.

"It's okay, Ben. We can share my sandwich. And we can still count the birds. Maybe we will see a nicer bird, like a robin or a sparrow."

Ben smiles and nods. He likes Mia and he likes birds, even if some of them are mean. He takes a bite of the sandwich and looks at the sky. He hopes to see a bird with a bright color or a funny song. He counts its wings in his head.

Once, there was a little flower who lived in a garden. Everyday, the flower wanted to grow bigger and bigger. But it was hard, because the price of growing was very high.

Every day, the little flower tried so hard. It kept trying with all it's might. But the price was still very high.

One day, the flower found something. It found a secret that it had not known before. This secret was unknown to everyone. With this secret, the flower felt stronger. And so, the flower kept growing and growing.

Finally, the little flower was big and strong. It was so happy that it had found the secret. Now it doesn't have to worry about the high price anymore. It can keep growing forever.

Once there was an ancient girl called Emma. She lived in a big house with a garden full of flowers and trees. One morning, Emma woke up and decided to take a walk in the garden. As she walked, she noticed something strange. She saw an old book and a poem written on some paper.

Emma was so curious about what it could be. She read the poem aloud, and suddenly a strange creature appeared in the sky above her. The creature said to Emma, "you must give me the book and the poem or else something bad will happen." Emma was scared, so she gave the creature the ancient book and the strange poem.

The creature was happy and said, "Now it's time for me to take revenge." Then, he took the ancient book and poem and flew away, leaving Emma behind. It was too late, and there was nothing she could do.

When Emma's parents heard what had happened, they were so sad. Emma never saw the creature or the ancient book and poem again. From then on, Emma was always cautious whenever she was in her garden.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and make patterns. One day, they visit Ben's grandma. She lives in a big house with a garden.

"Hello, Anna and Ben," grandma says. "Do you want to see my flowers?"

"Yes, please," Anna and Ben say. They follow grandma to the garden. There are many flowers of different colors and shapes. Grandma tells them the names of the flowers.

"This is a rose. It is red and has a nice smell. This is a sunflower. It is yellow and very big. This is a daisy. It is white and has a circle in the middle."

Anna and Ben look at the flowers. They see patterns in the petals and leaves. They try to make patterns with their blocks.

"Look, grandma," Anna says. "I made a pattern like a rose. It has red blocks and green blocks."

"That's very pretty, Anna," grandma says.

"Look, grandma," Ben says. "I made a pattern like a sunflower. It has yellow blocks and brown blocks."

"That's very clever, Ben," grandma says.

Grandma smiles and hugs them. She is happy to see them. She gives them cookies and milk.

"Thank you, grandma," Anna and Ben say. "We like your flowers and your cookies."

"You're welcome, Anna and Ben," grandma says. "You are very good and sweet. I love you very much."

Anna and Ben love grandma too. They have a fun time visiting her. They make more patterns with their blocks and flowers. They are not serious. They are happy.

One day, a tall man went for a jog. He liked to run in the park. The sun was bright and the sky was blue. While he was jogging, he saw a little girl. The little girl was looking up at the sky.

The little girl said, "I want to catch a star." The tall man looked up and saw many stars in the sky. He wanted to help the little girl catch a star. So, he tried to jump high to reach a star. But he could not jump high enough.

The tall man and the little girl tried many times to catch a star. They jumped and jumped, but they could not reach the stars. They were very sad. The stars were too high in the sky. In the end, they could not catch a star, and they went home with no star.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish little boy named John. John was always running and jumping around, never listening to what his parents told him. One day, John decided to play in the garden, even though he was told not to. He was having so much fun that he didn't hear the alarm snap. 

John's mom had set the alarm to warn her of unwanted guests. But when it snapped, all John heard was a funny sound. He thought it was a game and he wanted to play it. He ran up to the fence and tried to snap the alarm, but nothing happened. He became angry and started to jump on the fence until it broke. 

Mom and dad were very angry with him and told him that it was very foolish to not listen to them. They said he had to say sorry for breaking the alarm and the fence. John was sad and he realised how foolish he had been. He said sorry and promised to always listen to his parents. From that day forward, he was always careful to obey mama and papa. 

The end.

Once there was a jolly little girl who was named Sue. Sue loved wheels and she had a little red tricycle. Every day, Sue would take her tricycle outside and throw her wheels in the air. She would giggle and laugh as the wheels went higher and higher until it finally came back down into her hands.

Sue's mom watched from the window, laughing and clapping. Sue loved when her mom watched and cheered. She would give her mom a big smile and threw her wheel again. She hoped that her wheel would go higher than ever before.

Then, one day, Sue discovered something amazing. She found out that she could throw the wheel so hard and so far that it would land all the way in the next yard. She was so excited and showed off her new trick to her mom. Her mom cheered and clapped even more.

Sue kept throwing the wheel and each time it would land farther than before. Sue was proud of her new trick and felt so jolly. She laughed and giggled with glee at her accomplishment.

The more Sue practiced, the better she became at throwing her wheel. She would spend all day long throwing her wheel and having lots of jolly fun. Sue was never happier than when she was throwing her wheel around and having a jolly time.

One day, Bob was feeling very miserable. He wanted to listen to music to make him feel better, so he printed out a special song. As he was printing the song, his mood began to lift and he started tapping his feet along to the rhythm.

When Bob got to the end of the song, he saw some unexpected notes. He started to get excited and couldn't wait to print the rest of it. When he finished printing out the music, there was a bright, cheerful tune playing. Bob sang along and started to feel much better.

Bob never expected that the miserable song he started to print out would turn into such a joyful one to sing along with. This experience taught Bob that no matter how miserable he felt, he should never give up hope â€“ there might be some unexpected happiness at the end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old and she had a pet puppy. The puppy was very playful and always running around the garden. But one day, Amy's mommy put up a fence in the garden made of wire. It was very high and the puppy was sad that she couldn't play as much anymore.

That night, Amy noticed the puppy outside the fence, trying to get back in the garden. She asked her mommy why the puppy couldn't get in, and her mommy said the fence was there to make sure the puppy behaved.

Amy felt frustrated. Even though she understood why the fence was there, she wanted to make her puppy happy. And so she decided to find a way for her puppy to still have fun.

The next day, Amy and her puppy went for a walk and she discovered a park with lots of wide open spaces and interesting toys. She brought the puppy to this park everyday so that it could have fun and use up its energy.

Amy was very happy that she had solved the problem. Her puppy was behaving and was happy again.

One day, a boy named Tim wanted to play a sport. He liked to run, jump, and have fun. Tim saw his friend, Sue, and asked her to play with him.

Sue looked troubled. She said, "I don't know how to play this sport, Tim." Tim smiled at her and said, "Don't worry, I will teach you. It's easy and fun!"

They started to play the sport. Tim showed Sue how to run and jump. They laughed and had a great time. Suddenly, they heard someone yell, "Help!"

Tim and Sue ran to see who needed help. It was their friend, Ben. He was stuck in a tree. Tim and Sue helped Ben get down from the tree. Ben was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim and Sue!"

Now, all three friends played the sport together. They ran, jumped, and had a lot of fun. They learned that playing together and helping each other made everything more fun.

Once upon a time there was a penny. The penny was shiny and was very special. It wanted to do something that would make it honest. 

It decided to give to someone who needed it. It looked around and soon found a little girl. Her name was Joy and she was 3 years old. She had no money, so the penny thought she would be a good person to include. 

The penny called to Joy, held out in its shiny hand, and said: "Hey Joy, do you want me? I'm honest and I want to help you." 

Joy was so happy when she saw the penny! She smiled wide and said: "Oh penny, thank you so much! I will use you to buy candy and treats!" 

The penny was so happy to hear that. She knew she did the right thing and now Joy had money to make her happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the mall with her mommy. The mall was big and bright, but Lily was scared of the dark. She held her mommy's hand tightly and walked fast.

Lily saw a toy that she wanted. It was a big, fluffy teddy bear. She asked her mommy to buy it for her. Her mommy said no, but promised to buy it for her on their way back. Lily was happy and forgot about her fear of the dark.

On their way back, the mall was dark and quiet. Lily held her mommy's hand tightly again. Suddenly, she saw a man with a scary mask. She was scared, but her mommy told her not to worry. It was just a man in a costume.

Finally, they reached the toy store and Lily got her teddy bear. She hugged it tightly and felt safe. She realized that even though the mall was dark and scary, she was brave and had fun with her mommy.

One day Lilah saw something black and little in the corner of her room. She walked over to it and saw that it was a little black mouse. The mouse was standing on its back legs, looking around.

Lilah smiled and said hello to the mouse. The mouse didn't say anything, but it looked at her with its little black eyes.

Lilah decided to play a game with the mouse. Both of them stood up on their back legs and tried to see who could stay up the longest. It was a lot of fun for both of them!

At last, the mouse had to give up. All of the standing had made it very tired. It was time for both of them to go to sleep.

Lilah said goodnight to the mouse, then she got into bed and went to sleep.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run on the grass. They saw a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. The dog was friendly and wagged his tail. He came to Ben and Lily and licked their faces.

"Hello, doggy!" Ben said. He petted the dog's head and ears. "You are soft and warm."

"Can we hug him, mom?" Lily asked. She loved animals and wanted to cuddle the dog.

"Yes, you can, but be gentle," mom said. She smiled and watched her children hug the dog. The dog seemed to like it too. He made a happy sound in his throat.

Then they heard a deep voice calling the dog's name. It was the dog's owner, a man with a hat and a beard. He came to the park and saw Ben and Lily with his dog.

"Hi, there. I see you met Rex. He's a good boy, isn't he?" the man said.

"Yes, he is. We like him. He's friendly and soft," Ben said.

"We hugged him. He licked us," Lily said.

The man laughed and thanked Ben and Lily for being nice to his dog. He said they could play with Rex anytime they wanted. He put a leash on Rex and said goodbye.

"Bye, Rex. Bye, man," Ben and Lily said. They waved and watched them leave.

"Did you have fun, kids?" mom asked.

"Yes, mom. We had fun. We made a new friend," Ben and Lily said. They hugged mom and told her about Rex. Mom hugged them back and said she was proud of them. They walked home together, happy and tired.

One night, two brave animals were walking through a dark forest. The first animal was a big, strong bear. The second animal was a small, alert owl. 
The owl said, "The trees are so dark here. I can barely see!"
The bear said, "Don't be scared, little owl. I'm here with you."
The owl said, "Thank you, bear. I feel safer with you here."
Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. The bear started to tremble. He said, "Let's leave this place! Quickly!" 
The owl got alert and flapped its wings. Together, they ran through the forest until they emerged into the night sky, safe and sound. 
The bear hugged the owl and said, "We did it! We made it out of there together." 
The owl smiled and said, "Yes, we did." 
The two animals laughed happily. From then on, they were the best of friends.

Lily was a princess who had a big crown. She liked to wear it all the time and show it to everyone. She was very spoiled and did not like to share or be nice.

One day, she went to the park with her nanny. She saw some other children playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, but she did not want to take off her crown. She ran to the children and said, "Give me the ball! I am a princess and I can have whatever I want!"

The children did not like Lily. They said, "No, you cannot have the ball. You are rude and selfish. Go away!"

Lily was angry and tried to grab the ball. But she tripped and fell on the ground. Her crown flew off her head and landed in a puddle. It got dirty and wet.

Lily started to cry. She was very sad and scared. She worried that her crown was ruined and that her daddy would be mad at her. She said, "Help me! Help me! My crown is broken!"

The nanny came and picked up Lily. She said, "Don't worry, Lily. Your crown is not broken. It is just dirty. We can clean it and dry it. But you need to learn a lesson. You cannot be so spoiled and mean. You need to share and be nice. Then maybe the other children will play with you."

Lily nodded and said, "I'm sorry, nanny. I will try to be better. Can we go home and clean my crown?"

The nanny said, "Yes, we can. But first, you need to say sorry to the other children and give them back their ball."

Lily did as the nanny said. She said sorry and gave back the ball. The other children smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. Maybe next time you can play with us."

Lily smiled too and said, "Maybe I can. Thank you for being nice to me."

She held the nanny's hand and went home with her crown. She hoped that her daddy would not be mad at her. She also hoped that she would make some friends at the park. She decided to be less spoiled and more nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, they found a big slide and started to slide down it. Tweet was very happy and felt very lively.

Suddenly, Tweet saw a dove sitting on a nearby tree. The dove looked very sad. Tweet and his friends went to talk to the dove and found out that she had lost her baby bird. Tweet and his friends decided to help the dove find her baby bird.

They searched and searched until they found the baby bird hiding in a bush. The dove was very happy and thanked Tweet and his friends. They all went back to the slide and continued to play, feeling very happy and lively.

One day, a young boy and his mom went for a drive in their car. On the way, they saw a group of people marching down the street! The boy was very curious. He asked his mom what was going on.

His mom explained, "The people are marching because they want to make things better for everyone."

The boy thought that was a wonderful idea, so he asked his mom if they could march too. She smiled and said, "Yes, we can!"

The young boy and his mom jumped out of their car and joined the march. Everyone was very friendly and waved as they walked. They marched together for a long time and soon they arrived at their destination. 

The boy and his mom looked around and saw lots of other people who had also joined the march. It made the boy feel very happy and proud. 

His mom gave him a big hug and said, "I'm so proud of you for marching today!"

The little boy smiled and said, "Me too!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the rain. One day, Timmy found a plastic toy in the mud. It was wet and dirty, but Timmy didn't mind. He took the toy inside to show his mom. 

"Look, Mommy!" Timmy said as he held up the toy. "I found it outside in the rain. It's all wet!" 

Timmy's mom smiled and wiped the toy clean. She put it on a shelf to display it. Timmy was so happy that his toy was now dry and on display for everyone to see.

Mildly, Linda and Tom united together in the same place. They felt excited about the adventure that was about to come. Tom had a big bag full of toys in his hands. Linda was holding a lunchbox full of yummy treats. As the two friends explored their destination, they giggled and laughed. The place was full of hidden surprises, like colorful flowers and tall trees. They played little hide-and-seek and laughed when they found each other. At the end of the day, Linda and Tom were tired but happy. They knowing they were united together, they hugged each other goodnight and went off to dream sweet dreams.

Lily and Max were very happy. They moved to a new house with Mom and Dad. They had many boxes to unpack. They wanted to see their toys and books.

They found a big box in their room. It had a label that said "Lily and Max". They opened the box and saw many things. They saw their dolls, cars, puzzles, and crayons. They also saw a cord.

"What is this?" Lily asked, holding the cord.

"It is a cord for the lamp," Max said. "We need it to make light."

"Where do we put it?" Lily asked.

Max looked around the room. He saw a plug on the wall. He walked to the plug with the cord. He tried to put the cord in the plug, but it was too high. He jumped, but he could not reach it.

"Help me, Lily," Max said.

Lily came to help Max. She stood on a chair and gave him a boost. Max stretched his arm and pushed the cord in the plug. The lamp turned on and made light.

"Yay, we did it!" Lily and Max cheered.

They were very successful. They unpacked the box and made light. They hugged each other and smiled. They liked their new room and their new house. They were very happy.

Once there was a little girl who was very tired and needed to go to sleep. She curled up into her soft bed and closed her eyes. The room was very peaceful and quiet. She felt so nice and cosy.

Just before she drifted off, her mum came in with a delicious cookie. She thanked her mum and took a big bite. It was so yummy that she finished it in no time.

Now feeling full and peaceful, she had no trouble going to sleep. She lay her head down and soon she was sleeping soundly. 

She had the most beautiful dreams of cookies and peaceful places. When morning came she woke up feeling very happy and refreshed.

Mary was a cheerful girl. She rode her bike all day with her friends. But her mom wanted Mary to be safe, so she wanted Mary to wear a helmet. Mary didn't understand why she had to wear the helmet, but she was a good girl and did it anyway.

One day, Mary's mom showed her a video of a bike accident. In the video, a girl had a bad accident and was very hurt. Mary was scared and started to cry. 

Her mom hugged her and told her that it was okay. She said that if the girl had been wearing a helmet, she wouldn't have been hurt. Mary understood then why she needed to wear the helmet when she rode her bike.

Mary was happy that she now understood why the helmet was important. She put her helmet on and rode her bike with her friends again. She was a cheerful girl, who was safe and could enjoy riding her bike.

Once upon a time, there was a crack outside in the grass. Two little bunnies were hopping through the meadow and they noticed it. One got curious and hopped over to have a look. The bunny felt something yucky on his feet and he quickly realized it was a disgusting slimy goo that was oozing out of the crack.

The bunny was so disgusted he hopped away to forget about what happened. The other bunny was having a lot of fun playing, but soon he forgot about his friend and hopped away.

The first bunny was all alone, but he eventually found another crack and he hopped over to have a look. This time, there was a surprise waiting for him! The crack was filled with delicious carrots and sweet berries.

The bunny enjoyed his feast and was soon hopping with joy. He had forgotten all about the disgusting slimy goo and was so happy to have found a delicious snack!

Jen and Ben were twins who liked to play in the dirt. They made mud pies and castles and pretended they were chefs and kings. One day, they found a big pile of dirt that was very smelly. Jen said, "What is this? It smells bad." Ben said, "Maybe it is a special dirt that can improve our mud pies. Let's try it."

They took some of the smelly dirt and mixed it with water and grass. They made a big mud pie and put it on a plate. They were very proud of their work. They decided to give it to their mom as a surprise. They ran inside the house and said, "Mom, we made you something. Come and see."

Mom followed them outside and saw the mud pie. She smiled and said, "Wow, that looks very nice. What is it?" Jen and Ben said, "It is a mud pie. We used a special dirt that can improve it. Try it, mom. It is yummy." Mom was curious and took a bite of the mud pie. She spit it out and said, "Blech! This is not mud. This is poop! Where did you get this dirt?"

Jen and Ben pointed to the pile of smelly dirt. Mom looked closer and saw a sign that said, "Warning: Dog poop. Do not touch." She realized that the twins had used dog poop to make their mud pie. She was very angry and said, "Jen and Ben, this is very naughty and gross. You could get sick from this. Go to your room and wash your hands and mouth. No more playing in the dirt for a week."

Jen and Ben felt very sorry and ashamed. They had tried to improve their mud pie, but they had made a big mistake. They wished they had not used the smelly dirt. They learned a hard lesson that day. The end.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl named Jane. She loved playing outdoors in the sunshine. One day, she went to walk along the beach. She stumbled across something curious - an empty sea! Jane could not believe her eyes. 

She took a few steps closer to the sea and saw a small fish caught in a net. Without hesitation, she jumped in and started trying to free the little fish.

"What are you doing?" asked a voice behind her.

Jane turned around and saw a friendly old man.

"I'm trying to rescue the fish," she said.

The old man smiled. "You're a brave girl!"

Together they managed to rescue the fish, set it free back into the sea, and Jane went home a happy girl.

Once upon a time, there was a man called Bob. Bob was honest and kind and he always told the truth.

One day, Bob was walking through the forest when he saw a log on the ground. It seemed strange so he decided to take a closer look. Bob noticed there was something written on the log. He squinted and read, "If you tell the truth then good things will happen". 

Bob smiled and spoke aloud, "I always tell the truth so maybe something good is about to happen". 

Bob took the log home and kept it safe. Every day he tried to think of good things to do because telling the truth was always important to Bob.

Eventually, Bob heard about a poor family who needed help. He decided to give them some food and money so they could have a better life. 

As soon as Bob arrived at the family's house, the father said, â€œThank you for being so honest and kind". Bob just smiled and thought to himself that the log seemed right. Good things happen when you tell the truth.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Abigail. She was very helpless, and she wanted some coins. One day, she found a large bag of coins in the park. She was so delighted! Abigail quickly grabbed some coins, ready to treat herself.

But then, a mean boy came along. He saw the helpless little girl with coins, and wanted to spoil her fun. The mean boy snatched all the coins away and ran off.

Abigail felt very upset. She wanted to get back the coins so badly, but she was too helpless to get them back. So she sadly went home.

The next day, Abigail returned to the park, hoping the mean boy would be gone. But he was still there! But then, Abigail had an idea. She quickly grabbed some rocks, and threw them at the mean boy. The boy was so scared, he ran away and dropped Abigail's coins.

Abigail was so happy - she got her coins back! She filled her pockets with the coins, feeling very proud of herself. From then on, Abigail never let anyone spoil her fun again!

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They saw many flowers and bugs and birds. Lily saw a daisy that was very thin. She ran to it and picked it up.

"Look, Tom, look!" she said. "I found a thin daisy. It is not like the other daisies. It is special."

Tom came to see the thin daisy. He smiled and nodded. He liked the thin daisy too. He pointed to another flower that was big and red.

"Look, Lily, look!" he said. "I found a big flower. It is not like the other flowers. It is special."

Lily came to see the big flower. She smiled and nodded. She liked the big flower too. She pointed to a bug that was green and shiny.

"Look, Tom, look!" she said. "I found a green bug. It is not like the other bugs. It is special."

Tom came to see the green bug. He smiled and nodded. He liked the green bug too. He pointed to a bird that was blue and yellow.

"Look, Lily, look!" he said. "I found a blue bird. It is not like the other birds. It is special."

Lily came to see the blue bird. She smiled and nodded. She liked the blue bird too. They held their special things and looked at each other.

"We are lucky," they said. "We have special things. We are special too."

Lily and Tom are playing in the garden. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to see what is under the tree.

"Can we lift the tree?" Lily asks Tom.

"No, the tree is too heavy. But maybe we can lift a root," Tom says. He points to a brown thing that sticks out of the ground.

Lily and Tom hold the root and pull hard. They lift the root a little bit. They see something moving under the root.

"Look, a mouse!" Lily says. She sees a small, gray animal with a long tail. The mouse looks scared.

"Hello, mouse. Don't be afraid. We are nice," Tom says. He smiles at the mouse.

The mouse sees that Lily and Tom are not mean. It comes out of the hole. It sniffs Lily's hand. Lily pets the mouse gently.

"You are so cute, mouse. Do you want to be our friend?" Lily asks.

The mouse nods. It squeaks happily. Lily and Tom laugh. They play with the mouse in the garden. They are happy. They have a new friend.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends; one was a pig called Percy and the other was a rabbit called Ralph. They loved playing in the garden together. One day, they decided to do something special. 

So, they ran around the garden together, covering all sorts of things with leaves. Percy made a leafy blanket and Ralph covered the garden stool with them. They had so much fun!

Then, Ralph hopped to the pond and noticed that it was getting a bit filthy. He wanted to find a way to clean it. Suddenly, he remembered an old bucket he had seen in the shed earlier. He quickly hopped to the shed, grabbed the bucket and went back to the pond. Together with Percy, they covered the pond with water from the bucket. They kept doing this until the pond was clean again. 

By the time they were done, the sun was setting and it was time for them to go home. The two friends were very proud of their hard work and had a great time.

Jim and his family lived in a nice house. Jim had a mom, a dad, and a little sister, who was three years old.

One day, Jim's little sister asked "Who do I belong to?" Jim looked at his parents, then said, "You belong to us! You are part of our family." 

His little sister smiled. Seeing her happy made him happy, too.

Jim said, "We can all work together to make our family successful." The little sister said, "Yes! Let's do it!" 

Jim's parents smiled and said, "You three make us very proud of our family." 

Jim, his sister, and parents went to the park and had a lot of fun, on this day and many more days. Together they all belonged to a wonderful family.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to play outside and chase squirrels. One day, Spot's owner brought home a newspaper. Spot was very curious and wanted to play with the newspaper. His owner warned him not to chew it because it was important. Spot listened and didn't chew the newspaper. Instead, he watched his owner read it with an enthusiastic look on his face. Spot thought the newspaper must be very interesting. From that day on, Spot would always get excited when his owner brought home the newspaper.

Lily and Ben went to the store with Mom. They wanted to buy a toy. Mom said they could choose one toy each. Lily and Ben were happy.

They looked at many toys. Lily saw a doll with a pink dress. She liked it. She said, "Mom, can I have this doll?" Mom said, "Yes, you can. That's a nice doll." Lily hugged the doll.

Ben saw a car with big wheels. He liked it. He said, "Mom, can I have this car?" Mom said, "Yes, you can. That's a cool car." Ben grabbed the car.

They went to the counter to pay. There was a man there. He was rude. He said, "Hurry up, I don't have all day." He took the toys and threw them in a bag. He did not say thank you or smile.

Lily and Ben were sad. They did not like the rude man. Mom was angry. She said, "That was not nice. You should be polite to your customers." The man did not care. He said, "Whatever. Next!"

Mom took the bag and said, "Come on, kids. Let's go home. We don't need to stay here." Lily and Ben followed Mom. They held their toys. They hoped the rude man would learn to be nice. They were glad they had each other.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they find a big gray hat in the closet. It is their dad's hat. Ben wants to wear the hat. He puts it on his head. He says, "Look at me! I am a big man!"

Sam wants to wear the hat too. He says, "No, Ben! It is my turn! Give me the hat!" He tries to pull the hat from Ben's head. Ben holds the hat tight. He says, "No, Sam! It is mine! Go away!"

They start to fight. They push and pull and shout. The hat falls to the floor. They both run to get it. They bump their heads. They cry.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the closet. She sees the hat and the boys. She says, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting? This is not your hat. This is dad's hat. You should not take his things without asking. You should share and be nice."

She picks up the hat. She puts it on her head. She says, "Now, I am a big man!" She smiles. The boys stop crying. They laugh. They say, "No, mom! You are a big woman! You are funny!"

Mom hugs the boys. She says, "I love you, Ben and Sam. You are my big boys. But you are still little. You have a lot to learn and gain. Now, let's put the hat back and play something else."

Molly and Grandma were walking through the town. Molly was very sad and she kept looking down. Grandma asked her why she was feeling so blue. Molly said, "My toy is broken and now I'm feeling so guilty, too."

Grandma said, "My dear, I know something that will make you feel much better. I know of a special place where broken toys can be traded."

Molly's eyes lit up. She said, "Really? Can we go there now?" Grandma smiled and said, "Yes, but we must hurry!"

They soon arrived at the toy store. Molly was amazed by all the different toys she saw. She chose a brand new doll and couldn't wait to take it home.

Grandma asked, "Are you happy now, sweetie?" Molly nodded and gave her a big hug. She said, "Thank you so much, Grandma. I'm so happy!"

Grandma hugged her back and wiped away a few of Molly's tears of joy. Molly was so relieved, she was no longer feeling guilty, and the sadness was all gone. Grandma smiled and said, "That's what trade is all about!"

Once upon a time, there was a big, fat cat named Whiskers. Whiskers loved to play outside, but one day he got lost. He wandered around for a long time until he found himself at a big stadium.

Whiskers was scared and didn't know what to do. But then he saw a kind man who worked at the stadium. The man saw Whiskers and knew he needed help. He picked up Whiskers and took him to a safe place.

Whiskers was so happy that the man saved him. He purred and cuddled up next to the man. From that day on, Whiskers knew that he was safe and loved.

Once upon a time there was a little guy named Rex. He was only three years old, but he was very brave. One day, Rex was playing in the backyard and he noticed something zipping around in the sky. He looked closer and realised it was a cell! It was so cool and it was zipping back and forth with such a flexible flight pattern. Rex wanted to have a go at flying it, so he ran to the garage to get a ladder. He climbed up as high as he could, grabbed the cell and hoped on. He zipped through the air faster and faster. Rex had so much fun that day and he couldn't wait to go zipping around with his cell again the next day.

Once upon a time there lived a family in a small town. The family had two small kids named Tommy and Jenna. Tommy and Jenna were very curious about the town and wanted to explore it.

One day, Tommy and Jenna's mom said, "You can go and explore the town, as long as it is regular. Come back before night."

Tommy and Jenna could not wait and they went out to explore the town. They went to the park and saw many new sights. They saw the fountain, the trees, and the playground. It was so much fun.

On their way home, Tommy and Jenna heard music coming from a small cafe. They wanted to try it and see what it was. Tommy and Jenna went inside the cafe and listened to the music. They loved the music so much that they started to dance.

The family had a great experience exploring the town and they promised to do it again. Tommy and Jenna knew that by trying new things, they would always find something exciting!

Once upon a time there was a farmer who wanted to store a lot of wheat. So he went to the store and bought lots of wheat, and he stored it in a big barn. The farmer was so happy! He went around telling everybody about his new store of wheat. 

But after a while the farmer got bored with just storing the wheat. He wanted to do something fun. So he took down the old barn and he built a playground. Now he could have fun playing with the wheat. He could even use it to make a big wheat castle when he was feeling bored. 

The farmer was very happy with his playground. He built it so high, he could almost see the sun and moon! The farmer played in his wheat playground every day and was no longer bored.

Once upon a time there was a mama bear and a baby bear. Mama bear was very hungry, so she said to her baby bear, "Let's go eat some stuff!"

The two bears walked to a big tree and saw that it had something tasty inside. Mama bear licked her lips and said, "Let's open it and see what's inside!"

Baby bear was very excited, and he said, "I love to eat stuff! Let's do it!" So mama bear and baby bear opened the tree and found a big yummy honeycomb. They both ate the sweet stuff until it was all gone.

Mama bear said to her baby bear, "That was so yummy! Thank you for helping me find it."

Baby bear smiled and said, "We make a great team! Let's do it again soon!" And so they did, and they ate lots more yummy stuff together.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bossy bird named Betty. Betty lived in a big nest in a tall tree. She loved to tell the other birds what to do.

One day, a new bird named Tim came to the tree. Betty told Tim to help her fix the nest. But Tim did not want to help. He said, "I disagree. I want to play."

Betty got mad at Tim. She told him to leave the tree. But the other birds liked Tim. They told Betty she was too bossy. They all played together and had lots of fun.

In the end, Betty learned that it was not nice to be bossy. She joined the other birds and they all played happily together. The birds became good friends and lived happily in their big nest.

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there was a funny lion named Leo. Leo liked to play with his friends, the monkey and the elephant. They played games all day and had lots of fun.

One day, Leo and his friends saw a fire in the jungle. They were scared and did not know what to do. The monkey said, "We need to put out the fire! Let's all work together!"

Leo used his strong roar to blow the fire away, while the elephant used his long nose to spray water on the fire. The monkey threw dirt on the fire to help put it out. They all worked together, and soon the fire was gone.

After the fire was out, the friends were very happy. They knew they had done a good job. Leo said, "We make a great team! Let's promise to always help each other." The monkey and the elephant agreed, and they all played happily ever after.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a wide bench near the slide. They run to the bench and sit on it.

"Look, a bird!" Mia says. She points to a small bird on the grass. The bird has a red head and a yellow belly.

"Wow, it is pretty!" Tom says. He wants to see the bird better. He gets off the bench and walks to the bird.

"Tom, be careful!" Mia says. She knows the bird is shy. She stays on the bench and watches Tom.

Tom is very quiet. He moves slowly to the bird. He reaches out his hand. He wants to touch the bird. He pokes the bird with his finger.

"Tweet!" The bird is scared. It flies away. It goes to a tree.

"Tom, you made the bird go away!" Mia says. She is sad. She likes the bird.

"Sorry, Mia. I just wanted to say hello to the bird." Tom says. He is sorry too. He goes back to the bench.

"It is okay, Tom. Maybe the bird will come back later." Mia says. She smiles at Tom. They are still friends.

They sit on the bench and wait for the bird. They see other things in the park. They see a dog, a ball, and a flower. They have fun. They are happy.

Tommy and his mommy went to the pool. The pool was nice and warm. The water was gentle and it sparkled in the sun. Tommy really enjoyed playing in the water.

Mommy showed Tommy different things in the pool. He tried to swim with gentle moves like a fish, and then floated on his back. He laughed and laughed with joy.

He also had fun playing games. He splashed in the water and kicked with his little feet. Mommy asked him to be careful and gentle, but he was having so much fun he didn't always listen! 

By the end of the day, Tommy was so tired from all the swimming and playing. He was so happy that he'd been able to enjoy the pool.

Once upon a time, there was a lively prince who loved to play jokes on his friends. One day, the prince's friend, a cute little rabbit, came to visit him. The rabbit said, "Prince, do you want to play a game with me?"

The prince replied, "Yes, I love games! What game do you want to play?"

The rabbit said, "Let's play a joke on your cook. We can put a fake spider in his soup and see what he does!"

The prince laughed and said, "That's a funny joke! Let's do it!"

They put the fake spider in the soup and waited for the cook to come. When the cook saw the spider, he jumped and screamed. Then he realized it was just a joke and laughed with the prince and the rabbit.

From that day on, the prince and the rabbit loved to play jokes on their friends and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her favorite toy, a red string. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her toys and put them away. Lily didn't want to stop playing with her string and felt anxious about putting it away. 

Lily's mom said, "Lily, it's time to put your toys away now." 

Lily replied, "But I don't want to put my string away. I feel anxious without it." 

Her mom said, "I understand, but it's important to clean up after ourselves. Let's put your string away and we can play with it again later." 

Lily reluctantly agreed and shut her toy box with a sigh. Later, when Lily wanted to play with her string again, she felt happy to see that it was still there and she learned that sometimes it's okay to put things away for a little while. The end. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to clean up after ourselves and sometimes we need to put things away for a little while, but they will still be there when we want to play with them again.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit who was very rude. He never said please or thank you, or even hello. One day the rabbit decided to slide down the hill in the park. As he slid down, he saw a little girl sitting at the bottom. 

The rabbit stopped at the bottom and said, "Why are you so rude?"  

The little girl replied, "I'm not rude. I'm just sitting here enjoying the day." 

The rabbit thought for a moment and then said, "Well, if you don't mind, I'm going to slide back up the hill and do it again." 

The little girl smiled and said, "Sure, that sounds like fun!" So the rabbit went back up the hill and slid down again. The little girl laughed as the rabbit went back up again. They played the game for a while, until the rabbit was too tired to go up the hill one more time. 

The little girl thanked the rabbit for the fun game. The rabbit was shocked by the little girl's politeness. He thanked her in return and then waved goodbye as he hopped away.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Mark. Mark was three years old and loved to have fun. One day, he was playing outside when he found a journal. The journal was sweet. When Mark opened the journal he let out a big scream!

Mark was so happy that he kept screaming and jumping up and down. He jumped so high that his neighbours came over to see what was happening. When they saw the journal, they asked Mark to show them what was inside.

Mark said thank you and opened the journal. Inside the journal, he saw many colourful pictures and stories. He was so excited, he screamed again. His friends and neighbours all laughed because it was so cute.

Mark thanked everyone for helping him find the journal. He hugged everyone goodbye and went back inside with his sweet journal. He was so happy to have found it!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big bush with red berries. They want to pick some berries and eat them.

"Look, Ben, berries!" Anna says. "They are red and sweet. Let's get some."

"OK, Anna, but be careful. Some berries are bad. They can make you sick." Ben says.

They go to the bush and pick some berries. They put them in a basket. They find a shady spot under a tree. They sit down and eat some berries. They are yummy.

"Anna, do you want some more berries?" Ben asks. He has some left in his basket.

"No, thank you, Ben. I am full. You can have them." Anna says. She is kind. She likes to share.

"Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend." Ben says. He is happy. He likes to play with Anna.

They smile at each other. They are friends. They like to play in the park. They like to eat berries. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. She wanted to do something special, so she decided to learn how to ride a bike. Ellie tried and tried, but she kept falling down. One day, she finally succeeded! She rode her bike all the way to the store to buy a newspaper.

The newspaper was very large, and Ellie had trouble carrying it home. She asked her friend, a small mouse named Max, for help. Max was happy to help, and together they carried the large newspaper back to Ellie's house.

Ellie was so proud of herself for learning how to ride a bike and for getting the large newspaper home with Max's help. She knew that she could succeed at anything she put her mind to with a little bit of practice and help from her friends.

A young boy was unpackinng his suitcase. Inside it was a castle! He was so excited to put it together. He quickly started sorting out the pieces and found all the special parts he needed. With help from his mom and dad, the young boy soon finished building the castle. It was beautiful, with towers and doors and windows. The castle was even big enough to have a tea party inside. The boy was so proud of his work!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who was very polite. He loved to watch his mommy bake in the kitchen.

Today, his mommy was baking some toast. She put the bread in the toaster and then waited. Soon, the toaster beeped and out popped the hot toast.

The little boy loved the smell of the toast. He was so excited to eat it! His mommy smiled and served him the toast with some butter.

The little boy ate the toast with a big smile on his face. He said "Thank you, mommy" in a polite voice. His mommy was so proud of her little boy. She gave him a big hug and said "You're very welcome!". 

The little boy was so happy. He loved when his mommy would bake toast for him!

Once there was a little girl. She liked to run. She saw a red road and wanted to run on it. The road was long, so she ran very fast. She liked the way the wind whistled in her ears. Suddenly, she saw a big red truck coming down the road. She ran out of the way so that she could be safe. She laughed with glee and kept running. She ran and ran until she got to the end of the road. There was a big, red house there and she ran into the yard. She had a lot of fun playing there. When it was time to go home she waved goodbye to the red house and started running back down the road. She thought about how happy she was and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a stable. Inside the stable were two ponies. The ponies were happy and enjoyed jumping around their home.

One day, one of the ponies made a mistake and knocked over a bucket. The other pony got mad and started to yell.

The yelling frightened the other pony. He ran outside and didn't come back. The pony inside the stable knew he had made the other one angry and he felt very sorry.

For days and days, the pony was alone. He missed his friend and hoped that he would come back. Then one day, he heard a familiar voice. It was his friend!

It turned out his friend had been looking for new places to play. The two ponies were so happy to be together again and they hugged each other and jumped around the stable. From then on, the two ponies stayed together and were never scared or mad at each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a colorful folder with her all the time. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She met a little boy named Max. Max asked, "What's in your folder?" Lily shrugged and said, "Just some papers." Max asked if he could see them. Lily opened her folder and showed Max her drawings. Max said, "Wow, your drawings are so pretty!" Lily smiled and said, "Thank you!"

Ben and Lily were playing in their room. They had many toys and books and pictures. Lily liked to look at the pictures in the frames on the wall. She saw one of her and Ben when they were babies. They were smiling and hugging.

"Look, Ben, this is us!" Lily said, pointing at the frame.

Ben came over and looked. He did not like the picture. He thought he looked silly and small. He wanted to be big and strong.

"I don't like this picture. It is bad. Take it off the wall!" Ben said, grabbing the frame.

"No, Ben, don't! It is a nice picture. Mommy and Daddy gave it to us. They love us!" Lily said, holding the frame.

Ben and Lily pulled and pushed. The frame fell to the floor. It broke. The glass cracked. The picture tore. Ben and Lily gasped.

They heard Mommy coming up the stairs. They were scared. They knew Mommy would be angry. They did not want to get in trouble.

"Quick, hide the frame!" Ben whispered.

"Where?" Lily asked.

"Under the bed!" Ben said.

They pushed the frame under the bed. They hoped Mommy would not see it. They sat on the bed and pretended to read a book.

Mommy opened the door. She smiled at Ben and Lily.

"Hello, my sweeties. What are you doing?" Mommy asked.

"We are reading a book, Mommy. It is a good book. It has animals and colors and numbers." Lily said.

"That's wonderful, my darlings. I'm so proud of you. Can I see the book?" Mommy asked.

Ben and Lily showed Mommy the book. Mommy looked at the book. She saw something shiny under the bed. She frowned.

"What is that under the bed?" Mommy asked.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They felt guilty and sorry.

"Mommy, we are sorry. We broke the frame. We had a fight. We did not mean to. Please don't be mad." Lily said.

Mommy sighed. She bent down and pulled out the frame. She saw the broken glass and the torn picture. She felt sad and angry.

"Ben, Lily, this is not okay. This is a very bad thing. You broke the frame. You ruined the picture. You lied to me. You hurt each other. Why did you do that?" Mommy asked.

Ben and Lily hung their heads. They did not have a good answer. They knew they were wrong.

"Mommy, we are sorry. We love you. We love each other. We will not do it again. Please forgive us." Ben said.

Mommy looked at Ben and Lily. She saw their tears and their remorse. She loved them very much. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I love you too, Ben and Lily. I forgive you. But you have to learn from this. You have to be careful with your things. You have to be kind to each other. You have to tell me the truth. Do you understand?" Mommy asked.

"Yes, Mommy, we understand. We will do better. Thank you, Mommy." Ben and Lily said.

Mommy smiled. She took the frame and the picture. She said she would try to fix them. She said they would talk more later. She said she was glad they were her children. She left the room.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They felt relieved and grateful. They hugged and said sorry. They decided to play nicely. They did not want to break anything else. They did not want to slap each other. They did not want to hide anything from Mommy. They wanted to be good.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who loved to go for walks. Every day he had the same routine. He would get dressed, put on a hat and make his way down the path.

On one particular day, he noticed two children playing in the dirt. He smiled and said a polite hello. The children waved back. He loved to see the children being so polite.

The old man had an idea. He took out a piece of paper from his pocket, and using a stick, he drew a path in the sand. It began from the children and spread out in different directions.

The children were so surprised and delighted by the old man's kindness. They thanked him for the path and waved goodbye. The old man smiled and waved back as he made his way down the path.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in the pool. They had a jolly time splashing and swimming with their toys. But one day, Tom wanted to lay on the big floaty and not share it with Lily.

"Tom, can I have a turn on the floaty?" Lily asked.

"No, it's mine. Go away!" Tom said.

Lily felt sad and angry. She tried to pull the floaty away from Tom, but he held on tight. They started to fight and yell.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. "You need to share and be kind to each other. If you can't play nicely, you have to get out of the pool."

Tom and Lily did not want to get out of the pool. They liked to swim and have fun. They looked at each other and felt sorry.

"Sorry, Lily. I was mean. You can have the floaty," Tom said.

"Sorry, Tom. I was rude. You can have it too," Lily said.

They hugged and smiled. They decided to share the floaty and take turns. They had a jolly time again.

Mom was happy to see them playing nicely. She said, "Good job, Tom and Lily. You learned to share and be kind. That's what makes a good swimmer and a good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a modest little girl who loved to sing. She loved to make up little poems and sing them. Every day, she woke up to sing her happy song.

One day, she decided to take her singing outside. She skipped and sang out loud as she went. The birds flew down to listen to her song. They twittered and chirped along with her.

The girl kept singing. Her voice was so sweet! The trees and the flowers enjoyed her singing too. They swayed and danced along with her. 

When the girl finished singing, she was so happy. She felt so proud! She waved goodbye to her friends and skipped off home, still singing her poem.

Once upon a time there was a tired little bear. He was tired because he'd been walking all day. â€œI wish I had someone to help me,â€ he thought. Little did he know, he wasn't alone!

Suddenly, a rabbit popped out from behind a tree. The bear was so surprised he almost snapped! â€œWhat are you doing here?â€ the bear asked.

â€œI'm here to help you,â€ the rabbit said. â€œBut only if you can tell me the truth.â€

The bear was confused. â€œWhat kind of truth?â€ he asked.

The rabbit said, â€œIf you want my help, you must promise to tell me why you're so tired.â€

The bear thought for a moment. Did he really want to tell the truth? He was scared of what might happen. But in the end, he decided to be brave. â€œI'm tired, because I've been walking all day looking for something. I don't know what it is,â€ he said.

The rabbit smiled. â€œThat's what I wanted to hear! Now, come with me and you'll find what you're looking for.â€ And so off they went, and together, the bear and the rabbit found what he was looking for.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Sally. Sally was very excited for her very first day at school. She heard that it was going to be noisy and full of fun adventures.
