Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play on her porch, which was painted purple. One day, Lily's friend called her on the phone and asked if she wanted to play outside. 

Lily said, "Yes, I want to play! Come over to my purple porch." 

Her friend replied, "Okay, I will come over soon." 

Lily waited on the porch for her friend to arrive. When her friend finally came, they played together and had lots of fun. They even found a purple flower in the garden. 

Lily said, "Look at this pretty purple flower!" 

Her friend said, "Wow, it's so beautiful." 

After they played for a while, Lily's friend had to go home. Lily said, "Goodbye, friend. Come play again soon!" 

Her friend replied, "I will call you later to make plans." 

Lily smiled and waved goodbye as her friend walked away. She was happy to have such a good friend to play with on her purple porch.

Once upon a time, there was a bird called Marty. Marty had soft and fluffy wings, and she liked to fly in the sky. One day, Marty flew near a skull. She was so scared and wanted to fly away, but when she looked closely she saw a big shiny coin in the skullâ€™s eye socket.

She was so curious that she flew down to take a closer look. It felt brave, but her heart was beating so fast. When she got close, she noticed a sparkle. She flew in and grabbed the shiny coin with her tiny beak.

Marty was so grateful for finding the coin. She thanked the skull, then held the coin close to her heart and flew away. Marty used the coin to buy nice things for her family, and she was very happy. She now believes that everything we need is right in front of us, just waiting to be found.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a special toy that she loved very much. One day, she went to play with it but she forgot where she put it. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it.

Lily's mom saw her looking sad and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she lost her toy and couldn't find it. Her mom helped her look for it and they finally found it under the bed. But when they picked it up, they saw that it had a leak and was broken.

Lily was sad that her toy was broken, but her mom told her not to worry. She said they could fix it and make it as good as new. They took the toy to a special place where it could be fixed. When they got it back, it was all fixed and the leak was gone. But Lily's mom had hidden a surprise inside the toy. When Lily played with it, she found a little note that said "I love you". Lily was so happy and hugged her mom tightly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run fast. One day, she was running so fast that she tripped and hurt her toe. It hurt a lot and she cried.

Her mom came over and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

"I hurt my toe," Lily said, still crying.

Her mom said, "Let's wash it and put a band-aid on it. We have to be slow and gentle so it doesn't hurt more."

Lily's mom washed her toe and put a band-aid on it. But the next day, Lily's toe was still hurting. They went to the doctor and found out that she had broken her toe. Lily had to wear a cast and couldn't run fast anymore. She was sad that she couldn't play like she used to.

Once upon a time there was a modern tree. It had many branches and one special branch in the middle. Every morning, a bird would come and mark the branch with its beak. Every day the bird got bigger and bigger and every day the branch got shorter and shorter. The modern tree was very proud of the bird; it was the most special thing in the tree's life.

The bird's markings became a symbol of protection and love. Everyone in the forest knew that the modern tree was the bird's home and they respected it more each day.

One day a storm came and knocked down the modern tree. All the branches were broken except one, the marked branch remained intact and out of the storm's grasp. The bird had marked the branch with an extra bit of care and love. Thanks to that, the branch and the bird survived.

The branch was a symbol of hope and protection in the forest. It showed that love always prevailed and that it was strong enough toweather any storm.

It was a sunny morning and a little girl was taking a walk with her puppy. Her puppy was very excited and pulled at the leash, but the girl was very gentle with him. Suddenly, they heard something and the puppy jumped, making the girl so clumsy that she dropped the leash.

"Oh no!" She said.

The puppy ran off, so the girl started running after him. She ran around the whole park, but she could not find him anywhere. She was about to cry when she finally saw him behind a bush. He was busy cleaning himself.

The girl was so relieved and ran to him. She hugged him tightly and said, "Please don't run away again. I was so scared!"

The puppy looked at her with his big eyes and gave her a big kiss. From then on, she never let go of his leash.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big lime tree. The tree has many green fruits.

"Look, limes!" Lila says. "I like limes. They are sour and yummy."

"Me too," Ben says. "Let's pick some."

They walk to the tree. But the tree is very tall. They cannot reach the limes.

"How can we get them?" Lila asks.

Ben has an idea. He sees a big stick on the ground. He picks it up.

"Maybe we can use this," he says. "I can poke the limes and make them fall."

He tries to poke a lime. But the stick is too short. He cannot touch the lime.

"Can you help me?" he asks Lila.

Lila nods. She holds the stick with Ben. They try to poke a lime together. But the stick is still too short.

They see a big rock near the tree. They have another idea.

"Maybe we can stand on the rock," Lila says. "Then we can be taller."

They walk to the rock. They put the stick on the rock. They climb on the rock. They hold the stick again.

They are nervous. The rock is high. They are afraid to fall.

"Be careful," Lila says.

"You too," Ben says.

They poke a lime. The lime moves. It falls to the ground.

"Yay, we did it!" they say.

They poke another lime. It falls too. They poke more limes. They make a pile of limes.

They are happy. They jump off the rock. They pick up the limes.

"Let's eat them," Lila says.

"OK," Ben says.

They peel the limes. They bite the limes. They make funny faces.

"Mmm, sour and yummy," they say.

They share the limes. They smile. They are friends.

Once there was a tiny fish named Sam. Sam wanted to explore the deep ocean. He swam around, looking at all of the beautiful things. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise.

He swam towards it and saw a whale with a big, deep voice. The whale said, â€œPlease help me. I need to reach the ship at the other side of the sea.â€

Sam was curious and asked the big whale, â€œHow can I help you?â€

The whale answered, â€œI need you to take this order to the ship so they can fulfill it.â€

Sam said â€œSure thing!â€ and swam away. He swam fast and far. He reached the ship and gave them the order.

The whale was so happy that Sam could help him. He said, â€œThank you for being brave and helping me reach the ship!â€ Sam smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™re welcome!â€ Then he swam back to the deep ocean and explored some more.

One day, there was a planet that wanted to sell something. It was so excited and it hoped that someone would buy it. But when the day came, nobody wanted to buy it. The planet was so sad and ashamed.

Suddenly, a little boy came. He looked at the planet and he said, "I want to buy it!" The planet couldn't believe it. It was so happy! The little boy bought the planet and took it with him.

The planet was happy that it had a good home. It was no longer ashamed of itself. The little boy loved the planet and they were very happy together. They were going to be best friends forever!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they go to the lake with their mom and dad. The lake is big and blue. They see some ducks and fish.

Anna and Ben want to feed the ducks. They have some bread. They break the bread into small pieces. They throw the pieces into the water. The ducks swim and eat the bread. Anna and Ben are happy.

But then, they see something strange. A big, round, yellow thing is floating on the water. It looks like a ball. Anna and Ben are confused. What is it? They ask their mom and dad.

Their mom and dad laugh. They tell Anna and Ben that it is a pumpkin. Someone put the pumpkin on the water for fun. They say that the pumpkin is very light. It does not weigh much. That is why it can float.

Anna and Ben are curious. They want to touch the pumpkin. They ask their mom and dad if they can go near it. Their mom and dad say yes, but they have to be careful. They have to wear life jackets. They have to hold their hands.

Anna and Ben put on their life jackets. They hold their mom and dad's hands. They walk to the edge of the water. They reach out to the pumpkin. They feel its smooth skin. They push it gently. It bobs up and down. They giggle.

Anna and Ben have fun with the pumpkin. They think it is funny. They wonder who put it there. They wonder if the ducks like it. They wonder if they can carve it for Halloween. They have many questions. They have a good day at the lake.

Once upon a time there was a friendly bear. He loved to go for long walks in the woods. So every day he would get dressed and go for a walk. 

One day, the friendly bear thought he should explore further than he had before. He walked and walked until he could not see the trees anymore. He started to feel scared. 

He noticed a big, scary lion standing in the middle of the path. The lion growled at the friendly bear and showed his big, sharp teeth. The friendly bear was so scared he started to run. 

But the lion was faster. He caught up to the friendly bear and devoured him. 

The friendly bear never went on another walk again.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the sunshine with his friends. But one day, the sky turned dark and it started to rain. Timmy's mommy told him it was time to go inside and wait for the storm to end.

Timmy didn't like the dark and the thunder made him scared. But his mommy hugged him and told him everything would be okay. They snuggled up on the couch and read books until the storm ended and the sun came back out.

After the storm ended, Timmy went outside to play with his friends again. They jumped in puddles and laughed and had so much fun. Timmy was happy that the dark and scary storm had ended and the sun was shining again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her yard. One day, her mom took her to the park to play. While they were walking, Lily saw a big, tall tree. It was so big that it made her feel small.

Lily's mom said, "Look at that cheerful tree, Lily. It's so big and strong!" Lily looked up at the tree and smiled.

Suddenly, Lily heard a little boy mention something to his mom. He said, "I want to climb that tree!" His mom said, "No, it's too dangerous. Maybe we can find a different tree to climb." Lily thought about it and said, "I know a smaller tree we can climb. It's over there!" The little boy was happy and they all went to climb the smaller tree together. They had so much fun playing together and making new friends.

Once there was a little boy named Jimmy. Jimmy loved to explore and try new things.One day he found a door that was shut. He knew he wasn't allowed to open it, so he just stood there. 

Jimmy decided to ask his mom if he could open the door. She said "Yes, you may open the door."

Jimmy opened the door and was surprised by what he found. Inside the room was a unique oat. It was a special oat that had interesting different colors. 

Jimmy was so excited to see the unique oat. He quickly shut the door again and ran to his mom to tell her what he had found. His mom was so proud of him for finding something so special. 

From then on, Jimmy went exploring every day, hoping to find something new and unique just like the oat!

Once there was a brave little girl. She loved to explore and try new things.
One day, she saw a big line of people. She asked her mom, "What's the line for?"
Her mom smiled and said, "It's a line to go to the park. Would you like to join it?"

The little girl was very brave and excited to join the line. She kept her head held high and shuffled along with the group of people.

When it was finally her turn she stepped up to the gate and said, "I'd like to come in please."
The guard smiled and said, "You must be very brave to be in this line."

The little girl felt proud and smiled back. Then she skipped into the park, feeling excited for all that the day ahead held.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day she wanted to go on a search of her own. She grabbed her bag and found a hat to keep her head warm. Then, she stepped outside.

The little girl laid her bag on the ground and began to look around. She saw some flowers and a bright sun in the sky. She heard the birds singing and the sound of the wind.

Next, the little girl laid down on the ground and looked up at the sky. She noticed the fluffy clouds and the big blue sky. She closed her eyes and felt the warm sun on her skin.

The little girl enjoyed being outside and looked for rocks and bugs to explore. As the sun began to set, she laid her head down and fell asleep on the ground. The little girl had a wonderful day and look forward to many more search adventures.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a cat named Zigzag. Zigzag loved to eat tasty food. One day, Zigzag saw a big, tasty cake on a table. It was so pretty and smelled so good.

Zigzag wanted the cake, but there was a little dog named Spot guarding it. Spot said, "This is my cake! You can't have it!" Zigzag knew he had to fight Spot to get the cake.

Zigzag and Spot fought for the cake. They ran around the room, chasing each other. Finally, Zigzag jumped high and grabbed the cake with his paws. Spot was sad, but Zigzag said, "We can share the cake, Spot!"

Spot and Zigzag ate the tasty cake together. They became good friends and promised to share all their food from then on. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She left the house early one morning to go visit her favorite vendor in town. When she arrived all she found was an empty market with no sign of her beloved vendor. She was so sad and a tear ran down her cheek. 

Just then Jane heard a voice call out to her. "Where did you think I was little one?" 

Jane looked up and saw her vendor standing right there. She ran up to him and hugged him tight. "I missed you!" she said. 

The vendor hugged her back and said, "I've been working really hard to make the market better, so I had to leave for a while. I'm glad you came back to see me!" 

Jane and the vendor shared a hug and Jane said goodbye. She went home feeling happy that she had found her beloved vendor again.

The sun was shining. Tom was happy. He was in the garden and he had lots of fun things to play with.

He grabbed a bucket and filled it with water. He beamed with joy as he poured the water into a tub. It made a splash and a sound.

Tom had fun splashing about in the tub. He made lots of different sounds. He felt so safe and a big smile spread across his face.

When he had enough, he stepped out and poured out the water from the tub. All that was left was laughing, splashing and having fun. Tom smiled and ran inside to grab a snack.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel colors. One day, she felt dizzy because she played too much. Her mom told her to rest and unpack her toys.

Lily started to unpack her toys and found her pastel colors. She wanted to draw a big sun and flowers. But she remembered that she was dizzy. She thought, "I should listen to mom and rest first."

After resting, Lily felt better. She was not dizzy anymore. She unpacked her pastel colors and drew a beautiful picture. She learned that it is good to listen to mom and take care of herself.

Fred showed Dad around his preschool. The room was big and had a lot of fun toys in it. Dad smiled at all the bright, colourful blocks and dolls.

Next, Fred took Dad on a tour of his favourite spot: the craft table. The table was full of interesting and exciting things for Fred to do. Dad was amazed by all the wonderful things to discover!

The tour continued outside. The playground was full of slides, swings and sand-pits. Dad got to try them all out and Fred laughed as Dad went very fast down the slide.

The tour ended in the dull classroom. Fred showed Dad the little desk he drew pictures at and the bookshelf full of all his favourite stories. Dad was so proud to see all the things his little Fred had been learning about.

Once upon a time there was a fox who wanted to go on an adventure. He wanted to explore the world, so he began to pack his bag. He put some food, a blanket and some toys in his bag.

The fox looked at the bag and smiled. He was ready to go! He bounded off into the forest, with his tail held high. He was so excited.

Suddenly, the fox heard a noise. It was a fierce roar! He stopped and looked around. It was a bear!

The fox nervously asked, "What do you want?" 

The bear growled, "I was just looking for someone like you to help me with something."

The fox was relieved and agreed to help the bear. The bear explained that he was trying to pack for an adventure, just like the fox. The fox showed the bear how to pack the bag and before long the bear was ready to go.

The bear smiled at the fox and said, "Thank you for your help! I would've never gotten this done without you!" 

The fox waved goodbye as the bear bounded away. He was proud to have helped out a fierce creature like the bear. And he was proud of himself, too.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a bike with pedals that he loved to ride. One day, he saw a girl crying on the sidewalk. He asked her what was wrong.

The girl said she was lost and didn't know how to get home. Timmy didn't know where she lived, but he wanted to help. He asked his mom for help, and she called the police. The police found the girl's home and took her there safely.

Timmy felt happy that he could help someone who was lost. He didn't want to be ignorant and not help someone who needed it. From that day on, he always tried to be kind and helpful to others.

Once there was a boy who loved to play outside. His name was Jack. One day he went to a park and saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it.

He grabbed onto a branch and started to climb. Unfortunately, his shoe's buckle got stuck on the tree's bark. He said to himself, â€œWhat should I do now?â€ 

Then, he noticed a sharp stone nearby. He grabbed it and used it to cut the buckle. He yelped in surprise when the buckle flew off and landed on the ground. He was finally free!

He then continued to climb the tree. He climbed higher and higher until he reached the top. He looked around and sighed in delight. The view from the top of the tree was so exciting!

But after some time, he got bored of it. So, he started to climb down. He was glad that he could see the world from the top of the tree even though it was only temporary.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to play in the pond and splash around with his friends. One day, Ducky saw a shiny wheel floating in the water. Ducky was curious and wanted to play with the wheel, but his mother warned him to be careful and not to play with things that were not his.

Ducky ignored his mother's warning and went to play with the wheel. He splashed around with it and had so much fun. But suddenly, the wheel started to spin too fast and Ducky couldn't keep up. He tried to swim away, but the wheel hit him and he got hurt.

Ducky realized that he should have listened to his mother and not played with things that didn't belong to him. The moral of the story is to always be careful and listen to your parents.

Once upon a time, there was a healthy little boy named Johnny. He was very excited to go down to the river with his dad. His dad had brought a kayak to seat Johnny in so he could go paddling. But when they got to the river, Johnny found out that the kayak had a big hole in it.

When his dad saw the hole, he said, "Oh no, Johnny! What a mess! I'm sorry, but you won't be able to go kayaking today."

Johnny was very disappointed, and he started to cry. "But why not? I'm healthy and I want to go paddling!"

His dad shrugged, "I'm sorry, but this kayak isn't safe. We'll have to wait until I get a new one for you."

So, Johnny had to go home without paddling. He was very sad and he couldn't understand why he couldn't go paddling. He wished he had a healthy kayak so he could go and explore the river. But his wish didn't come true, and he was stuck with a hole-filled kayak which he couldn't seat in.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her red boots everywhere she went. One day, she was playing with her friend Tommy when he noticed her boots.

Tommy said, "Lily, those boots are so interesting! Where did you get them?"

Lily smiled and said, "My mommy bought them for me. They are my favorite boots!"

Tommy replied, "I wish I had boots like that. Can I try them on?"

Lily was happy to share her boots with her friend. As Tommy put on the boots, he noticed they were a little big for him. "Lily, these boots are too big for me. Can you help me find boots that fit me?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I know! Let's go to the store and find boots that fit you. Then we can play together in our boots!"

Tommy was excited and said, "That's a great idea, Lily! Let's go increase our boot collection!"

Once upon a time, there was a happy little plant that lived in a big pot. The plant was green and tall and it made the room feel calm. Every day, the plant would soak up the sun and grow bigger and stronger.

One day, a little girl came to visit the plant. She liked the plant very much and she wanted to wrap it up in a big hug. But the plant was too tall and too prickly, so the little girl just gave it a pat and went away.

Later that day, a big storm came and the wind blew very hard. The plant tried to hold on, but it was too weak. The pot fell over and the plant was hurt. The little girl came back to see what had happened, but it was too late. The plant was gone.

The little girl felt very sad. She wished she had wrapped the plant in a big, warm hug when she had the chance. From then on, she made sure to give all the plants she met a big hug, just in case they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a new toy that she loved to touch and play with every day. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She brought her new toy with her and showed it to her friends. They all wanted to touch and play with it too.

Lily said, "I hope my toy doesn't get lost or broken." Her friends promised to take good care of it. But while they were playing, a big dog came and took Lily's toy away. Lily cried and cried because she loved her new toy so much and it was now gone forever.

Lily's friends tried to find the toy, but they couldn't. Lily went home feeling sad and didn't want to play with anything else. Her mom tried to cheer her up, but nothing worked. Lily learned that sometimes bad things happen, even when we hope they won't.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They like to run and jump on the grass. They see a large dog with brown fur. The dog is friendly and wags its tail.

"Hello, dog!" Lily says. "Can we pet you?"

The dog barks and licks Lily's face. She giggles and strokes his fur. Tom joins her and pets the dog too.

The dog is happy and shakes his body. He makes the grass fly in the air. Lily and Tom laugh and cover their eyes.

"Wow, dog, you are strong!" Tom says. "You can shake the grass like a wind!"

The dog barks again and runs around them. He wants to play more. Lily and Tom chase him and have fun. They love the large dog and the grass.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends. One was the ocean and the other was the shore. The two were very loyal to each other. The ocean would send waves to its friend, the shore. 

On one warm day, the ocean asked the shore, "Will you guess what I am thinking?" The shore thought for a moment and then replied, "I think you are thinking about how nice it is to have me here?"

The ocean roared with laughter. "Yes, that is exactly what I was thinking. I am so lucky to have you here," it said.

The two friends enjoyed the sunny day together. They watched the beautiful sunset and shared stories until it was time for the ocean to go to bed. 

The loyal friends said goodnight and hugged each other tightly. They knew they would still be friends forever, no matter what.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. She had a bucket with her and she was carrying it around. The bucket was very heavy and Jane was struggling to carry it.

Suddenly, her brother Tommy came out to help her. Tommy took the heavy bucket from Jane and put it down on the ground. Jane looked at Tommy and smiled. Although Tommy had taken the bucket from her, Jane was happy because he had offered his help. 

Tommy said to Jane, "Sorry for taking the bucket from you, Jane. Can you forgive me?" Jane nodded in agreement and hugged Tommy. 

From that day forward, Jane and Tommy became even better friends. They always helped each other, even with the heavy bucket. They knew that no matter what, they could always forgive and love each other.

It was a bright and sunny day, and Tommy was walking around, wondering what he could do. As he looked around, he saw a pond and remembered his friend Robbie telling him about how he liked to cut stones in the pond.

Tommy decided it would be a fun thing to try, and so he ran to the pond and got to work. He squatted down, his little hands scooping out mounds of mud and stones. He put the stones in his pocket and was pleased to find quite a few cool shapes.

He looked around the pond and wondered if he could find something even more exciting. Suddenly, something caught his eye in the water. It was a funny looking fish! He could tell it was a special one, and so he slowly tried to reach out and grab it. Eventually, he got hold of the fish and was so proud of himself. 

He ran home to tell his mum and show her the funny fish he had found. Everyone was so amazed, as they had never seen such an amazing fish before. Tommy knew that this would be something he'd remember forever!

Once there was a girl who loved to dress up. Every Tuesday she chose a new outfit. She had a thick yellow dress that she especially loved. She wore it to the park. Her friends all cheered when they saw her. She felt like a princess!

When she got home, she hung up her dress and showed her mom. Her mom said it looked beautiful.

"Can I wear it to school tomorrow?" the girl asked.

"Yes, that's fine," said her mom.

The next day, the girl proudly wore her thick yellow dress to school. Her friends loved it and so did her teachers. Everyone said it was the prettiest dress!

The girl was so happy that she wore her thick yellow dress every Tuesday from then on. She said it made her feel special.

Once upon a time, there was a mole who wanted to learn more about the world. Every day, the mole would study. One day, the mole saw a very light in the sky. The mole was amazed and curious, so he decided to study it. He looked up information and asked many questions. Eventually, the mole discovered that it was the moon. He was so happy that he had studied and now he knew the answer. The mole smiled, thanked the moon and went back to his burrow. From then on, the mole would look to the sky and study whenever he saw the light of the moon.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing outside. She saw dark clouds in the sky and heard a loud sound. "What's that noise?" she asked her mom. "That's thunder," replied her mom. "It's important to go inside when you hear thunder."

Lily went inside and sat on the couch with her mom. "Can we play a game?" she asked. "Sure, what game do you want to play?" asked her mom. "Let's lean back and forth," said Lily. They leaned back and forth on the couch and giggled.

Suddenly, there was a big clap of thunder. "That was loud!" said Lily. "I'm scared." "It's okay," said her mom. "I'm here with you." They cuddled on the couch until the thunder stopped. "Thanks for being here, mom," said Lily. "You're so important to me."

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. Joe loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Joe and his friends were playing in the park when they saw something funny. It was a rod. The rod was very long. Joe and his friends were scared, but they decided to have some fun with it.

Joe picked up the rod and said, "Let's pretend this is a light saber like from Star Wars." His friends were so excited. They all ran around playing and laughing with it. When it started to get dark, they were all ready to go home.

Joe said, "Wait, I want to take this rod home." His friends said, "No, it will scare your mom." Joe said, "It won't scare her. I'll think of a good story to tell her." So Joe took the rod home.

When Joe got to his house, his mom asked him why he had a rod. Joe replied, "Mom, this rod is my light saber and I need it to save the world." His mom smiled and said, "Okay. You can keep it. But you be careful!" Joe was so happy. He had a lot of fun playing with his new light saber.

Once there was a boy who liked to pull things. He pulled strings, he pulled towels, he pulled things from the cupboard. One day he saw something quite interesting. It was a big piece of cloth and it had a very strange texture. He pushed his hand against it and he liked the way it felt. He decided to pull it and the cloth began to move. He was very curious and he kept pulling until the cloth was in a line. He looked at it and smiled.

Suddenly, he felt a helpful hand pat his shoulder. It was his mom! â€œLetâ€™s tie the piece of cloth together so that itâ€™s easier to keep it in one placeâ€, she said. The boy nodded and they both pulled the cloth until they had made a beautiful knot. The boy smiled once again, feeling very proud of his work. He knew he could always count on his mom's helpful hands.

Once there was a girl named Piper. She was only 3 years old, but she loved tasks. No matter how small or big the task seemed, Piper was there to fill it. 

One day, Piper decided to go for a walk. She stopped to admire the flowers and saw a task no one had filled before. The task looked different from all the other tasks Piper had seen before. 

Piper bravely decided to fill the task, no matter the size or difficulty. But the task was too big for her to fill alone. So instead of trying to do it on her own, Piper asked her parents and friends to help. 

Soon, all the different tasks were finished. Piper's parents and friends were very proud of her. Together they had learned an important lesson: no task is too big when you ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to surf on the big waves at the beach. One day, she saw a purple shell in the sand. "I want to touch it!" she said excitedly.

But just as she reached out her hand, a seagull swooped down and snatched the shell away. Lily was sad and cried out, "That was my purple shell!"

Suddenly, a big wave came and knocked the seagull off course. The shell fell from its beak and landed right in front of Lily. She picked it up and smiled, "I got it back! Now I can touch it all I want."

Once upon a time there was a hairy monster called Bob. Bob had a lot of paint. He liked to make a lot of messes and he used his paint to make them.

One day, Bob was in his house, making a mess with his paint. Suddenly, he heard a voice say, "Bob, please clean up your mess!"

Bob looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. Then he realised that it was his mum! She was standing in the doorway, looking at Bob's mess.

Bob said to his mum, "Sorry, Mum. I'll clean it up now."

So he got a cloth and some water and he started to clean up the paint. Soon his house was clean again.

Mum was very happy and said, "Well done, Bob! You're such a good cleaner!"

Bob felt happy and proud. From that day on, he made sure to always clean up after he made a mess.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a charming umbrella that she loved to use on rainy days. One day, Lily went for a walk with her umbrella when it started to turn very windy. Suddenly, a gust of wind blew her umbrella away and she couldn't catch it. 

Lily felt sad because she loved her charming umbrella so much. She looked for it everywhere but couldn't find it. She felt very upset and cried a lot. Her parents tried to comfort her but nothing worked. 

Days passed and the weather turned sunny again. Lily forgot about her charming umbrella and played with her toys. However, one day, when she was playing outside, she saw her umbrella in a tree. She was very happy and ran to get it. But as she reached for it, she slipped and fell down. She hurt herself badly and had to go to the hospital. From that day on, Lily learned to be careful and never forgot her charming umbrella again.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim had a violin. He loved to play it every day. One day, Tim saw a big race happening in his town. He wanted to join the race, but he was sad because he did not know how to run fast.

Tim went to his mom and said, "Mom, I want to join the race, but I am too slow." His mom smiled and said, "Why don't you play your violin while you run? It will make you happy, and you will not feel slow anymore."

So, Tim took his violin and joined the race. He started to play and run at the same time. At first, he was a little miserable because it was hard to do both. But as he played more, he started to feel better.

The other kids in the race heard Tim's violin and began to smile. They liked the music, and it made them run faster too. In the end, they all finished the race together, laughing and smiling.

From that day on, Tim played his violin at every race in the town. He learned that even if he was not the fastest runner, he could still make others happy with his music. And that made Tim very happy too.

There was an old man who loved to learn things. He liked to learn new songs, poems, and stories. One day, the old man went to the park. It was a gray day. 

At the park, he saw a group of children playing. He wanted to learn something from them. Then he saw a little boy reciting a poem. The old man watched and listened. He learned the poem by heart. 

The old man went home feeling very happy. He decided to write down the poem he had learned from the little boy. He put it in a small gray box. 

Now, the old man always kept the poem in the gray box. Whenever he missed his friends, he opened the box and read the poem out loud. He always smiled and felt better again.

Bob was a three year old child. He liked to play outside and slide down the slide in his backyard.

One day, Bob's mom told him that she was getting married. "What is marriage?" asked Bob.

"Marriage is when two people love each other and decide to stay together forever," His mom explained to him.

While sliding down the slide, Bob thought about what his mom had said.

Suddenly, Bob saw a big dead bug on the slide. "Oh no!" he said in surprise.

His mom came to check what was wrong. "Don't worry," she said, "It's just a dead bug."

Bob said, "But why is it dead?" 

His mom smiled and said, "Some things just don't last forever - like marriage." 

Bob smiled and thought, "I understand now - marriage is forever." He accepted the bug as a symbol of commitment, understanding and love.

Once upon a time there was a guard. He was very nervous because he had to stay awake all night. He was watching over something special. He was very careful and he watched all night. 

When morning came the guard was very tired. He had been so busy watching that he hadn't slept at all. He needed to sleep. So he found a nice, comfortable spot and dozed off. 

But soon the guard was being watched. A sneaky fox had seen the guard asleep and was getting closer and closer. The fox was looking for something special that the guard was protecting.
 
The guard woke up and was very scared. He was no longer nervous, he was very scared. He saw the fox and he jumped up. He made lots of noise and waved his arms. The fox was so scared that it ran away!

The guard was very happy. He was sure he had saved something special. He knew that he had to stay awake so he stayed on guard for the rest of the night. From then on he was never so nervous and he made sure he slept enough.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in the bath with their toys. They have a boat, a duck, a fish and a frog. They make bubbles with the soap and splash each other.

One day, they see a new soap on the shelf. It is big and round and has a picture of a star on it. They wonder what it is.

"Can we use the new soap?" Tom asks Lily.

"I don't know. Maybe it is not for us. Maybe it is for Mom or Dad." Lily says.

They decide to discuss it with their toys. They ask the boat, the duck, the fish and the frog what they think.

The boat says, "The new soap is too big for me. I like the small soap that makes me slippery and fast."

The duck says, "The new soap is too round for me. I like the flat soap that I can quack on and make noise."

The fish says, "The new soap is too dry for me. I like the wet soap that I can swim in and make bubbles."

The frog says, "The new soap is too shiny for me. I like the dull soap that I can hide in and surprise you."

Tom and Lily listen to their toys. They think they are smart. They agree that the new soap is not for them. They put it back on the shelf and use the old soap that they like. They have fun in the bath with their toys. They are happy.

Jimmy always listened to the grown-ups. He thought it was fun to be bossy and show off.

One day, a grown-up told Jimmy that if he could reach the top shelf, he could get a reward. Jimmy felt excited. He ran over and jumped as high as he could, with all his might.

It worked! He managed to reach the shelf and grabbed the big box. As he opened the box, he saw lots of colourful sweets inside. Jimmy cheered with excitement and ate all the sweets, one by one.

He felt so proud of himself, that he had reached the top shelf and found a delicious reward. Now he wanted to reach her even higher!

Once upon a time, there lived an eager little mouse. He loved to explore the world and see all the wonderful things the world had to offer. One day, he was exploring an old barn when he saw an unusual trap. He wanted to see what it was, but his mother had always warned him about such traps. But the little mouse was too curious and he couldn't help himself. He carefully poked his little nose closer and closer, until it was just inches from the trap. Suddenly, the trap snapped suddenly shut, trapping the poor little mouse inside. 

The little mouse was so scared and sad. He called out for help, but no one heard him. Suddenly, he heard a noise outside the barn, and it was his mother! She had been searching everywhere for him, and when she heard him, she quickly came to the rescue. She carefully opened the trap and the little mouse was freed. 

The mouse was so happy to be back with his mother. She told him sternly, "I warned you about traps, but you didn't listen! Next time, you better listen to me." the little mouse promised he will never do it again, and he was more careful from then on.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tony and Lola. They were playing together in the park and having lots of fun. Tony was stacking toy blocks to build a tower, but Lola hadn't brought any of her own.

Suddenly, a big boy came up. He was very rude. He told Lola to leave and pushed Tony away so he could play with the blocks instead. Tony was sad that the big boy was being so mean!

But then Lola had a great idea. She asked all the other kids in the park if they had any blocks for Tony to use. Soon, there was a big stack of blocks for Tony to build with! Everyone applauded and the big rude boy went away. 

From then on, Tony and Lola taught all their friends to behave nicely. They told them that it's always better to be kind and share, not to be rude and take away what belongs to others. Everyone agreed and they all made sure to play nice every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lizzy. She loved to ride her bike. 

One day, Lizzy was riding her bike in the park when she came across a big bush. She stopped to look at it and thought it was pretty. 

Suddenly, a helpful little rabbit appeared from behind the bush. Lizzy was so excited that she wanted to give him a hug. 

But the rabbit hopped away and Lizzy followed him. The rabbit went around the bush in circles, while Lizzy rode her bike around. 

They continued to ride and run around the bush together until the sun went down. 

After that day, Lizzy and the rabbit played together every day. The helpful little rabbit made Lizzy the happiest girl in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to festivals because they made her happy. One day, Lily and her mom went to a festival. There were lots of people and things to see. 

Lily saw a balloon that she really wanted, but her mom didn't have any money to buy it. So, Lily went up to the balloon man and said, "Excuse me, can I request a balloon please?" The balloon man smiled and gave her a big red balloon. 

Lily was so happy and she danced around with her balloon. She saw a little boy who looked sad, so she went up to him and said, "Do you want to play with my balloon? It will make you happy." The little boy smiled and played with Lily and her balloon. They had so much fun together at the festival.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sue. One day, Sue was walking through a forest. She saw a big and juicy piece of fruit. She wanted it - so she took it! 

But when Sue took the fruit, the branch it was growing from broke from the tree. Sue felt sad and worried. She knew she should not have broken it.

Just then, Sue heard a voice. She saw a kind man standing next to her. He said, "Don't worry. I understand you wanted the fruit. You can take it, it's okay."

Sue was very happy and thanked the kind man. She took the fruit and said goodbye. From then on Sue was always careful around nature and never took things that did not belong to her.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with their scooters in the park. Anna has a pink scooter and Ben has a blue scooter. They zoom around the grass and the trees, laughing and having fun.

One day, they see a new boy in the park. He has a big, shiny scooter. It has lights and sounds and stickers. Anna and Ben feel curious. They want to see the new scooter. They go to the new boy and say hello.

"Hi, I'm Anna and this is Ben. We like your scooter. Can we try it?" Anna asks.

The new boy looks at them and frowns. He does not feel friendly. He feels mean. He says, "No, you can't. This is my scooter. Go away. You have silly scooters. They are small and dirty and boring."

Anna and Ben feel sad and angry. They do not like the new boy. They think he is rude and selfish. They say, "Your scooter is not nice. It is loud and ugly and silly. You are not nice. You are mean and greedy and nasty."

The new boy feels mad and hurt. He does not like Anna and Ben. He thinks they are mean and jealous. He says, "You are liars. My scooter is the best. You are the worst. You are stupid and dumb and lame."

Then, he does something very bad. He pushes Anna and Ben off their scooters. He grabs their scooters and runs away. He laughs and says, "Ha ha, now I have three scooters. You have none. You are losers. I am the winner."

Anna and Ben feel shocked and scared. They fall to the ground and cry. They do not have their scooters. They do not have their fun. They do not have their friend. They have nothing. They feel very, very sad. The end.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a boy named Tim. Tim was a deaf boy, but he had a big heart. He loved to play with his toy blocks and make tall stacks with them.

One day, Tim was playing with his blocks when he started to imagine. He imagined that his stacks of blocks were giant towers in a far away land. He was a brave knight who protected the towers from dragons.

Tim played and played, and his stacks grew taller and taller. His mom and dad watched with big smiles on their faces. They were so proud of their brave little boy. And even though Tim was deaf, he knew he could do anything he imagined.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a teddy bear. One day, Lily's mommy took her to a big store where there were many things to buy. Lily saw a toy that she really liked, but it was very expensive. She said to her mommy, "I want that toy, but it's too much money." 

Her mommy replied, "Yes, it's a luxury item. Maybe we can save up for it another day." 

Lily looked sad, but then she saw a shelf with some candy on it. She asked her mommy if she could have some, but the candy was too high for her to reach. Her mommy gently lifted her up so she could get some. Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, mommy! You are the best!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, she fell down and hurt her knee. Her mommy put a bandage on her knee to make it feel better. 

Lily's friend, Jack, came to play with her. Jack said, "Lily, let's play a game. I will hide and you have to find me." Lily agreed and started to look for Jack. 

While she was looking for Jack, she saw a bench. She thought, "I am tired, I will sit on the bench for a little bit." But the bench was hot because it was in the sun. Lily said, "Ouch! The bench is hot!" 

Suddenly, Lily heard Jack laughing. He had been hiding behind the bench. Lily said, "Jack, you scared me! But it's okay now, my knee feels better with the bandage on." They continued to play together and had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found a blue truck in the junk pile outside his house. It was dirty and old, but Timmy loved it anyway.

Timmy spent all day cleaning the truck until it was shiny and new. He played with it for hours, driving it around the house and making vroom vroom noises. But then, something strange happened. The truck started to slow down and eventually stopped moving altogether.

Timmy was sad that his new truck had stopped working. But then, his dad came by and helped him fix it. He passed some tools to Timmy and showed him how to open up the truck and fix the engine. Timmy was so happy when the truck started working again. He learned that even though something might seem like junk, it can still be useful and bring joy.

Once upon a time, there was a team of animals. They were friends and liked to play together. One day, they decided to have a picnic. They spread out a big blanket on the grass and put their food on it. They had sandwiches, fruit, and mild cheese. 

As they ate, they talked about how much fun they were having. Suddenly, they heard a noise. It was a little bird who had hurt its wing. The team of animals knew they had to help. They spread out another blanket and gently picked up the bird. 

Together, they took care of the little bird and made sure it was okay. They felt happy that they could help. From that day on, the team of animals knew they could always count on each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was walking in the forest when she saw a flame. She got scared and started to cry.

Suddenly, a kind fox appeared and asked, "Why are you crying, little one?" Lily replied, "I saw a scary flame and I don't know what to do."

The fox suggested, "Let's go and find some water to put out the flame." So they went to the nearby river and filled a bucket with water. They returned to the flame and poured the water on it. The flame disappeared and Lily was no longer scared.

"Thank you, Mr. Fox," said Lily. "You helped me when I was scared." The fox smiled and said, "That's what friends are for." And from that day on, they became the best of friends and went on many more adventures together.

Mommy and Daddy wanted to buy a new toy. They wanted something that made nice sounds, and they wanted it to be organized. So they went to the toy store. 

When they got to the store, there were so many toys. Mommy and Daddy looked around, but couldn't find what they wanted. 

Then, Mommy found the perfect toy! It had lots of buttons, and each button made a different sound. There were all the sounds of animals, like horses and cats. There were musical sounds, like a drum and a guitar. And everything was very organized.

Mommy and Daddy bought the toy, and they were so happy. They went home and showed the toy to the little boy. He was so excited! 

They showed him how to make the sounds, and the little boy has been playing with it ever since. Now it's the favorite toy in the house!

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Amy. Amy was very sleepy. She put on her pajamas and went to bed.

In the middle of the night, Amy heard a soft sound. She opened her eyes and saw a friendly ghost. The ghost said, "Hello, Amy! I am here to help you."

Amy asked the ghost, "Can you help me pick a dream?" The ghost smiled and said, "Of course! Let's pick a happy dream for you." Together, they picked a dream about playing in a big park with lots of friends.

Amy said, "Thank you, ghost!" The ghost smiled and said, "You're welcome. Now, go back to sleep and enjoy your dream." Amy closed her eyes, feeling happy and safe with her new friend.

And so, Amy had a wonderful dream, thanks to the kind ghost. From that night on, the ghost would always visit Amy and help her pick the best dreams, and they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very excited because it was nearly her birthday. Sarah wanted to decorate her house for the big day.

The first task was to hang lots of streamers. She carefully taped colorful streamers all around the walls. Then she hung a big picture of her and her friends on the wall. It looked perfect!

Next it was time to hang the balloons. Sarah went around the room and carefully put up red, blue and green balloons. She popped them and laughed with joy!

Finally, Sarah was ready to hang the birthday banner. She strung it up over the door and it looked perfect!

Sarah had done a great job decorating. She smiled with pride and clapped her hands at her task. It was perfect for her birthday party.

Zara loved to play her flute. She liked to make music with her mouth and fingers. She had a blue flute that her dad gave her. He said it was a special flute that could make magic sounds.

One day, Zara was playing her flute in the garden. She saw a butterfly with many colors. She wanted to make friends with it. She played a soft and sweet tune on her flute. The butterfly came closer and closer. It landed on her nose. Zara giggled.

"Hello, butterfly," she said. "Do you like my music?"

The butterfly nodded. It flapped its wings. It made a sound like a bell. Zara was amazed.

"Wow, you can talk!" she said. "Can you teach me how to make that sound?"

The butterfly nodded again. It flew up and down. It said, "Follow me, Zara. I will show you a secret place where you can make more magic sounds."

Zara was curious. She wanted to see the secret place. She followed the butterfly with her flute. They zoomed through the air. They passed the trees, the flowers, and the birds. They went higher and higher. Zara felt warm and happy.

Soon, they reached a big cloud. The cloud was white and fluffy. It looked like a castle. The butterfly said, "This is the secret place, Zara. This is where the music fairies live. They can make any sound you can imagine. They will teach you how to play your flute better. Do you want to meet them?"

Zara nodded. She was excited. She said, "Yes, please. I want to meet the music fairies. I want to learn more music. Thank you, butterfly. You are a good friend."

The butterfly smiled. It said, "You are welcome, Zara. You are a good friend, too. Come on, let's go inside. The music fairies are waiting for you."

They entered the cloud castle. Zara saw many fairies with different flutes. They played beautiful and wonderful music. Zara felt like she was in a dream. She joined them and played her flute. She learned new sounds and songs. She had fun. She was happy. She thanked the butterfly and the fairies for their gift. They hugged her and said, "You are welcome, Zara. You have a special flute and a special heart. You can make magic music. You can come back anytime you want. We are always here for you."

Zara smiled. She said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. I will come back soon. I love you all."

She flew back to the garden with the butterfly. She played her flute for her dad. He was proud of her. He said, "You are amazing, Zara. You have learned so much. Where did you go?"

Zara said, "I went to the secret place with the butterfly. I met the music fairies. They taught me how to play my flute better. They are my friends. They are magic."

Her dad hugged her. He said, "You are magic, too, Zara. You are my little star. I love you."

Zara hugged him back. She said, "I love you, too, dad. You are my hero. You gave me the best gift ever. You gave me my flute."

Once there was a slow turtle called Freddie. Freddie was always a bit slow but he loved to explore the world. Everywhere he went he made sure he included lots of friends in the adventure. 

One day Freddie decided to go on an extra special adventure - he was going to try to find a hidden beach! He set off in the morning, packing a lunch with him. As he walked along he met lots of different animals and included them in his journey.

Finally, they reached a vast stretch of beach. As they walked along they were amazed by how much there was to explore. They went in and out of rock pools, filling up shells with treasures they collected.

When it was time to go home, Freddie gave all his treasures to the animals he had included on his journey. He was especially careful to make sure he left the slowest turtle some extra special treats for the journey home!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride the subway train with his mommy. One day, Timmy and his mommy were riding the blue subway train when they heard a loud noise.

"What was that noise?" asked Timmy.

"I don't know," said mommy, "but don't worry, I will protect you."

Suddenly, the subway train stopped moving. Timmy looked out the window and saw a big blue truck blocking the tracks.

"Oh no!" cried Timmy, "How will we get home?"

"Don't worry," said mommy, "I will protect you and we will find a way home." 

Mommy called a taxi and they got home safely. Timmy was so happy that his mommy was there to protect him.

Once upon a time, there was a silly bunny named Benny. Benny liked to hop and play all day. One day, Benny was very hungry and had no food to eat. His mommy bunny went to the garden to provide some carrots for him. But Benny didn't want carrots, he wanted candy!

Benny went to the store to find candy, but he didn't have any money. He saw a steel jar full of candy and he stole it. Benny was happy to have candy, but he didn't know it was wrong to steal. The store owner saw Benny and called the police.

Benny got in trouble and had to go to jail. He missed his mommy bunny and wished he had just eaten the carrots she provided. The end.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play outside. He saw a big tent in his yard. "Wow!" he said. "I want to play in the tent!" Tim went inside the tent to play.

Inside the tent, Tim found a toy. The toy could record sounds. "This is fun!" he said. He recorded his voice, saying "Hello!" Tim played with the toy for a while. But then, he had a difficult time. The toy stopped working. "Oh no!" Tim said. "Why did it stop?"

Tim went to his mom and asked, "Mom, can you fix my toy?" His mom tried to fix the toy, but she could not. She said, "I am sorry, Tim. The toy is broken." Tim was very sad. He could not play with the toy anymore. The tent was not fun without the toy.

Once upon a time there was a helpful princess. She really loved to go skipping around her castle. Every morning she skipped through the colourful gardens and waved at the friendly birds.  

One day the princess skipped into the bedroom and found that the mattress was missing. She was so sad until a helpful little mouse appeared and said:

"Don't worry, Princess! I know where the mattress is. Follow me!"

The princess followed him down the hallway and around a corner, where she saw the mattress tucked away in a corner.

The princess thanked the helpful little mouse and then jumped onto the mattress and started skipping around her bedroom. She was so happy that she was able to find the mattress to skip on again. 

The princess smiled the whole day and thanked the helpful little mouse for his help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she was running around and she saw a big hole in the ground. She thought it was incredible because it was so big.

Lily decided to jump over the hole, but she missed and fell in! She was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, her mommy came and helped her out of the hole. Lily was so happy to be safe and back on the ground.

From that day on, Lily was more careful when she played outside. She didn't want to miss and fall in another hole. But she still thought the hole was incredible and would always stop to look at it when she passed by.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were married. They were very happy together. One day, they wanted to play a fun game of hide and seek. The husband said, â€œLetâ€™s go hide and you find me!â€ The wife agreed and began to look for her husband. 

She looked everywhere, but she couldnâ€™t find him. She shouted, â€œWhere are you?â€

Suddenly, the husband popped out from behind a smelly old bush. The wife started to giggle, and the husband said â€œDid you find me?â€

The wife said â€œYes, I did! That was fun!â€ The two friends hugged each other and went back home. They promised to play this game again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play basketball with her friends at the park. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new impressive basketball. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to show it to her friends.

But when she got to the park, she saw that the basketball hoop was broken. Lily's friends were sad and didn't know what to do. But Lily had an idea. She remembered her dad had a tool to fix things. She ran home and asked her dad to come with her to the park.

Together, they fixed the hoop and Lily's friends were so happy. They started playing basketball again with Lily's new impressive basketball. Lily prevented her friends from being sad and they all had a great time playing together with the basketball in the basket.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bicycle. His bicycle was huge, and he felt like a superhero when he rode it. One day, Timmy wanted to paint his bicycle. He got out his paintbrush and some paint and started to paint. He painted his bicycle blue and green, just like his favorite superhero. When he finished painting, he rode his huge, colorful bicycle all around the park. Everyone who saw him thought his bicycle was the coolest thing they had ever seen. From that day on, Timmy loved his bicycle even more because it was unique and special, just like him.

Once upon a time there was a boy who wanted some pants. The boy asked his mom for some, but she said no. The boy was sad, so he started to cry. He demanded for the pants and said he wouldn't stop crying until he had them.

Mama was tired of the crying and wanted to make the boy happy, so she searched for the perfect pants. Finally, she found some long pants that were just the right size. She showed her son the pants and he was so excited!

The boy put on the pants right away and ran to the mirror. He looked in the mirror and saw that he looked much better than before. He was so proud of his new long pants. He ran around, spinning and twirling and showing off his pants.

Mama laughed as she watched her son having so much fun. She was glad she could make him happy. She was glad he finally had the long pants he wanted so much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susan. Susan was a curious child and always alert. Every day she wanted to go on an adventure! 

One day Susan was playing in her backyard when she saw a big sack. She couldn't resist the urge to investigate and when she opened it, she found a sign. It had a picture of a bird and an arrow pointing in a certain direction. 

Susan was sure that the sign meant adventure and she decided to follow the arrow. She carried the sack with her and walked until she reached the end of the arrow. 

When she arrived at the end of the arrow she saw an amazing lake surrounded by trees and birds singing everywhere! The sight filled her with joy. Susan then placed the sign she found in the sack on a nearby tree and began exploring the lake. 

At the end of the day she returned home with many stories and memories to last a lifetime. From then on, whenever she was alert, Susan was sure that something special was happening.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun and pick pretty flowers. One day, she found a gentle butterfly sitting on a flower. She watched it for a while and then gently touched its wing. The butterfly flew away, leaving a small mark on the flower. 

Lily continued to play and soon found herself in a field of colorful flowers. She picked a few and brought them home to show her mommy. Her mommy was happy and put the flowers in a vase. Lily was proud of her flower picking and went to bed dreaming of more gentle butterflies and pretty flowers.

The sun was bright and shiny. Jack loved the warmth it gave. Jack was always happy when the sun was out.

Suddenly, Jack heard a noise that sounded like clapping. He looked around and saw a big flame in the sky. The flame was moving up and down and it made clapping noises.

Jack smiled at the flame and it smiled back. Jack held his hands together very tight and waved at the flame. The flame waved back, then flew away.

Jack watched it for a few minutes until it was gone. He knew he had made a new friend. Jack clapped his hands and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. Jack was three years old. He wanted to go out and have some fun. 

Every day, Jack's parents would take him to the playground. It was a great place to play. Jack loved ringing the bell and playing with the swings and slides.

One day, Jack heard a strange noise. It sounded like a bell ringing. He looked around and saw a big, red telephone box. Inside was a telephone and it was ringing. 

Jack went to his dad and asked, "What is that?"

His dad said, "It's a telephone. Come and rub the buttons. It makes a great sound!"

So, Jack went to the telephone and rubbed the buttons. He was so excited to hear it ring and he kept rubbing the buttons.

The little boy was so happy and he smiled from ear to ear. He said, "This is great!"

Lily likes to play with her doll. She gives her doll a name. She calls her doll Mia. Lily and Mia do many things together. They eat, sleep, dress, and sing.

One day, Lily's mom says they have to go to grandma's house. Lily is happy. She loves grandma. She wants to bring Mia with her. But mom says no. Mom says Mia is too big for the car. Mom says she will send Mia to grandma's house later.

Lily is sad. She does not want to leave Mia alone. She hugs Mia and gives her a kiss. She says, "Don't worry, Mia. I will see you soon. Mom will send you to grandma's house. You will be safe and happy there."

Lily puts Mia in a big box. She writes Mia's name on the box. She draws a heart and a smiley face. She puts some toys and a blanket in the box. She says, "This is for you, Mia. You can play with these and keep warm. I love you, Mia."

Mom helps Lily close the box. She puts a sticker on the box. She says, "This is the address of grandma's house. The mailman will take the box and send it to grandma's house. He will be careful and fast. Mia will be there soon."

Lily and mom go to the car. Lily waves to the box. She says, "Bye, Mia. Have a good trip. I will see you at grandma's house. I can't wait to play with you again."

Mom drives to grandma's house. Lily looks out the window. She thinks of Mia. She hopes Mia is not scared or lonely. She hopes Mia is ready to see her.

At grandma's house, Lily runs to the door. She knocks and shouts, "Grandma, grandma, I'm here! Where is Mia? Did she arrive?"

Grandma opens the door. She smiles and hugs Lily. She says, "Hello, Lily. I'm so happy to see you. Yes, Mia arrived. She is in the living room. She is waiting for you."

Lily runs to the living room. She sees the box. She tears it open. She sees Mia. She is so happy. She picks up Mia and cuddles her. She says, "Mia, Mia, you're here! I missed you so much. Are you okay? Did you have a good trip?"

Mia looks at Lily. She smiles and nods. She says, "Lily, Lily, I'm here! I missed you too. I'm okay. I had a good trip. The mailman was nice. He gave me a rub on the head. He said you love me very much. He said you are ready to play with me."

Lily and Mia hug and kiss. They are so happy. They thank mom and grandma. They say, "Thank you for sending Mia to grandma's house. Thank you for taking care of Mia. Thank you for being so kind."

Mom and grandma smile. They say, "You're welcome, Lily and Mia. We love you very much. We are glad you are together. Now, let's have some fun."

One day, Sam and Susie were playing near a beach. They saw the tide washing in and out. Suddenly, Sam had an idea. He said, "Let's build a sandcastle!" Susie thought it sounded like fun.

They started digging and using sticks to make a castle. But the tide kept coming in and washing away the sand castle. Sam was getting frustrated. Then, he had a new idea. He said, "Susie, I have a request. Can you help me find something foolish that will help us keep the tide away?"

Susie thought was a great idea! She searched around and soon she found a big rock. It was perfect! She brought it over and helped Sam put it in front of the sandcastle. The rock kept the tide away and their castle was not washed away! Sam and Susie were very happy and clapped their hands.

Once upon a time, there was a family that lived in a small house. They were very happy together. Suddenly, a terrible storm came. It rained so hard that the roof of the house began to leak. The family was afraid and didn't know what to do.

Mama said, "I wish we had some sunshine."

The father said, "We have to surrender. There is no way to fix the roof against this storm."

The family was very sad. They went outside to see the damage. Everything looked terrible. The father wanted to try to make the best of it, but it seemed like too much work. So in the end, the family had to surrender to the storm and leave the house.

It was a sad ending and the family was very unhappy to have to leave their home. But there was nothing they could do. No amount of sunshine could stop the storm.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks of different colors and sizes. They make a big road with blocks and tape on the floor. They pretend the road is a nation. They give their nation a name. They call it Carland.

One day, they decide to have a race in Carland. They each choose a car and a truck. They line them up at the start of the road. They say, "Ready, set, go!" They push their cars and trucks along the road. They make noises like engines and horns. They have fun.

But then, they reach a bridge. The bridge is made of two books and a ruler. The bridge is too narrow for both cars and trucks. Tom and Lily stop. They look at each other. They do not know what to do.

Tom says, "I want to go first. My car is faster than yours." Lily says, "No, I want to go first. My truck is bigger than yours." They start to argue. They are not happy.

Then, they have an idea. They are creative. They say, "Why don't we make the bridge wider?" They find more books and rulers. They add them to the bridge. They make the bridge wide enough for both cars and trucks. They smile. They say, "Now we can both go." They continue the race. They reach the end of the road. They cheer. They are friends again. They hug. They say, "That was a fun race. Let's play again." They are happy.

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Jack and Harry. Jack was very tired because he had been running around. One day he wanted to play with a toy but Harry wanted to play something else. Jack was feeling very tired and he wanted to rest, but Harry wanted to keep playing until dark. 

Jack was getting more and more tired and he wanted to rest. But Harry wanted to keep playing. Suddenly, Jack said a very special number and to Jack's surprise it worked! He had used the number to make a motion to make Harry tired too.

Harry swayed his arms and his legs and he got very tired. Both the brothers were now tired, but Jack was happy that he could finally rest. The brothers both lay down and fell asleep.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a fat object. It was in a box and no one knew what was inside. One day, a small boy decided to open it. He was very curious.

The boy used both of his hands and pulled at the lid. The object popped open with a loud bang!

The boy was so excited. Inside the box was a big, fat puppy! He was cute and fluffy with big brown eyes.

The little boy jumped up and down with happiness. He hugged the puppy and it licked him back. The boy and the puppy became the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Jack. He lived in a house with his mom and dad.

One day, his dad asked him to do something. His dad said, "Jack, please turn on the tap for me." Jack was happy to help his dad so he ran to the tap and he turned it on with his tiny hands.

Next, his mom asked him to do something. She said, "Jack, please bring me the heavy bag from the corner of the room." Jack was a bit scared because the bag was heavy but he was brave, so he tried and he lifted the heavy bag. When he brought the bag to his mom, she said, "Well done, Jack!"

Jack felt so happy to help his parents. He was their little helper!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy who loved to play at the beach. One sunny day, she found a beautiful shell near the water. It was not an ordinary shell; it was big and shiny with many colors.

Amy picked up the shell and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a pretty shell!" she said. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a lovely shell, Amy. Let's take it home and soak it in water to clean it."

When they got home, Amy filled a bowl with water and put the shell in it. She watched as the shell soaked in the water, becoming even more beautiful. She couldn't wait to show her friends the special shell she had found.

The next day, Amy took the shell to show her friends at the playground. They all gathered around and admired the beautiful shell. Amy felt happy that she found such a special treasure at the beach.

From that day on, Amy and her friends would always search for more special shells at the beach. They loved finding new treasures and sharing them with each other. And they all knew that even an ordinary day could become a magical adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a happy child named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the bright sunshine. One day, while playing in the park, Timmy found a shiny rock. He picked it up and showed it to his mom. She helped him reveal that it was actually a diamond! Timmy was so happy and showed all his friends his bright, sparkly treasure. From that day on, Timmy always kept his special diamond close to him.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. It was her birthday today and she was very happy. She waited for her friends to come to her party but she was getting impatient.

Finally, Lily's friends arrived and they all sang "Happy Birthday" to her. Lily blew out the candles and made a wish. She opened her presents and was very happy. She hugged her friends and thanked them for coming to her party. It was the best birthday ever!

Lila and Tom were twins. They liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big peach tree. It had many ripe peaches. They wanted to pick some.

"Let's get a peach, Tom," Lila said.

"OK, Lila, but how?" Tom asked.

They looked around. They saw a stool. They dragged it to the tree. They put it under a branch. Lila climbed on the stool. She reached for a peach. But it was too high.

"Step on my shoulders, Lila," Tom said.

"Are you sure, Tom?" Lila asked.

"Yes, Lila, I'm strong," Tom said.

Lila stepped on Tom's shoulders. She was careful not to hurt him. She grabbed a peach. It was soft and juicy. She smiled.

"I got one, Tom!" Lila said.

"Good, Lila, now give me one," Tom said.

Lila threw a peach to Tom. He caught it. They got off the stool. They sat on the grass. They bit into their peaches. They were sweet and yummy. They were happy.

"This is the best peach ever, Lila," Tom said.

"I agree, Tom, this is a normal peach," Lila said.

They laughed. They ate their peaches. They thanked the tree. They hugged each other. They went back to play. They loved the garden. They loved the peaches. They loved each other.

Once upon a time there was an elderly man who lived near an ocean. He loved the ocean and even though he couldn't fit in the ocean, he loved to just stand by it and look out at it.

One day he wanted to go for a walk near the ocean. He put on his hat and his walking shoes and grabbed his walking stick. He walked to the ocean and stood by it. He felt happy and content as he watched the waves rolling in.

Suddenly, he saw something small and black swimming in the waves. He moved closer to the water and noticed that it was a small seal pup. It was struggling and he could see it was too small to fit in the ocean.

The elderly man reached in and gently lifted the pup out of the water. He cradled it in his arms and took it back to his house. He made a safe, warm bed for it and fed it a nice meal.

The seal pup was happy in its new home and the elderly man was thrilled to have a new friend. They became good friends and the seal pup grew stronger and bigger everyday. Soon it was big enough to fit in the ocean and the man watched proudly as it said goodbye and swam off into the ocean.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very stubborn and he wanted to follow the drain. The drain was big and shiny and the little boy was excited to explore it. 

The little boy started to follow the drain, but it was very slippery. He struggled and slipped and tried to go further. But he couldn't go very far, because the drain was too slippery and too big for him. 

He kept trying and trying, but he just couldn't follow the drain. But he was very stubborn and so he kept trying. Finally, after all his hard work, the little boy managed to follow the drain all the way to the end. He was so proud of himself for being able to do it. 

The end.

One day, Mama and her three-year-old son, Tim, went to the park. Tim saw some children playing in the sandbox and wanted to join them.

Mama said, "Wait here and stand still. I'm going to get something from the car."

Tim waited and stood still, but he was getting impatient. When Mama came back, she was carrying two buckets filled with sand.

Mama said, "Tim, carry this bucket. It won't be too heavy for you."

Tim looked at the bucket and it seemed heavy to him. "That's too heavy, Mama," he said.

Mama looked at him, her face a bit stern. "I wouldn't ask if it was too heavy, Tim. That's rude. Can you try?"

Tim nodded and grabbed the bucket. He was surprised when he found that he couldn't lift it. But Mama had already started walking towards the sandbox, so Tim tried again. This time, he was able to stand up with the bucket in his hands. 

He smiled to himself, proud that he was able to lift the weight. Mama smiled at him too and said, "Good job, Timmy. Let's go show the other kids."

John and Sarah were playing together in their backyard when they found a piece of metal. It was shiny and reflective and they couldn't wait to show their parents. 

John asked Sarah, "What should we do with the metal?"

Sarah thought for a moment, then said, "Let's take it to Mommy and Daddy!" With that, they ran off excitedly, ready to surprise their parents. 

They raced into the house, and shouted, "Mommy, Daddy! Look what we found!" 

Their parents were very surprised and asked, "Where did you find this piece of metal?" 

John and Sarah were so proud of their discovery, and couldn't wait to tell the story. They recounted that they found the metal outside in the backyard and it was so shiny and reflective. 

Their parents smiled, and said, "Well, why don't you two take it around the neighbourhood and see if you can return it to its rightful owner. If nobody takes it, you two can keep it!". 

John and Sarah were so cheerful and excited about the prospect of helping find the true owner of the metal, that they grabbed it and set off, ready to call on their neighbours.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old and she loved to explore the world around her.
