Lily saw Tom run out of the hole. She saw the raccoon chase him. She was shocked. She did not know there was a raccoon in the big tree. She said, "Tom, watch out! There is a raccoon!" She ran after him. They both ran to the other side of the park. They did not stop until they were safe.

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They were glad they were okay. They looked at the big tree. They did not like it anymore. They said, "Let's never play near the big tree again. It is too scary." They decided to play somewhere else. They found a sandbox. They thought it was fun. They forgot about the big tree and the raccoon. They did not try to scare each other again. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go to the market with her mom. They would buy fruits, vegetables, and other yummy food.

One day, Lily saw a big, red apple at the market. She wanted it, but her mom said no. When her mom was not looking, Lily took the apple. She felt guilty because she knew it was wrong.

When they got home, Lily's mom asked her, "Did you take the apple from the market?" Lily did not answer at first. Then, she said, "Yes, I did. I am sorry." Her mom hugged her and said, "Thank you for telling the truth. Next time, we will ask before we take something."

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play together. One day, they went to the shop with their mom. Mom gave them some money to buy a toy each. Sara saw a big doll that she wanted. Tom saw a small car that he liked.

"Can I have this doll, mom?" Sara asked.

"Sure, honey, you have enough money for it," mom said.

"Can I have this car, mom?" Tom asked.

"Sorry, sweetie, you don't have enough money for it. You can choose something cheaper," mom said.

Tom felt miserable. He wanted the car so much. He looked at Sara's doll and felt angry. He thought Sara was lucky and he was not.

"Mom, can we go home now?" Tom said.

"Okay, let's go," mom said.

On the way home, Sara noticed that Tom was sad. She felt sorry for him. She remembered that Tom liked cars a lot. She had an idea.

"Tom, do you want to play with my doll?" Sara asked.

"No, thank you. I don't like dolls," Tom said.

"Then, do you want to trade with me? You can have my doll and I can have your money. Then you can buy the car you want," Sara said.

Tom was surprised. He looked at Sara and saw that she was smiling. He realized that Sara was kind and generous. He felt happy.

"Really? You would do that for me?" Tom asked.

"Yes, of course. You are my brother and I love you. I don't mind playing with something cheaper. I just want you to be happy," Sara said.

Tom hugged Sara and thanked her. He gave her his money and took her doll. He ran back to the shop and bought the car he wanted. He and Sara played together with their new toys. They both felt happy.

Mom watched them and smiled. She was proud of them. She thought they learned a valuable lesson. She thought they learned that sharing is caring and that happiness is not about having the most expensive things, but about including others and being kind.

Tommy was a happy boy. One day, he wanted to collect something special. He thought and thought and then he knew. Tommy wanted to collect his wife! His Daddy said his wife was dead. This made Tommy very sad. 

Tommyâ€™s Daddy said, â€œDonâ€™t worry, Tommy. You canâ€™t get your wife back, sheâ€™s gone forever. But we can go together and collect something else special.â€ So, Tommy and his Daddy went out. 

They collected lots of stones and leaves and feathers. They put them all in a special jar. When they got home, Daddy showed Tommy how to make a picture with the stones and leaves. 

The picture was very pretty and it made Tommy happy. He loved his new special thing he had collected. His Daddy hugged him and said, â€œSee? Itâ€™s ok to be sad but you can still find happiness in things.â€

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw and paint. He would use his crayons and markers to create pictures of animals and trees. One day, he drew a big, scary wolf. The wolf had sharp teeth and looked very hungry. 

Timmy's mom saw the drawing and said, "Wow, that's a great wolf you created, Timmy!" Timmy felt proud of his drawing. 

Later that day, it started to rain outside. Timmy looked out the window and saw that everything was wet. He decided to put on his raincoat and boots and go outside to play. As he was splashing in the puddles, he heard a howl. He turned around and saw the same wolf he had drawn earlier! 

But instead of being scared, Timmy remembered that he had created the wolf himself. He walked up to the wolf and said, "Hello, Mr. Wolf. Do you want to play with me in the rain?" The wolf wagged his tail and they played together until the rain stopped. From that day on, Timmy and the wolf became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play on the swing in her backyard. She would swing back and forth, feeling the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. But sometimes, she felt lonely because she didn't have anyone to play with.

One day, Lily saw a little bird perched on a branch nearby. She tried to talk to the bird, but it flew away. Lily felt sad and lonely again. Later that day, she found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and decided to make a wish.

"I wish I could have a friend to swing with," she said.

The next day, Lily went outside to swing and saw a little boy walking by. She smiled and said hello. The boy smiled back and asked if he could swing with her. Lily was so happy! She led the boy to the swing and they swung together, laughing and having fun. Lily realized that sometimes, wishes really do come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy because it was sweet. Her mommy would always buy her candy and she would own a lot of it. 

One day, Lily was playing with her toys and found a stuffed animal with a soft texture. She hugged it tightly and loved how it felt. She wanted to take it with her everywhere she went and own it forever. 

At bedtime, Lily snuggled with her stuffed animal and ate some candy. She felt happy because she owned two things she loved - something sweet and something soft. She fell asleep with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a big family living in a warm house. Every evening, mummy would come home from work.

Mummy said to her three children: "Who would like a big salad for dinner?"

The children said: "Yay!"
They went to the kitchen and started making the salad. 
Mummy brought out some tomatoes and cucumbers from the fridge. The children cut them into small pieces and put them in the salad bowl.

Mummy said: "Let's go sit in the dining room and eat our warm salad."

The children ran into the dining room and sat in their chairs. Mummy served the warm salad to everyone and they all started eating. They all enjoyed their dinner and it was so yummy!

Tommy was playing in his room when his friend Sarah came to visit. Sarah was always so noisy and loud. Tommy asked, "Why are you so noisy?"

Sarah just laughed and said, "I am excited to see you!"

"Oh," said Tommy, not sure what to do.

Sarah said, "Let's go to bed now. We can sleep in my bed together."

Tommy was so happy to have a friend to sleep with, so he said, "Yes, let's go!"

The two friends had a wonderful time sleeping in Sarah's bed until morning. Tommy was so happy that he had a new and noisy friend like Sarah.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were very brave. Their names were Molly and Jack. Molly and Jack were walking in the woods one day, when suddenly they heard something. It sounded like a voice, but it wasn't human. Molly and Jack were scared.

Jack wanted to find out what was making the noise. He told Molly to stay where she was, and that he would go and investigate. Molly was scared, but she nodded her head and said okay. 

Jack walked slowly through the trees until he spotted a spark coming from just ahead. It looked like it was coming from the bushes. He took a deep breath, and cautiously moved forward. He soon saw what was causing the spark. It was a fairy, and she was telling a story.

The fairy was telling a story about a scary dragon. Jack and Molly listened intently. Then when the story was over, they thanked the fairy and walked away. As they did, they looked back at the spark and smiled.

Once upon a time there was a charming little girl. She loved to go outside and play.
One day she saw a board by the side of the street. She went up and touched it with her finger. She felt a tiny pinch!
The girl was confused. She looked around, but couldn't see where the pinch came from. She decided to take the board and look more closely.

When she picked it up, something unexpected happened. A little mouse peeked out from behind the board! He was wearing a tiny hat and had a little bell around his neck. The girl found the mouse very charming and smiled.

The mouse scurried away, but the girl didn't follow. She just kept the board and kept smiling. From then on, she kept the board with her and always took it with her when she went to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the store to buy some candy. Lily saw a pretty diary and asked her mommy if they could buy it. Her mommy said no because they didn't have enough money.

Lily was sad and started crying. A little boy saw her crying and asked her what was wrong. Lily told him that she wanted the diary but her mommy said no. The little boy said he had some money and could buy it for her.

Lily was very happy and thanked the little boy. But when they left the store, a big dog came and took the diary away from Lily. She was so sad and cried even more. The little boy said he was sorry but couldn't do anything to help. Lily and her mommy went home without any candy or diary.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess who wore a veil on her head. The veil was like a pretty scarf that covered her hair. The princess loved her veil because it made her feel special and pretty.

One day, the princess was going to a big party. She needed a dependable horse to take her there. She asked her friend who had many horses to supply her with one. Her friend gave her a strong and dependable horse that would take her to the party safely.

As the princess rode on the horse, her veil fluttered in the wind. She felt happy and excited to go to the party. When she arrived, everyone admired her beautiful veil and the dependable horse that brought her there. The princess had a wonderful time and was grateful to her friend for supplying her with such a great horse.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on an adventure in the forest and lost one of her shoes. 

Lily looked all around but couldn't find her shoe. She felt sad and scared because she didn't want to go home with only one shoe. Suddenly, she saw a little squirrel who had her shoe in its mouth. 

Lily asked the squirrel to give back her shoe, but the squirrel didn't want to part with it. So, Lily had an idea. She took off her other shoe and gave it to the squirrel. The squirrel was happy with the new shoe and gave back Lily's lost shoe. 

Lily was so happy that she had both of her shoes again. She thanked the squirrel and continued on her adventure, feeling grateful and excited for what else she might discover.

Once upon a time there was a little elephant. She was so quiet and gentle. Every day she liked to rub her trunk on a big tree in the park. She would pat it softly and make the leaves rustle. 

One day when the elephant was rubbing her trunk, she heard a noise coming from the grass. She stopped rubbing and looked around. To her surprise, she saw a little bug scurrying around. 

The elephant was so curious about the bug, she stood still and watched him for a while. She followed the bug and watched it hop around the park. She got closer and closer as it climbed onto a leaf and rubbed its belly. 

The elephant found it so funny, she started to giggle. Then, she bent her trunk down close to the bug and blew it gently. The bug felt so safe with the elephant, they were both very quiet. The elephant wanted to play and took the bug in her trunk and started to rub it softly. 

The bug tickled and started to giggle too. The elephant was so happy and wished to keep the bug forever. But, she knew she had to take care of the bug and put it back in the grass. The bug waved goodbye and the elephant smiled. She knew they would always be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, her friend Timmy came over to play. 

Lily showed Timmy all of her toys, but Timmy didn't like them. He said, "I disagree, these toys are boring." 

Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. She remembered that she had a special toy in her room, but it was locked in a box. 

Lily went to find the key and when she came back, she showed Timmy her special toy. Timmy was amazed and said, "Wow, you are so organized to keep your toys safe like that." 

Lily felt happy that Timmy liked her special toy and they continued to play together. From that day on, Lily learned that even when people disagree, there is always a way to find a solution and make everyone happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park to play. He loved to play on the swings and slide. The sun was shining, and the sky was blue. Tim was having a lot of fun.

As it started to get dark, Tim saw a stranger. The stranger said, "Hi, do you want to play with me?" Tim looked at the stranger and thought for a moment. He remembered his mom told him not to talk to strangers.

Tim said, "No, thank you. I need to go home now." He ran back to his mom, who was waiting for him. She was happy that Tim remembered her advice. They went home together, and Tim told her all about his day at the park.

Once there was a smart man. He liked to use his hammer. Every day he would use it to fix things.

One day he was washing his clothes. He was in the middle of washing them when the hammer fell in the water. The man was very sad.

He thought and thought until he had an idea. He put his hand in the water and felt around until he found the hammer. He then took it out and dried it off with a cloth.

The man was happy. His hammer was clean again, thanks to his smart thinking. From then on, he was careful not to let it near the water again.

Once upon a time, there was a row of pretty flowers. The flowers were red, blue, and yellow. They lived in a big garden with their friend, the deaf cat named Fluffy.

One day, Fluffy the cat was sad. She could not hear the birds sing. She could not hear the bees buzz. She wanted to hear her friends, the flowers, talk. So, Fluffy asked the flowers for help.

The flowers wanted to help their friend. They thought and thought. Then, they had an idea. They danced and moved in the wind. Fluffy saw the flowers dance and felt happy. Now, Fluffy and the flowers could talk and play together. And they lived happily in the big garden.

Once upon a time, a long time ago, there was an ancient spark. It was so old that no one remembered its name. But it could be heard rumbling deep in the ground.

One day, a little boy was walking in the forest. He heard a noise he had never heard before. It sounded like a spark! The boy was excited, so he followed the noise until he saw it.

The spark was bright and shining. It seemed to be calling him. He put his hands over the spark and suddenly he could feel its ancient power. He felt the spark jump through his arms and into his heart. He knew that the spark was meant to be with him.

The boy took the spark home and showed it to his mom. She smiled and said, "That is special. It must be magical!" The boy knew his spark was special. He kept it safe and shared its joy with everyone.

Sara and Ben were playing in the backyard. They saw a big pile of leaves that their dad had raked. They wanted to jump in the leaves and have fun.

"Can we jump in the leaves, dad?" Sara asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Don't go near the fire pit. It is very hot and dangerous," dad said.

Sara and Ben nodded and ran to the leaves. They jumped and laughed and threw leaves in the air. They felt happy and warm.

But then Ben saw something shiny in the fire pit. It looked like a spark. He was curious and wanted to see it better. He walked closer to the fire pit.

"Ben, no! Come back!" Sara shouted. She saw the fire pit and remembered what dad said. She was scared for Ben.

Ben did not listen. He reached out his hand to touch the spark. But the spark was not alone. There was a thick smoke and a loud crackle. Ben felt a pain in his hand and a heat in his face. He screamed and pulled back his hand.

Dad heard the scream and ran to the fire pit. He saw Ben crying and holding his hand. He saw the smoke and the spark. He was angry and worried.

"Ben, what did you do? I told you not to go near the fire pit. You could have been hurt very badly. Let me see your hand," dad said.

He took Ben's hand and looked at it. It was red and swollen. He wrapped it in a cloth and hugged Ben.

"I'm sorry, dad. I wanted to see the spark. It seemed pretty. I didn't know it was hot and bad," Ben said.

"I know, Ben. But you have to listen to me. The fire pit is not a toy. It is for grown-ups only. The spark can burn you and make you sick. You have to be careful and stay away from it. Do you understand?" dad said.

"Yes, dad. I understand. I'm sorry. I won't do it again," Ben said.

Dad kissed Ben's head and carried him inside. He gave him some ice and some medicine. He told him to rest and be brave.

Sara followed them inside. She felt sorry for Ben. She also felt a little scared of the fire pit. She decided to play with her dolls instead. She hoped Ben would feel better soon.

Ben and Mia were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big, fat cake on the table. It looked yummy. They wanted to eat some.

"Can we have cake, Mom?" Ben asked.

Mom was in the living room. She did not answer. She was busy talking on the phone.

Ben and Mia looked at each other. They decided to take some cake. They climbed on a chair and reached for a knife. They wanted to cut a slice.

But the knife was sharp and heavy. Ben dropped it on the floor. It made a loud noise. Mom heard it and came running.

"What are you doing?" Mom asked. She saw the knife and the cake. She was angry.

"We wanted cake, Mom," Mia said.

Mom shook her head. She took the knife and the cake away. She said, "No cake for you. It is not time for cake. It is time for lunch. And you should never touch a knife. It is dangerous. You could hurt yourself or someone else."

Ben and Mia felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We will not touch a knife again."

Mom hugged them. She said, "I love you, but you have to listen to me. I know what is good for you. Now, let's go and have some soup and bread. Maybe later, you can have a small piece of cake, if you are good."

Once upon a time, there was a warm sunny day. A little boy named Tim and his dog, Max, went outside to play. They liked to organize their toys. Yesterday, they had put all their toys in a big box.

Tim said, "Max, let's organize our toys today!" Max barked happily. They took out all the toys from the box. They put the cars in one pile, the balls in another pile, and the blocks in a third pile. Tim and Max were very happy.

After they organized the toys, Tim and Max played all day. They played with the cars, the balls, and the blocks. They had so much fun in the warm sun. When it was time to go inside, they put all the toys back in the box. They couldn't wait to play again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a bright little girl named Lola. She was full of energy and always eager for adventure. One day, Lola's parents encouraged her to take a tour of a nearby ancient cave.

Lola was so excited and she couldn't wait to explore the place. So she put on a warm jacket and started walking toward the cave. As she approached the entrance, Lola heard strange noises coming from inside. But she wasn't scared and kept going.

Eventually, Lola made it to the end of the cave and found an old piece of artwork. She touched it and it suddenly crumbled into a million pieces. Lola was devastated and quickly ran away, not wanting to be in trouble. 

Unfortunately, Lola's parents were very angry. They had encouraged her to go to the ancient cave, but they hadn't prepared her for the consequences of her actions. In the end, Lola had to accept she had made a bad choice and be punished for it.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a young girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mom cook. She always wore her favorite apron when she cooked.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to separate the eggs. Lily did not know how to do it, so she asked her mom, "How do I separate the eggs, Mom?" Her mom said, "You break the egg and let the yellow part stay in one half, and the white part go into the other half."

Lily tried to separate the eggs, but she made a big mess. The yellow part and the white part mixed together. Lily's mom was not happy. She said, "Lily, you did not do it right. Now we cannot make the cake." Lily was sad and cried. The cake was not made, and they had a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was a little caterpillar named Wally. Wally loved to crawl around in the grass and eat leaves. One day, Wally saw a waffle on the ground. He thought it looked yummy, so he crawled over to it and took a bite. It was very delicious!

But then, Wally started to feel uncomfortable. His tummy didn't feel good. He realized that he should stick to eating leaves instead of waffles. From that day on, Wally only ate leaves and never felt uncomfortable again.

Sara was very excited. The hospital was going to take an x-ray of her arm! She was only three years old and it was her first time.

The doctor put Sara's arm on a special table and said, "Look! We need to load your arm onto the machine." Sara watched as they loaded her arm onto the x-ray machine.

The x-ray machine made a loud noise and the lights were so bright that Sara had to close her eyes. She was embarrassed but smiled and giggled when the doctor said, "You are doing a great job!"

When the x-ray was done, the doctor helped Sara load her arm off the machine. Sara was so happy that she couldn't wait to tell everyone about it.

The little girl was very sad. She was walking in the woods and found a cupboard. It was very big and tall, and it was filled with water up to the top. The little girl looked inside and saw some fish splashing around. She smiled and quickly reached in to try to touch one. She was so sad no more. The fish were so fun and exciting to watch. As she touched one of them, it splashed water everywhere. Drops of water were all over the little girl, and she couldn't stop laughing. Suddenly, she saw another cupboard in the distance and she ran over to it. She couldn't wait to see what new and exciting things were inside.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They saw a big bowl of fruit on the table. Sara wanted to try a lemon. She picked one up and smelled it. It smelled sour.

"Can I eat this?" she asked Ben.

Ben shook his head. "No, it is not good. It will make your face funny."

Sara did not believe him. She wanted to see for herself. She bit the lemon. It was very sour. She made a face and spit it out. She did not like it at all.

"See, I told you," Ben said. He laughed at Sara's face.

Sara was angry. She did not like being laughed at. She picked up the lemon again and slapped Ben with it. Ben was surprised. He felt the lemon juice on his cheek. It stung.

"Ow, that hurts!" he cried. He rubbed his cheek.

Sara felt bad. She did not mean to hurt Ben. She just wanted him to stop laughing. She said sorry to Ben.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I did not mean to slap you. I was just mad."

Ben forgave Sara. He said sorry too.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I did not mean to laugh at you. I was just joking."

They hugged and made up. They decided to play with something else. They left the lemon on the table.

An elderly lady came into the kitchen. She saw the lemon on the table. She wondered who left it there. She picked it up and smelled it. It smelled sour.

She smiled. She liked lemons. She squeezed the lemon into a glass of water. She added some sugar and stirred it. She drank it. It was sweet and sour. She liked it a lot.

She said thank you to the lemon. She did not know who slapped it. She did not care. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a can of spray and wanted to try it. She asked her mom if she could use it, but her mom said no because it was dangerous.

Lily waited until noon when her mom was taking a nap. She snuck outside and sprayed the flowers, the grass, and even her dog. It was so much fun, but it made a big, messy mess.

When her mom woke up, she saw the mess and asked Lily what happened. Lily told her that she sprayed everything with the can. Her mom was very upset and told Lily that it was dangerous and she could have hurt herself or someone else.

Lily felt bad and promised to never do it again. But the bad ending was that her mom had to spend the rest of the day cleaning up the messy mess.

Bea looked out to sea and smiled. She could see a graceful dolphin jumping up in the air and splashing back down again. It was so much fun to watch.

Her mom took her hand and said "Come on, Bea. The sun is setting." Together they walked to the beach.

When they reached the beach, Bea ran to the edge of the water. She put out her hands and splashed the cool sea water over her arms and legs. It felt so refreshing. Then it was time to dry off.

Bea stood in the warm sun and watched as the dolphin jumped back and forth in the sea. She felt the sun's warm rays on her back, dried off, and smiled.

The sun went down and Bea and her mom went home. Bea had had a lovely time at the beach, watching the graceful dolphin.

Once upon a time, there was a slow banana. He was very special and big. Every day he would play with the other fruit and vegetables in the garden but he was always sad. He wished he could do more, but no one seemed to believe in him.

One day, he heard a voice whisper, "Believe in yourself, slow banana!" He didn't know where the voice came from, but he listened. He started to believe in himself and soon he was having so much fun! He would run fast with the apples and swing high in the trees with the kiwi. 

At night, he would sit under the stars and share stories with the other fruit and vegetables. They all believed in the slow banana and all the wonderful things he could do. 

The slow banana was happy and all his friends were too. Now, they all believe in each other and that's how it's stayed ever since.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Mark and Ben. Mark was always the leader and he had big ideas. He decided one day that they should put all of their adventures into a special file. 

"Let's create a file," said Mark. "That way we can remember all the cool things we do together."

Ben agreed. "That's a great idea," he said.

So every day when they went on trips or tried something new, they wrote it all down in their special file. Soon, their file became very popular with other kids too.

One day, Mark and Ben decided to start a new file. This time it was for helping other kids. 

They asked all the children in their neighbourhood what they wanted to do and together they wrote it all down.

At the end of the day, the two friends had created a very special file. It was filled with lots of good ideas that everyone could enjoy.

Mark and Ben were very proud of their accomplishment and they decided that they would keep adding to the file every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch her favorite show on TV. One day, she went to the park to play. There she met a boy named Timmy. They played together and became friends.

Lily was a big fan of Timmy's bright yellow shirt. She told him how much she liked it. Timmy was happy to hear that and said, "I got it from my mom."

Suddenly, a big dog came running towards them. Lily got scared and ran away. Timmy tried to protect her, but the dog bit him. Lily cried and called for help.

The ambulance came and took Timmy to the hospital. Lily felt sad and realized that she should have stayed with her friend. The moral of the story is that we should always be there for our friends, even when we are scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink juice and watch cartoons on TV. One day, Lily's mom gave her a glass of fine apple juice to drink while she watched her favorite cartoon. 

As Lily drank her juice, she noticed that her cartoon was not playing on the TV. She asked her mom why she couldn't watch her cartoon. Her mom explained that the TV was broken, but it would be fine soon. 

Lily finished her juice and decided to play with her toys while she waited for the TV to be fixed. She was happy because she had her favorite drink and her toys to play with. After a little while, her mom fixed the TV and Lily was able to watch her cartoon again. She was so happy and grateful for her mom and her fine apple juice.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom was only three years old, but he was very brave. One day, Tom was playing in his backyard when he saw an umbrella lying on the ground. It looked like it had been hidden there. 

Tom got curious. He picked up the umbrella and opened it up. Suddenly, the umbrella started to spin around in a circle! Tom was so surprised he jumped back and the umbrella fell to the ground.

Tom started to laugh and picked up the umbrella again. He waved it around and said, â€œIâ€™m a superhero!â€

Tom couldn't help but laugh. He ran back to his house and said to his mom, â€œI found an umbrella and I hid it in a bush!â€ 

His mom smiled, â€œThatâ€™s so clever, Tom. Why donâ€™t you go find it again?â€

Tom smiled and ran back outside to look for the hidden umbrella. He was so proud of himself!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Tom and Alisa. They often liked to go for walks together. On one such day, they went to a nearby park and discussed a very special building. 

Tom said, â€œI know of a very special building. It looks so good!â€

Alisa asked, â€œWhat is it?â€ 

Tom replied, â€œIt is a castle. Let us go there and have a look.â€

They quickly walked to the castle and stood in front of its tall walls. It looked very grand and Alisa said, â€œIt looks so good!â€

Tom said, â€œYes, it is so grand and beautiful.â€ 

They both enjoyed looking at the castle. Tom and Alisa felt happy and looked forward to discussing more buildings.

Once there was a pretty cable. It was so smooth and glistening in the sun. Everyone wanted to touch it.

One day, a man came to take away the cable. He held it between his hands and shook it. It felt different, as if something magical was happening.

Then, the man put the cable in a machine. He turned it on and it made a loud humming noise. Suddenly, something amazing happened. The cable came alive and started bouncing around.

The little cable was shaking with joy and kept bouncing around the room. Everyone laughed and watched with delight. It was so much fun to see the cable shaking so fast.

Finally, the man took the cable out of the machine. It was still shaking a little, but was no longer bouncing around the room. The cable was happy and so was everyone else!

Once upon a time there was a cherry tree in a big field. One day, the tree was busy loading lots of big and juicy cherries. It was a mysterious sight to see! Everyone in the village wanted to get a cherry, but they were too high up the tree. 

The village men thought of a plan. They brought a ladder and tried to climb up the tree to get the cherries. But the ladder was too small and it didn't reach the cherries. 

Then a clever girl had an idea. She told the village men to get a long piece of string and tie it to the cherries. She then pulled the string until the cherries fell down from the tree. Everyone was so happy and the girl was very proud. 

The village men loaded all the cherries into a big basket and took them back to the village. Everyone had a wonderful time enjoying the delicious cherries. It was such a mysterious and wonderful day!

One day, a charming little rabbit was hopping through the woods. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It was a missile entering the sky! The rabbit was scared, but he was also curious. He decided to follow the missile to see where it was going.

The rabbit hopped for a long time before he saw a big castle up ahead. The missile had gone straight to the top, and it disappeared into the castle. The rabbit was so excited! He wanted to explore the castle and find out what was inside.

The rabbit hopped up to the castle and peeked through the gate. It was so big and beautiful. He carefully opened the gate and entered the courtyard. Suddenly, he heard a voice coming from inside the castle. It was the most charming voice he had ever heard.

The rabbit hopped towards the sound and saw the most amazing sight. A beautiful princess was standing inside the castle, singing a sweet song. The rabbit was so happy that he had been brave enough to follow the missile to this magical place. He knew he was going to have the most wonderful day.

The sun was shining and the sky was a peaceful blue. Tommy was playing in the garden when he saw an aeroplane flying across the sky. He shouted "Wow!" and watched it fly away in the distance.

Tommy wanted to fly too. He waved his hands and leaped into the air, trying to fly after the aeroplane. His mom heard him and came over, putting her hands on his shoulders.

"You can't fly, Tommy. But don't worry. I have a surprise for you," said his mom, and she snapped her fingers.

Suddenly, the garden filled with floating bubbles! Tommy giggled with joy and jumped up and down, trying to catch them. Each time he popped one, Tommy laughed and clapped his hands. He even managed to catch a few in his hands and blow them away. It was so much fun!

When all the bubbles had snapped away, Tommy flopped on the grass and looked up at the sky. He thought about the aeroplane he had seen earlier, wishing he could take a journey and explore the world. But for now, he was just happy to watch the clouds drift by, peaceful and free.

It was a warm and sunny day in the park. Johnny, who was three years old, saw a slide. He was so excited that he ran to it and was ready to slide down. But the slide came with a surprise. There was a dishwasher near the slide that made a loud noise every time it moved. Johnny was scared at first and did not want to go down the slide.

After watching other children have fun on the slide, Johnny eventually gained the courage to go down it. He took a deep breath and went for it. On the way down, Johnny heard the loud dishwasher sound again and was so scared that he almost fell off the slide. But then he realized that the noise was not coming from the dishwasher but from the slide itself! It was a loud thump every time he slid down.

As he continued to slide, Johnny got used to the loud thumping sound and began to enjoy the ride even more. It was almost like music to him! He eventually became so brave that he went back to the slide again and again.

Johnny smiled with joy and felt so proud as he finished sliding. He had gone through his fear of the loud dishwasher and was now cheerful every time he heard it. Johnny now knows that he should never be scared of loud noises, but embrace them with excitement.

Once upon a time, there was a kind young boy called Jack. Every day, he liked to play in the big park near his house.

One day, Jack's mom said to him, â€œI have to go out for a little bit, so you need to stay here and play. Donâ€™t worry, I wonâ€™t be gone long.â€

Lily was sad. She missed her mom. Her mom went to a distant place for work. She said she would come back soon, but Lily did not know when.

She hugged her teddy bear and cried. She wanted her mom to comfort her. She wanted to hear her voice and feel her hand.

Then she heard a knock on the door. She wiped her tears and opened it. It was her dad. He smiled and said, "Hi, Lily. I have a surprise for you."

He held a phone in his hand. He said, "Look, it's mom. She wants to talk to you."

Lily's eyes lit up. She took the phone and said, "Mom, mom, I miss you!"

She heard her mom's voice. She said, "I miss you too, Lily. I love you so much. I'm sorry I have to be in a distant place, but I'll be back soon. How are you?"

Lily told her mom about her day. She told her about her teddy bear, her friends, and her dad. She said, "I'm okay, mom. But I wish you were here."

Her mom said, "I wish that too, Lily. But I'm proud of you for being brave and strong. You're my sweet girl. And you know what? I have a gift for you. I sent it with dad. He'll give it to you after we finish talking."

Lily was curious. She said, "What is it, mom?"

Her mom said, "It's something to comfort you when you miss me. It's something to remind you of me. It's something to hold in your hand."

Lily said, "What is it, mom? Tell me, tell me!"

Her mom said, "It's a surprise, Lily. You'll see. I love you, Lily. I'll talk to you again soon. Bye, bye."

Lily said, "Bye, bye, mom. I love you too."

She gave the phone back to her dad. He hugged her and said, "You're a good girl, Lily. And you're very lucky. Your mom loves you a lot. And so do I."

He said, "Are you ready for your surprise?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, yes, yes!"

Her dad reached into his pocket and pulled out a small box. He opened it and showed it to Lily. It was a necklace. It had a heart-shaped pendant. It was shiny and pretty.

He said, "This is your gift from mom. She made it for you. She said it's a piece of her heart. She said you can wear it and feel her love. She said it will comfort you when you miss her. She said it will remind you of her. She said it will hold her hand."

Lily gasped. She said, "Wow, wow, wow! It's beautiful, dad. Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad."

She put the necklace around her neck. She felt the pendant on her chest. She felt warm and happy. She felt her mom's love. She felt her mom's hand.

She smiled and said, "I love it, dad. I love you, dad. I love mom. I love you both."

She hugged her dad and her teddy bear. She felt comforted. She felt loved. She felt less sad.

One day, Bob the whale was swimming in the ocean. He felt something wet on his back and knew he needed to clean himself. He stopped to take a break and called to his friend Jimmy the starfish. 

"Jimmy," he said, "I think I need help cleaning myself." 

Jimmy smiled and said, "I'm here to help! Let me take a look." 

Jimmy looked at Bob's back and saw that it was very thin. He knew that he could help Bob clean it.

Jimmy swam around Bob, spraying water everywhere. He rubbed Bob's back with a soft cloth until it was clean and shiny. 

When Jimmy was finished, Bob smiled. "Thanks for helping me clean, Jimmy," he said. 

Jimmy said, "It's my pleasure. It's important to keep yourself nice and clean!" 

Bob thanked Jimmy again and the two of them continued to swim around, happy that Bob was now clean again.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jake. Jake was three years old and he had a pet dog named Spot. Every morning Jake and Spot would go for a walk in the park. 

One day, Jake and Spot were walking in the park when Jake saw a little dish on the ground. He picked it up and thought it was very pretty. He wanted to take it home and make something good from it. 

Jake thought about it for a while and then he had an idea. He could make a cake in the dish! He could give it to Spot as a treat! 

So Jake and Spot went home, and Jake got all the ingredients he needed to make the cake. He mixed them all together in the dish, and then put it in the oven. 

After a while, Jake took the cake out of the oven. It looked really good. He gave it to Spot as a treat, and Spot loved it! 

Jake was so happy, and he was proud of himself for thinking of such a good idea. He cuddled up with Spot and they both enjoyed the cake together. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a shy boy. He had a question but was too afraid to ask.

One day, he was walking in the park. He saw a pretty girl. He wanted to talk to her but felt nervous.

Then he heard someone call his name. It was the pretty girl. She asked him his question and he told her. She smiled and said she knew the answer.

The shy boy was so happy that he gave her a kiss. The girl was so surprised.

They both smiled and laughed. From that day forward, they were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a lively spider. The spider liked to go on adventures. One day, he decided to load up his backpacks with all the things he would need. He packed food and water, and a map.

Then, he set off on his journey. He went over hills and through fields. He climbed up a mountain and even went swimming in a lake. Along the way, he made lots of friends.

The lively spider had the most amazing adventures. Everywhere he went, he brought laughter and smiles to everyone. He had a great time and was always ready for more! 

Eventually, his journey came to an end. He loaded up his backpack one last time, said goodbye to his friends, and started his trip back home. He had had the most amazing time, and he couldn't wait to tell everyone about his adventures.

Lily and Tom were adventurous kids. They liked to explore the world and find new things. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's go in and see!" said Tom.

"OK, but be careful!" said Lily.

They climbed down the hole and saw a dark tunnel. They walked along the tunnel, holding hands. They saw shiny rocks and strange bugs. They heard a loud roar.

"What was that?" asked Lily.

"I don't know, but it sounds scary!" said Tom.

They wanted to go back, but they could not find the way. They were lost.

"Help! Help!" they shouted.

But no one heard them. They remained in the hole, alone and afraid. They never saw the world again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to talk to her friends and family. One day, her mom gave her a camera to take pictures. Lily was very happy because it was an original camera. She took pictures of her toys and her cat. Then, she showed the pictures to her friends and they talked about them. Lily felt very proud of her pictures and her original camera. The end.

Tim and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big tent with many animals inside. They want to go and look at them.

"Can we go, Mom?" Tim asks.

"OK, but be careful and stay close to me," Mom says.

They go inside the tent and see many animals. They see a lion, a monkey, a zebra, and a leopard. The leopard is sleeping on a big rock. He has spots on his fur.

"Wow, look at the leopard!" Mia says. "He is so pretty!"

She goes closer to the leopard and tries to touch him. But the leopard wakes up and sees Mia. He is angry. He does not like strangers. He growls and shows his teeth.

"Roar!" the leopard says.

Mia is scared. She runs back to Tim and Mom. The leopard jumps off the rock and chases Mia.

"Help!" Mia cries.

Mom grabs Mia and covers her with her coat. She protects her from the leopard. Tim runs to a man who works in the tent. He tells him about the leopard.

"Help! The leopard is angry and wants to hurt Mia!" Tim says.

The man hears Tim and sees the leopard. He gets a big net and throws it over the leopard. He catches the leopard and puts him back on the rock.

"Sorry, kids. The leopard is not used to people. He is not a pet. He is a wild animal. You should not go near him or touch him. He can be dangerous," the man says.

Mom hugs Mia and Tim. She is glad they are safe.

"Thank you, sir. We are sorry. We did not know. We will not do it again," Mom says.

The man smiles and nods. He gives them some stickers of animals. They say sorry to the leopard and leave the tent. They go to the swings and have fun. They learn to respect the animals and their space.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very happy and excited, but she was feeling dizzy. She decided to join a game, but she didn't know what to do. 

The game was called 'Under'. The little girl looked under the chair and saw a big surprise - a toy! She was so happy that she couldn't stop smiling. She grabbed the toy and started playing.

The little girl had fun playing with her toy. She played until she got dizzy and felt like she was going to fall down. 

So, the little girl stopped playing and lay down. She snuggled her toy and closed her eyes. After a while, she felt better. Then, she got up and joined the game again.

Anna and Ben were twins. They liked to play and laugh together. But they did not like to get haircuts. They thought haircuts were scary. They did not want to go to the salon with Mom.

"Come on, kids, it's time to go," Mom said. "You need a haircut. Your hair is too long and messy."

"No, Mom, no!" Anna and Ben said. They ran and hid under the bed. They hoped Mom would not find them.

But Mom was smart. She knew where they were. She smiled and said, "Okay, if you don't want to go, I have a surprise for you. I have a lovely gift for you. Do you want to see it?"

Anna and Ben were curious. They liked surprises. They liked gifts. They crawled out from under the bed. They followed Mom to the living room.

There, they saw a big box with a bow. Mom said, "This is for you. Go ahead, open it."

"Surprise!" Mom said. "Now you can give each other a haircut. Isn't that fun?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They looked at the scissors. They looked at Mom. They did not think it was fun. They thought it was scary. They wished they had gone to the salon. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we changed our minds. Can we please go to the salon?"

Lily and Max liked to play in the park. They ran, jumped, and slid on the grass and the swings. One day, they saw a big statue of a lion in the park. It looked very scary, with sharp teeth and claws.

"Let's go see the lion!" Max said. He was brave and curious.

Max laughed. "Don't be silly, Lily. It's not a real lion. It's just a statue. It can't move or talk or bite. Come on, I'll show you."

He took Lily's hand and walked towards the statue. Lily trembled. She did not want to go near the lion. She closed her eyes and hoped it would go away.

When they reached the statue, Max touched its nose and mane. He smiled and said, "See, Lily? It's just a statue. It's made of stone. It's not scary at all. You can touch it too."

Lily opened her eyes and looked at the statue. It was still and quiet. It did not roar or snap. It looked like a big toy. She felt a little better. She reached out and touched its ear. It was cold and hard.

"You're right, Max. It's just a statue. It's not scary at all. It's kind of nice." She said.

Max and Lily hugged the statue and pretended it was their friend. They named it Leo and told it stories. They had fun with the statue. They were happy and organized. They put their toys in a bag and said goodbye to Leo. They promised to come back and play with him again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She wanted to have an adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a good boy, but sometimes he would scream. He would scream when he was sad, and he would scream when he was mad. One day, Tim found a smooth rock. He liked the rock very much, so he took it to his secret chamber in his room.

In the chamber, Tim would play with his toys and the smooth rock. But one day, his friend, Lily, came to play with him. When Tim showed her the smooth rock, Lily wanted to play with it too. Tim did not want to share the rock, so he screamed at Lily. Lily was sad and left Tim's house.

Tim felt bad for making Lily sad. He thought about what he did and decided to share the smooth rock with her. The next day, Tim went to Lily's house and gave her the rock. They played together and had lots of fun. Tim learned that sharing is good and it makes others happy.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. But sometimes their toys are messy. Mom says they have to sort their toys before they can watch TV.

Lily and Ben start to sort their toys. Lily puts the dolls in a pink basket. Ben puts the cars in a blue box. They work together to sort the blocks by color and shape. They put the books on the shelf.

"Look, Mom, we sorted our toys!" Lily says. She is proud of her work.

"Good job, Lily and Ben!" Mom says. She smiles and gives them a hug. "You are very helpful and smart. I love you both."

Lily and Ben hug Mom back. They feel happy and warm. They think Mom is the best.

"Can we watch TV now?" Ben asks.

"Sure, you can watch TV for a little while. But first, let me show you something." Mom says. She takes them to the window and points outside.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says. She sees a big rainbow in the sky. It has many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

Once upon a time there was a bossy little girl. Every day she would boss her mom and dad around.

Her parents were tired of it and they decided to punish her. They told her she had to go to the hospital.

The little girl was scared and didn't want to go. But her parents said she had to.

When she got to the hospital, she was surprised. All the doctors and nurses were nice to her. They smiled and gave her toys and candy.

Finally, her parents came to get her. They were sorry they had punished her. But they said it was important to be nice and listen.

The little girl learned her lesson. She hadn't been nice before, but now she was very polite. And she never bossed her parents around again.

Once there was a nice little girl who wanted to buy an ice cream with her pocket money. She went to the store, but then realised she only had a few cents.

Suddenly, the little girl saw a mint growing by the store entrance. She carefully picked it and showed it the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper smiled and said, "If you pay with the mint, I will give you an ice cream for free!"

The little girl was so happy, and thanked the shopkeeper. She paid with the mint, and got the yummy ice cream she wanted.

The little girl was very happy and enjoyed her nice treat. She was glad that she was able to pay with the mint and get her ice cream.

Lucy was excited. She was waiting in front of a big locked door. Her dad was with her. He was unlocking the door with a really big key.

When he opened the door, Lucy saw that behind it was an oak tree. It was so big! She looked up and saw lots of leaves and branches.

Her dad put his hand on her shoulder and pointed to something on the tree. He showed her a little bird's nest filled with feathers.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who loved to play with water. One day, she decided to pour water on her bed. She thought it would be fun to jump on the wet sheet. But her mom saw what she did and got angry. She scolded Lily and told her not to pour water on her bed again.

Lily felt sad and went to her room. She saw her long hair in the mirror and decided to cut it to make herself feel better. She took a pair of scissors and started cutting her hair. But she accidentally cut too much and her hair became very short. She started crying and her mom came to see what happened.

Her mom tried to fix her hair but it was too short. Lily had to go to school with short hair and all her friends laughed at her. She felt embarrassed and wished she had not poured water on her bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was very tired, so every day she would take a nap. One day, she decided to take a test while she was napping. As she was sleeping, she heard a loud noise and suddenly her test was split into two pieces! Jill was so shocked that she quickly woke up. She was very surprised to see that the pieces of her test were spread all over. 

Jill quickly grabbed the pieces and put them back together. But no matter how hard she tried, the paper wouldn't stay together. She was getting tired from trying so hard and she knew she had to find a better way. 

She thought for a second and then had an idea! She got some glue from the kitchen and then carefully put the pieces of her test back together. After a few minutes, the test was together again! 

Jill was so relieved that she decided to take another nap. As she slept, she dreamed of all the tests she would split in the future!

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to watch television after school. They watched cartoons and games and animals. But their mom said they had to complete their homework first. She gave them books and pencils and paper.

Tim did his homework quickly. He wrote his name and drew some shapes and numbers. He showed his mom his paper. She smiled and said, "Good job, Tim. You are very smart. You can watch television now." Tim was proud. He ran to the living room and turned on the television.

Sam did not do his homework. He did not like to write or draw. He wanted to watch television. He hid his books and pencils and paper under his bed. He sneaked to the living room and joined Tim. He pretended he did his homework too.

But their mom knew. She checked under Sam's bed and found his books and pencils and paper. She was angry. She went to the living room and turned off the television. She said, "Sam, you did not do your homework. You lied to me. You cannot watch television. You have to go to your room and do your homework now." Sam was sad. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't like homework. I like television." But mom did not listen. She took him to his room and closed the door.

Tim felt sorry for Sam. He wanted to share his television with him. But he also wanted to watch his favorite show. He did not know what to do. He looked at the television. He looked at Sam's door. He felt bad. He wished they both did their homework. He wished they both could watch television. He wished they both were proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved quizzes. He would make a quiz everyday and ask his friends to play. 

One day, the boy received an invitation to take a special quiz. He was excited because he had never seen a quiz like this before. 

He followed the invitation and it took him to a sour garden. He was surprised to see many sweet and sour fruits growing in the garden. He opened the door and walked in. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice say, "Welcome!" He saw a thick, green monster at the center of the garden. It was the quiz monster. The boy was a bit scared but he was also very excited. 

The monster asked him many simple questions and the boy answered them one by one. Finally, the monster said that he had passed the quiz. The boy thanked the monster and ran home, full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was only three years old and very spoiled. Everywhere she went, people told her she was the best.

One day, the little girl was walking with her mother and saw a big bowl of ice cream. Eager to have it, she asked for some, but her mother said no. She scowled and let out a big yawn.

The next day, the little girl and her mother were walking by the same bowl of ice cream. The little girl's mother said, "We can have some ice cream now, if you still want it." The little girl smiled and said yes.

When they arrived at the bowl of ice cream, a big crowd had gathered. They were all yawning and complaining that the ice cream was cold. The little girl still wanted the ice cream and asked her mother why everyone was yawning.

Her mother explained that too much of a good thing can be bad. If people economize what they have, they can stay happy. The lesson here is that too much of a good thing can be spoiled, and it's okay to take things in moderation.

Once there was a little boy called Jack who was always very excited. One day he went outside to play and gathered some big stones. His mom noticed and said, "Jack, what are you doing with all those stones?".

Jack smiled and said, "I'm going to remove my stomach!" 

His mom looked so surprised! She said, "You can't remove your stomach. It's not possible and you can get hurt if you try." 

Jack listened carefully and thought for a while. Finally he said, "I know Mommy. I was just pretending. I knew it wouldn't be possible." 

His mom said, "That's my clever boy. You should always use your brain before doing something. It's better to think twice before acting." 

Jack smiled and agreed. He was excited to learn this new lesson and knew that if he used his brain before doing something, he could stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to have tea parties with her toys. One day, she invited her teddy bear to join her for tea. But when she poured the tea, she accidentally spilled it on her teddy bear. 

"Oh no!" cried Lily. "I'm worried that I ruined my teddy bear."

Lily was relieved and happy to hear this. They continued to have their tea party and enjoyed each other's company. From that day on, Lily knew that spending time with loved ones was more important than things like tea.

Lila was a compassionate girl who liked to help animals. One day, she found a bird with a broken wing in her garden. She gently picked up the bird and brought it inside. She asked her mom to prepare a box with some soft cloth and water for the bird.

"Mom, can we keep the bird until it gets better?" Lila asked.

"Well, we can try, but we have to be very careful. The bird might be scared or hurt. We have to let it rest and not touch it too much," Mom said.

Lila nodded and put the bird in the box. She noticed that one of its feathers was loose. She carefully took the feather and put it in her pocket. She thought it was very pretty and soft.

The next day, Lila checked on the bird. It looked a little better. It moved its wing a little and made a small sound. Lila smiled and whispered, "Hello, bird. I'm Lila. I'm your friend. I hope you feel better soon."

The bird looked at Lila with its bright eyes. It seemed to understand. It made another sound and tilted its head. Lila felt happy. She took out the feather from her pocket and showed it to the bird.

"Look, this is your feather. It fell off yesterday. It's very pretty. Can I keep it? It reminds me of you," Lila said.

The bird nodded and flapped its wing. It seemed to say yes. Lila thanked the bird and put the feather in her hair. She thought they looked like friends. She hoped the bird would get better soon and fly again. She was a compassionate girl who liked to help animals.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She was very worried, because she had lost her favorite toy. One night, while she was crying in bed, she heard a gentle hooting sound. Molly opened her window and a friendly owl flew in. 

Molly was surprised, but the owl only wanted to help. It flew around the room, searching until it found Molly's toy. It bowed its wings and dropped the toy in Molly's lap. 

Molly was amazed and asked the owl, â€œWhat are you?â€

Molly thanked the owl and fell asleep with a smile on her face. From that day on, Molly was sure that owls were magical creatures who could make any worries go away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around in the park. One day, she fell and got a cut on her knee. It hurt a lot and she started to cry.

Her mommy saw her crying and asked, "What happened, Lily? Did you hurt yourself?"
