Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a very special bow. It was a soft pink bow with sparkles. Every day the little girl would show her bow to all her friends.

One day, the little girl decided she wanted to show even more people her bow. So she went to the park. As she walked around the park, the little girl held her bow out for everyone to see.

People smiled and waved when they saw the little girlâ€™s bow. Some even stopped and said how pretty it was. Everyone loved the little girlâ€™s bow.

At the end of the day, the little girl was so happy. She had shown so many people her bow and everyone seemed to really enjoy it. She went home with the biggest smile on her face.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went for a walk with her mom. They saw a brilliant blue butterfly. Lucy wanted to catch it, so she tried to squeeze her hand to grab it. But the butterfly flew away.

"Mom, I wanted to catch the butterfly!" Lucy said. Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Lucy. Let's try to find another one."

They walked and walked until they saw another blue butterfly. Lucy tried to squeeze her hand again to catch it. This time, she was gentle and the butterfly stayed in her hand. "I did it, Mom!" Lucy said happily.

Her mom was proud of her. "Well done, Lucy! Now, let's let the butterfly go and watch it fly away." Lucy opened her hand and the blue butterfly flew away. They both smiled as they watched it fly into the sky.

Jill went to the subway with her mom. She was excited because she was going to pick out a toy. Mom said Jill could pick out any toy she liked. 

When they got there, Jill wanted to get a big, purple bear. But it was too expensive for her mom. She refused to buy it for Jill.

Jill felt sad, but her mom smiled and said, â€œDonâ€™t worry. You can pick out something else.â€ She was being kind.

Jill spotted an orange elephant toy. It was just the right size and it was much cheaper. She smiled and asked mom if she could have it. 

Mom said, â€œYes! It looks like a much better choice!â€ She hugged Jill and said, â€œThank you for being so kind and understanding.â€

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day she found a bookshelf and wanted to find out what was inside. Her parents had warned her not to investigate bookshelves alone, but she decided to delay and open it anyways. When she got close, she noticed that the bookshelf was very dangerous. She found herself trapped and realized it was too late - she couldn't get out. From then on, the little girl always listened to her parents and never delayed doing the things they said.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big stick on the ground. Ben picked it up and said, "Look, I have a sword!"

Lily said, "No, it's not a sword. It's a wand. I can do magic with it!"

They started to argue. Ben wanted to be a knight and Lily wanted to be a fairy. They pulled the stick from each other.

Suddenly, a man came over. He was wearing a suit and a hat. He looked angry. He said, "Hey, that's my stick! Give it back to me!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They did not know the man. They said, "Sorry, sir. We did not know it was yours. Why do you need a stick?"

The man said, "It's not a stick. It's a cane. It helps me walk. It's very expensive. It's made of wood and gold. It was a gift from my friend."

Ben and Lily felt sorry for the man. They gave him the stick. They said, "We're sorry, sir. We hope you can walk well with your cane."

The man said, "Thank you, kids. You are very kind. Here, take this." He gave them a coin. He said, "You can buy some candy with this. But don't play with other people's things. They might be important to them."

Ben and Lily said, "Thank you, sir. We won't do it again. We'll be careful."

They ran to the candy store. They bought some candy. They shared it with each other. They said, "We learned something today. We should not take what is not ours. And we should not fight over a stick. We can have fun with other things."

They smiled and hugged. They went back to the park. They played with a ball and a kite. They had a lot of fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to gather rocks and sticks from the forest. He would put them in his backpack and show them to his mom and dad.

One day, Timmy and his friend Sally went on a walk in the forest. They saw a beautiful view of the mountains and the trees. Sally said, "Wow, this view is so pretty!"

Timmy agreed and said, "I like to gather rocks and sticks here. Do you want to help me?"

Sally said yes and they started to gather rocks and sticks. But then, they found something disgusting. It was a smelly old shoe. Timmy said, "Ew, that's disgusting! Let's leave it here." And they continued to gather rocks and sticks until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially when it was cold outside. One day, Lily went outside to play and it was very, very cold. She put on her warm coat, hat, and gloves and started to play.

As she was playing, she saw a skeleton decoration in her neighbor's yard. It was very scary, but Lily thought it was cool. She went closer to take a look, but suddenly she heard a loud noise. It was her mom calling her to come inside for some hot chocolate.

Lily ran back to her house, but she felt uncomfortable. She couldn't feel her fingers or toes. When she got inside, her mom helped her take off her coat and gloves. As soon as she took off her gloves, she realized her fingers were frozen! Her mom quickly put them under warm water to help them thaw.

From that day on, Lily learned to be careful when playing outside in the cold. She also learned that skeletons can be scary, but they are just decorations and not real.

Once upon a time there were two rabbits. They were hopping around in a field looking for something tasty to eat.

Suddenly, one of the rabbits stopped hopping. "Look over there,â€ it said. â€œIt's a pretty carrot!"

The other rabbit hopped to the carrot and said, â€œIt looks delicious.â€

The first rabbit smiled and said, â€œLet's share it! I'll offer half of it to you.â€

The second rabbit was happy. â€œYes please! I love carrots.â€

So the two rabbits shared the pretty carrot while hopping around in the field. They had a lot of fun and ate the whole carrot!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Alice. One day, she was at home when she heard a loud noise coming from the kitchen. She was brave, so she decided to go see what was happening.

When she got to the kitchen, she found her brother sitting on the floor, surrounded by broken dishes. The pieces of glass were all around him and he was crying. Alice wanted to know what had happened, so she asked him, "What happened?"

He answered, "I was playing with the dishes, but it was dangerous. I was trying to make a tower but I didn't succeed. Now, look at all the mess that I made!"

Alice could see that her brother was very sad, so she comforted him and said, "It's okay. You shouldn't play with dangerous things. Next time, don't mess with the kitchen. Let's clean up this mess together, alright?"

Her brother nodded and they cleaned up the mess together.

The moral of the story is that it is dangerous to play with dangerous things, and it's important to listen to your older siblings, who will often be able to advise you on how to behave safely.

Once there was a boy named Tom who loved adventure. His parents decided to take him on a safari so he could see the amazing animals. He was very excited!

They went to Africa and drove through the jungle in a big jeep. Tom saw so many animals he had never seen before! He watched huge elephants, tiny squirrels and powerful lions. All the animals were so amazing and beautiful.

He was so happy and excited that he wanted to make sure he always remembered them. He wanted to value all the animals he saw.

But then one afternoon, they visited a lake. Sadly, they found it covered with dead fish. It made Tom so sad and he didn't have anything good to say. He wanted to remind himself to always value all the living creatures he could find.

Tom's safari taught him an important lesson - to value all living things, no matter where he goes in the world.

Once upon a time there lived a small boy. His name was James. He was very ordinary.

One day, James found a puzzle. It was beautiful and it had many pieces. James was curious and wanted to put it together.

He worked very hard and very carefully. He tried to balance all the pieces. He knew it was important to balance them carefully in the right shape and spot. 

After a few hours of hard work, James finally finished the puzzle. He was so proud and excited! 

He showed it to his mum and dad. They were so happy and proud of him. James smiled and was happy too. 

The end.

Billy was a three year old boy. He used to love playing in his grandparents' house. It was fun and old. 
One day, he woke up early. His grandfather was already hard at work in the backyard. Billy looked around and saw his grandmother baking in the kitchen. 
Billy went to his grandfather and asked, "What are you doing grandpa?"
Grandpa smiled, "I'm fixing the old fence in the backyard."
Billy was excited. He asked if he could help. Grandpa said, "Yes, of course. Come with me and you can help me with the old work."
Billy smiled, and followed his grandpa to the backyard. He was so excited to help his grandpa with the old work.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to race them on the dirt path and make vroom noises. Tom had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They both loved their cars very much.

One day, a big dog came into the garden. He saw the toy cars and thought they were bones. He ran towards them and grabbed Tom's red car in his mouth. He bit it hard and tore off one of the wheels. Tom saw this and was very upset. He cried and shouted at the dog.

"Bad dog! Give me back my car! You broke it!" Tom said.

Lily heard Tom and came to see what was wrong. She saw the dog with the red car and felt sorry for Tom. She also felt scared of the dog. She wanted to help Tom, but she did not know what to do.

She remembered that her mom had told her to be kind to animals, even if they did something wrong. She also remembered that her mom had given her a bag of dog treats. She ran to get the bag and came back to the garden. She waved the bag at the dog and said in a soft voice.

"Hello, dog. Do you want a treat? Let go of the car and I will give you one."

The dog smelled the treat and let go of the car. He wagged his tail and came closer to Lily. Lily gave him a treat and petted him gently. The dog licked her hand and barked happily.

Tom stopped crying and picked up his car. He saw that the wheel was gone and felt sad. He looked at Lily and the dog and felt a little better. He said to Lily.

"Thank you, Lily. You are very brave and nice. I'm sorry I yelled at the dog. He did not know it was my car."

Lily smiled and said to Tom.

"You're welcome, Tom. I'm sorry your car is broken. Maybe we can fix it together. Or we can share my car. It has four wheels."

Tom nodded and said to Lily.

"Okay, Lily. You are a good friend. And the dog is not so bad. Maybe we can play with him too."

They hugged each other and played with the dog and the cars. They learned that being kind and forgiving is better than being angry and mean. They also learned that sharing and helping is more fun than fighting and hurting. They had a happy day in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a family with a mom, a dad, a big sister, and a little brother. They lived in a small house with a big tree in the yard. The family was broken because they didn't talk to each other. They were always sad and didn't play together.

One day, the big sister said, "I want to solve this problem. Let's talk and play together." The little brother said, "Yes, I want to be happy." So, they went to their mom and dad and asked them to join them.

The family started to talk and play together. They laughed and had fun. The broken family became happy again. They learned that talking and playing together can solve problems and make everyone happy. And they lived happily ever after.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big yellow truck. The truck has many bananas. Lily and Tom love bananas. They run to the truck and ask the man, "Can we have some bananas, please?"

The man is nice. He smiles and says, "Sure, you can have some bananas. But you have to do something for me first. You have to make me laugh. Can you do that?"

Lily and Tom think. They want to make the man laugh. They look at each other and nod. They have an idea. They start to act silly. They make funny faces, they jump up and down, they sing a silly song. They do everything they can to make the man laugh.

The man watches them. He starts to giggle. Then he starts to chuckle. Then he starts to laugh out loud. He laughs so hard that he drops some bananas. Lily and Tom are happy. They made the man laugh. They pick up the bananas and say, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

The man says, "You're welcome, you're welcome, you're welcome! You are very funny and very smart. You can have as many bananas as you want. Enjoy!"

Lily and Tom hug the man. They take the bananas and run to the bench. They peel the bananas and eat them. They are sweet and yummy. They share some bananas with the birds and the squirrels. They are happy and full. They smile and say, "This was an easy and fun day. We love bananas and we love the man. He is our new friend."

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. Joe was very busy. Every day he tried to do lots of things, like playing with his toys. 

One day, Joe wanted to try something different. So he grabbed a football and went outside to play. He tried very hard to kick the football, but it was difficult. But Joe was determined to try again, and he kept trying until he got it right!

After that, Joe was very happy. He started playing with the football all the time. He tried different types of throws and catches. He even tried to make the football do tricks!

He played for hours until it started to get dark. Joe was so busy playing with the football that he didn't even realize the time had passed by so quickly. 

The next day, Joe was ready to try it all over again. He couldn't wait to get back out there and have some more fun with the football.

Once upon a time, there lived a King and Queen in a new palace. The King and Queen were very happy and liked living in their palace. One day, the King wanted to go for a walk outside the palace. 

The Queen was worried that something might happen to the King so she asked the castle guards to prevent him from leaving the palace. The castle guards said yes, and the King was not allowed to go for his walk.

The King was very upset about this and stormed off to another part of the palace. He stayed in a room for hours, not talking to anyone. The Queen was worried and wanted to make the King happy again.

So she ordered some of the castle guards to bring her a present. The present was a new toy palace and when the King saw it, he was so excited! He hugged the Queen and thanked her for the new palace. After that, the King was much happier and the castle guards were allowed to prevent him from going outside anymore. The King and Queen lived happily ever after in their new palace.

Once upon a time there was an elephant who had a special trunk. He could use it to make things disappear! But everything had a result. Every time he used it, something hidden would appear. 

One day, he tried to use it again. He made his favourite toy disappear. But the result was a surprise. Instead of a hidden toy, he found a hidden treasure! He was so excited! He found lots of jewels and coins. 

The elephant was so happy that his trunk had worked. He kept it safe and only used it for very special things. He never wanted the treasure to disappear!

The end!

Once upon a time there was a wreck. It was sitting very still in the sea. It had been there for a very long time, too.

One day a small boat came close to the wreck. Inside the boat was a brave little girl called Jenny. She wanted to explore the wreck.

Jenny carefully stepped onto the fragile wreck. She looked around and saw so many exciting things. Then she heard a noise, so she quickly closed her eyes. Jenny stayed very still and waited.

When she opened her eyes, everything was quiet. Jenny had been very scared, but she was brave. She continued exploring the wreck.

The end.

The little girl was busy by the tree. She had a zipper in her hands and was looking for something. Suddenly, she saw a big bear coming down the hill. She was so scared, she dropped the zipper! The big bear saw the zipper and started to destroy it. The little girl was so sad. She wanted to keep her zipper, but the bear was too strong. The bear kept destroying until there was nothing left of the zipper. The little girl was so busy trying to save her zipper, but it was too late. She ran away quickly, and the bear never came back.

One day, a little mouse named Mimi wanted to find a new home. She was tired of living in a hole under a big tree. She wanted to see more of the world and have some fun. So she packed a small bag with some cheese and nuts and said goodbye to her mother.

"Be careful, Mimi," her mother said. "The world is big and scary. There are many things that can hurt you. Stay away from cats and traps and loud noises."

"I will, Mom," Mimi said. "But I also want to explore and learn and make friends. Maybe I will find a nice place to live and a nice song to sing."

Mimi kissed her mother and crawled out of the hole. She looked around and saw many things. She saw grass and flowers and bugs and birds. She saw a pond and a bridge and a boat. She saw a house and a fence and a dog. She was curious and excited, but also a little scared.

She decided to follow a path that led to a hill. She thought maybe she could find a cozy cave or a hollow log to live in. As she crawled, she heard a strange sound. It was a deep and low sound, like a big drum. It made her ears hurt and her heart beat fast. She wondered what it was and where it came from.

She crawled faster and faster, hoping to get away from the sound. But the sound got louder and louder, until she reached the top of the hill. There she saw a huge and scary thing. It was a car, and it was coming right at her. It had four round wheels and a shiny metal body and a loud horn. It looked like a monster, and it was making the deep sound.

Mimi was so afraid that she froze. She could not move or scream or run. She thought she was going to die. But then she heard another sound. It was a high and sweet sound, like a little bell. It made her ears happy and her heart calm. She wondered what it was and where it came from.

She looked up and saw a small and friendly thing. It was a bird, and it was flying above her. It had two soft wings and a colorful feather and a cute beak. It looked like a friend, and it was making the sweet sound.

"Hello, little mouse," the bird said. "You are in danger. The car is coming. You have to move. Come with me. I will help you."

Mimi was so grateful that she nodded. She trusted the bird and followed its voice. She crawled as fast as she could, away from the car and toward the bird. The bird flew ahead and guided her to a safe place. It was a bush, and it had many leaves and berries and nests. It looked like a home, and it had many songs.

"Here you are, little mouse," the bird said. "You are safe now. This is my home, and you are welcome. You can stay here as long as you like. You can eat and rest and play. You can listen and learn and sing. You have found a nice place to live and a nice song to sing."

Mimi was so happy that she smiled. She thanked the bird and hugged its wing. She made a new friend and found a new home. She ate and rested and played. She listened and learned and sang. She had a wonderful day and a wonderful life. She was glad she had left her hole and followed her dream.

Once there was a thin girl named Claire. Claire always wanted to feel relaxed, but couldn't find a way. She was too weighed down by her worries. She wanted to feel as light as a feather, so she could float away. 

One day she decided to go find a way to relax. She ran and ran until she stumbled upon a beautiful pond. It sparkled in the sun, like a thousand diamonds. She stepped in and felt the cool water wrap around her feet.

Slowly, she relaxed. She walked deeper into the middle of the pond, feeling the weight from her worries slowly wash away. Claire let out a deep breath and smiled as she felt the water kiss her skin.

The gentle sway of the water seemed to help her mind feel better as she floated on top. Her worries seemed weightless, and she felt free and happy for the first time in a long time. 

Claire stayed there for a while and enjoyed the peace, until she was ready to go home. She emerged from the pond feeling thin and relaxed. She could never forget the magic of the pond, and still visits it whenever she needs to feel the weightless freedom it brings.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, her little brother came and broke her favorite toy. Lily was very angry and sad. She wanted to hit her brother, but her mom told her that hitting is not a good thing to do. 

Instead, her mom told her to replace her broken toy with a new one. Lily went to the toy store and found a new toy that she liked even more than her old one. She felt happy and peaceful again. 

From that day on, Lily learned that when something bad happens, it's better to find a harmless solution instead of getting angry or violent. She also learned that sometimes, replacing something old with something new can bring even more joy.

Once there was a little boy. His name was Joe. Joe was very adventurous, so one day he decided to explore the woods near his house. He trusted his feet and started walking. 

After a while, Joe found a cave. He was curious and wanted to go inside, but he was a bit scared. Then he heard someone singing. It was a beautiful voice! Joe was now brave and went deeper into the cave. 

When he got inside, Joe saw a very messy little house. He looked around, but nobody was there. He noticed something small in the corner - it was a tiny hand. It was holding something bright and shiny. Joe picked up the hand and it felt warm. 

He laughed when he realized it was a toy. Joe placed the hand on the table and started playing with the toy. He soon trusted the cave and stayed a little longer. 

Joe was happy and excited. He thanked the mysterious cave for the wonderful adventures. A few days later, Joe left the cave with lots of special memories.

Once upon a time there was a very angry lizard. He was so mad that he started to stomp and yell. All of the other animals were scared of him. Then a small rabbit spoke up, "Lizard, why are you so angry?"

The lizard yelled back, "I am angry because my home is no longer here. Something bad happened and now it is gone."

The rabbit thought for a moment and then said, "I know what you can do! Follow me and I will take you to a new home. I know the perfect place!'

The angry lizard followed the rabbit and they both came across a beautiful lake. The lizard was so happy with his new home that he stopped being angry. From then on, the lizard and the rabbit had fun playing at the lake. They became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy who loved his mum very much. His mum would always spoil him with the best treats. One day, the town was surprised by a flood. The flood was harmless, but it made a lot of trouble. The boy's mum quickly grabbed him and ran away. She knew it was dangerous and wanted to make sure he was safe.

The mum was very brave. She ran very fast, jumping over puddles and screaming away from the floods. The boy was scared, but as they kept running he felt more relaxed. Eventually they reached safety, and the water stopped following them.

The boy hugged his mum tight and thanked her for protecting him from the flood. She smiled and then spoiled him with his favorite treat. He was overjoyed and felt so special that his mum had saved him from the flood. From then on, the boy would always remember how his mum had spoiled and protected him.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the zoo with her mom and dad. She liked to see all the different animals, but her favorite was the tiger. She wanted to get closer to the big cat, but her mom said no.

"Too dangerous, Mia. The tiger might hurt you. Stay with us, please."

But Mia was curious and brave. She saw a small hole in the fence and crawled through it. She ran towards the tiger's cage, hoping to see its stripes and whiskers. She did not see the sign that said "Do not feed the animals".

The tiger saw Mia and growled. He was hungry and angry. He did not like people coming into his space. He jumped at the cage, trying to reach Mia. Mia was scared and screamed. She dropped her bag of popcorn on the ground.

The tiger smelled the popcorn and stopped growling. He liked popcorn. He licked his lips and pawed at the cage, wanting to get some. Mia saw that the tiger was not mean, just hungry. She felt sorry for him. She picked up some popcorn and threw it to the tiger. The tiger ate it and purred. He looked at Mia with his big yellow eyes and smiled.

"Thank you, little girl. You are compassionate. You share your food with me. You are my friend."

Mia smiled back. She was happy that the tiger was happy. She wanted to play with him, but she heard her mom and dad calling her name. They were worried and angry. They had seen her go through the hole and run to the tiger. They came to get her and take her back to safety.

"Mia, what were you thinking? You could have been hurt by the tiger. He is a wild animal, not a pet. You were very naughty. We are going home now."

Mia was sad. She did not want to leave the tiger. She waved goodbye to him and said sorry.

"Bye, tiger. I'm sorry I made you mad. You are my friend. I hope you get more popcorn."

The tiger waved back and said thank you.

"Bye, little girl. I'm sorry I scared you. You are my friend. I hope you come back soon."

Anna was a wealthy child. She had many toys and dresses and books. She lived in a big house with her parents and her nanny. But Anna was not happy. She wanted to have friends and play with other children.

One day, Anna saw some children dancing in the park. They had music and balloons and smiles. They looked so happy and free. Anna wanted to join them, but she was afraid. She did not know how to dance or how to talk to them. She thought they would not like her because she was different.

But then, one of the children saw Anna and waved at her. He was a boy with curly hair and brown eyes. He ran to Anna and said, "Hi, I'm Ben. Do you want to dance with us?" Anna was surprised and shy. She nodded and followed Ben to the park.

Ben introduced Anna to the other children. They were kind and friendly. They taught Anna how to dance and how to play games. They shared their balloons and snacks with her. Anna felt happy and warm. She forgot about her toys and dresses and books. She only cared about her new friends.

Anna danced with the children until the sun set. She laughed and sang and had fun. She thanked Ben and the others for inviting her. They hugged her and said, "You're welcome, Anna. You're our friend. Come back tomorrow and dance with us again." Anna smiled and nodded. She ran to her nanny and said, "I had the best day ever. I made friends and I learned how to dance. Can we come back tomorrow?" The nanny smiled and said, "Of course, Anna. I'm glad you're happy." Anna hugged the nanny and said, "I'm happy, too."

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy aeroplane. Every day, it would chug and zoom around in the sky.

One day, it was going to celebrate its birthday.

But then a troublesome bird flew into its path and pecked its wing! The aeroplane was so clumsy it couldn't get away.

"Let me go!" the aeroplane cried. But the bird just kept pecking.

Suddenly, the friendly wind blew by.

"I know!" shouted the wind. "Let's celebrate your birthday and have a dance!"

The aeroplane and bird both starting dancing together in the sky. They were so happy they forgot all about the pecking.

They went on and celebrated the aeroplane's birthday. Together they roared in the sky until the sun set.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to find treasure. He asked his mom and she said, "Yes, but it won't be easy. It might be difficult."

So, the little boy set off on his adventure. He looked everywhere, in the mountains, in the river, even in the fields, but he couldn't find any treasure.

He was beginning to get very frustrated, so he went even farther
until he stumbled across a cave. He went inside and saw a sparkle deep inside. He went closer and he saw it was treasure!

But as he grabbed it, he heard a loud noise. He panicked and he ran away as fast as he could. He was so happy and excited that he'd found the treasure!

Davey saw something interesting on the street. It was a bright red license! He stopped and started to stare. He saw the license was made of a very shiny and smooth plastic. Davey thought it was so cool he had to take a closer look. He crouched down to get a better view. From up close he could see the license had many tiny numbers, little pictures and lots of fun colors. Davey just kept staring. He thought the license was amazing. Suddenly, he heard his mom calling his name. Davey looked up and it was time to go. He waved goodbye to the interesting license and ran off.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mae. Mae had lots of friends. One day, Mae and her friends wanted to pick some squash from the garden. As they were picking, Mae saw something purple in the garden. 

"What is that?" asked Mae.

"It looks like a purple squash!" said her friends as they walked closer to it.

They all admired the bright purple squash. They were so excited!

But then they saw something in the garden that made everyone feel a bit sad. A mean wolf had come along and snatched the purple squash!

Mae and her friends were so mad! They ran right up to the wolf and shouted. 

"Hey! Give us back our squash! It belongs to us!" shouted Mae and her friends.

The wolf was so scared that he dropped the purple squash and ran away as fast as he could.

Mae and her friends cheered. They thanked each other for being brave and scaring away the wolf. They all ran back home with the purple squash and enjoyed it together. 

Mae was so happy and thankful for her friends. No one had been hurt and they all got the squash back. It was a happy ending for Mae and her friends!

Max was in his room, playing with his toy cars. His mom stood in the doorway, with a nosy look on her face.

"Max, are you ready to take a swim?" asked his mom.

Max was excited! He loved swimming in the big pool. He gathered up his swim gear and followed his mom outside.

The big pool was so big and shiny. Max jumped in with a huge splash. His mom laughed and smiled. Max was so happy he forgot all about his toy cars.

Max had been swimming for what felt like forever, when he heard something strange. It was the sound of a big crowd of people!

Max and his mom were about to find out what all the excitement was about. As they got closer, he saw a huge parade coming down the street. He wondered why everyone was so nosy and what they were doing.

Suddenly, his mom stopped and smiled. Max looked ahead and saw a big float with all of his toy cars on it. Everyone was cheering and celebrating Max and his toy cars. 

Max couldn't believe it! His mom had planned a surprise parade for him! He was so excited and hugged his mom tight. Today might have started with a swim, but it turned into a day he'd never forget.

Once, there was a little girl who was very tired. She was holding a blue jug. She went outside and saw a car that was going backward. It was reversing! She smiled and said, "Reverse!"

The car kept reversing until it stopped and the driver got out. He saw the little girl with the jug. He smiled and said, "Are you going to fill the jug with water?"

The little girl nodded and they both walked to the riverbank. The driver filled the jug with fresh water and the little girl was so happy. She thanked the driver and went home.

The little girl was no longer tired. She drank the water from the jug and felt much better. She was so glad the driver stopped to help her!

Once upon a time, there was a clown named Joe. Joe was bossy and he liked to make people laugh. Joe had a bucket and every day he would pour the bucket full of water and make bubbles.

One day Joe decided to go around to all the houses in the town. He knocked on the door and asked to pour some bubbles. Everyone thought this was a great idea and opened their doors to Joe.

Joe went to every house and made lots of bubbles. He was having lots of fun. Then, he went to the last house. The family shook their heads and said no to Joe. Joe was very bossy and he got angry.

He poured the bucket full of bubbles on all the people in the family. Everyone started screaming and running around. Joe was so embarrassed. He put the bucket down, ran away and never came back.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in their big house. They had many toys and clothes and books, but their favorite thing was their comb. The comb was very special, because it could glow in the dark. When they combed their hair with it, their hair would shine like stars.

One night, they decided to sneak out of their room and explore the house with their comb. They turned off the lights and held the comb in front of them. They saw many things that looked different in the dark. They saw the big sofa, the shiny vase, the soft rug, and the tall clock. They giggled and whispered as they walked around.

"Look, Anna, there is a door we never opened!" Ben said, pointing to a small door under the stairs. "Let's see what's inside!"

"OK, Ben, but be careful!" Anna said, following him. They opened the door and saw a dark and dusty room. There were boxes and bags and old things piled up. They used their comb to see better.

"Wow, look at all this stuff!" Ben said, picking up a hat and a coat. "Maybe this was our grandpa's room. He was very rich and traveled a lot."

"Maybe, Ben, but we should not touch his things. They are very old and fragile." Anna said, looking at a picture of a smiling man. "He looks nice. I wish we met him."

"Me too, Anna. He must have had many stories to tell." Ben said, putting the hat and coat back. "Hey, what's that?" He saw something shiny under a box. He moved the box and found a necklace with a big jewel. The jewel was red and sparkled in the dark.

"Wow, Ben, that's beautiful!" Anna said, admiring the necklace. "It glows like our comb!"

"Maybe it's magic, Anna. Maybe it can grant wishes." Ben said, holding the necklace. "What would you wish for?"

"I don't know, Ben. We already have everything we need. We have a big house, many toys, and each other." Anna said, smiling. "What would you wish for?"

"I would wish for the same, Anna. And maybe for some cookies." Ben said, laughing. "Come on, let's go back to our room. It's late and we don't want to get in trouble."

"OK, Ben, let's go. But let's leave the necklace here. It belongs to grandpa. Maybe he will come back for it someday." Anna said, putting the necklace back under the box. "Maybe he will be happy to see that we found his comb."

They closed the door and ran back to their room. They combed their hair with their comb and tucked themselves in bed. They dreamed of grandpa and his adventures. They were happy and rich.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go sailing with his dad. They would go out on their boat and feel the wind in their hair. One day, they went out to sea and Timmy saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. He knew it meant a storm was coming. 

Timmy's dad told him to mark the spot where they were so they could come back to it later. Timmy took a crayon and drew a big X on the map. They sailed away, but the storm got worse and worse. The wind was blowing so hard that the sail ripped! 

Timmy's dad was sorry that they couldn't sail anymore, but he was glad they marked the spot on the map. They were able to find their way back home safely. Timmy learned that it's important to be prepared and to mark important things so you can find them later.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to create things. He was always making something new and interesting. One day, the boy wanted to make something extra special. So, he asked his mom for some silver. She gave him some silver and the boy went to work. He worked and worked until he created a beautiful silver crown. He was so proud of his creation, he wanted to show it off. 

The next day, the boy and his mom went to a party. Everyone was so impressed when they saw the boy's crown. They asked where he got it and the boy said he'd created it himself. Everyone was amazed and asked if he could create something for all of them. 

The boy said, "Yes! I can create something for all of you." He showed them all that he was an amazing creator with an interesting knack for silver. Everyone was so proud of him and the boy was very happy with all of the praise.

The sun was glowing up in the sky and it was a beautiful day. A little girl named Lucy walked down the street. She saw a black bird on the sidewalk. Lucy was sorry because she thought she had scared the bird away. 

Suddenly, the bird began to glow! It glowed so brightly that Lucy had to put her hands up over her eyes. She was so amazed. The bird flew up in the sky and lit up the whole sky with its glowing feathers. Lucy felt so happy looking up and seeing a glowing bird. 

Then, the little bird landed back on the sidewalk by Lucy. She excitedly petted its head and asked it to never leave. The glowing bird moved closer to her as if it agreed, and Lucy smiled with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved eating celery because it was crunchy and good for her. One day, her mom bought a thick celery that was hard to chew. 

Lily tried to eat it, but it was too hard. She said, "Mommy, this celery is too thick. Can you help me?" 

Her mom replied, "Sure, let me cut it for you." 

As her mom was cutting the celery, Lily accidentally slapped her hand. She quickly said, "I'm sorry, Mommy!" 

"It's okay, Lily. Just be careful next time," her mom said with a smile. 

From then on, Lily knew to be careful when her mom was cutting thick celery.

Ben and Mia are playing with their toy cars in the living room. They like to imagine that they are the owners of a modern car shop. They pretend to fix, wash and sell the cars to their customers.

"Hello, welcome to Ben and Mia's car shop!" Ben says to a teddy bear. "What can we do for you today?"

"I want a new car," the teddy bear says. "A fast and shiny one."

"OK, we have many cars to choose from," Mia says. "Look at this red one. It has four doors, a big trunk and a horn that goes beep beep!"

"I like it, I like it!" the teddy bear says. "How much is it?"

"It is ten cookies," Ben says. "But we can give you a discount if you trade in your old car."

"Deal!" the teddy bear says. He gives Ben his old car and ten cookies. He takes the red car and drives away happily.

"Wow, we are good at selling cars!" Mia says.

"Yes, we are!" Ben says. "We have the best car shop in the world!"

They high-five each other and continue to play with their toy cars. They imagine that they are the owners of a modern car shop. They have a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. She was 3 years old and she was very brave.

One day, Lucy heard that the church was in danger. She knew she had to act quickly to save it.

She asked her Mum, â€œMum, can I go? Please? I have to save the church!â€

Mum replied, â€œYes Lucy, you can go but be careful!â€

Lucy was really brave and ran to the church as fast as she could. When she got there, she saw that a giant bushfire was burning close by and it was getting bigger and bigger. Lucy knew she had to be fast, so she started to cry and shout for help.

Suddenly, someone came running from the other side of the church. It was Lucyâ€™s big brother! He had brought lots of buckets of water with him. Together, they filled the buckets with water and quickly ran around the church to put out the fire.

By the time the fire was extinguished, Lucy and her brother were both exhausted and very bitter. But despite their tiredness, they were happy that they had saved the church.

Grandma loves her grandbaby very much. She always finds new ways to show her love. One day, Grandma decided to write a beautiful poem for grandbaby. She wrote about how grandbaby is always smiling, and how much Grandma loves to spend time with her. Grandma showed her grandbaby the poem, and grandbaby was so excited. She loved it! Every time Grandma came over, the grandbaby would ask to hear the poem again. Grandma was so happy that grandbaby loved the poem so much. It made Grandma loving her grandbaby even more. Grandma always told her grandbaby that she was the most beautiful person in the world. Grandma's love was so special and it made grandbaby feel so special too.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. They needed to buy a mixer for their kitchen. Tim was very excited to help his mom choose the mixer.

In the store, Tim saw many mixers. He looked at all of them and said, "Mom, I like this one!" His mom looked at the mixer he chose and said, "Good job, Tim! This mixer is perfect for us." They put the mixer in their cart and went to pay.

As they walked to the cashier, Tim felt embarrassed because he tripped and fell. His mom helped him up and said, "It's okay, Tim. Everyone falls sometimes. Let's go home and use our new mixer to make a yummy cake!" Tim smiled and they went home to enjoy their new mixer.

Once there was a little girl who was very hungry. She was looking for something to eat, so she decided to make a sandwich. She grabbed two slices of bread and put some meat and cheese in between.

The little girl felt very happy with her sandwich, but then she saw something very ugly. It was a big, slimy insect that was touching the sandwich. She screamed and jumped away!

The insect didn't mean any harm and just wanted to eat the sandwich. So, the little girl helped the bug safely away from the sandwich. 

But she still didn't want to touch the sandwich, so she made another one without any touch from the bug. It tasted even better than the first one!

Once upon a time, there was a little pupil named Tim. Tim was a very helpful boy. He liked to help his friends and family. One day, Tim saw a small, helpless bird on the ground. The bird could not fly and looked very sad.

Tim wanted to help the bird, so he gently touched it. The bird looked at Tim with big, thankful eyes. Tim thought of a plan to help the bird fly again. He asked his friends to help him find a safe place for the bird to rest.

Together, Tim and his friends found a soft nest for the bird. They put the bird in the nest and watched it get better. Soon, the bird could fly again. It was so happy and flew high in the sky. Tim and his friends felt very proud and happy that they could help the helpless bird.

One day, a mouse saw a big piece of cheese on a table. He was very hungry and wanted to eat it. But he was not stupid. He knew that cheese was a trap. He looked around and saw a wire and a spring. If he touched the cheese, the wire would pull the spring and a cage would fall on him.

He thought of a way to get the cheese without getting caught. He found a stick and a stone. He set the stick on the wire and the stone on the stick. Then he pushed the stone with his nose. The stick moved and the wire pulled the spring. The cage fell on the table, but the mouse was not under it. He was safe.

He ran to the cheese and took a big bite. He was very happy and proud. He had outsmarted the trap. He did not know that a cat was watching him from behind a curtain. The cat was very hungry and wanted to eat him. But he was not stupid. He waited for the mouse to finish the cheese and run away. Then he followed him quietly.

The mouse did not see the cat. He was too busy looking for more cheese. He ran into a hole in the wall. The cat ran after him. But he was too big to fit in the hole. He scratched and clawed at the wall, but he could not reach the mouse. He was angry and frustrated.

The mouse heard the cat and laughed. He had outsmarted the cat. He was safe in his hole. He had cheese in his belly. He was very happy and proud. He did not know that a snake was living in the hole. The snake was very hungry and wanted to eat him. But he was not stupid. He waited for the mouse to come closer. Then he struck.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to make something interesting. He looked around his garden and saw a worm. He thought it looked interesting, so he picked it up.

The boy wanted to make something special for the worm, so he asked his mom for help. She helped him find some dirt and grass for the worm to eat. She also found some sticks for the worm to make a cozy home.

The boy and his mom worked together to build a nice new home for the worm. The worm loved its new home! It was cozy and it had everything the worm needed.

The boy was so proud that he made something so interesting for the worm. He couldn't have done it without help from his mom!

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her son. The little boy was only three years old but he already loved helping his mom.

One day, his mom was making a delicious dessert. She was mixing the batter in a bowl when she realized she had left her apron in the other room. She asked her son, "Will you please return the apron to me?" His face lit up and he said yes.

The little boy ran to the other room and found the apron. He returned it to his his mom and she thanked him with a big smile. She said, "You're a big help! Let's put the apron on you." 

The boy was embarrassed, but he wanted to help his mom. So he put the apron on and helped stir the batter for the dessert. 

When the cake was finished, his mom proudly said, "Thanks for the help! You made this cake so perfect!" The little boy was so happy. He knew he had been helpful. â€‹

Once upon a time, in a friendly town, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily liked to play outside with her friends. They would run, jump, and laugh all day long.

One day, Lily found a small box with a lock on it. She did not know what was inside. Lily showed the box to her friends. They all wanted to open the lock and see what was inside.

Lily and her friends tried to open the lock. They pulled, they pushed, and they turned it. Finally, the lock opened! Inside the box, they found pretty, shiny stones. Lily and her friends shared the stones and played with them. They were so happy to find the pretty stones in their friendly town.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, while playing, Lily saw a big dragon flying in the sky. She was scared and ran to her mom.

"Mommy, mommy, there is a dragon in the sky!" she said.

"Don't worry, Lily. Dragons are not real. It's just a bird," her mom said, trying to calm her down.

Suddenly, a charming prince appeared and offered to help Lily. "Don't be afraid, little one. I will protect you from the dragon," he said.

Lily was so happy that the prince was there to help her. She thanked him and they all played together in the park. From that day on, Lily knew that if she ever saw a dragon again, she could count on her charming prince to protect her.

There were two twins, Mary and Max. Mary was very curious, while Max was very ignorant. They went out for a walk and came across a pond, where Max wanted to rest. Mary thought it was such a beautiful day that she kept walking.

Max got angry and yelled at Mary for ignoring him. Mary saw that Max was sad, so she ran back to him, agreed to rest and hugged Max. They sat near the pond and watched the birds fly in the sky. Mary and Max shared a happy moment.

After resting for a while, Mary saw a frog and said,"Look, Max! I found a frog!" Max laughed, and they both ran after the frog and tried to catch it.

They were so happy to be together, so they decided to rest at the pond for the rest of the day and gaze up at the blue sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine, but sometimes it rained. One day, Lily woke up with an itch on her arm. It was a mild itch, but it bothered her all day.

As the day went on, the sky started to get dark and cloudy. Lily's mom said, "I think it might rain today." Lily looked out the window and saw the dark clouds. She remembered the itch on her arm and said, "I hope it doesn't rain, my arm itches."

Later that afternoon, Lily and her mom went to the park to play. They had a lot of fun swinging and sliding, but then they heard a sound. It was the sound of raindrops falling on the ground. Lily's mom said, "Quick, let's go home before we get too wet!" As they ran home, Lily felt the raindrops on her arm and realized that the rain had washed away her itch. She was happy that the rain had come.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Jane. Jane was three years old and very silly. She would often do foolish things without thinking first.

One day, Jane's pet cat knocked over the milk. Jane took a whip and tried to fix it. But of course, the milk stayed on the floor. 

Her mum came in and saw the mess. She told Jane that whips would not help fix the milk! She took a cloth and cleaned up the milk.

Jane learned a valuable lesson that day - never be a foolish girl and try to fix things with silly tools.

Jack and his mom were in the park. While they were sitting under a tree, Jack saw a box. He got up and went to touch the box.

Mom: "What are you doing Jack?"

Jack: "I saw a box. I'm going to touch it." 

Mom: "Remember to be serious. You can touch it, but be careful."

So Jack reached out and touched the box with his little finger. It was cold and hard. He looked up to see his mom watching him. He smiled and looked back at the box.

Jack touched the box all around. As he touched it, he noticed there was a crack on one side. With his little hands, Jack opened the box. Inside, he found a tiny robot! 

Jack was so excited, he forgot to be serious. His mom laughed and hugged him. 

It was a very special moment for Jack and his mom. They both knew that this tiny robot was a special gift, just for them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride the bus with her mom to go to the park. One day, they got on the bus and sat down next to an old lady who was deaf. Lily tried to talk to her, but the old lady couldn't hear her.

When they got off the bus, Lily's mom asked her if she wanted to go to the ice cream shop. But Lily refused because she wanted to go back on the bus and talk to the old lady. Her mom didn't understand why, but Lily just wanted to make sure the old lady was okay.

So they got back on the bus and Lily sat next to the old lady again. She waved her hands and smiled at her, and the old lady smiled back. Even though the old lady couldn't hear her, Lily knew she was happy. From that day on, Lily always looked for the old lady on the bus and they became good friends.

Once upon a time, a little ant named Andy wanted to find some food. He crawled and crawled until he found a big piece of candy. It looked amazing! But when he tried to take it back to his home, a big, mean bird swooped down and took it away. Andy was sad and hungry.

He decided to ask his ant friends if they had any food to share. But they didn't have any, and they were all worried about something else. They had heard that a thief had stolen all the money from their ant hill! They needed the money to buy food and build a new home.

Andy had an idea. He remembered seeing a shiny coin on the ground earlier. He crawled back to where he saw it and found it again. He brought it back to his friends and they were amazed. It wasn't enough to buy everything they needed, but it was a start. They thanked Andy for his help and together they worked to build a new home and find more food.

One day, a boy wanted to go on an adventure. He asked his mom if he could travel. His mom told him yes, but only if he brought his hat and sunscreen.

The boy was very excited. He took off and began his journey. Everywhere he went, he looked for a large prize. However, he couldn't find anything.

He kept searching and searching until one day he saw a large treasure box. He had finally found his prize! He opened the box and saw it was filled with colourful stones. 

The boy was so delighted by his discovery. He had found the perfect prize to bring home from his travel! He put the stones in his pocket and ran home to tell his mom all about his adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play at the beach with his family. They would build sandcastles and collect seashells. One day, Timmy saw a boat in the distant water. He asked his dad if they could race the boat. 

Dad said, "Sure, let's race to the shore!" Timmy was so excited. He ran as fast as he could, feeling the sand between his toes. He looked back and saw his dad was right behind him. They both reached the shore at the same time. 

Timmy was so happy that he won the race. He looked out to the distant water and saw the boat was gone. He asked his dad where it went. Dad said, "Maybe it went to another shore." Timmy smiled and went back to building sandcastles with his family.

Once upon a time there was a car. One day the car needed to park and the driver found a nice tidy spot.

The car parked carefully and then the driver went to do some errands. When the driver came back, the car was a wreck! It was all banged up and there was no sign of the driver.

The driver looked around and found out that the car had been crashed into by another driver. Everyone was really sad about the wrecked car.

But then someone had an idea. A group of people came together to help tidy up the car. They fixed all the dents and washed the car so it looked like new.

When they were done the driver returned and the car looked as good as new. Everyone was happy that the car was tidied up and safe again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. Molly had a great big, hairy dog. They were very happy together.

One day, Molly and her dog were out walking in the park when they heard a noise. Molly was scared and she hugged her dog tight. Then something strange happened. A ghost appeared beneath a tree. It was a very strange sight. 

Molly's dog growled at the ghost. The ghost ran away and Molly felt brave. 

"What was that, Molly?" asked her dog. 

"I don't know," replied Molly. 

As they continued their walk, Molly noticed something strange. Whenever Molly said the word "yield", ghosts appeared from the trees! She had the magic power to make ghosts yield.

Molly was excited and scared at the same time. She decided to keep this magic to herself. Molly went home and hugged her hairy dog. She knew she was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's mom took him to a store to buy a new toy car. Timmy was so excited to see all the different cars on the shelves.

He found a red car that he really liked, but it was in a frame. Timmy asked his mom, "Can we take it out of the frame?" His mom said, "No, that's an original car and it needs to stay in the frame."

Suddenly, another little boy came up and tried to pinch Timmy's new car. Timmy said, "Hey, that's not nice! That's my car!" The other little boy said sorry and walked away. Timmy was happy to have his new car and he put it on his shelf at home, still in its original frame.

Once upon a time there was a smart bear named Chris. He loved exploring the forest and looking for new things.

One day, as he was walking through the forest, he observed some nice fruit on a tree. He wanted to try it, so he climbed onto the tree and picked the fruit with his paws. 

When he tasted the fruit, it was sweeter than anything he had ever tasted before! He was so happy that he started to jump up and down in joy.

While he enjoyed the fruit, a rabbit came hopping by. The rabbit saw the bear and asked him, "What are you doing?"
Chris smiled and said, "I'm eating the yummy fruit I found on this tree and it's so delicious!"
The rabbit's eyes widened and he said, "Wow, I want some too!"
Chris laughed and said, "Come on up! I'll share it with you."

So the bear and the rabbit enjoyed the tasty fruit together, and they became the best of friends. From then on the two of them were always seen exploring the forest and discovering new things.

One day, Mama wanted a new TV. She wanted a TV that was thin and would fit in the wall. So, Mama went to the store and bought a thin TV.

When Mama got home, she called Papa to help her replace the old TV with the thin one. Papa opened up the wall and took out the old TV. Then, he put the thin TV in the wall and hooked it up.

Mama was very excited to see the new TV in the wall! The TV was so thin and it looked perfect! Mama and Papa watched TV together and had a great time. 

From then on, the thin TV was a part of the family and everyone loved it!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy's big brother came into his room and asked to play with him. Timmy was happy to share his toys.

They played together for a while, but then Timmy's big brother got mad and started to destroy Timmy's toy gear. Timmy was worried and didn't know what to do. He asked his big brother, "Why did you break my toys?"

His big brother said, "I'm sorry, I was just angry. I'll buy you new toys." Timmy forgave his big brother and they hugged. From then on, they played together nicely and never destroyed anything again. The end.

Once there was a girl who was very tall. She was three years old and her name was Sarah. Every day she liked to play in the garden with her friends. One day she was playing tag and wanted to have extra fun. So Sarah decided to try to zip around the garden. 

Sarah tried to zip but it was too hard. She kept falling over. Sarah felt a bit sad. Then her friend Lucy came over. Lucy said that she could help Sarah learn how to zip. 

Lucy showed Sarah how to zip back and forth. Soon Sarah was zipping like a professional! She was so happy. All of Sarah's friends cheered for her. Sarah felt like the best three year old in the world!

Once there was a lake. And in the lake there was a little dove. Every day the dove would come down and have a swim in the lake. 

One day the dove was being very lively in the lake, splishing and splashing around. Then, all of a sudden, it started raining. The dove just kept on playing, not realizing that the rain was so heavy. 

The dove was getting very soaked! Pretty soon the lake was full of water and the dove was dripping wet. 

An old lady saw what was happening and shouted to the dove, "Little dove, come here!"

The dove heard the old lady and quickly flew away from the lake. The old lady opened her front door and said, "Come on in here and I'll give you something to help you get dry." 

So the dove went in and the old lady wrapped it in a warm towel. After a few minutes, the dove was nice and dry. 

The old lady said, "There, that wasn't so bad, was it? Now, don't forget to be careful next time around!" 

The dove nodded its little head and thanked the old lady before it flew back to the lake. 

From then on the dove was extra careful when it went swimming in the lake. Even though it still splished and splashed around, it made sure not to get soaking wet again!

One day, a girl named Sue had a basket. Sue loved her basket because it was very good at holding things. She could put her toys, food, and other stuff in it. Sue thought her basket was reliable.

Sue wanted to show her friend, Tom, her basket. She went outside and saw Tom. "Look at my basket!" Sue said to Tom. Tom looked at the basket and thought it was nice. But Tom wanted to see if it was strong. He took the basket and started to run with it.

Sue did not want Tom to run with her basket. She was scared that he would break it. Sue ran after Tom and said, "Stop! Please give me my basket back!" Tom stopped running and looked at Sue. He saw that she was upset.

Tom said sorry to Sue and gave her back the basket. Sue was happy to have her basket back. They both learned that it is important to be careful with other people's things. And Sue learned that her basket was strong and reliable, even when Tom ran with it.

Once upon a time there was a dog named Spot. He was a very happy pup and loved to play with his friends. One day Spot and his friends went for a walk in the park. They had lots of fun running around and playing games. 

Spot's friend Lola said, "Let's go for a walk and explore!" 

Spot took off running and Lola followed. They went all around the park and before they knew it, it was getting dark. 

Lola said, "Let's go home now, Spot." 

Spot didn't want to go home, so he took off running again. Lola shouted, "Spot, come back, heel!" 

Spot slowed down and remembered that he had to listen when someone said "heel" so he slowly made his way back to Lola. He walked next to her with a long leash and stayed close. 

When they got home, Spot was so proud that he had listened to Lola and stayed close. From then on he remembered to take "heel" very seriously!

Sara and Ben like to play outside. But today, the sky is gray and the rain is falling. Sara and Ben are sad. They want to have fun.

They look for a place to play. They see a big tree. The tree has many leaves. The leaves keep the rain away. Sara and Ben run to the tree. They find a hole under the tree. The hole is hidden by the roots. Sara and Ben crawl into the hole.

Inside the hole, Sara and Ben are happy. They have a secret place. They can play and talk and laugh. They do not care about the rain. They keep each other warm and cozy. They pretend they are animals or pirates or fairies. They have many stories to tell.

She asked him if he wanted to play with her kite. He said yes. He thanked her. He ran with her. They played with the kite. They shared the kite. They saw the rainbow. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Bob. Bob liked to bounce around and have lots of fun. One day he was feeling particularly bouncy, so he decided to go and explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a sister named Rose who loved to play with her. One day, Lily and Rose went to the park to play. They played on the swings and slides, but then Lily saw a pretty necklace in the grass.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy. She had big eyes and a big heart. She loved to play and explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a big box of socks. She loved her socks very much. Every day, Sue would put on a new pair of socks. She liked to wear socks that were bright and fun.

One day, Sue could not find her favorite socks. She looked all around her room. "Oh no," she said, "I need to find my socks!" Sue's mom heard her and came to help. "Sue, you must be alert and look carefully," her mom said. Sue nodded and started to search again.

Once upon a time there was a little turtle called Tim. Tim liked to swim in the big ocean and chase tiny fishies. But one day, Tim began to worry. He heard about a big and enormous whale who scared all the fish in the sea. Tim was so worried â€“ what if this whale took all the fish away?

There were two friends, Rory and Jack. Rory had a strong brush. Jack asked Rory why he had the brush. Rory said, "I need it to learn how to brush my hair." Jack said," That's smart! Can I learn too?" Rory said, "Sure! Just watch me."

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big cave. They want to go inside and see what is there.

But Tom and Sue have a quarrel. Tom says he should go first, because he is bigger and stronger. Sue says she should go first, because she is smarter and faster. They yell and push each other. They are not nice.

Once there was a furry creature. It lived deep in the forest. It had two big eyes, two small ears and two soft paws. Its name was Fuzzy.

One day, Fuzzy found a crystal in the forest. It was sparkly and shiny. The crystal glittered in the sun and Fuzzy wanted to keep it.

Fuzzy asked the crystal, "Can I pick you up?"

The crystal didn't answer.

Then Fuzzy said, "I'll weigh you. If you're light enough I'll take you with me."

So Fuzzy weighed the crystal, and it was light enough. Fuzzy put it in his pocket and took it with him.

Fuzzy was so happy, he jumped into the air and started to cry. His crystal had made him so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to clean up her toys. Lily didn't want to clean up, so she ignored her mommy and kept playing. 

Later that day, Lily spilled her juice all over the floor. Her mommy asked her to grab the mop and clean it up. Lily didn't want to do it, but she remembered how she ignored her mommy earlier. So, she grabbed the mop and cleaned up the juice. 

After she finished, Lily felt proud of herself for being a good listener. Her mommy hugged her and said, "You did a great job, Lily. It's important to listen and help out when you can." From that day on, Lily always listened to her mommy and helped clean up.

John loved exploring the world. Every day, he took his bike and went for a ride around the neighbourhood. One day, he was riding his bike when it got dark. He got scared and wanted to go home. But his parents encouraged him to keep going. 

John told them, â€œBut it's dark outside.â€
