John was a little boy. He lived in a small house. One day, it got very cold outside. So cold, that John started to feel frightened. He wanted to find a way to keep warm. He looked around the house but he couldn't find anything.

Suddenly, John saw a big sack. He knew that the sack would be warm. He jumped and grabbed it. The sack was so warm, it felt like a hug! He wrapped the sack around himself and it was so cozy and warm.

John felt safe and happy. He ran around the house, having fun. Even though it was cold outside, John was warm and happy inside the sack.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved lollipops and always asked his mom for one when they went to the store. One day, Timmy saw a lollipop in the store and he was eager to have it. He asked his mom if he could have it, but she said no because they didn't have enough money.

Timmy was sad and started to cry. A man overheard Timmy crying and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told the man about the lollipop and how he wanted it so badly. The man said he would buy it for Timmy and gave him the lollipop.

But when Timmy got home, he accidentally dropped the lollipop and it broke. He was so upset and cried even harder. His mom tried to comfort him, but he was too sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a duck who lived by a big river. The duck loved to swim in the river and catch fish for dinner. One day, the duck saw a big fish swimming in the river. The duck wanted to catch the fish, but it was too fast.

The duck went to a store to buy a fishing net. The store had many nets, but they were all too expensive. The duck demanded that the store owner sell a cheap net. Finally, the store owner sold a cheap net to the duck.

The duck went back to the river and used the net to catch the big fish. The duck was very happy and had a delicious dinner. From that day on, the duck always used the cheap net to catch fish in the river. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a curious cow who was always looking for something new. One day the cow decided to explore beyond its usual boundaries. But what the cow didn't know was that the new path ahead would separate it from the other cows for a very long time. 

The cow kept going, more curious than ever before. As it walked further away, the other cows noticed and started to call out. But the cow kept walking and eventually the sound of the other cows faded away. 

Everything seemed unfamiliar, but the cow was determined to keep going. Unfortunately, the cow didn't realize how far it had gone and before long it was completely lost. 

The cow looked around, but all the scenery seemed strange and unfamiliar. Then, just as the cow started to worry, it heard the sound of the other cows again. The cow followed the sound and eventually it found its way back to where it had started. 

The cow was relieved to be back with the other cows and it never ventured that far away again. However, it did remain curious about what was out there beyond its familiar boundaries.

Tim and Kim are twins who like to play with toys. They have many toys, but they want more. They see a big box in the living room. It is a gift for their dad. It has a tag that says "Do not open until his birthday".

Tim and Kim are curious. They want to know what is inside the box. They think of a creative plan. They poke a small hole in the box with a pencil. They peek through the hole. They see something shiny and round. They think it is a ball.

They poke another hole in the box. They see something long and thin. They think it is a stick. They poke more holes in the box. They see something black and square. They think it is a book. They are happy. They think they have found many toys for themselves.

But they are wrong. The shiny and round thing is a watch. The long and thin thing is a tie. The black and square thing is a wallet. They are not toys. They are things for their dad. They are his birthday gift.

Their mom comes in the living room. She sees the box with many holes. She is angry. She asks Tim and Kim what they have done. They are scared. They tell her the truth. They say they are sorry.

Their mom tells them they have broken the law. The law is a rule that everyone must follow. The law says you must not open other people's gifts. The law says you must respect other people's things. The law says you must be honest and kind.

Tim and Kim feel bad. They have learned a lesson. They say they will not break the law again. They say they will wait until their dad's birthday to see his gift. They say they will hug him and say happy birthday. They say they will play with their own toys and share them with each other. They say they will be good twins. Their mom smiles. She forgives them. She hugs them and says she loves them.

Once upon a time, there was a kind lady who had a baby. The baby loved soft things, especially a cloth that the lady always used to wrap him up in. One day, the lady had to go to the store to buy some food for her family. She asked her friend to come over and deliver the cloth to the baby if he woke up and cried for it. 

While the lady was away, the baby woke up and cried for his soft cloth. The friend came over and saw the baby crying. She remembered what the lady had said and gave the baby the cloth. The baby stopped crying and smiled. He hugged the cloth tightly and fell asleep again.

When the lady came back from the store, she saw the cloth in the baby's arms and knew her friend had delivered it to him. She was happy that her baby had his soft cloth and thanked her friend for being so helpful. From that day on, the baby always had his soft cloth with him, and he was a happy baby. The end.

Lily loved to imagine. She liked to pretend she was a princess, a pirate, or a fairy. She liked to make up stories with her toys and draw pictures of her adventures. Sometimes, she imagined she was a cat.

One day, she found a can of tuna in the kitchen. She knew that cats liked tuna, so she decided to open it and share it with her stuffed kitty. She was very eager to taste it. She used a can opener and a spoon and put some tuna on a plate.

"Here you go, kitty," she said. "This is your favorite food. Let's eat it together and be happy."

She took a bite of the tuna and made a face. It was not what she expected. It was salty and fishy and mushy. She did not like it at all. She spat it out and gave the rest to her kitty.

"Yuck, kitty," she said. "This is not good. How can you eat this? I don't want to be a cat anymore. I want to be something else."

She threw away the plate and the can and ran to her room. She looked at her toys and books and wondered what to imagine next. Maybe she could be a dog, or a bird, or a dinosaur. She smiled and picked up her favorite dinosaur toy.

"Roar, dinosaur," she said. "Let's go on a big adventure. Maybe we can find some yummy food that is not tuna."

Once upon a time there was a bear who was sad because he couldn't see his friends, who were all polar bears. He wanted to join them but he didn't know what to do.

One day his mommy took him to the hospital for an x-ray, which made the bear very worried. But then the doctor said that he was healthy and he could now join his friends.

The bear was glad and he ran and jumped at the thought of seeing all his friends. He ran so fast he got to the beach before all the others. He waited and waited until finally his friends appeared on the shore. 

The bear joined in the fun and they all frolicked in the waves and played games together until the sun went down. They said their goodbyes and the bear was happy to have joined them.

Once upon a time, there was a new bird named Bob. Bob was a very happy bird. He loved to fly and soar high in the sky. Every day, he played with his friends in the big blue sky.

One day, Bob saw a strange thing on the ground. It was a toilet. He had never seen a toilet before. Bob was very curious about the toilet. He flew down to take a closer look. The toilet was white and shiny.

Bob wanted to show his friends the toilet. He called his friends, and they all came to see the new thing. They played around the toilet and had a lot of fun. Then, they all went back to the sky to soar and play together. And they lived happily ever after.

Jim was a chubby 3 year old boy who loved to eat. One day, he reached for his spoon, but it wasn't there! He turned to his mom and asked, "Where's my spoon?"

Mom replied, "I lent it to your sister. She needed it for her lunch."

"Can I have it back?" Jim asked.

"Sure," Mom said, handing him the spoon. "Here you go!"

Jim smiled and scooped up a big spoonful of food to eat. He was so happy to have his spoon back.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish. The fish lived in a big, soft pond. The fish could swim around the pond and go anywhere it wanted. 

One day, the fish asked its friends if they believed in magic. But itâ€™s friends said no, thereâ€™s no such thing. 

But then the fish found a magical stone at the bottom of the pond. It was so soft and brightly coloured that it must have been magical. 

The fish was so excited! It took the magical stone back to itâ€™s friends and showed them. Its friends gasped, it was so beautiful. 

Then the fish said: â€œYou should believe in magic!â€

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Joe and Tim. Joe was very worried that the snowman that he and his brother had built would melt away. He tried to think of a way to keep the snowman alive.

Suddenly, Tim had an idea. He smiled and suggested to Joe that they should sing a song to the snowman. Joe looked at his brother, sceptically, but then remembered his dad telling him that music can sometimes work miracles.

So, Joe and Tim sang a song to the snowman. And their song seemed to work! The sun stopped out and the snowman didn't melt away. 

Joe and Tim were so happy that their snowman survived. Joe learned that the power of songs can help people to feel more safe and happy. The moral of the story is that when you are worried, it is important to remember that music can have a powerful effect.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a cozy nest on top of a big chimney. One day, Tweety saw a big storm coming. Tweety was worried that the wind would blow the chimney down, and the nest would fall with it.

Tweety tried to fly away, but the wind was too strong. So, Tweety decided to lean against the side of the chimney to hold it up. Tweety stayed there all night, holding the chimney up with all its might.

In the morning, the storm had passed, and Tweety was tired but happy. Tweety learned that when you care about something, you should do whatever you can to protect it. And that's why Tweety was a hero that day.

Once upon a time, there was a kind dog named Max. Max liked to jog in the park every day. One day, while jogging, Max met a new friend. The new friend was a cat named Tom.

Max and Tom played in the park. They ran and jumped and had fun. Then, Max said, "Let's go to my house and rest by the fireplace." Tom said, "Yes, that sounds nice."

Max and Tom went to Max's house. They sat by the warm fireplace and talked. They were happy to be friends. From that day on, Max and Tom were always together, playing and being kind to each other.

Once upon a time, a pretty little girl named Faith was about to turn three years old. On this special day, her parents planned a birthday party for her.

When Faith heard the news, she was so excited that she started to run around the house. She ran from one room to the other and shouted, â€œYay, I'm turning three!"

Faith's parents smiled at her and said, â€œYou are so pretty, Faith! We can't believe how fast the year has gone!

After the fun of running around, Faith took a break and looked around the house admiring at all the decorations her parents had done for her.

â€œMommy, Daddy, thank you for making this day so special," said Faith.

Her parents smiled and hugged her, â€œIt's our pleasure, sweetheart. Let's have a great time today!â€ 

And they all did. They ate cake, danced around, and eventually, the party was over.

Faith was so happy and content with the day she had, that she started to run around the house again, shouting and singing about how she was now three years old.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Bob. He was three years old and he loved to play. One day Bob's mommy said, "Let's go to the cold maze!". So off they went.

The maze was big and twisty. Bob got lost! He couldn't find his mommy. He was so scared. He shouted, "Mommy!" But she couldn't hear him. He started to miss her.

But then he saw a friendly lady. She said, "Do you want help finding your mommy?" Bob was so happy. She helped him find his way back.

At last, Bob found his mommy. She was so glad to see him. She said, "I missed you so much!". Bob smiled and said, "Me too!" And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a lion who liked to move around. Every morning he would get up and move around the jungle looking for food. One day he saw a group of animals.

The lion said, "Hello, who are you?"

The animals replied, "We are regular animals and we live around here."

The lion smiled and said, "It's nice to meet you. May I join you as you move around today?"

The animals smiled and said, "Yes, you may!"

So the lion and the animals moved together. They enjoyed visiting all the different places in the jungle, and having fun together. 

At the end of the day, the lion thanked the animals for showing him around the jungle and the animals thanked the lion for joining them. 

The lion said goodbye and moved away. But the animals knew he'd be back soon and they looked forward to spending time with their new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Max. Max loved to play with his ball and chew on his bone. One day, Max saw a big dog in the park and got very scared. He ran away and hid behind a tree.

Max's friend, a little girl named Lily, saw him hiding and asked, "What's wrong, Max?"

"I saw a big dog and it scared me," Max replied.

"Don't be scared," Lily said. "That dog is friendly. He just wants to play with you."

Max wasn't sure, but Lily's words excited him. He slowly came out from behind the tree and saw that the big dog was wagging his tail and smiling.

Max and the big dog played together and Max even shared his bone with him. From that day on, Max wasn't scared of big dogs anymore. He was excited to make new friends.

Lila and Ben like to draw. They use crayons and paper to make images of animals, people and things. They are proud of their images and want to show them to their mom and dad.

They find some tape and hang their images on the wall. Lila hangs her image of a mighty lion. Ben hangs his image of a big truck. They smile and clap their hands.

But then, Ben sees Lila's image and wants it. He thinks it is better than his image. He pulls Lila's image from the wall and tries to hang it in his place. Lila sees Ben and gets angry. She wants her image back. She pulls Ben's image from the wall and tries to hang it in her place.

They start to fight and tug and yell. Their images tear and fall to the floor. They cry and make a mess.

Mom and dad hear the noise and come to see what is wrong. They see Lila and Ben and their images. They are not happy. They tell Lila and Ben to stop fighting and to share. They help them to fix their images and to hang them on the wall again. They hug them and tell them they love them.

Lila and Ben say sorry to each other and to mom and dad. They look at their images and see they are both good. They say they like each other's images and they are both mighty. They smile and hold hands.

Once upon a time there was a jolly turkey named Tom. He was so happy and loved to smile. He was always asking people for things. One day he requested to visit the playground. Everybody said yes, so off he went.

At the playground Tom saw lots of exciting things. There were swings, slides and sandboxes. Tom liked playing on the swings the most. He would swing so high that his feathers were rustling in the wind.

Tom was having so much fun at the playground, but it started to get dark. His tummy was rumbling, so he decided to request for some food. He asked for some yummy turkey and everyone said yes. He was so happy.

Tom ate his turkey and he was full up and feeling extra jolly. He thanked everyone and waddled back home. He was so happy that he had made some requests and they were all granted!

John was very sad. He was sitting in his room with a small drum in his hands. He looked out of the window and thought about how he wished he could move away and be happy again. He started banging his drum and humming a silly song. Suddenly, his mum opened the door and said, "What's this noise?" 
John smiled and said he wanted to move away. His mum smiled and said, "You don't have to move away John, you can be happy here too." She put her hand on his shoulder and said, "Let's go to the park and have some fun. That will make you feel better." 
John smiled and put his drum down. He took his mum's hand and the two of them started to move away. By the time they reached the park, John was no longer feeling so sad.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tim. He was very creative and liked to make things. Every day he liked to think of new ideas. One day he had a clever plan. So he decided to try it out. He worked very hard and it began to happen.

Before long, Tim was having lots of success! He was so pleased and excited. His family and friends were really proud of him. Everywhere he went, people were talking about his different, creative ideas.

He was so successful that he even started a special club where he taught other people his ideas. Everybody loved it and they all had lots of fun.

In the end, Tim's plan became very successful. His creativity had made it happen!

The curtains were hanging cleanly in the windows of the little room. Every day, the girl would run in and whisper secrets to them. She hadn't noticed it before, but today, when she was talking in her very quietest voice, the curtains rustled as if in response. Her eyes grew wider as she heard what sounded like an echo of her own whisper. 

Curious, she asked the curtains, "Can you understand me?". The curtains didn't move. She whispered the question again and waited. She heard a faint whispering in response, but it wasn't the same as if she were speaking. This whisper felt different somehow. 

The girl waited and listened. Suddenly, the curtains moved again. This time they were pushing back, inviting her closer. As the girl looked closer, she saw a crack in the window and she could now hear more clearly the voice she had heard earlier. "Come here," it said. 

The girl took a deep breath, trembling with anticipation and excitement. She stepped closer and the curtain parted. Behind it was a secret garden. Everything was clean and vibrant and the girl felt more alive than she had ever felt before. She was finally on an adventure of her own. 

The girl and the whisper from the curtains had a lot more to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was a frightened cat who lived in a small house with a kind girl named Lucy. One day, Fluffy saw a strip of paper on the floor. She was scared of it because it was new to her.

Lucy saw Fluffy looking at the strip of paper. She wanted to support Fluffy and help her not be scared. Lucy said, "Don't be scared, Fluffy. It's just a strip of paper. It won't hurt you."

Fluffy listened to Lucy and started to feel better. She played with the strip of paper and found out it was fun. With Lucy's support, Fluffy was not frightened anymore. They played together and were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a family. They lived in a big house with a garden. The family had a dog named Max. Max was very dependable. He always played with the children and protected them.

One day, the family went for a walk in the park. They saw a beautiful flower. The little girl said, "I admire this flower. It is so pretty." Her brother said, "Yes, it is." 

Suddenly, Max started barking. A cat had climbed up a tree and was stuck. The family tried to help the cat, but they couldn't reach it. Max ran to get help. He found a man who climbed up the tree and rescued the cat.

After that, the family and Max continued their walk. They were happy to have a dependable dog like Max.

Tommy was so excited. His dad had just taken him to the park. He looked around and saw children playing on the slides and swings.

Tommy decided to do something different. He wanted to climb the tree! It was tall and covered in green leaves. He started to climb, and before he knew it, he was at the top.

Tommy looked around proudly. He could see the whole park from here. Suddenly, he saw something red in the grass. It was a baseball! He climbed back down to the ground and grabbed it.

The baseball felt an icy cold. But it didn't stop Tommy from enjoying it. He threw the ball in the air and caught it again. He would show everyone at home that he did something special today!

Jill was in the park. She saw a really high tree. She wanted to jump up to the top. But it looked really difficult. Suddenly, she saw a razor at the base of the tree. She thought it might make it easier to climb up.

"I can try and climb up with the razor," said Jill.

So she grabbed the razor and tried to pull herself up the tree. But it was still too difficult.

Suddenly, her big brother, Jake, came over. He saw what she was doing.

"Come on, Jill. I'll help you," said Jake.

Jake started to hold the razor for Jill. Together, they carefully climbed up the tree. Jill and Jake high-fived each other at the top.

"I did it! I jumped to the top of the tree! Thanks, Big Brother," said Jill.

"Anytime, little Sis," said Jake.

They celebrated at the top of the tree for a few minutes before carefully climbing down. Jill was so happy she could jump to the top of the tree with Jake's help.

Sara was a kind girl who liked to help animals. One day, she saw a bird with a hurt wing in her garden. She ran to get some bread and water for the bird. She also found a soft vest in her closet that she did not wear anymore. She wrapped the vest around the bird to keep it warm and cozy.

The bird was scared at first, but soon it felt Sara's gentle touch and heard her sweet voice. Sara told the bird that she would take care of it until it could fly again. She named the bird Fluffy and made a nest for it in a box. Every day, she fed Fluffy and sang to it.

After a few weeks, Fluffy's wing was healed. Sara was happy, but also sad. She knew that Fluffy belonged to the sky, not to a box. She decided to let Fluffy go, even though she would miss it. She took Fluffy to the garden and opened the vest. Fluffy looked at Sara with gratitude and love. Then it spread its wings and flew away.

Sara watched Fluffy soar in the air. She felt a tear roll down her cheek. She whispered, "Goodbye, Fluffy. Thank you for being my friend." She smiled and waved. She learned that sometimes, the best way to show love is to let go.

The moral value of the story is: Love means caring for someone and letting them be free.

Once upon a time there was a smart girl called Jane. Jane asked her parents for money every day. Her parents said, "No! You have to work for your money!"

One day Jane asked her friend Molly, "Do you have money?" Molly said, "No, but I want money. How can I get money?"

Jane said, "You can be smart and work. Then you will get money!" Molly said, "Ok, let's work together!"

So the two of them started working together. After a few weeks they had some money. Molly and Jane were very happy! They had lots of fun spending their money.

Once upon a time there was a very helpful little girl named Beth. She was three years old and liked to give her parents a helping hand wherever she could.

One day, Beth's parents had to sell some of their old stuff. They had some gray gear that was too old to keep. Beth really liked the gear, so she asked her parents why they were selling it.

Her father said "Well, Beth, we can't keep these things forever. It's important to sell old things in order to make room for something new".

Beth understood and decided to help her parents. She helped them to pack their old gray gear and sell it to whoever was interested. 

Beth learned an important lesson that day: it's better to let go of old things in order to make space for new ones. People should not get too attached to the things they have, because eventually they have to be sold and moved on. Thus, Beth learned to appreciate the things she had, rather than clinging to them forever.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park. They had a big box of crayons and some paper. They liked to draw pictures of animals and flowers and cars.

"Look, I drew a bird!" Lily said, holding up her paper. "It can fly in the sky. It has blue feathers and a yellow beak."

"That's nice, Lily," Sam said. "But I drew a plane. It can fly faster and higher than a bird. It has red wings and a silver body."

They both showed their pictures to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. She smiled and praised them.

"Your pictures are very pretty," she said. "But you know what? You can both fly too. You can fly with your imagination. You can pretend to be anything you want."

"Really?" Lily and Sam asked.

"Yes, really," mom said. "Here, let me show you. Take a crayon and close your eyes. Think of something you want to be. Then draw it on your paper."

Lily and Sam did as mom said. They took a crayon and closed their eyes. They thought hard.

Lily thought of a butterfly. She wanted to be a butterfly with colorful wings and a curly antenna. She wanted to fly from flower to flower and sip nectar.

Sam thought of a rocket. He wanted to be a rocket with a fiery tail and a shiny nose. He wanted to fly to the moon and the stars and see new things.

They opened their eyes and drew their pictures. They were very proud of them.

"Look, mom, I'm a butterfly!" Lily said.

"Look, mom, I'm a rocket!" Sam said.

Mom looked at their pictures and hugged them.

"You are both amazing," she said. "You can fly with your crayons and your imagination. You can be anything you want."

The little girl skipped down the hall. She saw a colorful bag and wondered what was inside. She carried the bag to the living room where she saw a surprise. There were lots of colorful balloons waiting for her! She was so excited she started to play and laugh.

The little girl carried the balloons back down the hall to the kitchen. She found another surprise: a colorful cake! It was pink, purple, yellow and green. She wanted to eat it right away but decided to carry it back to the living room.

The little girl had a lot of fun that day. She carried the cake and balloons back down the hall and into her bedroom. There was a colorful dress and accessories waiting for her there. She smiled and knew the day was going to be lots of fun.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Emma and Jack. One day, they wanted to discuss furniture.

"Let's talk about furniture," said Emma.

"Yes," said Jack.

They looked around the room and saw a small table.

"What is that?" asked Emma pointing to the table.

"That is a small table," answered Jack.

They looked at the small table and discussed what they could do with it.

"We could use it as a game table," said Emma.

"Yes!" said Jack.

They discussed other ideas until they had the perfect plan. They agreed to use the small table as a game table. They laughed and cheered and had lots of fun.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who lived in a village. He loved to play on the swing in his garden each day. One morning when he went outside to play he saw a little white mouse running around in a hurry.

The boy said "Hi, little mouse! What are you doing in such a hurry?"

The mouse stopped and said "I am trying to find some food for my family. They're hungry and I want to help them".

The boy smiled and said "I can help you too! Come with me".

The boy and the mouse went to the boy's house and the boy reached into the cupboard. He took out a generous bag of food and handed it to the mouse.

The mouse was so happy and said "Thank you so much! You are very generous".

The boy smiled and said "It was my pleasure to help. We should always be kind to others and help when we can".

The little mouse hopped off happily with the food and the boy went back to his swing. He had learned an important lesson that day - that we should always be generous and helpful to others.

Once upon a time there was a little green peanut. He was very happy and loved to bounce around. One day he went to visit a nice big tree. But when he got there, he met a hungry squirrel. The squirrel said, "Hey little peanut!" He smiled and said hello. But then the squirrel lunged forward and tried to bite the green peanut! The peanut got scared and ran away as fast as he could. He didn't want to be eaten!

He kept running until he found a safe place. Luckily, it was a big open field filled with lots of food. The peanut was so happy to find so much food. He ate until he was full. So the little green peanut lived happily ever after and never had to worry about the squirrel trying to bite him again.

Max was running around in the backyard with his mom and dad. Max was having so much fun when he tripped, and fell into the mud. He was all covered in the sticky, messy mud, and it was making a big mess.

Max and his parents were very surprised and started to laugh. Max felt very embarrassed but his parents told him that there was nothing to be ashamed of. Max's dad went inside and got some rags and buckets of water to help clean up the mess.

Max and his parents spent a few minutes cleaning up the mud and then his mom and dad took him inside for a warm bath and some clean clothes. Max felt much better after being all cleaned up and knew that it was okay to make mistakes.

Once there was a big teddy bear named Bert. He was dropped into a tall tree and he couldn't get out. He called out for help, but nobody could hear him. He felt so sad, until he saw a little bird land on a branch nearby. 

The bird introduced himself as Tiny. Tiny said that he knew a way to help Bert, but he wouldnâ€™t teach him unless Bert promised to spread some love. Bert had no idea what this meant, but Tiny promised if he did, he would be able to get down from that tree. 

So Bert agreed to listen. Tiny said he should give a big squeeze and a wide smile to everyone he met. Bert felt silly, but he was determined to get down from the tree, so he promised to give everyone a squeeze and a smile.

The next day, Bert saw a young girl in the park who was crying. Bert walked over and gave her a big squeeze and a wide smile. The little girl was so happy, she gave Bert a photo of them together. 

Bert was so pleased he waved goodbye, then looked up to the sky, and shouted, â€œThank you, Tiny!â€. He had learned that by giving a simple hug and smile, he could spread a little joy and make the world a better place.

Once upon a time there was a brave bunny. He was so brave that one evening he decided to leave the safety of his burrow. As he poked his head out into the darkness, he heard a strange noise. It was a clapping sound, like someone was applauding.

He hopped out and found a little mouse. The mouse was applauding the brave bunny for having the courage to leave his burrow at night. The bunny was so happy to hear the applause that he decided to stay out and explore the night.

As he continued to explore, the bunny discovered a night full of surprises. He heard beautiful music and saw stars twinkling in the sky. With the mouse beside him, he felt like nothing could scare him.

The bunny and the mouse taught us all that it is important to be brave and explore the world, even at night. Applaud those who have the courage to adventure and discover the beauty of the darkness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the pool with her friends. One day, Lily's friend dared her to jump off the high diving board. Lily was scared because it was very high, but she didn't want to look like a scaredy-cat in front of her friends, so she agreed.

Lily climbed up the ladder and stood at the edge of the diving board. She looked down and it seemed very far away. She felt scared and didn't want to jump anymore. But her friend shouted, "Come on, Lily! You can do it!" So, Lily took a deep breath and jumped into the pool.

After she got out of the pool, Lily's friend said, "Wow, you're so brave! I could never do that." Lily felt happy that she had dared to do something scary. She learned that sometimes it's okay to be scared, but it's important to be brave too. And she also learned that being harsh to someone is not a good idea, because it can hurt their feelings.

Molly was happy. She knew it was a special day. She put on a pretty dress and ran outside.

A big group of people were there, singing and smiling. They were all excited!

"It's a birthday party for me!" said Molly.

"Yes, it is! Happy birthday Molly!" everyone said.

Molly smiled. There were presents on a big table and a big cake with lots of candles.

There were even presents from Mommy. One was a pretty wrap with flowers on it.

Molly opened it and found a very interesting toy inside. It made different sounds when she pressed its buttons.

Everyone sang happy birthday while Molly blew out her candles. Then they all danced and laughed.

Molly was so happy! It was the best birthday ever.

Once, there was a man who loved to bring things home. One day he had brought home some ink.

"What have you brought home?" asked the little three year old girl.

"I brought some ink, it'll be fun to draw with," the man said. 

The little girl was excited and ran to get her pencils and paper. But when she opened the jar of ink, she was surprised. It was a bad colour!

"This ink is bad!" said the little girl sadly.

The man was sorry to learn that the ink was bad and decided he would go back out and find some more ink in a better colour.

"I'll bring back some better ink so you can draw with it and have fun," he said. 

The little girl smiled and waited for the man to come back. He eventually returned with some ink in a great colour, and the little girl was so happy! She made the most beautiful pictures with the new ink. And that's how the bad ink was brought home and changed for the better.

Once upon a time, Annie had a diary. It was bright pink and shiny. Every day, she would write silly things in it. Things like her favourite animals and her best friends names. Whenever Annie had a secret, she would write it down in her diary.

One day, Annie wanted to show her diary to her best friend. She thought it was silly and wanted to share it. So she ran out of her house to find her friend. She ran and ran until she found her.

Then, Annie showed her diary to her friend. Her friend thought it was so silly and the two laughed until their tummies hurt. From then on, the two friends had lots of fun looking through Annie's diary together.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to eat carrots, but one day he wanted to try something new. He asked his mom for some cauliflower. She cooked it for him, but Benny didn't like it. 

Benny decided to go on an adventure to find something he would like to eat. He hopped around the forest and found a patch of carrots. But then, he saw something burning in the distance. 

Benny hopped over to see what was happening. It was a campfire! Some friendly animals were roasting marshmallows over the fire. Benny joined them and had a great time. He even tried some roasted cauliflower and found out he liked it when it was cooked over a fire. From that day on, Benny was an adventurous eater.

Jill was a young girl. She loved to perform. Every day, she would practice her moves. One day, she had a special performance.

First, Jill put on her costume. Then she got her sausage. She needed it for her performance. She was ready.

Jill began her performance. She was gentle. She moved her arms and legs slowly. She twirled around in circles. Everyone clapped.

Jill's performance was a big success. Her sausage stayed safe the entire time. Everyone cheered when she finished. Jill was so proud of her performance.

Once upon a time, there was a big store in a small town. This store had many different things. People liked to go there to buy things they needed.

One day, a comet fell from the sky. It was shiny and very different from the things in the store. Everyone in the town wanted to see the comet. They all went to the store to look at the comet.

The store owner put the comet in the store window so everyone could see it. The comet made the store even more special. People from other towns came to see the comet too. The store and the comet made everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and make things with her hands. One day, she decided to design a special present for her mommy's birthday. She drew a pretty picture of a flower and made a necklace out of beads.

But then, Lily saw an ugly bug crawling on the edge of a cliff. She didn't want it to fall, so she carefully picked it up and put it on a leaf. She felt happy that she could help the bug and make it safe.

When Lily gave her mommy the present, she loved it so much. Lily felt proud of herself for making something beautiful for her mommy and for helping the bug. She knew that even though things might look ugly or scary at first, she could always find a way to make them better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her.

One day, Amy went for a walk in the park with her mom. She noticed some flowers and pointed them out to her mom. She then noticed a big puddle with a beautiful rainbow in it! 

"Look Mommy!" Amy exclaimed, "A rainbow!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's right sweetie, but we need to keep walking. We should hurry so we can get back home before dinner."

Amy kept walking, but then she noticed something else. In the corner of the park, there was a little kitten with a big sad face. Amy wanted to help, so she went to the kitten. She noticed that the kitten was very hungry and had no food available.

Amy looked up at her mom and said, "Mommy, can we help the kitten? Can we give it some food?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, sweetie. Let's find some food for this little one."

They worked together to find some food, and when they did, they gave it to the kitten. The kitten was so happy and thanked them with a big purr.

Amy and her mom continued on their walk, but Amy never forgot the kitten's happy face.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy called Tom. Tom liked to explore the world around him. One day, Tom was playing near a stream. He saw a delicate butterfly flying closely above the water.

Tom said to the butterfly, "Hi butterfly! I want to dive too!" The butterfly smiled and said, "That is a very good idea! But you must be careful."

Tom got into the stream. He was very excited. He wanted to dive as deep as he could. He pushed himself hard into the stream. Suddenly he felt his feet reaching a soft, sand floor. He opened his eyes and looked around. The water was so clear he could see all the rocks and fish around him.

Tom enjoyed swimming in the stream, he almost forgot to come back up. He remembered just in time and carefully climbed back up to the surface. He said goodbye to the butterfly and ran off to tell his friends his new adventure.

Ben and Lily are twins who like to play with their toys. They have many toys of different shapes, colors and sizes. Sometimes they make a mess and their mom asks them to sort their toys. Sorting means putting the same kind of toys together in a box or a basket.

One day, Ben and Lily decide to sort their toys in a new way. They want to see who has more muscle. Muscle is what makes you strong and able to lift heavy things. They each take a big box and start putting their toys inside. They try to find the heaviest toys they have, like cars, trucks, balls and books.

"Look, Lily, I have more muscle than you!" Ben says, as he lifts his box with both hands. "My box is heavier than yours!"

"No, Ben, I have more muscle than you!" Lily says, as she lifts her box with one hand. "My box is heavier than yours!"

They both walk to the living room, where their mom is sitting on the couch. They want to show her their boxes and see who has more muscle. But as they walk, they don't see the rug on the floor. They trip over the rug and fall down. Their boxes spill over and their toys scatter everywhere.

"Oh no!" Ben and Lily say together. "We made a mess!"

Their mom gets up and helps them stand up. She sees their toys all over the floor. She is not angry, but she is surprised.

"What were you doing, Ben and Lily?" she asks.

"We were sorting our toys, mom," Ben says.

"We wanted to see who has more muscle, mom," Lily says.

Their mom smiles and hugs them. She thinks they are very adventurous. Adventurous means liking to try new things and have fun.

"That's very creative, Ben and Lily," she says. "But maybe next time, you can sort your toys by shape or color or size. That way, you won't make such a big mess."

"Okay, mom," Ben and Lily say. "We're sorry for the mess."

They help their mom pick up their toys and put them back in their boxes. They sort them by shape or color or size. They still have fun, but they also learn to be tidy. They are happy and proud of their toys and their muscle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat cauliflower because it was her favorite vegetable. One day, Lily's mom asked her if she wanted to send some cauliflower to her grandma who lived far away. Lily was very enthusiastic about this idea and immediately said yes.

Once upon a time, there was a big tank. The tank was very long and it was used to hold water. The water made the tank feel heavy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She dreamed of flying around like a bird. So she found an old mattress and put it on the ground. She closed her eyes and pretended to be a bird. She zooming around the sky!

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was only three years old. One day, he wanted to make some jam.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and collect pretty rocks. One day, she found a shiny jar that was ready to be filled with her treasures. 

But then, a big dog came running towards her and scared her. Lily dropped the jar and it broke into many pieces. She started to frown and feel sad. 

Lily tried to put the pieces back together, but it was too late. She couldn't fix the jar and all her pretty rocks were lost. She felt very upset and cried. 

From that day on, Lily learned to be careful with her things and to watch out for big dogs. She also learned that accidents can happen and sometimes things can't be fixed.

Once upon a time, there was a huge bookcase. It was full of colorful books. A little girl named Lily loved to read the books from the bookcase. One day, she saw a new book on the top shelf. She wanted to read it very much.

Lily tried to reach the new book, but she was too small. Her big brother, Tom, saw her struggle. He said, "I can help you get the book, but you have to give me your candy." Lily didn't want to give away her candy, but she really wanted the new book. So, she agreed and gave Tom her candy.

Tom got the new book for Lily. But when he gave it to her, he spread jam on the pages. Lily was sad and cried. She couldn't read the new book. Tom laughed and ate her candy. The book was ruined, and Lily didn't have any candy left.

One day, there were two boys. They were best friends. They played together all the time.

But then, something happened. They had an argument and they split up. They argued over a toy they both wanted and they yelled at each other.

The law says that friends should not fight. It was bad to argue. The boys felt very guilty.

They both decided that it was time to make up. They hugged each other and promised to never fight again. They stayed friends forever.

Once there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day, she saw a big, unknown door in the forest. She slowly opened the door and saw a giant. The giant smiled at the little girl and offered her some cookies.

The little girl was so scared that she couldn't move. She slowly said "No, thank you".

The giant said, "It's alright, I understand. Would you like to see what else I have to offer?"

The little girl nodded her head and the giant showed her his treasure. It was full of wondrous and strange things. The giant said, "Please take what you like."

The little girl couldn't believe her eyes. She chose a necklace with a shimmering stone. The giant said, "May this necklace bring you happiness." The little girl thanked the giant, put on the necklace and ran back home.

She told everyone about her adventure and always wore the necklace. The little girl was never scared to explore the unknown again.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Anna. One day she went to the village to collect some rice. She saw a group of children playing a game. 
Anna approached the children and asked: "Can I join in?" 
The children replied: "Yes, of course you can! We are collecting rice for the village." 
So together they collected all the rice in the village. Then they shared the rice so that each family had enough to eat. 
When the rice was shared, Anna said: "That was fun! I'm glad that you, young children, are so generous and helpful." 
The children smiled, proud of their accomplishment, and thanked Anna for helping them. 
The End.

Clarissa was feeling very grumpy as she watched the soldiers walk by. "What's wrong?" Her mother asked. "Why don't you play with them in the garden?"

Clarissa shook her head, "No. I don't like the soldiers." But her mother smiled and said, "Maybe you'll change your mind. Come and play with them in the garden".

So Clarissa went outside. She thought about running away but everything inside her was telling her to give them a chance. As she stepped out of the house, the soldiers saw her and called her name.

Clarissa was still feeling grumpy so instead of walking toward them, she ran away and started to weep. The soldiers were startled by her reaction but they followed her anyway and finally caught up to her.

"What's wrong?" Asked one of the soldiers. Clarissa wiped her eyes and said, "I was just thinking that sometimes you have to give people a chance". And with that, the soldiers welcomed her as a friend and she learned that soldiers were not so scary after all.

Once there was a spider. His name was Cleary. He was a very trusty spider. 

One day, Cleary was walking through the garden. Suddenly, he heard a loud voice calling out to him. 

"Cleary! Can I trust you?" said the voice.

Cleary didn't know who was talking to him, so he replied "Yes."

The voice then said, "I'm in big trouble. Can you help me?" 

Cleary replied, "Of course! What do you need?" 

The voice replied, "I need you to climb that tall tree and get me some acorns. Can you do it?"

Cleary looked up and saw the tall tree. He knew it was a big job for a little spider, but he was determined. 

"Yes, I can do it," he told the voice.

So, Cleary made his way up the tree, and soon enough he had a clear view of the ground below. He was able to pick the acorns quickly and safely, and he brought them back to the voice. 

The voice thanked Cleary for trusting him. Cleary was very proud of himself and went home, happy that he could help a friend in need.

Once there was a boy. He wanted to eat something healthy, so he went to the garden. In the garden he saw something red and round. It was a radish. The boy was very excited and he took the radish. He was happy because the radish was very useful for eating.

The boy brought the radish home and washed it. Then he cut it into small pieces and put some salt on it. He was so happy that he ate it all up in no time.

The boy was so happy because the radish was delicious. Eating the radish made him feel strong and healthy, so he decided to eat radishes every day. 

From then on, radishes were always part of the boy's diet, and he always remembered how useful they were for a healthy and yummy snack.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. His name was James. Every day, James would record things with his special toy. He had lots of fun recording things. 

One day, while he was recording, James saw some gum on the ground. He picked it up and put it in his pocket. He was so excited! 

But then, his mom came and saw the gum. She said he should not have taken it! James was so frustrated. 

His mom said he had to put the gum back. But James thought of a good idea. He said that he could record it so he could remember it. His mom agreed, and James was so happy. 

So, he recorded the gum in his special toy, and from then on, he never forgot about it.

Mark was pretending he was a tiger. He growled like a tiger and waved his arms like a tiger. He was so good at pretending that he even forgot he was really Mark.

His mother came in to his playroom and said, "Mark! What are you doing?" Mark replied, "I'm pretending I'm a tiger!"

Mark's mom looked around the room and saw a thick blanket on the floor. Then she said to Mark, "Let's pretend the blanket is a jungle! You can be the tiger and I'll be the monkey!"

Mark said with excitement, "Let's do it!"

So both Mark and his mom pretended their blanket was a jungle. They hopped and jumped around the room like monkeys and tigers. They pretended for a long time, playing different roles and having lots of fun.

Eventually, Mark's mom said, "Let's stop pretending now, Mark. It's time for dinner!"

So Mark put his tiger costume away, gave his mom a big hug, and said, "Thanks for playing with me!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very tall for his age. He loved looking up at the sky and imagining all the things in the world. One day, Timmy went to the park to play. He saw a girl named Sally and asked if she wanted to play with him.

Sally said, "Sure! What do you want to play?"

Timmy said, "Let's add some blocks to my tower and make it taller than the world!"

Sally smiled and said, "That sounds like fun! Let's do it!"

So, Timmy and Sally added blocks to the tower and it grew taller and taller. When they were done, Timmy looked up at the tower and said, "Wow! It's taller than the world!"

Sally laughed and said, "No silly, it's not taller than the world. But it's still really tall!"

Timmy smiled and said, "Thanks for helping me make it taller, Sally. You're a great friend!"

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He was a very curious boy who loved adventure. One day Jack decided to go for a walk. He found a magical path which seemed very inviting. He felt so excited that he decided to go explore it. 

As Jack walked on the charming path he stopped to explore the different things he could touch, see, and hear. Suddenly, he felt something tickle his tongue. Looking around he found a tree with bright yellow fruits. Jack decided to taste one and it was so sweet! He tasted so many different fruits on the path. 

Jack had a wonderful time on the path and he would never forget the delicious taste of the fruits.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures in her backyard. One day, she saw a butterfly fluttering around and she wanted to catch it. She tried to grab it with her hands, but it flew away.

Lily's mom came outside and saw her daughter looking sad. "What's wrong, sweetie?" she asked. "I wanted to catch the butterfly, but it flew away," Lily replied. "Don't worry, there are plenty of other butterflies to catch in life," her mom said.

Lily went back to playing with her toys, but she saw a shiny bracelet on the ground. "Look, Mommy, I found something!" she exclaimed. Her mom looked at it and said, "That looks cheap, it's probably not worth much."

But Lily loved the bracelet and wore it every day. One day, she went to the park and a stranger grabbed the bracelet off her wrist and ran away. Lily was so sad that she lost her special bracelet and her mom told her that sometimes bad things happen in life.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Jack. Jack had to go on a trip to another country, but he forgot his passport at home. Jack was very sad because he couldn't go on his trip without his passport. 

Luckily, Jack's friend came to the rescue. His friend said he would deliver the passport to Jack at the airport. Jack was very happy and thanked his friend. 

When Jack's friend arrived at the airport, he gave Jack his passport. Jack looked at the passport and thought it was very dull. But he was happy because he could now go on his trip. Jack hugged his friend and said thank you again. 

From that day forward, Jack always remembered to check if he had his passport before going on a trip.

Once upon a time, there was a weird rocket. The rocket wanted to go to the moon, but it wasn't sure how. Suddenly, the rocket spotted a big cloth nearby. The cloth was really big and fluffy.

The rocket zoomed over to the cloth and said "Hello! Can you help me get to the moon?". The cloth was so excited and nodded its head. It said "Yes! I can help you!".

The cloth began to wipe the rocket with a special soapy liquid. The rocket felt so clean and smooth after the cloth was done. The rocket thanked the cloth and gave it a big hug.

Finally the rocket was ready to go the the moon. The rocket flew away and waved goodbye to the cloth. The cloth was so happy for the rocket and smiled as it watched the rocket take off.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to class every day with her friends. One day, it was very hot outside and they were all feeling tired. But their teacher encouraged them to keep learning and trying their best.

Lily felt happy when her teacher said that. She knew that she could do it, even though she was feeling hot and tired. So, she listened carefully and did all her classwork. Her friends did the same, and they all felt proud of themselves when they finished.

After class, Lily and her friends went outside to play in the shade. They talked about how good they felt for doing their best in class. Lily's teacher came outside too and told them how proud she was of them. They all smiled and felt happy together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play her guitar. She would play it every day and sing songs for her friends and family. One day, her friend Jack came over and asked if he could play with her guitar too. Lily didn't want to share because she was impatient and wanted to play alone.

Jack said, "Please, Lily, can I play too?" 

Lily disagreed and said, "No, it's mine!"

Jack felt sad and left the house. Later that day, Lily tried to play her guitar, but it wouldn't make any sounds. She realized that she had broken it by playing too hard. Lily felt very upset and wished she had let Jack play with her guitar earlier. 

From that day on, Lily learned to share and be patient with her friends. She also learned to take better care of her guitar so that it would last a long time.

Once upon a time, there lived a gentle raven. His name was Robert and he wanted to build something special. 

Every day, Robert worked hard to build his dream. He gathered details from the ground, moving rocks and twigs around, collecting delicate little pieces. 

One day, Robert's cousin called out from the sky, "What are you doing, Robert?" Robert smiled and said "I'm building something special, a delicate piece of art made with love!" 

Robert's cousin smiled and nodded, "That sounds wonderful! I can't wait to see it!" 

Robert worked hard over the next weeks and months and he eventually completed his dream. And when his family saw it they all agreed it was truly the most delicate and beautiful thing they had ever seen.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to go to the park with their mom. The park has a big slide, a swing, and a train. The train is their favorite. It goes around the park and makes a loud noise.

One day, mom says they can go to the park after lunch. Anna and Ben are very happy. They eat their sandwiches and drink their juice. Then they put on their hats and shoes. They are ready to go.

At the park, they see the train. It is red and shiny. It has many seats and windows. They run to the train station. They see a man with a hat and a whistle. He is the train driver.

"Hello, little ones," he says. "Do you want to ride the train?"

"Yes, please!" Anna and Ben say together. They are very enthusiastic.

"OK, then. You need a ticket to ride the train. Do you have a ticket?" the train driver asks.

Anna and Ben look at each other. They do not have a ticket. They do not know what a ticket is.

"Mom, what is a ticket?" Anna asks.

"A ticket is a small paper that you give to the train driver. It shows that you can ride the train. It costs some money," mom explains.

"Oh, I see. Can we have a ticket, mom?" Ben requests.

"Sure, sweetie. I have some money in my purse. Let me buy you a ticket," mom says.

She goes to the ticket booth and gives some money to the lady. The lady gives her two tickets. Mom gives one ticket to Anna and one ticket to Ben.

"Here you go, kids. This is your ticket. Hold it in your hand and give it to the train driver," mom says.

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben say. They hold their tickets and go to the train. They give their tickets to the train driver. He smiles and takes them.

"Welcome aboard, kids. Find a seat and enjoy the ride," he says.

Anna and Ben find a seat near the window. They wave to mom. Mom waves back. The train driver blows his whistle and the train starts to move. Anna and Ben are very excited. They look out the window and see the park. They see the slide, the swing, and the flowers. They see the birds, the dogs, and the people. They see the sun, the sky, and the clouds. They hear the train go choo-choo. They feel the wind in their hair. They have a lot of fun. They love the train.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they find a big map in the park. The map shows many roads and places.

"Let's play with the map!" Tim says. "We can pretend we are drivers and go to different places."

"OK!" Sam says. "But we have to be careful. The map is not ours. We have to give it back when we are done."

They spread the map on the grass and put their cars and trucks on it. They make noises and talk to each other.

"Vroom, vroom! I am going to the zoo!" Tim says.

"Beeep, beeep! I am going to the beach!" Sam says.

They have fun with the map. But they do not see a man walking towards them. The man is deaf. He cannot hear their noises. He is looking for his map. He lost it in the park.

The man sees his map on the grass. He is happy. He picks it up and folds it. He does not see the cars and trucks on it. He puts the map in his pocket and walks away.

Tim and Sam are shocked. They see their cars and trucks gone with the map. They run after the man. They shout and wave.

"Hey, hey! Stop, stop! That is our map! That is our map!" Tim says.

"Give us back our cars and trucks! Give us back our cars and trucks!" Sam says.

But the man does not hear them. He does not stop. He walks fast. He speeds away.

Tim and Sam are sad. They cry. They lost their map and their cars and trucks. They wish they had been more careful. They wish they had not played with the map. They learn a lesson. They learn to respect other people's things. They learn to share and be kind.

Once there was a patient little girl. She was always kind and thoughtful. One day her parents had to go away so she stayed with her Grandma. Grandma was very kind, and she promised to take good care of the little girl. 

Grandma suggested they make some cookies for the neighbours. They went to the kitchen and began mixing ingredients. Then Grandma showed the little girl how to turn the oven on. The cookies filled the house with a delicious smell. 

When the cookies were ready, Grandma put them in a big basket and they turned to leave the house. On their way to the neighbours' house, they ran into a homeless man. The little girl was grateful for the opportunity to help, so she gave the man all the cookies. 

The man was so pleased and thankful. He thanked them with a big smile. In return, the little girl smiled and was proud to have been so patient and kind. They thanked the man and turned back to Grandma's house. 

Grandma and the little girl were feeling very happy. Grandma said she was proud of the little girl, and the girl felt grateful to have a dear Grandma to share this moment with.

Mummy had a big jar of jam. It was big and messy. Little Jack wanted the jam. He asked mum, she said no but he didn't listen. He tried to carry the jam to his bedroom but he was too little and he dropped it. The jam went everywhere. It was a big, messy mess! 

Mummy was very mad. She said no more jam for Jack. Jack was very sad, but he understood why mummy was mad. 

So mummy cleaned up the mess and gave Jack a big hug. She said if Jack ever wanted jam again he had to ask first. Jack said he would never try to carry the jam on his own again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the library with her mommy. They found a book about animals and Lily loved it. She wanted to keep the book forever, so she asked her mommy to print it. 

Lily's mommy said they couldn't print the book because it belonged to the library. Lily got upset and started to cry. Her mommy told her to be quiet because the library was a place of silence. 

Lily didn't want to be quiet, so she ran away from her mommy and hid in a dark corner of the library. She was scared and wanted her mommy to find her. But her mommy couldn't find her because Lily was hiding so well. 

When the library closed, Lily was still hiding in the dark. She was all alone and scared. She cried and cried, but nobody came to help her. The library was silent and nobody knew she was there. Poor Lily was stuck in the dark all night long.

Once upon a time there was a famous flower. It was colourful and beautiful. Every morning it would bloom bright and early. One day, the flower heard about a holiday.

It said to itself, "I need to get ready for this holiday. I have to bloom even brighter".

So it started getting ready. It grew its petals wider, making it even more beautiful than ever.

On the day of the holiday, the flower was ready. It was so colourful and amazing that everyone noticed it. Kids laughed and clapped when they saw it bloom. The flower felt so happy to be part of the celebration.

The flower received lots of compliments from everyone. It was the most famous flower in town and it had lots of fun on the holiday.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to help his mommy cook in the kitchen. One day, his mommy asked him to help chop some vegetables with a knife. Timmy was excited to help, but he didn't know how to use a knife. His mommy showed him how to hold the knife and be careful.

As Timmy was chopping the vegetables, he noticed a shiny knife on the counter. It was an ordinary knife, but it looked so cool. Timmy wanted to play with it, but he knew he shouldn't. He resisted the temptation to touch the knife and kept chopping the vegetables.

After they finished cooking, Timmy's mommy praised him for being a good helper and for resisting the temptation to play with the knife. Timmy learned that it's important to be careful with dangerous things and to resist doing things that could hurt him or others.

Once there was an orange potato. He loved to sneeze. Every day he would go up to the top of the hill and sneeze loudly. All the animals around him could hear him.

One day, a squirrel and some other animals came to see him. The orange potato was so happy to have company. He showed them some of his sneezes. He was so good at it that the squirrel began to try it too.

Soon, the whole group of animals were sneezing. They would sneeze so loud that the birds in the sky flew away. The orange potato was so proud that all his friends were learning to sneeze.

From then on, the orange potato and his friends would have sneezing contests to see who could sneeze the loudest. They were so silly!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the forest near her house. One day, she met a friendly rabbit named Benny. They played together and had a lot of fun.

As they were playing, Benny noticed something strange. He said, "Lily, look over there. I see a dangerous snake!" Lily was scared and asked, "What should we do?" Benny replied, "Let's examine the situation and find an exit."

They looked around and found a small hole in a tree. They quickly ran towards it and squeezed through. They were safe! Lily thanked Benny for his help and promised to always be careful when exploring the forest. From that day on, they always looked out for each other and had many more adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved the outdoors. One day, she decided to go for a walk with her mom. As they were walking, they heard a big splash. It was coming from a big, blue pond. The girl asked her mom, "Can I splash too?" Her mom said, "Yes!" So the girl and her mom ran to the pond and splashed and splashed. The girl laughed and screamed with delight.

Then, the girl and her mom went to a mailbox. The girl was curious. She asked her mom what a mailbox was for. Her mom said, "Mailbox is for sending letters!" The little girl thought that was so cool. She couldn't wait to write a letter and send it to her best friend.

Afterwards, the girl and her mom went to the store. The girl saw a delicious ice cream cone. She asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said yes and the girl ate every last lick of that ice cream cone. It tasted so yummy.

The girl and her mom had a wonderful day. Splashing in the pond, discovering mailboxes and eating delicious ice cream made it a day to never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a happy sun. The sun was very warm and made everything feel nice. One day, the sun woke up and saw a valley. The valley was very big and had lots of green trees.

The sun decided to wave to the valley to say hello. The valley waved back and the sun was very happy. The sun kept shining and making everything warm. The valley was happy too and all the animals that lived there were happy too.

The sun and the valley became friends and every day the sun would wave to the valley and the valley would wave back. They liked each other very much and were always happy together.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who lived in the forest. One day, he met a little bird who was lost. "Can you help me find my way home?" asked the bird. "Sure, I can help you," replied the bear. They walked and walked, but they couldn't find the bird's home.

Then the bear said, "Imagine if we could fly like you, we could find your home faster." The bird said, "I can't carry you, but I can show you the way." The bear followed the bird, but he got tired and hungry. Suddenly, he saw a comb on the ground. "I'll eat this comb," he thought. But the comb got stuck in his throat and he couldn't breathe. The bird tried to help, but it was too late. The bear had died.

The little bird was sad and flew away, still lost in the forest. The end.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy cup who lived in an enormous castle. Every day the cup would march through the castle's grand hallways, admiring its beauty.

One day, the cup was strolling through the corridors when it ran into a tiny mouse. The cup stopped and asked the mouse, "What are you doing here?" The mouse replied, "I am looking for food. I haven't eaten anything in days!"

The cup felt sorry for the mouse and decided to help. It marched to the castle kitchen and brought back a cup filled with cheese. The mouse was thrilled and thanked the cup for its help.

The cup smiled and said, "You're welcome! It's so important to help those who are less fortunate than us." The mouse nodded in agreement and happily scurried off to enjoy its meal. 

From then on, the wealthy cup was known as the most generous in the castle.

Once there was a little bird who wanted to win a race. All the other birds were ready and excited for the race, but the little bird was nervous. He just wanted to do his best and was hopeful for success. 

The race began and the little bird flew with all his might. He felt happy and blew through the wind with joy. He worked very hard and was determined to win. 

The little bird had almost made it across the finish line when he began to slip and fall behind. He looked sad and tired, but he did not give up! With one last burst of energy, the little bird flew over the finish line and won the race!

Everyone was so glad the little bird had won. Bird friends cheered and celebrated with him. The little bird was filled with accomplishment and joy. He had achieved success and was proud. 

The little bird was glad he had won the race and happy he could make all his bird friends proud. It was a special moment he would never forget.

Tommy was playing in the park with his friend. He saw the big icy pond and wanted to go look at it. His friend warned him not to, it looked cold after all!

Tommy walked closer and closer to the edge of the pond. His legs started to tremble as he looked at the icy water. "Let's go, Tommy!" his friend said.

But Tommy wanted to get closer, he wanted to touch the icy surface. His legs trembled even more.

"Don't go closer!" his friend said. "It's too icy!"

Tommy didn't listen and took one last step towards the water. Suddenly, the ice cracked and Tommy screamed! His friend quickly helped him out and they ran away.

From then on, Tommy was careful when going near icy ponds. He had a lot of fun with his friend, and he always listened to his advice.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named James. He lived in a nice house with his parents and his puppy. 

One day, it started to rain a lot. It kept raining and soon it started to flood. Everywhere was so wet, and James was feeling helpless.

He decided to go look for help. James walked around outside, but nobody was there. Then he saw a big boat. It was the boat of a kind boatman. 

The boatman looked at James and asked why he was out in the flood. James told him his family was stuck in their house and he was looking for help. The kind boatman agreed to help and took James to his house. 

When James got to his house, the boatman and James helped his family to get out of the house. They all got in the boat and soon were finally safe. 

James was so happy to find help. He thanked the kind boatman for saving his family. Everybody was happy and safe again.

Once upon a time there was a mama and a baby. The mama wanted the baby to be obedient, so she always said "Stop!" when the baby started to do something wrong. 

One day, the mama and baby were walking together. They stopped at a place with a menu. The mama looked at the menu and showed the baby all the nice things she could have. The baby was excited, but obedient, so she didn't make a fuss. 

When the mama was done reading the menu, she said to the baby, "That's enough. Stop looking at it now." 

The baby did as she was told, and the mama bought her something nice from the menu. They ate it together and the baby was happy because she had been obedient. 

The mama and baby went home, content with their day. The baby had learned an important lesson: it's always good to be obedient!

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was a selfish boy. He did not like to share his things with others. One day, his mom brought home a big bag of vegetables. She wanted to explain to Tim why it was important to share.

"Tim," said Mom, "we need to share these vegetables with our neighbors. It is not good to be selfish." Tim did not want to share the vegetables. He wanted to keep them all for himself. But Mom told him, "If you share, you will make others happy."

Tim thought about it and then said, "No, I don't want to share." So, he took the vegetables and hid them in his room. The neighbors were sad because they had no food to eat. They knocked on Tim's door and asked if he had any food to share. Tim did not want to share, so he said no.

That night, Tim ate all the vegetables by himself. He felt very full and sick. He wished he had listened to his mom and shared with the neighbors. But now, it was too late. The vegetables were gone, and Tim felt very bad.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have a lot of fun. But after a while, they feel tired and hungry.

"Let's go home and eat," says Anna.

"OK," says Ben. "But can we stop at the ice cream truck first?"

They see the ice cream truck near the gate. They run to it and wait in line. They see many flavors of ice cream. They have to choose one.

"What do you want?" asks the ice cream man.

"I want chocolate," says Anna.

"I want strawberry," says Ben.

The ice cream man gives them their cones. They pay him and say thank you. They lick their ice cream and smile.

They walk home with their ice cream. They see their mom waiting for them at the door.

"Hi, kids," says mom. "Did you have fun at the park?"

"Yes, mom," says Anna. "We played a lot. But we are tired and hungry."

"We have some soup and bread for lunch," says mom. "But first, finish your ice cream and wash your hands."

"OK, mom," says Ben. "Can we rest after lunch?"

"Of course, you can," says mom. "You can rest on the couch or in your bed. But first, eat your lunch and follow the order."

Anna and Ben nod. They finish their ice cream and wash their hands. They sit at the table and eat their soup and bread. They feel warm and full. They thank mom and go to rest. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a wild animal that was very lonely. He wandered around in the forest all day, but he never found any other animals. One day he saw a big shadow in the forest and he panicked. He ran as fast as he could away from the scary shadow.

But as he ran, he suddenly found himself in a clearing where he saw lots of animals playing in the sunshine. After that he wasnâ€™t scared anymore, and he realised that he should never panic without knowing what something is.

The animals welcomed him, and he was no longer lonely. From that day on, he was very happy to be part of the group.

The moral of the story is that you should never be afraid of something until you know what it is. Donâ€™t panic!

Once upon a time, there was a big, black dog named Max. Max was very restless because he needed to go for a walk. His owner, a little girl named Lily, saw that Max was feeling sad and decided to take him for a walk. 

As they were walking, Max saw a ball in the park and needed to play with it. Lily threw the ball for Max and he chased it. Max was so happy that he wagged his tail and barked with joy. 

After playing with the ball, Max was tired and needed to rest. Lily took Max home and he fell asleep on his cozy bed. Max dreamed about playing with the ball and felt happy knowing that he had a good day with his best friend, Lily.

Ben and Lily were playing with their wagon in the backyard. They liked to fill it with toys and pretend they were going on a trip. Ben was very organized. He put all the cars in one corner, all the dolls in another, and all the books in the middle. Lily was not so organized. She liked to mix everything up and make funny noises.

"Ben, can I question you something?" Lily asked.

"Sure, what is it?" Ben said.

"Why do you make everything so neat? It is more fun to make a mess!" Lily said.

Ben thought for a moment. He liked to have everything in order. It made him feel calm and happy.

"I like to make everything neat because it helps me find what I want. And it looks nice too. Don't you like to make things nice?" Ben said.

Lily shrugged. She liked to make things fun. She did not care if they were nice or not.

"I like to make things fun because it makes me laugh and have a good time. And it looks funny too. Don't you like to make things funny?" Lily said.

Ben smiled. He liked to make things fun too. He did not mind if they were funny or not.

"I like to make things fun too, sometimes. But not always. Sometimes I like to make things nice. Can we do both?" Ben said.

Lily nodded. She liked to do both too. She did not mind if they were nice or not.

"Okay, we can do both. How about we take turns? You can make things nice, and then I can make things funny. And then we can switch. Does that sound good?" Lily said.

Ben agreed. He liked to take turns. He thought it was fair and kind.

"Okay, that sounds good. Let's do that. You can go first. What do you want to make nice?" Ben said.

Lily looked at the wagon. She saw a red car, a blue doll, and a green book. She had an idea.

"I want to make a rainbow. Watch this!" Lily said.

She took the car, the doll, and the book, and arranged them in a row on the wagon. She added a yellow ball, an orange crayon, and a purple hat. She made a rainbow with the toys.

"Look, Ben, I made a rainbow! Isn't it nice?" Lily said.

Ben looked at the rainbow. He thought it was very nice. He also thought it was very funny.

"Yes, Lily, you made a rainbow. It is very nice. And very funny. Good job!" Ben said.

He clapped his hands and laughed. Lily clapped her hands and laughed too. They were happy. They liked to play with their wagon. They liked to make things nice and funny. They liked to question each other. They liked to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved his toy car with a motor. He would play with it every day and make it go vroom vroom. 

One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy was so proud to show his friend his toy car. His friend liked it too and asked if he could own one too. 

Timmy said yes and they played together with their toy cars. They had so much fun that they didn't even notice it was time for lunch. Timmy's mom called them in and they happily ran inside, still talking about their toy cars.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside, but today it was gloomy and rainy. Timmy was sad because he couldn't play outside. He sat inside and watched the raindrops fall on the window.

Suddenly, Timmy had an idea. He went to get his bucket and filled it with water from the sink. He pretended he was outside in the rain, splashing around with his bucket. Timmy had so much fun, he started to dream about being outside in the sunshine.

The rain stopped and the sun came out. Timmy was so happy! He ran outside with his bucket and played in the puddles. Timmy knew that even when things seem gloomy, there is always a way to have fun and dream about better days.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because she was going on a holiday with her family. They were going to the beach!

When they arrived, Lily saw the big blue ocean and heard the waves crashing. She said, "I hear the ocean! It sounds like music!" 

But after a few days, Lily got bored. She said to her mom, "This is boring. Can we do something fun?" 

Her mom said, "Let's build a sandcastle!" So they built a big sandcastle together. Lily was happy again and said, "This is the best holiday ever!"
