"Please help me restore my magic," she said.

The child was eager to help. "I'll look for the magical items," he said. 

The child and the fairy began their search for magical items. Soon, they found a special bracelet, a sparkling wand and a shiny crown. With these items, the fairy's magic was fully restored! 

The fairy was so happy. "Thank you for your help," she said as she hugged the child. 

The child was so excited. He had helped restore a real fairy's magical powers and that made him happy!

Little Thomas was sad. He had not seen the sunrise yet that day. He really wanted to see it.

Mama knew how much Thomas wanted to see the sunrise so she decided to take him outside. She held his hand and they walked out in the garden.

Thomas was so excited to be outside. He looked up at the sky and saw the most beautiful sunrise he had ever seen! He smiled and was so happy.

Mama showed Thomas the little birds singing in the trees. He smiled and clapped his hands in delight. She also showed him the beautiful colours of the sunrise that spread all across the sky.

Thomas was so happy to have seen the sunrise. He thanked Mama for showing him and she hugged him tightly. The sun was now up in the sky and Thomas knew a new day was here.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a weak old man named Tom. Tom had a big iron, which he used to press his clothes. One day, he needed help with his iron because it was too heavy for him.

Tom went to his friend, Sam, and said, "Sam, please help me with my iron. I am too weak to use it." Sam agreed and said, "Sure, Tom. I will help you." So, Sam went to Tom's house and helped him press his clothes with the iron.

After they were done, Tom thanked Sam and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I am always here to help you." And from that day on, they became the best of friends and always helped each other when they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to her grandma's house because she always had cookies and milk for her. But one day, Lily's little brother spilled milk on the table and made a big mess. 

Grandma got upset and started to quarrel with Lily's brother. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. She remembered her mom telling her to always be helpful, so she went to the kitchen to get a napkin to clean up the mess. 

As she was cleaning, Lily noticed a smelly odor coming from the trash can. She knew that her grandma had forgotten to take out the trash. So, she took the trash out and put a new bag in the can. 

When Grandma saw what Lily had done, she smiled and gave her a big hug. Lily felt happy that she could help and make things better. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be helpful and to keep things clean and tidy.

It was a cold day. The trees were all icy. Kids were outside playing, running and laughing.

In one corner of the playground, a little girl named Emma was drawing in the sand. She was putting patterns and shapes together to design different things.

Suddenly, she saw her friend, Mia, walking towards her. "Hi Mia!" Emma said.

Mia was carrying a big envelope. She said, "I got a surprise for you!"

Emma was so excited that she started jumping. She said, "Let's open it and see what's inside!"

Mia opened the envelope and out came a big icy lolly. Emma was so happy.

She said, "Thanks Mia! I love my surprise!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Pauline. Pauline wanted to fly one day, but she knew that was impossible because she was too heavy. She was embarrassed about her weight and tried to stop eating so much food.

One day, Pauline's mommy decided to help her. She suggested that Pauline go for a walk every day, to help her become lighter. Pauline was happy with this plan and started walking every day.

Soon, she started to feel lighter and happier. She soon found that she had prevented herself from getting any heavier. Pauline was so pleased with herself!

Every day she went for a walk, and she soon found that she had become the lightest she had ever been. She was so proud of herself that she could fly now! She was no longer embarrassed about her weight and did her best to stay healthy and fit.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was walking on the beach one day when she found a beautiful shell. She picked it up and was admiring it when suddenly a big wave came and washed the shell away.

Lucy was very sad and was about to cry, but then she heard a noise behind her. It was something big and it was coming closer! Lucy was scared.

She turned around and saw a dangerous-looking animal. She had never seen anything like it before. It had a big, sharp claw and it was snapping at her. Lucy was so scared that she ran away as fast as she could.

Luckily, she managed to get away from the dangerous animal. But from that day on, Lucy was careful when she went near the shell on the beach. She didn't want to get scared again!

Once upon a time, there was a famous airport. All the people around it knew how famous it was. Everyday, many people would miss the airport, because it was so special.

One day, something bad happened. All the people were running away and leaving the airport. It was a sad moment, because everyone missed the airport so much.

When they were gone, there were only a few people left. The airport had no more visitors. It felt so lonely. Then, people started to forget the airport. Everyone stopped talking about it and the famous airport was forgotten. 

The airport was all alone and it missed the people who used to visit it. It was a bad ending for the airport and all the people who used to miss it.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was troubled. He did not feel happy. He did not know why.

One day he heard a story. This story was about a kind princess. She was kind to everyone. Everyone in the land was happy when she was around.

The boy was interested in the story. He decided to find the princess. He walked and walked until he found her palace.

The princess saw the boy and she smiled. She could tell he was troubled so she asked him what was wrong. The boy told her his story and she listened carefully.

The princess was very kind. She hugged the boy and told him everything would be alright. She showed him around the palace and had fun.

The boy smiled and felt happy. He was no longer troubled. He thanked the princess and went home, happy and content.

Sara was very sad. She had a toy cat that she loved very much. She played with it every day and hugged it at night. But one day, her brother Tom took her toy cat and pulled it very hard. He wanted to see how far it could stretch. He did not care that he was hurting Sara's toy cat.

"Stop it! Stop it!" Sara cried. "You are being terrible! Give me back my toy cat!"

But Tom did not listen. He laughed and pulled harder. He did not see that the toy cat was tearing apart. He did not hear the toy cat make a sad sound. He did not feel Sara's tears on his arm.

Suddenly, the toy cat broke. The stuffing came out and the head fell off. Tom dropped the toy cat and looked at it. He was shocked. He did not mean to break it. He just wanted to have some fun.

Sara ran to the toy cat and picked it up. She sobbed and tried to put it back together. But it was too late. The toy cat was ruined. Sara looked at Tom with anger and sadness.

"You are very bad!" she shouted. "You broke my toy cat! You are not my brother anymore!"

She ran away with the toy cat and locked herself in her room. Tom felt very sorry. He did not know how to fix his mistake. He wished he had not been so terrible. He wished he had not stretched Sara's toy cat. He wished he could make Sara happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Rosie. She loved playing outside and was always so excited to wear her red boots! 
One day, Rosie was playing in the park and when it was time to go home, she couldn't find her boots anywhere. She started to cry, asking everyone if anyone had seen them. Then, a kind old man said he had seen her boots somewhere in the park.

Rosie and the man went to look for the boots. After a few minutes of searching, the man found the boots under a tree - and they were still red!

Rosie was so happy and thanked the old man. She put on the boots and ran home, making sure never to forget them again. 
She still wears her red boots every day, for playing in the park and for other adventures.

Avery was so excited. She had been playing with her puzzle when Mom said it was time for a nap. Avery was very tired, but she did not want to miss out on her wild puzzle.

So Avery thought of a plan. She put the puzzle pieces carefully under her pillow and then crawled into bed. Mom tucked her in and Avery closed her eyes.

She pretended to be asleep, but behind her closed eyes, she was thinking about her wild puzzle. Avery felt the pieces under her pillow and imagined all the wonderful shapes and colors.

Soon, Avery felt her eyes getting heavy and she slowly drifted off to sleep. In her dream, Avery worked on her wild puzzle and solved it in no time. She dreamed of wild animals, shapes and colors.

When she woke up, Avery smiled. She grabbed the puzzle pieces from under her pillow and began to work on it again. It was almost complete and Avery felt wonderful. She continued to work on her wild puzzle until it was finished.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. The bird was very loud and liked to sing all day long. One morning, the sun started to rise and the bird woke up. It looked out of its nest and saw the sun in the sky. The bird started to sing even louder because it was happy. The end.

One day, Dan and his mom went to the store. As they walked around, Dan spotted a bookcase. He quickly started to run!

His mom smiled, and said, "Come join me here. It's okay."

Dan ran over and asked, "What is it?"

His mom said, "It's a bookcase. You can put your books on it." 

Dan thought for a moment, then said, "I want to join!"

His mom gave a slow nod, and said, "Well, okay. Here, take my hand and we'll walk to it together." 

Eventually, they reached the bookcase. Dan looked up and said, "It's really big!"

His mom chuckled and said, "Yes it is. But we'll go slow. We'll figure out how to get it home, okay?" 

Dan smiled and said, "Yes, okay!" So Dan and his mom went slow and carefully carried the bookcase home, already looking forward to all the fun reading they would do together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and loved to explore. Today, Alice wanted to go for a walk in the park. 

Alice grabbed her coat and she went outside with her puppy, Fluffy. In the park, Alice saw a big, green tree and decided to climb it. 

Alice: "Wow! It looks so easy."

Alice easily climbed up to the top of the tree and found a secret hiding spot. Inside the secret spot was a pack of yummy gum!

Alice: "Oh wow! I can have a yummy gum!"

Alice chewed some gum, but she started to get sleepy. She curled up in the tree and fell asleep. When she woke up, the sun was setting and night had come. 

Alice's puppy, Fluffy, was still waiting for her at the bottom of the tree. They both went home and Alice had a great adventure. She thanked the tree for its easy climb and went to bed. 

Alice was so happy and content with her day that night she had the sweetest sleep.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite thing was to jump on their big mattress. They pretended it was a trampoline, a boat, or a castle.

One day, their mom told them she had a surprise for them. She said she had mailed a letter to Santa, and he would send them a gift soon. Tom and Lily were very excited. They wondered what Santa would bring them.

The next week, a big box arrived at their door. Their mom said it was from Santa, and they could open it together. Tom and Lily ran to the box and tore off the paper. Inside, they saw another mattress. It was smaller and thinner than their old one.

"What is this?" Tom asked. "This is not a gift. This is stupid."

Lily agreed. She felt sad and angry. "Why did Santa send us this? We already have a mattress. We don't need another one."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Santa didn't send you this mattress. He sent you something else. This mattress is for your new baby brother, who will come soon. He will sleep in your room with you, and he will need a place to rest. This is his gift from Santa."

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt confused and curious. They had never seen a baby before. They wondered what he would look like, and how he would play with them.

"Can we still jump on our mattress?" Tom asked.

"Of course you can," their mom said. "But you have to be careful and gentle with your baby brother. He is very small and fragile. You have to share your toys and your space with him. He will be your best friend."

Tom and Lily nodded. They decided to give the new mattress a chance. They moved it next to their old one, and made a cozy nest for their baby brother. They hoped he would like it. They also hoped he would like to jump with them, when he was bigger. They thanked Santa for his gift, and waited for their baby brother to come.

Once upon a time there was a daddy. He was a big, strong daddy who had a messy house. He wanted to clean it up, but it was much too big a job. 

So the daddy decided to gather his little one. He said, "You help me clean up this mess, and we'll have a nice time together!". His little one was so excited to help.

So together, the daddy and his little one began to gather the mess. They put toys in the toy box, crayons in the color box, and books in the book shelf. With lots of hard work and laughter, the little one's daddy finished cleaning up the house. 

The daddy and the little one were both very happy. The little one was proud that he had helped his daddy clean and tidy the house. The daddy was proud too, popping bubble wrap with his little one afterwards - it was a job well done!

Once there was a little boy who had a favourite truck that he liked to play with. Every day he would take it with him to the park to show his friends. One day when he went to the park he met a new boy who asked to play with his truck. The little boy was hesitant but he decided to be honest and accept the new boy.

At first, the little boy worried that the new boy might not be kind and careful with his truck. But the new boy said he would be gentle, so the little boy accepted the offer and let him borrow the truck.

The new boy played very nicely with it, and when the time came to go home, he gave back the truck even better than it was before.

The little boy learned an important lesson when the new boy was honest with him. He learned that it is okay to accept help from others, even when it can be scary that things might not work out. Being honest and true will bring great rewards in the end.

Once there was a boy who had a very gifted sister. He wanted to mention her to everyone he met. He knew she was special and he wanted everyone to know it too.

Everyday he brought her up in conversation. Whenever he saw his friends he talked about her. He told them about her cool hobbies, her intelligence and her kind heart.

His sister was thrilled when she found out how much he admired her. She was touched he was so eager to mention her to other people.

The two were closer than ever, and the boy continued to mention his sister to everyone he met. He was so proud and couldn't wait to show her off to the world!

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a broken toy. The toy was very sad. It could not play with the other toys. One day, the toy had an idea. It wanted to gather all the toys and fix them.

The broken toy told all the other toys about its plan. They all agreed to help. They worked together to gather all the broken toys in the village. They wanted to fix them before the sunset.

But as the sun began to set, the toys realized they could not fix all the broken toys in time. The sunset came, and the broken toys were still broken. The toys felt sad that they could not help their friends. The broken toy's plan did not work, and they all went to sleep with heavy hearts.

Lily was a little bird who loved to fly. She liked to soar high in the sky and feel the wind on her wings. She also liked to sing sweet songs to her friends and family.

One day, Lily smelled something yummy. She followed her nose and saw a big pie on a window sill. It was round and brown and had steam coming out of it. Lily thought it was a gift for her. She flew closer and closer to the pie.

But the pie was not for Lily. It was for Mrs. Jones, who had baked it for her husband. She saw Lily trying to take a bite of her pie and shouted, "Shoo, shoo, go away, you naughty bird!" She waved her arms and scared Lily.

Lily was so frightened that she flew away very fast. But she was not careful and hit a branch on a tree. She fell to the ground and hurt her wing. She cried and cried, because her wing was delicate and now it was broken.

Luckily, Lily's friends and family heard her cry and came to help her. They carried her to a safe place and wrapped her wing with a soft cloth. They gave her some seeds and berries to make her feel better. They told her that she should not try to eat pies that belong to people, because they are hot and dangerous. They also told her that she was a good bird and they loved her very much.

Lily learned her lesson and said sorry to Mrs. Jones. She also thanked her friends and family for taking care of her. She hoped that her wing would heal soon, so she could fly and sing again. She also hoped that Mrs. Jones would make another pie, and maybe share a little piece with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to sing and dance. Her dream was to sing at the opera. Lucy was very patient, always waiting for her chance to shine.

One day, Lucy's mom said, "Today we will go to the opera!" Lucy was so excited. When they got there, Lucy saw a big stage. She wanted to sing on that stage. She asked her mom, "Can I sing on the stage, please?" Her mom said, "Not today, Lucy. But if you keep practicing, maybe one day you can."

At the opera, they saw a play about a fire. The fire was big and red, and it burned very bright. Lucy watched the play and thought about how she would sing on that stage one day.

Lucy went home and practiced her singing every day. She was patient and never gave up. And one day, her dream came true. She sang at the opera, and everyone clapped for her. Lucy was so happy, and she knew that being patient had helped her reach her dream.

Sara and Ben are playing in the yard. They see a big hole in the fence. Sara wants to go and look. Ben warns her.

"No, Sara, do not go. Mom said it is bad. There are mean dogs on the other side. They can bite you."

But Sara does not listen. She is curious. She crawls through the hole. Ben follows her. He is scared.

They see a big dog house. There is a sign that says "Beware of Rex". Rex is a big, black dog. He is sleeping on a rag. He looks angry.

Sara and Ben are quiet. They do not want to wake up Rex. They try to go back to the hole. But Rex hears them. He opens his eyes. He growls. He jumps up. He runs after them.

Sara and Ben scream. They run fast. They reach the hole. They crawl through. Rex cannot fit. He barks. He bites the fence.

Sara and Ben are safe. They hug each other. They are sorry. They say to each other.

"We should have listened to Ben. He was right. Rex is mean. We will not go there again."

Mom hears them. She comes out. She sees the hole. She sees Rex. She is angry. She scolds them.

"You are naughty. You did not obey me. You could have been hurt. You are lucky Rex did not catch you. You will not play in the yard for a week. You will stay inside."

Sara and Ben are sad. They cry. They say to Mom.

"We are sorry, Mom. We learned our lesson. We will not do it again."

Mom hugs them. She is still angry. But she loves them. She says to them.

"I love you, Sara and Ben. But you have to be careful. You have to listen to me. And to each other. You have to be good."

Sara and Ben nod. They say to Mom.

"We love you, Mom. We will be good. We will listen to you. And to each other."

Mom smiles. She is cheerful. She says to them.

"Good. Now, let's go inside. And have some cookies."

Once upon a time, there was a panda. He was a very friendly panda and his name was Pete. One day, Pete's mommy said to him, "Pete, you are going to meet someone special today." Pete was very excited.

When he got to the special place, he saw a girl. Her name was Lydia. She was a very nice girl. Lydia and Pete said hello and introduced themselves to each other.

Pete thought Lydia was really nice and he really liked her. He asked her to come and play with him. Lydia said yes!

The two of them had a really nice time together. They played tag and hide and go seek. Lydia even showed Pete a special tight hug. Pete thought the hug was really nice. 

The two of them became the best of friends after their introduction. Every day, they would go to the park and play together until it was time for Pete to go home. It was a tight friendship that lasted for many years.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jenny. She was three years old and loved playing in the park.

One day, Jenny was at the park when it started to rain. She got very wet.

Jenny's mother saw her and ran over to her. She said, "Let's go home and examine the makeup you are wearing."

Jenny happily said, "Okay!" and followed her mum home.

When they got home, Jenny's mother said, "Let's examine your makeup and see if it's still on properly."

Jenny examined it carefully, and found that it was still on, even though she had been out in the rain.

Jenny's mother smiled and said, "Well done. Now, go and find something else to play with."

Jenny smiled and thanked her mother. And she had a wonderful time playing with her toys at home.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy family who owned a purple house. They all lived happily together in this pretty house, until one day a problem happened.

Suddenly, the house started to shake and roll! Everyone inside the house became scared and started to panic. They started running and screaming as the house shook harder and harder.

Finally, it stopped shaking and the family could get out of the house. When they did, they saw that their purple house had moved across the street! They were so scared that all they could do was laugh.

They found out that an old rich man had moved their house from one side of the street to the other side. All the family laughed so much, knowing that everything was now back to being happy and safe. The end.

One day, a happy cat named Tom found a radio. He lay down next to it and listened to fun songs. He liked the music and started to dance. Tom was so happy that he wanted to show his friend, Sam the dog.

Tom went to Sam's house and said, "Sam, come see what I found! It plays fun songs!" Sam came with Tom to see the radio. They both lay down and listened to the music. They were very happy and danced together.

But then, the radio stopped playing music. Tom and Sam were sad. They tried to make it work, but they could not. They lay down next to the radio, not happy anymore. The fun songs were gone, and they missed them.

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Lily. She loved to dance and twirl around in her pretty dress. One day, she went to visit her friend who lived in a big house with lots of toys. Her friend's dad was a wealthy man who had a big knife collection. 

Lily and her friend were playing with dolls when they heard music coming from the living room. They went to see and found the dad dancing with his wife. They looked so happy and free. Lily wanted to dance too, so she started to move her body to the beat. 

Suddenly, the dad stopped and showed them his knife collection. Lily was amazed by how shiny and sharp they were. But she knew that knives were not toys and should only be used by grown-ups. So, she went back to dancing with her friend, feeling grateful for the simple joys in life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she found a big sheet in her house. It was clear and shiny. Lily decided to use the sheet to play hide and seek with her friends.

She hid under the sheet and waited for her friends to find her. They looked everywhere but they couldn't find her. Lily giggled as she heard her friends calling her name. She was happy that the clear sheet helped her hide so well.

Finally, Lily's friends found her under the sheet. They all laughed and played together. Lily was happy that she found the sheet and had so much fun playing with her friends.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were superheroes and villains. Sara was the good superhero and Tom was the bad villain. They ran around the room, making noises and having fun.

But then, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It sounded like a big crash. They stopped playing and looked at each other. They were frightened. What was that noise? They wondered.

They decided to go and see what happened. They held hands and walked slowly to the kitchen. They saw their mom and dad standing by the counter. There was a broken plate on the floor and some food spilled. Their mom and dad looked angry and sad.

"What happened?" Sara asked.

"We had a fight," their mom said. "We were arguing about something and we dropped the plate. We're sorry we scared you."

Sara and Tom felt sorry for their mom and dad. They didn't like to see them fight. They wanted them to be happy and love each other.

They hugged their mom and dad and said, "We love you. Please don't fight. Please unite."

Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them back. They said, "We love you too. You're right. We shouldn't fight. We should unite. We're sorry we made a mess. Let's clean it up together."

They all worked together to clean up the kitchen. Then they went back to the living room. They turned on the screen and watched a funny movie. They laughed and cuddled on the couch. They were happy and united.

"Lucy, I just want to show you a little bit of wonder. Why don't you come with me and we can explore the woods together."

But the fairy remained cheerful and said, "Don't worry, I'm here to protect you. So please, come explore with me and together we will find some peace."

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He liked to travel on his boat. One day, he woke up feeling grumpy. He didn't know why he felt that way. He went to his boat and started to sail. 

As he sailed, he saw many things like fish and birds. He felt a little better. Then, he saw a big whale. The whale was so big that the sailor felt small. The sailor forgot about feeling grumpy and felt happy to see the whale. 

After a while, the sailor went back home. He felt tired but happy he had traveled and saw many things. He went to bed and had good dreams about his adventure on his boat. The end.

Sara was a smart girl who liked to read books and learn new things. She had many books in her room, but she wanted more. She asked her mom and dad to buy her more books, but they said no. They said she had enough books and she should share them with her brother and sister.

Sara was not happy. She did not want to share her books. She thought her brother and sister were not smart enough to read them. She sighed and went to her room. She locked the door and started to read a book about the weather. She liked to learn about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow.

But soon she heard a knock on the door. It was her brother. He said he wanted to read the book about the weather with her. He said he liked to learn about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow too. Sara said no. She said the book was hers and he could not read it. She told him to go away.

Her brother was sad. He sighed and went to his room. He did not have many books, but he had a toy car. He liked to play with his toy car and make it go fast. He thought maybe Sara would like to play with his toy car too. He went to her door again and knocked. He said he wanted to share his toy car with her. He said they could play together and have fun.

Sara said no. She said she did not like toy cars. She said they were boring and silly. She told him to go away again.

Her brother was very sad. He sighed and went to his room. He did not want to play with his toy car alone. He wished Sara would be nice to him and share her books.

But Sara did not care. She kept reading her book about the weather. She thought she was very smart and did not need anyone else.

But then something happened. The weather changed. It started to rain very hard. The rain made a loud noise on the roof and the windows. Sara was scared. She did not like the rain. She wanted it to stop. She wanted to see the sun again.

She ran to her mom and dad. She said she was afraid of the rain. She asked them to make it stop. They said they could not make it stop. They said the rain was part of the weather and they had to wait for it to pass. They said they could read a book or play a game to pass the time.

Sara said she did not want to read a book or play a game. She said she wanted to see the sun. She said she hated the rain. She said she hated the weather.

Her mom and dad looked at her. They said she was not being smart. They said she was being selfish and rude. They said she should be grateful for the books she had and the weather she had. They said she should be kind to her brother and sister and share with them. They said they loved her, but they were disappointed in her.

Sara felt bad. She realized she had been wrong. She realized she had hurt her brother and sister. She realized she had been ungrateful and foolish. She sighed and said she was sorry. She said she wanted to be smart and nice. She said she wanted to share her books and play with her brother and sister. She said she loved them and the weather.

Her mom and dad smiled. They said they were proud of her. They said they forgave her. They said they loved her too. They hugged her and said they would read a book and play a game with her and her brother and sister.

Sara was happy. She ran to her room and opened the door. She saw her brother and sister waiting for her. They had brought their books and toys. They said they wanted to share with her and learn with her and have fun with her. They said they loved her and the weather.

Sara smiled. She said she loved them and the weather too. She said she was sorry for being mean. She said she wanted to be smart and nice. She said she wanted to share her books and play with their toys. She said they were the best brother and sister ever.

They hugged and laughed. They read the book about the weather and played with the toy car. They learned about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow. They had fun and were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she decided to pretend that she was a princess. She put on a sparkly dress and a tiara on her head.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, she saw a beautiful rose. She was curious about it and wanted to touch it. But her mother warned her, "Don't touch the rose, Lily. It has thorns that can hurt you."
