It was a bird singing in a nearby tree. It was the most peaceful sound Joanna had ever heard. She stopped and just stared at the bird. 

The bird was so pretty, with its colorful feathers and its long beak. Joanna felt so relaxed and she was filled with joy. She just wanted to stay and stare at the bird forever. 

But after a while, Joanna knew it was time to go home. She said goodbye to the bird, waved at the field of corn and walked away, feeling so peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear. He was very boring and didn't like to play. One day, a little girl came to visit the bear. She tried to make him smile by telling him funny jokes and silly stories. But the bear just looked at her with a sad face.

The little girl didn't give up. She brought her favorite toy, a colorful ball, and asked the bear to play with her. At first, the bear didn't want to, but then he saw how happy the little girl was. He started to play with her and even smiled a little bit.

From that day on, the bear wasn't boring anymore. He would play with the little girl every time she visited him. And every time they played, the bear would smile a big, happy smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he always had trouble finding them because they were all over the place. One day, Timmy's mom came into his room and said, "Timmy, let's organize your toys so you can find them easily." 

Timmy was excited to organize his toys because he wanted to be smart like his mom. They started by putting all the cars in one pile, all the blocks in another pile, and all the stuffed animals in a third pile. Timmy's mom showed him how to put the toys in their right places, so he could find them when he wanted to play. 

After they finished organizing, Timmy felt proud of himself. He said to his mom, "Look, Mommy! I'm smart like you now!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you are, Timmy. And now you can play with your toys without any trouble finding them." Timmy was happy and played with his toys all day long, knowing exactly where to find them.

Once there was a little girl who lived in a house. She was only three years old, but she was very passionate about her home. Every day she would go outside and run around with her friends. She would laugh and play, and be so filled with joy.

But one day, the little girl noticed something strange. She saw that the other houses around hers were run down and not hopping with the same energy they used to have. She was curious and concerned, but she tried to stay hopeful.

That night she talked to her mom and asked her what was happening with the houses. Her mom explained that many people had been struggling and had to move away. The little girl's heart filled with compassion and she was determined to figure out a way to help.

The next day she gathered her friends together to brainstorm ideas about how to give back to the community. They talked and shared, and finally settled on a plan. They would collect canned goods from their local food bank and then bring them over to the empty houses. They felt filled with hope, knowing that even the little things they do can make a big difference.

The little girl and her friends had started something that was wonderful and compassionate. And they taught all their friends and family that itâ€™s never too late to hope.

Ben was restless. He did not want to nap. He wanted to play with his cars and trucks. But Mom said he had to nap. She put him in his bed and gave him a kiss. She said she would make tuna for lunch. Ben liked tuna.

But Ben did not sleep. He tossed and turned. He kicked his blanket. He looked at his cars and trucks on the shelf. He wanted them. He got out of his bed and tiptoed to the shelf. He reached for his red truck. But it was too high. He stretched and stretched. He lost his balance and fell.

He hit his head on the floor. It hurt. He screamed. He screamed loud. Mom heard him. She ran to his room. She saw him on the floor. She saw the blood on his head. She was scared. She picked him up and hugged him. She said it was okay. She said she would take him to the doctor.

Ben cried. He did not want to go to the doctor. He wanted his red truck. He wanted his tuna. He wanted his mom. He was restless. He screamed.

Ben and Lily were very hot and thirsty. They had been walking in the sand for a long time. They wanted to find water and shade. They saw a big hill in front of them. Ben said, "Maybe there is something good behind the hill. Let's go and see."

They climbed the hill and looked down. They saw a green place with trees and a pond. They ran down the hill and into the green place. They felt happy and cool. They drank some water and ate some fruits. They said, "This is an oasis. It is a new and nice place for us."

But they did not know that someone else lived in the oasis. It was a big and mean lion. He saw Ben and Lily and wanted to eat them. He hid behind a tree and waited for them to come closer. He acted like he was not there.

Ben and Lily saw a big and soft bed of grass. They wanted to rest and sleep. They walked towards the bed of grass. They did not see the lion. The lion got ready to jump on them.

But then they heard a loud roar. It was another lion. He was bigger and stronger than the first lion. He lived on the other side of the oasis. He did not like the first lion. He wanted to chase him away. He ran towards the first lion and attacked him.

Ben and Lily heard the roar and saw the lions. They were scared and ran away. They climbed the hill and looked back. They saw the lions fighting and biting. They said, "The oasis is not a safe place for us. Let's go and find another place." They left the oasis and walked in the sand again. They hoped to find a better place.

The windy day was quiet and still. Little Timmy decided to take a walk. As he walked he found something smelly. It was a box! Curious, he opened it to explore. Suddenly a giant dragon flew out of the box! Timmy was so scared, he stood there and couldn't move.

"RRAAAAAAAAWR!" The dragon bellowed.

"I am here to strike!"

Timmy was so scared, he didn't know what to do. Suddenly he heard a wise old voice. It said,

"Do not be afraid, Timmy. Strike the dragon with your courage."

So Timmy gathered up all his courage and shouted,

"No! You will not strike me!"

The dragon was so surprised. He flew away, never to be seen again.

The windy day was quiet again and Timmy felt proud of his bravery.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Molly. Molly was very brave, so one day she decided she wanted to explore a cave. 

Molly found the cave and she yawned as she looked inside. She was very excited because she knew it was a rare cave. Molly had never seen a cave like this before, and she was eager to find out what was inside. 

Molly shrugged, took a deep breath and entered the cave. She was surprised to find that it was very dark, but she kept exploring and soon she saw something. It was a small sparkling rock. Molly's eyes widened with excitement. She had never seen a rock so rare before. 

Molly was so tired from exploring the cave, so she yawned and decided to take the rare rock home with her. Molly was so happy she had found such a special stone. She thanked the cave for the adventure, and she smiled on her way back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls and running around in the park. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She was having so much fun that she didn't notice her favorite doll was missing.

Lily looked everywhere for her doll, but she couldn't find it. She started to cry and a kind lady asked her what happened. Lily told the lady about her missing doll.

The lady called the police and they came to help. They searched the whole park and found Lily's doll, but it was broken. Lily was very sad and cried even more. The police tried to cheer her up, but it didn't work.

Lily went home with her broken doll and her parents tried to fix it, but it was too broken. Lily was sad for a long time and never went to the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved sunflowers and would always pick them to give to her mom. One day, she saw a modern vase and thought it would look nice with her sunflowers. She begged her mom to buy it for her.

When they got home, Lily put her sunflowers in the modern vase. But she didn't realize that the vase was too heavy for the table. Later that day, the vase fell and broke into tiny pieces. Lily was sad that her vase was gone, but her mom told her that it was a lesson to be careful with things.

The next day, Lily was playing outside when she saw a butterfly. She wanted to catch it, but it flew away. Then, she saw a sunflower and wanted to pick it, but it was frozen. Lily remembered her lesson and knew that she couldn't force things to happen. She decided to leave the sunflower where it was and went back inside to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found a can of gas in his backyard. He thought it looked interesting and decided to play with it.

Suddenly, the gas disappeared and Timmy was confused. He looked around but couldn't see it anywhere. Then, he smelled something disgusting and realized the gas had turned into a bad smell.

Timmy learned that gas can be dangerous and should never be played with. He promised to always ask an adult before touching anything that he doesn't understand.

Once upon a time, there was a big van. The van was very pretty and graceful. It had many colors on it. People liked to look at the van when it went by.

One day, the van wanted to go very fast. It wanted to speed down the road. So, the van went faster and faster. It zoomed by trees and houses. The people who saw the van were very surprised.

But, the van did not see a big rock in the road. The van hit the rock and went boom! The pretty van was not so pretty anymore. The people were sad to see the van all broken. And that is the end of the story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends went to the park to play. They saw a big, tough dog in the park. Timmy's friend said, "That dog looks scary."

Timmy said, "Don't worry. I know what to do. Watch this!" Timmy picked up a stick and threw it far away. The dog ran after the stick and Timmy and his friends were safe.

Later that day, Timmy and his friends saw a big, round spring in the park. Timmy said, "Let's turn the spring and see what happens!" They turned the spring and water came out. Timmy's friends were so happy and they all laughed and played in the water. Timmy was proud that he knew what to do with the dog and the spring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look what I got, Timmy! It's a coin!" said Lily.

"Wow, that's so cool! You're so strong for finding it," replied Timmy.

Lily felt proud of herself for being strong and finding the coin. She decided to save it in her piggy bank at home. From that day on, Lily always looked for coins when she played outside with her friends. She wanted to get more coins and become even stronger.

Once upon a time, a big elephant was walking in the jungle. The elephant was very hungry and was looking for something yummy to eat. Suddenly, he saw a banana tree and went to eat some bananas. 

After the elephant ate the bananas, he felt happy and full. Then, he saw a little boy and said, "Thank you for letting me eat your bananas." The little boy smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Elephant."

The elephant continued to walk through the jungle, feeling happy and satisfied. He saw some other animals and said hello to them. The animals were happy to see the friendly elephant and they played together. The end.

Mama was sad. She said Benny must go to bed. Benny didn't want to sleep. He wanted to play on the lawn outside. So he asked mama with his sad eyes if he could just stay outside for a few minutes, but mama said no.

Mama hugged Benny and he could tell she was sad. He patted her arm and said it was ok. Benny knew he had to sleep, so he said goodbye to the lawn and went inside his bedroom.

Benny snuggled under his covers and thought about the lawn until he was so sleepy, he closed his eyes and soon he was dreaming. In his dreams he played in the lawn, running and laughing until he woke up in the morning. 

Mama was there in the morning, giving Benny a big hug. She said sleep was important and he had to go to bed early the next night too. But Benny smiled and said the lawn was very fun and he was glad he got to dream about it. Mama smiled too and said they could go back to the lawn soon.

Once upon a time, there was a generous blueberry bush. Every day, it would give out blueberries to the people in the town. They were always so happy when the blueberries came! One day, however, something strange happened. All of the blueberries disappeared! Where did they go? Everyone searched for them but no one could find out. Suddenly, it started to rain, and that's when the mystery was solved. It turned out that the generous blueberry bush had hidden all of its blueberries inside the raindrops to keep them safe! And they all lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a man with a big, bushy mustache. He loved his mustache very much and would stroke it all day long. One day, he went outside and it was very cold. The wind was blowing and there was icy snow on the ground. 

The man decided to go inside and make some hot cocoa to warm up. He got out a big pot and added some milk and cocoa powder. He stirred it all together and it started to smell really good. 

As he was pouring the hot cocoa into his mug, he accidentally spilled some on his mustache. It was now covered in brown, chocolaty goodness! He couldn't help but laugh as he licked the hot cocoa off his mustache. From that day on, he always added a little extra cocoa powder to his hot cocoa to make it extra chocolatey. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to a restaurant with her mommy and daddy. When they got there, Lily spilled some juice on her dress. Her mommy gave her a napkin to wipe it off.

After they ate, Lily felt very tired. She asked her mommy if they could go home so she could take a nap. Her mommy said yes and they left the restaurant.

When they got home, Lily's mommy sent her to her room to take a nap. Lily slept for a long time and when she woke up, her face was pale because she was still very tired. But then she remembered that she had a fun day with her mommy and daddy and that made her happy again. The end.

Once there was a smart little boy. He loved to learn new things. So his mom got him a bookcase. He was so excited! He put all of his books in the bookcase and he could easily find them whenever he wanted. 

One day the little boy was very hungry so he went to the kitchen. There was something new on the table to eat. He looked closer and saw that it was a delicious apple. He ate it up and smiled! 

He was feeling full and happy so he thought he should practice being smart. He went back to his bookcase and found one of his books. He read it and felt smarter already. He loved to eat that apple and read his book!

Tim and Jen are friends. They live in a small house on a busy street. Every morning, they wake up early and go to school. They like to learn new things and play with their classmates.

One day, Tim and Jen see a big sign on their way to school. The sign says "Garage Sale". They see many things on the grass: toys, books, clothes, and more. They look at each other and smile. They have some money in their pockets. They want to buy something cheap and fun.

They run to the garage sale and look around. They see a ball, a doll, a car, and a puzzle. They like them all, but they can only buy one thing each. They have to choose.

Tim sees a big teddy bear. He likes teddy bears. He picks it up and hugs it. He asks the lady, "How much for the bear?"

The lady smiles and says, "One dollar. It's very cheap."

Tim is happy. He gives the lady one dollar and takes the bear. He says, "Thank you. I love the bear."

Jen sees a shiny necklace. She likes shiny things. She picks it up and puts it around her neck. She asks the lady, "How much for the necklace?"

The lady frowns and says, "Five dollars. It's very expensive."

Jen is sad. She only has two dollars. She can't buy the necklace. She says, "Sorry. I can't buy the necklace."

She puts it back and looks for something else. She sees a book. She likes books. She picks it up and opens it. She sees pictures and words. She asks the lady, "How much for the book?"

The lady smiles and says, "One dollar. It's very cheap."

Jen is happy. She gives the lady one dollar and takes the book. She says, "Thank you. I love the book."

Tim and Jen are happy. They have bought something cheap and fun. They hug each other and say, "Let's go to school and show our friends."

They run to school with their new things. They don't know that the teddy bear has a hole and the book has a surprise. They will find out soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Timmy saw a bee buzzing around him. He was scared of the bee because he didn't want to get stung. But then, the bee landed on a flower and Timmy saw that it was a brown bee. He thought it was very pretty.

Timmy wanted to know more about the bee, so he asked his mom. His mom told him that bees are very important because they help flowers grow. Timmy was happy to learn something new. From that day on, Timmy wasn't scared of bees anymore. He knew that they were helpful little creatures.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little girl. She liked to go to church. One day, the little girl got dressed in her best clothes and left to go to church with her mommy. 

When they arrived, they opened the door and it was so smelly inside! The little girl didn't like it, so her mommy said it was time to leave. 

The little girl felt sad, but then she had a good idea. She asked her mommy if they could please go to the park. Her mommy said yes, so they left the smelly church and went to the park. 

There were so many fun things to do at the park. The little girl and her mommy had a great time, even better than church! 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a team of animals who wanted to play together. The team had a lion, a zebra, a monkey, and a giraffe. They all loved playing together and having fun. One day, the lion wanted to play a game where he would always be the winner. He was being selfish and didn't think about how the other animals would feel. 

The zebra and the monkey didn't like the lion's game, but they didn't say anything. The giraffe noticed how unhappy the other animals were and decided to speak up. She pointed out that the lion's game was not fair and that they should all have a chance to win. The lion realized that he was being selfish and agreed to change the game. 

From that day on, the team played games that were fair for everyone. They all had fun and enjoyed playing together. The moral of the story is that it's important to think about others and not just yourself. It's always better to be a team player than a selfish one.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big slide and wanted to play. He climbed up and slid down the slide. It was so much fun!

Then, Tim saw a girl named Sue holding a big balloon. "Hi Sue, can I play with your balloon?" he asked. Sue said, "Yes, but be careful. My mommy gave it to me for my birthday." They played with the balloon and had a great time.

Later, they got hungry and went to Tim's house for a snack. Tim's mommy gave them spicy chips. Sue didn't like spicy food, but she didn't want to be rude. She tried the chips and said, "Thank you, but I can't eat spicy food." Tim's mommy understood and gave her a different snack.

The moral of the story is to be honest and kind to others. If you don't like something, it's okay to say so politely.

Jill and Tom were going to a show. They were very happy. They put on their clean clothes and shoes. Mom and Dad drove them to the big hall. There were many people and seats.

"Can we sit in the front?" Jill asked.

"Sorry, honey, those seats are for the VIPs," Dad said.

"What are VIPs?" Tom wondered.

"They are very important people who pay a lot of money to see the show," Mom explained.

Jill and Tom were not very important people, but they did not mind. They found some nice seats in the middle. They waited for the show to start.

Soon, the lights went down and the curtain went up. The show was about a princess and a dragon. The princess was very brave and smart. She tricked the dragon and saved the kingdom. The dragon was very funny and silly. He made everyone laugh.

Jill and Tom liked the show very much. They clapped their hands and cheered. They applauded the princess and the dragon. They also applauded the other actors and the music.

At the end of the show, the princess and the dragon came to the front of the stage. They bowed and smiled. They saw Jill and Tom in the crowd. They waved at them.

"Hey, you two, come here!" the princess called.

Jill and Tom were surprised. They looked at Mom and Dad. Mom and Dad nodded. They got up and walked to the stage.

The princess and the dragon hugged them and gave them flowers. They said they were the best audience ever. They said they wanted to make them VIPs for the day. They invited them to go backstage and see the costumes and props.

Jill and Tom were very happy. They thanked the princess and the dragon. They followed them to the open door behind the curtain. They saw many things and people. They had a lot of fun.

Mom and Dad were very proud. They took pictures and videos. They said it was a very special day. They said they were very lucky to have such wonderful kids.

Once upon a time there was a small, special bird called a laser. He lived all alone in the blue sky and wanted to have a friend to share it all with.

One day he saw a small, colourful bird flying past and shouted, "Hello! Can we be friends?" The bird said, "Yes! Let's be friends!"

They flew high up into the sky and played together. They had so much fun and even made a game to see who could zoom the fastest around the clouds. Laser won every time.

After they had been flying together, they flew back down and Laser thanked the colourful little friend. "I had such a great time!" he said.

The colourful little bird said, "Me, too! I am so happy we are friends. I will come back to see you again soon."

And so they said goodbye, and the laser flew happily off into the blue sky with a big, happy smile on his face.

Once upon a time, in a big blue sea, there lived a clean oyster named Ollie. Ollie loved to play with his friends, the fish and the crabs. They would swim and dance together all day long.

One day, Ollie and his friend, Fifi the fish, were playing a game. They were taking turns hiding and finding each other. Ollie was hiding, and Fifi was looking for him. But Fifi couldn't find Ollie anywhere. She got sad and started to cry.

Ollie heard Fifi crying and came out of his hiding place. "Why are you crying?" asked Ollie. Fifi said, "I couldn't find you, and I thought you were lost." Ollie felt bad for making Fifi cry. "I'm sorry, Fifi. Please forgive me," Ollie said. Fifi smiled and said, "Of course, Ollie. I forgive you. Let's play another game."

So, Ollie and Fifi played a new game and had lots of fun. They were happy and laughed together. From that day on, they always made sure to play games that made both of them happy. And they were the best of friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane was feeling very sad and unhappy. Her best friends comforted her with a hug.

"What's wrong, Jane?" they asked.

"I feel guilty," Jane answered.

Jane's friends were very worried and wanted to help her.

"We can take a walk in the park" one friend said. "The fresh air and oxygen will make you feel better."

So, the three friends went for a walk in the park together. As they walked and talked, Jane began to feel much better. The fresh air made her feel calmer and the oxygen helped her to think more clearly.

When they eventually returned home, Jane smiled. Her friends were happy to see her smile again.

Now, whenever Jane feels guilty, her friends are there to comfort her with a hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Julia. She was very organized and loved to play with her friends. Every day, she would explore the garden behind her house.

One day, while she was playing, she heard a loud scream. She stopped and looked around, but she couldn't see anyone. Suddenly, a fairy appeared out of nowhere.

The fairy said, "You must leave here right now! If you don't, something bad will happen." But Julia was too scared to move. She started to scream.

The fairy shouted, "Hurry! The monster is coming!" With that, she waved her magical wand and disappeared.

As soon as the fairy left, Julia heard a loud roar coming from the forest and the ground began to shake. Suddenly a huge monster appeared. It was too late for Julia. She started to scream but it was too late. The monster snatched Julia and was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went for a walk in the forest with her mom. Suddenly, they saw a big tree that was starting to rot. "Look, Mommy! The tree is getting sick," said Lily. Her mom explained that sometimes trees get old and start to rot, just like people.

As they continued their walk, they came across a mysterious house. "Welcome, travelers!" said a voice from inside. Lily and her mom were surprised but decided to go in. Inside the house, they met a friendly old lady who offered them cookies and tea. "This house is very mysterious," said Lily. "Yes, it is," replied the old lady with a smile.

After their snack, Lily and her mom continued their walk. They talked about the rotting tree and the mysterious house they had just visited. "I love going for walks with you, Mommy," said Lily. "Me too, sweetie," replied her mom. And they continued on their adventure in the forest.

John wanted a skull. He saw one in a shop and it looked really cool. He asked his mom for it but she said no. John felt sad and started to cry. 
 
John went to the woods with his mom and he found a skull. It was heavy and he was very excited. He asked his mom if he could keep it but again she said no. 
 
John was determined to have a skull. He asked his mom if he could make one. She said yes and gave him some clay. He made it with her help and painted it white. 
 
John was very proud of his skull. He wanted to keep it forever. His mom was happy to let him keep it, it made John very happy!

It was a sunny day and a little girl named Ella was playing in the park. All of a sudden, her friend smiled and pointed up at the sky. Ella looked up and saw a kite flying in the air with a long tail. Its colors were bright and beautiful! She was so excited that she hopped up and down.

Next, her friend pointed to a boat which was floating on the river. It had a big sail which was blowing in the wind. Ella felt a bit fearful but she was very curious. She wanted to get closer so she ran down to the riverbanks and watched the boat drift away.

Ellaâ€™s friend pointed out to the sea. She slowly walked over to the edge of the sea and looked out. What she saw made her feel a bit more fearful. A huge ship was sailing off into the distant horizon. Its sails were so big and the water was so deep! Ella couldnâ€™t help but feel a bit scared but she was happy to have such an exciting adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play and discover new things. One day, she found a birdcage in her room. It was big and empty. Lily wanted to find a bird to put in the birdcage.

She went outside and saw a bird in a tree. "Come here, bird," Lily said. The bird flew down and landed on her hand. Lily was so happy! She put the bird in the birdcage and went to show her mom.

"Look, Mommy! I found a bird for the birdcage!" Lily said. But her mommy looked sorry. "Oh, Lily," she said, "that bird needs to be free. It is not happy in the birdcage." Lily didn't want the bird to be unhappy, so she opened the birdcage to let it go. But the bird didn't fly away. It was too late. The bird was not moving anymore. Lily was very sad and sorry for putting the bird in the birdcage.

Mia was going on a trip with her mom and dad. She was very excited to see new places and people. She had her own luggage, a small pink suitcase with wheels and stickers. She wanted to be independent and carry her luggage by herself.

"Can I pull my luggage, Mommy?" she asked.

"Of course, sweetie, but you have to stay close to us and follow the signs," Mommy said.

Mia nodded and grabbed the handle of her suitcase. She felt proud and happy as she walked with her parents to the big airport.

At the airport, there were many people and machines. Mia saw a big belt that moved the luggage to a hole. She wondered where the luggage went.

"Mommy, where is our luggage going?" she asked.

"It's going to the plane, sweetie. We have to accept a ticket from the lady and then we can go to the plane too," Mommy said.

Mia watched as Mommy gave the lady their passports and got some tickets. Then the lady took Mia's suitcase and put it on the belt.

"Bye-bye, luggage!" Mia said.

"Don't worry, sweetie, you'll see your luggage again when we get to our destination," Mommy said.

Mia felt a little sad to see her suitcase go, but she trusted Mommy. She accepted her ticket and held Mommy's hand as they walked to the plane. She was ready for her adventure.

Tim and Jen like to play in the park. They like to run, slide and swing. They also like to look for rocks. They find big rocks, small rocks, round rocks and flat rocks. They put the rocks in a bucket.

One day, they see a fat squirrel in a tree. The squirrel has a nut in its mouth. Tim and Jen want to give the squirrel a rock. They think the squirrel will like it. They pick a shiny rock from the bucket.

Tim says, "I will bring the rock to the squirrel." He holds the rock in his hand. He walks to the tree. He looks up. The squirrel is still there. Tim says, "Hello, squirrel. Do you want a rock?"

The squirrel sees Tim. It sees the rock. It does not like the rock. It thinks the rock is bad. It drops the nut. It makes a loud noise. It runs away.

Tim is sad. He says, "The squirrel does not want the rock. The squirrel is scared of the rock." He drops the rock. He goes back to Jen.

Jen says, "It's OK, Tim. The squirrel likes nuts, not rocks. We can keep the rocks. We can make a rock castle." She smiles. She gives Tim a hug.

Tim and Jen are happy. They use the rocks to make a castle. They play with the castle. They forget about the squirrel. They have fun.

Jack didn't like to keep still. He liked to be busy! So he took a step outside his house and saw something he liked - a playground! He kept walking and soon he was at the playground, where he kept running and jumping. He stepped on the swing and it kept going higher and higher. He felt so happy! He kept playing for hours and was so busy trying lots of different things. By the time he was ready to go home, he was very tired. He kept walking until he reached his house and went inside to have dinner. He was so happy that he had such a busy and fun day!

Once there was a little ant who was feeling very brave. He wanted to go on a great adventure, so he headed outside. As he was walking, he noticed a fierce bear. The ant froze when he saw the bear, and the bear saw the ant too. The ant asked the bear, "Why are you so fierce?".

The bear replied, "I'm fierce because I'm looking for a brave friend to help me on my journey. If you are brave enough to help me, I will be very grateful".

The ant thought about this and decided that he would help the bear on his journey. The two of them travelled together and had a lot of fun. The ant soon learned that the bear was not so fierce after all.

The ant was glad that he was brave enough to help the bear and they both discovered a new adventure together.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old, and full of energy. She loved to run and play, especially with her pup, Charlie.

One day, Lucy had the idea to teach Charlie her special trick. She kneeled down next to him and said, â€˜Charlie, Iâ€™m gonna show you how to be a smart pup.â€™ She held out her foot and said, â€˜Put your heel on my foot, like this.â€™

Charlie tried his best, but he was just too stupid. Lucy said in a loud, clear voice, â€˜Charlie, you need to believe in yourself. You can do this!â€™ Charlie tried again and this time he got his heel on Lucyâ€™s foot.

Lucy clapped and cheered, â€˜You did it, Charlie! You can be so smart, if you just believe in yourself!â€™ 

Charlie wagged his tail in happiness as he and Lucy celebrated their new trick.

Once upon a time, there was a litttle girl. She had black hair and black eyes and she was very brave. She wanted to explore the world.

One day she decided to find a well in the forest. She walked and walked until she finally found it. It was very deep and dark. She wanted to see how deep it was so she decided to throw a rock into the bottom.

The water was so dark that she couldn't see the bottom. She was scared, but she was excited too. She wanted to get to the bottom, so she decided not to quit.

She found a big black handkerchief in her pocket and tied it to a tree trunk. She held onto the end of it and stepped carefully into the well. Lower and lower she went, the handkerchief unwinding until she finally reached the bottom.

But it was dark and scary, and she was beginning to feel scared. She suddenly had the urge to quit and go back up, so she quickly let go of the handkerchief and started climbing back up.

When she reached the top, she was so relieved. She knew she had done the right thing and made the right decision to quit when she did.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a generous man named Tom. He loved to share his toys and food with all his friends. Everyone in the town liked Tom because he was so kind.

One day, a big storm came to the town. The wind started to move things around. Trees fell down, and houses shook. Everyone was scared. Tom wanted to help his friends, but he didn't know how.

Tom thought and thought. Then, he got an idea. He went to each house and asked if they needed help. He moved the fallen trees and fixed the broken things. The people in the town were happy because Tom was so generous. They all worked together to make the town nice again. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old and very excited to go on her first vacation with her family. But when they got to the airport, Lucy realized she had forgotten her passport! 

Everyone was very sad and frustrated. Lucy felt very restless and did not know what to do. Her mum said, "Lucy, I'm so sorry! We will have to go home now."

Lucy was so unhappy. She looked at her mum and said sadly, "I miss my passport". 

Mum felt really bad. She remembered that Lucy's passport was in her little suitcase at home. She took Lucy's hand in hers and said, "Come on, let's go home and get it!"

Lucy smiled and said, "Yay!" The whole family were so happy to finally go on their holiday. They all had a wonderful time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. He had a big collection of them, but his favorite was a mighty red firetruck.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He brought his firetruck with him, but he accidentally left it on a bench. When he returned to look for it, the firetruck was gone.

Timmy searched everywhere for his firetruck, but he couldn't find it. He felt sad and disappointed. Later that day, Timmy's dad found a matchbox firetruck at a store and bought it for him. Timmy was happy to have a new firetruck, but it wasn't as mighty as his old one.

The next day, Timmy went back to the park to play. As he was leaving, he saw a boy playing with his old firetruck. Timmy was happy to see it again, but he was also sad that it wasn't his anymore. He returned home with his new firetruck, but he missed his old one.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her dolls and have tea parties with her stuffed animals. One day, Lily's mom told her it was time for a haircut. Lily didn't want a haircut because she loved her long hair that she could shake back and forth.

But Lily's mom said, "Your hair is getting too long and it's making you hot. You'll feel much better with a nice haircut."

Lily didn't like the sound of that, but she trusted her mom. So, they went to the hair salon and Lily sat in the big chair. The hairdresser started to cut Lily's hair and Lily was nervous. But then, the hairdresser showed Lily how she could shake her new haircut and it made her feel better.

Lily was so happy with her new haircut that she couldn't stop shaking her head and saying, "Thank you, Mom!"

Once upon a time, there was a robot named Max. Max was always very crazy, and he liked to do lots of silly things. One day, the robot decided to gather a bunch of friends. So, Max asked all his friends if they wanted to come along. His friends were scared, because they thought Max was too wild and crazy. But Max promised he would be careful.

The robot and his friends had an amazing time together. They played games, enjoyed music, and went on wild adventures. Max was very happy to have made so many friends!

But one day, Max got very angry. He wanted his friends to join him in doing something extra-crazy. But since his friends were scared, they refused. This made Max really mad, so he flew away.

But no matter how far Max flew, his friends still wouldn't come. He was all alone and very sad. Without his friends, Max realized that being too crazy isn't always best.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved dinosaurs and always played with his toy ones. One day, he went to the park and saw a big dinosaur statue. He was so enthusiastic and ran towards it to touch it. But then, he slipped on a banana peel and fell down. His mom came running to help him up and he felt better. From that day on, Tim was more careful when he ran around.

Once upon a time, there was a tall bear. He had a big fluffy tail. The bear loved to go on adventures. One day he went to the forest to find something new and exciting.

As he was walking, he heard a sound. Something was squeezing his tail. The bear looked around, but he couldn't see what was squeezing his tail. He jumped and looked around to find the culprit. He saw a small rabbit in the bushes.

The bear asked the rabbit why it was squeezing his tail. The rabbit said it was because it was scared. The bear smiled and said it was ok. He asked the rabbit if it wanted to come on an adventure with him. The rabbit hopped up and down with excitement.

The bear and the rabbit had lots of fun exploring the forest. They looked in every bush and every tree. The bear would protect the rabbit if he got scared or hugged his tail if it was shaking. They both made sure to have a very fun and safe adventure. 

When it was time to go home, the bear and the rabbit said goodbye to each other. The bear thought to himself that although using his tail was a bit uncomfortable, he was glad it helped the rabbit feel safe enough to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her carry some groceries from the car. Timmy was scared because the bags were heavy and he didn't want to drop them. 

"Mommy, I'm fearful. I can't carry the weight of the bags," Timmy said.

"It's okay, Timmy. I'll help you. Just keep holding onto the bag and walk slowly," said his mom.

Timmy listened to his mom and was able to carry the bags without dropping them. He felt proud of himself and happy to have helped his mom. From that day on, Timmy learned that he could do things even if they seemed scary at first.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved balloons very much. One day, she went to a party and got a red balloon. She was so happy and played with it all day. 

At night, Lily was feeling very sleepy. She hugged her balloon and went to bed. But in the morning, she woke up and forgot where her balloon was. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. She was sad and cried a little.

But then, Lily's mom found the balloon under her bed. Lily was so happy and hugged her balloon tight. She played with it all day again and never forgot where it was. The end.

One day, a little girl was out in her garden. She looked up at the sky and saw a white nut. It was so bright and shiny! She wondered where it had come from and what it was.

The little girl wanted to touch the nut, so she jumped up and reached out for it. But it was too high in the sky for her to reach. She was disappointed.

Suddenly, a magical light appeared in the sky. It lit up the nut and the garden. The girl was amazed! She asked the light what it was and why it had shown up.

The light said it was there to show her something special. It said the nut was full of wonderful secrets, waiting to be discovered.

The little girl felt excited. She couldn't wait to explore the magical nut! She said a big thank you to the light, and went off to look at the nut up close.

Sara and Ben are playing on the beach. They like to make sand castles and dig holes. They see a big boat in the water. It has a flag and an anchor.

"Look, Ben, a boat!" Sara says. "Let's wave to the people on the boat!"

They wave their hands and shout hello. Some people on the boat wave back and smile. They are happy to see the children.

"Can we go on the boat, Sara?" Ben asks. "I want to see the anchor. It is shiny and heavy."

"No, Ben, we can't go on the boat. It is too far and too big. We have to stay on the beach. Mom and Dad are watching us." Sara says.

They keep playing on the beach. They find some shells and stones. They make a messy pile of them next to their sand castle. They pretend it is their treasure.

"Look, Sara, we have a lot of treasure!" Ben says. "We are rich and brave. We can buy anything we want."

"Yes, Ben, we have a lot of treasure. But we have to share it with Mom and Dad. They are nice and love us." Sara says.

They hug each other and laugh. They are happy to play on the beach. They wave to the boat again. The boat waves back and sails away.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She was only three years old.

On a gloomy day, Lucy was playing in her bedroom when something made her scream. She was so scared!

She looked around the room, and saw a big, old book on the shelf. She didn't know where the book had come from.

Lucy loudly screamed again, but then something strange happened. The book started talking!

"Don't be scared, Lucy," said the book. "I'm a magical book, and I can help you."

Lucy was so happy! She stopped screaming, and the gloomy day suddenly felt bright and happy.

Once there was a little girl named Sue. She was only three years old and always liked to explore and find new things. One day when she was playing, she found some sunglasses in the grass. She picked them up and realize how useful they could be.

Sue tried on the sunglasses and they were the perfect size. She liked how they made everything look yellowish, like the sun was shining brighter. She was so excited that she went running around to show her parents her new discovery. 

They recognized the sunglasses as an old pair that had been lost years ago. They were so surprised to see Sue with them, and even more impressed with how useful she thought they were. 

From that day, Sue always wore her sunglasses when she went outside. They made her feel special, like she had discovered something amazing. She never stopped finding new things that made her day brighter.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest. She saw a sign that said "Beware of the big, scary wolf". Lily felt fearful and wanted to go back home. 

Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Hello, little girl. What's wrong?" It was a wise old owl. Lily told the owl about the sign and the wolf. The owl said, "Don't worry, I can solve this problem. Follow me." 

The owl led Lily to a clearing where the wolf was waiting. The wolf looked scary, but the owl said, "Don't be afraid. The wolf is not so bad. He just wants to be friends." The wolf and Lily became friends and played together. 

The moral of the story is that sometimes things are not as scary as they seem. It's important to face our fears and give others a chance.

One morning, Joe and his dad went to the park. Joe was excited to play football with his dad. His dad brought a ball, but it was too heavy for Joe to carry. His dad said, "Let's weigh it." He found a big rock and put it on one side of the scale. Then he put the ball on the other side, and the rock was heavier. 

Joe said, "Why do we weigh the ball?" 

His dad said, "So we can make sure it's fit for playing." 

They put the ball on the ground and kicked it around. After a while, Joe got tired and his dad said, "Time to go home." 

Joe said, "But I want to play more football!" 

His dad got a smaller ball and said, "This one is lighter, so it won't weigh us down. Let's take it home to play with later." 

Joe was happy and they went home. He knew he would have lots of fun playing with his dad and the football.

Once upon a time there was a powerful dreamer. She wanted to travel the world and see new places. So she got her passport ready and she jumped onto her bed. She jumped high, higher, and even higher. Up, up, up and away she went, high above the clouds and far away. She flew above the seas and oceans and could see all different kinds of lands. She floated across the continents and even saw the sand in the Sahara desert. She was so happy, but the time eventually came for her to go back home. With one final and powerful jump she zipped back like a lightning bolt and landed back in her bed. She kept her passport close to her heart and knew that one day her dream of exploring the world would come true.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane loved to write! She wrote stories and poems every day.

One day Jane wore her new shoes to go for a walk. They had big thick heels. After a while Jane felt very tired, so she sat down to rest.

But when she looked down she noticed that the heel of her shoe was stuck in an icy crack in the sidewalk. Jane tried to pull it out, but it was stuck!

Suddenly Jane remembered a story her grandfather had told her - if you write on icy things with your finger, the ice will melt and you can pull it out.

So Jane took out a pencil and wrote on the icy crack. Sure enough, it started melting! Jane was able to twist and pull the heel of her shoe free.

Jane was so pleased she skipped the rest of the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong castle. In the castle lived a king, a queen, and their little girl. They were very happy and healthy. Every day, they would eat good food, play games, and laugh a lot.

One day, the king said to the queen, "We need to pass the special key to our little girl. It will help her open the secret door in the castle." The queen nodded and smiled. The little girl did not know about the secret door yet, but she would find out soon.

The next day, the king and queen gave the special key to their little girl. They told her, "This key will open a secret door. You will find something very special inside." The little girl was so excited! She ran around the castle, trying to find the secret door. Finally, she found it and opened it with the special key. Inside, she saw a beautiful garden with lots of healthy fruit trees and colorful flowers. She knew this was a magical place where she could play and be happy forever.

Once upon a time there was a bear called Brownie. Brownie was the most playful bear in the forest. He would run and scramble around, always looking for something new to play with.

One summer, Brownie met a duck. The duck chattered away and asked Brownie if he could go and explore the forest together. Brownie thought it sounded like fun and said yes. 

The two of them had a great time playing and exploring the woods. But one day, Brownie got a bit too playful and accidentally stepped on the duck's foot without meaning to. The poor duck was crying and so was Brownie. 

The duck said to Brownie, "You should be more careful, it hurts when you step on me." Brownie, feeling very sorry, said, "I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to hurt you. Please forgive me." The little duck smiled and said, "It's ok, I forgive you." 

The moral of this story is that it's important to forgive others and to be careful when playing so that no one else gets hurt.

There were two friends called Peter and Molly. Peter had a toy truck that he liked playing with. One day, Molly wanted to play too so Peter said she could join.

Molly was very excited and ran over, but as she did, she accidentally bumped the truck and it broke. Peter did not know what to do, but Molly remembered they had an exit to the garden.

Together they went out to the garden where they could play together. Luckily, there were lots of toys available for them to use. They played and laughed together, and Peter forgot all about the broken truck. They had so much fun that they stayed until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie. The birdie lived in a tree. Every day, the birdie would sing and play with its friends. One day, the birdie saw a worm on the ground. The birdie wanted to eat the worm, but the worm was dirty. The birdie knew it needed to clean the worm before eating it. So, the birdie took the worm to a puddle of water and washed it clean.

Later that day, the birdie was flying in the sky when it saw a leaf fall from a tree. The leaf was red and yellow. The birdie thought it looked pretty, so it picked it up with its beak. Suddenly, the birdie saw a cat coming towards it. The birdie got scared and dropped the leaf. The leaf fell to the ground and the birdie flew away.

The next day, the birdie went back to the spot where it dropped the leaf. It saw that the leaf was all crumpled and dead. The birdie felt sad because it liked the leaf so much. But then, the birdie remembered that it had friends to play with and sing with. So, the birdie flew back to its tree and sang a happy song.

Once upon a time, there was a modern tube. It was filled with candy and surprises, and everyone wanted it. But it was guarded by a mean dragon. The dragon roared and was very scary. Everyone was so scared that no one dared go up to the dragon.

Then one day, a brave girl came to the tube. She was determined to get the tube. She asked the dragon nicely if she could have it, but it didn't work. The dragon roared even louder and became more scary.

But the girl wasn't scared. She kept asking the dragon again and again until the dragon finally surrendered. He gave her the tube and she happily ran away with it.

The girl then shared all the goodies in the tube with everyone in the village. Everybody cheered and thanked her for her bravery. The girl smiled and everyone lived happily ever after.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their new toy. It was a big red ambulance that could spin and make noises. They took turns pushing it on the grass and watching it spin around.

"Look, Lily, it's spinning so fast!" Ben said.

"It's so fun, Ben, can I try again?" Lily asked.

"Okay, but be careful, don't let it go too far," Ben said.

Lily pushed the ambulance with all her might and it spun faster and faster. But it also went farther and farther, until it hit a big rock and flew into the air. Lily and Ben gasped as they saw the ambulance crash on the ground and break into pieces.

"Oh no, our ambulance!" Lily cried.

"It's okay, Lily, don't cry, we can fix it," Ben said.

He ran to the ambulance and picked up the pieces. He tried to put them back together, but they didn't fit. The wheels were bent, the siren was broken, and the soft red paint was scratched.

"It's not okay, Ben, it's ruined, we can't fix it," Lily said.

She hugged the ambulance and sobbed. Ben felt sad too. He hugged Lily and the ambulance and said,

"I'm sorry, Lily, it was an accident, I didn't mean to break it. Maybe we can get a new one, or play with something else."

Lily looked at Ben and saw that he was sorry. She wiped her tears and said,

"It's okay, Ben, I'm sorry too, I pushed it too hard. Maybe we can get a new one, or play with something else."

They smiled at each other and put the ambulance in their backpack. They decided to play on the swings instead. They still had fun, even without the ambulance. They learned to be careful with their toys and to share them with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy with a big, brave heart. He loved to explore the world around him and would often go on long adventures with his family.

One day, his family decided to go on a hike through a nearby forest. Everything was calm and peaceful until suddenly, a loud sound filled the air. It was thunder! The boy was terrified and didn't know what to do. He started to shake and cry.

But his family members quickly came to the rescue. They held him tight and told him that it was just thunder and nothing to be scared of. They led him through the forest and stayed close by, comforted him until he was calmed down. 

Gradually, the boy began to feel more brave and the fear that had taken over him slowly disappeared. With his family by his side, he was able to lead himself through the forest and make it out safely. 

This experience taught the young boy a valuable lesson-sometimes life can be a bit frightening, but if you keep a steady and brave heart, you'll eventually make it out okay!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to go camping with his family. They would pack their bags and drive to the woods where they would set up their tent and make a fire. Timmy loved to roast marshmallows and sing songs around the campfire.

One day, Timmy's dad said they couldn't go camping because it was too expensive. Timmy was sad, but he didn't give up hope. He decided to save his money by doing chores around the house. He washed dishes, swept the floor, and even helped his mom with the laundry.

After a while, Timmy had saved enough money to pay for the camping trip himself. He was so proud of himself and couldn't wait to tell his dad. When they arrived at the campsite, Timmy's dad was surprised to see that his son had saved enough money to pay for the trip. Timmy smiled and said, "I told you I could do it. I counted my money and I knew I had enough." Timmy's dad was proud of him and they had the best camping trip ever.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a reliable dog named Spot. Spot was always there to help his friends. One day, his friend, a little cat named Fluffy, had an itch on her back.

Spot saw Fluffy trying to remove the itch, but she could not reach it. Spot wanted to help his friend, so he used his paw to remove the itch for her. Fluffy was very happy and said, "Thank you, Spot!"

From that day on, Spot and Fluffy played together all the time. They knew they could always count on each other. And whenever Fluffy had an itch, she knew her reliable friend Spot would be there to help her remove it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a best friend named Max who lived next door. They loved to play together every day.

One day, Max decided to surprise Lily with an amazing gift. He had found a pretty flower in his garden and wanted to give it to her. When Lily saw the flower, she was so happy and gave Max a big hug.

"Thank you, Max! You are the best friend ever!" said Lily.

Max smiled and said, "I wanted to make you happy because that's what friends do. We always try to make each other happy."

Lily learned that day that being a good friend means doing nice things for each other and making each other happy. She was grateful to have such a wonderful friend like Max.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Ruth. She was three years old and she loved to explore. One day, she was walking around outside in the garden and she saw a big purple bush. She leaned over to look at it, and she saw a big shadow underneath it. She got so excited and wanted to see what was making the shadow. She leaned in closer, and suddenly a big purple bird flew out from underneath! She laughed and chased after it. The bird flew around the garden and Ruth followed it. Finally, the bird flew away and Ruth watched it until it was out of sight. Ruth smiled and imagined being able to fly like the purple bird. She thanked the purple bush and hurried inside. Ruth couldn't wait to tell her mom and dad about the big purple bird!

This is the story of a little dog named Woof. Woof loved playing with his bone. He would chew on it, roll it around and even take it to bed with him. Woofâ€™s bone was very special to him and he valued it more than anything else.

One day, Woof went for a walk and he brought his bone with him. Suddenly, he heard a loud growl. It scared Woof so much that he dropped his bone and ran away as fast as he could.

When Woof returned home, he looked everywhere for his bone but he couldnâ€™t find it. He was so sad to have lost his most prized possession. Woof even looked under the bed, but it was gone.

It was such a scary experience, but Woof eventually stopped worrying and found out that the scariest things can also be the most valuable.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were playing in the garden when suddenly Jack said, "Let's go on a march!"
 Jill was so excited and she said, "Yes, that would be fun!"

So the two friends set off together on their march. They started walking, and then running, but when they got to a lake, Jack said, "Let's stop and sort out the stones and pebbles around the edge". So the two of them did.

But after they had been sorting for a while, Jill started to get anxious. She said to Jack, "This is taking too long. Can we go now?" Jack looked up and said, "Just one more minute."

But time passed and they were still sorting, and Jill felt more and more anxious. She said, "Please, Jack, can we go now?" But still Jack said, "Just another few seconds".

But then suddenly it began to rain, and there was a thunder-storm. Jill and Jack had to run for cover, but Jill was too anxious and she slipped in the mud. Jack tried to help, but he flew onto the ground too. The two friends were both very sad and in the end they had to go home without having a march.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily saw a picture of an otter in a book and she wanted to see one in real life. So, she asked her mommy if they could go on an adventure to search for an otter.

Lily and her mommy packed a picnic and drove to a distant lake. When they arrived, Lily saw lots of ducks and fish, but no otters. She was sad, but her mommy told her to keep looking. Suddenly, Lily saw a cute little otter swimming in the lake! She was so happy and excited that she jumped up and down.

Lily and her mommy watched the otter play in the water for a while, and then they had their picnic. Lily felt so lucky to have seen an otter, and she couldn't wait to tell all her friends about her adventure. From that day on, Lily loved searching for new animals and exploring the world around her.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with toys in the playroom. Tom has a big file with many papers. He likes to draw and write on them. Lily has a modern phone. She likes to talk and answer calls.

One day, Tom and Lily have a fight. Tom wants to play with Lily's phone. He thinks it is fun and shiny. Lily wants to play with Tom's file. She thinks it is colorful and creative. They do not want to share their toys. They yell and pull and push.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the playroom. She sees Tom and Lily fighting. She is not happy. She takes away the phone and the file. She says, "You need to learn to share and be nice. No phone and no file for you today. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Tom and Lily are sad and sorry. They do not like to fight. They do not like to lose their toys. They go to their rooms and think. They miss each other. They want to play again.

They knock on the wall. They say, "I am sorry. I want to be your friend. Can we share and play?" They hear each other. They smile and nod. They hug and make up. They go back to the playroom. They share the phone and the file. They have fun and laugh. Mom sees them. She is happy. She says, "You are good friends. You can have your phone and your file back. But remember to share and be nice." Tom and Lily say, "Thank you, Mom. We will." They hug Mom and play. They are happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong man with a big, strong mustache. He was very proud of his mustache and would comb it every day. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice his mustache had fallen off. He looked and looked but he couldn't find it anywhere. He felt sad because he loved his mustache so much. But then his friends helped him look and they found it in the grass. He was so happy to have his mustache back on his face.

Once there was a clever dog. He loved to joke and make his friends laugh. One day, he and his friends were walking down the street when they saw an automobile. It made a loud sound and all of the friends laughed.

The dog was the most intelligent. He ran up to the car and started waving at the driver. He joked that he wanted a ride, but the driver just shook his head and drove away.

The dog and his friends laughed even harder. Everyone thought that it was very funny. They could all tell that the dog was very intelligent and they all admired him.

The dog and his friends had a lot of fun that day. They laughed and joked until they couldn't laugh anymore. They said goodbye and went their separate ways. That day, the dog's intelligent jokes made everyone happy.

Anna and Ben are best friends. They like to play with their toys, draw pictures and read books. Sometimes they also like to discuss things that they see or hear.

One day, they are playing with their blocks in the living room. They are building a big tower with different colors. Anna picks up a blue block and says, "This is my favorite color. What is your favorite color, Ben?"

Ben thinks for a moment and says, "I like green. It is the color of the grass and the trees. And the frogs. Frogs are funny."

Anna nods and says, "Green is nice too. But I like blue more. It is the color of the sky and the water. And the birds. Birds are pretty."

They keep talking about their favorite colors and why they like them. They are having fun and learning new words.

But soon they start to feel tired. Their eyes are heavy and their mouths are yawning. They look at each other and say, "Maybe we should take a nap."

They agree and put their blocks away. They find their blankets and pillows and lie down on the couch. They snuggle up and close their eyes. They are very cozy and happy.

They have a perfect nap. They dream of blue skies and green grass. And frogs and birds. And their friendship.

Joey was walking in the park when he saw a hurt lip on the ground. He wondered what it was. He bent down and looked closely at it. He touched it and it was soft and round.

Joey wondered what it was doing on the ground. He walked a bit further and saw a little girl who was crying. Joey went up to her. She said that she had fallen down and hurt her lip.

Joey felt sorry for the little girl. He gave her a hug and helped her stand up. He told her that she would be OK and that her lip would soon be better.

The little girl smiled and thanked Joey. Joey smiled back and then went back to exploring the park. He continued to wonder about the little girl's hurt lip.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had a big idea. She wanted to deliver food to her friend, Tom, who lived far away. Mia put the food in a big box and started her journey.

As Mia walked, she saw a big hill. She was tired, but she knew she had to keep going. She walked up the hill and then down the other side. When she got to the bottom, she looked inside the box. The box was empty! All the food was gone.

Mia was sad. She didn't know what to do. She tried to find the food, but it was nowhere. She couldn't deliver the food to Tom. She went back home with the empty box and cried. Tom never got the food, and Mia's big idea didn't work.

Once upon a Sunday, a beautiful little girl with long golden hair went out for a walk. She skipped around in the soft grass with glee, and stopped to look at a cute little bunny hopping by. It was so adorable! She wanted to pick it up, but it scampered away.

The little girl was feeling sad, until she heard a whisper coming from a nearby tree. She looked up and saw a lovely little bird. Its feathers were an array of colours and it sang a sweet song. The little girl was captivated.

The whisper became louder, and the little girl slowly moved towards the tree. As she got closer, she heard the bird whisper, "Hello". She felt so happy! She whispered back, "Hello, Mr. Bird. How are you?". 

The two of them talked and talked, until they were both so giddy that they started to giggle. They had such a wonderful time, until suddenly the sun was setting, and the little girl had to go home. She said her goodbyes to the little bird, feeling the best she had all day. She waved goodbye to Mr. Bird and skipped away, feeling happier than ever.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had a doll, a ball, a car and a bear. She loved her bear the most. She took him everywhere with her. She hugged him, kissed him and talked to him.

One day, Lily's mom said it was time to bathe. Lily did not want to bathe. She wanted to play more. She ran away from her mom and hid under the bed with her bear. Her mom looked for her and called her name. Lily did not answer. She was quiet and still.

But Lily did not know that there was a trap under the bed. It was a mouse trap that her dad had set to catch the mice. Lily's bear touched the trap and it snapped. It hurt the bear's paw and made a loud noise. Lily was scared and upset. She cried out loud and came out from under the bed. Her mom heard her and came to see what was wrong.

She saw Lily and her bear. She saw the trap and the blood. She felt sorry for Lily and her bear. She took them to the bathroom and cleaned the bear's paw. She put a bandage on it and gave it a kiss. She told Lily that the trap was not for her or her bear. It was for the mice that ate the cheese. She said she was sorry and she loved her.

Lily hugged her mom and her bear. She said she was sorry too and she loved them. She said she would bathe now and be a good girl. She said she would be careful and not touch the traps. She said she hoped the mice would not hurt her bear again. Her mom smiled and said she hoped so too. She said they would play more after the bath. Lily nodded and smiled. She was happy and calm. She and her bear went to bathe with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the woods. One day, she was walking by a stream when she felt very thirsty. She looked at the stream and saw the water was clear and clean. She bent down and drank some water.

As she was walking back home, she saw a big, scary bear. The bear looked hungry and ready to attack. Lily was very scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she remembered the stream and the water she drank. She picked up a small rock and threw it into the stream. The bear heard the sound and ran towards the stream to catch the fish.

Lily was safe and happy that she was able to use the stream to protect herself. From that day on, she always made sure to have a drink of water from the stream before going on her adventures in the woods.

Once there was a rabbit who loved to hop. Every morning he hopped around his cozy burrow. One day he saw something shiny on the ground. It was a ticket! He grabbed the ticket and hopped away.

The ticket was for a very special event. The rabbit hopped as fast as he could to get ready. He ran to the event and handed the ticket to a nice lady. She gave him a red ticket and pointed him in another direction. 

The rabbit hopped to the old building. Inside he saw a table with a big bowl in the middle. He hopped closer and saw that the bowl was filled with sour candy. He grabbed one and hopped away, ready to enjoy his treat.

The rabbit was so happy that he hopped all the way back home. He carefully put the ticket in a special spot in his burrow and hopped onto his bed. With a big smile on his face, he fell asleep, dreaming of sour candy!

Maddie and Brynn were best friends. They loved to splash in the ocean and play in the sand. One sunny day Maddie said she had something special to show Brynn. As Brynn followed Maddie, she felt curious and excited.

When they arrived at the beach, Brynn saw a message written on the sand. She gasped and said, "What does it mean?" Maddie waved her hand to the sky, pointing out the birds above. Brynn gasped again, as Maddie said, "It's a message from the sky".

Brynn asked, "What does it mean?" Maddie smiled and said, "It's a message of kindness". Brynn felt a tear come to her eye as Maddie explained, "We must be kind to everyone, no matter what".

Maddie sobbed and said, "Sometimes I'm not very kind and it makes me feel ashamed". Brynn reached out to give Maddie a hug, and Maddie said, "Thanks for understanding". 

Brynn and Maddie stayed at the beach for a long time, looking up at the sky and feeling grateful for the special message.

Patch the rabbit was having a hard time finding somewhere to hide. Everywhere she looked, there were too many cats around. She hopped along, searching for a safe spot, when she heard a friendly voice.

"Hi, Patch!" it said.

Patch looked up to see her friend Ben. He was a kind boy who loved animals.

"I have a spot for you to hide," he said.

Patch followed Ben to his back yard. He showed her his special hideaway. It was a thick patch of tall grass.

"Stay here," said Ben. "It's hard for the cats to find you in here."

Patch hopped into the thick patch of grass and stayed there until she was sure it was safe to come out.

Thank you Ben, she thought. I'm so happy to have found a place to hide.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun.

One day, they see a big truck in the park. The truck is noisy. It makes loud sounds. Vroom, vroom, beep, beep. Lila and Ben are curious. They want to see the truck.

They go near the truck. They see a man. The man is holding a palm. The palm is green and tall. The man is putting the palm in the truck.

"Hello, man," Lila says. "What are you doing with the palm?"

"Hello, kids," the man says. "I am taking the palm to a new place. The palm is too big for the park. It needs more space."

"Can we go with you?" Ben asks. "We want to see the new place."

"Sorry, kids," the man says. "You cannot go with me. The truck is full. And the new place is far. You have to stay in the park. But you can wave goodbye to the palm."

Lila and Ben are sad. They like the palm. They hug the palm. They say goodbye to the palm. They wave to the man and the truck. The truck leaves the park. The truck is noisy. Vroom, vroom, beep, beep.

Lila and Ben look at the empty spot. The spot is where the palm was. The spot is now small and brown. Lila and Ben are sad.

"Let's play," Lila says. "Maybe we can find a new friend in the park."

"OK," Ben says. "Let's play."

They run, jump, slide and swing. They have fun. They end the day with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play in the bushes outside his house. One day, Timmy saw a big, scary bug in the bush. He got scared and tried to run away, but he accidentally broke a branch. 

Timmy felt sad because he didn't mean to break the branch. But then he remembered that his mom told him to be brave and face his fears. So, Timmy took a deep breath and went back to the bush. 

He saw that the bug was actually very small and harmless. Timmy felt brave for facing his fear and he even made a new friend - the little bug. From that day on, Timmy played in the bush with his new friend and never broke any branches again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong truck that worked all day. It was so enthusiastic that everyone smiled when it drove by.

One day, the truck decided to take a break from work and rest near a lake. As it lay in the sun, the truck said a silent prayer.

"Please, let me have a peaceful and happy life," it prayed.

Just then, a nearby 3-year-old child playing with a toy truck noticed the big truck. The child smiled and waved at the truck and the truck waved back.

The little truck and the big truck beeped and chugged, making happy noises all the while. The child knew the truck was praying and they both shared a special moment of peace and joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the snow and build igloos with his dad.

One day, Timmy's dad said to him, "Timmy, let's print some pictures of our igloo so we can show your mom." Timmy thought it was a good idea and they went inside to print the pictures.

As they were printing, Timmy's dad noticed how thoughtful Timmy looked. "What are you thinking about, Timmy?" his dad asked. Timmy replied, "I'm thinking about how much fun we had building our igloo together."

Timmy's dad smiled and gave him a big hug. "I'm glad we made such great memories, Timmy. Let's go build another igloo tomorrow!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. Joe wanted to buy a new toy, but he didn't have enough money. Joe asked his mom what to do.

His mom said, â€œJoe, if you want to buy a toy, you need to save your money.â€ So Joe started saving his money.

Each week, Joe put some pennies in a jar. After a few weeks, Joe had enough money to buy the toy. He was so happy!

He went to the store with his mom and saw the toy. The price was on a sign. It was very big and Joe was scared. His mom asked, â€œDo you think it's worth it?â€

Joe thought about it, and noticed that the toy looked a bit boring. But, he knew it would include lots of fun, so he decided it was worth it. He paid the price and left the store with his new toy.

From then on, Joe always tried to save his money for fun stuff. Nothing was too expensive and boring for Joe, because he knew his money could buy lots of fun!

Once upon a time there was a small dog. He had a clear collar. He liked to use it to go for walks.

One day the dog went for a walk with his collar. It was a sunny day and the dog enjoyed seeing new things. 

Suddenly, the dog saw something sparkly in the grass. He couldn't resist! He used his collar to tug it out. But it was stuck tight!

The small dog used all his might and finally managed to pull it out. It was a shiny charm. The dog put it around his collar. He was so happy!

Now, every time the dog goes for a walk everyone sees his sparkling clear collar.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat oranges, they were her favorite fruit. One day, she found a lucky penny on the ground and was very happy. She put it in her pocket and went to play outside.

While she was playing, she saw a butterfly. She tried to catch it, but it was too fast. Then, she saw a flower and went to smell it. When she came back, she realized she had lost her lucky penny. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it.

Lily was very sad, but then she saw her mom coming. Her mom gave her a big hug and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can find your lucky penny together." They searched and searched until finally, they found it close to a tree. Lily was so happy and felt very lucky. She hugged her mom and ate an orange to celebrate.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Diana. Diana was three years old and was always looking for something fun to do. One day, Diana went out to the backyard with her basket. She wanted to collect things from the trees.

She found a big banana tree and decided to collect some bananas. She reached up to get the bananas but was too small.

So, she shouted loudly for her mom. Her mom came and was so surprised to see Diana. "What are you doing?" asked her mom.

Diana waved her basket and said, "Collecting bananas! Can you help me?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Of course I can help."

So, Diana and her mom worked together to collect all the bananas from the banana tree. After they were done, Diana was so happy! She ran off with her basket, excited to show her dad her collection.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was very polite and every day she said â€œPleaseâ€ and â€œThank youâ€ when asking for things. One day Jane wanted to play with the toys in the cupboard. She asked her mum whether she could climb inside but her mum said no.

Jane really wanted to play with the toys. So when her mum got busy, she decided to climb into the cupboard. Without waiting for an answer she opened the door and went inside. 

Inside the cupboard it was dark and there were creatures living there! Jane was so scared. She quickly tried to get out, but the cupboard door wouldn't open. 

Jane started to scream and cry for help. Eventually her mum heard her cries and opened the cupboard door. Jane was relieved when she got out. Her mum was disappointed that Jane had been so naughty, but was still pleased that she was safe. 

Despite being so polite, Jane learnt her lesson and was careful to never disobey her mumâ€™s wishes again.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the museum with her mom. Lucy was very excited to see all the things inside. Her mom said, "I will explain everything you see, so you can learn a lot today."

In the museum, Lucy saw a big, green dinosaur. She was a little scared, but her mom explained that it was just a big toy. Lucy felt better and wanted to see more. She saw a pretty painting of a girl with a nice dress. Lucy felt envious of the girl's dress and wished she had one like it.

Later, they saw a big door with a sign that said "Surprise Room." Lucy's mom said, "Let's go inside and see what's there." When they went in, Lucy saw a beautiful dress just like the one in the painting! Her mom said, "I knew you would like it, so I got it for you." Lucy was so happy and couldn't wait to wear her new dress.

Once there was a boy. He was called Tim. He wanted to learn something new. He saw a television and went to see what it was. 

He saw pictures and heard strange noises coming from it. Tim was fascinated by it. 

He asked his mom about the television. She told him that he could learn a lot from it by watching. Tim was happy.
