He watched different programs on the television every day. He liked to see the rare scenes and animals on the screen. He learned a lot of new things. 

Tim started enjoying learning new things with the help of the television. He was very happy and this made his parents happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Bob who loved to wander. One hot summer morning, Bob hopped along a path that led to a pine forest. Bob sniffed the air and was so excited! 

When Bob reached the forest, the big pine trees were refreshingly cool and shady. He hopped around the trunks, running and exploring happily. Suddenly, Bob stopped and looked around. He was lost!
 
Bob started to worry. He wondered how he would ever find his way out of the forest. Just then, a friendly starling flew down and landed on a branch next to Bob.

"Excuse me," Bob said. "Can you help me get out of this pine forest?"

The starling smiled, "I sure can! Just follow this path and it will take you home." 

Bob thanked the kind bird and hopped away. He kept his eyes on the path until he reached the other side of the forest. Finally, he made it back home in time for dinner.

Lucy was a 3 year old who loved to write. She had a special pencil and paper, given to her by her mom. One day, she decided to go outside and write. She saw a very tough looking insect. It had bright colors, which made it look even tougher.

Lucy started to write a story about the insect. She wrote about how tough it looked and the colors it had. She practiced her letters and tried to write longer words. 

After some time, she noticed the insect was still there. She looked closely and admired its colors and strength. She even wrote about how hard the insect was working, too. 

When she finished writing, she looked around and noticed the insect was still there. She smiled and waved goodbye to the insect as it flew away.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the pool. Lily can swim very well. Ben is learning to swim. He is persistent. He tries hard every day.

One day, Lily and Ben see a big piece of cheese floating in the pool. They are curious. They want to taste it. They swim towards it.

"Who put cheese in the pool?" Lily asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it fell from the sky," Ben says.

They reach the cheese. They take a bite. It is not cheese. It is soap. It tastes bad. They spit it out.

"Yuck! This is not cheese. This is soap. It makes bubbles in my mouth," Lily says.

"Me too. It is icky. Let's throw it away," Ben says.

They throw the soap out of the pool. They rinse their mouths with water. They laugh.

"That was a silly cheese. It tricked us," Lily says.

"Yes, it did. But we are smart. We know cheese is not soap," Ben says.

They swim away. They have fun. They are happy.

John looked around the big hotel. Everywhere he looked he saw tall walls and long hallways. He couldn't believe his eyes! 
John looked away until he heard something. "Please, follow me," a voice said. He followed the voice and soon came to a very big room. He felt happy knowing he could play here.

John looked out the window. There were lots of colorful cars outside and people walking around. He smiled and said "This is so cool!"

John then ran to the hotel's restaurant. He saw all kinds of food and drinks. His mouth started to water. He asked the waiter, "Can I please have a cookie?" The waiter smiled and said, "Of course!" 

John was so excited to be at the big hotel. He wished he could stay there forever.

One day a young mouse wanted to play a game. He saw a wire on the floor and had an idea. The mouse wanted to hide and have his friends try to find him. He scurried beneath the wire and hid there.

His friends came around to look for him. They looked in the tall grass and behind the logs, but they could not find the mouse. His friends kept looking, but the young mouse stayed hidden beneath the wire.

After a while, the mouse's friends gave up, because they could not find him. But then, the mouse popped out from beneath the wire, and all of his friends were surprised. They were so excited they played the hiding game again and again!

Tina was a 3 year old girl who loved mail. She and her mom would go to the mailbox every day to see if something special had arrived. One morning, when they opened the mailbox, to Tina's surprise, she saw a purple envelope. She was so excited she could hardly contain herself! She hugged the envelop and thanked her Mom for helping her get it. 

Tina couldn't wait to see what was inside. She tore it open and pulled out a beautifully hand-painted purple card that said "Thank You". She thanked her Mom again for helping her get the mail. 

Tina was very happy. She went to show it to her friends. Everyone was so excited that they all wanted to thank her for sharing it with them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play games with his uncle. His uncle was very fun and always made Tim laugh. One day, they played a game to see who could win.

Tim's uncle said, "Let's play a game. If you win, I will buy you a toy from the cheap store." Tim was very excited and wanted to win the game. They played and played, and Tim tried his best to win.

Finally, Tim won the game! He was so happy and proud. His uncle took him to the cheap store and Tim picked out a toy. They went home and played with the toy all day. Tim loved his uncle and the fun times they had together.

Once upon a time there was a little automobile. She was small and shiny, just the right size for a three-year-old. Every day she drove around town and made lots of new friends.

One day she thought it was time to explore the world outside of town. She waved goodbye to her friends and drove off.

After a while, she came to a very big and busy city. Everywhere she looked there were big cars, trucks, buses and motorcycles. She felt a bit scared and lost.

Then she heard a friendly voice. It was a bus driver, who said "Welcome, little automobile. I'm so happy you made it to the city!" 

The little automobile was so pleased to be welcomed. From then on, she was no longer afraid of the city. Everywhere she went, people welcomed her with a smile. 

The little automobile had lots of wonderful adventures in the city. She was very happy and thanked the bus driver for welcoming her.

Once upon a time, there was a fat monster. He was tall and mighty and made children afraid.

One day, a 3 year old girl was walking alone in the forest. Suddenly, she saw the fat monster looking her way. She yelled in surprise and started to run away.

The monster caught up to her. The little girl trembled in fear. But the monster spoke softly.

"Don't worry, I won't hurt you," said the monster.
"Really?" asked the girl.
"Yes, I promise," replied the monster.

The little girl smiled in relief and thanked the monster. The monster winked and disappeared into the shadows.

The little girl told everyone in the village about the friendly fat monster. She shared the monsterâ€™s promise to never hurt anyone. Everyone believed her and were thankful for the generous monster. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. But Tweet was lonely because she had no friends. One day, Tweet saw a big tree with many birds sitting on its branches. Tweet wanted to sit with them and make new friends.

But as Tweet got closer, she saw that the birds were smoking. Tweet didn't like the smoke because it made her cough. She decided not to sit with them and flew away. 

As Tweet continued to fly, she saw a small bush with a little bird sitting on it. The bird looked sad and lonely, just like Tweet. Tweet decided to sit next to the bird and sing a song. The little bird loved the song and started to sing along. Tweet was happy because she made a new friend and wasn't lonely anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Max. Max liked to play in the park with his new friend, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily found a pretty flower and wanted to hold it, but the wind was blowing too hard and she was afraid it would fly away. Max saw that Lily was sad, so he gently picked up the flower in his mouth and brought it over to her. Lily was so happy and gave Max a big hug. She knew that Max was a good dog and that he would always be her friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to take his friend to the beach. The boy asked his mom if he could borrow the car to get to the beach. His mom said yes, so the boy and his friend jumped in the car and drove off. 

The boy drove the car very fast, and soon enough arrived at the beach. The friends got out of the car and had lots of fun. They took off their shoes and ran around on the sand, built sand castles and even put their feet in the water. 

When they were finished playing, the boy said goodbye to his friend and lent him the car to go home. Then the boy walked back home. He was very happy that he was able to lend his friend the car so he could have fun at the beach.

Once upon a time there were two brothers named Billy and Joe. They both loved to explore the outdoors and always looked for adventure. One afternoon, they decided to take a walk in the woods.

Suddenly, something strange happenned. A glowing ball of light started to appear and floated above the trees. Billy and Joe were so amazed!

"We must catch it!" yelled Billy.

But each time the boys tried to get close to the ball, it would vanish! No matter how persistent they were, they were unable to catch it. 

Eventually, they had to give up. Joe said, "Let's go home now, brother. We'll come back another day and search some more." 

Billy and Joe happily returned home that morning, with an exciting secret to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the beach with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went to the beach and Lily saw a mighty wave coming towards her. She got scared and ran to her mommy.

"Mommy, mommy, look at the big wave!" said Lily.

"It's okay, sweetie. Waves are fun. Let's go splash in the water!" said her mommy.

Lily and her mommy went into the water and started splashing around. They laughed and had so much fun. Lily loved the beach and didn't want to leave. But eventually, it was time to go home. As they were leaving, Lily said, "Mommy, can we come back to the beach and splash in the waves again?"

"Of course, we can come back anytime you want!" said her mommy.

And with that, Lily was happy and excited to come back to the beach and play in the waves again.

One day, a little girl named Ava went on an adventure. She went to a place that was very dark and cold. Ava was feeling scared so she closed her eyes and started to pray. She asked God to help her and make her feel better.

Suddenly there was a sound. Ava opened her eyes and saw a skeleton! Ava was still scared but this time she was also curious. She approached the skeleton and noticed it had a clear necklace. She looked closer and saw that it was a magical crystal called the brave heart crystal.

Ava was so excited that she closed her eyes again. She prayed again, this time it was to thank God for helping her on her adventure. When she opened her eyes, the skeleton was gone. She was courageous now and decided to carry on with her adventure. 

Ava never forgot her brave heart crystal. Every time she closed her eyes, she would pray and thank God for the clear necklace that granted her the courage to do anything.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her three-year-old daughter. The mom said to the daughter, "It's almost bedtime, but if you want, we can go to the park before you go to sleep." The daughter said, "Yay!"

So, they went to the park. It was full of noisy children playing games. The mom allowed her daughter to play one of them. She could go down the slide and then eat ice-cream! 

The daughter was so happy! She went down the slide again and again and then she ate a delicious ice-cream cone. She was so excited!

After a few minutes, the mom said, "It's time to go home now." The daughter was sad, but she knew it was almost time for her to go to bed. 

The mother hugged her daughter and said, "I am so proud of you for being such a good girl. As a reward, you can eat ice-cream again tomorrow." The daughter was very happy and she said, "Yay!"

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who lived in the woods. He was a very timid bunny, and he always trembled whenever he heard a strange noise.
One day he hopped to the clearing near his home. He heard a rustling sound and started to tremble again. Suddenly he saw a little fox. The fox smiled at the bunny and asked if he wanted to play.

The bunny was scared at first, but something about the fox's smile made him feel calmer. The bunny smiled back and nodded his head. He started to hop around, and the fox followed. They chased each other around, playing hide and seek and tumbling about in bliss.

The bunny felt so happy he almost forgot about his trembling. He was so pleased that he hopped up to the fox and asked if he could give him a rub. The fox was glad and leaned in while the bunny gave him a big rub on the back.

Then, suddenly, the fox's face changed. He looked sad and started to back away. The bunny was confused and asked him what was wrong. The fox shook his head and said he had to leave. Feeling miserable, the bunny watched as the fox ran away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy had a special thumb; it glowed brightly in the night. Daisy took good care of it, because it was very expensive. 

One morning, Daisy's mom noticed the glowing thumb and asked her, "What is that on your hand, Daisy?"

"It's my thumb!" answered Daisy, beaming.

"It's so beautiful!" said Daisy's mom. "But why is it so special?"

"Because it cost lots of money," Daisy said proudly. 

"I'm sure you take good care of it," her mother replied.

And Daisy did just that. She kept her thumb safe and clean, and she showed it off to everyone who asked. Daisy's special thumb was something she took great care of.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and laugh with her friends. One day, she went to the park and met a boy named Max.

Max said, "Hi, my name is Max. What's your name?"

Lily said, "My name is Lily. Do you want to play with me?"

Max said, "Sure, let's play on the swings!"

After playing for a while, Max said, "I have to go home now. See you later!"

Lily said, "Okay, bye Max. Don't forget to mail me a letter!"

Max said, "I won't forget. Have a good life!"

Lily felt a bitter feeling in her heart when Max left, but she knew she would see him again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved very much. He always said "mine" when someone tried to take it away. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his car.

At the park, Timmy saw a big dog. The dog was very slow and lazy. Timmy thought the dog was cute and wanted to pet him. But when Timmy tried to pet the dog, the dog bit him! 

Timmy cried and cried. His mommy took him to the hospital, but the doctor couldn't make Timmy feel better. Timmy never played with his toy car again because he was too scared to go to the park. The end.

Once upon a time there was an old man. His name was Jack. Jack lived in a small house in the woods. Every day he went out and caught fish. One day, it started to rain. Jack was not scared of the rain. He named it "Cuddles". Cuddles made Jack happy. He smiled and sang as the rain fell. After a while, the rain stopped. All the animals in the woods were happy too. They named the old man Jack the Rain-Maker. From that day onwards, Jack was the happiest man in the whole forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to wear her red vest. She wore it everywhere she went, even when it was hot outside. Her dog, Max, was always loyal to her and followed her around wherever she went. 

One day, Lily and Max went to the park to play. There, they met a kind old man who admired Lily's vest. He told her that red was his favorite color and that he used to wear a vest just like hers when he was young. 

Lily was happy to hear that the man liked her vest and she felt proud to wear it. She thanked him for his kind words and Max wagged his tail happily. From that day on, Lily wore her red vest with even more pride, knowing that someone admired it just like she did.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack who had a very difficult time with math. His mommy tried to help him understand the Math better, but it was still hard for him. 

One day, Jack got mad because he felt like he wasn't making enough progress. He threw his pencil to the ground and shouted in anger. His mommy said, â€œIt's okay, Jack. Don't be upset - math isn't easy.â€

Jack looked at his mom and said, â€œBut I'm trying my best! Why can't I do this?â€ His mommy smiled and said, â€œSometimes it takes a little bit of extra effort, but I know you can do it. You just need to be patient and keep trying. I forgive you for getting angry.â€

Jack was happy that his mommy understood and he felt a bit better. He picked up his pencil and tried again. Although math was still difficult, Jack eventually got it. His patience and extra effort paid off!

Once upon a time there was a lively cat called Max. Every day Max would run around playing and having fun. But after a long day, Max needed to rest.

So Max went to his special spot in the garden, under a big tree. Max turned into a little hanger and hung from the branch of the tree. Max was so comfortable that he closed his eyes and began to rest. 

Max had a great rest, he felt so happy and refreshed. He stayed there for a few hours, until he was ready to wake up and start again. With a little yawn and a stretch, Max hopped off the branch, ready for another lively day!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety lived in a tree on the earth. One day, Tweety was flying in the sky when he saw a big, bad cat. The cat was staring at Tweety with hungry eyes. Tweety felt anxious and scared.

Tweety knew that the cat wanted to eat him, so he flew away as fast as he could. But the cat was very fast too and kept chasing Tweety. Tweety hated the cat for trying to eat him. He wished the cat would leave him alone.

Finally, Tweety found a safe place to hide. He was happy to be away from the cat and back on the earth. From then on, Tweety always made sure to watch out for the cat and stay safe.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys and watch videos. But sometimes they fight over the same video. One day, they both want to watch the video of the funny animals. They grab the video from each other and pull hard. The video breaks in two. Lily and Ben are sad and angry.

"It's your fault!" Lily says to Ben. "You pulled too hard!"

"No, it's your fault!" Ben says to Lily. "You grabbed it first!"

They start to cry and yell. Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the broken video and the twins.

"What happened here?" Mom asks. "Why did you break the video?"

Lily and Ben ignore Mom. They are still mad at each other. They don't want to talk to Mom or to each other.

Mom is not happy. She picks up the broken video and puts it in the trash. She tells Lily and Ben to go to their rooms and think about what they did. She says they can't watch any videos until they say sorry to each other and to her.

Lily and Ben go to their rooms. They sit on their beds and pout. They don't like being alone. They miss watching videos. They miss playing with toys. They miss each other.

After a while, they feel sorry. They realize they were wrong to fight over the video. They realize they were rude to ignore Mom. They want to make up and be friends again.

They get up from their beds and go to the hall. They see each other and smile. They hug and say sorry.

"I'm sorry I broke the video," Lily says.

"I'm sorry I yelled at you," Ben says.

They go to Mom and say sorry to her too. Mom hugs them and says she forgives them. She says she loves them and she is glad they are friends again.

She says they can watch a new video of the funny animals. She says they have to share and be nice to each other.

Lily and Ben agree. They thank Mom and go to the living room. They watch the new video and laugh. They are happy and they don't fight anymore.

Once upon a time, two best friends were playing on a ship. The first friend was very happy and content, while the other was jealous. The jealous friend started to complain. He wished he could have what his friend had. He said he wanted to be happy too. 

But then something magical happened. His friend took his hand and smiled. He said, "If you share what you have, you can be happy too!" Suddenly, the stealing feeling of jealousy vanished. The second friend smiled, understanding what his friend has said. He decided to be generous and share his toys with other children on the ship. 

Everybody was so happy, including the jealous friend. He had learned a valuable lesson and the two friends were now closer than ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very excited because he was going to take a bath. He loved playing with his toy boat and making big splashes in the water. 

"Mom, can I have the soap?" Tim asked. His mom gave him the soap, and he started to make lots of bubbles. But then, he saw a big spider on the wall. Tim began to panic. "Mom, help! There's a spider!" he cried.

His mom came running and saw the spider. But when she tried to catch it, the spider jumped into the water. Tim screamed and jumped out of the tub. The spider swam away, and Tim was too scared to take a bath again.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. They were very excited about the party. Jack had a big red balloon for Jill.

When Jill saw the balloon she was so surprised.
Jack asked her: "Do you like the balloon?"
Jill replied: "I love it so much. Thank you Jack!".

Jack said: "Let's fly it in the garden!". 

So they flew the balloon in the garden and had a lot of fun. But suddenly, a grumpy old cat came out of nowhere. Jack was too scared to do anything and he hid behind Jill.

Jill was brave. She replied: "Go away, cat! We are just playing with the balloon together!"

The cat grumpily meowed and went away. 

After that, Jack and Jill had an even bigger smile on their faces as they flew the balloon together and shouted with joy!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named May. She was a brave, adventurous soul and loved exploring. She had heard stories of a sailor who lived in a small boat on the nearby lake.

So one day, May asked her parents if she could go find the sailor. At first, her parents were unsure and did not allow her to go. But she was persuasive, so they eventually agreed but warned her to be careful.

May excitedly walked to the lake and found the sailor. He was wearing a big coat because it was cold. The sailor welcomed May and let her get into his boat. He told her about his adventures and let her use the oar to try and make the boat sail. Together, May and the sailor sailed around the lake for hours until it got dark.

The sailor sent May home and waved goodbye as she left. May had a wonderful day and thanked her parents for allowing her to go.

John and his grandma went for a walk in the park. They noticed a big tree with a big hole. Grandma said to him, "I think we can peek inside the hole." John was curious and excited. He went closer to the hole and peered inside. 

He saw something shiny. It was a saw! It was very regular and it looked like new. Grandma asked him, "What did you find?" John replied, "I saw a saw!" She smiled and said, "Let's take it home and you can use it for your regular work." 

John was very pleased. He couldn't wait to use the saw and start making things. He thanked Grandma for the nice surprise and they both skipped off happily, holding the saw between them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a fearful boy. He was scared of many things like bugs, loud noises, and the dark. Tim had a toy named Mr. Bear. Mr. Bear was Tim's best friend, and he was not scared of anything.

One day, Tim and Mr. Bear went outside to play. They saw a big tree with a swing attached to it. Tim wanted to go on the swing, but he was scared. Mr. Bear said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will go on the swing with you." Tim felt better with Mr. Bear by his side.

As they were swinging, Tim saw a big bug. He was scared, but Mr. Bear told him not to be afraid. Tim closed his eyes and when he opened them, the bug was gone from his sight. Tim felt brave with Mr. Bear, and they played happily outside all day.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little girl named Lucy. Every night when Lucy went to bed, her mommy would come and whisper to her, "Do you accept love into your bedroom?"

Lucy always smiled and nodded her head yes.

One night, when Lucy's mommy came to whisper to her, Lucy asked, "What is accept?"

Her mommy smiled sweetly and said, "Accepting love means knowing you are loved and accepted no matter what. You can bring love into your bedroom just by accepting it."

Lucy smiled and said, "I accept love into my bedroom."

Her mommy hugged her and said, "That's my brave girl. I love you."

The next morning when Lucy woke up, she felt peaceful and happy, knowing she was loved and accepted. She smiled and rushed off to start her day.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little girl. Her name was Jill. She loved playing with her blanket. She would cuddle it on the sofa and carry it to bed. Everyday, she would send kisses to her blanket.

One night, Jill had a surprise. She was so excited. In the night sky, she saw a big, bright shooting star. She knew that shooting stars made wishes come true. So she wished for something special for her blanket.

Suddenly, the sky lit up with sparkles. A glittery parcel filled with special things fell on her blanket. She opened the parcel and inside she found sparkly ribbons, and beautiful new fabric, and enough stuff to make a whole new blanket. Jill squealed with delight.

She spent all night making her blanket even more special. Whenever she finished, she wrapped it up then sent it a big hug. The next morning, Jill opened the blanket to see a lively, colourful new blanket inside. She said â€œThis is the best birthday present ever!â€, and happily ran off to show it all her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color. One day, she drew a pretty shape with lots of colors. She was so happy with her drawing that she fell asleep and started to dream about it.

In her dream, Lily's shape became a magical creature and started to fly around her room. It was a very fun dream! When she woke up, she wanted to show her drawing to her friends at school. But then she remembered that her friends were very competitive and she didn't want them to make fun of her drawing.

Lily decided to be brave and show her drawing anyway. To her surprise, her friends loved it and thought it was very pretty. They even asked her to teach them how to draw shapes like that. Lily was so happy and proud of herself. From that day on, she never let her fear of being judged stop her from sharing her art with others.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who lived in the cold, snowy forest. The bird was not like the other birds. He had a special song that he sang. Every day he would use his beautiful voice and sing his song.

One day, an icy storm came to the forest. It was so cold that the bird almost couldn't fly! Just as the little bird was getting ready to give up and go home, he heard a familiar voice.

"Little bird, don't worry! I can deliver your song so that everyone in the forest can hear it!" said the voice. It was his best friend, a squirrel. 

The little bird was so happy. He thanked his friend, and the two of them quickly made a plan. The squirrel used his tail to help his friend fly, and in no time, the bird was singing his beautiful song all over the icy forest. Everyone enjoyed hearing his song, and the little bird was so proud of his special delivery. 

The squirrel had given the little bird the perfect gift - the gift of music!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Penny who liked to explore the world.

One day, Penny was walking in the park when she saw something shiny. She leaned over and picked it up - it was a penny!

Penny smiled happily and put the penny in her pocket. She decided to taste it. It was metal and cold, but kind of sweet too.

Suddenly, Penny heard a voice. It was a little boy who came up to her and said, "Why are you tasting that penny?"

Penny was confused and didn't know what to say. After a moment, she simply replied, "I wanted to see what it tasted like!" 

The little boy smiled and said, "That sounds interesting. I think I'll try it too!"

They both tasted the penny. It was cold and sweet, but also a little bit sour. They smiled and laughed and decided to share the penny they had found.

Penny and the little boy shared the penny between them and enjoyed the taste. They were very happy with their discovery, and went off exploring the park together.

One day, a modest bunny named Bob went to the garden. He saw a big cauliflower. He wanted to eat it, but the cauliflower was not good. It had started to rot.

Bob said, "Oh no! I can't eat this cauliflower. What will I do?" A little bug heard Bob and came to help. The bug said, "I can help you fix the cauliflower."

The bug and Bob worked together. They took away the bad part of the cauliflower. Now, the cauliflower was good to eat. Bob was happy and said, "Thank you, little bug!" They became good friends and shared the cauliflower.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy bear who wanted to find some food. He looked and looked but couldn't find anything.

He was feeling very sad, when he spotted a cave. He was hoping he might find something tasty to eat inside.

The bear walked into the cave. "Hello!" he called out.

A little mouse poked his head out. "What do you want?" he asked the bear.

"I'm looking for something to eat," said the bear.

The mouse smiled. "I've got just the thing!" he said, scurrying off into a corner and coming back with some tasty berries.

"Yum!" said the bear as he ate the berries.

The mouse watched as the clumsy bear stumbled around the cave, eating the berries.

When the bear was done, he thanked the mouse for the delicious snack.

"You're welcome," said the mouse. "Come by any time you're hungry!"

The bear smiled and waved goodbye as he walked out of the cave, much happier than when he had arrived.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who loved to cook. She always went to the kitchen to make yummy food for her family. But one day, the mommy got sick and couldn't cook anymore. Her family was sad because they missed the normal food that mommy used to provide.

So, the daddy decided to help. He went to the kitchen and tried to cook like mommy. It was hard, but he did his best. He made a normal meal for his family, and they were happy. They said, "Daddy, you're the best! Thank you for providing us with delicious food."

From that day on, the daddy cooked every day. He learned how to make different dishes and his family loved them all. Even when mommy got better, the daddy still cooked because he loved to provide for his family. And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He didn't know why, but he was so mad. He started to run down the street, gripping a stick in his hand. Suddenly, he felt like he had to use it. He was so angry, so he struck the ground so hard with the stick. Unfortunately, he made a big hole in the ground.

The little boy felt really stupid. He saw a big man walking down the street and he knew he was in trouble. He was so scared that he ran away as fast as he could. 

The man was mad too, so he chased after him. The little boy was so scared, he ran and ran until he found his way home. He was safe and the man was gone. 

The little boy learned his lesson. He knew he should never be so angry and stupid like that again. He never went down that street again. 

The end.

Once there was a noisy march. Little Nathan was very curious to see what was going on. He ran outside and saw all the people marching together. It was very exciting and Nathan thought it was, too! 

When the march got closer and closer to his house, the noise got louder and louder. All the screaming and shouting made Nathan scared. He tried to close the windows to block out the noise, but it was still very loud. 

His mum saw he was upset. She went outside and saw the march. Then she went back inside and comforted Nathan. She told him that the march was peaceful and that the people were just being noisy. 

Eventually, the march moved on and there was peace once again. Nathan was thankful that it didn't disturb his sleep too much. That evening he learned a valuable lesson: sometimes life can be noisy but that it's always best to stay calm and not get too worked up.

Dancer was distant, but not always. Every day, she danced with her friends in the field. The sun shone and the wind blew through her hair.

One day, Dancer was feeling lonely and started to lie down in the grass. Her friends asked if she was okay but she just nodded and smiled.

They kept dancing, but she stayed in the same spot. She felt like she was too far away to join in.

That night, the stars shone brighter than usual. Somehow, the distance between Dancer and her friends seemed smaller. She felt happy again.

The next day, they danced together in the field. All the worries of being distant had disappeared. Everything was perfect.

Lily liked to dance when it rained. She put on her boots and coat and ran outside. She jumped in the puddles and spun around. She felt happy and free.

She saw a bird on the ground. It was not moving. It had wet feathers and closed eyes. Lily felt sad and curious. She bent down and touched the bird. It was cold and stiff.

"Is the bird dead?" she asked her mom, who came out to look for her.

"Yes, sweetie, the bird is dead. It means it can't breathe or fly or sing anymore. It's very sad, but sometimes it happens," her mom said, hugging her.

"Can we help the bird?" Lily asked.

"We can't make the bird alive again, but we can be kind and gentle. We can bury the bird in the garden and say a prayer. We can remember the bird and how it danced in the sky," her mom said.

Lily nodded. She and her mom dug a hole and put the bird in it. They covered it with dirt and flowers. They said thank you to the bird for its beauty and music. They said goodbye to the bird and hoped it was happy in heaven.

Then they went inside and had some hot chocolate. Lily still liked to dance when it rained, but she also liked to watch the birds and listen to their songs. She learned that life was precious and fragile, and that she should be grateful and kind.

Lily and Tom were twins. They liked to play with their toys. One day, they went to the store with Mom. Mom said they could each pick one toy.

Lily saw a small doll with a pink dress. She liked it very much. She took it from the shelf and hugged it. Tom saw a big truck with lights and sounds. He liked it very much. He took it from the shelf and pushed it.

"Look, Mom, I want this doll!" Lily said.

"Look, Mom, I want this truck!" Tom said.

Mom looked at the toys. She said they were too expensive. She said they could only get one toy to share.

Tommy liked to soar in the air. He had a big red kite that he flew with his dad in the park. He felt happy when he saw his kite go up and down and left and right. He liked to make his kite do tricks and loops.

The little girl took a deep breath and she started to feel better. She realized that sometimes it's important to just to stop and take a break, and to listen to your heart.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Dan and John. They liked to do a lot of fun things together.

One day, they decided to go outside and play. They went to the park. John said, "Let's shoot a hoop". Dan nodded and they both ran over to the hoop.

Once upon a time, there was a kitty named Mittens. Mittens liked to play with yarn and chase mice. One day, Mittens saw an ashtray on the table. Mittens thought it looked like a toy and decided to play with it. Mittens stood on her hind legs and reached up to grab the ashtray.

Mittens ran away and hid under the bed. She didn't come out for a long time. When she finally did come out, she saw that her owner had gotten a new kitty. Mittens felt even sadder and knew that she had been replaced. From that day on, Mittens was very lonely and missed her owner very much.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a long, silver pitchfork. Every day, the farmer used it to work in the fields, but one day after he finished, the farmer accidentally left the pitchfork in the field!

The farmer was very worried, so he asked his neighbor, "Would you lend me your pitchfork, so I can finish my work?" 

The neighbor was very nice and said, "Yes, I will lend it to you." 

The farmer was very thankful. He returned the pitchfork the next day and said, "Next time, I will remember to bring my pitchfork with me."

The neighbor nodded and said, "It's important to be prepared, and to be a good neighbor by lending and helping each other. We should all lend a helping hand, just as I did today." 

The moral of the story is that it is important to be prepared, but it is also important to be a good neighbor and lend a helping hand when others are in need!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy and always had a big smile on her face. One day, she went to the candy store with her mom. She saw a jar of sour gummies and said, "Mommy, can we get those?"

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny who loved to play in the field. One day, the bunny met a little girl who was picking flowers. "Hi there!" said the bunny. "Do you want to play with me?" 

"Yes, please!" said the little girl. They played together, hopping and laughing in the field. Suddenly, a big, mean dog came running towards them. The bunny tried to run away, but the dog caught him and bit him. The little girl was very sad and cried a lot. 

The bunny was hurt badly and had to go to the hospital. The little girl visited him every day, but the bunny was too hurt to play anymore. The little girl felt very sorry and wished she could make him better. But the bunny never got better, and one day he died. The little girl was very sad and cried a lot again. Once upon a time, there was a lazy pig who was wallowing in the mud. He enjoyed feeling the mud melt away as he moved around.

One day, he decided he was too hot and needed to cool off. He decided to roll in the mud and felt it start to melt away under him. As the mud melted, he felt cooler and lay there contentedly.

His friends, the cow and the sheep, watched him from a distance. They were very impressed by his lazy behaviour and thought it was a great way to cool off.

Eventually, the sun went down and it got cooler. The lazy pig got up and shook off the mud. He snuggled down with his friends and they went to sleep feeling very content. 

The next day, the pig and his friends returned to the same spot, but the mud had all melted away. They were a bit sad, but knew it would be back soon enough.

Spot was a dog who liked to play with his friends. He had a ball, a bone and a rope. He was happy when he shared his toys with other dogs. But one day, he saw a new dog in the park. The new dog was very tall and had long hair. Spot was afraid of the new dog.

"Who are you?" Spot asked the new dog.

"I am Fluffy. I just moved here with my family. Can I play with you?" Fluffy said.

Spot did not want to play with Fluffy. He thought Fluffy was too big and too different. He wanted to keep his toys for himself. He growled at Fluffy and ran away with his ball, his bone and his rope.

Fluffy was sad. He did not understand why Spot did not like him. He wanted to make friends and have fun. He followed Spot and tried to talk to him.

"Please, Spot, don't be mean. I just want to be your friend. Can I have one of your toys?" Fluffy said.

Spot did not listen to Fluffy. He was angry and scared. He screamed at Fluffy and bit his tail.

"Go away, Fluffy! You are not welcome here! These are my toys and you can't have them!" Spot said.

Fluffy yelped in pain and ran away. He cried and looked for his family. He felt lonely and hurt.

Spot was proud of himself. He thought he had scared Fluffy away. He had his toys and his park. He did not need anyone else. He played with his ball, his bone and his rope. But soon, he got bored. He looked around and saw no other dogs. He had no one to play with. He felt lonely and sad.

He realized he had made a mistake. He had been rude and selfish. He had hurt Fluffy's feelings. He had lost a chance to make a new friend. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He decided to look for Fluffy and apologize. He hoped Fluffy would forgive him and play with him. He learned that being kind and sharing is better than being mean and greedy. He learned that being different is not bad. He learned that everyone needs a friend.

Mummy was at home and feeling a bit dizzy. She decided to organize a nice dinner for everyone! She ran to the kitchen and started humming. She grabbed all the tasty ingredients and mixed them together. Pretty soon, the kitchen smelled delicious!

Tom and Lily are playing in the garden. They have a toy shovel and a bucket. They dig a hole in the dirt. They want to bury something.

"What can we bury?" Tom asks.

Lily looks around. She sees a chicken. The chicken is white and fluffy. It is pecking at the grass.

"Let's bury the chicken!" Lily says.

Tom and Lily run to the chicken. They try to catch it. But the chicken is alert. It sees them coming. It clucks and flaps its wings. It runs away.

"Come back, chicken!" Tom and Lily shout.

The chicken is fast. It dodges and weaves. It hides behind a bush. Tom and Lily follow it. They are having fun.

But then they hear a voice. It is Mom.

"Tom! Lily! What are you doing?" Mom asks.

Tom and Lily stop. They look at Mom. They see her face. She is not happy.

"We are playing bury," Tom says.

"The chicken," Lily says.

Mom gasps. She sees the chicken. The chicken is scared. It clucks and flaps its wings.

"Tom! Lily! That is not a toy! That is a real chicken! You can't bury a real chicken!" Mom says.

Tom and Lily are confused. They don't understand.

"Why not?" Tom asks.

Tom and Lily are sorry. They didn't know. They didn't mean to hurt the chicken.

Mom hugs them. She is not angry. She is glad they are safe.

"It's okay, Tom and Lily. I know you were just playing. But you have to be careful. You have to respect the animals. They are not toys. They are living beings. Do you understand?" Mom says.

Tom and Lily nod. They understand.

"Yes, Mom," Tom says.

"Yes, Mom," Lily says.

Mom smiles. She takes the chicken. She puts it back in the coop. She gives it some corn. The chicken is happy. It clucks and pecks.

Tom and Lily watch. They feel bad. They want to make up with the chicken.

"Can we say sorry to the chicken?" Tom asks.

"Can we pet the chicken?" Lily asks.

Mom nods. She lets them. Tom and Lily go to the coop. They say sorry to the chicken. They pet the chicken. The chicken is calm. It lets them.

Tom and Lily are happy. They have a new friend. They learn a new lesson.

The end.
