Kari was jealous. She wanted to play with the blocks, too. She began to cry.

The other child came over to Kari. "You can play with me," he said. Kari felt much better and was very happy.

The two of them played with the blocks together. They built a tower that was very tall. Kari was so proud of what they had built. 

Mum watched them from a distance and smiled. She said, "I'm so glad you found a friend to play with."

Once there was a boy named Benny. He was three years old and loved to go to school. He would get dressed in the morning, put on his backpack and walk to school. He was always very quiet on the way because he wanted to pay attention and learn.

When Benny got to school, he was so excited to see all his friends! He and his friends would giggle and run around the playground together, but whenever the teacher asked a question they had to be very quiet and listen.

At the end of the school day, Benny's mom would come to pick him up. She would always pay him a compliment, like how smart she thought he was or how quiet he had been during class. Then they would go home together and Benny would tell her all about his day. 

Benny loved going to school and was so excited to learn each day. He was always a very quiet and attentive boy, who always paid attention in class.

Once upon a time, there was a poor missile. The missile's friends would always part, leaving it all alone. One day, a big bird flew in and saw how sad the poor missile was.

The bird said, "Don't be sad, poor missile. I will stay with you and be your friend! I will never part!" 

The missile felt much better and the two of them became the best of friends. Every day, the bird and the missile would fly around together and have lots of fun! 

The missile was so happy to have found a friend and it never had to feel sad and alone again. The poor missile and the kind bird remained friends forever and never parted.

Mum was driving in the car with her little girl. She was looking forward to their vacation.

Mum said to little girl, "We're going to have so much fun on our vacation".

Little girl smiled and said, "Can I drive too?".

Mum laughed and said, "No, sweetie, you're a bit too young to drive yet." 

Little girl pouted and said, "Oh okay."

Mum said, "But I promise it will be a fun and slow drive, okay?".

Little girl smiled and said, "Okay!"

So Mum drove slow and they arrived at their destination, ready to start their vacation.

Every morning, Dad made eggs for breakfast. He cracked the eggs into a bowl and whisked them quickly. Then he poured them into a hot pan and made the eggs sizzle. Then he flipped them over and lightly buttered them. 

Mum loved eating Dad's eggs. She would close her eyes, bite into them and say 'mmmm'. It made Dad very happy. 

One morning, when Mum was feeling very dizzy, Dad made her an extra special egg. He used lots of butter and let the egg fry until it was nice and crispy on the outside. Mum ate the egg and felt better right away. She said, 'Thanks, Dad. You make the best eggs!' Dad smiled and gave her a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect coins. One day, she found a shiny coin on the ground. It was very thin and she was very happy. 

Lily went to her friend, Timmy, to show him her special coin. "Look, Timmy! I found a shiny coin!" she said. Timmy nodded his head and said, "Wow, that's so cool!" 

Lily and Timmy decided to go to the store to buy some candy with the coin. They walked to the candy aisle and picked out their favorite sweets. When they got to the cashier, Lily handed the thin coin to the lady. The lady smiled and said, "Thank you, sweetie!" 

Lily and Timmy walked out of the store, holding their candy. "That was fun, let's do it again sometime," said Timmy. Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, let's find more coins!" And they walked away, happy and content with their treasure.

Once upon a time there was a famous little sailboat. It liked to go on adventures in the big blue sea. One day, the sailboat poked its head out of the water and looked around. It saw a big school of fish swimming by and wanted to follow them. The sailboat waited for the fish to swim closer. Then, it carefully poked its head into the school of fish and made friends. The fish showed the sailboat all around the ocean, from the warm shallow waters to the deep, dark cool waters full of treasure. The sailboat made lots of new friends that day and soon it was the most famous sailboat in the sea!

Once upon a time, there was a bunny who liked to explore. He saw an open door one day and decided to go in. Inside, there was a weird seat that he had never seen before. He hopped onto it and saw a bright light! The bunny was so excited for what he might find!

He put his paws up to the light and opened it. He peeked inside, and to his surprise, he found a basket of treats! The bunny couldn't believe it! He grabbed a snack and jumped off the weird seat.

The bunny was so excited to share the treats with his friends. He hopped out of the room and opened the door. Then he hopped away with his basket of snacks. The end.

Jack and Jane were playing a game. They were running around trying to catch each other. They were laughing and having fun. Suddenly, Jack stumbled and fell down.

Jack looked a little sad. Jane quickly said, "It's ok! Don't worry."

"What kind of game do you want to play next?" she asked.

Jack thought for a bit and then he said, "Let's play hide-and-seek. That's an easy game and I like it."

So, they started to play hide-and-seek. Jane hid first, but then Jack couldn't find her. He stumbled all around the house, trying to find Jane, but he couldn't locate her.

Finally, Jane jumped out from behind the sofa and yelled, "I'm here!"

Jack started laughing. Jane said, "Let's play again. We can play it as many times as you want!"

Jack smiled and then shouted, "Yes! Let's do it!"

They had lots of fun playing hide-and-seek and then playing even more games. Jack and Jane had a happy day together.

Once upon a time, there was a poor girl. She was looking for something but she didn't know what. So she searched and searched every day for weeks. Until one day, she stumbled across a plate! She was so excited that she had found it. She decided to take it back home to show her parents. When she got home, she showed the plate to her parents. They were so happy and proud of her for finding a plate! The plate helped their poor family by giving them something to eat their food on. From then on, the poor girl enjoyed searching for new things every day. She never knew what she would find but that was the fun of it. 

The end!

Mia was a chubby baby who loved to chew on everything. She chewed on her toys, her blanket, her fingers and even her hair. She liked to make loud noises with her mouth and teeth.

One day, Mia saw a bottle on the table. It was shiny and red and had a funny shape. She crawled over to the bottle and grabbed it with her hands. She put the bottle in her mouth and tried to chew on it. But the bottle was hard and smooth and did not taste good. Mia made a face and spat out the bottle.

"Hey, that's my bottle!" said Ben, who was Mia's big brother. He ran over to the table and took the bottle from Mia. "You can't chew on that, it's not for babies. It's for blowing bubbles!"

Ben showed Mia how to blow bubbles with the bottle. He squeezed the bottle and made a lot of tiny bubbles come out. The bubbles were shiny and colorful and floated in the air. Mia clapped her hands and laughed. She wanted to blow bubbles too.

"Can I try?" she asked Ben.

"Okay, but be careful," said Ben. He gave the bottle back to Mia and helped her hold it. He told her to blow gently and not to chew. Mia followed his instructions and blew a big bubble. She was very happy and proud. She blew another bubble and another. She forgot about chewing and enjoyed the bubbles with Ben.

One day, 2 friends were playing near a line. The line was very long and tough. The friends were smiling and having fun. Suddenly, they saw a large gust of wind. The gust of wind was so strong that it separated the line! The friends had never seen anything like it before.

The friends looked around trying to figure out what to do. Then, they realized that they needed to put the line back together. They worked together and pulled really hard. It took them a long time, but eventually they got the line back to the way it was before.

The friends smiled at each other and hugged. They were so proud of themselves. They had worked together and shown that even tough lines can be separated and put back together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and twirl around in her room. One day, she saw a black dancer on TV and wanted to be just like her.

Lily went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, I want to be a dancer like the black lady on TV." Her mommy smiled and said, "Of course, you can be a dancer too! Let's spread out a blanket and have a dance party in the park."

So, they went to the park and spread out the blanket. Lily danced and twirled around while her mommy clapped and cheered. Suddenly, a little boy came up to them and said, "I want to dance too!"

Lily smiled and said, "Come dance with us!" They all danced together and had so much fun. From that day on, Lily knew that she could be any kind of dancer she wanted to be, even a black dancer like the one on TV.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she always had trouble putting them away on the shelf. One day, her mom asked her to clean up her toys and put them on the shelf. Lily didn't want to do it because she was being stubborn.

Her mom said, "Lily, if you don't clean up your toys, you won't be able to find them later. Let's measure how much time it takes to clean up and put them on the shelf." Lily didn't like to measure things, but she knew it was important to clean up her toys.

So, Lily started to clean up her toys and put them on the shelf. It took her only a few minutes to finish. Her mom said, "Wow, Lily! You did a great job. Now you can find your toys easily and play with them again. Remember, it's important to clean up after ourselves and put things on the shelf."

Lily learned her lesson and promised to clean up her toys every time she played with them. From that day on, Lily always put her toys on the shelf and never had trouble finding them again.

Once upon a time, there was a family who lived in a big house. They loved each other very much and always played together. One day, they went to the park to have a picnic. While they were eating, they saw a scary spider. 

The little boy said, "I wonder if the spider is friendly or scary." 

His mom said, "It's okay to be scared, but we shouldn't judge things by their looks. Maybe the spider is just trying to say hello." 

So the family decided to say hello to the spider. They saw that it was a friendly spider and they weren't scared anymore. They learned that sometimes things that seem scary can actually be nice. 

From that day on, the family always remembered to be kind to everyone, even if they looked scary.

Once upon a time, there was a parrot named Polly. Polly was very confused because she didn't know where her nest was. She flew around the jungle asking all the animals if they knew where her nest was, but nobody knew.

One day, Polly met a monkey named Max. Max asked Polly what was wrong, and Polly told him she was confused because she couldn't find her nest. Max said he knew where her nest was and offered to show her.

Polly was so happy and grateful that she gave Max a big hug. But then, Max slapped Polly on the back and said, "I was just joking, I don't know where your nest is." Polly was very sad and flew away.

The moral of the story is that it's not nice to play tricks on others, especially when they're asking for help.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big cooler near a bench. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's guess what's in the cooler," Lily said. "Maybe it's ice cream or cake or juice."

"Or maybe it's something else," Ben said. "Maybe it's a surprise or a toy or a pet."

They ran to the cooler and opened the lid. They were surprised by what they saw. It was a swan!

The swan was white and fluffy and graceful. It looked at them with its black eyes and made a soft sound. It was not angry or scared. It was calm and friendly.

"Wow, it's a swan!" Lily said. "How did it get in the cooler?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe someone put it there to keep it safe or to take it somewhere."

They heard a voice behind them. It was a man with a hat and a badge. He was smiling and holding a net.

"Hello, kids," he said. "I see you found my swan. I'm sorry for leaving it in the cooler. I'm a wildlife rescuer and I was taking it to a lake where it can live happily. It was injured by a car and I fixed it. The cooler was to keep it cool and comfortable."

"Can we pet it?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can," the man said. "But be gentle and quiet. It's a wild animal and it needs some space."

Lily and Ben petted the swan softly. It felt soft and warm. They thanked the man for saving the swan and letting them see it.

They watched as the man took the swan to his truck and drove away. They waved goodbye to the swan and hoped it would be happy in the lake.

They went back to playing in the park. They had a lot of fun and learned something new. They never forgot the day they guessed what was in the cooler.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a popular boy in his school. He had many friends who liked to play with him. Tim was nice and never teased anyone.

One Tuesday, Tim and his friends were playing in the park. They saw a new boy sitting alone. Tim went to the new boy and said, "Hi, I'm Tim. Do you want to play with us?" The new boy smiled and said, "Yes, thank you!"

As they played, one of Tim's friends started to tease the new boy. Tim said, "Stop teasing him. We should be nice to our new friend." Tim's friend said sorry, and they all played happily together. The new boy was happy to have nice friends like Tim, and they all had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Candice. She had big brown eyes and liked to wear dresses. Candice was cheerful and always had a smile on her face.

One day, Candice had a nightmare. She felt scared and sad and her stomach was in knots. She peeped out of the bedroom window, feeling afraid. 

Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Hello Candice, don't be scared." It was her daddy. He said, "don't worry, I'm here with you."

Candice smiled and felt a little better. Her daddy sat next to her and told her funny stories until the nightmare was gone. 

Candice felt safe and was no longer sad. She thanked her daddy and they hugged each other. 

The End!

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to build towers and castles with their blocks and dolls. They were having fun, but they also had to be careful. Their toys were fragile, and they could break if they threw them or dropped them.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. It was the wind, and it was very strong. It made the trees bend and the windows shake. Lily and Max looked at each other, scared. They heard their mom yell from the kitchen.

"Lily! Max! Come here, quick! There is a hurricane coming!"

A hurricane was a big storm with lots of wind and rain. It could be very dangerous, and it could hurt people and houses. Lily and Max ran to their mom, holding their toys. They did not want to leave them behind.

"Mom, what is a hurricane?" Lily asked.

"It's a bad weather that we have to stay away from. We have to go to the basement, where it's safe. Bring your toys, but don't drop them. They are fragile, remember?" Mom said.

"OK, mom. We will be careful." Max said.

They followed their mom to the basement, where they had some candles and blankets. They waited for the hurricane to pass, hoping that their house and their toys would be OK. They hugged each other and their mom, and tried to be brave.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red hero. He was very strong and brave. Everyone loved him because he always helped people when they needed it.

One day, a little girl was lost in the woods. She was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, she noticed the big, red hero coming towards her. He picked her up and carried her back to her family.

The little girl was so happy and grateful to the hero. She gave him a big hug and said thank you. From that day on, the hero became even more famous and loved by everyone in the town.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tom. Tom had a problem. His bike was broken and it wouldn't move. One day, Tom asked his dad for help. His dad said "We can fix it. I will teach you how."

Tom and his dad went outside to fix the bike. Tom wanted to do it, but his dad said "Let me show you how to repair it."

Tom watched his dad work, and eventually the bike was fixed. Tom's dad said "Now tell me what you learned?" 

Tom explained, "We have to take the bike apart and fix each piece. That will make it work again." 

His dad said, "That is right! Fixing things is important work." He gave Tom a big smile and a big hug.

Tom felt happy and proud. It was a miserable day when the bike was broken, but now it was better. Tom said, "Thank you for helping me learn to repair things. I love it!"

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Tilly. Tilly was very weak and couldn't run fast like the other mice. One day, Tilly got lost in a big maze. She didn't know how to get out and was feeling very scared. Suddenly, she heard some music and followed the sound until she found a group of friendly animals dancing. Tilly decided to join in and dance too. While she was dancing, she realized that she had found the way out of the maze. From that day on, Tilly wasn't afraid anymore and loved to dance with her new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his spinning top. He would spin it and watch it go round and round. Timmy thought it was the best toy ever.

One day, Timmy's little sister came into the room and started making noise. Timmy wanted her to be quiet so he could play with his top. He thought if he yelled at her, she would stop making noise.

But instead, his sister got scared and knocked over Timmy's top. It broke into tiny pieces. Timmy was very sad. He didn't think yelling was a good idea anymore.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very proud. She wanted to unlock something special. Every day she went outside looking for an acorn. One day, she found one! She was so happy that she wanted to unlock the acorn. 
She ran to the house and found a big key. She then used the key to unlock the acorn.
When she opened it, something very special happened. Out of the acorn came a bright light! It was a special surprise! The little girl was so excited and very proud. She had unlocked something amazing!
From then on, the little girl always kept her acorn close by, so she could unlock its magic whenever she wanted.

Once, there was a little girl called Tara. One day, her parents said she could pay for a scooter. Tara got very excited and could hardly wait to get her scooter.

Tara went with her parents to the shop. The shopkeeper told her she could pick a pink scooter or a green scooter. Tara chose the green one. Her parents paid the shopkeeper and Tara was so happy to have her own scooter.

At home, Tara went to the garden to find a hidden spot to keep her scooter. She found a spot behind some plants and there she kept her scooter safe.

Every day, Tara took out her scooter and rode it around her house. She felt so proud! She was very happy with her hidden little scooter.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Bob. Bob loved to sing. He had a big dream to sing on a stage. Bob had a friend named Cat. Cat was purple and liked to listen to Bob sing.

One day, Bob said to Cat, "I want to sing on a stage!" Cat said, "Yes, let's find a stage for you to sing on!" So, Bob and Cat went to find a stage. They found a big stage in the park.

Bob was very happy. He jumped on the stage and started to sing. People came to listen to Bob. But then, a big wind came. The wind blew Bob off the stage. Bob was sad and cried. The people left, and Bob could not sing on the stage anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a rich family. The family had a lot of money which they kept in a big can. One day, the little boy, called Tony, asked his father, "Can I take some of the money out?". His father replied, "No, Tony. You must save the money for something very special!".

Suddenly, Tony had an amazing idea; he wanted to buy a special tire for his bike. So, he asked his mother for some money. His mother hesitated for a bit, but then she gave him five coins. Tony smiled and rushed out of the house with excitement.

He came to the store and bought the tire. Then he zipped around his neighbourhood, faster than ever before! Tony felt very proud and happy. Everyone in the neighbourhood was surprised to see how fast he was zipping around on his bike.

After that, Tony put the money back in the big can, just like his father said. He was so proud of himself and he knew that he could zip faster and faster with his new tire.

Once upon a time, there was a big ship that sailed on the sea. The ship was very big and had many rooms. One day, a little boy went to the ship to see if there was a room available for him to stay. The captain of the ship said yes and showed the boy a room.

The boy was very happy and he ran to his room. He saw that there was a big window in his room and he could see the sea. He felt like he could spring from his bed and jump into the sea. But the captain said he couldn't do that because it was dangerous.

The boy stayed on the ship for many days and he had a lot of fun. He played with the other children on the ship and learned about the sea. He saw dolphins springing out of the water and he saw big whales swimming. When it was time to leave, the boy was sad but he was happy that he had a great adventure on the ship.

Once there was a bald man who wanted to sell his cactus. He went to the marketplace to find a buyer. He saw a little girl and asked her if she wanted to buy his cactus. She liked it very much, so she gave him some money and took the cactus away.

The man was very happy. He went to the shops to buy a new hat. He wanted a hat with a big brim that stopped the sun from getting in his eyes. He found a nice one and bought it.

The man wore the new hat everyday and always smiled when he saw his cactus in the little girlâ€™s window. He knew that it was in a safe and happy place. He loved seeing his cactus in its new home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big closet in her room. One night, Lily heard a noise coming from her closet. She was scared, so she called out, "Mommy, I'm scared! Can you check my closet?" 

Her mommy came in and said, "There's nothing in your closet, Lily. You can trust me." Lily felt better and went back to sleep. 

The next day, Lily's mommy noticed that Lily had a guilty look on her face. "What's wrong, Lily?" she asked. 

Lily said, "I'm sorry, mommy. I made a mess in my closet and I didn't want to tell you." Her mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You can always tell me the truth. Let's clean up the mess together." 

From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to trust her mommy and to always tell the truth, even if she feels guilty.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved summer. He loved to go outside and play in the sun, and he never wanted it to get dark.

One day, he found a baby bird who was all alone. He wanted to help it, so he decided to feed it. He found some worms for it to eat and he felt happy he was helping.

But then it started to get dark and the little boy wanted to go home and eat dinner. He was feeling guilty because he wanted to leave the little bird, so he found some more worms and left them for the bird.

The next morning, the little boy was happy to see the bird was still there and he fed it breakfast. He had helped the bird survive summer!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big bag of candy. Lily was so happy and wanted to eat all of it right away, but her mom told her to save some for later.

As Lily was walking to the park, she saw her friends playing on the swings. She ran over to join them, but she accidentally dropped her bag of candy. All of the candy spilled out and started rolling away. Lily tried to catch the candy, but it was too fast. She felt sad and wanted to cry.

But then, Lily remembered her mom's words and decided to resist the temptation to eat all the candy. Instead, she picked up the candy that she could and put it back in the bag. She shared the candy with her friends and they all had a generous amount. They played together happily and Lily felt proud of herself for resisting the urge to eat all the candy.

Mia and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. They are playful and happy. They run, jump, slide and swing. They listen to the birds and the wind.

One day, mom and dad bring a big basket to the park. They say they have a surprise for Mia and Ben. Mia and Ben are curious and excited. They wonder what is in the basket. They ask mom and dad, but they only smile and say, "You will see soon."

Mia and Ben play some more, but they keep looking at the basket. They want to know the surprise. They try to peek, but mom and dad stop them. They say, "Not yet, not yet. Wait a little more."

Finally, mom and dad call Mia and Ben. They say, "Come here, it's time for the surprise." Mia and Ben run to the basket. They open it and see many yummy things. They see sandwiches, cookies, fruits and juice. They say, "Wow, wow, wow. Thank you, mom and dad. This is the best surprise ever."

Mom and dad say, "You're welcome, Mia and Ben. We are proud of you. You are good and playful children. You listen to us and to nature. You deserve a special treat. Enjoy your picnic." Mia and Ben hug mom and dad. They sit on a blanket and eat the yummy things. They drink the juice and say, "Mmm, mmm, mmm. This is the best juice ever." They are happy and full. They love their mom and dad. They love their surprise. They love the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big, modern city. In this city, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a dream. She wanted to rescue animals that needed help. She told her mom and dad about her dream every day.

One day, Lily saw a small cat stuck in a tree. She knew this was her chance to rescue the cat, just like in her dream. Lily's dad helped her find a long stick. They used the stick to help the cat come down from the tree. The cat was very happy to be safe.

Lily felt proud that she could rescue the cat, just like she always dreamed. She knew that she could help more animals in the future. From that day on, Lily and her dad would go out and rescue animals together. They became known as the best animal rescuers in the modern city.

Once upon a time, there was a normal parrot named Percy. He loved to sit in his tree and watch the world around him. All day, he would watch the sun slowly bloom above the horizon and fade away with the night. 

One day, Percy saw something he had never seen before. It was a giant balloon, slowly making its way towards his tree. The balloon was full of bright colors and noisy sounds that filled Percy with excitement. He couldnâ€™t help but fly down and have a closer look. 

As Percy approached the balloon, he heard a curious voice calling out. â€œWhatâ€™s your name?â€ asked the voice. â€œMy name is Percy!â€ replied the parrot pleasantly. â€œWhat a nice nameâ€ replied the voice.

Percy and the voice chatted for hours, until the balloon and its companion disappeared over the horizon. After the balloon had gone, Percy spread his wings and flew up to his tree, feeling content and happy. Bloom by bloom, Percy continued to enjoy his view from up in the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, she went to the store with her mommy to buy more pastels. The lady at the store said they didn't have any pastels available. Lily was sad, but then she saw a toy that she liked. She asked her mommy if she could have it, but her mommy said no. Lily was upset and she accidentally snapped her favorite pastel in half. She felt even sadder now. But then her mommy gave her a big hug and told her they could try another store to find more pastels. Lily felt happy again.

Once upon a time there was a happy little boy named Dan. He was always loyal to his family, friends and neighbors. One day, Dan wanted to find something special to do, so he took his pet pup and headed out to explore the village.

As Dan walked along, he noticed an old man playing a violin. The old man was sad and lonely, and Dan wanted to help. He smiled and took his pup up to the old man. The man smiled back and handed Dan his violin. Dan was so excited and he said goodbye with a hug.

The pup and Dan went home and Dan took out the violin. He and the pup played it together and it sounded so nice. But the pup was tired, so Dan put the violin away in his bedroom.

The next morning, Dan woke up and saw that the violin was gone! Someone had stolen it during the night. Dan was so sad, but he didn't give up hope. He and the pup went back to the old man's house and told him what had happened.

The old man was so thankful and said they were the most loyal friends he had ever met. He said he would find a way to get the violin back.

The old man and Dan searched everywhere, but they couldn't find who had stolen the violin. Even so, they were determined to bring it back. Finally, after weeks of searching, the old man and Dan found the violin.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a shiny pebble on the ground. "Look, Mama! I found a pretty rock!" she said. Her mama smiled and said, "That's lovely, Lily. Why don't you put it in your pocket and we can show it to Daddy when he gets home?"

Later that day, Lily was playing with her spinning top when she saw a busy bee buzzing around the flowers. "Hi, little bee! Do you want to play with me?" she asked. But the bee was too busy collecting pollen to play.

As the sun started to set, Lily remembered the pebble in her pocket. "Mama, Daddy's home! Can I show him my pebble?" she asked. Mama nodded and Lily proudly showed Daddy her shiny find.

And as they sat outside watching the stars, Lily's spinning top spun round and round, and the busy bee buzzed off to its hive. And Lily fell asleep, dreaming of all the adventures she would have tomorrow.

Once upon a time there was a long, tall bird. It could balance in the air all day. One day, the bird decided to take a very long journey.

The bird flew so high, it could see the whole world. It soared for days, stopping to rest on tall trees. The bird flew over mountains, deserts and even oceans. Everywhere it went, it balanced in the air.

Finally, the bird arrived at a big, green field. Here it found a new home. The bird built its nest in a tall tree, and lived happily ever after.

Every day, it would balance in the air and fly around the field. The bird was very content in its long, beautiful home.

The bald man was walking along the beach when he saw a rock. He wanted to climb it, so he could see the ocean. He started walking up the rock, when suddenly he had an idea!

He pulled out the laser from his pocket and pointed it at the top of the rock. With a zap, he was suddenly standing on the top of the rock! He looked out over the ocean and smiled.

However, the rock was too high. Now he needed help getting down. He started waving his arms back and forth until he saw a boat in the distance.

The boat stopped near the rock, and a man yelled to the bald man, "Do you need help?" The bald man nodded, and the man on the boat threw a rope up to him.

The bald man quickly put the laser away and grabbed onto the rope. The man on the boat helped him climb down, and they both laughed. They waved goodbye as the boat sailed away. The bald man was very happy he had his laser to help him climb the rock!

Sam and Timmy were best friends. They played together every day.

One day, Timmy had an idea. He took a piece of paper and put it up in the tree. Then, he couldn't reach it.

"What should I do now?" Timmy asked. Sam whistled and pointed to an open window.

"Why don't you try climbing through the window?" he suggested.

Timmy smiled, then he carefully climbed up and reached the paper.

 When he got back, Sam smiled. "Let's go make something fun with the paper!" he said.

So, the two friends went inside and started having fun with the paper. They folded it, drew pictures on it and even invented a new game.

At the end of the day, they were very proud of what they had created. They had made something special, together.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old man who lived by the sea. He loved to fish on his boat every day. One day, he woke up early and went to the dock to get his boat ready. But he saw dark clouds in the sky and heard thunder rumbling. He knew a storm was coming.

He decided to go fishing anyway, but as he was sailing, the wind started to blow harder and the waves grew bigger. Suddenly, a huge lightning bolt struck the water near his boat, and he was scared. He quickly turned his boat around and headed back to shore.

When he got home, he realized that he should have listened to the signs of the storm and stayed on land. From that day on, he always checked the weather before going on his boat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with flowers in her garden. One day, she saw a beautiful flower that was about to bloom. She was so excited to see it!

Lily's mommy said, "We are going to the airport today. We are going on a trip!" Lily was happy but also a little bit naughty. She didn't want to leave her flowers behind.

When they got to the airport, Lily saw a man with a big hat. She asked him, "Do you like flowers?" The man smiled and said, "Yes, I do. They are so pretty when they bloom."

Lily was happy to hear that. She knew her flowers would bloom while she was away. When they came back from their trip, Lily ran to her garden and saw that her flowers had bloomed even more! She was so happy and thanked the man at the airport for talking about flowers with her.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to look for bugs and flowers. They saw a big bush with many red berries. Lily and Tom ran to the bush and picked some berries. They were sweet and juicy.

But then, Lily saw something on her hand. It was a yellow bug with black spots. It was crawling on her finger. Lily was scared of the bug. She did not like it. She screamed very loud. "Aaaah! A bug! A bug!"

Tom heard Lily scream. He looked at her hand and saw the bug. He was not scared of the bug. He liked it. He thought it was pretty and funny. He smiled and said, "Lily, don't scream. It's not a bad bug. It's a ladybug. It won't hurt you. It's your friend."

Lily stopped screaming and looked at Tom. She looked at the bug again. It was not so scary. It was yellow and black. It had six legs and two wings. It was a ladybug. Lily calmed down and said, "Sorry, bug. I didn't know you were a ladybug. You are pretty and funny. You can be my friend."

The ladybug tickled Lily's finger and flew away. Lily and Tom waved goodbye to the bug. They ate some more berries and played some more in the garden. They were happy and had fun.

John loved sports. He had a jump rope, a tennis racket and a basketball. One day, he had an idea. He wanted to recognize a fragile sport.

John thought and thought about what he could do. He thought about running, playing tag and hide and seek. Suddenly, he had an idea. John grabbed his big balls and went outside. 

John put the balls on the grass. Then he ran in circles around the balls. When he saw the balls move he jumped with joy. He wanted to recognize his fragile sport. 

John called his friend Bob to come and play. Bob was very excited. He joined the sport and they had lots of fun. 

John loved recognizing his fragile sport. He played it all the time with Bob and all his friends. To this day, they still play the fragile sport and have lots of fun.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a troubled little girl named Lily. She was always sad because she lost her favorite toy, a triangle. She looked everywhere in her house but could not find it.

One sunny day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a big puddle of water and thought her triangle might be there. She put her hand in the water to soak it and looked for her toy. She felt something at the bottom of the puddle.

Lily pulled it out and saw that it was her triangle! She was so happy that she found it. From that day on, Lily was never troubled again. She played with her triangle every day and always kept it close to her. And when she saw puddles, she would smile and remember how she found her toy.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy old man. He had a lot of money and a big house. One day he wanted to measure how big it was, so he grabbed his measuring tape and his hat and went outside.

He saw a little girl playing in his garden. She was about three years old. He asked her for help. "Can you hold this tape measure for me?", he said.

The little girl smiled and said, "Yes! It looks so fun!"

The old man was happy and began measuring. But then something went wrong. The tape measure snapped and the old man got very angry. He grabbed the little girl's arm and slapped her.

The little girl was shocked and started to cry. Tears dripped down her cheeks and her lip quivered. The old man felt so sorry. He gave her a big hug and said, "I'm so sorry. I never should have slapped you." 

The old man showed her some of his money and said, "I will buy you a toy to make it all better."

The little girl smiled and hugged the old man. "Thank you," she said. And from that day on, the old man never slapped anyone again.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play together. One day, they decided to make a cake for their moms. They found some flour, sugar, eggs, and milk in the kitchen. They mixed them in a big bowl and poured them in a pan. Then they put the pan in the oven and waited for the cake to bake.

While they were waiting, they saw a door in the wall that they had never noticed before. They were curious and wanted to see what was behind it. They opened the door and saw a dark and scary room. There were spiders, rats, and bats inside. They heard a loud growl and saw a big monster with sharp teeth and claws. They were very afraid and ran back to the kitchen.

They slammed the door behind them and locked it. They hugged each other and cried. They wished they had never opened the door. They learned that they should not go into places that they do not know. They should listen to their moms and stay safe.

Soon, the oven beeped and the cake was ready. It smelled yummy and looked delicious. They took it out and decorated it with frosting and sprinkles. They were happy and proud of their cake. They cut two slices and gave them to their moms. Their moms hugged them and thanked them. They said they were good and brave children. They ate the cake together and enjoyed it. They learned that they should make nice things for their moms and share them. They should be kind and grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big, black trunk in her room where she kept all her toys. Lily loved her toys very much, especially her favorite teddy bear.

One day, Lily's mom asked her if she wanted to go to the park. Lily said no because she wanted to stay home and play with her toys. Her mom said okay and left for the park without her.

Lily played with her toys all day, but when it was time for bed, she couldn't find her favorite teddy bear. She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. She searched and searched until she finally found it in the trunk. But when she picked it up, she heard a loud crack. The trunk had broken and all her toys were ruined.

Lily cried and cried because she valued her toys so much, but now they were all gone. She learned that sometimes it's better to go outside and have fun than to stay inside and play with toys all day.

Mum and Dad were very excited to take their little girl out for a picnic. She waved goodbye to Grandma, who happily gave them a big hug and a big kiss.

It was a beautiful day, and the little girl was so excited. The sun was shining, the clouds were white, and the birds were singing.

On their way to the picnic spot, they stopped to look up at the night sky. Little girl was amazed to see so many stars twinkling above. She said, "Mum, Dad, the stars look so beautiful!"

Mum and Dad hugged the little girl and comforted her with warm cuddles. They said, "Yes they do. Isn't it wonderful?"

They had a wonderful picnic that day, filled with love and laughter. Little Girl was so happy, and before they knew it, the day was over and it was time to go home.

As they walked hand in hand, the little girl looked up at the night sky and saw the stars twinkling. She smiled and said, "I love the stars, Mum and Dad." And they hugged her and reminded that they were always there to comfort her.

Little Jack was a bright and curious 3 year old. Every day he asked questions and explored the world around him.

Today, Jack and his mommy went to the post office. Jack was excited! He watched as mommy put letters in the mail. Jack loved to watch the post man take the letters away.

Once they were done mailing the letters, mommy and Jack went home. Jack noticed two soft little toes sticking out from under the couch. He quickly peeked under the couch and saw a kitten!

Jack was so happy that he had found a new playmate! The kitten's fur was soft and when it meowed Jack felt a little flutter in his tummy. He knew this would be a fun day! He and the kitten quickly became the best of friends.

One day, a girl named Lily wanted to bake a cake. She wanted to make the cake as a gift for her friend, Tom. Lily was very excited to make the cake smooth and pretty.

As Lily started to bake, her little brother, Sam, came into the kitchen. Sam wanted to help Lily, but he was too small. Lily said, "No, Sam, you can't help me." Sam was sad and cried.

Lily felt bad for Sam. She thought of a way to fix the problem. She asked Sam to help her put the gift in a box and make it look nice. Sam was happy again. They worked together and made the cake and gift look perfect for Tom.

Once upon a time, there was a unique little bird named Timmy. Timmy was very special because he could talk to people. One day, Timmy went to visit his friend, Sally the squirrel.

Sally was making cookies in her home. She had a big oven to bake the cookies. Timmy saw that Sally's oven was very hot. He wanted to help Sally, so he decided to warn her about the hot oven.

"Be careful, Sally! The oven is very hot!" Timmy said. Sally listened to Timmy's warning and was extra careful not to touch the hot oven. They both waited for the cookies to bake. When the cookies were ready, they shared the tasty treats and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Kim. Kim was only three years old and was very kind. 
One day, Kim was playing outside in the sunshine when she accidentally hurt her thumb. It hurt a lot and she started to cry. 
Suddenly, a warm breeze came by and made her feel better. Kim looked up and saw a magical fairy with sparkly wings. 
The fairy waved her wand and said a few magical words. Soon, her thumb was all better and felt warm and strong. 
Kim felt happy and smiled.
The fairy had restored Kim's thumb! 
Kim thanked the fairy for her special gift and promised to be more careful. 
The fairy smiled and flew away in a cloud of sparkles. 
Kim was so happy and held her thumb close. She knew she would never forget the magical fairy who had restored her thumb.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to the store with her mom. Lily saw a toy she really wanted, but her mom said they couldn't buy it. Lily got upset and started to cry. Her mom tried to calm her down by giving her a hug, but Lily kept crying.

Suddenly, Lily saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was barking loudly and looked very scary. Lily's mom was afraid, but she knew she had to lead Lily to safety. They ran to the nearest shelf and hid behind it. The dog ran past them and didn't see them.

Lily was still upset, but she felt safe with her mom. Her mom hugged her again and told her everything was okay. Lily felt better and stopped crying. From that day on, she knew that her mom would always lead her to safety when she was scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance to the rhythm of the music. One day, Lily's friend asked her to perform in front of many people. Lily felt scared and didn't know what to do. Her mom told her to be brave and try her best.

Lily's mom also recommended that she practice every day to get better. Lily listened to her mom and practiced every day. She felt more confident and brave. Finally, the day of the performance arrived. Lily danced to the rhythm of the music and did a great job. Everyone clapped and cheered for her. Lily felt very happy and proud of herself.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to play with her toys, but today was different. She was outside with her parents and there were a lot of people around. They were all wealthy people and were talking about something strange.

Lucy listened carefully, but the words were all strange to her. She then noticed one wealthy man pointing to his toes. She wondered why and asked her dad, "What's he pointing at?"

Her dad laughed and smiled, "That man is showing off his money! He's wealthy and he wants everyone to know."

This made little Lucy excited. She wished she had money too. She wanted to show off her wealth like the man.

But then her dad said something that made her sad. He said, "It's just playing pretend. You don't need money to have fun!"

So Lucy put away her dreams of being wealthy and went back to playing with her toys. But secretly she still hoped one day she could show off her own wealth too!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her crayons all day long. One day, Lily's mom told her to go outside and play. But Lily didn't want to stop drawing. She felt an urge to finish her picture.

So, Lily stayed inside and kept drawing. But after a while, she started to feel cold. She realized that she had left the window open. Her mom came back inside and saw that Lily was shivering. She told her that it's important to take care of yourself, even when you're doing something you love.

Lily learned that it's okay to have an urge to do something, but it's also important to take care of yourself and stay warm. From that day on, she made sure to close the window before she started drawing.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl who had a favorite scarf. Her mom always tied it very tight around her neck, and she loved it. One day, she went outside to play and when she came back, the scarf was not there anymore. She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. Tears filled her eyes and she started to cry.

Her mom saw her crying and asked what was wrong. The girl told her mom about the scarf. Suddenly, her mom bent down and felt around on the ground. She found the scarf! The girl was so excited and hugged her mom very tight.

The mom tied the scarf around the little girl's neck and smiled. She said that she would never lose the scarf again. The little girl wiped her tears away, smiled, and ran off to play. She wore her scarf everywhere, and never forgot to keep it tight.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a nice girl named Lily. Lily liked to play with her toys and have fun. One day, Lily found a box of matches. She knew matches could be dangerous, so she decided to show her mom.

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mom, look what I found!" Her mom saw the matches and told Lily not to play with them. She said, "Thank you for showing me, Lily. Matches can make fire, and fire can hurt us. Let's put them away."

The next day, Lily saw her friend Tom. Tom liked to complain a lot. He was always unhappy about something. Today, Tom was sad because he lost his toy car. Lily wanted to help Tom feel better, so she said, "Don't worry, Tom. We can find your toy car together."

Lily and Tom searched around the house and found the toy car under a chair. Tom was so happy, and he stopped complaining. Lily felt good because she helped her friend. From that day on, Tom learned to complain less and be more thankful for the nice things he had.

And every time Lily saw a match, she remembered to be careful and tell an adult. Lily and Tom played together and had lots of fun. They learned that being nice, helpful, and careful made them both happy.

Anna and Ben love to pretend. They like to play different games with their toys and their imagination. Today, they decide to pretend they are on a safari. They take their stuffed animals and put them in a big box. The box is their jeep. They also wear hats and binoculars.

"Look, Anna, there is a lion!" Ben says, pointing to his yellow toy. "He is very big and strong. We have to be careful."

Anna nods and looks through her binoculars. "Yes, he is. But he is also sleepy. He is lying under the tree. Maybe he just ate a zebra."

They drive their jeep to another spot. They see a giraffe, an elephant, a monkey and a snake. They are all different colors and sizes. They make noises like the animals.

"Wow, Ben, this is so fun!" Anna says. "I like all the animals. They are so amazing."

"Me too, Anna. But do you know which one is my favorite?" Ben asks.

"Which one, Ben?"

"The snake. He is very flexible. He can bend and twist and curl. He can go under and over and around. He is so cool."

Anna smiles. "He is cool, Ben. But he is also scary. He can bite and poison. He can squeeze and choke. He is so dangerous."

They both shiver. They decide to leave the snake alone. They drive their jeep to a safer place. They pretend they are on a safari. They have a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a cell that was very enthusiastic to move. So it decided to go on a journey. It moved slowly and carefully as it explored the world around it. As it moved, it saw many different and exciting things. It saw tall trees, brightly coloured flowers, butterflies, and even little furry animals. 

The awesome journey continued and the cell was so happy that it started to dance! It twirled and it hopped and it moved in all sorts of directions. It was such a happy cell.

But over time, the cell had travelled so much that it began to feel tired. It stopped moving and just lay in the sun, happy to just be alive and to have seen so much. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. He would run and jump and laugh with his friends. One day, Timmy saw a cactus and he wanted to touch it. But his mommy said no because the cactus had prickly needles that could hurt him.

Timmy didn't listen to his mommy and touched the cactus anyway. Ouch! The needles hurt his fingers and he cried. Timmy regretted not listening to his mommy.

After that day, Timmy became very intelligent. He learned that it's important to listen to his mommy and not touch things that could hurt him. He never touched a cactus again and was happy playing with his friends in the sunshine. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine and climb up high on the swing set. One day, her mommy asked her if she wanted to learn math. Lily didn't know what math was, but she trusted her mommy and said yes.

Her mommy taught her how to count to ten and Lily was so happy that she could do it all by herself. She felt so proud and high up in the sky like a bird. From that day on, Lily loved math and wanted to learn more.

Lily knew she could trust her mommy to teach her new things and help her grow. She loved spending time with her mommy and learning new things together. And every time she counted to ten, she felt like she was on top of the world.

Mummy was preparing something special. She was going to use her belt! She tied it around her waist. Two of her friends watched with curiosity. 

Mummy held up the belt and twirled it around. It was a big, long belt and it made everybody laugh. It was fun to watch her spin it around and around.

After a few minutes of twirling, it was time for something different. Mummy took off the belt and began to run around the room. She jumped up and down and made funny noises. Her friends thought it was so funny. They all laughed together.

Finally, after playing for a while, it was time to put the belt back on. Mummy put the belt on and it was time to do something boring. She sat down and made gentle, soothing moves with the belt. It was boring, but it was good for her body. 

Mummy and her friends practiced for a while. It was fun! They liked learning new ways of preparing the belt. Afterwards, they all felt better and relaxed.

Once upon a time, there was a big and mighty lion. He had a desk where he liked to sit and think. One day, his friend the zebra came to visit him. The lion asked the zebra if he wanted to play a game, but the zebra disagreed. 

The lion asked the zebra why he didn't want to play. The zebra said he was tired and wanted to rest. The lion understood and let the zebra take a nap on his desk. While the zebra slept, the lion quietly watched over him. 

When the zebra woke up, he thanked the lion for being such a good friend. They agreed to play a game together another day. The lion was happy that he could help his friend and the zebra was happy to have such a mighty friend.

Once upon a time there was a lamp. The lamp was very special. It was beautiful and bright. Every night the lamp would think about a special wish. One starry night the lamp really thought hard about the wish it wanted. It wanted to make the world a better place. Suddenly, the lamp was so bright and beautiful. It made everyone so happy. People all over the world were smiling. The lamp had made its special wish come true. And everyone was so glad.

Mama and Papa were getting married. Everyone was so excited and were talking and talking. Little Danny was so excited too. He wanted to crawl so he got on all fours and started to crawl around the room. Everyone was laughing and smiling as they watched him go. When Danny got to the carpet he got a bit dizzy and fell over. Everyone laughed and he laughed too. After the wedding everyone was so happy and went out to eat, but Danny still wanted to crawl. All night he crawled around, until the sun came up, and he was still crawling. Mama and Papa were so proud of their little crawler!

One day, Fred and Tom were walking together. While walking, Fred found a long, straight line in the ground. He wanted it for himself, but Tom also wanted it. Both of them argued and quarreled over the line.

Suddenly, an ugly monster appeared. It was big and scary. "What's going on?", bellowed the monster. It saw Fred and Tom arguing, so it made a decision. The monster decided to share the line with both of them. 

Then, the monster told them, "You both can have the line. Just don't quarrel anymore". 

Fred and Tom were very happy. They thanked the monster and hugged each other. They both agreed to never quarrel again. 

From that day on, Fred and Tom always shared the line and were very happy.

Once upon a time there was a little boy, who wanted to go on a boat. He was very excited, but he knew he had to collect things first to make his boat. He walked through the garden, looking for things to put in his boat.

The little boy found a big stick, some stones and a small leaf. He collected all these things in his hands and carried them to the lake. 

When he got to the lake, he put the things he had collected in the boat. Then he looked around, but the boat seemed very troubled. He wanted to go on a boat ride, but he didnâ€™t know how to make it go.

Just then, an older man came walking by. The little boy asked him: â€œHow do I make the boat move?â€

The man replied: â€œOh, you need to use a paddle if you want the boat to move. You can collect one from the shed over there.â€

The little boy was so happy and ran off to collect the paddle. With the paddle in his hands, he climbed into his boat and began to paddle. Soon the boat was gliding peacefully across the lake and the little boy was filled with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the grass. One day, she was playing with her friend, Timmy. Timmy said, "I'm glad we are friends, Lily." 

Lily smiled and said, "Me too, Timmy. Do you know why I love playing in the grass?" 

Timmy shook his head and said, "No, why?" 

Lily said, "I love feeling the soft grass on my feet. It makes me happy." 

Timmy said, "I like feeling the grass too. It tickles my toes!" 

Lily and Timmy played in the grass all day and had lots of fun. They both knew they would always be friends and have fun playing in the grass together.

Anna liked to wake up early and watch the sunrise. She liked how the sky changed colors and how the birds sang. She liked to sit on the window and feel the warm sun on her face. But she was lonely. She wished she had someone to share the sunrise with.

One day, she saw a boy walking on the street. He had a big backpack and a funny hat. He looked up and saw Anna on the window. He smiled and waved at her. Anna smiled and waved back. She felt happy. She wanted to talk to him.

She ran to the door and opened it. She called out to the boy. "Hi! What is your name? Do you want to see the sunrise with me?"

The boy stopped and looked at her. He said, "Hi! My name is Ben. I am going to school. I like the sunrise, but I have to mind the time. I don't want to be late."

Anna felt sad. She said, "Oh. I don't go to school. I stay at home with my mom. She is sick and needs me. I don't have any friends. I am lonely."

Ben felt sorry for her. He said, "I am sorry. That is hard. I have an idea. Why don't you come with me to school? You can meet my friends and learn new things. Maybe you will like it. And you can still see the sunrise on the way."

Anna liked the idea. She said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun. Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. Can I bring my mom?"

Ben said, "Of course. She can come too. Maybe she will feel better. Come on, let's go. The sunrise is waiting for us."

Anna and Ben held hands and walked to school. They saw the sunrise together. They saw the sky change colors and heard the birds sing. They felt the warm sun on their faces. They were not lonely anymore. They were happy. They had found a friend.

It was a hot day. The sun was so bright and hot that it made Sally feel tired. She wanted something sweet and delicious, so she went outside to look for sugar.

She walked up to the corner store, and there was the sugar she was looking for. She grabbed a small bag of sugar and was about to go, when she heard someone say, "Let's have a race!" It was some other children, and they were very competitive.

Sally loved to run, so she decided to join the race. They put the sugar down in a pile, and everyone started to race around the store. Sally ran as fast as she could, and soon she was ahead of everyone else.

Suddenly, she felt something hot on her foot. It was the sugar! It had been burning in the sun, and it burned her foot. She screamed and quickly ran away from the sugar. Everyone else stopped running and just watched her. 

Luckily, Sally was fine, but she never went near the sugar pile again. She learned that it was better to stay away from things that can burn you!

Mummy and Timmy were in the closet, looking for something. Mummy asked Timmy to pass her a hanger. Timmy refused because he wanted to pick it himself. Mummy told him that she needed the hanger, but Timmy shook his head and said no. He was being very rude.

Mummy was getting angry now. She told Timmy, "If you don't give me the hanger, you won't get any ice cream." Timmy still refused and said he wanted to pick it himself. He stomped his feet on the floor.

Mummy scolded Timmy and said, "That's not nice behaviour. You have to be polite. Give me the hanger please." Timmy looked at Mummy and said, "Okay." He reached up to the shelf, grabbed the hanger, and handed it to Mummy. Mummy smiled and gave Timmy a hug. "Thank you, my love."

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play outside after dinner. One night, they see the moon in the sky. It is big and bright and round.

"Look, the moon!" Tom says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Mia says. "Do you want to go to the moon?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He likes to go to new places. He nods and says, "Yes, I do! How can we go to the moon?"

Mia has an idea. She sees a big cardboard box in the yard. She urges Tom to follow her. She says, "We can use this box as a rocket. We can pretend to fly to the moon!"

Tom likes the idea. He helps Mia to move the box to a flat spot. They draw some buttons and windows on the box with crayons. They get inside the box and close the flap.

"Ready, set, go!" Mia says. She pushes a button and makes a loud noise. "Zoom, zoom, zoom!"

Tom joins in. He pushes another button and makes another noise. "Beep, beep, beep!"

They pretend to fly to the moon. They imagine they see stars and planets and comets. They have a lot of fun.

After a while, they hear a voice. It is Tom's mom. She calls them for bedtime.

"Tom, Mia, time to go inside!" she says. "It is late. You need to sleep."

Tom and Mia open the flap. They see Tom's mom smiling at them. She says, "Did you have a good trip to the moon?"

Tom and Mia nod and grin. They say, "Yes, we did! It was funny and fun!"

They get out of the box and hug Tom's mom. They say goodnight to each other and go inside. They dream of the moon and their rocket. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a child who liked to go for walks together. One day, when they stepped outside, the mom pointed to the sky and said to the child, "Look, can you see the sun up there? It looks so good and warm." The child was amazed and asked, "What is it for?" The mom said, "It is very valuable! It gives us light and warms us. We have to take care of it." 

The child was very intrigued and asked again, "What should we do to take care of it?" The mom thought for a moment and said, "We can go outside and play in the sun, it will make us feel good. And we can also cut back on things that harm the environment, so the sun will last forever." 

The child smiled and said, "I love the sun!" The mom smiled too and said, "Me too, sweetheart. We must remember to value the sun always."

Sara likes to play with her dolls. She has many dolls, but her favorite is Lily. Lily has long hair and a pretty dress. Sara talks to Lily and makes her tea and cake.

One day, Sara's mom says they have to go to the store. Sara wants to bring Lily with her. She puts Lily in her backpack and gets in the car. Mom drives to the store and parks. She tells Sara to stay close to her and not to run away.

Sara follows mom into the store. She sees many things. She sees apples, bananas, and oranges. She likes oranges. They are round and sweet and juicy. She wants to get one for Lily. She reaches for an orange, but another hand grabs it first.

"Hey, that's mine!" Sara says. She looks up and sees a boy. He is bigger than her and has a mean face. He holds the orange and laughs.

"No, it's mine!" the boy says. "You are too little to have oranges. Go away!"

Sara feels angry and sad. She wants the orange for Lily. She thinks the boy is rude and mean. She pulls on the orange, but the boy pulls harder. They tug and tug, but neither lets go.

"Stop it, both of you!" mom says. She hears the noise and comes over. She sees Sara and the boy fighting over the orange. She takes the orange from them and puts it back on the shelf.

"Sharing is nice, fighting is not," mom says. "You can't just take things from other people. You have to ask nicely or wait your turn."

Sara nods. She knows mom is right. She says sorry to the boy. The boy says sorry too. He looks less mean now. He says his name is Ben. He says he likes oranges too.
