Can we walk together?" Her parent smiled and said, "Of course! We can start again and walk together." And so, they continued their walk together, enjoying the beautiful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a smart dog named Max. Max was very good at fetching sticks and balls. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. They saw a little bird with a broken wing. 

Lily said, "Oh no, that bird is in trouble! We have to help it!" Max barked in agreement. They picked up the bird and took it to a kind lady who knew how to help animals. The lady said the bird needed rest and time to heal. 

Lily was sad that the bird was hurt, but Max had an idea. He said, "Lily, let's give the bird a kiss to make it feel better." Lily thought that was a great idea. They gently kissed the bird and Max wagged his tail. The bird chirped happily. 

After a few weeks, the bird was all better and ready to fly again. Lily and Max were happy to see the bird fly away. Lily said, "Max, you are so smart. Your idea to kiss the bird made it feel better." Max barked happily and licked Lily's face. They continued their walk in the park, happy that they helped the little bird in trouble.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Robert. He was very kind. He wanted to help all the animals in the world. 

One day, Robert was walking in the woods. He saw something. It was a skeleton! The skeleton looked so sad. Robert had a big heart and he felt compassion for the skeleton.

He tried to help it. But the skeleton was very brittle. When Robert touched it, it started to break. Robert felt so sorry that he had accidentally hurt the skeleton. He wished he could do something to help it.

Then, suddenly, the skeleton started to move. It turned into a beautiful bird. The bird flew away, and Robert was so happy. 

Robert had used his compassion to help the bird feel better. He was so proud of himself. He knew that he could always be kind and try to make the world a better place.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. Sometimes they share, but sometimes they fight. One day, they both want the same red car. They pull and tug and yell.

"Mine!" Anna says.

"No, mine!" Ben says.

They are so loud that Mom comes in. She looks sad and angry.

"Stop it, you two!" Mom says. "Why are you fighting over a toy? You have so many toys. Can't you be nice to each other?"

Anna and Ben stop and look at Mom. They realize that they are making Mom unhappy. They also realize that they love each other more than the red car. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, Mom," Anna says.

"Sorry, Mom," Ben says.

They hug Mom and then hug each other. They decide to take turns with the red car. They also find other toys to play with together. They laugh and smile and have fun.

Mom smiles too. She is glad that Anna and Ben are getting along. She says, "That's better. Now you are being good twins. I love you both very much."

Anna and Ben say, "We love you too, Mom."

They play in peace until it is time for dinner. They see the bright sun shining through the window. They think it is a beautiful day.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty princess named Lily. She had a white dress and a big smile. One day, she went to the park with her friends. They played on the slide and had so much fun! 

Lily loved the slide because it was so much fun to slide down. Her friends went down the slide too, and they laughed and giggled. Then, Lily saw a white butterfly and she chased it around the park. The butterfly was so pretty, with its white wings fluttering in the air. 

After playing all day, Lily went home and told her mom about her fun day at the park. She said, "Mommy, I slid down the slide and saw a pretty white butterfly!" Her mom smiled and gave her a big hug. It was a happy day for Lily and her friends.

One morning, Tom woke up and felt hungry. He got out of his bed and put on his slippers. He wanted to eat some toast with jam, his favorite breakfast. He walked to the kitchen, but he did not see his mom or dad. He saw a note on the table that said: "We are busy. We will be back soon. Love, Mom and Dad."

Tom felt sad and lonely. He did not know how to make toast by himself. He decided to wander around the house and look for something fun to do. He went to the living room and saw his toy cars. He played with them for a while, making vroom-vroom noises. He went to the bathroom and saw his rubber duck. He filled the sink with water and splashed with the duck. He went to his parents' bedroom and saw their big bed. He jumped on it and pretended to be a superhero.

He was having fun, but he was still hungry. He wished his mom and dad would come back soon and make him some toast. He heard a knock on the door. He ran to the door and opened it. He saw his grandma and grandpa standing there, smiling. They had a big basket with them.

"Hello, Tom!" they said. "We came to visit you and bring you some treats. Can we come in?"

Tom was very happy to see them. He hugged them and invited them in. He showed them his toys and his duck and his bed. They played with him and listened to his stories. They also brought him some toast with jam, his favorite breakfast. They ate together and talked and laughed.

Tom felt full and loved. He was glad his grandma and grandpa came to see him. He did not feel sad and lonely anymore. He wondered when his mom and dad would come back, but he knew they would be happy to see him too. He had a good day with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who had a watch. One day, he saw a bird that was in a difficult situation. The bird had gotten stuck in a bush. The little boy was very brave and wanted the bird to be okay. He said, "I can rescue you!"

He used his watch to time how long it took. He was very careful and after trying for a few minutes, he freed the bird from the bush! The bird thanked the little boy and flew away into the sky. 

The little boy was very proud of himself and he felt happy because he had rescued the bird. From then on, he always kept his watch close, so that he could rescue animals in need!

Once upon a time there was a young girl called Molly. She loved to skip in the park. One day, Molly decided to skip further than she ever had before. She skipped so far that she came upon a wide river. Molly was scared, but she wanted to cross the river to explore the other side. 

The river was quite wide, and the water was running quite fast. Molly looked around for a way to cross. Then, she found a very big, heavy log that she could use as a bridge. Taking a deep breath, Molly stepped on the log and began to skip down it, being very careful not to fall in the river. 

Finally, after a few skips, Molly got to the other side of the river. She looked around and noticed so many new places to explore. She had made it across the wide river all on her own! Taking a happy skip, Molly set off to explore the new side of the park.

Lily liked to bathe in the big tub with her toys. She had a duck, a frog, a boat and a diamond. The diamond was her favorite. It was shiny and sparkly and made her feel like a princess.

One day, when Lily was bathing, a bad man came into the house. He saw the diamond on the edge of the tub and wanted to take it. He was very sneaky and quiet. He reached for the diamond with his hand.

But Lily saw him. She was not afraid. She was brave and smart. She grabbed the diamond and threw it at the bad man's face. It hit him hard and made him cry. He ran away, leaving the diamond behind.

Lily's mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw Lily in the tub with the diamond and the bad man running out the door. She hugged Lily and told her she was a hero. She called the police and they came to catch the bad man.

Lily was happy and proud. She had saved her diamond and her mom. She finished her bath and dried off. She put the diamond in a safe place and went to bed. She dreamed of being a princess with a shiny and sparkly diamond.

Once there was a littel boy. He was walking home from school, when he saw a harmless animal. He stopped to look at it. He knew he should stay away, so he bent down and said shyly, "Hello there".

Suddenly, the animal made a strange noise. The little boy jumped back, scared. Then he heard a voice.

"Oh, don't worry. That's just my pet dog, Wiggles. He won't hurt you," said a voice.

The voice belonged to an old woman. She explained that Wiggles was harmless and she wanted the little boy to come closer.

The woman gave the little boy a towel and said, "Take this. Wipe your hands. Wiggles loves to be petted."

The little boy took the towel and petted Wiggles. He was so happy! The woman then warned him to never approach animals he doesn't know, for he didn't know if they were harmless or not.

The little boy thanked the woman and then went on his way. From then on, he knew to always listen carefully and be aware of his surroundings.

Lily was a girl who liked to help. She helped her mom cook, she helped her dad fix things, she helped her brother with his homework. She was very useful and everyone thanked her.

One day, Lily saw a big truck outside her house. It had many boxes and bags inside. Lily was curious and wanted to help. She asked the truck driver, "Can I help you?"

The truck driver smiled and said, "Sure, little girl. You can help me by taking these boxes and bags to the back of the truck. They are very light and easy to carry. Thank you for being so useful."

Lily was happy and started to take the boxes and bags to the back of the truck. She did not know that the truck driver was a bad man. He was stealing things from her house and putting them in his truck. He was lying to Lily and using her.

When Lily's mom came out of the house, she saw the truck and the boxes and bags. She screamed, "Stop! That's our stuff! That's a thief!"

The truck driver heard her and jumped into his truck. He drove away very fast, with Lily still in the back of the truck. He did not care about Lily. He only cared about the things he stole.

Lily was scared and sad. She wanted to go back to her mom and dad and brother. She wanted to be useful and thanked. But she was trapped in the truck with the bad man. She did not know what would happen to her. She cried and cried. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dog called Sprocket. He was a very enthusiastic pet. He loved going for runs and long walks.

One day, Sprocket was jumping around a lot and he suddenly got a pain in his bone. He yelped in pain and his owner quickly came to help.

The owner examined Sprocket's bone and saw that it had shrunk. So, the owner took Sprocket to the vet to get it fixed.

At the vet, the vet gave Sprocket some special medicine and wrapped his bone up tightly. After a few days, the bone was better.

Sprocket was happy and he was back to being his enthusiastic self again. He ran around with even more enthusiasm than before. Everyone was happy to see him back to being healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons. One day, Timmy went to the store with his mommy to buy some candy. While they were there, Timmy saw a furry monster toy that he really wanted. He begged his mommy to buy it for him, but she said they didn't have enough money. Timmy was sad, but his mommy promised to save up so they could buy it next time. 

The next day, Timmy went to his friend's house to play. His friend had the same furry monster toy that Timmy wanted. Timmy was so happy to play with it and he forgot all about wanting to buy one. He realized that playing with friends was more fun than having lots of toys. From that day on, Timmy spent more time playing with his friends and less time wanting to buy things.

Mira and Ravi are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find some clay near a pond. The clay is soft and wet. They can make shapes with it.

"Look, I made a ball!" Mira says. She rolls the clay in her hands. She throws the ball to Ravi.

"Wow, good throw!" Ravi says. He catches the ball. He makes a snake with the clay. He puts the snake on the ground. He makes it wiggle.

"Look, I made a snake!" Ravi says. He shows the snake to Mira.

"That's a funny snake!" Mira says. She laughs. She picks some flowers. She puts the flowers on the snake. She makes it pretty.

"Look, I made a flower snake!" Mira says. She shows the flower snake to Ravi.

"That's a pretty snake!" Ravi says. He smiles. He picks some stones. He puts the stones on the ball. He makes it shiny.

"Look, I made a shiny ball!" Ravi says. He shows the shiny ball to Mira.

"That's a shiny ball!" Mira says. She claps. She picks the ball and the snake. She gives them to Ravi.

"Here, these are for you!" Mira says. She hugs Ravi.

"Thank you, Mira!" Ravi says. He hugs Mira. He gives her the ball and the snake.

"Here, these are for you!" Ravi says. He kisses Mira.

They are happy. They are playful. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and make new things. He was always enthusiastic about trying new things and exploring the world around him. One day, Timmy decided to make a big tower out of blocks. He worked hard and built it up high, but then he got distracted and left it there.

Later that day, Timmy's little sister came into the room and saw the tower. She wanted to play with it too, but she accidentally knocked it over and all the blocks fell down. Timmy was upset and cried, but then he remembered something his mom had told him. She said that sometimes things change and we have to learn to adapt.

So Timmy decided to build a new tower, but this time he asked his sister to help him. Together, they built an even bigger tower and had lots of fun doing it. Timmy learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but with a little help and a positive attitude, we can still have fun and make something even better. And so, Timmy and his sister happily played with their tower, knowing that change can be a good thing.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy bear who was walking in the woods. As he walked, he saw a pole. He thought to himself, "I want to climb the pole!"

The bear tried to climb the pole but it was so slippery he couldn't get a good grip. He tried again, but still he couldn't climb it. He felt very frustrated and didn't know what to do.

Then he heard a voice behind him. It was a squirrel, smiling and looking up at the pole.

"Resist, bear," said the squirrel.

The bear looked at the squirrel and nodded. He got closer to the pole and tried to resist slipping. This time he managed to get a much better grip and soon he was standing at the top, smiling proudly.

The squirrel cheered him on, clapping and nodding. The bear waved happily to the squirrel, and the two friends went their separate ways.

The end.

Once there were two friends named Bob and Sam. They were playing together in the garden one day. Sam picked a flower and then pointed to a black bird in a tree. 
"What's that?" he asked Bob.    

Bob smiled and said, "That's a Crow. Listen, what sound does it make?"

Suddenly, the crow made a loud sound that sounded like "Caw, Caw!"

"That's a Caw," Bob smiled.

Sam laughed and said, "I think I should pick a better word next time!"

Bob smiled and nodded. "That's a good idea. We should always pick the right word to use when we talk to each other."

The moral of the story is that it is important to choose the right words when you talk to your friends. Being thoughtful and using kind words can help keep friendships strong.

Once upon a time there was a spot. It was a lonely spot, all by itself. One day it decided to move. It felt scared so it moved slowly and carefully. 

As it moved, the spot became a little less fearful. Soon, it started to move faster and faster. It kept going until it reached a new spot. It was a much better spot than the old one. 

The spot was so happy that it began to dance. It was a fun spot and it was no longer scared. It was happy to have moved and it was ready to meet new friends. 

The end.

Anna likes to play with her toy cars. She has many cars of different colors and shapes. She likes to make them zoom on the floor and pretend they are racing. Sometimes she attaches a string to a car and pulls it along.

One day, Anna finds a small car in her toy box. It is shiny and red and has a big number one on it. Anna thinks it is the fastest car of all. She wants to attach the string to it and make it zoom. But she cannot find the hole for the string. She looks and looks, but the car is too small.

She asks her brother Ben for help. Ben is older and knows many things. He comes to see the small car. He says, "This is not a toy car, Anna. This is a button. It belongs to Mom's coat. See, it has a loop on the back. That is how you attach it to the coat."

Anna is surprised. She did not know that buttons can look like cars. She says, "But I want to play with it. It is so pretty and fast."

Ben says, "You can play with it, but not with the string. The string will break the loop. And Mom will be sad if she loses her button. Why don't you use this big car instead? It has a hole for the string and it can zoom too."

Anna agrees. She gives the small car back to Ben and takes the big car. She attaches the string to it and makes it zoom on the floor. She is happy and so is Ben. They play together with their toy cars and have fun.

Sam was a horse who lived on a farm. He liked to run and jump and play with his friends. He also liked to eat hay, which was his food. Hay was soft and sweet and filled his belly.

One day, a big truck came to the farm. It had a lot of hay in the back. Sam was happy to see the hay. He thought it was for him and his friends. He ran to the truck and tried to get some hay. But the truck driver was not nice. He shouted at Sam and hit him with a stick. He said the hay was not for him. He said the hay was for other horses who were tough and strong and could work hard.

Sam was sad and hurt. He did not understand why the truck driver was so mean. He did not want to work hard. He just wanted to have fun and eat hay. He ran away from the truck and looked for his friends. But he could not find them. He saw that the truck driver had put them in a cage. He had taken them away from the farm. He had included them in the hay.

Sam was scared and lonely. He did not know what to do. He wanted his friends back. He wanted to eat hay with them. He wanted to run and jump and play with them. But he could not. He was left alone on the farm. He had no hay, no friends, and no fun. He had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anna. She was only three and wanted to try something new. She saw her mom in the kitchen and shouted, "Mommy, I want sauce!" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course honey." She opened the cupboard and got out a jar of red sauce. Anna was so excited to try it. She opened the jar and took a big spoonful. She licked the spoon and shouted, "Yum! It's delicious!"

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to draw with crayons. One day, they found a big eraser in the art room. They wondered what it could do.

"Let's try it on our drawings," Ben said. "Maybe it can make them better."

Anna agreed. They took the eraser and rubbed it on their papers. But instead of erasing the crayons, the eraser made them shrink. Their drawings became smaller and smaller until they were tiny dots.

"Oh no!" Anna cried. "What did we do?"

Ben was scared. He looked at the eraser and saw that it had a label. It said: "Magic eraser. Do not use on anything you want to keep. Warning: may cause shrinking."

"We used the wrong eraser!" Ben said. "This is a magic eraser. It makes things shrink."

Anna and Ben felt very embarrassed. They had ruined their drawings and wasted the crayons. They wished they had read the label before using the eraser.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful with things they did not know. They learned to read the labels and follow the instructions. They learned to respect the art supplies and not play with them. They said sorry to their teacher and promised to be more responsible. They hoped their drawings would grow back someday.

Once upon a time there was a jolly pan. He was very happy and he wanted to show everyone how much he valued them.

One day, the pan went to the garden and he saw a 3 year old who was playing with his toys. The pan opened his mouth and said "Hello!"

The 3 year old was surprised to see the talking pan. He said hello back and asked the pan what he was doing there.

The pan said, "I wanted to show you how much I value you, so I wanted to give you something special." The 3 year old was so happy and excited.

The pan gave him a big hug and said, "I hope you have a jolly day." The 3 year old hugged the pan back. He felt so special and loved that day.

One day, Jack was walking with his mom. They were talking about fashion. Jack loved wearing colorful clothes so he asked his mom if there was anything new he could wear.

Suddenly, Jack spotted his friend John. John was wearing a very cool cap on his head. It had a funny picture on it and Jack loved it.

John saw Jack looking at his cap and he began to tease Jack. John told him he could never wear the cap.

This made Jack sad. He told his mom he wished he had a cap like John.

His mom told him not to worry. She said she had seen a lot of different stylish caps that were available for sale.

Jack was so happy! He thanked his mom and couldn't wait to find the perfect cap.

He went on an adventure to find a cap that was perfect for him. He searched and searched until he finally found the perfect one - a red cap with a unicorn on it!

Now, Jack never gets teased by his friends and looks stylish at the same time. Fashion is available to everyone - even three year olds like him!

Every day, Mommy and Daddy went to work, but they always came home. One day they came home with something special. It was a rod! Mommy and Daddy were glad to have it.

The rod was for fishing. They took it to the lake and Mommy and Daddy put their rods in the water. They each caught a fish!

Mommy and Daddy were so glad. They said, "We must put the rods away now." They put the rods in the car and went home.

The next day, Mommy and Daddy were back at the lake. They had their rods and this time Daddy caught two fishes! Mommy caught one! They were both so glad.

They said, "Let's take the fish home and cook them for dinner." And that's what they did!

Anna and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a big pond with many ducks. The ducks were swimming and quacking. Anna and Ben wanted to feed the ducks. Mom gave them some bread.

"Here, duck, duck, duck!" Anna called. She threw a piece of bread into the water. A yellow duck came and ate it. Anna was happy. She threw another piece.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said. He threw a piece of bread too. But he threw it too far. It landed on the grass. A big white duck saw it and ran to get it. Ben was scared. He hid behind Mom.

"Quack, quack, quack!" The white duck said. It ate the bread and looked at Ben. It had bread crumbs on its beak. It was an impressive duck.

"Hello, duck," Mom said. "You are very hungry. Do you want more bread?" She gave Ben another piece. "Don't be afraid, Ben. The duck is friendly. You can feed it too. Just throw it closer to the water."

Ben nodded. He took the bread and threw it near the pond. The white duck waddled to it and ate it. Ben smiled. He threw another piece. The white duck quacked and ate it too.

"Good job, Ben," Mom said. "You are very brave. And you are very kind to the duck. Do you want to wipe its beak?"

Ben nodded again. He took a napkin and walked to the duck. The duck let him wipe its beak. It was soft and wet. Ben giggled. The duck quacked and nuzzled his hand.

"Thank you, duck," Ben said. "You are very nice. And you are very impressive."

The end.

Sara liked to chew on her crayons. She thought they were yummy and made her tongue different colors. Her mom was a painter and had many paints and brushes in her room. Sara wanted to be a painter too, but she was not allowed to touch the paints.

One day, Sara saw a pink paint can on the floor. It looked like a big crayon. She was curious and sneaky. She took the paint can and ran to her room. She opened the lid and dipped her hand in the paint. It was sticky and wet. She put her hand in her mouth and tried to chew on the paint. It was not yummy. It was yucky and bitter. She spat it out and cried.

"Mommy, mommy, help!" she shouted.

Her mom heard her and ran to her room. She saw Sara with paint all over her face and hands. She saw the paint can on the bed. She was angry and worried.

"Sara, what did you do? That is not a crayon, that is paint! You could get sick from that! Why did you chew on the paint?" she asked.

Sara was sorry and scared. She hugged her mom and said, "I wanted to be a painter like you, mommy. I wanted to make my tongue pink. I didn't know it was bad. I'm sorry, mommy."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "It's okay, Sara. I love you. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Paint is not for eating, it is for painting. Crayons are not for eating either, they are for coloring. Do you understand?"

Sara nodded and said, "Yes, mommy. I understand. I won't chew on paint or crayons anymore. Can I still be a painter?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course you can, Sara. But you have to use the right tools and follow the rules. How about we go to the bathroom and wash you up, and then I'll show you how to use a brush and a canvas?"

Sara smiled and said, "Yes, mommy. Thank you, mommy. I love you, mommy."

They went to the bathroom and cleaned up. Then they went to the painting room and had fun. Sara learned how to paint with a brush and a canvas. She made a beautiful picture of a pink flower. Her mom was proud and happy. She hung the picture on the wall and gave Sara a kiss. Sara was happy too. She decided she liked painting more than chewing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Joy. She was three years old and she loved to explore the world around her. Every day she would go out and explore the park near her house.

Joy was always filled with wonder. She would pick up flowers and leaves and just stare in amazement. She couldn't wait to explore more.

One day, Joy found a perfect rock in the park. Its smooth surface glimmered in the sunlight. Joy loved it and wanted to take it home with her. But when she went to grab it, it jumped right out of her hand!

Confused, Joy watched the rock bounce around, like it was dancing. Then, suddenly it stopped in front of Joy and said, "If you want, you can play with me. Just try and repeat my moves!"

Joy was so excited she started bouncing and twirling around, as the rock showed her how. Before she knew it, Joy was dancing all around the park, having the best time of her life.

There once was a very elderly man named Stanley. He had a bad cough that wouldn't go away. All day long he coughed, and he tried all sorts of different medicines. But nothing helped.

One day, Stanley's friend suggested that he try an unusual remedy. "Put yourself in the freezer for ten minutes", his friend said. Stanley thought this was a strange suggestion, but he was desperate to get better.

So Stanley put himself in his old freezer and stayed there until the timer went off. Amazingly, when he came out, his cough was gone! Stanley was healed!

Stanley was so happy that he quickly ran to tell his friend the good news. His friend smiled and said, "That's one powerful freezer!" Finally, Stanley was free from his cough and could enjoy life again.

Once upon a time, there lived an adventurous bunny. One morning, the bunny decided to spread its wings and soar. With a great spring, it launched straight up into the air and was filled with joy at the view before them.

â€œWow, I can see forever!â€ the bunny said happily as it circled high up in the sky.

On its travels, the bunny spotted something hairy tangled on a branch. The bunny flew down to investigate and saw it was a knot! As the bunny went closer, the knot began to move and it became very clear this was no ordinary knot.

â€œHello,â€ said the knot. â€œMy name is Hank. I am a magic knot and if you untie me I can make your soaring dreams come true.â€

The bunny was surprised but excited at the prospect of flying with its newfound friend.

â€œWhere do we start?â€ asked the bunny. 

â€œWell, first you must untie me!â€ said Hank.

The bunny set to work and eventually untied the knot. Suddenly, the knot began to glow and the bunny felt itself rising higher and higher until it was soaring above the clouds!

â€œThank you for setting me free!â€ said Hank. 

The bunny was filled with joy and flew with Hank through the skies for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a proud pirate. The pirate liked to take long trips in his wooden boat. He searched the sea every day for treasure.

One day, the proud pirate saw something very shiny. He knew it must be treasure. He followed the shiny thing to a small island. He showed the other pirates the wonderful treasure he found.

The other pirates were so happy! They asked the proud pirate to show them how to find more treasure. The proud pirate smiled and said he would.

The proud pirate showed the other pirates how to look for treasure in the sea. They sailed together for many days and found lots of treasure. The proud pirate was very happy. 

The proud pirate promised to show the other pirates new and exciting things as long as they stayed friends. The pirate and his friends went on many more adventures and found lots of treasure! 

They lived happily ever after!

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He had a very hungry tummy and wanted something delicious. He asked his mommy for something to eat. His mommy gave him a tight little container of yogurt. He was very excited. He wanted to eat the yogurt all by himself.

So his mommy gave him a spoon. He held the spoon tight and started to scoop out the yogurt. He was happy, but he also wanted to share the yogurt with his mommy. 

He asked his mommy if he could separate some of the yogurt into two different containers. His mommy said yes, so he found two other containers. He scooped the yogurt into two parts and then he gave one to his mommy.

Jack and his mommy ate the yogurt together. They shared it and it tasted even more delicious! They both enjoyed the special moment.

Once upon a time, there was a duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the lake. Every day, Ducky would swim in the lake and play with his friends.

One day, Ducky saw a big cloud in the sky. He knew that it would rain soon. Ducky didn't want to get hurt by the rain, so he went to his home. Ducky waited for the rain to stop.

After the rain stopped, Ducky went back to the lake. But something was different. The lake had changed. The water was higher and it looked different. Ducky realized that the rain had made the lake change. But he was happy to be back in his favorite place to swim.

Once upon a time, there was a soldier. He was tall and strong, but he felt helpless. He was walking down a road, looking for help. Then, he saw a little boy in the grass.

The soldier asked the boy, "Do you know where I can find help?" The boy said, "Yes!" He showed the soldier a path leading to a big house. 

The soldier thanked the boy and began walking down the path. When he reached the house, he saw that there were many people there and they were all very friendly. They welcomed the soldier and offered him help.

The soldier was so happy that the little boy had shown him the path. Without the boy's help, he would have been helpless. The soldier thanked the boy for being so kind and helpful.

The little boy smiled and waved goodbye to the soldier. Then he skipped away, happy that he had been able to help.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy shark in the bathtub. One day, he tried to whistle a song while playing with his shark.

His mom heard him and said, "Timmy, that's a nice whistle! Are you having fun with your shark?"

Timmy replied, "Yes, Mommy! Shark is so fit and strong. He can swim very fast in the water."

Once there was a girl called Lara who needed to go on a special adventure. She took her brown passport and put it in her bag.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl who everyone liked very much. She had many friends and everyone wanted to play with her.

One day, a happy and enthusiastic girl named Amy was playing outside. She saw a big, shiny comet in the sky. The comet was very bright and pretty. Amy jumped up and down, clapping her hands. She wanted to tell her best friend, Tom, about the comet.

Amy ran to Tom's house and rang the doorbell. "Ring, ring!" The door opened, and Tom came out. Amy said, "Tom, come see the comet in the sky! It's so pretty!" Tom smiled and said, "Okay, Amy, let's go look at the comet together!"

Once upon a time there was a large cactus in the desert. Every day the sun shone down on the cactus. One day, a small bird flew into the cactus and got stuck. The cactus began to tremble! The bird was very scared and did not know what to do.

The lion was so big that its large shadow fell on the trembling cactus. Suddenly, the small bird flew out of the cactus and the lion quickly chased after it.

The cactus stopped trembling and was so relieved. The bird was safe! From then on the bird flew around the cactus, never again getting too close to it.

Once upon a time there was a rich family. The mom and dad were very happy and had a little boy. His name was Tim.
One day, Tim was playing outside and it was very windy. He felt a tickle in his nose and quickly put his hands over his face. Seconds later he sneezed really loud! His mom and dad laughed and gave him a big hug.

When Tim and his mom got home, Tim started to feel the same tickle in his nose he had the previous day. He put his hands over his face and sure enough, he sneezed! His mom laughed and gave him a hug. 

The End!

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big kite in the sky. It was red and yellow and had a long tail. Lily and Sam wanted to fly a kite too.

They did not care that their kite was not like the others. They were happy and proud of their kite. They hoped they could fly it again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a very old lion who lived in the jungle. He was very wise and always reminded all of the other jungle animals about how important it was to be kind and caring.

The journey was a success! The old lion reminded the animals that by being kind and caring to each other, they would make the jungle a better place. The old lion was very happy and the animals listened to him.

Once there was a clever pig. The pig loved to eat oats. He ate oats for his breakfast, lunch and dinner. He was always happy and he liked to be with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a toy car, a toy plane and a toy train. But, Timmy had a bad habit of tearing his toys apart when he got angry.

She also said that we should treat others' things with respect too. From that day on, Timmy learned to take care of his toys and not to tear them apart.

Jane was a brave little girl. She wanted to travel around the world. One day Jane decided to go on an adventure. She walked to the park and saw a big slide. She wanted to go on it. She climbed up the slide and slipped all the way down! Jane had so much fun. Suddenly, she noticed something dead near the slide. It was a bird! Jane was a bit scared, but she bravely continued her journey. She was so happy to travel around the park and experience new things.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Lucy and Sam. They were both very independent. One day, Lucy invited Sam to her house for an exciting surprise. 

When Sam arrived, he saw the inside of Lucy's house was full of jewelry! He asked Lucy, "Where did all the jewelry come from?"

Lucy replied, "My mom gave me jewelry for being so independent!" 

Sam was so impressed that he thought to himself, "My Mom never gifts me jewelry. Maybe if I acted more independent I'll also get jewelry like Lucy!"

The moral of the story is that good behavior is always rewarded. If you do things that make your parents proud, they will find special ways to show their love and appreciation.

Once upon a time, there was a poor dog named Max. Max was very sad because he had no home. He lived in a park and looked for food in the trash. One day, Max saw a cart with many toys. The cart was near a big store. Max thought the toys could make him happy.

Once upon a time there was a small boy called Jack. He had a neighbor called Bill. Jack and Bill didn't always get along as Bill could be quite grumpy. 

One day, Jack had a great idea. He was going to have a competition with Bill to see who could win! All the kids on the street were invited to join in the challenge.

Jack and Bill faced each other and each of them was given an orange. The challenge was to see who could squeeze the most juice out of their orange the fastest. 

The kids all cheered as Jack started to squeeze his orange with all of his might. Jack was squeezing so hard that the orange couldn't take it anymore and his orange exploded!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw pictures with crayons. One day, he drew a picture of a giraffe. The giraffe had a long neck and spots all over its body. Timmy was very proud of his original drawing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends saw a butterfly with colorful wings. They all ran after the butterfly, trying to catch it. But the butterfly flew away and they lost it.

Lily's friend, Timmy, raised a question, "How can we catch the butterfly?"

The moral of the story is that if you want something, you have to work for it. And sometimes, you have to think of creative solutions to achieve your goals.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big bush with red berries on it. They ran to the bush and picked some berries.

"These berries are cool and sweet," Lily said. "Let's eat them all!"

"No, we should not eat them all," Ben said. "Maybe some birds or animals want some berries too. We should share."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She wanted to eat all the berries. She pushed Ben away from the bush and grabbed more berries.

"Go away, Ben! These are my berries!" she shouted.

Ben was sad and angry. He did not like Lily's push. He walked away from the bush and looked for another place to play.

Soon, Lily felt sick. She ate too many berries and her tummy hurt. She wanted to find Ben and say sorry, but she did not know where he was. She was alone and scared.

She saw a bird flying over the bush. The bird saw the berries and wanted some too. The bird flew down and pecked at the berries. But Lily did not want to share. She tried to push the bird away, but the bird was faster and stronger. The bird pecked at Lily's hand and made it bleed.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lily cried. "That hurts! Go away, bird!"

But the bird did not go away. The bird called more birds and they all came to the bush. They pecked at the berries and at Lily. Lily was in pain and in trouble.

She wished she had listened to Ben. She wished she had shared the berries. She wished she had not pushed Ben away.

Moral: Sharing is caring. Pushing is mean.

One day, Jack went fishing with his dad. Jack loved to go fishing. His dad gave him a gentle fishing rod and told him to stir the water with it. Once upon a time, there was a sheep who had been getting a bit dull and grey. She was called Pat, and her wool was not as soft and fluffy as it used to be. She was feeling rather sad, and wasn't sure how to make things better.

One day, she decided to take a walk to ask someone for help. As she passed a field of tiny lambs, one of them stopped, looking up at Pat with their bright eyes. Pat explained how she was feeling dull and grey, and the lamb said "I think I know what you need! A bit of sun will help you sparkle up again. It will increase your energy!"

Pat was excited! She took a nap in a spot she felt sure was full of sunlight for the rest of the day. She woke feeling energized and her wool was soft and fluffy again. From that day forward, Pat made sure to take a sunbathing break each day, so her wool would never go dull again.

Bob was a person. He wanted to do something, but he was anxious. He was afraid he wouldn't do it right. He took a deep breath and tried. He was a little wobbly at first, but he kept trying. Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big bird in the sky. It was black and white and had a long neck. It was a swan.

"I want to soar like a swan," Lily said. "Can we do that, Tom?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had an idea. He took Lily's hand and ran to the swings. He helped her sit on one and pushed her gently. Lily felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She smiled and laughed.

"Tom, I'm soaring!" Lily said. "I feel like a swan!"

Tom smiled and joined her on the other swing. They swung higher and higher, back and forth. They felt free and happy.

They saw the swan fly over them. It honked softly and waved its wing. Tom and Lily waved back. They felt like they were friends with the swan.

They swung until they were tired. Then they slowed down and stopped. They got off the swings and hugged each other.

Once upon a time, there was a green slide. Every day it waited to be used, but no one ever did. Until one day, a little girl arrived. She was so excited when she saw the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her crayons. One day, she drew a fierce dragon with big teeth and a long tail. She was so proud of her drawing that she stared at it for a long time.

The end

Once upon a time, in a big brown house, there lived a little girl named Mia. Mia had a dog named Spot. Spot was very sick and Mia wanted to heal him.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to run around and play outside. One day, Max saw a big machine that could print things. Max thought it was funny how the machine made pictures on paper.

Once upon a time, there lived a small boy called Jack. He was 3 years old and he loved to explore the world. One day, Jack went out on an adventure. He went to a park where he could play and have fun.

One sunny day, Tom arrived at the park on his motorcycle. He saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was sad. Her ball was stuck in a tall tree.

"Can you help me?" asked Lily. "My ball is stuck!"

Tom smiled and said, "Don't worry, I will help you!" Tom was very strong. He shook the tree with his big hands. The ball fell down.

Lily was very happy. She said, "Thank you, Tom!" They played catch together and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play baseball with his friends. One day, Timmy hit the baseball so hard that it soared high into the sky! Timmy was so happy and proud.

But then, Timmy's friend Billy said, "Uh oh, Timmy. Look behind you." Timmy turned around and saw that his mom was watching him play. Timmy felt embarrassed because he thought he looked silly swinging his bat so hard.

But Timmy's mom said, "Don't be embarrassed, Timmy. You did a great job hitting the ball so high. I'm proud of you." Timmy felt happy again and continued to play baseball with his friends. They all had so much fun together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jimmy. He was three years old and loved to imagine. One morning he thought of something extra special. He imagined a magic spell!

Jimmy knew that spells were very powerful and he wanted to make one of his own. He started to think about what kind of spell he would make. Suddenly he had an idea!

He told his mom that he wanted to go outside and find some lovely things. She bundled him up and Jimmy went off. He searched around the garden and soon his bag was full of flowers, rocks, leaves and even a slimy worm.

Next, Jimmy found a corner of the garden that was extra filthy. It was full of mud and bugs. He found some crumbly dirt and scooped it up. He tucked it inside his bag and scurried home.

Back in his bedroom, Jimmy carefully poured the crumbly dirt onto the floor and began to form the letters of a spell with it. He imagined that someday this spell might make things better! Finally he said the magic words and the spell was cast.

Jimmy clapped his hands in joy. He had made a real, honest-to-goodness spell!

Once upon a time, there was a messy robot. People imagined how wonderful it would be to have a robot living with them. So, the people built the robot.

When the robot was finished, it looked so messy! Its wires, lines and parts were all jumbled up. Nobody knew what to do, so the robot just stayed messy.

One day, a little girl named Louise saw the robot. She wanted to help the robot be tidy. So, she spent time cleaning it, sorting the lines and putting its parts in the right places.

When Louise was finished, the robot was so neat! Everyone was so proud of Louise and they all celebrated with big smiles on their faces.

The robot will always remember the messy and neat moments with Louise and her friends.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was very excited when she heard the bell. It was big, noisy and bright. Jane wanted to see what was making all of the noise. She ran out her front door and to the end of the street. 

She saw a big truck with a big bell on top. It was so exciting for Jane. She waved and shouted to the driver of the truck, "Hey, can I ride in your truck?" 

The truck driver smiled and said, "Yes, of course! Hop on in." Jane was so thrilled to get a ride in the noisy but fun truck. She waved goodbye to her family and went off with the truck driver. 

The truck drove around the town and beeped the bell every time it stopped. Jane was so happy and excited to see all the wonderful things the town had to offer. Every time the bell sounded it made Jane happier and louder. 

The truck driver dropped Jane off at her house, honking the big bell goodbye. Jane thanked the driver and ran inside to tell her parents all about her exciting ride in the noisy bell truck.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Bob. Bob loved to sit on a twig in his incredible tree. The tree was very big and had lots of leaves.

One day, Bob saw a small cat named Tom. Tom was sad because he could not sit on a twig like Bob. Bob wanted to help Tom and be a good friend.

Bob had an idea. He found a strong twig for Tom to sit on. Tom was so happy and they both sat on their twigs together. The moral of the story is to always help your friends and share what you have.

The sun was shining brightly, and the birds were singing sweetly. It was a beautiful day for a walk.

Tom and his friends were walking down the path towards the ranch. They were all excited to see what was at the ranch.

When they arrived, they saw a big, red ranch. It was tall and had a lot of animals. They saw chickens, cows and horses. It was very exciting.

Tom went to the door and knocked. A tall man with a hat opened the door. He was a rich rancher. He welcomed them inside.

The rancher showed them around. They got to pet the horses and chickens. They also got to try some of the ranch's food. It was delicious!

When they were done, the rancher gave them each a special treat. He told them he was removing some of his animals and wanted them to have a nice gift for helping him. The kids were so excited and thanked him for the gifts.

Tom and his friends waved goodbye to the rancher and happily walked back home. It was a perfect day!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He liked to climb trees and play with his toys. One day, Timmy saw a bright staff on the ground. 

"Wow, that's a cool stick!" Timmy said.

"It's not a stick, it's a staff," said his mom.

"What's a staff?" asked Timmy.

"It's like a long stick that grown-ups use," said his mom.

Timmy picked up the staff and pretended to be a wizard. He waved the staff around and said, "Abracadabra!" Suddenly, he felt like he could climb even higher in the trees. "Look, Mom, I'm climbing higher than ever before!" Timmy exclaimed.

"That's because you have a magic staff," said his mom with a smile.

From that day on, Timmy always brought his bright staff with him when he went outside to play. He loved pretending to be a wizard and climbing trees with his magic staff.

Jen and Ben were twins who liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like hats and books and toys. One day, they saw a big chest in the corner. It was covered with dust and had a lock on it.

"Let's open it!" Jen said. "Maybe there is a treasure inside!"

"But how?" Ben asked. "We don't have a key."

Jen looked around and saw a small hole in the wall. She peeked inside and saw something shiny. She reached in and pulled out a key.

"Look, Ben, I found a key!" she whispered. "Maybe it fits the chest!"

They ran to the chest and tried the key. It turned and clicked. They lifted the lid and gasped. Inside, there was a beautiful dress, a pair of shoes, a necklace and a crown. They were all made of ice and sparkled in the light.

"Wow, they are so pretty!" Jen said. "Can I try them on?"

"OK, but be careful," Ben said. "They look very icy and cold."

Jen put on the dress, the shoes, the necklace and the crown. She felt like a princess. She twirled and danced in the attic. Ben clapped and cheered.

Suddenly, they heard a loud voice from downstairs.

"Jen! Ben! Time for lunch!" their mom called.

"Uh-oh, we have to go," Ben said. "Quick, put the things back in the chest!"

Jen nodded and took off the dress, the shoes, the necklace and the crown. She put them back in the chest and closed the lid. They ran downstairs, leaving the chest behind.

They never told anyone about their icy secret. But sometimes, they would go back to the attic and play with the ice things again. They wondered who made them and why they were in the chest. But they never found out. They just enjoyed their magic.

Lily liked to create things with her play-dough. She made balls, snakes, flowers and cakes. She was very proud of her creations and showed them to her mom and dad.

One day, she wanted to make something new. She looked around the kitchen and saw a big piece of beef on the counter. It was warm and red and smelled good. Lily thought it would be fun to make a play-dough beef. She took some brown play-dough and shaped it like the beef. She put some green play-dough on top to make parsley. She smiled and put her play-dough beef next to the real beef.

But then, her big brother Tom came into the kitchen. He was hungry and wanted a snack. He saw the two pieces of beef and thought they were both real. He grabbed the play-dough beef and took a big bite. He spat it out and made a face. He was angry and yelled at Lily.

"Lily, this is not beef, this is play-dough! You tricked me! You are a bad sister!"

Lily was scared and sad. She did not mean to trick Tom. She just wanted to create something new. She started to cry and ran to her mom.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the play-dough beef and the real beef and understood what happened. She hugged Lily and comforted her.

"Lily, it's okay. You did not do anything wrong. You were just playing and being creative. Tom did not know it was play-dough. He was just hungry and made a mistake. He is sorry, right Tom?"

Tom felt bad for making Lily cry. He realized she was not a bad sister. He was just a silly brother. He apologized to Lily and gave her a hug.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to yell at you. You are a good sister. You are very creative. Can I play with your play-dough too?"

Lily smiled and nodded. She forgave Tom and shared her play-dough with him. They played together and made more things. They had fun and were happy. Mom smiled and watched them. She was proud of her children. She put the real beef in the oven and made a warm and yummy dinner for them.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. Every day, they would fill a bucket with water from the well and carry it back to their house.

One day, Lily woke up early and saw that it was a beautiful day outside. She wanted to play in the sun, but her parents had to work hard to fill the bucket with water. Lily felt sad because she wanted to help them, but she was too little.

Suddenly, Lily had an idea! She ran to her mommy and daddy and asked if she could help fill the bucket with water. They were surprised but happy that she wanted to help. Together, they filled the bucket quickly and had the rest of the day to play in the sun. Lily felt proud that she could help her family.

Pam was playing with her toys when her mum came into the room. She had something special with her; a box of tape. It had been difficult for Pam's mum to find, but she had finally found it.

Pam was so excited and started to yell at her mum, "What can I do with it?"

Mum smiled and said, "This tape can fix things that have broken. For example, if you have broken a toy, we can try and use the tape to stick it together."

Pam thought this was the best thing ever, so she looked around to find something to fix. She soon found an old truck with a broken wheel and showed it to her mum. They carefully tried to use the tape to stick the wheel back on. It was difficult, but it worked in the end.

Pam was very happy. She hugged her mum and thanked her for bringing her the tape. From then on, Pam found lots of things to fix with the tape.

Once upon a time, there was a king who lived in a big palace. He had a lot of treasure, but he was very sad. One day, he decided to bury his treasure in the ground so nobody could take it. He dug a big hole and put all his treasure inside. 

After he buried his treasure, he felt even more miserable. He missed his treasure and wished he had it back. But he knew he couldn't dig it up again, so he decided to make the best of what he had left. 

He invited his friends to come and play with him in his palace. They played games, ate food, and had fun together. The king realized that even though he didn't have his treasure, he had something even more valuable - his friends. From that day on, he wasn't so miserable anymore.

John was excited about his first day of summer camp. He told his mom that he wanted to go on a very special adventure. 

The next morning, he took the bus to the summer camp site. He looked around and saw lots of kids playing and holding smelly marshmallows.

John was excited to start. They had lots of stories to tell and he wanted to hear them all. But then John heard that the camp counselors wanted everyone to go to a special place that afternoon.

John wondered what this special place could be. He was curious. 

When they arrived, John couldn't believe his eyes. It was a river where kids could swim! He told the counselors that he wanted to jump in right away.

John had so much fun that he didn't even notice the smelly mud near the edge of the river. He quickly made lots of new friends. 

John learned from his first day at summer camp that if you are curious, you never know what new adventures you can find!

Once upon a time there was an animal named Willy. He was a small white rabbit. Every day he liked to go outside and play. On this day, Willy wanted to try something new. He decided to throw a rock. He picked up the rock and threw it as far as he could. 

Suddenly, he heard a strong voice. "Stop! What are you doing?" Willy looked around but he couldn't see anyone. He turned to the sky and saw an eagle circling above him. It was the eagle's voice that he heard. 

Willy was surprised. He had never seen an eagle up close before. "What are you doing?" asked the eagle again. Willy replied that he was just throwing a rock. The eagle nodded and told him to be careful. 

Willy thanked the eagle and watched as it flew away. He was glad to have heard the strong voice of the eagle. From then on, Willy knew to be careful when throwing things. The end.

Once there was a kid named Lucy. She was three. One day, she wanted to wear her new pants. But Mommy said no. Lucy was very sad. She started to cry and insisted on wearing her new pants.

Mommy said no again, but Lucy still insisted. When Daddy saw that, he said that if Lucy was quiet, he might let her wear her new pants. 

So Lucy stayed very quiet. She also gave Mommy a big hug. Mommy said okay, and Lucy put on her new pants! She was so happy! 

She twirled around and showed everyone her new pants. Everyone was so proud of her and they all cheered. Lucy was so proud to be allowed to wear her new pants.

Tommy was so excited! He had waited a long time for today. Outside, the sun was shining and everything was so colorful. Today, he was getting a new bed. As he walked home, he could hardly contain his joy.

When he arrived, his new bed was waiting for him. It had thick covers and pillows. Best of all, it had a slide! Tommy couldn't wait to try it out. He ran around the bed, admiring it.

His mother showed him how to use the slide. First, he had to climb up the ladder to the top of the bed. Then, he had to sit down at the end of the slide. And finally, he had to push off.

Tommy practiced a few times, getting the hang of how to slide down the bed's slide. The more he practiced, the farther he could go. Soon he was sliding down the slide faster and further than ever before! 

The slide was so much fun. Tommy laughed and cheered with joy. The thick bed and slide made him feel like a special kid. He was so happy and thankful to have such a cool bed.

Sammy was walking in the park. He looked around and was so excited to see how colorful it was. Everywhere he looked he saw grass that was different colors! 

He took big steps to try and get a closer look. Under each step he took, he crushed the grass and could feel how soft it was. 

As he kept walking, he started to come across different kinds of bugs. Some of the bugs were green and some were yellow. He was so delighted to see all the colorful bugs playing around in the grass! 

He kept stepping and coming across more and more fun things to explore. He was the happiest he'd ever been!

Once there was a mommy and a little girl. The little girl was very adorable and loved to take care of her special plant. Every morning she would give it water and talk to it. 

One day the mommy had to go away for a few days so she asked the little girl to keep her plant safe. The little girl promised to keep it safe and gave her plant a big hug goodbye.

When the mommy came back, she was so surprised to see the little girl's special plant. It had grown so big and had so many beautiful flowers. The little girl was so proud of her plant and the mommy was amazed by how much the little girl had cared for it. 

The mommy couldn't believe how much the little girl had grown. She was so sweet, so determined, and kept her promise to keep her plant safe. The mommy and little girl hugged and laughed together, admiring the adorable plant.

Kelsey and her best friend Jamie were having so much fun at the playground. When their parents came to pick them up, Kelsey had an idea. She wanted to have a sleepover under a tent! Her Mom and Dad said yes, so the two friends jumped up and down with excitement. 

Kelsey's Mom and Dad quickly set up the tent in the backyard. Then, they all said goodnight and Jamie and Kelsey went inside. Inside the tent, there was a special secret. But Kelsey and Jamie couldn't find it! 

They searched high and low and got frustrated. Then, Jamie found a zipper on the bottom of the tent. She pulled it up and separated the two sides of the tent. Suddenly, they saw the special secret! 

Kelsey and Jamie both screamed in excitement. It was a big bag of games, books and snacks. All night they played, read, and ate snacks. They had so much fun, they didn't want the night to ever end!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Max. He was three years old and always wanted to do something special. One day, he noticed a poem on the wall. It was in big, colourful letters and he liked the way it looked. He decided that he wanted to make one too.

Max grabbed a piece of paper and a pencil. He started writing. He tried to make a poem, but it was too hard! He got bored and it seemed like it was never going to be right. 

Suddenly, he had an idea. He got his favourite toy, a drum, and started to make a beat. He started to follow the beat as he walked around the room. Max repeated the beat again and again - it was like a poem!

Max was excited and smiled as he kept repeating the beat. He knew he was really onto something special. With every strike of the drum he made it more and more exciting.

Max was very proud of his work. He knew it was the best poem ever made and that it was more than just a boring poem. He knew that he had created something truly special and it would last forever.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to be spies and catch a thief who was stealing cookies from the kitchen. They put on their spy hats and glasses and prepared a trap. They tied a string to a chair and hid behind the sofa.

"Shh, we have to be quiet and wait for the thief," Ben whispered to Lily.

"I hope he comes soon, I'm hungry," Lily whispered back.

They waited and waited until they heard a noise. It was their big brother Tom, who sneaked into the kitchen and opened the cookie jar. He reached for a cookie, but as he did, he pulled the string and the chair fell on him with a loud bang.

"Ow, what was that?" Tom shouted.

"We got you, thief! You are under arrest!" Ben and Lily jumped out and pointed their fingers at him.

"Thief? What are you talking about? I was just having a snack," Tom said.

"You were stealing our cookies, we saw you," Lily said.

"No, I wasn't, these are my cookies too," Tom said.

"No, they are not, they are ours, we made them with Mom," Ben said.

They argued and argued until Mom came in and saw the mess.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked.

"Mom, Tom is a thief, he stole our cookies," Ben and Lily said.

"Mom, they are spies, they set a trap for me," Tom said.

Mom looked at them and smiled. She knew they were just playing, but she also had a surprise for them.

"Actually, you are all wrong. These are not your cookies, they are mine. I made them for a special occasion. Do you know what today is?" Mom asked.

They thought for a moment and then realized.

"It's your birthday, Mom!" they said.

"Yes, it is. And these are my birthday cookies. But I'm happy to share them with you, if you promise to clean up this mess and give me a hug," Mom said.

They agreed and hugged Mom. They said sorry to each other and helped Mom clean up. Then they ate the cookies and sang happy birthday to Mom. They had an amazing day.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide.

"Let me go first!" Tom says. He runs to the slide. He climbs up the ladder. He sits on the slide. He slides down fast. He laughs.

"Wow, that looks cool!" Sue says. She runs to the slide. She climbs up the ladder. She sits on the slide. She slides down fast. She smiles.

They take turns on the slide. They have fun. They slide down many times.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a fire truck. It has a siren and a horn. It comes to the park. It stops near the slide.

"What is that?" Tom asks. He is scared.

"It is a fire truck. It helps people when there is a fire." Sue says. She is curious.

They see some firemen. They wear helmets and coats. They have hoses and axes. They go to the exit of the park. They see some smoke. There is a fire in a house.

"Look, they are going to put out the fire." Sue says. She points to the firemen.

"Can we watch?" Tom asks. He wants to see the firemen.

"No, we have to stay away. It is not safe." Sue says. She knows the fire is dangerous.

They go to the bench. They sit on the bench. They watch the firemen from far away. They hope everyone is okay. They are glad the firemen are here. They think the firemen are cool.

Once upon a time there was a persistent little bird. The bird liked to wear its yellow feathers proudly. Every day it would go searching for food. 

One day, the bird wanted to find some wheat to eat. It looked and looked but couldn't find any wheat. It kept searching and searching, everywhere it could look.

Suddenly, the bird noticed a wheat field. It quickly flew down and started eating the wheat. It ate and ate, until it was full and happy.

The bird thanked the wheat for giving it food and flew away, wearing all its bright yellow feathers. From then on, the bird was always persistent in its hunt for food. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Claire. She was very brave and powerful. One day, she was playing in her yard when she saw a patient sitting on the grass. The patient was crying and seemed very sad. She went over to the patient and asked, "What's wrong?"

The patient told Claire that she had fallen from her bed earlier that day. Claire was determined to help the patient, so she put her powerful hands on the patient's back and tried to lift them off the ground. But the patient was too heavy.

Claire thought and thought. She decided that the only way she could help the patient was to get help from her mom and dad. She ran into her home and called her parents. Then they all helped the patient back onto her bed.

The patient thanked Claire and said, "You are a very brave and powerful girl!" Claire smiled. She was happy she was able to help.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the garden. They had a big ball, a small bike and a hop rope. They liked to hop on the rope and see who could hop more times. One day, they saw a glass on the table near the door. It was Mom's glass. She liked to drink water from it.

"Look, a glass!" said Ben. "Let's hop with it!"

"No, Ben, that's Mom's glass. She will be mad if we take it," said Lily.

But Ben did not listen. He took the glass and ran to the garden. He started to hop with the glass in his hand. He thought it was fun.

Lily followed him and said, "Ben, stop! You will drop the glass and break it!"

But Ben did not stop. He hopped and hopped until he tripped on a stone. The glass fell from his hand and broke into many pieces. Ben was scared. He saw the glass was messy and sharp. He cut his finger on a piece. He cried.

Lily ran to him and said, "Ben, are you okay? Let me see your finger."

She saw the blood and said, "We need to tell Mom. She will help you."

They went to the door and saw Mom. She was angry and sad. She saw the broken glass and Ben's finger.

"Ben, what did you do? Why did you take my glass? You could have hurt yourself and Lily. That was very naughty and dangerous," she said.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I wanted to hop with the glass. It was fun. But I dropped it and broke it. And I cut my finger. It hurts," said Ben.

Mom hugged him and said, "I'm glad you are sorry, Ben. But you need to learn to listen to Lily and me. We tell you things for your own good. And you need to respect other people's things. You can't take them without asking. That's not nice. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom. I understand. I won't do it again. I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Mom," said Ben.

Mom cleaned his finger and put a band-aid on it. She said, "It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you need to be more careful and responsible. And you need to help me clean up the mess. Can you do that?"

"Yes, Mom. I can do that," said Ben.

He and Lily helped Mom pick up the pieces of glass and throw them away. They said sorry to Mom again and gave her a hug. Mom smiled and said, "I love you, Ben and Lily. You are good kids. But please, don't hop with glass again. Hop with the rope. It's safer and more fun."

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They saw a big white dog near the fence. The dog looked friendly and wagged its tail.

"Let's go and pet the dog!" Lily said. She liked animals and wanted to make a new friend.

Ben was not sure. He was afraid of big dogs. He remembered when a dog bit his cousin and made him cry. "No, Lily, we should not. Mommy said to stay away from strange dogs. They might be mean or sick."

But Lily did not listen. She urged Ben to come with her. She said the dog was nice and would not hurt them. She ran to the fence and called the dog. The dog came closer and licked her hand.

"See, Ben, he likes me! He is so soft and warm. Come and pet him too!" Lily said.

Ben was still scared, but he did not want to make Lily sad. He was grateful that she was his friend and always shared her toys with him. He walked slowly to the fence and reached out his hand.

But the dog did not like Ben. He growled and barked and showed his teeth. He jumped and bit Ben's arm. Ben screamed and fell to the ground. He was bleeding and hurting.

Lily was shocked and scared. She did not know what to do. She cried and shouted for help.

A man came and pulled the dog away. He said he was sorry and that the dog was not his. He said he found the dog on the street and thought he was lost. He said he would call an ambulance and the police.

Lily and Ben were taken to the hospital. Ben had to get stitches and shots. He was very brave, but he was also very angry. He did not want to talk to Lily. He said she was stupid and mean and that he hated her.

Lily was very sorry and sad. She did not mean to hurt Ben. She just wanted to pet the dog. She wished she had listened to Ben and stayed away from the dog. She wished she could say sorry and make Ben her friend again. But Ben did not want to hear her. He turned his head and closed his eyes.

Once there was a little boy and he wanted to learn. He went to the chest every day and found something new to learn. One day he found a lesson that was very harsh. He tried and tried to learn the lesson, but it seemed too difficult. Then he remembered something his teacher said. She said, "Sometimes when something seems too hard, take a break and come back to it later. You will find it suddenly becomes easier." 
So he decided to take a break and came back to the lesson the next day. To his surprise, the lesson was not so harsh anymore and he was able to learn it quickly! He was so relieved and happy to have learnt the lesson. From then on, he made sure to take breaks when things seemed too difficult so that he could easily learn new things.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim had a hurt wing and could not fly. Tim was frustrated because he wanted to play with his friends in the sky. Tim's mom told him that his wing would heal soon. Tim felt a little better.

One day, Tim saw a man walking with a message. The man looked lost. Tim wanted to help the man. So, Tim hopped and hopped to show the man the way. The man followed Tim and found his way. The man was very happy and thanked Tim.

Tim felt proud that he could help the man, even with his hurt wing. As the days passed, Tim's wing healed. He could fly again and play with his friends in the sky. Tim was happy and never forgot the time he helped the man with the message.

Anna and Ben were going on a trip with their mom and dad. They had a lot of luggage to pack in the car. Anna had a small pink suitcase with her toys and clothes. Ben had a big blue suitcase with his books and games. Mom and dad had two enormous suitcases with everything else.

"Are we ready to go?" dad asked.

"Yes, we are!" Anna and Ben said.

They got in the car and drove to the airport. They were very excited to see the planes and the clouds. They checked in their luggage and got their boarding passes. They walked to the gate and waited for their flight.

"Look, there's our plane!" Ben pointed.

"It's so big!" Anna said.

They followed mom and dad to the plane and found their seats. They buckled their seat belts and listened to the pilot. The plane started to move and then went up in the air.

"Wow, we're flying!" Anna and Ben said.

They looked out the window and saw the sky and the land. They played with their toys and books and ate some snacks. They had a lot of fun.

But then, something bad happened. The pilot said there was a problem with the plane and they had to land right away. Anna and Ben were scared. They held mom and dad's hands and prayed.

The plane landed safely on a field. Everyone was okay, but the plane was broken. The pilot said they had to wait for another plane to come and pick them up. They got out of the plane and took their luggage.

"Where are we?" Anna asked.

"I don't know, sweetie. Somewhere far away," mom said.

They saw some people and animals coming to see them. They looked different from them. They spoke a different language. They wore different clothes. They were curious and friendly.

"Hello, who are you?" one of them asked.

"Hello, we are Anna and Ben and mom and dad. We were flying to see grandma and grandpa, but our plane broke down. We're sorry to bother you," dad said.

"You're not bothering us. You're welcome here. We're sorry for your trouble. We're here to help you. Come, we have a place for you to stay and some food for you to eat," one of them said.

They followed them to a village. They saw some houses and farms and schools and shops. They saw some children playing and laughing. They saw some adults working and singing. They saw some animals running and jumping. They smelled some flowers and fruits and bread. They felt some warmth and kindness and peace.

"Wow, this is a nice place!" Ben said.

"Yes, it is!" Anna said.

They thanked the people for their hospitality. They shared their luggage with them. They gave them some toys and books and clothes. They received some gifts and hugs and smiles. They learned some words and songs and games. They made some friends and memories and stories.

They waited for the other plane to come and save them. They were happy and grateful and hopeful. They were not afraid anymore. They were not alone anymore. They were part of a new family.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor named Jack. Jack loved to play with his boat in the water. He would sail and sail until the sun went down. 

One day, Jack met a little girl named Lily. She thought Jack's boat was very interesting. "Can I play with your boat?" she asked. "Of course!" Jack replied. 

So, Lily and Jack played with the boat together. They sailed and sailed until they reached a beautiful island. "Wow, this is so interesting!" Lily exclaimed. Jack smiled and said, "I love sailing to new places and making new friends." 

From that day on, Jack and Lily would often play together with the boat. They sailed to many interesting places and had lots of fun. The end.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his dad. They brought a toy bow and arrow to play with. Tim was very excited to play with his new toy. He held the bow and arrow in his hands, feeling very happy.
