Once upon a time there was a girl named Chloe. She loved to play outside. She brought her toy and went to the park.

Today, the sky was very clear. The sun was shining bright, but there was a tall tree that gave Chloe shade.

Chloe liked the shade. It was cool and cozy. She found a big blanket and wrapped herself in it. She giggled and smiled. She was happy and comfortable.

Soon, she fell asleep in the shade. She dreamed of things she wanted to do in the park. When Chloe woke up, she was ready to play!

One day a little girl was walking in the park. She saw something shiny and red on the ground. She went over to take a look and saw that it was a big, shiny apple! She was so excited and picked it up. 

She brushed off the dirt and brushed it against her jeans. Then the girl bit into the apple, but it tasted very sour. She stuck out her tongue and made a face. She decided to throw the apple away and it went flying into the bushes. 

Suddenly a big dog appeared in the bushes! The dog ran out and quickly grabbed the apple. He wagged his tail and ran away with it. 

The little girl was surprised! She watched the dog run away with the dirty apple. She smiled and went on her way.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly building. It had tall walls, no windows, and no colors. No one ever stopped to look at the building. Everyone thought it was too ugly to look at.

One day, a little bird saw the building. It flew up to it and started to dance. She flapped her wings, sang a song, and spun around.

The other birds in the sky were amazed. They had never seen anyone dance around an ugly building before! They joined the little bird and soon the sky was filled with music and dances.

The citizens of the town looked up. They saw the birds and the ugly building, filled with light and life. Seeing the birds made the citizens realize that the building wasn't so ugly after all.

The moral of the story is that everyone has something to offer and beauty is in the eye of the beholder. You never know what someone or something can come to mean to you until you take the time to look.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and often got scared of the dark. 

One night, Lucy was lying in bed when she heard a voice. It said "Choose one note and you will get your reward". Lucy was fearful, so she decided to go take a look. 

When she reached the hallway, she saw a pile of notes on the floor. Then the voice said again "Choose one note!"

Lucy carefully picked up one note and said "This one!" The voice replied "Very well, here is your reward". 

Suddenly, a bright light filled the hall. Lucy was no longer scared, because she knew that the mysterious voice was there to protect her.

Once upon a time there was an ugly toast. He was very sad because no one wanted to eat him. Everywhere he went, people shied away from him. 

One day, a little boy named Sam saw the toast. He thought the toast looked delicious and he wanted to help. 

So, Sam and his mom worked together to make the toast special. They decorated it with butter and jam. 

When it was ready, Sam received the toast. He was so excited. He bit into the toast and it tasted amazing. 

From that day forward, the ugly toast became a happy toast! Everyone wanted to eat him now and he was not sad anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear was very sleepy. He yawned a big yawn. He walked into the deep woods to find a nice spot to sleep.

In the woods, the bear saw a peach tree. The tree had many big, yummy peaches. The bear said, "I want to eat the peaches before I sleep." So, he picked some peaches and ate them. They were so sweet!

A little bird saw the bear eating the peaches. The bird flew to the bear and said, "Can I have a peach too?" The bear said, "Yes, you can have one." The bird and the bear ate the peaches together. Then, they both yawned and went to sleep under the peach tree.

Once upon a time, there was a big, expensive train. The train loved to go fast on its track. It went through the town every day. The people in the town liked to watch the train go by.

One day, the sky was dark and it started to pour. The rain came down very hard. The train still wanted to go fast on its track, even in the rain. The people in the town told the train to be careful, but the train did not listen.

The train went too fast on the wet track. It slipped and fell off the track. The train was very sad and could not go fast anymore. The people in the town were sad too. The train had to stay still and not move because it was broken.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sally. Sally liked to laugh, but had a hard time understanding the language of the people around her. One day, Sally was walking around her neighborhood when she saw a great big tree. She ran up to the tree and started to jump around it, laughing.

Suddenly, a little bird flew down from the tree and landed on a nearby branch. The bird looked at Sally and spoke in a strange language that Sally didn't understand. Sally was very surprised and just stared at the bird. 

The bird noticed Sally's confusion, so he started speaking in a different language. He said, "Why do you look so sad? Let's have a laugh!"

Sally was excited and she clapped her hands in joy. She looked at the bird and began to laugh. The bird laughed too. It was a bitter laugh, but Sally thought the bird was funny and kept laughing. 

After a while, Sally was able to understand some of the little bird's language. They became best friends and chatted all the time, laughing together. From that day on, they were the happiest friends in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved wearing her favorite red skirt every day. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she saw a cute puppy and wanted to pet it. But the puppy bit her on the hand, and it hurt a lot. 

Lily cried out in pain, and her friends rushed to her side. "What happened?" they asked. "The puppy bit me," Lily said, showing them her hand. "Oh no," her friends said, feeling sorry for her. 

Lily's mom took her to the hospital, and the doctor gave her some medicine. But even with the medicine, her hand still hurt. She couldn't wear her favorite red skirt anymore because it hurt to put it on. Lily was sad that she couldn't wear her favorite skirt, but she knew she had to take care of her hand. And so, she learned to love another skirt just as much, even though it wasn't red.

Tommy liked to play with his toy truck. It was red and shiny and had big wheels. It was his favorite toy and he did not like to share it. He always said, "This is mine, mine, mine!"

One day, Tommy went to the park with his mom and his truck. He saw some other kids playing with sand and buckets. He wanted to join them, but he did not want to leave his truck. He decided to take his truck with him and squeeze it in his hand.

He walked over to the kids and said, "Hi, can I play with you?" The kids looked at him and smiled. They said, "Sure, you can play with us. What do you have in your hand?"

Tommy felt shy and did not want to show them his truck. He squeezed it harder and said, "Nothing, nothing, nothing!"

But the kids were curious and wanted to see his truck. They tried to pull his hand open, but Tommy resisted. He said, "No, no, no! This is mine, mine, mine!"

The kids did not like Tommy's attitude and started to tease him. They said, "What are you hiding? Is it a baby toy? Are you a baby?"

Tommy felt embarrassed and angry. He did not like to be called a baby. He did not like to be teased. He did not like to share his truck. He started to cry and ran back to his mom.

His mom saw him crying and hugged him. She asked him, "What's wrong, Tommy? Why are you crying?"

Tommy told her what happened and showed her his truck. He said, "They were mean to me. They wanted to see my truck, but I did not want to show them. It is mine, mine, mine!"

His mom kissed him and said, "I know you love your truck, Tommy, but sometimes it is nice to share with others. Sharing can make you and your friends happy. Maybe you can try to share your truck next time and see how it feels."

Tommy thought about what his mom said. He felt a little sorry for being rude to the kids. He wondered if they would still want to play with him. He decided to give sharing a try. He said, "Okay, mom, I will try to share my truck next time. Maybe they will like it too."

His mom smiled and said, "That's a good idea, Tommy. I'm proud of you. Now, let's go and have some fun at the park."

Mum and Dad took their 3 year old daughter to the pet shop. She was so excited to see all the puppies and kittens. "Can I get a kitten, please Mum and Dad?" she asked. Mum and Dad looked at each other and grinned.

"We will have to manage. We don't have much money for a pet," said Dad.

Little girl was disappointed and started to walk away. Suddenly, she saw the most adorable little kitten in a cage. She gasped.

"Can I get him, Mum and Dad? Please?"

But Mum and Dad noticed that the kitten was too quiet, almost fake.

"That kitten isn't real, honey," said Mum.

Little girl was so sad that she couldn't get the kitten. But Mum and Dad smiled, gave her a big hug and told her that they could manage to buy her an ice cream on the way home.

Little girl was so excited and beamed with joy. They all laughed and went off to get an ice cream. Even though she didn't have a real live kitten, she was very happy.

Mommy wanted to measure little Bobby. She held him up against the wall, and asked him a question. "How tall are you?" Bobby thought before he answered. He knew it was a very important measure. He said, "I'm two feet tall!" Mommy smiled and said, "That's wonderful! You're growing so fast." 

But then Mommy came and asked Bobby another question. She asked, "What's the biggest number?" Bobby thought about it for a minute, and then he said, "I think it's one hundred." Mommy frowned and shook her head. She said, "That's very foolish - there are much bigger numbers than that!" Bobby knew Mommy was right, so he said, "Oops!" and began to think of bigger numbers. He shouted out, "A million!" Mommy smiled again and said, "That's much better." 

Mommy was happy to measure Bobby, and he was happy to answer her questions. Together, they had a lot of fun.

One day, Mom and Jack were in the garden. Jack looked around and saw all the different colors of the flowers. "Mom, can I pick one?" he asked.

Mom nodded. "Yes," she said. "Pick a big, reliable one that won't break when you bring it inside."

Jack thought and thought, then picked a pink one that was very big. He put it in his pocket. But when he got home, he realized the petals had fallen off his flower. 

Jack was sad. How could he show Mom something reliable now? He asked his friend Paul for help. Paul said he could help, but first Jack had to do something for him. 

Jack said okay, and Paul told him to pick one extra flower from the garden to bring to him. Jack nodded, went back to the garden, and carefully chose a yellow flower. 

Jack brought the yellow flower to Paul, who said thanks and gave Jack some seeds from his garden. Jack planted the seeds in his garden, and now every summer Jack can see his reliable flowers growing!

Once there was a boy who liked to run. Every day he ran faster and faster. He was so fast that he seemed to float rather than run! One day, his mommy gave him a weight to carry. It was big and heavy, but the boy didnâ€™t mind. He held on tightly and ran with it, as if it were nothing.

He ran for hours and hours, never stopping for a rest. The weight grew heavier and heavier, but the boy never thought about it. He kept on running, ever faster and ever further.

Then, all of a sudden, the boy felt himself trip! He had been so careless, he couldnâ€™t keep his footing. He had been running too fast and too far, with too much weight in his hands. The weight had been too heavy for him, and as he fell, he knew that he had gone much too far. Now it was time to turn around and run back home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to visit his grandma's house because she always had cookies and milk. One day, Timmy's cousin came over to visit too. But Timmy and his cousin started to quarrel over who got to eat the last cookie. They were both very angry and yelling at each other. 

Timmy's grandma heard the commotion and came into the room. She saw the disgusting mess of crumbs and spilled milk on the floor. She told Timmy and his cousin that it was not nice to fight over things like cookies. They should share and be kind to each other. 

Timmy and his cousin felt bad and apologized. They cleaned up the mess together and shared the last cookie. From then on, they learned to share and not quarrel over things. Grandma was very proud of them and they all enjoyed their visit together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a creative chicken who always wanted to pay for things. He would always bring his coins when he went to the store with his family.

One day, he decided that he wanted to pay for the chicken he saw in the store. He asked his mom for the coins and she gave them to him. The chicken counted his coins and saw he had enough money to pay for the chicken.

The chicken was very excited and ran to the counter to pay. The store owner was very surprised to see the chicken paying and gave him the chicken.

The chicken put the chicken in his basket, thanked the store owner and went home. 

He was very proud that he was able to pay for the chicken all by himself and enjoyed the chicken for dinner with his family.

Henry and his mom went to the bakery. He was so excited! He saw lots of different types of pastry in the window. He saw the flaky croissants and the soft donuts with sprinkles.

He decided he wanted the pastry with the creamy filling. His mom smiled and said, "Okay, I'll get it for you." Henry's eyes lit up!

Henry watched as the baker placed the pastry in a white bag. He could hardly contain his excitement. He zipped up the bag and grabbed it.

His mom held him close as they left the bakery. Henry felt so happy with his pastry. He could already taste it!

On their walk home, Henry noticed a graceful butterfly. He pointed to it and his mom nodded and smiled. The butterfly fluttered in the wind and slowly flew away. Henry watched it zip past him, amazed at how graceful it was. He couldn't help but smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play hide and seek with her friends. She had a hidden spot where no one could find her. It was behind a big tree in her backyard.

One day, Sue's big sister, Ann, had an important exam. Ann was worried about the exam and needed help to find her lucky pen. Sue knew where the pen was and wanted to help her sister. So Sue decided to lead Ann to the hidden spot.

Sue took Ann's hand and led her to the big tree in the backyard. Ann was happy when she saw her lucky pen hidden there. She hugged Sue and thanked her for helping. Ann went to take her exam and did very well. Sue was proud of her sister and happy that she could help. They played hide and seek together after Ann's exam, and it was a fun day for both of them.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man. Every day he would sit outside in his garden and watch the birds. One day, a magical fairy appeared and gave the elderly man something special - a microscope! She said it would provide him with a wonderful new experience. 

The elderly man was delighted and thanked the fairy. With his new microscope he could see things he never could before. He spent all day looking into flowers, peering into plants and watching insects.

The elderly man was so excited and fascinated by all that he could see that he shared his new microscope with all his friends. His friends were amazed. One by one they looked into the special microscope and into a whole new world. 

The elderly man was happy. He was glad he could provide his friends with a wonderful experience. They thanked him and continued to look into the microscope until the sun went down. 

The elderly man hugged the magical fairy, who smiled, waved and disappeared into the night. 

The end!

Tom and Mia lived in a small village with their mom and dad. They liked to play outside with their friends, but sometimes they had to help with chores. One day, mom asked them to go to the market and buy some bread and milk.

"Be careful, and stay together," mom said. "The market is close, but there are many people and cars."

Tom and Mia nodded and took a basket. They held hands and walked along the road. They saw some cows, some flowers, and some birds. They said hello to their neighbors.

When they reached the market, they saw many stalls with different things. They smelled fruits, cheese, and fish. They heard people talking, laughing, and bargaining. They looked for the bread and milk.

"Here they are," Tom said, pointing to a stall. He gave the seller some coins and took a loaf of bread and a bottle of milk. He put them in the basket.

"Thank you," Mia said, smiling.

"You're welcome," the seller said. "You are very polite and dependable children. Your mom must be proud of you."

Tom and Mia blushed and thanked him again. They turned to go back to the village.

"Wait," the seller said. "Take this, too." He handed them a small bag of cookies.

"For us?" Tom asked, surprised.

"Yes, for you," the seller said. "A gift for being such good customers. Enjoy!"

Tom and Mia thanked him once more and hugged him. They were very happy and excited. They ran back to the village, holding hands and sharing the cookies. They couldn't wait to tell mom about their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lucy. She was very helpful and always wanted to make people happy.

One day, Lucy went to the meadow with her mum. She saw many sheep there, all happily eating the grass. They were so funny! Lucy wanted to make them happy, so she started to rock the sheep.

The sheep were so happy that Lucy was rocking them! They started wiggling around, and baaing loudly. Lucy laughed so much - she had never seen such happy sheep before!

The sheep enjoyed Lucy's rocking so much, they wanted her to do it all day. Whenever they saw Lucy, they would run over to her, asking her to rock them again. Lucy became the most helpful sheep rocker in the meadow!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved blueberries. She would eat them every day for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. One day, she went to the store with her mom to buy some more blueberries.

At the store, they met a man who had a big spray bottle. "What's that?" asked Lily.

"It's a reliable bug spray," said the man. "It keeps bugs away from the blueberries."

"Oh no," said Lily. "I don't want bugs near my blueberries."

But then, another man came and said, "No, don't spray that. It's bad for the environment."

Lily's mom didn't know what to do. "What should we do?" she asked Lily.

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Let's just buy the blueberries and wash them really well when we get home."

And that's what they did. They bought the blueberries, washed them really well, and enjoyed a delicious blueberry snack. The end.

Once there was a girl called Jane who lived close to the beach. Every day, she loved to go down to the sand and wave at the sea.

One day, Jane was feeling restless, so she decided to take a walk up the beach. As she walked, she saw a big grill ahead of her.

"Hello, grill," said Jane. "Where are you going?"

The grill was silent.

Jane was disappointed. She waved to the grill and said, "Bye bye!"

Jane continued to walk up the beach until she reached the end. She looked back one final time and waved to the grill one last time. Then, she turned around and went home.

Once upon a time there was a happy family. They lived in a big house with a garden at the back. In the garden were lots of bright and pretty flowers. Every day the family would go out and play in the garden together. 

The little boy loved to pick daisies and make daisy chains. Sometimes he would play in the mud and his mommy would laugh. His daddy and big sister would play hide and seek and laugh too. 

One day, the family wanted to make the garden even more beautiful. They wanted to buy a very expensive slide that they could all play on. So they saved up some money and bought the slide. 

On hot summer days, the family would slide down the shiny slide and laugh and laugh. The garden was so much fun! They all agreed that it was the best garden ever.

Once upon a time, there was a tall fox who lived in the forest. She was very curious, and every day she liked to study the forest animals. One day, she asked a rabbit who was hopping by, "Do you know what I study every day?"

The rabbit looked up and said, "No, I don't know, what do you study?".

The fox replied, "I like to study the animals that live in the forest. I like to find out how they live and what they do."

The rabbit said, "That sounds very interesting! I wish I could study too."

The fox smiled and said, "You can. Just come with me tomorrow, and I will show you how to study the animals in the forest".

The rabbit was very happy and the next day they both went off together to study the animals in the forest. They had lots of fun, and they both learnt a lot.

Once upon a time, a girl named Lily wanted to bake a cake. She went to the kitchen and got some flour, sugar, and eggs. She mixed them all together and put the batter in the oven. 

While the cake was baking, Lily thought of something interesting to do. She decided to draw a picture of her cake. She took out her crayons and drew a big, colorful cake with lots of frosting and sprinkles. 

Finally, the cake was done baking. Lily took it out of the oven and let it cool. She cut a big slice and ate it with her family. It was the most delicious cake she had ever made!

Once there was a tall boy. He was trying to decide what he should do. He thought and thought but he just couldn't make up his mind.

Suddenly he had an idea. He decided to get his knife. With the knife he knew he could do many things. He figured solving his problem would be easy.

So he took the knife and went outside. He started cutting a tree with it. After a little bit, he had enough wood to build something. He made a tall house on the ground.

He was very pleased with his work. He had decided what he wanted to do and he had made it happen. It was his special tall house and he was proud.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Tom and Rufus. They liked to do fun things together like play games and explore. 

One day, Rufus had an idea. He wanted to build a castle with paper and a tool called scissors. Tom thought it was a brilliant idea, so he decided to help.

Rufus took out a bunch of colored paper and his scissors. They worked together, folding and cutting and snipping. Tom thought it was really fun!

Suddenly, Rufus got bossy. He said it was his castle and started telling Tom what to do. Tom was a little annoyed, but he kept helping. 

After a while, they completed the castle. Both of them were very proud of their work. From now on, whenever they needed a castle, they knew that they could make one together.

Lily looked up at her mom. "Can I watch a video?" she asked. 

Her mom smiled. "Yes, you can watch a video," she said. 

Lily clapped her hands in excitement and ran to the living room. She saw the video was already playing. It had some harsh sounds, but they were fun! She sat in front of the television and watched the video.

Suddenly, a loud noise made Lily jump. "What was that?" asked Lily.
 
Her mom looked over to her. "It's just the video," she said. "It can be a bit harsh at times."

Lily smiled and turned back to the television. She watched the rest of the video and enjoyed it very much. 

When it was over, Lily looked up at her mom again. "Can I watch another one?" she asked. 

Her mom chuckled and said, "Sure, why not?" 

Lily smiled and ran to the living room again to watch another video.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They saw a big, furry animal with a long neck. It was eating leaves from a tall tree.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily said. "What is it?"

"I think it's a giraffe," Max said. "It can stretch its neck very high."

Lily and Max wanted to see the giraffe better. They ran closer to the fence. The giraffe saw them and lowered its head.

"Hello, giraffe," Lily said. "You are so pretty. Can we pet you?"

The giraffe nodded and let Lily and Max touch its soft fur. It licked their hands with its long tongue.

"Tickles!" Max giggled. "You are so friendly, giraffe."

The giraffe smiled and stretched its neck again. It reached for a juicy leaf and ate it.

"Yum, yum," Lily said. "Do you like leaves, giraffe?"

The giraffe nodded and made a happy sound. It shared some leaves with Lily and Max.

"Thank you, giraffe," Lily and Max said. "You are so nice. We like you."

The giraffe nodded and waved its tail. It liked Lily and Max too. They were so cute.

Tom likes to watch the big crane at the building site. The crane can lift heavy things and move them in the air. Tom wants to see the crane up close, but his mom says it is too dangerous.

One day, Tom sees a chance to sneak away from his mom. He runs to the fence and climbs over it. He steps on the dirt and rocks and walks towards the crane. He thinks the crane is very tall and strong.

But Tom does not see the big hole in the ground. He steps too far and falls into the hole. He cries out loud and feels scared. He cannot climb out of the hole. He wishes he had listened to his mom.

Soon, his mom hears his cry and runs to the fence. She sees Tom in the hole and calls for help. The crane operator hears her and stops the crane. He lowers the crane hook and lifts Tom out of the hole. He puts Tom on the ground and gives him a hug.

Tom is happy to be safe, but he is also sorry. He says sorry to his mom and the crane operator. He says he will not run away again. He learns that the crane is not a toy, but a tool. He also learns that the ground can have thick holes that can hurt him. He thanks the crane operator for saving him and goes home with his mom. He still likes to watch the crane, but from a distance.

Once upon a time, there was a king. The king was very powerful and could do a lot of amazing things. One day, the king and his court were playing in the park.

The king decided to skip. He skipped in big circles and jumped as high as he could. Everyone giggled and clapped as the king skipped around.

Suddenly, a big storm passed over the park and the king got wet. All of his friends felt sorry and apologized to the king. The kind king said it was okay and hugged everyone.

The king and his court finished their game and the king skipped away to his castle. Everyone skipped and laughed all the way home.

One sunny day, Jimmy found an old bicycle in the grass. It was hairy with lots of rust. He couldn't wait to try it! Jimmy ran to get his older brother Dave, who was very happy to help him.

"Let's push it to the street," said Dave. So they both grabbed the handle bars and pushed the old bicycle. 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was Jimmy's dad! "You kids stop right now!" he said in a angry voice. Jimmy and Dave were scared.

But it was too late. When they looked down, they saw that a strange hairy creature surged out of the bike. It had sharp teeth and long claws. Then it angrily growled at Jimmy and Dave. 

The two brothers ran away in terror, leaving the old bicycle behind. They never saw it again, or the creature that had grown out of it.

Once upon a time there was a humble dog. She loved to bounce and jump around. Every morning she would wake up and start bouncing and be very happy.

One day, the humble dog wanted to find a friend. She could not find anyone so she kept bouncing around, looking for one. Suddenly, she saw a little boy. He had a big smile and he was bouncing too!

The humble dog was so happy. She ran to the little boy and joined him in his bouncing. Soon they were having so much fun together!

The boy and the humble dog made a good team. They bounced around until they were too tired and had to stop. They were best friends and did this every day.

The humble dog and the boy were happy together because they knew that no matter what happened, they would always have each other.

Once there was a young boy. He loved to play outside in the sun. One day he put on his special suit, with shiny buttons and a bowtie. He looked very fancy.

He jumped and skipped outside, and before he knew it, the sun was setting. He decided to try and stay out a little longer. Just then, he felt something soft and wet on his face. He had to blink!

It started to rain. The young boy ran back inside, blinking away the raindrops. He was very wet, but safe and dry in his house.

When he took off his suit, it was still sparkly clean. He smiled, happy to have kept it safe from the wet rain.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy was walking in the forest when he saw a skull. The skull looked tough and scary, but Teddy knew it was just a bone.

Teddy decided to settle down by the skull and take a nap. As he was sleeping, he dreamed of all the adventures he had in the forest. When he woke up, he felt refreshed and ready to explore some more.

Teddy said goodbye to the skull and continued his journey through the forest. He knew that he would encounter many tough obstacles along the way, but he was brave and determined to face them all.

Lily was sick. She had a cough and a fever. Mommy took her to the doctor. Lily did not like the doctor. He was loud and scary. He looked at her ears and throat. He gave her a shot. Lily cried.

Mommy hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie. The shot will make you feel better. You are very brave." Lily sniffed and nodded. She wanted to go home.

The doctor gave Mommy a paper. He said, "Take this to the nurse. She will give you some medicine for Lily." Mommy and Lily walked to the nurse. The nurse was nice. She had a bright smile and a pink dress. She gave Lily a sticker and a lollipop. She said, "You did a great job, Lily. I hope you get well soon."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, nurse." She liked the nurse. She was kind and gentle. She gave Lily the medicine and a cup of water. She said, "Drink this, Lily. It will help your cough and fever. You have to take it every day until you are better."

Mommy and Lily said goodbye to the nurse. They went to the car. Mommy buckled Lily in her seat. She said, "Let's go home, Lily. You can rest and play with your toys. I love you, Lily." Lily said, "I love you, Mommy." She felt a little better. She licked her lollipop and looked at her sticker. She was glad the doctor and the nurse were done. She hoped she would not be sick again.

Pip and Rita were best friends. Together, they liked to gaze at the block tower Pip's dad had built. It was so tall, it reached the clouds! Every day, they'd share stories, play and laugh.

But one day, Pip had a very lazy idea. "Let's take all the blocks away," said Pip. Before she could stop herself, Rita agreed.

The children gleefully gathered all the blocks, one by one and placed them in a pile. When they had finished, they looked at each other with mischievous grins. 

Just then, Pip's dad walked in.  "What have you two been up to?" He said, slightly angry.

Pip and Rita stuttered and Pip replied, "We were taking the blocks away".

Pip's dad stood tall and held his finger up. "Always think before doing something," he said. "Taking the blocks away breaks the tower. Working together builds it up!" 

The two children looked at each other and dropped the blocks. They went back to the tower and placed the blocks carefully together. They said together, "We will work together and make this tower even higher!"

The moral of this story is that you should always think before doing something. Working together will always help you build something better than when you break it apart.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lil who loved to slide. Every day she went to her special place to slide down the hill.

One day, she went out with her dad to her special place. When they got there, she saw a little boy all alone. She could tell he was sad, so she went over to him.

â€œWhatâ€™s wrong?â€, asked Lil.

The little boy said he had lost his toy and didn't know what to do.

Lil felt so compassionate, so she said â€œI can help you lookâ€.

So they searched up and down the hill until they found the toy. The little boy was so happy! He thanked Lil and they hugged and parted ways.

Lil was so proud of herself â€“ she knew she was a compassionate friend! Then, she smiled, ran back up the hill and slide down the hill one more time.

Tim was a famous mouse. He liked to find food in the big house. He was not afraid of the cat or the dog. He was very fast and smart.

One day, he saw a big piece of cheese on a board. He ran to get it. But it was a trap! A metal thing snapped on his tail. It hurt a lot. He tried to pull away, but he could not. He was stuck.

He heard the cat coming. He was scared. He wanted to resist. He did not want to be the cat's lunch. He looked around. He saw a hole in the wall. He had an idea.

He bit the cheese hard. He threw it to the hole. The cat saw the cheese. He ran to the hole. He tried to get it. He stuck his head in the hole. He could not get out.

Tim used his teeth to open the trap. He freed his tail. He ran away. He was safe. He was happy. He was still famous.

Once upon a time, there was a little turtle called Nick. He wanted to find something exciting, so he decided to go for a walk. He noticed an unusual shell by the edge of the shore. Nick thought it was the most beautiful thing he had ever seen, and he decided to take it home with him. 

When he arrived home, Nick's mom was very angry. She said that it was wrong for Nick to take someone else's shell and that he had to put it back. Nick was very sad. He argued that no one had ever told him not to take it, but his mom didn't listen. 

Nick couldn't bear the thought of leaving it behind, so he decided to come up with a plan. With a trembling voice, he told his mom that he wanted to share his shell with the whole world. He asked her if he could put it in a museum so that everyone could enjoy it. 

Nick's mom thought it was an unusual plan, but she decided to let him try providing he could find a museum that accepted his shell. So, Nick went on a journey and eventually found a museum that was willing to accept the shell. 

Nick was very proud of himself, and his mom was very proud of him. They both learned an important lesson that day: it's OK to make unusual decisions, as long as you're doing it for the right reasons.

Once upon a time, there was a nurse who was very kind. Every day she helped people feel better by giving them medicine and care.

One day, the nurse noticed that the people she was helping were not getting better. The medicine she was giving them was not working. She knew she had to do something to help.

She decided to increase the amount of medicine she was giving them. She gave them more and more each day until the medicine began to work.

The nurse was so happy that she did a dance. She was glad she was able to help the people feel better again.

But one day the medicine started tasting bitter. Everyone was worried and didn't know what to do.

But the nurse had an idea. She added some sweet juice to the medicine. This made it taste better and it still helped people get better.

The nurse was so happy she had figured out how to help people. Everyone was thankful for her hard work and kindness!

One day, a little boy wanted to stretch his legs. He went to his garden, where he saw a big box. It looked very interesting. He ran to it and opened it, and found lots of toys inside. 

He heard a noisy sound coming from the box. He peered into it, and found a toy car inside. He was so excited, he picked it up and began to stretch out the car's wheels. He pressed the button and the car began to move. He loved it so much that he started running around with it. 

The little boy had a good time stretching his legs and playing with the toy car. He had a lot of fun that day, and will surely remember it forever.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play and have fun. But they do not like to go to school. School is boring. They have to sit and listen to the teacher. The teacher talks a lot. She gives them a lecture. A lecture is when someone tells you what to do or what not to do.

One day, Tim and Kim forget to do their homework. They forget because they are busy playing with their toys. They do not remember until they are in the car with their mom. They are scared. They do not want to get a lecture from the teacher.

"Mom, we forget to do our homework," Tim says.

"Me too," Kim says.

"Oh no, that is not good," mom says. "You have to do your homework every day. Homework is important. It helps you learn and grow. If you do not do your homework, the teacher will be angry. She will give you a lecture. And you will have to stay after school."

Tim and Kim feel sorry. They do not want to make mom or the teacher angry. They do not want to get a lecture. They do not want to stay after school. They want to go home and play.

"Mom, we are sorry," Tim says.

"Me too," Kim says.

"Can you forgive us?" Tim says.

"Me too," Kim says.

Mom smiles. She loves Tim and Kim. She knows they are good kids. But they have to learn to be responsible.

"I forgive you, but you have to promise me something," mom says.

"What?" Tim and Kim say.

"You have to promise me that you will do your homework every day. And you will listen to the teacher. And you will not forget again. OK?"

"OK," Tim and Kim say.

They hug mom. They are happy. They do not want to forget again. They want to make mom and the teacher proud. They want to learn and grow. And they want to have fun. But not when they have homework.

Once there was a girl. She was a very special girl and could do something very few people can do. She could reverse! She was such a brilliant reverser that everyone in her town was jealous of her. 

One day, she went to the park so she could show everyone her special skill, reversing. Everyone was so amazed, they wanted to be like the girl. They wanted to learn how to reverse just like her. 

The girl was happy that she had so many admirers. She decided to teach them all how to reverse! Little by little, they began to learn and soon they were all very good reversers. 

The girl took great joy in watching her friends get better and better. But deep down inside she was a bit jealous that now they could all do what she could do! 

But then, the girl realized something important. She realized that she wasn't jealous at all â€” she was proud! She was proud of her friends, and especially proud of herself, for passing on the special skill of reversing.

Tommy was a 3 year old boy who loved to explore. Today he was exploring his living room, looking for something interesting. He spotted something he had never seen before: a bookshelf. 

He walked over to it and stared at it in wonder. He had never seen so many books all in one place! He started to reach for one of the books but then stopped himself. "I can't reach," he said to himself. 

Tommy looked around the room, trying to figure out what to do. Suddenly he remembered something his mom had said to him before. "If you want to be successful, you need to ask for help". 

So bravely he asked his mom, "Mommy, can I have help to reach the bookshelf?" His mom smiled and said, "Of course you can, Tommy. I'll help you go get the books."

Tommy and his mom happily went to the bookshelf, and together they picked out a book that Tommy liked. He was so excited to have his own book! He hugged the book to his chest and showed it proudly to his mom.

From then on, Tommy asked his mom for help to reach the bookshelf every day. It didn't take long before Tommy became really successful at choosing just the right book to read.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty skirt that she loved to wear. One day, she noticed that her skirt had some dirt on it. So, she asked her mommy if she could clean it. Her mommy gave her a cloth and some polish. Lily used the polish to clean her skirt and it looked shiny and new again. 

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a girl wearing an unknown skirt. Lily thought it looked very pretty. She went up to the girl and said, "I like your skirt!" The girl smiled and said thank you. They became friends and played together all day. From that day on, Lily always remembered to polish her skirt and make new friends.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to observe the flowers and the bugs. They saw a big green lily with a yellow center. It smelled nice.

"Look, Ben, a lily!" Anna said. "It is so pretty!"

Ben nodded. He wanted to touch the lily. He reached out his hand. But a bee flew out of the lily. It buzzed loudly.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. He pulled back his hand. The bee had stung him. It hurt a lot.

Anna ran to him. She hugged him. She was sorry for him.

"Don't cry, Ben. I will get mom. She will make it better." Anna said.

She ran to the house. She called mom. Mom came with some ice and a band-aid. She put the ice on Ben's hand. She kissed it. She put the band-aid on it.

"There, there, Ben. You will be okay. The bee was just scared. It did not mean to hurt you." Mom said.

Ben felt a little better. He smiled at mom. He thanked her.

"Can we still observe the flowers, mom?" Anna asked.

"Sure, honey. But be careful. Some flowers have bees. They are good for the flowers, but they can sting. You have to look, but not touch." Mom said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They learned something new. They went back to the garden. They observed the flowers and the bugs. But they did not touch the lily. They left it for the bee.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going on a trip. Lily was so excited! She ran to her room to pack her things.

As she was packing, Lily accidentally closed the door on her finger. It hurt a lot and she started to cry. Her mom came to see what happened and gave her a hug. She told Lily that they would take care of her finger and it would feel better soon.

The next day, Lily and her family went on their trip. It was a gloomy day, but they didn't mind. They had fun playing games and singing songs in the car. Lily was happy she packed her favorite toy to play with. She knew it was going to be a great adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jack. He was very eager to see the moon. Every night, he would look up to the sky, but the moon was never there.

One night, Jack decided he was going to go outside and find the moon. He ran out and looked up, but he could not see it. He was very sad.

Suddenly, he heard a voice.

"If you want to see the moon, you have to slap it," the voice said.

Jack was confused. He had never heard of slapping the moon before. But he was still eager, so he tried it. He slapped his hand up in the sky, and to his surprise, the moon suddenly appeared!

He was so happy that he had found the moon, and quickly he ran back inside to tell his family the good news. Everyone was very excited, and they all went outside to take a look at the beautiful moon in the night sky.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Kiki and Kaio. They loved to go on adventures. One day they decided to go riding to explore the world.

They went outside and saw the soil. It was full of fun creatures. Kaio wanted to go down and play in the soil, but Kiki discouraged him. She said, "Kaio, soil is dirty and you'll ruin your clothes. Let's stay up here and go riding instead."

Kaio did not want to go riding, but decided to listen to his friend. As they rode around they ended up at a beautiful lake. Kiki told Kaio, "Look, the lake is so much nicer than the soil! We should always pick nice places to explore, not dirty ones like the soil." 

Kaio was sad he didn't get the play in the soil he wanted, but understood the moral of the story. In the end, Kiki and Kaio had a fun ride and Kaio was happy that he listened to his friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside on the green grass. One day, she found a purple flower on the ground. She picked it up and smelled it. It smelled so good!

Lily wanted to keep the flower forever, so she asked her mommy to print a picture of it. Her mommy printed the picture and Lily was very happy. She put the picture in her pocket and went to play.

But later, when Lily went back to get the picture, it was gone! She looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. She was so sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a sad little deer. Everywhere the deer went, it shivered. It was so cold, no matter where it went. 

One day, something amazing happened. It found a shiny piece of gear! The deer knew that the gear was something special, and it was the key to staying warm. The deer put it on, and suddenly it felt so much better. 

The deer kept the gear on wherever it went. Now it was nice and warm, and never felt cold again. 

One day, it ran into a big and scary creature. It was a giant bear and it was deaf! But the deer was not scared, because it was wearing its special gear and felt so safe and snug. 

The deer skipped away and never saw the giant bear again. It was happy, because it was never cold anymore. The deer thanked the gear for keeping it so warm. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a very elderly man with a very important name. He lived in a village far away and he was the best at scoring points in the village. Every day he played a game with the other villagers, and he always scored the most points.

One day, the elderly man's name was called out aloud. Everyone became very quiet and listened. He had been chosen to receive a special medal for his skill in scoring points. Everyone cheered as he stepped forward and the mayor put the medal around his neck. The elderly man smiled proudly as he looked at the shiny medal.

The villagers all started to chant the elderly man's name and the sound echoed through the village. He was so happy to have his name remembered and celebrated by all.

The elderly man went home that day feeling very proud. He kept the medal around his neck and even slept with it on. The next morning he woke up and put it on again, ready for the day. And from then on, he was known as the one with the best points-scoring skills in the village.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was only three years old and loved dressing up in costumes. One of her favorite costumes was a blue fairy costume.

One day, Lily wanted to add something extra to her costume. She thought that a pair of magic wings would make it even better. But her mom said that wings would cost too much money. Lily was sad and asked her dad for help.

But dad said the same thing. He said it was not worth spending the money on wings. Lily was so unhappy that she started to cry.

Her parents tried to comfort her, but she would not listen. Eventually they had to leave her alone in her room.

The moral of the story is to be content with what you have. It is not always necessary to add more things to make you happy. Just being yourself is enough.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to dance and hop around all day long. One day, Benny found a shiny hammer on the ground. He picked up the hammer and started to play with it. He hit a rock with the hammer and it made a loud sound! Benny thought it was so funny.

Suddenly, Benny heard a serious voice behind him. It was his mommy. She told him that the hammer was not a toy and he should be careful with it. Benny felt bad that he didn't know it was serious. He promised his mommy that he would be careful with the hammer and never play with it again. From that day on, Benny just danced and hopped around all day long, just like he loved to do.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They had many toys, but they also liked to look inside the cabinet where Mom kept the cookies. Sometimes, Mom gave them a cookie as a treat, but only one each.

One day, Mom went to the store and told Lily and Ben to be good and not touch the cabinet. Lily and Ben nodded, but as soon as Mom left, they ran to the kitchen. They saw that the cabinet was open, and there was a big jar of cookies inside.

"Wow, look at all the cookies!" Lily said. "Let's take some and eat them!"

"No, we can't do that!" Ben said. "Mom said not to touch the cabinet. It's not nice to take things without asking."

"But Mom won't know!" Lily said. "She won't count the cookies. And they look so yummy!"

Lily and Ben disagreed. They started to argue and pull the jar. They did not hear Mom come back from the store. She saw them fighting over the cookies and was very angry.

"Lily and Ben, what are you doing?" Mom said. "You broke the rule and disobeyed me. You are not supposed to touch the cabinet. And you are not supposed to fight with each other. You are twins, you should share and be kind."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They dropped the jar and hugged each other. They said sorry to Mom and to each other. Mom forgave them, but she said they had to learn their lesson. She took away the jar of cookies and said they could not have any for a week.

Lily and Ben realized they made a mistake. They wished they had listened to Mom and to Ben. They learned that it is better to follow the rules and to respect each other. They decided to play with their toys instead of the cookies. They also decided to agree more and disagree less.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his black toy car. He played with it every day, and it made him very happy.

One day, Tim's black toy car broke. He was very sad. His mommy saw him crying and asked what was wrong. Tim showed her the broken car. Mommy said, "Don't worry, we can replace it with a new one."

So, Tim and his mommy went to the toy store to find a new black car to play with. They found a shiny black car that Tim liked. Mommy bought it for him, and they went home.

Tim was so happy to have a new black car to play with. He played with it all day and forgot about the broken one. And from that day on, Tim always took good care of his new car, and they had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time there lived a silly boy. He loved to play and have fun every day. He especially loved to read books. One evening he decided to take out a novel to enjoy.

As he opened the book, the boy was amazed at the wonderful words he read. He smiled and giggled as he read, forgetting about the world around him. He immediately became lost in the fun story.

The boy read and read until it was time for bed. Even then, the foolish boy still wanted to keep reading. He quickly put the book away, knowing that he would enjoy it the next day.

The next evening the silly boy took out the novel again. He read and giggled until it was time for sleep. He tucked the book away, knowing that he could enjoy it again the next night.

The little boy loved his novel, learning more and more with each page he read. He never felt foolish for enjoying the book, because it made him so happy. The boy kept reading every night, and that made his heart fuller and fuller.

Once there was a motorcycle. It was red and shiny and everyone wanted to ride it. One day, a little boy and his mommy decided to take the motorcycle for a ride. But when they got on it, it started to rot. The little boy was scared and wanted to get off, but his mom said they had to stay and wait.

They waited and waited until the motorcycle had rotted away. Now it was all rusty and slow. But there was still something special about the old motorcycle. The little boy was no longer scared. He liked the motorcycle, even though it was old and slow.

They kept riding the old, slow motorcycle together. Whenever it got too slow, the mommy would just give it a little push. The little boy loved riding on it, even though it was slow and scary sometimes.

Together, the little boy and his mommy enjoyed the rides, no matter how slow the old motorcycle went.

Mama and Papa took Jack and Jam to the beach. They were so excited. Jack and Jam went and built a hut in the sand. They pushed the sand around until it was big and strong. Mama and Papa were very proud. 

Jack and Jam played for a long time. They were so happy. But then it started to rain. They had to leave the beach. Jack and Jam were upset. They didn't want to leave the hut behind. 

Mama and Papa carried Jack and Jam away from the beach. But before they left, Papa pushed the hut over. Jack and Jam were so sad. But then Mama said it was ok. They could build a new hut when they came back to the beach. 

Jack and Jam felt better. They were still upset, but they knew they would be able to build a new hut. Mama and Papa were so happy they could make Jack and Jam smile.

Once upon a time, there was a theater. Inside the theater, there was a clown. The clown was so stupid! He laughed and smiled but didn't do anything else.

One day, the clown had had enough of being so silly. He decided he wanted to rise up! He jumped off the stage and started to do flips in the air. Everyone in the theater cheered for the clown. They were so happy to see him rise up!

The clown had shown everyone that he could rise up. He smiled and took a big bow. From then on, he wasn't so stupid. He knew he could make people proud!

Sara was playing with her dolls in her room. She liked to make them talk and dress them up. She had a big box of clothes and shoes for them. She wanted to show her dolls to her friend Lily, who was coming over soon.

She heard the doorbell ring. She ran downstairs to see Lily. Lily had a big smile on her face. She had a new doll in her arms. It was very pretty, with long blonde hair and a pink dress. Sara was happy to see Lily and her new doll.

"Come on, let's go upstairs," Sara said. "I want to show you my dolls too. I have many of them. They are very fun to play with."

Lily nodded and followed Sara upstairs. They went into Sara's room and saw the box of clothes and shoes. They started to take out the dolls and try different outfits on them. They had a lot of fun.

But then Sara noticed something. Lily's doll looked very pale. It did not have any color on its cheeks or lips. It looked sick. Sara was worried.

"Lily, is your doll okay?" Sara asked. "It looks very pale. Does it need some medicine?"

Lily shook her head. She looked sad.

"No, it's not okay," Lily said. "It's a special doll. It's a doll of my sister. My sister was very sick and she died. My mom gave me this doll to remember her. She said it looks just like her."

Sara felt very sorry for Lily. She hugged her and said, "I'm so sorry, Lily. Your sister was very beautiful. I'm sure she loved you very much. And I love you too. You are my best friend."

Lily smiled and hugged Sara back. She said, "Thank you, Sara. You are very kind. And I love you too. You are my best friend."

They wiped their tears and continued to play with their dolls. They made them happy and healthy. They made them laugh and sing. They were happy to have each other.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to stack blocks, but he always got frustrated when his tower would fall down. One day, Timmy's friend gifted him a special set of blocks. They were very easy to stack and didn't fall down easily. Timmy was very happy and thanked his friend.

But one day, Timmy's little sister came and knocked over his tower of blocks. Timmy got very angry and started to scream at his sister. His mom came in and told him that it wasn't nice to scream at his sister. She reminded him that it was just a tower of blocks and that he could always build another one.

From that day on, Timmy learned to control his anger and not to scream at others. He realized that it was more important to be kind to his sister than to have a perfect tower of blocks. And he continued to enjoy stacking his gifted blocks, but now he did it with a smile on his face.

Anna was sleeping in her bed. She had a nice dream about a big cake with many candles. She wanted to eat the cake, but then she heard a noise. It was her mom and dad. They came into her room and said, "Happy birthday, Anna!"

Anna opened her eyes and saw them. They had a big smile and a big box. They put the box on her bed and said, "This is a present for you, Anna. Do you want to open it?"

Anna was very happy. She said, "Yes, yes, I want to open it!" She tore the paper and saw a beautiful doll. The doll had long hair, a pink dress and a hat. Anna hugged the doll and said, "Thank you, mom and dad! She is so nice! What is her name?"

Mom and dad said, "You can name her whatever you want, Anna. She is your new friend."

Anna thought for a moment and said, "I will name her Lily. Lily is a nice name for a nice doll."

Mom and dad kissed Anna and said, "We love you, Anna. You are a nice girl. Have a nice day!"

Anna said, "I love you, too. I will have a nice day with Lily. Can we have cake now?"

Mom and dad laughed and said, "Of course, we can have cake now. Come on, let's go to the kitchen and celebrate your birthday!"

Anna got out of her bed and took Lily with her. She was very happy. It was a nice day.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the mud. One day, Lily was playing with her friend Timmy when they heard a loud noise. They looked up and saw a big bird flying in the sky.

"We have to help the bird get out of the mud," said Lily.

Together, Lily and Timmy pulled the bird out of the mud and it flew away. They felt proud of themselves for helping the bird. From that day on, Lily and Timmy knew that they could do anything if they worked together.

Once upon a time there was an old store. It was very dark inside the store, but suddenly something magical happened. A big light started to glow. It shone very brightly and lit up the store. 

The glow made the store look more beautiful and interesting. Lots of people stopped to admire the bright light. 

One of those people was a little 3 year old girl. She thought the store was very exciting because of the glow. She watched it dance around and light up all the old things in the store.

The girl laughed with delight as the light made the store look special and new. Soon she started to glow too, just as brightly as the store's light. 

The little girl was filled with joy, and she enjoyed watching the glow until it was time to go home.

Lila and Tom are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. They want to try it.

"Let's go, Lila!" Tom says. He runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder.

"Wait for me, Tom!" Lila says. She follows him, but she is slower. She is afraid of heights.

Tom reaches the top of the slide. He looks down and smiles. He sits on the slide and pushes himself. He slides down fast and laughs.

"Wow, that was fun!" he says. He stands up and looks for Lila.

Lila is still on the ladder. She is near the top, but she is scared. She holds on tight and does not move.

"Come on, Lila! It's not scary!" Tom says. He tries to help her.

Lila shakes her head. She does not want to slide. She wants to go back.

"Please, Tom, let's go back!" she says. She starts to cry.

Tom feels sorry for Lila. He loves his sister. He climbs up the ladder again. He reaches Lila and hugs her.

"It's okay, Lila. We can go back. Don't cry," he says. He helps her down the ladder.

They walk back to the ground. Lila wipes her tears. She sees Tom's hand. He has a red mark on his thumb.

"What happened, Tom?" she asks.

"I hurt my thumb. I stepped on a rock when I slid down," he says. He shows her his thumb.

Lila kisses his thumb. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. Does it hurt?"

Tom smiles. He says, "No, it's fine. Thank you, Lila. You are the best sister ever."

They hug each other. They are happy. They are original twins. They go to play with other things in the park.

Once there was a little boy called Mike. Mike was three years old and he loved movies. He always asked his parents if he could watch a movie.

One day, Mike requested to watch a movie but his parents said the movie was too dull for him. Mike was disappointed that he could not watch the movie.

Mike became very upset so his parents decided to make a special movie for him. They used lots of bright colours, funny characters and exciting music.

Mike loved his new movie. He smiled and laughed and danced around the room.

From then on, Mike would always request that he watch his special movie whenever he wanted to watch a movie.

Once upon a time, there was a kind lady who loved to help others. She had a big heart and always wanted to make people happy. One day, she went for a walk and saw a little boy who had hurt his foot. She felt sad for him and wanted to help.

The lady asked the boy if he needed any help and he said yes. She took him to her house and gave him a bandage for his foot. She was very compassionate and made sure he felt better. The boy was happy and thanked the lady for her kindness.

From that day on, the lady and the boy became good friends. They would often go for walks together and see all the beautiful things around them. The lady always made sure the boy was safe and happy. They both knew that they had a special bond because of the lady's compassionate heart.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sally. Sally was three years old and she lived in a small village. Each day, Sally would play in the woods near her home.

One day as Sally was playing, she heard a strange sound. She stopped and listened, but couldn't quite make it out. Then a voice from the shadows said, "Don't worry, Sally, it's only me". 

Sally recognised the voice and recognised the face in the shadows. It was Bill the ghost. Bill had been visiting Sally's village for years. 

Sally was worried, so she asked Bill what was he doing there. Bill told Sally he was trying to find something amazing. He said it was going to be a surprise and that he would come back soon. 

So Sally waited in the woods to see what Bill the ghost was up to. Soon enough he returned with an amazing treasure. Sally was so glad that she wasn't worried any more. 

Turns out the amazing treasure was a magical key that could open any door in the world. Now Sally and Bill were going on magical adventures, no longer having to worry about what might lie behind each door.

Tom and Lily were making a cake with Mom. They liked to help Mom in the kitchen. They had eggs, flour, sugar, butter, and milk. Mom gave them a big bowl and a spoon.

"Can I stir, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Yes, you can stir, Tom. But be careful, don't spill," Mom said.

Tom took the spoon and started to stir the cake mix. He stirred and stirred. He liked to see the mix change. It was yellow and smooth.

"Can I stir, too?" Lily asked.

"Sure, you can stir, too, Lily. But wait for your turn," Mom said.

Lily waited for Tom to finish. Then she took the spoon and stirred the cake mix. She stirred and stirred. She liked to hear the mix make noises. It was squishy and bubbly.

Mom poured the cake mix into a pan. She put the pan in the oven. She set the timer.

"Now we have to wait for the cake to bake," Mom said.

Tom and Lily went to the window. They looked outside. It was a sunny day. The sunshine was bright and warm. They saw green grass and green trees. They saw birds and butterflies.

"Can we go outside, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Yes, you can go outside, Tom. But put on your hats and sunscreen," Mom said.

Tom and Lily put on their hats and sunscreen. They ran outside. They played in the sunshine. They had fun.

Soon, the timer beeped. The cake was ready. Mom took the cake out of the oven. She let it cool. She put frosting and sprinkles on it.

"Come inside, Tom and Lily. The cake is done," Mom called.

Tom and Lily ran inside. They smelled the cake. It smelled yummy. They saw the cake. It looked pretty.

"Can we have some cake, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Yes, you can have some cake, Lily. But wash your hands first," Mom said.

Tom and Lily washed their hands. Mom cut the cake. She gave them each a slice. They ate the cake. It tasted delicious.

"Thank you, Mom. The cake is good," Tom said.

"Thank you, Mom. The cake is good," Lily said.

"You're welcome, Tom and Lily. I'm glad you like it. And thank you for helping me," Mom said.

They hugged Mom. They smiled. They were happy.

The little girl was very tired. She had been walking for a long time and her feet were so heavy. She had been looking for an exit, but she couldn't find it.

But then, she noticed something at the end of the long hallway. She couldn't see it very well, but it looked like it could be an exit.

The little girl was so happy. She kept walking, and soon she reached the exit. She opened the door and saw daylight!

The little girl was free. She stepped out into the sunshine and ran down the street. She had finally reached her exit, and she was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom had a tool. It was a big, clear net. He liked to play with his net in the park.

One day, Tom saw a cat. The cat was stuck in a tree. Tom wanted to help the cat. He said, "Don't worry, cat. I will use my net to prevent you from falling." The cat looked at Tom and said, "Meow."

Tom tried to use his net to help the cat. But the net was not strong. The cat fell from the tree. Tom was sad. The cat was hurt. Tom learned that his net was not a good tool to prevent the cat from falling.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with blocks. They make different shapes and colors with the blocks. They have fun.

One day, they want to make a big tower with all the blocks. They start to stack the blocks on top of each other. They try to make a pattern with the blocks. They use red, blue, yellow and green blocks. They make a pattern like this: red, blue, yellow, green, red, blue, yellow, green.

They are happy with their pattern. They want to make the tower higher and higher. They reach for more blocks. But they have no more blocks. They have used all the blocks.

They are sad. They want more blocks. They ask their mom for more blocks.

"Mom, can we have more blocks?" they say.

"Sorry, sweeties, we have no more blocks at home," mom says. "But we can go to the store and buy some more blocks. Do you want to go to the store with me?"

"Yes, yes, yes!" Lily and Ben say. They are excited. They want to go to the store.

They put on their shoes and coats. They hold mom's hand. They go to the store.

At the store, they see many blocks. They see big blocks and small blocks. They see blocks with letters and numbers. They see blocks with animals and cars. They see blocks with different shapes and colors.

Mom smiles. She says, "OK, sweeties, you can have this box. But you have to share the blocks. And you have to be careful with the tower. Don't make it too high. It might fall down and hurt you."

Lily and Ben nod. They say, "OK, mom. We will share the blocks. And we will be careful with the tower. Thank you, mom. You are the best mom."

Mom hugs them. She says, "You are welcome, sweeties. You are the best twins. I love you."

They love mom. They are happy. They buy the box with stars and moons. They go home. They make a new pattern with the stars and moons. They make a mighty tower with the stars and moons. They have fun.

One day, a small girl called Lucy went outside to play in the park. She liked to make friends with the animals, so she looked around. Suddenly, she saw a pigeon come slowly down to the ground. She was excited and ran over.

When they were finished, the elderly lady thanked the young girl. "Here, let me give you something for helping me," she said. She took out a jar of cream and gave it to the girl.

The young girl was very happy and thanked the elderly lady again. She took the jar of cream and ran back home, while the elderly lady stayed outside in her garden.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly elephant named Elsie. Elsie loved to march around the jungle. She would march to the bottom of the tall trees, around the pond, and up the hill. Elsie also liked to share her marching adventures with her friends.

Finally, it was time to march back to the jungle. Elsie and her friends said goodbye to the townspeople and trotted back to their home. They ran, they skipped, and they galloped through the jungle.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to clap her hands and dance around. One day, Lily went to a lecture with her mom. The lecture was about being kind to others.

Once there was a little boy who did something very naughty. He was feeling so sad and bad about what he had done, but he knew he had to tell his mum. They went together to the station and sat there. The little boy was feeling uncomfortable and didn't want to move. But his mum's loving arms were warm and comforting, so he started to feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a rat who was very disagreeable. He would always argue and quibble with the other animals. Every time they tried to do something fun, the rat disagreed and said it was too boring.

Once upon a time, there was a man who wanted to find something special. He decided he would go on a journey to find it. He set off into the night with only a map and a sack full of treasures. He drove and drove, but soon he came to a wreck. He was so sad, but he kept going.

Kylie and her mommy were inside the mall. Kylie saw a beautiful dress that was so pretty! She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom refused. Then Kylie started to cry.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a mole digging a hole in the ground. She recognized the mole because she had seen one before in a book.

At that moment, a little girl walking by noticed the pigeon. She was only three years old. She said "Hello, Pigeon. Those apples look yummy!"

The pigeon smiled. But it looked a bit down. "I'm so tired after eating all these apples," it groaned. "I wish I could take a nap."

The little girl smiled. She said, "Why don't you rest here in the park? I'll watch over you and make sure nothing bad happens."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah was very excited for her holiday with her family. They were going to the beach, and she couldn't wait to play in the sand and swim in the sea.

Lily liked to sign. She learned how to sign from her mom, who was deaf. Lily could talk and hear, but she loved to sign with her mom and other deaf people. She thought it was fun and beautiful.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. It was cold, so she wore her coat. Her coat was old and had holes, but it was warm and cozy. Lily did not mind. She was happy to play with her mom and the other kids.

At the park, Lily saw a boy who was alone. He looked sad and poor. He had no coat, only a thin shirt. He shivered in the wind. Lily felt sorry for him. She wanted to be his friend.

She ran to him and smiled. She signed, "Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?" The boy looked at her and frowned. He did not understand. He shook his head and said, "I don't know sign. I can't hear you."

Lily was surprised. She did not know he was deaf, too. She felt bad for him. He had no coat and no sign. He must be very lonely. She wanted to help him.

She took off her coat and wrapped it around him. He felt the warmth and smiled. He hugged her and said, "Thank you. You are very kind." Lily smiled back. She signed, "You're welcome. I'm glad to share. Do you want to learn sign? I can teach you."

The boy nodded. He wanted to learn sign. He wanted to talk to Lily and her mom and other deaf people. He wanted to have friends. He said, "Yes, please. I want to learn sign. Will you be my friend?"

Lily nodded. She wanted to be his friend. She said, "Yes, of course. I will be your friend. Come, let's play with my mom. She will be happy to meet you."

They ran to Lily's mom, who was waiting for them. She saw them holding hands and wearing Lily's coat. She smiled and signed, "Hello, who is this?" Lily signed, "This is my new friend. He is deaf, too. He has no coat and no sign. I gave him my coat and I will teach him sign. He is very nice."

Lily's mom was proud of her. She hugged them both and signed, "You are very generous and sweet, Lily. I'm happy you found a new friend. He is very lucky to have you. And you are very lucky to have him. You both have something to give and something to learn. You both have a lot of love."

They all smiled and signed. They played and laughed. They felt warm and happy. They were not poor. They had each other. They had sign. They had a coat.

Once upon a time, there was an unknown king. He was an old and powerful king, who ruled over his kingdom with an iron fist. But even he was scared of one thing; the snap. Nobody knew what the snap was, only that it was something to fear.

The king returned to his kingdom and snapped his fingers - just like the snap he had seen. The people of the kingdom knew something was different, and they began to treat their king with more respect.

The king declared that the snap was his special helper and messenger, and from that day forward, the people of the kingdom saw the snap as a sign of the unknown king's power.
