Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a razor and he liked to shave his dad's beard. One day, Timmy's dad got angry because Timmy cut his face. Timmy felt sad because he didn't mean to hurt his dad.

Timmy's mom saw him frown and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about what happened with his dad. His mom was thoughtful and told Timmy that he should be careful with the razor. Timmy promised to be more careful next time.

From that day on, Timmy was more careful when he shaved his dad's beard. He didn't want to hurt him again. Timmy's dad was happy that Timmy learned his lesson and they continued to shave together.

Yesterday, Amy went to the park. She found a new toy there. It was a splitting toy she had never seen before. She asked her mom if she could have it. Mom said yes and Amy was very happy. She hugged the new splitting toy and went home.

At home, Amy couldn't wait to try the toy. She put it on the table and tried it out. She laughed when it split into two pieces. She said "look! It splits!" She thought it was the most amazing thing ever. 

Then Amy showed the toy to her friend Billy. He was just as excited and they both took turns splitting it. They did it until it was getting late, then they said goodbye. 

Amy was so proud of her new splitting toy. She said to herself "I will play with it tomorrow too!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and sail her toy boat in the pond. One day, Lily's mom gave her a cup of juice to drink. Lily was so excited to drink the juice, but she accidentally spilled it all over her dress.

Lily's mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We'll go inside and change your dress." But Lily was persistent. She said, "No, Mommy. I want to sail my boat first." So, Lily sailed her boat in the pond with her wet dress.

After a while, Lily's boat got stuck in some weeds. She tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge. Then, a kind old man came by and asked, "Do you need help?"

Lily said, "Yes, please." The old man helped her get the boat unstuck and said, "Remember, Lily, it's okay to ask for help when you need it. And next time, be careful with your juice." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you!" From then on, Lily always asked for help when she needed it and never spilled her juice again.

Anna and Ben were on the same team for the game. They had to get the ball from the other team and put it in the goal. Anna was good at running and Ben was good at kicking. They liked to play together.

But the other team was bigger and stronger. They pushed and pulled and took the ball away. Anna and Ben tried to resist, but they could not get the ball back. They felt sad and angry.

"Let's try again," Anna said to Ben. "We can do it if we work together."

"OK," Ben said. "But we have to be gentle. We don't want to hurt anyone."

They waited for the right moment. When the other team was not looking, they ran to the ball. Anna grabbed it and passed it to Ben. Ben kicked it hard and fast. The ball flew past the other team and into the goal.

"Yay!" Anna and Ben shouted. "We did it! We scored!"

They hugged and high-fived. The other team looked surprised and upset. But then they clapped and smiled.

"Good job," one of them said. "That was a nice play."

"Thank you," Anna and Ben said. "You played well too."

They shook hands and hugged. They learned that they could resist and win, but they also had to be gentle and kind. They were happy to be on the same team.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy and she loved decorating. She found an old ornament in her backyard and wanted to share her find with her friends.

So, Lucy invited her friends over. She wanted to show them the old ornament she found. Her friends were excited and happy.

When they arrived, Lucy showed them the old ornament. Her friends were amazed and asked her how she found it.

"I was walking slow in the backyard and I saw something shiny," Lucy said. 

Her friends thought it was so cool. They asked Lucy if they could keep it for a few days and Lucy said yes. 

So, her friends took the old ornament to their house and said, "Thanks for inviting us over, Lucy!"

Lily and Ben are at the park with their mom. They like to play on the swings and the slide. They also like to watch the sky and see the birds and the clouds.

"Look, mom, a jet!" Ben says, pointing at a big, shiny plane that makes a loud noise. "It is so fast and loud!"

"Yes, it is, Ben. Do you know where it is going?" mom asks.

"Maybe it is going to another park, or to the zoo, or to the moon!" Ben says, making up stories.

Lily laughs. She likes Ben's stories. She also likes the jet. She wants to fly in a jet one day.

"Can we fly in a jet, mom?" Lily asks.

"Maybe one day, Lily. But flying in a jet is not easy. You need a ticket, and a suitcase, and you have to be very polite to the people who work at the airport and on the plane," mom says.

"I can be polite, mom. I can say please and thank you and excuse me," Lily says.

"Me too, mom. I can be polite," Ben says.

Mom smiles. She is proud of her polite children. She hugs them and says, "I love you, Lily and Ben. You are very good children. And maybe one day, we can fly in a jet together and see new places and have fun."

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to help. She lived near a river, so one day she decided to help the animals that lived in the water. 

She went to the river and looked for a way to help. She saw a boat and asked, 
"Can I borrow the boat? I want to help the animals."

The boatman said, "The boat is very cheap. You can borrow it and help the animals." 

The girl was so happy! She got in the boat and started to help. She gave the animals food and they were so happy to see her. 

The girl helped and the animals were so grateful. They waved goodbye as she sailed away in the boat. 

The girl learned that helping is a good thing. And she was so proud that she could help the animals by the river.

Once there was a little boy called Toby. He loved to go on nature walks. One day he went to the shore with his mommy. He saw something that made him very happy. It was a cute little boat! Toby demanded that his mommy take him for a ride in the boat.

They got in the boat and putted off to the middle of the sea. Toby looked all around and saw many fish swimming near the shore. They were so colourful and Toby thought they were so cute. As the boat continued to sail, Toby felt the breeze on his face. He loved feeling the wind blow against him.

When they finally reached the edge of the shore they got out of the boat. Toby was so happy he had gone on a boat ride with his mommy. He shouted in joy as he ran some more nature walks along the shore. He had a great day with his mommy, and he couldn't wait to do it all again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She had big, bright dreams. Every night she would dream of wonderful things, like castles and fairy queens. One day, Lucy saw a big, yellow butterfly. It was so pretty and it flew so gracefully through the sunshine. This made Lucy have a big dream - to fly like the butterfly!

Lucy became very creative. She tried lots of ways to make her dream come true. She used a broom, some washing line and even a wooden box. Nothing worked though.

Just when Lucy was about to give up, an old man gave her some wise advice. He said, "Lucy, sometimes dreams don't come true in the way we think. But if you use your creative ideas and keep trying, you might find your dreams come true in different ways!"

Lucy was so happy to hear this. She said thank you and never stopped believing in her dreams. She never stopped being creative, and eventually her dream came true - in her own special way!

The moral of the story is that with courage and creativity, you can make your dreams come true!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was very excited to go to the park with her mommy. They packed a picnic basket with yummy snacks and drinks. When they arrived at the park, they saw a police car and a man in handcuffs.

Lily asked her mommy, "Why is that man in jail?" Her mommy explained that sometimes people do bad things and they have to stay in jail as a punishment.

Lily felt sad for the man, but she was still excited to play in the park. She ran around and had fun on the swings and slide. When it was time to go home, Lily said, "Mommy, can we come back to the park tomorrow?" Her mommy replied, "Sure, we can stay here as long as we want."

Once upon a time there was a girl called Amy. One day, Amy arrived at a big gate. She was very excited. The gate was crazy! Amy looked up and saw some magical creatures flying around. Amy could not believe her eyes!

Amy ran up to the gate and began to pull at it. But the gate wouldn't open! Then Amy heard a noise - it was the gatekeeper! He was coming to help. The gatekeeper opened the gate for Amy and she stepped through it.

On the other side of the gate, Amy saw a magical world with castles, mountains and animals. Amy was so happy. She ran around exploring the new world and having fun.

At the end of the day, Amy went back through the gate and arrived back home. She was full of stories to tell her family and friends!

Once upon a time, there was a clever little girl. Her name was Sarah and she loved to play in the park.

On this day, she was playing on the swing. It was so much fun! She kept swinging higher and higher. Suddenly, Sarah felt something behind her. She looked back and saw a big pot. She was so surprised! 

She got off the swing to take a closer look. It was made of clay and had a pretty design. Sarah smiled when she noticed it had a little handle. She picked up the pot and began to swing with it. 

The pot had just the right weight, and Sarah really liked how it felt. She felt so clever and powerful. She swung with the pot for a long time, and had lots of fun. 

When it was time to go home, Sarah took the pot with her. She was sure she would find a fun way to play with it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she decided to have a tea party with her stuffed animals. She planned everything carefully, making sure to set the table with cups, saucers, and plates.

As she was pouring the tea, she noticed one of her stuffed animals, a bear named Teddy, was looking sad. She asked him what was wrong, and he told her he was feeling sick. Lily knew she had to be patient with Teddy and take care of him.

After the tea party was over, Lily put Teddy to bed and read him a story. She made sure he had plenty of water and a soft pillow to rest on. She was fair to all her stuffed animals, but she knew Teddy needed extra attention.

The next day, when Lily woke up, she was happy to see that Teddy was feeling better. She had planned to take him on a picnic, and she was glad he was well enough to come along. Lily learned that being patient and fair with her toys was important, and that taking care of them when they were sick was the right thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a very adventurous boy. He wanted to have some fun, so he went to the forest. He saw a big piece of wood and he wanted to pull it. He grabbed hold of it and started to pull. He tugged and tugged, but the wood wouldn't move. He tried and tried, but he couldn't get it to budge!

Then a big, furry bear came along and saw what the boy was doing. He said, "Let me help you." He grabbed hold of the wood and pulled with all his might. With the bear's help, the wood moved a little.

The boy and the bear kept pulling, and before long, the wood started to move more and more. The boy was so happy that he clapped his hands and cheered. After a lot of hard work, the wood was finally free! 
The boy thanked the bear for all his help. They said their goodbyes, and the boy went home feeling very accomplished. What an adventurous day it had been!

James was walking in the forest. He loved to explore the trees. Suddenly, he heard a voice. It said, "You there! Put up your weapon!" James was so scared. He looked around and saw a stranger. He was so tall and he had a cold look on his face. 

"What do you want?" asked James. 

"I want you to mark the tree," the stranger said. He gave James a long stick with a point on the end. 

James looked at the tree carefully. It was so big. He slowly started to mark it with the stick. The stranger smiled and said, "Good job!"

James finished marking the tree. He put down the weapon and ran away quickly. He was so relieved to leave the scary stranger. 

James kept exploring the forest. He thought it was such a special place. He couldn't wait to come back again.

Once there was a little boy who loved to play in the sun every day. He loved to run and laugh and make new friends. One day, he decided to go for a picnic with his mom. It was a mild day, so they packed a tasty meal to eat.

They spread out a big blanket and settled down in the sun. They each enjoyed a delicious meal, which made them both happy. Suddenly the wind started to blow, and it made the little boy's eyes water a bit. He sneezed too. 

His mom grabbed a towel and started to dry him up. She dried his eyes and his nose to make them feel better. Then she wiped away all the tiny crumbs from their meal, so that the little boy would have a nice clean blanket to play on. 

The sun smiled down on them and the little boy was very happy. He laughed and giggled and ran around in circles until it was time to go home. He gave his mom a big hug and thanked her for a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to visit his friends every day. One day, Benny saw a hole in the ground. He thought it would be fun to jump in it. But, Benny was not wise and did not know that the hole was very deep.

Benny jumped in the hole and could not get out. He cried and cried for help. Luckily, his wise friend, the owl, heard him and came to rescue him. The owl used his strong wings to lift Benny out of the hole.

Benny learned a valuable lesson that day. He realized that it is important to be wise and think before doing something. He also learned that it is important to have good friends who will help you when you are in trouble. From that day on, Benny never jumped into any holes again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She was a regular girl who loved to play outside in the wind. One day, Lily decided she wanted to wrap herself up in the wind like a blanket.
She ran outside and spun around and around, trying to wrap the wind around her. Suddenly, a loud noise came from above and Lily looked up to see her mom watching her.

"Lily, what are you doing?" asked her mom.

"I wanted to wrap the wind around me like a blanket," Lily said.

Her mom smiled. "That's very sweet of you, but you can't wrap the wind around you. The wind is free like the birds and can't be locked away in a blanket. You should take time to appreciate it, but not try to contain it."

Lily thought about what her mom said and understood the lesson. From then on, whenever Lily was outside and felt the wind, she would take a deep breath, smile and think about how lucky she was to feel it.

Mama and Jenny were on a long camping trip. They spread out the tent and set up their chairs by the campfire. Mama asked Jenny if she wanted to build a fort of logs. 

"Yes, Mama!" Jenny said excitedly.

So Mama and Jenny began stacking up the logs to make a fort. Mama asked Jenny "Are you sure it's tall enough?" 

But Jenny didn't answer. Mama looked up and saw Jenny running off into the distant forest.

Mama called out "Jenny, where are you going?"

But Jenny just kept running and disappeared among the trees. 

Mama knew Jenny can be adventurous, so she grabbed a flashlight and went after her. She found Jenny quickly, deep in the woods.

"Jenny, why did you run off so quickly?" asked Mama.

"I heard an animal in the woods, and I wanted to see it," said Jenny.

Mama smiled and hugged Jenny tightly. "We should quit exploring now," said Mama.

Jenny nodded and they went back to their campsite to pack up the tent. 

Mama promised Jenny that they could come camping again soon, so Jenny was happy as they drove away from the distant forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow because it was so cold and made her cheeks turn red. One day, Lily met a charming little snowman named Frosty. Frosty had a carrot nose and a hat on his head. They became friends and played together every day.

One day, Lily's mom lit a fire in the fireplace to keep the house warm. Lily asked her mom, "What does burn mean?" Her mom explained that it meant to turn something into ashes by using fire. Lily was sad because she thought about Frosty melting away if he got too close to the fire.

Later that day, Lily and Frosty were playing outside when they saw smoke rising from Lily's house. They ran inside and saw that the fire had gotten out of control. Frosty quickly ran to the fireplace and used his body to put out the flames. Lily was so grateful to her charming friend for saving her house. From that day on, Lily and Frosty played together every day and never got too close to anything that could burn.

John woke up and opened his eyes. He looked around his bedroom. John's bedroom had a big bed and a toy sack on the floor. He grabbed the sack and opened it. Inside he found lots of fun toys. He was excited!

John was about to play when he heard someone knocking at the door. It was his grandmother. John was so excited. "Welcome grandmother!" he said. 

Grandmother walked in with a big smile. She had a big sack in her hands. "I brought you a surprise," said Grandmother. John opened the sack and saw lots of candy inside. He was so happy! 

John said 'thank you' to his grandmother and ate the candy. After he ate them, he felt a little bit ashamed. He had eaten all the candy without sharing. 

Grandmother smiled. She said, "It's okay to feel ashamed. But then you can say sorry, and be more generous next time." John hugged his grandmother and said, "I'm sorry and I'll share next time!" Grandmother nodded with a smile.

One day, a dark cloud brought a flood. The flood was big and strong. Everybody was scared and ran home. All the animals ran away too! 
The water came higher and higher. It was dark outside and the water was very cold. The trees and houses were all wet. 
But the sun came out and brought the flood back down. Everybody was happy and could go outside again. They all cheered and hugged each other when the water was gone. 
It was a happy day when the dark cloud brought the flood but the sun and everyone brought it back down.

Once upon a time, there was a little child. The child was playing in a muddy puddle and was having lots of fun! But soon the child was very dirty and needed a wash.

The child's mama saw her and smiled. She was so happy to see the child having so much fun, but knew it was time for a wash. The mama was so compassionate, she said "come, it's time for a wash".

So the child begrudgingly followed her mama to the bathroom. The mama filled the bath with warm water, and began to scrub the child until she was nice and clean. The child felt so much better after the wash, and was so grateful to her mama for taking such good care of her. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ali. She loved to sing and dance, and she was always in the rhythm. One day, Ali was walking around in the park when she saw a man. He seemed rude and mean. 

"Hi, whatâ€™s your name?" Ali asked.

The man said nothing and went away. Ali was sad and felt very lonely.

The next day, Ali went to the park again, but this time she was more careful. When the man showed up once again, Ali decided to stay away from him. She kept a distance and watched him carefully. Suddenly, the man turned around and shouted at Ali in a very rude way.

Ali was very scared and quickly ran home.

The moral of this story is: always be careful of strangers and don't talk to them. It's better to stay away and not get too close.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little pup. His name was Copper and he was so excited to explore the world. As Copper ran around, he noticed a big red toy car. He wanted to drive it and pretend he was a real driver, so he grabbed the car and started running in reverse.

He was so proud of himself, running in reverse like an adult! But then, Copper tripped and the toy car fell over. Copper started to cry and all his pride was gone.

He was so sad. He didn't know what to do until he heard a voice. It was his mom. She said he was still cute, even when he made mistakes. Copper smiled and his mom hugged him and said "Next time, try going forward instead of in reverse and you'll stay safe!"

So Copper listened to his mom and started driving around the house safely, going forwards. He had so much fun and he was proud he listened to his mommy!

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He was very scary, but also very colorful. He had a red mane and yellow fur. One day, it rained and the lion got wet. He did not like being wet, so he went to a sunny spot to dry off. 

The lion lay in the sun and his fur started to dry. It felt good to be warm and dry again. A little bird saw the lion and asked why he was so colorful. The lion said it was because he liked to look pretty. 

The bird thought that was silly, but the lion didn't mind. He was just happy to be dry and warm in the sun. From then on, whenever it rained, the lion would find a sunny spot to dry off and show off his colorful fur. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pair of scissors that she used to cut paper and make pretty crafts. One day, Lily went to the store with her mom and saw a toy that she really wanted. But it was too expensive and her mom said no. 

Lily felt sad and started to cry. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can make our own toy at home with your scissors and some paper!" Lily's face lit up and she started to clap with joy. 

They went home and made a beautiful paper butterfly together. Lily was so happy and proud of her creation, and she realized that sometimes the best things in life don't have to be expensive. She hugged her mom and they both clapped in celebration of their fun afternoon together.

There was once a little boy who wanted something to trust. One day he went to the pond and looked in the water, and he saw a fish. The boy had a feeling of wonder and he knew he could trust the fish. Together they had many adventures.

The boy and the fish got along really well, but luck ran out one day. The boy was playing in a rough part of the forest, and he couldn't find the fish anywhere. He was worried and scared, but then he remembered to trust and wonder. Suddenly, the fish appeared out of the water and the boy was so happy.

From then on, the boy and the fish were best friends and the boy trusted the fish with all his heart. Everywhere the boy went, the fish would magically show up and follow him. They never stopped trusting each other and always stuck together no matter how rough the journey got.

John was walking in the park. He saw something shiny and picked it up. It was a battery! He was so excited. He wanted to show everyone.

John started walking faster, but he was running too fast. He tripped and started to fall. His battery flew out of his hands and rolled away.

John was so sad. He wanted to find his battery. He asked his mom if she could help him. His mom said yes. They started to look.

John and his mom looked for a long time. They could not find the battery. John was about to give up, when he saw something! It was his battery! He was so happy.

John picked the battery up. He knew it was important so he held it tight. He thanked his mom for helping him. They both smiled and walked back home.

Jim was a dancer. He owned his own theatre, where people regularly came to see him perform. One day, a little girl named Sally walked into his theatre. She was only 3 years old.

Jim smiled when he saw her. â€œHello there!â€ he said. â€œDo you like dancing?â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat grapes, especially the yellow ones. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a little boy who looked sad. Lily went over to him and gave him a big hug. The boy smiled and they became friends. They played together and ate some yummy yellow grapes. From that day on, they were always happy when they saw each other at the park.

Once upon a time there were two nations that were very far apart. One nation was very small and the other nation was very big. The two nations did not get along. 

One day, a thick fog rolled in and the two nations could no longer see each other. They had no idea the other nation was still there. 

The small nation had an idea. They asked their good friend, a big elephant, if they could borrow his trunk. The elephant agreed and gave them a very long trunk. 

The small nation tied their end of the trunk to their village tree and they called out to the other nation. They asked them to accept the trunk and connect it to their village. 

The other nation was scared at first, but they accepted the trunk. As soon as they tied their end to the tree, the fog lifted and the two nations were very happy to see each other again. They became friends and traveled often between the two villages.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat avocados because they were green and yummy. One day, Lily's mom brought home a big, messy avocado for her to eat.

Lily's face lit up with excitement when she saw the avocado. She grabbed it with her little hands and started to eat it. But soon she realized that it was too messy and she didn't know how to eat it properly.

Lily's mom saw her struggling and said, "Lily, let me show you how to eat the avocado. You have to act like a big girl and use a spoon to scoop it out." Lily listened carefully and soon she was eating the avocado like a pro. She felt proud of herself and happy that she learned something new. From that day on, Lily always ate her avocados with a spoon and never made a messy avocado again.

Once there was an ant who was very modest. He never took more than he needed, so all his friends liked him. 

One day, he had to carry a fork to the top of a hill. But he was so tiny, he couldn't carry it by himself. So he asked his friends for help. 

But his friends were too busy doing their own thing, so the ant had to carry the fork all by himself. He suffered along the way, and it took him a long time to make it to the top. 

When he got there, he was exhausted. But he was so proud of himself for making it to the top. He felt happy that he had done it all by himself.

Once there was a little girl named Chloe who loved to cook. Every day, she would go to the kitchen, and make something tasty for everyone to try.

Today, Chloe wanted to cook something special. She thought about it for a moment and then came up with a great idea. She ran outside to her lawn, and there collected lots of yummy flowers, bright and colourful.

Once she'd collected enough flowers, Chloe ran back into the kitchen. She began to wash and chop the flowers until they were all ready. Then she put the flowers in a pot and cooked them up with some butter and sugar.

When the flowers were cooked, Chloe added them to some Strawberry ice-cream. Everyone thought it tasted so good, they all cheered and laughed. They had created a delicious and bright treat.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely girl named Lily. She had a pretty skirt that she loved to wear. It was her favorite because it was pink and had flowers on it.

One sunny day, Lily wanted to help her mom. Her mom was busy polishing the table to make it shiny and clean. Lily asked if she could help polish, too. Her mom said yes and gave her a soft cloth to use.

Lily was very happy to help. She polished the table carefully, making sure not to get her pretty skirt dirty. When they were done, the table looked shiny and new. Lily's mom was proud of her and they both had big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. The mommy loved to teach the little girl all sorts of things. She taught her to read, to write and to be kind. But the most important thing she taught her was about sugar. She showed her how sugar can be tasty but it is not good for your body. She said that sugar should only be eaten once in a while and never too much.

When the little girl asked how sugar can be bad, the mommy showed her. She took the little girl to the kitchen and showed her the sugar. It was white and sparkly and looked so sweet. The mommy showed the little girl that if she ate too much it could make her feel bad.

The mommy also taught the little girl how to keep her body clean. She said that it was very important to wash her hands and face often. She said that every day she should take a nice warm bath. The mommy showed her how to use the soap and wash her body. The little girl felt so clean and fresh afterwards.

The little girl learned many things from her mommy. She learned to eat sugar in moderation and to keep her body clean. She was so thankful for the things her mommy taught her.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to splash in the puddles and make mud pies. They saw a big hole in the ground with a metal cover. It was a drain.

"Let's open it and see what's inside," Tom said. He pulled on the cover, but it was too heavy.

"Maybe there are monsters or treasure in there," Lily said. She helped Tom push the cover, but it did not move.

They heard a loud noise. It was Mom. She was holding a hose. She was going to water the flowers.

"Hi, kids. Do you want to help me?" Mom asked. She smiled and offered them the hose.

Tom and Lily nodded. They liked to help Mom. They took the hose and sprayed water on the flowers. They also sprayed water on each other and laughed.

But they sprayed too much water. The puddles grew bigger and bigger. The water reached the drain. The cover slid off and fell into the hole.

"Uh-oh," Tom and Lily said. They ran to the drain and looked inside. It was dark and wet. They saw the cover at the bottom. They also saw something shiny.

"Look, it's a coin!" Lily said. "Maybe it's a treasure!"

She reached for the coin, but Tom stopped her.

"No, don't go in there. It's dangerous. Mom will be angry," he said.

He was right. Mom came and saw the open drain. She was angry and scared.

"Kids, what have you done? That's very naughty and unsafe. You could have fallen in and hurt yourself. Come here right now!" she said.

She took the hose and turned it off. She picked up Tom and Lily and carried them inside. She gave them a bath and a scolding. She told them to never play with the drain again.

Tom and Lily were sorry. They said they were sorry to Mom. They also said they were sorry to the coin. They hoped it was not lonely in the wet drain.

Once upon a time, there was a new hammer. The hammer lived in a big box with other tools. One day, a kind man took the hammer out of the box. The man wanted to fix a broken chair. The hammer was very excited to help.

The man said, "Hammer, can you supply me with your help?" The hammer said, "Yes, I can help you fix the chair!" The man and the hammer worked together. They hit the nails into the chair until it was all fixed.

When they finished, the man was very happy. He said, "Thank you, hammer, for supplying your help!" The hammer felt proud and glad to be useful. From that day on, the hammer and the man became good friends, and they fixed many things together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cup that she loved to drink juice from every day. The cup was dependable and never spilled.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and brought her cup with her. She played on the swings and the slide, but then she noticed her cup was missing. She asked her mom if she had seen it, but her mom questioned her and said she didn't know.

Lily looked everywhere for her cup, but she couldn't find it. She felt sad and didn't want to play anymore. When it was time to go home, Lily still didn't have her cup. She cried all the way home. It was a bad ending to a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going on a camping trip. Timmy was very excited! 

As they were packing, Timmy's mom reminded him to bring his flashlight. Timmy grabbed his flashlight and put it in his backpack. 

When they arrived at the campsite, Timmy wanted to explore right away. He saw a beautiful lake and wanted to go swimming. But his mom told him they needed to set up the tent first. Timmy was impatient and wanted to hurry up, but he knew he had to help his mom. 

That night, when it got dark, Timmy was glad he brought his flashlight. They used it to find their way back to the tent. Timmy realized that it was important to be patient and listen to his mom's advice. He learned that sometimes it's bitter to wait, but it's worth it in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spicy food and she would always ask her mom to make her food extra spicy. One day, Lily's mom made her a big plate of spicy noodles for lunch. 

As Lily was eating her noodles, she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her mouth. She realized that she had accidentally swallowed a spicy chili pepper whole! Lily started to panic and cry. Her mom knew it was an emergency and quickly called the doctor. 

When the doctor arrived, he knew just what to do. He gave Lily a special medicine that would make the spicy feeling go away. Before leaving, the doctor gave Lily a big kiss on the forehead and told her to be more careful when eating spicy food. From that day on, Lily always made sure to chew her food carefully before swallowing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma loved to go on adventures.
One day, Emma decided to visit her Aunt Kathy's house. When she arrived at her Aunt Kathy's house there was a charming porch on the front. 
Emma was so excited to play on the porch. She climbed up the stairs and explored every nook and corner. Then, she heard a voice.

"Hi Emma!" said the voice.

"Who said that?" asked Emma curiously.

The voice said again, "It's me, your Aunt Kathy! I'm so happy you're here to visit. I'm so glad you love the porch!" 

Emma smiled and said, "I love it! It's so charming and fun to explore!"

Aunt Kathy and Emma had a blast playing on the porch. They made memories that would last forever. 

The end.

Once upon a long time ago, there was a wise and intelligent man. He would hang around the village and help people with their problems. One day, he decided to climb the mountain and hang up a wish in a great big tree. As he climbed higher, he noticed that larger and larger birds were flying around him and making a lot of noise. But he kept on climbing until he reached the top of the mountain.

When he arrived at the top, he opened the pouch he had been carrying and he took out a little bit of his wisdom and hung it in the big tree. All of the birds were still making noise, so he whispered something in the tree. Then he made his way back to the village.

For days and weeks, the man wondered if his wish would ever come true. Then one day, something amazing happened. There was a knock at his door and the man opened it to find a very intelligent child standing there. He welcomed the child in and asked him what he wanted. The child said he had come for the wisdom that was hanging in the tree!

The man was amazed and very pleased that his wish had come true. He knew at once that this child had come for the wisdom and that he must have been sent by the birds! The man was delighted to share his wisdom with the child and the two of them had lots of fun. From then on, the child was considered a very wise and intelligent person in the

Tommy was grumpy. He did not want to go to bed. He wanted to watch TV with Mom and Dad. But Mom said, "No, Tommy, it is late. You need to sleep. Come on, let's go to the bathroom and brush your teeth."

Tommy followed Mom to the bathroom, but he was not happy. He did not want to brush his teeth. He wanted to play. He saw a towel on the rack. He had an idea. He grabbed the towel and wrapped it around his neck. He said, "Look, Mom, I am a superhero. I can fly and save the world."

Mom smiled. She said, "Wow, Tommy, you are a great superhero. You can perform amazing feats. But you know what else superheroes do? They take care of their teeth. They brush them every night before they go to bed. That makes them strong and healthy. Do you want to be a strong and healthy superhero, Tommy?"

Tommy thought for a moment. He liked being a superhero. He wanted to be strong and healthy. He said, "OK, Mom, I will brush my teeth. But can I keep the towel? I want to wear it in bed. Maybe I will have a dream about flying and saving the world."

Mom said, "Sure, Tommy, you can keep the towel. But only if you promise to sleep well and not stay up too late. Deal?"

Tommy nodded. He said, "Deal, Mom. Thank you. I love you."

Mom said, "I love you too, Tommy. Good night, my superhero."

She kissed him on the forehead and tucked him in. She turned off the light and left the room. Tommy closed his eyes and hugged the towel. He felt less grumpy. He felt happy. He fell asleep and dreamed of flying and saving the world.

Tim likes to jog with his dad. They jog in the park and see many things. They see birds, flowers, dogs and people. Tim likes to say hello to everyone. He is a compassionate boy.

One day, they jog near a big drain. The drain has a metal cover with holes. Tim is curious and looks inside. He sees water and mud. He wants to touch it, but his dad says no. He says the drain is dirty and dangerous.

Tim listens to his dad, but he sees something shiny in the drain. It is a coin. He thinks it is a treasure. He reaches for it, but his dad stops him. He says the coin is not worth it. He says he has a better treasure for him.

He takes out a small box from his pocket and gives it to Tim. Tim opens it and sees a compass. It is a gift from his dad. He says the compass can help him find his way. He says he loves him very much.

Tim hugs his dad and says thank you. He is very happy. He puts the compass in his pocket and holds his dad's hand. They jog away from the drain and continue their adventure.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She loved nature. Every day, she would take a thin stick and go walking in the forest.

One day, Lucy saw a bird flapping his wings in the sky. She wanted to fly like the bird, so she asked her mom for help. She requested for some wings.

Her mom smiled lovingly and told Lucy that only nature can give her wings. She said, â€œLook around you, Lucy! Nature has many gifts to offer.â€

Lucy looked around. The trees were waving in the breeze, the little birds were chirping happily and the sun was shining brightly. Lucy smiled and said, â€œYes, nature is a wonderful place!â€

From that day on, Lucy would always take a thin stick and explore her beautiful nature. She knew that if she was patient, nature would reward her with the gift of wings one day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was a reliable friend, always helping others when they needed it. Tim had a big toy box with lots of fun toys to play with. He liked to play with his toy cars and his toy animals.

One day, Tim was playing with his toys when he felt like he needed to go to the toilet. He ran to the bathroom as fast as his little legs could carry him. Tim was very proud that he could use the toilet all by himself.

After Tim used the toilet, he went back to play with his toys. But, he could not find his favorite toy car. Tim started to cry because he was very sad. His mom came to help him look for the toy car. They searched everywhere, and finally, they found it under the couch. Tim was so happy, and he stopped crying. He thanked his mom and continued playing with his toys, knowing that his mom was always there to help him.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toy animals. Anna has a lion and Ben has a giraffe. They make the animals talk to each other.

"Hello, lion. I am giraffe. Do you want to be friends?" Ben says.

"Yes, giraffe. I want to be friends. You are very tall and I am very strong. We can help each other," Anna says.

They play for a long time, making the animals run, jump, and eat. They have fun and laugh a lot.

Soon, it is evening. The sky is dark and the stars are bright. Anna and Ben's mom calls them.

"Anna, Ben, it is time to go to bed. Come and brush your teeth and put on your pajamas," mom says.

Anna and Ben do not want to stop playing. They want to play more with their animals.

"Mom, can we play a little more? Please, please, please?" Anna says.

"Mom, we are having so much fun. Just a little more?" Ben says.

Mom smiles and shakes her head. She is patient with them.

"No, my loves. You have played enough for today. You need to sleep and rest. You can play more tomorrow. Come on, let's go," mom says.

Anna and Ben sigh. They know mom is right. They pick up their animals and hug them.

"Good night, lion. Good night, giraffe. Thank you for being my friend," Anna says.

"Good night, giraffe. Good night, lion. You are my best friend," Ben says.

They put their animals on their beds and follow mom. Before they go to their rooms, they bow to each other.

"Good night, Anna. Good night, Ben. You are my best sister/brother," they say.

They kiss mom and go to sleep. They dream of their animals and their friendship.

Once there was a baby who was very sleepy. She wanted to go and see the stadium, but she was too sleepy to walk. So she decided to crawl instead. She crawled and crawled until she arrived at the stadium. There were lots of people there and she was so excited! She crawled around and around to explore the stadium and she was very happy. When she was done exploring, she curled up in a corner and fell asleep. She was so happy and content after her adventure at the stadium.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved pie and would always ask her mommy to make some. One day, her mommy made a delicious apple pie and Lily was very enthusiastic about it. She couldn't wait to eat it!

As she took a bite, she felt the ground tremble. She was scared and didn't know what to do. But then she realized it was just her tummy rumbling because she was so hungry. She laughed and ate more pie.

From then on, Lily would always get enthusiastic about pie and her tummy would tremble with excitement. And every time she ate pie, she would remember the time her tummy trembled and she would laugh.

Tom and Lily are twins. They like to play in their house. Sometimes they play with their toys, sometimes they play with their dog, and sometimes they play on the stair.

One day, they decide to play on the stair. They take their pillows and blankets and make a fort. They pretend they are in a castle and they are the king and the queen. They enjoy their game very much.

But their mom is working in her room. She needs to be quiet. She does not like the noise that Tom and Lily make on the stair. She tells them to stop and play somewhere else.

Tom and Lily are sad. They do not want to leave their fort. They do not want to make their mom angry. They think of a way to play on the stair and be quiet.

They find some books and crayons. They sit on the stair and read and draw. They whisper to each other and giggle softly. They enjoy their new game too.

Their mom is happy. She can work in her room and be quiet. She is proud of Tom and Lily for being good and creative. She gives them a hug and a kiss and tells them she loves them.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. She was three years old and loved the springtime. She loved the colorful flowers, the butterflys and the birds that she would see outside. 

One day, Daisy was out in the garden looking at the bright purple flowers. She wanted to pick one so she could keep it forever, but deep down she knew she couldn't. She sighed, and instead collected some stones scattered around the flowerbed.

That night, she showed her stones to her mom. Her mom smiled, and said "It's ok if you take something out of nature as long as you put something back too". She then helped Daisy make her very own purple flower out of the stones she had collected. 

Daisy was so happy! She had learnt an important lesson - always leave nature as you found it, and maybe even add back something extra. She smiled, waved goodbye to her precious purple flower, and went off to bed dreaming of more adventures in springtime.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie. The birdie had a pretty feather on its tail. The feather was yellow and soft. One day, the birdie flew very fast and the feather fell off. 

A little girl saw the feather on the ground. She wanted to grab it. She ran to the feather and picked it up with her hand. The feather felt ticklish on her hand. She smiled and showed it to her mommy. 

Mommy said, "That's a beautiful feather! Where did you get it?" The little girl said, "From a birdie! It flew very fast!" Mommy smiled and hugged her little girl. They both looked at the feather and felt happy.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn cat named Tom. Tom loved to sit on the porch all day. He would watch the birds and the bugs. One day, a little girl named Lisa came to play with Tom.

"Tom, let's play!" Lisa said. But Tom was stubborn and did not want to play. He just sat on the porch, watching the birds and the bugs. Lisa tried to make Tom play, but he would not move.

Finally, Lisa had an idea. She took a ball and threw it near the edge of the porch. Tom saw the ball and wanted to catch it. He jumped off the porch to get the ball. But, Tom did not see a big hole in the ground near the porch.

Tom fell into the hole and could not get out. Lisa was sad and cried. She called for help, but no one came. The stubborn cat stayed in the hole and never got out. The end.

John and his mommy went for a walk. They looked up and saw a pale bull. It was very big. John was scared and he held on to mommy's hand. The bull was standing in the field looking around. Then he started to walk away.

John looked at mommy and asked if they could get closer to the bull. Mommy said no and held John tight. They watched as the bull walked further away.

John asked if he could pet the bull. Mommy told him maybe when he was older.

John looked sad, but then saw a bird in the sky and smiled. He watched as the bird flew away. Then he and his mommy started walking back home.

Once there was a duck who was very rich. She lived in a big pond and had a lot of friends. One day, the duck decided she wanted to borrow an opinion.

"Who will lend me an opinion?" she asked her friends.

One of her friends, a frog, said, "I can help you with that!"

The duck was grateful and took the frog's advice. She soon had a very good opinion and was very happy. 

"Thank you for lending me your opinion," she said to her friend. 

The frog smiled. "You're welcome. It's always a pleasure to lend a helping hand." 

And from that day on, the duck was even richer in her opinion.

Once upon a time, there lived a mighty folder that could reverse time. One day, a 3-year-old named Jax was playing in the garden when he noticed something strange. He saw the mighty folder lying in the grass, shining in the sun. Jax was curious, so he picked it up and held it in his hands. 

"Wow!" he said, examining its shimmering surface. Suddenly, he heard a voice in his head. 

"This folder can reverse time," the voice said. "But be careful; reversing time can be dangerous." Jax was confused but he put the folder away in his pocket and finished playing. 

The next day, Jax forgot all about the folder until he heard news that his best friend was sick. Jax felt sad and wished he could do something to help his friend. So he took the folder out of his pocket and opened it. To his surprise, time began to move backward and his friend was cured! 

Jax had used the folder's mighty power to reverse time and save his friend. From then on, he vowed to never use the power of the folder carelessly.

One day, Mommy and Daddy took John to the beach. John was excited! He saw the tide coming in and out and watched the birds flying around.

Mommy and Daddy went for a walk to explore the beach and offered John a snack. But he wanted something special. So they offered him an ice cream. John was so happy!

John was embarrassed when he dropped some of his ice cream. It spilled all over the sand. He didn't know what to do and he felt embarrassed.

Mommy and Daddy told him it was ok. They offered him a towel to clean up and hugged him tight. Daddy said that everyone makes mistakes, even grownups like them! That made John feel better. 

With a full tummy and a happy heart, John watched the tide come in and out until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was an little girl called Mia. She was very clever and she loved fashion. Every day she would pick out an outfit and wear it proudly. But some days it was hard to choose what to wear.

One day Mia started feeling a bit sad. She didn't know why, but it felt quite bitter. She decided to go for a walk and see if it would help her feel better. On her walk she saw a lady walking down the street in the most beautiful clothes.

Mia stopped and looked in amazement. This lady had the most incredible fashion she had ever seen. Mia smiled for the first time that day. She knew she wanted to make her own fashion, just like the lady down the street.

So, with a new found confidence Mia started making her own outfits. She made clothes that were as beautiful as the lady on the street, but they were different and special. She put them on with a great big smile, knowing she could share her fashion with the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she wanted to have a party with her friends. So, she decided to invite them over to her house. She made pretty invitations with colorful paper and stickers.

Suddenly, there was an emergency! The cake she baked fell on the floor and broke into pieces. Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. But, she remembered that she was creative. She decided to make cupcakes instead and decorate them with sprinkles and frosting.

When her friends arrived, they were happy to see the pretty cupcakes. They played games and danced to music. Lily was happy that her friends came to her party and that she was able to be creative and make something yummy for them to eat.

Charlie was excited to help cook dinner. He had a surprise for his mom. He gathered the ingredients from the kitchen, ready to make soup. He poured ingredients into a pot, one by one to match the recipe.

He stirred the soup with a spoon and it started to bubble. It smelled delicious! He carefully poured the soup into a bowl and grabbed a spoon to test it.

It was just right! He was becoming more and more independent every day. His mom was so proud as she watched him make her soup.

Charlie served his mom the soup for dinner and she smiled with delight. She enjoyed every spoonful of his delicious work.

Charlie was happy to show his mom just how independent he was. He had made the perfect match.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a bird with enormous wings. The bird was very nice and liked to help others. One day, the bird met a small ant who was lost.

The ant said, "Please help me find my way home." The bird, using its big wings, ordered the ant to climb on its back. The bird flew high and looked for the ant's home.

After a while, they found the ant's home. The ant was very happy and thanked the bird. The bird felt good for helping the ant. From that day on, they became very good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big meeting with her friends at the park. Lily was very excited to see her friends and play with them. She asked her mom for some money to buy ice cream.

Her mom said, "Sure, but you have to pay for it." Lily nodded her head and put the money in her pocket. When she got to the park, her friends were already there. They were playing a fierce game of tag. Lily joined in and had so much fun.

After playing, they all sat down to eat their ice cream. Lily paid for hers and her friend's ice cream. Her friends were happy and thanked her. Lily was happy too because she got to see her friends and had a lot of fun.

John was eager to go to the park yesterday. He asked his mum excitedly if he could go. His mum said "Yes you can go, but only if you promise me you'll be careful".

John promised his mum he would be safe and he ran outside. When he arrived he saw a new boy playing in the sandpit. He eagerly made his way over to the boy. The boy stopped playing and said "Hello".
John was delighted to have a new friend and he ran to get his favourite bucket and spade to show him. He quickly ran back and the new boy said "What's your name?".
John said "I'm John. What's yours?".
The boy said "My name is Dave. Hey, I have a good joke."
John was eagerly waiting to hear it.

Suddenly a gang of kids walked up to Dave and said "I'm sure it won't be a good joke. I bet you can't even tell it".
Dave looked scared and said "We can joke tomorrow, I don't want to tell it today."
John felt disappointed and watched as the gang of kids made Dave leave the park.

John sadly walked home, wishing that he hadn't promised his mum to be careful as he would have had the chance to share the joke with Dave.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy was very curious and loved to explore new places. One day, he found himself in a big room filled with lots of cheese. Timmy was so excited and started to eat all the cheese he could find. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise and saw a big cat coming towards him. Timmy was scared and knew he had to escape. He quickly ran towards a small hole in the wall and squeezed through it. 

As he was running away, he saw a needle on the ground. He remembered his mother telling him to never touch needles because they could hurt him. Timmy felt lucky that he didn't step on it and continued to run. 

After a while, Timmy realized that he had eaten too much cheese and his stomach felt very empty. He learned that even though something might look good, it doesn't mean it's always good for you. From that day on, Timmy was more careful and always listened to his mother's advice.

One day, a little girl named Sarah had an exciting day ahead of her. She was going to the park with her parents! She jumped around with glee. 

When they arrived at the park, Sarah saw that it was big and beautiful. She could hardly contain her excitement. All around, the trees were tall and green and the sky was a pale blue.

Sarah's father said, "It's time to go inside the park, Sarah. Are you ready?" Sarah happily nodded yes and followed her dad. She looked around. Everything was new and exciting - there were lots of other children playing, birds singing and lots of tall, green trees. 

Suddenly, Sarah heard her father call out, "It's time for ice cream!" She was so excited that she ran to where her father had ordered the ice cream for her.

Sarah smiled with delight; all of her anticipation had paid off with a delicious treat! The ice cream was creamy and sweet. She knew her day at the park would be a great one!

Timmy was on his way to the park with his dad. He had never been there before, so he was excited and filled with wonder. He had never seen a cooler filled with such colorful drinks before. His dad said he could have one, but only if he promised to be responsible.

At the park, Timmy was filled with even more wonder as he saw all the different things there was to do. He wanted to do them all, but his dad said he could only pick one and that he must stay where he could be seen. 

Timmy chose to go on the swings and had so much fun that he almost forgot about the cooler. But then he started to get thirsty and remembered. He asked his dad if he could have one of the drinks, but his dad said no. He said that he wouldn't be responsible if he had one. 

Timmy was so upset that he started to cry. He felt so disappointed and wasn't sure what to do. Suddenly, his dad knelt down, looked him in the eyes and said, "Listen, Timmy. You can have a drink, but only if you promise to be responsible and share with your friends.â€ Timmy smiled, wiped away his tears and ran off to grab a colorful drink from the cooler!

Once there was a little girl named Jenny. One day, she wanted to play on the slide at the park. When she got there, she noticed something was not quite right. "My slide is broken!" she said. 

Jenny's mom comforted her and said, "It's ok. We can fix it". So they went to the park store and looked at all the tools. Jenny found an organized set of tools with just what they needed.

Jenny and her mom went back to the slide and got to work. They worked together to repair the slide and made sure it was safe and sturdy.

When they were done, Jenny stepped back and smiled. "We did it!" she said.

"Yes, we did!" said her mom. "Now let's go and have some fun on the slide!"

Jenny cheered and ran to the slide. She had a wonderful time, thanks to her mom's help to repair the slide.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were playing together in the park on a sunny day. 
Suddenly, they heard a loud scream, coming from a tree. Jack and Jill were very scared, so they ran to the tree to find out what it was. 
When they reached the tree, they saw a small bird sitting on a plate. The plate looked very dry, so Jack and Jill thought the bird must have been very thirsty. 
"We need to get this bird some water," Jack said. 
Jill nodded in agreement and the two friends ran off to find the bird some water. They soon came back with a full plate of cool, refreshing water. 
The bird was so thankful and started to drink the water. After it was done, the bird flew away with a happy chirp. 
Jack and Jill were so relieved to have helped the bird and returned home with a big smile on their faces.

"Once upon a time there was a small, harmless mouse. The mouse liked to chew and escape from danger.

One day, the mouse spotted a giant piece of cheese in the corner of the room. Chewing as fast as possible, the mouse was determined to find a way to escape with her prize.

Suddenly, the mouse freezeed as it heard a gruff voice speaking. It was an evil cat, who planned to catch the mouse in his claws and make it his next snack.

The mouse quickly devised a plan. She started to chew her way through the floorboards, desperately seeking an escape. Finally, the mouse had made a hole big enough to fit her body throught to freedom.

But it was too late! The cat had spotted the mouse just as she was soaring through the hole, and lunged toward her with claws outstretched. 

The mouse had no choice but to frantically run away and leave her cheese as the cat's reward. She was lucky to escape, but the cheese was gone without a trace.

The End"

Bob and his mom were at the park. It was a sunny day and Bob was happy to be outside.

Bob pointed at the playground and said, "Mom, can I go there?" His mom nodded and said, "Yes, have fun!"

Bob ran to the playground and looked around. He saw something very impressive. There was a tall rail next to a slide.

He wanted to try it, so he put his hands on the rail and tried to climb over it. It was tall, but he was determined. He put his foot on the rail, then he put his other foot on the rail too. Finally, he made it over the rail!

Bob was so proud of himself. He clapped and jumped. He had done something impressive!

The little girl gazed up at the enormous dove. It was so big that she could barely make out the details. Its wings were a soft grey colour and its eyes were bright and shiny.

The girl was amazed by the bird. She felt a special kind of energy coming from it. It was like the dove had a secret, but she couldn't quite understand it.

She had never seen such a beautiful creature, so she just stood there looking at it, mesmerised by its beauty. She reached out her hand and let the dove gently nuzzle it.

The dove and girl stared at each other. She felt she could understand everything the dove was trying to tell her. In that moment, she felt deeply connected to the bird.

Jeff was a brave child. His mom gave him a new folder for him to keep his toys in. He carefully tucked it away under his bed. But he couldn't sleep that night. He was too excited.

He thought of an adventure he wanted to try. He wanted to move his folder to the other side of the room. He knew it would be a big challenge and thought that only brave children would dare to do it.

So, Jeff took a deep breath and carefully crawled out of bed. He held his folder tight and tip-toed to the other side of the room. All the while he was scared but excited at the same time. He made it all the way there, placed his folder down and quickly crawled back in bed.

Jeff was very pleased with himself. He felt so brave that he beamed with pride for the rest of the night. Even though he was quite sleepy, he just stared at his folders, thinking about his daring adventure and all the exciting things he could store in it.

Once there was a bulb that was pale. It was very lonely. One day, it heard a noise coming from outside. It was a loud sound that made the bulb very scared. 

The bulb looked outside and saw two little children running around in the garden. 

The bulb thought that it would be nice to make friends with them. So, it separated itself from the ground and rolled towards the children. 

The children were so excited to see the bulb! They were so happy that they started playing together.

The pale bulb was now part of a happy family. They would play together in the garden every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to eat some spaghetti for dinner, but she couldn't find her fork. She looked everywhere in the kitchen, but it was nowhere to be found.

Lily's mom came into the kitchen and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her that she couldn't find her fork. Her mom asked her if she believed that it could be in her room. Lily thought about it and said, "Yes, I believe it could be in my room!"

So Lily went to her room and looked around. She found her fork under her bed! She was so happy and ran back to her mom to show her. Her mom said, "Wow, you're so smart for thinking to look in your room! Now let's eat some spaghetti with your fork."

Joey was very ready for his day. He hopped out of bed and put on his shoes. He grabbed a board and went outside. He could see his friends playing in the park.

Joey went to the playground. He put his board down and was ready to play. He saw a tall slide and ran to it. He climbed up the ladder and got to the top of the slide. Then he held on tight and bounced down!

When he reached the bottom, Joey felt so happy. He got back up again and did it again. Joey bounced down the slide again and again. He couldn't get enough of it!

At the end of the day, Joey was tired but he had had so much fun. He put his board away and went inside to get ready for bed. Joey knew that the next day he would come back and bounce on the slide again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy brought home a big box. "Let's unpack it together," said mommy. Lily was excited to see what was inside. 

As they opened the box, Lily saw something yummy. "Muffins!" she exclaimed. Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, we're lucky to have them." They ate the muffins together and they were very delicious. 

Later that day, Lily went to play outside. She saw her friend Timmy and said, "I had a muffin today! It was so yummy!" Timmy was excited and said, "I want to try one too!" Lily remembered that her mommy had packed an extra muffin. She ran back home to get it for Timmy. 

When she arrived home, she saw the box was still open. She looked inside and saw a toy she had been wanting for a long time. She knew it was meant for her, but she also knew how much Timmy wanted a muffin. She thought about it for a moment and then decided to give the toy to Timmy instead. When she gave the toy to Timmy, he was so happy and said, "Lily, you're the best friend ever!" From that day on, they shared everything they had and were always lucky to have each other.

Once there were two friends, a kitten and a puppy. The puppy and kitten loved to play together every day. One day, they decided they should get a treat.

The puppy wanted to get a rare cookie, but the kitten wanted to get ice cream. The puppy and kitten could not agree. 

The puppy said, â€œI want the rare cookie!â€

The kitten said, â€œNo! I want ice cream!â€

The puppy insisted on the rare cookie and the kitten insisted on ice cream. They argued and disagreed until they were too angry to talk to each other.

The puppy sadly walked away, never to see the kitten again. The kitten was left with no treat at all.

Lily and Ben were on a big train with their mom and dad. They were going to visit their grandma and grandpa in another town. Lily and Ben liked to look out the window and see the trees, the houses, and the animals.

"Look, Ben, a cow!" Lily said, pointing to a black and white cow in a field.

"Moo!" Ben said, making a cow sound.

Mom gave them each a sandwich and a juice box. They were hungry from the long ride.

"Thank you, mom," Lily and Ben said.

They opened their sandwiches and took a bite. Lily chewed her cheese sandwich slowly and carefully. She was thoughtful and did not want to make a mess. Ben chewed his ham sandwich fast and loud. He was excited and did not care about the crumbs.

"Ben, chew quietly, please," mom said. "And don't drop your sandwich on the floor."

"Sorry, mom," Ben said. He tried to chew quieter, but he still dropped some ham on his lap.

Lily giggled. She gave Ben a napkin and helped him clean up.

"You are a good sister, Lily," Ben said.

"You are a good brother, Ben," Lily said.

They smiled and hugged each other. They finished their sandwiches and juice boxes and threw the trash in a bin.

The train stopped at a station. They heard a loud voice say, "This is our stop. Please get off the train with your bags."

"Come on, kids, let's go," dad said. He took their bags and held their hands.

They got off the train and saw their grandma and grandpa waiting for them. They ran to them and gave them big hugs and kisses.

"Hello, Lily and Ben, we are so happy to see you!" grandma and grandpa said.

"We are happy to see you too!" Lily and Ben said.

They all walked to the car and drove to grandma and grandpa's house. They had a fun and happy time together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was only three years old. One day, Sarah decided to go to the garden to pick some radishes.

As Sarah approached the garden, she got a little scared. But she reminded herself that radishes were her favorite vegetable, and so she kept walking. 

Once there, she began gathering her vegetables. She filled her basket but then noticed an old, black snake in the corner of the garden. Sarah was very scared and immediately wanted to quit. But then she remembered how much she loved radishes, so she took a deep breath and kept picking. 

The snake watched her, but then quietly slithered away. When Sarah was all done, she proudly showed her parents the basket full of radishes. Her parents were so proud of her, and Sarah felt brave and proud too!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to compete in races. She was very competitive and would practice every day. She was always determined to win each race.

One day, she went to the meadow to practice. As she was running, she noticed a herd of sheep standing in the meadow. She smiled and stopped to watch them.

The little girl noticed that the sheep were not running in a race. They were content to just stand there and the little girl thought that it was beautiful. She thought that it was ok to stand and be content with who she was and let her competitors run their own race.

The little girl learned an important lesson that day; it was ok to be competitive and practice for races, but it was also ok to stand still sometimes and be at peace.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They like to run and jump on the grass. They see a big slide and want to try it. Sara goes first. She climbs up the ladder and slides down fast. She laughs and says, "That was fun!"

Ben follows her. He climbs up the ladder too, but he is clumsy. He slips and falls off the ladder. He lands on the grass and gets dirty. He cries and says, "Ow, ow, ow!"

Sara runs to him and hugs him. She says, "Don't cry, Ben. You are okay. You just need to wash the dirt off." She helps him stand up and takes him to the fountain. She turns on the water and washes his face and hands. She says, "There, you are clean now. Do you feel better?"

Ben nods and smiles. He says, "Thank you, Sara. You are a good friend. Can we play some more?"

Sara says, "Yes, we can. But be careful on the ladder, okay?"

Ben says, "Okay, I will. Come on, let's go!" They run back to the slide and have more fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She was three years old. She loved to play with her colorful scarves. 
One day she asked her mom if she could help cook for dinner. Her mom smiled and said, "Of course!" 
Molly helped her mom mix together all the delicious ingredients for the dinner. 
When it was done her mom tasted it and said, "This is delicious!". 
Molly wanted to taste it too, so she asked for a spoon. Her mom said, "No, you have to wait until after dinner". 
Molly was sad, but she waited patiently. 
At dinner time, her mom said, "Molly, you did such a great job helping to make this delicious dinner! Here, have a little taste". 
Molly tasted it and smiled.

The moral of the story is to be patient and wait for the right time. If you wait, you'll be rewarded. And if you work hard, you'll be proud of your accomplishments.

Once upon a time, Jack invited his best friends to his house to celebrate. They each brought something special to share. Gerry brought cookies, Joanne brought balloons, and Bill brought a tea set. They set up the tea set and shared tea and stories. They each laughed and celebrated all afternoon.

At the end of the party, Jack said to his friends, "Thank you for being here. I'm very lucky to have such loyal friends like you." They all hugged and said goodbye. 

The next day, Jack went to visit them and said, "Let's celebrate again someday. I think next time we should have a picnic in the park." Joanne said, "That sounds like a great idea!" as she hopped up and down with excitement. They all agreed and made plans for their next party. 

The end.

Once there was a brave little boy called John. He had big blue eyes and a funny pointy nose. One day, he wanted to race his friends. He ran so fast that he was the winner. After he raced, he was smiling from ear to ear. He was so proud of himself for being so brave and running so fast. 

The next week, John had a race against his classmates. He was excited and raced as fast as he could. His nose was scrunched up as he ran and he shouted, "I'm going to win!" 

John was so determined, he won the race. His friends cheered for him and he was so happy. He had been very brave. He was the fastest and they all applauded his effort. 

John learned that day that no matter what, if you are brave and try your best, you can do great things.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. But they do not like to share. They always fight over who gets what.

One day, Mom gives them a big box. She says it is a gift for both of them. She tells them to wrap it with paper and ribbon. She says they can open it on their birthday.

Lila and Ben are happy. They want to see what is inside the box. They go to their room with the box. They find some paper and ribbon. They start to wrap the box.

But then they start to argue. Lila wants to use the pink paper. Ben wants to use the blue paper. Lila says pink is better. Ben says blue is better. They pull and tug on the paper. They rip it apart.

They get angry. They start to hit each other. They use their hands and feet. They hurt each other. They cry and scream.

Mom hears the noise. She runs to their room. She sees the mess. She sees the torn paper and ribbon. She sees the box. She sees Lila and Ben. They are bleeding and bruised. They have different marks on their faces and bodies.

Mom is sad and mad. She says they are naughty and mean. She says they do not deserve the gift. She takes the box away. She says they will not get it on their birthday. She says they will get nothing.

Lila and Ben are sorry. They say they are sorry. They hug each other. They want the gift back. They want Mom to forgive them.

But it is too late. Mom is gone. The box is gone. The gift is gone. Lila and Ben are alone. They have nothing. They have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little spider named Charlotte. She lived in a big tree with her family. One day, she woke up and saw a cobweb on her head. She didn't like it because it was different from the other cobwebs she had made before.

She went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, look at my cobweb. It's different from the others." Her mommy said, "It's okay, Charlotte. Everyone makes different things. Your cobweb is still beautiful."

Charlotte felt happy and decided to make more cobwebs. She worked hard and made many different cobwebs. As the sun started to rise, she looked at her cobwebs and felt proud of herself. She said to her family, "Look at my cobwebs. They are different but still pretty."

Her family looked at her cobwebs and said, "Wow, Charlotte! You are a great spider. Your cobwebs are amazing!" Charlotte felt happy and went to sleep, dreaming of making more different cobwebs.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. Mommy, Daddy, and their little girl, Lily. They loved to play and have fun together. But one day, Daddy accidentally broke Mommy's favorite vase. 

Mommy was sad because the vase was very special to her. But Daddy said he would repair it, and Mommy felt better. 

As they waited for the vase to be fixed, Mommy and Daddy talked about their marriage. They said they were excited to be together and promised to always love each other. 

Finally, the vase was repaired and Mommy was very happy. The family hugged and played together, and they knew their love would always be strong.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom loved to sleep all day and play all night. One sunny day, Tom went for a walk in the park.

In the park, Tom met a small frog. The frog said, "Hi! I can do a spell to give you a big hug. Do you want one?" Tom said, "Yes, I like hugs!"

The frog did the spell and gave Tom a big squeeze. Tom felt so happy and warm from the hug. They became good friends and played together every day. And Tom was not so lazy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a bird who liked to joke. He was a funny bird and he loved to make people laugh.

One day, he saw a mosquito buzzing around in the sunlight. The bird had an idea. He told the mosquito a joke.

The mosquito laughed so hard that it flew away into the light. The bird was so tickled that he flew off, too.

The bird and the mosquito flew around in the light, laughing and joking. They had the best time ever.

The bird and the mosquito laughed until the sun went down. Then, they had to say goodbye. But, the bird promised he would find the mosquito again soon.

The bird and mosquito were the best of friends and they always shared a good joke.

Once there was a little girl. She was very sad because she had done something wrong. She was scared and didnâ€™t know what to do.

Suddenly she saw a light from the window and it felt like it was coming from the sky. It filled her heart with warmth and she started to feel better.

She realised that it was time to forgive herself. She ran outside and saw that the sky was full of gas that shone like stars in the night. She realised that forgiveness was everywhere and it made her feel better.

The little girl smiled. She knew that forgiving herself was the right thing to do. From that moment on she was happy, and felt like she had been forgiven.

One warm summer day, a small girl named Charlotte ran out to the backyard with glee. She was so excited for a new adventure that day! She noticed a beautiful palm tree in the center of the backyard and ran towards it.

When she made it to the base of the palms, she saw an ant on the ground inching its way up the trunk at a slow, steady pace. Charlotte watched it for a few moments, and then said, â€œhello ant! Why are you running so slow?â€

The ant looked up at her and said, â€œI'm running slow because I'm trying to reach the top of this palm tree, and that's a long way to go!â€

Charlotte smiled, and she said, â€œthen let's both run together, so you can get there faster!â€ 

The ant smiled back and said, â€œthat sounds like a great idea!â€ So, the two of them started running together up the palm tree, faster and faster. Eventually, they made it to the top!

Charlotte and the ant stopped at the top of the palm and looked down. They both smiled and Charlotte said, â€œthank you for running with me, my little ant friend. That was lots of fun!â€

The ant nodded and said, â€œme too, Charlotte. Until next time!â€ And with that, they went

Once there was a little girl named Susie. She was three and she loved to explore. One day she saw a silly little snake in the garden. It was orange and yellow.

Susie was scared of snakes, but she was brave. She stepped closer and watched the snake. She saw that it was eating flowers and leaves. Before long, she didn't feel scared anymore.

That day, Susie decided to help the snake. She brought some of her mom's special fertilizer, and sprinkled it onto the soil. She also found some plants to help it find food.

After a few days, the garden started to look better. The weeds were gone and the plants were growing. The snake was getting bigger and happier.

Susie was so proud of her work! She had helped the silly little snake improve its home.

Once upon a time there was a modest family. They had a baby daughter, who was very special. Her parents loved her very much. 

One day, the baby's father went to drop off some presents at her nursery. As he was walking in, he heard his daughter's laugh ringing out across the room! He smiled and opened the door.

He saw his daughter sat on the floor with her friends. She was wearing a pretty pink dress and was playing with a toy. Her father smiled. 

Out of the blue, the telephone rang. The baby's father started to walk over to answer it, but the baby daughter stretched out her arms and called, "Daddy! I answer it!" 

Her father smiled, and handed her the phone. She said hello in her sweetest voice and listened. After a few moments, she handed the phone back to her father and smiled.

Her father hugged her and said, "You were so brave, and so modest; you did a great job answering the telephone." His daughter was very proud of herself. 

And from that day on, the baby daughter was known in the family as the one who always answered the phone!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was walking with his mommy when he saw a big chimney on a house. He stopped and stared at the chimney because it was so big and tall.
