Once there was a little girl named Sue. She liked to travel. One day Sue decided to go on an adventure with her orange shoes. She put on her orange shoes and took off down the street. Sue enjoyed traveling around town and saw lots of interesting things.

Finally, Sueâ€™s feet began to get tired. She stopped to take a break. Sue plopped down and took off her orange shoes. Then she dug around in her pocket and found some treats! Yum!

Sue ate her treats and rested for a bit. Then she put her orange shoes back on and started to travel again. Sue had lots of fun exploring with her orange shoes!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the beach. The beach had sand, water, and a big sun. Lily liked to make sand castles and swim in the water.

One day, Lily saw a big crab. The crab looked bad. Lily was scared. She did not want the crab to hurt her sand castle. So, Lily asked her mom for help. Her mom told her to believe in herself and be brave.

Lily took a deep breath and walked up to the crab. She told the crab, "Please don't be bad. Let's be friends." The crab smiled and they played together. Lily learned that if she believed in herself, she could make friends with anyone.

Once upon a time, there was a small child who was playing with his favorite toy truck. He was so happy that he drove it around the room with a big smile on his face.

Suddenly, the doorbell rang. The child quickly put the truck back in its chamber and shut the door tightly. He rushed to the front door to answer the door.

When he opened it, there was a big dog standing in front of the door. The dog was looking up at the child in an excited way. The child was scared and tried to close the door, but the dog stuck his paw in between to stop him.

The child shouted, "Go away!" but the dog would not leave. He barked and wagged his tail, begging for attention. After some coaxing, the child dropped his defenses and started petting the dog. 

Little did the child know, this was the same dog that kidnapped his favorite toy truck earlier that morning. His truck was still in the chamber, hidden away from view! But the child was about to find out the truth very soonâ€¦

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Bear and Rabbit. Bear was big and tall and Rabbit was tiny and small. One day, Rabbit wanted to find the dragon. Bear told Rabbit it was too dangerous to go. But Rabbit wanted to explore and examine the dragon for himself.

Bear and Rabbit went on an adventure to find the dragon. Finally, they arrived at a clearing in the forest and there was a tall dragon! Rabbit was so excited but Bear felt scared. They stood looking at the dragon for a long time.

Rabbit wanted to take a closer look and started to step closer but Bear stopped him. Bear said it was too dangerous and they needed to leave. Rabbit didn't want to listen and stepped closer to the dragon. Suddenly, the ground started to shake and the dragon opened its mouth and roared!

Bear and Rabbit quickly ran back to safety and Bear was glad they had listened to him. They both knew it was too dangerous to examine the dragon, but they were happy they had gone on an adventure. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very graceful and she loved to dance. One day, she was going to a big dance party. She put on her best dress and her shiny shoes. But then, her mommy said they had to delay going to the party because they needed to wait for her little brother to finish his nap. The girl was sad, but she decided to practice her dance moves while she waited. Finally, her brother woke up and they went to the party. The girl danced so gracefully that everyone clapped and cheered for her. She was very happy and proud of herself. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He was so excited because he knew that something special was going to happen. He waited and waited, and then finally, it did! A treasure appeared at his feet! It was a big box filled with delicious treats. The boy couldn't believe his eyes! He opened the box and inside he found chocolates, cakes and a big jar of sweets. Every single one was so delicious that he could hardly choose which one to eat first. He was very happy because this was the best treasure ever!

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl named Sarah. She loved to explore the world around her. One day, Sarah decided to dare herself and go explore a forest. She walked through the trees and saw different animals. Everywhere she looked, everything seemed so new and exciting.

But then Sarah noticed something strange! Everything began to look the same and she started to feel a little dizzy. Sarah was feeling scared because she was lost in the forest. She started to cry, and a rabbit came to her side. He said, "Don't worry Sarah, I will help you find your way out of the forest."

The rabbit hopped and hopped, leading Sarah out of the forest. Sarah smiled and thanked the rabbit. She was so happy to be back in a place she recognized. From then on, she was no longer scared to explore and she would always remember the forest.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they decided to be explorers in the jungle. They put on their hats and backpacks and grabbed their binoculars and maps.

"Let's go find some animals!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful. The jungle can be dangerous," Ben said.

They walked around the backyard, looking for signs of wildlife. They saw a bird, a squirrel, and a butterfly. They pretended they were monkeys, snakes, and parrots. They had a lot of fun.

Then, they heard a loud roar. They stopped and looked around. They saw a big, furry, brown bear coming out of the bushes. They were scared.

"Run!" Ben shouted.

They ran as fast as they could, but the bear was faster. It caught up with them and blocked their way.

"Please, don't hurt us!" Lily cried.

The bear looked at them and tilted its head. It sniffed them and licked them. It was not a mean bear. It was a friendly bear.

"Hello, little ones. I'm sorry I scared you. I was just curious. What are you doing here?" the bear asked.

"We're explorers. We're looking for animals in the jungle," Ben said.

The bear smiled. "Well, you found me. I'm an animal in the jungle. But this is not a real jungle. This is your backyard. I live in the woods behind your house. I sometimes come here to relax and eat some berries."

Lily and Ben were surprised. They did not know they had a bear neighbor. They felt silly for being afraid.

"Wow, you can talk. You're a very polite bear. Can we be your friends?" Lily asked.

The bear nodded. "Of course. You can be my friends. But you have to be careful. Not all animals are nice like me. Some are wild and dangerous. You should always ask your parents before you go exploring."

Lily and Ben agreed. They thanked the bear for being kind and invited him to play with them. The bear accepted. They had a picnic, played hide and seek, and told stories. They had a wonderful time.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to see the bright and pretty fireworks in the sky. One day, her mommy and daddy said they would allow her to see the fireworks show at the park.

Lily was so jolly and excited! She put on her favorite dress and ran to the park with her parents. When they arrived, the sky was dark and the stars were shining. Suddenly, the fireworks started to light up the sky with beautiful colors.

Lily clapped her hands and laughed with joy. She was so happy that her mommy and daddy allowed her to see the fireworks. From that day on, every time there was a fireworks show, Lily would remember that jolly night at the park.

Ben and Mia were playing in the park with their bikes. They liked to ride fast and make noises. They saw a big hill and wanted to go down it.

"Let's race!" Ben said. "I bet I can go faster than you!"

"OK!" Mia said. "But be careful. There is a cable at the bottom of the hill. It is for the lights. We have to stop before we hit it."

They got ready and started to pedal. They went down the hill very fast. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and shouted.

But Ben did not listen to Mia. He wanted to win. He did not look at the cable. He did not stop. He hit the cable with his bike. He fell off and hurt his leg. He started to scream.

Mia stopped and ran to him. She saw the blood on his leg. She felt sorry for him. She said, "Ben, why did you not stop? I told you about the cable. You were not wise. You were silly. Now you are hurt."

Ben cried and said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I wanted to win. I did not think. You were wise. You were careful. Can you help me?"

Mia nodded and said, "Yes, I can help you. But first, we have to call Mom. She will know what to do. She will take you to the doctor. He will make your leg better."

She took out her phone and called Mom. She told her what happened. Mom said she would come right away. She told them to stay where they were and not to move.

Mia hugged Ben and said, "Don't worry, Ben. It will be OK. Mom is coming. She will help you. And I will stay with you. You are my brother. I love you."

Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Mia. You are my sister. I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the sunshine and chase after butterflies. One day, he saw a big turkey in his backyard. Timmy had never seen a turkey before, but he thought it looked funny with its wobbly head and feathers. 

Timmy went closer to the turkey, but it started to scream loudly and flap its wings. Timmy got scared and ran away. Later that day, Timmy's mom cooked a big turkey for dinner. Timmy didn't know it was the same turkey he saw earlier. 

When Timmy saw the turkey on his plate, he screamed and cried. He didn't want to eat the turkey that he had seen earlier. But his mom insisted he eat it, and Timmy had to obey. He ate the turkey, but he felt sad and scared. He didn't like eating an unknown animal that he had seen alive earlier that day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were both so excited to play together outdoors. They looked up and saw a beautiful white bird soaring in the sky.

â€œWow, look at that bird soar!â€ shouted Jack. 

Jill replied, â€œLetâ€™s be like the bird and soar too!â€

Jack saw a broken branch on the ground, so he picked it up and said, â€œLetâ€™s pretend this branch is like a plane.â€

So Jack and Jill hugged the branch, closed their eyes and imagined they were soaring in the sky. They hummed and soared around each other, pretending to make plane noises.

They had so much fun pretending to be a plane, but it was time for them to go home. They hugged the branch one last time, thanked it for the fun, and said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard, where she had a big tree with lots of branches to climb. One day, while she was playing, she saw a raven sitting on a branch. The raven looked at Lily and said, "Hello little girl, can you bring me some food?"

Lily was surprised that the raven could talk, but she wanted to help. She went inside and brought some bread crumbs. The raven ate them and said, "Thank you, you are a dependable friend."

From that day on, Lily would bring food for the raven every day. They became good friends and would talk for hours. One day, the raven said, "Lily, I have to go now. But I will always remember you as my dependable friend."

Lily was sad to see the raven go, but she knew they would always be friends. She looked up at the tree and smiled, knowing that her new friend would always be there, even if she couldn't see him.

Once there was a mother and daughter. The daughter loved to explore the world. Everywhere she went she found interesting objects. Today, her mother wanted to encourage her to explore the nearby woods. 

The mother was a bit worried since she had never been this far before. She smiled at her daughter and said in a gentle voice, "Let's go explore the woods. I'm sure we'll see something lovely there."

They set off on their adventure and soon they started to see things they hadn't seen before. They could hear birds singing from the treetops and discover different kinds of rocks and leaves. Then, they came upon a pond.

In the pond, the daughter was delighted to see a frog. The mother chuckled as her daughter ran to get a closer look.

Together, they spent the time exploring and observing the different objects their eyes found. When the sun started to set, the daughter thanked her mother for encouraging her on this lovely adventure. The mother smiled, happy that her daughter had such a wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man who loved to swim in the river. He had a dog named Spot who loved to play fetch with a bone. One day, the man and Spot went to the river to swim and play.

As they were swimming, a big fish jumped out of the water and scared Spot. "Woof woof! Scary!" barked Spot. The man laughed and said, "Don't worry, Spot. The fish won't hurt us."

But as they continued to swim, the man suddenly felt something grab his leg. It was a big alligator! "Help! Help!" he cried. Spot tried to save him by biting the alligator's tail, but it was too late. The alligator took the man underwater and he never came back up.

Spot was very sad and went home alone without his owner. He missed the man and the bone they used to play with. From that day on, Spot never went back to the river again.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Spot. Spot loved to play and chase his tail. One day, Spot went for a walk with his owner, Sarah. Sarah let Spot off his leash so he could run and play. Spot was having so much fun that he didn't notice when Sarah started to leave.

"Spot, come on! We have to go home now," Sarah called.

Spot didn't want to leave yet, but he knew he had to go with Sarah. He wagged his tail happily and followed her home.

When they got home, Sarah gave Spot a treat. Spot was so grateful that he licked Sarah's face. "Thank you for the treat!" Spot barked happily.

Sarah smiled and scratched Spot's tail. "You're welcome, Spot. I'm grateful to have you as my puppy."

The little boy's eyes lit up with surprise when he saw the tall building. It seemed to be glowing in the sunlight. He wanted to go closer and explore it. 

So, the little boy started to walk towards the building. He was so excited! But when he got close to the building, something strange happened. He felt a vast, empty feeling inside. He tried to understand why he felt this way.

Suddenly, he heard a loud sound. Then he felt a big gust of wind. The tall building was starting to shake and crumble. He was scared and ran away from the building, but it was too late. The building crashed down and the little boy was sadly trapped beneath it. He cried for help, but no one heard him. 

The little boy will never forget that tall glowing building and the immense feeling of surprise he felt that day. Sadly, the surprise had a bad ending.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. They walked slow on the sand, looking for shells. Tim found a big, pretty shell and showed it to his mom. She smiled and said, "What a nice shell, Tim!"

A little crab came out of the shell and said, "Hello! I'm Carl the Crab. Can we play?" Tim was happy to meet Carl. They played a fun game where Carl would hide in the sand and Tim would try to find him. Each time Tim found Carl, he would repeat, "I found you, Carl!"

As the sun went down, Tim knew it was time to go home. He said goodbye to Carl and thanked him for playing. Carl went back into his shell and waved goodbye with his little claw. Tim and his mom walked slow back to their car, excited to come back to the beach another day.

John was feeling brave today. He decided he wanted to order his own lunch and asked his mum for the menu. She showed it to him and he carefully looked over all the choices. He was excited to find something he liked and after a few minutes, he made up his mind. 

"I'd like a sandwich, please," he requested bravely. His mum smiled and said, "Good choice! Would you like some chips with that?" 

"Yes, please," John replied.

His mum made the sandwich and added some chips to the plate. She handed it over to John, who was very proud of himself. 

"Thanks mum," he said, taking a big bite of the delicious sandwich. "Yum!"

One day, Jimmy was bouncing a ball against the fence in his yard. Suddenly, the fence revealed a graceful fairy in a sparkly dress. She smiled at Jimmy and said, â€œHello there!â€

Jimmy was so surprised he dropped the ball and asked, â€œWho are you?â€

The fairy laughed and said, â€œMy name is Clara. I want to show you something special.â€ She waved her wand and the fence opened up to reveal a beautiful flower garden. Jimmyâ€™s eyes lit up and he said, â€œWow!â€

Clara smiled and said, â€œThis is my garden and it is my job to make sure it looks graceful. Now, go explore!â€

Jimmy was amazed, so he ran around the garden, looking at all the different kinds of flowers. After he finished exploring, he thanked Clara for showing him such a special place. She smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™re welcome! Now, I must go back to my job of keeping the garden looking graceful. Goodbye!â€

And with that, Clara disappeared behind the fence. Jimmy smiled and continued bouncing the ball against the fence, hopeful that one day Clara would come back and reveal her magical garden again.

One day, little Jimmy was playing in the park when he noticed something unusual. He saw a pine tree at the very edge of the park and it was bigger than all the other trees. Jimmy thought to himself, â€œThere must be something special about this tree.â€

Jimmy wanted to find out, so he ran over to the tree and started to search for something under its branches. Jimmy searched for a few minutes, but nothing unusual came up until he heard a small voice. 

â€œHey, Jimmy,â€ the voice said. â€œDo you want some help searching?â€ 
Jimmy was so surprised he couldnâ€™t move! After a while, he saw a tiny man standing between the pine needles. The man smiled at Jimmy and said, â€œWeâ€™ll look together and I bet weâ€™ll find something special.â€

Jimmy agreed and the small man pointed at something in a hole in the tree. Jimmy looked closer and there it was--a tiny box with a beautiful, shiny diamond inside it! Jimmy was so surprised he almost dropped the box.

Jimmy had found the most unusual thing in the park and he was so excited he ran to show it to his mom. He knew that this moment would stay with him forever!

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tap in the park. The tap is ugly. It is brown and rusty. It has a hole in it.

Tim and Sam want to see what is in the hole. They go near the tap. They hear a noise. It is a hiss. They are scared. They think it is a snake.

They run away from the tap. They find a bench. They sit on the bench. They are safe. They are happy.

But then, they see something. It is not a snake. It is water. The water comes out of the hole. The water is fast and strong. The water hits the tap. The tap breaks. The water goes everywhere.

Tim and Sam are wet. They are cold. They are sad. They do not like the tap. They do not like the water. They want to go home.

The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the bathroom. They liked to pretend they were pirates and use the towels as sails and the brushes as swords. They saw a shiny thing on the sink. It was a razor. Tom wanted to play with it.

"Look, Lily, a treasure!" he said. "Let's see what it can do."

He picked up the razor and tried to cut the towel. But the razor was sharp and it cut his finger. He cried out in pain and dropped the razor. It broke into pieces and they scattered on the floor.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Tom shouted. "It hurts, it hurts!"

Lily ran to him and saw the blood on his finger. She was scared and sorry.

"Tom, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" she said. "You shouldn't play with that. It's not a treasure, it's a razor. It's for grown-ups, not for kids. It's dangerous and disgusting."

She wrapped his finger with a tissue and hugged him. She heard their mom coming.

"Mom, mom, help!" she called. "Tom cut his finger with a razor. It was an accident, we were playing pirates."

Their mom came into the bathroom and saw the mess. She was angry and worried.

"What have you done?" she asked. "How did you get the razor? You know you're not allowed to touch it. It's very sharp and it can hurt you. Look at all the blood and the broken pieces. It's disgusting and unsafe. You could have cut yourself worse or stepped on them."

She took Tom and Lily to the kitchen and cleaned and bandaged Tom's finger. She gave them both a hug and a kiss.

"I'm glad you're okay, Tom," she said. "But you have to be more careful and listen to me. Razors are not toys, they are tools. And you have to respect them and leave them alone. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said he was sorry. He felt bad and stupid.

"I understand, mom," he said. "I'm sorry, mom. I won't play with razors again. I don't like them. They're disgusting and they hurt."

Lily nodded and said she was sorry too. She felt guilty and sad.

"I'm sorry, mom," she said. "I should have stopped Tom. I don't like razors either. They're disgusting and they scare me."

Their mom smiled and said she forgave them. She told them to be more careful and to play with safer things. She said she loved them and they were her treasures. She took them to their room and gave them some books and toys. They said they loved her too and they were sorry. They hugged and kissed her and said they would be good. They learned their lesson and never played with razors again.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play and run in the big park. He was a very happy dog.

One day, Buddy saw a girl named Sue. Sue was sad because she lost her toy. Buddy wanted to help, so he kneeled next to her. He wanted to make her smile.

Buddy had an idea. He started to sing a song for Sue. Sue laughed and clapped her hands. They played and sang together. They became best friends and were happy ever after.

Lily and Max were playing with their toys in the yard. Lily had a doll and Max had a truck. Max liked to make loud noises with his truck and pretend it was driving on the grass. Lily liked to imagine that her doll was a princess and talk to her softly.

"Vroom, vroom, beep, beep!" Max shouted, as he moved his truck closer to Lily and her doll. "Move out of the way, princess! My truck is faster and stronger than you!"

"Stop it, Max!" Lily said, as she hugged her doll. "You are being mean and ignorant. You don't know anything about princesses. They are kind and smart and beautiful. And they don't like noisy trucks!"

"Ha, ha, ha!" Max laughed, as he pushed his truck into Lily and her doll. "You are silly and boring, Lily. You don't know anything about trucks. They are fun and powerful and cool. And they don't care about stupid dolls!"

Lily and Max started to argue and fight. They did not listen to each other or share their toys. They did not have fun or learn anything new.

Mom heard the noise and came to the yard. She saw Lily and Max crying and angry. She saw the doll and the truck on the ground. She was not happy.

"What is going on here?" Mom asked, as she picked up the doll and the truck. "Why are you fighting over your toys? Why are you not playing nicely?"

Lily and Max tried to explain, but they only blamed each other. They said that the other one was ignorant and did not understand their toys.

Mom shook her head and sighed. She sat down with Lily and Max and gave them back their toys. She looked at them with love and said:

"Lily and Max, you are both wrong. You are not ignorant, but you are acting like it. You are not respecting each other or your toys. You are missing a chance to imagine and explore together. You can learn from each other and have more fun if you share your toys and your ideas. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded and felt sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to try to play together and imagine new things. They asked Mom to join them and tell them stories about princesses and trucks. They smiled and laughed and had fun. They were not ignorant anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a humble little mouse who lived in the dark corner of a big barn. Every night, the little mouse would sneak around and try to get any food he could find.

One night as the mouse crept along, he saw a big crack in the barn wall. The little mouse peeked through the crack and saw a bowl of food on the other side. He wanted to get it, so he started to dig.

The little mouse kept digging and digging until he had made a way through the wall. But when he tried to crawl through, he was stopped by a big cat that growled "What are you doing here little mouse?!".

The little mouse was scared but he was also very brave. He replied "I am just trying to get some food to eat. I am very humble and I will not bother you anymore".

The big cat stared at the little mouse for a moment, then he said "You may get the food this one time, but never come back again". The little mouse smiled with relief and quickly grabbed the food. Then he ran back to the dark corner of the barn.

Once upon a time there was an ancient tree. It was an old tree, but it was very strong. Every morning, a little girl would come and grab its leaves. She would use them to make a special tea.

One day, the little girl noticed something strange about the tree's leaves. Instead of being soft and green, they felt like paper! When she looked more closely, the little girl saw that the leaves had writing on them! She was so excited.

She quickly grabbed the leaves, and ran home with them. She boiled some water and made the tea. When she tasted it, the little girl could not believe her luck! The tea tasted like nothing she had ever tasted before.

The little girl was so pleased with her discovery. She kept the ancient leaves, so she could make the special tea over and over again. 

Every day she would go to the tree and grab its leaves. She was so happy that the ancient tree had given her such a special treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to create things with his toys. One day, he wanted to make a ship. He took his blocks and started to build.

Tim worked hard on his ship. His friend, Sam, came over to play. Sam was impatient. He said, "Hurry up, Tim! Let's play now!" But Tim wanted to finish his ship first.

Finally, the ship was done. Tim and Sam played with the ship all day. They pretended it was sailing on the water. They had so much fun together. And Sam learned that sometimes, it's good to wait for something special.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they found a big box of old clothes and things in the attic. They decided to dress up and have fun.

Lily put on a long dress and a hat with feathers. She looked like a fancy lady. Ben put on a coat and a hat with a brim. He looked like a detective. But he wanted something more.

"I know!" he said. "I need a mustache!" He looked around and saw a black marker. He grabbed it and drew a mustache on his face. He smiled and said, "Now I look like a real detective!"

Lily laughed and said, "You look silly, Ben! That's not a real mustache! That's just a line on your face!"

Ben felt sad. He wanted to look like a real detective. He said, "But I don't have a real mustache. How can I get one?"

Lily thought for a moment. She was a thoughtful sister. She wanted to make Ben happy. She said, "I have an idea! Come with me!"

She took Ben to the kitchen. She opened the cupboard and took out a jar of peanut butter. She said, "This is how we can decorate your mustache!"

She took a spoon and scooped some peanut butter. She spread it on Ben's face, over the marker line. She said, "There! Now you have a real mustache! And it smells good, too!"

Ben looked in the mirror. He saw his mustache. It was brown and sticky and shiny. He said, "Wow! Thank you, Lily! You are the best sister ever! Now I look like a real detective!"

Lily hugged him and said, "You're welcome, Ben! You are the best brother ever! Now let's go play pretend!"

They ran back to the attic, happy and excited. They did not notice the dog that followed them. The dog smelled the peanut butter. The dog liked peanut butter. The dog licked his lips. He had a plan. He was going to get a tasty treat.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was playing in the park. She had a yummy bottle of juice with her. Suddenly, she saw a butterfly and ran after it. When she came back, she couldn't find her bottle. She asked her friend, "Did you see my bottle? I lose it." Her friend said, "No, I didn't see it. Let's look for it together." They looked everywhere but couldn't find it. Lily was sad because she loved her yummy juice. Her friend said, "Don't worry, we can get you a new bottle." They went to the store and got a new bottle of juice. Lily was happy again and said, "Thank you for helping me."

Once there was a young girl who wanted to go for a swim. She had a special key that would unlock a secret door. She was so excited and put the key into the lock. She heard a click and the door opened! She stepped into a magical place full of water. She knew it was a swimming pool and couldn't wait to dive in. 

The girl took off her shoes and clothes and jumped in. She swam and played in the water like a fish. She laughed and splashed until she was very tired. Then, she slowly got out and put back on her clothes. 

She had a wonderful time and couldn't wait to come back. She hugged her key tightly, happy that it unlocked such a fun place. She put the key away and ran off to tell her friends about her adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a laser. It was very very shiny and it glowed like a star. One day, a little boy saw it and said, "Wow!" He wanted to play with the laser so he waved his hands and the laser moved around. It was so much fun!

The boy played with the laser all day, moving it in the air and making it twinkle. After a while, he was so hungry that he stopped playing and looked around. Suddenly, he saw a tasty treat on the ground. It was a big cookie with a big smiley face. It looked yummy!

The boy got very excited and waved his hands for the laser to come to him. He put the laser on top of the cookie and bam! - the cookie was gone. Where did it go? It flew up in the air and was never seen again! 

The boy was very satisfied and said, "Yum! That was a tasty treat!"  He played with the laser some more and went home with a happy heart.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy lion who loved to count. One day, he was walking through the woods and came across a beautiful music box. He was so excited he started counting the notes he could hear.

But as he was counting, he made too much noise and disturbed a sleeping bear. The bear was so mad, he roared and chased the lion away. 

The lion was scared and ran all the way home. He was so embarrassed and sad that he couldn't enjoy the music and counting anymore. 

The next day, the lion tried to count again, but very quietly this time. He enjoyed the music just as much and had more fun. 

The lion learned that being nosy and making too much noise is not always a good idea. Everyone else is trying to enjoy the music as well - it's always important to be considerate of others.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. Joe loved to eat vegetables! Every day he would eat a different vegetable. 

One day he went to the store with his Mom. Joe wanted to buy some carrots, but his Mom said they were out of money. Joe sighed. He was very sad he couldn't buy any carrots. 

A few days later, Joe was playing in the garden. He noticed a large carrot sticking out of the ground. Joe felt so happy! He pulled the carrot out of the ground and took a big bite. 

Suddenly, his Mom came outside. She saw the carrot and became very angry. She scolded Joe for taking the carrot without asking. Joe felt so ashamed. 

His Mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, but next time, ask me first!" Joe nodded, and vowed he would never take a vegetable without asking again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She had a pretty yellow dress with lots of buttons. She liked to wear it because it felt very tight around her.

One day, Amy decided to go for a walk. She ran down the street and across the park. It was so much fun! She was laughing and playing along the way.

Finally, she reached a big hill at the end of the park. Amy walked up to the top of the hill. When she got there, she saw a huge button right in front of her! It was bigger than any button she had ever seen before.

She reached out and pressed the button. Suddenly, everything around her started to move! The hill began to get tighter and tighter, like it was squeezing her!

Amy was so scared! But just when she thought she couldn't take it anymore, the tightness around her loosened up and she was able to take a big breath of fresh air.

Amy was so relieved â€“ and she learned a valuable lesson about being careful when playing around a big hill!

Once upon a time there was a strong dog called Max. He was always looking for adventures. Today, he had a really big adventure planned! 

Max wanted to climb the highest mountain. He was so excited that he started running as fast as he could. He soon reached the top of the mountain.

He was almost at the peak when he hit a problem. There was a big, bad cooler blocking his way! Max growled and barked, but the cooler didn't move. He tried to move the cooler, but it was too heavy.

Max was struggling. He just wanted to get to the top of the mountain! Then, he suddenly had an idea - he could get his friends to help him!

Max ran swiftly down the mountain as he searched for his friends. He soon found them and he begged them to come back and help him move the cooler. His friends agreed and they all ran back up the mountain.

When they reached the cooler, all of them pushed and pulled together with all their might. Finally, the cooler moved away and Max was able to reach the top of the mountain! He waved goodbye to his friends and he shouted: "I did it!" 

And so, Max's big adventure came to a happy ending.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat dinner. Mommy was cooking in the kitchen. She had a big pot of water on the stove. She put some potatoes in the water. She said, "The potatoes will be soft and yummy soon. But don't touch the pot. It is very hot and dangerous. You can get hurt."

Lily and Tom nodded. They played with their toys in the living room. They waited for the potatoes to be ready. They smelled something good. They heard Mommy say, "Dinner is ready. Come and eat."

Lily and Tom ran to the kitchen. They saw Mommy put some potatoes on their plates. She also gave them some cheese and broccoli. They said, "Thank you, Mommy. This looks delicious."

They started to eat. They liked the potatoes. They were soft and yummy. They also liked the cheese and broccoli. They ate everything on their plates. They said, "We are full. We finished our dinner."

Mommy smiled. She said, "I'm proud of you. You ate all your vegetables. You can have some dessert now. How about some ice cream?"

Lily and Tom cheered. They said, "Yes, please. We love ice cream."

Mommy gave them some ice cream. They ate it with spoons. They licked their lips. They said, "This is the best dinner ever. Thank you, Mommy."

Mommy hugged them. She said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. I love you."

Once, there was a little girl who had an orange ball. She insisted she keep it close, so she held it in her hands all day long.

One day, she was playing with her orange ball where she met a confused puppy. The puppy kept wanting to play with her ball, but the little girl insisted that the puppy play with something else. 

The puppy wouldn't listen, and the little girl got more and more mad. Finally, she screamed and ran away with her orange ball. 

The puppy was sad and confused. He wanted the little girl and her orange ball to come back! He barked and whined, but the little girl had gone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the garden with her toys. One day, she found a pretty flower and picked it up. She held it tight in her hand and showed it to her mom.

Mom said, "That flower is poison. You shouldn't hold it."

But Lily was stubborn and didn't listen. She held the flower tightly and refused to let go.

Suddenly, Lily felt sick and her hand started to hurt. She cried out for her mom, but it was too late. The poison had made her very sick and she had to go to the hospital.

The moral of the story is that we should always listen to our parents and not hold things that can hurt us.

Little Jane was playing outside her house one day. She spotted a mule, and something incredible happened. The mule started to hide behind a bush. Jane was amazed and started counting the mule's steps. She was so excited that when the mule disappeared, she wanted to hide too.

So, she jumped on top of a pile of leaves and hid. She listened and waited for the mule to come back. She heard a rustling noise and peeped her head out. It was the mule! Jane giggled with delight and the mule brayed in response.

They played hide and seek for hours, until it was time for Jane to go back inside. She thanked the mule for the incredible time she had and waved goodbye as the mule ran off.

Jane smiled as she walked back inside. That was an incredible day, she thought to herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bottle that she loved very much. It was pink and had a picture of a bunny on it. Lily always carried it with her wherever she went.

One day, Lily was playing in the park with her obedient dog, Max. She left her bottle on a bench while she went to play on the swings. When she came back, her bottle had vanished! She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found.

Lily was very sad and cried a lot. Max tried to comfort her, but it didn't help. That night, Lily went to bed without her bottle and had trouble sleeping. She missed it so much.

The next day, Lily and Max went back to the park. As they were walking, they saw a little boy with a pink bottle that looked just like Lily's. When they got closer, they saw that it was indeed Lily's bottle! The little boy had taken it, but his mom made him give it back. Lily was so happy to have her bottle back, but she learned a valuable lesson to always keep it close to her.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His mommy gave him a spool of thread for his birthday. The thread was clean and pretty. He was so excited to have it. 

The boy wanted to play with the thread. He asked his mommy for a needle so he could make something special. His mommy brought him a sharp needle. He was so excited. 

The boy took the thread and needle and got to work. He threaded the needle and began to sew. He made a beautiful blanket. He was so proud of it. 

After he was done with the blanket, he showed it to his mommy. She was so happy. She hugged her son and thanked him for making such a beautiful creation. Everyone was happy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy called Sam. He was always very quiet and liked making gentle sounds. One day, Sam's mommy told him, "It's time to go outside and play with your friends, Sam!" Sam was tired, so he replied, "No mommy, I wanna stay home." 

Mommy was frustrated. She came over to Sam's room, knelt down beside him and said, "Go out now, Sam. It's important for you to spend time outside with your friends." Sam didn't want to listen and just stayed in bed.

But mommy kept on encouraging him. She said, "If you go outside, you'll make great sounds with your friends. Come on now, you won't regret it!" Sam thought about it and got out of bed. 

At first, Sam was tired and a bit grumpy, but after playing outside a while, he started to make all kinds of happy sounds with his friends. He could hardly believe all the fun things they did! 

At last, it was time to go inside. Sam was so joyful and thanked his mommy for encouraging him go out. This story teaches us that it's important to take the time out of our day to enjoy nature, spend time with friends and make happy sounds.

Once upon a time there was a fair flea who wanted to find a place to fit. He looked left, he looked right, but he couldn't find a spot that was just right. He flew up high in the sky and he flew low and all around, but he just couldn't find a place to fit. He began to get very tired and he was about to give up when he saw a big dog, stretching and laying in the sun. The fair flea watched for a bit and, when the big dog stood up and started running around, a space was formed between his shoulders. The flea flew in quickly, putting himself in just the right spot! He fit perfectly and from that spot he could see everything. And so the fair flea found his place and he was very happy. The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big tree with many monkeys. The monkeys are funny. They jump and swing and make noises.

Tom and Mia want to see the monkeys closer. They go to the tree and look up. One monkey is very small and cute. It has brown fur and a long tail. Tom likes the monkey. He wants to take it home.

"Look, Mia, this monkey is so sweet. I want to take it with me. It can be my pet," Tom says.

"No, Tom, you can't take the monkey. The monkey belongs to the tree and its family. It will be sad and scared if you take it. It will miss its home and its friends. It will be helpless," Mia says.

"But I will be nice to the monkey. I will give it food and toys and hugs. It will be happy with me," Tom says.

Tom reaches his hand to grab the monkey. The monkey sees Tom and gets scared. It screams and bites Tom's finger. Tom cries and lets go of the monkey. The monkey runs away to its mother. The other monkeys get angry and throw nuts and sticks at Tom and Mia. Tom and Mia run away from the tree. They are hurt and sorry.

"Ow, ow, ow, that monkey hurt me. It was mean and bad," Tom says.

"No, Tom, the monkey was not mean and bad. It was scared and angry. You were mean and bad. You tried to take the monkey away from its home. You made it helpless. You should say sorry to the monkey and leave it alone," Mia says.

Tom thinks for a moment. He feels bad for what he did. He knows Mia is right. He says sorry to the monkey and to Mia. He promises to never take a monkey again. He learns to respect the animals and their homes. He and Mia go to play with other toys in the park. They are friends again. The monkeys are happy too. They go back to their fun in the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl named Daisy. She liked to pinch things. One day, in the park, she saw an opera. She liked how it sounded, so she pinched it. But when she pinched it, a big spark came out! Daisy was so surprised she started to laugh. Then Daisy pinched the opera again and again, and the sparks kept coming. She was very happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and watch videos on her tablet. One day, she tried to watch a video but it wouldn't work. She got very upset and said, "I hate this tablet!"

Her mom tried to fix it, but it still wouldn't work. Lily's dad suggested they try watching the video on the TV instead. They found a tube that connected the tablet to the TV and soon the video was playing. Lily was so happy and said, "Wow, that was fast!"

From then on, Lily always used the tube to watch videos on the TV. She never hated her tablet again because she knew there was another way to watch her favorite shows.

Once upon a time, there was a gloomy tree in the middle of a dark forest. It was tall and strong, but something seemed wrong.

One day, a boy came to the tree. He tapped the bark with his little hand and said, "Hello tree!" But the tree didn't answer back. The boy looked up and saw a hole in the top of the tree with a door shut tight.

He knocked on the door and said, "Who's in there?" But all he heard was silence. Then he said, "Please come out!" In a moment, someone opened the door and the boy saw an old man.

The man said, "I have been living in this tree for many years, since I was a young boy! But it's getting too dark in here, I've got to go." Then the man grabbed a bag and stepped out into the sunlight. He thanked the boy and said goodbye.

The old man wandered off and the boy watched him go. He waved goodbye and shut the door. The tree seemed a bit gloomier now, but it was still the same old tree. And the boy smiled, knowing the old man was looking for a new home.

One day, a little girl named Lucy woke up. The sun was shining and Lucy felt full of happiness.

She wanted to explore the beach. She ran out of the house and towards the shore. Once she got there, she was amazed. She saw the pretty sand and the turquoise sea.

Lucy got closer to take a look at some shells. Suddenly, she heard some laughter and she felt embarrassed!

She looked around and noticed two people watching her. It was her parents! They were amazed by the joy that their little girl had shown.

Lucy smiled, waved at them and then ran off to continue exploring the shore.

Once upon a time, in a modest little house, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy weapon, a small sword. He loved to play with it every day.

One day, Tim was playing with his toy sword in the park. A bigger boy named Max came up to Tim and tried to take his toy weapon away. Tim did not want to give it to Max. They both wanted the toy sword.

Tim was scared but he knew what to do. He went to his mom and told her what happened. His mom went to Max's mom and told her too. Max's mom told Max to give the toy sword back to Tim.

Tim was happy to have his toy sword back. He played with it all day long. He learned that it is important to tell someone when you need help. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play with their ball on the pitch. One day, they had a quarrel because they both wanted to play with the ball at the same time. They were both angry and didn't talk to each other.

The next day, they came back to the pitch. It was very quiet because nobody was there. Timmy and Tommy felt sad because they missed playing together. They decided to say sorry to each other and play together again. They had so much fun and promised to never quarrel again.

Once upon a time, there was a pale bunny named Bobo. Bobo lived in a big forest with many friends. Every day, Bobo played with his friends and had a lot of fun.

One day, Bobo and his friends wanted to have a race. They wanted to see who was the fastest. They all lined up and got ready to run. "Hurry!" said Bobo's friend, the bird. So, they all started to run as fast as they could.

Bobo ran and ran, and he was very fast. He passed all his friends and reached the finish line first. Everyone cheered for Bobo. It was a big success! Bobo was very happy and proud. From that day on, Bobo and his friends had many more races and fun times together.

Lily liked to design things. She had many crayons and papers and stickers. She made pictures of flowers and animals and stars. She liked to give her pictures to her friends and family.

One day, Lily's mom said they would have a party. It was Lily's birthday soon. Lily was happy and curious. She wanted to know what kind of party it would be. She asked her mom many questions.

Mom said it would be a surprise. She said Lily could help her design the party. Lily was excited. She said she wanted to make invitations and decorations and games. Mom smiled and said yes.

They went to the store and bought many things. They bought balloons and streamers and hats. They bought cake and candles and candy. They bought cards and pens and stamps.

They came home and started to design the party. Lily wrote her name and drew a heart on each card. She asked mom to write the date and time and address. She put a stamp on each card and put them in the mailbox. She blew up the balloons and tied them to the chairs. She hung the streamers and hats on the walls. She made a sign that said "Happy Birthday Lily". She set up the games and prizes on the table.

Lily was proud of her design. She said it was the best party ever. She hugged her mom and said thank you. Mom hugged her back and said you're welcome. She said she loved her very much. Lily said she loved her too. She said she couldn't wait for the party. She said she wondered who would come. She was very curious.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was an ordinary dog with a brown collar. One day, Max went for a walk with his owner, Lily. They were having a good time until a big thunderstorm came.

Max was scared of the loud thunder and ran away from Lily. He ran and ran until he saw a cat. Max wanted to play with the cat, but the cat didn't want to play. The cat hissed at Max and Max got angry. He tried to strike the cat with his paw, but he missed.

Suddenly, a car came and hit Max. Lily came running and saw that Max was hurt. She took him to the vet, but it was too late. Max had passed away. Lily was very sad and wished Max had stayed with her instead of running away.

Once upon a time there was a restless girl who wanted to see the world. One night, she decided to go on an adventure. She put on her shoes and grabbed a lantern and went out the door.

The night air was cool and the stars twinkled brightly. She started walking, but soon became lost. Her lantern seemed too far away, and she felt scared.

Suddenly, she heard a noise and something appear in front of her. It was a magical creature! It had bright eyes and lots of feathers. It looked so friendly and full of love.

The creature said she'd help her find her way. Hand in hand, they made their way back home. As the morning sun rose, the girl knew the creature couldn't stay, so the creature disappeared.

The little girl was so happy she'd found her way home. She knew this adventure was full of love and she would never forget it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in her backyard. One day, she saw a spider spinning a web on a tree. The spider looked very busy. 

Lily went closer to the spider and said, "Hello, Mr. Spider. What are you doing?" 

The spider replied, "I am making a web. It is my home." 

Lily was amazed and asked, "Can you tell me more about your home?" 

The spider happily told Lily all about his web and how he catches bugs to eat. Lily listened carefully and was fascinated by the spider's story. From that day on, Lily visited the spider every day to hear more stories about his busy life in his web.

Sara liked to study. She liked to look at books and learn new things. She liked to study animals and colors and shapes. She had a big book with many pictures of animals. She studied it every day.

One day, her mom said, "Sara, it is time to stop studying. It is time to eat dinner. You can study more later."

Sara did not want to stop. She wanted to study more. She said, "No, mom. I want to study. I want to see the lion and the zebra and the elephant."

Her mom said, "Sara, you have to eat dinner. You need food to grow and be strong. And if you eat dinner, you can have dessert. Do you like dessert?"

Sara liked dessert. She liked cake and ice cream and cookies. She thought for a moment. She said, "OK, mom. I will eat dinner. But can I take my book with me?"

Her mom smiled. She said, "Yes, you can take your book with you. But you have to eat your food, too. And you have to listen to me and dad. We want to talk to you and hear about your day."

Sara nodded. She said, "OK, mom. I will eat and listen. And then I can have dessert and study more."

Her mom hugged her. She said, "You are a good girl, Sara. I am proud of you. You are very smart and cheerful. I love you."

Sara hugged her back. She said, "I love you, too, mom. And I love to study."

Once upon a time there lived a small mouse. He lived in a dark cave and wanted to find the light. He tried to find a way out of the cave but it was full of twists and turns. He could not find his way out. 

One day he decided to escape. He ran as fast as he could but the darkness seemed to go on forever. He could barely see anything and became scared. But then he saw a small light in the distance! He followed the light until it was brighter and brighter. 

He was very slow, but he kept going until he reached the outside of the cave. He was so happy to finally see the daylight! He felt freedom and relief. He ran around, enjoying the sunlight, until he saw a bolt of lightening across the sky. He was mesmerised. He had finally escaped the darkness and found the light.

Once upon a time there was a guitar. It was blue. The guitar was in a big room. In the room was a man. The man was happy. He be smiling. The man had the blue guitar. He played it. The music be sweet. The man be playing the guitar all day. He be singing too. He be happy and the music be nice. The day was over and the man put the blue guitar away. He said goodbye to the guitar. That night the guitar be safe and happy. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to draw and cut paper to make things. He made an original picture of a big tree with lots of leaves. He was so happy with it that he showed it to everyone he knew.

One day, Tim went to the park to play. He saw a bird that he wanted to catch. He imagined how fun it would be to have a pet bird. So, he chased the bird around the park. But, the bird flew away and Tim got lost in the park.

Tim was very scared and wished he had never chased the bird. He realized that it was not kind to try to catch wild animals. He learned that it is important to be happy with the things we create and not to harm others.

Once upon a time, there were two fish. One was big and the other was small. 
One day, the two fish went for a swim and suddenly they heard a big roar. The big fish said to the small fish, "What was that noise?" 
The small fish said, "I don't know." 
Suddenly, they saw a big shell floating by. The shell was roaring. The big fish said, "That's a shell roaring!" 
The small fish smiled and said, "That's so cool!" 
They kept swimming until they reached a big rock and there was a big crab sitting on top. The crab was also roaring. The fish were so surprised and excited. 
Then the big fish said, "Let's go back. We can learn more about roaring shells and other things." 
And so the two fish swam away, learning more about roaring shells and other things. The end.

One day, a lazy cat named Tom found a trumpet in the park. Tom was very happy and wanted to play it. He tried to blow into the trumpet, but no sound came out. Tom was sad and didn't know what to do.

Tom saw his friend, a duck named Dina, swimming in a pond. "Dina, can you help me play the trumpet?" Tom asked. Dina thought for a moment and said, "You need to bathe the trumpet first. It might be dirty."

Tom took the trumpet to the pond and bathed it. He washed it very well. Then, he tried to play it again. This time, a beautiful sound came out. Tom and Dina danced and laughed as Tom played the trumpet. They had a fun day at the park with their new trumpet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lisa. She wanted to be big and strong like her Mom, who was very patient.

One day, while they were shopping, Lisa saw a pretty skirt that she wanted to wear. Her Mom said, â€œIf you can be patient and do your chores, we'll complete your shopping."

Lisa was so excited, so she ran home, finished her chores and waited for her Mom.

Finally, her Mom arrived and said "You've been so patient Lisa, so here is the skirt you were looking for.â€ Lisa smiled and thanked her Mom for being so kind.

The pair returned home happy and Lisa put on her new skirt, feeling proud as she could now be as big and strong as her Mom. She would never forget the lesson she learned - to be patient no matter what.

Toby was having a hard day. He had tried so hard to do tough things but they had all been too tough for him. He picked up a truck but it slipped out of his hands and dropped right onto the floor. Toby started to cry, so his mom came over to him and said, 

"Don't worry, Toby! It's ok if you drop things. We all make mistakes."

Toby sniffled and nodded. Then his mom said, 

"Let's go get our truck and try again. It won't be so tough, I promise." 

So Toby followed his mom and they picked up their truck together. Toby gave it his best try, but this time he was able to hold onto it without it dropping. Toby smiled and his mom said, 

"See, you can do tough things, Toby!" 

Toby was proud of himself, and he was very relieved that he didn't have to drop the truck again.

Once upon a time, there was a large bird. Its name was Bob. Bob had a special license. With this license, he was allowed to walk wherever he wanted. 

One day, Bob decided to go for a walk. He was so excited about it. He spread his wings, flapped them and soared up into the sky. 

Just when he was about to start his walk, he suddenly heard something. It was a voice.

"Hey Bob! Where are you going?"

He looked around and saw a small bird flying beside him. 

"Oh hello there! I'm going on a walk!", he said to the small bird. 

"Can I come with you?", the small bird asked. 

"Yes, of course you can, but you'll need a license. Do you have one?", Bob asked.

The small bird sadly shook its head. 

"Don't worry, I can help you get one. Just follow me and I'll show you the steps to get your own special license", said Bob. 

The small bird was so excited and followed Bob on the walk. In the end, both Bob and the small bird had their own licenses and were allowed to walk wherever they wanted!

Once upon a time, there was an image. It was hidden in a dark corner so nobody could see it. But it was still there!

One day, a little boy found the image. He knew it was hidden so he was very excited. He wanted to take the image outside to show his friends.

But when he tried to pick up the image, it fell apart. It was old and had rotted away. The little boy was very sad. He wanted to show the image to his friends, but it was gone.

He tried to remember the image in his head. He thought he could tell his friends what the image looked like. He knew he would never forget the hidden image.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her spinning top. One day, she was playing with her top when she heard a loud noise outside. She looked out the window and saw a man playing a trumpet.

Lily was nervous because she had never seen a trumpet before. She asked her mom, "What's that noise?" Her mom replied, "That's a man playing a trumpet. It makes music."

Lily was curious, so she went outside to listen. The man saw her and said, "Do you want to try playing my trumpet?" Lily was excited and said yes. She took the trumpet and blew into it, but nothing happened. The man said, "You have to spin the mouthpiece to make it work." Lily spun the mouthpiece and suddenly music came out. She was so happy and danced along to the music. From that day on, Lily loved to spin the trumpet's mouthpiece and make music.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very excited to go on a big trip, but he needed a passport. His mommy had a folded passport in her pocket. It was very tough so it wouldn't bend when she sat down. 

The little boy came over to his mommy and asked if he could see it. His mommy took out the folded passport and showed it to him. He was so excited to see it! 

His mommy opened the passport and showed him all the pictures. She told him to be very careful because it was tough! The little boy helped his mommy fold the passport and put it back in her pocket. 

Then, the little boy and his mommy went to the airport. He was very happy to get his new passport and take his special trip.

Ben and Mia are twins. They like to play with their stuff. They have many toys, books, and games. But they do not like to share. They always want the same stuff.

One day, they find a big box in their room. It has a label that says "Match and Learn". Inside the box, there are many cards with pictures and words. The cards are in pairs. The twins want to play with the cards.

"Let me have this card!" Ben says. He grabs a card with a picture of a dog.

"No, I want it!" Mia says. She pulls the card from Ben's hand.

"It is mine!" Ben says. He pushes Mia.

"Ow!" Mia says. She cries.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the room. She sees the twins fighting over the cards.

"What is going on here?" Mom says. She is not happy.

"Ben is spoiled!" Mia says. "He took my card!"

"Mia is spoiled!" Ben says. "She wanted my card!"

Mom shakes her head. She picks up the box. She reads the label.

"These cards are for matching and learning," Mom says. "You have to find the card that matches the picture or the word. Then you can learn something new. But you have to play nicely and share. Do you understand?"

The twins nod. They feel sorry.

"Can we try again?" Ben says.

"Yes, please," Mia says.

Mom smiles. She gives them the cards. She helps them to match and learn. The twins have fun. They share their stuff. They are not spoiled. They are happy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lucy loved to wander near the beach. She liked to look for shells in the sand. One sunny day, she went to the beach with her mom and dad.

As Lucy wandered, she saw a big, shiny shell. It was a rare shell! It was so pretty and special. Lucy picked up the shell and showed it to her mom and dad. They were very happy for her.

Lucy took the rare shell home and put it on her shelf. She loved to look at it every day. It reminded her of the fun day she had at the beach with her mom and dad. And they all lived happily ever after.

Ben and Lily wanted to help Mom make cookies. They put on their aprons and went to the kitchen. Mom smiled and said, "You can help me mix the dough and cut the shapes. But be careful, the stove is hot and we don't want to make a mess."

Ben and Lily nodded and climbed on the chairs. Mom gave them a big bowl and a wooden spoon. They took turns to pour the flour, the sugar, the butter and the eggs. They stirred and stirred until the dough was soft and sticky. Mom said, "Good job! Now we can roll the dough and use the cookie cutters."

Ben and Lily sprinkled some flour on the table and on the rolling pin. They rolled the dough flat and thin. They had many cookie cutters: stars, hearts, circles, flowers and animals. They pressed them on the dough and made many shapes. They put them on a baking tray. Mom said, "Very nice! Now we can put them in the oven. But remember, the stove is hot, so let me do it."

Mom opened the oven and slid the tray inside. She set the timer and said, "We have to wait for 15 minutes. Then the cookies will be ready. Do you want to help me clean up the kitchen?" Ben and Lily looked at the table. It was messy. There was flour, dough and crumbs everywhere. They said, "Yes, Mom, we want to help."

They got off the chairs and knelt on the floor. They picked up the cookie cutters and the rolling pin and put them in the sink. They wiped the table with a cloth. They swept the floor with a broom. They threw the trash in the bin. Mom said, "Thank you, Ben and Lily. You are very helpful and sweet. Now let's see if the cookies are done."

They heard the timer beep. Mom took out the tray and put it on a rack. The cookies were golden and smelled yummy. Mom said, "They look delicious. Let's wait for them to cool down a bit. Then we can eat them and share them with Dad and Grandma. You can choose your favorite shapes." Ben and Lily clapped and cheered. They were happy. They helped Mom make cookies and they cleaned up the kitchen. They were good children.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet rat named Ratty. Ratty was a cool rat, with soft fur and bright eyes. Lily loved to play with Ratty every day.

One day, Lily and Ratty went for a walk in the park. They saw many animals like ducks, birds, and squirrels. Suddenly, Lily recognized her friend Timmy. Timmy was also in the park with his dog.

Lily and Timmy played together while Ratty watched from his cage. They had so much fun playing together that they didn't even notice the time passing. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to Timmy and his dog and gave Ratty a big hug. She knew that Ratty was the coolest pet she could ever have.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She loved to play with her drum every day. One day, she was playing her drum in the park when a boy came up to her. "Can I play with your drum?" asked the boy. "Sure!" said Lily. 

The boy rubbed his hands together and started to play the drum. Lily was happy that she made a new friend. They played together for a while until the boy accidentally hit the drum too hard and it broke. "Oh no!" said Lily. "My drum is broken." 

Lily was sad because she loved her drum so much. She went home crying, and her mom asked her what happened. "My drum is broken," said Lily. Her mom tried to fix it, but it was too broken to be fixed. Lily was very sad and missed her drum very much. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Bob. Bob really wanted to be a gardener when he grew up. He loved playing in the garden and looking for special things like roots.

One day Bob went out to the garden to look for a special root. He saw a big puddle and hoped he could find something special in the wet mud near the puddle. He carefully put his hands in the mud. He felt something squishy and hard. He carefully pulled it out and saw a big, brown root.

Bob was so excited. He ran inside to show his mom the special root he found. His mom was very proud of Bob and told him he could be a gardener just like he wanted when he grew up.

Bob was very happy. He kept the special root safe and hoped he would someday find more special things in the garden.

Lily was restless. She did not want to go to bed. She wanted to play with her toys and watch TV. But Mom said it was time to sleep.

"Come on, Lily, you need to rest. You had a busy day. You spent a lot of time at the park with your friends. You rode the swings and the slide. You had fun, right?" Mom said.

"Yes, Mom, I had fun. But I'm not sleepy. Can I have some water?" Lily asked.

"OK, you can have some water. But then you have to brush your teeth and go to the bathroom. And then you have to go to bed. No more excuses, OK?" Mom said.

"OK, Mom," Lily said. She drank some water and went to the bathroom. She brushed her teeth and put on her pajamas. She hugged Mom and said good night.

Mom tucked her in and kissed her forehead. She turned off the light and left the room.

Lily closed her eyes and tried to sleep. But she was still restless. She heard a noise outside. She wondered what it was. She got up and looked out the window. She saw a big, bright moon. She saw some stars. She saw a cat on the fence. She smiled. She liked the night. She wished she could stay up and watch it.

She heard Mom's footsteps in the hall. She quickly got back into bed and pretended to sleep. She hoped Mom would not come in and see her. She hoped Mom would not be mad at her. She hoped she would fall asleep soon. She was restless, but she was also tired. She yawned and cuddled her teddy bear. She closed her eyes and dreamed of the moon and the stars and the cat.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play in the forest. They had a favorite tree, a big pine, where they built a fort with sticks and leaves. They felt safe and happy in their fort.

One day, a storm came and the wind was very strong. It made loud noises and shook the trees. Ben and Lily ran to their fort to hide. They saw that the pine was bending and cracking. They were scared that it would fall and break their fort.

"Ben, what if the pine falls?" Lily asked, worry in her voice.

"I don't know, Lily. Maybe we should go home and wait for the storm to stop," Ben said, worry in his voice too.

"But I don't want to leave our fort. It's our special place," Lily said, holding on to the pine.

Ben looked at his sister and saw that she loved the pine as much as he did. He loved his sister more than the pine. He decided to be brave and normal.

"Lily, it's okay. We can always make another fort. But we can't make another you or me. Come on, let's go home. Mom and dad will be worry too," Ben said, holding his sister's hand.

Lily nodded and let go of the pine. She trusted her brother and followed him. They ran home and hugged their mom and dad. They told them about the pine and the fort.

Mom and dad smiled and praised them for being smart and caring. They said that the pine was strong and would survive the storm. They said that the fort was fun and creative, but not as important as their safety and love.

Ben and Lily learned that sometimes they had to let go of things they liked to protect things they loved. They learned that worry was normal, but they could overcome it with courage and trust. They learned that the forest was a wonderful place to play, but home was a wonderful place to stay.

But the lotion was not good for dolls. It made Anna's hair sticky and messy. It also got on Anna's dress and shoes and stained them. Lily tried to wash the lotion off, but it did not come off. She started to cry. She had ruined her favorite doll.

Mom heard Lily crying and came to her room. She saw the lotion bottle and the doll. She was angry and sad. She said to Lily, "What have you done? This lotion is for my skin, not for dolls. Lily agreed and said, "Yes, Mom. That sounds like a good idea. Thank you, Mom. You are the best."

Mom and Lily cleaned up the lotion and put Anna in a new dress. They also found a ribbon and a hat for her. Lily hugged Anna and said, "You are still my favorite doll, Anna. I'm sorry I was foolish and put lotion on you. But you are still pretty and I still love you."

Anna did not say anything, because she was a doll. But she looked happy and shiny in her new outfit. And Lily was happy, too. She learned a lesson and she still had her mom and her doll. She did not demand anything else.
