Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy was a different rabbit because he had a very big spring in his step. He loved to hop and jump all day long.

One sunny day, Remy saw a stand with many colorful balloons. He met a little girl named Lucy. Lucy said, "Hi, Remy! Would you like a balloon?" Remy nodded and picked a big, blue balloon. Lucy tied the balloon to Remy's tail.

As Remy hopped away, he felt the balloon tugging at his tail. He was scared but then he remembered his big spring. Remy took a deep breath and jumped as high as he could. The balloon lifted him up into the sky.

Remy looked down and saw all his friends cheering for him. He felt so happy and proud. The moral of the story is to always believe in yourself and use your special talents to help others.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. Tom was three years old and very curious. Every day he would explore outside, looking for something new to learn.

One day, Tom was walking through the grass when he spotted an original goose. He'd never seen a goose before and was excited to get closer. He requested to the goose if he could approach, but the goose didn't answer. Tom walked up to the goose and asked again. This time, the goose finally responded.

"I'm looking for food," said the goose. "If you help me find food, I can show you something special."

Tom was intrigued. He agreed to help and the pair set off to search for food. Eventually, they found some tasty insects and the goose was very grateful.

It was then that the goose revealed its secret. It told Tom that it could fly! Tom was so excited that he couldn't believe it. The goose asked him if he wanted to ride and Tom could only nod in agreement. 

The original goose took flight, with Tom on its back. Tom couldn't believe his luck as he had asked for adventure, and the goose had granted his request!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby girl. She loved going to the park and meeting new friends. One day, she went to the park and saw a strawberry bush. She was so excited!

She went closer and saw that there were strawberies growing all over the bush. With a smile on her face, she picked a few of the sweet, juicy strawberries and started eating them right away. Yum!

Suddenly, there was a funny noise behind her. When she looked back, she saw her new friends, a puppy and a kitty, laughing at her! They thought it was funny to see her eating the strawberries.

The girl laughed too. She thought it was funny and shared some of the strawberries with her new friends. Then, they all played and laughed together in the park for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was always very happy, and she loved to share.

One day, she had a special surprise for a friend. She had a box of colorful cereal. She was so excited to share it with her friend.

When the girl arrived at her friend's house, they both gave each other a big hug.

"What do you have in the box?" asked the friend.

"It's a surprise!" said the girl with a smile.

They opened the box together and the friend gasped in surprise when she saw the colorful cereal.

"I thought you might like them," said the girl happily.

The two friends shared some of the cereal and talked about their day. After they ate, they hugged again.

The girl knew that sharing the cereal with her friend made them both so happy. And she was grateful that her friend was willing to share.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Susy and Joe. They were best friends, and did everything together. One day, they decided to go to the beach. They had a lot of fun. The sun was shining, and the sand felt warm.

The two friends found a big shell. It was very shiny, and it was the perfect shape. Susy and Joe both thought it was the most wonderful thing they had ever seen. They both wanted the shell, and they started to argue.

Susy started to yell. "I saw it first! It's mine!", she shouted. Joe was angry. He started to yell too. "No! I saw it first! It's mine!", he shouted. 

Suddenly a third person appeared. He was very popular around the beach. He had a kind smile. He quietly said "I think it would be nice if you two shared the shell. That way, you could both be happy."

But Susy and Joe didn't listen. They just kept yelling and arguing. The popular man sadly shook his head and walked away. 

Susy and Joe never got to keep the shell. In the end, neither one was happy.

Once there was a cute little girl named Lilly. Lilly had just turned three and her mom and dad wanted to give her a special present. So they gave her a microscope!

Lilly was so excited to have her very own microscope, so she could look at tiny things. She asked her mom and dad to help her use it, and they were happy to support her. 

Lilly spent all day looking at things through her microscope, like a spider on a leaf, a bug on the windowsill, and even the dust on her carpet! She was so curious and amazed by what she saw!

When it was time for bed, Lilly went to sleep dreaming about all the tiny things that were now visible to her. Thanks to her parents' support, Lilly now knew how amazing the world was, even to the tiniest detail.

Emma and her mom went for a walk on a sunny day. They saw a daisy in the grass and Emma said, â€œLook! A daisy!â€ Her mom smiled and said, â€œLet's open it up and see how many petals it has.â€ Emma bent down to the daisy and opened it carefully. Inside the daisy were five normal petals. Emma was so happy to see the daisy and smiled. She told her mom she wanted to pick the daisy and take it home. Her mom said yes and together they carefully picked the daisy. Emma held onto the daisy as they continued their walk and gave the daisy big hugs all the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Joy. She was outside playing with her friends when they noticed a big block of ice.

"Let's keep the ice!" said Joy.

Her friends weren't sure, but Joy said it would be fair. So they all decided to keep it and take it back to their house.

They used their hands and feet to push and pull the ice. It was hard work, but they were excited to have found such a big block of ice.

When they finally got the ice back to their house, they were excited to play with it. They got some buckets and turned the block of ice into a big ice castle.

They ran around it, splashed in it, and had lots of fun. 

When it was time to go home, Joy said, "Let's keep the ice for next time."

So they covered the ice block with a big blanket and put some rocks around it to hold the blanket in place.

The next time Joy and her friends came to play, the ice was still kept. They all cheered and had lots of fun.

Joy was happy that she thought to keep the ice and that it all had worked out fair for everyone. The end.

Once there was a loyal dog named Spot. Spot lived with a family who loved him very much. Everyday, Spot wore a special sweater. Spot followed the family everywhere and always stayed close.

One day Spot heard shouting outside. He ran outside and saw a big cat. It was trying to fight with the family's pet bunny. Spot bravely ran in and started to bark. The cat was scared away and the bunny was safe.

Spot was very proud of himself. He looked very handsome in his special sweater. The family praised him for being so brave and loyal. Spot wagged his tail and knew he had saved the day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a crazy toy named Spike. Spike was a funny toy with a big smile and wild hair. Amy loved to play with Spike all day long.

One day, Amy decided to sort her toys. She put all the big toys in one box and all the small toys in another box. Spike wanted to help Amy sort the toys. Spike said, "Amy, can I help you sort the toys?" Amy smiled and said, "Yes, Spike, you can help me."

Spike and Amy worked together to sort the toys. They laughed and had fun while they worked. When they finished, Amy gave Spike a big hug. "Thank you for helping me, Spike," said Amy. Spike smiled and said, "You're welcome, Amy. I love to help you." And they continued to play happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenny. She lived in a small village near the woods. 

One day, Jenny went to explore the woods. As she was walking she saw a vine on an old tree. She went to grab it when she noticed something strange â€“ it was moving! 

Curious, Jenny tugged at the vine. To her surprise, a small creature popped out!

"Hi!" said the creature. "I'm Pete the cat! I was stuck here and wanted to escape!" 

Jenny smiled and said, "Oh! Let me help you. I'm sure I can get you unstuck." 

Jenny and Pete worked together to free the vine from the tree. Jenny then grabbed a clean cloth from her pocket and carefully wiped of the dirt from the vine. 

Finally, Pete was free! He thanked Jenny for her help before running off into the woods. 

Jenny smiled as she watched him run away. She was happy to help Pete escape.

Lila and Ben were playing with a toy car in the yard. They liked to make the car go fast and make loud noises. But then the car stopped working. Lila and Ben looked at the car and saw a screw was loose.

"Uh oh, the car is broken," Lila said.

"Maybe we can fix it," Ben said. He picked up the screw and tried to put it back in the hole. But it was too hard. He pushed and twisted, but the screw did not fit.

"Quit it, Ben, you are making it worse," Lila said. She grabbed the screw from Ben and tried to do it herself. But she also could not fix the car.

"Quit it, Lila, you are wasting time," Ben said. He snatched the screw from Lila and threw it away.

"Hey, don't do that, we need the screw," Lila said. She ran after the screw and picked it up. But then she heard a loud bark. A big dog was coming towards her. The dog looked angry and hungry.

"Help, Ben, help!" Lila shouted. She dropped the screw and ran back to Ben. The dog chased her and tried to bite her.

Ben saw the dog and got scared. He grabbed Lila's hand and pulled her towards the house. They ran as fast as they could and slammed the door behind them. The dog barked and scratched at the door, but could not get in.

Lila and Ben hugged each other and breathed hard. They were safe inside the house. They did not care about the car or the screw anymore. They just wanted to stay away from the dog.

"Are you okay, Lila?" Ben asked.

"Yes, I'm okay, Ben. Thank you for saving me," Lila said.

"You're welcome, Lila. I'm sorry for being mean to you," Ben said.

"It's okay, Ben. I'm sorry for being mean to you too," Lila said.

They smiled and hugged again. They were happy to have each other as friends. They decided to quit playing with the car and find another toy to play with. A toy that did not need a screw.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. Anna had a doll that she loved very much. Ben had a car that he liked to zoom around. Sometimes, they would share their toys, but sometimes they would fight over them.

One day, Anna wanted to play with Ben's car, but Ben said no. He said it was his car and he did not want to give it to her. Anna was envious of Ben's car. She thought it was more fun than her doll. She tried to grab the car from Ben, but he held it tight. They started to tug and pull on the car.

Suddenly, they felt the floor shake. They heard a loud noise. They saw things fall from the shelves. It was an earthquake! They were scared and let go of the car. They ran to their mom, who was in the kitchen. She hugged them and told them to stay calm. She said they had to go outside, where it was safer.

They followed their mom to the door, but Anna remembered her doll. She had left it on the couch. She did not want to lose her doll. She ran back to get it. Ben saw her and followed her. He did not want to leave her alone.

They reached the couch and saw the car and the doll on the floor. The car was broken. One of its wheels had come off. The doll was fine. Anna picked up the doll and hugged it. She felt sorry for Ben. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Your car is broken. Do you want to play with my doll?"

Ben looked at the car and felt sad. He said, "It's okay, Anna. It was just a toy. I'm glad you and your doll are okay. Thank you for sharing with me."

They hugged each other and returned to their mom. She was happy to see them. She said, "I'm proud of you, Anna and Ben. You were brave and kind. You learned to share and care. Now let's go outside and wait for the earthquake to stop."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside every day. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to have a picnic at the park. Lily was so excited!

As they were getting ready, Lily's mom reminded her to pack her toys and snacks. "Remember to be organized, Lily," she said. Lily nodded and promised to be organized.

When they arrived at the park, Lily saw her friends playing. She ran over to join them, but soon realized she forgot her toys. "Oh no!" she cried. "I forgot my toys!"

Her mom reminded her about being organized, but Lily was too upset to listen. Her friends shared their toys, but Lily was sad she didn't have her own.

Later that day, Lily's mom took her for a jog around the park. As they were jogging, they saw a little boy who didn't have any toys to play with. Lily remembered how sad she felt earlier and decided to share her toys with the boy. The little boy was so happy and thanked Lily.

Lily learned that being organized is important, but sharing and kindness is also important. She felt happy knowing she made someone else's day better.

Tom and Lily wanted to decorate their shirts for the party. They had many colors and stickers to make them pretty. Tom liked blue and green, and Lily liked pink and yellow.

They put their shirts on the table and started to paint and stick. Tom made a big star on his shirt, and Lily made a flower. They were happy with their work.

But then they saw their cat, Milo, jump on the table. Milo was curious and wanted to play. He ran over their shirts and made them dirty. He also scratched some of the stickers off.

"Oh no!" Tom and Lily cried. "Milo, you ruined our shirts!"

Milo looked at them and meowed. He did not know he did something bad.

Mom came in and saw the mess. She was not angry, but she was sad. She said, "I'm sorry, kids. Your shirts are not good for the party now. Maybe we can find some new ones in your closet."

Tom and Lily were sad too. They liked their shirts. They did not want to wear other ones.

But then they had an idea. They said, "Mom, can we decorate some new shirts with Milo? He can help us make them pretty. He is a wise cat. He can learn from his mistake."

Mom smiled and said, "That is a very kind and clever idea. I think Milo would like that. Let's go and find some new shirts and more colors and stickers. Maybe you can make some paw prints or whiskers on your shirts. That would be fun."

Tom and Lily nodded and hugged Milo. They said, "We love you, Milo. You are our friend. Come and decorate with us."

Milo purred and followed them. He was happy too. He wanted to decorate and be good. He learned from Tom and Lily. They were wise kids.

The poor boy wept. He had found a skull in his backyard and wasn't sure what to do. He wondered why someone had left the skull there and what it meant.

He picked the skull up and examined it closely. He sighed, still feeling sad and confused. He wanted to make sure the skull was taken care of, so he carefully put it back down.

The poor boy continued to weep. He did not know what to do with the skull. Was it a sign? He just wanted to know why it was there.

He decided to go to his mom and ask him what he should do. His mom told him to bury the skull in the ground and to pray for the person the skull belonged to. The poor boy felt comforted and said a prayer before burying the skull. 

The boy felt better after burying the skull. He no longer wept. Instead, he was filled with an understanding that everything happens for a reason and that the skull had been given to him for a reason.

Once upon a time, there was a happy, wealthy pup named Lucy. One day, Lucy's mommy decided to take her to the veterinarian to get her a check-up. 

At the veterinarian, Lucy was a bit scared, but the vet soon made her feel better by giving her lots of petting and attention. The veterinarian was very nice and asked Mommy if she would like to invite Lucy back for a check-up next month! 

Lucy's mommy happily accepted the invitation and thanked the veterinarian for her kind offer. She was even more thankful when the veterinarian suggested that Lucy may not need to come back next month since she was very healthy. 

Mommy and Lucy thanked the vet once again before heading home. They were both very happy that the vet had invited them back for a check-up in the future. Lucy's mommy was especially pleased that her pup was in such good health! 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo liked to swim in the ocean with his friends. One day, Nemo saw a big shiny thing in the water. He wanted to see what it was, so he decided to dive down.

As Nemo got closer, he realized it was a refrigerator! Nemo thought it was cool and wanted to explore it. But as he swam closer, he accidentally bumped into the refrigerator and it fell on top of him. Nemo was hurt and couldn't swim back up to the surface.

Nemo's friends looked for him but they couldn't find him. Sadly, Nemo was stuck under the refrigerator and couldn't get out. He couldn't breathe and eventually, he passed away. His friends were very sad and missed him very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her shiny magnet. One day, Lily's mom brought home a big box from the store. Lily was so excited to see what was inside.

When they opened the box, Lily saw a beautiful glass vase. Her mom warned her that it was fragile and could break easily. Lily decided to put her magnet on top of the vase to make it look pretty. But as she walked away, she accidentally bumped into the table.

Suddenly, the magnet flew off the vase and stuck to the fridge. Lily was sad that her plan didn't work out, but she was happy that the vase didn't break. From then on, Lily decided to be more careful with fragile things and found new ways to use her magnet.

There were two friends, Jake and Jane. They were playing in the park when Jane saw a bucket hanging from a tree. She looked up and said, "What is that?"

Jake looked up and said, "That's a bucket."

Jane asked, "What's it doing there?"

Jake laughed. "That's for collecting the leaves when it's fall," he said.

Jane thought for a minute and then got a serious look on her face. "I have an idea," she said. "Let's hang it from the swings and see if we can get higher."

"That sounds seriously fun," said Jake. "Let's give it a try!"

So they took the bucket and hung it from the swings. Jane and Jake took turns sitting in the bucket and swinging higher and higher. They laughed and shouted with joy as they flew through the air. Soon, they were the highest in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Lily. She loved to go for walks in the park. One day, she met a rude man who said mean things to her. 

The woman asked, "Why are you being rude to me?" 

The man replied, "I don't like people who go for walks in the park." 

The woman didn't let the man's words hurt her feelings. She continued to go for walks in the park every day. 

One day, the man saw the woman again and apologized for being rude. He said, "I was wrong to say mean things to you. Can we be friends?" 

The woman smiled and said, "Of course! I'm happy to go for a walk with you." And from that day on, they went for walks in the park together and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a large house. He loved to travel and see new places. One day, he met a little girl who asked him where he was going. The old man replied, "I am going to travel to see new things."

The little girl asked, "Can I come with you? I want to see new things too!" The old man smiled and said, "Of course you can come with me!"

They packed their bags and set off on their journey. They traveled far and wide, seeing many new and exciting things. The little girl was so happy she got to go on an adventure with the old man.

When they returned home, the little girl told her parents all about their travels. She said, "We went to many places and saw many things. The old man's house was very large, and he loved to travel!" Her parents were happy to hear about their adventure and the little girl felt proud to have gone on such a big journey.

John and his mom went out for a walk. They walked a long way, until they came to a distant lake.

John said: â€œMom, I see a lock. Can I take it?â€

Mom said: â€œNo, John. That lock is not ours. We never take things that do not belong to us.â€

John and his mom kept walking until they came to a big, tall tree.

â€œCan I take this little stick for my boat?â€ John asked.

â€œYes, you can take the stick,â€ Mom said.

John was very happy. He took the stick and put it in his pocket. He and Mom walked all the way back home.

John was glad he didnâ€™t take the lock. It was not nice to take something that wasnâ€™t his. He learned that it is better to take things that belong to him and his family.

Once upon a time, there was a mysterious hat. A small bunny wanted to find out what it was. He was brave, so he hopped up and touched it with his paw. But suddenly, the hat started to rot! The bunny was so surprised, he hopped away. He couldn't believe what happened.

The bunny went to get his friend, a fox. The fox wanted to figure out why the hat was rotting. He sniffed it and said, "Maybe it was too old?" The bunny was confused. He had never seen anything like it before. 

The two friends decided to find the owner of the mysterious hat. So, they set off on an adventure. Along the way, they met a friendly bear. The bear said he knew the owner of the hat. The fox and the bunny were excited! 

Eventually, they came to a large cave. The bear told them to wait outside while he went inside. A few minutes later, the bear came out with an old man. The old man was the owner of the mysterious, rotting hat! 

The bunny and the fox were so relieved. They thanked the bear for his help, and promised to visit him again soon. Then the bunny and the fox said goodbye to the old man and continued on their journey.

Once upon a time there was a sunflower. Every morning, it would wake up and feel the warmth of the sun and it was happy. But one day, something unexpected happened. A big, dark cloud blocked out the sun and the sunflower became fearful. It didn't like the shadows that the cloud was creating.

Just then, a little bird flew down. It saw the sad sunflower and said, "Why don't I help? I can feed you some extra special sunflower seeds!" The sunflower was so happy. It smiled and thanked the bird.

Every day, the little bird came back and fed the sunflower until the dark cloud went away. Now the sunflower is happy and full of sunshine every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the store with her mommy. They wanted to buy a soft blanket for her bed. While they were walking around the store, they saw a big leopard toy. 

Lily said to her mommy, "I want to buy the leopard toy, please!" 

Her mommy said, "Okay, we can buy the leopard toy and the soft blanket for your bed." 

Lily was very happy and hugged her new leopard toy. When they got home, she put the soft blanket on her bed and cuddled with her new friend, the leopard. They both slept soundly all night long.

Once there was a little girl, she was very patient. She had a special bell that she loved to ring. Every time she rang it the sound was so sweet and happy! 

One day she went for a walk down the road. As she walked along the road she saw something very special. It was a house, a very beautiful house with a big garden. 

The girl was so excited and she rang her bell. She could feel the happiness inside her heart as the sound of her bell echoed through the air. 

The girl continued down the road, ringing her bell as she went. Everywhere she went the lovely sound of her bell made her feel so happy and content. 

The little girl might have been small but she was very patient. She kept ringing her bell until she went back home.

Anna and Ben were playing hide and seek in the big house. Anna was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Ben ran to the living room and saw a long curtain that touched the floor. He thought it was a good place to hide behind. He moved the curtain a little and went inside.

Anna counted to ten and then opened her eyes. She looked around and tried to find Ben. She saw the toys, the sofa, the table, and the window. She did not see Ben. She wondered where he was. She walked to the living room and saw the curtain. She thought maybe Ben was behind it.

She walked to the curtain and pulled it back. She saw Ben, but she also saw something else. It was a big, furry, unknown animal. It had sharp teeth and claws and it growled at them. Anna and Ben were very scared. They did not know what to do.

They remembered what their mom had told them. She had said, "If you ever see an unknown animal, do not touch it or run away. Stay calm and trust me. I will come and help you." Anna and Ben trusted their mom. They held hands and said, "Mom, mom, help us!"

Their mom heard them and came to the living room. She saw the animal and recognized it. It was a bear that had escaped from the zoo. She grabbed a broom and chased it away. She hugged Anna and Ben and said, "You are very brave and smart. You did the right thing. I am proud of you." Anna and Ben were happy and relieved. They thanked their mom and said, "We love you, mom." They decided to play a different game.

One day, John and his mommy went to the store to buy something special. When they arrived, there was a big, new bicycle in the window. John was so excited that he couldn't stop jumping. His mommy said they could take it home as a surprise. When they got home, they put the bicycle outside and John went to get his tools. He used a wrench to carefully unpack the bicycle and put it together. When John finished he was so proud. He couldn't believe his mom got him such a new, beautiful bicycle. He couldn't wait to ride it!

Once upon a time there was a new zip. It seemed shiny and sparkly, and everyone wanted to try it. One day, two children, Jimmy and Jane, were out in the park. They ran to the new zip and climbed up the steps. They put their hands on the handle and pulled it together. They could feel a wiggle and a buzz, then click! Suddenly the zip seemed to come alive. Together, Jimmy and Jane laughed as they flew down the zip line. They went so fast and felt so free, like they were flying! When they were done, they were both laughing so hard they could barely stand up. They looked at each other and smiled, they had had so much fun. They thanked the new zip for a wonderful time, then ran off to play.

One night, Sarah went outside to look up at the sky. She noticed something special. At the top of the tall house, a chimney was wearing a hat of smoke. Sarah smiled. She thought it was very cool.

Sarah was tired, so she decided to go back inside for bedtime. As she stepped in through the door, she looked back up at the chimney one last time. It was still wearing its hat of smoke.

In the morning, Sarah went outside again to see if the chimney was still wearing its hat. Sure enough, there it was, wearing its smoke hat high up on the tall house.

Sarah thought the chimney was very special. She also thought it was very cool that the chimney was always wearing a hat of smoke at night. Sarah was tired again, but this time, she was tired from smiling so much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old and loved to explore. Today she was playing in her garden when she saw a triangle. She picked it up and it was filthy. But she didn't care and hugged it.

Suddenly, a voice said, "Why are you hugging that triangle?" Lily laughed and said, "Because I like it!"

The voice belonged to her grandmother. She smiled and said, "It looks like it needs a good wash first. Let's go to the bathroom and give it a rinse."

So together, Lily and her grandmother washed the triangle in the sink until it was shiny and clean. Afterwards, Lily hugged her triangle tightly and thanked her grandmother.

From that day forward, the triangle was Lily's favorite toy and she hugged it every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a dependable star. She shined brightly every night and was an important part of the night sky. 

One day someone asked the star why she never lied. She smiled and said it was because she was dependable.

One night, another star came and asked her why she was so dependable. She said it was because it made her happy. The other star thought she was silly, so he decided to try lying. 

The star tried to lie, but he just couldn't do it. He was too used to being dependable. So, he decided to stick to being honest just like the first star. 

They both shone together in the night sky, dependable and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb the big mountain near her house. One day, she took a picnic with her and sat at the top of the mountain. She tasted her favorite sandwich and felt happy. Suddenly, she saw a bird flying with a broken wing. She felt upset for the bird and wanted to help. She climbed down the mountain and took the bird to her mom. Her mom fixed the bird's wing and they released it back into the sky. Lily felt happy again and climbed back up the mountain to enjoy the beautiful view.

Once upon a time, there was a big, noisy whale. He loved to swim and play in the sea. One day, he saw a little fish swimming nearby. The whale wanted to play with the fish, but he didn't know how to be gentle. So he threw the fish into the air and caught it again. The fish felt scared and didn't want to play with the whale anymore.

The whale felt sad when he saw that the fish was scared. He realized that he had been too rough and didn't want to hurt anyone again. From that day on, the whale learned to be gentle and kind to all the sea creatures. He made lots of new friends and they all loved to play together.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be kind and gentle to others, even if we are big and strong. We should always think about how our actions might affect others and try to be gentle with them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom asked her to step on a stool to reach the rice on the top shelf. Lily was very helpful and did as her mom asked.

While they were cooking, Lily's mom accidentally spilled some rice on the floor. Lily said, "Don't worry, Mommy. I'll help you clean it up." She grabbed a broom and swept the rice into a pile. Then, she used a dustpan to scoop it up.

Lily's mom was so proud of her helpful daughter. She said, "Thank you for being such a good helper, Lily." Lily smiled and said, "I love helping you, Mommy." And they continued cooking together, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, he put on his favorite red cap and went outside to play.

As he was playing, he heard a noise. Timmy felt anxious and wanted to know what was making the noise. He decided to peek behind the bushes to see what was there.

To his surprise, he saw a little bunny hopping around. Timmy smiled and felt happy. He slowly approached the bunny and the bunny didn't run away. Timmy felt proud that he was brave enough to peek behind the bushes and make a new friend.

Henry was a shy boy and he liked to play alone. One day, he was playing in the park when he heard someone calling out his name. When Henry looked up, he saw his friend Sadie running towards him and asking if he wanted to play tag. At first, Henry was very nervous, but there was something about Sadie that made him feel comfortable. He said yes and they began to play. 

Soon, they were running all around the playground, both having a lot of fun. But when it was time to get ice-cream, Sadie mentioned something strange to Henry. She said, "I heard that if you tell the truth all the time, you can do anything you want." Henry had never heard of this before, so he asked his parents about it. 

His parents told him that it was true, but that it was also very important to be careful about what he said. Henry thanked them and promised to be careful. From then on, Henry became more confident, even though he was still a bit shy. He was always honest and found himself doing lots of things he never thought he could do!

Once upon a time there was a very sad boy. He was always very sad because he had a secret that no one else knew. This secret made him suffer very much. His secret was hidden away deep inside his heart and he never wanted anyone to find it.

One day the boy went to the store and bought a special lotion. It was a magical lotion that was said to give a person strength when they were sad. So the boy decided to try it and see if it helped his suffering.

He opened the bottle and ran the lotion all over his body. He laughed as he felt the healing power of the lotion work its magic. He felt happiness and relief from the secret he had been keeping for so long.

The boy was so thankful for the lotion that he went around and told everyone about it. Everyone was amazed at the power of this lotion to help him. Finally, his secret was hidden no more.

Once there was a family of three who lived together. Mom, Dad, and Baby. Mom and Dad disagreed about what to make for dinner. Dad wanted to make a steak, but Mom wanted to make a pan of macaroni and cheese. Baby wanted both! Mom and Dad disagreed and eventually Dad made the steak.

Mom went to check on Baby and found that he had taken a pan from the kitchen. Mom asked Baby what he was doing and he said he was making macaroni and cheese. Mom was a bit jealous that Baby wanted to make macaroni and cheese instead of steak.

So, Mom and Dad decided to work together to make both the steak and the macaroni and cheese. They all ate together and it was a delicious dinner. From then on, Mom, Dad and Baby agreed to disagree and make both meals whenever they had disagreements.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved Sundays because that was the day her family went to the park. One Sunday, Lily woke up feeling grumpy. She didn't want to go to the park.

Her mom asked her, "Why are you grumpy, Lily?"

"I don't want to go to the park," Lily replied.

Her mom said, "Let's reverse your mood. We can play a game on the way there."

Lily smiled and they played a game of counting trees. When they got to the park, Lily had so much fun that she forgot why she was grumpy in the first place.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to reverse our mood and find ways to make ourselves happy.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big plastic toy in his room. It was very pretty. He wanted to show it to his friend, Sue.

Tim went to Sue's house and said, "Look at my toy! It is big and pretty!" Sue looked at the toy and said, "Oh, it is so pretty! I like it!" They played with the toy all day long.

Later, Tim's mom called him home. When he got home, his mom asked, "Where did you get that toy?" Tim felt funny and said, "I found it in my room." His mom said, "That toy is not yours. It belongs to your sister. You should not take things that are not yours." Tim felt bad and was embarrass. He said sorry to his mom and sister. He went back to Sue's house and told her the truth. They promised to always share and play with their own toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was three years old and very curious. One day, she was exploring her grandma's house when she found a beautiful stove. Anna was so excited, she ran over to her grandma to tell her all about it.

Grandma smiled and said, "Yes, that old stove is very special. It's been in the family for a very long time and it still works!"

Anna wanted to learn more about the stove, so Grandma showed her how it worked. She explained that you had to put wood inside and then light it with matches. Then, the stove would give off heat and cook food.

Anna was amazed. She thought the stove was so beautiful. She asked if she could turn the stove on, but Grandma said she was too young.

Anna was a bit disappointed, but then Grandma said that when she was a bit older, she could help out in the kitchen with the stove and make lots of delicious treats. Anna was so excited!

The two of them spent the rest of the day talking about the beautiful old stove and all the delicious food they could make with it. Anna loved visiting Grandma's house and hearing all the stories she had to tell.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toy cars on the floor. They make zoom sounds as they move the cars around. They pretend the cars are racing and chasing each other.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Tom says. "My car is faster than yours!"

"No, it's not!" Lily says. "My car is more attractive than yours!"

They look at each other's cars. Tom's car is red and shiny. Lily's car is pink and sparkly. They both think their car is the best.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise outside. They stop playing and listen. It sounds like a real car, but much louder and faster.

"What is that?" Tom asks.

"Let's go and see!" Lily says.

They run to the window and look outside. They see a big, black car zooming down the street. It has a blue light on top and a siren that goes woo-woo-woo. It is a police car.

"Wow!" Tom says. "That car is so cool!"

"Yeah!" Lily says. "That car is faster and more attractive than our cars!"

They watch the police car zoom away. They wonder where it is going and what it is doing. They wish they could ride in it.

They go back to their toy cars. They pretend their cars are police cars too. They make siren sounds and zoom sounds as they play.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Tom says. "We are the police!"

"Woo-woo-woo!" Lily says. "We catch the bad guys!"

They have fun playing with their toy cars. They listen to each other and share their cars. They are happy.

Once there was a soldier who wanted to pay for a surprise. He had to be flexible so he searched everywhere for the right thing. He found a wonderful toy that was perfect. He paid the storekeeper and put the toy in his pocket. 

On the way home, he started to worry because the toy did not look very sturdy. Suddenly, he saw a big tree. He had an idea! He took out the flexible toy and tied it to the tree. It was perfect! 

Now, when he came back home with the surprise, he waited for the smile on his friends face. The soldier had paid for a wonderful surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a smart rabbit named Harry. Harry had a big, fluffy patch of fur on his back that shined like the stars.

One day, Harry hopped around in the forest and saw a bear. The bear said to him, "Why don't you come to my house? We can play together!"

Harry was a bit worried, but he wanted to be brave, so he went with the bear.

The bear showed Harry around his house. Harry saw lots of fun things like books, toys, and tasty food.

The bear said, "Let's spend the night here!"

Harry didn't want to spend the night, but the bear was so eager, he couldn't say no.

Harry stayed awake all night, feeling scared and nervous. In the morning, the bear asked Harry to stay longer, but Harry said no. He was very smart and knew it was time to go home.

Harry hopped away and never went back to the bear's house. Instead, he continued spending his time in the forest, looking for more fun adventures.

Once upon a time there was a little mouse. She was called Millie. One day Millie heard a strange noise coming from a big old barn. Millie went to see what the noise was. 

When Millie went inside the barn she was very confused. She couldn't see anything. Suddenly, the door of the barn opened and a sheep walked inside. The sheep looked at Millie and said, 'I think I have found a place where I will fit!' Millie was so surprised. The sheep was very happy. 

Millie then realised that the noise she heard was the sheep looking for a place where it could fit in. Millie thought that the barn was the perfect place for the sheep. Millie smiled as she left the barn and thought, 'What a nice home for the sheep!'

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy rabbit named Benny. Benny was always tripping and falling over his own feet. One day, Benny decided to start practicing his hopping so he wouldn't be so clumsy. He hopped and hopped until he got tired.

Suddenly, Benny noticed that his shoelaces were untied. He knew that if he didn't tie them up, he would trip and fall again. So, he sat down and tied his shoelaces in a big knot. Benny was proud of himself for starting to practice and for tying his own shoelaces. From that day on, Benny hopped around much more confidently and never tripped over his own feet again.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were astronauts and explore the stars. They had some equipment that they made from boxes and bottles. They had a rocket, a helmet, a radio and a telescope.

"Are you ready, Anna?" Ben asked. He put on his helmet and held his radio. "We are going to blast off to the moon!"

"Yes, Ben!" Anna said. She put on her helmet and knelt next to the rocket. "Let's go!"

They counted down from ten and then made a loud noise. They lifted the rocket and ran around the park. They pretended they saw planets and aliens and meteors. They had a lot of fun.

But then they saw something else. It was a small, furry animal. It had long ears, a fluffy tail and a pink nose. It was hopping around the grass and nibbling on some carrots.

"Look, Ben!" Anna said. "What is that?"

Ben looked through his telescope. He smiled. "It's a bunny, Anna! A cute bunny!"

"Can we pet it, Ben?" Anna asked. She loved animals.

Ben nodded. He put down his telescope and radio. He walked slowly towards the bunny. He reached out his hand.

But the bunny was scared. It saw Ben and ran away. It hopped over a fence and disappeared.

"Aw, no!" Ben said. He was sad. He wanted to pet the bunny.

"Me too!" Anna said. She was sad too.

They went back to their equipment. They looked at each other.

"Maybe we can find another bunny, Ben," Anna said.

"Maybe, Anna," Ben said. "Or maybe we can find something else. Something even more cute and fun."

They smiled. They put on their helmets again. They knelt next to the rocket.

"Are you ready, Anna?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben!" Anna said.

They counted down from ten and then made a loud noise. They lifted the rocket and ran around the park. They pretended they were astronauts and explore the stars. They had a lot of fun.

John was a little boy with a pocket full of blue buttons. He showed them to his mom and she said that they were so pretty. But when John went to school, he put the buttons in his pocket and forgot all about them. 

After school, John was walking home when he saw his friend's toy car. He wanted it so badly but he remembered that he had no money. He thought about taking the buttons from his pocket, but knew it wasn't the right thing to do. He sadly had to walk away.

When he got home, John reached into his pocket and felt the buttons he had forgotten about. He knew he had made the wrong choice and he felt so sad. He wished he had been able to buy his friend's car, but he knew it was too late. He had a deep regret for not listening to his mom. 

John realized that his mom was right and he should always save his treasures. From that day on, John kept his buttons safe in a special box. He never wanted to make the same mistake again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was a shy three year old with big dreams. One day, she decided to make her dreams come true and set out to find a way to succeed.

In her search, Jane found a pin. It was made of metal and glimmered in the dark. Jane gasped with excitement, as she was sure this was the key to her success. She grabbed the pin and immediately started walking home.

On the way, she met an old man who asked, "What have you found, little girl?" Jane proudly replied, "I found a pin, and with it, I'm going to succeed!"

The old man smiled and said, "Good luck, little one, and follow your dreams."

From then on, Jane kept the pin close to her and never let go of her dreams. With the help of her pin, she was able to succeed in her dreams and live happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing with her toys in her room when she heard a noise outside. She looked out the window and saw a graceful deer in her garden. 

Lily wanted to go outside and see the deer up close, but it was getting dark outside. She asked her mommy if she could go outside, but her mommy said no because it was too dark. 

Lily was sad, but then she had an idea. She asked her mommy if they could turn on the porch light so she could see the deer better. Her mommy agreed and they turned on the light. 

Lily looked out the window again and saw the graceful deer in the light. She was so happy and said, "Mommy, I want to see the deer every night!" Her mommy smiled and said, "We can try, Lily." 

From that night on, Lily and her mommy turned on the porch light every night so Lily could see the graceful deer in their garden.

Mary was a brave little girl, but the doctors needed to give her an operation. Mary was scared, but the doctors told her it was nothing to worry about. Mary's family was by her side and they all hugged her, telling her that everything would be OK.

The operation was tricky and took a long time, but Mary was very brave and didn't cry. Afterwards, she was very tired and sleepy. So the doctors fed her some special medicine to make her feel better.

The medicine was an ignorant colour and tasted rather yucky, but it was what she needed. After serving the medicine, Mary was soon feeling sleepy and thankful to be given the medicine that would make her stronger.

Mary went home feeling better, and her family fed her some yummy food to make her happy. She was very thankful for the loving care she was given during the operation. Mary knew she was in good hands and wouldn't ever be afraid of operations again.

Once upon a time, there was a green frog named Bob. Bob lived in a big pond. He liked to jump and play with his friends. One day, Bob saw a big jar of cream. He did not know what it was.

Bob and his friends went to look at the cream. They jumped into the jar to see what it was like. The cream was wet and sticky. They had fun playing in it. But then, the sun came out and the cream began to dry. 

Bob and his friends started to feel stuck in the dry cream. They tried to jump out, but they could not. They were scared. Then, a big bird saw them and helped them get out of the jar. Bob and his friends were so happy to be free. They thanked the bird and went back to their pond to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside and collect pebbles. One day, he found a very pretty pebble and decided to keep it. 

As Timmy was walking home, he saw his friend, Sally. Sally looked troubled, so Timmy asked her what was wrong. Sally said she lost her favorite toy and couldn't find it anywhere. 

Timmy wanted to help Sally, so he suggested they watch the ground for her toy while they walked home together. As they were walking and watching, Timmy saw something shiny. It was Sally's toy! They were both very happy and Timmy gave Sally his pretty pebble to make her feel better.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a grumpy old man named Mr. Brown. He lived in a little house with his cat, Kitty. Mr. Brown did not like to talk to people. He only liked to count his numbers.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lucy came to visit Mr. Brown. She knocked on his door and said, "Hello, Mr. Brown! Can I give you a big smile?" Mr. Brown opened the door and looked at Lucy. He did not say anything, but he showed her his numbers.

Lucy liked the numbers and said, "Wow, Mr. Brown! You have so many numbers! Can you give me one?" Mr. Brown thought about it and then gave Lucy a number. Lucy was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Brown!"

After that day, Lucy would visit Mr. Brown and his cat, Kitty, every day. They would play with the numbers and laugh together. Mr. Brown was not grumpy anymore. He learned that giving made him happy. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once Upon a Time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was feeling cold on a chilly day. Her toes began to shiver, and she could not get warm.

Daisy looked up at the sky and noticed a big, enormous bus in the distance. She figured if she hopped on the bus, she would get warmer. So with a hop, skip, and a jump, Daisy made her way to the enormous bus.

Daisy hopped onto the bus and a warm feeling filled her body. She no longer felt cold and her toes stopped shivering. Daisy looked around the bus and saw her friends on there, smiling and laughing. She grinned from ear to ear and had a wonderful time on the bus. 

The bus drove on and on, taking Daisy and her friends to a warm and cozy place. Daisy never had to shiver again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Allie. Allie was three years old and loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Allie's dad said to her, "Let's go get the swing!" The swing looked very impressive. Allie ran to it and said, "Daddy, can we swing on it?"

Daddy laughed and said, "Of course, my little one! I just need to release it from the tree first." Allie watched as Daddy released the swing from the tree. Once it was free, Allie hopped on and said, "This will be so much fun!"
 
Daddy pushed Allie on the swing, higher and higher until she reached the sky! Allie felt so happy and free as the wind flew through her hair. She felt so impressed by her swing and couldn't believe how lucky she was to have it. 

When Allie was done swinging, she jumped off and hugged her daddy. She said, "Thank you Daddy, I had so much fun!" Daddy smiled and said, "You're welcome sweetheart, I'm glad you like it!"

Allie and Daddy continued to play the rest of the day. Allie spent the rest of her days playing on her impressive swing.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was John and he was three years old.

John was thirsty, so he went looking for something to drink. He walked and walked and eventually he found a pond. He saw the water and went over to drink it.

There was a frog in the pond. The frog said "Do not drink the water! It is not safe for you to drink." John didn't listen, he was too thirsty so he drank the water.

When he got home his mom was very angry. She said "John, why did you drink that water?" John did not understand why she was so angry.

His mom explained, "The pond water is not safe to drink, it could make you sick." John was sad and said he was sorry.

His mom hugged him and said "It is ok, but next time if someone tells you not to do something, please listen. You could have become very sick!"

John nodded his head and promised he would listen next time. He was glad to be home and safe.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Buddy. He lived in a big forest with lots of interesting stuff all around. One day he wanted to go exploring and see what was hiding in the trees and bushes.

He quietly tiptoed around and peeked in different places. Then all of a sudden he spotted something sparkly beneath a bush. He cautiously crept closer and peeked underneath.

Buddy smiled in surprise. Beneath the bush was a big magical chest. He opened it up and discovered a lot of interesting treasures! But the chest was so big that Buddy didn't know what to do with it.

Then a rabbit hopped over and said, â€œYou can hide your stuff in there, it will be safe!â€

Buddy looked at his forest friend in amazement, but then thought it was a great idea. He gathered up all his special things and put them carefully inside the chest. Whenever he wanted to go exploring again, he knew his stuff would be safely tucked away. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a friend named Sammy. They liked to play together every day. One day, Timmy noticed that Sammy's toy was broken. He tried to fix it, but he couldn't. Sammy was sad and demanded a new toy. 

Timmy's parents told him that he couldn't afford to buy a new toy for Sammy. Timmy was sad because he didn't want his friend to be sad. He thought and thought until he had an idea. 

The next day, Timmy brought a box to Sammy's house. Sammy was curious and opened the box. Inside the box was a brand new toy! Sammy was so happy and hugged Timmy tightly. Timmy felt happy too because he made his friend happy. 

From that day on, Timmy and Sammy played together every day with their new toys. Timmy learned that it's important to be a good friend and help others when they're feeling dull.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He was only three years old and he wanted to explore the world. He had a special chamber that he could trust and keep all of his treasures safe. One day he decided to explore his back yard. He was amazed at how charming the trees and the birds were.

As he wandered about he found a magic doorway leading deep into the earth. He wondered what it would be like to explore this magical chamber. So he grabbed his trusty flashlight and started his adventure.

Jack made it to the chamber and he was so excited. Inside he found a charming mouse who gave him a friendly smile. He wanted to stay and explore longer but he had to get back home soon.

Jack knew he could trust the chamber and he thanked the mouse before heading back home. From then on, he visited the chamber every chance he got, and he learned lots of amazing things. Jack will always remember the charming chamber and how much he trusted it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with cards. She had a charming deck of cards that she would always carry with her. One day, she met a boy named Jack who also loved cards.

"Can I join you?" Jack asked.

"Yes, you can!" Lily replied.

The two of them played cards together and had a lot of fun. But then, Jack got very angry when he lost a game. He grabbed Lily's charming deck of cards and tore them all up.

Lily was very sad and cried. She learned that sometimes it's not safe to join with others who might not be kind.

Mommy made dinner and put it in the oven. She noticed that the oven was not clean, so she got a cloth and began to wipe it.

Danny looked at Mommy and asked, "Why are you cleaning the oven?"

Mommy said, "I need to clean the oven so that I can cook the food safely. If the inside is not clean, food can slip and get burned."

Danny saw that the oven needed to be really clean and said, "Let me help you." So, together they wiped the inside of the oven until it was nice and clean.

When they finished, Mommy said, "Now that the oven is clean, we can cook dinner without worrying that things will slip and get burned."

The moral of this story is that it is important to keep your oven clean in order to cook safely.

Anna loves to look at the sky and see the aeroplanes fly by. She wonders where they are going and what they are doing. She wants to go on an aeroplane someday and see new places and people.

Every night, Anna dreams of flying on an aeroplane. She dreams of sitting in a big seat with a window and a tray. She dreams of eating yummy snacks and watching funny shows. She dreams of looking out the window and seeing the clouds and the stars.

One day, Anna's mum tells her that they are going on a trip. They pack their bags and go to the airport. Anna is very excited and nervous. She sees many aeroplanes on the ground and in the air. She hears them make loud noises and sees them move fast.

Anna and her mum get on an aeroplane. It is very big and clean. Anna finds her seat and buckles her belt. She looks out the window and sees the wing and the wheel. She smiles and holds her mum's hand.

The aeroplane takes off and flies high. Anna feels like she is in her dream. She eats yummy snacks and watches funny shows. She looks out the window and sees the clouds and the stars. She is very happy and says, "I love aeroplanes!"

Once upon a time, there was a gray bird who loved to sing. Every morning, the bird twittered and sang the happiest songs that it could find. 
One day, the bird flew over a lady's garden and saw something very special- a ripe avocado! The bird swooped down and grabbed the avocado in it's beak. 
The bird decided to fly high into the sky and find a nice spot to enjoy its snack. As it flew higher and higher, the bird sang a happy song while munching on its prize. 
The bird continued to sing even after the avocado was gone, until finally the sun began to set and the bird flew home. 
The end.

John liked to study. He was very smart for a 3 year old. He loved to go to school and learn new things. One day, John left school and saw a big, red house. It was so pretty. He wanted to learn more about it, so he did some studying. He asked his dad all sorts of questions. He learned that the house was built many years ago and was a special home for a family. John thought this was so cool. He loved learning new things and wanted to know even more. He vowed to himself to keep studying and keep learning.

One day, there was a powerful cabinet in a room. Nothing could disturb it. But then a little three-year-old girl came along. She wanted to see what was inside the cabinet. She tugged and pulled but the cabinet was too powerful for her to open. 

The girl grabbed a nearby chair and used it to climb up to the top of the cabinet. Then she stretched her arm out and pulled the cabinet door open. Inside the cabinet, the girl found lots of interesting things!

The girl was so excited that she began jumping around the room. The powerful cabinet shook and wiggled and finally, it crashed to the ground! The girl jumped in surprise and ran out of the room.

From then on, the girl never disturbed the powerful cabinet again!

Once upon a time, there was a big snake. He slithered through the forest and stopped to rest in a sunny spot. Suddenly, he smelt something rotten far away. He followed his nose and found a big pile of rotten fruit. He curled up in the pile and got very comfortable.

Suddenly, he was disturbed by the sound of a small voice. He lifted his head and saw a little girl who couldn't have been more than three-years-old. He wondered what she was doing there.

The girl noticed the snake and said, "Hello big snake. What are you doing?"

The snake replied, "I am sleeping in this big pile of rotten fruit. It smells very nice and it is very comfortable."

The little girl looked delighted. She clapped her hands and said, "I love rotten fruit! Can I sleep here too?"

"Of course you can!" said the big snake.

So, the little girl lay down next to the snake and they both drifted off to sleep in the pile of rotten fruit. They both dreamed happily ever after.

The bookshelf was very big and very heavy. Dad wanted to know how heavy it was, so he asked Mom to help him weigh it. They got the kitchen scale and put the bookshelf on top of it. When they saw the numbers, they knew how heavy it was.

The bookshelf was too heavy for one person to lift. Dad said it was too weak and that it needed to be stronger. Mom and Dad took their tools and got to work. They strengthened the bookshelf and made it stronger. 

The next day, Dad weighed it again. This time, the bookshelf was much lighter. Dad said it was perfect now! Mom and Dad were very happy and they both gave the bookshelf a big hug.

Once there was a friendly little kangaroo. She used to play in the big, green park every day. One day, she decided to go on an adventure and explore the park.

The kangaroo saw a big tree and thought it would be fun to climb it. So she hopped to the trunk, and started to climb. Up and up she went, until she reached the top. From up there she could see the whole park. She felt so successful!

But while she was basking in the view, her foot slipped and she fell all the way down. Luckily, there was a big, soft cushion nearby that the kangaroo fell on. She was so happy to have landed safely on the cushion, and she decided to stay there for a while and admire the view from her spot on the cushion. She had a wonderful time exploring the park.

Once there was two friends, Jack and Molly. They raced everyday after school. Molly was always faster than Jack. One day it was especially hot.
Jack said to Molly, "let's race one last time before I go to do some work". Molly was excited and agreed.

They ran together, competing over the pink track. Fast, fast, faster they raced! But suddenly the track sloped downwards and Molly was in the lead. Jack was trying his hardest to make up his speed, but it was too late: Molly crossed the finish line first.

Jack was so sad. He wished that he had been faster and that he had won the race. Jack turned around and started walking to do his work. From behind him he heard a loud thud. Molly had tripped and fell down on the track. She was hurt, and there was no way Jack could help her. He sadly said goodbye, and continued on to do his work.

Tom and Lily were hungry. They wanted to eat lunch. They looked in the fridge. They saw a bowl of salad. It had lettuce, tomatoes, cheese and eggs.

"Can we have salad, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Sure, honey. But be careful. Some of the salad is old. It might rot. Rot means bad and yucky. You don't want to eat rot salad. It will make you sick." Mom said.

"How do we know which salad is rot and which is not?" Lily asked.

"Look at the color and the smell. If the salad is brown or green or smells funny, it is rot. If the salad is fresh and crisp and smells good, it is not rot. You can also ask me if you are not sure." Mom said.

Tom and Lily took some salad from the bowl. They checked the color and the smell. They found some good salad and some rot salad. They put the good salad on their plates and threw the rot salad in the trash.

"Mom, can we have some dressing for the salad?" Tom asked.

"Of course, dear. What kind of dressing do you like?" Mom asked.

"I like ranch dressing. It is creamy and yummy." Tom said.

"I like honey mustard dressing. It is sweet and tangy." Lily said.

Mom smiled. She was generous. She gave Tom and Lily some dressing for their salad. They poured the dressing on their salad and mixed it well. They ate their salad and enjoyed it.

"Thank you, Mom. The salad was delicious." Tom and Lily said.

"You're welcome, my loves. I'm glad you liked it. And I'm proud of you for being smart and careful with the salad. You don't want to eat rot food. It is bad for you." Mom said.

They hugged Mom and gave her a kiss. They were happy and full. They cleaned their plates and put them in the sink. They went to play with their toys. They had a good lunch.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Chris. Chris was three years old and he was very brave. His favourite thing to do was to go to the circus. One day Chris went to the circus and he saw a clown. He was so excited and started to laugh. The clown saw Chris and he bent down and said to him, "Why are you so proud Chris?

Chris smiled and said, "I'm proud because I'm brave enough to come here to the circus by myself."

The clown laughed and said, "You should always be proud of yourself! Being brave is an amazing thing!"

Chris nodded and was so proud that he offered to help the clown with his show. The clown was so happy and he said to Chris, "Thank you for your help! Now let's start the show!"

Chris smiled and was so excited to help the clown. Together the clown and Chris put on an amazing show for all the people at the circus. They did tricks, made people laugh and everyone was very happy.

At the end of the show, everyone gave Chris and the clown a big round of applause. Chris was so proud of himself that he couldn't stop smiling. He looked up at the clown and gave him a big thumbs up.

The clown smiled and said, "Thanks for your help Chris, you really made this show amazing!"

Chris was beaming with pride as he walked out of the

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk with her cane because it helped her balance. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and saw a pretty balloon. She wanted to hold it, but it kept floating away. 

Her mommy had an idea and gave her a string to attach to the balloon. Lily was so happy because now she could hold the balloon without it flying away. They played at the park for a while and then decided to have a snack.
