They kept walking until they reached the lake. They stopped to rest and noticed how grey the water was and how bitter the air smelled. Bob shivered, feeling a bit scared. 

Sarah put her arm around him. She said, "Let's jog back and the guard will keep us safe." So, they started jogging and Bob felt happy again. When they reached back home, they were laughing and smiling. Then they said goodbye, until the next time they would go for a jog together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Lily's mom gave her a pair of gloves to wear outside. But Lily didn't like them because they were ugly and didn't match her coat.

Lily's mom said, "Let's measure your hands to make sure we get the right size gloves for you." They found out that Lily needed a smaller size. So, they went to the store and found a pretty pair of gloves that matched her coat perfectly.

Lily was so happy with her new gloves. She played outside in the snow and her hands stayed warm and cozy. From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to measure things to make sure they fit just right.

Once upon a Wednesday, there was a little girl who was very excited. She woke up and got out of bed. She put on her shoes and took a big step forward. She stepped over to her closet and opened the door. Inside, she saw a beautiful dress! She picked it up, stepped over to the mirror, and put it on. She twirled around and smiled. Then she stepped back to her closet and pulled out a pair of sparkly shoes. She stepped back to the mirror and put them on. She looked so pretty! She was so excited to go out and explore the world. She took a few steps to the door and opened it, and stepped outside for the first time. She smiled and the world was her oyster.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his toys and going outside to play. One day, Timmy's mom took him to a soccer game. Timmy saw the players running and kicking the ball. He wanted to play too!

After the game, Timmy saw a man holding a big shiny trophy. Timmy asked the man, "What's that?" The man said, "It's a trophy. We won the game, so we get to keep it." Timmy was cheerful and wanted to win a trophy too.

Timmy's mom signed him up for a soccer team. Timmy practiced and practiced until he knew how to play well. Finally, it was time for the big game. Timmy's team won and they got a shiny trophy just like the man had. Timmy was so happy and knew he did a good job.

Once upon a time, there was a poor, little rabbit named Sarah. She was all alone and feeling very sad. She wanted a friend, but all of her friends were too busy to come and play with her.

Suddenly, Sarah spotted a melon in the garden. She got a big idea. She decided to take it and give it to her friend. 

So Sarah took the melon in her hands and began to run. She ran through the garden and ran and ran until she reached her friend's house.

"Hello! I have got a melon for you," Sarah said. Her friend was delighted and said, "Thank you, Sarah. This is so kind of you."

Sarah and her friend laughed and played together. From then onwards, they were the best of friends. Finally, Sarah was no longer poor - she was wealthy with friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a unique nurse named Sue. Sue had a big hat with lots of colors. She worked in a place where kids go when they don't feel good.

One day, a girl named Lily came to see Sue. Lily had a red face and was very hot. Sue wanted to help her feel better. Sue said, "Let's play a game called 'guess.' I will guess what you need, and you tell me if I am right."

First, Sue guessed that Lily needed a cold drink. Lily said yes, and drank some water. Then, Sue guessed that Lily needed a cool cloth for her head. Lily said yes again, and Sue put a wet cloth on her head. Sue guessed many things to help Lily feel better.

After some time, Lily started to feel good again. She thanked Sue for playing the 'guess' game and for being a unique nurse. Lily went home with a big smile on her face. Sue was happy that she could help Lily and all the other kids too.

Once upon a time there was a nice house. Inside the house lived a family of five. There were two big people, two small people and a baby.

One day the baby was playing near a big box. When the baby opened the box she revealed a surprise. What was inside? It was a yummy chocolate cake! The baby was so excited and started to laugh and jump.

The two big people were surprised by the discovery and soon the whole house smelled like a yummy cake. It was so delicious! The two small people were very happy and smiled. The family all ate some of the yummy cake and it was gone soon.

The family was very happy and enjoyed the special surprise the baby had revealed.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong robot made of steel. He was very powerful and could lift heavy things with ease. One day, he was walking in the park and he saw a little girl crying. He went to her and asked her what was wrong. She said that she had torn her favorite teddy bear and couldn't fix it.

The robot felt sad for the little girl and wanted to help her. He used his powerful arms to tear a piece of steel from his body and gave it to her. He showed her how to use it to fix her teddy bear. The little girl was very happy and hugged the robot, thanking him for his kindness.

From that day on, the robot and the little girl became friends. They would often play together in the park and the robot would always be there to help her whenever she needed it. And the little girl never forgot how the robot had torn a piece of steel from his body to help her fix her teddy bear.

Once upon a time there was a pot. It was very special, but very expensive. One day, the pot was sitting in a room when suddenly, it started to sneeze. The pot sneezed and sneezed until everyone in the room was all tickled. Everyone was so surprised because never before had a pot sneezed before!

No one knew what to do. So, one brave person decided to see why the pot was sneezing. The person opened the lid of the pot and out flew a small mouse with a big, red nose. The mouse had jumped inside the pot and sneezed, which is why the pot was sneezing!

Now that the mystery was solved, everyone laughed and had a good time. The small mouse soon found its way out of the room and the pot was no longer sneezing. The pot was thankfully very special, but also very expensive.

Once upon a time, there was a little flower. The flower was very small and didn't look very pretty. But one day, the flower started to bloom! It grew bigger and bigger and soon it was the most impressive flower in the garden.

One day, a little boy saw the flower and thought it looked so nice. He decided to pick it and take it home. But when he got home, he realized he didn't have a suit to put the flower in. He looked and looked until he found a small suit that his teddy bear used to wear. He put the flower in the suit and it looked even more impressive than before!

The little boy was so happy with his new flower friend. He took care of it every day and watched it bloom even more. And every time he saw the flower in its suit, he smiled and felt proud.

Once there was a poor family who lived in a small house. One day they decided to go to the shop to buy some food. When they got there, they saw that the shop had split into two. The shop keeper was very sad, because the poor family had no money to help him fix it. So mum, dad and the children worked together and used their hands to rebuild the shop. The shop keeper was very thankful for their help! After a few hours, the shop was fixed and the happy family could buy their food. It was a good day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was 3 years old and loved to explore. One day, Jane asked her mom, "Can I go outside and explore?" Her mom said, "Yes, but don't go too far!"

Jane smiled and said, "Okey dokey!" She put on her coat and ran outside. She saw the sun, the trees, and the flowers -- her eyes sparkled! Jane made her way to the park.

Once she arrived, she noticed a group of kids playing. One of them said to Jane, "Hi, do you want to play too?"

Jane shrugged and replied, "I don't know how to play." The kids laughed and said, "It's easy! We'll show you."

So the kids taught Jane how to play. She listened carefully and before she knew it, she was having a really good time! And they all lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time, there lived a tiny girl named Lucy. She was very independent and lived by herself. One day, she decided she wanted to get married.

She went to the ice cream shop and bought a delicious cone. She found a butterfly and asked if he wanted to marry her.

The butterfly politely replied, "I'm sorry little one, I just don't think marriage is for me. Why don't you find someone else to marry?"

Lucy thought for a moment and then said, "Ok, I guess I'll just keep being independent".

She enjoyed her ice cream cone and realized that being independent was ok after all. She had fun doing whatever she wanted and living a life without having to answer to anyone else.

Once there was a tall boy. He was so excited because he was going to the kitchen.

The boy bounded down the hall, laughing and hopping the whole way. When he entered the kitchen, his eyes twinkled in amazement.

"Wow!" he shouted.

The kitchen was filled with cookies, cakes, and goodies of all shapes and sizes. Everything was so colorful and inviting.

The boy's mom smiled and said, "Do you want to try something?"

The boy nodded so fast his head was a blur. He grabbed a cookie and took a big bite. It was delicious. He chewed and smiled even wider.

From that day on, the kitchen became the boy's favorite place. Every time he went in there he was filled with excitement. He could hardly wait to see what new delicious treats his mom had made.

One morning, the sun rose in the sky. It was a peaceful sunrise, with birds singing and animals playing.

Mama and Daddy were in the kitchen, talking in low voices. Mama had caught Sammy, the little boy, breaking something in the house. She was telling Daddy that Sammy needed to learn he couldn't break things. 

Daddy agreed with Mama, and said that Sammy needed to be punished. So they made a plan.

The next day, they took Sammy outside when the sun rose. Sammy was confused, but they said they were going to have a special lesson. On the grass, they had Sammy write with a stick, 'I must not break things.' All morning Sammy wrote this, so he would remember. By the time the sun was high in the sky, Sammy was done writing. 

Mama and Daddy looked at the words. They said Sammy had been punished, and now he must always remember to be careful. Sammy nodded, and said he would. 

Mama and Daddy hugged Sammy. Then they all went inside, happy and together.

Once there was a boy named Tony. He loved sailing in his boat and looking for oysters to open with his big knife. One day, Tony went to the sea and loaded his boat with food and supplies. 

As the boat sailed, Tony looked out and saw the bright blue sea. Then, he glanced over and noticed a big rock with something shiny inside. He knew it was an oyster and loaded his boat with it. 

"Wow!" Tony shouted. "I'm gonna open this oyster!"

But, when Tony took out his knife and tried to open the oyster, he realized it was too hard. He tried again and again, but with no success. Tony felt frustrated, but he was determined to open the oyster. 

Finally, Tony thought of a plan. He gathered all of his strength and loaded both his hands against the oyster. With one final push, Tony opened the oyster and found a big pearl inside.

He smiled and said, "I did it!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Max. He was three years old and loved playing in the garden with his toys.

One day when Max was outside, he noticed a big sandwich. It looked so yummy! Max loved sandwiches and wanted to eat it very badly. He went to pick it up, but then he remembered his mummy had said always to ask before taking something that wasn't his.

So Max asked sadly, "Can I have the sandwich, please?" But the person who had made the sandwich refused him.

Max was very sad but then he noticed something else - it was an ordinary sandwich like the ones his mummy made for him! Now he knew he didn't need the sandwich - he could go home and eat a sandwich that mummy had made for him.

Max learnt a lesson that day - that it doesn't always pay to take something which isn't yours!

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. Sometimes they fought over who got to play with what.

One day, their mom told them to clean up their room. She said they had to put their toys in the right places and make their beds. She said she would check on them in ten minutes.

Anna and Ben looked at their room. It was very messy. There were toys everywhere, on the floor, on the bed, on the desk. They did not know where to start.

"I want to play with the train," Ben said.

"No, I want to play with the train," Anna said.

They started to pull the train from each other.

"Stop it, you two," their mom said, coming back to the room. "You have not cleaned up your room yet. You have to settle this and be organized. How about you take turns with the train? Anna, you can play with it for five minutes, then give it to Ben. Ben, you can play with it for five minutes, then put it away. Then you can both help each other clean up the rest of the toys. OK?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They agreed to share the train and be organized. They played with the train for five minutes each, then put it in the toy box. They also picked up their other toys and put them in the right places. They made their beds and folded their clothes.

Their mom came back to the room again. She smiled when she saw how clean and organized it was.

"Good job, Anna and Ben," she said. "You settled your problem and worked together. I am proud of you. Now you can have a snack and watch a show."

Anna and Ben hugged their mom and thanked her. They were happy that they cleaned up their room and shared their toys. They learned that being organized and settling things was better than fighting and being messy.

Once upon a time, in a small hut, there lived a loyal dog named Spot. Spot loved his family very much. He always stayed close to the hut to keep his family safe.

One sunny day, Spot saw a bird outside the hut. The bird said, "Hello, loyal dog! Do you want to play with me?" Spot replied, "Yes, I would love to play, but I must stay near my hut to watch over my family."

The bird understood and said, "That's okay, I can play near the hut too." So, Spot and the bird played together all day long. They had lots of fun and became good friends.

The next day, the bird came back to the hut and asked Spot, "Do you want to play again today?" Spot replied, "Yes, I would love to play with you again." So, they played together near the hut every day, and Spot always kept his family safe.

Once upon a time, there was a bright child named Mia. She was always looking for ways to explore and have fun. One day, Mia and her mom were camping in the woods. They set up their tent and made a campfire. 

Mia declared, "Mom, let's go explore the woods!" 
But her mom said, "No, Mia. It's getting dark, the woods can be dangerous. You could get lost or hurt."

Mia thought for a moment, and then she said, "I'm strong and I'm very bright. I know I can find my way back if something does happen."

Her mom thought for a moment, then finally yielded. She said, "Alright, Mia. I can tell you're a brave girl, so I trust you. Just stick to the path and come back before it gets too dark."

Mia was so excited! She grabbed her flashlight and ventured off into the woods. She loved exploring and discovering new things. She confidently made her way along the path, looking for things to explore. 

But then, something unexpected happened. Mia took a wrong turn and got lost! She tried to get back to the path, but with the darkness, it was hard to find her way. Suddenly, she saw a bright light coming through the bushes. It was her mom, who had followed her in the dark. 

Mia's mom hugged her

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety had a lovely yellow wing and loved to fly around and sing. One day, Tweety met a little mouse named Jerry. 

"Hi, Jerry! Do you want to play hide and seek with me?" asked Tweety.

"Yes, I love to play hide and seek!" replied Jerry.

Tweety and Jerry played hide and seek for a while, but then Tweety noticed that Jerry was hiding in a dangerous place. "Jerry, come out! You're hiding in a place where the cat can catch you!" warned Tweety.

Jerry listened to Tweety and quickly ran away to a safer place. "Thank you, Tweety! You're a good friend and you saved my life!" said Jerry.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be a good friend and help others, even if it means telling them things they don't want to hear.

Once there was a little boy named Ted. He loved to explore his neighbourhood and one day he decided to go on a big adventure. He grabbed his favourite basket and began carrying it around the neighbourhood. He passed by a farmer's field and some pretty trees but eventually he found himself in a thick forest. 

Suddenly, Ted tripped and fell down, hurting his ankle. He cried out in pain, but there was nobody around to help. He couldn't carry his basket any more, so he put it down and tried to limp home. 

Just as Ted was about to give up, he heard a voice. It was the farmer! The farmer had heard Ted's cries and had followed him into the forest. He fixed Ted's ankle and then carried the heavy basket for Ted.

The farmer then helped Ted all the way back home. Ted thanked the farmer and never strayed from home again - at least not without his trusted basket!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Molly. She was very excited to explore the world, so she wandered everywhere she could.

One day, Molly saw something magical, it was a sparkly rainbow that was in the sky. She wanted to get closer to it, so she walked towards it, but she was a bit scared.

A friendly voice said, "It's ok Molly, you can be safe, just follow me!" She looked up to see a beautiful fairy. Molly felt safe, so they wandered together until they reached the rainbow.

The fairy waved her wand and said, "I'm sorry you can't touch the rainbow Molly, but here, I've brought something special for you!" With a few more waves of her wand, a tiny sparkly butterfly appeared right in front of them.

Molly was delighted! She thanked the fairy kindly as she held the butterfly in her hands. Molly then said goodbye to the fairy and wandered off, with her new magical friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly and sing all day long. One day, Tweety was flying over a busy ground when he saw a big, mean cat. The cat wanted to eat Tweety for dinner!

Tweety quickly flew away, but the cat chased after him. Tweety was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, he saw a group of other birds on the ground. He flew down and asked for their help. "Please help me, the cat is chasing me!" he said.

The other birds recognized that Tweety was in trouble, so they all flew up and surrounded the cat. They chirped and flapped their wings, scaring the cat away. Tweety was so grateful to his new bird friends. He learned that it's always good to ask for help when you need it and that friends will always be there to protect you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad. One day, Lily went outside to play and saw a big mill in the distance. She ran over to see it up close. The mill was very tall and had big blades that spun around and around in the wind. 

Suddenly, Lily heard her mom calling her name. She ran back to the house and saw that her little brother had spilled his juice all over the floor. Her mom was very angry and said she would punish him by making him clean it up. Lily felt sad for her brother, but knew he had to learn not to make a mess. 

That night, Lily's mom made a bitter vegetable for dinner. Lily didn't like the taste, but she knew she had to eat it all or else her mom would punish her too. After dinner, Lily went to bed and dreamed about the big mill. She hoped one day she could go back and see it again.

One day, a small boy saw a bookcase. He was so excited and wanted to stay with the bookcase. He ran over to it. The boy found that the bookcase was small, but it had lots of books inside. He started to take them out one by one and look at them. He especially liked the one with colorful pictures. He wanted to read it but he couldn't since it was too hard.

The boy learned that the best thing to do was to stay and look at the bookcase. He would look around for a while and read the colorful pictures in the book. He was happy and content.

Then the boy had an idea. He decided to make his own bookcase. He thought and he thought. He was so excited with his idea that he went and got some wood and tools and started to build it.

When he was done, he stepped back and looked at it. He was so proud of his work. It was small but he liked it just the same. He put some books he had been given into it and was so happy. Now, he could stay with his own bookcase and read the books whenever he wanted. He liked it so much that he never wanted to leave it again.

The player was wet. He had been playing in the rain, and now he was wet. He kept playing, even though his pyjamas were heavy and wet. He kept going, and running around, having fun. He twirled and turned, and his wet pyjamas flapping around him.

The player felt happy, and he kept doing his dance. He laughed and smiled, as the rain kept falling. But soon, he started feeling cold. So, he stopped and saw the big puddles on the ground. He wanted to keep playing, but he knew he had to go in. He was already very wet!

So he ran inside, and then changed out of his wet pyjamas. He put on some warm, dry clothes and shoes. And once he was dry and warm again, he started to play again. He smiled, because he had kept playing even when it was wet.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved playing football. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends. They were having fun, kicking the ball back and forth. But then, the ball went too far and landed in a deep hole.

The boy tried to reach for the ball, but it was too deep. His friends tried to help, but they couldn't reach it either. They started to argue about who was going to get the ball out. The boy felt sad because he didn't want to lose his favorite football.

Suddenly, a kind man walked by and saw what was happening. He asked the boy what was wrong and the boy explained the situation. The man laid down on the ground and reached deep into the hole. He grabbed the ball and gave it back to the boy. The boy was happy again and thanked the man for his help. They all continued to play football together, having fun and forgetting about the conflict.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very excited because he was going to visit his grandma's house. But when Timmy got to his grandma's house, he realized that he forgot his key at home. Timmy felt sad and scared because he couldn't get into the house.

Timmy's grandma saw that he was upset and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her that he forgot his key and couldn't get into the house. His grandma told him not to worry and that they would find a way to get inside. They looked around and saw an incredible tree with branches that reached up to the window.

Timmy's grandma told him to choose which branch he wanted to climb on, and he picked the biggest one. He climbed up the branch and reached the window. He opened it and climbed inside. Timmy was very happy that he was able to get into the house with the help of his grandma and the incredible tree.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely little engine named Ellie. She lived in a big park with trees and a pond. Ellie had no friends to play with, and she felt very sad.

One sunny day, a duck named Danny waddled up to Ellie. "Hi!" said Danny. "I live in the pond. What's your name?" Ellie smiled and said, "I'm Ellie the engine. I live here in the park." Danny and Ellie talked and played all day long. They liked to race around the park together.

As the sun went down, Ellie and Danny said goodbye. "I had fun today," said Ellie. "Me too!" said Danny. "Let's play again tomorrow!" From that day on, Ellie the lonely engine was not lonely anymore. She had a best friend, Danny the duck, to play with in the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house near a big forest. One day, she wanted to visit a village she had heard about. She asked her mom if she could go, and her mom said yes.

Lily walked and walked until she finally arrived at the village. But it was a gloomy village with no one around. She felt scared and alone. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise coming from a nearby house. She went closer to investigate, but it was a bad idea.

The noise was coming from a monster who lived in the house. The monster saw Lily and chased after her. Lily ran and ran until she finally made it back home. She was safe, but she never wanted to visit that gloomy village again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red bus. It had a driver who drove it every day. One day, the bus saw a scary cat. The cat had big, sharp teeth and it made the bus very scared.

The bus yelled to the driver, "Help me! There is a scary cat!" The driver looked at the cat and said, "Do not worry, bus. I will help you." The driver honked the horn very loud. The scary cat heard the loud noise and ran away.

The bus was very happy. The driver and the bus went on their way. They were not scared anymore. They had a good day and saw many friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird lived on a hill. Every day, the bird would sing and whistle. One day, the bird found some berries. The berries were very sour. The bird didn't like the sour berries. So, the bird decided to whistle a sad song. But then, the bird remembered that there were other berries on the other side of the hill. The bird flew over the hill and found some sweet berries. The bird was very happy and whistled a happy song.

Once upon a time there was a monkey who liked to display his banana everywhere he went. Everywhere he went, people would look in amazement at the size of the banana. One day he went to a park with his banana, but he was not alone. There was a troubled little elephant there. The little elephant was curious about the banana and so he asked the monkey if he could show him his banana.

The monkey was worried. He was enjoying displaying his banana, but he was also troubled. He knew the banana was very big and the little elephant was very small. He was scared the elephant would get hurt.

Eventually, the monkey decided to do the kindest thing. He gave the banana to the little elephant to enjoy. Seeing the elephant so happy with the banana filled the monkey with joy. He had been kind and generous, and the little elephant was so delighted.

The story teaches us that kindness is important. In the face of a troubled little elephant, the monkey chose to give away his banana instead of showing off. Even though he was afraid, his generous spirit won through in the end - and it is this that counts the most.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy loved going on picnics with his friends. One day, Teddy and his friends went on a picnic in the forest. They had sandwiches, juice, and fruit.

After they finished eating, Teddy's friend, Rabbit, left the picnic area very messy. Teddy was upset because he liked things to be tidy. He asked Rabbit to clean up, but Rabbit didn't want to.

Teddy was sad and didn't know what to do. He decided to leave the picnic area and go home. Rabbit felt bad and realized he should have cleaned up. The next time they went on a picnic, Rabbit made sure to clean up and keep things tidy. Teddy was happy, and they all had a great time together.

Once upon a time there lived a boy named Pete. Pete wanted to climb to the top of a tall tree. The tree was very high, but Pete was very persistent.

Pete's mom saw him and said, "Pete, that tree is too high! You can't climb it!"

But Pete wouldn't listen. He kept trying to climb higher and higher. He just wouldn't give up.

Finally, Pete made it to the top of the tree. At the top, he found a giant bowl of salad. He was so excited that he started to eat it with his hands.

Suddenly, Pete started to slip. He tried to grab onto the tree, but his hands were too greasy from the salad. He tumbled down and landed with a thud on the ground.

The next day, Pete was very sad. He went back to the tree, but he knew he would never climb it again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very happy and liked to play with her toys.
One day she wanted to explore and see what was around her. She put on her shoes and ran outside.

When she looked up, she saw a big tree with a rope dangling from a branch. She wanted to climb the tree and see what was at the top.

She grabbed hold of the rope and started to climb higher and higher. She was so pleased with herself that she could climb so high. 

At the top of the tree was a nest. Inside the nest was a small safe. The girl was so curious that she wanted to open the safe. 

But when she opened the safe, all she saw was a note inside. On the note the word "selfish" was written. The girl knew that the safe was not for her and so she decided to leave it where it was and climb down the tree.

The little girl learned a valuable lesson - being selfish is not okay.

One foggy morning, a stubborn little girl decided to go to the park. She had so many plans and was so excited to explore her new surroundings. 

As she entered the park gates, she peeked around to see what she could find. She noticed a tall slide, some swings, and a pond with some ducks. 

The little girl approached the slide and was about to climb it, when suddenly the fog thickened and the air became too dark to stay outside. She decided to go home and come back later. 

Before she left, she peeked one last time at the pond with the ducks, hoping that when she returned the fog would have gone away.

One day, a clown went to the park. He was wearing a big, colourful hat and sunnies. He was getting ready to perform a show.

The children were so excited; they couldn't wait to see the clown. They clapped and jumped around. The clown jumped up and down too, always smiling.

The clown started the show and started to juggle the bright, shiny balls. The children laughed and clapped their hands. But then the juggled balls fell on the ground. The clown was so impatient, he felt very sad.

But then suddenly, a small boy picked up the balls and gave them back to the clown. The clown thanked him with a big smile and started juggling again. He performed his show and everyone had lots of fun. They all thanked the little boy for being so helpful.

Max was a harmless puppy. He was so happy to be outside, and he loved wielding his leash. Sometimes, he'd walk down the street and meet other puppies. But today, he was all alone. He sighed. Then, he heard a bark! It was a golden retriever, and it was inviting him to play. Max jumped around and smiled. Now he wasn't alone.

He and the golden retriever had a lot of fun together. They ran around and barked. Then, it was time to go back home. Max sighed one last time. He wanted to stay and play, but he knew it was time to go. So, with his leash in hand, he walked back home to his loving family.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah who was three years old. She was always very curious. One day Sarah went for a walk with her mom. As they were walking outside, Sarah saw a drain in the road. She asked her mom what it was and her mom said it was a drain. 

Sarah wanted to know more about drains, so she decided to look inside. She carefully watched as her mom lifted the cover of the drain. She saw a big, deep hole that seemed very cold. 

Sarah soon decided what she would do. She was going to put a little rock into the drain to see what would happen. She looked a few rocks on the side of the road and chose one. She carefully placed the rock into the drain and waited. 

All of a sudden, Sarah saw the rock move lower and lower into the drain. After a few seconds, it disappeared from view. Sarah was amazed and knew she had made an important discovery.

Henry and his mom were going to the park. But before they left, they needed to get a ride. So mom called a yellow taxi. They got inside and Henry was so excited! He shouted "Taxi! Taxi!". The driver smiled and drove them away.

When they arrived at the park, Henry was so happy to see lots of swings and even a slide! He ran and played for a few hours. Finally, it was time to go home. Mom asked the driver to take them back. 

On the way back, Henry noticed a sign. He asked his mom what it said. Mom said it said 'Baby on Board', and that it meant a baby was inside this car. "Can you show me where the bathroom is?" asked Lily.

"Sure," said her friend, "It's down the hall."

Lily went to the bathroom but when she came out, she saw a big dog. The dog barked loudly and Lily was frightened. Her friend saw what happened and ran to her.

"Don't be scared," said her friend, "The dog is friendly."

Lily felt better and thanked her friend. They played with the toy car together and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a very kind lady who lived in a town. Everyday she would open up her door and wait for people to come.
Week after week, she waited but no one ever came. One day, the kind lady was so sad that it started to rain.
As the raindrops fell, she started to cry. Suddenly, something magical happened. All her sadness started to melt away.
The kind lady looked up and saw the sun had come out. She smiled and knew that everything was going to be alright!
As she waited, the kind lady noticed a little girl walking toward her.
"Hello, I am so happy you are here!" said the kind lady.
The little girl replied "I saw you here all alone every day, so I wanted to come visit you!"
The kind lady was so surprised and happy. From that day onwards, the kind lady and the little girl were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family who loved to drink grape juice. One day, they went to a big store to buy some grape juice. They found a bottle of grape juice that was very special. The bottle was big and had a shiny label that said "brilliant wine". They bought the bottle and took it home.

The family opened the bottle and poured the wine into glasses. They tasted the wine and it was very yummy. But they decided that the wine was not for them. They wanted to return the wine to the store and get their money back. So they put the wine back into the bottle and went back to the store.

When they got to the store, they gave the bottle of wine to the nice lady at the counter. They told her that they wanted to return the wine because it was not what they wanted. The lady smiled and gave them their money back. The family was happy that they could return the wine and get their money back. They went home and drank their grape juice, which was still their favorite drink. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a fierce bear who wanted to find something cool. He looked in the woods and he looked in the lake, but he couldn't find anything he liked. 

Suddenly he saw a cooler! It was filled with yummy treats, so the bear decided to crawl over and get some of the treats for himself. 

He opened the cooler and started to eat all the treats he found. He was so happy he was grunting and growling with each bite. 

The bear fell asleep with a full stomach, feeling very content. He had found something cool and he was very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big, tall giraffe. He had a long neck and spots all over his body. One day, he was very hungry and wanted to eat some leaves from the trees. But the trees were too tall for him to reach. 

Just then, a little boy came by and saw the giraffe. He wanted to help the giraffe, so he climbed up the tree and picked some leaves. He fed the leaves to the giraffe and the giraffe was very happy.

The giraffe was so grateful for the boy's help that he decided to tell him a story. The story was about a little bird who wanted to learn how to fly. The boy listened to the story and was very happy. From that day on, the boy and the giraffe became good friends and helped each other whenever they could.

Once there was a bee called Buzz. He wanted to take a ride so he asked his friends for help. His friend, Honey, said, "Yes, let's go for a ride!"
So Buzz and Honey flew to a big blue hive. Buzz was so excited about the ride. He was so happy that he flew and spun in the air. 

When they got to the hive, Buzz explored all the nooks and crannies, searching for something sweet. Eventually, he found a pot of honey. He ate so much that he had a stomachache. But it was worth it! 

Suddenly, they heard a loud buzzing. A gang of bees were flying around the hive! Buzz and Honey were so scared! They flew away as fast as they could. 

Finally, they made it back to their home. They were so tired from their ride, but they had lots of fun and were glad they went.

Brianna clapped her hands together as she ran to the little hut in the forest. It was sweet with flowers all around it. 

"Hey there," said a voice coming from inside the hut. 

"Hello!" said Brianna with a smile.

"Who are you?" asked the voice. 

"My name is Brianna," said the little girl.

"Do you want to come in?" asked the voice. 

Brianna hopped inside and saw a small, yellow bird sitting on a branch.

"Nice to meet you," said the bird. 

"Nice to meet you too," said Brianna.

The bird started to clap and sing a sweet song. Brianna started to clap and sing too. They sang and clapped for a long time. 

When they finished, the bird said goodbye and flew away. Brianna waved goodbye and started to walk back home. She was humming the sweet song she had just heard.

Once upon a time, there was a big lake. Many ducks used to swim in it. One day, two ducks started to fight. They were angry with each other. They flapped their wings and quacked loudly. 

Suddenly, they fell into the lake. They started to splash and swim. They forgot about their fight. They were happy to swim in the cool water. 

After a while, they came out of the lake. They were wet but proud of themselves. They had swum very well. They looked at each other and smiled. They were no longer angry. They were friends again.

Once upon a time, there lived a beautiful turkey. She was proud of her feathers and enjoyed the warm sunshine each day.

One day, the turkey went to the river to take a bath. She slipped on a rock and fell into the river. "Help! Help!" the turkey squawked.

Then, a little boy heard her cries for help. He was only three years old, but he was brave and determined to help the turkey. He ran to the river and reached in to grab the turkey. 

"There, there," said the little boy as he scooped up the turkey. He was very proud of what he had done, and he held the turkey close so she would know she was safe. 

The turkey was so happy to be safe and dry. She thanked the little boy with a gentle nudge.

The little boy and the turkey both beamed with pride. From then on, they were the best of friends and always looked out for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a quiet girl named Abi. Abi was three years old and loved to visit her family. Every time Abi went to visit her family, they would hug her and tell her how much they believed in her.

One day, Abi went to visit her Grandma's house. Grandma had a big garden, and Abi wanted to explore it. When she went into the garden, she saw a lot of colorful flowers and big trees. Abi smiled and took a deep breath. She believed that one day she could be as strong as the big trees.

Grandma saw how happy Abi was in the garden, and she believed that Abi would always stay happy. So, she told Abi to come back and visit as often as she wanted. Abi thanked Grandma, and then she went home.

Abi always remembered that visit to her Grandma's house. It felt so quiet and peaceful, and she believed that if she held on to that feeling, it would make her brave and strong!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a colorful shield that she loved to play with. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her shield. She saw a boy who was sad because he lost his toy. Lily wanted to help the boy, so she signed to him that she would help him find his toy. 

Lily and the boy looked all around the park, but they couldn't find the toy. Lily didn't give up, though. She kept looking until they finally found the toy. The boy was so happy and he thanked Lily for helping him. 

Lily learned that it's important to help others when they need it. She felt proud of herself for being kind and helpful. From that day on, Lily always carried her colorful shield with her, as a reminder to be a good friend and help others.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to play with his friends at the park. They would run and jump and laugh together. 

One day, Max's friend Spot invited him to a lab. Max was curious and excited to see what a lab was. When he got there, he saw lots of beakers and test tubes. Spot's owner was a scientist and she was doing experiments. 

Max and Spot started to play a game of fetch in the lab. They were both very competitive and wanted to win. Max threw the ball far and Spot ran to get it. They both laughed when Spot accidentally knocked over a beaker. Luckily, nothing broke and they continued to play. Max had a great time at the lab with his friend Spot.

Lily was a cat who liked to sleep on the sofa. The sofa was warm and soft and smelled like her owner. Her owner was a nice lady who gave her food and milk and petted her every day.

One day, a new cat came to the house. His name was Tom and he was big and black and had green eyes. He looked at Lily and said, "This is my sofa now. Go away, little cat."

Lily was scared and angry. She did not want to share her sofa with Tom. She said, "No, this is my sofa. You are not the owner. You are a bad cat. Go away, big cat."

Tom did not listen. He jumped on the sofa and pushed Lily off. He curled up on the warm spot and purred. He had stolen Lily's sofa.

Lily ran to her owner and meowed. She wanted her owner to help her. Her owner saw what Tom had done and frowned. She picked up Tom and said, "No, no, no. You are not a nice cat. You cannot steal Lily's sofa. Lily is my cat and she is a good cat. You have to go back to your own house."

She took Tom outside and closed the door. She went back to Lily and hugged her. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Tom was a naughty cat. He will not bother you again. You can have your sofa back. I love you, Lily."

Lily was happy and relieved. She snuggled with her owner on the sofa and purred. She had her warm and soft and nice sofa back. She loved her owner too.

Once upon a time there was a nice girl called Lisa. Lisa wanted to go to the big, important maze. But before she could go, Lisa had to do something first.

She had to clean the maze!

So Lisa got all the cleaning things she needed and started to clean. She had a mop for mopping the floor and a brush for brushing the walls. She had to be very careful because the maze was important!

When Lisa had finished cleaning, the maze looked so beautiful. Lisa was very proud of her work and skipped around the maze.

Lisa was finally ready to go to the maze. She went in and had a lovely time. She explored all the different corners and pathways and it felt like she was discovering a new world.

The end.

Jill was a bossy girl who liked to tell other kids what to do. She had a big envelope with stickers and crayons that she did not want to share. She kept the envelope in her backpack and guarded it all the time.

One day, Tom saw the envelope and wanted to see what was inside. He was curious and liked to draw. He waited until Jill was busy playing with her doll and sneaked to her backpack. He opened the zipper and took out the envelope.

"Hey, that's mine!" Jill shouted when she saw Tom. She ran to him and tried to grab the envelope. Tom held it tight and said, "No, let me see. You have so many stickers and crayons. You can share some with me."

Jill was angry and pinched Tom's arm hard. Tom cried out and dropped the envelope. The stickers and crayons spilled out on the floor. Jill picked up the envelope and stuffed everything back in. She glared at Tom and said, "You are a bad boy. You should not touch my things. Go away!"

Tom rubbed his arm and felt sad. He did not want to be friends with Jill anymore. He thought she was mean and selfish. He went to find another kid who would play with him nicely. He hoped Jill would learn to be nicer and share her things.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Steve. He was very alert and liked to run around outside. One day, he wanted a cookie, so he asked his mom for one. She said yes, and he went to the kitchen to get it. 

Steve saw a special cookie jar on the counter. It was shaped like a train and had a lid on it. Steve grabbed the lid and tried to lift it up, but it was too heavy. He asked his mom to help.

His mom picked up the lid and loaded it into the back of the train. When she opened it up, Steve could see all kinds of delicious cookies inside! He picked out one that looked good and asked his mom for it. She said yes, and Steve went off to eat his cookie. He couldn't believe his luck! 

From that day on, Steve was the happiest little boy around. He was always so alert, just waiting for the moment when he could eat another cookie from the special cookie jar.

Once there was a boy who loved to run and play. One day, he heard a soft glowing sound coming from the trees. He was curious and went to investigate. 

When he got there, he saw a cone that was glowing. It was very beautiful and seemed very helpful. The boy reached out and touched it.

Suddenly the cone started to get bigger and bigger. It grew until it became as big as a house. The boy was scared but the cone was very friendly. It said it would help him so he was no longer afraid.

The cone gave the boy a big hug. Then it gave him some special powers. He could now fly and make things glow. With the help of the cone, the boy could do things he never thought possible. He was so excited! 

The boy decided to go home and show his family his new magical powers. He thanked the cone for its help before flying off into the sky.

Timmy was feeling bored, so he asked his Mommy for something fun. His Mommy thought for a minute, and then had an easy idea. She asked Timmy if he wanted to help her load the groceries from the car.

Timmy was so excited. He ran outside with Mommy, and when they got to the car, Timmy immediately started helping. He grabbed the bags and brought them inside. It was so easy that Timmy finished loading all of the groceries in one minute!

Mommy was so proud of Timmy and hugged him tight. She promised that anytime Timmy wanted to help with the groceries, he could. Timmy smiled, happy to have found something fun to do.

Once upon a time, there was a cow. He was a very soft cow, with a warm and gentle coat. The cow liked to lay in the sun and eat sweet grass with his friends.

One day, the cow found a book. It was a big book with lots of writing inside. The cow was curious and wanted to see what the book said.

He asked his friends if he should read it. His friends thought it was a great idea. So, the cow opened the book and started to read.

He read and read and read. It was difficult, but the cow kept going. After a while, he finished the book and was very proud of himself.

The cow thought that reading was fun. He went back every day and read more books. He also taught his friends to read. Pretty soon, everyone was reading!

Once upon a time, there was a harmless little mouse called Max. He wanted to build a house in the woods but he had no hammer. He asked the little birds in the trees if they had seen one but alas, they had not.

So Max decided to find a human to help him. He found a kind old lady who listened to his request. She had a hammer but she told Max that it didn't belong to him and insisted he take it back to her when he was done.

Max agreed and set off to build his house but as soon as he struck the woods with the hammer, something extraordinary happened! The trees and rocks started to move and create a house for Max! He was so delighted but he made sure to take the hammer back to the old lady.

Even though the hammer had worked its magic, the old lady still insisted Max take it back to her. Max thanked her for her kindness and promised he'd return it.

The old lady smiled and waved goodbye to Max, happy that her harmless little mouse had found a home and a way to stay safe in the woods.

Once, there was a little girl who loved to hop. One day, she hopped all the way to a pond. When she arrived, she saw a big, white goose. The goose hissed and looked dangerous.

The little girl was scared, so she stepped back a little and said, "Hello, Mr. Goose. I'm sorry I scared you."

The goose seemed angry and stood tall, with his wings spread wide. He said, "If you want to stay here, you'll have to hop away!"

The little girl was scared, but she knew she had to be brave. She took a deep breath and said, "No. I won't go. I want to stay here and play."

The goose was so surprised that he stepped back and hissed again. The little girl smiled and said, "It's okay. I just want to be friends."

The goose suddenly seemed less dangerous. He shook his feathers and said, "Well, if you want to be friends, then you'll need to hop with me around the pond."

The little girl grabbed the goose's wing and hopped around the pond. They were the best of friends and hop around the pond every day.

Once upon a time, there was a dad and a daughter. Dad was in the garden and his daughter wanted to help him, so she asked him if she could use his pin. Dad said no, but the little girl was determined. She reached out to take the pin but dad quickly smacked her hand away. "No!" he said.

The little girl was fearful but she reached out to take the pin again. She picked up the pin and held it in her hand. Dad saw her and he ran towards her, but it was too late. The pin was already in her hand.

The little girl looked up at her dad, expecting to be punished. Instead, dad's face changed. He looked sad and he gently took the pin from her hand. As he did, the pin accidentally pricked the little girl's thumb and she screamed in pain.

The next morning, dad rushed her to the hospital. The doctor told him that the little girl had been infected by a virus. Dad was very upset and wished he had been more careful.

Sadly, the virus was too powerful for the little girl and she passed away several days later. Dad was devastated and buried her in the garden, close to where the pin had been.

Once there was a small bell that lived in a school. Every morning the little bell would ring very deep and loud. The bell was so proud it could do its job.

Every day, students from far and wide would come to the school and hear the bell's deep ringing. They would come from the hills and the valleys. The ringing was so deep, it could wake up everyone in the whole town.

Some days were extra fun for the bell. It would be picked up by the sweetest children of all. The children in the school would take turns ringing it. 

The bell loved ringing so much, it wished this could go on forever. But soon, school would be over and it would have to wait until the next day to hear the children laughing and ringing the bell again.

Mollie enjoyed playing with her toys every day. One day when she was playing outside, she found an old pin. It looked interesting, so she kept it. That night, she showed her mom the pin.

Mollie's mom was troubled. She said, "Mollie, that pin does not belong to you. You must give it back to its rightful owner."

Mollie was sad. She wanted to keep the pin, so she reluctantly agreed to put it back.

The next day, Mollie went outside to return the pin. But when she found the spot where she had found it, it was gone. She was very sad. She was sure someone else now had the pin that she wanted to keep.

I went to the store with my mom. She was looking for a special plant. It had to fit in a special spot in our house. She was looking for a sunflower! We saw a big pot of bright yellow flowers. They were perfect! My mom printed some paper and we paid for them.

When we arrived home, we put the sunflower in the special spot. It fit perfectly! We gave it some water and some sunshine. It was so happy.

Every day I would sit and look at the sunflower. Its tall stem made it seem so strong. Its yellow petals were so beautiful. It looked like it was smiling!

When it was time for dinner, I would give the sunflower one last look before I went inside. Seeing it made me feel so happy. That sunflower was a perfect fit!

Every morning, Mommy would get up early and prepare breakfast for everyone. She cooked nice eggs and made toast.

But this morning was different. Mommy grabbed a special box from the cupboard and was very happy. Inside the box was a flute!

Mommy said it was a surprise and she was going to prepare a nice surprise with the flute. She began playing a song with the flute and it was so beautiful!

When Daddy and the kids woke up, they all smiled at how nice the music was. Mommy had prepared a special treat for them all. They loved it so much!

Once upon a time there was a little bird named Rupert. Rupert was always very peaceful and he loved to spend the mornings singing in the tree. One morning, Rupert was singing his song and he saw a little caterpillar named Carly walking underneath the tree.

Rupert looked down and said "Hello Carly, what are you doing down there?"

Carly said, "I'm trying to find a way to cross this river but it's so wide I don't know how I'll get over."

Rupert said, "Don't worry, I can help you! Let me fly down and I'll carry you on my neck across the river."

Carly was so excited. Rupert flew down to the river and perched on the bank. Carly climbed onto Rupert's neck and he flew over, carrying her safely across the river.

When they finally reached the other side, Rupert said, "Carly, you can now go on your way. I hope you learned that if you help others, you'll get help in return!"

Carly was very thankful for Rupert's help and with a smile she waved goodbye and continued on her way.

Rupert watched Carly go and then he flew back across the river, reversing the journey that he had taken with Carly on his neck. He was very grateful that he could help Carly and remembered the lesson that he had learnt: that it's important to help others.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jenny. She was very happy to be three. One day, Jenny asked her mom for a present. Her mom said she would have to be very good first. 

Jenny knew she wasn't always good, so she tried her very best. She shared her toys with her friends and obeyed her mom. 

When the day came to get her present, Jenny was so excited! Her mom handed her a shiny box. Jenny opened it and found a beautiful doll inside! 

Jenny was feeling so guilty she had asked for a present that she started to cry. Her mom said it was alright, that she loved Jenny no matter what. 

Jenny hugged her mom and thanked her for the present. Her mom said that no matter how bad Jenny felt, her mom would always love her.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Bob. Bob wanted to pay for some pie. He went to a shop and gave the man at the counter some money.

The man gave him a normal pie. Bob was so happy! He said thank you and took a big bite.

The pie was so yummy! Bob smiled and began to eat it quickly. When he finished, he was so full he couldn't eat any more. He paid for the pie and left the shop.

Bob said he would come back for more pie soon. He couldn't wait!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very hungry and wanted to eat a waffle. She went to her mommy and said, "Mommy, can I have a waffle please?"

Mommy said, "Sure, Lily. Let's go to the kitchen and make a waffle."

Lily was happy and excited. She went to the kitchen and helped her mommy make a waffle. When the waffle was done, Lily said, "Yummy! This waffle is normal. I can see it's going to be delicious!"

One day, a little girl named Mia found a big purple cat. The cat was very sad. Mia asked the cat, "Why are you sad?" The cat said, "I want some cream, but I don't dare to ask anyone."

Mia wanted to help the cat. She went to her mom and said, "Mom, can I have some cream for my new friend?" Her mom gave her a small bowl of cream.

Mia took the cream to the purple cat. The cat was very happy. It said, "Thank you, Mia!" The cat ate the cream and smiled. Now, Mia and the purple cat are best friends. They play together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Jane. Jane was three years old and very brave. She wanted to find something special, so she set off on an adventure.

Jane walked through a dark forest when she spotted something shiny in the sky. She looked up as a sparkly shield floated down from the stars. Jane thought it was a magical shield, so she reached up to catch it.

Jane was excited when she held the shield in her hands. It sparkled in the sun and was full of original colours. Jane imagined the amazing things that could be done with this shield.

Suddenly, a voice called out, "hello Jane!" Jane looked around but couldn't see who it was.

The voice said, "I'm the Guardian of the Magical Shield. I have been waiting for someone brave enough to find my shield. Now that you have it, use it to protect yourself and others." Jane was very happy and thanked the Guardian.

She carefully placed the original shield around her shoulders and went off to explore the world. Jane knew that with the shield, she could find all the exciting new things she was looking for.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his football. His football was the most special thing he had. One day, Timmy went to play with his friends in the park. But when he got there, he realized he forgot to unlock his door. 

Timmy was very sad because he couldn't play with his football. He tried to open the door, but it was locked. Suddenly, he remembered that his dad had given him a special key to unlock the door. Timmy found the key and unlocked the door. 

He was so happy that he could finally play with his ordinary football. Timmy and his friends played for hours until it was time to go home. Timmy went to bed that night feeling very proud of himself for unlocking the door and getting to play with his football.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a girl named Mia. Mia loved to play dress-up. She liked to try on all kinds of clothes. She had a big box full of dresses, hats, and shoes. Mia liked to make her own fashion.

One day, Mia was troubled. She could not find her favorite hat. She looked in her big box, under her bed, and in her closet. But the hat was not there. Mia was very sad.

Mia's mom saw that Mia was troubled. She told Mia to try looking in the laundry room. Mia went to the laundry room and found her favorite hat! She was so happy. Mia put on her hat and went outside to play with her friends. They all loved her fashion and had a great day playing dress-up together.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man. His name was Tom. Tom loved to cook yummy food. He made pancakes, eggs, and bacon for breakfast. He also made soup and sandwiches for lunch. For dinner, he cooked spaghetti and meatballs.

One day, Tom went to the store to buy a new motor for his car. When he got home, he put the motor in his car and fixed it. His car was now working again!

Tom was a very thoughtful man. He always helped his friends and family. He cooked meals for them and fixed things when they were broken. Everyone loved Tom because he was kind and helpful.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she was walking in the park when she saw a sad boy sitting on a bench. 

"Hi there, what's wrong?" asked Lily.

"I lost my favorite pole," replied the boy. "I can't fish without it."

Lily cared about the boy's feelings and wanted to help him. She looked around and found a cheerful yellow stick. "Here, you can use this one!" she said, handing it to him.

The boy smiled and thanked her. "This is perfect! Thank you so much!" he exclaimed. 

Lily was happy to have made a new friend and the boy was grateful for her kindness. From that day on, they would often play together in the park and go fishing with the cheerful yellow pole.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cake very much. One day, her mommy baked a cake for her. It was a big cake with lots of frosting on top. Lily was very happy and she ate the cake very quickly. 

As she ate the cake, she made loud noises because it was so yummy. Her mommy laughed and said, "Lily, you are so silly!" Lily giggled and kept eating the cake until it was all gone. 

After she finished eating, Lily felt very full and happy. She gave her mommy a big hug and said, "Thank you for the cake, mommy. It was the best cake ever!"

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big tree with red apples on it. They wanted to pick some apples and eat them.

"Look, Sam, apples!" Tim said. "Let's get some!"

"OK, Tim, but be careful. The tree is very high and the apples are very far," Sam said.

Tim and Sam found a big stick and tried to reach the apples. They pushed and pulled the stick, but they could not get any apples. They tried harder and harder, but the stick broke and fell on the ground.

"Ow, Tim, that hurt!" Sam said. "The stick hit my leg!"

"I'm sorry, Sam, I didn't mean to hurt you," Tim said. "Let's try again with another stick."

"No, Tim, I don't want to try again. It's too hard and dangerous. And maybe the apples are not good. Maybe they belong to someone else. Maybe they are unknown apples," Sam said.

"Unknown apples? What does that mean?" Tim asked.

"It means we don't know where they come from, or who they are for, or what they taste like. Maybe they are sour, or bitter, or rotten. Maybe they have worms, or bugs, or poison. Maybe they are not for us," Sam said.

"Wow, Sam, you are very smart. You know a lot of words. How do you know all that?" Tim asked.

"I know because I listen to Mom and Dad. They always tell us to be careful and respectful and not to take things that are not ours. They repeat it a lot, so I remember it," Sam said.

"Oh, I see. I should listen to Mom and Dad too. They repeat it because they love us and want us to be safe and happy. I'm sorry I didn't listen before. Let's go home and tell them we love them too," Tim said.

"OK, Tim, let's go home. And maybe they will give us some good apples that they bought from the store," Sam said.

Tim and Sam hugged and walked home. They learned that it is better to listen to their parents and not to take unknown things. They also learned that apples are not always easy to get, but they are always sweet to share.

One day, Jimmy was feeling very curious. He wanted to see what he could find and collect. So he went outside with his bucket and looked around. 

He found lots of interesting things. Small leaves, shiny stones and sticks too. But then he came across something even more fascinating. It was a battery! It was shiny and round and it made Jimmy smile. 

He put it in his bucket and kept walking. Soon, he had collected lots of things, but the battery was the best discovery of all. 

When he went back home, he showed all the items he found to his mom. He was so proud of his collection. Jimmy was so happy that he had gone out and been so curious!

Once there was a little boy who was playing in his bathtub. He had lots of fun, splashing the water with his hands. He started to get all wet so his mommy gave him a big bar of soap. 

He started to play with the soap and it made big bubbles. The little boy loved the bubbles, they felt so nice on his skin. He wanted to keep playing with them but soon they were all gone.

The little boy wanted more bubbles so he grabbed his toy alligator. He put some fake soap in the alligators mouth and splashed it in the water. Suddenly, lots of bubbles started to appear. 

The little boy was so excited to have more bubbles that he forgot he was playing in the bathtub. He had such a great time making bubbles with his alligator that he forgot to get all clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a hand and she used it to walk. She was bored of just walking. She wanted to do something more fun. 

One day, her mom told her that she could go to the park. She was so excited to go! She put on her shoes and grabbed her mom's hand. She squealed with joy. 

When they arrived, she ran around and had a lot of fun. Then, her mom said "Let's go to the lake." The little girl was confused. She didn't want to walk it, especially since the lake was far away. 

Her mom smiled and said, "We can take the car to get there! Would you like that?" The little girl was so excited. She nodded and laughed, "Yes, I would!" 

So, the little girl and her mom walked to the car, hopped in and drove to the lake. She was so happy that she wasn't bored anymore. Now, she could have a fun time at the lake.

Bob was a young boy. He had two parents and they loved him very much. They were married and Bob thought marriage was fine. Everyday, his parents spoiled him with toys and love. But one day, something changed.

Bob's parents started to fight a lot. He was so sad. He didn't understand why they were fighting. He wanted them to be happy like before. He hated seeing them fight.

One day, his father left. Bob missed him and felt very sad. But soon his mother told him that his father wouldn't be coming back. She said that they weren't married anymore.

Bob was so sad. He hated that his parents weren't married anymore. He missed his father but was glad they weren't fighting anymore. Still, he wished they could be married and happy like before.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved dinosaurs. He had a big toy dinosaur that he played with every day. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play. As they were walking, Timmy saw a big green dinosaur statue.

Timmy ran up to the statue and hugged it. He loved how comfortable it felt. Suddenly, Timmy's toy dinosaur fell out of his pocket and landed on the ground. Timmy picked it up and put it in his mouth to chew on it like he always did.

But then, something strange happened. The big green dinosaur statue started to move! It came to life and started walking towards Timmy. Timmy was scared at first, but then he realized that the dinosaur just wanted to play. They played together all day and Timmy was so happy. From that day on, Timmy knew that anything was possible and that sometimes, the things we love can come to life.

Mama and Daddy had a very special plan. They wanted to invite someone special to their house to play. But who should they invite?

Mama and Daddy both had an idea. Mama wanted to invite Grandma, while Daddy wanted to invite the neighbour. Both of them were very stubborn.

"Let's ask the little one," Mama said with a smile. So they asked the three-year-old. The little one said: "Let's invite Grandma and the neighbour!"

Mama and Daddy felt better. So they invited both Grandma and the neighbour to come play outside in the grounds. But little did they know that the two were not very friendly.

When Grandma and the neighbour met on the ground, they were not very warm. They argued for a long time about who should be there to play. Mama and Daddy were very sad.

Suddenly the argument became so loud that Mama and Daddy had to intervene. The two got so mad that they decided that they would never step on the ground together again. 

Mama and Daddy were very disappointed. Their plan to have a special playday had gone wrong. They soon learned that being stubborn can have very bad results.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her favorite suit, a pink one with flowers on it. One night, Lily went to bed and started to dream. In her dream, she was flying high in the sky and could see all the stars. Suddenly, she heard a voice saying, "You look so pretty in your suit, Lily." 

Lily turned around and saw a friendly bird who was flying next to her. "Thank you," Lily replied with a smile. "I love my suit." 

The bird then said, "I have a bitter taste in my mouth. Do you know why?" 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Maybe you ate something that wasn't yummy." 

The bird nodded and said, "You're right. I ate a worm that tasted bitter." 

Lily and the bird continued to fly together in the dream, chatting about their favorite things. When Lily woke up the next morning, she remembered her dream and smiled. She put on her pink suit and went outside to play with her friends, hoping to see the friendly bird again in her dreams.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Suzie. Suzie was very excited because her mom said they were going on a surprise. Suzie's eyes lit up as she imagined all the fun things she would do.

She hopped into the car and her mom started to drive. Suzie rubbed the window with her hand as they drove down the street. Then they stopped and her mom said "We're here!"

Suzie opened the door, and to her surprise there was a big, silly clown waiting for her. She was so happy she couldn't believe it. She ran up to the clown and hugged him tight. The clown gave her a big, stupid smile and pulled out a big box of toys for her. She laughed and thanked him.

Suzie spent the whole day playing with the clown and her toys. She was so happy and excited, she couldn't help but rub her hands together with joy. What a surprise!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lu. She loved to laugh and play. One day, she went to the park with her family. Lu was so excited to ride on the slides and play on the swings. 

At the park, there were two boys who were teasing Lu. They laughed at her and made fun of Lu. But Lu stayed very brave and she didn't let them make her cry. 

Then it was time for Lu to go home. After a long day, she was happy to jump onto her mattress. It was soft and it was quiet on the mattress. Lu was happy and calm. 

But soon, some noisy noise came from the living room. It sounded like the two boys were still teasing Lu! The noise was very loud. Lu didn't like it one bit. 

But then, her mom and dad called the boys over to their home. They gave them a big hug and told them that teasing is not nice. Lu was happy to know that her family was looking out for her.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Sarah and Harry. Sarah was dependable and always eager to help. One day, Sarah and Harry were playing with cars and dollies in the garden. 

Suddenly, Sarah heard her mom calling from inside the house, "Sarah, can you please help Mommy in the kitchen?". 

Sarah quickly ran inside to help. When she arrived, she saw her mom looking for a fork in one of the kitchen drawers. Sarah opened the drawer and smiled as she spotted the fork. She gave it to her mom, saying "Mommy, here's the fork". 

Her mom smiled. "Oh, thank you Sarah", she said. She gave a Sarah a hug and said "I knew I could always depend on you". 

Sarah was very happy and knew that she had helped her mom. She ran back outside to tell Harry the good news. 

The two friends laughed and smiled together. They knew that Sarah was dependable and always ready to help.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She had long dark hair and big brown eyes. 

Every day Sarah would go to the river to bathe. She liked to sing her songs while she was playing with the fishes. One day, Sarah was in the river and she noticed a veil floating near her. 

"What is this?" said Sarah. She picked up the veil and tried it on. It made her feel special.

A moment later, some boys came by and saw Sarah in the veil. They started to laugh at her, which made Sarah feel very ashamed. She quickly took off the veil, tucked it under her arm and ran away. 

But in the morning, Sarah felt brave. She went back to the river and put the veil back in the water. 

Then she smiled, said goodbye to the veil and went back home.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Tom. Tom had a big imagination. Every day, he would pretend to be something different. Today, he wanted to be a postman.

Tom took out a piece of paper and some crayons. He drew a picture of a letter on the paper and he pretended to put a stamp on it. He smiled and said, "I'm a postman and this letter is for my friend."

Tom ran to his friend's house and gave her the letter. His friend opened the letter and found a healthy snack inside. She smiled and said, "Thank you for the letter, Tom! It was very nice of you to bring me a present!"

Tom was so happy to hear this. He waved goodbye to his friend and went back home, pretending to be a postman again. He was on a mission to deliver his letters to everyone he could find.

Once upon a time there was a rabbit who was very alert. She was always watching to see what animals were around. One day she was out hopping in the grass when she heard a loud noise. It was a hammer.

"Hello!" she said, "Who is there?"

The hammer answered back.

"It's me," he said. "I am a hammer and I am here to help build something."

The rabbit thought this was a great idea. She crawled over to the hammer to take a closer look.

"What are you making?" she asked.

The hammer replied, "I am building a house for the other animals. We have to work together to get it done in time."

The rabbit was so excited that she started helping the hammer. Together they worked to build the house and soon it was finished. All the animals were so grateful for the new house and they thanked the rabbit and the hammer.

The rabbit was alert and happy that she had been able to help out. She hopped away into the sunset, and all the animals were happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She had a scooter and she loved it. She was so cheerful about riding around.

One day, she was riding her scooter when she noticed a butterfly. She got off her scooter so she could watch the butterfly. Suddenly, it flew away. She felt sad.

But then, she had an idea! She got back on her scooter and started to ride. She shouted, "I'm gonna release you!" She watched the butterfly fly away.

She was so happy! The butterfly was free and she was free to ride her scooter again. The little girl smiled as she rode, feeling cheerful and free.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to have a race to see who could run the fastest. Timmy was determined to win.

As the race started, Timmy ran as fast as he could. He felt his heart beating fast and his breath getting tight. But he didn't give up. He kept running and running until he finally reached the finish line. He raised his arms up in victory and shouted, "I won!"

His friends came over and congratulated him. "You did it, Timmy! You ran so fast!" one of them said. Timmy smiled and waved at them. "Thanks, guys! It was a tough race, but I did it!" he replied.

From that day on, Timmy felt proud of himself for winning the race. He knew that if he worked hard and never gave up, he could achieve anything he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to drive his toy car around the house. One day, he went to the park with his mom and dad. They played on the swings and slides. Timmy loved the rhythm of the swings.

After playing, they went to get ice cream. Timmy wanted a smelly flavor, like stinky cheese. But his mom and dad said no, so he chose chocolate instead. They drove home in their car, singing songs and laughing.

Suddenly, a big truck crashed into their car. Timmy was scared and hurt. His mom and dad were hurt too. They went to the hospital, but the doctors couldn't save them. Timmy was now alone and sad. He missed his mom and dad very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she found a rope on the ground. She picked it up and saw that it had a knot in the middle. She tried to untie the knot, but it was too hard. So, she decided to stretch the rope to see if it would come undone. 

Lily pulled and pulled on the rope until it finally stretched enough for her to untie the knot. She was so happy and proud of herself for being so strong. She decided to share her rope with her friends and they all played tug-of-war together. 

Lily was very generous and let her friends have turns with the rope. They all had so much fun playing together in the sunshine. From that day on, Lily always looked for ways to help her friends and be a generous little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy princess who had found some treasure. She was so happy, she started to spin around. 

The princess spun and spun until she was so dizzy, she couldn't stand. She fell onto the ground and the treasure went flying all over the place. 

Suddenly, a small mouse appeared and asked, "Why are you spinning, Princess?" 

The princess replied, "I was so excited about finding this treasure that I got carried away!"

The mouse smiled, and said, "That's okay! Let's gather up the treasure and you can spin all you want!" 

So the two of them gathered up all the treasure, and the princess spun until she was dizzy again. 

When everything was back in its place, the mouse said, "That was so fun! We should do it again!"

The princess replied, "Yes, let's! I'm never going to stop spinning!"

And so the princess and the mouse enjoyed their spinning treasure adventure every day.

Once upon a time there was a girl. Her name was Sue. Every day Sue loved to dance. 

One day, Sue asked her mommy for a special pair of gloves. Her mommy said yes and gave her a pair of red gloves that sparkled in the sun.

Sue put on her new gloves and danced in her backyard. She spun and twirled until the sun started to set. Soon the air was getting hot.

Sue took off the red gloves and put them into her pocket. She kept on dancing until her mommy called her inside.

The next day, Sue put on the red gloves and danced some more! She was so happy that she had a special way to dance and keep cool.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. Jack always wanted to play outside, but he was not allowed to go too fast. One day, Jack couldn't help but speed around the garden. His mom saw and quickly ran to get his apron. She put it on Jack and said, now you can play out here but be sure to go at a mild speed. 

Jack was so happy to be able to play, and he happily ran around in his apron. He chased his friends and went down the slide at a mild speed. Suddenly, Jack started to speed and his apron swished in the wind. Jack's mom called for him to come back and slow down, but Jack wanted to play a bit longer.

In the end, Jack's mom let him play at a mild speed as long as he wanted! Jack enjoyed playing and having fun with his friends, all while wearing his apron and going at a mild speed.
